name: Booru
description: A large, widely used tag set, mainly for illustrations. No franchises, characters or artists. Contains NSFW tags.

entries.name: 1girl
entries.description: Exactly one female character is shown, the most common of the count tags. Dolls count when they act on their own, a [figure](#figure) inside a painting only when she is central to the work, and an implied presence never does.

entries.name: solo
entries.description: Exactly one person appears in the picture, with [no](#no) other characters anywhere in frame and only one copy of that character. Does not [cover](#cover) multiple views of the same character, [dual_persona](#dual_persona), or [time_paradox](#time_paradox); when the person is the focus among [faceless](#faceless) background [people](#people), use [solo_focus](#solo_focus) instead.

entries.name: 1boy
entries.description: Exactly one male character is shown. A [doll](#doll) or similar [figure](#figure) counts only when it acts under its own power, a man inside a painting or poster only when he matters to the work, and someone merely implied off-screen not at all.

entries.name: multiple_girls
entries.description: More than one female character appears in the picture. Pair it with the exact count — [2girls](#2girls), [3girls](#3girls) and so on — wherever the number [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: 2girls
entries.description: Two female characters are shown. Animate dolls count, a [figure](#figure) inside a painting or photograph counts only when she matters to the work, and an implied presence does not.

entries.name: multiple_boys
entries.description: More than one male character appears in the picture. Pair it with the exact count — [2boys](#2boys), [3boys](#3boys) and so on — wherever the number [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: 2boys
entries.description: Two male characters are shown. Dolls count only when they act under their own power, a man inside a painting only when he is central to the work, and someone implied off-screen not at all.

entries.name: 3girls
entries.description: Three female characters are shown. Animate dolls count, a [figure](#figure) inside a painting only when she matters to the work, and someone merely implied does not.

entries.name: 4girls
entries.description: Four female characters are shown. Animate dolls count, painted or photographed figures only when they matter to the work, and implied ones do not.

entries.name: 6+girls
entries.description: Six or more female characters share the picture. Animate dolls count, figures on paintings, photographs or statues only when they matter to the work, and someone addressed off-screen does not.

entries.name: 3boys
entries.description: Three male characters are shown. Dolls count only when they act on their own, painted or photographed figures only when central to the work, and implied ones not at all.

entries.name: 1other
entries.description: One character whose [sex](#sex) cannot be [determined](#determined): the face is hidden, the design is [androgynous](#androgynous), the being has [no](#no) sex, or it was never settled. Visible traits move it to [1girl](#1girl) or [1boy](#1boy), and animals and [futanari](#futanari) are outside it.

entries.name: 5girls
entries.description: Five female characters are shown, the top of the [numbered](#numbered) girl tags; six or more take [6+girls](#6+girls). Animate dolls count and an implied presence does not.

entries.name: 4boys
entries.description: Four male characters are shown. Dolls count only when animate, a [figure](#figure) inside a painting only when central to the work, and an implied presence not at all.

entries.name: 6+boys
entries.description: Six or more male characters share the picture. Dolls count only when they act on their own, painted figures only when central to the work, and an implied [crowd](#crowd) off-screen not at all.

entries.name: 5boys
entries.description: Five male characters are shown, the highest of the [numbered](#numbered) boy tags; anything beyond takes [6+boys](#6+boys). Dolls count only when animate and merely implied figures not at all.

entries.name: multiple_others
entries.description: More than one character whose [sex](#sex) is ambiguous or absent — robots, creatures and figures the picture never settles. It is the counterpart of [multiple_boys](#multiple_boys) and [multiple_girls](#multiple_girls).

entries.name: everyone
entries.description: The picture [gathers](#gathers) all, or nearly all, of a series' [cast](#cast). Add character_request if some of them cannot be named. Vast crossovers of fifty figures and more take [absolutely_everyone](#absolutely_everyone) instead.

entries.name: 2others
entries.description: Two characters whose [sex](#sex) is ambiguous, undetermined or outside the male-female [split](#split). Pair it with [ambiguous_gender](#ambiguous_gender) or [androgynous](#androgynous) where those fit; dolls count only when animate and implied figures never do.

entries.name: 2futa
entries.description: Exactly two [futanari](#futanari) characters appear, counted the same way the boy and girl counts are. Other [people](#people) may share the picture with them without changing the number.

entries.name: 3others
entries.description: Three characters whose [sex](#sex) is ambiguous, undetermined or non-binary. Add [ambiguous_gender](#ambiguous_gender) or [androgynous](#androgynous) where they fit; only animate dolls count and implied figures do not.

entries.name: 6+others
entries.description: Six or more characters of ambiguous, undetermined or non-binary [sex](#sex). Combine with [ambiguous_gender](#ambiguous_gender) or [androgynous](#androgynous) where those fit; dolls count only when animate.

entries.name: group_picture
entries.description: A picture of at least three characters arranged so each gets roughly equal [space](#space) and attention, like a team photo. Not for one character in focus with the rest pushed to the background.

entries.name: 4others
entries.description: Four characters of ambiguous, undetermined or non-binary [sex](#sex). Add [ambiguous_gender](#ambiguous_gender) or [androgynous](#androgynous) where those apply; animate dolls count and implied figures never do.

entries.name: absolutely_everyone
entries.description: The picture is [crowded](#crowded) with an absurd number of characters, fifty or more as a rough [guide](#guide). It usually [gathers](#gathers) the whole [cast](#cast) of a long series or every member of some [sweeping](#sweeping) category.

entries.name: 5others
entries.description: Five characters whose [sex](#sex) is ambiguous, undetermined or non-binary. Only animate figures count, so faces inside a painting or someone merely spoken to off-screen do not.

entries.name: male_focus
entries.description: Only male characters appear, or the picture rests overwhelmingly on them. It does not apply where a man is incidental to a [landscape](#landscape) or some other subject.

entries.name: solo_focus
entries.description: Several [people](#people) are present, but the picture is built around only one of them, with the rest anonymous, [faceless](#faceless), [cropped](#cropped), or reduced to background figures such as bystanders or an out-of-frame partner. When nobody else is visible at all, use [solo](#solo) instead.

entries.name: no_humans
entries.description: Nothing human or humanlike appears, which rules out androids, youkai, living dolls, [monster](#monster) girls and furries too. What is left is [scenery](#scenery), animals, plants or objects.

entries.name: other_focus
entries.description: The picture is about characters of [no](#no) or ambiguous gender, such as robots, mascots or genderless creatures, with [people](#people) at most incidental. Not for a scene where such a character is only a minor element beside [scenery](#scenery) or a human subject.

entries.name: artist_self-insert
entries.description: The artist appears inside their own picture, as a [portrait](#portrait), an avatar, an invented persona, or an existing character [standing](#standing) in for them. Common in [comic](#comic) strips and commentary drawings.

entries.name: clone
entries.description: Two or more identical copies of one character share a scene, dressed alike and reacting to each other. Not for a character who merely is somebody's clone, and not for [multiple_views](#multiple_views), where separate drawings share [no](#no) [space](#space).

entries.name: crowd
entries.description: A mass of bystanders filling the scene, generally drawn without faces or full detail and sometimes merging into one another. They are background, with the actual subjects tagged separately.

entries.name: people
entries.description: Anonymous background figures filling out a scene without being its subject, drawn small, distant or indistinct. They do not count toward [multiple_girls](#multiple_girls) or [multiple_boys](#multiple_boys); where there are many, use [crowd](#crowd).

entries.name: cameo
entries.description: A character from some other work turns up in passing: in the [crowd](#crowd), on a poster, as a [figure](#figure), charm or [phone](#phone) [strap](#strap). They are decoration rather than the subject of the picture.

entries.name: audience
entries.description: A [crowd](#crowd) gathered to [watch](#watch) something, generally seated or [standing](#standing) before a [stage](#stage) and turned toward it. Tag the performance itself as [well](#well), such as [concert](#concert) or stage.

entries.name: crowded
entries.description: So many [people](#people) packed into the scene that the press of bodies is what the picture is about, rather than any one [figure](#figure). Trains, festivals and busy [shopping](#shopping) streets are the usual settings.

entries.name: not_present
entries.description: A [gag](#gag) for [crowded](#crowded) group pictures: somebody who could not be fitted into the scene appears only as a small [portrait](#portrait) pasted into a [corner](#corner), as if asking not to be forgotten. It shows up on [cast](#cast) line-ups and yearbook shots.

entries.name: clothes_only
entries.description: The picture shows garments by themselves, with [no](#no) character present at all, worn or otherwise. Typical of [costume](#costume) design sheets and [merchandise](#merchandise) illustrations.

entries.name: age_difference
entries.description: Two or more [people](#people) interacting with a plainly visible gap in age, read from build, [height](#height) and [facial](#facial) maturity alone. It does not apply where the gap is only known from outside the picture.

entries.name: mature_female
entries.description: A woman drawn as attractive and middle-aged: softened lines on the face, a fuller [belly](#belly) and a curvier build than a younger character gets. Simply being a mother in the story is not enough on its own; she has to look older.

entries.name: child
entries.description: A character of either [sex](#sex) who is plainly a young child. A short character with adult proportions is [petite](#petite) and one drawn younger than their usual age is [aged_down](#aged_down); sexual or suggestive pictures take loli or shota, which this [tag](#tag) excludes.

entries.name: mature_male
entries.description: A man drawn as attractive and middle-aged or older, often with visible [facial](#facial) or body hair. Pair with [old_man](#old_man) when an elderly man is drawn in an appealing rather than frail way.

entries.name: old
entries.description: A character who reads as elderly, roughly past fifty or sixty, with grey hair, lined skin or a bent frame. A normally young character drawn at a greater age takes [aged_up](#aged_up) instead.

entries.name: old_man
entries.description: An elderly male character, greying or [balding](#balding) with lined skin. Add [mature_male](#mature_male) where he is drawn as attractive; a younger man aged past his usual years is [aged_up](#aged_up).

entries.name: baby
entries.description: A very young [child](#child), newly or recently born, generally held, [swaddled](#swaddled), [lying](#lying) in a cot or being fed. Once the child is up and [walking](#walking), [toddler](#toddler) or child is the better fit.

entries.name: old_woman
entries.description: An elderly female character with grey hair and lined skin. Pair it with [mature_female](#mature_female) where she is drawn as attractive; a young woman aged forward is [aged_up](#aged_up).

entries.name: toddler
entries.description: A very small [child](#child) past infancy who moves about on their own, roughly three to five years [old](#old). Older than a [baby](#baby) and younger than a child; keep it away from sexual pictures, which have their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: lolibaba
entries.description: A character with a child's body who is in [truth](#truth) far older, given away by archaic speech, an elderly manner or dialogue that says so outright. The gap between appearance and age is the whole point.

entries.name: osugaki
entries.description: A cheeky young boy who taunts and provokes adults, usually in a sexual register. The masculine counterpart to the [mesugaki](#mesugaki) archetype, and generally overlapping with shota.

entries.name: otoko_no_ko
entries.description: A male character feminine enough in look or manner to pass as a girl, whether or not he is [crossdressing](#crossdressing). If his [sex](#sex) is [plain](#plain) from a thumbnail without seeing genitals, this is not the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: crossdressing
entries.description: Wearing [clothes](#clothes) conventionally cut for the other [sex](#sex): a man in a [dress](#dress), a woman in a [tuxedo](#tuxedo). Covers both directions, including men whose [disguise](#disguise) fools nobody; a convincingly feminine male takes [otoko_no_ko](#otoko_no_ko). A [futanari](#futanari) in menswear counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: androgynous
entries.description: Face or body drawn so that whether the [figure](#figure) is male or female cannot be settled, which many [otoko_no_ko](#otoko_no_ko), [bishounen](#bishounen) and [reverse_trap](#reverse_trap) designs play on. Where the ambiguity comes only from clothing, angle or distance, [ambiguous_gender](#ambiguous_gender) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: crossdressing_(mtf)
entries.description: A male character in women's clothing, whether a [dress](#dress), a [skirt](#skirt) or a girl's uniform. Applies equally to a convincing look and an obvious [gag](#gag).

entries.name: bishounen
entries.description: A pretty boy drawn with delicate features, slender eyes, long lashes, flowing hair and long limbs, whose beauty is the point of the picture. He should still read as male: add [androgynous](#androgynous) for strongly feminine traits, and [otoko_no_ko](#otoko_no_ko) when he could pass for a girl.

entries.name: tomboy
entries.description: A girl who acts in a boyish, sporty way, usually dressed like a boy and often short-haired. Behaviour is the criterion; short hair alone does not qualify, and a masculine look without the attitude is [reverse_trap](#reverse_trap) instead.

entries.name: manly
entries.description: A picture [leaning](#leaning) hard on conventional machismo: [heavy](#heavy) muscle, wide stances, [weightlifting](#weightlifting), a fight about to break out. Often sits beside [muscular](#muscular) and [male_focus](#male_focus).

entries.name: ambiguous_gender
entries.description: The picture gives [no](#no) way to tell whether a [figure](#figure) is male or female, because they are in full armour, far off or barely in frame. Where the features are visible but deliberately in between, [androgynous](#androgynous) fits instead.

entries.name: reverse_trap
entries.description: A female character whose looks and manner read as masculine enough that other characters mistake her for a boy until told otherwise, often dressed accordingly. If the [sex](#sex) is obvious from a thumbnail alone the [tag](#tag) does not apply; [tomboy](#tomboy) is the milder, overlapping neighbour.

entries.name: male_maid
entries.description: A male character wearing [maid](#maid) [dress](#dress), a common form of [crossdressing](#crossdressing). The mirrored case, a woman in butler's [clothes](#clothes), is [female_butler](#female_butler).

entries.name: crossdressing_(ftm)
entries.description: A female character dressed in menswear, from a tailored [suit](#suit) to a boy's [school](#school) uniform. It [notes](#notes) what she is wearing, not that she is being presented as male.

entries.name: jimiko
entries.description: A [plain](#plain), mousy or unassuming girl, drawn with [glasses](#glasses), [unkempt](#unkempt) hair, thick eyebrows, braids or [twintails](#twintails), [freckles](#freckles) or tired eyes. It describes bearing and look rather than actual homeliness.

entries.name: girly_boy
entries.description: A boy who reads plainly as male but behaves in a markedly feminine way, through coquettish [posing](#posing), an interest in [fashion](#fashion) and cute things, or [makeup](#makeup) and jewellery. Different from [otoko_no_ko](#otoko_no_ko), where the body rather than the manner is feminine, and wearing a [dress](#dress) alone does not qualify.

entries.name: fabulous
entries.description: A male character [playing](#playing) it flamboyant and theatrical: grand [poses](#poses), sparkles, rainbows, pastel flourishes. It says nothing about his build or about who he is drawn to.

entries.name: siblings
entries.description: Two or more [brothers](#brothers) and/or [sisters](#sisters) appear together in the picture. Narrow it with sisters or brothers when the sexes match; a mixed pair is covered by [brother_and_sister](#brother_and_sister).

entries.name: couple
entries.description: Two [people](#people) shown to be fond of each other, both present in the picture and both taking part. One partner shying away, or a canon pairing doing nothing [affectionate](#affectionate), does not qualify, and consensual [sex](#sex) alone is not enough.

entries.name: sisters
entries.description: Two or more sisters share the picture. A subset of [siblings](#siblings); [brothers](#brothers) is the male counterpart.

entries.name: parent_and_child
entries.description: A parent shown together with their [child](#child), without saying which of either. Prefer the specific pairing wherever it is clear, such as [mother_and_daughter](#mother_and_daughter) or [father_and_son](#father_and_son), and leave this vague one alone.

entries.name: twins
entries.description: Two [siblings](#siblings) born together, in anime most often drawn as identical-looking girls. Also applies to characters established as fraternal twins even when their appearance differs.

entries.name: brother_and_sister
entries.description: One boy and one girl who share parents, shown together. Since kinship is hard to read off a picture, it is safest on named characters known to be related; add [brothers](#brothers) or [sisters](#sisters) when more of either appear.

entries.name: mother_and_child
entries.description: A mother together with her [child](#child) where the child's [sex](#sex) is unclear or simply beside the point. It also covers pairs who are not related at all and are only [playing](#playing) at the relationship.

entries.name: mother_and_daughter
entries.description: A mother and her daughter together: either a girl beside a clearly older woman, or two named characters whose story establishes them as such. Where the child's [sex](#sex) cannot be read, the general mother-and-child [tag](#tag) applies.

entries.name: brothers
entries.description: Two or more males who share a parent, shown together. A brother pictured with his sister is [brother_and_sister](#brother_and_sister).

entries.name: mother_and_son
entries.description: A mother and her son together: a boy beside a visibly older woman, or two named characters known to stand in that relationship. If the child's [sex](#sex) is unclear, use the general mother-and-child [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bride
entries.description: A woman, or a man dressed as one, appearing as the bride at a [wedding](#wedding), typically in a long white [gown](#gown) with a [veil](#veil) and a [bouquet](#bouquet). The outfit takes [wedding_dress](#wedding_dress) and [bridal_veil](#bridal_veil), the partner is [groom](#groom), and the occasion is wedding.

entries.name: father_and_daughter
entries.description: A father and his daughter together, whether two characters known to be related or a young girl beside a clearly older man in a parental scene. A non-sexual relationship [tag](#tag); the whole household is [family](#family).

entries.name: family
entries.description: Parents together with their children as a household, the group complete; guardians count and grandparents may join them. A single parent with one [child](#child) takes the specific pair [tag](#tag) such as [mother_and_daughter](#mother_and_daughter).

entries.name: husband_and_wife
entries.description: A married man and woman appear together, whether canonically married or clearly shown as such by [wedding](#wedding) rings or a ceremony. If the marriage happens later in a story, the picture should show them after it.

entries.name: father_and_son
entries.description: A father and his son together, either known relatives or a boy with a much older man in a parental scene. A non-sexual relationship [tag](#tag); for the household as a whole use [family](#family).

entries.name: friends
entries.description: Two or more characters shown as close companions with an evident bond, outside romance and outside [family](#family) ties. Playful or [affectionate](#affectionate) interaction between them is the usual signal.

entries.name: wife_and_wife
entries.description: Two women shown together as each other's wife, whether canonically married or simply depicted that way. If the marriage happens later in the story, something in the picture, such as a [wedding](#wedding) [ring](#ring), should show they are already wed.

entries.name: cousins
entries.description: Two or more characters who are cousins, [sharing](#sharing) grandparents or some other ancestor. A [plain](#plain) [family](#family) relationship with nothing sexual attached.

entries.name: look-alike
entries.description: Two or more different characters who resemble one another closely enough for the likeness to be the point, whether from one series or from separate ones. The same character appearing twice is [dual_persona](#dual_persona) or [multiple_persona](#multiple_persona) instead.

entries.name: teenage_girl_and_younger_boy
entries.description: A pairing in which an adolescent girl is plainly older than the boy beside her, the gap in [height](#height) and build making it obvious. Used for sibling, babysitting and similar pairings.

entries.name: groom
entries.description: A man, or a cross-dressing woman, being married at a [wedding](#wedding), typically in a [tuxedo](#tuxedo) or formal [suit](#suit) beside a [bride](#bride).

entries.name: triplets
entries.description: Three [siblings](#siblings) born together, most often drawn as identical look-alikes; a fraternal set is simply three [people](#people) known to share a birth despite looking different. The identical version is by far the more common depiction.

entries.name: step-siblings
entries.description: Characters who are [siblings](#siblings) only through adoption or a parent's marriage, [sharing](#sharing) [no](#no) [blood](#blood). Covers any mix of sexes; [step-brothers](#step-brothers), [step-sisters](#step-sisters) and [step-brother_and_step-sister](#step-brother_and_step-sister) say which.

entries.name: aunt_and_nephew
entries.description: A boy appears together with his mother's or father's sister. It is the [family](#family) relationship being recorded, not any particular activity between them.

entries.name: sextuplets
entries.description: Six [siblings](#siblings) born at once, drawn as a set and very often identical. Rare enough in fiction that the Matsuno [brothers](#brothers) are the standard example.

entries.name: aunt_and_niece
entries.description: A girl appears together with her mother's or father's sister. The [tag](#tag) records the [family](#family) tie rather than what the two are doing.

entries.name: country_connection
entries.description: The characters brought together in the picture all come from the same country or birthplace, and that shared origin is why they appear side by side. It also covers a single character shown among the sights and symbols of their homeland.

entries.name: uncle_and_niece
entries.description: A man shown together with his sibling's daughter. The [family](#family) tie between the two is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: husband_and_husband
entries.description: Two men in the picture are married to one another, in canon or as the art presents them. Rings or a [wedding](#wedding) setting usually carry the point.

entries.name: rivalry
entries.description: Two characters set against each other in a contest of superiority, from sparring glares to open [competition](#competition). It need not turn violent, and when it does the tone is often playful rather than hostile.

entries.name: quintuplets
entries.description: Five [siblings](#siblings) born of the same birth, usually drawn at the same age and often the same [sex](#sex). Rare enough in fiction that a single well-known manga [family](#family) dominates how the [tag](#tag) gets used.

entries.name: grandfather_and_grandson
entries.description: An older man shown together with his grandson, two generations in one picture. What they are doing does not matter for the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: polygamy
entries.description: One person married to several spouses, drawn as a shared household or a group [wedding](#wedding). Usually one man with several wives, though the reverse arrangement appears too.

entries.name: grandmother_and_granddaughter
entries.description: An older woman shown with her son's or daughter's daughter. Fiction being what it is, the grandmother is often drawn looking [no](#no) older than the girl.

entries.name: rivals
entries.description: The pair themselves, presented as each other's opposite number. The relationship is competitive but not necessarily hostile, and often carries mutual respect.

entries.name: grandfather_and_granddaughter
entries.description: An older man pictured together with his son's or daughter's daughter. The [family](#family) tie is what is recorded, whatever the two are doing.

entries.name: half-siblings
entries.description: Brothers and [sisters](#sisters) who share only one parent. A [family](#family) [label](#label) rather than something visible in the drawing itself.

entries.name: grandmother_and_grandson
entries.description: An older woman pictured together with her grandson. The relationship alone is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: uncle_and_nephew
entries.description: A man shown together with his sibling's son. The [family](#family) tie between the two is what the [tag](#tag) records, whatever they are doing in the scene.

entries.name: male_harem
entries.description: One character [surrounded](#surrounded) by three or more men who all show open affection for them, the [mirror](#mirror) of the usual [harem](#harem) setup. With only two admirers it is a boy [sandwich](#sandwich) instead.

entries.name: step-sisters
entries.description: Two or more girls related as [sisters](#sisters) through adoption or a parent's remarriage instead of by birth.

entries.name: master_and_servant
entries.description: Two characters in a service relationship, one plainly attending on the other: [pouring](#pouring) [tea](#tea), [kneeling](#kneeling), [holding](#holding) out a [coat](#coat). Covers butlers, maids and retainers with the person they wait on.

entries.name: husband_and_wives
entries.description: One man appears with two or more women he is married to. A polygamous arrangement rather than an ordinary [couple](#couple).

entries.name: step-brother_and_step-sister
entries.description: A boy and a girl who count as [siblings](#siblings) through adoption or through their parents marrying, with [no](#no) [blood](#blood) between them. The relationship itself is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: ancestor_and_descendant
entries.description: Two figures separated by generations appear together, one descended from the other. Time-travel and family-legacy pictures use it, and the [family](#family) resemblance is usually the point.

entries.name: siscon
entries.description: A character whose behavior toward a sister goes to extremes, whether doting, boastful or outright unsettling. Covers sister-like bonds without a [blood](#blood) relation, but not a mutual romance, which belongs with the [incest](#incest) tags.

entries.name: step-brothers
entries.description: Two or more boys who became [brothers](#brothers) by adoption or by a parent's remarriage rather than by birth. Nothing about the picture beyond that connection is implied.

entries.name: family_portrait
entries.description: A deliberately composed group image of relatives, at least a parent with their children, arranged the way a photograph or a painted [portrait](#portrait) would be.

entries.name: creator_and_creation
entries.description: A character appears together with the real person who made them, be that author, artist or designer. Usually drawn for an [anniversary](#anniversary) or a farewell.

entries.name: maid
entries.description: A character in Western-style domestic service [dress](#dress), marked out by a white frilled [headdress](#headdress) and [apron](#apron) over a [dark](#dark) dress. Japanese-styled maids are [wa_maid](#wa_maid), and somebody not usually in service put into the outfit also takes [enmaided](#enmaided).

entries.name: waitress
entries.description: A character in a waitress uniform, whatever their gender, [serving](#serving) [food](#food) or [drink](#drink) in a [restaurant](#restaurant) or [cafe](#cafe). Do not mix up with [maid](#maid) even when the uniform looks similar; chain-specific uniforms have their own tags.

entries.name: butler
entries.description: A male household servant in formal [dress](#dress) — [tailcoat](#tailcoat), [waistcoat](#waistcoat) and [gloves](#gloves) — attending a wealthy employer. The counterpart to the [maid](#maid) in domestic settings.

entries.name: chef
entries.description: Somebody shown as a professional cook, marked out by the [double-breasted](#double-breasted) white or black [jacket](#jacket), [tall](#tall) or pillbox [hat](#hat) and [apron](#apron). The hat by itself is [chef_hat](#chef_hat), and the act of preparing [food](#food) is [cooking](#cooking).

entries.name: bartender
entries.description: The person [serving](#serving) drinks behind a bar [counter](#counter), often in a [waistcoat](#waistcoat) and [bow](#bow) tie, [shaking](#shaking) a [cocktail](#cocktail) or [polishing](#polishing) a [glass](#glass). Add [bar_(place)](#bar_(place)) for the setting.

entries.name: waiter
entries.description: A man [serving](#serving) at a [restaurant](#restaurant) or [cafe](#cafe), taking orders and bringing [food](#food) to tables, usually in a waiter's uniform. The female counterpart is [waitress](#waitress).

entries.name: travel_attendant
entries.description: Cabin or [carriage](#carriage) [staff](#staff) who look after passengers aboard planes, ships and sleeper trains. Recognisable by a service uniform, [neckerchief](#neckerchief) and cap that mark the job.

entries.name: flight_attendant
entries.description: Cabin crew employed by an airline to look after passengers in the air, shown in the trim [jacket](#jacket), [scarf](#scarf) and small cap of the job. The person's role is what is tagged; the outfit alone is a uniform.

entries.name: female_butler
entries.description: A woman in the [tailcoat](#tailcoat), [waistcoat](#waistcoat) and white [gloves](#gloves) of a [butler](#butler) rather than in [maid](#maid) [dress](#dress). The [mirror](#mirror) image of a man in a maid outfit.

entries.name: victorian_maid
entries.description: A household servant in period [dress](#dress) rather than the short frilly modern outfit: floor-length [skirt](#skirt), long [apron](#apron) and a soft mob cap. The clothing marks her as [staff](#staff) of the nineteenth century.

entries.name: oiran
entries.description: A courtesan of the highest rank in the [old](#old) pleasure quarters, dressed in layered [kimono](#kimono) with the [obi](#obi) knotted at the front and a [crown](#crown) of hairpins. She is not a [geisha](#geisha), who dresses far more soberly and sells [no](#no) such company.

entries.name: store_clerk
entries.description: Somebody [working](#working) the [counter](#counter) of a convenience store or a small [shop](#shop), usually in the shop's [apron](#apron) or uniform. The job is what the [tag](#tag) names, not the [building](#building).

entries.name: barista
entries.description: Someone [working](#working) the [counter](#counter) of a [cafe](#cafe), [pulling](#pulling) espresso and steaming [milk](#milk), usually in an [apron](#apron). Keep the role apart from a [bartender](#bartender), who serves [alcohol](#alcohol).

entries.name: cashier
entries.description: The worker who takes payment at a [shop](#shop) or convenience store till, usually uniformed and [standing](#standing) behind the register. Often shown handing [back](#back) change or a bagged purchase.

entries.name: carhop
entries.description: A server who carries [food](#food) out to customers [waiting](#waiting) in their cars at a drive-in. Nearly always drawn as the American 1950s [figure](#figure): uniform, roller [skates](#skates) and a [tray](#tray) of burgers and shakes.

entries.name: nakai_(waitress)
entries.description: A [waitress](#waitress) at a traditional Japanese inn or [restaurant](#restaurant), generally in [kimono](#kimono) and [apron](#apron). She serves guests at low tables in [tatami](#tatami) rooms rather than across a [counter](#counter).

entries.name: yuujo
entries.description: A courtesan of pre-modern Japan, typically drawn in a [kimono](#kimono) [slipping](#slipping) loosely off the shoulders with an elaborate hairstyle bristling with ornamental pins. Common settings are a lavish [interior](#interior) or a night-time [bridge](#bridge), with the more accomplished [oiran](#oiran) ranked above ordinary practitioners.

entries.name: croupier
entries.description: The dealer [working](#working) a [casino](#casino) [table](#table), handing out cards or [spinning](#spinning) the [wheel](#wheel), taking in bets and paying out. Women are usually drawn in a [waistcoat](#waistcoat) over a [shirt](#shirt) and [necktie](#necktie), with a [miniskirt](#miniskirt) or slacks below.

entries.name: hostess
entries.description: A woman [working](#working) as a paid companion in a club, [pouring](#pouring) drinks and keeping male customers [talking](#talking). She is usually shown dressed up in a bar setting.

entries.name: barmaid
entries.description: A woman [serving](#serving) drinks in a bar or [tavern](#tavern), frequently [carrying](#carrying) several [beer](#beer) steins at once. Medieval and [fantasy](#fantasy) settings are where she appears most.

entries.name: merchant
entries.description: Someone who trades goods for a living, from a shopkeeper behind a [counter](#counter) to a traveling peddler with a pack of wares. Covers both fixed shops and itinerant dealers.

entries.name: ninja
entries.description: A covert agent or mercenary of Japanese tradition, trained in stealth, [disguise](#disguise) and unorthodox [fighting](#fighting). A female one is a kunoichi, which is the same [tag](#tag) here.

entries.name: police
entries.description: Anything to do with the police: officers, their uniforms, cars, stations, and equipment, or a scene of an [arrest](#arrest). Add [police_uniform](#police_uniform), [policewoman](#policewoman), or [police_car](#police_car) for the specifics.

entries.name: knight
entries.description: An armoured [warrior](#warrior) in the [medieval](#medieval) European mould, recognised by some combination of [sword](#sword) or [lance](#lance), [shield](#shield), [plate](#plate) armour and a mount. The same [figure](#figure) in Japanese armour with a [katana](#katana) is a [samurai](#samurai).

entries.name: policewoman
entries.description: A character in a female-style [police](#police) uniform, often with a [pencil](#pencil) [skirt](#skirt), [handcuffs](#handcuffs), and a [handgun](#handgun), regardless of the wearer's actual [sex](#sex). Tag [police_uniform](#police_uniform) alongside it.

entries.name: sailor
entries.description: A character dressed as a mariner or naval seaman in a sailor's uniform, with sailor [hat](#hat) and [collar](#collar). Only for the actual seafaring uniform; the Japanese [school](#school) [serafuku](#serafuku) is its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pirate
entries.description: A character presented as a sea raider, usually in the popular Golden Age style with [tricorne](#tricorne), [coat](#coat), [cutlass](#cutlass), [eyepatch](#eyepatch) or [hook](#hook). Tag the gear separately; a skull-and-crossbones motif on its own is not enough.

entries.name: soldier
entries.description: A uniformed member of an [army](#army), typically shown with a [helmet](#helmet), body [armor](#armor), and a service [weapon](#weapon). Special forces get the separate [military_operator](#military_operator) [tag](#tag); armed fighters with [no](#no) clear [military](#military) affiliation go untagged.

entries.name: samurai
entries.description: A feudal Japanese [warrior](#warrior) in traditional armour, usually with a [katana](#katana) or other Japanese [weapon](#weapon). Tag the armour and weapon separately.

entries.name: shinsengumi
entries.description: The late-Edo shogunate [police](#police) force of Kyoto, recognizable by their light-blue [haori](#haori) trimmed with a white mountain-stripe pattern on the sleeves. Covers historical and fictional depictions of the group and its officers.

entries.name: warrior
entries.description: A fighter from an ancient or [medieval](#medieval) setting, typically in piecemeal armour with a [heavy](#heavy) [sword](#sword) or [axe](#axe), or the RPG class of that name. Uniformed modern fighters are [soldier](#soldier) rather than this.

entries.name: detective
entries.description: A character shown investigating crimes, whether a [police](#police) detective with a [badge](#badge) or a private investigator. The stock look follows the famous consulting detective: [trench](#trench) [coat](#coat), [deerstalker](#deerstalker), magnifying [glass](#glass), sometimes a pipe.

entries.name: astronaut
entries.description: A person trained for spaceflight, generally recognizable by a sealed [suit](#suit) and a [helmet](#helmet) with a wide visor. Tag [spacesuit](#spacesuit) and the setting alongside.

entries.name: pilot
entries.description: A character who flies an [aircraft](#aircraft) or comparable craft, from a fighter to an airliner or a [space](#space) fighter, usually marked by a flight [suit](#suit), a [helmet](#helmet) or a [cockpit](#cockpit). Tag the aircraft as [well](#well) when it is shown.

entries.name: army
entries.description: A large body of soldiers shown together, or the ground [branch](#branch) of a nation's forces. Tag the uniforms, weapons and setting alongside.

entries.name: japan_national_police
entries.description: Japan's [police](#police) as shown by uniform and equipment. Blue or white shirts with blue trousers and vests, round caps on women officers, black-and-white cars under red lamps, and blue buses and helicopters all count.

entries.name: policeman
entries.description: A male character in [police](#police) uniform, [serving](#serving) as an officer. Tag [police_uniform](#police_uniform) alongside him; a female officer takes [policewoman](#policewoman) instead.

entries.name: standard_bearer
entries.description: The person who carries a unit's [flag](#flag) or [banner](#banner) held aloft as a rallying mark, seen with armies, parades and religious processions.

entries.name: amazon_warrior
entries.description: A woman fighter in the mould of the all-female [warrior](#warrior) nation of Greek legend, usually with [spear](#spear) or [bow](#bow), light armour and a hard bearing. Use it for the role rather than for any named character.

entries.name: military_operator
entries.description: A special-forces [soldier](#soldier) kitted out in full tactical gear: [plate](#plate) carrier, [helmet](#helmet), [night](#night) vision and a [rifle](#rifle) hung with optics and a [suppressor](#suppressor). Colored berets often mark which particular unit they belong to.

entries.name: japan_self-defense_force
entries.description: Japan's modern armed forces taken as a whole, covering the land, sea and air branches together. Use a [branch](#branch) [tag](#tag) instead when the picture makes clear which arm is meant.

entries.name: lifeguard
entries.description: Someone posted to [watch](#watch) swimmers and pull them out of trouble at a [beach](#beach) or [pool](#pool). Marked out by red swimwear, a [whistle](#whistle) and a [rescue](#rescue) float.

entries.name: firefighter
entries.description: Someone trained to fight fires and carry [people](#people) out of them, in [heavy](#heavy) protective gear with [helmet](#helmet), [hose](#hose) and [axe](#axe). The occupation is what the picture is showing.

entries.name: soviet_army
entries.description: The Red Army and its successor, the land forces of the Soviet Union from 1917 until the state's dissolution in 1991. Its uniforms, [insignia](#insignia), and equipment are what identify it in a picture.

entries.name: people's_liberation_army
entries.description: The armed forces of China, identified by their uniforms, [insignia](#insignia) or equipment. It covers every [branch](#branch), from ground troops to the navy and the air arm.

entries.name: japan_maritime_self-defense_force
entries.description: The naval [branch](#branch) of Japan's post-war forces, with white [dress](#dress) uniforms and grey escort ships officially rated as destroyers. It kept a good many customs from the [old](#old) imperial navy.

entries.name: japan_ground_self-defense_force
entries.description: Japan's land [branch](#branch), marked by [olive](#olive) [fatigues](#fatigues), home-built armoured vehicles and its own [insignia](#insignia). It is one of the three arms of the country's post-war forces.

entries.name: barbarian
entries.description: A fighter styled as wild or primitive: furs and hide, rough [leather](#leather) straps, [heavy](#heavy) weapons and almost [no](#no) armour. A stock [warrior](#warrior) type of [fantasy](#fantasy) settings.

entries.name: german_army
entries.description: German land forces of any period, recognised by [insignia](#insignia), identifiable vehicles or the uniform a character wears. Add the [tag](#tag) for the particular era when it [can](#can) be told apart.

entries.name: space_marine
entries.description: A [soldier](#soldier) equipped and trained to fight aboard ships and on other worlds, typically in sealed powered [armor](#armor) with a [heavy](#heavy) [rifle](#rifle). The Warhammer 40,000 versions go under their own specific names rather than this one.

entries.name: scout_movement
entries.description: The youth scouting organisation and its age bands, read from neckerchiefs, merit badges and khaki [dress](#dress). Covers both the boys' and girls' branches.

entries.name: s.w.a.t.
entries.description: Police tactical units sent against armed or barricaded threats, kitted out with body armour, helmets, breaching gear and heavier firearms than ordinary officers carry. They appear as a stacked team rather than lone patrolmen.

entries.name: japan_air_self-defense_force
entries.description: The air [branch](#branch) of Japan's post-war forces, shown through its fighters, roundels and blue-grey flight gear. It sits under the broader self-defense force.

entries.name: dragoon
entries.description: A [knight](#knight) in dragon-styled [plate](#plate) who fights with a [lance](#lance) or other [polearm](#polearm), often leaping from a great [height](#height) or [riding](#riding) a [dragon](#dragon) into [battle](#battle). Also called a dragon knight.

entries.name: sheriff_(western)
entries.description: The lawman of an American frontier [town](#town), marked by a star [badge](#badge), a wide-brimmed [hat](#hat) and a [holstered](#holstered) [revolver](#revolver). Refers to the role in general rather than any one character.

entries.name: security_guard
entries.description: Someone employed to [watch](#watch) over a [building](#building), event, or checkpoint, in uniform and [carrying](#carrying) a [radio](#radio), [badge](#badge), and often a [torch](#torch).

entries.name: bodyguard
entries.description: Somebody hired to stand [watch](#watch) over an important person and put themselves between them and harm. Dark [suit](#suit), [earpiece](#earpiece) and [sunglasses](#sunglasses) are the visual shorthand.

entries.name: cavalry
entries.description: Soldiers who fight from the [back](#back) of a mount, normally horses though camels and elephants served as [well](#well), used as scouts, skirmishers or shock troops. They [suit](#suit) [battle](#battle) scenes up to the First World War, after which engines took over.

entries.name: british_army
entries.description: The land forces of the United Kingdom, identified by their uniforms, [insignia](#insignia), vehicles or [heraldry](#heraldry). Berets, regimental cap badges and disruptive-pattern [camouflage](#camouflage) are the usual cues.

entries.name: guard
entries.description: Someone posted to [watch](#watch) a [gate](#gate), wall or [building](#building), dressed in the livery or armour of the place they serve and often [holding](#holding) a [polearm](#polearm). Modern equivalents belong under [security_guard](#security_guard) or [bodyguard](#bodyguard) instead.

entries.name: french_army
entries.description: France's land forces, recognised from uniforms, [insignia](#insignia) or identifiable vehicles. It applies to the [emblem](#emblem), the equipment or a character wearing the kit.

entries.name: military_police
entries.description: Soldiers who [police](#police) the armed forces themselves, dressed much like ordinary troops but set apart by armbands, [helmet](#helmet) lettering and their own distinct [insignia](#insignia).

entries.name: riot_police
entries.description: Police in [heavy](#heavy) protective gear sent against crowds and disturbances, drawn with black body armour, visored helmets and [transparent](#transparent) shields. They usually appear as a line or formation rather than as individuals.

entries.name: combat_medic
entries.description: A [soldier](#soldier) whose work is treating the wounded in the [field](#field). Drawn in [military](#military) [dress](#dress) with a medical [bag](#bag) or a red [cross](#cross) marking.

entries.name: nurse
entries.description: Someone dressed for nursing work, usually in a white [dress](#dress) with a [nurse_cap](#nurse_cap) in the manner of the twentieth century rather than in present-day scrubs. The outfit and uniform spellings fold in here, so the [tag](#tag) serves for both the job and the [costume](#costume).

entries.name: teacher
entries.description: Someone shown acting as an educator, whether at a blackboard, in a [classroom](#classroom), or otherwise identifiable as the person leading a lesson. Add [teacher_and_student](#teacher_and_student) when a pupil appears too.

entries.name: teacher_and_student
entries.description: An educator and their pupil both appear in the same picture. The pairing itself is what the [tag](#tag) records, so combine it with [teacher](#teacher) and any [classroom](#classroom) setting tags.

entries.name: doctor
entries.description: A character presented as a medical physician, generally in a white [coat](#coat) with a [stethoscope](#stethoscope), seeing to patients alongside nurses.

entries.name: school_nurse
entries.description: The [staff](#staff) member who runs the [school](#school) [infirmary](#infirmary), patching up scrapes and sending pupils off to lie down. Usually drawn in a white [coat](#coat) over ordinary [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: scientist
entries.description: Somebody presented as a researcher, with the lab [coat](#coat), [goggles](#goggles), [notes](#notes) and equipment that mark the trade.

entries.name: kindergarten_teacher
entries.description: An adult who minds and teaches preschool children, generally drawn in an [apron](#apron) among a [crowd](#crowd) of small pupils. The [tag](#tag) records the role rather than any particular outfit.

entries.name: shosei
entries.description: A live-in student houseboy of the Meiji and Taisho eras, [working](#working) as a servant in exchange for room, board and schooling. Recognizable by a western [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt) worn under [kimono](#kimono) and [hakama](#hakama), sometimes with a student cap.

entries.name: plague_doctor
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) in the historic plague physician's [dress](#dress): a waxed [leather](#leather) [overcoat](#overcoat), [gloves](#gloves), [boots](#boots), a wide [hat](#hat), and a [stick](#stick) for examining patients at arm's length, usually finished with the beaked [mask](#mask). A favourite of gothic and horror settings.

entries.name: dentist
entries.description: Somebody [working](#working) on [teeth](#teeth), drilling, [cleaning](#cleaning) or peering into an open mouth, usually gowned with a [mirror](#mirror) and probe in hand. The [reclining](#reclining) [chair](#chair) and overhead [lamp](#lamp) set the scene.

entries.name: virtual_youtuber
entries.description: A streamer or [video](#video) creator performing through a 2D or 3D avatar, on video platforms or elsewhere. Covers real performers, parodies, fictional ones and references to them; [friends](#friends) and [family](#family) of one do not count unless they are one too.

entries.name: cheerleader
entries.description: Somebody who performs cheerleading, generally a girl in the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top and short [pleated](#pleated) [skirt](#skirt) of the sport, pom-poms in hand. Tag the individual garments separately.

entries.name: idol
entries.description: A young pop entertainer who sings and dances in showy [stage](#stage) [dress](#dress), in the Japanese sense of the word. For the [costume](#costume) by itself use [idol_clothes](#idol_clothes).

entries.name: race_queen
entries.description: A promotional [model](#model) at a motorsport event, dressed in a skimpy sponsor-branded outfit, classically a crop top with a [miniskirt](#miniskirt) or [shorts](#shorts). Often shown [holding](#holding) a [parasol](#parasol); combine with the outfit tags shown.

entries.name: dancer
entries.description: A character in the [costume](#costume) of a performing dancer: loose, body-revealing garments finished with jewellery, circlets and veils. The [tag](#tag) describes the female outfit and is not normally put on male characters.

entries.name: utaite
entries.description: An [internet](#internet) [cover](#cover) singer who [rose](#rose) to notice on video-sharing sites and later platforms, drawn as themselves or their performing persona. A category of real performers, some of whom now also work as VTubers.

entries.name: voice_actor
entries.description: A real-life voice actor appears in the picture. Reserved for actual [people](#people), not the characters they voice; for jokes built on shared casting see [voice_actor_connection](#voice_actor_connection).

entries.name: mascot
entries.description: A character [standing](#standing) as the [emblem](#emblem) of a team, a company or a series, whether a costumed [figure](#figure) or a small cute [creature](#creature). It marks the being itself, not [merchandise](#merchandise) printed with it.

entries.name: ballerina
entries.description: A woman who dances [ballet](#ballet), shown in a [tutu](#tutu), [leotard](#leotard) and soft [slippers](#slippers), often up on her [toes](#toes) or [holding](#holding) a classical line. The [dancing](#dancing) itself is ballet, and the [clothes](#clothes) carry tags of their own.

entries.name: jester
entries.description: Somebody dressed and behaving as a court fool or wandering entertainer, in patched bright colours with a belled cap and often a mock sceptre. When only the [hat](#hat) is at issue, [jester_cap](#jester_cap) covers it.

entries.name: clown
entries.description: A [circus](#circus) entertainer in greasepaint, red [nose](#nose), bright [wig](#wig) and baggy motley. Jesters, Pierrot figures and other [comic](#comic) performers have their own tags.

entries.name: magician
entries.description: Somebody dressed as the stock [stage](#stage) conjurer, in a top [hat](#hat) with tails or an outfit built from formal wear. It records the look, and [no](#no) trick has to be under way.

entries.name: stripper
entries.description: A performer whose job is [undressing](#undressing) for a paying [audience](#audience), typically shown in a tiny [bikini](#bikini) or [lingerie](#lingerie) and [dancing](#dancing) near a [pole](#pole) in a club setting. Tag the person, and add [stripper_pole](#stripper_pole) when one appears.

entries.name: band_(music)
entries.description: A group of musicians [playing](#playing) together, each on an [instrument](#instrument) of their own, guitars and bass and drums and keys. It is for the ensemble as a unit rather than for a single performer.

entries.name: wrestler
entries.description: A wrestler identified by trade, dressed in a [singlet](#singlet), trunks, or a costumed [ring](#ring) persona. It covers amateur sport and theatrical professional [wrestling](#wrestling) alike.

entries.name: coach
entries.description: The person who trains and directs an athlete or a team, typically in a tracksuit with a [whistle](#whistle) or a [clipboard](#clipboard). Shown [giving](#giving) instruction from the sideline rather than competing.

entries.name: dj
entries.description: Working turntables or a mixer at a club, one headphone [cup](#cup) pressed against an ear and records or a [controller](#controller) under the hands. Radio announcers are not what this covers.

entries.name: conductor
entries.description: The person leading an [orchestra](#orchestra), band or choir, baton in hand and often in white [gloves](#gloves) and tails. Railway [staff](#staff) are [train_conductor](#train_conductor).

entries.name: goalkeeper
entries.description: The player defending the [net](#net), marked out from teammates by [gloves](#gloves) and a differently coloured kit. Drawn [diving](#diving), [catching](#catching) or [waiting](#waiting) on the [goal](#goal) line.

entries.name: ouendan
entries.description: Japan's traditional male cheer squad, rallying a team by [shouting](#shouting) and sharp gestures rather than [acrobatics](#acrobatics). Marked out by the long [gakuran](#gakuran) [coat](#coat), a [hachimaki](#hachimaki) [headband](#headband), an [armband](#armband) and sometimes white [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: gladiator
entries.description: An [arena](#arena) fighter putting on a spectacle for a [crowd](#crowd), kitted out in showy and impractical arms and armour. Men are often bare-chested and women in [bikini](#bikini) armour; the [idea](#idea) comes from ancient Rome.

entries.name: geisha
entries.description: A trained Japanese entertainer in white face [makeup](#makeup), a formal [kimono](#kimono) and a sculpted [wig](#wig), hosting guests with dance, [music](#music) and conversation. Tag the person in that role; the garment itself is kimono.

entries.name: bard
entries.description: A poet-musician of a [medieval](#medieval) or [fantasy](#fantasy) world, travelling with a lute, [lyre](#lyre) or similar [instrument](#instrument). Games [cast](#cast) the role as a support who heals or strengthens allies through [music](#music). Like other occupation tags it wants the instrument actually in the picture, not merely stated in a character's backstory.

entries.name: av_idol
entries.description: A performer in Japanese adult videos, shown at work or presented in that role, whether posed for a shoot, filmed, or answering an [interview](#interview). It describes the occupation rather than any particular act.

entries.name: luchador
entries.description: A [masked](#masked) [wrestler](#wrestler) in the Mexican tradition, in a brightly coloured full-face [hood](#hood) and often a matching [cape](#cape) and trunks. The [tag](#tag) has spread to masked wrestlers from elsewhere, tiger-masked Japanese ones especially.

entries.name: boxer
entries.description: A fighter who competes at [boxing](#boxing), normally shown in padded [gloves](#gloves), trunks and hand wraps. Do not mix it up with [boxers](#boxers), which are [underwear](#underwear).

entries.name: catcher_(baseball)
entries.description: The fielder [squatting](#squatting) behind home [plate](#plate) to take the pitcher's throws, call the pitches and [guard](#guard) the plate against runners. Heavy gear marks the role out: caged [mask](#mask), chest padding and shin guards.

entries.name: jockey
entries.description: A rider in [racing](#racing) silks and [helmet](#helmet), crouched high above the [saddle](#saddle) on very short stirrups. The racing kit is what sets it apart from ordinary horseback [riding](#riding).

entries.name: matador
entries.description: A bullfighter of the Spanish tradition, in an embroidered [suit](#suit) of lights, [working](#working) a red [cloth](#cloth) on a [stick](#stick) and often [holding](#holding) a slim [sword](#sword). Used for the person in the role, not merely for a red [cape](#cape).

entries.name: referee
entries.description: The official who enforces the rules of a match, recognisable by a striped [shirt](#shirt), a [whistle](#whistle), or a raised signalling arm. Appears in sports and [wrestling](#wrestling) scenes rather than as a competitor.

entries.name: umpire
entries.description: The official who rules on play in a sport, [calling](#calling) balls, fouls and outs. A [baseball](#baseball) version comes with [mask](#mask), chest protector and a [dark](#dark) uniform.

entries.name: tsukkomi
entries.description: The sharp-witted half of a Japanese comedy duo, whose job is to cut in and correct the foolish partner's jokes. Often drawn mid-retort, sometimes delivering a light [smack](#smack) to the other's head.

entries.name: miko
entries.description: A character wearing the traditional [shrine](#shrine) maiden outfit: a red [hakama](#hakama) worn over a white [kosode](#kosode). A shrine attendant dressed in other clothing takes [nontraditional_miko](#nontraditional_miko) instead.

entries.name: witch
entries.description: A [magic](#magic) user, usually female, drawn in the classic mould: a pointed [witch_hat](#witch_hat), a long black [dress](#dress), a [broom](#broom), and sometimes a black [cat](#cat). Halloween-themed pictures often add pumpkins; the [hat](#hat) and dress tags alone [cover](#cover) just the outfit, while series-specific witches keep their own separate tags.

entries.name: nun
entries.description: A woman living under religious vows, drawn in the long [habit](#habit), [wimple](#wimple) and [veil](#veil) of her order and often with a [cross](#cross) at the breast. Covers Christian, Buddhist and other traditions along with armed [fantasy](#fantasy) [sisters](#sisters); the [restrained](#restrained) historical outfit is [traditional_nun](#traditional_nun) rather than the sexualised versions common in anime.

entries.name: priest
entries.description: A character [serving](#serving) as clergy, drawn in a [cassock](#cassock) or [habit](#habit) with a clerical [collar](#collar), [stole](#stole) or [mitre](#mitre). Shrine maidens are [miko](#miko) and nuns are [nun](#nun); use priest for the ordained [figure](#figure).

entries.name: wizard
entries.description: A practitioner of [magic](#magic) in the classic mould: an [old](#old) man in a [tall](#tall) [hat](#hat) and long robes [carrying](#carrying) a wooden [staff](#staff), in the manner of Gandalf. It also serves as a common video-game class, with [witch](#witch) usually [standing](#standing) as its female counterpart.

entries.name: onmyouji
entries.description: A practitioner of the [old](#old) Japanese court art of divination and exorcism, usually drawn in Heian robes and a [tall](#tall) black cap with talismans or a summoned servant to hand.

entries.name: priestess
entries.description: A woman [holding](#holding) religious [office](#office), drawn as a [shrine](#shrine) maiden, a [nun](#nun), or a robed [fantasy](#fantasy) [cleric](#cleric). Her vestments and [ritual](#ritual) gear usually carry the [reading](#reading).

entries.name: monk
entries.description: A man living under religious vows: a Buddhist [priest](#priest) with shaved head, [robe](#robe) and prayer [beads](#beads), or a tonsured Western brother in a hooded [habit](#habit). It covers both traditions, in a [temple](#temple) or out in the world.

entries.name: buddhist_nun
entries.description: A woman ordained in Buddhism, shown with a shaved head and [plain](#plain) monastic robes. Prayer [beads](#beads) and a [temple](#temple) setting normally accompany her.

entries.name: necromancer
entries.description: A [magic](#magic) user who raises and commands the dead. Skeletons, [rotting](#rotting) servants, [dark](#dark) robes and a [staff](#staff) or [grimoire](#grimoire) usually appear alongside.

entries.name: religious_offering
entries.description: Money, [food](#food) or goods presented to a [temple](#temple), [shrine](#shrine), or [church](#church), laid on an [altar](#altar) or dropped into a [box](#box). For simply handing something to another person, the [giving](#giving) [tag](#tag) applies instead.

entries.name: paladin
entries.description: A holy [warrior](#warrior) in armour, [bound](#bound) by a religious oath and part [knight](#knight), part [priest](#priest). Shield, [sword](#sword) and radiant or blessed effects are the usual markers.

entries.name: cleric
entries.description: A robed religious character who heals and fights, the priestly member of a [fantasy](#fantasy) adventuring [party](#party). Usually carries a [staff](#staff) or [mace](#mace) and wears a holy symbol.

entries.name: muslim
entries.description: A character shown as a follower of Islam, marked by [dress](#dress) such as a [hijab](#hijab) or thobe, by prayer, or by a mosque behind them. The religious identity is what is recorded, not any single garment.

entries.name: office_lady
entries.description: A woman in a clerical or secretarial job, known in Japanese as an OL. She is usually drawn in a [blouse](#blouse) with a [pencil](#pencil) [skirt](#skirt) or a business [suit](#suit), at a [desk](#desk) or on the commute.

entries.name: salaryman
entries.description: A Japanese white-collar [office](#office) worker, drawn in a collared white [shirt](#shirt), [necktie](#necktie) and [suit](#suit), often with a [briefcase](#briefcase), and typically overworked. Tag the outfit parts as [well](#well).

entries.name: housewife
entries.description: A woman shown [running](#running) a household, [cooking](#cooking), [cleaning](#cleaning) or minding children. It applies wherever she is presented that way, even if it is not her canonical occupation.

entries.name: cowboy
entries.description: A cattle herder of the American West, or somebody dressed as one: brimmed [hat](#hat), [boots](#boots), [neckerchief](#neckerchief) and often a [revolver](#revolver) at the hip. A woman in the same [dress](#dress) takes [cowgirl_(western)](#cowgirl_(western)).

entries.name: mechanic
entries.description: A tradesperson who builds, services and repairs [machinery](#machinery), whether cars, trucks or [mecha](#mecha). Usually drawn [holding](#holding) [tools](#tools), with oil-smeared hands and wearing coveralls.

entries.name: train_conductor
entries.description: Railway crew responsible for everything about a train's journey besides actually [driving](#driving) it: checking tickets, [watching](#watching) the doors, coupling cars and keeping to the timetable. Marked out by a peaked cap and uniform [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: cowgirl_(western)
entries.description: A woman in Western ranch [dress](#dress): brimmed [hat](#hat), [boots](#boots), [denim](#denim) or fringed [leather](#leather). Not to be [confused](#confused) with the [sex](#sex) position that shares the word.

entries.name: tour_guide
entries.description: Someone leading a group of visitors around a site or [city](#city), typically marked by a raised [flag](#flag) or [pointer](#pointer), a name [badge](#badge) and a rehearsed commentary. Common in sightseeing and travel scenes.

entries.name: delivery
entries.description: Somebody bringing a parcel or a takeaway order to a [door](#door) for a living, [box](#box) in hand. Frequently framed from inside the [entrance](#entrance) with the door [standing](#standing) open.

entries.name: neet
entries.description: Somebody with [no](#no) job, schooling or [training](#training), usually shown holed up at home among games, snacks and clutter. It is related to but distinct from a [hikikomori](#hikikomori), who has withdrawn from other [people](#people) altogether.

entries.name: blacksmith
entries.description: Somebody who works [hot](#hot) iron or steel at a forge, shaping [tools](#tools) and weapons with [hammer](#hammer), [tongs](#tongs) and [anvil](#anvil). Sparks, a [heavy](#heavy) [apron](#apron) and a [glowing](#glowing) [furnace](#furnace) usually come with them.

entries.name: farmer
entries.description: Somebody who works the land or keeps livestock for a living, usually in practical [clothes](#clothes) with a straw [hat](#hat), [boots](#boots) or a [hoe](#hoe). It records the occupation, not the place.

entries.name: judge
entries.description: A person acting as judge, whether robed behind a [courtroom](#courtroom) [bench](#bench) or scoring a contest from the sidelines. The role is what is being tagged, not any verdict.

entries.name: politician
entries.description: A real-world political [figure](#figure) appearing in the artwork, in [office](#office) [dress](#dress) or [working](#working) a [podium](#podium). Invented rulers and [fantasy](#fantasy) nobles do not qualify.

entries.name: mailman
entries.description: A postal worker on a round, [carrying](#carrying) letters and parcels in a shoulder [bag](#bag) and usually uniformed. It covers carriers of either [sex](#sex).

entries.name: paparazzi
entries.description: Photographers who chase celebrities for candid pictures, drawn as a crowding wall of lenses and flashes. Use it for the pack; one person with a [camera](#camera) is just a [photographer](#photographer).

entries.name: reporter
entries.description: Someone whose job is gathering [news](#news) and passing it on, shown with a [notepad](#notepad), [microphone](#microphone), or [camera](#camera) crew. Covers journalists in the [field](#field) as [well](#well) as [studio](#studio) presenters [reading](#reading) the news.

entries.name: photographer
entries.description: Somebody [working](#working) a [camera](#camera), for a living or for fun, often crouching or [leaning](#leaning) to frame the shot. Use it for the person taking the picture; the staged session itself is [photo_shoot](#photo_shoot).

entries.name: construction_worker
entries.description: Somebody employed on [building](#building) work, generally in a hard [hat](#hat), work [boots](#boots) and high-visibility gear, with [tools](#tools) and [scaffolding](#scaffolding) around them.

entries.name: florist
entries.description: Someone who sells and arranges flowers for a living, shown among buckets of blooms, [wrapping](#wrapping) [paper](#paper) and [ribbon](#ribbon). The job identifies the person; the premises are a [flower](#flower) [shop](#shop).

entries.name: zookeeper
entries.description: Someone employed to feed and care for animals in captivity, usually shown in a work uniform [carrying](#carrying) feed, a [bucket](#bucket) or a [hose](#hose). The [tag](#tag) is about the job being performed.

entries.name: charro
entries.description: A Mexican horseman in traditional [dress](#dress): a broad [sombrero](#sombrero), a close-fitting embroidered [suit](#suit), a short [jacket](#jacket) [heavy](#heavy) with silver. Bandits and gunmen of the same era wear the outfit too.

entries.name: engineer
entries.description: Somebody whose work is [building](#building), wiring or [repairing](#repairing) [machinery](#machinery), shown with [tools](#tools), a hard [hat](#hat), coveralls or a [bench](#bench) of parts. The job is what counts, not the [clothes](#clothes) by themselves.

entries.name: delinquent
entries.description: A rebellious young troublemaker, most often a teenage student, in the mould of the Japanese yankee, [sukeban](#sukeban), [banchou](#banchou) or [bousouzoku](#bousouzoku), or of greasers and punks elsewhere. Attitude, hair and an altered uniform mark them rather than one fixed outfit.

entries.name: prisoner
entries.description: A person shown as an inmate, marked out by an orange [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit), black-and-white stripes, or another jailhouse outfit. Cuffs, chains and a cell are frequent companions but not required.

entries.name: pimp
entries.description: A character styled after the flashy procurer stereotype: fur [coat](#coat), wide-brimmed [hat](#hat), gaudy rings and a [cane](#cane). It is used as much for the swagger and the look as for the occupation itself.

entries.name: banchou
entries.description: The classic Japanese [school](#school) tough at the head of a gang, in the 1970s mould. He wears his uniform [jacket](#jacket) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders like a [cape](#cape), an aviator cap or similar [headgear](#headgear), and a bare chest wrapped in [sarashi](#sarashi).

entries.name: sukeban
entries.description: The boss of a girls' [delinquent](#delinquent) gang, a stock Japanese archetype drawn with an ankle-length modified uniform [skirt](#skirt), bleached or permed hair and often chest [wrapping](#wrapping) under the [jacket](#jacket). The look reads as tough rather than as ordinary schoolwear.

entries.name: yakuza
entries.description: Members of Japanese organised crime, typically drawn in sharp suits with permed hair, a missing fingertip and sprawling [irezumi](#irezumi) tattoos. Covers both the individual members and the gangs they belong to.

entries.name: phantom_thief
entries.description: A theatrical burglar who announces the crime in advance and carries it off with a flourish, usually in a [suit](#suit), [cape](#cape), top [hat](#hat) or [mask](#mask). The archetype descends from Arsene Lupin and his many manga heirs.

entries.name: mafia
entries.description: Organised-crime figures in the Sicilian mould, with sharp black suits, fedoras, expensive [drink](#drink) and a [handgun](#handgun) or submachine [gun](#gun) close by. The picture should look and act the part; [writing](#writing) a character as a criminal is not enough on its own.

entries.name: assassin
entries.description: A killer [working](#working) for hire, usually drawn with concealed blades, close [dark](#dark) clothing and a [hood](#hood) or [mask](#mask). Rooftops and shadows are the usual company.

entries.name: gangster
entries.description: A member of an organised criminal outfit such as a [mafia](#mafia) [family](#family), a [yakuza](#yakuza) clan or a [street](#street) gang, read from the [suit](#suit), the tattoos or the company kept. Sits alongside crime and mob scenes.

entries.name: thief
entries.description: Somebody who steals, marked out by a [mask](#mask), a swag [bag](#bag), a lockpick, or simply by being [caught](#caught) mid-theft. The word also names a class in many games, which carries its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bousouzoku
entries.description: A member of the Japanese biker-gang subculture: wraparound shades, a long slogan [headband](#headband), a [pompadour](#pompadour), and either a doctored [school](#school) uniform or a boiler [suit](#suit) with the gang's name across the [back](#back). Their bikes and cars are heavily modified.

entries.name: gopnik
entries.description: The Russian street-delinquent type: striped tracksuit, flat cap, [sunflower](#sunflower) seeds and a deep flat-footed squat. Cheap [drink](#drink) and blocky [concrete](#concrete) housing usually fill in the background.

entries.name: slave
entries.description: A character shown as someone's property: [chained](#chained) hands, a [collar](#collar) and [leash](#leash), [rags](#rags), or being sold or ordered around. Often, but not always, in a sexual setting.

entries.name: princess
entries.description: A royal daughter, usually recognisable by an elaborate [gown](#gown), [jewelry](#jewelry) and a [tiara](#tiara) or small [crown](#crown). The male counterpart is [prince](#prince).

entries.name: queen
entries.description: A woman who rules in her own right or has married into royalty, marked out by a [crown](#crown), [throne](#throne), regalia, or courtly [dress](#dress). Bearing and setting carry the role as much as any single object does.

entries.name: prince
entries.description: A [king](#king) or queen's son, marked out by a coronet, a [sash](#sash) and formal court [dress](#dress). Storybook and [fantasy](#fantasy) versions dominate; the female counterpart is a [princess](#princess).

entries.name: king
entries.description: A male sovereign, or a [figure](#figure) treated as one, marked out by a [crown](#crown), a [robe](#robe) and a sceptre. The [chess](#chess) piece and the [playing](#playing) [card](#card) of the same name have separate tags.

entries.name: pharaoh
entries.description: A character in ancient Egyptian royal [dress](#dress): the striped [nemes](#nemes) headcloth, a false [beard](#beard), and the crook and [flail](#flail). It fits figures merely implied to hold that rank as [well](#well).

entries.name: furry
entries.description: Anthropomorphic [animal](#animal) characters, generally [carrying](#carrying) body fur, [feathers](#feathers) or [scales](#scales) along with an animal face. A character with only ears and a [tail](#tail) is kemonomimi, and [monster](#monster) girls with human faces do not qualify.

entries.name: animal
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) that really exists, or once did, appears somewhere in the picture. Invented beasts such as griffins go to [monster](#monster) or creature instead, and one drawn far larger than the [people](#people) beside it takes [oversized_animal](#oversized_animal).

entries.name: furry_female
entries.description: A female anthropomorphic [animal](#animal) character, with an animal face and a body covered in fur, [feathers](#feathers) or [scales](#scales). Add the species; a girl with nothing but animal ears and a [tail](#tail) is kemonomimi rather than this.

entries.name: furry_male
entries.description: A male anthropomorphic [animal](#animal) character, with an animal face and a body covered in fur, [feathers](#feathers) or [scales](#scales). Add the species; a boy with nothing but animal ears and a [tail](#tail) is kemonomimi rather than this.

entries.name: taur
entries.description: A body with the full four-legged form of an [animal](#animal) and a humanoid [torso](#torso) rising where the [neck](#neck) would sit, as with a [centaur](#centaur). Lamias, harpies and mermaids do not qualify, since their lower half is not a complete animal body.

entries.name: digitigrade
entries.description: Legs that stand on the [toes](#toes) with the heel carried high, [giving](#giving) the reverse-jointed look of a [dog](#dog), [cat](#cat) or [bird](#bird) leg. What appears to be a backward knee is the heel; the real knee sits higher and is often hard to spot.

entries.name: centauroid
entries.description: The same arrangement as a [centaur](#centaur), but the lower body belongs to some other [animal](#animal): a [spider](#spider), a [deer](#deer), a [snake](#snake), a [beetle](#beetle). A general term for the [taur](#taur) build when the base [creature](#creature) is not a [horse](#horse).

entries.name: animal_head
entries.description: A humanoid body [carrying](#carrying) a creature's head where a human one belongs, from a [bear](#bear) to a sea [slug](#slug). The reverse arrangement is [human_head](#human_head), and it counts as [furry](#furry) only when the rest of the body is [animal](#animal) as [well](#well).

entries.name: human_head
entries.description: A human head sits on a body that is not human at all. The reverse case is [animal_head](#animal_head), and a head with [no](#no) body under it is a severed or disembodied head.

entries.name: furry_and_animal
entries.description: An anthro character shown alongside an ordinary non-anthro [animal](#animal), frequently of the same species. The [contrast](#contrast) between the two is generally the point of the picture.

entries.name: creature
entries.description: A small invented [animal](#animal) that is not meant to be frightening: a magical girl's companion, a series [mascot](#mascot), a helpful little being. Anything large or menacing is a [monster](#monster) instead.

entries.name: clothed_animal
entries.description: A non-anthropomorphic [animal](#animal) wearing human clothing, such as a [dog](#dog) in a jumper or a [cat](#cat) in a [hat](#hat). Anthro characters, who stand upright and behave like [people](#people), are not this.

entries.name: snail
entries.description: A gastropod with a [coiled](#coiled) [shell](#shell) it [can](#can) retreat into. Without the shell it is a [slug](#slug).

entries.name: pet
entries.description: A tame [animal](#animal) kept by a character, or a character treated as one, with a [collar](#collar), a [leash](#leash) or a [food](#food) [bowl](#bowl). The fetish role-play in which a person acts as somebody's animal is [pet_play](#pet_play).

entries.name: worm
entries.description: Worms in the picture, drawn as soft segmented tubes in [soil](#soil), on a [hook](#hook), or [crawling](#crawling) somewhere. Caterpillars and other larvae generally take their own separate tags.

entries.name: parasite
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) fastened onto or embedded in a host's body and plainly visible in the picture, often worm-like but by [no](#no) means always. Used broadly, including where the host appears to be controlled by whatever has attached itself.

entries.name: undersized_animal
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) drawn far smaller than its real counterpart, such as a palm-sized [elephant](#elephant) or a pocket-sized [dragon](#dragon). The shrunken scale is the point, usually played for charm.

entries.name: slug
entries.description: A land-dwelling gastropod with a soft body and [no](#no) [shell](#shell), leaving a slime trail as it moves. Once a shell is present the [creature](#creature) is a [snail](#snail) instead.

entries.name: dead_animal
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) shown dead: a carcass on the ground, hunted game, a [bird](#bird) gone limp. It says nothing about the cause, and bloody cases carry gore tags alongside.

entries.name: hatching
entries.description: A young [animal](#animal) [breaking](#breaking) out of its [egg](#egg), [shell](#shell) cracked and the newborn [pushing](#pushing) free. For the shading technique of ruled lines use [hatching_(texture)](#hatching_(texture)).

entries.name: prehistoric_animal
entries.description: Creatures from the deep past drawn alive rather than as fossils: mammoths, sabre-toothed cats, trilobites and their kin. Dinosaurs proper have a [tag](#tag) of their own.
