entries.name: winged_animal
entries.description: An ordinary [animal](#animal), such as a [cat](#cat), [dog](#dog), or [fish](#fish), drawn with [wings](#wings) it would never actually grow. Dream sequences and light [fantasy](#fantasy) settings lean on the [idea](#idea) most.

entries.name: elf
entries.description: A slender, long-lived humanoid marked out by pointed ears, in anime art almost always young-looking and often blonde. Half-elves are drawn much the same way and are hard to tell apart; dark-skinned versions are [dark_elf](#dark_elf).

entries.name: fairy
entries.description: A small magical being of human shape, playful by [nature](#nature) and usually pale-skinned with gossamer [wings](#wings). Small size is typical but not required. Add [fairy_wings](#fairy_wings) where the wings show.

entries.name: mermaid
entries.description: A woman with a fish's [tail](#tail) in place of [legs](#legs), the classic sea-dwelling [creature](#creature) of myth. The male counterpart is [merman](#merman).

entries.name: shark_girl
entries.description: A girl with [shark](#shark) traits: a fin, a shark [tail](#tail), sharp [teeth](#teeth), or [gills](#gills). Usually tagged together with [mermaid](#mermaid) or [fish_girl](#fish_girl), depending on her lower body.

entries.name: dark_elf
entries.description: An [elf](#elf) of the [dark](#dark) or drow kind, often written as a separate elven [people](#people) tied to the underworld and to villainy, though many settings make them nothing of the sort. Dark-skinned elves and characters who carry the [title](#title) both take it.

entries.name: orc
entries.description: A brutish [fantasy](#fantasy) humanoid, generally green or grey-skinned with [tusks](#tusks), pointed ears and a [heavy](#heavy) or [muscular](#muscular) build; Japanese art often gives the males pig-like snouts. Females are drawn [tall](#tall) and voluptuous, and orcs are stock partners for elves in adult work.

entries.name: lamia
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) girl whose human upper body ends in a long serpent's coil instead of [legs](#legs). Naga names the same design, the [choice](#choice) between the two being mostly [habit](#habit).

entries.name: harpy
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) girl built on a [bird](#bird): [wings](#wings) in place of arms, or heavily feathered arms beside a pair of wings, and taloned [feet](#feet). Some are built on dinosaurs or other creatures instead, and the classical form gives a woman's head to a bird's body.

entries.name: goblin
entries.description: A small green-skinned humanoid with [fangs](#fangs), a hooked [nose](#nose) and big pointed ears, weaker but craftier than an [orc](#orc). Fantasy settings [cast](#cast) them as low-ranking villains and hereditary enemies of elves.

entries.name: cyclops
entries.description: A being with a single large eye set in the middle of the [forehead](#forehead). The Greek sort are drawn as giants, while the Japanese kind descended from the hitotsume-kozou keep human proportions; monoeye is another name for them.

entries.name: centaur
entries.description: A human upper body rises where a horse's [neck](#neck) and head would be, joined to the full equine body and its four [legs](#legs). It is the oldest and most [familiar](#familiar) of the [taur](#taur) builds.

entries.name: dwarf
entries.description: A short, stocky humanoid of [fantasy](#fantasy), classically bearded and tied to mining and metalwork. Only use it where the build is actually shown: roughly a child's [height](#height) with a [heavy](#heavy) frame for it, not merely a short human.

entries.name: snake_hair
entries.description: Hair made of or evocative of snakes, fully or in part, the gorgon look, sometimes on a [snake](#snake) [tail](#tail) or elsewhere than the scalp. Reference the myth itself with medusa_(mythology), and [petrification](#petrification) when her power shows.

entries.name: snake_girl
entries.description: A female character with serpent features: slit pupils, a forked [tongue](#tongue), [scales](#scales) and a [snake](#snake) [tail](#tail). A full serpent lower body puts her in [lamia](#lamia) territory as [well](#well).

entries.name: scylla
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) girl with a human upper body and [octopus](#octopus) [tentacles](#tentacles) in place of [legs](#legs), in the style of Monster Musume's Octo or Disney's Ursula. The Greek mythological [figure](#figure) of the same name is tagged separately as scylla_(mythology).

entries.name: minotaur
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) with the head of a [bull](#bull) or [cow](#cow) set on a human body. A character with only cow [horns](#horns), ears or a [tail](#tail) but an otherwise human face is instead [cow_girl](#cow_girl) or [cow_boy](#cow_boy).

entries.name: female_goblin
entries.description: A [goblin](#goblin) who is female, usually small with green skin, pointed ears and little [fangs](#fangs) after the [fantasy](#fantasy) stereotype.

entries.name: arachne
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) girl whose body below the waist is entirely a spider's, a human [torso](#torso) rising from the thorax, often with extra eyes. Spider parts alone are not enough: a girl keeping human [legs](#legs) takes [arthropod_limbs](#arthropod_limbs), and the same build on another [creature](#creature) is [centauroid](#centauroid).

entries.name: merman
entries.description: A man with a fish's [tail](#tail) for a lower body, the male counterpart to a [mermaid](#mermaid). Not the same as fishmen, who keep [legs](#legs) but carry fish-like features across their whole body.

entries.name: halfling
entries.description: A small humanoid race of [fantasy](#fantasy) settings, adult but child-sized, often with curly hair and large bare [feet](#feet). Stands in for the hobbit under a name games [can](#can) use freely.

entries.name: ogre
entries.description: A big, brutish humanoid out of western folklore, heavy-set and shaggy with an appetite to match. Later drawings give it coloured skin and [horns](#horns); the Japanese equivalent is drawn as an [oni](#oni), and the name invites confusion with the [orc](#orc).

entries.name: kneeless_mermaid
entries.description: A merfolk design whose lower half flows like a real [fish](#fish) or sea mammal, curving smoothly instead of [bending](#bending) where a hidden knee would be. Fins [pointing](#pointing) the right way for the [creature](#creature) help, and the lower body must be visible for it to apply.

entries.name: female_orc
entries.description: An [orc](#orc) woman, green or grey skinned with [tusks](#tusks) and a [heavy](#heavy) frame. She is usually drawn with more muscle and bulk than the human women around her.

entries.name: shark_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [shark](#shark) traits such as pointed [teeth](#teeth), gill slits, a dorsal fin, or a shark's [tail](#tail). Sits between [merman](#merman) and monster-boy designs.

entries.name: lizardman
entries.description: A reptilian humanoid [walking](#walking) upright, covered in [scales](#scales) and usually given a [snout](#snout) and a [tail](#tail). A stock [fantasy](#fantasy) race, most often drawn as a [warrior](#warrior) or [tribal](#tribal) fighter.

entries.name: half-harpy
entries.description: A bird-like [monster](#monster) girl with notable avian traits, such as [wings](#wings) on the [back](#back) and taloned [feet](#feet), but ordinary arms rather than wings for arms. Where the arms themselves are wings, [harpy](#harpy) is the correct [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: harpy_boy
entries.description: A male character on the [harpy](#harpy) plan, human above and [bird](#bird) below, with [wings](#wings) for arms and clawed [feet](#feet). Feathered [legs](#legs) and a fanned [tail](#tail) are usual.

entries.name: unicorn_girl
entries.description: A human-shaped girl [carrying](#carrying) [unicorn](#unicorn) traits, most often a single [spiral](#spiral) horn on the brow, sometimes paired with equine ears or a [tail](#tail). The horn alone on an otherwise ordinary [figure](#figure) is enough to read this way.

entries.name: satyr
entries.description: A woodland being out of Greek myth with a human [torso](#torso) and the [legs](#legs), [hooves](#hooves), ears and curling [horns](#horns) of a [goat](#goat). Usually shaggy from the waist down.

entries.name: octopus_boy
entries.description: A male [figure](#figure) human above the waist and [octopus](#octopus) below, arms in place of [legs](#legs). He is the counterpart of the [scylla](#scylla) [monster](#monster) girl.

entries.name: snake_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) serpent traits: narrow slit pupils, a [tongue](#tongue) that forks, scaled skin and a reptilian [tail](#tail). He may keep human [legs](#legs) or taper into a coil below the waist.

entries.name: dryad
entries.description: A female [tree](#tree) [spirit](#spirit) out of Greek myth, part woman and part [plant](#plant), with bark, leaves or living branches growing from her body. Bound to one particular tree or grove.

entries.name: troll
entries.description: A brutish humanoid drawn from Norse folklore, later reshaped by modern [fantasy](#fantasy) fiction into a hulking, grey- or brown-skinned [creature](#creature) of great strength and little wit. Older-style depictions lean closer to lumpy giants with oversized noses and ears.

entries.name: lamia_boy
entries.description: A male [figure](#figure) with a human [torso](#torso) above a long snake's [tail](#tail) in place of [legs](#legs). The word naga attaches to this version more readily than to the female one.

entries.name: gnome
entries.description: A small [underground](#underground) humanoid from European folklore, drawn as a stout bearded [figure](#figure) in a pointed cap. Fantasy settings [cast](#cast) them as earth elementals, tinkerers and pranksters, and [garden](#garden) statues of them are a stock joke.

entries.name: yeti_(creature)
entries.description: The shaggy ape-like beast of Himalayan legend, drawn [tall](#tall), white-furred and at home in [snow](#snow) and thin air. Close kin to the abominable [snowman](#snowman) and to western sasquatch designs.

entries.name: demon_girl
entries.description: A female character with a demonic look: [demon_horns](#demon_horns), [fangs](#fangs), [glowing](#glowing) eyes, pointed ears, coloured skin or sclera, [demon_wings](#demon_wings) and a long [tail](#tail). Succubi are almost always drawn as [demon](#demon) girls.

entries.name: ghost
entries.description: The [spirit](#spirit) of a dead person appearing as an apparition, frequently [translucent](#translucent) and trailing a wispy [tail](#tail) where the [legs](#legs) would be. Costumes [imitating](#imitating) one are [ghost_costume](#ghost_costume).

entries.name: oni
entries.description: A horned [demon](#demon) of Japanese folklore, traditionally red- or blue-skinned in a tiger-stripe [loincloth](#loincloth) with a [studded](#studded) club to hand. Modern characters usually keep nothing but the pair of [horns](#horns). Closely tied to the bean-throwing of Setsubun.

entries.name: angel
entries.description: A heavenly being, most often drawn as a human [figure](#figure) with white feathered [wings](#wings) and a [halo](#halo), though designs vary widely. It names what the character is; [angel_wings](#angel_wings) and halo describe the parts themselves.

entries.name: vampire
entries.description: A blood-drinking being of folklore, shown with [fangs](#fangs), predatory eyes and pale skin, sometimes bat [wings](#wings) or a [cape](#cape). Apply the [tag](#tag) only when such traits are actually visible, not simply because a character is a vampire within their own story.

entries.name: demon
entries.description: A non-human [creature](#creature) of demonic build, typically with [fangs](#fangs), [horns](#horns), [glowing](#glowing) eyes, [claws](#claws), [hooves](#hooves), [wings](#wings) and a long [tail](#tail). Only for non-human demons; a person with such features is [demon_girl](#demon_girl) or [demon_boy](#demon_boy).

entries.name: kitsune
entries.description: A [fox](#fox) [spirit](#spirit) of Japanese folklore, a shapeshifter said to grow another [tail](#tail) every hundred years up to nine. Use it for characters presented as fox spirits; one with all nine tails is a [kyuubi](#kyuubi).

entries.name: skeleton
entries.description: A full set of bones, whether an [x-ray](#x-ray) view, remains left behind, or a [walking](#walking) skeleton character. Animated ones also take [undead](#undead); non-human bones are [animal_skeleton](#animal_skeleton).

entries.name: nekomata
entries.description: A two-tailed [cat](#cat) [spirit](#spirit) of Japanese folklore, appearing either as a cat or as a catlike person. Where a single [tail](#tail) merely splits at the end, [forked_tail](#forked_tail) is accurate rather than [multiple_tails](#multiple_tails).

entries.name: demon_boy
entries.description: A male character with a demonic look: [horns](#horns), [fangs](#fangs), [glowing](#glowing) eyes, [claws](#claws), [wings](#wings) or a long [tail](#tail). Incubi are nearly always drawn this way.

entries.name: jiangshi
entries.description: A Chinese [hopping](#hopping) [undead](#undead) that drains the life from the living, closer in [idea](#idea) to a [zombie](#zombie) than to a [vampire](#vampire). A [paper](#paper) charm on the [forehead](#forehead) and a round official's cap are the usual markers; a living character merely dressed that way is [jiangshi_costume](#jiangshi_costume).

entries.name: zombie
entries.description: A reanimated [corpse](#corpse) showing visible signs of [death](#death) or decay: greyish or greenish skin, blank eyes, festering wounds and a stiff, shambling gait. Applies to what the picture actually shows, regardless of whether the character is canonically [undead](#undead).

entries.name: kyuubi
entries.description: A [fox](#fox), or fox girl, bearing nine tails, which in Japanese lore is the [height](#height) of a kitsune's age and power. The Korean kumiho and the Chinese huli jing fall under it as [well](#well).

entries.name: angel_girl
entries.description: A young woman with the trappings of an [angel](#angel), typically white feathered [wings](#wings) and a [halo](#halo) [floating](#floating) above her head. The design stays human in shape with the heavenly parts added.

entries.name: fallen_angel
entries.description: An [angel](#angel) turned to evil, marked out by black [wings](#wings), a [broken](#broken) or crooked [halo](#halo) and sometimes [horns](#horns). The angelic shape still shows beneath the [corruption](#corruption).

entries.name: spirit
entries.description: A supernatural being drawn from folklore or belief, such as a [ghost](#ghost), ancestral presence or [nature](#nature) spirit, often shown [translucent](#translucent) or [glowing](#glowing). Also covers a departed soul appearing in a scene.

entries.name: traditional_youkai
entries.description: A Japanese folklore [spirit](#spirit) drawn in its classical form, such as a [kappa](#kappa), a [hannya](#hannya) mask-faced woman or an akaname. A character merely stated to be a youkai does not qualify unless the [creature](#creature) itself is humanoid to begin with.

entries.name: werewolf
entries.description: A human who transforms into a [wolf](#wolf) or a wolf-like beast-man, classically under a full [moon](#moon). Tag either the wolf form or a mid-transformation state.

entries.name: undead
entries.description: A being that has died yet still moves and acts, whether bodiless like a [ghost](#ghost) or physical like a [zombie](#zombie), [vampire](#vampire) or [skeleton](#skeleton). Add the specific [creature](#creature) [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: shikigami
entries.description: A summoned [spirit](#spirit) drawn from onmyoudo mysticism, usually depicted as a small [paper](#paper) [figure](#figure) brought to life or shape-shifted into another form. Tag alongside the [onmyouji](#onmyouji) who controls it.

entries.name: angel_and_devil
entries.description: An [angel](#angel) and a [demon](#demon) appear together, usually staged as a [contrast](#contrast) of light against [dark](#dark) or as a romantic pair. It also covers the two tiny figures perched on somebody's shoulders [arguing](#arguing) over their conscience.

entries.name: tengu
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) of Japanese folklore, drawn either as a crow-headed winged humanoid or as a red-faced, long-nosed man with [wings](#wings). Typical [dress](#dress) includes a [tall](#tall) [hat](#hat), a [mountain](#mountain) ascetic's outfit, one-toothed clogs and a feather fan.

entries.name: mummy
entries.description: A dried and preserved [corpse](#corpse) [bound](#bound) in wrappings for burial, in the ancient Egyptian manner or through extreme [cold](#cold) and dry conditions. It is usually drawn as a shambling bandaged [undead](#undead) [figure](#figure).

entries.name: red_oni
entries.description: An [oni](#oni) with red skin or an otherwise red colour scheme. Frequently paired with a blue oni as a contrasting duo, the red one played as fiery and impulsive against the blue one's cool detachment.

entries.name: ghost_girl
entries.description: A female [spirit](#spirit) of the dead, drawn [semi-transparent](#semi-transparent), [floating](#floating), or with the pale skin and white burial [dress](#dress) of Japanese [ghost](#ghost) stories. The [plain](#plain) ghost [tag](#tag) and the male counterpart sit beside it.

entries.name: valkyrie
entries.description: A [battle](#battle) maiden of Norse myth who chooses who falls in combat, typically drawn as an armoured [warrior](#warrior) woman with a winged [helmet](#helmet) or feathered [wings](#wings), often [carrying](#carrying) a [spear](#spear) or [sword](#sword).

entries.name: sheet_ghost
entries.description: The cartoon [ghost](#ghost) drawn as a [floating](#floating) white [cloth](#cloth) with two [dark](#dark) eye holes cut into it. Also covers a person dressed up in a [plain](#plain) sheet for the same effect.

entries.name: dullahan
entries.description: A being whose head comes away from the body, carried under an arm or hovering nearby while the body walks on. Irish legend gives a [headless](#headless) rider; anime often gives a girl with a detachable head, sometimes an empty [suit](#suit) of armour.

entries.name: kappa
entries.description: A child-sized [river](#river) [spirit](#spirit) with webbed hands and [feet](#feet), a beaked or ape-like face, a [shell](#shell) on its [back](#back) and a dish of [water](#water) set into the top of its head. It is famous for its appetite for cucumbers.

entries.name: shinigami
entries.description: A Japanese [death](#death) [spirit](#spirit) that [gathers](#gathers) souls, typically one of an entire race of such beings rather than a single personified [figure](#figure). Modern designs often borrow the [scythe](#scythe) and [hood](#hood) of the European Reaper.

entries.name: seraph
entries.description: An [angel](#angel) [carrying](#carrying) six [wings](#wings), ranked at the top of Christian angel lore and closest to God. The extra pairs, rather than any particular [robe](#robe), set it apart from a [plain](#plain) angel.

entries.name: yuki_onna
entries.description: A pale, long-haired yokai of Japanese folklore who appears out of [winter](#winter) storms, her skin [blending](#blending) into [falling](#falling) [snow](#snow) until she looks almost ghostly. Artists usually give her a [cold](#cold), still beauty, occasionally with darker or demonic undertones.

entries.name: genie
entries.description: A wish-granting [spirit](#spirit) of Middle Eastern legend, drawn with a smoky [tail](#tail) instead of [legs](#legs), a [lamp](#lamp) nearby, or Arabian-styled [dress](#dress). Djinn falls under the same name.

entries.name: blue_oni
entries.description: An [ogre](#ogre) from Japanese folklore with blue skin or a blue colour scheme, horned and usually powerfully built. It is often set beside a red counterpart, the pairing [playing](#playing) the blue one as the [cooler](#cooler) and more calculating head.

entries.name: tiefling
entries.description: A humanoid with infernal ancestry, borrowed from tabletop [fantasy](#fantasy): [horns](#horns), a long [tail](#tail) and skin in red, violet or near black. Essentially the demon-blooded adventurer rather than a [demon](#demon) proper.

entries.name: bakeneko
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) [spirit](#spirit) with supernatural powers: it conjures ghostly flames, walks upright on its hind [legs](#legs) and creeps into people's dreams. It is drawn far larger than a real cat and [can](#can) take human shape, while the forked-tailed sort goes by [nekomata](#nekomata).

entries.name: tsukumogami
entries.description: A household object that wakes up as a [spirit](#spirit) once it reaches a hundred years of age. Umbrellas, lanterns and [sandals](#sandals) sprouting eyes and limbs are the classic forms.

entries.name: lich
entries.description: An [undead](#undead) spellcaster with a skeletal or shrivelled body who has kept both wits and [magic](#magic). Usually robed, crowned or armoured, unlike a mindless [walking](#walking) [corpse](#corpse).

entries.name: futakuchi-onna
entries.description: A youkai woman [hiding](#hiding) a second mouth beneath the hair at the [back](#back) of her [skull](#skull), which she feeds using strands moved like limbs. Her hair is normally drawn as prehensile.

entries.name: skull_head
entries.description: A living character whose head is a bare [skull](#skull) while the rest of the body is [flesh](#flesh). Not for actual skeletons, and not the same as wearing a skull-shaped [mask](#mask).

entries.name: biblically_accurate_angel
entries.description: An [angel](#angel) drawn as the Book of Ezekiel describes rather than as a winged person: rings covered in eyes, several [animal](#animal) faces at once and tiers of [wings](#wings). Deliberately [alien](#alien) and unsettling, and often played for a joke.

entries.name: shoulder_angel
entries.description: A [miniature](#miniature) winged [figure](#figure) perched on someone's shoulder, voicing the responsible side of an inner argument. Usually paired opposite a matching [shoulder_devil](#shoulder_devil), both scaled down to hand size.

entries.name: cherub
entries.description: A chubby winged [baby](#baby) of the kind western painting scatters through religious and romantic scenes. Give it a [bow](#bow) and love-arrows and it becomes a [cupid](#cupid), and the many-faced beings of scripture [bear](#bear) [no](#no) resemblance at all.

entries.name: shoulder_devil
entries.description: A tiny horned [figure](#figure) perched on someone's shoulder, urging them toward the selfish or mischievous [choice](#choice). Normally paired opposite a [shoulder_angel](#shoulder_angel) on the other side.

entries.name: zashiki-warashi
entries.description: A child-shaped household [spirit](#spirit) of Japanese folklore, said to bring a [family](#family) good fortune while it stays and misfortune once it leaves. Drawn as a small [child](#child) in old-fashioned [clothes](#clothes), typically in a [tatami](#tatami) room, and said to be glimpsed only as it departs.

entries.name: horse_girl
entries.description: A human girl with [horse](#horse) traits, usually horse ears and a horse [tail](#tail); [pegasus](#pegasus) and [unicorn](#unicorn) girls count too. Characters with horse [legs](#legs) or a horse body, such as centaurs, do not.

entries.name: cat_girl
entries.description: A female character [carrying](#carrying) genuine feline traits, ears on the head or a [tail](#tail) behind. Costume ears alone take [cat_ears](#cat_ears) with a [costume](#costume) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: monster_girl
entries.description: A girl who is part human and part [monster](#monster): [lamia](#lamia), [harpy](#harpy), [centaur](#centaur), [mermaid](#mermaid), slime girl, [arachne](#arachne). Ordinary [cat](#cat) girls, and [demon](#demon) or [dragon](#dragon) girls [carrying](#carrying) nothing but [horns](#horns), [wings](#wings) or a [tail](#tail), are not included.

entries.name: fox_girl
entries.description: A girl who genuinely carries the features of a [fox](#fox), most often the pointed ears and the bushy brush behind her. Kitsune characters are the classic case, and a mere [costume](#costume) does not qualify.

entries.name: dragon_girl
entries.description: A woman or girl built with draconic features, anything from a modest pair of [horns](#horns) and a [tail](#tail) to a shapeshifter who turns into the beast outright. The [animal](#animal) itself is [dragon](#dragon), and every dragon-blooded person belongs here.

entries.name: rabbit_girl
entries.description: A female character with genuine [rabbit](#rabbit) features, such as real ears or a [tail](#tail). The leotard-and-headband [costume](#costume) is called [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny) despite the similar nickname; combine this [tag](#tag) with [rabbit_ears](#rabbit_ears).

entries.name: kemonomimi_mode
entries.description: A character who normally has [no](#no) [animal](#animal) traits is drawn with ears, a [tail](#tail) or a [patch](#patch) of fur added. Ears worn as an accessory are [fake_animal_ears](#fake_animal_ears), and a [snout](#snout) or a full [coat](#coat) of fur makes it [furrification](#furrification) instead.

entries.name: wolf_girl
entries.description: A girl or woman with [wolf](#wolf) features, typically [wolf_ears](#wolf_ears) and a [wolf_tail](#wolf_tail) on an otherwise human body. A fully anthro wolf takes wolf together with anthro instead, while the male counterpart is [wolf_boy](#wolf_boy).

entries.name: dog_girl
entries.description: A girl with canine traits, [dog_ears](#dog_ears) and a [dog_tail](#dog_tail) chief among them, otherwise built like a person. The [animal](#animal) itself is [dog](#dog).

entries.name: cat_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) genuine feline traits, ears on the head or a [tail](#tail) behind. Ears that are only part of a [costume](#costume) take [cat_ears](#cat_ears) with a costume [tag](#tag).

entries.name: cow_girl
entries.description: A girl given [cow](#cow) features or dressed in them: ears, [horns](#horns), a tufted [tail](#tail), [patch](#patch) print, a [bell](#bell), and often a [heavy](#heavy) bust. A hooded [suit](#suit) is [cow_costume](#cow_costume), and the [sex](#sex) position [sharing](#sharing) the word is [cowgirl_position](#cowgirl_position).

entries.name: mouse_girl
entries.description: A girl whose own body carries rodent traits, typically round ears and a thin bare [tail](#tail), rather than a [costume](#costume). Rat girls are covered too.

entries.name: monster_boy
entries.description: A male who is part human and part [monster](#monster): [centaur](#centaur), [merman](#merman), [lizardman](#lizardman), [minotaur](#minotaur), slime boy and the like. Plain animal-eared boys and named types such as [demon](#demon) boys fall outside it.

entries.name: ox_girl
entries.description: A girl with the ears, tufted [tail](#tail) and often the [horns](#horns) of an ox. A regular sight in Year of the Ox illustrations.

entries.name: arthropod_girl
entries.description: A girl with insect or arthropod features on a human body, such as [antennae](#antennae), [wings](#wings), compound eyes or extra limbs. Tag the particular kind, [bee_girl](#bee_girl) or [spider_girl](#spider_girl), where it is recognizable.

entries.name: dog_boy
entries.description: A boy with canine traits, [dog_ears](#dog_ears) and a [dog_tail](#dog_tail) chief among them, otherwise built like a person. The [animal](#animal) itself is [dog](#dog).

entries.name: tiger_girl
entries.description: A female character with intrinsic [tiger](#tiger) features such as ears, a [tail](#tail) or stripes. Add [tiger_ears](#tiger_ears) and [tiger_tail](#tiger_tail) for the specific features.

entries.name: raccoon_girl
entries.description: A girl with genuine [raccoon](#raccoon) or [tanuki](#tanuki) features, such as ears and a ringed [tail](#tail). Confusion between the two real animals means their traits are often mixed on the same character.

entries.name: wolf_boy
entries.description: A boy or man [carrying](#carrying) [wolf](#wolf) traits, typically [wolf_ears](#wolf_ears) and a [wolf_tail](#wolf_tail), on an otherwise human body. A fully anthro wolf is tagged wolf together with anthro instead.

entries.name: fox_boy
entries.description: A boy who genuinely carries the features of a [fox](#fox), the ears and the brush being the usual pair, rather than wearing them as a [costume](#costume). He is the male counterpart to [fox_girl](#fox_girl).

entries.name: dragon_boy
entries.description: A male character with draconic traits such as [horns](#horns), [wings](#wings) or a serpentine [tail](#tail), otherwise built like a person. The beast itself is [dragon](#dragon).

entries.name: lion_girl
entries.description: A girl with [lion](#lion) traits such as rounded ears, a tufted [tail](#tail) or a [mane](#mane), a variant of the [cat_girl](#cat_girl). Pair it with [lion_ears](#lion_ears) and [lion_tail](#lion_tail).

entries.name: slime_girl
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) girl whose body is [translucent](#translucent), viscous [liquid](#liquid) shaped like a human, sometimes half-puddled on the [floor](#floor). Add [core](#core) when a nucleus is visible inside her.

entries.name: bird_girl
entries.description: A girl with [bird](#bird) features such as [feathers](#feathers), [wings](#wings) or a [tail](#tail) on a human body. Unlike a [harpy](#harpy), she does not usually count as a [monster_girl](#monster_girl).

entries.name: sheep_girl
entries.description: A girl with [sheep](#sheep) features such as curled [horns](#horns), floppy ears or a woolly [coat](#coat). Often mistaken for [goat_girl](#goat_girl), though [goat](#goat) horns curve without spiralling and goat tails point up while sheep tails hang down.

entries.name: plant_girl
entries.description: A feminine humanoid whose body is partly [plant](#plant), such as one growing from a large [flower](#flower) or rooted like a [mandragora](#mandragora). A less human or non-feminine version of the same [idea](#idea) is [plant_monster](#plant_monster).

entries.name: tiger_boy
entries.description: A male character with [tiger](#tiger) traits such as striped ears, a [tail](#tail) or orange-and-black fur. Add [tiger_ears](#tiger_ears) and [tiger_tail](#tiger_tail) for the specific features.

entries.name: squirrel_girl
entries.description: A girl with [squirrel](#squirrel) traits such as pointed ears or a bushy [tail](#tail). Characters formally named Squirrel Girl are tagged by their own character tags instead.

entries.name: fish_girl
entries.description: A fish-like [monster](#monster) girl who keeps human [legs](#legs), marked out by head [fins](#fins), [scales](#scales), [gills](#gills) or webbed hands and [feet](#feet). She may have a [tail](#tail) besides; where the lower body cannot be seen, fall [back](#back) on [mermaid](#mermaid).

entries.name: rabbit_boy
entries.description: A male character with genuine [rabbit](#rabbit) traits, such as real ears or a [tail](#tail), rather than a [costume](#costume). A boy dressed in a bunnysuit instead is [male_playboy_bunny](#male_playboy_bunny).

entries.name: jellyfish_girl
entries.description: A girl shaped around [jellyfish](#jellyfish) [anatomy](#anatomy): a see-through [bell](#bell) worn like a [hood](#hood) or a [skirt](#skirt), [tentacles](#tentacles) in place of loose hair, limbs you [can](#can) look through. She is nearly always adrift [underwater](#underwater).

entries.name: deer_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [deer](#deer) traits such as [deer_ears](#deer_ears), [antlers](#antlers) or a [deer_tail](#deer_tail), with the rest of her built as human. The [animal](#animal) itself takes deer, and the male counterpart is [deer_boy](#deer_boy).

entries.name: bear_girl
entries.description: A girl with [bear](#bear) traits such as round ears and a short [tail](#tail), a kemonomimi type. A fully anthropomorphic bear takes the [plain](#plain) bear [tag](#tag).

entries.name: goat_girl
entries.description: A girl or female humanoid with [goat](#goat) traits such as [goat_ears](#goat_ears), [goat_horns](#goat_horns), a goat [tail](#tail) or [horizontal_pupils](#horizontal_pupils). Keep her apart from [sheep_girl](#sheep_girl): goat [horns](#horns) curve without coiling round, and a goat's upper lip is not divided.

entries.name: panther_girl
entries.description: A girl with black-panther traits such as [panther_ears](#panther_ears), a long [dark](#dark) [tail](#tail) or black fur. Drawn in a dark colour scheme, especially among [furry](#furry) characters.

entries.name: bat_girl
entries.description: A girl whose own body carries bat traits, typically bat ears and leathery [wings](#wings). She is a monster-girl or kemonomimi type and has nothing to do with the American comics heroine of a similar name.

entries.name: lion_boy
entries.description: A boy or man with genuine [lion](#lion) features such as [lion_ears](#lion_ears), a [lion_tail](#lion_tail) or a [mane](#mane), while staying mostly human in shape. The male counterpart of [lion_girl](#lion_girl).

entries.name: cow_boy
entries.description: A male character given [cow](#cow) features or dressed in them: ears, [horns](#horns), a tufted [tail](#tail), patch-printed [clothes](#clothes), a [bell](#bell), ear tags. A full hooded [suit](#suit) is [cow_costume](#cow_costume), a bull-headed being is a [minotaur](#minotaur), and the Wild West sort is [cowboy_western](#cowboy_western).

entries.name: frog_girl
entries.description: A female character with amphibian features such as a long [sticky](#sticky) [tongue](#tongue), webbed fingers and [toes](#toes) and wide-set eyes. She belongs with the other animal-girl types rather than with fully anthro frogs.

entries.name: bear_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [bear](#bear) traits, typically round ears and a stubby [tail](#tail) on an otherwise human body. The male counterpart of [bear_girl](#bear_girl); a fully anthropomorphic bear is tagged bear instead.

entries.name: reptile_girl
entries.description: A girl with reptilian features such as a [lizard](#lizard) [tail](#tail), [scales](#scales), or slit pupils on an otherwise human body. A monster-girl type; a fully scaled anthro character is a reptile instead.

entries.name: fish_boy
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) boy [carrying](#carrying) obvious [fish](#fish) traits — [gills](#gills), [scales](#scales) over the body, head [fins](#fins), odd skin colour — while still [standing](#standing) on two [legs](#legs). A [merman](#merman), whose only fishy part is his [tail](#tail), is something else.

entries.name: bird_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [bird](#bird) traits such as [feathers](#feathers), [wings](#wings) or a [tail](#tail) on an otherwise human body. The male counterpart to [bird_girl](#bird_girl).

entries.name: arthropod_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) insect or other arthropod traits on an otherwise human body: [antennae](#antennae), a [carapace](#carapace), compound eyes, [wings](#wings) or extra limbs. Name the particular [creature](#creature) where it [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: goat_boy
entries.description: A boy given [goat](#goat) features: curving [horns](#horns), drooping ears, a stubby [tail](#tail), sometimes hooved [legs](#legs). The male counterpart to [goat_girl](#goat_girl).

entries.name: monkey_girl
entries.description: A girl given [monkey](#monkey) features — round ears, a long [tail](#tail), sometimes fur at the wrists and ankles — on an otherwise human body. The traits are part of her, not something pulled on.

entries.name: hedgehog_girl
entries.description: A girl with [hedgehog](#hedgehog) features of her own: [spines](#spines) among or in place of the hair, hedgehog ears, now and then a short [tail](#tail).

entries.name: bee_girl
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) girl built on a [bee](#bee): [antennae](#antennae), large faceted eyes, a striped abdomen with a [stinger](#stinger) and thin [translucent](#translucent) [wings](#wings). The traits are part of her rather than something she has put on.

entries.name: monkey_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [monkey](#monkey) traits — rounded ears, a long curling [tail](#tail), sometimes a [patch](#patch) of fur — on a body that is otherwise human. The features are his own rather than a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: horse_boy
entries.description: A boy or man with [horse](#horse) traits, such as ears, [tail](#tail) and [mane](#mane), on an otherwise human two-legged body. Pegasus, pony and [unicorn](#unicorn) boys count as [well](#well); centaurs do not.

entries.name: weasel_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [weasel](#weasel) traits, typically the ears and a long slim [tail](#tail), while the rest of her stays human. Stoats and ferrets of the same [family](#family) fall under this too.

entries.name: hedgehog_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [hedgehog](#hedgehog) traits on an otherwise human body: quills over the head and [back](#back), rounded ears, sometimes a stub of a [tail](#tail).

entries.name: moth_girl
entries.description: A girl built on [moth](#moth) traits: plumed [antennae](#antennae), dusty [patterned](#patterned) [wings](#wings) and often a thick [fluffy](#fluffy) [collar](#collar). Artists like to joke about her being drawn to lamps.

entries.name: hyena_boy
entries.description: A male character given [hyena](#hyena) features on an otherwise human build: rounded ears, a short bristling [tail](#tail), spotted [markings](#markings). He stands upright rather than going on all fours, and is the counterpart of [hyena_girl](#hyena_girl).

entries.name: owl_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [owl](#owl) traits: feathered arms or hair, ear tufts, a [beak](#beak), or a spread of [tail](#tail) [feathers](#feathers). One of the [bird](#bird) members of the animal-girl [family](#family).

entries.name: orca_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [orca](#orca) traits: black-and-white [markings](#markings), a fluked [tail](#tail) and often [fins](#fins) or a dorsal ridge. The cetacean member of the animal-girl [family](#family).

entries.name: reptile_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) reptilian features on an otherwise human frame, such as patches of [scales](#scales), a [lizard](#lizard) [tail](#tail), or slitted eyes. The female counterpart is [reptile_girl](#reptile_girl).

entries.name: raccoon_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) [raccoon](#raccoon) or [tanuki](#tanuki) traits, typically the ears and a ringed [tail](#tail), on an otherwise human body. Use the girl equivalent for female characters.

entries.name: squid_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [squid](#squid) traits such as tentacle-like hair, [fins](#fins), suckers or a mantle worn like a [hood](#hood). One of several sea-creature [monster](#monster) girls.

entries.name: snow_leopard_girl
entries.description: A female character with [snow](#snow) [leopard](#leopard) traits, most often the pale rounded ears and a long spotted [tail](#tail), her coloring generally [following](#following) the animal's grey and [cream](#cream) palette.

entries.name: chipmunk_girl
entries.description: A girl built on [chipmunk](#chipmunk) features, generally the small round ears and a striped bushy [tail](#tail) on an otherwise human body. For the [animal](#animal) itself use chipmunk.

entries.name: jaguar_girl
entries.description: A girl with [jaguar](#jaguar) traits, typically spotted ears and [tail](#tail) and sometimes rosettes on her skin. The spotting is what separates her from a [plain](#plain) [cat_girl](#cat_girl).

entries.name: leopard_girl
entries.description: A girl with built-in [leopard](#leopard) features such as spotted ears, a [tail](#tail) and rosettes on the skin. Snow leopard characters count as their own kind despite the shared name.

entries.name: penguin_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [penguin](#penguin) traits: a beaked [hood](#hood) or [headdress](#headdress), flipper-like arms, a stubby [tail](#tail), or black-and-white colouring laid out the way the bird's is.

entries.name: reindeer_girl
entries.description: A girl with [reindeer](#reindeer) traits: branching [antlers](#antlers), [furry](#furry) ears, and often a short [tail](#tail), on a human body. Christmas artwork is where most of them appear.

entries.name: leopard_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [leopard](#leopard) traits such as spotted ears, a spotted [tail](#tail) or rosette [markings](#markings), while otherwise human in build.

entries.name: dolphin_girl
entries.description: A girl with cetacean traits: a dorsal fin, a fluked [tail](#tail), smooth grey and white skin, sometimes a [blowhole](#blowhole). The body otherwise stays human.

entries.name: jackal_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [jackal](#jackal) traits, most often the [tall](#tall) pointed ears and the [tail](#tail), with the rest of him human. Egyptian-flavoured designs after Anubis are common.

entries.name: pig_girl
entries.description: A girl with [pig](#pig) features set on a human body: a snub [snout](#snout), small round ears, sometimes a curled [tail](#tail). One of the animal-girl [family](#family), beside [cat_girl](#cat_girl) and its relatives.

entries.name: hyena_girl
entries.description: A female character [carrying](#carrying) [hyena](#hyena) traits such as rounded ears, a short [tail](#tail) and spotted fur while keeping a human body. She is drawn upright, not as a four-legged beast.

entries.name: red_panda_girl
entries.description: A girl given red [panda](#panda) features, the round furred ears, the ringed bushy [tail](#tail), and often the pale face [markings](#markings), on a human body. Used for the kemonomimi styling rather than a full anthro character.

entries.name: deer_boy
entries.description: A male character with cervine traits: ears, [antlers](#antlers), a short flagged [tail](#tail), sometimes [hooves](#hooves). The female version is [deer_girl](#deer_girl), and a fully [animal](#animal) build takes the anthro tags.

entries.name: panda_boy
entries.description: A boy with [panda](#panda) features: round black ears, [dark](#dark) eye patches, often a stubby [tail](#tail). The male counterpart of [panda_girl](#panda_girl).

entries.name: slug_girl
entries.description: A female [monster](#monster) character with [slug](#slug) traits: eyestalks or [antennae](#antennae), a slick body and often a soft [muscular](#muscular) foot in place of [legs](#legs). Unlike a [snail](#snail) girl she carries [no](#no) [shell](#shell).

entries.name: panda_girl
entries.description: A girl with [panda](#panda) traits such as rounded black ears, [dark](#dark) eye [markings](#markings) or a short [tail](#tail). One of the bear-based [animal](#animal) girls.

entries.name: mouse_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) mouse traits such as round ears and a thin bare [tail](#tail), human in every other respect. The features belong to his body rather than to a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: cockroach_girl
entries.description: An insect girl built on a [cockroach](#cockroach), with [antennae](#antennae), brown [carapace](#carapace) plates and often wing cases over a human frame. One of the arthropod monster-girl designs.

entries.name: ferret_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [ferret](#ferret) traits, usually the small rounded ears and a long slim [tail](#tail), on an otherwise human body. One of the wider [family](#family) of animal-eared characters.

entries.name: komainu_boy
entries.description: A male character given the ears, [tail](#tail) and [mane](#mane) of a [shrine](#shrine) guardian lion-dog on an otherwise human body. A shrine-flavoured cousin of the usual animal-eared boys.

entries.name: sea_slug_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) sea [slug](#slug) traits, most often frilled head appendages and vivid trailing growths down her [back](#back). Usually paired with [sea_slug_ears](#sea_slug_ears).

entries.name: snow_leopard_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) [snow](#snow) [leopard](#leopard) traits, usually rounded pale ears and a long, thickly furred rosetted [tail](#tail), with the rest of his body [reading](#reading) as human.

entries.name: dinosaur_girl
entries.description: A female character given saurian traits such as [scales](#scales), a thick [tail](#tail) or clawed [feet](#feet), otherwise built like a person. Sits beside the other part-animal [people](#people) rather than with the beasts.

entries.name: slime_boy
entries.description: A male [monster](#monster) character whose body is made of [translucent](#translucent) gelatinous fluid, often with objects or bubbles visible suspended inside him. His [outline](#outline) may wobble, drip or lose shape entirely.

entries.name: whale_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [whale](#whale) features such as a fluked [tail](#tail), [fins](#fins) or a [blowhole](#blowhole) while otherwise staying human in shape. Ocean settings and blue-grey coloring usually accompany her.

entries.name: sheep_boy
entries.description: A boy drawn with [sheep](#sheep) traits: curled [horns](#horns), drooping woolly ears, sometimes a fleecy [collar](#collar) or a short [tail](#tail).

entries.name: komainu_girl
entries.description: A girl given the ears and thick [tail](#tail) of the stone lion-dogs that [guard](#guard) [shrine](#shrine) gates. Shrine grounds and miko-styled [dress](#dress) are the usual accompaniment.

entries.name: jaguar_boy
entries.description: A boy given [jaguar](#jaguar) traits, generally rounded spotted ears and a spotted [tail](#tail) on an otherwise human body. Cat_boy, [tiger_boy](#tiger_boy) or [panther_boy](#panther_boy) [suit](#suit) better when the [markings](#markings) say so.

entries.name: hamster_girl
entries.description: A girl given [hamster](#hamster) features: round ears, a stump of a [tail](#tail), tiny paws and often bulging cheeks. The degree varies from a human with ears added to a fully rodent-faced character.

entries.name: eel_boy
entries.description: A boy built partly as an [eel](#eel), usually with a long finned lower body where the [legs](#legs) would be. The eel answer to merfolk designs.

entries.name: boar_boy
entries.description: A boy with [boar](#boar) features, as a rule the ears and a pair of small [tusks](#tusks), human in every other respect. He belongs with the pig-derived animal-eared characters rather than with full anthro designs.

entries.name: alpaca_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [alpaca](#alpaca) traits, generally [fluffy](#fluffy) upright ears, a woolly [mane](#mane) of hair and sometimes a short [tail](#tail). Her body stays human with the [animal](#animal) parts added on.

entries.name: mantis_girl
entries.description: A girl built on praying-mantis lines, with scythed forelimbs, insect [wings](#wings) or a chitinous [shell](#shell) over an otherwise human shape. Generally a [monster](#monster) girl.

entries.name: dinosaur_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) saurian traits: scaled skin, a [heavy](#heavy) [tail](#tail), clawed hands, sometimes a [crest](#crest). The body stays broadly human, since a full beast belongs under the [animal](#animal) tags.

entries.name: otter_girl
entries.description: A girl with [otter](#otter) features: rounded ears, [whiskers](#whiskers) and a thick tapering [tail](#tail). She sits with the other river-mammal [animal](#animal) girls.

entries.name: pig_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) porcine traits on an otherwise human body: a [snout](#snout), small rounded ears, sometimes a curled [tail](#tail). The female counterpart is [pig_girl](#pig_girl).

entries.name: cheetah_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) cheetah traits: round spotted ears, a long spotted [tail](#tail), the [dark](#dark) tear lines [running](#running) down from the eyes. Designs built around speed favour her.

entries.name: frog_boy
entries.description: A male character built on amphibian traits: a wide mouth, bulging eyes, webbed hands and often green skin. Ranges from a mascot-shaped [creature](#creature) to a boy who carries only a hint of the [frog](#frog) about him.

entries.name: cross-species_cosplay
entries.description: An animal-eared character sporting the ears and [tail](#tail) of a different [animal](#animal), such as a [fox](#fox) girl fitted out as a [rabbit](#rabbit). The borrowed features may have grown on her or be worn as fakes.

entries.name: scorpion_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [scorpion](#scorpion) traits: at minimum the stinging [tail](#tail), sometimes pincer hands, a chitinous lower body, or hair shaped like the creature's [legs](#legs). Tag [monster_girl](#monster_girl) as [well](#well) when the design is far enough from human.

entries.name: skunk_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) skunk features, typically the ears and the broad striped [tail](#tail). Otherwise built as an ordinary human.

entries.name: zebra_girl
entries.description: A character [carrying](#carrying) [zebra](#zebra) traits, such as striped ears, [mane](#mane), [tail](#tail) or body [markings](#markings), on an otherwise human body. One of the animal-girl designs rather than a full anthro build.

entries.name: ant_girl
entries.description: A girl built on an [ant](#ant), human in shape but [carrying](#carrying) [antennae](#antennae), chitin plating and sometimes an extra pair of limbs. One of the insect-based [monster](#monster) girl designs.

entries.name: giraffe_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [giraffe](#giraffe) traits: the ears, the knob-like [horns](#horns), patched skin or an elongated [neck](#neck). Sits with the other animal-eared girls.

entries.name: snail_girl
entries.description: A female [monster](#monster) character [carrying](#carrying) a snail's [shell](#shell) on her [back](#back), often with a slick foot instead of [legs](#legs) and eyestalk-like [antennae](#antennae) on her head. Without the shell she would be a [slug](#slug) girl.

entries.name: panther_boy
entries.description: A male character with black-panther traits, usually the ears and [tail](#tail), and in [furry](#furry) work [dark](#dark) fur in black or deep purple. Use it for the character; the separate features have tags of their own.

entries.name: capybara_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [capybara](#capybara) traits — the small round ears, blunt features and unbothered calm of the [animal](#animal). A [hot](#hot) spring is usually somewhere nearby.

entries.name: centipede_girl
entries.description: A girl built along [centipede](#centipede) lines: a long segmented lower body of many [legs](#legs), [antennae](#antennae), plated armour down the [back](#back). Add [monster_girl](#monster_girl) once those parts dominate the design.

entries.name: crocodile_boy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) [crocodilian](#crocodilian) traits: a scaled hide, a long toothy [snout](#snout) or a [heavy](#heavy) ridged [tail](#tail). It runs from an otherwise human boy with a few reptile features to a fully scaled one.

entries.name: rhinoceros_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) genuine [rhinoceros](#rhinoceros) traits, such as the ears, a [nose](#nose) horn or a stubby [tail](#tail). Not to be [confused](#confused) with someone simply wearing a rhino [costume](#costume).

entries.name: chinchilla_girl
entries.description: A girl given chinchilla features on an otherwise human body: the wide round ears, a thick bushy [tail](#tail), soft grey colouring. One of the rarer rodent varieties of animal-eared character.

entries.name: squirrel_boy
entries.description: A boy [carrying](#carrying) [squirrel](#squirrel) features, most often tufted ears and a large bushy [tail](#tail). Buck [teeth](#teeth) and small paw-like hands sometimes come with them.

entries.name: chameleon_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [chameleon](#chameleon) traits: independently swivelling eyes, a curling prehensile [tail](#tail), scaly patches, sometimes skin that shifts colour. Add [monster_girl](#monster_girl) once the reptile parts take over the design.

entries.name: crab_girl
entries.description: A girl built with [crab](#crab) features: [pincers](#pincers), a [shell](#shell) across the [back](#back), stalked eyes or jointed [legs](#legs). A monster-girl design rather than a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: axolotl_girl
entries.description: A girl given [axolotl](#axolotl) features: frilled pink gill stalks sprouting at the sides of her head, that wide upturned mouth, and sometimes a flat [paddle](#paddle) [tail](#tail). Everything else stays human, in the usual monster-girl pattern.

entries.name: butterfly_girl
entries.description: A girl built on a [butterfly](#butterfly): [wings](#wings) spread from her [back](#back), [antennae](#antennae) above the brow, and often [patterned](#patterned) limbs. One of the arthropod [monster](#monster) girls.

entries.name: donkey_girl
entries.description: A girl with [donkey](#donkey) traits, most often the long tapering ears and sometimes a tufted [tail](#tail) or [hooves](#hooves). The body otherwise stays human, as with [cat_girl](#cat_girl) and [horse_girl](#horse_girl).

entries.name: stoat_girl
entries.description: A girl with the ears and [tail](#tail) of a stoat, human otherwise. Her slim build, small rounded ears and dark-tipped tail set her apart from other weasel-type kemonomimi.

entries.name: plant_boy
entries.description: A male character built from [vines](#vines), leaves and [petals](#petals) while still keeping a humanoid shape. A growth that is not humanoid is [plant_monster](#plant_monster) instead, and merely commanding plants is a different concept entirely.

entries.name: moose_girl
entries.description: A girl [carrying](#carrying) [moose](#moose) traits, most often the wide ears and a set of palmate [antlers](#antlers), on a body that is otherwise human. The features are her own rather than a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: alien
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) that is visibly not from Earth. It does not apply to extraterrestrials drawn indistinguishably from humans, since only what is shown counts.

entries.name: spider_girl
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) girl with [spider](#spider) features: eight limbs in total, the ability to spin webbing, sometimes hair styled like spider [legs](#legs), and often a full spider abdomen beneath a humanoid [torso](#torso). Tag the character type, not simply a spider in the scene.

entries.name: eldritch_abomination
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) of cosmic horror whose shape ignores natural law, all [tentacles](#tentacles), stray eyes and impossible [geometry](#geometry). The look is meant to be maddening; Lovecraft's pantheon is the [model](#model).

entries.name: twi'lek
entries.description: A humanoid [alien](#alien) species marked by a pair of long fleshy head-tails [hanging](#hanging) from the [skull](#skull) in place of hair. Drawn from a well-known science-fiction film series.

entries.name: cupid
entries.description: The Roman god of desire, drawn as a winged archer whose arrows make [people](#people) fall in love. Modern versions make him a chubby winged infant; an unarmed one of those is a [cherub](#cherub) instead.

entries.name: spider_boy
entries.description: A male character built on a [spider](#spider), [blending](#blending) human features with arachnid ones such as extra eyes, additional limbs, or a bulbous abdomen. The counterpart to [spider_girl](#spider_girl).

entries.name: mindflayer
entries.description: A humanoid with purple skin and a squid-like head, face [tentacles](#tentacles) trailing over the mouth. Dominates minds telepathically and feeds on brains.

entries.name: dog
entries.description: A dog of any breed, kept as a [pet](#pet) or [running](#running) wild; the individual breeds have their own spellings. A person [carrying](#carrying) dog features is [dog_girl](#dog_girl) or [dog_boy](#dog_boy).

entries.name: fox
entries.description: The actual [animal](#animal): a small bushy-tailed canine with a long [snout](#snout), usually red but drawn in yellow, brown, grey, white or black too. It also covers a depiction of one, such as a painting or a [mask](#mask); human characters with fox traits use [fox_ears](#fox_ears), [fox_tail](#fox_tail) or [fox_girl](#fox_girl).

entries.name: wolf
entries.description: The grey wolf, a large wild canine with a bushy [tail](#tail), big paws, and a [coat](#coat) that ranges from mottled grey to white, red, brown, or black. It covers both the [animal](#animal) itself and an anthro wolf, while a girl with wolf ears instead takes [wolf_girl](#wolf_girl).

entries.name: tanuki
entries.description: The Japanese [raccoon](#raccoon) [dog](#dog), folklore's playful shape-shifting [spirit](#spirit), drawn with brown fur, a round [belly](#belly) and, in traditional statues, famously oversized [testicles](#testicles). Not the same [animal](#animal) as a raccoon, which has grey fur and a different face.

entries.name: shiba_inu
entries.description: The compact Japanese [dog](#dog) breed with a fox-like face, a curled [fluffy](#fluffy) [tail](#tail) and typically [tan](#tan) fur, smaller than an akita. Tag with dog.

entries.name: puppy
entries.description: A young [dog](#dog), from newborn up to roughly a year [old](#old), drawn with the rounded body and oversized paws of a juvenile. A dog-eared human [child](#child) does not count as a puppy.

entries.name: white_dog
entries.description: A [dog](#dog) with an all-white [coat](#coat), from spitz breeds to shaggy mongrels. A white-furred [wolf](#wolf) instead falls under [white_wolf](#white_wolf).

entries.name: welsh_corgi
entries.description: A short-legged herding [dog](#dog) with a long low body, big upright ears and a fox-like face. Both the stubby-tailed and the longer-tailed varieties count.

entries.name: great_pyrenees
entries.description: A large white livestock guardian from the mountains between France and Spain, thick-coated and calm in bearing. Drawn as a gentle [giant](#giant) of a [dog](#dog).

entries.name: dobermann
entries.description: The sleek German guard-dog breed, short-coated in black and [tan](#tan) with a long muzzle and often [cropped](#cropped) upright ears. Drawn as an [animal](#animal) or worked into an anthro design.

entries.name: husky
entries.description: The cold-weather [sled](#sled) [dog](#dog) with upright ears, a thick grey-and-white [coat](#coat) and often blue eyes. It appears as an [animal](#animal), as a feral character or as an anthro one.

entries.name: fennec_fox
entries.description: The tiny [desert](#desert) [fox](#fox) of North Africa, sandy-coated with enormous ears. Drawn as a real [animal](#animal) or as an anthro character; the ears are the giveaway.

entries.name: white_wolf
entries.description: A [wolf](#wolf) with an entirely white [coat](#coat), drawn as an [animal](#animal) rather than a person. Arctic settings and spiritual imagery both favour it.

entries.name: samoyed_(dog)
entries.description: A medium-sized Siberian sledding breed with a dense white or [cream](#cream) double [coat](#coat), pricked ears and a [tail](#tail) carried over the [spine](#spine).

entries.name: pomeranian_(dog)
entries.description: A [toy](#toy) spitz breed with a dense double [coat](#coat), small pricked ears and a plumed [tail](#tail). Bred down from larger [sled](#sled) dogs and long popular as a lapdog.

entries.name: golden_retriever
entries.description: A large Scottish gundog with a dense golden [coat](#coat), a feathered [tail](#tail) and a famously mild temper. Drawn as a [family](#family) [pet](#pet) and as a byword for friendliness.

entries.name: multiple_dogs
entries.description: More than one [dog](#dog) in the picture. Once the pack grows large enough that [counting](#counting) stops mattering, too_many_dogs takes over.

entries.name: german_shepherd
entries.description: A large [working](#working) [dog](#dog) with big upright ears, a level [muscular](#muscular) [back](#back) and a bushy downward-curving [tail](#tail), coated in black and [tan](#tan), black or grey. Also called an Alsatian, and the [tag](#tag) covers both animals and characters of the breed.

entries.name: brown_dog
entries.description: A [dog](#dog) with a brown [coat](#coat), of any breed or size. The [shade](#shade) runs from light [tan](#tan) through to deep [chocolate](#chocolate).

entries.name: pug
entries.description: A small companion [dog](#dog) of Chinese origin, with a flat wrinkled face, bulging eyes, and a [tail](#tail) curled over the [back](#back). Bold and stubborn despite its size.

entries.name: chihuahua
entries.description: A tiny [toy](#toy) [dog](#dog) with a domed [skull](#skull), huge round eyes and upright ears. Its outsized attitude relative to its size is usually part of the joke.

entries.name: black_dog
entries.description: A [dog](#dog) with a black [coat](#coat), of any breed. The colour is the whole of what it records, so add the breed alongside it where that [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: bernese_mountain_dog
entries.description: A big [heavy](#heavy) Swiss [working](#working) [dog](#dog) in a long tricolour [coat](#coat): black body, white blaze and chest, [rust](#rust) [markings](#markings) above the eyes and down the [legs](#legs). Drawn as a [pet](#pet), a companion or the basis of a dog character.

entries.name: boston_terrier
entries.description: A small compact [dog](#dog) with upright ears, a flat short muzzle and a stubby [tail](#tail). White across the chest and face against a [dark](#dark) [coat](#coat) gives it a dinner-jacket look.

entries.name: jackal
entries.description: The jackal, a slim wild canine of Africa and Asia, whether as a [plain](#plain) [animal](#animal), a feral character or an anthro one. It often lies behind Anubis-styled designs.

entries.name: border_collie
entries.description: A medium herding [dog](#dog) with a lean athletic frame and a moderately long [coat](#coat), generally black and white and sometimes touched with [tan](#tan). Known as a sheepdog and as an agility competitor.

entries.name: st_bernard
entries.description: A huge Alpine [rescue](#rescue) [dog](#dog) with a [heavy](#heavy) white-and-brown [coat](#coat), drooping jowls and a famously gentle temper. Popular imagination always adds the small brandy [barrel](#barrel) at its [collar](#collar).

entries.name: grey_wolf
entries.description: A [wolf](#wolf) drawn in the ordinary grey [coat](#coat) of the species, shown as an [animal](#animal) rather than a person. Pictured alone, [running](#running) with a pack, or [howling](#howling).

entries.name: dachshund
entries.description: The long-bodied, short-legged hound also called a [sausage](#sausage) or wiener [dog](#dog). Drawn as a [pet](#pet) in the scene, or as the breed a dog character is modelled on.

entries.name: dalmatian
entries.description: A [dog](#dog) with a white [coat](#coat) scattered with black [spots](#spots), drawn as an [animal](#animal) or as an anthro character. The breed carries associations with [fire](#fire) stations and with the film about a hundred and one of them.

entries.name: beagle
entries.description: A compact scent hound with a domed [skull](#skull), long soft ears and a smooth white, [tan](#tan) and black [coat](#coat). The best-known cartoon [dog](#dog) of the American [newspaper](#newspaper) strips is one.

entries.name: poodle
entries.description: A curly-coated [dog](#dog) with long [legs](#legs), drooping ears and a puffed [tail](#tail), bred in everything from [toy](#toy) to standard size. Frequently drawn with the clipped show trim.

entries.name: afghan_hound
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), slender sighthound whose long silky [coat](#coat) hangs from its body in [curtains](#curtains). The narrow muzzle and flowing hair make it instantly recognisable among [dog](#dog) breeds.

entries.name: papillon_(dog)
entries.description: A small French [toy](#toy) breed named for its [butterfly](#butterfly) ears, which stand upright, set wide and fringed with long silky fur. Fine-boned, with a plumed [tail](#tail) carried over the [back](#back).

entries.name: cat
entries.description: A domestic cat, and also cat-shaped things such as plush cats, cat spirits and bodiless cat heads. A person with feline ears is a [cat_girl](#cat_girl) or [cat_boy](#cat_boy) rather than this.

entries.name: black_cat
entries.description: A real [cat](#cat) with black fur, kept as a [pet](#pet), a companion or a witch's [familiar](#familiar). A person with cat ears is [cat_girl](#cat_girl) rather than this.

entries.name: white_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) with all-white fur, evoking the [maneki-neko](#maneki-neko) lucky cat and ideas of purity. A real [animal](#animal) or feral character rather than a cat girl.

entries.name: tiger
entries.description: The striped big [cat](#cat) itself, orange or white with [dark](#dark) vertical stripes, whether a real [animal](#animal), a feral or an anthro character. Tiger-eared humans use [tiger_ears](#tiger_ears) or [tiger_girl](#tiger_girl) instead.

entries.name: lion
entries.description: The maned big [cat](#cat), drawn as a real [animal](#animal), an anthro or a feral, males and lionesses alike. A human character [carrying](#carrying) lion traits is [lion_girl](#lion_girl) or [lion_boy](#lion_boy).

entries.name: white_tiger
entries.description: A [tiger](#tiger) whose [coat](#coat) is white with [dark](#dark) stripes, the rare colour variant [familiar](#familiar) from zoos and legend. Tag tiger as [well](#well); a character with tiger ears coloured white is tagged through its ears and hair colour instead.

entries.name: grey_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) with grey fur, from a solid blue-grey [coat](#coat) to a grey tabby. Hairless breeds whose skin reads grey count as [well](#well).

entries.name: orange_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) whose [coat](#coat) is ginger over most or all of its body, tabby striping included. Only the colour matters; breed and pose are tagged elsewhere.

entries.name: kitten
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) drawn as a juvenile. Since cats are often rendered small anyway, [judge](#judge) by proportions: stubby limbs, a round face, oversized eyes and a thin, underdeveloped [tail](#tail).

entries.name: brown_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) with brown fur, whether a solid [coat](#coat) or a tabby's warm brown striping. It may be a [pet](#pet) in the scene or a companion [animal](#animal).

entries.name: calico_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) whose fur carries white, black and orange in separate patches. The patches always fall asymmetrically, never as a regular pattern.

entries.name: too_many_cats
entries.description: At least six real cats crowding the scene, and usually far more. Cat-eared girls and other catlike characters do not count towards it.

entries.name: tabby_cat
entries.description: A domestic [cat](#cat) with a striped, blotched or spotted [coat](#coat) and the characteristic M-shaped mark on its [forehead](#forehead). The pattern appears in brown, grey and orange and shows up across almost any breed.

entries.name: multiple_cats
entries.description: More than one [cat](#cat) in the frame. It counts actual animals rather than characters given cat ears and a [tail](#tail).

entries.name: snow_leopard
entries.description: A pale, thick-tailed big [cat](#cat) marked with [dark](#dark) rosettes, native to high [mountain](#mountain) ranges. Genetically it sits closer to tigers than to true leopards despite the name. Covers both anthro and feral depictions.

entries.name: siamese_cat
entries.description: A slender short-haired [cat](#cat) breed from Thailand with a light [coat](#coat) and [dark](#dark) coloring concentrated on the face, ears and extremities. Its blue eyes and wedge-shaped head make it easy to recognize.

entries.name: black_panther
entries.description: A [leopard](#leopard) or [jaguar](#jaguar) whose [coat](#coat) is so [dark](#dark) that the rosettes barely read against it. Treat it as a colour variant rather than a species of its own, since the underlying spot pattern often still shows faintly in [strong](#strong) light.

entries.name: leopard
entries.description: The spotted big [cat](#cat) of Africa and southern Asia, drawn as a real [animal](#animal) or in anthro form, including pale and melanistic coats. The much smaller leopard_cat is a different species.

entries.name: purple_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) drawn with purple fur, a colour [choice](#choice) that belongs to stylised, magical, or cartoon designs rather than any real [coat](#coat).

entries.name: yellow_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) with yellow or golden fur, drawn realistically or in cartoon style. The [tag](#tag) [notes](#notes) the colour, not a particular breed.

entries.name: pink_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) whose fur is pink rather than any natural [shade](#shade). Nearly always a stylised, cartoon or [fantasy](#fantasy) [animal](#animal) instead of a [realistic](#realistic) one.

entries.name: tuxedo_cat
entries.description: A domestic [cat](#cat) coloured black above and white below, the white usually covering the muzzle, chest, [belly](#belly) and paws. The [split](#split) colouring reads like a small [animal](#animal) dressed for [evening](#evening) wear.

entries.name: serval
entries.description: An African wild [cat](#cat) built [tall](#tall) and narrow, with very long [legs](#legs), outsized ears, and a tawny [coat](#coat) blotched in black. The Kemono Friends character with this design has her own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: blue_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) with blue fur, either an invented colour or the greyish [coat](#coat) that breeders call blue. It is an actual [animal](#animal) rather than a person wearing cat ears.

entries.name: cathead
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) reduced to nothing but a head, with ears, [whiskers](#whiskers) and now and then a stray [tail](#tail), [no](#no) body attached. It also covers an absurdly oversized cat head dropped into a scene where it does not belong.

entries.name: jaguar
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy) spotted [cat](#cat) of the Americas, told from a [leopard](#leopard) by its broader head, stockier build and the small [dots](#dots) inside each rosette. This is the [animal](#animal) itself in the scene.

entries.name: scottish_fold
entries.description: A round-headed [cat](#cat) whose ears fold forward flat against the [skull](#skull), [giving](#giving) it an owlish face. The [coat](#coat) may be short or long and comes in any colour.

entries.name: leopon_(animal)
entries.description: The hybrid offspring of a male [leopard](#leopard) and a lioness, drawn with a spotted [coat](#coat) and a thin, patchy [mane](#mane).

entries.name: green_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) whose fur is green, which puts it in stylised or fantastical territory rather than natural. What the [tag](#tag) records is the body colour.

entries.name: red_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) whose fur is red. The colour is what the [tag](#tag) records, not the breed.

entries.name: horse
entries.description: A horse as an [animal](#animal): ridden, harnessed, [racing](#racing) or [standing](#standing) in a [field](#field). A human girl with horse ears and [tail](#tail) is [horse_girl](#horse_girl) instead.

entries.name: sheep
entries.description: A sheep or ram, woolly-coated and often [carrying](#carrying) curled [horns](#horns). A crudely drawn, near-featureless sheep takes simple_sheep instead; lambs, [sheep_girl](#sheep_girl) and [sheep_ears](#sheep_ears) have their own separate tags.

entries.name: pig
entries.description: The [farm](#farm) [animal](#animal), from a full-grown sow down to a [piglet](#piglet), drawn realistically or as a cartoon. It also covers objects made in that shape, such as plush toys and [money](#money) banks.

entries.name: cow
entries.description: The four-legged [farm](#farm) [animal](#animal) itself, with small [horns](#horns) or none at all. A horned male is a [bull](#bull), and cow girls, cow print and cow-themed outfits are separate matters.

entries.name: deer
entries.description: The antlered [forest](#forest) ruminant, doe, stag or [reindeer](#reindeer), drawn as an ordinary [animal](#animal) or as an anthro character. A person [carrying](#carrying) deer traits is [deer_girl](#deer_girl) or [deer_boy](#deer_boy).

entries.name: reindeer
entries.description: A reindeer, or caribou, the antlered arctic [deer](#deer) best known for [pulling](#pulling) Santa's [sleigh](#sleigh). Covers real animals, anthro reindeer, and Christmas scenes featuring the [animal](#animal) itself.

entries.name: goat
entries.description: A hardy horned ruminant with backward-sweeping [horns](#horns) and, on males, a [beard](#beard). Covers [farm](#farm) animals, wild goats and goat characters alike.

entries.name: boar
entries.description: The wild boar, a bristly brown cousin of the [pig](#pig) with short [tusks](#tusks) and [heavy](#heavy) shoulders. It appears as a live [animal](#animal), as quarry in a hunt, and as the pig of the Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac).

entries.name: bull
entries.description: A male bovine, heavier and more thickly muscled than a [cow](#cow), with [horns](#horns) growing out to the sides of the [skull](#skull). Oxen fall under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pony_(animal)
entries.description: A small, stocky breed of [horse](#horse), distinguished from full-sized horses mainly by size and proportion. Also used for small horse-like characters drawn in a similar cartoon style, real, anthro or feral.

entries.name: giraffe
entries.description: The tallest land [animal](#animal), with a towering [neck](#neck), stilt [legs](#legs) and a [coat](#coat) of brown patches on [cream](#cream). Covers the animal itself and giraffe-based characters.

entries.name: alpaca
entries.description: A small South American camelid with a woolly fleece, long [neck](#neck) and blunt face, like a compact [llama](#llama). Its [comic](#comic) expression has made it a recurring cute [animal](#animal).

entries.name: lamb
entries.description: A young [sheep](#sheep), drawn with a soft curly fleece, stubby [legs](#legs) and an outsized head. For the [meat](#meat) rather than the [animal](#animal), a [food](#food) [tag](#tag) applies.

entries.name: piglet
entries.description: A young [pig](#pig), [boar](#boar) or warthog, small and round with an oversized head. Shown trotting through [farm](#farm) scenes or cradled in somebody's arms.

entries.name: white_horse
entries.description: A [horse](#horse) whose [coat](#coat) and [mane](#mane) are white all over, with pale skin beneath. Most animals that look white are technically greys, but the [tag](#tag) follows what's actually drawn.

entries.name: tapir
entries.description: A stocky herbivore related to horses and rhinos, with a short, [flexible](#flexible) trunk-like [snout](#snout), native to Central and South American forests and to Southeast Asia. Young tapirs are striped and spotted; the [animal](#animal) appears both plainly and as the basis for character designs.

entries.name: camel
entries.description: A long-legged [desert](#desert) mammal with a curving [neck](#neck) and either one fatty hump or two. It turns up as a mount or pack [animal](#animal) in desert and caravan scenes.

entries.name: zebra
entries.description: A striped African equine, drawn either as an ordinary [animal](#animal) or as an anthropomorphic character. Pair it with equine and striped to describe the [coat](#coat) pattern itself.

entries.name: donkey
entries.description: A donkey: smaller than a [horse](#horse), with far longer ears, a short upright [mane](#mane) and a straighter [back](#back). Drawn as an [animal](#animal) or worked into an anthro design.

entries.name: fawn
entries.description: A [deer](#deer) in its first year, small-bodied and long-legged, usually still spotted. Antlers are absent or barely begun.

entries.name: llama
entries.description: A long-necked South American camelid with a shaggy fleece and curved banana-shaped ears, kept for [wool](#wool) and for [carrying](#carrying) loads. It is larger and longer in the body than an [alpaca](#alpaca), with a less woolly face.

entries.name: moose
entries.description: The largest of the [deer](#deer): high shoulders, a drooping muzzle, a flap of skin [hanging](#hanging) at the throat and broad flattened [antlers](#antlers). The same [animal](#animal) in Europe and Asia goes by elk.

entries.name: rabbit
entries.description: An actual rabbit or hare appears as an [animal](#animal) in the picture, long-eared with [strong](#strong) hind [legs](#legs) and a short [tail](#tail); the two look similar enough to share one [tag](#tag). A human with rabbit traits is [rabbit_girl](#rabbit_girl) or [rabbit_boy](#rabbit_boy), and the [leotard](#leotard) [costume](#costume) is [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny).

entries.name: mouse_(animal)
entries.description: A small rodent with a pointed [snout](#snout), round ears and a long bare [tail](#tail). The [tag](#tag) takes in rats as [well](#well); the [computer](#computer) [pointing](#pointing) [device](#device) is a separate tag.

entries.name: hamster
entries.description: A small round rodent with stuffable cheek pouches and barely any [tail](#tail), most often drawn as somebody's [pet](#pet). Covers the [plain](#plain) [animal](#animal) as [well](#well) as hamsters in cages, wheels and cupped hands.

entries.name: squirrel
entries.description: A small rodent with a large bushy [tail](#tail), usually shown [eating](#eating) nuts or perched on a [branch](#branch). Tag the [animal](#animal) itself; a character with squirrel features has its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: angora_rabbit
entries.description: A domestic [rabbit](#rabbit) breed [carrying](#carrying) an enormous [coat](#coat) of soft [wool](#wool), so shaggy that the face nearly vanishes into it. Ordinary short-haired breeds take the [plain](#plain) rabbit [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: white_rabbit_(animal)
entries.description: A [rabbit](#rabbit) with white fur, often given pink or red eyes. The real [animal](#animal) itself, not a character dressed in bunny gear.

entries.name: capybara
entries.description: The largest living rodent, a barrel-bodied South American grazer about the size of a [pig](#pig), with a blunt muzzle and small high-set ears. Often drawn [sitting](#sitting) placidly in [hot](#hot) [water](#water).

entries.name: guinea_pig
entries.description: A tailless South American rodent with a rounded, stout body, roughly twice the size of a common rat. Kept as a [pet](#pet) and known for the squeaky wheek it lets out when [excited](#excited) or [hungry](#hungry).

entries.name: chipmunk
