entries.description: A small striped rodent of the [squirrel](#squirrel) [family](#family), with [dark](#dark) bands down its [back](#back) and cheek pouches it packs with seeds and nuts. Covers the real [animal](#animal) and clearly chipmunk-based creatures.

entries.name: too_many_rabbits
entries.description: Five or more live rabbits filling the scene. Plush bunnies and girls with [rabbit](#rabbit) ears are not what it is for.

entries.name: chinchilla_(animal)
entries.description: The small Andean rodent itself, thickly furred in soft grey with large cupped ears and a bushy curling [tail](#tail). Use it for the real [creature](#creature) or a [pet](#pet) in the scene rather than for a character wearing chinchilla traits.

entries.name: black_rabbit_(animal)
entries.description: A real [rabbit](#rabbit) with black fur, present in the picture as an [animal](#animal). A person wearing bunny ears is not this; the animal-eared tags [cover](#cover) that instead.

entries.name: rabbit_head
entries.description: A rabbit's head is the subject, whether attached to a full character or drawn on its own. Long ears, a [split](#split) upper lip, and a [twitching](#twitching) [nose](#nose) give the shape away.

entries.name: flying_squirrel
entries.description: A [squirrel](#squirrel) with a skin membrane stretched between its limbs, gliding with all four [legs](#legs) spread wide. It also covers characters copying that spread-eagled pose or wearing such a [suit](#suit).

entries.name: beaver
entries.description: A stout semiaquatic rodent with a broad flat scaly [tail](#tail), orange [chisel](#chisel) [teeth](#teeth), webbed hind [feet](#feet) and dense brown fur, famous for felling trees and damming streams. A character wearing only the ears or the tail takes [beaver_ears](#beaver_ears) or [beaver_tail](#beaver_tail).

entries.name: bear
entries.description: The big [furry](#furry) mammal with [heavy](#heavy) [claws](#claws) and a large appetite, drawn as a real [animal](#animal), a [mascot](#mascot) or a furry character. The word doubles as gay slang for a heavy [hairy](#hairy) man, so it also appears on [muscular](#muscular) male art; polar bears and stuffed teddies have their own tags.

entries.name: panda
entries.description: The [giant](#giant) panda, a black-and-white [bear](#bear) from China with [dark](#dark) patches around the eyes and ears and a dark band over the shoulders. Covers the live [animal](#animal), plush versions and mascots alike.

entries.name: raccoon
entries.description: The North American [animal](#animal) with a black [mask](#mask) across the eyes, grey fur, a ringed [tail](#tail), and unusually nimble front paws. Frequently [confused](#confused) with the [tanuki](#tanuki), a different Asian animal with brown fur and [no](#no) hand-like paws.

entries.name: polar_bear
entries.description: The large white-furred [bear](#bear) of the Arctic, shown as a real [animal](#animal), an anthro, or a [mascot](#mascot). Tag bear alongside it, plus anthro or feral as fits.

entries.name: otter
entries.description: The sleek semi-aquatic mustelid, drawn as a real [animal](#animal) or as an anthro character. Often shown [floating](#floating) on its [back](#back) or [holding](#holding) a shellfish.

entries.name: ferret
entries.description: The domesticated polecat, a long slender mustelid with brown, black, white or mixed fur. It appears as a [pet](#pet), a [mascot](#mascot) or an [animal](#animal) character.

entries.name: weasel
entries.description: A small, slender-bodied mustelid, covering weasels, stoats and their close relatives, drawn feral or as an anthro character. Add mammal alongside for the broader classification.

entries.name: red_panda
entries.description: A red [panda](#panda) or a character based on one: a reddish-brown [coat](#coat), white face [markings](#markings), and a long ringed [tail](#tail). Easily mistaken for a [raccoon](#raccoon) or [tanuki](#tanuki), though it is its own species, unrelated to the [giant](#giant) panda.

entries.name: ermine
entries.description: A stoat in its white [winter](#winter) [coat](#coat), keeping the black tip on its [tail](#tail). Long-bodied and short-legged; the same [animal](#animal) in brown [summer](#summer) fur is simply a stoat.

entries.name: whale
entries.description: A huge marine mammal with a smooth body, horizontal [tail](#tail) flukes and a [blowhole](#blowhole). Appears as a real [animal](#animal), a background [creature](#creature), or drawn as an anthro character.

entries.name: dolphin
entries.description: A dolphin, the small social toothed [whale](#whale); porpoises and belugas are gathered here as [well](#well). Used for the [animal](#animal) in any drawing style.

entries.name: seal_(animal)
entries.description: The round-bodied, sleek-furred marine mammal of [cold](#cold) coasts. Distinct from a sea [lion](#lion), which has visible ear flaps and [can](#can) walk on its [flippers](#flippers).

entries.name: orca
entries.description: The black-and-white marine predator called a killer [whale](#whale), biologically the largest of the dolphins. Several metres long and without natural predators, it often stands in for power at sea.

entries.name: flying_whale
entries.description: A [whale](#whale) [drifting](#drifting) through the [sky](#sky) as though air were [water](#water), a [staple](#staple) of dreamlike and [fantasy](#fantasy) landscapes. Its size measured against clouds or rooftops is usually the point.

entries.name: blue_whale
entries.description: The largest [animal](#animal) alive, a baleen [whale](#whale) with a long mottled blue-grey body and a [pleated](#pleated) throat. Drawn at sea, breaching, or [swimming](#swimming) through an imaginary [sky](#sky).

entries.name: humpback_whale
entries.description: A large baleen [whale](#whale) recognised by its enormously long [flippers](#flippers) and the knobs studding its head. It is famous for [launching](#launching) itself clear of the [water](#water), which is how pictures usually show it.

entries.name: sea_lion
entries.description: A marine mammal with four [flippers](#flippers) and small visible ear flaps. Its hind flippers [swing](#swing) forward so it [can](#can) walk on land, which a true seal cannot do.

entries.name: narwhal
entries.description: The Arctic [whale](#whale) [carrying](#carrying) a single long [spiral](#spiral) tusk out of its head. It is drawn as the [animal](#animal) itself or borrowed by character designs that want the horn.

entries.name: beluga_whale
entries.description: A small white Arctic [whale](#whale) with a bulging [forehead](#forehead), [no](#no) dorsal fin and a mouth curved into a permanent [smile](#smile). It appears as an [animal](#animal), a plush [toy](#toy) or the basis of a character design.

entries.name: walrus
entries.description: A bulky Arctic sea mammal with a bristling moustache of [whiskers](#whiskers) and two long [tusks](#tusks) [pointing](#pointing) down. Usually drawn hauled out on [ice](#ice) or [rock](#rock).

entries.name: bat_(animal)
entries.description: The winged mammal, drawn as a real [animal](#animal), a swarm against the [night](#night), a cute [mascot](#mascot) or a [furry](#furry) character. It is not the sporting bat; Halloween and [vampire](#vampire) scenes call on it constantly.

entries.name: monkey
entries.description: A tailed primate, Old World or New World, but not an [ape](#ape) and not a human. It applies whether the [animal](#animal) is drawn on all fours or given a person's build.

entries.name: hedgehog
entries.description: A small spined mammal with a rounded muzzle that curls up when alarmed. It covers the ordinary [animal](#animal) as [well](#well) as upright anthro characters built on one.

entries.name: elephant
entries.description: The largest land [animal](#animal), [heavy](#heavy) and grey with a long trunk, broad ears and [tusks](#tusks). Drawn realistically, in a cartoon style, or as an anthro character.

entries.name: gorilla
entries.description: The heavy-built African great [ape](#ape), black-haired with long arms, a low brow and a huge chest. Appears as an [animal](#animal), as a strongman [gag](#gag) and in the [familiar](#familiar) chest-beating pose.

entries.name: ape
entries.description: A large tailless primate: [gorilla](#gorilla), chimpanzee, orangutan, gibbon and their relatives. Used both for [realistic](#realistic) animals and as the base of beast-man designs.

entries.name: koala
entries.description: A stocky Australian marsupial with round [fluffy](#fluffy) ears, a big [dark](#dark) [nose](#nose) and grey fur, usually shown [clinging](#clinging) to a eucalyptus trunk. It eats leaves and sleeps most of the [day](#day).

entries.name: hippopotamus
entries.description: The bulky semi-aquatic African herbivore with a broad [snout](#snout), tiny ears and an enormous gape. It is generally drawn wallowing in a [river](#river).

entries.name: mole_(animal)
entries.description: A small burrowing mammal with a cylindrical body, velvety fur, pinprick eyes and broad spade-like front paws. The beauty spot on skin is a different [tag](#tag) entirely.

entries.name: armadillo
entries.description: A burrowing mammal plated in bony bands over [back](#back) and head, with a long [snout](#snout) and [heavy](#heavy) [digging](#digging) [claws](#claws). Drawn as the [animal](#animal) itself or used as the basis for an anthro character.

entries.name: hyena
entries.description: A spotted or striped African carnivore with a sloping [back](#back) and broad rounded ears. It turns up as a [plain](#plain) [animal](#animal), as a feral character or as an anthro one. Its habits straddle [cat](#cat) and [dog](#dog): feline grooming, canine [hunting](#hunting).

entries.name: rhinoceros
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy), thick-skinned herbivore with one or two [horns](#horns) on its [snout](#snout), native to Africa and southern Asia. Drawn either as a real [animal](#animal) or as the basis for a bulky anthro character.

entries.name: kangaroo
entries.description: The big-footed, thick-tailed Australian marsupial, drawn as an [animal](#animal) or as an upright anthro character. Mothers are often given the [pouch](#pouch) as a defining detail.

entries.name: platypus
entries.description: A semi-aquatic Australian mammal with a duck-like bill, webbed [feet](#feet) and a broad flat [tail](#tail). It lays eggs, and the males carry a venomous spur on the hind leg.

entries.name: anteater
entries.description: A long-snouted mammal with [heavy](#heavy) [digging](#digging) [claws](#claws), a narrow probing [tongue](#tongue) and a bushy [tail](#tail). Drawn either as the real [animal](#animal) or used as the base of an anthro design.

entries.name: mammoth
entries.description: An extinct [elephant](#elephant) with long strongly curving [tusks](#tusks), the northern kinds under a thick shaggy [coat](#coat). Drawn in ice-age scenes or [standing](#standing) as a [museum](#museum) [skeleton](#skeleton).

entries.name: bird
entries.description: Any bird present as an [animal](#animal), from a [sparrow](#sparrow) on a [branch](#branch) to an [owl](#owl), a [crow](#crow) or a [flock](#flock) crossing the [sky](#sky). Add the species where it [can](#can) be told; a bird reduced to a simple V shape is [simple_bird](#simple_bird).

entries.name: penguin
entries.description: A flightless [swimming](#swimming) [bird](#bird) [standing](#standing) upright in black-and-white plumage, from the emperor down to the little blue. Real birds, mascots and plush versions all count.

entries.name: chick
entries.description: A young [bird](#bird), most typically the [fluffy](#fluffy) yellow chick of a hen, though any nestling counts. Grown domestic fowl are [chicken](#chicken).

entries.name: crow
entries.description: A crow, raven or any of the similar large black corvids, present as a [bird](#bird) in the scene or as a character's companion. Rooks, jackdaws and their relatives fall under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: duck
entries.description: The [wading](#wading) waterfowl with its broad flat bill, wild or domestic. Japanese keeps separate words for the tame and the wild sort.

entries.name: seagull
entries.description: A gull, the white-and-grey sea [bird](#bird) common at beaches and harbours. Often just a background detail of a coastal scene.

entries.name: chicken
entries.description: The living domestic fowl, hen or cockerel, whether as an [animal](#animal) or an anthro character. Cooked [meat](#meat) is [chicken_(food)](#chicken_(food)) and a hatchling is [chick](#chick).

entries.name: owl
entries.description: A night-hunting [bird](#bird) with a flat round face and big forward-facing eyes. Some kinds carry feather tufts on the head that only look like ears; drawn as wildlife, as a companion or as a [mascot](#mascot).

entries.name: white_bird
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) with white plumage, such as a [dove](#dove), [swan](#swan), [seagull](#seagull) or egret, drawn real or as an anthro character. Add the species where it's identifiable.

entries.name: dove
entries.description: A white or mostly white dove, the peace-dove sort of the [pigeon](#pigeon) [family](#family). Grey and blue-grey birds of the same family are tagged pigeon.

entries.name: eagle
entries.description: A big [bird](#bird) of prey with broad [wings](#wings), a hooked [beak](#beak) and famously sharp eyes. Drawn as a live bird, as a heraldic [device](#device), or as an anthro character.

entries.name: flock
entries.description: Many birds of one kind clustered or [flying](#flying) together as a group. Birds merely scattered about a scene are [too_many_birds](#too_many_birds), though a character [surrounded](#surrounded) by startled birds does count.

entries.name: pigeon
entries.description: The grey [city](#city) [bird](#bird), usually shown in flocks on squares, rooftops and [window](#window) ledges. An all-white bird of the same build is a [dove](#dove) rather than this.

entries.name: sparrow
entries.description: A small brown songbird of the sparrow [family](#family) or a lookalike, such as the [tree](#tree) sparrow or [house](#house) sparrow. Tag the [bird](#bird) itself, whether perched or in flight.

entries.name: parrot
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) with a stout hooked [beak](#beak) and two [toes](#toes) forward, two [back](#back), usually brightly coloured: macaws, cockatoos, budgerigars and their relatives. Frequently perched on a pirate's shoulder.

entries.name: black_bird
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) whose plumage is black. Very often a [crow](#crow) or raven, though not always, so add the species [tag](#tag) once it [can](#can) be identified.

entries.name: crane_(animal)
entries.description: The [tall](#tall), long-necked, long-legged [bird](#bird), in Japanese art usually the red-crowned kind with its scarlet [forehead](#forehead) and black [markings](#markings). Herons and storks are different birds.

entries.name: duckling
entries.description: A [baby](#baby) [duck](#duck), drawn as a small round [ball](#ball) of yellow [fluff](#fluff). Usually paddling after a parent or cupped in somebody's hands.

entries.name: blue_bird
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) with blue plumage, present in the picture as an [animal](#animal). It is broader than the [bluebird](#bluebird) [tag](#tag), which names one particular thrush.

entries.name: hawk
entries.description: A medium-sized [bird](#bird) of prey with a hooked [beak](#beak), broad [wings](#wings) and gripping [talons](#talons). Often drawn perched on a falconer's glove or [dropping](#dropping) on prey.

entries.name: rooster
entries.description: A male [chicken](#chicken), distinguished by his [tall](#tall) [comb](#comb), wattles and long arching [tail](#tail) [feathers](#feathers). Appears crowing at [dawn](#dawn) and in new year imagery.

entries.name: tit_(bird)
entries.description: A small round songbird of the Paridae [family](#family), such as a great tit or a blue tit, with a stubby bill and a boldly marked cap. Usually perched on a [branch](#branch), a [wire](#wire) or a fingertip.

entries.name: bald_eagle
entries.description: A large North American [raptor](#raptor), [dark](#dark) brown in the body with a white head and [tail](#tail) and a hooked yellow [beak](#beak). It serves as the national [bird](#bird) and [emblem](#emblem) of the United States.

entries.name: swan
entries.description: A large white waterbird with a long curving [neck](#neck), short [legs](#legs) and webbed [feet](#feet). Carries connotations of grace and purity and often turns up on lakes or in ballet-themed pictures. Implies [bird](#bird).

entries.name: eurasian_tree_sparrow
entries.description: A small brown [sparrow](#sparrow) with a [chestnut](#chestnut) cap and a black spot on each white cheek. The common sparrow of Japan and a regular in seasonal artwork.

entries.name: goose
entries.description: A large long-necked waterfowl, heavier than a [duck](#duck) and [lighter](#lighter) than a [swan](#swan). Shown [swimming](#swimming), waddling or [flying](#flying) in a V; its honking bad temper is a [running](#running) joke.

entries.name: flamingo
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) pink [wading](#wading) [bird](#bird) on stilt [legs](#legs), with a long curving [neck](#neck) and a [beak](#beak) kinked sharply downward. Frequently drawn [standing](#standing) on one leg in shallow [water](#water).

entries.name: falcon
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) of prey with long tapered [wings](#wings) built for speed and quick turns, killing with a notched [beak](#beak) instead of the [talons](#talons) a [hawk](#hawk) uses. Kestrels, merlins and peregrines all belong here.

entries.name: ostrich
entries.description: The flightless African [bird](#bird), the largest living species, with a long bare [neck](#neck), shaggy body plumage and powerful two-toed [legs](#legs). Males are black with white trim, females brown throughout.

entries.name: yellow_bird
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) with yellow plumage, anything from a canary or a [chick](#chick) to a simplified cartoon bird. Recorded for its colour rather than its species.

entries.name: peacock
entries.description: The male peafowl, with a deep blue [neck](#neck), a [crest](#crest) of tuft-tipped [feathers](#feathers) and an enormous [train](#train) of eye-spotted plumes he [can](#can) fan out behind him. The drab brown female is the peahen.

entries.name: emperor_penguin
entries.description: The biggest [penguin](#penguin): black [back](#back), white front, and orange-yellow patches at the sides of the head and upper chest. Chicks are grey with black heads and white faces. The [king](#king) penguin is the lookalike to rule out.

entries.name: long-tailed_tit
entries.description: A tiny round songbird in white, black and pink whose slender [tail](#tail) is longer than the rest of its body. It is generally drawn as a [fluffy](#fluffy) [ball](#ball) perched on a bare [twig](#twig).

entries.name: too_many_birds
entries.description: Birds in such numbers that the [flock](#flock) takes over the picture, filling the [sky](#sky), the ground or the character they are perched on.

entries.name: swallow_(bird)
entries.description: A small, fast [bird](#bird) with a forked [tail](#tail) and long pointed [wings](#wings), often drawn in flight or perched at a [nest](#nest). For the act of [swallowing](#swallowing) something, use the separate verb [tag](#tag). Implies bird.

entries.name: bluebird
entries.description: A small thrush with blue upperparts, sometimes over a rose-beige breast, long treated as a [sign](#sign) of happiness. It lacks the [crest](#crest) and [dark](#dark) [collar](#collar) that mark out a blue jay.

entries.name: toucan
entries.description: A large South American [bird](#bird) with an oversized, brightly banded bill and mostly [dark](#dark) plumage. Instantly recognizable by its bill alone, out of proportion to the rest of the body.

entries.name: seabird
entries.description: Birds that make their living off the sea, such as gulls, terns and albatrosses, wheeling over the [water](#water) or perched on rocks and pilings.

entries.name: parakeet
entries.description: Any of the small long-tailed parrots, most often the green or blue budgerigar kept as a [pet](#pet). Drawn perched on a finger, in a [cage](#cage), or [riding](#riding) a shoulder.

entries.name: cockatiel
entries.description: A small crested [parrot](#parrot) from Australia, widely kept as a [pet](#pet) and known by the round orange [patch](#patch) on each cheek. Grey and white is the [familiar](#familiar) colouring, though many mutations exist.

entries.name: red-crowned_crane
entries.description: A large East Asian crane, [snow](#snow) white with black on the secondary flight [feathers](#feathers) and [neck](#neck), marked by a bare [patch](#patch) of red skin on the [crown](#crown). In Chinese and Japanese art it stands for long life and fidelity.

entries.name: penguin_chick
entries.description: A young [penguin](#penguin) in its [fluffy](#fluffy) grey or brown down, rounder and softer than the adult and without the sharp black-and-white [markings](#markings).

entries.name: macaw
entries.description: A large, vividly coloured [parrot](#parrot) with a very long [tail](#tail) and a [heavy](#heavy) hooked [beak](#beak), usually red, blue or yellow. The species are told apart mainly by wing colour and by the bare [patterned](#patterned) [patch](#patch) on the face.

entries.name: finch
entries.description: A small perching [bird](#bird) with a stout conical [beak](#beak) for cracking seeds, often brightly coloured. A loose term covering many similar songbirds rather than one species.

entries.name: shoebill
entries.description: A huge grey African [wading](#wading) [bird](#bird) with a broad, clog-shaped bill and a fixed, unblinking stare, known for [standing](#standing) motionless while [hunting](#hunting). Enjoys an [internet](#internet) reputation in Japan as comically menacing. Implies bird.

entries.name: japanese_white-eye
entries.description: A small olive-green songbird with a bold white [ring](#ring) round each eye and a yellow throat. A favourite of traditional painting, it is usually perched among [plum](#plum) or [cherry](#cherry) blossom.

entries.name: humboldt_penguin
entries.description: A medium-sized South American [penguin](#penguin) with a white band curving around the face and throat and a pink [patch](#patch) at the base of the bill. Those [markings](#markings) separate it from the African, Magellanic and Galapagos species.

entries.name: green_bird
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) whose plumage is green, most often a [parakeet](#parakeet), [parrot](#parrot) or small songbird. The colour may [cover](#cover) the whole [animal](#animal) or only the [back](#back) and [wings](#wings).

entries.name: too_many_chicks
entries.description: A [crowd](#crowd) of [fluffy](#fluffy) yellow chicks heaped around a character. Often a [running](#running) joke where some unrelated number decides how many there are.

entries.name: hummingbird
entries.description: A tiny [bird](#bird) hovering on blurred [wings](#wings), usually [feeding](#feeding) at a [flower](#flower). Native to the Americas and nearly always drawn beside blossoms.

entries.name: ratite
entries.description: The large flightless birds built along the [ostrich](#ostrich) plan, including ostriches, emus, cassowaries, and moa, along with fictional birds [sharing](#sharing) the same long-legged shape. Terror birds and oversized chicks do not belong under this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: cockatoo
entries.description: A large [parrot](#parrot) from Australia and nearby islands with a fan of [feathers](#feathers) it [can](#can) raise on its head. Most are white with a yellow or pink wash, though some species come in black or [salmon](#salmon).

entries.name: kiwi_(bird)
entries.description: A stout flightless [bird](#bird) from New Zealand, roughly chicken-sized, with shaggy hair-like brown plumage and a long thin bill whose [nostrils](#nostrils) sit at the tip. Not the [fruit](#fruit) of the same name.

entries.name: java_sparrow
entries.description: A stout little [finch](#finch) with a grey body, a boldly marked black-and-white head and a [heavy](#heavy) pink [beak](#beak), long kept as a [cage](#cage) [bird](#bird) in Japan. An all-white strain appears just as often in pictures.

entries.name: pelican
entries.description: A large [water](#water) [bird](#bird) with an enormous bill and the stretchy throat [pouch](#pouch) it scoops [fish](#fish) into. Plumage runs white, grey or brown, often with [dark](#dark) flight [feathers](#feathers).

entries.name: secretarybird
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) African [bird](#bird) that hunts on foot, with long bare [legs](#legs), a hooked bill, and a spray of quills [standing](#standing) out behind its head. Famous for stamping on snakes.

entries.name: snake
entries.description: A legless reptile of the serpent kind, [coiled](#coiled), slithering or wrapped around a character. A snake always has a discernible head, unlike a [worm](#worm).

entries.name: frog
entries.description: A tailless amphibian with a squat body, smooth damp skin and long [folded](#folded) hind [legs](#legs). Covers [realistic](#realistic) frogs, cartoon ones and frog characters alike.

entries.name: dinosaur
entries.description: One of the great extinct reptiles, drawn realistically or as a cartoon. The name stretches to [cover](#cover) other prehistoric reptile-like beasts that are not strictly dinosaurs.

entries.name: turtle_shell
entries.description: A turtle's [shell](#shell) shown worn by an anthropomorphic character or [lying](#lying) discarded on its own. Not needed for an ordinary [turtle](#turtle), whose shell is already implied.

entries.name: turtle
entries.description: A shelled reptile, drawn realistically, kept as a [pet](#pet), or scaled up to fantastic size, sometimes large enough to carry islands or whole worlds on its [back](#back). Tortoises share the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: white_snake
entries.description: A living [snake](#snake) with white [scales](#scales), rather than a printed pattern. In Japanese and Chinese folklore a white snake is a lucky or divine omen, so it often keeps company with [shrine](#shrine) maidens and [spirit](#spirit) characters; [tag](#tag) snake as [well](#well).

entries.name: lizard
entries.description: A four-legged reptile with a long [tail](#tail), movable eyelids and rough scaly skin, drawn as wildlife, as a [pet](#pet) or as the basis of a scaled character. It takes in geckos, iguanas and unnamed lizards alike.

entries.name: crocodilian
entries.description: The catch-all for crocodiles, alligators, caimans and gharials, all long-snouted and much alike. Add the specific species when the [snout](#snout) or another detail makes it clear.

entries.name: tyrannosaurus_rex
entries.description: The best-known [dinosaur](#dinosaur) of all, a [giant](#giant) two-legged meat-eater with a huge head and small two-fingered arms. Its fame rests on several near-complete [fossil](#fossil) skeletons and its [screen](#screen) career as the archetypal predator.

entries.name: crocodile
entries.description: The big long-jawed [river](#river) reptile, drawn as an [animal](#animal) or as an anthro character. Alligators and caimans have tags of their own within the same [family](#family).

entries.name: axolotl
entries.description: A Mexican [salamander](#salamander) that never grows out of its larval form, with feathery [gills](#gills) [fanning](#fanning) from either side of the head and a wide, permanently smiling mouth. It is usually drawn pale pink on short stubby [legs](#legs).

entries.name: triceratops
entries.description: A stocky, horned [dinosaur](#dinosaur) with a broad bony [neck](#neck) frill, one [nose](#nose) horn and two long brow [horns](#horns). Drawn as a [plain](#plain) [animal](#animal), an anthropomorphised character, or worn as a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: cobra_(animal)
entries.description: The hooded venomous [snake](#snake) of Africa and Asia, [spreading](#spreading) the skin of its [neck](#neck) into a wide [flare](#flare) as it rears up. Use it when the [animal](#animal) itself is in the picture.

entries.name: sea_turtle
entries.description: A [turtle](#turtle) built for open [water](#water), with a flattened, streamlined [shell](#shell) and front limbs shaped into long paddling [flippers](#flippers).

entries.name: chameleon
entries.description: A [lizard](#lizard) whose turret eyes swivel independently, gripping branches with pincer [feet](#feet) and a coiling [tail](#tail). Several species shift the colour of their skin, which is what they are known for.

entries.name: frozen_frog
entries.description: A [frog](#frog) [caught](#caught) inside a block of [ice](#ice). It became a [running](#running) joke in Touhou art, where one ice [fairy](#fairy) freezes them for sport.

entries.name: pterosaur
entries.description: A [flying](#flying) reptile of the Mesozoic era, gliding on skin-membrane [wings](#wings) rather than [feathers](#feathers), often crested and long-beaked. Despite frequently [sharing](#sharing) a scene with them, it is not a [dinosaur](#dinosaur).

entries.name: gecko
entries.description: A small insect-eating [lizard](#lizard) with broad [clinging](#clinging) toe pads and large lidless eyes, often kept as a [pet](#pet). Covers both the [animal](#animal) itself and gecko-based characters.

entries.name: alligator
entries.description: A big scaly reptile with a broad [snout](#snout), [heavy](#heavy) jaws and a long thick [tail](#tail). It appears as an [animal](#animal) or, in [furry](#furry) work, as an upright character.

entries.name: toad_(animal)
entries.description: A stout amphibian with dry warty skin, short [legs](#legs), crests behind the eyes and dull colouring, given to [crawling](#crawling) more than leaping. Frogs are the smooth, slim, long-jumping counterpart.

entries.name: tortoise
entries.description: A land-dwelling [turtle](#turtle) with a [tall](#tall) domed [shell](#shell) and thick, pillar-like [legs](#legs) built for [walking](#walking) rather than [swimming](#swimming). The shell shape and stumpy legs set it apart from an aquatic turtle.

entries.name: salamander
entries.description: A slender amphibian with a blunt [snout](#snout), short [legs](#legs) and a long [tail](#tail). Old folklore linked it to [fire](#fire), so [fantasy](#fantasy) art often turns it into a flame-dwelling beast or elemental.

entries.name: red_snake
entries.description: A [snake](#snake) with red [scales](#scales), [coiled](#coiled) in the scene or wound around a character. Red ones tend to be drawn as ominous or supernatural rather than as an identified species.

entries.name: tadpole
entries.description: The larval [stage](#stage) of a [frog](#frog) or toad: a round body with a long finned [tail](#tail) and [no](#no) [legs](#legs) yet. Usually drawn in a [pond](#pond), a [jar](#jar) or a [rice](#rice) paddy.

entries.name: iguana
entries.description: A large [lizard](#lizard) with a ridge of [spines](#spines) down the [back](#back) and [tail](#tail) and a loose flap of skin under the chin. The green iguana is the [model](#model), though drawn colours range [well](#well) past green.

entries.name: black_snake
entries.description: A [snake](#snake) with black [scales](#scales), [coiled](#coiled), draped over somebody or crossing the scene. Only the colour is claimed; which species it is stays open.

entries.name: raptor
entries.description: A loose [label](#label) for the small, agile meat-eating dinosaurs built along the sickle-clawed hunter body plan. Used for the general shape rather than any precisely identified species.

entries.name: fish
entries.description: A living fish, scaled and gilled, [swimming](#swimming), held up or kept in a [tank](#tank). Fish prepared to eat is [fish_(food)](#fish_(food)).

entries.name: starfish
entries.description: A five-armed sea star, alive on the [shore](#shore) or seabed, or a dried one used as [beach](#beach) decoration or a hair accessory. Not a [fish](#fish) despite the name.

entries.name: crab
entries.description: The sideways-walking [crustacean](#crustacean) with a broad flat [shell](#shell), stalked eyes and [pincers](#pincers), alive on a [beach](#beach) or served up as [food](#food). Crab-themed characters take their own tags.

entries.name: jellyfish
entries.description: A jellyfish, its [translucent](#translucent) [bell](#bell) trailing long [tentacles](#tentacles) behind it. Artists often use one decoratively, [drifting](#drifting) through an [underwater](#underwater) scene or [floating](#floating) as a motif.

entries.name: octopus
entries.description: The eight-armed sea [creature](#creature), drawn true to life, cartoonishly or as a [mascot](#mascot). Suckered limbs [reaching](#reaching) for a character are tagged [tentacles](#tentacles) rather than this.

entries.name: goldfish
entries.description: The domesticated orange freshwater [fish](#fish), kept in bowls, tanks and [garden](#garden) ponds. It recurs as a summer-festival motif and on [yukata](#yukata) prints.

entries.name: shark
entries.description: A shark, the toothy, cartilaginous [ocean](#ocean) predator, in any generic depiction. When the species is recognisable, add great_white_shark, [hammerhead_shark](#hammerhead_shark), [whale_shark](#whale_shark), or the like.

entries.name: shrimp
entries.description: A long-antennaed [crustacean](#crustacean) with a segmented body, shown [swimming](#swimming) in [water](#water) or served as [food](#food). Battered and deep-fried it becomes [shrimp_tempura](#shrimp_tempura).

entries.name: coral
entries.description: Coral colonies in the picture, branching or rounded, generally reef [scenery](#scenery) around [fish](#fish), divers or mermaids. Not for the colour that shares the name.

entries.name: squid
entries.description: A live squid shown with its mantle, eight arms and two longer [tentacles](#tentacles). Squid served as [food](#food) is tagged calamari, [ikayaki](#ikayaki) or similar instead.

entries.name: tropical_fish
entries.description: Brightly coloured [fish](#fish) native to warm waters, such as [clownfish](#clownfish) or [angelfish](#angelfish), shown [swimming](#swimming) free or kept in an [aquarium](#aquarium). Tag the specific species separately when it is identifiable.

entries.name: koi
entries.description: Ornamental [carp](#carp) patched in white, orange, red and black, [swimming](#swimming) in a [pond](#pond) or used as a decorative motif on [cloth](#cloth). They are a stock element of Japanese [garden](#garden) scenes.

entries.name: clownfish
entries.description: The small orange or red reef [fish](#fish) banded in white that shelters among sea anemones. Shown [swimming](#swimming), kept in a [tank](#tank), or used as the basis of a character.

entries.name: bagged_fish
entries.description: A live [fish](#fish), nearly always a [goldfish](#goldfish), held in a clear plastic [bag](#bag) of [water](#water). It is the prize from goldfish scooping at a [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival), so [yukata](#yukata) and stalls tend to be close by.

entries.name: flying_fish
entries.description: Either [fish](#fish) drawn moving through open air as though it were [water](#water), or the real species whose enlarged pectoral [fins](#fins) let it glide above the [waves](#waves). The [tag](#tag) is used both ways.

entries.name: anglerfish
entries.description: A bony [fish](#fish) with a fleshy lure growing from its head to draw prey in, the deep-sea kind with a [glowing](#glowing) bulb being the best known. Frogfish and sea toads belong to the same group.

entries.name: eel
entries.description: A [fish](#fish) with a very long snakelike body, which may or may not show [fins](#fins). Drawn alive in [water](#water), wriggling in a hand, or grilled and laid over [rice](#rice).

entries.name: manta_ray
entries.description: A very large [ocean](#ocean) ray with broad triangular [wings](#wings) and a pair of horn-like lobes that funnel plankton into its mouth. Unlike a [stingray](#stingray), its mouth opens at the front of the head rather than underneath.

entries.name: saury
entries.description: A long slim silver [fish](#fish) with a beaked lower [jaw](#jaw). In Japan it stands for [autumn](#autumn), grilled whole with [salt](#salt) and served with grated [daikon](#daikon).

entries.name: school_of_fish
entries.description: A dense mass of one kind of [fish](#fish) [swimming](#swimming) as a body, from a small cluster to a wheeling wall of thousands.

entries.name: tuna
entries.description: A large, streamlined [ocean](#ocean) [fish](#fish) with crescent-shaped [fins](#fins) built for speed, prized both as [food](#food) and as a sport catch. Often drawn whole and oversized in a character's arms, or cut into blocks for [sashimi](#sashimi).

entries.name: butterflyfish
entries.description: A small [tropical](#tropical) reef [fish](#fish) with a deep, flattened body and vivid bands [running](#running) through its [fins](#fins) and face. It belongs in reef and [aquarium](#aquarium) scenes.

entries.name: clam
entries.description: A bivalve mollusc closed inside two hinged shells, alive on the seabed or served up as [food](#food). Oversized versions turn up as [fantasy](#fantasy) set [dressing](#dressing).

entries.name: lobster
entries.description: A large marine [crustacean](#crustacean) with stalked eyes, long [antennae](#antennae) and a pair of [heavy](#heavy) [pincers](#pincers) at the front. It appears alive in the [water](#water) or cooked red on a [plate](#plate), and spiny lobsters are not told apart from it.

entries.name: angelfish
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), flattened freshwater [fish](#fish) with long trailing [fins](#fins), kept in home aquariums. The name also takes in the brightly [patterned](#patterned) marine angelfish of [coral](#coral) reefs.

entries.name: crustacean
entries.description: Shelled aquatic arthropods such as crabs, [shrimp](#shrimp), lobsters and [crayfish](#crayfish), set apart from insects and spiders by their branching jointed limbs. Applies to them alive and to them served up as [food](#food).

entries.name: stingray
entries.description: A flat-bodied ray with broad winglike [fins](#fins) and a [whip](#whip) [tail](#tail) [carrying](#carrying) one or more barbed [spines](#spines) near its base. Drawn gliding through [water](#water), in aquariums, or as the basis for a character.

entries.name: seahorse
entries.description: A small, upright [fish](#fish) with a horse-like head, ridged bony armour along the body, and a curling [tail](#tail) that grips onto weed.

entries.name: isopod
entries.description: A flattened, many-segmented [crustacean](#crustacean) with rows of short [legs](#legs), taking in wharf roaches, sea slaters and the pale deep-sea giants. Land-living relatives such as pillbugs and woodlice have tags of their own.

entries.name: hermit_crab
entries.description: A soft-bodied [crab](#crab) living inside a borrowed [seashell](#seashell), hauling it along and [pulling](#pulling) in when startled. Sometimes drawn using a tin, a [cup](#cup) or another found [container](#container) instead.

entries.name: umbrella_octopus
entries.description: A deep-sea [octopus](#octopus) whose arms are joined by a web of skin, so it opens out like a [parasol](#parasol) when it swims. Small ear-like [fins](#fins) sit on top of its head.

entries.name: puffer_fish
entries.description: A stubby [fish](#fish) known for swelling into a spiny [ball](#ball) when it feels threatened. Most kinds carry a [strong](#strong) toxin, though a few are prepared as a delicacy when handled with care.

entries.name: sea_slug
entries.description: A shell-less marine mollusc, usually drawn in vivid colours with frilled or branching growths along its [back](#back).

entries.name: surgeonfish
entries.description: A [family](#family) of flat, disc-shaped reef [fish](#fish) that includes the bright blue tang and the yellow tang, named for the sharp [spine](#spine) at the base of the [tail](#tail). Implies fish.

entries.name: catfish
entries.description: A bottom-dwelling [fish](#fish) known by the whisker-like barbels trailing from its mouth. Besides ponds and rivers it appears in Japanese art as the [giant](#giant) namazu blamed for earthquakes.

entries.name: whale_shark
entries.description: The largest living [fish](#fish), a broad-mouthed filter feeder [patterned](#patterned) with pale [spots](#spots) on [dark](#dark) skin. Harmless despite its size, usually drawn gliding through open [water](#water).

entries.name: oarfish
entries.description: An enormous ribbon-thin [fish](#fish) of deep [water](#water), silver-sided with red [fins](#fins) [running](#running) the length of its [back](#back). Japanese tradition treats it as a messenger sent up from the sea god's [palace](#palace).

entries.name: sea_urchin
entries.description: A round, spine-covered echinoderm [sitting](#sitting) on the sea [floor](#floor) or wedged into [rock](#rock). Its [roe](#roe) is eaten as uni.

entries.name: scallop
entries.description: A bivalve with a flat ribbed fan of a [shell](#shell). The thick round muscle that snaps the halves shut is the part served on a [plate](#plate).

entries.name: carp
entries.description: A heavy-bodied freshwater [fish](#fish) with large [scales](#scales) and barbels at the mouth; [koi](#koi) are one of its kinds. Common in [garden](#garden) ponds, on streamer banners and in traditional motifs.

entries.name: moorish_idol
entries.description: A disc-shaped reef [fish](#fish) banded in black, white and yellow, with a pointed [snout](#snout) and a long streamer trailing from the dorsal fin. Its black triangular [tail](#tail) separates it from the [butterflyfish](#butterflyfish) it otherwise resembles.

entries.name: hammerhead_shark
entries.description: A [shark](#shark) of the Sphyrnidae [family](#family), recognisable by the flattened bar of a head with an eye set at each end. Use it for the real [animal](#animal) and for shark characters built on that [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: swordfish
entries.description: A large, fast [ocean](#ocean) predator with a long, flattened bill projecting from its upper [jaw](#jaw) like a blade. The Japanese term for it also covers the marlin and sailfish, so it is worth checking which billfish is actually drawn.

entries.name: leech
entries.description: A segmented [worm](#worm) that clamps onto a host and drinks its [blood](#blood). It appears in swamp scenes, [parasite](#parasite) imagery and horror work.

entries.name: nautilus_(animal)
entries.description: A cephalopod living inside a [coiled](#coiled) chambered [shell](#shell), with a fringe of short [tentacles](#tentacles) at the [opening](#opening). Little changed for millions of years, it is drawn [swimming](#swimming) or as an empty shell.

entries.name: coelacanth
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) deep-water [fish](#fish) long believed extinct until living ones turned up in the twentieth century. It is known by its fleshy lobed [fins](#fins) and the broad diamond-shaped fin near the [tail](#tail).

entries.name: sea_anemone
entries.description: A soft marine [animal](#animal) anchored to [rock](#rock), its mouth ringed by a [crown](#crown) of [waving](#waving), stinging [tentacles](#tentacles).

entries.name: regal_blue_tang
entries.description: A flat oval reef [fish](#fish) with a vivid blue body, a black brushstroke marking and a yellow [tail](#tail). Best known outside aquariums as Dory's species in Finding Nemo.

entries.name: sea_cucumber
entries.description: A soft, leathery echinoderm shaped roughly like the [vegetable](#vegetable) it is named for, [lying](#lying) along the sea [bed](#bed).

entries.name: ocean_sunfish
entries.description: The mola, a vast flattened disc of a [fish](#fish) that looks as though its [tail](#tail) had been sheared off behind the [fins](#fins). Usually drawn [drifting](#drifting) near the surface.

entries.name: salmon_(fish)
entries.description: The live [fish](#fish), silver-flanked with a hooked [jaw](#jaw) on spawning males. Often drawn leaping up a [river](#river) or clamped in a bear's mouth.

entries.name: siamese_fighting_fish
entries.description: The betta, a small freshwater [fish](#fish) native to Southeast Asia. Aquarium strains are bred for [saturated](#saturated) colors and long trailing [fins](#fins), which is how art almost always shows it, while wild fish are drab and short-finned.

entries.name: crayfish
entries.description: A small freshwater [crustacean](#crustacean) shaped like a [miniature](#miniature) [lobster](#lobster), with [pincers](#pincers) and a fanned [tail](#tail). Catching them in a [stream](#stream) is a [summer](#summer) pastime in art.

entries.name: yellow_tang
entries.description: A bright yellow [surgeonfish](#surgeonfish) with a flat disc-shaped body and a pointed [snout](#snout), [familiar](#familiar) from reef aquariums. Usually shown [swimming](#swimming) in a [tank](#tank) or among [coral](#coral).

entries.name: bug
entries.description: Any insect, [spider](#spider) or similar small arthropod with a segmented body and jointed [legs](#legs) — bees, beetles, moths, centipedes and worms alike. Add the specific creature's [tag](#tag) wherever one exists.

entries.name: butterfly
entries.description: A day-flying insect with broad, usually brightly [patterned](#patterned) [wings](#wings), drawn fluttering or at rest. Named kinds such as the monarch and swallowtail fall under it.

entries.name: blue_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with blue [wings](#wings), either a real insect in the scene or a magical motif [drifting](#drifting) around a character. Whole swarms of them are common in dramatic illustrations.

entries.name: spider_web
entries.description: A web of [silk](#silk) threads spun by a [spider](#spider), whether a fresh [orb](#orb) web or dusty cobwebs gathered in a [corner](#corner). Tag the web object itself, not a printed motif based on it.

entries.name: spider
entries.description: An eight-legged arachnid with a two-part body, often shown [spinning](#spinning) or [resting](#resting) in a web. For a girl with spider traits, use [spider_girl](#spider_girl) instead.

entries.name: white_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with white [wings](#wings), whether a real insect or a [drifting](#drifting) motif drawn around the character.

entries.name: yellow_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with yellow [wings](#wings), real or decorative, somewhere in the picture. Tag butterfly alongside; butterfly-shaped hair ornaments are a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: purple_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with purple [wings](#wings), whether a live insect in the scene or a decorative motif such as a hair ornament shaped like one. Combine with butterfly.

entries.name: moth
entries.description: The night-flying cousin of the [butterfly](#butterfly), usually drawn furry-bodied with feathery [antennae](#antennae) and [wings](#wings) held out flat. Silkworm moths are included.

entries.name: bee
entries.description: The striped insect that flies from [flower](#flower) to flower and makes [honey](#honey), drawn as a real bee among blossoms, a swarm, a [mascot](#mascot) or a bee-themed character. Honeycomb and beekeeping scenes call on it as [well](#well).

entries.name: ladybug
entries.description: A small domed [beetle](#beetle) whose red, orange or yellow wing cases are spotted with black. It usually appears perched on a [leaf](#leaf), a fingertip or somebody's hair.

entries.name: beetle
entries.description: A hard-shelled insect whose forewings have hardened into a case over the [flying](#flying) pair, such as a stag or [rhinoceros](#rhinoceros) beetle. These are the prize catch of Japanese [summer](#summer) [bug](#bug) [hunting](#hunting); the Volkswagen [car](#car) of that name is something else.

entries.name: dragonfly
entries.description: A dragonfly, the slender insect with huge compound eyes and two pairs of clear veined [wings](#wings). A [summer](#summer) motif in Japanese imagery.

entries.name: red_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) whose [wings](#wings) are red, either fluttering through the scene or [resting](#resting) on a character. Red ones are often used as an ominous or symbolic touch rather than [plain](#plain) wildlife.

entries.name: centipede
entries.description: A long arthropod of many segments, each [carrying](#carrying) its own pair of [legs](#legs), with venomous [claws](#claws) at the head end. It turns up as a [crawling](#crawling) pest, as a summoned [familiar](#familiar) and, scaled up enormously, as a [monster](#monster).

entries.name: cockroach
entries.description: The flat brown household pest, usually drawn scuttling out to horrify somebody. In Japanese comedy the dread of it runs deep enough that characters avoid saying its name.

entries.name: fly
entries.description: A two-winged insect of the housefly kind, buzzing about or settled on a surface. It is often added to underline that a place or a thing has been left filthy.

entries.name: pink_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with pink [wings](#wings), fluttering through the scene or settled on a hand, a [flower](#flower) or a shoulder. A colour variant of the ordinary butterfly.

entries.name: firefly
entries.description: The small [beetle](#beetle) that glows after [dark](#dark), shown as the insect itself or as a single [drifting](#drifting) point of light. Many nameless glows with [no](#no) insect visible are [fireflies](#fireflies) instead.

entries.name: rhinoceros_beetle
entries.description: A large [scarab](#scarab) [beetle](#beetle) with a curved horn projecting from its head or thorax. Kept as a [pet](#pet) and used for beetle [fighting](#fighting) in Japan, so it often turns up in [summer](#summer) scenes with children.

entries.name: caterpillar
entries.description: The larval [stage](#stage) of a [butterfly](#butterfly) or a [moth](#moth), a soft ringed crawler that is often striped, [furry](#furry) or bristling with [spines](#spines). Found on leaves and twigs, sometimes [riding](#riding) along as a small companion.

entries.name: ant
entries.description: A small insect with a pinched, segmented body, six [legs](#legs), [biting](#biting) jaws and bent [antennae](#antennae). Drawn black, brown or red, and frequently [marching](#marching) in a line.

entries.name: black_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with black [wings](#wings), drawn as an insect in the scene or swarming around a character. It carries ominous and funereal overtones in many pictures.

entries.name: green_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with green [wings](#wings), flitting through the scene or settled on a hand, [flower](#flower) or shoulder. It usually serves as a decorative accent rather than as wildlife.

entries.name: praying_mantis
entries.description: A long-bodied insect that holds its spined forelegs [folded](#folded) up in front as if at prayer. Usually green or brown, and often drawn [rearing](#rearing) with [wings](#wings) flared in [threat](#threat).

entries.name: orange_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with orange [wings](#wings), in flight through the scene or settled on a character or a [plant](#plant).

entries.name: cicada
entries.description: A stout insect with broad [transparent](#transparent) veined [wings](#wings), the males famous for their loud droning [racket](#racket). In Japanese art its call stands in for the heat of high [summer](#summer).

entries.name: grasshopper
entries.description: A long-bodied [jumping](#jumping) insect with [folded](#folded) hind [legs](#legs) and long [antennae](#antennae). It belongs to [summer](#summer) and countryside scenes, and its shape underlies several [masked](#masked) hero designs.

entries.name: scorpion
entries.description: An eight-legged arachnid with grasping [pincers](#pincers) in front and a segmented [tail](#tail) curled forward over its [back](#back), tipped with a venomous sting.

entries.name: wasp
entries.description: A stinging insect with a pinched waist, smooth hairless body and clear [wings](#wings). Bees are rounder and [furry](#furry), while wasps carry heavier jaws.

entries.name: mosquito
entries.description: A slender long-legged [fly](#fly) with a needle-like proboscis. Only the females take [blood](#blood), and their bites spread disease; usually drawn pestering somebody on a [summer](#summer) [evening](#evening).

entries.name: cocoon
entries.description: A spun casing wrapped tight around a body, whether the [silk](#silk) a [caterpillar](#caterpillar) makes for itself or the webbing a [spider](#spider) binds prey in. Fiction also uses it as the [shell](#shell) something emerges transformed from.

entries.name: pillbug
entries.description: A small grey land [crustacean](#crustacean) armoured in overlapping plates that rolls into a tight [ball](#ball) when disturbed. Also known as a roly-poly or a woodlouse.

entries.name: stag_beetle
entries.description: A [beetle](#beetle) with huge branching jaws recalling a stag's [antlers](#antlers), used by males to wrestle [rivals](#rivals). A popular [summer](#summer) catch for children in Japan.

entries.name: too_many_butterflies
entries.description: Butterflies swarming through the frame past any hope of [counting](#counting), around a [figure](#figure) or across the whole background.

entries.name: larva
entries.description: The grub or [caterpillar](#caterpillar) [stage](#stage) of an insect, soft and segmented before it changes form. It appears as ordinary wildlife and equally as a swarming [monster](#monster).

entries.name: maggot
entries.description: Pale legless [fly](#fly) larvae, drawn squirming in spoiled [food](#food), refuse or [rotting](#rotting) [flesh](#flesh). Almost always present to make a scene repulsive.

entries.name: earthworm
entries.description: A soft ringed [worm](#worm) without [legs](#legs), pinkish brown and built for burrowing. Shows up in turned [soil](#soil), in [fishing](#fishing) scenes, or [dangling](#dangling) from somebody's fingers.

entries.name: monarch_butterfly
entries.description: A large orange [butterfly](#butterfly) veined heavily in black with white flecks around the rim, famous for its long migrations across North America. Its milkweed diet leaves it foul-tasting to birds.

entries.name: scarab
entries.description: A stout [beetle](#beetle) with a hard rounded [carapace](#carapace). Best known from Egyptian art, where it is carved as an [amulet](#amulet) or shown [rolling](#rolling) its [ball](#ball) of dung.

entries.name: grey_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with grey [wings](#wings), in flight or settled somewhere in the scene. The muted colouring suits sombre and gothic palettes.

entries.name: brown_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with brown [wings](#wings), in flight, at rest or as one of a swarm.

entries.name: tentacles
entries.description: Long, [flexible](#flexible), boneless limbs belonging to an [octopus](#octopus), a [monster](#monster), a plant's [vines](#vines) or another [creature](#creature), present somewhere in the picture. Neutral by itself; a sexual use of them is [tentacle_sex](#tentacle_sex).

entries.name: monster
entries.description: A large, frightening non-human thing, [tentacles](#tentacles) optional. Something small or harmless is a [creature](#creature) instead, and a [giant](#giant) Japanese-style beast takes [kaiju](#kaiju).

entries.name: dragon
entries.description: The mythical beast itself, most often a large winged four-legged reptile, though countless variants exist. Only for the [creature](#creature): a person with draconic traits is [dragon_girl](#dragon_girl) or [dragon_boy](#dragon_boy).

entries.name: eastern_dragon
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) built the East Asian way: a long serpentine body, [whiskers](#whiskers), antler-like [horns](#horns) and generally [no](#no) [wings](#wings). The winged western sort takes the [plain](#plain) dragon name.

entries.name: kaiju
entries.description: A [giant](#giant) [monster](#monster) of the kind that stars in Japanese [creature](#creature) films, towering over buildings and crowds. It covers both the famous [screen](#screen) monsters and original beasts drawn in the same vein.

entries.name: slime_(creature)
entries.description: The [blob](#blob) [monster](#monster) of RPGs, usually a rounded gel body with eyes, in the Dragon Quest mould. For goo as a substance or tentacle lubricant use [slime_(substance)](#slime_(substance)).

entries.name: giant_monster
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) of enormous size looming over its surroundings. Closely tied to [kaiju](#kaiju), which names the same [idea](#idea) in the city-stomping tradition.

entries.name: unicorn
entries.description: A mythical [horse](#horse) bearing a single horn on its [forehead](#forehead), traditionally white and associated with purity and European [heraldry](#heraldry). Add [wings](#wings) as [well](#well) and the correct [tag](#tag) becomes [winged_unicorn](#winged_unicorn) instead.

entries.name: western_dragon
entries.description: The European-style [dragon](#dragon): a thick-bodied, lizard-like reptile with four [legs](#legs), a long [neck](#neck) and [tail](#tail), and usually bat-like [wings](#wings), mostly seen [walking](#walking) on all fours. A slimmer, serpentine dragon is [eastern_dragon](#eastern_dragon) instead.

entries.name: chimera
entries.description: A mythical beast assembled from parts of different animals, classically a lion's head, a goat's body and a serpent for a [tail](#tail). The word is also used loosely for any [creature](#creature) [stitched](#stitched) together from mismatched species.

entries.name: pegasus
entries.description: A winged [horse](#horse) out of Greek myth, drawn with feathered [wings](#wings) and able to [fly](#fly). A horse with both wings and a single horn is [winged_unicorn](#winged_unicorn) instead.

entries.name: wyvern
entries.description: A dragon-like [creature](#creature) [standing](#standing) on two [legs](#legs) with two [wings](#wings) rather than four legs and a pair of wings; a more serpentine variant does away with the hind legs entirely, keeping only the wings. Tag [dragon](#dragon) alongside it.

entries.name: blob
entries.description: A soft, shapeless [creature](#creature) with [no](#no) arms or [legs](#legs), though eyes and a mouth are common enough. Slimes and similar squishy monsters belong here.

entries.name: phoenix
entries.description: A sacred [bird](#bird) that burns and rises again out of its own [ashes](#ashes), drawn with brilliant scarlet and [gold](#gold) plumage and a long [sweeping](#sweeping) [tail](#tail). It stands for rebirth and the endless turn of [death](#death) into life.

entries.name: small_dragon
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) rendered far below the usual scale of the species, often [no](#no) larger than a [cat](#cat) or a [bird](#bird). Too small to be ridden, it typically perches on a shoulder or curls up in someone's arms.

entries.name: mimic
entries.description: A [monster](#monster) that disguises itself as ordinary [scenery](#scenery) and strikes at whoever comes near, [opening](#opening) into a fanged mouth. Most often takes the shape of a [treasure](#treasure) chest, though doors and books occur too.

entries.name: familiar
entries.description: A small magical [creature](#creature) that attends or serves a spellcaster, often summoned by them. A catch-all for little companion beings; reach for a species [tag](#tag) where the [animal](#animal) is recognisable.

entries.name: elemental_(creature)
entries.description: A being whose body is the element it belongs to: [walking](#walking) flame, flowing [water](#water), animate stone, a whirl of air, usually in rough human shape. Ice, [lightning](#lightning) and [plant](#plant) versions turn up as [well](#well).

entries.name: mimic_chest
entries.description: The chest-shaped form of a [mimic](#mimic) [monster](#monster): a [treasure](#treasure) [box](#box) whose [lid](#lid) springs open onto [teeth](#teeth) and a long [tongue](#tongue). By far the most commonly drawn version of the [creature](#creature).

entries.name: griffin
entries.description: A mythical beast with the body of a [lion](#lion) and the head and [wings](#wings) of an [eagle](#eagle). Applies to the [creature](#creature) itself, whether feral, anthropomorphised or ridden as a mount.

entries.name: mini_dragon
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) small enough to perch on a shoulder, sit in cupped hands or curl up on a [lap](#lap), keeping full dragon [anatomy](#anatomy) shrunk to [pet](#pet) scale.

entries.name: hydra
entries.description: A many-headed serpent of Greek myth that grows a fresh head for every one cut off. Modern pictures usually give it a draconic build rather than a snake's.

entries.name: sphinx
entries.description: The lion-bodied [creature](#creature) of Egyptian and Greek tradition. Egyptian versions carry a human, ram, or [falcon](#falcon) head and [guard](#guard) sacred ground; the Greek version has a woman's upper body and kills travelers who fail her riddle.

entries.name: cerberus
entries.description: The many-headed hound guarding the [entrance](#entrance) to the underworld in Greek and Roman myth, normally given three heads and sometimes a serpent for a [tail](#tail). The name gets used loosely for any [dog](#dog) with more than one head.

entries.name: moon_rabbit
entries.description: The [rabbit](#rabbit) said to live on the [moon](#moon): pounding [mochi](#mochi) in the Japanese telling, [mixing](#mixing) the elixir of life in the Chinese one. Usually drawn [mallet](#mallet) in hand against a full moon.

entries.name: gargoyle
entries.description: A winged, stone-skinned [creature](#creature) crouched on gothic stonework, sometimes shown waking and [climbing](#climbing) down. Drawn with [folded](#folded) bat [wings](#wings), [horns](#horns) and clawed [feet](#feet).

entries.name: fire_elemental
entries.description: A being made of [fire](#fire) itself, [burning](#burning) with [no](#no) fuel and [holding](#holding) its own shape. Usually drawn as a hovering flame with a face, or as a humanoid [figure](#figure) of fire.

entries.name: tsuchinoko
entries.description: A Japanese cryptid resembling a short, thick-bodied [snake](#snake), with a middle far wider than its head or [tail](#tail). Folklore gives it [fangs](#fangs) and venom like a viper, though in art it usually reads as a comical [fat](#fat) little serpent.

entries.name: winged_unicorn
entries.description: A [horse](#horse) bearing both [wings](#wings) and a single horn on its [forehead](#forehead), [blending](#blending) a [pegasus](#pegasus) with a [unicorn](#unicorn). It is often called an alicorn, a term especially [familiar](#familiar) from My Little Pony art.

entries.name: feathered_dragon
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) covered in [feathers](#feathers) instead of, or as [well](#well) as, [scales](#scales), with plumed [wings](#wings) and often a [crest](#crest). Serpent gods of the Quetzalcoatl kind are the usual [model](#model).

entries.name: shachihoko
entries.description: A Japanese folk beast with a tiger's head on a fish's body, said to call [rain](#rain) and [guard](#guard) against [fire](#fire). Best known from the paired gilded figures arching on [castle](#castle) roof ridges.

entries.name: nue
entries.description: A [chimera](#chimera) of Japanese folklore with a monkey's head, a tanuki's body, [tiger](#tiger) [legs](#legs) and a [snake](#snake) for a [tail](#tail). It is treated as an omen of misfortune.

entries.name: cabbit
entries.description: An invented [animal](#animal) crossing a [cat](#cat) with a [rabbit](#rabbit): a feline face and body [carrying](#carrying) long ears and [strong](#strong) hind [legs](#legs).

entries.name: baku_(creature)
entries.description: A dream-eating [spirit](#spirit) built on the shape of a [tapir](#tapir), with a long [flexible](#flexible) [snout](#snout) and a [heavy](#heavy) body. Folklore has it swallow the nightmares of whoever is asleep nearby.

entries.name: chupacabra
entries.description: A cryptid of Latin American folklore, drawn as a spiny hairless [dog](#dog) or lizard-like beast that drains the [blood](#blood) of livestock. Its name is Spanish for goat-sucker.

entries.name: yatagarasu
entries.description: The three-legged [crow](#crow) of East Asian myth, taken as a messenger of the gods and a token of the [sun](#sun). Drawn as a black [bird](#bird) with an extra leg, sometimes set against a solar disc.

entries.name: kraken
entries.description: An enormous sea [monster](#monster) out of Norse legend, drawn as a [giant](#giant) [squid](#squid) or [octopus](#octopus). It usually rises from the [waves](#waves) with its arms wrapped around a [ship](#ship).

entries.name: robot
entries.description: A mechanical or electronic [machine](#machine) acting on its own, from [giant](#giant) [mecha](#mecha) to small helper bots. A human-looking one is [android](#android) or [robot_girl](#robot_girl); a piloted mecha is tagged mecha as [well](#well).

entries.name: mecha
entries.description: Giant or piloted robots and oversized robotic machines, most often set in [science](#science) fiction: [mobile](#mobile) suits, walker vehicles and similar hardware. Does not [cover](#cover) power [armor](#armor) or ordinary sci-fi gadgets.

entries.name: android
entries.description: A [robot](#robot) built to pass for human, with a fully human face and something like skin, but [giving](#giving) itself away through [joints](#joints), ports, [seams](#seams) or cables. A plainly non-human [machine](#machine) is a humanoid robot, and a person fitted with mechanical parts is a [cyborg](#cyborg).

entries.name: mecha_musume
entries.description: Hardware of any kind turned into a cute girl, wearing the machine's parts as gear or clothing. Common for [military](#military) equipment but also applied to cars, trains and game consoles.

entries.name: cyborg
entries.description: A body that is part [flesh](#flesh) and part [machine](#machine), generally a human fitted with mechanical limbs, plating or implants. If the metal reads as something added onto a living body this is the [tag](#tag); where nothing organic [can](#can) be made out, use [android](#android).

entries.name: robot_girl
entries.description: A gynoid, a [robot](#robot) built to look like a woman or girl. Visible mechanical [joints](#joints), panels or a metal body usually give it away; one that passes as fully human is usually [android](#android) instead.

entries.name: v-fin
entries.description: A V- or U-shaped [crest](#crest) fitted to the head of a [mecha](#mecha), [serving](#serving) as an antenna or sensor, best known from a long-running giant-robot franchise. Other franchises' robots use the same design element, so the shape alone does not point to any one series.

entries.name: humanoid_robot
entries.description: A [robot](#robot) built on a two-legged, two-armed human plan but plainly mechanical, without a face that could pass for human. A [machine](#machine) that could pass as a person is an [android](#android), and piloted [mecha](#mecha) are tagged separately.

entries.name: non-humanoid_robot
entries.description: A [robot](#robot) built to [no](#no) human plan: robot animals, pods, walkers, [spider](#spider) tanks and the like. Anything with a broadly human body and limbs falls outside it.

entries.name: drone
entries.description: An unmanned craft of the air, ground or sea, flown by remote control or by its own software. Covers small [camera](#camera) quadcopters as [well](#well) as [military](#military) machines.

entries.name: one-eyed_mecha
entries.description: A [giant](#giant) [robot](#robot) whose head carries one eye or sensor, often [sliding](#sliding) along a visor slit, in place of a matched pair.

entries.name: robot_animal
entries.description: A [robot](#robot) built in the shape of an [animal](#animal), such as a mechanical [dog](#dog) or [bird](#bird). A non-humanoid robot; a real animal fitted with cybernetic parts does not count.

entries.name: walker_(robot)
entries.description: A striding [war](#war) [machine](#machine) on two or more [legs](#legs), usually without a head or arms and often with backward-jointed limbs. Humanoid [mecha](#mecha) are a different thing entirely.

entries.name: clothed_robot
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) that plainly reads as a machine is wearing human clothing, which lands as incongruous. Keep it for obviously robotic bodies; a lifelike [android](#android) in [clothes](#clothes) does not qualify.

entries.name: golem
entries.description: A humanoid [figure](#figure) built from lifeless matter and [animated](#animated) by [magic](#magic), traditionally [clay](#clay) but often stone, iron or wood. Strong and obedient but dull-witted, and the harder its material the stronger it is.

entries.name: robot_dragon
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) assembled entirely from mechanical parts, or a [machine](#machine) designed in a dragon's shape. It overlaps with [mecha](#mecha) when the thing is piloted or weaponised.

entries.name: robot_dog
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) built in the shape of a [dog](#dog), whether a rounded [toy](#toy) companion or an armoured four-legged unit. It behaves as a [pet](#pet) or a tool rather than a character with a human form.

entries.name: vernier_thrusters
entries.description: Small auxiliary [rocket](#rocket) nozzles used for fine adjustments to a craft's heading, attitude or speed, [sitting](#sitting) alongside the main engines. Standard fittings on [mecha](#mecha) and [spacecraft](#spacecraft) designs, often shown [firing](#firing) in short bursts.

entries.name: robot_bird
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) shaped like a [bird](#bird), from [clockwork](#clockwork) songbirds to armed drones with [wings](#wings). The bird form is deliberate rather than incidental.

entries.name: colossus
entries.description: A vast animate [figure](#figure) raised out of stone, metal or other lifeless material. Greek myth supplies the name, and in pictures it looms far above the human characters.

entries.name: mecha_danshi
entries.description: Machinery or hardware personified as a cute boy, keeping recognisable parts of the original equipment as clothing, limbs or [accessories](#accessories). The male counterpart to [mecha_musume](#mecha_musume).

entries.name: robot_fish
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) shaped like a [fish](#fish), with plated [scales](#scales), a jointed [tail](#tail) and often a visible propulsion unit. Usually shown [swimming](#swimming) or acting as a submersible [drone](#drone).

entries.name: karakasa_obake
entries.description: An [old](#old) oil-paper [umbrella](#umbrella) come to life, [hopping](#hopping) on a single leg with one big eye and a lolling [tongue](#tongue). It is the best known of the household objects that turn into spirits with age.

entries.name: object_head
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) with an otherwise ordinary human body whose head is some lifeless thing instead: a [television](#television), a [lamp](#lamp), a [box](#box). Tag the kind of object as [well](#well) wherever one exists.

entries.name: living_clothes
entries.description: Clothing that moves, speaks or wears an expression of its own, behaving as a [creature](#creature) rather than a garment. Only use it where the outfit is visibly alive in the picture; knowing that a character's [costume](#costume) is sentient elsewhere is not enough.

entries.name: food-themed_creature
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) or small beast made out of an item of [food](#food), such as a [cat](#cat) with a [bread](#bread) loaf for a body. The reverse case, food shaped like an animal, is [animal-themed_food](#animal-themed_food).

entries.name: alraune
entries.description: A [plant](#plant) woman whose lower body grows out of a large [flower](#flower), often with green skin and [vines](#vines) for limbs. A girl who merely carries a few floral traits is a [plant_girl](#plant_girl) instead.

entries.name: plant_monster
entries.description: A moving, predatory [plant](#plant) that seizes and swallows, usually with vine-tentacles or a maw modelled on a flytrap or pitcher plant. Humanoid versions belong under [plant_girl](#plant_girl) or [plant_boy](#plant_boy) instead.

entries.name: mushroom_girl
entries.description: A girl built out of fungus, with a cap for a [hat](#hat) or a head, stalk-like limbs and sometimes [gills](#gills) or [drifting](#drifting) spores. One of the plant-creature turns on the [monster](#monster) girl [idea](#idea).

entries.name: animate_object
entries.description: Something that ought to be lifeless moves and behaves as though alive: a [walking](#walking) [chair](#chair), a chatty [sword](#sword), a [teapot](#teapot) with opinions. Reanimated [flesh](#flesh) such as zombies falls outside it.

entries.name: mandragora
entries.description: A [plant](#plant) [monster](#monster) of folklore whose root grows in the shape of a small person and which screams fatally as it is [torn](#torn) from the [soil](#soil). Drawn as a living [creature](#creature) rather than a harvested root.

entries.name: living_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) that is plainly a living thing, with eyes, a mouth or exposed [flesh](#flesh) worked into the blade, [barrel](#barrel) or haft. It may blink, speak or writhe in its wielder's grip.

entries.name: carnivorous_plant
entries.description: A [plant](#plant) that traps and eats living prey, drawn as an unnamed toothed maw on a stalk rather than any real species. Usually a hazard in a [dungeon](#dungeon) or [jungle](#jungle), or an outright [monster](#monster).

entries.name: jack-o'-lantern_head
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) whose head is a hollowed [pumpkin](#pumpkin) lit from within, on an otherwise ordinary body. It covers both a [mask](#mask) worn over the head and a [creature](#creature) genuinely built that way.

entries.name: chouchin_obake
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [lantern](#lantern) come alive as a [spirit](#spirit), its body [split](#split) open into a wide mouth with a lolling [tongue](#tongue) and a single eye above. A close relative of the [animated](#animated) [umbrella](#umbrella) spirit.

entries.name: long_hair
entries.description: Hair [falling](#falling) below the shoulders and [reaching](#reaching) down to about the waist. Shoulder-length hair is [medium_hair](#medium_hair), past the waist is [very_long_hair](#very_long_hair), and hair trailing beyond [floor](#floor) length is [absurdly_long_hair](#absurdly_long_hair).

entries.name: short_hair
entries.description: Hair that reaches the [neck](#neck) but stops above the shoulders, as in a bob cut or an [undercut](#undercut). Ear length or shorter is [very_short_hair](#very_short_hair), and shoulder length is [medium_hair](#medium_hair).

entries.name: very_long_hair
entries.description: Hair [falling](#falling) below the waist, down to as far as the [feet](#feet). Hair ending at or above the waist is [long_hair](#long_hair); hair that trails past the [floor](#floor) is [absurdly_long_hair](#absurdly_long_hair).

entries.name: medium_hair
entries.description: Hair [reaching](#reaching) roughly to the shoulders, longer than [short_hair](#short_hair) but not yet long enough to count as [long_hair](#long_hair). The midpoint on the hair-length scale from [bald](#bald) to [very_long_hair](#very_long_hair).

entries.name: short_hair_with_long_locks
entries.description: A short haircut kept [back](#back) except for one or two locks left as long as [long_hair](#long_hair). Front locks also take [sidelocks](#sidelocks); locks at the back must clearly hang from otherwise short hair rather than a gathered [ponytail](#ponytail).

entries.name: absurdly_long_hair
entries.description: Hair longer than the character is [tall](#tall), so that they could stand on it. Waist-to-floor length is [very_long_hair](#very_long_hair); this is the step past the [floor](#floor) and includes it.

entries.name: very_short_hair
entries.description: Hair [cropped](#cropped) to [jaw](#jaw) or ear length or shorter: pixie [cuts](#cuts), crew cuts and buzz cuts. Hair [reaching](#reaching) between the chin and the shoulders is [short_hair](#short_hair); none at all is [bald](#bald).

entries.name: bald
entries.description: No hair on top of the head, which includes men keeping a fringe only around the sides. It is the bottom of the hair-length scale, below [very_short_hair](#very_short_hair), and covers shaved and naturally hairless heads alike.

entries.name: bald_male
entries.description: A male character whose scalp carries [no](#no) hair. Where a fringe still clings around the sides and the [back](#back), [balding](#balding) is the better fit.

entries.name: balding
entries.description: Enough hair has gone for the scalp to show through, though a fringe still remains around the sides and the [back](#back). It is one step short of fully [bald](#bald).

entries.name: bald_spot
entries.description: A [patch](#patch) of bare scalp where the hair has thinned away entirely, usually at the [crown](#crown), while the rest of the head still has [cover](#cover). It is often played for laughs on older men.

entries.name: shaved_head
entries.description: Hair clipped down to [stubble](#stubble), shorter than any regular crop, distinguished from true baldness only by a faint tint of colour left on the scalp.

entries.name: bald_girl
entries.description: A female character with [no](#no) hair on her head at all, whether shaved off, lost or never grown. Anything still present, however short, belongs on the length scale from [very_short_hair](#very_short_hair) upward.

entries.name: receding_hairline
entries.description: Hair has thinned [back](#back) from the temples and [forehead](#forehead), leaving the front of the scalp bare while growth continues further behind. Usually drawn on older male characters as a [marker](#marker) of age.

entries.name: twintails
entries.description: All the hair gathered into two tails, one on each side of the head, with nothing left [hanging](#hanging) free beyond bangs and [sidelocks](#sidelocks). If some hair still falls loose it is [two_side_up](#two_side_up) instead; two [animal](#animal) tails on a body are [multiple_tails](#multiple_tails), not this.

entries.name: ponytail
entries.description: Hair gathered at the [back](#back) of the head and tied so it hangs free from that point. Only for a single [plain](#plain) ponytail at the back; [side_ponytail](#side_ponytail), [twintails](#twintails) and [braided_ponytail](#braided_ponytail) have their own tags.

entries.name: hair_bun
entries.description: Hair wrapped into a round bun on the head, single or double, in any position. Add [double_bun](#double_bun), [cone_hair_bun](#cone_hair_bun) or [braided_bun](#braided_bun) where the shape is specific.

entries.name: side_ponytail
entries.description: Hair gathered into a [tail](#tail) fixed at one side of the head instead of the [back](#back). Do not add [ponytail](#ponytail), which is reserved for the rear position; [one_side_up](#one_side_up) covers a small tied tuft with the rest of the hair left loose.

entries.name: two_side_up
