entries.description: Part of the hair is gathered into a tie at each side of the head while the rest falls loose down the [back](#back). Neither the size of the tied sections nor the loose hair matters, only that some hair remains free; with everything tied up it becomes [twintails](#twintails) instead.

entries.name: double_bun
entries.description: Hair gathered into two round buns, one to each side of the head, the odango style. A single bun is [hair_bun](#hair_bun) on its own.

entries.name: low_twintails
entries.description: Twintails gathered at or below ear level instead of high on the head, so the tails hang from the [nape](#nape) or from behind the ears. Tied high, they are simply [twintails](#twintails).

entries.name: one_side_up
entries.description: Some of the hair is gathered and tied at one side of the head while the rest hangs loose, the single-sided form of [two_side_up](#two_side_up). A [side_ponytail](#side_ponytail) takes up nearly everything, and an untied tuft [standing](#standing) out on its own is [side_ahoge](#side_ahoge).

entries.name: high_ponytail
entries.description: Hair gathered and tied near the [crown](#crown) at the [back](#back) of the head rather than down at the [nape](#nape). A [tail](#tail) [bound](#bound) low is [low_ponytail](#low_ponytail), and one pulled high and off to one side is [high_side_ponytail](#high_side_ponytail).

entries.name: single_hair_bun
entries.description: The hair is [coiled](#coiled) into one round bun, usually at the [back](#back) or top of the head. Two buns are [double_bun](#double_bun); a bun set to the side is [single_side_bun](#single_side_bun).

entries.name: short_twintails
entries.description: Twintails that hang about shoulder length or shorter. Where only part of the hair is tied up, use [two_side_up](#two_side_up) instead. Implies [twintails](#twintails).

entries.name: low_ponytail
entries.description: A [ponytail](#ponytail) tied low on the head, typically at the [nape](#nape) of the [neck](#neck). One gathered high on the [crown](#crown) is a [high_ponytail](#high_ponytail).

entries.name: low-tied_long_hair
entries.description: Long hair gathered with a [ribbon](#ribbon), [bow](#bow) or [scrunchie](#scrunchie) partway down its length or near the end, rather than up at the head. A tie at the [nape](#nape) that makes a [tail](#tail) is [low_ponytail](#low_ponytail) instead.

entries.name: half_updo
entries.description: The hair at the temples is pulled [back](#back) into a bun, short [ponytail](#ponytail), [braid](#braid) or a [bow](#bow) at the back of the head, while the rest hangs loose. A hair bow or [ribbon](#ribbon) fastening it is often visible from the front.

entries.name: short_ponytail
entries.description: A [ponytail](#ponytail) gathered unusually short, often ending above the [nape](#nape). Tag with ponytail.

entries.name: single_side_bun
entries.description: One hair bun placed off to one side rather than at the [back](#back). Two of them make [double_bun](#double_bun); add [side_up_bun](#side_up_bun) when the rest of the hair hangs loose.

entries.name: folded_ponytail
entries.description: A [ponytail](#ponytail) turned up against the [back](#back) of the head and held with a tie or wrapped around itself. The [tail](#tail) ends up short and rounded rather than trailing down.

entries.name: cone_hair_bun
entries.description: Hair buns shaped into cones or pointed knobs, whether a single one or a pair. Hair pulled into sharp [spikes](#spikes) is [hair_horns](#hair_horns), and [hairpods](#hairpods), [animal](#animal) ears and beehive styles are separate again.

entries.name: topknot
entries.description: Hair gathered and tied into a tuft on the [crown](#crown) of the head, whether the [samurai](#samurai) style or a modern bun-like knot. Add [hair_bun](#hair_bun) when it is [coiled](#coiled) rather than loose.

entries.name: front_ponytail
entries.description: Hair gathered and tied so the [tail](#tail) hangs down in front, under the chin, instead of at the [back](#back) of the head. A distinctive style rather than a stray [lock](#lock) pulled forward.

entries.name: multi-tied_hair
entries.description: A [ponytail](#ponytail), [twintails](#twintails) or a sidelock [bound](#bound) at several points down its length, [giving](#giving) a segmented, sausage-string look. Quite different from a [braid](#braid), where the hair is woven.

entries.name: bun_with_braided_base
entries.description: A hair bun ringed at its base by a plait of the same hair. Not to be [confused](#confused) with [braided_bun](#braided_bun), where the bun is itself [coiled](#coiled) out of a [braid](#braid).

entries.name: quad_tails
entries.description: Hair divided into four separate tails, typically worn as four pigtails around the head. Three sections is [tri_tails](#tri_tails) and five is quin_tails.

entries.name: updo
entries.description: Hair arranged to be held up off the [neck](#neck) with clips, bands or braids, ranging from a simple bun to an elaborate formal style. Ponytails technically qualify, but the term is mostly reserved for the fancier arrangements.

entries.name: high_side_ponytail
entries.description: A side [tail](#tail) [bound](#bound) high, close to the top of the head, so it falls over one side of the face or shoulder. Tied further down it is simply [side_ponytail](#side_ponytail).

entries.name: wide_ponytail
entries.description: A [ponytail](#ponytail) that fans out behind the head, staying thick and voluminous rather than narrowing where it is tied. Tag ponytail alongside it.

entries.name: long_twintails
entries.description: Hair gathered into two tails that hang to the waist or beyond. It combines the [twintails](#twintails) style with considerable length.

entries.name: tri_tails
entries.description: A hairstyle in which the hair is divided into three tied sections, for example [two_side_up](#two_side_up) combined with a separate [ponytail](#ponytail) at the [back](#back). Count the tied tails themselves, not the loose bangs.

entries.name: split_ponytail
entries.description: A single [ponytail](#ponytail) that forks near its base into two or more tails. Different from [twintails](#twintails), which are tied as separate bunches from the start.

entries.name: side_up_bun
entries.description: One or two buns sit at the side of the head while the rest of the hair hangs loose, the bun counterpart of [one_side_up](#one_side_up). Add [single_side_bun](#single_side_bun) for one bun or [double_bun](#double_bun) for a matching pair.

entries.name: doughnut_hair_bun
entries.description: A bun rolled over a ring-shaped [hairdressing](#hairdressing) form, so it sits as a smooth even [circle](#circle) rather than a [coiled](#coiled) odango. Where the difference cannot be told, leave it off; [hair_rings](#hair_rings) are something else.

entries.name: drill_ponytail
entries.description: A [ponytail](#ponytail) whose gathered length is curled into a single conical drill-shaped ringlet. The [drill](#drill) shape belongs to the [tail](#tail) rather than to the whole head of hair.

entries.name: short_sidetail
entries.description: A side [ponytail](#ponytail) gathered short, usually ending somewhere between the [crown](#crown) and the chin, the side-tail equivalent of [short_ponytail](#short_ponytail).

entries.name: low_side_ponytail
entries.description: Hair gathered to one side and tied near the [nape](#nape) or below the ear, so the [tail](#tail) falls forward over a shoulder. Tied higher, beside the [temple](#temple), it is a [plain](#plain) [side_ponytail](#side_ponytail).

entries.name: short_side_ponytail
entries.description: Hair gathered at one side of the head into a stubby [tail](#tail) that reaches [no](#no) further than the shoulder.

entries.name: uneven_twintails
entries.description: Twintails drawn with one side noticeably longer than the other, [breaking](#breaking) the usual [symmetry](#symmetry) of the style.

entries.name: folded_hair
entries.description: Hair doubled [back](#back) along its own length and tied or tucked so that it hangs far shorter than it really is. A [folded_ponytail](#folded_ponytail) is the commonest form.

entries.name: quad_drills
entries.description: Four corkscrew [ringlets](#ringlets) of [drill](#drill) hair worn together, usually paired on each side of the head. A denser take on the twin drills common to ojou-sama character designs.

entries.name: shuangyaji
entries.description: A Chinese style with the hair gathered into two coils or loops set high on the head or above the temples, sometimes braided. Historically worn by young girls and maidservants; not to be [confused](#confused) with [mizura](#mizura), the men's equivalent style.

entries.name: feixianji_(hairstyle)
entries.description: A Chinese court hairstyle with two large loose loops of hair rising over the head and [leaning](#leaning) [back](#back), suggesting [rabbit](#rabbit) ears or a [bow](#bow). Bigger and slacker than the Japanese chigomage; a related form lets the loops hang down the sides.

entries.name: nihongami
entries.description: Historical Japanese hairstyles, waxed and [folded](#folded) into looped [shapes](#shapes) that once signalled a woman's age and marital [standing](#standing). Geisha and [oiran](#oiran) wear the most elaborate arrangements.

entries.name: beehive_hairdo
entries.description: Long hair teased and piled into a [tall](#tall) cone above the head, [leaning](#leaning) [back](#back) a little so the [silhouette](#silhouette) recalls a woven hive. It carries [strong](#strong) 1960s associations and suits prim older-woman designs.

entries.name: afro_puffs
entries.description: Two rounded buns of tightly curled hair, one on either side of the head. The [coiled](#coiled) texture is what separates them from ordinary double buns.

entries.name: folded_twintails
entries.description: Twin tails looped [back](#back) over the [crown](#crown) so each forms a slack [ring](#ring) rather than [hanging](#hanging) free. The bulk of the hair ends up [sitting](#sitting) high on the head.

entries.name: heart_hair_bun
entries.description: One or more buns wound into a [heart](#heart) shape instead of a round knot.

entries.name: hair_half_undone
entries.description: One of a matched pair of tails or braids has come loose while its twin still holds. Often shown part-way through letting the hair down or putting it [back](#back) up.

entries.name: mizura
entries.description: An ancient Japanese men's hairstyle: the hair [split](#split) into two side bundles, each looped down and [back](#back) up and [bound](#bound) with cord or a hair [tube](#tube). Distinct from [shuangyaji](#shuangyaji), a similar-looking style worn by girls higher on the head.

entries.name: flower-shaped_hair
entries.description: Hair gathered and tied so its loops make the [outline](#outline) of a blossom on the head. The [petals](#petals) are hair itself, not an ornament [pinned](#pinned) in place.

entries.name: katsuyamamage
entries.description: An Edo-period women's style in which the gathered hair is tied up and then looped into a wide [standing](#standing) [ring](#ring) above the [crown](#crown). It is named after a celebrated courtesan who wore it.

entries.name: tri_rod
entries.description: Hair gathered into three thick, straight rod-shaped lengths rather than braids or curls. The stiff cylindrical [silhouette](#silhouette) is what sets it apart from an ordinary tied [tail](#tail).

entries.name: chonmage
entries.description: The traditional Japanese men's [topknot](#topknot), the [crown](#crown) shaved bare and the remaining hair [oiled](#oiled) and [folded](#folded) forward across it. Standard on [samurai](#samurai) characters and still worn by [sumo](#sumo) wrestlers; the version [standing](#standing) upright is chasenmage.

entries.name: tri_drills
entries.description: Hair worked into three tight corkscrew curls of the [drill](#drill) type. The usual layout is one coil in the middle with one at each side.

entries.name: datehyogo
entries.description: An elaborate traditional [updo](#updo) of Edo-era courtesans, the hair swept up into wide looped masses with a rounded [silhouette](#silhouette). The related yokohyogo is more triangular, though drawing styles blur the difference.

entries.name: braid
entries.description: Three or more strands of hair woven into a plait, singly or several at once. Say which arrangement with [single_braid](#single_braid), [twin_braids](#twin_braids), [side_braid](#side_braid), french_braid, [braided_ponytail](#braided_ponytail) or [braided_bun](#braided_bun); twisted or multi-tied hair is something else.

entries.name: twin_braids
entries.description: Two braided lengths of hair, either [hanging](#hanging) at the sides like [sidelocks](#sidelocks) or behind the ears like [twintails](#twintails). Tied low they read as [low_twin_braids](#low_twin_braids); two full-length braids at the [back](#back) also count as twintails.

entries.name: single_braid
entries.description: The hair is gathered into exactly one [braid](#braid), typically [hanging](#hanging) down the [back](#back) where a [ponytail](#ponytail) would sit. Two braids are called [twin_braids](#twin_braids).

entries.name: side_braid
entries.description: A single [braid](#braid) [hanging](#hanging) down beside the face rather than at the [back](#back) of the head. Two matching braids are [side_braids](#side_braids); a braid that starts at the back of the head is a [braided_ponytail](#braided_ponytail) instead.

entries.name: braided_ponytail
entries.description: Hair gathered at one point on the [back](#back) of the head and plaited from there down, like a [ponytail](#ponytail) that has been braided. Add [single_braid](#single_braid) when it is the only plait, leave ponytail off since that means loose hair, and use [side_braid](#side_braid) if it hangs to one side.

entries.name: crown_braid
entries.description: A [braid](#braid) taken around the top of the head so that it rings it like a [hairband](#hairband). The mainstay of [princess](#princess) and milkmaid styling.

entries.name: half_up_braid
entries.description: A [braid](#braid) that loops around the [back](#back) of the head in the manner of a half [updo](#updo), with the rest of the hair loose. A visible [tail](#tail) from the loop's centre makes it [half_up_half_down_braid](#half_up_half_down_braid); around the top of the head it is [crown_braid](#crown_braid), around the [nape](#nape) nape_braid.

entries.name: low_twin_braids
entries.description: Two braids tied low, below ear level, usually taken from the [back](#back) of the hair rather than from the [sidelocks](#sidelocks). Braids started up near the [crown](#crown) are ordinary [twin_braids](#twin_braids).

entries.name: braided_bun
entries.description: A bun [coiled](#coiled) up out of a [braid](#braid), so the plaited texture shows in the knot itself. A [plain](#plain) bun with a separate braid wound round its base is [bun_with_braided_base](#bun_with_braided_base).

entries.name: side_braids
entries.description: A [braid](#braid) hangs down beside the face on both sides. With a braid on only one side, use [side_braid](#side_braid) instead.

entries.name: braided_bangs
entries.description: The front hair is plaited, or a [braid](#braid) runs across the [forehead](#forehead) as part of the fringe. It usually sits alongside loose bangs rather than replacing them.

entries.name: long_braid
entries.description: A [braid](#braid) noticeably longer than usual, [falling](#falling) to the buttocks or beyond. It generally accompanies [very_long_hair](#very_long_hair).

entries.name: braided_hair_rings
entries.description: The looped rings of hair [hanging](#hanging) beside the head are made of plaited strands rather than loose ones, [giving](#giving) each [ring](#ring) a rope-like texture. Pon de ring hair is the other name for the style.

entries.name: braided_base
entries.description: The hair is plaited tight against the scalp at the roots, and that plaiting forms the foundation the rest of the style rises or falls from. The [braid](#braid) lies flat on the head instead of [hanging](#hanging) free.

entries.name: low-braided_long_hair
entries.description: Long hair left loose at the top and braided only from below the shoulders downward. Where ribbons secure the start of the [braid](#braid) consider [multi-tied_hair](#multi-tied_hair), and a braid begun up at the head is a high-ended braid.

entries.name: multiple_braids
entries.description: Hair worked into more than two braids at once. A single plait uses [braid](#braid) and a matched pair uses [twin_braids](#twin_braids) instead.

entries.name: single_braided_sidelock
entries.description: One [lock](#lock) beside the face is plaited while the rest of the hair hangs loose. The [braid](#braid) usually falls in front of the shoulder on one side only.

entries.name: braided_twintails
entries.description: Hair tied into two tails, each of which is plaited rather than left [hanging](#hanging) loose. Ribbons or ties finishing off the ends are a common addition.

entries.name: braided_sidelocks
entries.description: Both of the strands framing the face in front of the ears are worked into plaits. Whatever happens to the rest of the hair is a separate matter, and it is often left loose.

entries.name: braided_sidelock
entries.description: One [lock](#lock) in front of the ear, on either or both sides, has been plaited while the rest hangs loose. A plait anywhere else on the head is [side_braid](#side_braid).

entries.name: ponytail_with_braided_base
entries.description: A [ponytail](#ponytail) whose gathering point is wrapped in a plait rather than a [plain](#plain) band. Only the base is braided; a [tail](#tail) that is itself plaited is a [braided_ponytail](#braided_ponytail).

entries.name: ribbon_braid
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) woven through a [braid](#braid) along its length rather than only [tying](#tying) off the end. Combine with braid and [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon).

entries.name: half_up_half_down_braid
entries.description: A [braid](#braid) that loops behind the head while a loose [tail](#tail) falls from the centre of that loop. Only [tag](#tag) it when the tail [can](#can) be seen; otherwise [half_up_braid](#half_up_braid) applies.

entries.name: tri_braids
entries.description: Hair worked into exactly three braids. The arrangement varies: one [running](#running) down the [back](#back) with two at the sides, or all three gathered together.

entries.name: half_crown_braid
entries.description: A [braid](#braid) [running](#running) around part of the head like a [headband](#headband) while the remaining hair hangs loose. Sits between a full [crown](#crown) braid and [plain](#plain) loose hair.

entries.name: quad_braids
entries.description: Hair plaited into four separate braids at once, whether left [hanging](#hanging), looped up, or [pinned](#pinned) in place. Two braids instead is [twin_braids](#twin_braids).

entries.name: short_braid
entries.description: Hair plaited into a [braid](#braid) that runs only a short way, ending around the [jaw](#jaw) or the [nape](#nape) rather than continuing down the [back](#back).

entries.name: cornrows
entries.description: Hair braided flat against the scalp in parallel rows, the braids [standing](#standing) raised in lines [running](#running) [back](#back) over the head. The parting pattern is part of the style.

entries.name: front_braid
entries.description: Hair braided and brought round to hang beneath the chin, like a [ponytail](#ponytail) pulled to the front. Braids that merely fall forward over a shoulder are not this.

entries.name: folded_braid
entries.description: A plait doubled [back](#back) on itself and [pinned](#pinned), or drawn through a hair [ring](#ring), so it hangs as a compact loop instead of a free [tail](#tail). Formal and traditional styles use it.

entries.name: hair_intakes
entries.description: Two forward-facing scoops of hair on top of the head, as on Astolfo, Nero Claudius and Ouro Kronii. Exaggerated further, they become [hair_ears](#hair_ears).

entries.name: bob_cut
entries.description: A short cut whose [weight](#weight) falls in an even line somewhere between the ears and the chin, frequently finished with blunt ends. It pairs with [short_hair](#short_hair); a chin-length version with straight [sidelocks](#sidelocks) may read as a [hime_cut](#hime_cut).

entries.name: drill_hair
entries.description: Hair curled into pointed conical [ringlets](#ringlets) like a [screw](#screw), the tate roll of haughty rich-girl characters. Curls without that cone shape are ringlets; combined with [twintails](#twintails) it gives twin drills.

entries.name: spiked_hair
entries.description: Hair styled into sharp points sticking outward or upward, the wild look typical of shounen protagonists like Goku, Cloud, or Naruto. Seen mostly, but not exclusively, on male characters.

entries.name: twin_drills
entries.description: Drill_hair arranged as two corkscrew curls, one on each side of the head like [twintails](#twintails). A hallmark of haughty ojou-sama characters.

entries.name: hair_rings
entries.description: Hair styled into [ring](#ring) or loop [shapes](#shapes), as in the Chinese feixianji style. Ring-shaped ornaments worn in the hair are [ring_hair_ornament](#ring_hair_ornament) instead.

entries.name: asymmetrical_hair
entries.description: A hairstyle whose sides refuse to match, with far more length or volume kept on one side than the other. Pair it with [asymmetrical_bangs](#asymmetrical_bangs) or [asymmetrical_sidelocks](#asymmetrical_sidelocks) when the fringe or the locks by the ears are what differ.

entries.name: blunt_ends
entries.description: The tips of the hair are cut level, so the ends read as flat separate strands. It concerns the hair at the [back](#back) and sides rather than the fringe, though it often turns up with [blunt_bangs](#blunt_bangs).

entries.name: hime_cut
entries.description: Long straight hair with blunt bangs and blunt-ended [sidelocks](#sidelocks) framing the face. All three elements have to be present; wavy or shorter hair with straight bangs does not qualify.

entries.name: flipped_hair
entries.description: Hair whose ends curl outward, away from face and [neck](#neck). A styling trait, not the act of [tossing](#tossing) the hair with a hand, which is [hair_flip](#hair_flip).

entries.name: undercut
entries.description: Hair buzzed or shaved short around the sides and [back](#back), with the top left long and swept over, slicked back or [hanging](#hanging) forward. A 1920s style revived in the 2010s for both men and women.

entries.name: curtained_hair
entries.description: A fringe that lifts into a brief [arch](#arch) and falls again while the bangs part to either side, framing the [forehead](#forehead) like drawn [curtains](#curtains). Chiefly a male style, though women wear it as a secondary trait.

entries.name: pointy_hair
entries.description: Hair with two or more cone-shaped tufts that rise upward, often looking like a pair of [animal](#animal) ears. Hair that is spiky all over, or flat side flaps, take their own separate tags.

entries.name: bow-shaped_hair
entries.description: Hair styled or growing into the [outline](#outline) of a [bow](#bow), loops and all. A real bow tied into the hair is [hair_bow](#hair_bow); where the hair forms two such [shapes](#shapes), the paired [tag](#tag) may fit as [well](#well).

entries.name: parted_hair
entries.description: Hair with a visible part line along the scalp, most often a centre part seen from above or from behind. It concerns the [crown](#crown), not the fringe, since a [split](#split) fringe is [parted_bangs](#parted_bangs).

entries.name: inverted_bob
entries.description: A bob worn short at the [nape](#nape) and growing steadily longer toward the face. The lengthening has to be gradual, [giving](#giving) the hair a forward-tilting wedge.

entries.name: pompadour
entries.description: Hair swept up and [back](#back) from the [forehead](#forehead) into a [tall](#tall) roll on top of the head, often drawn to absurd [height](#height). Associated with rockers, delinquents and rebels.

entries.name: hair_horns
entries.description: Hair tied or sticking up into two tight horn-like points. Like [cone_hair_bun](#cone_hair_bun) but tighter and pointed, or simply a natural spike of hair [reading](#reading) as [horns](#horns).

entries.name: wolf_cut
entries.description: A shaggy, layered haircut with volume on top and thinned-out lengths from the [nape](#nape) down, including the rounded jellyfish-cut variant. It should not be mistaken for a [mullet](#mullet), which is kept short at the sides.

entries.name: mohawk
entries.description: The sides of the head shaved or clipped short, leaving a band of hair [running](#running) front to [back](#back) over the [crown](#crown). It counts whether the strip stands up in gelled [spikes](#spikes) or falls flat.

entries.name: dreadlocks
entries.description: Hair matted and twisted into long rope-like locks [hanging](#hanging) all round the head. Each [lock](#lock) keeps its own thickness rather than [lying](#lying) flat like a plaited [braid](#braid).

entries.name: buzz_cut
entries.description: Hair clipped uniformly short all over with electric [clippers](#clippers), the cut of recruits and [school](#school) [baseball](#baseball) players. Leaving the top longer makes it an [undercut](#undercut) instead.

entries.name: afro
entries.description: Hair [standing](#standing) out from the head in a large rounded mass. It is often a [gag](#gag) result of an [explosion](#explosion), and a truly enormous one also takes huge_afro.

entries.name: horn-shaped_hair
entries.description: Locks of hair are styled into points that rise from the head like a pair of [horns](#horns). Only the hair does it; real horns growing from the [skull](#skull) are tagged separately.

entries.name: bowl_cut
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) short cut of a single length all the way round, as though a [bowl](#bowl) had been set on the head and everything below its rim trimmed away. Usually goes with blunt bangs and short hair.

entries.name: hair_ears
entries.description: Hair styled so that it sticks up like a pair of [animal](#animal) ears, from extreme [hair_intakes](#hair_intakes), cone buns or [hair_flaps](#hair_flaps). Add [impossible_hair](#impossible_hair) when the effect looks unrealistic.

entries.name: wig
entries.description: A hairpiece worn over a character's real hair, used for [cosplay](#cosplay), [disguise](#disguise), or [hiding](#hiding) baldness. Reserve it for pictures that make clear the hair is false, such as a wig [slipping](#slipping) or being held apart from the head.

entries.name: hair_extensions
entries.description: Added lengths of hair clipped or woven into a character's own, often in a contrasting colour or visibly attached at a band.

entries.name: sidecut
entries.description: One side of the head is shaved close while the rest of the hair keeps its normal length. Implies [asymmetrical_hair](#asymmetrical_hair) and [undercut](#undercut).

entries.name: side_drill
entries.description: Hair twisted into a single drill-shaped curl that hangs off to one side of the head. Distinct from [drill_sidelocks](#drill_sidelocks), where the curls form the [sidelocks](#sidelocks) themselves.

entries.name: pixie_cut
entries.description: A very short women's haircut, roughly [jaw](#jaw) length or less, with volume kept toward the [crown](#crown) and often a [sweeping](#sweeping) fringe near the eyes. Low-maintenance in look, it is frequently given to tomboyish characters.

entries.name: mullet
entries.description: Hair kept short at the front and sides but left long down the [back](#back). A narrow [lock](#lock) tied or braided at the [nape](#nape) turns it into a rattail instead.

entries.name: heart_hair
entries.description: The main mass of the hair is styled into a [heart](#heart) [outline](#outline). Hearts made only by a stray [lock](#lock), an antenna strand or hair at the [nape](#nape) have separate tags.

entries.name: widow's_peak
entries.description: The hairline dips to a point at the centre of the [forehead](#forehead) instead of [running](#running) straight across. It is a natural feature rather than a styling [choice](#choice), so hair merely arranged into a peak does not count, and enough of the hairline must be visible to confirm it.

entries.name: flattop
entries.description: A cut where the hair on the [crown](#crown) stands upright and is trimmed level, so the head reads as a flat plane from the front or the side. The sides are usually clipped very short.

entries.name: hairstyle_switch
entries.description: Two characters have swapped the hairstyles they normally wear. A single character borrowing somebody else's look takes [borrowed_hairstyle](#borrowed_hairstyle), and hair_length_switch is added when the length swaps too.

entries.name: single_drill
entries.description: One corkscrew curl worn as a [ponytail](#ponytail) or side [tail](#tail), where [twin_drills](#twin_drills) would have a matching pair. The rest of the hair is styled normally.

entries.name: tall_hair
entries.description: Hair built upward so it stands [well](#well) above the [crown](#crown), whether [spiked](#spiked), teased or piled high. About vertical [height](#height) rather than overall length.

entries.name: low_drills
entries.description: Hair that falls straight for most of its length and only coils into a [drill](#drill) toward the ends. Ringlets [running](#running) the whole way are [drill_hair](#drill_hair) instead.

entries.name: quiff
entries.description: Hair at the front is brushed up and [back](#back) off the [forehead](#forehead) into a [standing](#standing) wave. Best known as the [signature](#signature) look of a famous boy [reporter](#reporter), and also a [staple](#staple) of rockabilly styling.

entries.name: hairstyle_connection
entries.description: Two or more characters from unrelated series shown together because their hair is cut and styled almost identically. Colour may differ; the shape has to match.

entries.name: matching_hairstyle
entries.description: Two or more characters wearing their hair the same way, often to show kinship, a shared club or deliberate imitation. Only the style has to agree, and the colour may differ.

entries.name: crew_cut
entries.description: Hair clipped very short all over, left a [shade](#shade) longer on top and shaved close at the sides and [neck](#neck). Standard on soldiers and on schoolboys.

entries.name: comb_over
entries.description: Hair grown long at one side and swept across a [bald](#bald) or thinning [crown](#crown). Almost always on an older male character, and usually played for laughs.

entries.name: ahoge
entries.description: A single [lock](#lock) [standing](#standing) up from the top of the head, usually short and thick. One small and unstyled is a [cowlick](#cowlick), and two or more thin strands are [antenna_hair](#antenna_hair). Add [expressive_hair](#expressive_hair) where it bends with the character's mood.

entries.name: sidelocks
entries.description: Long strands of hair [hanging](#hanging) down just in front of the ears, framing the face. Extremely common in anime hairstyles; a lone strand on one side alone is [single_sidelock](#single_sidelock).

entries.name: antenna_hair
entries.description: Two or more thin locks [standing](#standing) up from the top of the head like a pair of feelers. A single upright strand is [ahoge](#ahoge) instead.

entries.name: hair_over_shoulder
entries.description: Long hair or a [ponytail](#ponytail) draped forward over one shoulder instead of [falling](#falling) down the [back](#back). Hair tied under the chin is [front_ponytail](#front_ponytail), braided there [front_braid](#front_braid).

entries.name: hair_flaps
entries.description: Tufts of hair sticking out from the sides of the head, often drawn moving expressively like ears. Familiar from remodeled Yuudachi and Shigure.

entries.name: tentacle_hair
entries.description: Hair made of moving [tentacles](#tentacles) rather than ordinary strands, seen on squid- or octopus-themed characters. It may or may not animate on its own; [prehensile_hair](#prehensile_hair) marks the cases where it does.

entries.name: hair_behind_ear
entries.description: A [lock](#lock) of hair tucked behind the ear to keep it off the face. The act of tucking it is hair_tucking.

entries.name: huge_ahoge
entries.description: An [ahoge](#ahoge) of absurd size, at least as [tall](#tall) or as long as the character's head. A strand of ordinary length is simply ahoge.

entries.name: long_sidelocks
entries.description: Locks framing the face at either side that reach the shoulders or further. Shorter ones take the [plain](#plain) [sidelocks](#sidelocks) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: heart_ahoge
entries.description: The stray [lock](#lock) [standing](#standing) up from the head bends into a [heart](#heart), expressive hair marking its owner as delighted or smitten. Several strands together making one is [heart_antenna_hair](#heart_antenna_hair).

entries.name: single_sidelock
entries.description: Only one [lock](#lock) of hair hangs in front of an ear, the other side bare. Often combined with [asymmetrical_hair](#asymmetrical_hair) or [asymmetrical_sidelocks](#asymmetrical_sidelocks).

entries.name: single_hair_intake
entries.description: A single scoop-shaped loop of hair over the head, instead of the paired loops of [hair_intakes](#hair_intakes).

entries.name: cowlick
entries.description: A stubborn [lock](#lock) that sticks straight out or lies against the run of the rest of the hair, often a whorl at the [crown](#crown) or hairline. Shorter and less deliberate than an [ahoge](#ahoge), though the two overlap.

entries.name: loose_hair_strand
entries.description: A single stray hair drawn out of place, rendered as one thin stroke apart from the rest. It is not for clumps, wedges, [ahoge](#ahoge) or [sidelocks](#sidelocks), which have tags of their own.

entries.name: drill_sidelocks
entries.description: The locks framing the face curled into drill-shaped [ringlets](#ringlets). Not to be mixed up with [side_drill](#side_drill).

entries.name: low-tied_sidelocks
entries.description: Sidelocks [bound](#bound) with a tie partway down or at their ends, so each hangs beside the face as a small [tail](#tail). The rest of the hair may be loose or styled quite separately.

entries.name: asymmetrical_sidelocks
entries.description: The strands [falling](#falling) in front of the ears are unequal, longer or thicker on one side than on the other. Add [asymmetrical_hair](#asymmetrical_hair) as [well](#well) when the rest of the style is lopsided too.

entries.name: blunt_tresses
entries.description: Sidelocks, [ringlets](#ringlets) or other separated locks trimmed off flat at the bottom, often [bound](#bound) with a tie so they hang like tassels. Not the same as [blunt_ends](#blunt_ends), which is about the straight-cut hair at the [back](#back).

entries.name: side_ahoge
entries.description: A stray strand of hair sticking out from the side of the head rather than the top. It reads as a natural [cowlick](#cowlick), unlike [one_side_up](#one_side_up), where a tuft is deliberately tied.

entries.name: blunt_sidelocks
entries.description: The locks framing the face finish in a flat level cut instead of tapering to a point. A [hime_cut](#hime_cut) has the same ends, but that whole combination is named by its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: lone_nape_hair
entries.description: One or more small tufts [standing](#standing) out at the [back](#back) of the [neck](#neck), shaped much like an [ahoge](#ahoge) or a [cowlick](#cowlick). They usually show once the rest of the hair is gathered into a [ponytail](#ponytail), bun or [twintails](#twintails).

entries.name: sidelocks_tied_back
entries.description: Long [sidelocks](#sidelocks) drawn [back](#back) and gathered into a bun or [ponytail](#ponytail) behind the head, drooping in a loose U-shape on either side rather than pulled taut. With only one sidelock tied back, use [asymmetrical_hair](#asymmetrical_hair) instead.

entries.name: detached_ahoge
entries.description: An [ahoge](#ahoge) drawn [floating](#floating) clear of the head instead of springing from the hair. A [comic](#comic) exaggeration of the usual stray strand.

entries.name: ahoge_wag
entries.description: The lone strand on top of the head swings from side to side like a dog's [tail](#tail). It gives the hair a will of its own and usually reads as excitement or delight.

entries.name: curly_sidelocks
entries.description: Sidelocks with a visible curl in them, softer and looser than [drill_hair](#drill_hair). Usually short and thin, though longer strands may curl only near the top.

entries.name: heart_antenna_hair
entries.description: Two strands [standing](#standing) up from the head curve toward each other and close into a [heart](#heart). A sweeter form of [plain](#plain) [antenna_hair](#antenna_hair).

entries.name: lightning_ahoge
entries.description: A single strand of hair [standing](#standing) up in a jagged bolt shape. It often works as expressive hair, spiking with shock or temper.

entries.name: hair_around_ear
entries.description: A [lock](#lock) braided or wound around the ear, or an ear [poking](#poking) out through a tied strand. A small styling detail rather than a whole hairstyle.

entries.name: wavy_sidelocks
entries.description: The strands framing the face fall in loose [waves](#waves) rather than [hanging](#hanging) straight. Describes the [sidelocks](#sidelocks) specifically, whatever the rest of the hair is doing.

entries.name: hair_tuft
entries.description: A small isolated clump of hair [standing](#standing) apart from the rest, softer and rounder than a spike. Often sits at the [crown](#crown) or beside the ears.

entries.name: wilted_ahoge
entries.description: The stray strand [standing](#standing) up from a character's head droops, bends, or curls to show they are tired, [sad](#sad), or dejected. It is expressive hair that shifts with mood rather than a fixed style.

entries.name: no_ahoge
entries.description: A character whose design includes a stray upright strand of hair is drawn without it, smoothing the [outline](#outline) of the head. When the strand is being pulled off in the picture, ahoge_removed fits instead.

entries.name: hair_between_eyes
entries.description: A [lock](#lock) of the fringe hangs down the middle of the [forehead](#forehead) far enough to reach between the eyes. Extremely common on anime characters.

entries.name: blunt_bangs
entries.description: The fringe is cut in one straight line right across the [forehead](#forehead). It cannot coexist with swept or asymmetrical bangs, and together with long hair and straight-cut [sidelocks](#sidelocks) it makes a [hime_cut](#hime_cut).

entries.name: hair_over_one_eye
entries.description: Hair covers one of the eyes, a look typical of [shy](#shy) or mysterious characters. Both eyes covered is [hair_over_eyes](#hair_over_eyes) instead.

entries.name: parted_bangs
entries.description: A fringe clearly [split](#split) into two sides, leaving the middle of the [forehead](#forehead) bare. One of the most common bang styles; a part along the [crown](#crown) of the head is [parted_hair](#parted_hair).

entries.name: swept_bangs
entries.description: A fringe brushed loosely to one side, without the crisp, defined parting line of parted bangs.

entries.name: eyes_visible_through_hair
entries.description: The eyes show through bangs that ought to [cover](#cover) them, as though the hair were [transparent](#transparent). A quirk of anime drawing, and it counts even when only the lashes come through.

entries.name: crossed_bangs
entries.description: Strands of the fringe [lying](#lying) over one another in a [cross](#cross) above the [forehead](#forehead). A way of drawing bangs, separate from [hair_between_eyes](#hair_between_eyes).

entries.name: double-parted_bangs
entries.description: Bangs parted at two separate points, generally one to each side of the [forehead](#forehead), leaving a [lock](#lock) [hanging](#hanging) between the gaps.

entries.name: asymmetrical_bangs
entries.description: The fringe is cut or combed so one side is short or swept [back](#back) while the other hangs long. Bangs uneven only because of a side part are [parted_bangs](#parted_bangs) or [swept_bangs](#swept_bangs).

entries.name: long_bangs
entries.description: A fringe grown long enough to hang past the eyes. It usually comes with [hair_over_eyes](#hair_over_eyes), [hair_over_one_eye](#hair_over_one_eye) or [hair_between_eyes](#hair_between_eyes).

entries.name: hair_over_eyes
entries.description: Long bangs hang over both eyes, [hiding](#hiding) them. When only one eye is covered use [hair_over_one_eye](#hair_over_one_eye) instead.

entries.name: long_hair_between_eyes
entries.description: A [lock](#lock) [hanging](#hanging) between the eyes that is unusually long, [reaching](#reaching) toward or past the mouth. It is the more pronounced form of [hair_between_eyes](#hair_between_eyes).

entries.name: diagonal_bangs
entries.description: A fringe cut along a slanted line, long at one side of the [forehead](#forehead) and growing shorter toward the other. A deliberately asymmetric cut.

entries.name: center-flap_bangs
entries.description: Blunt-ended fringe hair cut or combed away at both temples, leaving a distinct panel [hanging](#hanging) over the middle of the [forehead](#forehead). The look overlaps with [double-parted_bangs](#double-parted_bangs).

entries.name: choppy_bangs
entries.description: A fringe drawn noticeably thin, its strands roughly as wide as the gaps between them, so the [forehead](#forehead) shows through. A popular real-world Japanese style.

entries.name: wispy_bangs
entries.description: Bangs made of a few thin strands with wide gaps of visible skin between them, most common on male characters with medium-length fringe. Narrower gaps between the strands make it choppy bangs instead.

entries.name: sparse_bangs
entries.description: A thin fringe of separated strands over the [forehead](#forehead), letting skin show between them. Lighter than [blunt_bangs](#blunt_bangs) and less deliberate-looking than [parted_bangs](#parted_bangs).

entries.name: bangs_pinned_back
entries.description: The fringe is held off the [forehead](#forehead) by a clip, [pin](#pin), ornament or [hairband](#hairband), leaving the brow exposed. Compare [hair_slicked_back](#hair_slicked_back), where nothing holds the hair in place, and [hair_pulled_back](#hair_pulled_back), which draws [back](#back) the whole head of hair.

entries.name: short_bangs
entries.description: A fringe cut shorter than usual, exposing the [forehead](#forehead) and showing the whole of the eyebrows at minimum.

entries.name: arched_bangs
entries.description: The fringe cut or set so that it curves upward across the [forehead](#forehead) rather than [falling](#falling) straight. Blunt bangs seen from a low angle [can](#can) look like this, and should not be tagged so.

entries.name: cut_bangs
entries.description: A fringe with strands left uncut or trimmed to uneven lengths, [giving](#giving) a choppy edge either by intent or by [accident](#accident). The unevenness is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: side_part
entries.description: The hair is divided along a line [well](#well) to the left or right of center, leaving one side heavier and the other [lighter](#lighter). If the [split](#split) is visible from the roots, [parted_hair](#parted_hair) applies too; loosely combed side fringe is [swept_bangs](#swept_bangs) instead.

entries.name: fanged_bangs
entries.description: The fringe tapers into one or two long pointed strands at its outer edges, [reaching](#reaching) about eye level like a pair of [teeth](#teeth). Thinner than [sidelocks](#sidelocks) and clearly grown out of the bangs; one side alone is enough.

entries.name: hair_between_horns
entries.description: Forward-set [horns](#horns) with the fringe [sweeping](#sweeping) through the gap between them. Common on characters whose horns grow from the [forehead](#forehead), and often seen with centre-parted bangs.

entries.name: single_bang
entries.description: A lone strand of fringe [hanging](#hanging) down the [forehead](#forehead) while the rest of the hair is swept [back](#back). Often a narrow [lock](#lock) [falling](#falling) between or beside the eyes.

entries.name: flipped_bangs
entries.description: The front hair curls upward at the ends instead of [hanging](#hanging) flat over the [forehead](#forehead). It [can](#can) be combined with [flipped_hair](#flipped_hair) when the rest turns out as [well](#well).

entries.name: v-bangs
entries.description: A straight fringe that hangs longer at the centre than at the sides, tapering to a point over the [forehead](#forehead) in a V shape. A variation on blunt bangs.

entries.name: middle_part
entries.description: Hair divided down the center of the head so it falls evenly to both sides of the face, leaving the [forehead](#forehead) open.

entries.name: hair_behind_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) [sitting](#sitting) normally on the face, but with the frame [lying](#lying) in front of the fringe instead of the usual way round. Does not apply when the eyewear is pushed onto the head or merely glimpsed beneath the hair.

entries.name: sideless_bangs
entries.description: A fringe covering only the middle of the [forehead](#forehead) while the areas toward the temples are left uncovered, so the bangs read as a narrow central block. The sides fall in with the rest of the hair instead of framing the face.

entries.name: blonde_hair
entries.description: Hair in blonde or yellow, anywhere from pale platinum through to deep [gold](#gold). It is one of the most frequent hair colours in this style of art.

entries.name: black_hair
entries.description: Hair coloured black, by a wide margin the commonest hair colour in this vocabulary. Hair with a clear blue [cast](#cast) is [dark_blue_hair](#dark_blue_hair) and hair [leaning](#leaning) warm or brownish is [brown_hair](#brown_hair); only true black belongs here.

entries.name: brown_hair
entries.description: Hair coloured brown, [running](#running) from light [chestnut](#chestnut) to nearly black. Lighting pushes it up against the black, orange and red hair tags, so pick the colour the hair actually reads as.

entries.name: blue_hair
entries.description: Hair coloured blue, from pale [sky](#sky) tones down to navy. Lighting blurs it against [aqua_hair](#aqua_hair), so go by the dominant hue; a bluish black belongs to [dark_blue_hair](#dark_blue_hair) or [black_hair](#black_hair).

entries.name: pink_hair
entries.description: Hair coloured pink, magenta shades included. The boundary against [purple_hair](#purple_hair) and [red_hair](#red_hair) is a matter of judgement and lighting, so borderline cases overlap.

entries.name: multicolored_hair
entries.description: Hair [carrying](#carrying) more than one colour, whether as streaks, dyed tips, a gradient or a differently coloured inner layer. Tag each colour present as [well](#well).

entries.name: white_hair
entries.description: Hair colored white. Compare it against other white objects in the picture: if it looks darker or tinted, use [grey_hair](#grey_hair), [pink_hair](#pink_hair) or [purple_hair](#purple_hair) instead.

entries.name: grey_hair
entries.description: The character's hair is grey. Light blue, aqua and purple hair [can](#can) read the same way, and grey is also used to [shade](#shade) white hair: compare it with how white clothing in the picture is shaded, and if they match, [tag](#tag) [white_hair](#white_hair) instead.

entries.name: purple_hair
entries.description: Hair that is purple, lavender, or violet. Because [shade](#shade) judgement is subjective and lighting varies, borderline cases overlap with [blue_hair](#blue_hair), [pink_hair](#pink_hair), and light_purple_hair.

entries.name: red_hair
entries.description: Hair drawn in a true red, brighter than the auburn [shade](#shade) that real [people](#people) call red hair. Colour judgement is subjective and lighting shifts it, so the boundary with [orange_hair](#orange_hair) and [brown_hair](#brown_hair) is [blurry](#blurry).

entries.name: green_hair
entries.description: The character's hair is green. Since [shade](#shade) judgement is loose and lighting varies, [lighter](#lighter) bluish tones sit awkwardly between this and [aqua_hair](#aqua_hair).

entries.name: orange_hair
entries.description: Hair in orange. Depending on [shade](#shade) and lighting it borders on [blonde_hair](#blonde_hair), [brown_hair](#brown_hair) and [red_hair](#red_hair), so uncertain cases are settled by eye.

entries.name: streaked_hair
entries.description: Hair that is mostly one colour with one or several narrow streaks in another [shade](#shade). Use it for highlights; hair [split](#split) into large blocks of colour is [two-tone_hair](#two-tone_hair) instead.

entries.name: two-tone_hair
entries.description: Hair in two distinct colours. A sharp boundary is a [plain](#plain) [split](#split), while a blended one also earns [gradient_hair](#gradient_hair); a vertical left-right divide adds [split-color_hair](#split-color_hair).

entries.name: gradient_hair
entries.description: Hair [fading](#fading) gradually from one colour into another, most often paling or changing hue toward the tips. Tag every colour in the blend that [can](#can) be told apart.

entries.name: aqua_hair
entries.description: Blue-green hair. Colour perception and lighting make it [shade](#shade) into [blue_hair](#blue_hair) and [green_hair](#green_hair), so borderline cases [can](#can) go either way.

entries.name: colored_inner_hair
entries.description: The under layer of the hair is a different colour from the outer, showing wherever inner strands fall into view. Where each layer is one flat colour it is also [two-tone_hair](#two-tone_hair).

entries.name: light_blue_hair
entries.description: A pale [sky](#sky) or electric [shade](#shade) of blue hair, which [can](#can) read as silver under some lighting. Greenish turquoise shades are [aqua_hair](#aqua_hair) instead.

entries.name: split-color_hair
entries.description: Hair divided down the middle into two distinct colours, one to each side, rather than blended or streaked. The halves need not be equal in size but must read clearly as two separate colours.

entries.name: dark_blue_hair
entries.description: Hair in a blue plainly deeper than the standard bright [shade](#shade), navy or close to it. Where [no](#no) blue [can](#can) be made out at all, [black_hair](#black_hair) is the correct [tag](#tag).

entries.name: colored_tips
entries.description: The hair changes colour abruptly at the very ends, as with a dip dye. A gradual blend from root to tip is [gradient_hair](#gradient_hair) instead.

entries.name: white_streaks
entries.description: Narrow streaks of white [running](#running) through hair of a darker base colour, whether dyed, natural, or a [sign](#sign) of age. Only part of the head is affected, unlike hair that is entirely white.

entries.name: red_streaks
entries.description: Hair [carrying](#carrying) bands of red through a differently coloured base, [running](#running) the length of the strands. Differs from an evenly two-tone head, where the colours [split](#split) into solid blocks.

entries.name: roots_(hair)
entries.description: Hair whose roots at the scalp differ in colour from the rest, visible at the parting. Reads as either grown-out dye or a deliberate style, most often [dark](#dark) roots under blonde hair.

entries.name: blue_streaks
entries.description: Bands of blue [running](#running) through hair that is otherwise another colour. It marks visible streaks rather than a head dyed blue throughout.

entries.name: pink_streaks
entries.description: Bands of pink [running](#running) through hair of another base colour, drawn as distinct sections rather than a blend. The base [shade](#shade) still leads and takes its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: dyed_bangs
entries.description: The fringe carries a colour the hair behind it does not, and all of the fringe is that colour. A few thin streaks of another [shade](#shade) inside it are fine, but partly coloured bangs, a [crown](#crown) [sharing](#sharing) the colour, or bangs you cannot fully see do not qualify.

entries.name: yellow_hair
entries.description: Hair of a [saturated](#saturated) yellow, brighter and flatter than natural blonde. Where the hair reads as a real fair [shade](#shade), [blonde_hair](#blonde_hair) is the [tag](#tag) to use instead.

entries.name: rainbow_hair
entries.description: Hair colored across the whole spectrum, usually [blending](#blending) from red through violet as a gradient or in bands. A mere two or three colors together is not enough for this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: striped_hair
entries.description: Hair [carrying](#carrying) bands of a second colour [running](#running) through it, drawn as distinct stripes rather than a smooth gradient or a single dyed streak.

entries.name: hair_color_connection
entries.description: Three or more characters grouped together because they share the same hair colour, as the point of the picture. Characters [sharing](#sharing) a hairstyle instead take [hairstyle_connection](#hairstyle_connection).

entries.name: single_hair_streak
entries.description: One [lock](#lock) in a color different from the rest of the head. Usually placed in the fringe or beside the face where it reads clearly.

entries.name: green_streaks
entries.description: Streaked hair in which the added strands are green over a base of another colour. The streaks may be a few strands or a broad band.

entries.name: patterned_hair
entries.description: Hair [carrying](#carrying) a design that real hair could never hold, stars or checks [sitting](#sitting) on the strands as if painted there. Gradients and streaks are physically possible and belong to [gradient_hair](#gradient_hair) or [streaked_hair](#streaked_hair).

entries.name: dyed_ahoge
entries.description: The stray strand [standing](#standing) up from the head is coloured differently from the hair it grows out of. The second colour has to [cover](#cover) most of the strand; only the end differing is [colored_tips](#colored_tips), and a colour that turns up elsewhere in the hair is [two-tone_hair](#two-tone_hair).

entries.name: spotted_hair
entries.description: Hair [patterned](#patterned) with rounded patches of a second colour rather than streaks or a smooth gradient. Mostly seen on characters whose [animal](#animal) [coat](#coat) [markings](#markings) carry up into their hair.

entries.name: polka_dot_hair
entries.description: Hair marked with round [spots](#spots) in a second colour, an unnatural pattern seen on cartoon animals and stylised designs. Treated as a colouring quirk rather than as an ornament.

entries.name: orange_highlights
entries.description: Orange streaks [running](#running) through hair of a different base colour. The main [shade](#shade) keeps its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: yellow_highlights
entries.description: Yellow streaks [running](#running) through hair of another base colour.

entries.name: brown_highlights
entries.description: Brown streaks run through hair of a different base colour. The main colour keeps its own [tag](#tag) alongside this one.

entries.name: grey_highlights
entries.description: Grey strands worked through hair of another base colour. The dominant colour keeps its own [tag](#tag) alongside this one.

entries.name: floating_hair
entries.description: Hair lifted by [wind](#wind) or [drifting](#drifting) in the air rather than [falling](#falling). It does not [cover](#cover) hair that is merely [messy](#messy) or styled to defy gravity, and hair laid over a surface, hair fanned out on one, and hair magically detached from the head each have tags of their own.

entries.name: wavy_hair
entries.description: Hair [falling](#falling) in gentle [waves](#waves) rather than [lying](#lying) straight or coiling into tight curls. Tighter spirals belong to [curly_hair](#curly_hair) instead.

entries.name: straight_hair
entries.description: Hair that falls straight from root to tip, with [no](#no) [waves](#waves), curls or kinks anywhere along its length. The default hair texture against which [wavy_hair](#wavy_hair) and [curly_hair](#curly_hair) stand out as the exceptions.

entries.name: messy_hair
entries.description: Unkempt, tousled hair from poor grooming or from just having gotten out of [bed](#bed). Often paired with waking-up scenes.

entries.name: curly_hair
entries.description: Hair with natural-looking coils, whether the character was born with it or permed it. Tight [ringlets](#ringlets) are [drill_hair](#drill_hair), and looser undulations are [wavy_hair](#wavy_hair).

entries.name: waving_hair
entries.description: Hair lifted and rippling in long curves as though [caught](#caught) in a breeze or trailing behind a moving [figure](#figure). It describes motion, not a permanent wave in the strands.

entries.name: hair_down
entries.description: A character who usually wears their hair up, in a [ponytail](#ponytail) or bun, is shown with it loose. For a short-haired character drawn with longer hair use [alternate_hair_length](#alternate_hair_length) instead.

entries.name: hair_spread_out
entries.description: Long hair fanned out across a surface by gravity, typically under a girl [lying](#lying) on her [back](#back) or trailing on the [floor](#floor) from absurdly long hair.

entries.name: wet_hair
entries.description: Hair soaked and [hanging](#hanging) in [dripping](#dripping) strands, as after a [bath](#bath), a [rain](#rain) shower or a swim.

entries.name: hair_slicked_back
entries.description: Hair combed [back](#back) from the face and held with mousse or pomade. Hair merely tied back is [hair_pulled_back](#hair_pulled_back); only the fringe held back is [bangs_pinned_back](#bangs_pinned_back).

entries.name: hair_up
entries.description: A character who usually wears their hair loose has it [pinned](#pinned) or tied up instead, as a bun, [folded](#folded) [ponytail](#ponytail) or similar. Tag it for the change from the usual look, not for every [updo](#updo) in general.

entries.name: big_hair
entries.description: Hair with unusual bulk, puffing outward or piling up [well](#well) beyond the [outline](#outline) of the head. It describes volume rather than length, so it sits happily beside any length [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hair_pulled_back
entries.description: Hair drawn [back](#back) off the face into a [ponytail](#ponytail) or bun, exposing the [forehead](#forehead). Hair fixed back with product is [hair_slicked_back](#hair_slicked_back); only the fringe [pinned](#pinned) back is [bangs_pinned_back](#bangs_pinned_back).

entries.name: ringlets
entries.description: Hair curled into [hanging](#hanging) cylindrical coils. Not [drill_hair](#drill_hair), whose curls taper into cones rather than staying tube-shaped.

entries.name: hair_flowing_over
entries.description: Long hair draped over an object or uneven surface so it follows the shape, showing believable hair physics. Hair blown by [wind](#wind) is [floating_hair](#floating_hair); hair fanned across a flat surface is [hair_spread_out](#hair_spread_out).

entries.name: enpera
entries.description: Hair puffing out above a [scarf](#scarf), a high [collar](#collar), or [headphones](#headphones) worn round the [neck](#neck). The name comes from a squid's fin, which the shape resembles. A winter-clothing look.

entries.name: spread_out_hair
entries.description: Long hair fanned out across a [pillow](#pillow), the ground or the surface of [water](#water), usually seen from directly above a character [lying](#lying) down.

entries.name: fiery_hair
entries.description: Hair that is made of [fire](#fire) or drawn as [burning](#burning) flame. Common on fire-elemental characters; a flame only at the tips belongs to another [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hair_through_headwear
entries.description: Locks of hair pass through a [hat](#hat), [hood](#hood) or other headwear, sometimes through holes drawn for the purpose, such as a [ponytail](#ponytail) out the [back](#back) of a cap.

entries.name: prehensile_hair
entries.description: Hair that moves and grips by its owner's will, forming hands, [tentacles](#tentacles) or limbs. Hair that merely reacts to emotion, drooping or perking, is [expressive_hair](#expressive_hair) instead.

entries.name: fluffy_hair
entries.description: Hair drawn soft and voluminous, puffing outward around the head instead of [lying](#lying) flat. It is a texture trait, separate from [messy_hair](#messy_hair) and from [curly_hair](#curly_hair).

entries.name: expressive_hair
entries.description: Hair that moves with the feeling: [flapping](#flapping) when [excited](#excited), drooping when downcast, an [ahoge](#ahoge) [bending](#bending) into a [heart](#heart). Hair used as a limb, tool or [weapon](#weapon) is [prehensile_hair](#prehensile_hair).

entries.name: crystal_hair
entries.description: Hair made of gemlike [crystal](#crystal), or drawn with a hard faceted texture. Belongs to [gem](#gem) beings and similar [fantasy](#fantasy) designs.

entries.name: glowing_hair
entries.description: Hair that emits light of its own, frequently [throwing](#throwing) that light onto the face or the surroundings. It marks magical power, an [energy](#energy) form or another supernatural state.

entries.name: liquid_hair
entries.description: Hair drawn as flowing [water](#water) or another fluid rather than as strands, common on water spirits and bottle-themed designs.

entries.name: detached_hair
entries.description: Hair wholly or partly separated from the head it belongs to, [drifting](#drifting) beside its owner. Nearly always a [comic](#comic) effect rather than an [injury](#injury).

entries.name: hair_vines
entries.description: Creepers and [climbing](#climbing) plants growing in place of hair, sometimes flowering. Seen on dryads, [plant](#plant) girls and other [overgrown](#overgrown) creatures.

entries.name: kishimen_hair
entries.description: Hair drawn as a mass of thin, flat, ribbon-like strands, named after a flat [wheat](#wheat) noodle. It describes how the hair is rendered rather than how it is cut.

entries.name: starry_hair
entries.description: Hair that holds stars or a starry-sky pattern within it, often on the inner layer. A fantastical hair effect.

entries.name: hair_over_face
entries.description: Hair hangs down and obscures a good part of the face, roughly a third or more of it. If only the eyes vanish behind it use [hair_over_eyes](#hair_over_eyes) instead.

entries.name: hair_floating_upwards
entries.description: Hair lifting and streaming up away from the head as though gravity had let go. Used [underwater](#underwater), during bursts of power and in dramatic falls.

entries.name: plant_hair
entries.description: Hair made of leaves, [vines](#vines), or [petals](#petals) in place of ordinary strands. Common on dryads, [flower](#flower) spirits, and other plant-bodied characters.

entries.name: severed_hair
entries.description: Cut hair drawn as a thing in its own right, [no](#no) longer growing from anyone's head. Can be one [drifting](#drifting) strand or a whole shorn [lock](#lock) on the ground.

entries.name: unkempt
entries.description: Hair left without any care taken over it: not tangled enough to call truly [messy](#messy), but plainly unbrushed and unarranged. Often paired with exhaustion, nervousness or fright.

entries.name: living_hair
entries.description: Hair that behaves as though alive, coiling, [rearing](#rearing) or striking like a [nest](#nest) of snakes. It is often prehensile enough to grip objects or hold somebody fast.

entries.name: hair_through_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) pulled up with hair [spilling](#spilling) out of it, whether through an [opening](#opening), past the edge, or bunched free at the [back](#back). Common with long ponytails and with [animal](#animal) ears.

entries.name: translucent_hair
entries.description: Hair drawn so that things behind it show faintly through the strands themselves, a stylistic [choice](#choice) often used for [glowing](#glowing) or ethereal characters. Seeing background between separate locks does not count, and eyes showing through the bangs get their own [tag](#tag), [eyes_visible_through_hair](#eyes_visible_through_hair).

entries.name: impossible_hair
entries.description: Hair that ignores gravity: buns too [heavy](#heavy) for any [neck](#neck), long hair that stays put while the character hangs upside down, [shapes](#shapes) [no](#no) styling could hold. Physics rather than length is the point.

entries.name: hair_over_mouth
entries.description: A fall of hair [lying](#lying) across the [lips](#lips) and lower face while the eyes stay clear. A narrower case than hair covering the whole face.

entries.name: hair_branch
entries.description: Hair that grows as, or is shaped into, [tree](#tree) branches, sometimes sprouting leaves and twigs. Typical of [nature](#nature) spirits and plant-themed designs.

entries.name: hair_scarf
entries.description: A very long [braid](#braid) or [mane](#mane) wound about the [neck](#neck) and shoulders the way a [scarf](#scarf) would be. The hair is [standing](#standing) in for a garment.

entries.name: hair_undone
entries.description: Hair that has just come loose, with the [ribbon](#ribbon) or tie visibly [slipping](#slipping) away. Captures that moment rather than the settled state covered by [hair_down](#hair_down).

entries.name: cloud_hair
entries.description: Hair drawn as [cloud](#cloud), either literally made of vapour or shaped into soft billowing puffs. A common design [choice](#choice) for [sky](#sky), weather and dream themed characters.

entries.name: food-themed_hair
entries.description: Hair that is literally made of [food](#food), styled out of [noodles](#noodles), [cream](#cream), [fruit](#fruit) or the like. Hair merely coloured or decorated to suggest a food does not count.

entries.name: lion_hair
entries.description: Hair drawn as a thick shaggy mass framing the whole head, echoing a lion's [mane](#mane) without the character actually being one.

entries.name: wavy_ends
entries.description: Hair that falls straight for most of its length and breaks into loose [waves](#waves) only at the tips. A gentler look than hair that's wavy throughout.

entries.name: cable_hair
entries.description: Hair formed from cables or wires rather than strands, [hanging](#hanging) in thick insulated lengths. A design cue for androids, robots and [mecha](#mecha).

entries.name: hair_wagging
entries.description: A length of hair [swinging](#swinging) [back](#back) and forth the way a [happy](#happy) [tail](#tail) would. A cartoon [device](#device) for showing eagerness or delight.

entries.name: hair_in_another's_mouth
entries.description: A strand of one character's hair ends up between somebody else's [lips](#lips) or [teeth](#teeth). Turns up in close embraces and in scenes of [biting](#biting) or [pulling](#pulling).

entries.name: blue_eyes
entries.description: Irises coloured blue, among the most frequent eye colours in this style of art. Lighting and shading blur it against [aqua_eyes](#aqua_eyes), so [judge](#judge) by whichever hue dominates.

entries.name: red_eyes
entries.description: The irises are red. Colour judgement and lighting cause overlap with [orange_eyes](#orange_eyes) and [brown_eyes](#brown_eyes); eyes reddened by irritation or [crying](#crying) are [bloodshot_eyes](#bloodshot_eyes) instead.

entries.name: green_eyes
entries.description: The character's irises are green. Because [shade](#shade) judgement is subjective and lighting shifts it further, there is real overlap with [aqua_eyes](#aqua_eyes); choose whichever reads closer.

entries.name: brown_eyes
entries.description: Eyes coloured brown, taking in light hazel through to deep [chocolate](#chocolate). Lighting and shading make it overlap with the black, orange and red eye colours, so go by what the eyes read as.

entries.name: purple_eyes
entries.description: The character's irises are purple or violet. Because [shade](#shade) judgement is subjective and lighting varies, borderline cases overlap with [blue_eyes](#blue_eyes) and [pink_eyes](#pink_eyes).

entries.name: yellow_eyes
entries.description: Irises in yellow, [gold](#gold), amber or hazel. Lighting and colour judgement blur the line with [orange_eyes](#orange_eyes), so the two overlap; yellow pupils or a yellow sclera have their own separate tags.

entries.name: pink_eyes
entries.description: A character whose irises are pink. Because [shade](#shade) and lighting are judged by eye, the [tag](#tag) overlaps with [purple_eyes](#purple_eyes) and [red_eyes](#red_eyes) at the edges.

entries.name: black_eyes
entries.description: Irises coloured black, or so [dark](#dark) that they read as black. A bruised eye is [bruised_eye](#bruised_eye), and irises that melt into the pupil as one flat dot are [solid_circle_pupils](#solid_circle_pupils).

entries.name: grey_eyes
entries.description: The character's irises are grey or silver. Depending on lighting and shading the [shade](#shade) [can](#can) overlap with [black_eyes](#black_eyes) or [white_eyes](#white_eyes).

entries.name: aqua_eyes
entries.description: Blue-green eyes. Because colour judgement is subjective and lighting shifts the [reading](#reading), this overlaps heavily with [blue_eyes](#blue_eyes) and [green_eyes](#green_eyes).

entries.name: orange_eyes
entries.description: A character whose irises are orange. Shade and lighting put it close to [yellow_eyes](#yellow_eyes), [red_eyes](#red_eyes) and [brown_eyes](#brown_eyes), so borderline cases come down to judgement.

entries.name: heterochromia
entries.description: The two eyes have irises of different colours. Tag each colour as [well](#well); when a single iris holds more than one colour the [tag](#tag) is [multicolored_eyes](#multicolored_eyes) instead.

entries.name: multicolored_eyes
entries.description: More than one colour inside a single iris, as with gradient eyes. Two eyes that differ from each other in colour are [heterochromia](#heterochromia) instead.

entries.name: white_eyes
entries.description: Irises colored white, which overlaps with [grey_eyes](#grey_eyes) depending on the lighting. Eyes that are solid white with [no](#no) visible iris at all are [blank_eyes](#blank_eyes) instead.

entries.name: two-tone_eyes
entries.description: Each eye holds two clearly distinct colours, for instance a [ring](#ring) of one [shade](#shade) around a pupil area of another. If the shades blend smoothly it is [gradient_eyes](#gradient_eyes) instead, and different colours in each separate eye is [heterochromia](#heterochromia).

entries.name: gradient_eyes
entries.description: Irises whose colour blends smoothly from one hue into another, blue [melting](#melting) into pink at the bottom for instance. A form of [multicolored_eyes](#multicolored_eyes); [tag](#tag) each colour that shows.

entries.name: rainbow_eyes
entries.description: Irises [carrying](#carrying) several spectrum colors at once, either as concentric rings or blended across the eye. Distinct from [heterochromia](#heterochromia), where each eye is instead a single different color.

entries.name: no_heterochromia
entries.description: A character famous for mismatched eyes is given two of the same colour. Swapping the two usual colours between the eyes counts as [well](#well); replacing the pupils entirely does not.

entries.name: pale_eye
entries.description: An eye drawn in a washed-out, nearly colourless [shade](#shade), the iris barely separable from the white around it. Often a [sign](#sign) of blindness, possession or something not quite human.

entries.name: symbol-shaped_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn as a symbol or small object, such as hearts, stars or dollar signs, while the rest of the eye looks otherwise ordinary. Eyes replaced entirely by a symbol do not count, and [writing](#writing) in the pupil is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: heart-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as hearts inside otherwise ordinary eyes, marking infatuation or sexual pleasure. Whole eyes drawn as hearts are [heart-shaped_eyes](#heart-shaped_eyes); a [heart](#heart) [floating](#floating) on the iris is [heart_in_eye](#heart_in_eye).

entries.name: bright_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn [lighter](#lighter) than the iris around them, so the eye reads inverted. It is a stylistic [choice](#choice) rather than an anatomical one; where the pupils are pure white, add [white_pupils](#white_pupils).

entries.name: slit_pupils
entries.description: Pupils stretched into a vertical or horizontal slit, as in cats, snakes and goats, and on dragons, vampires and demons. Sharp [tsurime](#tsurime) eyes with small pupils do not count.

entries.name: white_pupils
entries.description: The pupil itself is white rather than the usual [dark](#dark) dot, [giving](#giving) the eye a [glowing](#glowing) or hollow look. Frequently seen on drawn masks, spirits and stylized characters; a colored iris around it is tagged separately.

entries.name: colored_sclera
entries.description: The white of the eye is drawn in another colour, commonly black, red or yellow. A frequent mark of demons, monsters and [possessed](#possessed) characters.

entries.name: glowing_eyes
entries.description: Both eyes [shining](#shining) brighter than [nature](#nature) allows, whether as a permanent trait of the character, a [sign](#sign) that a power is being used, or a [comic](#comic) cue that they are about to pounce. A single lit eye is [glowing_eye](#glowing_eye).

entries.name: empty_eyes
entries.description: Eyes with [no](#no) highlight or [glint](#glint), filled with flat, dull colour. Used for a blank stare, numbness, rage, madness, mind control, blindness, unconsciousness or [death](#death). Also called dead eyes.

entries.name: black_sclera
entries.description: The whites of the eyes are filled black rather than white, a look reserved for demons, monsters and corrupted characters. Only that surrounding area is described, so the iris colour is tagged separately.

entries.name: o_o
entries.description: Eyes rendered as flat white discs ringed in thick black, a shorthand for startled [staring](#staring). Filled in black they are [solid_circle_eyes](#solid_circle_eyes), and [blank_eyes](#blank_eyes) does not apply here.

entries.name: ringed_eyes
entries.description: Eyes whose iris and pupil are drawn as concentric rings. A few rings [can](#can) be a simple stylistic [choice](#choice); many rings usually give a crazed or hypnotised look.

entries.name: star-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils themselves are drawn as stars. A star merely drawn inside an otherwise ordinary eye is [star_in_eye](#star_in_eye), and this should not be [confused](#confused) with cross- or diamond-shaped pupils.

entries.name: symbol_in_eye
entries.description: A symbol placed somewhere in the eye other than the pupil itself, such as a [flower](#flower) in the iris or a highlight shaped like a star. Kept separate from [symbol-shaped_pupils](#symbol-shaped_pupils).

entries.name: eyeball
entries.description: Eyeballs with a presence of their own: [floating](#floating), held in a hand, scattered on the ground, set into clothing or into a [forehead](#forehead). Use it where the eye is an object or a motif rather than an ordinary part of a face.

entries.name: no_pupils
entries.description: Eyes drawn without pupils, leaving a [plain](#plain) iris or a blank surface. It suits [possessed](#possessed), [dazed](#dazed) or otherworldly characters.

entries.name: constricted_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn far smaller than usual, sometimes as tiny [dots](#dots), from terror, shock, madness or [glaring](#glaring) light. A [staple](#staple) of horror scenes and unhinged [expressions](#expressions).

entries.name: red_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn in red instead of black. Distinct from [red_eyes](#red_eyes), where the iris is red, and from [red_sclera](#red_sclera), where the white of the eye is red.

entries.name: yellow_sclera
entries.description: The normally white part of the eye is yellow, a look for demons, monsters, cats and sickly characters. Tag [colored_sclera](#colored_sclera) as [well](#well); the iris colour is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: glowing_eye
entries.description: A single eye radiating light, usually from a power in use, a cybernetic replacement or a supernatural cause. When both eyes glow, use [glowing_eyes](#glowing_eyes).

entries.name: sparkling_eyes
entries.description: Star-shaped glints drawn inside the eyes next to the pupil, conveying excitement, wonder, or delight. The pupils themselves keep their ordinary shape.

entries.name: blank_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn with neither iris nor pupil, leaving only the sclera. Shock, possession, blindness and stylised designs all use it; [empty_eyes](#empty_eyes) covers dull eyes that still have irises.

entries.name: cross-shaped_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn as a plus or a [dagger](#dagger) shape and belonging to the character by default. Distinct from the + + of eyes [shining](#shining) with excitement and the [x](#x) x of dead eyes, both of which are momentary [expressions](#expressions).

entries.name: solid_oval_eyes
entries.description: Eyes rendered as [plain](#plain) black ovals with [no](#no) inner detail, a common shorthand in [chibi](#chibi) and simplified character designs.

entries.name: diamond-shaped_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn as diamonds or rhombuses instead of round [dots](#dots) or slits. Not to be [confused](#confused) with [star-shaped_pupils](#star-shaped_pupils) or [cross-shaped_pupils](#cross-shaped_pupils), which are their own tags.

entries.name: mismatched_pupils
entries.description: Pupils of different [shapes](#shapes) or colors in each eye, often one drawn as a symbol shape beside an ordinary one.

entries.name: no_eyes
entries.description: The eyes are missing, [buried](#buried) under hair, or lost in [shadow](#shadow) for dramatic effect, and sometimes simply never drawn. Empty sockets are [hollow_eyes](#hollow_eyes).

entries.name: star_in_eye
entries.description: A star shape drawn inside the eye while the pupil keeps its own separate shape. When the pupil itself becomes the star, use [star-shaped_pupils](#star-shaped_pupils) instead.

entries.name: heart_in_eye
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) is drawn inside the eye, on the iris, while the pupil keeps its ordinary shape. Where the pupil itself is the heart, use [heart-shaped_pupils](#heart-shaped_pupils).

entries.name: solid_circle_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn as [plain](#plain) filled circles, black or another flat color, typical of [chibi](#chibi) faces. Oval versions are [solid_oval_eyes](#solid_oval_eyes), and solid white circles are [o_o](#o_o) instead.

entries.name: flower-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as the [outline](#outline) of a [flower](#flower). Not [flower_in_eye](#flower_in_eye), where a flower pattern covers the iris instead.

entries.name: red_sclera
entries.description: The white of the eye drawn red, a mark of demons, possession or monstrous designs. Not [red_eyes](#red_eyes), where the iris is red, and not [red_pupils](#red_pupils), where the pupil is red.

entries.name: pink_pupils
