entries.description: The pupils are drawn pink rather than black. The iris colour is recorded separately, so this often sits beside a different eye colour.

entries.name: yellow_pupils
entries.description: The pupils themselves are yellow. Different from [yellow_eyes](#yellow_eyes), which refers to the iris, and from [yellow_sclera](#yellow_sclera), where the white of the eye is yellow.

entries.name: blue_pupils
entries.description: The pupil at the centre of the eye is blue instead of black, often set against an iris of another colour. Record the iris colour with its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: horizontal_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are wide horizontal [bars](#bars) or rectangles instead of round [dots](#dots), as in goats, [sheep](#sheep), horses, octopuses and some frogs. Animal-themed characters and demons wear them most.

entries.name: x-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as X [shapes](#shapes), a stylized look for mischievous or unusual characters. Distinct from the closed [x_x](#x_x) eyes or plus-shaped pupils; [tag](#tag) [symbol-shaped_pupils](#symbol-shaped_pupils) alongside.

entries.name: flaming_eye
entries.description: One eye gives off [fire](#fire), flame rising from the socket. Add [eye_trail](#eye_trail) where the fire draws out behind the character; both eyes alight is [flaming_eyes](#flaming_eyes).

entries.name: solid_eyes
entries.description: Eyes filled entirely with one flat color, with [no](#no) separate iris, pupil, or sclera drawn in. Reserve it for a colored fill; a white fill is [blank_eyes](#blank_eyes) instead.

entries.name: blue_sclera
entries.description: The white of the eye is blue, so the whole [eyeball](#eyeball) reads as coloured. Frequent on demons, machines and heavily stylised designs, and it pairs with almost any iris colour.

entries.name: drop-shaped_pupils
entries.description: Pupils shaped like a [falling](#falling) drop of [liquid](#liquid), narrow at the top and round below. One of the symbol-shaped pupil designs.

entries.name: no_sclera
entries.description: Eyes with [no](#no) white part, so the pupils sit directly on skin-coloured or darkened eye areas. It gives a blank, inhuman look to the face.

Both eyes are reduced to a pair of small [dots](#dots), a shorthand seen on [chibi](#chibi) figures and blank reactions. Where the eyes are large enough to read as filled circles or ovals, [solid_circle_eyes](#solid_circle_eyes) or [solid_oval_eyes](#solid_oval_eyes) fit better.

entries.name: power_symbol-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils take the shape of the power on/off icon, a [circle](#circle) [broken](#broken) by a vertical stroke. Tag [symbol-shaped_pupils](#symbol-shaped_pupils) with it.

entries.name: rabbit-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as tiny [rabbit](#rabbit) silhouettes, a playful design touch often seen on rabbit-themed characters. Combine with [symbol-shaped_pupils](#symbol-shaped_pupils).

entries.name: hollow_eyes
entries.description: The eyes are drawn as [dark](#dark) empty voids with [no](#no) iris and no highlight, as though the sockets held nothing. Ghosts, the [possessed](#possessed) and characters in shock wear them most.

entries.name: green_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are green instead of the usual black. This is separate from [green_eyes](#green_eyes), where the colour belongs to the iris.

entries.name: cephalopod_eyes
entries.description: Pupils drawn as a horizontal [figure](#figure) eight or [dumbbell](#dumbbell), the shape an [octopus](#octopus) or [squid](#squid) has. Faint versions look much like horizontal rectangles, and [horizontal_pupils](#horizontal_pupils) or [slit_pupils](#slit_pupils) may describe those better.

entries.name: purple_pupils
entries.description: The pupils themselves are purple rather than black, a stylistic or supernatural detail. Combine with an iris colour [tag](#tag) such as [purple_eyes](#purple_eyes) when both apply.

entries.name: green_sclera
entries.description: The eye's white is drawn green instead. It is a [familiar](#familiar) look on monsters, demons and [possessed](#possessed) characters, and it leaves the iris colour free to be tagged on its own.

entries.name: white_sclera
entries.description: The whites of the eyes drawn as [plain](#plain) white rather than black or another colour. It mainly gets noted on non-human characters, where a default sclera colour cannot be assumed.

entries.name: flower_in_eye
entries.description: A blossom design sits inside the iris itself, patterning the coloured part of the eye. Keep it apart from flower-shaped pupils, where only the pupil takes that form.

entries.name: square_pupils
entries.description: Pupils shaped as squares rather than circles or slits, often marking a constructed or otherwise non-human character.

entries.name: mismatched_sclera
entries.description: The whites of the eyes colored differently in each eye - one white and one black sclera, say, with matching irises. Kaneki Ken's ghoul eye from Tokyo Ghoul is the well-known example.

entries.name: solid_circle_pupils
entries.description: Wide, round eyes with large solid black pupils, the classic look conveying shock, an unsettling stare, or [wide-eyed](#wide-eyed) wonder.

entries.name: grey_sclera
entries.description: The eye's white is grey rather than white, which darkens the whole look of the gaze. It is common on [undead](#undead), corrupted and non-human characters.

entries.name: wavy_eyes
entries.description: Eyes outlined with a wobbly, wavy line instead of a smooth curve, signalling sadness, pleading or a puppy-dog appeal. Sometimes it's simply part of an artist's style.

Almond-shaped eyes [split](#split) by an upright slit, an [emoticon](#emoticon) that stands in for a cat's gaze. It differs from [slit_pupils](#slit_pupils), which sits inside an ordinarily drawn eye.

entries.name: dashed_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn as a single struck-through line or dash, most often signalling overwhelming pleasure. A stylised mark rather than a statement about eye shape or colour.

entries.name: butterfly-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as butterflies rather than round [dots](#dots). One of the symbol-shaped pupil variants, used for a whimsical or enchanted look.

entries.name: orange_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn orange rather than the usual black, often against an iris of another colour. A design touch common on non-human and supernatural characters.

entries.name: bloodshot_eyes
entries.description: Whites of the eyes reddened with visible [veins](#veins), from irritation, exhaustion, weeping or fury. Red_eyes describes the iris and is a different thing entirely.

entries.name: eye_reflection
entries.description: Something in the scene shows up mirrored in a character's eyes: another person, a [screen](#screen), a flame. Used where the [reflection](#reflection) is clearly drawn in rather than merely a highlight.

entries.name: heart-shaped_eyes
entries.description: The eyes themselves are drawn as hearts, cartoon-fashion, marking a character as [lovestruck](#lovestruck). Hearts [sitting](#sitting) inside otherwise normal eyes belong to [heart_in_eye](#heart_in_eye), or to [heart-shaped_pupils](#heart-shaped_pupils) where the pupil is the [heart](#heart).

entries.name: clock_eyes
entries.description: Pupils drawn as [clock](#clock) faces, complete with hands or numerals. A common design cue for characters [bound](#bound) up with time or with [hypnosis](#hypnosis).

entries.name: pink_sclera
entries.description: The white of the eye rendered pink, so the whole [eyeball](#eyeball) reads as coloured. Not for bloodshot eyes, where red [veins](#veins) show against white.

entries.name: wide_oval_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn as flat white ovals stretched [sideways](#sideways), a shorthand for shock most common in [chibi](#chibi) art and [gag](#gag) panels. A version filled with solid colour instead is [solid_oval_eyes](#solid_oval_eyes).

entries.name: purple_sclera
entries.description: The part of the eye that would ordinarily be white is instead rendered purple. Common on demons, monsters, and corrupted characters, and separate from the iris colour.

entries.name: extra_pupils
entries.description: More than one pupil inside a single eye, whether a tidy pair or a scatter of them. A design cue for [possessed](#possessed), eldritch or otherwise inhuman characters.

entries.name: orange_sclera
entries.description: The part of the eye that is usually white is orange instead, framing the iris. A quick way of marking demons, monsters and corrupted characters.

entries.name: triangle-shaped_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn as triangles rather than round or slit [shapes](#shapes), [pointing](#pointing) up, down or to the side. One of several symbol-shaped pupil variants used to mark inhuman or stylised eyes.

entries.name: crosshair_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn as targeting reticles, lines [running](#running) through them instead of a [plain](#plain) round shape. Signals a sharpshooter, or a targeting system coming online.

entries.name: flaming_eyes
entries.description: Fire pours from both eyes or licks up around them, [standing](#standing) in for fury, resolve or raw power at work. Distinct from eyes that merely glow.

entries.name: aqua_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are blue-green instead of black. Where the [shade](#shade) sits between hues this overlaps with the blue and green pupil tags, and the lighting often decides which reads best.

entries.name: wall-eyed
entries.description: Both eyes drift outward, each [pointing](#pointing) away from the other. The opposite of [cross-eyed](#cross-eyed), and usually drawn for a [dazed](#dazed) or [comic](#comic) effect.

entries.name: dilated_pupils
entries.description: Pupils blown much wider than usual against the iris. Depending on the rest of the face this reads as infatuation, shock, [drugs](#drugs), or simply a [dark](#dark) room.

entries.name: shiny_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn with [strong](#strong), glossy highlights, the reflections large and bright enough that the surface reads as [wet](#wet).

entries.name: text_in_eyes
entries.description: Writing is drawn inside the pupils, so the eyes themselves carry a word or phrase, usually [standing](#standing) in for a character's thought. Pictures rather than letters make it [symbol-shaped_pupils](#symbol-shaped_pupils) instead.

entries.name: grey_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn grey instead of black, which softens the gaze. This differs from [grey_eyes](#grey_eyes), where the iris carries the colour.

entries.name: googly_eyes
entries.description: Round cartoon eyes with loose black pupils [rolling](#rolling) about inside them, drawn for a [gag](#gag) or [stuck](#stuck) on as plastic craft discs. They carry silliness rather than any real expression.

entries.name: rectangular_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn as horizontal [bars](#bars) rather than circles or slits, the shape found in goats, [sheep](#sheep), and frogs. Gives a character an [alien](#alien) or livestock-like stare.

entries.name: small_pupils
entries.description: Pupils shrunk to pinpricks inside a wide iris or sclera. Artists use the contraction for shock, fear, madness or a sudden loss of composure.

entries.name: paw-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as little paw prints, a central pad with toe [beads](#beads) above it, in place of ordinary round ones. One of the symbol-shaped pupil variants, usually signalling [animal](#animal) delight.

entries.name: brown_sclera
entries.description: The part of the eye that would ordinarily be white is brown instead, so the whole [eyeball](#eyeball) reads as coloured. It usually marks a [demon](#demon), beast or other non-human character.

entries.name: lens_eye
entries.description: A human-shaped character whose eyes are built like [camera](#camera) optics, given away by concentric rings inside the iris. Reserved for humanoids, since outright machines are assumed to see this way anyway.

entries.name: brown_pupils
entries.description: The pupil itself is drawn brown instead of black. It [can](#can) sit inside an iris of a completely different colour, which is what sets it apart from [brown_eyes](#brown_eyes).

entries.name: clover-shaped_pupils
entries.description: Pupils drawn as [clover](#clover) leaves rather than round [dots](#dots). One of the symbol-pupil designs, generally marking a character as lucky or magically charged.

entries.name: dot_pupils
entries.description: Pupils shrunk to tiny points inside otherwise ordinary eyes, which gives a startled, blank or unhinged look. Often paired with an open mouth at a moment of shock.

entries.name: glowing_pupils
entries.description: Only the pupils give off light, the rest of the eye staying ordinary, so the glow sits at the centre. Narrower than [glowing_eyes](#glowing_eyes), where the whole eye lights up.

entries.name: fish-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as little [fish](#fish) outlines instead of circles or slits. A stylised [sign](#sign) of an aquatic character or of a love of fish.

entries.name: mystic_eyes
entries.description: Eyes that hold a supernatural power, given an odd colour, an inscribed [ring](#ring) or a glow to set them apart from ordinary ones. What the power actually does varies from design to design; the marked look is the common [thread](#thread).

entries.name: sun-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupil is drawn as a small [sun](#sun) with radiating points instead of a [plain](#plain) [circle](#circle), usually signalling a magical, divine or otherwise non-human [nature](#nature).

entries.name: spiral-only_eyes
entries.description: The whole eye is rendered as a single coiling [spiral](#spiral) rather than a normal iris and pupil, the standard shorthand for dizziness or a knockout. Where only the iris carries the spiral, [@_@](#@_@) is used instead.

entries.name: aqua_sclera
entries.description: The part of the eye that is normally white is blue-green instead. A design [choice](#choice) marking a character as inhuman, [possessed](#possessed) or otherwise not right.

entries.name: square_eyes
entries.description: Eyes or irises drawn as squares instead of the usual rounded shape, [giving](#giving) a look that reads as artificial, robotic or comically blank.

entries.name: mismatched_irises
entries.description: One iris is drawn noticeably larger, or shaped differently, than the other. Two eyes with different colored irises altogether is [heterochromia](#heterochromia).

entries.name: sunburst_iris
entries.description: An iris [carrying](#carrying) fine lines that radiate out from the pupil like the spokes of a [wheel](#wheel), [giving](#giving) the eye a jewel-like depth. Often drawn on characters meant to look otherworldly.

entries.name: squiggle_eyes
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as wavering squiggles, showing a character rattled, unhinged or unable to focus. Common in both comedy and horror.
One pupil is drawn as a plus [sign](#sign) and the other as a minus. It is a graphic joke about a [dazed](#dazed), short-circuited state rather than any real feature of the eye.

entries.name: lightning_bolt-shaped_pupils
entries.description: The pupils are drawn as zig-zag bolts instead of round [shapes](#shapes), usually on electricity-themed characters.

entries.name: black_pupils
entries.description: Pupils filled solid black at the centre of the eye. The claim covers the pupil alone, so the surrounding iris still needs its own eye colour [tag](#tag).

entries.name: eyelashes
entries.description: Lashes given particular attention by the artist, drawn long, thick or hair by hair. Not for every face with visible lashes, only where they are clearly emphasized.

entries.name: tsurime
entries.description: Eyes whose upper lids slant upward toward the temples, [giving](#giving) a sharp, assertive look often given to strong-willed characters. The downward-slanting counterpart, [tareme](#tareme), reads instead as soft or gentle.

entries.name: tareme
entries.description: Eyes whose outer corners droop [well](#well) below the inner ones, [giving](#giving) a soft, gentle look usually assigned to mild-mannered characters. The sharp, upward-slanting opposite is [tsurime](#tsurime).

entries.name: colored_eyelashes
entries.description: The lash line and eye [outline](#outline) are drawn in a colour other than black, often picking up the hair colour. Add [eyelashes](#eyelashes) when the lashes themselves are prominent, and keep it apart from [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow).

entries.name: bags_under_eyes
entries.description: Dark rings or puffy shadows drawn directly beneath the eyes. They stand for exhaustion, sleeplessness or stress, or simply give a character a gloomy, unsettling [cast](#cast); on some they are a permanent feature.

entries.name: sanpaku
entries.description: Eyes where the white shows on three sides of the iris even at rest, [giving](#giving) a tired, intense or dangerous look. Sometimes called dead [fish](#fish) eyes; the four-sided extreme is shihakugan.

entries.name: long_eyelashes
entries.description: Eyelashes drawn markedly longer than normal, usually as a glamorous exaggeration. They are common on mature designs and on heavily made-up faces.

entries.name: uneven_eyes
entries.description: Both eyes are open but to different widths, one wide and one narrowed. If one eye is fully shut instead, use [one_eye_closed](#one_eye_closed).

entries.name: aegyo_sal
entries.description: The small soft ridge of [fat](#fat) [sitting](#sitting) just below the lower [lid](#lid), prized in Korean beauty culture for making a face look younger. It is not the [dark](#dark), sunken [bags_under_eyes](#bags_under_eyes).

entries.name: puffy_eyelids
entries.description: Swollen, thick-looking lids [sitting](#sitting) above the eyes, [giving](#giving) a [heavy](#heavy) or [sleepy](#sleepy) look. Often drawn right after [crying](#crying) or on a character who has only just woken up.

entries.name: thick_eyelashes
entries.description: Lashes far heavier and more prominent than usual, sometimes clumped together and visible even in a thumbnail. Largely a matter of the artist's own style.

entries.name: white_eyelashes
entries.description: Eyelashes drawn white instead of [dark](#dark), usually matching white or silver hair. A form of colored [eyelashes](#eyelashes).

entries.name: button_eyes
entries.description: Eyes made from sewn-on [buttons](#buttons), as on a rag [doll](#doll), a plush [toy](#toy) or a [hat](#hat) with a face. It gives whatever wears them a [stitched](#stitched), handmade look.

entries.name: compound_eyes
entries.description: Eyes with a faceted, mesh-like surface, as insects, spiders and crustaceans have. Found on creatures and on bug-themed characters alike.

entries.name: <o>_<o>
entries.description: Eyes drawn as [almond](#almond) outlines with a small round pupil in each, matching the [emoticon](#emoticon). The stylised shape is often used for a [deadpan](#deadpan) or faintly unsettling stare.

entries.name: lower_eyelashes_only
entries.description: Lashes are drawn, often exaggerated, below the eye while the upper [lid](#lid) carries none. Sometimes an artist's [habit](#habit), sometimes part of a character's official design.

entries.name: lazy_eye
entries.description: One eye points in a different direction from the other. It may be drawn on purpose to suggest a medical condition or an unhinged character, or it may simply be a slip by the artist.

entries.name: mismatched_eyelashes
entries.description: Lashes colored differently from the hair, or each eye given its own separate lash color, often alongside [heterochromia](#heterochromia). Only applies where the lashes are already colored to begin with.

entries.name: pac-man_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn as [plain](#plain) circles with a wedge bitten out of them, exactly like the [arcade](#arcade) character. Cartoon shorthand used on [gag](#gag) faces and on heavily simplified designs.

entries.name: eye_socket
entries.description: The bony hollow that holds the eye, seen on a [skull](#skull) or where an eye is gone. Often drawn [dark](#dark) and empty, sometimes with a light [burning](#burning) inside it.

entries.name: mature_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn narrower with faint creases at the corners, a design cue used to read as adult or older rather than the wide round eyes given to younger characters. A stylistic trait rather than an expression.

entries.name: very_big_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn enormous even by anime standards, covering at least half the area of the face. Typical of [chibi](#chibi) figures, older shoujo art and visual novel character portraits, and usually loaded with highlights and [heavy](#heavy) lashes.

entries.name: v-shaped_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows angled down toward the [nose](#nose) so they form a V, [reading](#reading) as mischief, smugness, anger or irritation. Usually paired with a mouth [emoticon](#emoticon), so that a smiling face with these brows becomes the classic devious expression.

entries.name: thick_eyebrows
entries.description: Brows drawn as bold blobs or [bars](#bars) rather than the usual thin lines. In more [realistic](#realistic) styles, they should be at least a finger's width to qualify.

entries.name: furrowed_brow
entries.description: A creased [forehead](#forehead) from concentration, worry or anger, usually drawn as eyebrows whose inner ends bend upward rather than as actual wrinkles. Eyebrows merely raised in a gentle curve do not need it.

entries.name: raised_eyebrows
entries.description: Both eyebrows lift above their [resting](#resting) position, commonly signaling surprise, worry, or heightened attention. A single lifted brow instead is [raised_eyebrow](#raised_eyebrow).

entries.name: eyebrows_hidden_by_hair
entries.description: The eyebrows are wholly or partly covered by bangs or other hair and do not show through it at all. If they are drawn visible through the fringe, this does not apply.

entries.name: short_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows that [cover](#cover) only part of the brow ridge, whether plucked shorter than usual or simply drawn that way as a character trait.

entries.name: raised_inner_eyebrows
entries.description: The ends of the eyebrows nearest the [nose](#nose) tilt upward while the outer ends stay low, [bending](#bending) the whole brow line. Reads as pleading or fright in one direction, and as a [smug](#smug), superior look in the other.

entries.name: raised_eyebrow
entries.description: One eyebrow lifts while the other stays down, a look that reads as doubt, amusement, or smugness, or as a suggestive expression when paired with [naughty_face](#naughty_face). Both brows lifted at once is [raised_eyebrows](#raised_eyebrows).

entries.name: forked_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows that [split](#split) into two prongs at their outer ends. The trait normally marks a fierce or hot-blooded character, and often accompanies [thick_eyebrows](#thick_eyebrows).

entries.name: eyebrow_cut
entries.description: One or more thin vertical slits shaved into an eyebrow, also called notches. A [delinquent](#delinquent) and street-fashion look, often drawn together with a [scar](#scar) across the eye.

entries.name: curly_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows drawn with a curl or a [spiral](#spiral) worked into them, a stylised feature marking out certain characters. It stays constant rather than changing with the expression.

entries.name: no_eyebrows
entries.description: A face drawn with [no](#no) eyebrows at all. Do not use it when hair, a [hat](#hat) or anything else merely hides where they would be.

entries.name: huge_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows as large as or larger than the character's eyes, past what [thick_eyebrows](#thick_eyebrows) describes. Bara art and burly male characters wear them most.

entries.name: mismatched_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows in a different color from the hair, thick enough to actually notice rather than drawn as pencil-thin lines.

entries.name: long_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows drawn long enough to run past the edge of the [forehead](#forehead), sometimes trailing down beside the face. A design quirk rather than a matter of grooming.

entries.name: cocked_eyebrow
entries.description: One eyebrow rises while the other drops, [giving](#giving) a look of doubt or dry amusement. The lowered brow is what separates it from a [plain](#plain) raised eyebrow.

entries.name: eyebrows_visible_through_hat
entries.description: The eyebrows are drawn showing through a [hat](#hat), [hood](#hood) or [helmet](#helmet) that would really hide them. A stylistic [convention](#convention), kept so the expression still reads.

entries.name: wavy_eyebrows
entries.description: Eyebrows drawn as wobbling lines instead of clean arcs. A cartoon shorthand for worry, [distress](#distress) or bewilderment.

entries.name: unibrow
entries.description: The two eyebrows meet above the [nose](#nose) and read as one continuous brow spanning the [forehead](#forehead), rather than two separate arches.

entries.name: eyebrows_visible_through_mask
entries.description: Eyebrows drawn over or through a [mask](#mask) that ought to [cover](#cover) them, so that the character's expression stays legible. The same [convention](#convention) as [eyebrows_visible_through_hat](#eyebrows_visible_through_hat), one layer further in.

entries.name: single_eyebrow
entries.description: Only one eyebrow exists on the face, the other simply absent rather than hidden behind hair. Not for [one-eyed](#one-eyed) beings such as cyclopes, and not the same as a [unibrow](#unibrow).

entries.name: mole
entries.description: A small [dark](#dark) spot on the skin, the beauty mark, wherever on the body it sits. Add the placement [tag](#tag) such as [mole_under_eye](#mole_under_eye) when the position is clear. The burrowing [animal](#animal) has a separate tag.

entries.name: mole_under_eye
entries.description: A beauty mark just below one eye, the so-called tear [mole](#mole). A very common piece of character design, and much the most used of the mole placements.

entries.name: lips
entries.description: The lips are drawn with visible shape and volume instead of a [plain](#plain) line, a feature of [realistic](#realistic) and mature styles. Related tags [cover](#cover) what they do, such as [parted_lips](#parted_lips), [pursed_lips](#pursed_lips) and [licking_lips](#licking_lips).

entries.name: dot_nose
entries.description: A [nose](#nose) drawn as one small dot rather than a line or a modelled shape, a common simplification in anime faces. It says how the nose is rendered, not what shape it is.

entries.name: mole_under_mouth
entries.description: A beauty mark below the lower lip, in the [space](#space) between mouth and chin. A [signature](#signature) feature on a number of well-known character designs.

entries.name: faceless
entries.description: The front of the head lies inside the frame, yet the face is not shown, whether hidden by hair or [shadow](#shadow) or simply left undrawn. A being that genuinely has [no](#no) face takes [hole_in_face](#hole_in_face) or [no_eyes](#no_eyes). Split by [sex](#sex) into [faceless_male](#faceless_male) and [faceless_female](#faceless_female).

entries.name: freckles
entries.description: Small brownish pigment [spots](#spots) scattered on the skin, usually over the cheeks and the [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose). Freckles elsewhere on the body are [body_freckles](#body_freckles).

entries.name: forehead
entries.description: The forehead is given emphasis, usually because the hair is swept [back](#back) or parted to bare a wide or gleaming one. It marks a deliberate feature rather than any visible brow.

entries.name: east_asian
entries.description: The subject is drawn with East Asian features and colouring. Describes how the person looks, not where the scene is set or what they wear.

entries.name: faceless_male
entries.description: A male character whose face is left blank, shadowed or hidden, the anonymous partner of countless explicit scenes. His head must be within the picture, which excludes a viewpoint shot showing only the viewer's own body.

entries.name: mole_on_breast
entries.description: A beauty mark on the breast itself, a common design detail brought out by a deep neckline. A mark higher up on the breastbone takes the chest [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: red_lips
entries.description: Lips painted with red [lipstick](#lipstick), a [strong](#strong) visible red rather than a natural tint. Usually goes with the [makeup](#makeup) and lipstick tags.

entries.name: no_nose
entries.description: A face drawn with [no](#no) [nose](#nose) projecting from it at all, a common simplification in anime styles. Drawing one prominently instead is nose.

entries.name: nose
entries.description: A nose drawn with real shape and a visible [bridge](#bridge), more prominent than the usual anime shorthand. The opposite extreme is [dot_nose](#dot_nose).

entries.name: cat_nose
entries.description: A small feline [triangle](#triangle) stands in for the [nose](#nose) on an otherwise human face, usually with a short line [running](#running) down to the lip. It goes hand in hand with [cat](#cat) girl designs and a mouth drawn as a [w](#w).

entries.name: dog_nose
entries.description: The black, rounded, slightly moist [nose](#nose) of a canine set on a face, whether on an [animal](#animal), an anthro or a person given animal traits. Often drawn together with a muzzle or [whiskers](#whiskers).

entries.name: no_mouth
entries.description: No mouth is drawn on the face at all, sometimes by [accident](#accident) on a washed-out [scan](#scan), sometimes on purpose to convey blankness or indifference.

entries.name: faceless_female
entries.description: A female character whose features, above all the eyes, cannot be seen: covered by hair, lost in [shadow](#shadow) or never drawn at all. Her head has to be inside the picture, so a head [cropped](#cropped) away by the edge does not qualify.

entries.name: mole_on_neck
entries.description: A beauty mark on the throat or the side of the [neck](#neck), between the line of the [jaw](#jaw) and the [collarbone](#collarbone). A turned head or pinned-up hair is what puts it in view.

entries.name: multiple_moles
entries.description: A character marked with several moles about the face or body. The single beauty spot is covered by [mole](#mole) on its own.

entries.name: thick_lips
entries.description: Lips that are markedly full and prominent, [plump](#plump) on both the top and the bottom. Add [lipstick](#lipstick) when they are painted.

entries.name: mole_on_thigh
entries.description: A beauty mark on the thigh, a detail that shows with bare [legs](#legs) or short bottoms. Legwear pulled up over it hides it entirely.

entries.name: puffy_lips
entries.description: Full, soft [lips](#lips) that look noticeably swollen, sometimes [reading](#reading) as a permanent [pout](#pout). A feature of the mouth's own shape rather than any expression it happens to be making.

entries.name: ugly_man
entries.description: An unattractive male character, typically drawn [old](#old), [bald](#bald), overweight or all three. A recurring stock [figure](#figure) in adult work, often paired with an attractive woman.

entries.name: covered_face
entries.description: A character's face is blocked from view, wholly or in part, by a [mask](#mask), a hand, hair or a held object. Add [covered_eyes](#covered_eyes) or [covered_mouth](#covered_mouth) when only that part is hidden.

entries.name: nostrils
entries.description: The nasal openings are visibly drawn, on a [nose](#nose) or a [beak](#beak). They usually show when the head is seen from below or the nose is rendered in detail.

entries.name: green_lips
entries.description: The character's [lips](#lips) are green, whether from [lipstick](#lipstick) or from their own colouring. Under some lighting the [shade](#shade) blurs into the aqua and yellow variants.

entries.name: pointy_nose
entries.description: A long, prominent [nose](#nose) that dominates the face, as on witches, goblins and caricatured figures. An ordinary small anime nose does not qualify.

entries.name: mole_under_each_eye
entries.description: A matching beauty mark beneath both eyes, one to each side. The single-sided version is the ordinary under-eye [tag](#tag).

entries.name: mole_on_cheek
entries.description: A beauty mark set on the cheek, clear of both the eye above it and the [corner](#corner) of the mouth. Purely a question of where the spot falls on the face.

entries.name: cheek_bulge
entries.description: Something inside the mouth pushes a cheek outward: a sweet, a mouthful of [food](#food), a [tongue](#tongue) pressed against it. Pressure applied from outside the face is [cheek_poking](#cheek_poking).

entries.name: asian
entries.description: A person drawn with deliberately East Asian features, more closely observed than the ethnically vague default of the style. Reserve it for pictures where that is clearly part of the depiction.

entries.name: mole_on_ass
entries.description: A beauty mark on one of the buttocks, showing where the [ass](#ass) is bare or where the clothing exposes it. Nothing but the placement separates it from the other [mole](#mole) tags.

entries.name: big_nose
entries.description: A [nose](#nose) drawn conspicuously large, whether as caricature, as a [realistic](#realistic) touch or as a character's own feature. It stands out because most anime-style faces reduce the nose to a stroke.

entries.name: long_nose
entries.description: An unusually long [nose](#nose), as worn by a [tengu](#tengu), a [puppet](#puppet) [caught](#caught) in a lie or a caricatured [witch](#witch). A merely prominent but ordinary nose does not count.

entries.name: mole_above_mouth
entries.description: A beauty mark above the upper lip, on either the left or the right side. Its [height](#height) is what separates it from the marks below the mouth or out on the cheek.

entries.name: mole_on_stomach
entries.description: A beauty mark on the [belly](#belly) or close to the [navel](#navel). Crop tops, swimwear and a lifted [shirt](#shirt) are what let it show.

entries.name: puffy_cheeks
entries.description: Both cheeks [bulge](#bulge) outward, whether from a mouthful of [food](#food), held [breath](#breath) while pouting, or simply as a childish design touch. Pair with [pout](#pout) or [eating](#eating) where it fits; only one cheek puffed does not count.

entries.name: cheekbones
entries.description: The bones under the eyes are drawn as a defined, visible feature, [giving](#giving) the face a sharp or mature [structure](#structure). Adult and severe-looking designs make the most of them.

entries.name: mole_on_arm
entries.description: A beauty mark somewhere on the upper or lower arm. Bare arms or rolled sleeves are what let it show.

entries.name: mole_on_collarbone
entries.description: A beauty mark on or immediately beside the [collarbone](#collarbone). A wide neckline or bare shoulders are what bring it into view.

entries.name: mole_on_shoulder
entries.description: A beauty spot on the shoulder or the slope [running](#running) toward the [collarbone](#collarbone), put on show by bare shoulders or a loose neckline. A small detail, but a fixed part of some character designs.

entries.name: no_mole
entries.description: A character whose design carries a [mole](#mole) is drawn without it, whether by [choice](#choice) or oversight. It is a small design-deviation [tag](#tag).

entries.name: mob_face
entries.description: A named character drawn with the [plain](#plain), barely-featured face normally handed to background extras. The flattening is deliberate and is usually played for a laugh.

entries.name: mole_above_eye
entries.description: A beauty spot [sitting](#sitting) just over the eye, on the [lid](#lid) or up toward the brow. One of the placement tags that [pin](#pin) down where a [mole](#mole) falls.

entries.name: mole_on_armpit
entries.description: A beauty spot in the hollow of the armpit or on the skin beside it. It needs a raised arm or a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top before it [can](#can) be seen.

entries.name: wide_face
entries.description: A character's face rendered squashed horizontally into far wider proportions than normal. It is a comic-effect exaggeration rather than an actual [facial](#facial) feature.

entries.name: grey_lips
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) are grey, whether from [makeup](#makeup) or from the character's own colouring. Shade judgement being loose, it borders on the black and white variants.

entries.name: cleft_chin
entries.description: A chin [split](#split) down the middle by a vertical dimple, read as rugged and emphatically masculine. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a double chin, which is loose [flesh](#flesh) under the [jaw](#jaw).

entries.name: aquiline_nose
entries.description: A [nose](#nose) with a high, curved [bridge](#bridge) that reads as hooked or beak-like, clearest in [profile](#profile). One that instead breaks sharply at the brow, or juts straight outward, takes the [tag](#tag) for that shape.

entries.name: sunken_cheeks
entries.description: The cheeks curve inward, sometimes reduced to a pair of diagonal lines on the face. Can read as suction from the mouth, or as a [sign](#sign) of hunger, exhaustion, [despair](#despair) or approaching [death](#death).

entries.name: mole_on_chest
entries.description: A beauty spot on the upper chest or the breastbone. Anything [sitting](#sitting) on the breast itself belongs to the breast [mole](#mole) tags.

entries.name: mole_on_crotch
entries.description: A beauty spot on the pubic mound or on the bare skin around it, stopping short of the genitals themselves. A mark actually on them takes one of the more specific tags.

entries.name: white_lips
entries.description: Lips drawn white, whether from [lipstick](#lipstick) or an unnatural complexion. Lighting makes this hard to keep apart from [grey_lips](#grey_lips).

entries.name: mole_on_leg
entries.description: A beauty spot along the leg, anywhere from knee to ankle. Higher up it may be better served by the thigh, [ass](#ass) or [stomach](#stomach) placements.

entries.name: double_chin
entries.description: Enough soft [flesh](#flesh) beneath the [jaw](#jaw) that a second chin appears under the first, marking a [heavy](#heavy) or [plump](#plump) face. Hard to draw convincingly and therefore rare; not a cleft chin.

entries.name: mole_on_forehead
entries.description: A beauty spot on the [forehead](#forehead) above the brow line. It generally needs a fringe swept clear or [pinned](#pinned) [back](#back) to be visible.

entries.name: yurie_mouth
entries.description: A small mouth drawn as a bump projecting from the lower edge of the face [outline](#outline), beak-like when seen from the side. A soft, simplified shorthand common in gentle, cartoonish art styles.

entries.name: mole_on_back
entries.description: A beauty spot somewhere across the [back](#back). Backless clothing and views taken from behind are where it turns up.

entries.name: mole_on_nose
entries.description: A beauty spot on the [bridge](#bridge) or the tip of the [nose](#nose). Being so small, it usually only registers in a close view.

entries.name: man_face
entries.description: Heavy rugged masculine features on a character who should not have them, such as a young boy or a woman drawn unexpectedly craggy. Usually either a joke or a slip of the [pen](#pen).

entries.name: jaw
entries.description: The jaw treated as a subject in itself, from a [heavy](#heavy) human jawline to the hinged jaw of an [animal](#animal) or a [skull](#skull). Reach for it where that shape is what the picture dwells on.

entries.name: facial_hair
entries.description: Hair grown on the face: beards, moustaches, goatees, [sideburns](#sideburns) and [stubble](#stubble) in all their lengths. It works as the [umbrella](#umbrella) [tag](#tag), with the particular style added beside it. A [costume](#costume) piece is [fake_facial_hair](#fake_facial_hair).

entries.name: beard
entries.description: Hair growing over the chin, the cheeks and down the [neck](#neck). Growth confined to the chin is a [goatee](#goatee), and hair on the upper lip is a moustache, which [can](#can) be tagged alongside.

entries.name: stubble
entries.description: Short, freshly grown [facial](#facial) hair, the classic five o'clock [shadow](#shadow). Sometimes paired with [sideburns](#sideburns) or a [goatee](#goatee) as a deliberate [beard](#beard) style. Implies [facial_hair](#facial_hair).

entries.name: sideburns
entries.description: Strips of hair [running](#running) down each side of the face, starting at the hairline and [reaching](#reaching) past the ears. A grooming detail seen on many male characters; short regrowth there instead is [sideburns_stubble](#sideburns_stubble).

entries.name: mustache
entries.description: Facial hair grown along the upper lip beneath the [nose](#nose). It runs from a thin [pencil](#pencil) line to a broad [handlebar](#handlebar), and pairs with [beard](#beard) tags where the growth carries on to the chin.

entries.name: goatee
entries.description: Beard growth kept to a small tuft or a point on the chin, with the cheeks bare. A moustache above it is tagged separately.

entries.name: long_sideburns
entries.description: Sideburns [running](#running) past the ears and forward onto the cheeks, usually with [stubble](#stubble) or a [goatee](#goatee) on the chin. Where they merge with chin hair into one growth, add [beard](#beard) as [well](#well).

entries.name: beard_stubble
entries.description: Short coarse regrowth across the [jaw](#jaw) and cheeks, the unshaven look, whether neglect or a deliberate style. When only the upper lip is stubbled, use [mustache_stubble](#mustache_stubble) instead.

entries.name: full_beard
entries.description: Facial hair covering chin, cheeks and [sideburns](#sideburns) in one unbroken sweep. A moustache is tagged separately, since plenty of bearded anime characters go without one; thickness has its own tags.

entries.name: sideburns_stubble
entries.description: Short, coarse regrowth at the temples where [sideburns](#sideburns) or a [beard](#beard) were shaved, [giving](#giving) a rugged, [unfinished](#unfinished) look. Stubble limited to the [jaw](#jaw), lip or chin takes [beard_stubble](#beard_stubble), [mustache_stubble](#mustache_stubble) or [goatee_stubble](#goatee_stubble) instead.

entries.name: goatee_stubble
entries.description: Short coarse growth on the chin in the [outline](#outline) of a [goatee](#goatee), an unshaven look rather than a grown [beard](#beard). Stubble covering the whole [jaw](#jaw) or the upper lip is [beard_stubble](#beard_stubble).

entries.name: mustache_stubble
entries.description: Short unshaven growth confined to the upper lip, [giving](#giving) a rough look or forming part of a [facial](#facial) hair design. Stubble on the [jaw](#jaw) or chin is [beard](#beard) [stubble](#stubble) instead.

entries.name: long_beard
entries.description: A full [beard](#beard) [hanging](#hanging) down past the shoulders. One that reaches the [navel](#navel) or lower takes [very_long_beard](#very_long_beard) as [well](#well).

entries.name: thick_mustache
entries.description: A bushy, full [mustache](#mustache) covering the upper lip. Combine with [thick_beard](#thick_beard) for a complete set of [facial](#facial) hair.

entries.name: thick_beard
entries.description: A full [beard](#beard) covering much of the lower face and usually joining the [sideburns](#sideburns). Add [mustache](#mustache) when the upper lip is bearded too.

entries.name: sparse_stubble
entries.description: Light, patchy [facial](#facial) [stubble](#stubble) rather than a full [shadow](#shadow) or [beard](#beard), just a few short hairs across the chin or [jaw](#jaw).

entries.name: very_long_beard
entries.description: A full [beard](#beard) [reaching](#reaching) down past the [navel](#navel), [wizard](#wizard) style. A beard that passes the shoulders but not the [belly](#belly) is [long_beard](#long_beard) alone.

entries.name: mutton_chops
entries.description: Sideburns that stay narrow at the ear and [flare](#flare) wide and round toward the [jaw](#jaw). Left alone they resemble a [beard](#beard) with a bare chin; run into a [mustache](#mustache) they become friendly mutton chops.

entries.name: medium_sideburns
entries.description: Sideburns that reach past the middle of the ear but stop short of the [jaw](#jaw). A common masculine cue for characters too young or smooth-faced to grow a full [beard](#beard).

entries.name: long_mustache
entries.description: Upper-lip hair grown to a striking length, drooping to the chin or curling far past the [cheekbones](#cheekbones) where it defies gravity. Anything [reaching](#reaching) the chest is very_long_mustache.

entries.name: chinstrap_beard
entries.description: Facial hair trimmed to a narrow line that follows the [jaw](#jaw) and wraps around the chin, with the upper lip left bare. Thinner than a full [beard](#beard) and set lower than a [goatee](#goatee).

entries.name: connected_beard
entries.description: The moustache runs unbroken into the [beard](#beard) at both corners of the mouth, ringing it completely. It normally goes together with [full_beard](#full_beard) or [thick_beard](#thick_beard).

entries.name: two-tone_beard
entries.description: Facial hair [split](#split) between two clear colours, the same way head hair [can](#can) be two-toned. The divide may run down the middle, along the [jaw](#jaw), or between moustache and chin.

entries.name: braided_beard
entries.description: Facial hair worked into one or more plaits, whether a full [beard](#beard) or a long [goatee](#goatee). Dwarves, vikings and veteran warriors wear it most often, sometimes with rings or ties along its length.

entries.name: white_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard), moustache or [patch](#patch) of [stubble](#stubble) grown out white, usually marking an elderly character. The hair on the head carries its own separate color [tag](#tag).

entries.name: beard_over_mouth
entries.description: Facial hair grown so thick that it swallows the [lips](#lips), leaving [no](#no) mouth visible at all. Gruff [old](#old) men, dwarves and [mountain](#mountain) hermits wear it that way.

entries.name: blonde_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard), moustache or [stubble](#stubble) in blonde. Only the hair on the face is described, whatever colour sits on the head.

entries.name: pencil_mustache
entries.description: A very thin moustache drawn as a fine line along the upper lip, often [split](#split) at the centre. It reads as either dapper or comically sleazy.

entries.name: black_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard), moustache or [stubble](#stubble) in black. It records the colour only, whatever shape the growth happens to take.

entries.name: tied_beard
entries.description: A [beard](#beard) gathered and [bound](#bound) with a [ribbon](#ribbon), cord or band, sometimes divided into several segments. A grooming detail typical of dwarves, wizards and elderly warriors.

entries.name: purple_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard), moustache, or [stubble](#stubble) coloured purple, usually to match the character's head hair. Common on stylised and [fantasy](#fantasy) designs.

entries.name: soul_patch
entries.description: A small tuft of hair grown just below the lower lip and above the chin, with the rest of the face otherwise shaved. A compact [marker](#marker) of [facial](#facial) hair on adult male characters.

entries.name: brown_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard), moustache, [sideburns](#sideburns) or [stubble](#stubble) coloured brown. It applies to hair on the face however much or little there is.

entries.name: red_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard), moustache or [stubble](#stubble) that is ginger or auburn. It usually [matches](#matches) red hair on the head, and is common on [dwarf](#dwarf) and [viking](#viking) designs.

entries.name: stroking_beard
entries.description: A hand drawn along one's own [beard](#beard), typically while mulling something over. Reads as a [gesture](#gesture) of quiet thought or [smug](#smug) amusement.

entries.name: makeup
entries.description: Cosmetics visibly worn on the face: [lipstick](#lipstick), [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow), [mascara](#mascara), drawn-on liner. The products and [tools](#tools) themselves are [cosmetics](#cosmetics), and putting it on is [applying_makeup](#applying_makeup).

entries.name: lipstick
entries.description: Coloured [makeup](#makeup) on the [lips](#lips), red most commonly. The product in its [container](#container) is [lipstick_tube](#lipstick_tube), and a [kiss](#kiss) print left behind is [lipstick_mark](#lipstick_mark).

entries.name: eyeshadow
entries.description: Coloured powder on the eyelids to make the eyes stand out, drawn as a wash of red, purple, blue or another [shade](#shade) above the eye. A line along the lashes rather than colour on the [lid](#lid) is [eyeliner](#eyeliner).

entries.name: pink_lips
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) are drawn a noticeable pink, most often because [lipstick](#lipstick) has been applied. Use it where the mouth colour stands out from the face rather than for a default skin-toned mouth.

entries.name: eyeliner
entries.description: Makeup drawn as a line along the lash line to sharpen the eye or [flick](#flick) out into a wing. It shows as a [dark](#dark) [outline](#outline) framing the eye.

entries.name: facepaint
entries.description: Marks, symbols or patterns painted onto the skin of the face, from [tribal](#tribal) designs to sports colours. Paint splashed there by [accident](#accident) is a different [tag](#tag), and painting somebody else's face is [drawing_on_another's_face](#drawing_on_another's_face).

entries.name: red_eyeshadow
entries.description: Red [makeup](#makeup) on the eyelids, from a faint tint at the outer corners to a full crimson [lid](#lid), common on [oni](#oni) and Chinese-styled characters. Combine with [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow) and makeup; a red line along the lashes is [red_eyeliner](#red_eyeliner).

entries.name: red_eyeliner
entries.description: Eyeliner drawn in red, a look regarded as fierce and lucky in Chinese tradition and common on East Asian-styled characters. Combine with [eyeliner](#eyeliner) and [makeup](#makeup).

entries.name: purple_lips
entries.description: Lips coloured purple or lavender by [lipstick](#lipstick), or a lipstick [tube](#tube) shown in that [shade](#shade). Combine with lipstick and [makeup](#makeup); naturally purple [lips](#lips) on a coloured-skin character count too.

entries.name: black_lips
entries.description: Lips painted black, a gothic or villainous [makeup](#makeup) [choice](#choice). Use it where the colour is clearly deliberate makeup rather than shading or a species trait.

entries.name: blue_lips
entries.description: Lips coloured blue, generally blue [lipstick](#lipstick) on a cool-toned or [undead](#undead) design. It overlaps with [aqua_lips](#aqua_lips) and [purple_lips](#purple_lips) depending on the lighting.

entries.name: mascara
entries.description: Lashes thickened or lengthened with [cosmetics](#cosmetics). Only [tag](#tag) it where the [makeup](#makeup) is evident, such as other cosmetics worn, the [wand](#wand) in view, or the act of applying shown; defined lashes on their own are just [eyelashes](#eyelashes). Liner is a line along the [lid](#lid) and [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow) a coloured powder around the eye.

entries.name: pink_eyeshadow
entries.description: Pink colour worked across the eyelids as [makeup](#makeup), from a soft wash to a [heavy](#heavy) sweep. Liner in the same colour is [pink_eyeliner](#pink_eyeliner).

entries.name: blue_eyeshadow
entries.description: Blue colour brushed across the eyelids. Cool-toned and eighties-style [makeup](#makeup) use it most, often together with matching [eyeliner](#eyeliner).

entries.name: purple_eyeshadow
entries.description: Purple [makeup](#makeup) applied to the eyelids, ranging from a soft lavender wash to a [heavy](#heavy) violet smoky eye. Combine with [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow) and makeup; a line drawn only along the lashes is [eyeliner](#eyeliner) instead.

entries.name: hikimayu
entries.description: Eyebrows shaved away and repainted higher up the [forehead](#forehead) as small ovals or commas, a Japanese court cosmetic [running](#running) from the Heian period to the end of Edo. It turns up on noble ladies, historical characters and period [costume](#costume).

entries.name: runny_makeup
entries.description: Makeup smeared or [dripping](#dripping), [mascara](#mascara) and [eyeliner](#eyeliner) [running](#running) down the cheeks from [tears](#tears), [rain](#rain) or [sweat](#sweat). Usually shown alongside tears or [crying](#crying).

entries.name: black_eyeshadow
entries.description: Black [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow) worked over the lids, [giving](#giving) a smoky or gothic look. It may be a thin wash along the lash line or a [heavy](#heavy) smudge [reaching](#reaching) up to the brow.

entries.name: black_eyeliner
entries.description: Black [eyeliner](#eyeliner) drawn along the lash lines, showing as a [dark](#dark) rim or a flicked wing at the outer [corner](#corner). It is the commonest liner colour, and often the only [makeup](#makeup) a design carries.

entries.name: brown_lips
entries.description: Lips coloured brown with [lipstick](#lipstick), or a brown lipstick shown as an object. Add lipstick and [lips](#lips).

entries.name: green_eyeshadow
entries.description: Green colour worked onto the eyelids, from a faint wash to bold gothic or [fantasy](#fantasy) styling. Where the rest of the face is made up too, [tag](#tag) [makeup](#makeup) alongside it.

entries.name: drawn_whiskers
entries.description: Whisker lines inked or painted across the cheeks, often together with drawn ears and commonly the work of a [phone](#phone) [camera](#camera) filter. Not [whisker_markings](#whisker_markings), which belong to the character's own face.

entries.name: eyelash_ornament
entries.description: Decorations fixed to the [eyelashes](#eyelashes): tiny gems, [beads](#beads) or charms. A cosmetic addition rather than false lashes themselves, and seen on fashion-forward and [idol](#idol) characters.

entries.name: lipgloss
entries.description: A largely [transparent](#transparent) coating that leaves the [lips](#lips) wet-looking, with little or [no](#no) colour of its own. It may be clear, frosted, glittered or faintly tinted.

entries.name: eye_black
entries.description: Dark stripes smeared or taped under the eyes to cut glare, worn by [baseball](#baseball), football and [lacrosse](#lacrosse) players. Sports gear rather than [cosmetics](#cosmetics).

entries.name: grey_eyeshadow
entries.description: Grey colour brushed across the eyelids. It gives a cool, smoky look and suits tired or severe characters.

entries.name: blue_eyeliner
entries.description: Makeup drawing a blue line along the lash line, sometimes carried out into a wing. It is a line around the eye rather than colour spread across the [lid](#lid).

entries.name: smeared_lipstick
entries.description: Lipstick smudged past the lip line and across the surrounding skin. Kissing and [oral](#oral) [sex](#sex) are the usual causes, but [eating](#eating) or a careless wipe of the mouth produce the same look.

entries.name: yellow_lips
entries.description: Lips coloured yellow by [lipstick](#lipstick), an unusual [shade](#shade) generally chosen for a stylised, glamorous or inhuman look. It describes the [paint](#paint) rather than the mouth's shape.

entries.name: aqua_lips
entries.description: Lips coloured blue-green, by [paint](#paint) or by the character's own design. Judging the [shade](#shade) overlaps with the blue and green lip tags, and the lighting often decides.

entries.name: orange_lips
entries.description: Lips coloured orange, whether the [lipstick](#lipstick) is already on or a [tube](#tube) is being applied. Warm-toned [cosmetics](#cosmetics) rather than a natural lip [shade](#shade).

entries.name: orange_eyeshadow
entries.description: Orange colour swept over the eyelids, from a soft wash to a [heavy](#heavy) block. Often matched to a warm [lipstick](#lipstick) or liner in the same picture.

entries.name: pink_eyeliner
entries.description: Liner drawn along the lash line in pink rather than black or brown. One of the [makeup](#makeup) tags, often paired with [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow) in the same colour.

entries.name: yellow_eyeshadow
entries.description: Yellow colour worked onto the eyelids, sometimes blended up towards the brow. It is [makeup](#makeup) rather than a natural feature of the eyes.

entries.name: orange_eyeliner
entries.description: Liner drawn along the lash line in orange instead of the usual black or brown, generally as part of a full face of [makeup](#makeup).

entries.name: huadian
entries.description: Traditional Chinese face decoration painted on the [forehead](#forehead), between the brows, or on the cheeks and temples. Historically women's [makeup](#makeup), it is also given to men in Chinese-flavoured [fantasy](#fantasy), often to mark divinity or a non-human [nature](#nature).

entries.name: aqua_eyeshadow
entries.description: Blue-green colour brushed across the eyelids. Popular on [mermaid](#mermaid), [idol](#idol) and [stage](#stage) designs, where it is often matched to the hair or the [costume](#costume).

entries.name: purple_eyeliner
entries.description: Purple liner drawn along the lash line to [outline](#outline) the eye. A [makeup](#makeup) [choice](#choice), separate from whatever colour the eye itself is.

entries.name: rouge_(makeup)
entries.description: Colour applied to the cheeks to warm the complexion and lift the [cheekbones](#cheekbones). Distinguish it from a natural [blush](#blush), which is a reaction rather than [cosmetics](#cosmetics).

entries.name: brown_eyeshadow
entries.description: Eyeshadow in brown worked over the lids and into the creases. It reads as a warm neutral look rather than a bold colour statement.

entries.name: glitter_makeup
entries.description: Sparkling flecks worn on the face as [cosmetics](#cosmetics), most often across the eyelids or the [cheekbones](#cheekbones). A [festival](#festival), [stage](#stage) and [party](#party) look.

entries.name: white_facepaint
entries.description: White [paint](#paint) spread over the face, as on clowns, [geisha](#geisha), kabuki actors and [skull](#skull) designs. The skin beneath is a different color, which sets this apart from a naturally white complexion.

entries.name: green_eyeliner
entries.description: Green liner drawn along the lash line to frame the eye. Colour spread across the [lid](#lid) instead is [green_eyeshadow](#green_eyeshadow).

entries.name: white_eyeshadow
entries.description: White [shadow](#shadow) applied over the eyelid, distinct from white [eyeliner](#eyeliner), which follows the lash line instead.

entries.name: yellow_eyeliner
entries.description: Yellow [eyeliner](#eyeliner) traced along the lash line, framing the eyes in an unusual, often stylised [shade](#shade). It records cosmetic colour applied at the eye's edge rather than a natural eye tone.

entries.name: white_eyeliner
entries.description: White liner drawn along the lash line, [standing](#standing) out sharply against the skin.

entries.name: grey_eyeliner
entries.description: Grey liner drawn along the lash line, softer than the usual black. Colour spread over the [lid](#lid) instead is [grey_eyeshadow](#grey_eyeshadow).

entries.name: brown_eyeliner
entries.description: Eyeliner drawn in brown along the lash line. It is the liner alone that is brown, not the [shadow](#shadow) or the eye itself.

entries.name: teeth
entries.description: The teeth are clearly drawn and noticeable, as in a wide [grin](#grin), a snarl, a bite or a sob. Most art leaves an open mouth's teeth out, so [tag](#tag) only when they stand out.

entries.name: fang
entries.description: A single pointed canine [tooth](#tooth) stands out, the [familiar](#familiar) cute anime fang. Several such [teeth](#teeth) are [fangs](#fangs), one coloured like the surrounding skin is [skin_fang](#skin_fang), and a whole mouth of points is [sharp_teeth](#sharp_teeth).

entries.name: upper_teeth_only
entries.description: An open mouth drawn showing only the top row of [teeth](#teeth), with the lower row hidden or left out entirely.

entries.name: fangs
entries.description: Two or more prominent pointed canine [teeth](#teeth), as worn by vampires, wolves and monsters. A lone one is [fang](#fang), a whole mouth of points is [sharp_teeth](#sharp_teeth), and the big lower teeth of orcs are [tusks](#tusks).

entries.name: sharp_teeth
entries.description: A full mouth of pointed [teeth](#teeth), not just the canines as with [fangs](#fangs). Signals a fierce, mischievous or monstrous character, or is used purely as a stylistic [choice](#choice). Implies teeth.

entries.name: skin_fang
entries.description: A single [fang](#fang) drawn in skin tone as part of the mouth's [outline](#outline), instead of a separate white [tooth](#tooth). A stylistic shorthand common in cute art.

entries.name: round_teeth
entries.description: A wide open [smile](#smile) where the upper front [teeth](#teeth) are drawn as one smooth semicircle. Reads as youthful and playful; [buck_teeth](#buck_teeth) means only the two front teeth stand out.

entries.name: fang_out
entries.description: One [fang](#fang) shows outside a closed mouth, [poking](#poking) over the lip. The shut mouth is what separates it from a fang glimpsed inside an open one.

entries.name: tusks
entries.description: Long [teeth](#teeth) protruding past the [lips](#lips), usually enlarged lower canines as seen on orcs, boars and elephants. Fangs are smaller and hang from the upper [jaw](#jaw) instead.

entries.name: skin_fangs
entries.description: Two [fangs](#fangs) drawn as skin-coloured notches in the mouth [outline](#outline) rather than white [teeth](#teeth). The paired form of [skin_fang](#skin_fang).

entries.name: buck_teeth
entries.description: The two upper front [teeth](#teeth) jut forward far enough to be obvious even at rest. Common on mouse and [rabbit](#rabbit) characters, and used in caricature for nerds and yokels.

entries.name: fangs_out
entries.description: Both [fangs](#fangs) show outside a closed mouth, the two-tooth counterpart of [fang_out](#fang_out). Common on vampires and beast characters at rest.

entries.name: lip_fangs
entries.description: Pointed [teeth](#teeth) showing over the lip even with the mouth closed, [resting](#resting) against it or jutting past it.

entries.name: braces
entries.description: Orthodontic brackets bonded across the [teeth](#teeth) and joined by a [wire](#wire), sometimes with coloured elastics. They show whenever the mouth opens and are often used as shorthand for a young character.

entries.name: missing_tooth
entries.description: One or more [teeth](#teeth) are plainly absent, leaving a gap in the [smile](#smile). Reads as childhood, a recent scuffle, or simply a hard-lived character.

entries.name: yellow_teeth
entries.description: Teeth given a yellow [cast](#cast) instead of white, suggesting age, neglect or a grubby character. It is not always about hygiene; some designs simply use the colour as a stylistic [choice](#choice).

entries.name: tooth
entries.description: One single tooth as the subject: a lone [fang](#fang) in a [grin](#grin), a lost [milk](#milk) tooth held up, a tooth kept as a [trophy](#trophy). A full set on show is [teeth](#teeth) instead.

entries.name: tooth_gap
entries.description: A visible [space](#space) between two [teeth](#teeth), most often the front pair. Not the same thing as a [tooth](#tooth) being missing altogether.

entries.name: mandibles
entries.description: The paired [jaw](#jaw) appendages either side of an insect's mouth, used to grip and cut. Drawn on [bug](#bug) characters and on monsters given insect faces.

entries.name: gold_teeth
entries.description: One or more [teeth](#teeth) capped in [gold](#gold) that catch the light when the mouth opens. Read as a [sign](#sign) of wealth, roguishness or a criminal past.

entries.name: extra_teeth
entries.description: More [teeth](#teeth) than a mouth should hold: extra rows, a [crowded](#crowded) [jaw](#jaw), or teeth set where none belong. Usually a monstrous touch.

entries.name: single_tooth
entries.description: Just one [tooth](#tooth) is drawn in the open mouth, the rest of the row left out entirely. A shorthand of simplified and cartoonish art styles.

entries.name: broken_tooth
entries.description: A [tooth](#tooth) chipped, cracked or snapped off. A blow to the mouth is the usual cause, and [blood](#blood) or bruising often comes with it.

entries.name: chipped_tooth
entries.description: One of the visible [teeth](#teeth) has a [corner](#corner) [broken](#broken) away. Usually a permanent feature on brawlers and rough characters rather than a fresh [injury](#injury).

entries.name: dark_skin
entries.description: Skin darker than the pale tone anime characters usually carry, whether it is the figure's natural colouring, a [tan](#tan) or an alternate palette. The sex-specific [dark-skinned_female](#dark-skinned_female) and [dark-skinned_male](#dark-skinned_male) go alongside it.

entries.name: brown_skin
entries.description: Skin of a brown tone across the body. It covers naturally brown complexions as readily as non-human characters whose hide is drawn brown.

entries.name: dark-skinned_female
entries.description: A female character whose complexion is [dark](#dark), deeper than the pale tone anime figures usually carry. It sits alongside the general [dark_skin](#dark_skin) [tag](#tag) rather than replacing it.

entries.name: colored_skin
entries.description: Skin in a colour [no](#no) human has, blue, green, purple, grey and so on, worn by [fantasy](#fantasy) races, demons, aliens, zombies and the like. Individual shades have their own tags such as [blue_skin](#blue_skin).

entries.name: dark-skinned_male
entries.description: A male character whose complexion is [dark](#dark), deeper than the pale tone anime figures usually carry. It sits alongside the general [dark_skin](#dark_skin) [tag](#tag) rather than replacing it.

entries.name: tan
entries.description: Skin darkened by [sun](#sun) exposure. When the untanned areas normally covered by a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) are visible, add [tanlines](#tanlines) as [well](#well).

entries.name: pale_skin
entries.description: Skin noticeably [lighter](#lighter) than an ordinary complexion, looking drained of colour or bleached. Skin that is literally white belongs to [white_skin](#white_skin). Used to suggest sickliness, sheltered nobility or an unearthly [nature](#nature).

entries.name: white_skin
entries.description: Skin that is entirely white with [no](#no) underlying pigment, like [snow](#snow) or [milk](#milk), seen on ghosts, dolls, and certain monsters. A very light but still pinkish tone belongs to [pale_skin](#pale_skin) instead, and this is the counterpart to black skin among the coloured-skin tags.

entries.name: blue_skin
entries.description: Skin coloured blue, as on [ice](#ice) spirits, aliens, [oni](#oni) and the [undead](#undead). Where the blue body is covered in fur or [scales](#scales), [blue_fur](#blue_fur) or [blue_scales](#blue_scales) describes it better.

entries.name: tanlines
entries.description: A visible [border](#border) between tanned and untanned skin, left by clothing worn in the [sun](#sun), most often in the shape of a [swimsuit](#swimsuit).

entries.name: green_skin
entries.description: Skin drawn green, as on orcs, goblins, zombies and some aliens. It is one of the coloured-skin [family](#family) rather than a [tan](#tan) or shading effect.

entries.name: white_fur
entries.description: Body fur that is white, on an [animal](#animal), an anthro character, or a kemonomimi's ears and [tail](#tail). Fur trim sewn onto clothing is the separate [fur_trim](#fur_trim) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: body_fur
entries.description: Fur growing from the character's own body instead of trimming their [clothes](#clothes), standard on anthro characters and many [monster](#monster) designs. Fur on a [coat](#coat) or a [collar](#collar) is [fur_(clothing)](#fur_(clothing)); unusually [heavy](#heavy) hair on a human may read as this too.

entries.name: multicolored_skin
entries.description: A character whose skin is made of two or more clearly separate colours, at least one of them unnatural — a body [split](#split) evenly between blue and red, for example. Natural variation such as [tan](#tan) lines, [blush](#blush) or bruising does not count; [tag](#tag) every skin colour present.

entries.name: grey_skin
entries.description: Skin drawn grey, as on zombies, golems, drow and some demons. Very light natural skin is [pale_skin](#pale_skin) and does not belong here.

entries.name: purple_skin
entries.description: A character whose skin is purple, typical of demons, aliens, or ghosts. Combine with [colored_skin](#colored_skin); fur or [scales](#scales) in purple take their own tags.

entries.name: red_skin
entries.description: A character whose skin is red all over, as on many [demon](#demon) girls and red [oni](#oni). A [blush](#blush) or [sunburn](#sunburn) does not count; the whole body has to read as red.

entries.name: two-tone_skin
entries.description: Skin coloured in exactly two distinct tones, as on demons or [patterned](#patterned) [monster](#monster) girls. Natural variation such as a [tan](#tan) or bruising does not count, and both skin colours should be tagged where possible.

entries.name: pink_skin
entries.description: A character whose skin is pink rather than any human tone, typical of demons, slimes, aliens and [fantasy](#fantasy) races. Ordinary flushed or blushing skin does not qualify.

entries.name: one-piece_tan
entries.description: Tan lines in the shape of a one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) or [leotard](#leotard), a pale [torso](#torso) set against darker arms, shoulders and [legs](#legs).

entries.name: brown_fur
entries.description: The character's own body fur is brown, on an anthro, feral or beast-eared design. Brown fur trimming a garment is [fur_trim](#fur_trim), not this.

entries.name: black_skin
entries.description: Skin coloured black like [ink](#ink) or [coal](#coal), seen on [shadow](#shadow) beings, demons and stylised designs; the counterpart to [white_skin](#white_skin). A [dark](#dark) human complexion is [dark_skin](#dark_skin), [very_dark_skin](#very_dark_skin) or [tan](#tan) and never this.

entries.name: black_fur
entries.description: Body fur coloured black, on an anthro, a feral [animal](#animal) or a furred humanoid. Add the species and any second fur colour; fur edging on clothing is [fur_trim](#fur_trim) instead.

entries.name: armpit_hair
entries.description: Hair growing in the hollow of the armpit, seen when the arm goes up. Goes together with [armpits](#armpits) and [body_hair](#body_hair).

entries.name: yellow_fur
entries.description: A character's body fur is yellow, as on Pikachu-like creatures, lions or golden anthros. Tag fur or the species alongside.

entries.name: very_dark_skin
entries.description: Skin a step deeper than [dark_skin](#dark_skin), generally used for characters drawn as Black. Ordinary [tan](#tan) or brown complexions stay at dark_skin.

entries.name: two-tone_fur
entries.description: A furred character whose [coat](#coat) shows exactly two colours, such as a brown body with a [cream](#cream) [belly](#belly). The two areas should read as clearly separate blocks of colour, not a gradient.

entries.name: colored_extremities
entries.description: Skin that shifts to another colour toward the hands or [feet](#feet), such as a demon's fingers darkening to black, either as a gradient or with a hard edge. Gloves, [socks](#socks), fur and [scales](#scales) in a different colour are not this.

entries.name: albino
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) with albinism, which wants all three signs together: white or grey hair, very pale skin, and eyes in red, pink, purple or blue. White hair on its own is simply [white_hair](#white_hair).

entries.name: blue_fur
entries.description: A furred body coloured blue, on an anthro, a feral [animal](#animal) or a furred humanoid. Pair it with the species and with any other fur colours present.

entries.name: hairy
entries.description: Visible, usually ungroomed body hair on at least two or three regions of the body, such as chest, arms and [legs](#legs). Hair in only one or two places takes the specific [tag](#tag) instead, such as [chest_hair](#chest_hair); thick fur-like growth over most of the body is [very_hairy](#very_hairy).

entries.name: arm_hair
entries.description: Visible hair on the [forearms](#forearms), sometimes [carrying](#carrying) on up to the shoulders. Usually drawn on men, and often together with [body_hair](#body_hair).

entries.name: yellow_skin
entries.description: Skin that is truly yellow, as on Simpsons-style characters, certain monsters or aliens. Not pale skin; [tag](#tag) [colored_skin](#colored_skin) as [well](#well).

entries.name: grey_fur
entries.description: A character whose body fur is grey, as on wolves, cats and many anthro designs. Fur used as trim on a garment is not covered here.

entries.name: pink_fur
entries.description: Body fur coloured pink on an [animal](#animal), a [furry](#furry) or a kemono character. A fur-trimmed garment is [fur_trim](#fur_trim) rather than this.

entries.name: bikini_tan
entries.description: Pale skin left in the shape of a [bikini](#bikini), or of a [bra](#bra) and [panties](#panties), where the [sun](#sun) did not reach. A particular form of [tanlines](#tanlines), and most obvious once the [swimsuit](#swimsuit) comes off.

entries.name: orange_fur
entries.description: Body fur in orange, as on foxes, tigers, ginger cats and many kemono designs. It covers animals, anthro characters and [animal](#animal) parts on a human alike.

entries.name: multicolored_fur
entries.description: A furred character or [animal](#animal) whose [coat](#coat) carries more than one colour, whether in patches, bands or a graded blend. Tag each colour present where it [can](#can) be named.

entries.name: body_hair
entries.description: Hair growing somewhere besides the scalp and face, on the arms, [legs](#legs), chest, [back](#back) or [belly](#belly), on a character of any [sex](#sex). Reach for it when [no](#no) narrower [tag](#tag) such as [chest_hair](#chest_hair) or [armpit_hair](#armpit_hair) applies; very thick growth may be [body_fur](#body_fur).

entries.name: cracked_skin
entries.description: Skin [split](#split) with cracks as though the character were made of stone, [porcelain](#porcelain) or dried [clay](#clay). Seen on golems, petrifying or corrupted characters and [broken](#broken) dolls; a [bleeding](#bleeding) wound is something else.

entries.name: red_fur
entries.description: A furred character whose [coat](#coat) is red, on an [animal](#animal), anthro or kemonomimi body. Describes the body's own fur; red fur on a garment is trim or a fur coat, not this.

entries.name: purple_fur
entries.description: Body fur that is purple, whether on an [animal](#animal), a [furry](#furry) character, or an animal-eared human's ears and [tail](#tail). Combine with fur and the relevant species.

entries.name: wrinkled_skin
entries.description: Lines and creases forming in the skin, most often from age though [sun](#sun) or hardship [can](#can) cause them too. It is a visual [marker](#marker) of an [old](#old) character, and pairs naturally with [old_woman](#old_woman) or [old_man](#old_man).

entries.name: patchwork_skin
entries.description: Skin made of separate pieces sewn together, sometimes visibly taken from more than one body, as on a stitched-together [creature](#creature) or a living [doll](#doll). Where the pieces differ in colour, [multicolored_skin](#multicolored_skin) fits as [well](#well).

entries.name: green_fur
entries.description: A character whose body fur is green, typically a green-furred [animal](#animal) or anthro. Fur used as trim on a garment is [fur_trim](#fur_trim) and does not belong here.

entries.name: orange_skin
entries.description: Skin that is literally orange, as on some monsters, aliens and cartoon designs. Neither a [tan](#tan) nor a [dark](#dark) complexion counts.

entries.name: gradient_skin
entries.description: Skin that blends gradually from one colour into one or more others across the body, arms darkening toward the hands for example. A kind of multicoloured skin; [tag](#tag) every skin colour involved.

entries.name: ganguro
entries.description: A loud [gyaru](#gyaru) look built on deeply tanned skin with orange or bleached hair, pale [lips](#lips), [heavy](#heavy) [dark](#dark) eye [makeup](#makeup) and bright [clothes](#clothes) on [platform](#platform) [shoes](#shoes). The [tan](#tan) reads as deliberately artificial rather than as [sun](#sun) on the skin.

entries.name: kuro_gyaru
entries.description: The deeply tanned strand of the [gyaru](#gyaru) look: a [dark](#dark) artificial [tan](#tan) set against bleached or pale hair, [heavy](#heavy) eye [makeup](#makeup) and showy [accessories](#accessories). It marks a styling [choice](#choice) rather than a natural complexion.

entries.name: see-through_body
entries.description: A character whose skin or whole body is [translucent](#translucent), so that things behind or inside show through, as with a [ghost](#ghost), a slime, or a [figure](#figure) [fading](#fading) away. May reveal bones or [organs](#organs); an entirely different image inside the body is [double_exposure](#double_exposure) instead.

entries.name: red_hands
entries.description: Hands whose skin is red while the rest of the body is another colour, as on some demons, spirits or [creature](#creature) designs. Skin-coloured hands do not count, nor do red [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: black_hands
entries.description: Hands coloured black while the rest of the skin or fur is another [shade](#shade), a marking rather than [gloves](#gloves). Disembodied black hands [reaching](#reaching) into the scene are shadow_hands.

entries.name: metal_skin
entries.description: Skin that genuinely reads as metal - with visible [seams](#seams), overlapping plates or a lustrous sheen - on androids, golems or elementals. Plain grey or yellow skin has its own tags, and whole [mecha](#mecha) without humanoid skin don't count.

entries.name: sparse_chest_hair
entries.description: Chest hair visible only over a small [patch](#patch), usually the upper or central chest, or drawn very thinly. The light end of the chest hair range.

entries.name: thick_chest_hair
entries.description: A dense [mat](#mat) of hair across a male character's chest. Pair with [chest_hair](#chest_hair) and [bare_pectorals](#bare_pectorals) or [topless_male](#topless_male) as fitting.

entries.name: sun_tattoo
entries.description: Pale skin left behind by a shaped covering, so the resulting [tan](#tan) takes on the crisp [outline](#outline) of a [tattoo](#tattoo). It is a tan line, not [ink](#ink); a real sun-shaped tattoo is tagged [sun_symbol](#sun_symbol) instead. Implies tan.

entries.name: aqua_skin
