entries.description: The skin itself is blue-green rather than any human tone. It marks aliens, spirits, slimes and similar non-human designs.

entries.name: pink_nose
entries.description: A pink [nose](#nose) or nose [leather](#leather), standard on cats, dogs and anthro characters and used for a rosy tip on human ones. One of the body-colour tags.

entries.name: armpit_hair_peek
entries.description: A few strands of underarm hair show past a lowered or slightly turned arm. Once the armpit is fully open to view, [plain](#plain) [armpit_hair](#armpit_hair) covers it.

entries.name: thick_arm_hair
entries.description: Noticeably [heavy](#heavy) hair growing on the [forearms](#forearms) and upper arms, drawn in rather than left smooth. Usually part of a rugged or bearish male design.

entries.name: thick_navel_hair
entries.description: A dense line of hair [running](#running) from the [navel](#navel) down the [stomach](#stomach), drawn in clearly. Often called a [happy](#happy) trail, and part of a [hairy](#hairy) male design.

entries.name: golden_arms
entries.description: Arms of [gold](#gold) instead of [flesh](#flesh), gleaming like [cast](#cast) metal from shoulder to fingertip. A feature of statue-like, crystalline and transformed characters.

entries.name: shorts_tan
entries.description: Pale bands on the upper [legs](#legs) left where [shorts](#shorts), swim trunks or [briefs](#briefs) kept off the [sun](#sun). Refers only to marks left by outer bottomwear, not a [bikini](#bikini) or a [shirt](#shirt). Implies [tanlines](#tanlines).

entries.name: sparse_navel_hair
entries.description: A faint trail of hair [running](#running) from the [navel](#navel) down the lower [belly](#belly), indicated with just a few soft strokes.

entries.name: sparse_arm_hair
entries.description: A light scatter of hair over the [forearms](#forearms), drawn as fine individual strokes rather than dense coverage. A small realism detail on adult figures.

entries.name: silver_skin
entries.description: Skin colored a reflective grey, as on statues, androids and other metallic beings. Painted with hard highlights rather than the soft shading of ordinary [flesh](#flesh).

entries.name: sparse_leg_hair
entries.description: A light covering of hair on the shins and [thighs](#thighs), drawn as scattered fine lines to give the [legs](#legs) a more naturalistic look.

entries.name: thick_leg_hair
entries.description: Heavy hair on the shins and [thighs](#thighs), drawn as visible strokes instead of smooth skin. Common on rugged male characters and on deliberately unidealised bodies.

entries.name: ass_hair
entries.description: Body hair growing on the buttocks, from a faint dusting to a [heavy](#heavy) covering. Usually drawn along with hair elsewhere on the body.

entries.name: spotted_fur
entries.description: Fur marked with a spotted pattern, as seen on cheetahs, leopards, hyenas or spotted dogs. Tag alongside the species and the fur's base colour.

entries.name: gold_skin
entries.description: Skin rendered in [gold](#gold), either as a metallic surface or as a deep gilded tone. Statues come to life, divine beings and gilded transformations wear it.

entries.name: back_hair
entries.description: Body hair growing across the [back](#back), generally [spreading](#spreading) down from the [nape](#nape) and the shoulders. How much there is varies from character to character, and it reads as a [marker](#marker) of a [hairy](#hairy) build.

entries.name: light-skinned_soles
entries.description: The undersides of the [feet](#feet) are drawn paler than the surrounding skin, generally on dark-skinned characters. Feet lightened only by [dirt](#dirt) or lighting are excluded.

entries.name: shirt_tan
entries.description: Pale skin where a [shirt](#shirt) or [tank](#tank) top covered the [torso](#torso), contrasted against tanned arms, [neck](#neck) and upper chest, printing the garment's [outline](#outline) onto the body. Implies [tanlines](#tanlines).

entries.name: armpit_stubble
entries.description: Short regrowth left after an armpit was shaved, drawn as a [shadow](#shadow) or a scatter of [dots](#dots). Smoothly hairless [armpits](#armpits) are not this.

entries.name: glowing_skin
entries.description: Skin that emits light rather than reflecting it, brightening the air around the body. Divine, spectral and transformed characters are drawn with it.

entries.name: striped_skin
entries.description: Stripes appearing directly on bare skin as part of a character's own colouring, without fur, [scales](#scales) or clothing [carrying](#carrying) the pattern.

entries.name: sunburn
entries.description: Skin flushed a [hot](#hot) red from too much [sun](#sun) or an intensely hot place. Unlike an ordinary [tan](#tan) the colour is [angry](#angry) and uneven, and it may be limited to the shoulders, [nose](#nose) and cheeks.

entries.name: revealing_tanlines
entries.description: Tan marks in unusual [shapes](#shapes) rather than the ordinary [swimsuit](#swimsuit) [outline](#outline), left by [rope](#rope) wrapped around the body, a [mask](#mask), straps, or lettering. The pattern says something about what was worn while [sunbathing](#sunbathing).

entries.name: shedding
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) or animal-featured character casting off its outer covering: fur coming away in clumps, [feathers](#feathers) [dropping](#dropping), or skin [peeling](#peeling) free. A natural cycle rather than an [injury](#injury).

entries.name: aqua_fur
entries.description: A creature's [coat](#coat) is blue-green, over the whole body or across a marked [patch](#patch). Used mostly on anthro and [animal](#animal) designs.

entries.name: light-skinned_palms
entries.description: The [palms](#palms) are drawn distinctly paler than the rest of the skin, a touch often given to very [dark](#dark) or unnaturally coloured characters. Palms merely [catching](#catching) the light do not count.

entries.name: shaved_body
entries.description: Body hair has been removed, leaving the arms, [legs](#legs), chest or [groin](#groin) smooth. Notable mainly on a character who would ordinarily be drawn with visible hair there.

entries.name: accessory_tan
entries.description: Pale marks left on tanned skin by something other than ordinary clothing, such as bracelets, straps, [gloves](#gloves) or legwear. The shape of the missing item stays readable in the untanned [patch](#patch).

entries.name: colored_armpit_hair
entries.description: Underarm hair drawn in a definite colour rather than a [plain](#plain) [dark](#dark) tone. Where it differs from the hair on the head, mismatched_armpit_hair applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: presenting_tanlines
entries.description: A [strap](#strap) is tugged aside or a hem lifted to reveal the pale band of skin left by a [swimsuit](#swimsuit). Usually done matter-of-factly rather than as a tease.

entries.name: starry_skin
entries.description: Skin [patterned](#patterned) with stars or a night-sky texture, as though the body were made of [space](#space). Common on cosmic and celestial characters.

entries.name: sparse_ass_hair
entries.description: A thin dusting of body hair across the buttocks, sketched as a few fine strands rather than thick growth.

entries.name: thick_ass_hair
entries.description: Visible hair growing across the buttocks, rendered as strokes rather than left bare. Goes with the same deliberately [hairy](#hairy) body styling as [heavy](#heavy) chest or leg hair.

entries.name: red_face
entries.description: The face is coloured red while the rest of the body may be a different [shade](#shade). Describes a body colour rather than a [blush](#blush).

entries.name: green_face
entries.description: The face is coloured green while the rest of the body may be shaded differently. It turns up most on masked-face [markings](#markings) in [furry](#furry) and [creature](#creature) designs.

entries.name: pink_face
entries.description: The face is coloured pink while the rest of the body may be another [shade](#shade). It records body colouring rather than a [blush](#blush).

entries.name: purple_face
entries.description: The face is coloured purple while the rest of the body may be a different [shade](#shade). Records a body colour, not an expression.

entries.name: facial_mark
entries.description: A simple mark on the face, drawn on, [stuck](#stuck) on, tattooed or born with, such as a stripe on the cheek or a symbol on the [forehead](#forehead). Elaborate designs belong to [facial_tattoo](#facial_tattoo), and scars and moles are excluded.

entries.name: veins
entries.description: Blood vessels [standing](#standing) out under the skin, drawn as raised lines on arms, hands, [breasts](#breasts) or genitals. Usually a [sign](#sign) of strain, muscle or arousal; a throbbing [forehead](#forehead) mark for anger has its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: forehead_mark
entries.description: Anything from a single dot to an elaborate [device](#device) set in the middle of the brow. It belongs to the skin rather than being an ornament worn there, and is a kind of [facial_mark](#facial_mark).

entries.name: whisker_markings
entries.description: Lines or [paint](#paint) drawn on the cheeks to resemble [animal](#animal) [whiskers](#whiskers). A [facial](#facial) mark rather than real whiskers, and not tied to any one specific character.

entries.name: body_markings
entries.description: Permanent patterns in the skin of a human-shaped character who is mutated, part [animal](#animal) or not human at all: lines, blocks of colour, animal-like patches. Deliberate [ink](#ink) is a [tattoo](#tattoo); on a [plain](#plain) human this is what a [birthmark](#birthmark) would be.

entries.name: lipstick_mark
entries.description: A lip-shaped print left by a made-up [kiss](#kiss) on skin, a [letter](#letter) or another surface. A [ring](#ring) around a [penis](#penis) is [lipstick_ring](#lipstick_ring), and words written in the stuff are lipstick_writing.

entries.name: body_freckles
entries.description: Freckles scattered over the shoulders, arms, chest or elsewhere on the body rather than only across the [nose](#nose) and cheeks. Freckles confined to the face take the [plain](#plain) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: teardrop_facial_mark
entries.description: A tear-shaped mark below one eye, drawn as part of a character's design or face [paint](#paint) rather than an actual [falling](#falling) tear. An inked version of the same shape is [teardrop_tattoo](#teardrop_tattoo).

entries.name: heart_facial_mark
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) marked on the face, usually on a cheek or below an eye. It is a mark or small [tattoo](#tattoo) on the skin rather than [makeup](#makeup) or a stuck-on [sticker](#sticker).

entries.name: veiny_arms
entries.description: Visible vein lines [running](#running) along the arms, a common detail on [muscular](#muscular) or straining characters.

entries.name: sticker_on_face
entries.description: A [sticker](#sticker) worn somewhere on the face, most often as a small decorative piece on the cheek. Functions like a temporary [tattoo](#tattoo) or a piece of [festival](#festival) face [paint](#paint).

entries.name: tiger_stripes
entries.description: Dark stripes in a [tiger](#tiger) pattern on skin or fur, as body [markings](#markings) rather than a print on [cloth](#cloth). Common on [tiger_girl](#tiger_girl) characters and anthro tigers.

entries.name: star_facial_mark
entries.description: A star-shaped mark or [tattoo](#tattoo) on the face, such as on a cheek or beneath an eye.

entries.name: birthmark
entries.description: A natural mark carried from birth, drawn as a [patch](#patch), blotch or spot of different colour somewhere on the body. Distinct from a small raised [mole](#mole) and from tattoos or painted [facial](#facial) marks.

entries.name: crescent_facial_mark
entries.description: A crescent-shaped mark or [tattoo](#tattoo) on the face, most often set on the [forehead](#forehead). A permanent marking rather than [makeup](#makeup).

entries.name: triangle_facial_mark
entries.description: A triangular mark on the face, whether painted, tattooed or natural to the character. It [can](#can) point in any direction and can be solid, outlined, or drawn as a [corner](#corner) wedge.

entries.name: calico
entries.description: A patchwork [coat](#coat) of white, orange and black, the tricolour marking of a mike [cat](#cat). It applies equally to cat girls, printed [cloth](#cloth) and anything else [carrying](#carrying) that combination.

entries.name: calico_(pattern)
entries.description: White, black and orange laid down in irregular patches, the [coat](#coat) pattern named after the [cat](#cat) that wears it. Used for the [markings](#markings) of animals and anthro characters alike.

entries.name: mark_under_eye
entries.description: A small painted or drawn mark directly beneath one eye, part of the character's face design rather than a blemish. A [plain](#plain) [dark](#dark) dot instead reads as a [mole](#mole).

entries.name: handprint
entries.description: The shape a hand leaves behind when it touches a surface, printed in [paint](#paint), [dust](#dust), [mud](#mud), [blood](#blood) or [flour](#flour). It also covers reddened marks left on skin by a slap or a grip.

entries.name: mark_under_both_eyes
entries.description: Matching marks [sitting](#sitting) below each eye, sometimes drawn straight onto the lower lids. Keep it for coloured or shaped marks, since two [plain](#plain) [dark](#dark) [dots](#dots) are [mole_under_each_eye](#mole_under_each_eye).

entries.name: freckles_on_body
entries.description: Freckles somewhere other than the face, across the arms, chest, [back](#back) or [legs](#legs). Use it when the spotting reaches past the usual cheeks-and-nose placement.

entries.name: bindi
entries.description: A coloured dot or small jewel worn at the centre of the [forehead](#forehead), a mark of Hindu, Jain and Buddhist practice. Where a forehead dot carries [no](#no) such meaning, [forehead_mark](#forehead_mark) or [circle_facial_mark](#circle_facial_mark) is the better [tag](#tag).

entries.name: circle_facial_mark
entries.description: A round mark on the face, painted or natural, such as a dot on the [forehead](#forehead) or a [circle](#circle) on each cheek. Only the shape matters; colour and placement vary freely.

entries.name: ear_birthmark
entries.description: A natural [dark](#dark) mark or [patch](#patch) on the skin of the ear. A small identifying feature, usually visible only in close views of the head.

entries.name: lipstick_mark_on_face
entries.description: A lip-shaped smear of [lipstick](#lipstick) on a cheek, [forehead](#forehead) or mouth, left behind by a [kiss](#kiss).

entries.name: striped_fur
entries.description: Fur that carries stripes, as on a [tiger](#tiger), [zebra](#zebra) or striped [cat](#cat). For anthro and feral characters; use striped_markings for stripes as a general marking pattern on other bodies.

entries.name: marking_on_cheek
entries.description: A painted, tattooed or natural mark on the cheek; one side or both qualify. Related to [facial_mark](#facial_mark) and to the [huadian](#huadian) worn on the [forehead](#forehead) in Chinese [dress](#dress).

entries.name: markings
entries.description: Patterns on skin or fur that are not tattoos: birthmarks, natural patches, lines that light up as a character powers up, or symbols set on the [forehead](#forehead) of a magical character. Writing put on with a [pen](#pen) belongs here too.

entries.name: veiny_hands
entries.description: The backs of the hands show pronounced [veins](#veins). It does not extend to veins on the [forearms](#forearms) or upper arms, which fall under [veiny_arms](#veiny_arms) instead.

entries.name: glowing_markings
entries.description: Runes, sigils, [tribal](#tribal) [shapes](#shapes) or [spots](#spots) on skin, fur or [scales](#scales) that give off light of their own. Magical, demonic and deep-sea-styled designs lean on them.

entries.name: ass_freckles
entries.description: Freckles scattered over the buttocks, usually matching the spotting found elsewhere on the body. Most often drawn on pale skin.

entries.name: diamond_facial_mark
entries.description: A rhombus drawn on the face, on the [forehead](#forehead), a cheek or beneath an eye, hollow or filled in any of its variants. A design element rather than [makeup](#makeup).

entries.name: purple_stripes
entries.description: Purple stripe [markings](#markings) across a body, usually over fur or [scales](#scales). The underlying base colour is recorded by a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: spots
entries.description: A pattern of rounded spots on a creature's fur, [scales](#scales) or skin, such as a leopard's rosettes or a dalmatian's [dots](#dots).

entries.name: heart_on_cheek
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) on the cheek, painted, [stuck](#stuck) on as a [sticker](#sticker), or part of the natural pattern of skin or fur.

entries.name: glowing_lines
entries.description: Bright lines [running](#running) across a body, most often on cyborgs, constructs and enchanted characters, though they [can](#can) read as a luminous [tattoo](#tattoo). Do not confuse them with [notice_lines](#notice_lines) or with a surrounding [aura](#aura).

entries.name: veiny_face
entries.description: Veins stand out across the face, on the temples, [forehead](#forehead) or cheeks, usually a [sign](#sign) of strain, rage or something inhuman.

entries.name: lipstick_mark_on_neck
entries.description: A [lipstick](#lipstick) print on the [neck](#neck), left by a [kiss](#kiss) from a made-up mouth.

entries.name: cross_facial_mark
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) of any variety marked on the face, whether a [birthmark](#birthmark), a [tattoo](#tattoo) or something painted on. It sits on the skin as part of the character, unlike a [comic](#comic) symbol [floating](#floating) beside the head.

entries.name: lipstick_mark_on_breast
entries.description: A [lipstick](#lipstick) print left on a breast by kissing or mouthing it.

entries.name: veiny_thighs
entries.description: Veins stand out visibly across the surface of the [thighs](#thighs), typically drawn on athletic or heavily muscled [legs](#legs), and often shown alongside [veiny_arms](#veiny_arms) or [veiny_hands](#veiny_hands) on the same [figure](#figure).

entries.name: lipstick_mark_on_ass
entries.description: A lip-shaped print of [lipstick](#lipstick) left on a buttock by a [kiss](#kiss).

entries.name: sticker_on_arm
entries.description: An adhesive [sticker](#sticker) pressed onto a character's bare arm, the kind handed out at events or peeled off a [toy](#toy) sheet. Small and bright, and usually at odds with the rest of the outfit.

entries.name: arm_markings
entries.description: Bands, stripes, [spots](#spots) or sigil-like [shapes](#shapes) [running](#running) along the arms, part of the skin or fur itself. Patterned sleeves and [ink](#ink) take other tags.

entries.name: lipstick_mark_on_stomach
entries.description: A [lipstick](#lipstick) print on the [belly](#belly), left behind by a [kiss](#kiss).

entries.name: sticker_on_leg
entries.description: A [sticker](#sticker) [stuck](#stuck) to a character's thigh or calf. Reads as playful decoration rather than a [tattoo](#tattoo) or a body marking.

entries.name: lichtenberg_figure
entries.description: A branching, fern-like tracery left behind by an electrical discharge, drawn across skin as a [lightning](#lightning) [scar](#scar) or [spreading](#spreading) over a surface.

entries.name: lipstick_mark_on_leg
entries.description: A [lipstick](#lipstick) print left on a thigh, knee or calf by a [kiss](#kiss).

entries.name: star_on_cheek
entries.description: A star drawn, painted or tattooed on a character's cheek. Common on idols, cheerleaders and festival-goers.

entries.name: flower_facial_mark
entries.description: A blossom-shaped mark [sitting](#sitting) on the skin of the face, on a cheek, [temple](#temple) or brow. It belongs to the character rather than being an object [resting](#resting) against the face; pair it with [flower_(symbol)](#flower_(symbol)) rather than [flower](#flower).

entries.name: veiny_neck
entries.description: Cords of vein stand out along the side or front of the [neck](#neck), usually drawn during exertion, [shouting](#shouting) or strain.

entries.name: teeth_print
entries.description: The mark a bite leaves behind: a curved row of dents pressed into skin, or a [crescent](#crescent) taken out of a piece of [food](#food). The [teeth](#teeth) themselves need not be visible in frame.

entries.name: orange_stripes
entries.description: Orange stripe [markings](#markings) across the body, most often on fur. The base colour of the body is tagged on its own.

entries.name: green_stripes
entries.description: Green stripe [markings](#markings) [running](#running) across a body, typically over fur or [scales](#scales). The underlying body colour keeps its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: grey_stripes
entries.description: Grey stripe [markings](#markings) on a body, most often across fur. The base colour of the body carries its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: brown_stripes
entries.description: Brown stripe [markings](#markings) [running](#running) across a body, most often over fur, [scales](#scales) or hide. Whatever base colour the body carries is tagged on its own.

entries.name: plump
entries.description: A softly rounded, slightly [heavy](#heavy) [figure](#figure) that stops short of [fat](#fat), with fuller [thighs](#thighs), [belly](#belly) and arms while still shapely. Do not use it for a merely [curvy](#curvy) body, and never combine it with fat or [obese](#obese).

entries.name: fat
entries.description: An overweight character, heavier than [plump](#plump) but short of [obese](#obese). It applies to any [sex](#sex) or species; add [fat_man](#fat_man), [fat_woman](#fat_woman) or another specific [tag](#tag) where one fits.

entries.name: fat_man
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) a great deal of extra [weight](#weight), often [cast](#cast) as the leering older man of explicit works. Not the wartime [bomb](#bomb) or the game [weapon](#weapon) of the same name.

entries.name: petite
entries.description: A small overall frame that still carries adult proportions such as gently curved hips. A [tall](#tall) slender woman is [skinny](#skinny), an impossibly tiny one is [minigirl](#minigirl) or [miniboy](#miniboy), and a short very [curvy](#curvy) one is [shortstack](#shortstack).

entries.name: fat_woman
entries.description: A heavyset female [figure](#figure) with a broad waist, full [belly](#belly) and thick limbs. It describes the build alone and says nothing about [dress](#dress) or action.

entries.name: skinny
entries.description: A noticeably thin frame with little body [fat](#fat), [ribs](#ribs) or bony limbs perhaps showing. A small girl of normal proportions is [petite](#petite); starvation-level thinness is [emaciated](#emaciated).

entries.name: shortstack
entries.description: A short adult [figure](#figure) with large [breasts](#breasts) and wide hips, typically of a [fantasy](#fantasy) race such as goblins but also seen on humans of similar proportions. Distinct from oppai_loli, who looks childlike apart from the curves.

entries.name: tall_female
entries.description: A woman drawn with the proportions of a [tall](#tall) person, shown as tall next to others or explicitly noted to be so. An elongated [figure](#figure) from artistic style alone does not qualify.

entries.name: tall
entries.description: An ambiguous [height](#height) [tag](#tag); prefer [tall_female](#tall_female) for a notably tall woman, [height_difference](#height_difference) for a [contrast](#contrast) between characters, or a height [chart](#chart) tag for the other senses of the word.

entries.name: obese
entries.description: A body far heavier than merely [fat](#fat), drawn with great bulk and deep folds. It sits at the top of the [weight](#weight) scale, a step above fat.

entries.name: muffin_top
entries.description: Flesh at the waist squeezed up and out over the band of trousers, a [skirt](#skirt) or [underwear](#underwear) cut too tight for it, [spilling](#spilling) above the waistline. The tightness of the garment is as much the subject as the body.

entries.name: fat_rolls
entries.description: Several creased folds of [flesh](#flesh) [stack](#stack) across the [belly](#belly) or the sides from [carrying](#carrying) extra [weight](#weight). A single [crease](#crease) on an otherwise ordinary [stomach](#stomach) is not enough; the folds need real bulk behind them.

entries.name: big_head
entries.description: The head is drawn out of proportion to the body beneath it. Chibi work pushes this furthest, letting the head outsize the rest of the [figure](#figure) so [expressions](#expressions) read clearly.

entries.name: emaciated
entries.description: Painfully thin: hollow cheeks, [ribs](#ribs) showing, limbs like sticks. It points to starvation, illness or utter exhaustion, where a merely slender [figure](#figure) would be slim or [skinny](#skinny).

entries.name: tall_male
entries.description: A male character drawn conspicuously [tall](#tall), usually made clear by [comparison](#comparison) with others in the frame rather than by his proportions alone.

entries.name: love_handles
entries.description: Soft pads of [fat](#fat) at the sides of the waist and the small of the [back](#back), bulging gently over a waistband. They mark a fuller, softer [figure](#figure) without implying obesity.

entries.name: small_head
entries.description: A head drawn too small for the body beneath it, [throwing](#throwing) the figure's proportions off. Counting how many head-heights [tall](#tall) the character stands is the quickest check, since roughly seven and a half is normal.

entries.name: bloated
entries.description: A [belly](#belly) swollen outward [well](#well) past the character's usual shape. Nothing is claimed about the cause, which may be overeating, [gas](#gas) or something held inside.

entries.name: muscular
entries.description: A visibly bulked-up physique — thick through the arms, [neck](#neck) and shoulders and broader all round — built by hard [training](#training) rather than merely defined. A lean athletic build is [toned](#toned), and the two never sit on one character; a wrestler's gut [can](#can) take [belly](#belly) or [plump](#plump) alongside, and bared [tissue](#tissue) in an [anatomy](#anatomy) drawing is exposed muscle.

entries.name: wide_hips
entries.description: Hips noticeably broader than average, at least as wide as the shoulders. It is a body-shape [tag](#tag) independent of pose, and often paired with [thick_thighs](#thick_thighs) or [curvy](#curvy).

entries.name: curvy
entries.description: A fuller, exaggerated feminine [figure](#figure): pronounced large [breasts](#breasts), wide hips and a marked waist. Merely having visible breasts or hips is not enough. Rounder, softer bodies take [plump](#plump) or [fat](#fat).

entries.name: abs
entries.description: Clearly defined [stomach](#stomach) muscles, the six-pack. A merely firm [belly](#belly) with a faint centre line is [linea_alba](#linea_alba), and muscles showing through tight opaque clothing take [covered_abs](#covered_abs).

entries.name: muscular_male
entries.description: A man built like a bodybuilder, with [heavy](#heavy) [biceps](#biceps), cut [abs](#abs), a deep chest and broad shoulders. Judge by overall thickness through the arms, [neck](#neck) and waist rather than chest size alone; a lean build is [toned](#toned), and a heavy gut [can](#can) add [belly](#belly) or [plump](#plump).

entries.name: toned
entries.description: A lean, athletic build with little [fat](#fat) and perhaps visible [abs](#abs), but slim rather than bulky; a runner rather than a bodybuilder. Never used together with [muscular](#muscular) on the same character, and pectoral size alone does not decide it.

entries.name: muscular_female
entries.description: A woman with [heavy](#heavy) trained musculature: thicker arms, [legs](#legs) and [torso](#torso) [reading](#reading) as [strong](#strong) without erasing her femininity. Abs alone fall short, a slim athletic build is [toned](#toned) instead, and women deliberately drawn to look like men do not belong here.

entries.name: toned_male
entries.description: A man with visible definition from low body [fat](#fat), lean rather than bulky, sometimes called ottermode. Not combined with [muscular](#muscular) on the same character, and [pectorals](#pectorals) alone are [no](#no) criterion.

entries.name: toned_female
entries.description: A woman with an athletic, lightly muscled body that stays feminine rather than bulky. Do not [tag](#tag) [muscular](#muscular) alongside it for a single character; a defined midline alone is [linea_alba](#linea_alba).

entries.name: narrow_waist
entries.description: A waist noticeably slimmer than the body around it. As a rough [guide](#guide), less than half the width of the hips, or about as narrow as the head.

entries.name: biceps
entries.description: The muscle on the front of the upper arm between shoulder and elbow, drawn large or held flexed. It goes with [muscular](#muscular) builds and with [poses](#poses) that leave the arm bare.

entries.name: forearms
entries.description: The stretch of arm between elbow and wrist drawn with pronounced muscle, especially flexed or with [veins](#veins) [standing](#standing) out. The attention paid to that section is the point of the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: covered_abs
entries.description: Stomach muscles [reading](#reading) as an [outline](#outline) through opaque, close-fitting clothing such as a [swimsuit](#swimsuit), [bodysuit](#bodysuit) or [leotard](#leotard). The [abs](#abs) are not bare; a visible [stomach](#stomach) takes the abs [tag](#tag).

entries.name: thick_arms
entries.description: Arms drawn heavier than the norm, whether in the forearm, the upper arm, or both. Often paired with [muscular](#muscular) or [plump](#plump) depending on the overall build.

entries.name: obliques
entries.description: Well-defined oblique muscles down the sides of the [belly](#belly), the ridges [running](#running) from the lower [ribs](#ribs) toward the [groin](#groin). Reserve it for visible muscle; [plain](#plain) hip lines and hip bones do not count, and it shows most readily on men.

entries.name: strongman_waist
entries.description: A thick, wide midsection typical of strongmen rather than the tapered waist of a bodybuilder, valuing raw power over a sculpted line. Pair with [belly](#belly) and [plump](#plump) for a softer look, but some visible muscle should still show.

entries.name: oversized_limbs
entries.description: A character design that gives the arms or [legs](#legs) proportions far beyond the rest of the body, and does so on purpose. Seen on certain [monster](#monster) girls and on heavily stylised fighters.

entries.name: broad_shoulders
entries.description: The shoulders are markedly wide against the waist, [giving](#giving) the [torso](#torso) a V-shaped [outline](#outline). It reads as a mark of a powerful or masculine build.

entries.name: asymmetrical_arms
entries.description: The arms do not match, one noticeably thicker, longer or more muscled than the other. Sometimes drawn as a joke about a character's habits.

entries.name: oversized_forearms
entries.description: Forearms and hands drawn much too large for the rest of the body. A deliberate design trait on brawlers, cartoon figures and [monster](#monster) characters rather than an anatomical slip.

entries.name: strong
entries.description: A character shown displaying outright superhuman strength, such as lifting or [breaking](#breaking) something far past ordinary human limits. It is the visible feat that earns the [tag](#tag), not simply a [muscular](#muscular) build.

entries.name: long_arms
entries.description: Arms drawn far longer than human proportion allows, and deliberately so, as a [creature](#creature) trait or a stylistic stretch. Accidental [distortion](#distortion) from [clumsy](#clumsy) drawing belongs to [bad_anatomy](#bad_anatomy).

entries.name: v-taper
entries.description: A build with broad shoulders, [back](#back) and traps narrowing down to a small waist, so the [torso](#torso) reads as a V. Usually drawn lean enough that the muscle shows through, the opposite of a thick-waisted strongman shape.

entries.name: back_muscles
entries.description: A [muscular](#muscular) [back](#back) drawn with its parts distinct: the broad [wings](#wings) of the lats, the ridge of the traps and the groove [running](#running) down the [spine](#spine). It is nearly always seen from behind with the [torso](#torso) bare or half-bare.

entries.name: hip_dips
entries.description: The line from waist to thigh steps inward instead of curving smoothly, leaving a notch at the side of the hip. It ranges from a faint dent to a squared or violin-like [outline](#outline); smoothly curved hips do not count.

entries.name: muscular_child
entries.description: A kid or young teenager drawn with a genuinely built physique rather than a merely trim one. The proportions should read as bodybuilding on a small frame.

entries.name: pear_shaped_figure
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) noticeably broader through the hips and [thighs](#thighs) than through the shoulders and chest, so the [silhouette](#silhouette) narrows as it rises.

entries.name: triceps
entries.description: The muscle on the [back](#back) of the upper arm, drawn with visible definition as a [marker](#marker) of a [toned](#toned) or [muscular](#muscular) build. Stands out most when the arm is posed so the muscle catches the light.

entries.name: shredded_muscles
entries.description: A build [carrying](#carrying) almost [no](#no) [fat](#fat) over the muscles, so each group reads as a separate, sharply defined shape and the [veins](#veins) stand out. Leaner and harder-edged than an ordinary [muscular](#muscular) physique.

entries.name: deltoids
entries.description: The rounded shoulder muscles [standing](#standing) out where the arm meets the [torso](#torso). Shows up on [muscular](#muscular) builds, generally alongside [abs](#abs) and other definition tags.

entries.name: long_torso
entries.description: A trunk drawn stretched out relative to the limbs, [pushing](#pushing) the waist and hips low down the [figure](#figure). Sometimes a deliberate stylisation, sometimes an error of proportion.

entries.name: box_body
entries.description: The [torso](#torso) is drawn as a flat rectangular block instead of an organic shape, with limbs [stuck](#stuck) onto its edges. Mascots, robots and heavily simplified cartoon designs are built this way.

entries.name: breasts
entries.description: The breasts are noticeable in the picture, clothed or bare. Add a size such as [small_breasts](#small_breasts), [medium_breasts](#medium_breasts) or [large_breasts](#large_breasts), and whatever is happening to them, from [cleavage](#cleavage) to [breast_press](#breast_press); a flat chest is not this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: large_breasts
entries.description: Breasts bigger than medium: roughly the volume of a sphere as wide as the character's face, but still smaller than her head. Anything past that is [huge_breasts](#huge_breasts).

entries.name: cleavage
entries.description: The [valley](#valley) between a woman's [breasts](#breasts), shown by a low neckline or an open top. Drawn as a single curve, or with a small extra line making a Y at the top; breasts held apart with [no](#no) valley is [breasts_apart](#breasts_apart).

entries.name: medium_breasts
entries.description: Breasts larger than a handful but smaller than the character's face - bigger than [small_breasts](#small_breasts), short of [large_breasts](#large_breasts). The middle step on the breast-size scale.

entries.name: small_breasts
entries.description: Breasts bigger than a [flat_chest](#flat_chest) but under [medium_breasts](#medium_breasts), roughly a palmful, an AA to B [cup](#cup). Tag beside [breasts](#breasts).

entries.name: huge_breasts
entries.description: Breasts bigger than the character's head but less than twice its size. One step above [large_breasts](#large_breasts) and below [gigantic_breasts](#gigantic_breasts) on the size [ladder](#ladder).

entries.name: flat_chest
entries.description: A female character with [no](#no) bust at all. Anything larger but still modest is [small_breasts](#small_breasts); a flat chest is not also tagged [breasts](#breasts), and the [tag](#tag) is not used for [child](#child) characters.

entries.name: pectorals
entries.description: A male character's chest muscles drawn as a feature in their own right, bare or shaped beneath clothing. Size variants are [large_pectorals](#large_pectorals) and [huge_pectorals](#huge_pectorals), and showing them through an [opening](#opening) is [pectoral_cleavage](#pectoral_cleavage).

entries.name: breasts_apart
entries.description: The [breasts](#breasts) sit [well](#well) apart, [pointing](#pointing) away from each other with the skin over the sternum in view, whether from gravity while [lying](#lying) down or from being held aside. It is the opposite of [cleavage](#cleavage), and does not [cover](#cover) breasts too small to meet or separated by an object in between.

entries.name: large_pectorals
entries.description: A male chest whose [pectorals](#pectorals) are markedly bigger than usual, roughly the size of the face or more. It normally goes with a [muscular](#muscular) build; on a slim one add [toned_male](#toned_male).

entries.name: between_breasts
entries.description: Something other than a [penis](#penis) is held or pressed in the [cleavage](#cleavage): a [necktie](#necktie), a [phone](#phone), a [card](#card), a [drink](#drink), or another person's arm or head. When it is a penis, the [tag](#tag) is [paizuri](#paizuri) instead.

entries.name: gigantic_breasts
entries.description: Breasts a step beyond [huge_breasts](#huge_breasts), each more than twice the size of the head. The top rung of the [ladder](#ladder) that runs from [flat_chest](#flat_chest) through [large_breasts](#large_breasts) and huge_breasts.

entries.name: hanging_breasts
entries.description: Breasts [heavy](#heavy) enough that, once their owner tips forward or stoops, they [swing](#swing) clear of the [torso](#torso) instead of [lying](#lying) against it. The angle of the pose is what makes the [tag](#tag) apply.

entries.name: bare_pectorals
entries.description: A male chest is exposed while the character still wears something on the upper body, whether revealing, [torn](#torn), [unfastened](#unfastened) or halfway off. Nude and [topless](#topless) characters are excluded, and partly covered pecs take [pectoral_cleavage](#pectoral_cleavage), [underpec](#underpec) or [sidepec](#sidepec).

entries.name: strap_gap
entries.description: A visible [space](#space) between a girl's chest and the straps of her [bra](#bra), [bikini](#bikini) or top, usually because of breast size or shape. If the gap comes from lifting the [strap](#strap), [tag](#tag) [strap_lift](#strap_lift) instead.

entries.name: pectoral_cleavage
entries.description: The groove between well-built male [pectorals](#pectorals) showing through an open [collar](#collar) or a low neckline, the male answer to [cleavage](#cleavage). Not for flat-chested men, and not once the chest is bare, which is [topless_male](#topless_male) or [bare_pectorals](#bare_pectorals). Add [sidepec](#sidepec) for [tank](#tank) tops and [overalls](#overalls).

entries.name: sagging_breasts
entries.description: Breasts drawn with a natural downward droop instead of the perky shape usual in anime art. Not for [breasts](#breasts) simply [hanging](#hanging) because the character bends forward; small breasts [can](#can) sag too, though it is rarer.

entries.name: hair_over_breasts
entries.description: A woman's long hair falls forward over her [breasts](#breasts), whether or not it hides anything. When it does hide the [nipples](#nipples), add [hair_censor](#hair_censor) alongside it.

entries.name: unaligned_breasts
entries.description: Breasts [pointing](#pointing) or [bouncing](#bouncing) in different directions, one tilted up while the other tilts down. Breasts pushed outward to the sides instead is [breasts_apart](#breasts_apart).

entries.name: perky_breasts
entries.description: Breasts that turn distinctly upward of their own accord, without a push-up [bra](#bra) [holding](#holding) them there. The opposite state is [sagging_breasts](#sagging_breasts).

entries.name: strap_between_breasts
entries.description: A shoulder [strap](#strap) from a [bag](#bag), [guitar](#guitar) or seat [belt](#belt) runs down between the [breasts](#breasts), pressing them apart. Known in Japan as pai-slash.

entries.name: veiny_breasts
entries.description: Veins showing through the skin of the [breasts](#breasts), often used as a [sign](#sign) of size, [lactation](#lactation) or pregnancy. The lines [can](#can) be faint, so look closely before applying the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pointy_breasts
entries.description: Breasts drawn with a conical, forward-jutting shape ending in a point, whether perky or sagging. A shape [tag](#tag), independent of size.

entries.name: between_pectorals
entries.description: An object pressed between a man's pectoral muscles, the male counterpart of [between_breasts](#between_breasts). When it is a [penis](#penis) the [tag](#tag) is [pecjob](#pecjob), and when it is another character's head, [head_between_pecs](#head_between_pecs).

entries.name: huge_pectorals
entries.description: Pectoral muscles larger than the character's head, common on non-human and heavily built male figures and sometimes drawn like [breasts](#breasts). An ordinary defined chest is simply [pectorals](#pectorals).

entries.name: puffy_chest
entries.description: A bare male chest with a soft rounded swell rather than a flat plane, [reading](#reading) much like an early-adolescent female chest. Distinct from [pectorals](#pectorals), which come from muscle rather than softness.

entries.name: hair_between_breasts
entries.description: A strand of long hair [hanging](#hanging) down the chest so that it drops into the [cleavage](#cleavage). Purely a [note](#note) about where the hair happens to lie.

entries.name: covered_pectorals
entries.description: The shape of the chest muscles pushes through a tight [shirt](#shirt) or [suit](#suit). The chest stays clothed and only its contour is visible.

entries.name: hair_over_one_breast
entries.description: Long hair draped across a single breast, leaving the other uncovered. Add [hair_censor](#hair_censor) when the strands actually conceal the nipple.

entries.name: inconvenient_breasts
entries.description: Breasts drawn large enough to be a nuisance: [blocking](#blocking) the view downward, [catching](#catching) in doorways, [knocking](#knocking) things over, straining a garment past its [seams](#seams). The trouble they cause is the joke.

entries.name: manboobs
entries.description: A male chest [carrying](#carrying) soft breast-like [fat](#fat) rather than flat or cut [pectorals](#pectorals), sometimes with raised [nipples](#nipples). Used both for overweight builds and as a deliberate feminising touch on slimmer figures; leave [muscular_male](#muscular_male) off unless the rest of the body supports it.

entries.name: male_with_breasts
entries.description: A character read as male who has a full pair of female [breasts](#breasts). Heavy or well-cut [pectorals](#pectorals) are something else and have their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: floating_breasts
entries.description: Breasts buoyed up by [water](#water) so they rest at the surface while their owner lies in a [bath](#bath), a [pool](#pool) or the sea. Buoyancy is the point, not merely being visible under water.

entries.name: bust_measuring
entries.description: A [tape](#tape) measure run around the chest to take a bust size, a fixture of the Japanese [school](#school) health check. It also covers [measuring](#measuring) other distances across the [breasts](#breasts).

entries.name: asymmetrical_breasts
entries.description: One breast is clearly larger than the other. Breasts that merely sit at different heights are [unaligned_breasts](#unaligned_breasts).

entries.name: udder
entries.description: The milk-producing sac [hanging](#hanging) beneath a [cow](#cow), [goat](#goat) or similar [animal](#animal), with teats [running](#running) along its underside. On anthro and monster-girl designs it often stands in for [breasts](#breasts).

entries.name: convenient_breasts
entries.description: The size of a character's chest is what solves the problem at hand: a flat chest slips through a narrow gap, a large one cushions a fall. Played for laughs, and the [mirror](#mirror) of [inconvenient_breasts](#inconvenient_breasts).

entries.name: stethoscope_between_breasts
entries.description: The head of a [stethoscope](#stethoscope) [resting](#resting) in a woman's [cleavage](#cleavage) with the tubing draped over her chest. Usually happens because the [instrument](#instrument) hangs from the [neck](#neck) and settles there, on [nurse](#nurse) and [doctor](#doctor) characters.

entries.name: ass
entries.description: The buttocks are visible or given [weight](#weight) in the picture, clothed or bare. When they are the main subject use [ass_focus](#ass_focus); the pack [animal](#animal) of the same name is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: thighs
entries.description: The upper [legs](#legs) are a prominent element of the picture, whether bare or covered by [thighhighs](#thighhighs), [pantyhose](#pantyhose) or other tight clothing. Rarely combined with legs unless both are clearly emphasised.

entries.name: barefoot
entries.description: The [feet](#feet) are entirely uncovered, with [no](#no) footwear, [socks](#socks) or legwear of any kind on them. It still applies to [nude](#nude) or swimsuit-clad characters, since undress alone does not mean the feet are shown; a character in socks with the [shoes](#shoes) off is [no_shoes](#no_shoes).

entries.name: feet
entries.description: One or both feet are shown prominently or drawn in detail. They still count inside [sandals](#sandals), [socks](#socks), [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or sheer legwear, but not when shut away in [shoes](#shoes). Add [foot_focus](#foot_focus) where the feet are the subject of the picture.

entries.name: toes
entries.description: The digits of the [feet](#feet) are visible and drawn out, usually on a [barefoot](#barefoot) character or through toeless footwear. Add feet and [foot_focus](#foot_focus) when they are emphasized.

entries.name: legs
entries.description: The legs are the point of the picture and shown along their whole length, not merely from the thigh down. Emphasis on the [thighs](#thighs) alone belongs to thighs.

entries.name: thick_thighs
entries.description: Thighs drawn substantially larger than a normal build, each roughly as wide as the character's waist. Merely visible [thighs](#thighs) are not enough on their own; use thighs alone for those.

entries.name: bare_legs
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) are uncovered from the thigh down to at least mid-shin, with [no](#no) trousers, long [skirt](#skirt), [thighhighs](#thighhighs), [pantyhose](#pantyhose) or footwear [reaching](#reaching) that far. Enough of the leg has to be in frame to tell; [nude](#nude) and [bottomless](#bottomless) characters take their own tags.

entries.name: zettai_ryouiki
entries.description: The band of bare thigh visible between a short [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) and the top of [thighhighs](#thighhighs), exposed simply because the skirt is too short to reach them rather than lifted or pulled aside. Doesn't apply to a single thighhigh, to [shorts](#shorts), or when [underwear](#underwear) or genitals are visible beneath the skirt, though thigh [boots](#boots) [can](#can) still qualify.

entries.name: soles
entries.description: The undersides of the [feet](#feet), mostly visible even at an angle. Counts whether bare or covered by form-fitting [socks](#socks) or [pantyhose](#pantyhose), but not when [shoes](#shoes) or baggy socks hide the foot's shape.

entries.name: huge_ass
entries.description: The buttocks are exaggerated [well](#well) beyond the body's proportions, [standing](#standing) far out behind the [figure](#figure). Wide hips and thick [thighs](#thighs) are separate matters, and a rear that only looks big because the character is bent over does not qualify.

entries.name: ass_visible_through_thighs
entries.description: The lower curve of the buttocks shows between the [thighs](#thighs) of a character facing the viewer. Add [thigh_gap](#thigh_gap) where the [legs](#legs) do not meet at all.

entries.name: thigh_gap
entries.description: A visible [space](#space) between the upper [thighs](#thighs) just below the [crotch](#crotch) while the [knees](#knees) or [legs](#legs) are held together. Depends on both body type and the legs being closed.

entries.name: butt_crack
entries.description: Only the top of the cleft between the buttocks shows, above loose or low-slung trousers, or where clothing is too small for the rear beneath it. When the whole backside is bare, [ass](#ass) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: long_legs
entries.description: Legs drawn clearly longer than average, as a rule of thumb longer than the upper body above them. Discount high heels when judging, since they only create the illusion of length.

entries.name: kneepits
entries.description: The hollow at the [back](#back) of the knee is on show and given some emphasis, usually when the [legs](#legs) are bent or raised. It is the leg's answer to [armpits](#armpits).

entries.name: knees
entries.description: The knee joint is a visible and noticeable part of the picture, as when the [legs](#legs) are drawn up or the shot is framed on them. Pads, [braces](#braces) and other things worn over them have tags of their own.

entries.name: animal_feet
entries.description: A humanoid whose [feet](#feet), often the shins with them, are shaped like an animal's hind paws or [hooves](#hooves). Meant for otherwise human figures, not for fully [furry](#furry) characters or real animals.

entries.name: leg_hair
entries.description: Hair visible on the [thighs](#thighs), shins or [calves](#calves), most often on male characters and occasionally [carrying](#carrying) onto the tops of the [feet](#feet).

entries.name: toe_scrunch
entries.description: Toes curled downward, either deliberately clenched or pressed into a curl by a surface. Common in foot-focused art and climax scenes.

entries.name: spread_toes
entries.description: Feet with the [toes](#toes) fanned apart, whether flexed that way on their own or pushed apart by hands or fingers wedged between them. A common focus in foot-centred art.

entries.name: hooves
entries.description: Hard keratin hooves at the ends of the [legs](#legs), as on horses, [deer](#deer), goats and cattle. They appear on animals, on feral characters, and on anthro or [demon](#demon) figures whose [feet](#feet) end that way.

entries.name: no_feet
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) naturally end without [feet](#feet), tapering to a point or something similar. It is not for amputees, nor for feet merely [cropped](#cropped) out of frame.

entries.name: flat_ass
entries.description: Buttocks that lie flat or barely stand out at all. The far end of the scale from [huge_ass](#huge_ass).

entries.name: bird_legs
entries.description: Legs built like a bird's, with [talons](#talons) and either [feathers](#feathers) or scaly skin, carried by an otherwise humanoid [figure](#figure). A defining feature of harpies.

entries.name: sharp_toenails
entries.description: Toenails drawn coming to a sharp point on an otherwise bare foot. Implies [toenails](#toenails).

entries.name: toe_spread
entries.description: The [toes](#toes) are splayed wide and tensed rather than [resting](#resting) together. Turns up during [stretching](#stretching), arousal or a reaction to being touched.

entries.name: single_bare_foot
entries.description: One foot is uncovered while the other still wears a shoe, sock or boot. Usually the result of one piece of footwear [slipping](#slipping) off or being kicked away.

entries.name: greek_toe
entries.description: Feet drawn with the second toe [reaching](#reaching) further than the big one, also called Morton's toe. The [toes](#toes) have to be visible for it to apply.

entries.name: single_bare_leg
entries.description: One leg is uncovered while the other wears legwear or a pant leg, an asymmetric look. Frequently the result of [single_thighhigh](#single_thighhigh), [single_leg_pantyhose](#single_leg_pantyhose) or [single_pantsleg](#single_pantsleg).

entries.name: slim_legs
entries.description: Legs drawn noticeably narrower and less muscled than the usual proportions, in the same way [flat_chest](#flat_chest) sits below the average bust. Since anime art tends to give [legs](#legs) extra mass, this often reads as the more [realistic](#realistic) option.

entries.name: thighs_together
entries.description: Full [thighs](#thighs) pressed against each other while [standing](#standing) or [resting](#resting), with [no](#no) gap left between them. Do not combine it with [crossed_legs](#crossed_legs) or a deliberately held legs-together pose.

entries.name: wiggling_toes
entries.description: The [toes](#toes) flex and splay in quick little movements. Bare [feet](#feet) are needed for the motion to read at all.

entries.name: arched_soles
entries.description: The underside of a foot curved rather than flat, the middle drawn up while [toes](#toes) and heel sit lower. Shows when a foot is raised, pointed or braced against something.

entries.name: reverse-jointed_legs
entries.description: Legs that bend backwards at the middle joint, like a bird's or a goat's, so the visible heel sits high and the character walks on the [toes](#toes). Common on beast-people, demons, and mechanical designs.

entries.name: webbed_feet
entries.description: Skin stretched between the [toes](#toes), as on ducks, frogs and otters. It marks a [swimming](#swimming) body plan even on an otherwise human-shaped character.

entries.name: calves
entries.description: The muscled [back](#back) of the lower leg between knee and ankle, drawn with enough attention that its shape is the point. Bare [legs](#legs) and athletic [poses](#poses) show it off most.

entries.name: animal_legs
entries.description: Legs built like a beast's, [bending](#bending) backwards at the hock and often ending in paws or [hooves](#hooves). Satyrs, kemono designs and [monster](#monster) girls are drawn this way.

entries.name: clawed_feet
entries.description: Bare [feet](#feet) whose [toes](#toes) end in [claws](#claws) or [talons](#talons) instead of nails. Typical of beast, [dragon](#dragon) and [monster](#monster) characters, and often paired with [digitigrade](#digitigrade) [legs](#legs).

entries.name: y_shaped_butt_crack
entries.description: The cleft between the buttocks drawn branching into a Y shape near the top, an exaggerated take on where the cheeks meet the lower [back](#back). It describes the linework itself, not any state of undress.

entries.name: long_toes
entries.description: Feet drawn with unusually elongated [toes](#toes), so that the foot looks slender and [reaching](#reaching). It describes proportion and has nothing to do with nail length.

entries.name: lap
entries.description: The flat [shelf](#shelf) the upper [thighs](#thighs) make when somebody is seated. It is usually worth noting because something or someone is [resting](#resting) on it.

entries.name: large_feet
entries.description: Feet drawn noticeably bigger than the rest of the character's proportions would suggest. It may be stylistic exaggeration or a deliberate emphasis on the [feet](#feet).

entries.name: no_toes
entries.description: Feet drawn with [no](#no) separate [toes](#toes), ending instead in a smooth rounded shape. It may be a stylistic shortcut or a feature of the body plan.

entries.name: nail_polish
entries.description: Coloured or glossy lacquer on the [fingernails](#fingernails) or [toenails](#toenails). Add the specific colour [tag](#tag) wherever the [shade](#shade) [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: fingernails
entries.description: The nails are drawn as real detail instead of the fingers tapering into stubs. Nails [reaching](#reaching) about a centimetre past the tip are [long_fingernails](#long_fingernails) and anything beyond that [very_long_fingernails](#very_long_fingernails); add [nail_polish](#nail_polish) or [nail_art](#nail_art) when they are painted or decorated.

entries.name: black_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted with black polish. Naturally black [claws](#claws) on a [creature](#creature) are not this, since what it records is [cosmetics](#cosmetics) rather than [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: claws
entries.description: Long pointed nails on an animal's paws, or on a character with animal-like hands and [feet](#feet). Ubiquitous on beast and [monster](#monster) designs; the worn [weapon](#weapon) is [claw_(weapon)](#claw_(weapon)) and the [gesture](#gesture) [claw_pose](#claw_pose).

entries.name: red_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted with red polish. Tag alongside [nail_polish](#nail_polish); naturally red [claws](#claws) on a [creature](#creature) are not this.

entries.name: toenails
entries.description: Toenails drawn distinctly rather than the [toes](#toes) being [plain](#plain) nubs. Add [toenail_polish](#toenail_polish) when painted, [long_toenails](#long_toenails) for extreme length and [nail_art](#nail_art) when decorated.

entries.name: blue_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted blue. Hands and [feet](#feet) count alike, and the polish need only be visible on one of them.

entries.name: pink_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted with pink polish, in any [shade](#shade) from pale to [hot](#hot) pink. Where several colours appear at once, [multicolored_nails](#multicolored_nails) fits better.

entries.name: long_fingernails
entries.description: Fingernails [reaching](#reaching) up to about a centimetre beyond the fingertips. Longer, claw-like nails are [very_long_fingernails](#very_long_fingernails), and painted ones add [nail_polish](#nail_polish).

entries.name: animal_hands
entries.description: A human character with paws for hands, either grown as part of the body or worn as paw [gloves](#gloves). Real animals and fully [furry](#furry) characters are excluded; add [paw_gloves](#paw_gloves) when the paws are plainly worn.

entries.name: toenail_polish
entries.description: Painted [toenails](#toenails) in any colour. Add the colour as with fingernail polish.

entries.name: purple_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted purple or lavender, on the hands, the [feet](#feet), or both. Combine with [nail_polish](#nail_polish); long purple [claws](#claws) on a [monster](#monster) character still count.

entries.name: sharp_fingernails
entries.description: Fingernails filed or naturally grown to a sharp point, distinct from [claws](#claws) in that they remain nails. Implies [fingernails](#fingernails).

entries.name: green_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted with green polish, a detail visible mostly in close views of the hands or [feet](#feet). Tag the hands or feet as [well](#well) where they carry the focus.

entries.name: aqua_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted a blue-green [shade](#shade). Add [nail_polish](#nail_polish) alongside, and the hand or foot [tag](#tag) where the nails are what the picture dwells on.

entries.name: yellow_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted yellow. Tag [nail_polish](#nail_polish) as [well](#well).

entries.name: multicolored_nails
entries.description: Nail polish in more than one colour: either each nail painted differently from its neighbours, or several colours worked onto a single nail as a [rainbow](#rainbow), a ladybird or another small design. Fingernails and [toenails](#toenails) both count.

entries.name: pawpads
entries.description: The soft cushioned pads under an animal's paws, the toe [beans](#beans), drawn on cats, dogs, [furry](#furry) characters and anyone with [animal](#animal) hands. Often shown with the paw turned toward the viewer.

entries.name: cat_paws
entries.description: A human or animal-eared character has [cat](#cat) paws in place of hands, or wears cat-paw [gloves](#gloves). Not for a real cat's paws, and hands merely posed like paws are [paw_pose](#paw_pose).

entries.name: orange_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted orange, frequently matched to the outfit. Add [long_fingernails](#long_fingernails) where the nails are also extended.

entries.name: talons
entries.description: The sharp, hooked [claws](#claws) on the [toes](#toes) of birds of prey, often given to harpies or other bird-legged characters. Non-hunting birds like doves have [plain](#plain) claws instead.

entries.name: white_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted with white polish.

entries.name: fewer_digits
entries.description: Hands or [feet](#feet) are drawn with fewer than five fingers or [toes](#toes). Usual on [monster](#monster) girls, [furry](#furry) characters and cartoon styles, and now and then simply a mistake.

entries.name: spread_fingers
entries.description: A hand with every finger splayed wide apart from the others, each digit clearly separated. Tagged when the fanned-out hand is a distinct feature of the picture.

entries.name: nail_art
entries.description: Fingernails decorated [well](#well) beyond a [plain](#plain) [coat](#coat) of varnish, with painted patterns, transfers or fixed-on ornaments. The decoration has to be clear enough to notice.

entries.name: very_long_fingernails
entries.description: Fingernails extending more than about a centimetre beyond the fingertips, claw-like. Shorter but still noticeable nails are [long_fingernails](#long_fingernails).

entries.name: palms
entries.description: The inner surfaces of the hands are put on show: held up toward the viewer, pressed flat against [glass](#glass), or drawn somewhere unexpected. Nothing to do with [palm_tree](#palm_tree).

entries.name: large_hands
entries.description: The hands are about as big as the head or larger, [perspective](#perspective) aside. It reads as a masculine trait and is also used to hint that a character is not entirely human; oversized [forearms](#forearms) are a separate matter.

entries.name: grey_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) that read grey, either painted with grey polish or naturally so. The natural version is common on zombies and other [undead](#undead).

entries.name: brown_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) coloured brown, almost always from polish. Add [nail_polish](#nail_polish) alongside it where the colour is clearly lacquered on.

entries.name: fake_nails
entries.description: Artificial nails glued over the [fingernails](#fingernails), generally long, shaped and painted. Shown being applied or simply worn, often alongside [nail_polish](#nail_polish).

entries.name: webbed_hands
entries.description: Skin stretched between the fingers like a frog's or duck's foot. A trait of aquatic characters such as mermaids, [kappa](#kappa) and [frog](#frog) [people](#people).

entries.name: long_toenails
entries.description: Toenails grown roughly a centimetre or more past the end of the toe. They tend to belong to a [witch](#witch), a [monster](#monster) or a feral design rather than to ordinary grooming.

entries.name: long_fingers
entries.description: Hands drawn with noticeably elongated fingers, [giving](#giving) them a slender, spidery look. It may be a deliberate part of the design or simply a slip of proportion.

entries.name: pincers
entries.description: The hinged [pinching](#pinching) [claws](#claws) of a [crab](#crab), [scorpion](#scorpion) or [beetle](#beetle), either on the [animal](#animal) itself or [standing](#standing) in for a character's hands. Two parts closing against each other define the shape.

entries.name: skeletal_hand
entries.description: A hand of naked [bone](#bone) on a body that is otherwise [flesh](#flesh) or metal. The bones may be joined by nothing visible at all.

entries.name: gradient_nails
entries.description: Nails whose colour fades along each one, or steps in [shade](#shade) from nail to nail. A manicure effect rather than natural colouring.

entries.name: wolf_paws
entries.description: Wolf-shaped paws with thick pads and blunt [claws](#claws), in place of ordinary hands or [feet](#feet). It describes [anatomy](#anatomy) rather than a glove or a boot.

entries.name: hand_hair
entries.description: Visible body hair growing on the [back](#back) of the hand. Hair on the fingers themselves is covered by [knuckle_hair](#knuckle_hair) instead.

entries.name: two-tone_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) painted in two colours, either alternating between nails or divided within each one. French tips and half-moon designs are typical examples.

entries.name: black_claws
entries.description: Long pointed [claws](#claws) in black, on an animal's paws or on a person given animal-like hands. The colour makes them read sharply against pale fur or skin.

entries.name: tiger_paws
entries.description: Large striped paws in place of hands, either grown or worn as padded [gloves](#gloves). Hands merely held in a paw-like shape belong to the paw pose [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: dragon_claw
entries.description: A dragon's scaled hand or foot, ending in [heavy](#heavy) curved [talons](#talons). May belong to a full [dragon](#dragon) or to a humanoid given draconic limbs.

entries.name: gold_nails
entries.description: Fingernails or [toenails](#toenails) lacquered in [gold](#gold), often with a metallic finish. One of the nail-polish colours.

entries.name: bear_paws
entries.description: Broad [heavy](#heavy) paws shaped like a bear's, with thick pads, short [toes](#toes) and blunt [digging](#digging) [claws](#claws). Worn by anthro bears or pulled on as [costume](#costume) mitts.

entries.name: dog_paws
entries.description: Canine paws in place of hands, pads and blunt [claws](#claws) included, or paw-shaped [gloves](#gloves) that imitate them. The rest of the body may be entirely human.

entries.name: taped_hands
entries.description: Hands and knuckles wrapped in strips of [tape](#tape) the way [boxers](#boxers) and martial artists prepare before a bout. Climbers and characters patching up a fresh [injury](#injury) wear the same wrap.

entries.name: knuckle_hair
entries.description: Hair growing visibly on the backs of the fingers beyond the knuckles. It marks a character as [hairy](#hairy) overall and appears mostly on rugged adult men.

entries.name: crab_claw
entries.description: A crab's pincer, on the [animal](#animal) itself or [standing](#standing) in for a character's hand. Monster girls and [crustacean](#crustacean) anthros are the usual carriers.

entries.name: no_hands
entries.description: The arms end in points, [fins](#fins) or smooth stumps instead of hands, as a natural feature of the design. Fish girls are often built this way; somebody who lost their hands is an [amputee](#amputee).

entries.name: cat_paw
entries.description: The padded forepaw of a [cat](#cat), either on the [animal](#animal) itself or [reaching](#reaching) into the frame from off [screen](#screen). Paw-shaped [mittens](#mittens) worn by a person are a separate matter.

entries.name: red_claws
entries.description: Pointed red [claws](#claws) on an animal's paws, or on a person whose nails have grown into claw-like points. The colour may be natural to the design or the result of polish.

entries.name: fingerprint
entries.description: The looping ridge pattern of a fingertip is drawn in, often reduced to a [plain](#plain) [spiral](#spiral). Artists most often add it to a finger pointed outward, for emphasis.

entries.name: cat_feet
entries.description: The paws and lower [legs](#legs) of an actual [cat](#cat), often drawn close up with the pads showing. Keep it for the [animal](#animal) itself, not for a person with paw-shaped hands or cat-themed [shoes](#shoes).

entries.name: silver_nails
entries.description: Fingernails painted a metallic silver-grey. Recorded as [grey_nails](#grey_nails) or [white_nails](#white_nails) instead, since the metallic tone is treated as a [shade](#shade) of one of those colors.

entries.name: small_hands
entries.description: Hands drawn out of proportion, too little for the body they belong to. A correctly sized adult hand reaches from chin to hairline when held against the face, so anything much shorter reads as an [anatomy](#anatomy) mistake.

entries.name: animal_ears
entries.description: Creature ears on a character, grown or worn, the look called kemonomimi. They sit either on top of the head or where human ears belong, and the top-of-head sort often leaves human ears in place as [well](#well). Add the specific kind, such as [cat_ears](#cat_ears).

entries.name: pointy_ears
entries.description: Ears that taper to a point, as on elves, Vulcans, demons and many [fantasy](#fantasy) races. Animal-like pointed ears on an otherwise human head [can](#can) also take it; true [animal](#animal) ears are tagged separately.

entries.name: cat_ears
entries.description: Feline ears on top of a character's head, whether genuinely part of the body or worn as a [fashion](#fashion) accessory. The nekomimi look, the commonest of all [animal](#animal) ears.

entries.name: rabbit_ears
entries.description: Long [rabbit](#rabbit) ears on a character, whether real or fake. Add [rabbit_girl](#rabbit_girl) or [rabbit_boy](#rabbit_boy) for genuine ones, [fake_animal_ears](#fake_animal_ears) for a [headband](#headband), and [kemonomimi_mode](#kemonomimi_mode) for a character who does not normally have them; hands mimicking ears instead is [rabbit_pose](#rabbit_pose).

entries.name: animal_ear_fluff
entries.description: Soft cottony tufts sprouting from inside a character's [animal](#animal) ears, usually white or a washed-out version of the surrounding fur. Fox ears carry it most often, though any kind [can](#can), and real animals count too.

entries.name: fox_ears
entries.description: Fox-like ears on an otherwise human character, typically long, sharply pointed and [lighter](#lighter) in tone than [wolf](#wolf) ears. They usually come paired with [fox_tail](#fox_tail).

entries.name: horse_ears
entries.description: Tall, tapering [horse](#horse) ears on a character, either grown naturally or worn as an accessory. They are the mark of horse girls and boys.

entries.name: wolf_ears
entries.description: Pointed, [furry](#furry) ears like a wolf's set on a character's head, coyote ears included under the same [tag](#tag). Tag [animal_ears](#animal_ears) alongside it, and [wolf_tail](#wolf_tail) where a [tail](#tail) is present too.

entries.name: extra_ears
entries.description: Human ears and [animal](#animal) ears both present on the same character. Fake ears on a [headband](#headband) do not count, and a second pair of animal ears is [multiple_animal_ears](#multiple_animal_ears).

entries.name: dog_ears
entries.description: Canine ears on a character's head, whether grown or clipped on as an accessory; the Japanese word is inumimi. The ears of wild [dog](#dog) species are gathered here too.

entries.name: mouse_ears
entries.description: Round rodent ears on a character's head, either their own or clipped on as an accessory. The shape is close to [bear](#bear) and [raccoon](#raccoon) ears, so the rest of the design settles which it is.

entries.name: cow_ears
entries.description: Cow ears on a character's head, grown or worn as an accessory, [standing](#standing) out [sideways](#sideways) below any [horns](#horns). Usually joined by [cow_horns](#cow_horns), [cow_tail](#cow_tail) and patch-printed clothing.

entries.name: ox_ears
entries.description: Cattle ears on an otherwise human head, broad and drooping and set low at the sides. Common on bovine characters and in Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac) pictures.

entries.name: tiger_ears
entries.description: Rounded striped ears of a [tiger](#tiger) on an otherwise human character. Add [tiger_girl](#tiger_girl) or [tiger_boy](#tiger_boy) and [tiger_tail](#tiger_tail).

entries.name: raccoon_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears of a [raccoon](#raccoon) or [tanuki](#tanuki) on a character, pooled into one [tag](#tag) since artists mix the two species freely. They [can](#can) resemble [bear_ears](#bear_ears); combine with [raccoon_girl](#raccoon_girl) or [raccoon_boy](#raccoon_boy) when the trait is genuine.

entries.name: ears_through_headwear
entries.description: Animal ears pushed out through holes cut in a [hat](#hat), [hood](#hood) or other headwear. The ears are the character's own; fake ones built into the hat are [animal_hat](#animal_hat) or [animal_hood](#animal_hood).

entries.name: lion_ears
entries.description: Small rounded [lion](#lion) ears on a human-shaped character rather than on the [animal](#animal) itself, usually together with [lion_tail](#lion_tail).

entries.name: bear_ears
entries.description: Small round ears of the kind a [bear](#bear) has, usually set on top of a humanoid character's head, or built into a [hood](#hood) or [costume](#costume). Add [bear_girl](#bear_girl) or [bear_boy](#bear_boy) when the character is a bear-eared person.

entries.name: floppy_ears
entries.description: Ears long enough to hang slack down the sides of the head, with [no](#no) ability to stand upright on their own, as on a lop [rabbit](#rabbit) or a hound. They should be fully or all but fully down unless a hand or a gust lifts them.

entries.name: bird_ears
entries.description: Bird-like ears on a humanoid, usually feathered tufts or small wing [shapes](#shapes), since real birds have nothing on the outside. They sit where human ears would.

entries.name: long_pointy_ears
entries.description: Pointed ears far longer than usual, [sweeping](#sweeping) [well](#well) out beyond the head. They are common on elves and on some [demon](#demon) designs.

entries.name: robot_ears
entries.description: Ear pieces on a [robot](#robot) character that look like [antennae](#antennae), speakers or other [machinery](#machinery) rather than actual ears. If they are shaped like human or [animal](#animal) ears, use [mechanical_ears](#mechanical_ears) instead.

entries.name: ears_down
entries.description: Animal ears that would normally stand upright turned downward, showing sadness, dismay or timidity. Ears that naturally hang are [droopy_ears](#droopy_ears), one dropped ear is unaligned_ears, and ears flat to the head are [floppy_ears](#floppy_ears).

entries.name: sheep_ears
entries.description: Drooping sheep-like ears on an otherwise human character, usually paired with [sheep_horns](#sheep_horns). Implies [animal_ears](#animal_ears).

entries.name: squirrel_ears
entries.description: A character wearing or possessing the small, rounded, tufted ears of a [squirrel](#squirrel). A kemonomimi feature often paired with [squirrel_tail](#squirrel_tail).

entries.name: deer_ears
entries.description: Animal ears modelled on a deer's, rounded and set out to the sides of the head, whether grown or worn. Reindeer ears belong here as [well](#well).

entries.name: notched_ear
entries.description: An ear with a piece missing from an [old](#old) [injury](#injury), usually a triangular nick but sometimes a [hole](#hole) or a lost tip. It appears on cats and other animals and on animal-eared characters.

entries.name: jackal_ears
entries.description: Tall, sharply pointed [animal](#animal) ears modelled on a jackal's, set on an otherwise human head. They [suit](#suit) Egyptian-themed and Anubis-inspired characters.

entries.name: goat_ears
entries.description: Ears shaped after a goat's, [hanging](#hanging) down or [standing](#standing) out to the sides. They usually come with [goat_horns](#goat_horns) on a [goat](#goat) character or a [satyr](#satyr).

entries.name: bat_ears
entries.description: Large pointed ears modelled on a bat's, growing from a humanoid character's head rather than belonging to an actual bat. Common on bat girls and on some [vampire](#vampire) and [demon](#demon) designs.

entries.name: panther_ears
entries.description: The ears of a black panther, in effect [leopard](#leopard) or [jaguar](#jaguar) ears coloured black, rounded and [dark](#dark). Usually paired with a dark [tail](#tail) or with black fur.

entries.name: colored_inner_animal_ears
entries.description: The inside of a pair of [animal](#animal) ears is an odd colour, neither a natural [flesh](#flesh) tone nor the character's hair or fur. Common on [fantasy](#fantasy) kemonomimi designs.

entries.name: mechanical_ears
entries.description: Artificial ears shaped to resemble real ones, worn by an [android](#android) or [cyborg](#cyborg). Antenna-like receivers instead take a [robot](#robot) ear [tag](#tag), and mechanical ears built into a [headset](#headset) also take the [animal](#animal) ear [headphones](#headphones) tag.

entries.name: panda_ears
entries.description: Round black [animal](#animal) ears modelled on a panda's, [sitting](#sitting) on top of the head. Often go with a black-and-white outfit or a [panda](#panda) [hood](#hood); the animal itself is panda.

entries.name: leopard_ears
entries.description: Rounded ears bearing a leopard's spotting, worn by an otherwise human character. Usually seen alongside [leopard_tail](#leopard_tail) and rosette [markings](#markings).

entries.name: jaguar_ears
entries.description: Rounded [animal](#animal) ears modelled on a jaguar's, tawny and often spotted, set on a human head. They usually come with [jaguar_tail](#jaguar_tail) and sometimes with [jaguar_print](#jaguar_print) clothing.

entries.name: ear_wiggle
entries.description: Both ears shown in motion, [twitching](#twitching) or swivelling, whether on purpose or by reflex. Small motion lines beside [animal](#animal) ears are the usual cue, and it signals attention or excitement.

entries.name: snow_leopard_ears
entries.description: Animal ears modeled on a [snow](#snow) leopard's: short, rounded, and set high on the head, in pale grey-white fur with [dark](#dark) [markings](#markings) along the edge.

entries.name: monkey_ears
entries.description: Rounded [monkey](#monkey) ears set on a character's head in place of human ones, marking them out as a monkey-type character. They replace the human ears rather than [sitting](#sitting) alongside them.

entries.name: lop_rabbit_ears
entries.description: Rabbit ears that droop down beside the head instead of [standing](#standing) upright, as on a lop-eared breed. They read as softer and more docile than pricked ears.

entries.name: weasel_ears
entries.description: Small rounded [animal](#animal) ears modeled on a [weasel](#weasel) or stoat, worn by a kemonomimi character. Usually paired with a matching [tail](#tail).

entries.name: large_ears
entries.description: Ears markedly bigger than normal for the character, whether human ears or [animal](#animal) ones such as a fennec's or an elephant's. It is a matter of proportion rather than of shape.
