entries.name: pig_ears
entries.description: A character with the small rounded or floppy ears of a [pig](#pig), usually pink inside. Frequently paired with a [snout](#snout) or a curled [tail](#tail) on an animal-featured character.

entries.name: owl_ears
entries.description: The feather tufts rising from the top of a horned owl's head, worn by owl-themed characters or clipped on as an accessory. They are not real ears, which sit at the sides of the face.

entries.name: droopy_ears
entries.description: Non-human ears that hang downward as a natural part of the design rather than as a passing mood. Normally upright ears that have dropped are [ears_down](#ears_down), a single dropped ear is unaligned_ears, and ears flat to the head are [floppy_ears](#floppy_ears).

entries.name: alpaca_ears
entries.description: Long, upright, [fluffy](#fluffy) ears modelled on an alpaca's, set on an otherwise human head. Llama-like ears are usually gathered here too.

entries.name: dragon_ears
entries.description: The ears of a dragon-blooded character, generally finned, webbed or hornlike rather than furred. Drawn together with [horns](#horns) and a [tail](#tail).

entries.name: hyena_ears
entries.description: Broad, blunt-tipped ears of the sort a [hyena](#hyena) carries, set on top of the head. They are wider and rounder than the pointed ears of a [dog](#dog) or a [wolf](#wolf).

entries.name: long_earlobes
entries.description: Earlobes that hang unusually low by [nature](#nature), with [no](#no) [piercing](#piercing) or [stretching](#stretching) involved, as in images of the Buddha. Lobes drawn out by gauges belong under [plug_(piercing)](#plug_(piercing)).

entries.name: otter_ears
entries.description: Small rounded [animal](#animal) ears modelled on an otter's, set on an otherwise human head.

entries.name: ears_visible_through_hair
entries.description: The ears show through hair that ought to be [hiding](#hiding) them, as though the hair were half [transparent](#transparent). A stylistic quirk of the same [family](#family) as [eyes_visible_through_hair](#eyes_visible_through_hair), and it fits human and [animal](#animal) ears alike.

entries.name: single_ear_down
entries.description: One [animal](#animal) ear droops or folds while the other stands upright, so the pair does not match. Often signals doubt, [listening](#listening) intently, or a lazy mood.

entries.name: tapir_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears with pale tips modeled on a tapir's, set on an otherwise human-looking head, usually paired with a matching [tail](#tail) or [snout](#snout).

entries.name: wing_ears
entries.description: Ears shaped like small [wings](#wings), sometimes feathered, [standing](#standing) out from the sides of the head. They are a design feature of fairies, elves, and various [monster](#monster) characters.

entries.name: moose_ears
entries.description: The broad rounded ears of a [moose](#moose) set on a character's head. Usually drawn together with the matching [antlers](#antlers) or [tail](#tail).

entries.name: implied_extra_ears
entries.description: Animal ears sit on top of the head with [no](#no) human ones in sight, yet something insists human ears are there under the hair: [earrings](#earrings), [headphones](#headphones), or somebody [leaning](#leaning) in to whisper. The contradiction is what is being tagged.

entries.name: red_panda_ears
entries.description: Rounded, thickly furred ears modelled on a red panda's, rust-coloured outside with pale fur inside and at the rims. They sit on the head of an otherwise human character.

entries.name: ears_through_hood
entries.description: Animal ears [standing](#standing) free through gaps or holes in a [hood](#hood) instead of being pressed flat under it. Common on [animal](#animal) hoodies and [kigurumi](#kigurumi).

entries.name: tied_ears
entries.description: Animal ears [bound](#bound) together or [folded](#folded) down and fastened with a [ribbon](#ribbon) or cord. Mostly decorative, occasionally a way of [holding](#holding) the character in place.

entries.name: chipmunk_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears modelled on a chipmunk's, set on a character's head. Usually joined by [chipmunk_tail](#chipmunk_tail) where the rest of the design follows the same [animal](#animal).

entries.name: very_long_ears
entries.description: Ears drawn far longer than the character's species or design would call for, sometimes [reaching](#reaching) past the shoulders. Common on [rabbit](#rabbit) and [elf](#elf) designs pushed to an extreme.

entries.name: komainu_ears
entries.description: Animal ears modelled on the [shrine](#shrine) guardian lion-dog: broad, a little floppy, and often set against a curly [mane](#mane). The stylised, statue-like shaping tells them from [plain](#plain) [dog](#dog) or [lion](#lion) ears.

entries.name: giraffe_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears set wide on the head in [giraffe](#giraffe) [fashion](#fashion), worn by an otherwise human character. Usually accompanied by the matching stubby [horns](#horns).

entries.name: ferret_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears set low and wide on the head, modelled on a ferret's, worn by an otherwise human character.

entries.name: beaver_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears modelled on a beaver's, set on an otherwise human head. Kemonomimi designs usually pair them with a [beaver](#beaver) [tail](#tail).

entries.name: mismatched_animal_ear_colors
entries.description: One of a character's [animal](#animal) ears is colored differently from the other. Not used for real animals, since this coloring pattern occurs naturally in [nature](#nature).

entries.name: hippopotamus_ears
entries.description: Small rounded hippo ears set high on an otherwise human head. They mark a character themed on the [animal](#animal).

entries.name: sea_slug_ears
entries.description: Soft, frilled appendages [standing](#standing) where ears would be, modelled on a sea slug's rhinophores. They are not really ears, only placed and read as such.

entries.name: hamster_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears modelled on a hamster's, [sitting](#sitting) high on the head. They usually come with the matching stubby [tail](#tail) and sometimes with padded cheeks.

entries.name: zebra_ears
entries.description: Animal ears modelled on a zebra's: [tall](#tall), rounded and banded in black and white, usually set on an otherwise human head. The striping is what separates them from [plain](#plain) [horse](#horse) ears.

entries.name: meerkat_ears
entries.description: Small, rounded ears set low on the sides of the head, copied from a meerkat onto an otherwise human character. A [marker](#marker) of a meerkat-themed animal-eared design.

entries.name: tasmanian_devil_ears
entries.description: Short, rounded ears modeled on a Tasmanian devil's, usually [dark](#dark) with pink inner skin, set on an otherwise human-looking head.

entries.name: anteater_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears set high on the head, taken from an [anteater](#anteater) and given to an otherwise human-shaped character. Much shorter and blunter than the [rabbit](#rabbit) or [fox](#fox) versions.

entries.name: visible_ears
entries.description: The ears are left uncovered by hair, [hat](#hat) or [hood](#hood) so their shape [can](#can) be seen. Useful for characters whose ears normally sit [buried](#buried) under a hairstyle.

entries.name: cheetah_ears
entries.description: Small rounded [animal](#animal) ears of the cheetah sort, usually [dark](#dark) on the [back](#back), growing from a human head. Spotted [markings](#markings) elsewhere on the body normally come with them.

entries.name: chinchilla_ears
entries.description: Large rounded [animal](#animal) ears modelled on a chinchilla, thin-skinned and broader than a mouse's, growing from a character's head. Usually part of a design that also carries [chinchilla_tail](#chinchilla_tail).

entries.name: gazelle_ears
entries.description: Narrow tapering ears modelled on a gazelle's, set on an otherwise human head. Part of the animal-eared [family](#family) alongside [deer](#deer) and antelope versions, and the [tag](#tag) covers oryx ears too.

entries.name: fiery_ears
entries.description: Ears made of flame, [burning](#burning) where ordinary ears would sit. It suits [fire](#fire) elementals and beast characters built around a flame theme.

entries.name: elephant_ears
entries.description: Broad, drooping ears taken from an [elephant](#elephant) and set on an otherwise human head. Far larger and rounder than the [cat](#cat) or [dog](#dog) ears usually drawn.

entries.name: skunk_ears
entries.description: Small rounded [animal](#animal) ears of the skunk kind, usually black with a white stripe [running](#running) between them. Nearly always paired with a matching bushy [tail](#tail).

entries.name: black_ears
entries.description: Ears coloured black, nearly always the [animal](#animal) ears of a kemonomimi or anthro character rather than human ones. Ears [dark](#dark) only at the points are black_ear_tips.

entries.name: rhinoceros_ears
entries.description: Small, rounded ears cupped forward like a rhinoceros's, worn on an otherwise human head. Usually paired with a matching horn or a grey skin tone.

entries.name: tamandua_ears
entries.description: Small, rounded ears modeled on a lesser anteater's, set high on an otherwise human-looking head.

entries.name: no_animal_ears
entries.description: Somebody who normally has [animal](#animal) ears appears without them, leaving an ordinary human head. It usually accompanies a humanised or redesigned take on the character.

entries.name: antelope_ears
entries.description: Narrow pointed ears in the manner of an antelope, set on a human-shaped head. Usually drawn alongside a matching pair of [horns](#horns).

entries.name: ear_tufts
entries.description: Long hairs sprouting from the very points of [animal](#animal) ears and [standing](#standing) [well](#well) beyond them, as on a lynx or a Maine Coon. Not the [fluff](#fluff) growing inside the ear, and the tuft must read as distinct from a merely pointed tip.

entries.name: ears_back
entries.description: Animal ears [pinned](#pinned) flat [back](#back) against the head, which in animals and in characters who have them signals fear, aggression or submission. Ears that merely droop are [ears_down](#ears_down).

entries.name: armadillo_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears modelled on an armadillo's, set on an otherwise human head. Often drawn with a plated band across the brow to match.

entries.name: boar_ears
entries.description: Boar ears set on an otherwise human head, small, rounded and [standing](#standing) up high. Tusks often accompany them.

entries.name: ears_under_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) or [hood](#hood) covers a character's [animal](#animal) ears wholly or partly, often squashing them out of their usual position. Headwear that sits between the ears without touching them does not count.

entries.name: donkey_ears
entries.description: Long upright ears, noticeably longer than a horse's and often [dark](#dark) at the tips. Worn by donkey-based characters and by [people](#people) given nothing but the ears.

entries.name: badger_ears
entries.description: Small rounded ears [carrying](#carrying) a badger's [dark](#dark) and pale banding, set on an otherwise human head. A matching [tail](#tail) generally comes with them.

entries.name: multiple_animal_ears
entries.description: A character [carrying](#carrying) more than one pair of [animal](#animal) ears at once, sometimes from different species. Grown ears and worn ones both count toward the number.

entries.name: ears_up
entries.description: Animal ears [standing](#standing) upright and turned toward something, alert. Shows attention, curiosity or excitement, and is the opposite of [ears_down](#ears_down) or [ears_back](#ears_back).

entries.name: flapping_ears
entries.description: Long or floppy [animal](#animal) ears [swinging](#swinging) about, set going by [running](#running), a shake of the head or [plain](#plain) excitement. Blur or trailing lines at the tips carry the motion.

entries.name: okapi_ears
entries.description: Large rounded ears taken from the okapi, generally drawn along with that animal's [dark](#dark) [coat](#coat) and striped hindquarters.

entries.name: camel_ears
entries.description: Ears modelled on a camel's: small, rounded and set low against the sides of the head. Worn by characters given [camel](#camel) traits rather than by the [animal](#animal) itself.

entries.name: detached_ears
entries.description: Ears [floating](#floating) clear of the head instead of joining it. Common on constructs, spirits and heavily stylised designs.

entries.name: lemur_ears
entries.description: Rounded, lightly tufted ears modelled on a lemur's, set on an otherwise human head.

entries.name: tail
entries.description: An animal-style appendage growing from the lower [back](#back), furred or scaled, typical of [animal](#animal) girls and anthro characters. Not usually tagged on an ordinary animal unless the tail itself is the focus or unusual for its species.

entries.name: cat_tail
entries.description: A character has a feline [tail](#tail), slim and usually curling at the tip. Normally paired with [cat_ears](#cat_ears) on a [cat](#cat) girl or cat boy.

entries.name: fox_tail
entries.description: One or more thick brush-like [fox](#fox) tails on a character. Add [multiple_tails](#multiple_tails) where several grow at once, as on a nine-tailed [kitsune](#kitsune).

entries.name: horse_tail
entries.description: The character has the long, flowing [tail](#tail) of a [horse](#horse) growing from the body. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [ponytail](#ponytail), which is a hairstyle.

entries.name: rabbit_tail
entries.description: A short, round [rabbit](#rabbit) [tail](#tail) on a character. Add [rabbit_girl](#rabbit_girl) or [rabbit_boy](#rabbit_boy) when it is a real feature, and [fake_tail](#fake_tail) when it belongs to a [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny) outfit.

entries.name: demon_tail
entries.description: A long thin whip-like [tail](#tail) ending in a spade point, standard equipment for demons and [demon](#demon) girls. A tail curled into a [heart](#heart) shape is [heart_tail](#heart_tail) instead.

entries.name: multiple_tails
entries.description: One character with more than one [tail](#tail), the nine-tailed [fox](#fox) being the standard case. Several characters with a tail each does not qualify.

entries.name: wolf_tail
entries.description: A bushy, wolf-like [tail](#tail) on a character, coyote tails included under the same [tag](#tag). Combine it with tail and, usually, [wolf_ears](#wolf_ears).

entries.name: dog_tail
entries.description: A canine [tail](#tail) on a character, grown or worn. The tails of wild [dog](#dog) species are included here.

entries.name: dragon_tail
entries.description: A dragon's [tail](#tail), long and scaled and often [spiked](#spiked) or finned, on a [creature](#creature) or on a character with draconic traits. Sometimes carried curled around the body.

entries.name: tail_ornament
entries.description: Any decoration fixed to a [tail](#tail): a [bow](#bow), [ribbon](#ribbon), [bell](#bell), [ring](#ring) or [piercing](#piercing).

entries.name: fish_tail
entries.description: A fish-like [tail](#tail) growing from the base of the [spine](#spine) on a character who still has ordinary [legs](#legs). Where the tail takes the place of the legs, the character is a [mermaid](#mermaid) or [merman](#merman).

entries.name: mouse_tail
entries.description: A thin, wiry, hairless rodent [tail](#tail) on a character or an [animal](#animal), quite unlike the furred tails of other creatures. It often curls or twitches to carry the mood.

entries.name: tail_raised
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) held up rather than left [hanging](#hanging) naturally. Distinct from a tail lifted to hoist clothing out of the way, and from a tail bristling as a defensive [display](#display).

entries.name: shark_tail
entries.description: A vertically finned [shark](#shark) [tail](#tail) on a character who still has ordinary [legs](#legs). Horizontal flukes are [cetacean_tail](#cetacean_tail) instead, and a character with [no](#no) legs at all takes [mermaid](#mermaid) or [merman](#merman). Implies [fish_tail](#fish_tail).

entries.name: two_tails
entries.description: A being with exactly two animal-type tails, both clearly visible at once. Not to be [confused](#confused) with the hairstyle [twintails](#twintails).

entries.name: black_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) coloured black, be it feline, canine, draconic or demonic. Add the kind of tail as [well](#well), since the colour alone does not say what it belongs to.

entries.name: raccoon_tail
entries.description: A bushy [tail](#tail) in the [raccoon](#raccoon) or [tanuki](#tanuki) style. Real raccoon tails are ringed and tanuki tails simply tipped, but the two are conflated so often in art that a single [tag](#tag) covers both.

entries.name: tiger_tail
entries.description: A long striped [tail](#tail) of a [tiger](#tiger) on a character. Usually paired with [tiger_ears](#tiger_ears).

entries.name: tail_wagging
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) [swinging](#swinging) [back](#back) and forth, usually drawn with motion lines. Dogs do it when [happy](#happy), cats when irritated.

entries.name: cow_tail
entries.description: A long thin [tail](#tail) ending in a tuft of hair, as a cow's does, whether grown or part of a [costume](#costume). Usually accompanied by [cow_ears](#cow_ears) and [cow_horns](#cow_horns).

entries.name: tail_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied onto a [tail](#tail).

entries.name: bird_tail
entries.description: A fan of [tail](#tail) [feathers](#feathers) like a bird's, growing from a humanoid or anthro character. Standard on [bird](#bird) girls, harpies and avian [furry](#furry) designs.

entries.name: prehensile_ribbon
entries.description: Ribbon-shaped appendages growing from the character's body that move like feelers or hands, gripping and probing. A [ribbon](#ribbon) carried as a prop or [weapon](#weapon) does not qualify; it has to be part of them.

entries.name: tail_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied onto a [tail](#tail).

entries.name: lion_tail
entries.description: A slender [tail](#tail) ending in a tuft, like a lion's, on a character who is otherwise human. Typically drawn with [lion_ears](#lion_ears).

entries.name: tail_through_clothes
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) passing through a [hole](#hole) or slit cut into clothing, usually at the rear. Add a cutout [tag](#tag) separately only when the [opening](#opening) itself is visible.

entries.name: striped_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) [carrying](#carrying) alternating bands of colour along its length, as seen on raccoons, lemurs or tigers. Implies tail.

entries.name: squirrel_tail
entries.description: A large, bushy [squirrel](#squirrel) [tail](#tail) on a character, typically curled upward. A kemonomimi feature often paired with [squirrel_ears](#squirrel_ears).

entries.name: snake_tail
entries.description: A character has a snake's [tail](#tail) while keeping ordinary [legs](#legs). A [snake](#snake) body in place of legs is [lamia](#lamia) instead.

entries.name: brown_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) coloured brown, be it a dog's, fox's, horse's, squirrel's or monkey's. Add tail and, where the [animal](#animal) is identifiable, the species-specific tail [tag](#tag).

entries.name: monkey_tail
entries.description: A long, [flexible](#flexible) [monkey](#monkey) [tail](#tail), [strong](#strong) enough to curl around a [branch](#branch) or an object and take the owner's [weight](#weight). Fits both animals and characters given one.

entries.name: white_tail
entries.description: A character's [tail](#tail) coloured entirely white, whatever the species: [fox](#fox), [wolf](#wolf), [cat](#cat), [dragon](#dragon), or otherwise. Tag tail and, where it applies, the species-specific tail [tag](#tag).

entries.name: very_long_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) so long that it goes [well](#well) beyond what [long_tail](#long_tail) would [cover](#cover), often trailing across the ground or coiling through the frame.

entries.name: flame-tipped_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that burns at its very end while the rest stays ordinary. A tail made of [fire](#fire) along its whole length is a [fiery_tail](#fiery_tail).

entries.name: ghost_tail
entries.description: A ghostly character whose lower body narrows into a [drifting](#drifting) wisp instead of [legs](#legs). A standard way of showing that a humanoid [figure](#figure) is a [spirit](#spirit).

entries.name: large_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) at least as large as the character it belongs to. Enormous [fox](#fox) and [squirrel](#squirrel) tails are the usual pairings.

entries.name: mechanical_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) built from visible [machine](#machine) parts, worn by a [robot](#robot), [cyborg](#cyborg), or a character with an artificial add-on rather than a natural one.

entries.name: long_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) noticeably longer than the character's [legs](#legs). Where the tail replaces the legs, as on a [mermaid](#mermaid) or a [lamia](#lamia), use it only when the length is striking for that kind, and leave it off in borderline cases.

entries.name: tail_bell
entries.description: A small [bell](#bell) worn on a [tail](#tail), usually tied on together with a tail [bow](#bow) or [ribbon](#ribbon).

entries.name: pink_tail
entries.description: The character has a pink [tail](#tail), whether an [animal](#animal) tail on a kemonomimi, a demon's tail or a feral creature's. Add the kind of tail as [well](#well), such as [cat_tail](#cat_tail) or [fox_tail](#fox_tail).

entries.name: tail_wrap
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) curled around another person or an object, functioning like a [hug](#hug) made with the tail.

entries.name: purple_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that is purple, on an animal-eared character, a [dragon](#dragon), or a [demon](#demon). Combine with tail and the type, such as [cat_tail](#cat_tail) or [dragon_tail](#dragon_tail).

entries.name: heart_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) — or several — curls round until it closes into a [heart](#heart), a Valentine joke or simply a show of fondness. Do not confuse it with a [demon](#demon) tail, whose tip is heart-shaped by design.

entries.name: lizard_tail
entries.description: A thick reptilian [tail](#tail) tapering to a point and scaled along its length, on a character who is otherwise human in shape. Salamander tails count as the same thing.

entries.name: grey_tail
entries.description: The character's [tail](#tail) is grey, as on a [wolf](#wolf), [cat](#cat), mouse or grey [dragon](#dragon). Tag the kind of tail as [well](#well) where it is distinctive.

entries.name: blue_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) coloured blue, on a [dragon](#dragon), [fox](#fox), [cat](#cat) or any other tailed character. Name the type of tail alongside it.

entries.name: spiked_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) bristling with [spikes](#spikes), common on dragons, dinosaurs, and monsters. Tag the tail feature itself.

entries.name: red_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that is red, on a [fox](#fox) girl, [dragon](#dragon), [demon](#demon) or any other tailed character. Describes the tail's colour, not a tail ornament.

entries.name: panther_tail
entries.description: The long, smooth, [dark](#dark) [tail](#tail) of a black panther growing from a character rather than from an [animal](#animal). Pair it with [panther_ears](#panther_ears) when more of the body plan shows.

entries.name: yellow_tail
entries.description: A character's [tail](#tail) is yellow, on a [fox](#fox), [lizard](#lizard), [dragon](#dragon) or other tailed being. Tag tail and the species tail.

entries.name: tail_grab
entries.description: A hand gripping a [tail](#tail), whether one's own or someone else's. For a tail doing the grabbing instead of being grabbed, see [holding_with_tail](#holding_with_tail) or [tail_wrap](#tail_wrap).

entries.name: cetacean_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) belonging to a [dolphin](#dolphin), [orca](#orca), [whale](#whale) or [narwhal](#narwhal), ending in flukes that spread [sideways](#sideways). Those horizontal [fins](#fins) are what separate it from a [fish](#fish) tail, whose fin stands upright.

entries.name: prehensile_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) used to grasp or hold things, wrapped around an object, a [branch](#branch) or another character. Tag tail with it.

entries.name: tail_between_legs
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) pulled forward between the [legs](#legs), the classic [animal](#animal) [sign](#sign) of fear or submission carried over to animal characters.

entries.name: green_tail
entries.description: The character's [tail](#tail) is green, whether a scaled [dragon](#dragon) tail, a [furry](#furry) [animal](#animal) tail or a plant-like one. Tag the kind of tail as [well](#well) where it is distinctive.

entries.name: short_tail
entries.description: A stubby [tail](#tail), seen on an [animal](#animal), an anthro or a kemonomimi character. Implies tail.

entries.name: eastern_dragon_tail
entries.description: The long serpentine [tail](#tail) of a Chinese-style [dragon](#dragon), furred along its [back](#back) and finishing in a tuft. Distinct from the smooth reptile tail of a western dragon.

entries.name: tail_ring
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) fitted onto a [tail](#tail), or a small [halo](#halo) [floating](#floating) near its tip.

entries.name: orange_tail
entries.description: The character's [tail](#tail) is orange, as on [fox](#fox) girls, tigers and many kemono designs. It covers animal-eared humans, anthros and animals alike.

entries.name: tail_around_own_leg
entries.description: A character's own [tail](#tail) curled around one of their [legs](#legs).

entries.name: tapir_tail
entries.description: A short, stubby [tail](#tail) like a tapir's given to a character.

entries.name: no_tail
entries.description: A character who officially has a [tail](#tail) is drawn without it, whether forgotten or deliberately left out. It is a small design-deviation [tag](#tag).

entries.name: crocodilian_tail
entries.description: A thick ridged [tail](#tail) of the [crocodile](#crocodile) or [alligator](#alligator) sort on a character, human-shaped or anthro. Common on reptile [monster](#monster) girls and scaled anthros.

entries.name: leopard_tail
entries.description: A long spotted feline [tail](#tail) on a character who is otherwise human, generally drawn together with [leopard_ears](#leopard_ears).

entries.name: jaguar_tail
entries.description: A long spotted [tail](#tail) marked with rosettes, of the kind a [jaguar](#jaguar) has. It nearly always comes paired with [jaguar_ears](#jaguar_ears).

entries.name: cable_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) made of electrical [cable](#cable) or [wire](#wire) [rope](#rope), frequently ending in a plug, connector, tool or blade. Robots, androids and [cyberpunk](#cyberpunk) characters carry them.

entries.name: snow_leopard_tail
entries.description: An unusually thick [tail](#tail) in pale fur scattered with [dark](#dark) rosettes, copied from a [snow](#snow) [leopard](#leopard). Its bulk compared to other [cat](#cat) tails is the identifying feature.

entries.name: deer_tail
entries.description: A short tufted [tail](#tail) modelled on a deer's or a reindeer's, worn or grown by a character or a [creature](#creature). It sits high and flags white underneath when raised.

entries.name: bear_tail
entries.description: A short stumpy [tail](#tail) like a bear's, on a humanoid or costumed character. It normally comes with [bear](#bear) ears.

entries.name: multicolored_tail
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) [tail](#tail) showing two or more distinct colours. Combinations drawn only from white, grey and black fall short on their own; such a [shade](#shade) counts only as one of three or more colours together.

entries.name: forked_tail
entries.description: A single [tail](#tail) that divides into two partway along its length. It differs from [multiple_tails](#multiple_tails), where several separate tails grow from the base.

entries.name: weasel_tail
entries.description: The long, slim, lightly furred [tail](#tail) of a [weasel](#weasel), stoat or [ferret](#ferret), often finished with a [dark](#dark) tip. It hangs low and trails behind the wearer.

entries.name: fiery_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) made of [fire](#fire), or [burning](#burning) along its whole length. When only the very tip is alight, the flame-tipped variant is the right [tag](#tag).

entries.name: goat_tail
entries.description: The short [tail](#tail) of a [goat](#goat), held upright and often finished with a tuft. It usually accompanies curved [horns](#horns) and [hooves](#hooves) on a caprine character.

entries.name: two-tone_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) [carrying](#carrying) exactly two colours, most often a base [shade](#shade) with a contrasting tip or underside. The narrower case of a multicoloured tail.

entries.name: otter_tail
entries.description: An otter's [tail](#tail), broad where it meets the body and flattening as it tapers to the tip, on a human or anthro character.

entries.name: sheep_tail
entries.description: The short, stubby, wool-covered [tail](#tail) of a [sheep](#sheep), appearing on an otherwise human or anthro body. Implies tail.

entries.name: pig_tail
entries.description: The short [tail](#tail) of a [pig](#pig), recognisable by the tight curl near its tip. Nothing to do with the hairstyle of the same English name, which is tagged [twintails](#twintails).

entries.name: fur-tipped_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) bare or scaled along its length that carries a tuft of fur at the very end, as on many [dragon](#dragon) designs. Tails furred from base to tip do not qualify.

entries.name: scorpion_tail
entries.description: A segmented arthropod [tail](#tail) ending in a venomous barb, usually carried arched forward over the [back](#back).

entries.name: gradient_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) whose colour blends steadily from base to tip instead of changing at a hard line. Tag every colour in the blend that [can](#can) be told apart.

entries.name: electric_plug_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that finishes in a mains plug rather than in fur or a point. The whole tail is often drawn as [flexible](#flexible) [cable](#cable), though it may just as [well](#well) be an ordinary tail with a plug at the tip.

entries.name: dinosaur_tail
entries.description: A thick saurian [tail](#tail) tapering to a point, scaled or ridged along its length, carried out behind the body as a counterweight. Marks a saurian character rather than a whole [animal](#animal).

entries.name: intertwined_tails
entries.description: Two tails wound around one another where their owners stand or sit close together. It works as a quiet [sign](#sign) of affection even when the characters touch nowhere else.

entries.name: hyena_tail
entries.description: A short, thick [tail](#tail) of the kind a [hyena](#hyena) carries, bushy along its length and often darkening toward the tip. It sits higher and stops shorter than a wolf's.

entries.name: sharp_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that narrows to an angular, blade-like point at the tip rather than tapering smoothly or ending in a tuft.

entries.name: penguin_tail
entries.description: The short stiff wedge of a penguin's [tail](#tail) on a character, set low on the [back](#back) and often spread into a small fan.

entries.name: chipmunk_tail
entries.description: A bushy upright [tail](#tail) of the [squirrel](#squirrel) kind, marked with the chipmunk's [dark](#dark) stripe. Nearly always drawn together with the matching ears.

entries.name: red_panda_tail
entries.description: A thick, bushy [tail](#tail) banded in [rust](#rust) and [cream](#cream), copied from a red [panda](#panda). Usually drawn as long as the character is [tall](#tall).

entries.name: alpaca_tail
entries.description: A short, thick, woolly [tail](#tail) like an alpaca's, carried low against the [back](#back). It appears on alpaca-themed characters and on costumes alike.

entries.name: stiff_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that would normally hang loose held rigid and straight out, betraying tension in the rest of the body. Most often anger, shock, fear or [pain](#pain), occasionally arousal.

entries.name: jackal_tail
entries.description: A slim straight [tail](#tail) with a [dark](#dark) bushy tip, of the kind a [jackal](#jackal) has. It is thinner than a [wolf_tail](#wolf_tail) and far less [fluffy](#fluffy) than a [fox_tail](#fox_tail).

entries.name: expressive_tail
entries.description: The [tail](#tail) does the emotional work, curling, bristling, wagging or [hanging](#hanging) low in step with the mood. Read it as body language rather than as [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: extra_tails
entries.description: More tails than the character normally carries, added on top of their usual number. A kitsune's regular nine are not extra and belong with [multiple_tails](#multiple_tails).

entries.name: tail_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) fastened to a character's [tail](#tail) as decoration, tucked into the fur or tied on. Works like a hair flower one limb further down.

entries.name: komainu_tail
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) upward-sweeping [tail](#tail) modelled on the guardian lion-dog statues found at shrines, drawn shaggy and curling. It normally arrives with the matching ears on the same character.

entries.name: ferret_tail
entries.description: A long slender [tail](#tail) with dense short fur, tapering the way a ferret's does. Nearly always paired with matching ears.

entries.name: tail_belt
entries.description: A [strap](#strap) or [belt](#belt) fitted around a [tail](#tail), either purely decorative or used to hold something to it, [sitting](#sitting) along the tail rather than at the waist.

entries.name: fuse_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) shaped like the [fuse](#fuse) of a [bomb](#bomb), commonly drawn lit and sputtering at the end. It belongs to explosive-themed characters and mascots.

entries.name: tail_pull
entries.description: Someone grabbing a [tail](#tail) and hauling on it, used for [teasing](#teasing), restraint or [dragging](#dragging) a character [back](#back). Usually gets a pained or startled reaction.

entries.name: chameleon_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) of the [chameleon](#chameleon) sort, tapering to a tight coil at the tip for gripping. Reptile-themed characters and animal-eared designs wear one.

entries.name: panda_tail
entries.description: The short rounded [tail](#tail) of a [panda](#panda), white with a [dark](#dark) edge, growing from a human or anthro [figure](#figure).

entries.name: beaver_tail
entries.description: A wide flattened [paddle](#paddle) of a [tail](#tail) with a scaly surface, taken from a [beaver](#beaver). It is distinctive enough to name the species by itself, and generally comes with beaver ears.

entries.name: curled_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) carried in a curve or a coil rather than [hanging](#hanging) straight, often arched up over the [back](#back). Typical of spitz-type dogs and of pigs.

entries.name: anteater_tail
entries.description: A long [tail](#tail) with the thick shaggy fur of an [anteater](#anteater), growing from an otherwise human [figure](#figure). Broader and coarser than a [fox](#fox) tail.

entries.name: cheetah_tail
entries.description: A long slim spotted [tail](#tail) of the cheetah sort, usually ringed towards the tip. It appears on animal-eared girls and on full anthro cheetahs alike.

entries.name: tail_under_clothes
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) emerging from beneath a [skirt](#skirt), [shorts](#shorts) or other bottomwear rather than through an [opening](#opening) made for it, with the hem simply draping over its base.

entries.name: tail_around_another's_leg
entries.description: A character's [tail](#tail) curls around someone else's leg, coiling or draped over it. Usually reads as affection, [teasing](#teasing), or a claim on the other person.

entries.name: tasmanian_devil_tail
entries.description: A short, thick [tail](#tail) modeled on a Tasmanian devil's, tapering to a blunt point on an otherwise human-shaped body. Generally paired with the matching ears.

entries.name: giraffe_tail
entries.description: A long thin [tail](#tail) ending in a [dark](#dark) [switch](#switch) of hair, taken from a [giraffe](#giraffe). Worn by animal-eared characters and giraffe-themed designs.

entries.name: skeletal_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) made of exposed vertebrae with little or [no](#no) [flesh](#flesh) on it. Belongs to [undead](#undead) beasts and decayed dragons more often than to living ones.

entries.name: skunk_tail
entries.description: A thick [plume](#plume) of a [tail](#tail) in skunk colouring, black with a white stripe or band. Held raised behind the character where its bulk shows.

entries.name: aqua_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) in blue-green, furred, scaled or finned. Add the kind of tail as [well](#well).

entries.name: moose_tail
entries.description: The short stubby [tail](#tail) of a [moose](#moose) on a character. A small detail that comes along with the ears and the [antlers](#antlers).

entries.name: meerkat_tail
entries.description: A thin tapering [tail](#tail) with a darker tip, borrowed from a meerkat and given to a human-shaped character. Usually paired with [meerkat_ears](#meerkat_ears) on the same design.

entries.name: bat_tail
entries.description: A short [tail](#tail) ending in a small pointed or leaf-shaped flap, copied from a bat. It nearly always comes with bat ears and [wings](#wings) on the same character.

entries.name: abdomen_tail
entries.description: A humanoid [figure](#figure) carries a segmented arthropod abdomen where a [tail](#tail) would sit, as on [bee](#bee), [spider](#spider) and [scorpion](#scorpion) girls. Fully taur-shaped insect bodies are built differently and are not covered.

entries.name: thick_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) notably wide or [fat](#fat) along its length, as on a [dragon](#dragon), [crocodile](#crocodile) or heavy-set canine in [furry](#furry) art.

entries.name: heart_tail_duo
entries.description: Two characters bring their tails together so the curves close into a [heart](#heart) between or above them. Not for one character shaping it with several tails.

entries.name: glowing_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that gives off light, either along its length or at the tip alone. Spirits, deep-water creatures and magical animals carry one.

entries.name: crystal_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) formed of [crystal](#crystal) instead of [flesh](#flesh) and fur, faceted and frequently see-through. Belongs to elemental and gemstone-themed characters.

entries.name: tamandua_tail
entries.description: The long, thick, partly bare prehensile [tail](#tail) of a lesser [anteater](#anteater), tapering toward a hairless gripping tip.

entries.name: zebra_tail
entries.description: A zebra's [tail](#tail): short-haired along most of its length with a striped, tufted end. Drawn on animal-eared characters and full anthros alike.

entries.name: snake_head_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that terminates in a second [snake](#snake) head, complete with eyes and mouth, so the limb [can](#can) bite. Distinct from a [plain](#plain) [snake_tail](#snake_tail), which simply tapers to a point.

entries.name: spotted_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) marked with [spots](#spots), usually continuing a pattern that runs across the [back](#back) and [legs](#legs). Typical of leopards, cheetahs, [deer](#deer) and hyenas.

entries.name: tail_around_arm
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) wound around an arm, either its owner's own or one held close. Long, [flexible](#flexible) tails make this easiest, and it often reads as a [nervous](#nervous) or coy [habit](#habit).

entries.name: tail_fondling
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) being stroked and petted gently rather than seized outright. The soft, lingering handling is what separates it from a tail grab or pull.

entries.name: tadpole_tail
entries.description: A character given the broad, flattened, finned [tail](#tail) of a [tadpole](#tadpole) rather than the round tail of a [fish](#fish) or mammal.

entries.name: trimmed_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) whose fur has clearly been cut, ending in a blunt or squared-off edge instead of tapering naturally. The effect resembles a straight fringe cut into a person's hair.

entries.name: elephant_tail
entries.description: A thin, tapering [tail](#tail) with a small tuft at the end, copied from an [elephant](#elephant) onto a human or humanoid body. Usually accompanied by [elephant_ears](#elephant_ears).

entries.name: tail_around_waist
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) encircling a waist, worn almost like a [belt](#belt) or draped across the hips, whether the owner's own or someone [standing](#standing) close.

entries.name: inconvenient_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) that gets in its owner's way, shut in a [door](#door), sat on, trailing through the [food](#food) or making [clothes](#clothes) and chairs [awkward](#awkward). The nuisance is the point of the picture.

entries.name: braided_tail
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) [tail](#tail) whose hair has been plaited along its length, sometimes tied off with a [ribbon](#ribbon) at the tip. Horses and lion-tailed characters are the usual candidates.

entries.name: chinchilla_tail
entries.description: A short, densely furred [tail](#tail) taken from a chinchilla, curving upward at the tip. Worn by rodent-themed characters, nearly always beside matching ears.

entries.name: gazelle_tail
entries.description: A short antelope [tail](#tail) tipped with a [dark](#dark) tuft, worn by a character who is otherwise human-bodied. Oryx tails are filed under the same name.

entries.name: okapi_tail
entries.description: A short tufted [tail](#tail) borrowed from the okapi, often [carrying](#carrying) the striped pattern of the animal's rear. Usually drawn together with [okapi_ears](#okapi_ears) on the same character.

entries.name: tail_removed
entries.description: A character who normally has a [tail](#tail) is shown without one, the stump or bare spot visible. The absence is deliberate rather than the tail simply being out of frame.

entries.name: wings
entries.description: A character has wings on the [back](#back), whether grown naturally or worn as an accessory. It is not used for an ordinary [bird](#bird); add the wing type, such as [feathered_wings](#feathered_wings), [bat_wings](#bat_wings), or [butterfly_wings](#butterfly_wings), along with its colour.

entries.name: head_wings
entries.description: Small [wings](#wings) growing from the sides of the head, standard on [demon](#demon) girls and [bird](#bird) girls. Hair styled into wing [shapes](#shapes) is [hair_wings](#hair_wings); wings mounted on headwear are [winged_helmet](#winged_helmet) or [winged_hat](#winged_hat).

entries.name: feathered_wings
entries.description: Wings clothed in [feathers](#feathers), as on birds and angels, rather than bat membrane or insect panes. The commonest wing type on angels and harpies.

entries.name: bat_wings
entries.description: Leathery membranous [wings](#wings) ribbed like a bat's, growing from the [back](#back) or, in smaller pairs, from the head. They are the standard wings of demons, succubi and vampires, opposite the feathered kind an [angel](#angel) wears.

entries.name: black_wings
entries.description: Wings in black, feathered or leathery, on angels, demons, crows and fallen heroes. Name the kind as [well](#well) with [bat_wings](#bat_wings) or [feathered_wings](#feathered_wings).

entries.name: demon_wings
entries.description: The [wings](#wings) of a [demon](#demon) girl or boy, or a pair worn as part of a demon [costume](#costume). They overlap heavily with [bat_wings](#bat_wings) but may carry [claws](#claws), unusual colours and more stylised [shapes](#shapes).

entries.name: white_wings
entries.description: Wings of any kind coloured white, most often the feathered pair of an [angel](#angel) but also [butterfly](#butterfly) or bat [shapes](#shapes). Tag [wings](#wings) alongside the wing type, such as [feathered_wings](#feathered_wings).

entries.name: angel_wings
entries.description: Large white feathered [wings](#wings) of the kind an [angel](#angel) wears. Feathered wings in another colour, or built like a bird's, are simply [feathered_wings](#feathered_wings).

entries.name: low_wings
entries.description: Wings growing from the lower [back](#back) or the hips rather than from the shoulders. The arrangement is common on succubi and on some [demon](#demon) designs.

entries.name: fairy_wings
entries.description: The [wings](#wings) of a [fairy](#fairy), ranging from insect-like membranes to [leaf](#leaf), petal or [crystal](#crystal) [shapes](#shapes). Butterfly wings are a separate [tag](#tag) and do not belong here.

entries.name: bird_wings
entries.description: Feathered [wings](#wings) shaped like a bird's, growing from a humanoid such as a [harpy](#harpy), [bird](#bird) girl or winged boy. Meant for winged [people](#people); an actual bird needs [no](#no) separate wing [tag](#tag).

entries.name: ice_wings
entries.description: Wings built out of [ice](#ice), with a crystalline, frost-covered surface. Only [tag](#tag) them where that icy texture is actually rendered, not for every cold-themed character.

entries.name: asymmetrical_wings
entries.description: The [wings](#wings) on either side do not match in size, shape or colour, as when a feathered one is paired with a leathery bat wing. It is the mismatch that matters, not the kind of wing.

entries.name: insect_wings
entries.description: Thin membranous [wings](#wings) veined like a bug's, growing from a character's [back](#back). Fairies, [bee](#bee) girls and [dragonfly](#dragonfly) designs carry them; wings [patterned](#patterned) like a butterfly's are [butterfly_wings](#butterfly_wings) instead.

entries.name: detached_wings
entries.description: Wings [floating](#floating) free of the [back](#back) rather than joined to it, frequently [glowing](#glowing) or plainly magical in origin. The visible gap is what separates them from ordinary [wings](#wings).

entries.name: single_wing
entries.description: A character has one wing where a pair would be expected, the other absent or severed. Tag alongside [wings](#wings).

entries.name: dragon_wings
entries.description: Membranous clawed [wings](#wings) of the draconic sort, on a [creature](#creature) or on a character given them. Often [folded](#folded) down against the [back](#back) when not in use.

entries.name: red_wings
entries.description: Wings of any type in red, feathered, bat-like, insect or [energy](#energy). Describes the [wings](#wings)' colour; add the wing type [tag](#tag) such as [bat_wings](#bat_wings).

entries.name: multiple_wings
entries.description: A character [carrying](#carrying) two or more pairs of [wings](#wings), such as a six-winged [seraph](#seraph) or a four-winged insect design. A single pair, however large, uses wings alone.

entries.name: blue_wings
entries.description: Wings of any [construction](#construction), feathered, membranous, insect or made of light, coloured blue. It describes the [wings](#wings) themselves; blue wing ornaments on clothing do not count.

entries.name: butterfly_wings
entries.description: The character carries [wings](#wings) shaped and [patterned](#patterned) like a butterfly's — broad, colourful and often part-translucent. Fairies and insect-themed characters wear them most.

entries.name: mini_wings
entries.description: Undersized [wings](#wings) on the [back](#back), too small to plausibly carry the character who has them.

entries.name: winged_arms
entries.description: Wings growing where a character's arms would normally be, as on harpies and other [bird](#bird) [people](#people). Tag [wings](#wings) alongside it, plus a type [tag](#tag) such as feathered or bat-like where it applies.

entries.name: mechanical_wings
entries.description: Wings built from metal and [machinery](#machinery), often detailed with hydraulics, cables, [gears](#gears) or small [glowing](#glowing) lights along the frame.

entries.name: multicolored_wings
entries.description: Wings [carrying](#carrying) two or more colours, blended as a gradient or [split](#split) into separate areas. Where one wing differs entirely from the other, [asymmetrical_wings](#asymmetrical_wings) applies, and pairs drawn only in [greyscale](#greyscale) fall outside the rule.

entries.name: purple_wings
entries.description: Wings that are purple, whether feathered, bat-like, or insect [wings](#wings). Combine with wings and the type, such as [bat_wings](#bat_wings) or [butterfly_wings](#butterfly_wings).

entries.name: crystal_wings
entries.description: Wings made of [crystal](#crystal) or [studded](#studded) with it, either fully crystalline or thin frames [carrying](#carrying) [floating](#floating) crystals where [feathers](#feathers) would be. A recurring design on gem-themed and fae characters.

entries.name: robot_wings
entries.description: Wings built from metal plates, panels or thruster assemblies rather than [feathers](#feathers) or skin. Common on [mecha](#mecha), angels rendered as machines and armoured flight suits.

entries.name: energy_wings
entries.description: Wings made of [glowing](#glowing) power or [magic](#magic) instead of [feathers](#feathers) or membrane, often [floating](#floating) free behind the [back](#back) rather than joined to it. Common on angels, magical girls and [mecha](#mecha).

entries.name: spread_wings
entries.description: Wings held fully open and put on [display](#display), best used when they are being shown off rather than used for [flying](#flying), since flight already implies open [wings](#wings).

entries.name: yellow_wings
entries.description: A pair of [wings](#wings) coloured yellow, feathered, insect or otherwise. Tag wings and the wing type.

entries.name: pink_wings
entries.description: Wings of any kind coloured pink, from feathered to bat-like, insect or [fairy](#fairy). Add the wing type [tag](#tag) such as [feathered_wings](#feathered_wings) or [butterfly_wings](#butterfly_wings).

entries.name: brown_wings
entries.description: Wings of any kind coloured brown — most often the feathered [wings](#wings) of a [hawk](#hawk) or [owl](#owl), or leathery bat wings. Add the wing type alongside it.

entries.name: no_wings
entries.description: A winged character shown without [wings](#wings), whether as an oversight across [comic](#comic) panels or a deliberate [choice](#choice). Wings tucked away but still glimpsed are wings_hidden.

entries.name: large_wings
entries.description: Wings at least three quarters of the body's [height](#height), or [reaching](#reaching) an arm's length when spread, with a broad surface. Size against the body is what the [tag](#tag) measures.

entries.name: wing_ornament
entries.description: A decorative accessory attached to a character's own [wings](#wings), such as rings, ribbons, or set jewels. It applies only to beings that actually have wings, not to wing-shaped jewellery worn elsewhere.

entries.name: oversized_wings
entries.description: Wings out of all proportion to the body they grow from, [spreading](#spreading) far wider than the [figure](#figure) itself. Used for dramatic silhouettes on angels, demons and dragons.

entries.name: transparent_wings
entries.description: Wings that are see-through in part or in whole, typical of insect, [fairy](#fairy) or energy-type [wings](#wings). Not to be [confused](#confused) with [drawn_wings](#drawn_wings), which are wings sketched onto the picture as a doodle rather than rendered wings.

entries.name: green_wings
entries.description: A pair of green [wings](#wings), feathered, insect-like or leathery, on a [bird](#bird), [fairy](#fairy) or [dragon](#dragon) character. Wings that fade between colours take [gradient_wings](#gradient_wings).

entries.name: grey_wings
entries.description: Wings, feathered or otherwise, coloured a [plain](#plain) grey rather than white, black or another [shade](#shade). Applies to birds, angels and any other winged character or [creature](#creature).

entries.name: glowing_wings
entries.description: A pair of [wings](#wings) made of light or [shining](#shining) with it, whether feathered, membranous or pure [energy](#energy). Angels, awakened forms and energy constructs wear them.

entries.name: gradient_wings
entries.description: Wings whose colour shifts gradually from one hue into another, white [feathers](#feathers) [fading](#fading) to blue at the tips for instance.

entries.name: torn_wings
entries.description: Wings that are ripped, tattered or otherwise [damaged](#damaged), common on fallen angels, cursed fairies or battle-worn dragons. Signals [injury](#injury) or decay rather than intact plumage or membrane.

entries.name: fiery_wings
entries.description: Wings made of flame, [burning](#burning) outward from the [back](#back) instead of [carrying](#carrying) [feathers](#feathers) or membrane. Phoenixes and [fire](#fire) spirits wear them.

entries.name: single_head_wing
entries.description: A lone wing growing from the side of the head, with [no](#no) [mirror](#mirror) on the other [temple](#temple). Small and ornamental rather than something to [fly](#fly) with.

entries.name: two-tone_wings
entries.description: Wings [carrying](#carrying) two colours, whether [split](#split) between upper and lower surfaces or shading from base to tip. When each wing is a different colour on its own, [asymmetrical_wings](#asymmetrical_wings) applies instead.

entries.name: hair_wings
entries.description: Wings formed out of a character's own hair rather than [feathers](#feathers) or membrane. Wings that sit on the head but are not made of hair take [head_wings](#head_wings) instead.

entries.name: mismatched_wings
entries.description: One character wearing two unlike [wings](#wings) - a feathered one beside a bat wing, say, or two different colors of the same kind. Unlike sets of wings on separate bodies are mixed_wings instead.

entries.name: moth_wings
entries.description: Broad scaled [wings](#wings) held out flat and [patterned](#patterned) in muted browns and greys, as a moth's are, rather than the brighter pair a [butterfly](#butterfly) folds upright. They may be spread wide or [lying](#lying) closed over the [back](#back).

entries.name: orange_wings
entries.description: Wings in orange, whether feathered, membranous, insect-like or made of light. Only the colour is recorded; shape and size have their own tags.

entries.name: pegasus_wings
entries.description: The feathered [wings](#wings) of a winged [horse](#horse), either on the [animal](#animal) itself or on a character borrowing the design. Their equine associations rather than their shape set them apart from [angel](#angel) wings.

entries.name: skeletal_wings
entries.description: Wings reduced to their [bone](#bone) frame, with the membrane or [feathers](#feathers) gone. A regular feature of liches, [undead](#undead) dragons and death-themed designs.

entries.name: aqua_wings
entries.description: Wings in pale blue-green, feathered, membranous or made of light. Add the wing type, such as [feathered_wings](#feathered_wings).

entries.name: ankle_wings
entries.description: Small [wings](#wings) at the [feet](#feet) or ankles, growing from the skin, fixed to the footwear or [floating](#floating) free alongside. The messenger-god look, also used on speed-themed designs.

entries.name: spiked_wings
entries.description: Wings whose edges or [joints](#joints) carry sharp points, sometimes paired with a barbed membrane. Typical of dragons, demons, and mechanical designs.

entries.name: metal_wings
entries.description: Wings built from plates, blades or [machinery](#machinery) in place of [feathers](#feathers) or membrane, fitted to mechanical angels and armored character designs.

entries.name: dragonfly_wings
entries.description: Long narrow [transparent](#transparent) [wings](#wings) finely veined like a dragonfly's, held flat out from the [back](#back). Used for fae and [sprite](#sprite) designs rather than feathered or bat wings.

entries.name: bee_wings
entries.description: A single pair of small rounded [transparent](#transparent) [wings](#wings) taken from a [bee](#bee), usually simplified to [plain](#plain) glassy [shapes](#shapes). Dragonfly and most other insect wings come as two pairs, though rapid beating [can](#can) blur the difference.

entries.name: leaf_wings
entries.description: Wings made out of leaves, or cut to the [outline](#outline) of one. Fairies, [plant](#plant) creatures and woodland spirits carry them.

entries.name: leg_wings
entries.description: Small [wings](#wings) [sitting](#sitting) somewhere on the leg above the ankle. They may grow from the limb, be fastened to footwear, or hover free beside it.

entries.name: plant_wings
entries.description: Wings formed from leaves, [petals](#petals), or [vines](#vines) instead of [feathers](#feathers) or membrane. A common feature on fairies and [nature](#nature) spirits.

entries.name: golden_wings
entries.description: Wings of [gold](#gold), whether feathered, plated or made of light. Angels, divine beasts and gilded machines carry them.

entries.name: rainbow_wings
entries.description: Wings whose [feathers](#feathers) or membrane carry the colors of the spectrum. Seen on fairies, angels, and other [fantasy](#fantasy) creatures, as [well](#well) as on pride-themed designs.

entries.name: wrist_wings
entries.description: Small [wings](#wings) growing from, or fastened at, the wrists. They read as decorative on some outfits and as genuine [anatomy](#anatomy) on [fairy](#fairy) and [demon](#demon) designs.

entries.name: cartoon_wings
entries.description: Wings drawn as a flat stylised shape with [no](#no) [feathers](#feathers) or membrane worked out. Often small joke [wings](#wings) sprouted for a single moment.

entries.name: horns
entries.description: One or more pointed horns grow from the character's head. Add [single_horn](#single_horn) when there is only one; projections that [fork](#fork) somewhere along their length are [antlers](#antlers) instead.

entries.name: demon_horns
entries.description: The [horns](#horns) of a [demon](#demon) girl or boy, either short stubby pairs curving up as in the [emoji](#emoji), or long [ornate](#ornate) ones recalling [goat](#goat) or [sheep](#sheep) horns and sometimes smooth and metallic. They rise from the sides or top of the head, unlike skin-covered horns set in the [forehead](#forehead).

entries.name: dragon_horns
entries.description: Horns of the draconic sort on a character or [creature](#creature), typically thick, ridged and swept [back](#back) over the [skull](#skull). Standard equipment on [dragon](#dragon) girls and boys.

entries.name: single_horn
entries.description: One horn grows from the character's head, [unicorn](#unicorn) or [oni](#oni) style. With two or more, use [horns](#horns) instead.

entries.name: black_horns
entries.description: Horns coloured black growing from a character's head, typical of demons, [oni](#oni) and [dragon](#dragon) girls. They may be short nubs or long [sweeping](#sweeping) curves.

entries.name: antennae
entries.description: Feeler [organs](#organs) rising from the head of an insect, a [crab](#crab) or a bug-like character, artificial copies included. Hair [standing](#standing) up in the same shape is [antenna_hair](#antenna_hair), and a [radio](#radio) [mast](#mast) is [radio_antenna](#radio_antenna).

entries.name: antlers
entries.description: Branched bony growths of the [deer](#deer) [family](#family), worn by characters, real animals and Eastern-style dragons alike. Unlike [horns](#horns) they [fork](#fork) and are [shed](#shed) each year; a bare [skull](#skull) [carrying](#carrying) them is [animal_skull](#animal_skull).

entries.name: cow_horns
entries.description: The short [horns](#horns) of a [cow](#cow) or [bull](#bull), curving outward from the sides of the head. Seen on cow girls, minotaurs and demon-styled designs, usually together with [cow_ears](#cow_ears).

entries.name: red_horns
entries.description: Horns growing from a character's head that are red, common on demons, [oni](#oni) and [dragon](#dragon) characters. Refers to the [horns](#horns)' own colour, not a red headwear ornament.

entries.name: ox_horns
entries.description: Cattle [horns](#horns) rising from the head, thick at the root and [sweeping](#sweeping) outward or up. They usually accompany [ox_ears](#ox_ears) on the same character.

entries.name: curled_horns
entries.description: Horns that [spiral](#spiral) or coil round like a ram's, worn by [sheep](#sheep) characters, demons and dragons. Set against straight [horns](#horns) and merely curved ones.

entries.name: skin-covered_horns
entries.description: Horns that share the body's skin colour and blend into the head without a visible [border](#border), sometimes darkening toward the tips. Tag beside [horns](#horns).

entries.name: goat_horns
entries.description: Horns of the [goat](#goat) kind, curving backward but staying largely upright rather than winding round the head. Fully [coiled](#coiled) [horns](#horns) are [sheep_horns](#sheep_horns) or [curled_horns](#curled_horns), a mix-up this [tag](#tag) attracts.

entries.name: sheep_horns
entries.description: Curled ram-like [horns](#horns) spiralling out beside the head. Implies horns.

entries.name: multiple_horns
entries.description: A character bearing more than two [horns](#horns), such as a smaller second pair set behind the first or a whole [crown](#crown) of them. An ordinary pair uses horns alone.

entries.name: white_horns
entries.description: Horns colored white or a pale [bone](#bone) [shade](#shade), seen on demons, dragons, [oni](#oni) and horned girls alike.

entries.name: small_horns
entries.description: Horns much smaller than usual, easy to mistake for hair ornaments or [animal](#animal) ears, as on many young [demon](#demon) characters.

entries.name: brown_horns
entries.description: Horns coloured brown, whether curling ram [horns](#horns), straight [spikes](#spikes) or small [demon](#demon) horns. Add horns.

entries.name: reindeer_antlers
entries.description: Branching [reindeer](#reindeer) [antlers](#antlers) on a character's head, whether grown or worn as a Christmas [headpiece](#headpiece). Usually part of a festive look with a santa [costume](#costume) or reindeer costume.

entries.name: asymmetrical_horns
entries.description: The [horns](#horns) on a character's head do not match, varying in length, shape or colour. A difference of length alone is [uneven_horns](#uneven_horns) and one of design or colour [mismatched_horns](#mismatched_horns); both tags go on a character showing both.

entries.name: yellow_horns
entries.description: A character's [horns](#horns) are yellow. Tag horns alongside.

entries.name: grey_horns
entries.description: The character's [horns](#horns) are grey, be they small nubs, curling ram horns or long [dragon](#dragon) horns. The rest of the body keeps its own colour tags.

entries.name: cone_horns
entries.description: Straight cone-shaped [horns](#horns), neither curled nor curved. The cartoon image of an [oni](#oni) is the usual source, generally a small pair on the [forehead](#forehead).

entries.name: broken_horn
entries.description: One of a character's [horns](#horns) has been snapped off or chipped short. When both are [damaged](#damaged), broken_horns covers it; add horns.

entries.name: blue_horns
entries.description: Horns coloured blue growing from the head, whether curved, straight or branching. Dragon girls and ice-themed demons carry them most often; [antlers](#antlers) have a [tag](#tag) of their own.

entries.name: multicolored_horns
entries.description: Horns showing two or more separate colours along their length. Where the colours blend smoothly into one another, gradient [horns](#horns) is the closer fit.

entries.name: mechanical_horns
entries.description: Horns that read as metal or cybernetic components rather than [bone](#bone) or keratin, often seen on androids or heavily armoured characters.

entries.name: deer_antlers
entries.description: The branching [antlers](#antlers) of a [deer](#deer) or [reindeer](#reindeer), growing from a character's or creature's head. Distinct from [horns](#horns), which are unbranched.

entries.name: striped_horns
entries.description: Horns banded with a second colour or tone along their length, a common design touch on demons, dragons and similar characters. Implies [horns](#horns).

entries.name: purple_horns
entries.description: Horns that are purple, on a [demon](#demon), [dragon](#dragon), [oni](#oni), or other horned character, whether a single horn or a pair. Combine with [horns](#horns) and the character's species [tag](#tag) where one applies.

entries.name: uneven_horns
entries.description: Horns of matching design but different lengths. Different colours add [mismatched_horns](#mismatched_horns), and entirely different styles use mismatched_horns on its own.

entries.name: eastern_dragon_horns
entries.description: Branching [horns](#horns) of the sort an East Asian [dragon](#dragon) wears, close to [antlers](#antlers) but with a shape of their own. Seen on dragon girls and other humanoid dragon designs.

entries.name: pink_horns
entries.description: One or more [horns](#horns) coloured pink growing from a character's head. Their shape, from small nubs to long curves, is recorded by the other horn tags.

entries.name: horns_through_headwear
entries.description: A character's real [horns](#horns) come out through holes in a [hat](#hat), [hood](#hood) or cap so that the headwear [can](#can) still be worn. It differs from [horned_headwear](#horned_headwear), where the horns are part of the accessory itself.

entries.name: fiery_horns
entries.description: Horns formed from [fire](#fire), or ordinary [horns](#horns) that appear to burn. Demon and [dragon](#dragon) designs with a flame motif carry them.

entries.name: antlers_through_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) or [helmet](#helmet) is worn with the [antlers](#antlers) pushed out through it rather than flattened beneath. Holes cut in the [crown](#crown) let the branches rise clear of the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: green_horns
entries.description: The character's [horns](#horns) are green, be they short nubs, curled ram horns or long [dragon](#dragon) horns. Horns that fade from one colour into another take [gradient_horns](#gradient_horns).

entries.name: glowing_horns
entries.description: One or more [horns](#horns) emitting light. Usually read as a [sign](#sign) of power, an awakened form or a demonic [nature](#nature).

entries.name: hair_on_horn
entries.description: Locks of hair [resting](#resting) over or draped across a character's [horns](#horns) or [antlers](#antlers).

entries.name: two-tone_horns
entries.description: Horns bearing exactly two colours, often a darker base [fading](#fading) or banding into a paler tip. The narrower case of multicoloured [horns](#horns).

entries.name: gradient_horns
entries.description: Horns whose colour shifts smoothly from base to tip, black [fading](#fading) into red for instance. A subset of [multicolored_horns](#multicolored_horns).

entries.name: long_horns
entries.description: Horns grown far beyond the length the design would ordinarily call for, [sweeping](#sweeping) [well](#well) clear of the [skull](#skull). Apply it alongside the [plain](#plain) [horns](#horns) [tag](#tag) rather than in place of it.

entries.name: orange_horns
entries.description: Horns growing from the head in orange, at any size from short nubs to long curving sweeps.

entries.name: large_horns
entries.description: Horns exaggerated in size against the head, [sweeping](#sweeping), curling or branching [well](#well) beyond it. Demons, dragons and [heavy](#heavy) beast designs carry them most often.

entries.name: tree_horns
entries.description: Horns or [antlers](#antlers) that [branch](#branch) like the limbs of a [tree](#tree), forking into twig-like tips. Artists often push the resemblance further by growing leaves, blossoms or small [fruit](#fruit) along them.

entries.name: huge_horns
entries.description: Horns considerably larger than the head they grow from, [heavy](#heavy) enough to look like a burden. Size against the character is what counts, not the shape.

entries.name: unicorn_horn
entries.description: A single horn rising from the centre of the [forehead](#forehead), ridged in rings or twisted like a corkscrew, as unicorns are conventionally drawn. Older usage called it an alicorn, though that word now usually means a winged [unicorn](#unicorn) instead.

entries.name: mismatched_horns
entries.description: The two [horns](#horns) differ from each other in color, shape or design. When both horns are the same kind and only their length differs, use [uneven_horns](#uneven_horns) instead.

entries.name: moth_antennae
entries.description: Feathery, frond-like [antennae](#antennae) rising from a character's head. Far bushier than the thin clubbed pair a [butterfly](#butterfly) carries.

entries.name: forward_facing_horns
entries.description: Horns that curve or jut toward the front rather than [sweeping](#sweeping) [back](#back) or [standing](#standing) upright. Their direction is the whole of what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: aqua_horns
entries.description: Horns growing from the head in a blue-green [shade](#shade). Common on [demon](#demon), [dragon](#dragon) and [oni](#oni) designs.

entries.name: giraffe_horns
entries.description: Short blunt knobs on top of the head, furred and rounded at the tip in the manner of a giraffe's ossicones. Far stubbier than the [horns](#horns) of [deer](#deer) or antelope characters.

entries.name: low_horns
entries.description: Horns emerging at or below ear level and growing outward or downward rather than rising from the [crown](#crown). They are frequently drawn curled.

entries.name: crystal_horns
entries.description: Horns made of [translucent](#translucent) [crystal](#crystal) instead of keratin, usually faceted and sometimes lit from inside. A common trait on [fantasy](#fantasy) and [monster](#monster) characters.

entries.name: curved_horns
entries.description: Horns that bend along their length rather than [running](#running) straight, swept [back](#back), hooked forward or arcing round. A frequent trait on demons and beast characters.

entries.name: gold_horns
entries.description: Horns coloured [gold](#gold), either polished metal or gilded [bone](#bone). Demonic, divine and dragon-blooded designs favour them.

entries.name: horns_through_hood
entries.description: Real [horns](#horns) pierce the [fabric](#fabric) of a [hood](#hood) and stand out through it, letting the hood sit properly on the head. A narrower case of horns passing through headwear.

entries.name: no_horns
entries.description: Horns belonging to a character's usual design are absent from the head. The [forehead](#forehead) and [crown](#crown) are drawn smooth, as on an ordinary human.

entries.name: antlers_through_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) is pulled up with [antlers](#antlers) coming out through slits in the [cloth](#cloth). The narrower case of [headgear](#headgear) worn around branching [horns](#horns).

entries.name: antelope_horns
entries.description: Slim [horns](#horns) [sweeping](#sweeping) [back](#back) or twisting upward as an antelope's do, growing from the head. Thinner and more graceful than bovine or [demon](#demon) horns.

entries.name: sprout_on_head
entries.description: A small [plant](#plant) [sprout](#sprout) growing directly from the top of a character's head, leaves included. Not to be [confused](#confused) with [antenna_hair](#antenna_hair), which is simply a stray strand.

entries.name: translucent_horns
entries.description: Horns that let light pass through, drawn as [glass](#glass), [crystal](#crystal) or amber rather than opaque keratin. Gives a character's [horns](#horns) a glassy or gem-like [quality](#quality).

entries.name: spiked_horns
entries.description: Horns whose surface carries extra points or barbs rather than [running](#running) smooth. Common on demons, dragons, and other monstrous characters.

entries.name: detached_horns
entries.description: Horns hovering beside or above the head without meeting the [skull](#skull). Used on designs where they read as ornament or [magic](#magic) rather than as [bone](#bone).

entries.name: moose_antlers
entries.description: Wide flattened [antlers](#antlers) with finger-like points along the rim, the rack carried by a [bull](#bull) [moose](#moose). Meant for characters given them rather than for the [animal](#animal) itself.

entries.name: gazelle_horns
entries.description: Slender [horns](#horns) rising from the head with the ringed texture and gentle backward sweep of a gazelle's. Common on antelope-themed animal-eared characters and horned [fantasy](#fantasy) designs.

entries.name: ice_horns
entries.description: Horns made of clear or frosted [ice](#ice) instead of [bone](#bone), [catching](#catching) light the way [glass](#glass) does. They belong to [winter](#winter) and [frost](#frost) characters.

entries.name: feathers
entries.description: Bird plumage, whether on [wings](#wings), growing from a character, [drifting](#drifting) loose in the air or used to [dress](#dress) hair and [clothes](#clothes). Colour variants fold into this [tag](#tag); feathers drifting down take [falling_feathers](#falling_feathers).

entries.name: fins
entries.description: Thin blade-like appendages growing from a body, on the head, arms, [back](#back) or elsewhere. Fish and aquatic characters carry them most, but any [creature](#creature) with a fin qualifies.

entries.name: scales
entries.description: Scaly skin like that of a reptile, [fish](#fish) or [dragon](#dragon), on an [animal](#animal), a [monster](#monster) or a partly scaled humanoid. For the weighing [instrument](#instrument) use [weighing_scale](#weighing_scale) instead.

entries.name: animal_nose
entries.description: The moist pad at the tip of a [snout](#snout), drawn as a black dot or a small [triangle](#triangle). It marks a character given a beast's [nose](#nose) in place of a human one, common on kemonomimi and anthro designs.

entries.name: head_fins
entries.description: Fins growing from the head, usually at ear [height](#height) or where ears would be. Mermaids, [fish](#fish) girls and other [water](#water) creatures wear them; add [animal_ears](#animal_ears) when they work as ears.

entries.name: whiskers
entries.description: The fine sensory hairs on an animal's [snout](#snout), drawn on cats, mice, seals and other creatures, feral or anthro. Cheek lines [imitating](#imitating) them on a human face are [whisker_markings](#whisker_markings) instead.

entries.name: snout
entries.description: The projecting nose-and-jaw portion of an animal's face, boxy on bears and big cats, tapered on canines, and flattened on pigs. Anthro characters usually show it clearly when drawn in [profile](#profile).

entries.name: white_feathers
entries.description: Loose white [feathers](#feathers) [drifting](#drifting) through the air or [lying](#lying) in the scene, often around angels or doves. Feathers still attached to [wings](#wings) aren't tagged this way.

entries.name: beak
entries.description: A bird's beak on a character who is otherwise humanoid or anthro, such as a [bird](#bird) girl or an avian [furry](#furry), rather than on an ordinary bird. It marks the mouth of feathered characters the way a muzzle does for mammals.

entries.name: suction_cups
entries.description: The natural suckers along the arms of an [octopus](#octopus), [squid](#squid) or similar cephalopod. Man-made devices [working](#working) the same way get their own tags, such as [breast_pump](#breast_pump) or [nipple_clamps](#nipple_clamps).

entries.name: fluffy
entries.description: A soft, light, airy texture that invites touching, most often thick [animal](#animal) fur, a bushy [tail](#tail) or downy [feathers](#feathers). It describes how something is drawn rather than what it is.

entries.name: feather_hair
entries.description: Feathers grow from the head among or in place of the hair, typical of [bird](#bird) girls and harpies. They are part of the body; [feathers](#feathers) merely worn in the hair are [feather_hair_ornament](#feather_hair_ornament).

entries.name: black_feathers
entries.description: Loose or decorative [feathers](#feathers) that are black, on clothing, in the hair or scattered through the scene. Not for feathers forming a wing; add [falling_feathers](#falling_feathers) when they drift through the air.

entries.name: neck_fur
entries.description: A thick ruff of fur around the [neck](#neck), common on anthro animals and [monster](#monster) girls. On a fully furred body it has to differ in colour or length from the [coat](#coat) elsewhere.

entries.name: fur_collar_(body_fur)
entries.description: A thick ruff of the character's own fur around the [neck](#neck) and chest, growing from the body rather than worn. Wolf, [lion](#lion) and [dragon](#dragon) designs carry it as a matter of course.

entries.name: yellow_feathers
entries.description: Loose or body [feathers](#feathers) coloured yellow, on a [bird](#bird), a [harpy](#harpy) or as decoration. Not for feathers that form part of a pair of [wings](#wings); those take [yellow_wings](#yellow_wings).

entries.name: blue_feathers
entries.description: Loose or decorative [feathers](#feathers) in blue, worn in the hair, fixed to clothing or [drifting](#drifting) through the scene. Feathers forming a wing are not covered by it.

entries.name: spiked_shell
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) or creature's [shell](#shell) that carries [spikes](#spikes), such as a Koopa's [back](#back) or a spiky [turtle](#turtle) or [snail](#snail). Refers to the body feature, not to [armor](#armor).

entries.name: gills
entries.description: Breathing slits on the [neck](#neck) or [ribs](#ribs) that let a [creature](#creature) take oxygen from [water](#water). Seen on [fish](#fish), sharks, mermaids and other sea-dwelling characters.

entries.name: red_feathers
entries.description: Red [feathers](#feathers) on a [costume](#costume), in the hair, or [drifting](#drifting) loose, but not the plumage of a wing, which takes its own wing [tag](#tag). Combine with feathers.

entries.name: black_scales
entries.description: Scales in black covering a [dragon](#dragon), [lizard](#lizard), [snake](#snake) or scaled humanoid, over the whole body or in patches. Pair it with the creature's own [tag](#tag) and with [scales](#scales).

entries.name: dorsal_fin
entries.description: A fin [standing](#standing) up along the [back](#back), as on a [shark](#shark), [dolphin](#dolphin) or [fish](#fish). Drawn on the [animal](#animal) itself or on a character given aquatic traits.
