entries.name: green_feathers
entries.description: Green [feathers](#feathers) on a character or [lying](#lying) loose in the scene, such as plumage or a feathered [headdress](#headdress). Feathers forming a wing are excluded and take [green_wings](#green_wings) instead.

entries.name: white_scales
entries.description: Scaled skin coloured white, seen on dragons, lizardfolk, mermaids, and similar beings. It names the visible [scales](#scales) themselves, not white scale-patterned armour or [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: carapace
entries.description: A hard natural [shell](#shell) covering the body like plated armour, jointed where the body bends. It belongs to insects, monsters and aliens far more often than to [people](#people).

entries.name: spines
entries.description: Stiff, pointed growths on an [animal](#animal) or character, such as porcupine quills, the rays of a [fish](#fish) fin, or a ridge [running](#running) down a monster's [back](#back). Plant [thorns](#thorns) use the separate thorns [tag](#tag), and the human backbone is an unrelated word.

entries.name: flippers
entries.description: Broad paddle-like limbs made for [swimming](#swimming), as on seals and turtles, and equally the long rubber [fins](#fins) a diver straps on. Which sense applies is read from whether they are [anatomy](#anatomy) or gear.

entries.name: mane
entries.description: Long thick hair or fur [running](#running) along an animal's [neck](#neck), as on a [lion](#lion) or a [horse](#horse). Applies to feral animals and to anthro or beast-featured characters alike.

entries.name: red_scales
entries.description: A scaled character whose [scales](#scales) are red, typical of dragons, lizards and [fish](#fish). Refers to body scales, not scale-patterned armour or clothing.

entries.name: green_scales
entries.description: A character whose [scales](#scales) are green, as on a [lizard](#lizard), [dragon](#dragon) or [fish](#fish) body. Teal shades fall under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: chest_tuft
entries.description: A prominent [patch](#patch) of longer fur sticking out from the chest of a [furry](#furry) character, in any colour. Anthro and feral canines, felines and other thick-coated species carry it.

entries.name: blue_scales
entries.description: Blue [scales](#scales) covering a [dragon](#dragon), [lizard](#lizard), [fish](#fish) or scaled character, over the whole body or in patches. Name the [creature](#creature) alongside it.

entries.name: blowhole
entries.description: The [breathing](#breathing) [opening](#opening) on top of a whale's or dolphin's head. It shows up on cetacean animals and on anthro characters built from them, sometimes spouting.

entries.name: brown_feathers
entries.description: Brown [feathers](#feathers) growing on the body, [tail](#tail) or [crest](#crest). Feathers making up a pair of [wings](#wings) are handled by the wing tags instead.

entries.name: peacock_feathers
entries.description: The long [train](#train) [feathers](#feathers) of a [peacock](#peacock), each closing in an [iridescent](#iridescent) blue-and-gold eye. Shown fanned on the [bird](#bird) itself, worn as ornament, or bundled into a fan.

entries.name: shark_fin
entries.description: A triangular dorsal fin, either [cutting](#cutting) the surface above a [shark](#shark) nobody [can](#can) see yet, or growing from a character's own [back](#back) or head.

entries.name: very_hairy
entries.description: Body hair thick enough to read as fur, spread over four or more areas of the body such as the [back](#back), arms, [feet](#feet) and chest together. Where hair shows only sparsely on two or three areas, [hairy](#hairy) is enough.

entries.name: pink_feathers
entries.description: Feathers coloured pink, growing on a body or [drifting](#drifting) loose through the air. Not for the plumage of [wings](#wings), which the wing colour tags [cover](#cover).

entries.name: stinger
entries.description: A sharp [piercing](#piercing) organ at the tip of a [tail](#tail) or abdomen, usually fed by a venom gland. Belongs to bees, wasps, scorpions and stingrays, and to characters who borrow those parts.

entries.name: lion_mane
entries.description: The thick ruff of hair ringing a lion's head and [neck](#neck), on the [animal](#animal) itself or on a lion-based character.

entries.name: purple_feathers
entries.description: Purple plumage on a [bird](#bird) or bird-like character. Feathers attached to a wing are covered by the wing's own colour [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: fluff
entries.description: Soft downy tufts of hair or fur drawn light and puffed out. It collects around [animal](#animal) ears, at the [neck](#neck), at the base of a [tail](#tail) and across the chest.

entries.name: grey_feathers
entries.description: Grey [feathers](#feathers) on a character or [lying](#lying) loose, whether body plumage or an ornament. Feathers that make up a wing are excluded and take the wing colour tags instead.

entries.name: pig_nose
entries.description: A flat upturned [snout](#snout) with two round [nostrils](#nostrils), taken from a [pig](#pig) and given to a character. It may sit on a fully porcine face or be the one [animal](#animal) trait on an otherwise human one.

entries.name: orange_feathers
entries.description: Orange plumage on a [bird](#bird), an avian character or a feathered ornament. Feathers forming [wings](#wings) are covered by the wing colour tags instead.

entries.name: chest_fur
entries.description: A [patch](#patch) of thicker, often paler fur across a creature's chest, [standing](#standing) out from the [coat](#coat) around it. Beast and anthro characters wear it as a [fluffy](#fluffy) ruff.

entries.name: arm_fins
entries.description: Fins [running](#running) along the forearm or trailing [back](#back) from the elbow, webbed or membranous. They belong to aquatic characters and water-flavoured dragons.

entries.name: purple_scales
entries.description: Scaled skin in purple or lavender, on a [dragon](#dragon), [lizard](#lizard), [fish](#fish), or other scaled character. Combine with [scales](#scales).

entries.name: yellow_scales
entries.description: Yellow scaled skin on a reptile, [dragon](#dragon) or [fish](#fish) character. Add [scales](#scales) and the species alongside.

entries.name: grey_scales
entries.description: A character whose [scales](#scales) are grey or silver, as on a [dragon](#dragon), [lizard](#lizard) or [shark](#shark) body. Only the scale colour is recorded here.

entries.name: snake_hood
entries.description: The flaring cobra [hood](#hood), formed by [ribs](#ribs) [spreading](#spreading) the skin behind the head. It frames the face on serpent characters and usually signals a [threat](#threat) [display](#display).

entries.name: green_mane
entries.description: A green [mane](#mane), the long hair-like fur [running](#running) along the [neck](#neck) of a [horse](#horse), [lion](#lion) or comparable [creature](#creature). The rest of the body keeps its own colour tags.

entries.name: grey_mane
entries.description: A grey [mane](#mane) [running](#running) along the [neck](#neck) of a [horse](#horse), [lion](#lion) or comparable [creature](#creature). Body and [tail](#tail) colours are recorded separately.

entries.name: orange_mane
entries.description: An orange [mane](#mane) [running](#running) along the [neck](#neck) of a [horse](#horse), [lion](#lion) or comparable [creature](#creature), or on a character [carrying](#carrying) such a trait.

entries.name: piercing
entries.description: Jewelry set through an [opening](#opening) made in the face or body: [nose](#nose), lip, eyebrow, [tongue](#tongue), [navel](#navel), nipple or genitals, and ear piercings other than [plain](#plain) lobes. Ordinary earlobe [earrings](#earrings) are earrings instead. Add the location [tag](#tag) where one exists.

entries.name: ear_piercing
entries.description: A [piercing](#piercing) through some part of the ear other than the lobe, such as the helix or the tragus. Ordinary lobe [jewelry](#jewelry) is [earrings](#earrings) and not this.

entries.name: nipple_piercing
entries.description: A [piercing](#piercing) driven through the nipple, most often [carrying](#carrying) a [nipple_bar](#nipple_bar) or [nipple_rings](#nipple_rings). Add [nipples](#nipples) when they are bare; an ornament that grips without passing through the [flesh](#flesh) is [nipple_sleeves](#nipple_sleeves).

entries.name: navel_piercing
entries.description: A [piercing](#piercing) through the rim of the [belly](#belly) button, usually a [ring](#ring) or a [barbell](#barbell). It shows on a character baring the [midriff](#midriff).

entries.name: barbell_piercing
entries.description: Piercing [jewelry](#jewelry) built as a straight shaft with a bead screwed onto each end, worn through the [tongue](#tongue), eyebrow, nipple or [navel](#navel). Curved and circular versions of the same design count as [well](#well).

entries.name: animal_ear_piercing
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or stud set through a character's [animal](#animal) ears rather than through human ones. Combine it with [animal_ears](#animal_ears) and with the kind of [piercing](#piercing).

entries.name: nipple_rings
entries.description: Rigid closed rings worn through the [nipples](#nipples). A bar, or a loop completed by something [flexible](#flexible) such as [chain](#chain), is [nipple_bar](#nipple_bar) instead; rings often carry chains, [weights](#weights) or other hangings.

entries.name: tongue_piercing
entries.description: A stud or [barbell](#barbell) through the [tongue](#tongue), visible when the mouth is open or the tongue is out.

entries.name: nose_piercing
entries.description: Any [piercing](#piercing) of the [nose](#nose), through a nostril, the septum or the [bridge](#bridge). A [ring](#ring) worn in one is [nose_ring](#nose_ring) as [well](#well).

entries.name: nipple_bar
entries.description: A [barbell](#barbell) through the nipple, most often a straight shaft with a bead screwed on at either end. Jewellery or a [chain](#chain) is sometimes hung from it.

entries.name: pussy_piercing
entries.description: A [piercing](#piercing) placed through the female genitals, most often at the clitoral [hood](#hood) or through the labia. Combine with [pussy](#pussy) and piercing to mark both the [anatomy](#anatomy) and the [jewelry](#jewelry).

entries.name: lip_piercing
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or stud set through the upper or lower lip, common on [punk](#punk) and gothic designs.

entries.name: eyebrow_piercing
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or [barbell](#barbell) set through the eyebrow, worn at one end of the brow. A common [facial](#facial) [piercing](#piercing) on [punk](#punk), [delinquent](#delinquent) and street-fashion characters.

entries.name: clitoris_piercing
entries.description: A [piercing](#piercing) set through the [clitoris](#clitoris), most often [carrying](#carrying) a [ring](#ring) or a small [barbell](#barbell). One kind of genital piercing, and frequently drawn alongside others.

entries.name: multiple_piercings
entries.description: Several piercings worn at the same site, such as a row of rings up one ear or a cluster through a single eyebrow. Piercings spread over different parts of the body are a separate matter.

entries.name: industrial_piercing
entries.description: A single straight [barbell](#barbell) [running](#running) through two holes in the upper cartilage of one ear. It is a form of ear [piercing](#piercing) rather than a lobe stud.

entries.name: linked_piercing
entries.description: Two piercings joined to one another, usually by a [chain](#chain), for instance between the [nipples](#nipples) or from an ear down to a lip.

entries.name: tail_piercing
entries.description: A [piercing](#piercing) set into a [tail](#tail).

entries.name: nose_ring
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) worn through a [piercing](#piercing) in the [nose](#nose), either in a nostril or through the septum between them. Septum rings hang below the tip and are the more conspicuous of the two.

entries.name: labret_piercing
entries.description: A [piercing](#piercing) through the lower lip, worn as a stud [sitting](#sitting) below it or as a [barbell](#barbell) set upright or across. It counts among lip piercings.

entries.name: mouth_piercing
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or stud set through the lip or the skin around the mouth, such as a labret or a pair of snakebites. Add the general [piercing](#piercing) [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: spiked_ear_piercing
entries.description: Ear [jewelry](#jewelry) ending in cones or points, worn through the lobe or up the cartilage. Often several at once for a [punk](#punk) look.

entries.name: nipple_chain
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) strung across the chest linking one pierced nipple to the other. It usually accompanies rings or [bars](#bars) [sitting](#sitting) in the piercings themselves.

entries.name: chin_piercing
entries.description: Jewellery through the chin or the skin just under the lower lip, usually a stud or a small [ring](#ring). It sits apart from lip piercings, which pass through the lip itself.

entries.name: labia_piercing
entries.description: Rings or barbells set through the labia. They are usually drawn as a matched pair, or as a row of small rings [running](#running) down one side.

entries.name: captive_bead_ring
entries.description: Body jewellery shaped as a [ring](#ring) closed by a single bead that clips between its two ends, held by the metal's own spring. Worn through ears, [lips](#lips), navels and [nipples](#nipples), sometimes with a charm [hanging](#hanging) off the bead.

entries.name: clitoris_ring
entries.description: A metal [hoop](#hoop) set through a [piercing](#piercing) in the [clitoris](#clitoris). Rendered as visible genital jewellery, and a narrower case of [clitoris_piercing](#clitoris_piercing).

entries.name: penis_piercing
entries.description: Jewelry pierced through the [penis](#penis): a [ring](#ring) through the glans, a bar under the shaft, or one set crosswise through the head.

entries.name: wing_piercing
entries.description: Rings or [studs](#studs) set through a wing's membrane or along its edge. It applies equally to a pair of [back](#back) [wings](#wings) and to small wings growing from the head.

entries.name: plug_(piercing)
entries.description: A thick cylindrical [piercing](#piercing) far wider than an ordinary stud, [holding](#holding) the pierced [hole](#hole) stretched open around it. Usually worn in the earlobe; a hollow one reads as a [flesh](#flesh) [tunnel](#tunnel) instead.

entries.name: nipple_tag
entries.description: The name-and-class [label](#label) Japanese schoolchildren [pin](#pin) to the chest of a uniform, worn here hung from a nipple [piercing](#piercing). Any similar identifying [tag](#tag) carried that way counts.

entries.name: bridge_piercing
entries.description: A [barbell](#barbell) set horizontally through the skin over the [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose), between or just above the eyes. It lies flat with a bead showing at either end.

entries.name: corset_piercing
entries.description: Rows of paired piercings laced together with [ribbon](#ribbon) or [chain](#chain) so the skin is criss-crossed like a laced [bodice](#bodice). They last days rather than years, and are done for photographs or as [piercing](#piercing) play.

entries.name: piercing_through_clothes
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or bar passing through the [fabric](#fabric) and the [flesh](#flesh) beneath it in one go. Distinct from a [piercing](#piercing) that merely shows through thin [cloth](#cloth), which is a covered piercing.

entries.name: covered_piercing
entries.description: The [outline](#outline) of a [piercing](#piercing) shows through clothing, most often at the nipple. The jewellery itself never comes into view.

entries.name: cheek_piercing
entries.description: Jewellery pushed through the cheek, usually a stud [sitting](#sitting) where a dimple would fall. They generally come as a pair, one on each side of the face.

entries.name: spike_piercing
entries.description: Body [jewelry](#jewelry) whose visible end tapers to a cone or point instead of a [ball](#ball). Worn in ears, [lips](#lips), brows, and elsewhere, and a [staple](#staple) of [punk](#punk) styling.

entries.name: lip_ring
entries.description: A lip [piercing](#piercing) fitted with a [ring](#ring) rather than a stud.

entries.name: piercing_pull
entries.description: A worn [piercing](#piercing) being tugged, whether by a hand, by a [chain](#chain) or [weight](#weight) [hanging](#hanging) from it, or by gravity alone. When the pull visibly stretches the pierced part, add the matching nipple or [clitoris](#clitoris) [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: horn_piercing
entries.description: Jewellery passes through a bore drilled in the horn, in the manner of an ear or lip [piercing](#piercing). Rings and [studs](#studs) are the usual fittings.

entries.name: areola_piercing
entries.description: Jewellery set through the areola rather than the nipple, so a [ring](#ring) or [barbell](#barbell) sits further out on the breast. It may appear beside a nipple [piercing](#piercing) or on its own.

entries.name: anti-eyebrow_piercing
entries.description: A stud set into the skin just below the brow or high on the cheekbone. Different from a [piercing](#piercing) that passes through the eyebrow itself.

entries.name: collarbone_piercing
entries.description: Jewellery set through the skin above the clavicle, usually a surface bar with a bead at either end. It counts as a body modification rather than as worn jewellery.

entries.name: single_nipple_piercing
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or bar through one nipple with the other left unpierced. The asymmetry is the point of the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: frenulum_piercing
entries.description: Jewellery set through the strip of skin under the head of the [penis](#penis), also called a frenum [piercing](#piercing). It is a single [ring](#ring) or bar, unlike the stacked row of a frenum [ladder](#ladder).

entries.name: piercing_hole
entries.description: An empty [piercing](#piercing) [hole](#hole), usually in the earlobe, plainly visible with nothing worn in it. Once a [ring](#ring) or stud is actually in place the ordinary piercing tags apply.

entries.name: clitoris_chain
entries.description: A clitoral [piercing](#piercing) linked by a fine [chain](#chain) to other jewellery, sometimes [running](#running) up to the [nipples](#nipples) or to a [collar](#collar). The connecting chain is the point, not the piercing on its own.

entries.name: tattoo
entries.description: Permanent colour worked into the skin to form a picture, symbol or text. Combine with the motif or the placement, such as [arm_tattoo](#arm_tattoo) or [dragon_tattoo](#dragon_tattoo), to say what it shows and where.

entries.name: arm_tattoo
entries.description: Ink on the arm, anything from a small mark to a full sleeve. Shoulder and forearm designs both count.

entries.name: shoulder_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) placed on the shoulder. Implies tattoo.

entries.name: pubic_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) placed on or just above the [crotch](#crotch). The classic form is a heart-shaped design over a woman's lower [belly](#belly), often implied to raise lust or fertility, or to mark the wearer as someone's property.

entries.name: facial_tattoo
entries.description: An inked design on the face, elaborate enough to read as a [tattoo](#tattoo). A single stripe or small symbol is [facial_mark](#facial_mark) instead.

entries.name: body_writing
entries.description: Words, letters or numbers written straight onto skin, from a name on a palm to [notes](#notes) down an arm to degrading labels in explicit work. Painted designs [carrying](#carrying) [no](#no) text are [bodypaint](#bodypaint).

entries.name: chest_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) on the upper chest: above the [breasts](#breasts) on a woman, anywhere across the chest or upper abdomen on a man. Ink elsewhere takes its own placement [tag](#tag).

entries.name: leg_tattoo
entries.description: Ink on the thigh, calf or anywhere else down the leg, from a small motif to a design covering the whole limb.

entries.name: number_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) consisting of a number, such as a serial, a year or a lucky [figure](#figure), inked anywhere on the body. It often marks a character as one of a batch or a series.

entries.name: neck_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) on the [neck](#neck), at the side, the front or the [nape](#nape), often showing above a [collar](#collar). Add the design tags for what it actually depicts.

entries.name: stomach_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) on the [belly](#belly), above the pubic area; one just above the [crotch](#crotch) is a [pubic_tattoo](#pubic_tattoo) instead.

entries.name: bodypaint
entries.description: Marks, stripes or designs painted onto skin, from [tribal](#tribal) patterns to full-body work [standing](#standing) in for clothing. Accidental splashes are [paint_on_body](#paint_on_body), text is [body_writing](#body_writing), and [paint](#paint) [imitating](#imitating) a garment takes [painted_clothes](#painted_clothes) as [well](#well).

entries.name: heart_tattoo
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) tattooed somewhere on the body. When it sits on the face, [heart_facial_mark](#heart_facial_mark) may [suit](#suit) better.

entries.name: breast_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) [sitting](#sitting) on the breast, from a small mark beside the nipple to a design spread across the chest. Add tattoo; [ink](#ink) low on the [belly](#belly) is [pubic_tattoo](#pubic_tattoo) or womb_tattoo.

entries.name: back_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) placed anywhere on the [back](#back), from between the shoulder blades down to the waist. It is often a large design viewed from behind; name the motif with a further [tag](#tag) where one applies.

entries.name: red_tattoo
entries.description: Ink worked into the skin in red rather than black, whether a small motif or a design covering a limb. Common on [demon](#demon), [oni](#oni) and tribal-styled characters.

entries.name: barcode_tattoo
entries.description: A [barcode](#barcode) inked into the skin, commonly on the [neck](#neck), wrist or hip, implying that the character is property, a product or a [clone](#clone). Androids and [cyberpunk](#cyberpunk) designs carry it most often.

entries.name: hand_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) inked on the hand, whether across the [back](#back), into the palm or down the fingers. The design is permanent marking rather than [paint](#paint) or a glove pattern.

entries.name: flower_tattoo
entries.description: Ink in the shape of a blossom on the skin, anywhere on the body. Both botanically accurate designs and heavily stylised ones apply.

entries.name: backpiece
entries.description: One large [tattoo](#tattoo) covering most of the [back](#back) as a single continuous composition rather than a collection of separate designs. Traditional Japanese [irezumi](#irezumi) is the form most often drawn.

entries.name: star_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) in the shape of a star symbol, anywhere on the body.

entries.name: full-body_tattoo
entries.description: Tattooing covering roughly two thirds of the body or more. Add the [plain](#plain) [tattoo](#tattoo) [tag](#tag) and any placement tags alongside it.

entries.name: forehead_tattoo
entries.description: Ink worked into the skin of the [forehead](#forehead), from a small symbol to a design [spreading](#spreading) over the brow. It differs from [forehead_mark](#forehead_mark), which is natural or magical, and from a jewel set there.

entries.name: glowing_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) that emits light, drawn with a [halo](#halo) around its lines or casting light onto nearby surfaces. Frequent on magical, cursed and corrupted characters.

entries.name: teardrop_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) shaped like a [falling](#falling) tear, most often inked beneath the eye. Being a permanent mark sets it apart from a drawn [facial](#facial) mark or a real tear.

entries.name: ass_tattoo
entries.description: Ink worked directly onto a buttock. A design [sitting](#sitting) just above them on the lower [back](#back) is a tramp stamp instead.

entries.name: winged_heart_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) of a [heart](#heart) with [wings](#wings) inked onto a character's skin. Tag tattoo alongside it, and add a location [tag](#tag) if one covers where it sits.

entries.name: tribal_tattoo
entries.description: Ink drawn in a [tribal](#tribal) design idiom: bold black bands, hooks and interlocking curves with [no](#no) shading. Usually laid over an arm, shoulder or [back](#back) so the pattern follows the muscle.

entries.name: butterfly_tattoo
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) inked into the skin, most often across the lower [back](#back), hip or shoulder.

entries.name: painted_clothes
entries.description: Bodypaint applied to imitate a garment, so a [figure](#figure) that reads as dressed is in fact bare. An exhibitionist conceit; [paint](#paint) splashed onto real clothing is [paint_on_clothes](#paint_on_clothes).

entries.name: dragon_tattoo
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) inked on the skin, usually sprawling across a [back](#back), a shoulder or an arm. Both the eastern serpentine style and the western winged one appear.

entries.name: cloud_tattoo
entries.description: A [cloud](#cloud) inked onto the skin, often in the curling stylised form borrowed from Chinese and Japanese design. Placement runs from a single shoulder to a whole [back](#back) piece.

entries.name: tramp_stamp
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) placed across the small of the [back](#back), just above the buttocks. Low-rise trousers or a [cropped](#cropped) top are what usually bring it into view.

entries.name: snake_tattoo
entries.description: Ink of a [snake](#snake) on the skin, often winding along an arm, up a leg or across the [back](#back) so the body follows the coil.

entries.name: finger_tattoo
entries.description: Ink [sitting](#sitting) on the fingers, often small letters or symbols spread one to a digit. It shows when the hand is raised or the fingers spread.

entries.name: branded
entries.description: A mark has been burned into the skin with a [hot](#hot) iron, leaving a raised [scar](#scar) in a deliberate shape. It reads as a [sign](#sign) of ownership, of [punishment](#punishment), or of belonging to some group.

entries.name: hip_tattoo
entries.description: Ink on the side of the hip, around waist or [groin](#groin) [height](#height). Anything set lower down the limb is a leg [tattoo](#tattoo) instead.

entries.name: eye_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) of an eye inked into the skin, anywhere on the body. Painted [eyeliner](#eyeliner) and [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow) are a different matter.

entries.name: irezumi
entries.description: Dense traditional tattooing that covers a broad sweep of skin, most often the whole [back](#back) or chest, worked in dragons, [carp](#carp), [waves](#waves) and blossom. It carries [heavy](#heavy) criminal-underworld associations.

entries.name: cross_tattoo
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) inked into the skin anywhere on the body, from a small mark beside the eye or on a hand to a large [ornate](#ornate) piece across the [back](#back).

entries.name: cheek_tattoo
entries.description: Ink on the cheek, from a small symbol to a design [spreading](#spreading) across the side of the face. Tribal patterns and clan marks are the usual forms.

entries.name: pink_tattoo
entries.description: Ink worked into the skin in pink rather than black or mixed colour. What the [tattoo](#tattoo) shows and where it sits are left to other tags.

entries.name: hair_tattoo
entries.description: A pattern shaved or dyed into a closely [cropped](#cropped) section of hair, most often at the side or [back](#back) of the head. Reads as [ink](#ink) on the scalp although it is cut into the hair itself.

entries.name: spider_tattoo
entries.description: A [spider](#spider) inked onto the skin, placed anywhere from the shoulder to the face. Reads as tough or dangerous, and is a [signature](#signature) detail on a few well-known characters.

entries.name: bat_tattoo
entries.description: A bat inked into the skin with its [wings](#wings) spread. Back, shoulder and hip are the usual placements.

entries.name: tongue_tattoo
entries.description: Ink marked onto the surface of the [tongue](#tongue), visible only while it is [stuck](#stuck) out. Can be lettering, a symbol or a solid [field](#field) of colour.

entries.name: stenciled_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) built from flat wedge-shaped [petals](#petals) with [no](#no) outlines at all, as if cut through a stencil. Frequently [monochrome](#monochrome) and paired with [thorns](#thorns), [vines](#vines) or a [dark](#dark) mood, though that is not a rule. It shows an open [bloom](#bloom) with irregular, widely spaced pieces, unlike the tighter mackintosh_rose [bud](#bud).

entries.name: skull_tattoo
entries.description: Ink of a [skull](#skull) on the skin, on the arm, [back](#back), chest or elsewhere. Ranges from a small [outline](#outline) to a large detailed piece.

entries.name: fish_tattoo
entries.description: A [fish](#fish) inked on the skin, most often a [koi](#koi) curling over a [back](#back) or an arm. The design is the [animal](#animal) itself, not a wider [water](#water) scene.

entries.name: wrist_tattoo
entries.description: Ink on the wrist, often a band, a small symbol, or a short line of [script](#script). Its placement keeps it visible even under ordinary clothing.

entries.name: head_tattoo
entries.description: Inked designs on the scalp, [temple](#temple) or [forehead](#forehead), generally shown on a shaved or part-shaved head.

entries.name: spade_tattoo
entries.description: A spade [card](#card) [suit](#suit) inked onto the skin, often small and placed on a hip, shoulder, or cheek.

entries.name: slave_brand
entries.description: A mark burned or cut into a character's skin that identifies them as owned property. It is usually placed somewhere visible, such as the shoulder, thigh or chest, and reads as a permanent [sign](#sign) of servitude rather than decoration.

entries.name: anchor_tattoo
entries.description: An [anchor](#anchor) inked into the skin, traditionally a sailor's mark and usually placed on a forearm or shoulder. Pirates and [old](#old) seamen wear it most often.

entries.name: scorpion_tattoo
entries.description: A [scorpion](#scorpion) inked onto the skin, most often across the shoulder, the small of the [back](#back) or a hip. Reads as a mark of menace on tough or criminal characters.

entries.name: midriff_tattoo
entries.description: A [tattoo](#tattoo) inked along the flanks or the small of the [back](#back) at waist level. A design across the front of the [belly](#belly) instead takes [stomach_tattoo](#stomach_tattoo).

entries.name: wing_tattoo
entries.description: Wings inked onto the skin, most often spread across the [back](#back) where real [wings](#wings) would sit. Bird, bat, and insect designs all count; only add wings alongside it if the character actually has some.

entries.name: spider_web_tattoo
entries.description: A cobweb inked on the skin, usually [fanning](#fanning) out from an elbow, shoulder, or the [neck](#neck). The design carries biker and [prison](#prison) associations that artists sometimes lean into.

entries.name: american_flag_tattoo
entries.description: The stars and stripes inked into the skin, most often on an arm, shoulder or [back](#back). Read it as body art rather than as a printed garment.

entries.name: forehead_writing
entries.description: Words or characters written across somebody's [forehead](#forehead), classically inked on while they slept. It is usually an [insult](#insult) or a joke at the sleeper's expense.

entries.name: no_tattoo
entries.description: Tattoos belonging to a character's usual design are missing from the skin, whether by the artist's [choice](#choice) or because the scene predates them.

entries.name: square_tattoo
entries.description: A [square](#square) shape inked onto the skin, left [plain](#plain) or filled with a design. Usually small and geometric.

entries.name: joints
entries.description: Articulated joints showing on a body: a doll's [ball](#ball) sockets, the segmented limbs of a [robot](#robot) or a [puppet](#puppet). It marks limbs that read as built rather than grown.

entries.name: mechanical_arms
entries.description: Machine-built arms, whether a character's cybernetic or prosthetic limbs or the arms of a [robot](#robot) or remote-operated [device](#device). Applies whether one arm or both are affected.

entries.name: doll_joints
entries.description: A living character whose limbs show visible [ball](#ball) [joints](#joints) where a doll's would be. Common on porcelain-doll designs, androids and some cyborgs.

entries.name: robot_joints
entries.description: Visibly mechanical [joints](#joints) at the elbows, [knees](#knees) or other limbs of a character, metallic in look. Doll_joints differ by showing gaps or [seams](#seams) like a ball-jointed [doll](#doll).

entries.name: prosthesis
entries.description: An artificial body part [standing](#standing) in for a missing limb, from a simple peg leg to a fully mechanical arm. Add [prosthetic_arm](#prosthetic_arm) or [prosthetic_leg](#prosthetic_leg) for which limb; a [robot](#robot) or full [cyborg](#cyborg) takes its own tags instead.

entries.name: single_mechanical_arm
entries.description: One arm is a mechanical [prosthesis](#prosthesis) or robotic limb while the other stays [flesh](#flesh). Tagged alongside [mechanical_arms](#mechanical_arms), which covers one arm or both.

entries.name: prosthetic_arm
entries.description: An artificial arm worn in place of a lost one, whether a [plain](#plain) [hook](#hook), a lifelike replacement, or an elaborate mechanical limb. For [machinery](#machinery) grafted onto an otherwise organic arm, mechanical_arm may also fit.

entries.name: mechanical_legs
entries.description: Machine-built [legs](#legs) on a character, ranging from a single prosthetic replacement to an entirely robotic lower body.

entries.name: mechabare
entries.description: A [robot](#robot), [android](#android) or [cyborg](#cyborg) with its mechanical insides on [display](#display): exposed circuitry, missing or [damaged](#damaged) limbs, or a cutaway view of otherwise inhuman parts. Not used for full-sized [mecha](#mecha), [plain](#plain) [doll](#doll) [joints](#joints) or ordinary machines.

entries.name: mechanical_hands
entries.description: Hands built from visible [machine](#machine) parts, whether a [prosthesis](#prosthesis) on an otherwise organic character or the hands of an [android](#android). Joints, plating and servos are usually on show.

entries.name: prosthetic_leg
entries.description: An artificial leg replacing a missing one, ranging from a simple peg or blade to a fully articulated mechanical limb. Often paired with [amputee](#amputee) where the loss itself is visible.

entries.name: mechanical_eyes
entries.description: Both eyes replaced by [machinery](#machinery), shown as lenses, apertures or [glowing](#glowing) sensors with visible [seams](#seams) around the sockets. Marks a character as an [android](#android) or someone cybernetically altered.

entries.name: artificial_eye
entries.description: A visibly man-made eye, from a [glass](#glass) prosthetic to a mechanical one with a lens and shutter. Only for eyes that look artificial, not for characters whose eyes merely happen to be so in their story.

entries.name: artificial_mechanical_eyes
entries.description: Eyes replaced by [machinery](#machinery): lenses, apertures and [glowing](#glowing) optics seated in metal housings. Standard on androids, cyborgs and rebuilt soldiers.

entries.name: mechanical_eye
entries.description: A single artificial eye of mechanical or cybernetic design, often [glowing](#glowing), lensed or visibly wired into the socket.

entries.name: single_mechanical_eye
entries.description: One eye is replaced by a [machine](#machine) part, [glowing](#glowing) lens or [camera](#camera) unit while the other stays organic. Marks a partial [cyborg](#cyborg) rather than a fully built [android](#android).

entries.name: single_mechanical_hand
entries.description: One hand is artificial, built from metal or plastic, while the other is [flesh](#flesh). Use the plural [mechanical_hands](#mechanical_hands) when either one or both hands may be [machine](#machine).

entries.name: hook_hand
entries.description: A metal [hook](#hook) takes the place of a missing hand, strapped on as a [prosthesis](#prosthesis) or worn as a [costume](#costume) piece. Pirates made the look famous.

entries.name: screw_in_head
entries.description: A bolt or [screw](#screw) driven through a character's head, usually protruding at both temples. The [signature](#signature) detail of a Frankenstein's-monster design.

entries.name: single_mechanical_leg
entries.description: A character with one artificial leg and one organic one. The plural [mechanical_legs](#mechanical_legs) is the broader [tag](#tag) covering either count.

entries.name: prosthetic_hand
entries.description: An artificial hand [standing](#standing) in for a lost one, used when only the hand is artificial or clothing hides everything above the wrist. A visibly artificial arm takes [prosthetic_arm](#prosthetic_arm) instead, and this is distinct from a mechanical_hand worn over a real one.

entries.name: mechanical_spine
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) backbone [running](#running) visibly down a character's [back](#back), whether exposed bare mechanism or an implant showing through parted skin.

entries.name: mechanical_hair
entries.description: Hair rendered as rigid metal or another clearly non-organic material, keeping the [outline](#outline) of an ordinary hairstyle while obviously not being real hair. Typically seen on robots and androids.

entries.name: key_in_head
entries.description: A [key](#key) stands out of someone's head, most often a wind-up key set into the [back](#back) or the side of the [skull](#skull). It marks the [figure](#figure) as [clockwork](#clockwork) or doll-like.

entries.name: exposed_internal_machinery
entries.description: Gears, pistons, cables and boards inside a [machine](#machine) or an [android](#android) lie open, through a [hatch](#hatch) or a smashed panel. Common for [damaged](#damaged) robots and for [maintenance](#maintenance) scenes.

entries.name: peg_leg
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) wooden or metal post [standing](#standing) in for a missing lower leg, strapped on below the knee. The old-fashioned [prosthesis](#prosthesis), firmly tied to pirates.

entries.name: subdermal_port
entries.description: A socket implanted flush with the skin, built to receive a plug or [cable](#cable). A science-fiction fixture on androids and cyborgs, loosely styled after real medical ports.

entries.name: false_arm
entries.description: An arm that is not [flesh](#flesh) yet still works as one, attached or held together by [magic](#magic), [machinery](#machinery) or some other material. The arm-specific case of [false_limb](#false_limb).

entries.name: false_limb
entries.description: A [working](#working) limb made of something other than the body's own [tissue](#tissue), kept in place by [magic](#magic), technology or sheer will. Unlike a lifeless prosthetic it moves as the character's own.

entries.name: prosthetic_weapon
entries.description: A missing limb replaced by a [weapon](#weapon) rather than an ordinary artificial one. The stump may end in a [gun](#gun) [barrel](#barrel), a blade, or a built-in claw.

entries.name: mechanical_foot
entries.description: A single foot made of mechanical parts, whether a [prosthesis](#prosthesis) fitted to a living leg or part of an entirely robotic body, with plating and [joints](#joints) on [display](#display).

entries.name: running_blades
entries.description: Curved carbon prosthetic [legs](#legs) that flex and spring [back](#back) like a blade, letting the wearer run and jump. They are the sprinting variety of artificial limb rather than an everyday [walking](#walking) [prosthesis](#prosthesis).

entries.name: drill_hand
entries.description: A [drill](#drill) in place of somebody's hand, either grown from the body or strapped on so it swallows the whole fist. Not hand_drill, which is an ordinary tool being held.

entries.name: third_eye
entries.description: An extra eye beyond the usual pair, not necessarily placed on the head. Add [extra_eyes](#extra_eyes) when there are more than three in total.

entries.name: disembodied_linked_eye
entries.description: A free-floating eye that still belongs to somebody, the tie drawn as a line, a cord or a trailing wisp. It roams on its own while remaining part of the character.

entries.name: disembodied_hand
entries.description: Hands [floating](#floating) in the frame with [no](#no) body joined to them, generally so that no [figure](#figure) blocks the view of the subject. A body merely [cropped](#cropped) away, or unseen behind a first-person [camera](#camera), does not count.

entries.name: stitches
entries.description: Visible [thread](#thread) sutures on skin or [fabric](#fabric), drawn as a train-track line or a row of X's, common on zombies, plush toys and mended wounds. Not [stitched](#stitched), the image-joining [tag](#tag).

entries.name: one-eyed
entries.description: The character has a single eye, whether born that way like a [cyclops](#cyclops) or having lost the other. An eye merely hidden behind hair or a [patch](#patch) is [one_eye_covered](#one_eye_covered).

entries.name: extra_arms
entries.description: More than two arms: a third growing out of a human body, a bolted-on mechanical one, or a [monster](#monster) with several pairs. Tentacles do not count.

entries.name: extra_eyes
entries.description: More than two eyes set into the body: a third on the [forehead](#forehead), a row down an arm, a spider's cluster. Loose eyeballs [floating](#floating) apart from the body do not qualify.

entries.name: amputee
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) missing all or part of one or more limbs. Where a replacement limb is worn, add [prosthesis](#prosthesis).

entries.name: missing_limb
entries.description: A character lacking at least one limb, though not every limb - [amputee](#amputee) is a natural companion [tag](#tag). Use [severed_limb](#severed_limb) when the detached limb itself is shown, and [cropped_arms](#cropped_arms) or [cropped_legs](#cropped_legs) when a limb is simply outside the frame.

entries.name: stitched_face
entries.description: Stitches [running](#running) across a large part of the face, on zombies, dolls and Frankenstein-style characters.

entries.name: disembodied_head
entries.description: A living character's head parted from the [neck](#neck) while their body stands in the same picture. A killing blow that takes the head off is [decapitation](#decapitation).

entries.name: mono-eye
entries.description: A single large eye where a pair would normally sit. Most [familiar](#familiar) on [mecha](#mecha) heads, where the lens slides along a horizontal slot as it tracks a [target](#target).

entries.name: arthropod_limbs
entries.description: A human character [carrying](#carrying) the [legs](#legs) or arms of an insect, [spider](#spider) or [crustacean](#crustacean), often sprouting from the [back](#back) or the sides. A body that is wholly spider below the waist is [arachne](#arachne) instead.

entries.name: extra_mouth
entries.description: A mouth where there should not be one — on a palm, a [stomach](#stomach), a [forehead](#forehead) — on top of the usual one on the face. A [monster](#monster) and body-horror trait.

entries.name: multiple_heads
entries.description: A being with more than one head and [neck](#neck), the shape of hydras, three-headed hounds and similar monsters. Several faces [sharing](#sharing) a single head is [extra_faces](#extra_faces) instead.

entries.name: stitched_mouth
entries.description: A mouth sewn shut or crossed with stitch marks, usually drawn as a simple row of X [shapes](#shapes). A common horror or ragdoll detail signalling the character cannot speak.

entries.name: headless
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) or object shown with [no](#no) head at all, as with a [dullahan](#dullahan) or a [broken](#broken) [statue](#statue). A head merely cut off by the frame is [head_out_of_frame](#head_out_of_frame).

entries.name: quadruple_amputee
entries.description: A character has lost both arms and both [legs](#legs), in whole or in part, leaving them unable to move without assistance. Japanese work often nicknames the [figure](#figure) daruma after the limbless [doll](#doll), and the depiction is frequently fetishistic.

entries.name: rayman_limbs
entries.description: Hands or [feet](#feet) float beside the body with [no](#no) arms or [legs](#legs) visibly connecting them, a cartoon body plan named for the character who popularized it and shared by several other franchises' mascots. Limbs with no body at all instead are [disembodied_hand](#disembodied_hand).

entries.name: stitched_arm
entries.description: An arm joined to the body with visible [stitches](#stitches) or heavily [stitched](#stitched) along its length, a [zombie](#zombie) or patchwork-doll look.

entries.name: multiple_legs
entries.description: A [creature](#creature), [monster](#monster) girl or [mecha](#mecha) whose natural build carries more than two [legs](#legs), a [spider](#spider) girl's eight being the usual case. Limbs abnormal for the character, such as a third leg on a human, are [extra_legs](#extra_legs).

entries.name: hole_on_body
entries.description: A clearly shaped void somewhere in the body, open on both sides so the view passes straight through. Whatever [organs](#organs) belong there are simply absent; the Arrancar of Bleach are the best-known example.

entries.name: extra_faces
entries.description: More than one face on a single character, the additional ones on the side of the head, the chest, the [stomach](#stomach) or elsewhere. No extra head is needed, which is what separates it from [multiple_heads](#multiple_heads).

entries.name: disembodied_eye
entries.description: One or more eyes [hanging](#hanging) in the air with [no](#no) body attached to them. They may [watch](#watch) from the background or hover close beside a character.

entries.name: double_amputee
entries.description: Two of the character's limbs are gone: both arms, both [legs](#legs), or one of each. The stumps may be left bare or fitted with prosthetics.

entries.name: hole_in_chest
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) runs clean through the character's chest, often with the background showing on the far side. It frequently turns up in scenes where the [heart](#heart) has been taken out of the body.

entries.name: stitched_torso
entries.description: Long [seams](#seams) of [thread](#thread) across the chest, [belly](#belly) or [back](#back), as though the body had been sewn together from pieces. Frequently paired with [zombie](#zombie) and patchwork character designs.

entries.name: stitched_neck
entries.description: A line of [thread](#thread) [stitches](#stitches) across the throat, usually where a head has been reattached. Standard shorthand for a reanimated [corpse](#corpse).

entries.name: stitched_leg
entries.description: A leg either attached to the body by [thread](#thread) or [carrying](#carrying) a long run of stitch marks along it. Common on zombies, sewn-together monsters and living dolls.

entries.name: skeletal_arm
entries.description: An arm made of bare [bone](#bone) attached to a body that is otherwise [flesh](#flesh) or [machine](#machine). Marks an [undead](#undead), cursed or partly rotted character rather than a full [skeleton](#skeleton).

entries.name: extra_breasts
entries.description: More than the usual pair of [breasts](#breasts), generally arranged in rows down the [torso](#torso). Common on [monster](#monster) girls and on multi-breasted [animal](#animal) characters.

entries.name: multiple_hands
entries.description: Either a character given more than the usual pair of hands, or a mass of disembodied hands [reaching](#reaching) in from nowhere. The second case is a [staple](#staple) of dream, horror and restraint scenes.

entries.name: extra_legs
entries.description: More [legs](#legs) than the character's own body plan calls for, such as a third leg on a human. A [spider](#spider) girl's full eight are normal for her and belong with [multiple_legs](#multiple_legs).

entries.name: conjoined
entries.description: Two or more bodies fused into one, [sharing](#sharing) a [torso](#torso) or limbs between them. Drawn either straight as a physical condition or as a [transformation](#transformation) [gag](#gag).

entries.name: tendril
entries.description: A thin, writhing growth extending from a body or a mass, heavier than a vine but slimmer than a full tentacle. It usually marks a corrupted or biologically transformed character.

entries.name: third_eye_on_chest
entries.description: An extra eye set into the chest or sternum, open alongside the ordinary pair on the face. Generally marks a demonic, divine or otherwise inhuman character.

entries.name: armless_amputee
entries.description: A character missing both arms, the stumps ending at the shoulder or partway down. Replacement limbs worn in their place take [prosthesis](#prosthesis) tags of their own.

entries.name: detached_arm
entries.description: An arm drawn with a gap where it should join the shoulder, hovering beside the body or [resting](#resting) apart from it. A design quirk or a magical effect rather than a severed limb.

entries.name: mutation
entries.description: Anatomy gone conspicuously wrong — spare limbs, misplaced features, warped proportions. The deformity is deliberate and meant to be noticed rather than a slip of the [pen](#pen).

entries.name: extra_hands
entries.description: More than two hands on one character. Sometimes an error, sometimes design: extra arms [carrying](#carrying) hands, or hands sprouting where none belong.

entries.name: too_many_eyes
entries.description: Eyes multiplied across a body, a face or a background in unsettling numbers, [well](#well) past a single extra pair. Usually drawn for horror.

entries.name: mechanical_tentacles
entries.description: Jointed robotic limbs or cables that move and grip like [tentacles](#tentacles), usually mounted on a back-worn [harness](#harness) rather than growing from the body naturally.

entries.name: triple_amputee
entries.description: A character missing three of their four limbs, whether entirely or from partway down. The stumps may be left bare, bandaged, or fitted with prosthetics.

entries.name: disembodied_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) [drifting](#drifting) free of any mouth and moving under its own power. Nearly always a magical or monstrous conceit.

entries.name: hollow_body
entries.description: The body or limbs are empty inside, [opening](#opening) onto [darkness](#darkness) or nothing at all. Hollow eyes or a hollow mouth alone do not qualify, though one character may show all three.

entries.name: detached_legs
entries.description: Legs drawn with a visible gap where they ought to meet the body, either built to come apart or [split](#split) for stylistic effect. When the separation is an [injury](#injury), [severed_limb](#severed_limb) applies instead.

entries.name: stitched_eye
entries.description: An eye sewn shut, with [thread](#thread) crossing the closed [lid](#lid), or more rarely [stitched](#stitched) straight into the face. A [staple](#staple) of horror and ragdoll designs.

entries.name: hole_in_head
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) pierces the head, either a neat gap belonging to the character's design or a wound left by something that passed through. It implies nothing about whether they are alive.

entries.name: hand_mouth
entries.description: A mouth [opening](#opening) in the middle of a palm, usually with [teeth](#teeth) or a [tongue](#tongue) inside. It belongs to body horror and to youkai designs rather than to ordinary [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: legless_amputee
entries.description: Both [legs](#legs) are gone, the stumps left bare or fitted with prosthetics. A [wheelchair](#wheelchair) or crutches often stand nearby.

entries.name: stitched_hand
entries.description: A hand joined on or mended with visible [thread](#thread), [seams](#seams) crossing the wrist or [running](#running) between the fingers. Part of the same patchwork look as other [stitched](#stitched) limbs.

entries.name: chest_mouth
entries.description: A [working](#working) mouth set into a character's chest, with [lips](#lips) and [teeth](#teeth) of its own. Monsters, eldritch designs and body horror use the feature.

entries.name: mixed_limbs
entries.description: One character whose arms or [legs](#legs) plainly belong to different species - a [griffin](#griffin) with a paw on one side and a talon on the other, say. Fits [monster](#monster) girls or boys given mismatched [animal](#animal) hands or [feet](#feet).

entries.name: hole_in_face
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) stands where the face ought to be. The far side need not be visible for it to apply, and horror pieces reach for it constantly.

entries.name: disembodied_torso
entries.description: A trunk shown with [no](#no) head or limbs joined to it, [standing](#standing) or [floating](#floating) by itself. A design conceit rather than the result of a wound.

entries.name: extra_tongue
entries.description: More than one [tongue](#tongue), either a second one outright or a tongue [split](#split) into separate [organs](#organs). It belongs to [monster](#monster) and [demon](#demon) designs.

entries.name: four_eyes
entries.description: A character [carrying](#carrying) two extra eyes beyond the usual pair, set on the face or the head. Monsters, aliens and spider-derived designs use it.

entries.name: blood
entries.description: Blood outside the body, from a [nosebleed](#nosebleed) or a grazed knee to spray across a wall or a [weapon](#weapon). Add the placement tags such as [blood_on_face](#blood_on_face) or [blood_on_weapon](#blood_on_weapon); a red [liquid](#liquid) nobody [can](#can) identify is [ambiguous_red_liquid](#ambiguous_red_liquid).

entries.name: scar
entries.description: A healed mark on the skin left by a cut, burn or other [old](#old) wound. Placement tags such as [scar_on_face](#scar_on_face), [scar_across_eye](#scar_across_eye) or [scar_on_chest](#scar_on_chest) say where it sits.

entries.name: scar_on_face
entries.description: Any [scar](#scar) somewhere on the face. Narrower placements like [scar_on_cheek](#scar_on_cheek), [scar_on_nose](#scar_on_nose), [scar_on_forehead](#scar_on_forehead) and [scar_on_mouth](#scar_on_mouth) imply it; it implies scar.

entries.name: blood_on_face
entries.description: Blood on the face, splashed there from somebody else or flowing from the character's own wound. Add [blood_from_mouth](#blood_from_mouth) or [nosebleed](#nosebleed) where the source is shown.

entries.name: injury
entries.description: A character has been physically hurt: [cuts](#cuts), bruises, [bleeding](#bleeding), [broken](#broken) bones, whether from a fight, an [accident](#accident) or [violence](#violence). Add the specific tags such as [blood](#blood), [scar](#scar), [bruise](#bruise) or [bandages](#bandages).

entries.name: scar_across_eye
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) [running](#running) vertically over one eye, a common mark for veteran fighters. Add [eyebrow_cut](#eyebrow_cut) when the scar visibly splits the eyebrow. Implies scar.

entries.name: blood_on_clothes
entries.description: Clothing stained or spattered with [blood](#blood), wherever the blood came from. Battle scenes often pair it with [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes).

entries.name: scar_on_cheek
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) [sitting](#sitting) on the cheek. Implies [scar_on_face](#scar_on_face); use [scar_across_eye](#scar_across_eye) instead when it runs through the eye.

entries.name: blood_on_hands
entries.description: Blood on the hands or fingers, from an [injury](#injury), from pressing a wound shut or from something the character has done.

entries.name: bruise
entries.description: A discoloured blotch under the skin — purple, blue or [fading](#fading) yellow — where a blunt blow has [broken](#broken) the capillaries beneath. Add the placement where one applies, such as [bruise_on_face](#bruise_on_face).

entries.name: scar_on_arm
entries.description: A healed [scar](#scar) somewhere on the character's arm, usually visible with short sleeves or bare arms. Implies scar; other placements have their own tags.

entries.name: blood_splatter
entries.description: Blood scattered messily across a surface, a wall, a [floor](#floor) or a person. It is usually what a spray leaves behind once it lands.

entries.name: scar_on_chest
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) visible on the chest, often exposed by open or absent clothing. For a scar on the [breasts](#breasts) specifically, [scar_on_breasts](#scar_on_breasts) exists.

entries.name: scar_between_breasts
entries.description: A healed wound down the sternum in the [valley](#valley) between the [breasts](#breasts), most often drawn as one long vertical line.

entries.name: sternum_scar
entries.description: A long vertical [scar](#scar) down the centre of the chest, the mark left by open-heart or chest [surgery](#surgery). Signals a history of [serious](#serious) [injury](#injury) or reconstruction.

entries.name: blood_from_mouth
entries.description: Blood trickling from the mouth, generally the [sign](#sign) of a [grave](#grave) internal [injury](#injury) or approaching [death](#death). A [split](#split) lip or a bitten [tongue](#tongue) [can](#can) produce it just as [well](#well).

entries.name: blood_on_weapon
entries.description: Any [weapon](#weapon) [carrying](#carrying) [blood](#blood), a [sword](#sword), [axe](#axe) or [spear](#spear) after it has struck. A [knife](#knife) [can](#can) take [blood_on_knife](#blood_on_knife) in addition.

entries.name: bite_mark
entries.description: The imprint [teeth](#teeth) leave behind after [biting](#biting), usually a [ring](#ring) of dents or reddened skin, though [food](#food) and objects [can](#can) carry one too. Use biting for the act while it is happening.

entries.name: slap_mark_on_ass
entries.description: A reddened [handprint](#handprint) left on the buttocks after a strike. The shape of the hand stays visible against the surrounding skin.

entries.name: scar_on_nose
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) across the [bridge](#bridge) or tip of the [nose](#nose), a frequent mark on rough or brawling characters. Implies [scar_on_face](#scar_on_face).

entries.name: bleeding
entries.description: Blood actively [running](#running) out of a wound or a cut, rather than dried or already splashed elsewhere. Bleeding from the monthly cycle takes [menstruation](#menstruation).

entries.name: cuts
entries.description: Slices or gashes opened in the skin by something sharp, from a shallow nick to a [sword](#sword) stroke. A form of [injury](#injury), usually drawn with [blood](#blood) at the edges.

entries.name: cross_scar
entries.description: A healed cross- or X-shaped [scar](#scar), often across a cheek, a [forehead](#forehead) or a chest as a character's identifying mark. The wound is long closed, not fresh.

entries.name: burn_scar
entries.description: The healed mark left by a [serious](#serious) burn: wide, uneven and rough-textured across the skin. It looks nothing like the thin clean line a cut leaves.

entries.name: scar_on_forehead
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) placed on the [forehead](#forehead), often shown under swept or short bangs. Implies [scar_on_face](#scar_on_face).

entries.name: scratches
entries.description: Shallow [cuts](#cuts) or [scrape](#scrape) marks on skin, [armor](#armor), weapons or another surface, left by [accident](#accident), combat or ordinary wear. Minor wounds qualify too; a deeper cut is an [injury](#injury) instead.

entries.name: slap_mark
entries.description: Red skin, often a hand print, left where someone was slapped, most commonly a cheek or the buttocks. In BDSM contexts it follows [spanking](#spanking).

entries.name: multiple_scars
entries.description: A character [carrying](#carrying) more than one [scar](#scar), often spread across different parts of the body. The count is what separates it from scar alone.

entries.name: hickey
entries.description: A reddish [bruise](#bruise) on the [neck](#neck) or arm left by hard kissing or sucking, where small vessels have [broken](#broken) under the skin. It is a mark in the skin rather than a print of [lips](#lips), which is [lipstick_mark](#lipstick_mark).

entries.name: scar_on_neck
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) on the [neck](#neck), such as a line across the throat. Implies scar.

entries.name: blood_from_eyes
entries.description: Blood [running](#running) out of the eyes, whether wept as bloody [tears](#tears) or [leaking](#leaking) from an [injury](#injury). Do not add tears unless ordinary tears are visible as [well](#well).

entries.name: blood_stain
entries.description: The mark left where [blood](#blood) soaked into [fabric](#fabric) or dried onto a surface. It reads darker and set rather than fresh and [running](#running).

entries.name: scar_on_stomach
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) on the [belly](#belly) or abdomen, usually visible with a bare [midriff](#midriff) or open clothing. Implies scar.

entries.name: pink_blood
entries.description: Blood drawn distinctly pink instead of red, a stylistic [choice](#choice) that softens [violence](#violence) or marks a non-human character. The wound itself is tagged as usual.

entries.name: scar_on_leg
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) on a leg, usually visible with [shorts](#shorts), a [skirt](#skirt) or bare [legs](#legs). Implies scar.

entries.name: blood_in_hair
entries.description: Blood matted into or streaked through the hair, from a head wound or from spray that landed there.

entries.name: bruise_on_face
entries.description: Bruising on the face: a swollen cheek, a marked [jaw](#jaw) or a darkened eye socket. Tag [bruise](#bruise) alongside it, and [injury](#injury) where the wider [tag](#tag) is wanted.

entries.name: head_bump
entries.description: A [comic](#comic) swelling raised on the head by a knock or a telling-off, drawn far larger than any real lump and often paired with crossed bandaids. It never stands for a [serious](#serious) [injury](#injury). Two heads [knocking](#knocking) together is [headbutt](#headbutt).

entries.name: object_through_head
entries.description: An object runs into a head or straight out the far side, whether an arrow, a blade or a [pencil](#pencil). It covers cartoon gags as readily as real impalement, so add wound or gore tags when the picture calls for them.

entries.name: blood_on_knife
entries.description: A [knife](#knife) with [blood](#blood) along its blade, just used or held out as a [threat](#threat). Larger weapons take [blood_on_weapon](#blood_on_weapon).

entries.name: blood_on_arm
entries.description: Blood visible on an arm, whether it came from the character's own wound or from somebody else. It sits on the skin, so a bloodied sleeve takes [blood_on_clothes](#blood_on_clothes).

entries.name: scar_on_mouth
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) crossing the [lips](#lips) or the [corner](#corner) of the mouth. Implies [scar_on_face](#scar_on_face).

entries.name: whip_marks
entries.description: Lash welts striping the skin, most often across the [back](#back), buttocks or [thighs](#thighs). Evidence that a [whipping](#whipping) happened rather than a depiction of the act itself.

entries.name: blood_on_ground
entries.description: Blood on the ground or [floor](#floor) as drops, smears or a [spreading](#spreading) [pool](#pool). A large [puddle](#puddle) [can](#can) take [pool_of_blood](#pool_of_blood) as [well](#well).

entries.name: self-harm
entries.description: A character deliberately injuring themselves, or fresh evidence of it, typically tied to depression or a suicidal state, though a [blood](#blood) offering counts as [well](#well). Indirect ways of harming oneself do not.

entries.name: scar_on_hand
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) somewhere on a hand, including the [back](#back) of the hand and the fingers. Implies scar.

entries.name: pool_of_blood
entries.description: A large [spill](#spill) of [blood](#blood) spread across the [floor](#floor) or ground, from a body or an unseen cause. It implies [serious](#serious) [violence](#violence) or [death](#death); [tag](#tag) blood with it.

entries.name: blood_drip
entries.description: Blood [running](#running) downward in visible drops or trails, off a wound, a blade or the lip of a surface. Add the source as [well](#well), such as [bleeding](#bleeding) or [blood_on_weapon](#blood_on_weapon).

entries.name: scar_on_shoulder
entries.description: A healed wound on the shoulder or the top of the upper arm, often visible because the garment leaves it bare.

entries.name: blood_on_leg
entries.description: Blood visible on a leg, from a wound there or carried over from somewhere else. Thigh, knee and shin all count, and the foot has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: blood_on_bandages
entries.description: Bandages soaked or spotted where [blood](#blood) has seeped through from the wound underneath. The [dressing](#dressing) is still in place, which is what separates it from an open [injury](#injury).

entries.name: self-harm_scar
entries.description: Healed marks left by earlier [cutting](#cutting), drawn as a row of short lines [running](#running) across a wrist, forearm, or thigh. Only [old](#old) scarring qualifies; fresh [bleeding](#bleeding) [cuts](#cuts) do not.

entries.name: scar_on_back
entries.description: Healed marks across the [back](#back), from a single clean line to a criss-cross of [old](#old) lash or blade wounds.

entries.name: bite_mark_on_neck
entries.description: Tooth impressions on the side or [back](#back) of the [neck](#neck). Common on [vampire](#vampire) victims and as a possessive mark left by a partner.

entries.name: scars_all_over
entries.description: Old wounds spread across most of the body rather than gathered in one place, with face, [torso](#torso), arms and [legs](#legs) all marked. Not for a single [scar](#scar) on a small [patch](#patch) of exposed skin.

entries.name: beaten
entries.description: Somebody shown after being physically worked over: swollen face, bruises, [torn](#torn) [clothes](#clothes), slumped or [collapsed](#collapsed). The picture holds the aftermath rather than the fight, and pairs naturally with [bruise](#bruise), [injury](#injury) or [blood](#blood).

entries.name: blood_on_chest
entries.description: Blood across the upper [torso](#torso), from a wound there or splashed in from elsewhere. It sits on the skin rather than on clothing.

entries.name: bite_mark_on_breast
entries.description: Tooth impressions on a breast, from a faint red [ring](#ring) to a bruised, [broken](#broken) mark. What is recorded is the mark left behind rather than the act itself.

entries.name: blood_on_neck
entries.description: Blood on the throat or the side of the [neck](#neck), often [running](#running) from two small punctures in [vampire](#vampire) pictures. A bite mark sometimes accompanies it.

entries.name: wrist_cutting
entries.description: Cuts across the wrist from [self-harm](#self-harm) or a [suicide](#suicide) attempt, including the instant just before or after. It is usually shown with a blade still in hand and [blood](#blood) [running](#running) down the arm.

entries.name: scar_on_tail
entries.description: A healed mark along a character's [tail](#tail), sometimes with a notch, kink or missing tip where the damage was done.

entries.name: blood_on_breasts
entries.description: Blood [running](#running) down or spattered across the [breasts](#breasts). It is the marking on the skin that counts, not whatever produced it.

entries.name: blood_in_mouth
entries.description: The inside of the mouth red with [blood](#blood), or a trickle escaping at the [corner](#corner) of the [lips](#lips). Somebody actively [coughing](#coughing) it up takes the coughing [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: blood_on_wall
entries.description: Blood marking a wall, flung across it or pressed onto it as handprints. It establishes [violence](#violence) without the act itself being shown.

entries.name: missing_eye
entries.description: One eye is absent entirely, leaving a shut [lid](#lid), an empty socket or a scarred hollow in its place. Often hidden behind an [eyepatch](#eyepatch) or a fall of hair.

entries.name: bite_mark_on_shoulder
entries.description: Tooth marks pressed into a shoulder, reddened or bruised and sometimes deep enough to bleed. Left over from a struggle or from somebody [biting](#biting) down during an embrace.

entries.name: glasgow_smile
entries.description: A wound slit from each [corner](#corner) of the mouth up the cheeks, leaving a permanent [forced](#forced) [grin](#grin). Drawn on knife-scarred villains and on the slit-mouthed woman of Japanese [urban](#urban) legend.

entries.name: bruised_eye
entries.description: Swollen, darkened skin ringing one eye after a punch or a fall — the classic black eye. It marks a fight that has already happened.

entries.name: blue_blood
entries.description: Blood rendered blue instead of red, common for aliens, monsters and machines. The wound and flow are drawn as usual and only the colour changes.

entries.name: arrow_in_body
entries.description: An arrow lodged in someone's [flesh](#flesh), most often the chest or the [back](#back), its shaft still [standing](#standing) out of the wound. Blood around the entry point is common.

entries.name: deep_wound
entries.description: A cut driven far enough through the skin that what lies beneath begins to show. Heavier than a scratch or a [bruise](#bruise), and normally drawn with [blood](#blood) [running](#running) from it.

entries.name: blood_on_body
entries.description: Blood spread across a character's skin over more than one area. Where only the hands, face or chest carry it, the narrower tags fit better.

entries.name: bleeding_from_forehead
entries.description: Blood [running](#running) down over the brow from a wound higher up the head, often out of sight beneath the hair. It commonly arrives together with [blood](#blood) smeared across the face.

entries.name: scar_on_breasts
entries.description: A healed wound somewhere on the [breasts](#breasts) themselves, whether a short nick or a long slash.

entries.name: blood_on_mouth
entries.description: Blood around the [lips](#lips) and the chin, from a bite taken out of somebody, a struck face or a [drink](#drink). It sits on the outside, unlike [blood](#blood) shown within the mouth.

entries.name: blood_spray
entries.description: Blood bursting outward through the air, generally in the instant after a blow lands. Wherever it comes down it leaves a [splatter](#splatter) behind.

entries.name: scrape
entries.description: A raw graze where the top layer of skin has been rubbed away, typically after a fall onto hard ground. Shown as a pink or red [patch](#patch) rather than a clean cut.

entries.name: scar_across_eyebrow
entries.description: A healed cut crossing the brow, usually leaving a bare gap through the eyebrow hair. A short, sharp mark that reads as a fighter's history.

entries.name: knifed
entries.description: A [comic](#comic) stabbing in which blades stay [planted](#planted) in the victim while they carry on largely unbothered. For a stabbing meant to be taken seriously, use [stab](#stab).

entries.name: blood_on_gloves
entries.description: Worn [gloves](#gloves) marked with [blood](#blood), keeping it off the skin beneath. Surgeons, fighters and killers account for most of them.

entries.name: bite_mark_on_thigh
entries.description: Tooth impressions on a thigh, usually high up where the skin is bare above legwear. The mark is what counts, not whoever put it there.

entries.name: bruise_on_leg
entries.description: Bruising on the leg, discolouring the thigh, knee or shin. Scrapes and plasters often keep it company.

entries.name: bruise_on_arm
entries.description: Bruising on the arm, over the forearm, elbow or shoulder. A hard grip, a fall or a scuffle is the usual cause.

entries.name: knife_in_head
entries.description: A blade is lodged in a character's [skull](#skull) and left sticking out. Depending on the drawing it is treated as a [serious](#serious) wound or as an absurd joke.

entries.name: gunshot_wound
entries.description: A [bullet](#bullet) [hole](#hole) in [flesh](#flesh), generally with [torn](#torn) [cloth](#cloth) and [bleeding](#bleeding) around it. Use it for the [injury](#injury) itself rather than the instant of being shot.

entries.name: blood_trail
entries.description: A line of [blood](#blood) drawn across the ground or a surface, marking where somebody was dragged or walked. It reads as a [path](#path) rather than a single [pool](#pool).

entries.name: blood_on_cheek
entries.description: A streak or smear of [blood](#blood) along the side of the face. It is often a graze, or a mark left there by somebody else's hand.

entries.name: blood_drop
entries.description: A single bead of [blood](#blood), [hanging](#hanging), [falling](#falling) or [resting](#resting) on a surface. It is small and isolated, unlike a [splatter](#splatter) or a [running](#running) [stream](#stream).

entries.name: broken_arm
entries.description: An arm hurt badly enough to be immobilised. It is usually drawn in a plaster [cast](#cast) and frequently carried in a sling.

entries.name: arrow_in_head
entries.description: An arrow [stuck](#stuck) into or driven clean through a character's head. Drawn as a [grave](#grave) wound in some pictures and as a joke in others.

entries.name: blood_on_feet
entries.description: Blood on the [soles](#soles) or the tops of bare [feet](#feet), often picked up by [walking](#walking) through it. Prints left across the [floor](#floor) frequently follow.

entries.name: no_scar
entries.description: A [scar](#scar) belonging to a character's design is absent from the skin, either by the artist's [choice](#choice) or because the scene comes before the wound.

entries.name: bite_mark_on_arm
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of [tooth](#tooth) impressions left on an arm, reddened, bruised or [broken](#broken). It records the mark only and says nothing about who made it.

entries.name: scraped_knee
entries.description: A grazed knee, the skin rubbed raw after a tumble. Often paired with a plaster [stuck](#stuck) over it and a wincing expression.

entries.name: slit_throat
entries.description: A horizontal cut opened across the [neck](#neck), usually [pouring](#pouring) [blood](#blood) down the chest. It appears as an [execution](#execution), a [murder](#murder) or a [suicide](#suicide), and is almost always depicted as fatal.

entries.name: scar_on_chin
entries.description: A healed mark on the point of the chin. A similar mark higher up on the side of the face is [scar_on_cheek](#scar_on_cheek).

entries.name: bloody_wings
entries.description: Wings stained or [dripping](#dripping) with [blood](#blood), feathered or membranous. Fallen-angel imagery leans on it, where the damage is half the point.

entries.name: coughing_blood
entries.description: Blood comes up out of the mouth as a character coughs, spattering a hand or the ground. Blood that only seeps at the lip is [blood_in_mouth](#blood_in_mouth) instead.

entries.name: slap_mark_on_face
entries.description: A red [handprint](#handprint) across a cheek from being struck. Usually accompanied by a shocked or tearful expression.

entries.name: blood_on_armor
entries.description: Blood smeared or spattered across worn armour plates. Whose [blood](#blood) it is stays unstated, only that the armour carries it.

entries.name: blood_on_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) marked with [blood](#blood), a favourite of horror and gothic pictures where the [stain](#stain) plays against pale [fabric](#fabric). The dress itself may be any colour at all.

entries.name: spitting_blood
entries.description: Blood leaving a character's mouth as they spit or cough it out, usually [following](#following) a [heavy](#heavy) blow or signalling [serious](#serious) illness.

entries.name: bloody_handprints
entries.description: The shape of a hand left in [blood](#blood) on a wall, a [window](#window) or another body. Fingers and palm have to be recognisable as such.

entries.name: blood_on_shoes
entries.description: Footwear stained with [blood](#blood), on the uppers or underneath. Bloody [footprints](#footprints) across the [floor](#floor) often go with it.

entries.name: bite_mark_on_ass
entries.description: Tooth impressions on a buttock, drawn as a reddened [crescent](#crescent) of dents pressed into the skin. The mark is what is recorded, left over from whoever bit down.

entries.name: bug_bite
entries.description: A small red welt raised on the skin where an insect has fed, mosquitoes being the usual culprit. Arms and [legs](#legs) are the common sites, often with the character [scratching](#scratching) at it.

entries.name: stylized_blood
entries.description: Blood drawn as flat [shapes](#shapes), ribbons or petal-like splashes rather than a [realistic](#realistic) fluid, keeping a violent image graphic and decorative instead of gory.

entries.name: sliced
entries.description: Something cut cleanly into separate pieces, typically by a blade, with the cut surfaces still lined up or just beginning to [slide](#slide) apart. Applies to bodies as [well](#well) as to objects severed in a single stroke.

entries.name: mastectomy_scar
entries.description: A matched pair of scars across the lower chest, [sitting](#sitting) just under the [pectorals](#pectorals) and sometimes curving up at the ends. Left by surgical removal of the [breasts](#breasts), so it reads as a transmasculine [marker](#marker) as much as a medical one.

entries.name: sprain
entries.description: A twisted joint, most often an ankle or wrist, drawn swollen or carefully favoured rather than [bleeding](#bleeding). The character is usually shown limping or cradling the limb.

entries.name: blood_on_axe
entries.description: An [axe](#axe) [carrying](#carrying) [blood](#blood) on its head or [handle](#handle), fresh and [dripping](#dripping) or long dried. The [weapon](#weapon) has plainly been used.

entries.name: blood_on_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) spotted or soaked with [blood](#blood), its [petals](#petals) stained red. Beauty set against [violence](#violence) is the usual reason for it.

entries.name: broken_leg
entries.description: A leg hurt badly enough to be immobilised. A plaster [cast](#cast) is the usual [sign](#sign), often with crutches to go with it.

entries.name: blood_on_mask
entries.description: A worn or held [mask](#mask) spattered with [blood](#blood). The face behind it stays hidden, which is much of the effect.
