entries.name: smeared_blood
entries.description: Blood dragged across a surface into a streak rather than left as drops or a [pool](#pool). Handprints on walls, wiped cheeks and trails along a [floor](#floor) all qualify.

entries.name: blood_on_teeth
entries.description: Red staining the [teeth](#teeth) inside an open mouth, after a bite or a blow. Bared [fangs](#fangs) with [blood](#blood) on them are a [staple](#staple) of predators and vampires.

entries.name: torn_skin
entries.description: Skin [split](#split) open, peeled [back](#back) or ripped away, showing whatever lies beneath it, from [flesh](#flesh) to [machinery](#machinery) to another form entirely.

entries.name: bandages
entries.description: Woven strips of [cloth](#cloth) wound around part of the body, whether as first aid, as support, or purely as an accessory. Pair it with a placement [tag](#tag) such as [bandaged_arm](#bandaged_arm); cloth binding the chest as a garment is [sarashi](#sarashi), and a small adhesive strip is a [bandaid](#bandaid).

entries.name: bandaid
entries.description: An adhesive plaster [stuck](#stuck) to the skin over a small cut or graze, or worn purely for the look. Pair it with a placement [tag](#tag) such as [bandaid_on_face](#bandaid_on_face); it is not the same object as [pasties](#pasties) or [maebari](#maebari) even when it covers a nipple or the [groin](#groin).

entries.name: bandaged_arm
entries.description: At least one arm is wrapped in bandage, whether for an [injury](#injury) or as part of the character's look. Wrapping confined to the wrist is [bandaged_wrist](#bandaged_wrist); once it covers the forearm or passes the elbow this is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bandaid_on_face
entries.description: An adhesive plaster somewhere on the face. Narrow it to [bandaid_on_cheek](#bandaid_on_cheek), [bandaid_on_nose](#bandaid_on_nose) or [bandaid_on_forehead](#bandaid_on_forehead) when the spot is clear; a wound [dressing](#dressing) wound on is [bandage_on_face](#bandage_on_face).

entries.name: bandaged_leg
entries.description: At least one leg wrapped in bandage, anywhere from the thigh down to the ankle. It stands for [injury](#injury) and equally for bandage worn as leg covering by fighters and [ninja](#ninja).

entries.name: bandaid_on_leg
entries.description: An adhesive plaster somewhere on the leg. Where the spot is clear, [bandaid_on_knee](#bandaid_on_knee) or [bandaid_on_thigh](#bandaid_on_thigh) is the better [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bandaid_on_nose
entries.description: An adhesive plaster across the [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose), shorthand for a sporty, boyish or accident-prone character. It falls within the wider [bandaid_on_face](#bandaid_on_face).

entries.name: bandaged_hand
entries.description: At least one hand wrapped in bandage across the palm and knuckles, either as a fighter's wrap or as a [dressing](#dressing). Wrapping on the fingers alone is [bandaged_fingers](#bandaged_fingers).

entries.name: bandaid_on_knee
entries.description: An adhesive plaster over the knee, the classic scraped knee of an energetic [child](#child) or an athlete. It falls within the wider [bandaid_on_leg](#bandaid_on_leg).

entries.name: bandaid_on_cheek
entries.description: An adhesive plaster on the cheek, a favourite mark for scrappy, tomboyish characters. It sits within the wider [bandaid_on_face](#bandaid_on_face).

entries.name: medical_eyepatch
entries.description: An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) worn to treat an eye, held on by an elastic [strap](#strap) or adhesive rather than for [costume](#costume). The common Japanese version is a [plain](#plain) white [square](#square), sometimes with small ventilation holes; [bandages](#bandages) wrapped over an eye instead take the bandage over one eye [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bandage_over_one_eye
entries.description: A rolled bandage or a broad adhesive [dressing](#dressing) covering one eye the way an [eyepatch](#eyepatch) would, implying an [injury](#injury) beneath it. A proper eyepatch is tagged separately.

entries.name: bandaged_head
entries.description: Bandage around all or part of the head, from a single band across the [forehead](#forehead) to a full mummy-like wrap. A wrap covering one eye alone is [bandage_over_one_eye](#bandage_over_one_eye).

entries.name: bandaged_neck
entries.description: Bandage wound around the [neck](#neck), suggesting a wound to the throat or worn much as a [choker](#choker) would be. Tag any visible [injury](#injury) separately.

entries.name: bandaid_on_arm
entries.description: An adhesive plaster [stuck](#stuck) somewhere on the arm, the elbow included. The wrist and the hand have placement tags of their own.

entries.name: crossed_bandaids
entries.description: Two adhesive [bandages](#bandages) overlapping into an X or a plus, usually [stuck](#stuck) on a cheek, a [nose](#nose) or a knee. Far more often a [comic](#comic) shorthand than a real [dressing](#dressing).

entries.name: bandage_on_face
entries.description: Wound bandage laid across part of the face, over the [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose) or a cheek. A small adhesive strip is [bandaid_on_face](#bandaid_on_face) instead, and a wrap covering the eye is [bandage_over_one_eye](#bandage_over_one_eye).

entries.name: gauze
entries.description: A [fabric](#fabric) pad taped over a wound too big for a [bandaid](#bandaid), or the roll that becomes a bandage when wound on. Placement tags such as [gauze_on_cheek](#gauze_on_cheek) or [gauze_over_eye](#gauze_over_eye) say where it sits.

entries.name: bandaid_on_hand
entries.description: An adhesive plaster on the hand or a finger, the sort of small cut that comes of [cooking](#cooking), craft work or a scuffle. Bandage wound around the whole hand is [bandaged_hand](#bandaged_hand) instead.

entries.name: intravenous_drip
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) of fluid hung above a patient, [running](#running) down a [tube](#tube) into a vein in the arm or hand. It sets a sickbed or [hospital](#hospital) scene, often together with [iv_stand](#iv_stand) and a hospital [bed](#bed).

entries.name: wheelchair
entries.description: A [chair](#chair) on wheels used as a mobility aid, pushed by hand, by an attendant, or driven by a motor. Its presence usually marks the seated character as injured, ill or disabled.

entries.name: bandaged_chest
entries.description: Bandage wound visibly around the [torso](#torso) at chest level, [dressing](#dressing) a wound or binding the chest flat. A [cloth](#cloth) wrap worn there as a garment is generally [sarashi](#sarashi).

entries.name: bandaged_wrist
entries.description: Bandage wrapped around the wrist and nothing beyond it. Once it covers most of the forearm or runs past the elbow, [bandaged_arm](#bandaged_arm) takes over.

entries.name: gauze_on_face
entries.description: A [square](#square) of medical [gauze](#gauze) taped somewhere on the face, whether cheek, [forehead](#forehead) or [jaw](#jaw). Reads as a recent beating or [accident](#accident) rather than a lasting condition.

entries.name: bandaid_on_thigh
entries.description: A plaster on the thigh, either covering a [scrape](#scrape) or worn as a decorative touch on bare [legs](#legs). Placement on the leg is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: gauze_on_cheek
entries.description: A [gauze](#gauze) pad taped to one cheek or both. A quick way to show a character who has been in a scrap.

entries.name: bandaid_on_forehead
entries.description: An adhesive plaster on the [forehead](#forehead), often half hidden under the fringe. It falls within the wider [bandaid_on_face](#bandaid_on_face).

entries.name: hospital_gown
entries.description: The thin loose [gown](#gown) given to patients, generally open or tied at the [back](#back). It marks somebody as a patient and often turns up with a [hospital](#hospital) [bed](#bed) or [bandages](#bandages).

entries.name: bandaged_fingers
entries.description: Bandage wrapped around one or more fingers while the rest of the hand stays uncovered. Once the palm is wrapped as [well](#well) it becomes [bandaged_hand](#bandaged_hand).

entries.name: bandaid_on_neck
entries.description: A plaster [stuck](#stuck) on the [neck](#neck) or the throat. It [can](#can) read as a [razor](#razor) nick, a scratch, or something being covered up.

entries.name: bandaid_on_head
entries.description: A plaster [stuck](#stuck) on the top or the side of the head, showing above or through the hair. It suggests a bump rather than a [serious](#serious) wound.

entries.name: cast
entries.description: A rigid [shell](#shell) moulded around an arm or a leg to hold a [broken](#broken) [bone](#bone) still while it knits. Signatures scrawled over the plaster are a common detail; the word has nothing to do with a work's ensemble of characters, which is [lineup](#lineup).

entries.name: bandaged_foot
entries.description: One or both [feet](#feet) wrapped in bandage, sometimes carried up over the ankle. The shoe is usually off or missing entirely.

entries.name: crutch
entries.description: A padded [stick](#stick) braced under the arm or gripped at the forearm to keep [weight](#weight) off an injured leg. Usually seen alongside a [cast](#cast) or bandaging.

entries.name: bandages_over_clothes
entries.description: Bandage wound on top of a garment rather than against the skin, crossing a sleeve, a [jacket](#jacket) or a [shirt](#shirt). It is far more often a styling [choice](#choice) than actual first aid.

entries.name: arm_sling
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) loop hung from the [neck](#neck) that cradles an injured forearm against the chest. Usually drawn together with a [cast](#cast) or bandaging.

entries.name: injection
entries.description: A [syringe](#syringe) pressed to the skin to push [medicine](#medicine) into the body. The [needle](#needle), the [barrel](#barrel) and often a swab or an outstretched arm make up the scene.

entries.name: bandaged_torso
entries.description: Bandage wound in bands around the chest and [stomach](#stomach), usually straight over bare skin. It is the standard [dressing](#dressing) for somebody recovering from a bad fight.

entries.name: bandaid_on_shoulder
entries.description: An adhesive plaster [stuck](#stuck) to the shoulder, visible where a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) or off-shoulder garment leaves the skin uncovered. Often one of several scattered over a rough-and-tumble character.

entries.name: wrapped_up
entries.description: Someone is bundled in [cloth](#cloth), [bandages](#bandages), or a [blanket](#blanket) wound around the body. The [wrapping](#wrapping) restricts movement, whether the mood reads as cosy or as [trapped](#trapped).

entries.name: black_bandages
entries.description: Wrapping [bandages](#bandages) in black rather than the usual white, wound round limbs, [torso](#torso) or head. They read as a style [choice](#choice) more than as medical [dressing](#dressing).

entries.name: cold_pack
entries.description: A cooling adhesive [patch](#patch) [stuck](#stuck) on the [forehead](#forehead) to bring a [fever](#fever) down or ease a [headache](#headache). In art it works as shorthand for being ill, or for [working](#working) late on something hard.

entries.name: bandages_over_eyes
entries.description: Bandage wound across both eyes, leaving the character unable to see. Where only one eye is covered, the single-eye version of the [tag](#tag) applies instead.

entries.name: gauze_on_knee
entries.description: A [gauze](#gauze) pad taped over the knee, the classic mark of a fall or a scraped-up [child](#child). Reads as a fresh graze rather than a [serious](#serious) [injury](#injury).

entries.name: bandaid_on_stomach
entries.description: An adhesive plaster [stuck](#stuck) to the [belly](#belly), seen where the [midriff](#midriff) is uncovered. It usually stands in for a small [scrape](#scrape) rather than a [serious](#serious) wound.

entries.name: red_bandage
entries.description: Wrappings of red [cloth](#cloth) wound around a limb, the [torso](#torso), or the head. May [cover](#cover) a genuine [injury](#injury) or be worn purely as a [costume](#costume) element, as in many martial-arts and shrine-maiden designs.

entries.name: bandage_on_knee
entries.description: Bandage wrapped around a knee, covering the cap. It frequently accompanies scuffs and grazes on an active character.

entries.name: bandage_on_hair
entries.description: A length of bandage wound into or tied around the hair, worn as an accessory rather than as a [dressing](#dressing). Check first whether [bandaged_head](#bandaged_head) or [bandaid_on_head](#bandaid_on_head) describes the picture better.

entries.name: powered_wheelchair
entries.description: A [wheelchair](#wheelchair) driven by a motor and steered by its occupant, usually with a [joystick](#joystick) on the [armrest](#armrest). Bulkier than a manual [chair](#chair), with a [battery](#battery) pack beneath the seat.

entries.name: loose_bandages
entries.description: Wrappings that have come undone and trail free from a limb or the head instead of [lying](#lying) flat against it. They suggest a [dressing](#dressing) applied in haste or left neglected.

entries.name: gauze_over_eye
entries.description: A [gauze](#gauze) pad laid across one eye or both, held by [tape](#tape) or a wrap around the head. Reads as treatment for an [injury](#injury) rather than as a decorative [eyepatch](#eyepatch).

entries.name: ice_pack
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) of [ice](#ice) held against the body to bring down a swelling, a [fever](#fever) or a sore spot. Comedy scenes [park](#park) one flat on top of the head.

entries.name: bandaged_tail
entries.description: A character's [tail](#tail) is wrapped in bandage over part or all of its length. It nearly always reads as an [injury](#injury) rather than as styling.

entries.name: first_aid
entries.description: Immediate treatment being given for an [injury](#injury): winding a bandage, [cleaning](#cleaning) a wound, sticking on a plaster. The [box](#box) of supplies by itself is [first_aid_kit](#first_aid_kit).

entries.name: gauze_on_leg
entries.description: Medical [gauze](#gauze) taped or wound around a thigh, shin or knee. Keep it for dressings on the lower limb; gauze elsewhere takes its own placement [tag](#tag) or the [plain](#plain) gauze tag.

entries.name: bandaged_ankle
entries.description: Bandage wrapped around the ankle, as after a [sprain](#sprain), sometimes carried a little way up the shin or under the heel.

entries.name: bandaid_on_foot
entries.description: A plaster [stuck](#stuck) on the foot, over a blistered heel or a stubbed toe. The character is generally [barefoot](#barefoot) where it shows.

entries.name: bandaid_on_clothes
entries.description: A plaster [stuck](#stuck) onto a garment instead of onto skin, patching a tear or worn as pure decoration. Jackets and caps in punkish designs carry them.

entries.name: gauze_on_arm
entries.description: A pad of medical [gauze](#gauze) taped to the upper or lower arm, covering a cut or an [injection](#injection) site. Smaller in [scope](#scope) than [wrapping](#wrapping) the whole limb in [bandages](#bandages).

entries.name: bandage_on_leg
entries.description: Bandage wound around part of a leg, at the thigh, shin or calf, with the rest of it left bare. It may be [dressing](#dressing) an [injury](#injury) or simply belong to the character's design.

entries.name: applying_bandages
entries.description: Somebody is winding or taping dressings over a wound, their own or another person's. The treatment is being carried out, not merely worn.

entries.name: bandaged_ear
entries.description: Bandage plainly wound around one ear or both, sometimes carried over the [crown](#crown) of the head. Animal-eared characters wear it after a fight.

entries.name: knee_brace
entries.description: A supportive sleeve or strapped frame worn around the knee joint. It signals an [injury](#injury), a recovery, or an athlete guarding the joint during sport.

entries.name: bandaid_on_ear
entries.description: A small adhesive plaster [stuck](#stuck) on an ear, human or [animal](#animal). It usually turns up alongside other scrapes on the same character.

entries.name: bandaid_on_breast
entries.description: A plaster [stuck](#stuck) on a breast, sometimes [serving](#serving) as the only thing over the nipple. It may be a genuine [dressing](#dressing) or purely a flourish in the character's design.

entries.name: bandaid_on_ass
entries.description: A small adhesive plaster [stuck](#stuck) on a buttock. Nothing about it requires the rest of the character to be undressed.

entries.name: pink_bandaid
entries.description: An adhesive plaster in pink [stuck](#stuck) over a small hurt on a cheek, a knee or a finger. Often more decorative than genuinely medical, especially when worn across the [nose](#nose).

entries.name: neck_brace
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) worn to hold the [neck](#neck) still after [injury](#injury) or [surgery](#surgery), either a soft padded band or a rigid moulded [shell](#shell). Racing drivers and impact athletes wear modified versions of the stiff type.

entries.name: pet_cone
entries.description: The wide plastic cone fastened round an animal's [neck](#neck) so it cannot lick or scratch at a [healing](#healing) wound. Also called an Elizabethan [collar](#collar), and sometimes put on a character in a [pet](#pet) role.

entries.name: bandaged_knees
entries.description: Bandage wound around both [knees](#knees) at once. It is a recurring look on characters who fight, [train](#train), or fall over a great deal.

entries.name: too_many_bandaids
entries.description: A character plastered with far more adhesive [bandages](#bandages) than any [injury](#injury) would call for, [stuck](#stuck) across the face, arms and [legs](#legs).

entries.name: stump_cover
entries.description: A fitted sleeve pulled over the end of an amputated limb, made of [cloth](#cloth) or [latex](#latex) and sometimes cinched with [ribbon](#ribbon). Worn where [no](#no) [prosthesis](#prosthesis) is fitted.

entries.name: leg_cast
entries.description: A rigid plaster or fibreglass [shell](#shell) moulded around a [broken](#broken) leg, sometimes covered in signatures. Crutches or a [wheelchair](#wheelchair) often appear with it.

entries.name: pregnant
entries.description: A character [carrying](#carrying) a [child](#child), shown by a visibly swollen [belly](#belly). Only the visible belly counts; [holding](#holding) a positive test is not enough. Inflation is a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: drunk
entries.description: Somebody intoxicated by [alcohol](#alcohol), flushed across the face, slurring or generally unsteady. The [drink](#drink) should be in the picture, or the [drinking](#drinking) spelled out in the text, before it applies.

entries.name: hot
entries.description: A character is suffering from heat: sweating, [fanning](#fanning) themselves, wilting in the [sun](#sun) or saying how warm it is. It is not a way of [calling](#calling) somebody attractive.

entries.name: unconscious
entries.description: A character has passed out from [injury](#injury), shock or exhaustion, often slumped over, carried or held by someone else. Ordinary sleep instead is the [sleeping](#sleeping) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: fainted
entries.description: The character has already passed out and lies limp and unresponsive, still [breathing](#breathing). It is the state after a collapse, neither sleep nor [death](#death).

entries.name: cold
entries.description: The character is visibly suffering from the [temperature](#temperature): shivering, arms wrapped tight, red [nose](#nose), [breath](#breath) showing white. It describes the person's state, not the [winter](#winter) setting around them.

entries.name: possessed
entries.description: A character's body is being controlled by another entity inhabiting it, such as a [ghost](#ghost) or [parasite](#parasite), often shown by changed eye colour or a different [reflection](#reflection). Unlike [mind_control](#mind_control), the intruder lives in the body rather than commanding it from outside.

entries.name: exhausted
entries.description: Worn out by hard physical effort: panting, slumped, drenched in [sweat](#sweat). Tiredness from want of sleep is [sleepy](#sleepy) instead. It usually follows exercise or a fight.

entries.name: drugged
entries.description: Somebody under the effect of a drug: eyes unfocused, limbs slack, the face flushed and dull. Often set up as incapacitation before a coercive scene.

entries.name: sick
entries.description: A character in poor health: feverish, [resting](#resting) in [bed](#bed) with a [cold](#cold), [coughing](#coughing), or [holding](#holding) a [thermometer](#thermometer). Describes illness rather than [injury](#injury) or [plain](#plain) exhaustion.

entries.name: blind
entries.description: A character who cannot see, indicated by clouded or permanently shut eyes, a [cane](#cane), scarring or a covering never taken off. Tag whatever evidence is visible, such as [blindfold](#blindfold) or [closed_eyes](#closed_eyes).

entries.name: giving_birth
entries.description: A character in labour, delivering a [child](#child). Normally drawn explicitly and tagged alongside pregnancy.

entries.name: tired_(fatigue)
entries.description: Worn down by effort instead of by lack of sleep: slumped shoulders, open-mouthed [breathing](#breathing), [sweat](#sweat), limbs that will not lift.

entries.name: drowning
entries.description: Somebody held under [water](#water) past the point of [holding](#holding) their [breath](#breath), thrashing, [sinking](#sinking) or already limp. Applies both to the struggle and to a character who has gone under for good.

entries.name: hungry
entries.description: A character is shown craving [food](#food): [drooling](#drooling) in front of a [meal](#meal), daydreaming of [dishes](#dishes), a [stomach](#stomach) [growling](#growling), or simply saying so.

entries.name: sneezing
entries.description: A character mid-sneeze, eyes squeezed shut and mouth open, sometimes with spray or a [sound](#sound) effect. In Japanese lore it means someone is [talking](#talking) about you.

entries.name: implied_pregnancy
entries.description: A hint that a character is expecting while her [belly](#belly) still shows nothing. A positive test [stick](#stick), a line of dialogue, [morning](#morning) sickness or a maternity charm carries it.

entries.name: dying
entries.description: Somebody at the edge of [death](#death): [collapsed](#collapsed), [bleeding](#bleeding) out or [fading](#fading), but not gone yet. The moment before, rather than a [corpse](#corpse).

entries.name: fever
entries.description: A character runs a high [temperature](#temperature) from illness, drawn with flushed cheeks, a damp [cloth](#cloth) on the [forehead](#forehead) and a [thermometer](#thermometer). Bedding, pyjamas and a [worried](#worried) visitor round the scene out.

entries.name: fetus
entries.description: An unborn [child](#child) shown inside the womb, generally through a cutaway or a see-through [belly](#belly). Early on it is little more than a curled shape; later it takes recognisable form. Pregnant belongs beside it when the mother is in view.

entries.name: fainting
entries.description: The moment consciousness goes: [knees](#knees) folding, eyes [rolling](#rolling) up, the body going slack as it drops. Shock, [blood](#blood) loss, heat or lack of air brings it on; the state afterwards is [fainted](#fainted).

entries.name: full_stomach
entries.description: Somebody who has eaten their fill and cannot face another bite, slumped [back](#back) or cradling their middle. The [belly](#belly) may be visibly swollen, but need not be.

entries.name: coughing
entries.description: A character coughs, mouth open and body hunched, often with a hand raised to it. Forceful and repeated, unlike a single sneeze.

entries.name: brain_freeze
entries.description: The sharp [headache](#headache) that follows [swallowing](#swallowing) something ice-cold too fast, drawn as a [wince](#wince) with a hand clapped to the [forehead](#forehead). The [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) or shaved ice that caused it is usually still in the other hand.

entries.name: dizzy
entries.description: The world is [spinning](#spinning): unsteady footing, eyes turned to swirls, sometimes stars or birds circling overhead. About the giddiness itself rather than whatever caused it.

entries.name: male_pregnancy
entries.description: A male character [carrying](#carrying) a pregnancy, shown by a rounded swollen [belly](#belly). Frequently overlaps with designs that give a man female [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: dazed
entries.description: Eyes unfocused and head lolling, sometimes with stars or spirals circling, the character unable to hold a thought. Follows a blow, a fall, [drink](#drink), rough [sex](#sex) or coming round after being knocked out.

entries.name: disheveled
entries.description: The character looks rumpled and uncared for, [clothes](#clothes) askew and hair out of order. The end of a long [day](#day), a scuffle, or simply [no](#no) grooming at all.

entries.name: ptsd
entries.description: Lingering trauma shown through flashbacks to combat or assault, constant wariness, or a sudden startled reaction to an ordinary [sound](#sound). Soldiers and other survivors of [violence](#violence) are the usual subjects.

entries.name: mute
entries.description: A character who cannot speak. Artists signal it with speech bubbles [holding](#holding) nothing but ellipses, with written [notes](#notes), or with signing hands.

entries.name: rotting
entries.description: Flesh, [fruit](#fruit) or material visibly [breaking](#breaking) down, with discolouration, sagging and gaps in the surface. Used for [undead](#undead) bodies and for decaying objects alike.

entries.name: heart_attack
entries.description: The [heart](#heart) gives out: the character clutches at their chest, face contorted, and buckles. Played straight in drama and comically as a reaction to a shock.

entries.name: headache
entries.description: A character is in [pain](#pain) in the head, usually clutching temples or [forehead](#forehead) with a screwed-up face. Stress, illness and too little sleep are the causes shown.

entries.name: stomach_ache
entries.description: Pain in the [belly](#belly) from nerves, hunger or something eaten badly. It counts when the picture shows it: a hand pressed to the midsection, a hunched posture, rumbling marks.

entries.name: hangover
entries.description: The [morning](#morning) after too much [drink](#drink): pallor, a throbbing head and a hand pressed to the [temple](#temple). Empty bottles, a darkened room and a [bucket](#bucket) often round out the scene.

entries.name: nausea
entries.description: The queasy look that comes before being [sick](#sick): a greenish [cast](#cast), a hand clapped over the mouth, a hunched posture. It need not lead to actual [vomiting](#vomiting).

entries.name: stoned
entries.description: A character visibly intoxicated on [marijuana](#marijuana) or a similar drug, drawn with reddened half-lidded eyes, a loose [grin](#grin) and an unfocused stare.

entries.name: choking_on_object
entries.description: Something lodged inside the windpipe, usually [food](#food), is [blocking](#blocking) a character's [breathing](#breathing). Pressure applied from outside the [neck](#neck) is [strangling](#strangling) instead, and both count as forms of [asphyxiation](#asphyxiation).

entries.name: sweat
entries.description: A few [beads](#beads) of perspiration on the skin from heat, effort or nerves, fewer than about five. Heavier sweating is [very_sweaty](#very_sweaty); a single oversized [comic](#comic) drop is [sweatdrop](#sweatdrop).

entries.name: sweaty_armpits
entries.description: Visible [sweat](#sweat) gathered in and around the [armpits](#armpits), from heat, exertion or nerves. Often shown together with raised arms.

entries.name: shiny_skin
entries.description: Skin drawn with specular highlights, usually suggesting [sweat](#sweat), oil or [water](#water). Applied whenever the skin carries a glossy sheen.

entries.name: saliva
entries.description: Visible spit, in the mouth, on the [tongue](#tongue), on skin or stretched in a [string](#string). Use only when the fluid is clearly saliva; spit [running](#running) from the mouth is [drooling](#drooling).

entries.name: wet
entries.description: The character or scene is soaked with [water](#water) or another watery [liquid](#liquid), including bodily fluids such as [pussy](#pussy) [juice](#juice). Add [wet_hair](#wet_hair) or [wet_clothes](#wet_clothes) for the specifics.

entries.name: saliva_trail_between_teeth
entries.description: Thin threads of spit stretched across an open mouth, bridging the upper and lower [teeth](#teeth). A shorthand for heat, exhaustion or arousal in an otherwise ordinary open-mouthed face.

entries.name: saliva_drip
entries.description: Saliva [dripping](#dripping) off the [tongue](#tongue), [lips](#lips) or chin in a [falling](#falling) drop or [thread](#thread). A step past [drooling](#drooling).

entries.name: steaming_body
entries.description: Steam rising off a character's body rather than from the surroundings, from heat, exertion or arousal. Steam only from the head out of embarrassment is [head_steam](#head_steam); visible [breath](#breath) is separate.

entries.name: saliva_trail
entries.description: A [string](#string) of [saliva](#saliva) stretched from the mouth to another mouth, an object or skin, most often right after a deep [kiss](#kiss). Tagged with saliva.

entries.name: food_on_face
entries.description: Crumbs, [sauce](#sauce) or scraps left [stuck](#stuck) to the face, generally after sloppy [eating](#eating). It reads as a cute or [comic](#comic) detail.

entries.name: dripping
entries.description: Liquid [running](#running) off a body, an object or clothing in drops. Counted as vague, so reach for [wet](#wet), [melting](#melting), [cumdrip](#cumdrip), [pussy_juice](#pussy_juice) or [bleeding](#bleeding) where one of them applies.

entries.name: dirty
entries.description: Mud, [soil](#soil) or grime on somebody or something. Where the mess sits on one particular part there are narrower spellings, such as [dirty_face](#dirty_face), [dirty_clothes](#dirty_clothes) and [dirty_feet](#dirty_feet).

entries.name: slime_(substance)
entries.description: Sticky, slick goo of non-bodily origin coating a character or scene. Frequently the lubricant in tentacle scenes or a monster's digestive fluid.

entries.name: very_sweaty
entries.description: Sweat [pouring](#pouring) off the character in many drops and streams, usually with other signs of exertion such as panting or [steam](#steam) rising from the body. A drop or two is just [sweat](#sweat).

entries.name: soap_bubbles
entries.description: Foam and suds worked up over the body while [bathing](#bathing) or [washing](#washing). Placed to hide nudity, the same [foam](#foam) becomes [soap_censor](#soap_censor).

entries.name: food_on_body
entries.description: Food lies on or covers the skin, whether spilled during [messy](#messy) [eating](#eating) or laid out deliberately with a person [serving](#serving) as the platter.

entries.name: snot
entries.description: Mucus [running](#running) from the [nose](#nose), typically brought on by [crying](#crying), illness, [cold](#cold) weather, or allergies. Often drawn alongside [tears](#tears) or a reddened nose.

entries.name: food_on_head
entries.description: An item of [food](#food) sits on top of the head, balanced deliberately or simply dropped there. Add [fruit_on_head](#fruit_on_head) when what is up there is [fruit](#fruit).

entries.name: lotion
entries.description: Cream or gel spread on the skin, such as [sunscreen](#sunscreen) or moisturiser, shown as the substance itself rather than its [container](#container). The [bottle](#bottle) it comes from is [lotion_bottle](#lotion_bottle).

entries.name: spill
entries.description: Liquid that has accidentally escaped its [container](#container) and pooled or run across a surface. Tag the resulting mess; the act of [pouring](#pouring) it out is [spilling](#spilling).

entries.name: submerged
entries.description: A character shown fully under the surface of [water](#water), whether in a [bath](#bath), a [pool](#pool) or the sea. For an object [underwater](#underwater) rather than a person, use [immersed](#immersed) instead.

entries.name: dirty_face
entries.description: Smudges of [mud](#mud), [soot](#soot) or grime across somebody's face. Despite the wording it has nothing to do with [naughty_face](#naughty_face) or [ahegao](#ahegao).

entries.name: melting
entries.description: A character or object drooping and [dripping](#dripping) as though turning to [liquid](#liquid), whether from [summer](#summer) heat, as an exaggeration of sweating, or as a stylistic [distortion](#distortion). A body actually merging into liquid is [dissolving](#dissolving) instead.

entries.name: liquid
entries.description: An unidentified, non-sexual fluid in the picture that cannot be [pinned](#pinned) down as [water](#water), [blood](#blood) or [paint](#paint). If it is a [drink](#drink) [tag](#tag) the beverage, a soaked character is [wet](#wet), and open water gets its own [scenery](#scenery) tag.

entries.name: spilling
entries.description: A character in the act of letting [liquid](#liquid) escape a [cup](#cup), [bottle](#bottle), or [bowl](#bowl), whether by [accident](#accident) or on purpose to tease. Compare [spill](#spill) for the mess already made.

entries.name: chocolate_on_body
entries.description: Chocolate smeared, poured or melted across bare skin, whether from [messy](#messy) [eating](#eating), a [spill](#spill) or deliberate play. A Valentine's [staple](#staple); particular [spots](#spots) have their own tags such as [chocolate_on_face](#chocolate_on_face) or [chocolate_on_hand](#chocolate_on_hand).

entries.name: messy
entries.description: A character smeared or splattered with something other than [cum](#cum), slime, [soap](#soap), [water](#water) or [sweat](#sweat) - spilled [food](#food), [batter](#batter), [sauce](#sauce) or [paint](#paint), usually from [cooking](#cooking) or [eating](#eating). Can read as suggestive, but is the non-sexual cousin of [bukkake](#bukkake).

entries.name: pouring_onto_self
entries.description: A character pours [liquid](#liquid), often [alcohol](#alcohol), [water](#water) or [milk](#milk), over their own body. Usually drawn for the [wet](#wet), [clinging](#clinging) effect; [tag](#tag) wet and the liquid as [well](#well).

entries.name: paint_splatter_on_face
entries.description: Paint flicked or smeared across someone's face, by [accident](#accident) or in play. Marks and designs painted on deliberately are [facepaint](#facepaint).

entries.name: food_on_breasts
entries.description: Food [resting](#resting) on or smeared across the [breasts](#breasts), from an accidental [spill](#spill) to a deliberate arrangement. A narrower case of [food_on_body](#food_on_body), often framed suggestively.

entries.name: rice_on_face
entries.description: Stray grains of [rice](#rice) [stuck](#stuck) to a character's cheek after [eating](#eating), a classic [sign](#sign) of a [messy](#messy) eater.

entries.name: dirty_feet
entries.description: Feet and [soles](#soles) coated in [dirt](#dirt) or [dust](#dust), generally the result of going about [barefoot](#barefoot). Common in [beach](#beach), countryside and barefoot-at-home scenes.

entries.name: cream_on_face
entries.description: A dab of [cream](#cream) left on the face after [eating](#eating) something cream-filled, a mild suggestive [gag](#gag). Any other [food](#food) smear is [food_on_face](#food_on_face), and it is never used for semen.

entries.name: runny_nose
entries.description: Mucus [running](#running) from the [nose](#nose), drawn as a drip or a trail on the upper lip. It signals a [cold](#cold), [crying](#crying) or cold weather.

entries.name: mud
entries.description: Earth churned together with [water](#water) into a thick paste, pooled underfoot or smeared across skin and clothing. What leaves a character filthy in [rain](#rain) and outdoor scenes.

entries.name: ambiguous_red_liquid
entries.description: Something red is spilt, smeared or [dripping](#dripping) and the picture never says what it is. Blood is the obvious [reading](#reading), but [juice](#juice), [wine](#wine) or [paint](#paint) stay just as possible, which is the point.

entries.name: food_on_hand
entries.description: Food [resting](#resting) on a palm or [clinging](#clinging) to the fingers, whether held out as an offer, balanced there, or left over from [eating](#eating).

entries.name: wet_face
entries.description: Water, [sweat](#sweat) or another [liquid](#liquid) [running](#running) over the face, leaving the skin glistening and hair [stuck](#stuck) to it. Common right after a swim, a shower or a bout of [crying](#crying).

entries.name: paint_on_body
entries.description: Paint splashed, smeared or handprinted onto bare skin, generally picked up by [accident](#accident) while [working](#working). Deliberate designs painted on the body are [bodypaint](#bodypaint).

entries.name: oiled
entries.description: Body oil has been rubbed over the skin, so the whole body carries [strong](#strong) wet-looking highlights. It differs from [sweat](#sweat) or [water](#water) in covering evenly and leaving [no](#no) drips.

entries.name: chocolate_on_face
entries.description: Runny [chocolate](#chocolate) is smeared or splashed across the face, most often around the mouth and cheeks. Common in [cooking](#cooking) scenes and messy-eating gags.

entries.name: snow_on_head
entries.description: A small cap of [snow](#snow) piled on top of someone's head or hair, usually played as a quiet [comic](#comic) detail showing how long they have been [waiting](#waiting) outside.

entries.name: grease_(mechanical)
entries.description: Dark [machine](#machine) lubricant, shown smeared across a mechanic's cheeks, hands and [overalls](#overalls) or coating a piece of [machinery](#machinery). Not the same thing as [cooking](#cooking) grease.

entries.name: black_liquid
entries.description: A [dark](#dark), unnamed fluid pooling, [dripping](#dripping) or [running](#running), frequently over a body. It stands in for [corruption](#corruption), [ink](#ink), tar and horror effects where the substance is left unexplained.

entries.name: food_between_breasts
entries.description: Something edible wedged into a [cleavage](#cleavage) and held there by the [breasts](#breasts). The pairing is played for laughs about as often as for suggestion.

entries.name: foaming_at_the_mouth
entries.description: White [froth](#froth) [spilling](#spilling) over the [lips](#lips), signalling [poison](#poison), rabid fury or a mind come loose. Toothbrushing gags use it too; [plain](#plain) drool and a [milk](#milk) lip are separate things.

entries.name: black_blood
entries.description: Blood drawn black rather than red, used for monsters, curses and stylised horror. Greyscale pictures do not count, since colour says nothing there.

entries.name: cream_on_body
entries.description: Confectionery [cream](#cream) is smeared over more of a character than just the face. It should read clearly as cream and not as some other substance.

entries.name: sweat_stain
entries.description: A [dark](#dark) damp [patch](#patch) left by [sweat](#sweat) soaking into a surface such as bedding, a [towel](#towel) or a [rock](#rock), sometimes an indicator of [after_sex](#after_sex). Damp patches on worn clothing are tagged sweaty [clothes](#clothes) instead.

entries.name: green_blood
entries.description: Blood drawn green rather than red, which marks the bleeder as something other than human: an [alien](#alien), an insect [creature](#creature), a [plant](#plant) being or a [monster](#monster). In every other respect it behaves like ordinary [blood](#blood).

entries.name: chocolate_on_hand
entries.description: Melted [chocolate](#chocolate) covers the fingers or the palm, often [dripping](#dripping) or being licked away. A constant of Valentine's chocolate-making pictures.

entries.name: licking_blood
entries.description: Blood is licked away, most often from a hand, a [weapon](#weapon), the [lips](#lips) or an open wound.

entries.name: snot_trail
entries.description: Mucus that has run down to or past the mouth rather than staying at the nostril. Always paired with the [plain](#plain) [snot](#snot) [tag](#tag), and shows up in scenes of [crying](#crying), sickness, or slapstick embarrassment.

entries.name: purple_blood
entries.description: Blood drawn in purple rather than red, a common shorthand for aliens, monsters, and demons. Also used to soften a wound scene stylistically.

entries.name: ice_cream_on_face
entries.description: A [blob](#blob) or smear of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) left on the cheeks or around the mouth after [eating](#eating). It is drawn to read as childish or endearing.

entries.name: cream_on_breasts
entries.description: Whipped or piped [cream](#cream) sits on a character's [breasts](#breasts), generally as part of a [dessert](#dessert) conceit. Fruit and [syrup](#syrup) often join it.

entries.name: pouring_onto_another
entries.description: One character tips a [container](#container) so its contents fall over somebody else: [water](#water), a [drink](#drink), [sauce](#sauce) or oil. Covers playful dousing as much as deliberate soaking.

entries.name: sticky
entries.description: A tacky residue [clinging](#clinging) to skin, hair or objects, drawn with stringy threads that stretch and glossy highlights. Covers [honey](#honey), [syrup](#syrup), [glue](#glue) and anything else that pulls into strands.

entries.name: dirty_hands
entries.description: Hands smeared with [mud](#mud), [soot](#soot), grease or [paint](#paint). Usually the leftovers of work or play that has only just finished.

entries.name: slimy
entries.description: A surface or body coated in thick viscous fluid that clings and drips in strands. The sheen and the stringy runoff are what mark it, whether the source is a [creature](#creature), [mud](#mud) or something secreted.

entries.name: sparkling_sweat
entries.description: Perspiration drawn with a [glint](#glint) or star effect, either laid over the droplets or scattered around a sweating character. It turns exertion glamorous rather than grimy.

entries.name: food_on_hair
entries.description: Food [sitting](#sitting) on or [caught](#caught) in the hair, dropped there, balanced as a joke, or worked through the strands.

entries.name: fake_blood
entries.description: Something red stands in for [blood](#blood): [ketchup](#ketchup), [jam](#jam), [paint](#paint), sweet bean paste. Look for the marks of a staged [injury](#injury), a crazed [grin](#grin) or a body [playing](#playing) dead before deciding a red [spill](#spill) is only pretend.

entries.name: ink_on_face
entries.description: Dark [ink](#ink) smeared or spattered across the cheeks, [nose](#nose) or [forehead](#forehead). It is usually picked up while [writing](#writing) or drawing, or left there by somebody else's [prank](#prank).

entries.name: chocolate_on_foot
entries.description: Liquid [chocolate](#chocolate) coats a foot or its [toes](#toes). Almost always a deliberately staged mess rather than something spilled while [cooking](#cooking).

entries.name: food_on_legs
entries.description: Food [lying](#lying) on the [legs](#legs) or [thighs](#thighs), across a [lap](#lap) or directly against bare skin.

entries.name: chocolate_on_legs
entries.description: Runny [chocolate](#chocolate) has been poured or spread over the [thighs](#thighs) or [calves](#calves). Generally a dessert-themed pin-up rather than a [kitchen](#kitchen) mishap.

entries.name: soot
entries.description: Black carbon residue from [burning](#burning), smeared across skin, clothing, or a surface. Explosions and fires leave characters coated in it, with darkened faces and singed hair.

entries.name: snow_on_body
entries.description: Snow settled across a character's shoulders, arms, or clothing rather than [falling](#falling) around them, suggesting they have been [standing](#standing) [outdoors](#outdoors) for some time.

entries.name: mouth_submerged
entries.description: The character sits low enough in [water](#water) that the surface [cuts](#cuts) across the mouth, leaving [nose](#nose) and eyes above it. Reads as [sulking](#sulking), [hiding](#hiding) or [blowing](#blowing) bubbles.

entries.name: petroleum
entries.description: Thick black crude oil straight out of the ground, gushing, pooling or filling a [drum](#drum). Cooking oil and oil rubbed on skin have tags of their own.

entries.name: foam_mustache
entries.description: A line of [froth](#froth) left across the upper lip after [drinking](#drinking) [beer](#beer) or [milk](#milk), or picked up from [soap](#soap) suds. It reads as a joke moustache rather than as real [facial](#facial) hair.

entries.name: ink_stain
entries.description: A [dark](#dark) [patch](#patch) of spilled [ink](#ink) soaked into [cloth](#cloth), [paper](#paper) or skin. It speaks of carelessness at a [desk](#desk) more often than anything deliberate.

entries.name: tanning_oil
entries.description: Oil rubbed onto the skin to encourage a [tan](#tan), shown either as the [bottle](#bottle) itself or as the slick sheen it leaves on shoulders, [back](#back) and [legs](#legs). A [beach](#beach) or [poolside](#poolside) prop, often applied by someone else.

entries.name: navel
entries.description: The [belly](#belly) button is in view, usually through nudity, a bare [stomach](#stomach), or midriff-baring [clothes](#clothes) such as a [bikini](#bikini) or tied [shirt](#shirt). One showing through [fabric](#fabric) is covered navel instead.

entries.name: collarbone
entries.description: The clavicles showing plainly, generally framed by a wide neckline, an off-shoulder top or a bare upper chest. One of the most heavily used [anatomy](#anatomy) tags.

entries.name: tongue
entries.description: The tongue is clearly visible inside an open mouth. When it sticks out past the [lips](#lips) use [tongue_out](#tongue_out); an unusually long one is [long_tongue](#long_tongue).

entries.name: pink_tongue
entries.description: A visible [tongue](#tongue) of ordinary pink, the commonest colour there is. Tagged where the tongue is actually shown, whether [stuck](#stuck) out, [licking](#licking) or [resting](#resting) in an open mouth.

entries.name: midriff
entries.description: A bare band of [stomach](#stomach) between a top and a bottom, covering up to about half the [belly](#belly), as with a [crop_top](#crop_top) worn over [pants](#pants). Doesn't apply to swimsuits, underwear-only outfits or nudity, nor to upper-body shots with [no](#no) bottom visible, unless the [underwear](#underwear) is being worn as outerwear.

entries.name: stomach
entries.description: A bare abdomen that is a prominent part of the picture, between [navel](#navel) and [groin](#groin). Unlike [midriff](#midriff) it applies with [underwear](#underwear), swimwear or nudity; the internal organ is [stomach_(organ)](#stomach_(organ)).

entries.name: armpits
entries.description: The hollow under the arm is on show, usually with an arm raised and a [sleeveless](#sleeveless), [strapless](#strapless) or bare top. When only the fold shows with the arm down, [armpit_crease](#armpit_crease) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: groin
entries.description: The V-shaped lines where the lower [belly](#belly) meets the [thighs](#thighs), visible above a [lowleg](#lowleg) waistband or beside the leg holes of a [highleg](#highleg) garment. Also called the adonis [belt](#belt) or hip lines; a safe [anatomy](#anatomy) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: covered_navel
entries.description: The dent of the [navel](#navel) shows through opaque skin-tight clothing such as a one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit), [bodysuit](#bodysuit) or [leotard](#leotard). A bare [belly](#belly) button is simply navel.

entries.name: back
entries.description: The expanse from the shoulders down to the top of the buttocks is on show and given real [weight](#weight) in the picture. Use it where the back is genuinely part of the composition rather than incidentally visible; a close view centred on it also takes [back_focus](#back_focus).

entries.name: belly
entries.description: A softly rounded, somewhat [plump](#plump) [midriff](#midriff) on show. A distinctly large [stomach](#stomach), from fullness, [fat](#fat) or pregnancy, is [big_belly](#big_belly) instead.

entries.name: armpit_crease
entries.description: The fold of skin where the arm meets the [torso](#torso), showing while the arm is lowered. Once the hollow itself is on view, [armpits](#armpits) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: midriff_peek
entries.description: A small sliver of [stomach](#stomach) showing, usually by [accident](#accident), under a riding-up [t-shirt](#t-shirt) or an [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) [shirt](#shirt). Less skin exposed than the main [midriff](#midriff) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: shoulder_blades
entries.description: The scapula [shapes](#shapes) visible through the skin of a bare [back](#back). Usually tagged alongside back and [from_behind](#from_behind).

entries.name: ribs
entries.description: A visible [outline](#outline) of the ribcage showing through the skin, on a thin, stretched or malnourished [figure](#figure). Cooked ribs served as a [meal](#meal) are a separate [food](#food) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: chest_hair
entries.description: Hair growing visibly on the chest, in any colour, length or thickness. It is nearly always drawn on men, though non-human humanoids of either [sex](#sex) may have it.

entries.name: neck
entries.description: The neck drawn so as to draw attention, either as the focus of the picture or through being unusually long or oddly proportioned. An ordinary neck goes untagged.

entries.name: navel_hair
entries.description: Body hair around the [navel](#navel) or [running](#running) down toward the pubic area, as a narrow line or an inverted V. Mostly drawn on adult men, and only rarely on women.

entries.name: dimples_of_venus
entries.description: A pair of small symmetrical hollows in the small of the [back](#back), [sitting](#sitting) just over the buttocks. Often faint, so they show up mainly in back views of a bared [torso](#torso).

entries.name: long_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) extended far enough to reach past the chin. Demons, frog-like characters and lewd [expressions](#expressions) carry it, generally together with [tongue_out](#tongue_out).

entries.name: linea_alba
entries.description: The faint vertical line down the middle of a [toned](#toned) [stomach](#stomach), the connective band that shows before any separate [abs](#abs) do. Use it where the [belly](#belly) has some definition but [no](#no) visible six-pack; the back's counterpart is [median_furrow](#median_furrow).

entries.name: covered_collarbone
entries.description: The line of the [collarbone](#collarbone) showing through clothing rather than on bare skin, typical of tight tops, bodysuits and swimsuits. An exposed one is simply collarbone.

entries.name: armpit_peek
entries.description: A glimpse of armpit through a gap in the clothing, visible only from a particular angle or because of how the body is turned. With the arm down and only the fold showing, [armpit_crease](#armpit_crease) applies.

entries.name: median_furrow
entries.description: The vertical groove [running](#running) down the centre of a bare [back](#back) along the line of the [spine](#spine). The equivalent line on the front of the [torso](#torso) is called linea alba.

entries.name: big_belly
entries.description: A [stomach](#stomach) that is markedly swollen, from a huge [meal](#meal), from [fat](#fat), or from pregnancy. Reserve it for pregnancy when the [belly](#belly) is large even for that state; a merely soft [midriff](#midriff) is belly, and the two are not used together.

entries.name: colored_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) in an uncommon colour, whether stained by [sweets](#sweets) and [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) or natural to a [monster](#monster) or a character with [colored_skin](#colored_skin).

entries.name: hip_bones
entries.description: The points of the pelvis stand out visibly at the front of the body. It goes with a slim [figure](#figure), a bare [midriff](#midriff) or bottoms worn low on the waist.

entries.name: adam's_apple
entries.description: The bump of the larynx at the front of the throat, drawn prominently on men and sometimes faintly on women. Worth tagging when the artist gives it real emphasis.

entries.name: nape
entries.description: The [back](#back) of the [neck](#neck), bared or made the focus of the picture. It has long been a mark of beauty in Japanese art, where an uncovered nape carried [strong](#strong) erotic [weight](#weight).

entries.name: forked_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) that splits near its tip the way a snake's does. It comes naturally to reptile characters and is handed to demons for the same [sinister](#sinister) association.

entries.name: blue_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) coloured blue, on monsters, reptilian characters or somebody who has just eaten something dyed. When the mouth is open and its [interior](#interior) is blue too, that counts here.

entries.name: groin_tendon
entries.description: Tendons [standing](#standing) out along the inner [thighs](#thighs) beside the [crotch](#crotch), forming a ridge with a hollow next to it, usually on [toned](#toned) figures.

entries.name: outie_navel
entries.description: A [belly](#belly) button that stands out from the [stomach](#stomach) rather than forming a dimple. Most often on [pregnant](#pregnant) characters as the belly stretches, but also on inflated bellies and simply as a body trait.

entries.name: spine
entries.description: The vertebral [column](#column) shown as visible [anatomy](#anatomy): a line of vertebrae along a bare [back](#back), or an exposed spine on a [skeleton](#skeleton) or [creature](#creature). Tag it when the backbone itself is drawn.

entries.name: protruding_navel
entries.description: A [belly](#belly) button that pushes outward instead of [sinking](#sinking) in, an outie. Sometimes exaggerated on a [pregnant](#pregnant) or heavily built character.

entries.name: purple_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) that is purple, usually on a [demon](#demon), [zombie](#zombie), or coloured-skin character. Also covers the inside of an open mouth being purple; combine with [colored_tongue](#colored_tongue) and [tongue_out](#tongue_out) where it shows.

entries.name: brain
entries.description: The wrinkled organ that sits inside the [skull](#skull), drawn as such. It appears in [anatomy](#anatomy) diagrams, in horror where a skull has been opened, and in gags that make a character's [thinking](#thinking) literal.

entries.name: heart_(organ)
entries.description: The beating organ itself, shown anatomically, cut open or held in a hand, rather than the ♥ [sign](#sign).

entries.name: long_neck
entries.description: A [neck](#neck) drawn longer than [anatomy](#anatomy) allows, as a stylistic stretch or as the trait of a non-human design. It is about proportion, not about how the head is held.

entries.name: very_long_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) at least as long as the character's face, often longer and frequently able to grip things. Used for monsters, demons and [comic](#comic) exaggeration alike.

entries.name: green_tongue
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) is coloured green. Where the mouth is open and the visible inside is green as [well](#well), that still counts under this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: core
entries.description: A solid opaque [ball](#ball) or lump suspended inside an otherwise see-through body, most often a slime. It reads as the creature's [heart](#heart) or control centre.

entries.name: navel_peek
entries.description: A glimpse of the [navel](#navel) through a gap in clothing — under a lifted hem, or between a short top and a waistband. Only the [midriff](#midriff) is uncovered.

entries.name: x_navel
entries.description: A [belly](#belly) button drawn as a small X mark rather than a dimple. A cartoon simplification common in [chibi](#chibi) and heavily stylised art.

entries.name: umbilical_cord
entries.description: The [rope](#rope) of [tissue](#tissue) joining a [fetus](#fetus) to the placenta, [carrying](#carrying) [blood](#blood) between mother and unborn [child](#child). Appears in birth scenes and in imagery that plays on gestation.

entries.name: grey_tongue
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) is grey rather than pink. It usually belongs to an [undead](#undead), monstrous or otherwise non-human character.

entries.name: yellow_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) coloured yellow rather than pink. If the inside of an open mouth shares that colour, it still counts.

entries.name: torso
entries.description: The trunk of the body treated as a subject in its own right: chest, [belly](#belly), [back](#back) and sides, apart from the head and limbs. Used when the framing or focus centres on this part of the body.

entries.name: thick_neck
entries.description: A [neck](#neck) drawn conspicuously wide, close to the width of the head, [giving](#giving) a [heavy](#heavy) and powerful look. Used for [muscular](#muscular) or brutish characters, and sometimes purely for [comic](#comic) effect.

entries.name: prehensile_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) long and [strong](#strong) enough to wrap around things and hold them, [standing](#standing) in for a hand. Usually drawn [hanging](#hanging) [well](#well) past the chin.

entries.name: no_navel
entries.description: The [belly](#belly) is in view and completely smooth, with [no](#no) [navel](#navel) on it. It covers both figures that ought to have one, where [artistic_error](#artistic_error) is worth adding, and constructs or creatures that would not.

entries.name: chest_hair_peek
entries.description: A tuft of body hair shows at an open [collar](#collar) or between undone [buttons](#buttons). Only that glimpse is visible, the chest itself staying covered.

entries.name: orange_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) coloured orange instead of pink. Where the rest of the visible mouth is orange too, it still counts.

entries.name: black_tongue
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) drawn black instead of pink, common on monsters, demons and certain beast characters. It only matters when the mouth opens far enough to show it.

entries.name: covered_armpit
entries.description: The hollow of the armpit shows as a shape through a close-fitting garment. Nothing is bared; only the contour comes through the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: aqua_tongue
entries.description: A visible [tongue](#tongue) coloured blue-green rather than pink. Usually a [sign](#sign) that the character is not human.

entries.name: excessive_armpit_hair
entries.description: Armpit hair grown [well](#well) past an ordinary tuft: thick, long, sometimes [spilling](#spilling) out beyond the arm. The exaggeration is what is being marked, since a normal amount has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: stomach_(organ)
entries.description: The digestive organ itself, seen in cutaway views, diagrams or [vore](#vore) art. For the [belly](#belly) as an outward part of the body, use [stomach](#stomach) instead.

entries.name: white_tongue
entries.description: A visible [tongue](#tongue) coloured white rather than the usual pink, typical of pale or [undead](#undead) characters.

entries.name: red_tongue
entries.description: A visible [tongue](#tongue) coloured red, deeper than the usual pink.

entries.name: brown_tongue
entries.description: A visible [tongue](#tongue) coloured brown rather than the usual pink. Almost always a beast, [demon](#demon) or other non-human character.

entries.name: smile
entries.description: The mouth curves upward at both ends in pleasure or happiness, the most common expression in the whole vocabulary. A wide open smile with [teeth](#teeth) showing is a [grin](#grin).

entries.name: grin
entries.description: A wide [smile](#smile) that bares the [teeth](#teeth). Do not pair it with [clenched_teeth](#clenched_teeth), and only add teeth on top of it when the teeth are drawn in real detail.

entries.name: happy
entries.description: The character plainly shows joy, contentment or pleasure. It usually comes across through laughter or a wide open-mouthed [smile](#smile) rather than a faint one.

entries.name: laughing
entries.description: A character laughs openly, mouth wide and eyes often screwed shut, sometimes with the head thrown [back](#back) or a hand raised. It is stronger than a [smile](#smile) or a [grin](#grin).

entries.name: excited
entries.description: Full of eagerness and anticipation, with wide eyes, a broad [smile](#smile) or energetic body language. Sparkling eyes and raised arms often come along. Not the sexual sense of the word.

entries.name: affectionate
entries.description: Characters showing warm, fond feelings for one another with nothing romantic or sexual about it, typically [family](#family) members or a person and an [animal](#animal). Romantic or sexual warmth goes to [hetero](#hetero), [yuri](#yuri) or [yaoi](#yaoi).

entries.name: motherly
entries.description: A woman behaving maternally toward someone younger — [comforting](#comforting), [feeding](#feeding) or advising them — whether or not the [child](#child) is hers. Not for sexual scenes, and not warranted merely because she is a grown woman.

entries.name: lovestruck
entries.description: Face and body give away helpless infatuation: dreamy unfocused eyes, a slack [smile](#smile), sometimes hearts [floating](#floating) about. The character is visibly smitten with somebody.

entries.name: foodgasm
entries.description: Overwhelming delight at [eating](#eating) something exquisite, drawn with flushed cheeks, streaming eyes and a rapturous face. It goes [well](#well) past simply enjoying a good [meal](#meal).

entries.name: giggling
entries.description: Quiet [restrained](#restrained) laughter, softer and less vocal than a full laugh and often [muffled](#muffled) behind a hand. Tends to come with flushed cheeks or [watering](#watering) eyes when the character is [fighting](#fighting) to stay quiet.

entries.name: ecstasy
entries.description: Overwhelming joy or bliss, so complete that the face has lost track of everything else. Not necessarily sexual, though it [can](#can) be.

entries.name: victory
entries.description: Somebody has won or finished what they set out to do, shown by [celebration](#celebration) or a [beaten](#beaten) opponent. It also covers pictures where a raised [v](#v) [sign](#sign) carries that same meaning.

entries.name: wince
entries.description: A face flinching involuntarily, eyes shut or narrowed and features drawn tight, from [pain](#pain), [distress](#distress), surprise, or acute embarrassment. It is often paired with [clenched_teeth](#clenched_teeth) or one shut eye.

entries.name: sad
entries.description: A character looking grieved or [unhappy](#unhappy), with downcast eyes, a drooping mouth or [tears](#tears). Tag what the character shows, not how the picture makes the viewer feel.

entries.name: gloom_(expression)
entries.description: A character visibly deflated by disappointment, usually for [comic](#comic) effect. Often drawn with [dark](#dark) vertical lines, a dark [aura](#aura) or [drifting](#drifting) soul flames around them.

entries.name: pain
entries.description: A character visibly hurting: wincing, tearing up, clutching the sore spot, or marked with [comic](#comic) pain lines and a little [lightning](#lightning) bolt over the [injury](#injury). Tag the cause as [well](#well), whether that is a [bruise](#bruise), a blow or [blood](#blood).

entries.name: depressed
entries.description: Heavy, hopeless low spirits: shoulders slumped, gaze on the [floor](#floor), sometimes a [dark](#dark) shading or a small [cloud](#cloud) overhead. Covers the passing mood as much as the illness.

entries.name: sad_smile
entries.description: A [smile](#smile) whose eyes and brows carry sorrow, so the whole expression reads as [unhappy](#unhappy) rather than pleased. Tears or downcast eyes often accompany it.

entries.name: sobbing
entries.description: Crying hard enough to shake the body, with the mouth wide open and [tears](#tears) streaming down. Sits [well](#well) past a merely [sad](#sad) face and past quiet, [restrained](#restrained) weeping.

entries.name: unhappy
entries.description: A quietly dejected face: the eyebrows angle up toward the middle of the [forehead](#forehead), the mouth turns down, and the eyes sit half-closed. Reads as gloom or disappointment rather than open [crying](#crying).

entries.name: begging
entries.description: A character pleading with somebody, for a favour, for mercy or for forgiveness. It is read from the desperate face and posture, often with clasped hands or a bowed head.

entries.name: lonely
entries.description: A character shown cut off from others and wanting company, the feeling carried by empty surroundings and a downcast face. Being merely the only [figure](#figure) in the frame is [solo](#solo) instead.

entries.name: despair
entries.description: Sorrow pushed past [crying](#crying) into blank hopelessness, the face gone slack or the head [buried](#buried) in the hands. Not the same as shame or embarrassment, and simplified [chibi](#chibi) faces [water](#water) the [tag](#tag) down.

entries.name: disappointed
entries.description: A let-down face: the mouth flattens, the eyes drop and the pose loses its [energy](#energy). Something hoped for failed to arrive, or fell short of what was expected.

entries.name: mourning
entries.description: Grief for someone who has died: a visit to a [grave](#grave), an offering set before a photograph, a [figure](#figure) in black with the head bowed. The dead are often present only as a picture or a name.

entries.name: angry
entries.description: The character is plainly mad, brows down and [teeth](#teeth) often bared, [glaring](#glaring) or with an [anger_vein](#anger_vein) popped at the [temple](#temple). Keep it for real anger: mild exasperation is [annoyed](#annoyed), and outright rage is [furious](#furious).

entries.name: annoyed
entries.description: Mild irritation, the flat and worn-out look of somebody enduring another's nonsense. Real anger is [angry](#angry) and rage is [furious](#furious), so keep this one for the low end of the scale.

entries.name: glaring
entries.description: A narrow-eyed look of anger or resentment, usually with a [frown](#frown) to match. Aimed either at another character or straight at the viewer.

entries.name: grumpy
entries.description: A sour, put-out face with lowered brows and a downturned mouth, radiating displeasure with everything nearby. Milder and more sustained than open anger.
A closed-mouth [frown](#frown) beneath sharply angled eyebrows. It usually carries anger or annoyance, though the same brow shape [can](#can) read as mere concentration.

entries.name: scowl
entries.description: A sour, hostile look of displeasure, brows drawn down and the mouth turned down at the corners. Stronger and more openly [angry](#angry) than a [plain](#plain) [frown](#frown) or a merely [annoyed](#annoyed) expression.

entries.name: grimace
entries.description: A twisted, pained face showing [pain](#pain), [disgust](#disgust), anger or discomfort, often paired with [clenched_teeth](#clenched_teeth). Use it for the distorted expression itself rather than a [plain](#plain) [frown](#frown).

entries.name: disgust
entries.description: Revulsion on the face: [nose](#nose) wrinkled, lip curled, eyes narrowed, often with the body [leaning](#leaning) [back](#back) from whatever caused it. Strong disapproval rather than [plain](#plain) anger.

entries.name: gesugao
entries.description: A sneering, contemptuous face that makes a character look cruel and pleased about it, built from a curled lip or nasty [grin](#grin) and narrowed eyes. Often put on a normally kind character to mark a [betrayal](#betrayal) or a hidden side.

entries.name: tantrum
entries.description: An outburst of rage or frustration: [flailing](#flailing) limbs, a [screaming](#screaming) face, stamped [feet](#feet), sometimes [throwing](#throwing) things or [rolling](#rolling) on the [floor](#floor). Children throw them to get their way, adults when their patience finally snaps.

entries.name: scolding
entries.description: One character telling another off in anger, usually with a jabbing finger, a wagging hand or fists on hips. Sometimes aimed straight out at the viewer.

entries.name: furious
entries.description: Anger at full boil — bared [teeth](#teeth), [standing](#standing) [veins](#veins), a character [well](#well) past reasoning. Far beyond the mild to moderate states covered by [annoyed](#annoyed) and [angry](#angry).

entries.name: frustrated
entries.description: A character thwarted or blocked, showing agitation and discontent — a [facepalm](#facepalm), gritted [teeth](#teeth), a hand dragged through the hair. Aimed at a situation rather than at another person, which sets it apart from [plain](#plain) anger.

entries.name: sneer
entries.description: A curled lip conveying flat contempt, as though the [target](#target) were beneath consideration. It is an extreme look best used sparingly; where there is [no](#no) [smile](#smile) at all, [disdain](#disdain) or [disgust](#disgust) fits better, and open hatred is a [scowl](#scowl).

entries.name: disdain
entries.description: Cold contempt aimed outward at somebody else: narrowed eyes, a raised chin, a lip curled in judgement. Where [smug](#smug) is satisfaction with oneself, this is a verdict on another.

entries.name: sulking
entries.description: A quiet, withdrawn [display](#display) of resentment, the face turned aside and the mouth set while the mood stays soured but unspoken. Reads as brooding annoyance rather than open anger, and often pairs with [pout](#pout) or [crossed_arms](#crossed_arms).

entries.name: puckered_face
entries.description: The whole face screwed up tight, eyes squeezed shut and the mouth drawn in. Usually the reaction to something sour, though it also serves as the [comic](#comic) aftermath of a [smack](#smack) to the head.

entries.name: growling
entries.description: A low threatening rumble, drawn with bared [teeth](#teeth), a wrinkled muzzle and often a written [sound](#sound) effect. Reads as a warning rather than an [attack](#attack) already begun.

entries.name: surprised
entries.description: One or more characters reacting with surprise or shock, shown through wide eyes, an open mouth or [comic](#comic) marks like a row of small carets beside the head.

entries.name: scared
entries.description: A character gripped by fear: [trembling](#trembling), wide eyes, [tears](#tears), [cowering](#cowering), shrunken pupils. Works for [comic](#comic) and [serious](#serious) pictures alike; a sudden jump-scare reaction is [surprised](#surprised) instead.

entries.name: nervous
entries.description: Somebody visibly on edge, [trembling](#trembling), flushed or sweating, often [working](#working) up to say something difficult or reacting to another's temper. The unease shows in the whole body, not the face alone.

entries.name: nervous_smile
entries.description: A [smile](#smile) pasted onto a face that plainly registers alarm, the [grin](#grin) of someone who knows things have gone wrong. The eyes and brows give away what the mouth is [hiding](#hiding).

entries.name: turn_pale
entries.description: A character's face drains of colour under shock, horror, [disgust](#disgust) or [despair](#despair), drawn as a bluish or white wash over the upper face, sometimes with vertical shading lines on the [forehead](#forehead). A face that is literally [sitting](#sitting) in [shadow](#shadow) is [shaded_face](#shaded_face) instead.

entries.name: worried
entries.description: A face showing anxiety or concern, typically through drawn brows, a small [frown](#frown), and troubled eyes. Use [scared](#scared) for stronger fear, and [nervous](#nervous) for jitters rather than concern.

entries.name: panicking
entries.description: A character visibly in a state of panic: [flailing](#flailing), [wide-eyed](#wide-eyed), coming apart. It [can](#can) be played broadly for laughs or drawn straight in a tense scene, while [plain](#plain) fear without the frenzy is [scared](#scared).

entries.name: horrified
entries.description: The face registers deep horror, some mixture of shock, fear and revulsion, usually with wide eyes and a [gaping](#gaping) mouth. It describes the character's reaction; a picture meant to frighten the viewer is [horror_(theme)](#horror_(theme)).

entries.name: breast_awe
entries.description: Somebody stares at another character's [breasts](#breasts), plainly astonished by the sight. The feeling is wonder rather than jealousy, though the moment usually plays for laughs.

entries.name: traumatized
entries.description: A character reeling from something terrible they have just witnessed or lived through, often drawn with a stunned face and hollow, unfocused eyes. The picture should make clear what caused the shock and that the reaction is genuine [distress](#distress).

entries.name: distress
entries.description: Fear and helplessness written on the face: brows pushed up, mouth open, eyes wide. The character is in trouble and it shows.

entries.name: awestruck
entries.description: A face [caught](#caught) in amazement: eyes wide, [lips](#lips) parted, the whole attention taken by whatever stands before them. It is used for wonder, not for arousal.

entries.name: flinch
entries.description: The body jerks [back](#back) sharply because something startled or hurt it, usually drawn with hard little lines springing off the shoulders or head. The smaller repeated jump of a body reacting to stimulation is [twitching](#twitching).

entries.name: embarrassed
entries.description: Self-conscious and [uncomfortable](#uncomfortable), generally blushing and looking away. Brought on by accidental exposure, a slip of the [tongue](#tongue) or [teasing](#teasing). Blush is the usual companion.

entries.name: expressionless
entries.description: A face [carrying](#carrying) [no](#no) emotion at all, blank for no evident reason. Different from [serious](#serious), where a [battle](#battle) or a [grave](#grave) moment explains the look. Also called a neutral expression.

entries.name: shame_(embarassment)
entries.description: The character is visibly ashamed: face lowered or turned aside, colour rising, shoulders pulled in. Heavier and more inward than the fluster of an ordinary joke.

entries.name: serious
entries.description: A [grave](#grave), solemn look, more intent than a blank [expressionless](#expressionless) face, usually given context such as a coming fight or bad [news](#news). Covers stern faces too.

entries.name: smirk
entries.description: A [smug](#smug), one-sided [smile](#smile), one [corner](#corner) of the mouth curled up. Compare smug, which is the attitude, and [grin](#grin).

entries.name: smug
entries.description: Self-satisfied superiority: a slight [smirk](#smirk), eyes narrowed or shut, often arms [folded](#folded). The expression rather than the [smile](#smile) alone, which is smirk.
A closed-mouth [smile](#smile) under sharply angled eyebrows, which turns the smile [smug](#smug), scheming or outright wicked. Compare [evil_smile](#evil_smile) for the openly malicious version.

entries.name: shy
entries.description: A character acting bashful or timid: a [flustered](#flustered) [blush](#blush), drawn-in brows, an averted look, perhaps clutching something like a stuffed [toy](#toy) for comfort. Reserved for visible discomfort at being noticed, not [plain](#plain) [embarrassed](#embarrassed).

entries.name: sleepy
entries.description: Drowsy at bedtime or just after waking: half-closed eyes, [yawning](#yawning), [rubbing](#rubbing) the eyes, [stretching](#stretching), sleep bubbles. Tiredness from exertion is [exhausted](#exhausted).

entries.name: yandere
entries.description: A character shows obsessive, possessive love that tips into menace or [violence](#violence), whether directed at the one they love or at anyone who gets too close. Tag it only when the picture shows the trait through expression or action, not simply because a character is canonically one.

entries.name: breast_envy
entries.description: A girl looks [jealous](#jealous) of, or deflated by, another character's obviously larger bust, often [glaring](#glaring) at it or clutching her own chest. Her feelings about her own size alone are [breast_conscious](#breast_conscious), and a direct [comparison](#comparison) between them is [breast_contest](#breast_contest).

entries.name: tired_(drowsy)
entries.description: Heavy lids and a slack face from wanting sleep, often with a yawn, a rubbed eye or a drooping head. The weariness is about rest rather than exertion.

entries.name: tsundere
entries.description: A character alternating between a [cold](#cold) or hostile surface and an [affectionate](#affectionate) side underneath, typically warming up gradually over the story. Tag it when the picture itself shows the trait in action, such as a [gift](#gift) handed over with a dismissive excuse.

entries.name: thinking
entries.description: A character is visibly pondering something, often with a hand at the chin or a [thought_bubble](#thought_bubble) showing what runs through their head. Covers readable unspoken thoughts as [well](#well).

entries.name: confused
entries.description: A bewildered look, often with a tilted head, a raised brow, a blank stare or a question mark [floating](#floating) alongside.

entries.name: flustered
entries.description: A character knocked off balance by something sudden, very often an unexpected romantic or sexual turn. Heavy [blush](#blush), wide eyes and [awkward](#awkward) [flailing](#flailing) gestures carry it.

entries.name: mesugaki
entries.description: The 'bratty' archetype: a young girl [taunting](#taunting) adults in a sexually charged, mocking way, typically with a [smug](#smug) expression, a single [fang](#fang), [twintails](#twintails) and skimpy [shorts](#shorts) or a [microskirt](#microskirt). Contrast with erogaki, who is seductive without the sass, and kusogaki, who is sassy without the sexual edge.

entries.name: unamused
entries.description: A flat, [deadpan](#deadpan) stare that says the character is not impressed, or is [waiting](#waiting) for a joke to land. Often paired with narrowed eyes or a closed mouth.

entries.name: doyagao
entries.description: A [smug](#smug), self-satisfied look: tight closed-lipped [smile](#smile), eyes shut or gleaming, brows in a proud V, often with hands [planted](#planted) on the hips. Funniest on a character pleased with something they in fact bungled.

entries.name: blank_stare
entries.description: A fixed stare with nothing readable behind it, the face slack and the eyes unfocused. Add [expressionless](#expressionless) or [empty_eyes](#empty_eyes) when those features are present.

entries.name: breast_conscious
