entries.description: A character frets over the size of her own chest, whether it is large, small or flat, and her face or hands say so. If a [bustier](#bustier) character nearby has set the feeling off use [breast_envy](#breast_envy), and flat_envy for the reverse case.

entries.name: determined
entries.description: A resolute, purposeful face: [jaw](#jaw) set, gaze steady, brows often drawn in, the character braced to see something through.

entries.name: bored
entries.description: Somebody with nothing to occupy them and [no](#no) interest in what is around them: half-lidded eyes, a chin propped on a hand, a listless slouch. Distinct from being tired and from a merely blank face.

entries.name: completely_unamused
entries.description: A flat, unimpressed face: level eyes, straight mouth, [no](#no) reaction whatever to what is going on. Frequently the [deadpan](#deadpan) half of a joke.

entries.name: crazy
entries.description: A character who looks unhinged, through wild eyes, a manic [grin](#grin) or deranged body language. Madness that grows out of obsessive love is [yandere](#yandere) instead.

entries.name: clueless
entries.description: The character has [no](#no) [idea](#idea) what is happening around them, missing a flirtation, a [threat](#threat) or a joke aimed squarely at them. Usually drawn with a blank or cheerfully vacant face.

entries.name: fidgeting
entries.description: Nervous or bashful restlessness, shown through twiddling fingers, shifting [feet](#feet) and a self-conscious look. A small uneasy motion rather than a large one.

entries.name: troll_face
entries.description: A wide, gloating [grin](#grin) paired with half-lidded eyes, drawn to provoke annoyance, borrowed from a well-known rage-comic [meme](#meme) face. The expression reads as spite at someone else's expense, unlike [doyagao](#doyagao), which is [smug](#smug) pride in one's own achievement.

entries.name: remembering
entries.description: A character deliberately calls a past moment to mind, usually shown with a faraway look beside an [inset](#inset) of the scene. When the memory forces itself on them instead, use [flashback](#flashback).

entries.name: rape_face
entries.description: A leering, predatory look, narrowed shifty eyes over a wide unpleasant [grin](#grin), suggesting a character is about to do something appalling. It describes the expression alone and says nothing about what actually happens in the picture.

entries.name: curious
entries.description: The character looks interested in something, [leaning](#leaning) toward it or peering closely with raised brows. Driven by wanting to know rather than by alarm.

entries.name: charisma_break
entries.description: A cool, composed front collapses into something undignified: panic, silliness, [plain](#plain) shock. Recognising the fall should need [no](#no) knowledge of the series.

entries.name: concentrating
entries.description: The character is fixed on the task in front of them, brow drawn and gaze steady. Aiming, [reading](#reading), threading a [needle](#needle) and similar moments all qualify.

entries.name: clumsy
entries.description: The character fumbles or trips through sheer awkwardness, [dropping](#dropping) what they carry or tangling their own [feet](#feet). Getting something wrong out of ignorance is a separate [idea](#idea) with its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: awkward
entries.description: Something accidental or badly timed has just happened and nobody knows what to say. Bodies go stiff, faces go blank, and the mood is [uncomfortable](#uncomfortable) rather than [angry](#angry) or funny.

entries.name: height_conscious
entries.description: A character is bothered about how [tall](#tall) or short they are: [sulking](#sulking) over it, [stretching](#stretching) up, [measuring](#measuring) themselves against a mark. When another character is the reason, height_envy applies too.

entries.name: unaware
entries.description: A character has [no](#no) [idea](#idea) what is happening around them, while the viewer plainly does. Often used where someone or something nearby is [watching](#watching) or acting without their notice.

entries.name: pensive
entries.description: A quiet inward expression: the character is [caught](#caught) up in their own thoughts, eyes lowered or unfocused and the mouth still.

entries.name: envy
entries.description: Wanting what somebody else has, shown as a sour [sideways](#sideways) look at another character or at the thing itself. Jealousy, the fear of losing something already held, is a different feeling.

entries.name: sour_(taste)
entries.description: The face pulled by a sharp, acidic taste: [lips](#lips) retracted, mouth puckered, eyes squeezed shut. Citrus [fruit](#fruit) is the usual cause.

entries.name: making_faces
entries.description: Deliberately [pulling](#pulling) a silly face: [tongue](#tongue) out, an eyelid dragged down, cheeks puffed. The exaggeration is put on, usually to amuse or [needle](#needle) somebody [watching](#watching).

entries.name: kuudere
entries.description: A character [holding](#holding) a [cold](#cold), blunt, aloof front with something warmer showing through underneath. A tsundere's [mask](#mask) is hot-tempered instead, and this works best when both sides of the manner appear at once.

entries.name: denial
entries.description: A character flatly refusing something plainly true, arms [folded](#folded) and face turned aside, protesting rather too hard. Played for comedy nearly every time.

entries.name: deadpan
entries.description: A completely flat [delivery](#delivery) in a moment that calls for a reaction, the face offering nothing at all. The humour lives in the gap between what is happening and the absence of any response.

entries.name: charisma_establishment
entries.description: The [mirror](#mirror) of charisma break, where a character snaps out of a loose, informal state into full commanding presence. The [switch](#switch) has to be sharp and has to happen inside the one picture, so expression sheets do not qualify.

entries.name: uncomfortable
entries.description: Someone visibly ill at ease, drawn with a stiff posture, a strained [smile](#smile) or an averted [glance](#glance). Awkward company, an unwanted situation or a physical annoyance [can](#can) all bring it on.

entries.name: closed_eyes
entries.description: Both eyes are shut, whether the character is smiling, asleep, calm or wincing. With only one eye shut, use [one_eye_closed](#one_eye_closed).

entries.name: one_eye_closed
entries.description: One eye is shut while the other stays open, for whatever reason: a wink, a [flinch](#flinch), taking aim. Combine it with the matching mouth tags such as [;d](#;d) or [;p](#;p), and add [wince](#wince) where the eye shuts from [pain](#pain) or shock.

entries.name: half-closed_eyes
entries.description: Both eyes are partly lowered, [reading](#reading) as drowsiness, boredom, [disdain](#disdain) or a seductive look depending on the rest of the face. For only one eye use [half-closed_eye](#half-closed_eye) instead.

The eyes close into upward arcs, the classic contented face. It nearly always accompanies a [smile](#smile) and reads as one even when the mouth is hidden; tightly crinkled eyes are [>_<](#>_<) instead.

entries.name: ;d
entries.description: A wide open-mouthed [grin](#grin) with one eye shut, the winking form of [:d](#:d). Stick the [tongue](#tongue) out with it and the [tag](#tag) becomes [;q](#;q).

Both eyes clench shut into angled slashes, often with the whole face scrunched up. It usually means delight, but [pain](#pain), embarrassment and misery all use it; gentler closed arcs are [^_^](#^_^).

entries.name: one_eye_covered
entries.description: One of the eyes is hidden entirely, by hair, a [patch](#patch), a hand or a [mask](#mask). Add whatever does the covering, such as [hair_over_one_eye](#hair_over_one_eye) or [eyepatch](#eyepatch).

Spirals fill the eyes, showing dizziness, confusion, being overwhelmed or knocked senseless, and occasionally drunkenness or rage. Irises naturally drawn as spirals count too; swirls painted on lenses are [coke-bottle_glasses](#coke-bottle_glasses).

entries.name: jitome
entries.description: Eyes drawn with a flat straight line along the top, [giving](#giving) a [bored](#bored), listless, unimpressed or [smug](#smug) look. It is an expression [device](#device) rather than a feature of the character's design.

entries.name: wide-eyed
entries.description: The eyes opened as far as they will go, with the sclera showing all the way around the iris. It reads as shock, fear, or intense surprise; pair it with [surprised](#surprised) or [scared](#scared) for the underlying emotion.

The eyes light up with a bright four-pointed [sparkle](#sparkle) [sitting](#sitting) in each iris, sometimes with more sparkles [drifting](#drifting) around the head. It reads as excitement or greed; pupils genuinely shaped like stars or crosses are something else.
Both eyes squint down into flat horizontal lines, with any mouth beneath. It usually means quiet contentment, but exasperation, embarrassment or drowsiness all fit.

entries.name: rolling_eyes
entries.description: Eyes rolled upward so the iris disappears toward the [lid](#lid). Most often part of an [ahegao](#ahegao) or [fucked_silly](#fucked_silly) expression of overwhelming pleasure; an innocent [glance](#glance) upward instead is [upturned_eyes](#upturned_eyes).
A closed-mouth [smile](#smile) with one eye shut, the ordinary wink. The same wink over an open [grin](#grin) is [;d](#;d) instead.

A stylised face where both eyes are drawn as [tall](#tall), narrow vertical [bars](#bars), [giving](#giving) a blank or [deadpan](#deadpan) look used for shock or an empty stare. One of a [family](#family) of symbol-shaped eyes alongside [o_o](#o_o) and [._.](#._.).

entries.name: covered_eyes
entries.description: Every one of a character's eyes is hidden, by hair, a [blindfold](#blindfold), headwear, a hand, an object or the angle of the view. A single hidden eye is [hair_over_one_eye](#hair_over_one_eye) or [covering_one_eye](#covering_one_eye); [tag](#tag) whatever is doing the [hiding](#hiding) as [well](#well).

entries.name: ;o
entries.description: One eye is closed while the mouth stands open, whether from a wink, a [wince](#wince) or a yawn. The open mouth on its own would be [:o](#:o).

The eyes become [tall](#tall) solid-white ovals ringed in [heavy](#heavy) black, a startled stare. Circular versions are [o_o](#o_o), horizontal ovals [wide_oval_eyes](#wide_oval_eyes) and filled-in black ones [solid_oval_eyes](#solid_oval_eyes); none of these count as [blank_eyes](#blank_eyes).

entries.name: blinking
entries.description: Eyes [caught](#caught) in the act of closing and [opening](#opening), which really only reads in animation. A still picture with shut eyes should take [closed_eyes](#closed_eyes), since a single frame cannot show the motion.

entries.name: ;p
entries.description: A wink with the [tongue](#tongue) [hanging](#hanging) downward out of the mouth. Tongue [sweeping](#sweeping) up along the lip alongside a wink is [;q](#;q) instead.

entries.name: half-closed_eye
entries.description: One eye is about half shut while the other is open, closed or hidden by hair, an [eyepatch](#eyepatch) or a [hat](#hat). Also applies to a [one-eyed](#one-eyed) character whose single eye is half closed. Both eyes half shut is [half-closed_eyes](#half-closed_eyes) instead.

entries.name: narrowed_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn narrow and tightened, [carrying](#carrying) suspicion, anger, concentration or a similarly guarded mood. Lids that droop rather than tighten are [half-closed_eyes](#half-closed_eyes).

entries.name: crazy_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn far too wide, the pupils unnaturally shrunken, blown open or stretched, marking psychosis, extreme [distress](#distress) or possession. A visual shorthand for an unhinged character.

entries.name: ;q
entries.description: A wink with the [tongue](#tongue) [licking](#licking) upward toward the top lip. Without the closed eye it would be [:q](#:q).

entries.name: u_u
entries.description: Closed eyes drawn as two small downward-curving arcs, a calmer cousin of the upward smiling-eyes mark. Reads as relaxed, resigned or lost in thought.

entries.name: >_o
entries.description: A wink in which the closed eye takes the tight angular slash of the [>_<](#>_<) face. The open eye stays drawn normally.

entries.name: unusually_open_eyes
entries.description: A character whose eyes are normally drawn shut or [squinting](#squinting) appears here with them fully open. Reserved for such characters specifically; ordinary open eyes on anyone else need [no](#no) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: upturned_eyes
entries.description: The eyes look upward relative to the face, often paired with the head tilted down and the brows raised, [reading](#reading) as coy, pleading or submissive. It also occurs naturally when a character looks up at a viewer positioned above them, and differs from [rolling_eyes](#rolling_eyes) in that something is actively being focused on.
The cat-like [sideways](#sideways) three of the mouth, drawn with one eye winked shut. Use [:3](#:3) when both eyes are open.

entries.name: x_x
entries.description: Both eyes drawn as X marks, the cartoon shorthand for a character who is knocked out, comically dead or utterly [exhausted](#exhausted). Often paired nearby with a lolling [tongue](#tongue) or [spiral](#spiral) eyes on another character.

entries.name: v-shaped_eyes
entries.description: The upper edge of each eye slopes down into a V, a [comic](#comic) shorthand for a jokingly evil or menacing look. Not to be [confused](#confused) with eyes closed into other [shapes](#shapes), which have their own separate tags.

entries.name: squinting
entries.description: Eyes narrowed partway shut, whether to see better, against bright light, or while peering closely at something. Compare [half-closed_eyes](#half-closed_eyes) for a relaxed or sultry look instead.

entries.name: bulging_eyes
entries.description: Eyes popping comically far out of their sockets. It exaggerates shock, awe or greed at whatever has just come into view.

entries.name: cross-eyed
entries.description: Both eyes turned in toward the [nose](#nose), either pulled there deliberately as a silly face or drawn as a permanent squint. Eyes splayed outward instead take [wall-eyed](#wall-eyed).
An [unhappy](#unhappy), downturned mouth combined with one eye squeezed shut. The wink softens the complaint into something closer to [teasing](#teasing).

entries.name: winking_(animated)
entries.description: An [animated](#animated) image in which an eye visibly closes and opens again. A still picture showing one shut eye takes [one_eye_closed](#one_eye_closed) instead, since that [tag](#tag) is meant to [cover](#cover) every such case there.
The pinched, angular [frown](#frown) of the [:<](#:<) face, drawn with one eye closed. The wink gives the sulk a playful edge.

entries.name: evil_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn to look threatening: narrowed, shadowed, sharply lit, or glinting with ill intent. The menace sits in the shaping of the eyes rather than in the whole face.

entries.name: eye_pop
entries.description: Eyeballs shooting out of their sockets in cartoon [fashion](#fashion), sometimes on stalks, driven by shock or surprise. The louder version of [bulging_eyes](#bulging_eyes).

entries.name: ;t
entries.description: One eye is winked shut while a cheek bunches against the lip and drags the mouth [sideways](#sideways). It happens when a character is irritated, [chewing](#chewing), or pressing their face into something.
The pointed, sly [smile](#smile) of the [:>](#:>) face paired with one closed eye. The result usually reads as [smug](#smug) or conspiratorial.

entries.name: pleading_eyes
entries.description: Wide, glossy eyes turned on someone in a silent request, usually drawn with extra highlights and the gaze tilted upward. Reads as wheedling or [begging](#begging) for a favour rather than [plain](#plain) sadness.

entries.name: asymmetrical_eyes
entries.description: The two eyes aim in different directions, one [drifting](#drifting) off while the other looks straight ahead, a trait often given to chameleon-like characters. Eyes of different colours are [heterochromia](#heterochromia), and lids opened to different widths are uneven eyes.
A puckered, number-three shaped mouth paired with one eye squeezed shut. The combination comes across as playful, or as a small pleased kiss-face.

Both eyes are drawn as [sideways](#sideways) threes, [giving](#giving) a [squinting](#squinting), unfocused look. It suits dopey or short-sighted characters and often turns up the moment their [glasses](#glasses) come off.

entries.name: opening_eyes
entries.description: The eyelids rise from a shut position, generally shown in animation as one slow movement. A blink begins and ends open and happens quickly, so [blinking](#blinking) covers that instead.
A flat, straight mouth combined with one closed eye. The blank line under the wink lands as [deadpan](#deadpan) or unimpressed.

entries.name: creepy_eyes
entries.description: Eyes drawn to unsettle: opened too wide, oddly lit, or missing their usual highlights. The rest of the face may stay perfectly calm.

entries.name: lowered_eyelids
entries.description: The upper lids hang partway across the eyes, producing a [heavy](#heavy), drowsy or unimpressed look. Eyes fully shut are [closed_eyes](#closed_eyes) instead.
One eye rolls upward while the other points down, the two drawn as a six and a nine. Either eye may take either role, and it has nothing to do with the sexual position of the same digits.
One eye is closed while the mouth sits in a slanted, uneven line. Together they read as awkwardness or wry resignation.

entries.name: looking_at_viewer
entries.description: The character's eyes meet the [camera](#camera), addressing whoever is looking at the picture. Eyes meeting between characters is [eye_contact](#eye_contact), and a face turned to the camera with the eyes shut or covered is [facing_viewer](#facing_viewer).

entries.name: looking_back
entries.description: A character glancing over their shoulder, the gaze turned between 135 and 180 degrees behind their front. It usually goes with [from_behind](#from_behind) and often with [looking_at_viewer](#looking_at_viewer) or [sideways_glance](#sideways_glance); with both eyes shut it is [facing_back](#facing_back).

entries.name: looking_at_another
entries.description: One character looking at another. Where the two meet each other's eyes, add [eye_contact](#eye_contact) as [well](#well).

entries.name: looking_to_the_side
entries.description: A gaze directed [sideways](#sideways), roughly 45 to 90 degrees off the character's own front. Add [sideways_glance](#sideways_glance) when only the eyes move, past 45 degrees to the rear it becomes [looking_back](#looking_back), and deliberately avoiding someone's eyes is [averting_eyes](#averting_eyes).

entries.name: looking_down
entries.description: A character's gaze angled downward relative to their own body. It often pairs with a [camera](#camera) set high, such as [from_above](#from_above).

entries.name: looking_up
entries.description: A gaze angled upward relative to the character's body, decided first by the eyes and then by the [neck](#neck). A head tipped right [back](#back) also takes [facing_up](#facing_up).

entries.name: eye_contact
entries.description: Two characters looking straight into each other's eyes. Simply facing one another, glancing away or looking at the viewer does not count. Contact lenses are an unrelated thing.

entries.name: looking_ahead
entries.description: A character looking straight in front of themselves, judged by their own body rather than by the [camera](#camera). If the gaze meets the viewer it is [looking_at_viewer](#looking_at_viewer) instead.

entries.name: sideways_glance
entries.description: Eyes looking out of their corners toward the side or over the shoulder while the head faces elsewhere. Occasionally aimed at the viewer; the giveaway is the pupils [sitting](#sitting) at the edge of the eye.

entries.name: looking_afar
entries.description: A character gazing off into the distance rather than at anything close by. It [can](#can) be combined with [looking_ahead](#looking_ahead) where that far gaze runs straight forward.

entries.name: averting_eyes
entries.description: The gaze is pulled deliberately away from the viewer or from the other person present, out of shyness, embarrassment, [sulking](#sulking) or [plain](#plain) annoyance. Combine it with whichever direction [tag](#tag) says where the eyes went instead.

entries.name: avoiding_eye_contact
entries.description: One character keeps their eyes off another's, glancing aside or down while the other looks straight at them. The refusal to meet the gaze is the whole point.

entries.name: looking_at_object
entries.description: A character clearly looking at some inanimate thing that is visible in the picture. Merely facing its direction does not count, and finer tags [cover](#cover) [reading](#reading), phones, screens, maps and watches.

entries.name: looking_at_animal
entries.description: A character's gaze fixed on an [animal](#animal) or an insect. The [creature](#creature) has to be visible in the frame and the look plainly aimed at it.

entries.name: staring
entries.description: A long, fixed, unblinking look at someone or something, the じ～ (jiii) of Japanese comics. Tag beside the direction of the gaze.

entries.name: looking_at_phone
entries.description: A character looking at a phone's [screen](#screen), most often while [holding](#holding) it. Add [holding_phone](#holding_phone) where that applies.

entries.name: looking_over_eyewear
entries.description: Peering over the top of [glasses](#glasses) or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) that sit low on the [nose](#nose) or are pulled down by hand. The result reads as sceptical, appraising or flirtatious.

entries.name: peeking
entries.description: A character watches something or someone while trying not to be spotted, spying from [cover](#cover) or through a gap. Where they lean out from behind an object, [peeking_out](#peeking_out) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: looking_at_mirror
entries.description: A character [studying](#studying) their own [reflection](#reflection) in a [mirror](#mirror), while making up, [brushing](#brushing) their [teeth](#teeth), fixing their hair or simply taking themselves in. Add reflection where the mirrored image is drawn.

entries.name: looking_at_breasts
entries.description: A character's eyes plainly settled on someone's [breasts](#breasts) or flat chest. Leave it off where the gaze cannot be read, or where a chest merely happens to be in front of them.

entries.name: looking_at_food
entries.description: A character gazing at [food](#food), whether hungrily, doubtfully or in dismay. The food should be visible, and once they start on it add [eating](#eating).

entries.name: looking_outside
entries.description: A character gazing out of a room, vehicle or other enclosed [space](#space), usually through a [window](#window). The reverse case is [looking_inside](#looking_inside).

entries.name: looking_at_hand
entries.description: A character looking at a single hand, usually their own, as when [studying](#studying) a [ring](#ring), a wound or something [resting](#resting) in the palm. Both hands together take [looking_at_hands](#looking_at_hands).

entries.name: downturned_eyes
entries.description: The eyes look downward without the head tipping to follow, the opposite of [upturned_eyes](#upturned_eyes). Glancing [sideways](#sideways) is [sideways_glance](#sideways_glance), and permanently sloping lids are [tareme](#tareme).

entries.name: looking_at_self
entries.description: A character regarding their own body or [reflection](#reflection), as when [dressing](#dressing), checking an outfit or [standing](#standing) at a [mirror](#mirror). Hands alone and mirrors have narrower tags, and a second version of the same character counts as [looking_at_another](#looking_at_another).

entries.name: looking_at_flowers
entries.description: The eyes rest on blossoms nearby, held in the hand, [standing](#standing) in a [vase](#vase) or spread across a [field](#field). The flowers have to be in frame for the gaze to be readable.

entries.name: looking_at_creature
entries.description: Somebody [watching](#watching) an [animal](#animal) or a fantastical beast that shares the frame, from a [house](#house) [cat](#cat) to a summoned [monster](#monster). The [creature](#creature) must be visible in the picture.

entries.name: looking_at_screen
entries.description: The gaze rests on a [display](#display) of some kind, from a handheld console to a [monitor](#monitor) or a [television](#television). It is about the eyes, not about the [device](#device).

entries.name: looking_at_ass
entries.description: One character's eyes are on another's backside, often without its owner noticing. It need not be bare; what matters is where the attention goes.

entries.name: looking_at_hands
entries.description: Eyes turned down to one's own hands, as when examining an [injury](#injury), new [gloves](#gloves) or something newly noticed about oneself. A broader self-inspection is [looking_at_self](#looking_at_self).

entries.name: looking_at_reflection
entries.description: Somebody [studying](#studying) their own image in a [mirror](#mirror), a [window](#window) or still [water](#water), with both the [figure](#figure) and the [reflection](#reflection) drawn. Where the surface is specifically a mirror, [looking_at_mirror](#looking_at_mirror) is the finer [tag](#tag).

entries.name: looking_through_scope
entries.description: One eye is pressed to an optic while the other is generally screwed shut. The [instrument](#instrument) may be a [rifle](#rifle) [scope](#scope), a [telescope](#telescope), a [spyglass](#spyglass) or a pair of [binoculars](#binoculars).

entries.name: looking_past_viewer
entries.description: The eyes aim slightly off the [camera](#camera), at something behind or beside whoever is looking. It reads as distraction or alarm rather than direct eye contact.

entries.name: glance
entries.description: Eyes flicked briefly to the side or towards something without the head [following](#following). Reads as a quick, half-committed look rather than a steady stare.

entries.name: looking_inside
entries.description: Standing outside, a character peers into a [building](#building), vehicle or other enclosed [space](#space), frequently through a pane of [glass](#glass). The reverse case is [looking_outside](#looking_outside).

entries.name: looking_at_pectorals
entries.description: The gaze settles on a [muscular](#muscular) male chest, the character's own or somebody else's. Looks aimed at [breasts](#breasts) carry their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: stare_down
entries.description: Two or more characters [lock](#lock) eyes in open hostility, neither willing to look away. A face-off before a fight or a quarrel.

entries.name: downcast_eyes
entries.description: The gaze drops toward the [floor](#floor) while the head stays roughly level. Suggests sadness, shame, shyness or quiet thought.

entries.name: looking_at_watch
entries.description: The eyes drop to a [wristwatch](#wristwatch) or [pocket](#pocket) [watch](#watch) to check the time, usually with an impatient or hurried air. The timepiece needs to be visible in the frame.

entries.name: looking_around
entries.description: The head swings from side to side as somebody scans their surroundings, on [guard](#guard) or checking what lies either way. Since a still picture cannot show the turning, artists add afterimages or motion lines to say so.

entries.name: closed_mouth
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) are held together with nothing of the mouth's [interior](#interior) showing. The opposite of [open_mouth](#open_mouth), and it still applies to a closed-lip [smile](#smile) or a [pout](#pout).

A closed mouth shaped like a three [lying](#lying) on its side, read as a cat's mouth and used for cuteness, innocence or mischief. Puckered [lips](#lips) are [o3o](#o3o), and the downturned version is [3:](#3:).

entries.name: frown
entries.description: The corners of the mouth pulled downward, [reading](#reading) as displeasure, disapproval, annoyance or [plain](#plain) unhappiness. It often travels with [furrowed_brow](#furrowed_brow) or a hard stare.

entries.name: wavy_mouth
entries.description: A mouth drawn as a squiggly line, showing fear, [distress](#distress) or embarrassment. Not to be mistaken for the cat-like [:3](#:3) mouth shape.

entries.name: light_smile
entries.description: A faint, gentle, usually closed-mouth [smile](#smile) in the manner of the Mona Lisa. It is kept apart from smile, which covers clearer and broader [expressions](#expressions).

entries.name: soft_smile
entries.description: A gentle, closed-mouth [smile](#smile) with relaxed eyes, [reading](#reading) as warmth rather than outright delight. Quieter than a [grin](#grin), and often paired with a calm or [affectionate](#affectionate) mood.

The mouth forms an upward-pointing chevron, [triangle](#triangle) or [teardrop](#teardrop), an inverted V of small pouting displeasure. It applies whether the whole mouth or only the upper lip takes that shape.

entries.name: :t
entries.description: A [pout](#pout) with one cheek puffed out, so the [lips](#lips) take a T shape. It reads as jealousy, indignation or boredom, and also serves for a character [chewing](#chewing) with a full mouth.

entries.name: pout
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) are pushed out or drawn to one side in a sulky expression of displeasure. Often paired with puffed cheeks, a [frown](#frown) or looking_away.

entries.name: covered_mouth
entries.description: A character's mouth is hidden behind a [scarf](#scarf), [mask](#mask), high [collar](#collar), held object or a hand. The covering need not touch the face, only block the mouth; doing it deliberately with one's own hands is [covering_own_mouth](#covering_own_mouth).

entries.name: split_mouth
entries.description: A stylized mouth drawn with a gap in the line so the stroke doesn't fully connect, most often on a closed mouth though open mouths [can](#can) use it too.

entries.name: evil_smile
entries.description: A scheming, [sinister](#sinister) [smile](#smile) that gives away bad intentions. Once the [teeth](#teeth) come into view it is also an [evil_grin](#evil_grin).
A small closed [smile](#smile) with one [corner](#corner) drawn to a point, matching the :> [emoticon](#emoticon). It usually comes across as cheeky or quietly pleased with itself.

entries.name: light_frown
entries.description: A slight downward set of the mouth, a mild or gentle displeasure. A pronounced one is [frown](#frown).
The mouth is a single slanted line, the shape of the :/ [emoticon](#emoticon). It carries doubt, ambivalence or mild distaste; the more distressed relative is [wavy_mouth](#wavy_mouth).

The mouth is a flat horizontal line, [giving](#giving) a blank, [unamused](#unamused) or quietly [unhappy](#unhappy) face. It implies [closed_mouth](#closed_mouth), and a line drawn at a slant is [:/](#:/) instead.

The cat-like [sideways](#sideways) three of the mouth, but pulled down at the corners into a [frown](#frown). It reads as [sulking](#sulking) or [plain](#plain) displeasure, where the contented version is [:3](#:3).

entries.name: sideways_mouth
entries.description: A drawing [convention](#convention) where a face shown in [profile](#profile) has its mouth placed on the cheek instead of the front, so the expression stays visible from that angle. The [lips](#lips) may still be sketched on the front too, [giving](#giving) a two-mouth look.

entries.name: evil_grin
entries.description: A menacing [grin](#grin) with the [teeth](#teeth) showing, promising something cruel or sadistic. If the mouth stays closed it is [evil_smile](#evil_smile) alone.

entries.name: dot_mouth
entries.description: A mouth reduced to a single small dot below the [nose](#nose), the most minimal way of drawing it shut. Common on [chibi](#chibi) and heavily simplified faces.

entries.name: puckered_lips
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) drawn pulled in and pushed forward into a kissing shape, often offered toward someone or straight at the viewer. A tight, disapproving press of the lips is [pursed_lips](#pursed_lips) instead.

entries.name: crazy_smile
entries.description: A [smile](#smile) that comes from depravity rather than happiness, its corners drawn up into sharp points, either a wide open [grin](#grin) or an extreme [smirk](#smirk), often over a shaded face. Typical of sadistic, unhinged or obsessive characters, and close kin to [evil_smile](#evil_smile).

entries.name: false_smile
entries.description: A [smile](#smile) that the situation, the dialogue or the body language exposes as insincere, covering shock, tension or held-back anger. Not for evil grins, hysterical laughter or a [yandere](#yandere) stare.

entries.name: o3o
entries.description: Lips pushed forward into a small loose pucker, the mouth the o3o [emoticon](#emoticon) stands for, generally played as a [comic](#comic) face fault. A cat-shaped mouth is [:3](#:3) instead.

entries.name: :x
entries.description: The mouth is a small [cross](#cross), either the [stitched](#stitched) seam on a plush [toy](#toy), rabbits especially, or a person keeping their [lips](#lips) firmly shut.

entries.name: c:
entries.description: A tight closed-lipped [smile](#smile) drawn as a small half-circle that curls in at the corners. It usually reads as [smug](#smug) or quietly pleased with itself.

entries.name: pursed_lips
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) are pressed firmly together into a thin line, usually signalling disapproval, restraint, or concentration. The forward-pushed kissing shape instead is [puckered_lips](#puckered_lips).

entries.name: holding_breath
entries.description: Underwater, the [lips](#lips) are pressed shut and the cheeks puffed as the character keeps their air in. It is meant for [people](#people) who need to breathe rather than mermaids and other water-dwellers, and it also turns up in [asphyxiation](#asphyxiation) and [ryona](#ryona) scenes.

entries.name: x3
entries.description: Squeezed-shut greater-than-less-than eyes paired with a cat-like [:3](#:3) mouth, an [emoticon](#emoticon) face for stifled laughter or delight at something cute. Tag :3 and the eye emoticon alongside it.

entries.name: forced_smile
entries.description: A [smile](#smile) that is not meant, either strained and [unhappy](#unhappy) or pushed physically into shape by somebody else's fingers. Tension around the eyes usually gives it away.

entries.name: :c
entries.description: The mouth curves into a broad C-shaped [frown](#frown). It reads as [sulking](#sulking), disappointment or a small [pout](#pout) rather than open weeping.

entries.name: :s
entries.description: The mouth wavers into an S shape, halfway between a [smile](#smile) and a [grimace](#grimace). It suits unease, doubt or a strained attempt at politeness.

entries.name: diamond_mouth
entries.description: The mouth drawn as a four-cornered rhombus, upper lip peaked and lower lip dipping to match. A stylised cartoon [reading](#reading) of dismay or surprise.

entries.name: crazy_grin
entries.description: A wide unhinged [smile](#smile) with the [teeth](#teeth) bared and the eyes open too far. It reads as madness rather than as joy.

entries.name: humming
entries.description: A tune is sung with the [lips](#lips) closed, drawn as a shut mouth with musical [notes](#notes) [floating](#floating) beside the head. Without the notes it simply reads as [closed_mouth](#closed_mouth).

entries.name: uwu
entries.description: A face made of two downward-curving closed eyes above a cat-like mouth. Reads as contentment, drowsiness, affection or smugness depending on the surrounding scene.

entries.name: heart-shaped_mouth
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) are drawn as a [heart](#heart) [outline](#outline), a stylised [sign](#sign) of adoration or excitement. Nothing anatomical is meant by it.
Eyes screwed shut into sharp angles above a mouth puckered into a three. It suits strain, cute frustration or an exaggerated kissing face.

entries.name: open_mouth
entries.description: The mouth is parted far enough that the inside could be seen. Only slightly separated [lips](#lips) are [parted_lips](#parted_lips), and the opposite state is [closed_mouth](#closed_mouth).

entries.name: :d
entries.description: A wide open-mouthed [smile](#smile) or [grin](#grin), the [emoticon](#emoticon) spelled in lower case for technical reasons. Add a wink and it becomes [;d](#;d), while a lowercase tongue-out shape is [:q](#:q) or [licking_lips](#licking_lips).

entries.name: parted_lips
entries.description: The mouth is only slightly open, the [lips](#lips) separated by a small gap, with or without [teeth](#teeth) showing. Softer than [open_mouth](#open_mouth) and distinct from [closed_mouth](#closed_mouth); often paired with [half-closed_eyes](#half-closed_eyes).

entries.name: :o
entries.description: A round open mouth at any size, the small [circle](#circle) of mild surprise. Add [parted_lips](#parted_lips) or [open_mouth](#open_mouth) alongside it depending on how far the mouth is opened.

entries.name: moaning
entries.description: Someone voicing a long low [sound](#sound) of pleasure or of [pain](#pain). It shows through the open mouth and the expression, through written sound effects beside the head, or audibly in [animated](#animated) work.

entries.name: talking
entries.description: A character shown speaking, indicated by an open mouth, gesturing hands or a speech [bubble](#bubble), in conversation or addressing someone.

entries.name: triangle_mouth
entries.description: An open mouth drawn as a simple [triangle](#triangle), often used for a shout or a startled yell. If the top comes to a point while the bottom stays rounded, that shape is [chestnut_mouth](#chestnut_mouth) instead.

entries.name: chestnut_mouth
entries.description: An open mouth drawn in the [outline](#outline) of a [chestnut](#chestnut), pointed at one end and rounded at the other, often with a row of round upper [teeth](#teeth). It sits close to a rounded [triangle](#triangle) mouth.

entries.name: shouting
entries.description: Yelling with a loud voice and the mouth wide open, whether in anger, excitement or simply to be heard at a distance. Two characters shouting at each other may also be [arguing](#arguing); [screaming](#screaming) is the more extreme form.

entries.name: yawning
entries.description: Mouth stretched wide in a yawn, eyes half or fully shut, sometimes with a tear at the [corner](#corner). Signals sleepiness or boredom and often accompanies [stretching](#stretching).

entries.name: d:
entries.description: A wide open mouth pulled down at the corners, the face of dismay or horror that the [emoticon](#emoticon) draws. It is written in lower case only because the [tag](#tag) cannot hold a capital.

entries.name: xd
entries.description: Tightly shut greater-than-less-than eyes with a wide-open grinning mouth, the [emoticon](#emoticon) face for a character who is [laughing](#laughing) or overjoyed. Tag the eye emoticon and the open-mouth [grin](#grin) alongside it.

entries.name: screaming
entries.description: A character yelling at full volume, whether from terror, [pain](#pain), rage, or the peak of [sex](#sex). A loud but composed shout is tagged [shouting](#shouting) instead.

entries.name: :i
entries.description: A closed mouth drawn as a horizontal bar with a short upright stroke at either end. It shows [breath](#breath) being held or [lips](#lips) pressed tight; [:t](#:t) is the related shape with a puffed cheek.

entries.name: cursing
entries.description: The character is swearing, whether the words are spelled out or replaced by a run of symbols. Usually paired with an [angry](#angry) or exasperated face.

entries.name: whispering
entries.description: One character speaks softly into another's ear, often with a hand cupped beside the mouth, to keep what's said private.

entries.name: rectangular_mouth
entries.description: The open mouth is drawn as a [box](#box) shape, [comic](#comic) shorthand for [shouting](#shouting), shock, or [deadpan](#deadpan) disbelief. Combine with [open_mouth](#open_mouth).

entries.name: >o<
entries.description: Eyes clenched into angled slashes above a round open mouth, as in a squeal or a yelp of [pain](#pain). It joins the [>_<](#>_<) eyes to the [:o](#:o) mouth.

entries.name: white_mouth
entries.description: The inside of an open mouth is filled with flat white instead of a drawn [tongue](#tongue) and throat. Distinct from visible [teeth](#teeth) and from the simplified notch [shapes](#shapes) artists use to suggest a [grin](#grin).

entries.name: blowing
entries.description: Air [forced](#forced) out through pursed [lips](#lips), to cool [food](#food), snuff a [candle](#candle), scatter [dandelion](#dandelion) seeds, inflate something or [sound](#sound) an [instrument](#instrument). Puffed cheeks usually give it away; reach for [blowing_bubbles](#blowing_bubbles) or [blowing_kiss](#blowing_kiss) where one of those fits.

entries.name: peanut_mouth
entries.description: A mouth drawn wider at its corners than in the middle, pinched at the centre so the [opening](#opening) reads as two lobes. A cartoon shape used for surprise or dopey pleasure.

entries.name: blowing_smoke
entries.description: Smoke pushed out from the mouth, exhaled by a smoker or blown away from another source such as a [gun](#gun) [barrel](#barrel). The visible [plume](#plume) is what the [tag](#tag) is about.

entries.name: roaring
entries.description: A character or beast [throwing](#throwing) its head up and letting out a loud [growling](#growling) bellow, mouth wide and [teeth](#teeth) bared. Usually meant as a [threat](#threat) or a [display](#display) of rage.

entries.name: whistling
entries.description: The [lips](#lips) are pursed into a tight [circle](#circle) and air is blown out to produce a tone, sometimes with musical [notes](#notes) [floating](#floating) nearby. Describes the mouth shape and act, not a [whistle](#whistle) held in the [teeth](#teeth).

entries.name: black_mouth
entries.description: The inside of the mouth drawn pitch black instead of pink, leaving the face hollow and uncanny. Used for horror scenes and for the unhinged grins of unstable characters.

entries.name: d;
entries.description: The same [gaping](#gaping) downturned mouth as [d:](#d:), with one eye squeezed shut alongside it. Reads as a pained [wince](#wince) or a wail of dismay.

entries.name: dx
entries.description: The [emoticon](#emoticon) face made of screwed-shut [>_<](#>_<) eyes over the wide [unhappy](#unhappy) mouth of D:. Reads as [pain](#pain), revulsion or dismay, and is not the delighted XD.

entries.name: jaw_drop
entries.description: The mouth gapes far wider than a [plain](#plain) [open_mouth](#open_mouth), the lower [jaw](#jaw) [hanging](#hanging) loose in shock or disbelief. Wide [staring](#staring) eyes generally come with it.

entries.name: blowing_whistle
entries.description: A [whistle](#whistle) held at or in the mouth and sounded, cheeks often puffed with the effort. Referees, coaches, [police](#police) and [train](#train) guards account for most of it.

entries.name: gasp
entries.description: A sharp intake of [breath](#breath), drawn as the mouth suddenly [opening](#opening) while the eyes widen. Marks surprise, alarm or a realisation arriving.

entries.name: howling
entries.description: A long drawn-out cry given with the head or muzzle raised, the way wolves, dogs and coyotes call. Musical [notes](#notes) or [sound](#sound) effects often mark it.

entries.name: barking
entries.description: A [dog](#dog), [wolf](#wolf) or other canine opens its mouth to bark, often with the [sound](#sound) drawn in beside it. It also covers a person barking in imitation.

entries.name: muffled
entries.description: A voice stifled at its source — a hand clamped over the mouth, a [gag](#gag), or a face pressed into [cloth](#cloth) — so that whatever is said comes out indistinct. Speech drawn for it is often wobbling or half-formed.

entries.name: meowing
entries.description: A character letting out a cat's cry, mouth open mid-meow. Fits actual cats, [cat](#cat) girls and [people](#people) playfully [imitating](#imitating) one.

entries.name: hollow_mouth
entries.description: The open mouth gives onto a [space](#space) far deeper than any real one, with [no](#no) [tongue](#tongue), palate or throat drawn inside. Teeth are usually absent too, which makes it read as uncanny rather than anatomical.

entries.name: inhaling
entries.description: Air being drawn in: a deep [breath](#breath) before speaking, a sniff at something scented, or a cartoon suction [dragging](#dragging) objects toward an open mouth. The intake itself is what is shown.

entries.name: shouting_with_hands
entries.description: One or both hands cupped around the mouth to carry the voice further, showing a character [calling](#calling) out to someone at a distance rather than speaking normally.

entries.name: hissing
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) or similar [creature](#creature) bares its [teeth](#teeth) and hisses, mouth wide and ears flattened, warning off whatever it has met. The fur is often drawn puffed up as [well](#well).

entries.name: tongue_out
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) extends beyond the [lips](#lips), lolling out or poked out as part of an expression. Licking something gets its own [licking](#licking) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: clenched_teeth
entries.description: Teeth pressed hard together and visible, from strain, anger, [pain](#pain) or grim resolve. The [lips](#lips) may be drawn [back](#back) or the mouth left open around them.

entries.name: drooling
entries.description: Saliva escaping the mouth, brought on by sleep, hunger, arousal or a daze. Where the drool is only suggested by a dent in the lower lip with [no](#no) [liquid](#liquid) drawn, that is [mouth_drool](#mouth_drool) rather than [saliva](#saliva).

entries.name: licking
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) touches an object, a person or a body part. Add the specific [target](#target) where one exists, such as [licking_finger](#licking_finger), [licking_another's_face](#licking_another's_face) or [licking_penis](#licking_penis), along with [tongue_out](#tongue_out).

entries.name: :p
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) pokes downward out of an otherwise closed mouth, a playful or [teasing](#teasing) face. With a wink it becomes [;p](#;p), and a tongue [running](#running) along the upper lip is [:q](#:q).

entries.name: :q
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) sweeps along the upper lip, a licking-lips face for anticipating something tasty or for [teasing](#teasing). Add a wink and it is [;q](#;q); a tongue [hanging](#hanging) downward is [:p](#:p).

entries.name: licking_lips
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) is drawn across one's own [lips](#lips), signalling appetite or anticipation for something about to be enjoyed, [food](#food) or otherwise. Licking someone else's lips is [licking_another's_lips](#licking_another's_lips).

entries.name: biting
entries.description: Teeth clamped on something, [piercing](#piercing) it or simply [holding](#holding) it: [food](#food), a glove, a finger, another character's ear or [tail](#tail), or one's own lip. Reach for the narrower [tag](#tag) where one exists, and use [bite_mark](#bite_mark) for the imprint afterwards.

entries.name: lower_teeth_only
entries.description: An open mouth drawn showing only the bottom row of [teeth](#teeth), the upper row left out. It turns up often in [laughing](#laughing) and [shouting](#shouting) faces seen from slightly above.

entries.name: mouth_drool
entries.description: Drooling shown as a dip or a [bulge](#bulge) in the [outline](#outline) of the mouth rather than as visible [saliva](#saliva) [running](#running) down the chin. The line of the [lips](#lips) does all the work.

entries.name: biting_own_lip
entries.description: A character [biting](#biting) their own lip, out of anxiety, suppressed pleasure, frustration or an effort to stay quiet. Biting someone else's lip during a [kiss](#kiss) belongs with the interaction tags.

entries.name: heart_in_mouth
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) is drawn inside an open mouth, generally [standing](#standing) in for the [tongue](#tongue). It usually comes with a wide [grin](#grin) and a playful or besotted mood.

entries.name: licking_finger
entries.description: A character licks a finger, their own or someone else's, whether [cleaning](#cleaning) off [food](#food) or making a suggestive [gesture](#gesture). Add [tongue_out](#tongue_out) where the [tongue](#tongue) is visible.

entries.name: uvula
entries.description: The small fleshy flap [hanging](#hanging) at the [back](#back) of the throat is drawn visible, which needs a mouth opened wide. Typically shows up in [screaming](#screaming), [yawning](#yawning), [singing](#singing) or [close-up](#close-up) [deepthroat](#deepthroat) scenes.

entries.name: spitting
entries.description: Saliva or phlegm [forced](#forced) out of the mouth, whether spat deliberately or sprayed out while [eating](#eating) or [drinking](#drinking).

entries.name: licking_another's_face
entries.description: One character runs their [tongue](#tongue) over another's face. Where the lick lands on the cheek or the [lips](#lips), the narrower [licking_another's_cheek](#licking_another's_cheek) and [licking_another's_lips](#licking_another's_lips) apply.

entries.name: biting_ear
entries.description: One character [nibbling](#nibbling) or [biting](#biting) another's ear, usually playfully or affectionately rather than to hurt. Add the pairing tags for the two involved.

entries.name: biting_glove
entries.description: A glove tugged with the [teeth](#teeth) to pull it on or off without using the other hand, a favourite dramatic [gesture](#gesture). Once the glove is already off and merely held in the mouth, [glove_in_mouth](#glove_in_mouth) takes over.

entries.name: licking_ear
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) makes contact with another character's ear, generally shown as [teasing](#teasing) or intimacy. Human and [animal](#animal) ears both count.

entries.name: licking_another's_neck
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) is drawn along the side or front of another character's [neck](#neck), usually as an intimate or predatory [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: finger_sucking
entries.description: A finger is drawn between the [lips](#lips) and sucked, either the character's own or somebody else's. Depending on the scene it reads as childish, absent-minded or suggestive.

entries.name: biting_neck
entries.description: Teeth set into another character's [neck](#neck). Vampires aside, it works as a possessive or intimate [gesture](#gesture) within an embrace.

entries.name: biting_own_finger
entries.description: A character with their own finger between their [teeth](#teeth), [reading](#reading) as nerves, longing or thought. Working on the nail itself is [nail_biting](#nail_biting).

entries.name: biting_finger
entries.description: A finger held between the [teeth](#teeth) without the picture saying whose it is. Prefer [biting_own_finger](#biting_own_finger) or [biting_another's_finger](#biting_another's_finger) wherever that [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: licking_another's_cheek
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) is drawn across somebody else's cheek. Depending on the scene it reads as affection, [teasing](#teasing) or something predatory.

entries.name: biting_clothes
entries.description: Fabric gripped between the [teeth](#teeth), such as a hem, a sleeve or a [strap](#strap), often while the hands are busy or as a suggestive [gesture](#gesture). Related to the broader [clothes_in_mouth](#clothes_in_mouth).

entries.name: licking_hand
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) touches the palm or [back](#back) of a hand rather than the fingers, one's own hand or another person's.

entries.name: biting_cheek
entries.description: Teeth closed gently on another character's cheek, generally as [teasing](#teasing) affection rather than an [attack](#attack). The jaws barely shut, so nothing is [broken](#broken).

entries.name: biting_head
entries.description: Jaws closed over another character's head, gnawing rather than [swallowing](#swallowing). Usually [comic](#comic), and distinct from [vore](#vore), where the victim actually goes down.

entries.name: finger_to_tongue
entries.description: A fingertip meets the extended [tongue](#tongue) with the mouth open around it, the finger never taken in. It sits next to [licking](#licking) a finger and to [finger_sucking](#finger_sucking).

entries.name: tehepero
entries.description: A cheeky apology face: [tongue](#tongue) out, one eye winked shut, and either a hand raised behind the head or a V-sign held to the cheek. It brushes off a blunder; tapping the head instead is [dojikko_pose](#dojikko_pose).

entries.name: licking_weapon
entries.description: A character runs their [tongue](#tongue) along a [weapon](#weapon), a blade, a [gun](#gun) [barrel](#barrel) or a [spear](#spear) point, as a [threat](#threat) or out of relish.

entries.name: biting_own_thumb
entries.description: The thumb pressed between the [teeth](#teeth), usually out of anxiety, frustration or [envy](#envy). When the teeth are [working](#working) the nail, [nail_biting](#nail_biting) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: biting_another's_finger
entries.description: Someone taking another character's finger between their [teeth](#teeth), lightly or hard. Not to be [confused](#confused) with [biting_own_finger](#biting_own_finger), which is a [habit](#habit) turned on oneself.

entries.name: biting_another's_tail
entries.description: One character [holding](#holding) another's [tail](#tail) in their mouth, usually in play or to keep them from [walking](#walking) off. For a character on their own tail, [biting_own_tail](#biting_own_tail) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: licking_navel
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) is applied to another character's [navel](#navel), with the licker bent low over the [stomach](#stomach).

entries.name: ^q^
entries.description: Happily closed caret eyes above a q-shaped mouth trailing drool. The face lands as blissful, dopey or lecherous delight.

entries.name: biting_another's_hand
entries.description: Teeth closed on somebody else's hand, whether in play, in defiance or in earnest to make them let go. The reaction of whoever is bitten usually settles which.

entries.name: licking_blade
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) is run along the flat or edge of a [knife](#knife) or [sword](#sword), a showy [gesture](#gesture) that usually reads as a [threat](#threat).

entries.name: biting_hair
entries.description: A strand of hair held in the mouth, the character's own or somebody else's, usually playfully or invitingly. Nothing is swallowed, which separates it from [eating_hair](#eating_hair).

entries.name: licking_stomach
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) is dragged across the [belly](#belly), generally another character's.

entries.name: nibbling
entries.description: Teeth work gently at something that is not [food](#food), such as a finger, a [pen](#pen), an ear or a cuff. There is [no](#no) attempt to bite through, only to worry at it.

entries.name: biting_own_tail
entries.description: A character [holding](#holding) their own [tail](#tail) in their mouth, [chewing](#chewing) it or simply gripping it. It reads as nerves, boredom or animal-like play.

entries.name: nail_biting
entries.description: Teeth [working](#working) at one's own [fingernails](#fingernails), a [habit](#habit) of nerves or [envy](#envy). Where the whole thumb is in the mouth rather than the nail, [biting](#biting) own thumb fits better.

entries.name: biting_shoulder
entries.description: Teeth set into somebody's shoulder, during a struggle, within an embrace, or to keep from [crying](#crying) out. Who is [biting](#biting) whom is left to the other tags.

entries.name: licking_leg
entries.description: A [tongue](#tongue) is drawn along another character's thigh, calf or shin.

entries.name: biting_arm
entries.description: Teeth sunk into an arm, either an opponent's during a struggle or the character's own to stifle a [sound](#sound). The surrounding scene decides which it is.

entries.name: biting_tongue
entries.description: The [tongue](#tongue) [caught](#caught) between the [teeth](#teeth), sometimes as a small painful [accident](#accident), sometimes as a playful or [concentrating](#concentrating) face.

entries.name: pill_on_tongue
entries.description: A tablet or capsule [resting](#resting) on an extended [tongue](#tongue), about to be swallowed or simply displayed. The open mouth and the [pill](#pill) together make the shot.

entries.name: licking_another's_lips
entries.description: One character licks another's [lips](#lips), normally at kissing distance with the faces almost touching.

entries.name: string_in_mouth
entries.description: A cord or [thread](#thread) gripped between the [teeth](#teeth), often while both hands are busy [tying](#tying) hair, lacing something or [wrapping](#wrapping) a parcel.

entries.name: blush
entries.description: Reddened cheeks or a flushed face, from embarrassment, heat, [drink](#drink) or arousal, drawn as a tint, as [hatching](#hatching) or as bold stripes. It covers the face alone; redness elsewhere on the body is [body_blush](#body_blush).

entries.name: tears
entries.description: Liquid runs from the eyes, whether from sorrow, [pain](#pain), laughter or joy. A purely comedic drawn tear belongs under [teardrop](#teardrop) instead.

entries.name: sweatdrop
entries.description: One oversized drop beside the head, the [comic](#comic) shorthand for nervousness or awkwardness. A normal-sized single drop is [small_sweatdrop](#small_sweatdrop); several drops together are [plain](#plain) [sweat](#sweat).

entries.name: nose_blush
entries.description: The [blush](#blush) spreads across the [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose) rather than [sitting](#sitting) on the cheeks alone. It reads as a stronger, more [flustered](#flustered) flush than a [plain](#plain) one.

entries.name: blush_stickers
entries.description: Blush drawn as flat ovals or circles pasted onto the cheeks, often outlined, instead of a soft gradient. Chibi, small children and [comic](#comic) reactions carry them, and the skin underneath need not be reddened at all.

entries.name: crying
entries.description: Tears [running](#running) from a character's eyes, usually out of sadness, [pain](#pain) or feeling overwhelmed. Add [crying_with_eyes_open](#crying_with_eyes_open) when the eyes stay open, and [tears](#tears) for the drops themselves.

entries.name: trembling
entries.description: The character shakes from [cold](#cold), fear, excitement or strain, typically drawn with small wavy lines along the body's [outline](#outline). Sharper, jagged lines instead mean [twitching](#twitching), a briefer and more violent motion.

entries.name: light_blush
entries.description: A faint reddening of the cheeks, visible but understated. A stronger flush takes [blush](#blush) or [full-face_blush](#full-face_blush).

entries.name: tearing_up
entries.description: Moisture wells up in the eyes just before [crying](#crying), with [no](#no) tear yet rolled down the cheek. A ripped garment or sheet of [paper](#paper) is a separate matter, covered by [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes) or [ripping](#ripping).

entries.name: heavy_breathing
entries.description: A character [pants](#pants) hard, mouth open, often with [sweat](#sweat) and [breath](#breath) marks drawn in. Exertion and arousal alike qualify; the [tag](#tag) says nothing about which.

entries.name: crying_with_eyes_open
entries.description: Tears [falling](#falling) from eyes that stay open instead of [squeezing](#squeezing) shut, which reads as shock, [despair](#despair) or fear. A narrower case of [crying](#crying).

entries.name: full-face_blush
entries.description: Blush spread across the entire face, [reaching](#reaching) up to the [forehead](#forehead) and down past the mouth instead of [sitting](#sitting) on the cheeks alone. Redness reaching only inward to the [nose](#nose) is [nose_blush](#nose_blush), and outward to the ears is [ear_blush](#ear_blush).

entries.name: nervous_sweating
entries.description: Large [beads](#beads) of [sweat](#sweat) brought on by fright, embarrassment or acute unease. Sweat from heat, effort or [sex](#sex) is [plain](#plain) sweat or [very_sweaty](#very_sweaty).

entries.name: nosebleed
entries.description: Blood runs from the [nose](#nose), either as the [comic](#comic) [sign](#sign) of sudden arousal or as the result of a blow. In the latter case add [injury](#injury).

entries.name: ear_blush
entries.description: The red of a [blush](#blush) has spread past the cheeks and reached the ears, which reads as [strong](#strong) embarrassment or arousal. It always comes with an ordinary blush.

entries.name: streaming_tears
entries.description: Tears drawn as two solid lines [running](#running) down the cheeks, or shooting [sideways](#sideways) away from the face for [comic](#comic) effect. A stronger form of [crying](#crying) than a few drops.

entries.name: teardrop
entries.description: A single stylised tear drawn for [comic](#comic) effect, usually solid in colour and attached right at the eye, much like a [sweatdrop](#sweatdrop). Where a character is genuinely [crying](#crying), or the tear reads as [transparent](#transparent), use [tears](#tears) instead.

entries.name: body_blush
entries.description: Skin reddened somewhere other than the face, across the shoulders, chest, [thighs](#thighs) or [knees](#knees), from heat, [cold](#cold), embarrassment or arousal. A flushed face on its own is simply [blush](#blush).

entries.name: small_sweatdrop
entries.description: A single normal-sized bead of [sweat](#sweat) on the face showing exasperation or surprise. The comically oversized version is [sweatdrop](#sweatdrop).

entries.name: happy_tears
entries.description: A character weeps out of happiness rather than sadness, [pain](#pain) or fear. Tears paired with a [smile](#smile) are the giveaway.

entries.name: shoulder_blush
entries.description: Blush marks drawn on the shoulders rather than the face, a flush [spreading](#spreading) over bare skin there.

entries.name: single_blush_sticker
entries.description: Only one of the round cartoon [blush](#blush) patches is visible on the face. Happens when the head is turned, or the other cheek is hidden behind hair.

entries.name: single_tear
entries.description: One drop [rolling](#rolling) down the cheek, the whole of the [crying](#crying) shown at once. Reads as quiet grief or [restrained](#restrained) feeling, unlike the [comic](#comic) [teardrop](#teardrop) used for jokes.

entries.name: knee_blush
entries.description: A pink flush drawn across a character's [knees](#knees), mirroring the [blush](#blush) on a face. It is a stylistic flourish rather than anything anatomical.

entries.name: hand_blush
entries.description: Pink flush drawn onto the hands themselves rather than the cheeks. It shows up on point-of-view hands and where somebody's colour shows through the fingers [hiding](#hiding) their face, putting embarrassment where a face cannot carry it.

entries.name: breathing
entries.description: The chest visibly rises and falls, tagged where an animation actually draws that motion. Visible white puffs in [cold](#cold) air are [breath](#breath) instead, and laboured panting is [heavy_breathing](#heavy_breathing).

entries.name: excessive_nosebleed
entries.description: A [nosebleed](#nosebleed) erupting as a jet or [fountain](#fountain) rather than a trickle. Comic shorthand for arousal or shock, played for laughs.

entries.name: blush_visible_through_hair
entries.description: The flush on the cheeks shows through hair [falling](#falling) across the face, the strands drawn as if partly [transparent](#transparent). The [blush](#blush) stays legible even though something covers it.

entries.name: trembling_legs
entries.description: Legs drawn with small wavy or jagged lines beside them to show a sustained shake from fear, exhaustion or strain. The [feet](#feet) may move along with the [legs](#legs), but the [shaking](#shaking) itself comes from the leg muscles.

entries.name: t_t
entries.description: A cartoonish [crying](#crying) face where each eye becomes a T shape with a thick [stream](#stream) of [tears](#tears) [pouring](#pouring) down. Reserve it for exaggerated, waterfall-style crying rather than ordinary welling eyes.

entries.name: tears_from_one_eye
entries.description: A single track of [tears](#tears) runs from one eye while the other stays dry, usually above an otherwise blank face. The [convention](#convention) reads as grief held in rather than openly wept.

entries.name: black_tears
entries.description: Tears [running](#running) black down the cheeks, whether from ruined [makeup](#makeup) or as a deliberately unsettling touch. The colour normally signals that something is wrong rather than ordinary weeping.

entries.name: dripping_eye
entries.description: An eye drawn as though it were [melting](#melting) and [sliding](#sliding) down the cheek. A stylised and deliberately unsettling way of rendering [tears](#tears).

entries.name: neck_blush
entries.description: Colour [spreading](#spreading) down over the throat instead of stopping at the cheeks. It reads as [strong](#strong) embarrassment or arousal rather than a mild fluster.

entries.name: glasses_with_tear
entries.description: Spectacles with a tear [caught](#caught) on the frame or [running](#running) down the lens. The eyewear carries the [crying](#crying) rather than the face alone.

entries.name: huffing
entries.description: Air is pushed out or drawn in as one [heavy](#heavy) audible [breath](#breath), from exertion, [sulking](#sulking), or deliberately taking in a scent. A visible puff of breath usually carries it.

entries.name: hair_blush
entries.description: The hair itself tinted pink as a stand-in for a flushed face, used when the cheeks are hidden or turned away. A stylised shorthand rather than real [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: full-body_blush
entries.description: Redness [spreading](#spreading) over the whole body rather than [resting](#resting) on the cheeks, from heat, arousal or acute embarrassment. Stronger than [body_blush](#body_blush), where some skin keeps its ordinary colour.

entries.name: colored_tears
entries.description: Tears drawn in a colour rather than [running](#running) clear. Blood weeping from the eyes and [mascara](#mascara) [washing](#washing) down the cheeks each have their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: flying_sweatdrops
entries.description: Sweat drops drawn flinging off the head or body in defiance of physics, marking panic, embarrassment or strain. A cartoon shorthand rather than [realistic](#realistic) perspiration.

A question mark stands alone in the picture, inside a [balloon](#balloon) or bare beside the head, marking wonder, confusion or curiosity. Several together are [??](#??), and one beside an exclamation mark is [!?](#!?).

entries.name: shaded_face
entries.description: The upper face or eyes darkened with [no](#no) real light source, signalling anger, [disgust](#disgust), shock, or a [sinister](#sinister) mood, sometimes played for comedy. Half the face shaded is [partially_shaded_face](#partially_shaded_face); [shadow](#shadow) from an actual light source is [shade](#shade).

A small [crown](#crown) of pointed marks, usually three, drawn beside the head for sudden realisation, surprise or shock. Do not confuse it with [notice_lines](#notice_lines), which radiate outward like spokes.

entries.name: anger_vein
entries.description: The [comic](#comic) mark of curved lines crossed to suggest a bulging vein, drawn on or [floating](#floating) beside a [forehead](#forehead) or a clenched fist. It stands for anger or irritation, and [can](#can) also sit inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) as something said.

Three or more [dots](#dots) hang beside a character as an ellipsis, [standing](#standing) for a wordless pause, an [awkward](#awkward) silence or simply having nothing to say. When a question mark closes the dots off, the [tag](#tag) becomes [...?](#...?) instead.

A lone exclamation mark floats near a character's head, bare on the panel or inside a [bubble](#bubble), marking a jolt of [comic](#comic) shock. Several stacked together are [!!](#!!), and one set beside a question mark is [!?](#!?).

entries.name: notice_lines
entries.description: Short lines radiate around a character's head to show that something has just [caught](#caught) their attention. They are also placed beside an object to point it out.

An exclamation mark and a question mark set side by side in either order, so the reaction is startled and disbelieving at once. The single interrobang glyph counts too; puzzlement without the shock is [??](#??) instead.

A curling, plus-shaped [scribble](#scribble) beside someone's head [standing](#standing) for laughter, cheerful chatter or the hum of a [crowd](#crowd), often in a scene that is otherwise quiet. The pointed marks of [^^^](#^^^) look similar but mean sudden realisation.

entries.name: squiggle
entries.description: A round [scribble](#scribble) drawn near a character's head to show grumbling, annoyance, embarrassment or frustration. Inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) it is also tagged [spoken_squiggle](#spoken_squiggle).

entries.name: puff_of_air
entries.description: A little cartoon gust drawn beside a character's face to show a huff, a [sigh](#sigh), exhaustion, or [smug](#smug) satisfaction. Not the same as the cat-mouth expression [:3](#:3), though the two get mixed up in [typing](#typing).

Two or more exclamation marks drawn together beside a character, [standing](#standing) for excitement, a sharp shock or a [stab](#stab) of [pain](#pain). Use it for any cluster of them outside a [bubble](#bubble), or inside one when nothing else is written there.

entries.name: zzz
entries.description: The letters drawn beside a [sleeping](#sleeping) or dozing character to represent [snoring](#snoring), usually [floating](#floating) near the head. Pair it with sleeping when the character is genuinely asleep rather than just pretending.

entries.name: squeans
entries.description: A mark beside the head made of dashes or small circles in a [ring](#ring), often with a curved line, showing sleepiness, drunkenness or dizziness. A [nose_bubble](#nose_bubble) is a separate sleep [sign](#sign).
Two, three or more question marks drawn together, a heavier bafflement than a single one. A little surprise [can](#can) ride along with it, though nothing like the jolt of [!?](#!?).

entries.name: sigh
entries.description: A character lets out a [breath](#breath), drawn as a small puff or [cloud](#cloud) beside the face. Can signal relief, weariness or exasperation depending on the scene.

entries.name: nose_bubble
entries.description: The cartoon [snot](#snot) [bubble](#bubble) swelling at the nostril of a [sleeping](#sleeping) or drowsy character, a manga shorthand for being fast asleep. It often turns up beside a [zzz](#zzz).

entries.name: giving_up_the_ghost
entries.description: The [comic](#comic) [gag](#gag) of a character's soul [drifting](#drifting) up out of their body after they are figuratively struck dead. The wispy [spirit](#spirit) is drawn escaping the mouth or hovering just above them.

entries.name: drawn_ears
entries.description: Animal ears added to a character as a doodle laid over the picture rather than as part of the body. Playful marking, often joined by [drawn_whiskers](#drawn_whiskers) or [drawn_tail](#drawn_tail).

Trailing [dots](#dots) closed off by a question mark, a puzzled silence in which the character says nothing while [working](#working) out what is happening. Use [...](#...) for the bare pause and [?](#?) for straightforward confusion.

entries.name: flying_teardrops
entries.description: Tears flung clear of the face and left [hanging](#hanging) in the air as arcs of droplets. A [comic](#comic) [crying](#crying) [convention](#convention) that ignores gravity entirely.

entries.name: happy_aura
entries.description: Radiating strokes drawn in a [ring](#ring) around a character, sometimes [floating](#floating) flowers instead, to show that they are delighted. The face has to [back](#back) it up, most often with a [smile](#smile), and [notice_lines](#notice_lines) may appear alongside.

entries.name: head_steam
entries.description: Steam or [smoke](#smoke) puffs from a character's head, the cartoon [sign](#sign) that embarrassment or temper has boiled over. A body steaming from a [bath](#bath) or real heat is a different thing.

entries.name: scribble
entries.description: A dense knot of looping lines with [no](#no) real shape, drawn beside a character's head to show irritation or a mind gone blank.

entries.name: drawn_wings
entries.description: Wings sketched in behind a character as an overlay instead of growing from the [back](#back). Usually half of a halo-and-wings joke about somebody being angelic.
An ellipsis followed by an exclamation mark, drawn as lettering beside the head rather than spoken as dialogue. It marks a silence that breaks open into surprise or sudden understanding.

entries.name: shout_lines
entries.description: Jagged [spikes](#spikes) drawn radiating from a character's head to signal that they are yelling. Also used when the shout is coming from just outside the panel.

entries.name: mushroom_on_head
entries.description: A [mushroom](#mushroom) sprouting from the top of a character's head. In manga shorthand it marks gloom or [sulking](#sulking), and some games use it for a status ailment.

entries.name: drawn_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) added to somebody as a doodle rather than real [anatomy](#anatomy). Frequently paired with [drawn_ears](#drawn_ears) for a mock [animal](#animal) look.

entries.name: spasm
entries.description: Sharp, spiky lines drawn bursting outward from a character's body or clothing to show a sudden jolt [running](#running) through them. Reads as being startled, thrilled, or hit by a shock.

entries.name: snort
entries.description: A short burst of air pushed sharply out through the [nose](#nose), drawn as one or two puffs beside the [nostrils](#nostrils). It reads as derision, impatience, or a stifled laugh in [people](#people), and as agitation in animals.

entries.name: idea
entries.description: The moment a character works something out, marked by a light bulb switching on above or beside the head. The bulb is what earns the [tag](#tag), not the expression on its own.

entries.name: comedic_sweatdrop
entries.description: A single oversized bead of [sweat](#sweat) drawn beside the head to mark awkwardness or nerves. Several smaller drops instead call for sweat.

entries.name: lightning_glare
entries.description: Two characters stare each other down so hard that [sparks](#sparks) visibly arc between their eyes. A [comic](#comic) shorthand for [rivalry](#rivalry) or open loathing.

entries.name: wink_star
entries.description: A star shoots out of a closed eye as a character winks, usually trailing a motion line that traces its [path](#path). Hearts and other small symbols get used for the same [gag](#gag).

entries.name: drawn_horns
entries.description: Horns sketched in above a head as an overlay instead of growing out of it. Usually a joke about mischief or a devilish streak.

entries.name: drawn_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) scribbled in above somebody's head instead of [sitting](#sitting) on it, understood as imaginary within the picture. A quick way of marking the winner or the favourite.

entries.name: buffering
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of [dots](#dots) or [bars](#bars), shaded or sized in sequence so it reads as a loading spinner, drawn over or beside a character. On a person it stands for a stalled mind: a realisation arriving late, or nothing happening at all.

entries.name: seeing_stars
entries.description: Stars orbiting a character's head to show they are [dazed](#dazed), stunned, or knocked [cold](#cold). Not for someone actually gazing up at a [night](#night) [sky](#sky), which is [starry_sky](#starry_sky) instead.

entries.name: standing
entries.description: A character upright on one or both [feet](#feet), whether standing still or [walking](#walking). Usually fully vertical; combine with [bent_over](#bent_over) or [leaning_forward](#leaning_forward) when the [torso](#torso) tilts away from that.

entries.name: kneeling
entries.description: One or both [knees](#knees) rest on the ground with the backside held off it. It is not [squatting](#squatting), where the knees stay up, nor [all_fours](#all_fours), where the hands are down too, nor [seiza](#seiza), where the sitter rests on their heels.

entries.name: leaning_forward
entries.description: The [torso](#torso) is angled forward a little, often with the hands braced on the [knees](#knees) or [thighs](#thighs), without going far enough to count as [bent_over](#bent_over). It is a standard pose for [presenting](#presenting) [cleavage](#cleavage) or a view down the front.

entries.name: squatting
entries.description: Crouched low with the [knees](#knees) deeply bent and the [weight](#weight) carried on the [feet](#feet) alone, with the knees kept off the ground. Once a knee touches down it becomes [kneeling](#kneeling) instead.

entries.name: bent_over
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) stay more or less upright while the [torso](#torso) folds forward toward horizontal and the rear pushes out. It covers [leaning](#leaning) over a [desk](#desk), picking something up, and [presenting](#presenting) in sexual top-down bottom-up scenes.

entries.name: floating
entries.description: A character hovers or drifts in the air with nothing propelling them, [no](#no) [wings](#wings) and no ground beneath. Bobbing on [water](#water) is [afloat](#afloat) instead.

entries.name: contrapposto
entries.description: Standing with the [weight](#weight) carried on one leg so the hips tilt and one juts out, the relaxed S-curve of classical [sculpture](#sculpture).

entries.name: upside-down
entries.description: The character or scene is inverted, head where the [feet](#feet) would ordinarily be, as when [hanging](#hanging) or [caught](#caught) mid-flip. Simply [lying](#lying) on the [back](#back) with the [legs](#legs) raised is not enough on its own.

entries.name: fighting_stance
entries.description: A ready stance taken facing an opponent, [feet](#feet) [planted](#planted) and hands or [weapon](#weapon) raised to strike or block. The character is braced for a fight rather than in the middle of one.

entries.name: arched_back
entries.description: The [spine](#spine) curved backwards so the chest lifts and the hips push forward, seen in stretches, strain and pin-up [poses](#poses). Leaning the other way instead is [bent_over](#bent_over).

entries.name: leaning_back
entries.description: A [standing](#standing) or seated character bends backwards at the waist, chest lifted. It is the opposite of [leaning_forward](#leaning_forward).
