entries.name: against_wall
entries.description: Leaning on a wall, [pushing](#pushing) off it or being held flat to it by somebody else. It covers idle propping as much as being [pinned](#pinned) there.

entries.name: posing
entries.description: A stance deliberately held for the viewer or a [camera](#camera) rather than arising out of an action. Covers [model](#model), hero and [idol](#idol) posturing alike.

entries.name: on_one_knee
entries.description: Kneeling with one knee down and the other raised. The pose reads as respect or devotion and is the standard stance for a proposal; both [knees](#knees) down is [plain](#plain) [kneeling](#kneeling).

entries.name: tiptoes
entries.description: Balancing on the tips of the [toes](#toes) with the heels raised, usually while [standing](#standing). Compare [heel_up](#heel_up) for a single lifted heel; on pointe [shoes](#shoes) it is en pointe.

entries.name: leaning_to_the_side
entries.description: The upper body tips [sideways](#sideways) while the hips stay put or angle the opposite way. A relaxed or inquisitive stance rather than a full bend at the waist.

entries.name: reclining
entries.description: A relaxed, half-sitting posture, [leaning](#leaning) [back](#back) on the elbows, a [cushion](#cushion), or a [chair](#chair) without [lying](#lying) fully flat. Combine with [sitting](#sitting) or lying depending on which the pose leans closer to.

entries.name: against_glass
entries.description: Skin or clothing pressed flat to a pane of [glass](#glass), usually seen from the far side with the [flesh](#flesh) [spreading](#spreading) out against it. Add the [tag](#tag) for whatever part is being squashed, such as [breast_press](#breast_press).

entries.name: twisted_torso
entries.description: The upper body rotated sharply relative to the hips, sometimes past what a real [spine](#spine) allows. A favourite pose for showing chest and rear together, with extreme cases [sliding](#sliding) into [bad_anatomy](#bad_anatomy).

entries.name: leaning
entries.description: A [standing](#standing) character tilts away from upright, propped against something or not, but without [bending](#bending) over. Add the direction, [leaning_forward](#leaning_forward) or [leaning_back](#leaning_back).

entries.name: midair
entries.description: A character shown fully off the ground with [no](#no) visible support, in a setting clear enough to make the [height](#height) obvious. On a blank or ambiguous background, [floating](#floating), [flying](#flying) or [jumping](#jumping) fits better.

entries.name: peeking_out
entries.description: A character leans partway out from behind a [corner](#corner), [doorway](#doorway), wall, [tree](#tree) or another person, so only some of them is visible. Any object [can](#can) serve as the [cover](#cover); [watching](#watching) unseen is [peeking](#peeking).

entries.name: flexible
entries.description: The character holds a position needing far more mobility than an ordinary body has, such as a [split](#split), a deep backbend or [legs](#legs) behind the head. Taken to extremes it becomes [contortion](#contortion).

entries.name: afloat
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) or object floats on or in [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid), [drifting](#drifting) at the surface or suspended below it. Hovering in mid-air is [floating](#floating) instead.

entries.name: stuck
entries.description: A character physically [trapped](#trapped) by their surroundings, wedged in a [doorway](#doorway), jammed in a narrow gap or [caught](#caught) in a tight [opening](#opening). Someone stuck partway through a wall gets [through_wall](#through_wall) instead.

entries.name: through_wall
entries.description: A body [caught](#caught) halfway through a wall, whether a [ghost](#ghost) passing through it, someone who rammed into it and got [stuck](#stuck), or a restraint used in a sexual scene. Different from noclip, where the wall's presence is ignored entirely rather than shown [blocking](#blocking) the body.

entries.name: zombie_pose
entries.description: Arms held straight out ahead with the hands [hanging](#hanging) limp or [reaching](#reaching), paired with a hunched, shuffling stance and a blank stare. The stock pose associated with zombies, [jiangshi](#jiangshi), and sleepwalkers in popular depictions.

entries.name: under_table
entries.description: A character crouched, [hiding](#hiding) or [sitting](#sitting) beneath a [table](#table) or [desk](#desk). For the heated Japanese table specifically, also add [under_kotatsu](#under_kotatsu).

entries.name: against_railing
entries.description: Leaning forward over a [railing](#railing) or [back](#back) onto it, typically on a [balcony](#balcony), [bridge](#bridge), [rooftop](#rooftop) or [walkway](#walkway). The rail carries part of the figure's [weight](#weight).

entries.name: leaning_on_object
entries.description: A character props themselves against a wall, [railing](#railing), [table](#table) or the like without [bending](#bending) fully over. Add the [tag](#tag) for whatever is taking the [weight](#weight).

entries.name: standing_on_liquid
entries.description: A character stands on the surface of [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid) as if it were solid ground, a supernatural or magical feat.

entries.name: against_tree
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) rests their [back](#back) on a [tree](#tree) trunk while [standing](#standing) or [sitting](#sitting), the trunk supporting them. The tree is part of the pose rather than [scenery](#scenery) behind it.

entries.name: hanging
entries.description: A character or [creature](#creature) dangles or hangs from something, such as a [branch](#branch), a [ledge](#ledge) or a [rope](#rope), with nothing [tying](#tying) them there. Execution by rope is [hanged](#hanged), and the [bondage](#bondage) posture is [suspension](#suspension).

entries.name: bowing
entries.description: Bending forward from the waist, or [kneeling](#kneeling) with the head lowered, toward somebody as greeting, thanks or apology. A full [prostration](#prostration) on the [floor](#floor) is [dogeza](#dogeza); a [stage](#stage) [bow](#bow) and a [curtsey](#curtsey) belong here too.

entries.name: curtsey
entries.description: A Western [bow](#bow) performed mostly by women, the [knees](#knees) [bending](#bending) slightly while the [skirt](#skirt) is usually held out to the sides. Only the bow qualifies: a [skirt_hold](#skirt_hold) with [no](#no) bend, even over crossed [legs](#legs) or a [gown](#gown), is not one.

entries.name: dynamic_pose
entries.description: The body [caught](#caught) in [strong](#strong), unusual motion, twisted or stretched out the way a [figure](#figure) study would set it. Common in fight art, though leaps, falls and dance qualify just as [well](#well).

entries.name: looking_through_own_legs
entries.description: A character bent right forward, looking [back](#back) at the viewer [upside-down](#upside-down) between their own [legs](#legs). It says what the character does, unlike [view_between_legs](#view_between_legs), which says where the [camera](#camera) sits, though both [can](#can) apply at once.

entries.name: balancing
entries.description: A character works to keep their own balance or to steady something else, [standing](#standing) one-footed on a rail or [holding](#holding) a [stack](#stack) of plates level on one hand. The struggle not to let it fall is what the picture shows.

entries.name: under_tree
entries.description: The subject is positioned beneath a tree's branches, whether [standing](#standing), [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying). Add [tree_shade](#tree_shade) as [well](#well) when the [shadow](#shadow) itself is the point.

entries.name: handstand
entries.description: A character balances [upside-down](#upside-down) on their hands with the arms straight. Balancing on a single arm is [one_arm_handstand](#one_arm_handstand), and on the fingertips it is standing_on_finger.

entries.name: hunched_over
entries.description: The upper body is leaned forward with a rounded, stooped [back](#back). It [can](#can) suggest exhaustion, age, creeping or shame.

entries.name: dogeza
entries.description: Kneeling on the ground and pressing the [forehead](#forehead) right down to the [floor](#floor), the deepest form of Japanese apology or entreaty. Struck without that intent, the same position is [prostration](#prostration).

entries.name: through_screen
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) passing bodily out of a [television](#television) or [computer](#computer) [screen](#screen), arriving into the room the way a certain long-haired [ghost](#ghost) famously did. It is one specific case of the broader [through_medium](#through_medium) [tag](#tag), reserved for [glass](#glass) screens rather than walls or other surfaces.

entries.name: prostration
entries.description: Kneeling with the head lowered to the ground and both hands flat in front, a [gesture](#gesture) of deep apology or submission. Known online by the [emoticon](#emoticon) orz or OTL, which sketches the bent [figure](#figure) in text.

entries.name: zero_gravity
entries.description: Weightlessness within a scene: hair, [fabric](#fabric), [liquid](#liquid) and loose objects drift instead of [falling](#falling), and anyone present hangs free in the air. Usually set inside a [spacecraft](#spacecraft) or out in open [space](#space).

entries.name: bent_over_furniture
entries.description: Somebody [folded](#folded) forward at the waist over a [table](#table), [chair](#chair), [railing](#railing) or [bed](#bed), with the furniture taking the [weight](#weight) of the upper body. That support is what separates it from a [plain](#plain) [bent_over](#bent_over).

entries.name: leaning_on_table
entries.description: A [table](#table), [desk](#desk) or [counter](#counter) takes the character's [weight](#weight), with elbows down, [palms](#palms) flat or a hip pressed to the edge. It is a [lounging](#lounging) or [waiting](#waiting) pose.

entries.name: cowering
entries.description: A character crouches low with arms [folded](#folded) over the head, braced against something frightening. The pose reads as fear rather than rest.

entries.name: sway_back
entries.description: Standing with the upper body tipped backward and nothing behind to lean on, so the [spine](#spine) curves and the hips push forward. Unsupported, unlike [leaning](#leaning) against a wall.

entries.name: henshin_pose
entries.description: The fixed stance struck to begin a [transformation](#transformation), arms and hands set in a prescribed order. Masked heroes and magical girls both have one, whether the change needs it or not.

entries.name: against_window
entries.description: Any part of a [window](#window) bears the character's [weight](#weight), frame and sill included. Where it is only the pane being pressed on, [against_glass](#against_glass) is the closer [tag](#tag).

entries.name: a-pose
entries.description: Standing with the arms straight but angled down and away from the body, tracing a [letter](#letter) A. Looser than a T-pose yet more deliberate than letting the arms hang, it turns up in outfit displays and modelling reference art.

entries.name: against_fence
entries.description: Someone leans [back](#back) on a [fence](#fence), or is pushed up against one, so that it takes their [weight](#weight). Merely [standing](#standing) near a fence does not count.

entries.name: en_pointe
entries.description: Balancing on the very tips of the [toes](#toes), the [ballet](#ballet) position that pointe [shoes](#shoes) are built to support. Standing on tiptoe, with the [weight](#weight) still on the [ball](#ball) of the foot, is a different thing.

entries.name: slouching
entries.description: Shoulders dropped and the upper [spine](#spine) curved forward in a loose, sagging stance. It is the mild version of a fully bent [back](#back), and reads as laziness, exhaustion or [defeat](#defeat).

entries.name: picking_up
entries.description: Bending or crouching to lift something off the ground, most often a dropped object. The stooped [back](#back) and the [reaching](#reaching) hand are what the [tag](#tag) records, whatever is being picked up.

entries.name: rearing
entries.description: A four-legged [animal](#animal) rises onto its hind [legs](#legs) with the front legs lifted off the ground, as a startled or [excited](#excited) [horse](#horse) might. A [taur](#taur) [can](#can) do this too, but a character with human shoulders [standing](#standing) upright is simply anthro.

entries.name: one_arm_handstand
entries.description: A [handstand](#handstand) balanced on a single hand, the other arm held clear of the ground or thrown out for balance. A show of strength, common in acrobatic and martial [poses](#poses).

entries.name: contortion
entries.description: The body is bent into a shape that looks impossible yet [can](#can) be reached with enough flexibility. The proportions have to stay anatomically [sound](#sound), or the picture is simply badly drawn.

entries.name: against_table
entries.description: A [table](#table) takes some of a figure's [weight](#weight), usually through arms braced on the edge or a hip pushed into it. Lying fully on the surface is [on_table](#on_table) instead.

entries.name: standing_on_object
entries.description: The character stands on top of something rather than on the ground itself, be it a [crate](#crate), a [rock](#rock), a [railing](#railing) or a vehicle roof.

entries.name: waiting
entries.description: Somebody idling until something happens, [standing](#standing) at a stop, [sitting](#sitting) on a [bench](#bench), checking the time. The stillness and the sense of expectation carry the picture.

entries.name: under_another's_clothes
entries.description: One character is tucked inside somebody else's clothing, hidden beneath a [coat](#coat), [shirt](#shirt) or [cloak](#cloak). Usually a small [figure](#figure) sheltering, [hiding](#hiding) or [sneaking](#sneaking) about there.

entries.name: through_window
entries.description: Somebody's upper body passing through a [window](#window) frame, [reaching](#reaching) in or [climbing](#climbing) out. Smashing the [glass](#glass) first is a separate [tag](#tag), as is merely [leaning](#leaning) on the sill or gazing outside.

entries.name: coiled
entries.description: A long serpentine body is wound into loops that rest on themselves. Used for snakes, naga tails and other elongated forms at rest.

entries.name: against_door
entries.description: The body rests on a [door](#door), whether casually propped there or pressed flat to it by somebody else. The door is what carries the [weight](#weight).

entries.name: slav_squatting
entries.description: A deep squat held with both heels flat on the ground rather than raised. Long known as an Asian-style rest position, it later became shorthand for Eastern European [street](#street) youth, and Japanese art reads the same pose as [delinquent](#delinquent) behaviour.

entries.name: under_umbrella
entries.description: One or more figures shelter beneath an open [umbrella](#umbrella). Two [people](#people) [crowded](#crowded) under a single one is the [familiar](#familiar) romantic version.

entries.name: downward_dog
entries.description: The [yoga](#yoga) posture with [palms](#palms) and [soles](#soles) on the [floor](#floor), hips pushed high and the body making an inverted V, head [hanging](#hanging) toward the [legs](#legs). Named for the way a [dog](#dog) stretches on waking.

entries.name: under_skirt
entries.description: A character or object positioned beneath somebody else's [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress), inside the [fabric](#fabric) rather than merely glimpsed from below. Small figures [hiding](#hiding) there are the usual case.

entries.name: leaning_out_of_window
entries.description: Someone bends forward through an open [window](#window), [torso](#torso) outside and elbows or hands [resting](#resting) on the sill. Typical of [calling](#calling) to a person below, greeting a visitor or [watching](#watching) the [street](#street).

entries.name: inugami-ke_no_ichizoku_pose
entries.description: A body driven head-first into [water](#water), [snow](#snow) or earth so that only the [legs](#legs) stand up out of it. Taken from a classic Japanese [detective](#detective) story in which a [corpse](#corpse) is found this way, it now serves as a [plain](#plain) visual [gag](#gag).

entries.name: against_rock
entries.description: The body rests on a [boulder](#boulder) or [rock](#rock) face, [sitting](#sitting) [back](#back) on it, [leaning](#leaning) or pressed to it. Common in outdoor, travel and [resting](#resting) scenes.

entries.name: dangling
entries.description: Something hangs loose and swings free: a leg over the edge of a seat, an object [swaying](#swaying) on a [string](#string), a [figure](#figure) suspended by one arm. The unsupported, [hanging](#hanging) [quality](#quality) is the point.

entries.name: arabesque_(pose)
entries.description: A [ballet](#ballet) position in which the [dancer](#dancer) balances on one straight leg while the other stretches straight out behind, usually at hip [height](#height) or higher. Arms may be spread or one raised, and a leg carried all the way to vertical also takes [standing_split](#standing_split).

entries.name: around_corner
entries.description: A character stands at the edge of a wall or [building](#building) [corner](#corner), often [leaning](#leaning) out to look past it. The stock setup for the running-late-for-school [collision](#collision).

entries.name: bent_back
entries.description: The [spine](#spine) curled forward into a C by [leaning](#leaning) over, so that the middle of the [back](#back) sits further back than the shoulders and hips do. It is the reverse of [arched_back](#arched_back) and not the same as a backbend; [spooning](#spooning) and curling around something produce it.

entries.name: balancing_on_head
entries.description: An object rests on top of somebody's head, held there by posture alone rather than by hand. Books, cups and small animals are the usual load.

entries.name: superhero_landing
entries.description: The crouched three-point [landing](#landing), one knee down, the other foot flat, a fist or open palm [planted](#planted) on the ground, head often lowered. Drawn as the moment of impact at the end of a drop or leap.

entries.name: against_mirror
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) leans or presses on a [mirror](#mirror), so their [reflection](#reflection) stands right beside them. The doubled image is usually the whole point of the composition.

entries.name: cramped
entries.description: One or more characters are wedged into a [space](#space) too small for them, movement restricted and posture [awkward](#awkward). Boxes, lockers and narrow gaps are the usual containers.

entries.name: through_ground
entries.description: A body is driven into or [stuck](#stuck) in the ground, head [buried](#buried) with [legs](#legs) [waving](#waving), or half a [figure](#figure) protruding from the earth. Usually the aftermath of a fall or a [comic](#comic) blow.

entries.name: frontbend
entries.description: A deep forward fold at the waist, the [torso](#torso) pressed flat against the [legs](#legs) and the head brought level with them. A [gymnastics](#gymnastics) and [stretching](#stretching) pose rather than a [casual](#casual) bend.

entries.name: behind_tree
entries.description: Somebody stands behind a [tree](#tree) trunk with part of the body hidden by it, usually peering around the edge. Hiding, [watching](#watching) and bashful [peeking](#peeking) scenes use it.

entries.name: ass_lift
entries.description: The hips are raised clear of whatever the character is [resting](#resting) on, buttocks pushed upward. Usually begins from [kneeling](#kneeling) or [lying](#lying) face down.

entries.name: body_bridge
entries.description: Lying face up and [pushing](#pushing) off both hands and [feet](#feet) so the [spine](#spine) arches and the [belly](#belly) becomes the highest point. Gymnastics and [yoga](#yoga) call the shape a [bridge](#bridge); it is a held stretch rather than [lying](#lying) down.

entries.name: leaning_against_motorcycle
entries.description: A character rests their [weight](#weight) against a parked [motorcycle](#motorcycle), propped on the seat, the handlebars or the frame. Sitting astride the [machine](#machine) is a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: standing_on_chair
entries.description: A character stands up on the seat of a [chair](#chair) rather than [sitting](#sitting) in it, often to reach something high or to make a declaration.

entries.name: hanging_on
entries.description: Clinging to something in order to stay up, whether a [ledge](#ledge), a [rope](#rope) or another person. The grip is the only thing keeping the character from [falling](#falling).

entries.name: leaning_on_weapon
entries.description: The character props their [weight](#weight) against a [weapon](#weapon) [planted](#planted) on the ground, a [sword](#sword), [spear](#spear) or [rifle](#rifle) stood upright and used like a [staff](#staff). It usually reads as exhaustion after a fight or a pause taken mid-battle.

entries.name: bending
entries.description: The [torso](#torso) tipped forward or to the side from the waist, generally to reach, look at or pick up something. The deep fold with the hips pushed [back](#back) is [bent_over](#bent_over) instead.

entries.name: kneeling_on_liquid
entries.description: A character kneels on the surface of a [liquid](#liquid), most often [water](#water), without [sinking](#sinking) into it. Ripples [spreading](#spreading) out beneath the [knees](#knees) are the usual treatment.

entries.name: pretzel_pose
entries.description: The body [folded](#folded) so the [legs](#legs) come up over the head while the [torso](#torso) stays in front of them, arms often bracing the position. A contortionist's shape, close to a well-known [yoga](#yoga) posture.

entries.name: against_pillar
entries.description: Someone rests their [back](#back) on a [column](#column), or is held against one, the [pillar](#pillar) [running](#running) the full [height](#height) of the [figure](#figure). It bears their [weight](#weight) rather than merely [standing](#standing) nearby.

entries.name: uneven_footing
entries.description: The character stands with their [feet](#feet) at different heights, one raised on a step, [rock](#rock), kerb or other surface. The tilted stance is the point, rather than any particular activity.

entries.name: leaning_against_vehicle
entries.description: Somebody props themselves on a [car](#car), [truck](#truck) or other vehicle instead of [standing](#standing) unsupported. The broader against_vehicle wording is now preferred for this.

entries.name: pigeon_pose
entries.description: A [yoga](#yoga) posture with one leg [folded](#folded) forward beneath the body and the other stretched straight [back](#back) along the [floor](#floor), chest lifted. It shows up in [stretching](#stretching), exercise and dance-practice scenes.

entries.name: leaning_on_animal
entries.description: A character rests against an [animal](#animal) or [creature](#creature), using its flank as a backrest or an [armrest](#armrest). It is usually a large mount or a [pet](#pet) [lying](#lying) down.

entries.name: villain_pose
entries.description: Legs straight and pressed together, arms [folded](#folded), hips pushed forward and chin raised, the arrogant stance of someone looking down on an opponent. Characters who hover strike it in [midair](#midair) with [toes](#toes) pointed at the ground.

entries.name: against_locker
entries.description: The body leans or is [pinned](#pinned) against a bank of metal lockers, the fixture of [school](#school) corridors and changing rooms. The doors take the [weight](#weight).

entries.name: bending_backward
entries.description: The upper body arches to the rear, chest [opening](#opening) and head [dropping](#dropping) [back](#back). Dance, [stretching](#stretching) and backbend [poses](#poses) use it; the forward counterpart is [bent_back](#bent_back).

entries.name: against_bookshelf
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) [leaning](#leaning) on, [pushing](#pushing) against or held up to a [bookshelf](#bookshelf), with the shelves taking their [weight](#weight). Sitting or perching on top of one is a different arrangement.

entries.name: sitting
entries.description: The character's bottom rests on a [chair](#chair), [floor](#floor), [bench](#bench) or other surface, possibly with the [legs](#legs) [folded](#folded) beneath. Knees on the ground instead is [kneeling](#kneeling), except for [seiza](#seiza); specific forms include [indian_style](#indian_style), [wariza](#wariza), [crossed_legs](#crossed_legs) and [sitting_backwards](#sitting_backwards).

entries.name: on_bed
entries.description: A character sits or lies on a [bed](#bed) or a [futon](#futon). Regularly combined with [lying](#lying), [sitting](#sitting) and [bedroom](#bedroom).

entries.name: straddling
entries.description: Sitting or [standing](#standing) with one leg on each side of something, such as a [horse](#horse), a [chair](#chair), a [fence](#fence) or another person.

entries.name: wariza
entries.description: Sitting on the [floor](#floor) with the [legs](#legs) bent [back](#back) on either side of the hips, the W-sitting typical of Japanese girls in informal settings. Legs [folded](#folded) to one side only is [yokozuwari](#yokozuwari).

entries.name: seiza
entries.description: The formal Japanese [kneeling](#kneeling) posture: [knees](#knees) on the [floor](#floor), [weight](#weight) [resting](#resting) on the heels, tops of the [feet](#feet) flat. Legs splayed to both sides is [wariza](#wariza) instead, and [folded](#folded) to one side is [yokozuwari](#yokozuwari).

entries.name: sitting_on_person
entries.description: A character uses someone else as a seat: [lap](#lap), [back](#back), shoulders or chest. Narrower tags include [sitting_on_lap](#sitting_on_lap) and [sitting_on_shoulder](#sitting_on_shoulder).

entries.name: on_floor
entries.description: A character sits, lies or kneels on an indoor [floor](#floor). Standing does not count, and the same posture out of doors is [on_ground](#on_ground).

entries.name: on_chair
entries.description: A character is on a [chair](#chair) in any posture at all: [sitting](#sitting) properly, [squatting](#squatting) on the seat, [standing](#standing) on it. Stools and couches have tags of their own.

entries.name: on_ground
entries.description: A character sits, lies or kneels on the earth [outdoors](#outdoors), be it [dirt](#dirt), [sand](#sand), [grass](#grass) or [pavement](#pavement), and a [towel](#towel) or [blanket](#blanket) underneath still counts. Not for anyone [standing](#standing), and [indoors](#indoors) it is [on_floor](#on_floor).

entries.name: yokozuwari
entries.description: A feminine informal [sitting](#sitting) posture, [kneeling](#kneeling) as in [seiza](#seiza) but with both [legs](#legs) [folded](#folded) out to one side. Legs splayed out on both sides is [wariza](#wariza); the male equivalent is agura. Tag sitting.

entries.name: on_couch
entries.description: A character sits, reclines or lies on a sofa. See [on_chair](#on_chair) and [on_stool](#on_stool) for other kinds of seat.

entries.name: indian_style
entries.description: Sitting on the [floor](#floor) with the [legs](#legs) [folded](#folded) and crossed at the ankles, called cross-legged in English and agura in Japanese, where it is the [casual](#casual) masculine way to sit. It has nothing to do with clothing from India.

entries.name: invisible_chair
entries.description: A character sits as though on a seat, yet nothing is drawn beneath them. The seat may be meant to be [invisible](#invisible), they may be [floating](#floating), or the artist simply left the background out; it is neither [tachi-e](#tachi-e) nor [faux_figurine](#faux_figurine).

entries.name: hugging_own_legs
entries.description: The arms are wrapped around one's own [knees](#knees) or [legs](#legs), nearly always while [sitting](#sitting); the Japanese gym-class sitting posture is included. It often reads as melancholy or thought. Lying curled up is [fetal_position](#fetal_position), and [wrapping](#wrapping) the legs around somebody else is [leg_lock](#leg_lock).

entries.name: sitting_on_lap
entries.description: A character sits in another's [lap](#lap), facing forward, [sideways](#sideways), or toward them. Falls under [sitting_on_person](#sitting_on_person).

entries.name: on_desk
entries.description: A character is up on a [desk](#desk), [sitting](#sitting) on it, [lying](#lying) across it or [reclining](#reclining) there. Merely [resting](#resting) an arm or a hand on one for support is against_desk.

entries.name: on_grass
entries.description: A character rests in full contact with [grass](#grass), generally [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying) [back](#back) on a lawn or a [meadow](#meadow).

entries.name: upright_straddle
entries.description: One character straddles another who is [sitting](#sitting) upright, facing them with [legs](#legs) wrapped around or [resting](#resting) to the sides. Known in the Kama Sutra as the [lotus](#lotus) position.

entries.name: sitting_on_face
entries.description: One character sits on another's face. May be a comedic [squash](#squash) or a sexual act; add [cunnilingus](#cunnilingus) or [anilingus](#anilingus) when it is.

entries.name: sitting_on_throne
entries.description: Seated on a [throne](#throne), often sprawled or with a leg crossed to signal authority. Common for royalty, [demon](#demon) lords and villains.

entries.name: on_table
entries.description: A character stands, sits, lies or otherwise rests on top of a [table](#table). Use it for anyone up on the surface, not for someone seated at it in the ordinary way.

entries.name: on_bench
entries.description: Someone is up on a [bench](#bench) in whatever posture, [sitting](#sitting), [lying](#lying), [squatting](#squatting) or [standing](#standing). Park and station scenes are the usual home for it.

entries.name: sitting_on_stairs
entries.description: A character seated on a flight of steps, [indoors](#indoors) or outside, such as a [shrine](#shrine) stairway or a [school](#school) staircase. Implies both [sitting](#sitting) and [stairs](#stairs).

entries.name: sitting_in_tree
entries.description: A character perches seated on a [tree](#tree) [branch](#branch), [legs](#legs) [dangling](#dangling) or drawn up. A character merely [climbing](#climbing) or [standing](#standing) in the tree takes [in_tree](#in_tree) alone instead.

entries.name: sitting_on_object
entries.description: Seated on some object with [no](#no) dedicated on_x [tag](#tag) of its own, such as a [desk](#desk) or a [rock](#rock). Prefer the specific tag where one already exists.

entries.name: on_motorcycle
entries.description: A character sits astride, rides or leans on a [motorcycle](#motorcycle), whether it is moving or parked. Add [riding](#riding) or [driving](#driving) tags when the [machine](#machine) is actually under way.

entries.name: on_rock
entries.description: A character is up on a [rock](#rock) or a [boulder](#boulder) in any posture, [lying](#lying), [sitting](#sitting), [squatting](#squatting) or [standing](#standing). Common on shorelines and mountainsides.

entries.name: on_stool
entries.description: A character is on a [stool](#stool), most often [sitting](#sitting), though [standing](#standing) or [squatting](#squatting) on it counts as [well](#well). See [on_chair](#on_chair) and [on_couch](#on_couch) for other seating.

entries.name: on_car
entries.description: A character sits, stands, rides or sprawls on the outside of a [car](#car), on the [bonnet](#bonnet) or the roof, whether parked or moving. Sitting inside does not count, nor does [sitting](#sitting) in the seat of a [convertible](#convertible).

entries.name: sitting_on_table
entries.description: A character sits on top of a [table](#table) rather than on a [chair](#chair) beside it, often with [legs](#legs) crossed or [dangling](#dangling). Compare [on_desk](#on_desk) for a [school](#school) or [office](#office) [desk](#desk).

entries.name: on_roof
entries.description: A character is up on the sloping roof of a [building](#building). Add [tile_roof](#tile_roof) where it fits, and [foot_dangle](#foot_dangle) if they sit at the edge with their [legs](#legs) [hanging](#hanging) over.

entries.name: sitting_backwards
entries.description: Sitting in a [chair](#chair) so that its backrest faces forward, often with the arms [resting](#resting) on top of it. A [casual](#casual), confident pose.

entries.name: on_railing
entries.description: A character sits, stands, climbs or lies on a [railing](#railing); for [sitting](#sitting), the whole seat should be up on the rail. Leaning against one is [against_railing](#against_railing).

entries.name: butterfly_sitting
entries.description: Sitting on the ground with the [knees](#knees) dropped out to the sides and both [soles](#soles) pressed against each other. The same shape as the stretch of that name.

entries.name: sitting_on_shoulder
entries.description: A small character sits on one shoulder of a larger one. Riding across both shoulders instead is [shoulder_carry](#shoulder_carry).

entries.name: on_scooter
entries.description: Someone sits or rests on a [scooter](#scooter), which may be parked at the kerb or under way. Add [riding](#riding) or [driving](#driving) tags when the [machine](#machine) is actually in motion.

entries.name: sitting_sideways
entries.description: Sitting with both [legs](#legs) swung off to one side of the seat rather than facing forward over it. Not a statement about which way the [chair](#chair) itself points; [riding](#riding) a [horse](#horse) or [broom](#broom) this way is [sidesaddle](#sidesaddle) instead.

entries.name: sitting_on_branch
entries.description: A character seated on a limb above the ground, [legs](#legs) often [hanging](#hanging) down. Usually a [tree](#tree) [branch](#branch), though sometimes a cut length [floating](#floating) on its own.

entries.name: on_innertube
entries.description: Someone sits inside or drapes over an inflatable [ring](#ring), [afloat](#afloat) in a [pool](#pool) or at the sea. The ring keeps them at the surface, so it goes with swimwear and [water](#water) scenes.

entries.name: on_tank
entries.description: Someone is perched on an armoured [tank](#tank), [riding](#riding) on the hull or [sitting](#sitting) up on the turret. Being inside the [hatch](#hatch) rather than on the plating does not count.

entries.name: sitting_on_water
entries.description: A character or object appears to rest at or just above a [water](#water) surface without clearly [sinking](#sinking) in. The [scope](#scope) of the [tag](#tag) is unsettled, so treat it cautiously and prefer the ordinary water and submersion tags instead.

entries.name: figure_four_sitting
entries.description: Seated with one ankle or calf laid across the opposite knee, the [legs](#legs) making a rough number four. A more open, sprawling sit than [plain](#plain) crossed legs.

entries.name: on_box
entries.description: A person or an [animal](#animal) is on top of a [box](#box) or a [crate](#crate), using it as a seat or as a step.

entries.name: on_water
entries.description: A person rests on top of [water](#water), [standing](#standing) on the surface, half-submerged in a shallow [pool](#pool) or [floating](#floating) in a [ring](#ring). Craft that need water to work, such as boats, do not count.

entries.name: on_pillow
entries.description: Someone rests on a [cushion](#cushion) or a [pillow](#pillow), [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying) on it rather than beside it. A head laid on another person's [thighs](#thighs) is [lap_pillow](#lap_pillow) instead.

entries.name: on_toilet
entries.description: A character sits on a lavatory, with the [lid](#lid) up or down. Nothing about the [tag](#tag) requires the [toilet](#toilet) to be in use; a [bored](#bored) perch on a closed lid counts.

entries.name: sitting_on_animal
entries.description: Somebody seated on the [back](#back) of an [animal](#animal), not necessarily to travel anywhere. Includes [resting](#resting) on a large [creature](#creature) as though it were furniture.

entries.name: on_boat
entries.description: Somebody stands, sits or lies aboard a [boat](#boat), whether it is tied up or moving through the [water](#water).

entries.name: on_crescent
entries.description: A character is settled in the curve of a [crescent](#crescent), most often a [fantasy](#fantasy) crescent [moon](#moon) [hanging](#hanging) in the [sky](#sky), [sitting](#sitting) or [reclining](#reclining) in the hollow.

entries.name: on_stairs
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) is on a flight of steps, [sitting](#sitting) on a tread, [standing](#standing) partway up or stretched along them.

entries.name: thigh_straddling
entries.description: One character sits astride another's thigh, [weight](#weight) carried on the leg rather than the hips. Often, though not always, a form of [grinding](#grinding).

entries.name: on_food
entries.description: A character is up on an oversized piece of [food](#food), treating a [cake](#cake), a [pastry](#pastry) or a [fruit](#fruit) as furniture.

entries.name: sitting_on_head
entries.description: One character perches on top of another's head, generally a small or [animal](#animal) companion [riding](#riding) a person. The one below usually looks resigned about it.

entries.name: sitting_on_tree_stump
entries.description: A character using the cut base of a felled [tree](#tree) as a [stool](#stool). Reads as a woodland rest stop.

entries.name: on_rooftop
entries.description: A character is on a flat roof built to be walked on, of the kind [school](#school) buildings and [apartment](#apartment) blocks have. A sloping roof never meant for [walking](#walking) takes [on_roof](#on_roof), and the two are never used together.

entries.name: on_moon
entries.description: A character stands or sits on the moon's own grey, cratered surface. Perching in a [crescent](#crescent) shape is [on_crescent](#on_crescent) instead.

entries.name: sitting_on_box
entries.description: Someone perched on a [crate](#crate), [carton](#carton) or packing [box](#box) as a makeshift seat. Storerooms, moving days and [back](#back) alleys are the usual settings.

entries.name: sitting_on_food
entries.description: A character seated on something edible, either a normal-sized person on a [giant](#giant) portion or a tiny one on ordinary [food](#food). A [staple](#staple) of dessert-themed and size-play illustrations.

entries.name: sitting_in_window
entries.description: A character perched in a [window](#window) [opening](#opening), often with the [legs](#legs) drawn up on the sill or [dangling](#dangling) outside. A stock quiet-moment composition with light coming from behind.

entries.name: sitting_on_pillow
entries.description: Someone seated on a [cushion](#cushion) set on the [floor](#floor) rather than on furniture. Standard for [tatami](#tatami) rooms, where a flat [zabuton](#zabuton) takes the place of a [chair](#chair).

entries.name: on_flower
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) sits, lies or stands on or inside a [giant](#giant) blossom, most often a tiny character [resting](#resting) among the [petals](#petals).

entries.name: on_cloud
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) rests on a [cloud](#cloud) as though it were solid footing, [sitting](#sitting), [lying](#lying), [squatting](#squatting) or [standing](#standing) on it.

entries.name: on_wall
entries.description: A character is up on top of a wall, [sitting](#sitting) along it, [standing](#standing) or [lying](#lying) out. Pressing or [leaning](#leaning) against its side instead is [against_wall](#against_wall).

entries.name: sitting_on_roof
entries.description: A character seated on the roof of a [building](#building), often on the ridge or a sloped tile surface. A favorite spot for [night](#night), [moon](#moon) and [rooftop](#rooftop) conversation scenes.

entries.name: on_branch
entries.description: A character is up on a [tree](#tree) [branch](#branch), [straddling](#straddling) it, [standing](#standing) along it or stretched out on it.

entries.name: on_animal
entries.description: A person or a [creature](#creature) sits, stands or lies on an animal's [back](#back), whether [riding](#riding) it or just [resting](#resting) there while it stands.

entries.name: sitting_between_lap
entries.description: Someone settled down in the [space](#space) between another person's spread [thighs](#thighs), usually with both facing the same way. Reads as an intimate but non-sexual [resting](#resting) arrangement.

entries.name: sitting_on_torii
entries.description: A character perched on the crossbeam of a [shrine](#shrine) [gate](#gate), high above the [path](#path) below. Common for spirits, foxes and other supernatural figures.

entries.name: on_truck
entries.description: Someone rides on a [truck](#truck) rather than in the cab: in the [bed](#bed), on the roof or up on the [bonnet](#bonnet).

entries.name: sitting_on_log
entries.description: A character seated on a fallen trunk or a cut length of timber. Turns up in [forest](#forest), campsite and roadside rest scenes.

entries.name: sitting_on_arm
entries.description: A small [figure](#figure) seated on somebody's outstretched forearm, or a character [sitting](#sitting) on the [armrest](#armrest) of a [chair](#chair). A size difference between the two usually makes the first [reading](#reading) obvious.

entries.name: sitting_on_ball
entries.description: A character seated on top of a [ball](#ball), most often a large exercise ball able to take the [weight](#weight). Balance is part of the appeal of the pose.

entries.name: lotus_position
entries.description: A cross-legged seat with each foot drawn up onto the opposite thigh, the classic [meditation](#meditation) posture of [yoga](#yoga) and Buddhist practice. Ordinary cross-legged [sitting](#sitting) is [indian_style](#indian_style) instead.

entries.name: on_tree
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) is up in a [tree](#tree), settled in the [fork](#fork) of the trunk or [standing](#standing) among the limbs.

entries.name: on_plate
entries.description: A character is laid out on a [serving](#serving) [plate](#plate) as though they were the course, either shrunk to its scale or with the plate drawn enormous.

entries.name: sitting_on_fence
entries.description: A character [sitting](#sitting) up on a [fence](#fence) or [railing](#railing). Because the top is narrow, they usually brace with the hands or lean [back](#back) against a post.

entries.name: sitting_on_hand
entries.description: A small [figure](#figure) seated in or on somebody's open palm. Depends on a large size difference between the two.

entries.name: on_counter
entries.description: Someone is up on a [kitchen](#kitchen) or [shop](#shop) [counter](#counter) rather than [standing](#standing) at it, perched on the edge or [lying](#lying) along the top.

entries.name: sitting_on_wall
entries.description: Someone seated on top of a low wall or parapet, [legs](#legs) [hanging](#hanging) over one side. Roadside, schoolyard and [rooftop](#rooftop) edges are the usual places.

entries.name: on_mecha
entries.description: A person or an [animal](#animal) sits, stands or lies on the hull of a [giant](#giant) [robot](#robot), small against the [machine](#machine).

entries.name: on_banana
entries.description: A character sits, lies or perches on an oversized [banana](#banana), or on something built to that shape. The [fruit](#fruit) is drawn far larger than life, which is the whole joke.

entries.name: on_piano
entries.description: One or more figures are up on top of a [piano](#piano), or [lying](#lying) across the open frame and strings of a grand.

entries.name: cat_loaf
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) settles with every leg [folded](#folded) away beneath it so the [outline](#outline) turns into a rounded [brick](#brick). Characters with feline traits sometimes get drawn [holding](#holding) the same shape.

entries.name: on_weapon
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) sits or reclines on a [weapon](#weapon), which means either a tiny character or a hugely oversized blade or [gun](#gun). A weapon slung across the [back](#back) is [weapon_on_back](#weapon_on_back).

entries.name: on_top_of_pole
entries.description: A character balances on the very top of a utility [pole](#pole), a [lamppost](#lamppost) or a similarly narrow perch.

entries.name: on_ladder
entries.description: A character is up on the rungs of a [ladder](#ladder), [standing](#standing), [sitting](#sitting) or crouching there. It covers both a [leaning](#leaning) ladder and a free-standing [stepladder](#stepladder).

entries.name: on_liquid
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) rests on the surface of a [liquid](#liquid) without [sinking](#sinking) into it, held up as though it were solid ground.

entries.name: sitting_on_drum
entries.description: Someone seated on a [drum](#drum), generally a big taiko or [barrel](#barrel) drum wide enough to hold a person. Festival and [music](#music) scenes account for most uses.

entries.name: sitting_on_books
entries.description: A character using a [pile](#pile) of books as a seat, whether from a shortage of chairs or because the [stack](#stack) is comically [tall](#tall). Library and study scenes account for most of these.

entries.name: lying
entries.description: A character lying flat on a surface, taking their [weight](#weight) on the [back](#back), side or [stomach](#stomach). Add [on_back](#on_back), [on_side](#on_side) or [on_stomach](#on_stomach) to say which way up.

entries.name: on_back
entries.description: The character lies face upward on their [back](#back). Compare [on_side](#on_side) and [on_stomach](#on_stomach); someone [lying](#lying) on another person is [lying_on_person](#lying_on_person).

entries.name: on_side
entries.description: A character lies on one side of the body. When it is hard to tell, check the hips: one raised above the other means this, level hips mean [on_stomach](#on_stomach).

entries.name: all_fours
entries.description: Hands and [knees](#knees) on the ground with the [torso](#torso) held clear, like a four-legged [animal](#animal) [standing](#standing). A hand plus a knee or a foot must be down; both knees lifted makes it [bear_position](#bear_position), and [bowing](#bowing) face to the [floor](#floor) is [prostration](#prostration).

entries.name: on_stomach
entries.description: A character lies face down with [belly](#belly), [crotch](#crotch) and usually [thighs](#thighs) flat against the surface. If one hip rides higher than the other, the pose is [on_side](#on_side).

entries.name: ass-up_face-down
entries.description: The face, chest or shoulders lie on the surface while the hips stay raised. Used for [sleeping](#sleeping) and [sulking](#sulking) as often as for anything provocative.

entries.name: under_covers
entries.description: A character tucked beneath a [blanket](#blanket) or [bed](#bed) sheet, typically [lying](#lying) in bed. If nothing is worn underneath, add [naked_sheet](#naked_sheet) as [well](#well).

entries.name: the_pose
entries.description: Lying face down with both lower [legs](#legs) raised so the [feet](#feet) point into the air, a pose that shows off the chest, rear and feet all at once. The feet must be visible for the [tag](#tag) to apply.

entries.name: head_on_pillow
entries.description: The head rests on a [pillow](#pillow), usually with the character [lying](#lying) on a [bed](#bed). Sleep is not required.

entries.name: fetal_position
entries.description: Lying on one side with the [knees](#knees) pulled to the chest and the arms drawn in tight, curled like an unborn [child](#child). It reads as sleep, [cold](#cold), fear or [despair](#despair).

entries.name: curled_up
entries.description: A character drawn into a tight [ball](#ball) with the [knees](#knees) pulled up to the chest, [lying](#lying) down or crouched, whether asleep, [hiding](#hiding) or self-comforting. Close relative of [fetal_position](#fetal_position).

entries.name: face_down
entries.description: The face is turned downward against the ground, a [pillow](#pillow) or another surface and touching it. It says where the head is, whatever the rest of the body may be doing.

entries.name: face_in_pillow
entries.description: The face is [buried](#buried) down into a [pillow](#pillow) so little or none of it [can](#can) be seen, usually on a [bed](#bed). Relief, frustration and [hiding](#hiding) from the world are the usual readings.

entries.name: lying_on_water
entries.description: The [figure](#figure) lies stretched out on a [water](#water) surface, face up and borne along by it. It covers fanciful cases where the body simply rests on top without [sinking](#sinking) in.

entries.name: arm_pillow
entries.description: The head rests on the character's own outstretched arm instead of a [cushion](#cushion), typically while [lying](#lying) on a [bed](#bed), the [floor](#floor) or a [desk](#desk). A common way to draw a nap taken where [no](#no) [pillow](#pillow) is at hand.

entries.name: spread_eagle_position
entries.description: Lying flat on the ground with the arms and [legs](#legs) thrown out to the sides. Known in Japanese as dainoji, after the character its shape resembles, and often used to show exhaustion or [heavy](#heavy) sleep.

entries.name: lounging
entries.description: Sprawled comfortably across furniture with nothing to do, draped over a sofa or propped among cushions with the limbs gone slack. The mood is idleness rather than sleep.

entries.name: chest_on_pillow
entries.description: A character lies face down with the chest propped on a [pillow](#pillow) or [cushion](#cushion), the rest of the body stretched out behind. A [lounging](#lounging) pose seen on beds and floors.

entries.name: bear_position
entries.description: The character supports themselves on hands and [feet](#feet) with both [knees](#knees) lifted clear of the [floor](#floor) and the hips high. It is close to top-down bottom-up, except that the front of the body is held [well](#well) up as well.

entries.name: collapsed
entries.description: The [figure](#figure) has gone down and lies where they fell, limbs loose and nothing braced. It suggests exhaustion, [defeat](#defeat) or unconsciousness rather than [lying](#lying) down by [choice](#choice).

entries.name: planking
entries.description: Lying stretched out rigid and face down across some surface, arms held straight at the sides. Born as a photographed stunt, it still reads as a deliberately silly pose.

entries.name: lying_on_animal
entries.description: A person stretched out across a beast and letting it carry their [weight](#weight), on a horse's [back](#back), a big [dog](#dog), or a [sleeping](#sleeping) [dragon](#dragon) used as a [mattress](#mattress). The [animal](#animal) is the surface being lain on.

entries.name: spread_legs
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) opened wide apart, usually while [lying](#lying) down, [sitting](#sitting) or during [sex](#sex). A [standing](#standing) [figure](#figure) with [feet](#feet) simply apart is better tagged [legs_apart](#legs_apart) unless the legs are truly splayed.

entries.name: standing_on_one_leg
entries.description: Balancing on a single foot with the other leg lifted clear of the ground, whether mid-kick, mid-stretch, or simply a playful pose.

entries.name: leg_up
entries.description: Any pose with a single leg raised off the ground, [standing](#standing), [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying). Both [legs](#legs) in the air is [legs_up](#legs_up), and a wide [sideways](#sideways) spread is [leg_lift](#leg_lift).

entries.name: crossed_legs
entries.description: One leg laid over the other at the calf, knee or thigh, [sitting](#sitting), [standing](#standing) or [lying](#lying) down; [tag](#tag) the posture as [well](#well). Crossing at the ankles is [crossed_ankles](#crossed_ankles), and the pretzel-style seated [cross](#cross) is [indian_style](#indian_style).

entries.name: knees_up
entries.description: Both [knees](#knees) point upward because the character sits, lies or floats with the [legs](#legs) bent. A single raised knee is [knee_up](#knee_up).

entries.name: legs_up
entries.description: Both [legs](#legs) are thrust into the air instead of [resting](#resting) on anything. Lying, [sitting](#sitting) and held [poses](#poses) all qualify; a single raised leg is [leg_up](#leg_up).

entries.name: knee_up
entries.description: A single knee is raised into the air, whether [sitting](#sitting), [lying](#lying) or [standing](#standing). Kneeling on one knee is [on_one_knee](#on_one_knee), and both [knees](#knees) raised is [knees_up](#knees_up).

entries.name: legs_apart
entries.description: A [standing](#standing) character holds their [legs](#legs) separated. Someone [lying](#lying) down or bent over with the legs open takes [spread_legs](#spread_legs) instead.

entries.name: between_legs
entries.description: An object set or held between somebody's [legs](#legs), or hands, arms or a [tail](#tail) tucked there, often coyly. Sexual situations have tags of their own, and a character looking [back](#back) through their own legs is [looking_through_own_legs](#looking_through_own_legs).

entries.name: legs_together
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) are held closed along their full length, [standing](#standing), [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying), crossed or not. If only the [knees](#knees) touch while the [feet](#feet) part use [knees_together_feet_apart](#knees_together_feet_apart); [contrast](#contrast) [legs_apart](#legs_apart) and [spread_legs](#spread_legs).

entries.name: knees_together_feet_apart
entries.description: The [knees](#knees) touch while the [feet](#feet) splay outward, a [pigeon-toed](#pigeon-toed) stance seen [standing](#standing), [sitting](#sitting) or crouching. It is generally read as [shy](#shy) or endearing.

entries.name: leg_lift
entries.description: One leg is raised up and out from the other so the [legs](#legs) end wide apart, one in the air and one supporting. Any single raised leg without that spread is [leg_up](#leg_up).

entries.name: split
entries.description: A gymnastic pose with the [legs](#legs) extended in opposite directions until they lie flat, either side to side or front to [back](#back). A version balanced on one leg is [standing_split](#standing_split).

entries.name: m_legs
entries.description: Legs spread and bent so that, with the [feet](#feet) near the buttocks and the [knees](#knees) near the chest, they trace the [letter](#letter) M. Both [legs](#legs) must be visible in that shape, and it is not for [wariza](#wariza), a leg [lock](#lock) or most [squatting](#squatting) [poses](#poses).

entries.name: pigeon-toed
entries.description: Feet turned inward so the [toes](#toes) point towards each other, whether [standing](#standing), [sitting](#sitting) or [walking](#walking). A bashful, cutesy stance, often drawn together with [knees_together_feet_apart](#knees_together_feet_apart).

entries.name: folded
entries.description: The upper [legs](#legs) are pressed [back](#back) as far as they will go, doubling the body over on itself. It most often serves to open the hips for a sexual act, with hands gripping the legs, bindings or tendrils keeping them there.

entries.name: feet_up
entries.description: A character lifts their [feet](#feet) clear of the ground, the feet themselves visible. Where only raised [legs](#legs) show and the feet do not, use [legs_up](#legs_up).

entries.name: standing_split
entries.description: Standing on one leg while the other is raised straight up so both [legs](#legs) form a vertical line, a [static](#static) balance pose rather than a kick in motion.

entries.name: knees_to_chest
entries.description: Both [knees](#knees) are pulled in tight against the chest, as when curling up or hugging one's own [legs](#legs). It often accompanies [hugging_own_legs](#hugging_own_legs).

entries.name: crossed_ankles
entries.description: One ankle laid over the other, whether the character stands, sits or lies down. Crossing higher up at the calf, knee or thigh is [crossed_legs](#crossed_legs).

entries.name: vertical_split
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) are opened into a full [split](#split) while the body stays upright, one leg raised high along the [torso](#torso) or held overhead. Requires considerable flexibility and is common in dance and martial arts [poses](#poses).

entries.name: foot_up
entries.description: One foot is braced on a raised surface such as a step, [chair](#chair) or wall, higher than the other. A foot lifted into open air is [leg_up](#leg_up), lifted [toes](#toes) are [toes_up](#toes_up) and a lifted heel is [heel_up](#heel_up).

entries.name: wide_spread_legs
entries.description: The [thighs](#thighs) opened extremely far apart, close to a full [split](#split), while [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying) on the [back](#back). An ordinary squat does not count, though the cowgirl position does; the pose has recently been tied to the [jack-o'-lantern](#jack-o'-lantern) challenge [meme](#meme).

entries.name: watson_cross
entries.description: Standing with the [legs](#legs) crossed at the calf, knee or thigh, a deliberate [posing](#posing) stance sometimes paired with a hand on the hip. Ankles crossed, or one leg simply hidden behind the other, doesn't count.

entries.name: leg_hold
entries.description: A character keeps one of their own [legs](#legs) raised in their hands, as in a [standing](#standing) [split](#split), or holds another character's legs up. Pair it with [leg_up](#leg_up) or [leg_lift](#leg_lift) for the raised limb.

entries.name: plantar_flexion
entries.description: The foot is pointed so the [toes](#toes) extend downward in line with the shin, as with a [ballerina](#ballerina) on pointe or a swimmer's kick. The opposite motion, toes pulled up toward the shin, is [dorsiflexion](#dorsiflexion).

entries.name: shoe_dangle
entries.description: A shoe [hanging](#hanging) loosely off the [toes](#toes), half slipped from the foot. Applies to [flats](#flats), heels, [boots](#boots) and [sandals](#sandals) alike; a foot actively gripping a shoe instead is [holding_with_feet](#holding_with_feet).

entries.name: holding_legs
entries.description: Both of the character's own [legs](#legs) are gripped with the hands, hugging the [knees](#knees) or [pulling](#pulling) the legs up while [lying](#lying) on the [back](#back).

entries.name: knees_apart_feet_together
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) make a diamond: the [knees](#knees) fall outward while the [feet](#feet) stay pressed together. It is common when [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying) with the [soles](#soles) touching.

entries.name: between_thighs
entries.description: An object held or [resting](#resting) between the [thighs](#thighs), or hands, arms or a [tail](#tail) tucked there, usually shyly. A whole person in that position is [between_legs](#between_legs), and sexual acts take their own tags.

entries.name: heel_up
entries.description: Standing with both [feet](#feet) down but one heel raised off the ground. With both heels up the pose is [tiptoes](#tiptoes).

entries.name: high_kick
entries.description: A kick that carries the foot above the kicker's own waist, often as high as the head. The leg is thrown upward rather than driven forward low.

entries.name: legs_over_head
entries.description: Both [legs](#legs) are carried up behind or above the character's own head, a pose of extreme flexibility. It turns up in [acrobatics](#acrobatics), [stretching](#stretching) and some [sex](#sex) positions; add the position's own [tag](#tag) where one applies.

entries.name: legs_folded
entries.description: One or both [knees](#knees) are bent right up so the calf lies flat against the [back](#back) of the thigh with [no](#no) gap between them. Typical of [kneeling](#kneeling), [seiza](#seiza) and [sitting](#sitting) with the [legs](#legs) tucked under.

entries.name: outstretched_leg
entries.description: One leg fully extended in a straight line, as in a stretch or a kick. Both [legs](#legs) straight takes [outstretched_legs](#outstretched_legs).

entries.name: bowlegged_pose
entries.description: Standing in a half squat with the [knees](#knees) turned outward and the hips pushed forward to present the [crotch](#crotch), often with the arms up behind the head. A full squat or a kneel is something else, and a seated or [lying](#lying) [figure](#figure) with parted knees is [spread_legs](#spread_legs).

entries.name: holding_own_leg
entries.description: The character grips one of their own [legs](#legs), hugging it in or keeping it raised. Sitting and [reclining](#reclining) [poses](#poses) are where it shows up most.

entries.name: dorsiflexion
entries.description: The foot or [toes](#toes) bent upward toward the shin, so the ankle creases and the sole shortens. The opposite direction is [plantar_flexion](#plantar_flexion).

entries.name: holding_leg
entries.description: A character takes hold of one of their own [legs](#legs), drawing it up or in towards the chest. When somebody else does the lifting a different [tag](#tag) covers it, and [holding_own_leg](#holding_own_leg) is the near neighbour.

entries.name: holding_own_foot
entries.description: A hand closes around the character's own foot or ankle, usually with a leg drawn up while seated. Massaging, [stretching](#stretching) and idle [poses](#poses) all count.

entries.name: feet_on_chair
entries.description: One or both [feet](#feet) are drawn up onto the very seat the character is [sitting](#sitting) on, [knees](#knees) raised. Thrones, sofas and benches count as much as chairs.

entries.name: feet_on_table
entries.description: The [feet](#feet) are propped up on a [table](#table), a [desk](#desk) or a [kotatsu](#kotatsu), a relaxed or arrogant attitude. The surface being meant for something else is what makes the pose read.

entries.name: hanging_legs
entries.description: Legs left to dangle with the [feet](#feet) clear of the ground, as when a character is lifted, held up or perched somewhere high. It frequently accompanies a marked [height](#height) difference between two figures.

entries.name: foot_dangle
entries.description: Sitting somewhere high enough that the [feet](#feet) [swing](#swing) free with nothing beneath them, plainly unable to reach the ground. Feet [submerged](#submerged) in [liquid](#liquid) belong to [soaking_feet](#soaking_feet) instead.

entries.name: outstretched_legs
entries.description: Both [legs](#legs) held fully straight, making one unbroken line from the hips down. A single extended leg is [outstretched_leg](#outstretched_leg).

entries.name: v_legs
entries.description: Both [legs](#legs) are raised and spread so their full length forms a V above the [torso](#torso), with [knees](#knees) kept nearly straight, most often seen [lying](#lying) on the [back](#back) or mid-kick. Not used for a [standing](#standing) character, where [legs_apart](#legs_apart) applies instead.

entries.name: sitting_split
entries.description: A middle [split](#split) with the [legs](#legs) stretched straight out to either side while the body sits or leans forward onto the [stomach](#stomach). A gymnastic and dance position rather than a [resting](#resting) one.

entries.name: heel_pop
entries.description: The heel lifts out of the [back](#back) of a shoe while the shoe itself stays flat on the ground. A shoe [swinging](#swinging) loose from the [toes](#toes) instead is [shoe_dangle](#shoe_dangle).

entries.name: legs_behind_head
entries.description: The [legs](#legs) are [folded](#folded) up so far that they come to rest behind the head or [neck](#neck). A forward-bending pose that demands real flexibility.

entries.name: knee_to_chest
entries.description: One knee is drawn up until it meets the [torso](#torso), whether the character is seated, [lying](#lying) or crouched. It often reads as guarded, [cold](#cold) or bashful.

entries.name: toes_up
entries.description: The [ball](#ball) of the foot stays on the ground while the [toes](#toes) lift clear of it. Once the whole foot leaves the [floor](#floor), a [leg_up](#leg_up) [tag](#tag) is the right one.

entries.name: side_sitting_split
entries.description: A seated straddle [split](#split) with the [legs](#legs) opened out to either side along the [floor](#floor). Distinguished from a [front-to-back](#front-to-back) split, where one leg goes forward and the other behind.

entries.name: standing_on_three_legs
entries.description: A four-legged [animal](#animal) or [taur](#taur) lifts one leg clear and balances on the remaining three, the many-legged equivalent of [standing_on_one_leg](#standing_on_one_leg).

entries.name: swinging_legs
entries.description: Legs [kicking](#kicking) loosely [back](#back) and forth because the seat is high enough that the [feet](#feet) cannot reach the ground. A relaxed, idle motion typical of [sitting](#sitting) on a wall, [bench](#bench) or [bed](#bed) edge.

entries.name: legs_on_table
entries.description: The [feet](#feet) or whole [legs](#legs) are propped up on a [table](#table) or [desk](#desk). It reads as relaxed, cocky or deliberately bad manners.

entries.name: between_feet
entries.description: Something held or [resting](#resting) in the gap between two [feet](#feet), often with the [soles](#soles) turned inward to grip it. It is usually drawn from low down with the feet nearest the viewer.

entries.name: outstretched_foot
entries.description: One foot pushed out toward the viewer or another character, the leg extended with sole or [toes](#toes) leading. Covers kicks, [teasing](#teasing) prods and a foot held out to be looked at.

entries.name: hand_up
entries.description: A single hand lifted to chest [height](#height) or above, as in a wave, a greeting or a raised palm. Both hands raised is [hands_up](#hands_up), and a hand carried above eye level is [arm_up](#arm_up).

entries.name: arm_up
entries.description: One arm raised to about eye level or higher. Both raised is [arms_up](#arms_up), [reaching](#reaching) forward is [outstretched_arm](#outstretched_arm), and a hand only at shoulder [height](#height) is [hand_up](#hand_up).

entries.name: arms_up
entries.description: Both arms raised to eye level or above. One arm is [arm_up](#arm_up), [reaching](#reaching) forward is [outstretched_arms](#outstretched_arms), and held straight out to the sides is [spread_arms](#spread_arms).

entries.name: hands_up
entries.description: Both hands are lifted to chest [height](#height) or above, as in surrender, [celebration](#celebration) or a wave. A single raised hand is [hand_up](#hand_up), and hands carried above eye level is [arms_up](#arms_up).

entries.name: hand_on_own_hip
entries.description: One hand is [planted](#planted) on the character's own hip with the elbow angled outward, a [casual](#casual) or self-assured stance. Doing it with both hands is [hands_on_own_hips](#hands_on_own_hips).

entries.name: arms_behind_back
entries.description: Both arms held behind the [back](#back), coyly clasped or [bound](#bound) there. Add [bondage](#bondage) when they are tied; one arm alone is [arm_behind_back](#arm_behind_back).

entries.name: arm_support
entries.description: The character carries their own [weight](#weight) on one or both arms, propped on a hand while [sitting](#sitting) or braced while [lying](#lying). Resting an arm without [leaning](#leaning) on it is [arm_rest](#arm_rest).

entries.name: crossed_arms
entries.description: Both arms [folded](#folded) over the front of the body. Read as a tough or haughty stance, a reaction to [cold](#cold), or a woman shielding her chest; add [covering_breasts](#covering_breasts) where that is the intent.

entries.name: outstretched_arms
entries.description: Both arms reach away from the body, forward or upward. A single arm takes [outstretched_arm](#outstretched_arm), and arms opened to the sides also take [spread_arms](#spread_arms).

entries.name: outstretched_arm
entries.description: One arm reaches straight away from the body, [pointing](#pointing) or grasping toward something. Both arms extended is [outstretched_arms](#outstretched_arms).

entries.name: clenched_hand
entries.description: One hand closed into a fist, the fingers pressed into the palm with the thumb over or inside them. Both hands in fists takes [clenched_hands](#clenched_hands).

entries.name: arms_behind_head
entries.description: Both arms [folded](#folded) up behind the character's own head, a relaxed stretch or a pin-up pose. One arm is [arm_behind_head](#arm_behind_head), and arms behind somebody else's head is [arms_around_neck](#arms_around_neck).

entries.name: interlocked_fingers
entries.description: Fingers are laced through one another rather than simply gripped. Add [holding_hands](#holding_hands) when the fingers belong to two [people](#people), and [own_hands_clasped](#own_hands_clasped) when one person does it palm against palm.

entries.name: arm_at_side
entries.description: One arm hangs quietly beside the body while the other is busy, [reaching](#reaching), propped on a hip or behind the head. With both [hanging](#hanging), use [arms_at_sides](#arms_at_sides).

entries.name: clenched_hands
entries.description: Both hands closed tightly into fists, out of determination, anger or tension. A single fist is [clenched_hand](#clenched_hand).

entries.name: arm_behind_back
entries.description: One arm held behind the [back](#back), whether the character puts it there or somebody else does. Both arms is [arms_behind_back](#arms_behind_back), and [bondage](#bondage) belongs with it when the arm is tied.

entries.name: arm_behind_head
entries.description: A single hand or arm tucked behind the character's own head, relaxed or coy. Both arms there is [arms_behind_head](#arms_behind_head).

entries.name: hand_in_pocket
entries.description: Exactly one hand is tucked away in a [pocket](#pocket), the other free. Two hands in two separate pockets is [hands_in_pockets](#hands_in_pockets), and two hands [sharing](#sharing) one pocket is [hands_in_pocket](#hands_in_pocket).

entries.name: hands_on_own_hips
entries.description: Both hands sit on the character's own hips with the elbows bowed outward, the stance called arms akimbo. It reads as confidence, impatience or a [scolding](#scolding); one hand is [hand_on_own_hip](#hand_on_own_hip).

entries.name: reaching
entries.description: A character stretches out a hand, leg, or held object toward something. Usually paired with [outstretched_arm](#outstretched_arm) or [outstretched_hand](#outstretched_hand); when the reach is aimed straight at the viewer, use [reaching_towards_viewer](#reaching_towards_viewer) instead.

entries.name: v_arms
entries.description: Both arms hang in front of the body with the hands meeting low, so the arms trace a V shape, conveying a prim and relaxed stance. A seated character [resting](#resting) hands in the [lap](#lap) is [hands_on_lap](#hands_on_lap) instead, and this differs from spread arms or the classic [victory](#victory) pose.

entries.name: arms_at_sides
entries.description: Both arms hang at rest beside the body, a still and neutral stance. When only one rests there, [arm_at_side](#arm_at_side) applies.

entries.name: hands_in_pockets
entries.description: Both hands are stowed away, one in each of two separate pockets. Where only one hand is pocketed, the [tag](#tag) is [hand_in_pocket](#hand_in_pocket).

entries.name: outstretched_hand
entries.description: A hand held out open toward something, palm up, down or [sideways](#sideways), often [reaching](#reaching) for the viewer. The upper arm may stay near the body; it is the hand that does the reaching.

entries.name: reaching_towards_viewer
entries.description: An arm extends straight toward the viewer as if the character were [reaching](#reaching) out of the picture, frequently drawn with [strong](#strong) [foreshortening](#foreshortening). Combine with [outstretched_arm](#outstretched_arm) and reaching.

entries.name: arm_between_own_legs
entries.description: An arm reaches down between the character's own [thighs](#thighs), typically while [sitting](#sitting) or [kneeling](#kneeling) with the [knees](#knees) held close. Often reads as bashful or self-conscious.

entries.name: spread_arms
entries.description: Both arms held straight out to the sides at shoulder [height](#height), as in a T-pose or a welcoming [gesture](#gesture). Reaching that is less strictly [sideways](#sideways) belongs under [outstretched_arms](#outstretched_arms) instead.

entries.name: open_hand
entries.description: A single hand held with the fingers extended rather than curled, as in a wave or a reach toward the viewer. Use [open_hands](#open_hands) when both are shown that way.

entries.name: arm_under_breasts
entries.description: One upper arm is tucked beneath the [breasts](#breasts), lifting them, while the other arm does something else. Both arms there is [arms_under_breasts](#arms_under_breasts).

entries.name: sheet_grab
entries.description: A hand clutching at the [bed](#bed) sheets, most often shown during [sex](#sex) or a moment of intense feeling. Tag with [bed_sheet](#bed_sheet) where the sheet itself is clearly visible.

entries.name: open_hands
entries.description: Both hands are shown with the fingers spread or extended, as in a shrug, a welcome or a [gesture](#gesture) of surrender. One hand alone takes [open_hand](#open_hand).

entries.name: elbow_rest
entries.description: One or both elbows propped on a surface: a [table](#table), a [ledge](#ledge), a [windowsill](#windowsill), another person. Often joined by chin_rest or [head_rest](#head_rest), and both elbows on a table is [elbows_on_table](#elbows_on_table).

entries.name: arms_under_breasts
entries.description: Both upper arms are tucked beneath the [breasts](#breasts) and push them up, frequently with the arms crossed. One arm there is [arm_under_breasts](#arm_under_breasts).

entries.name: steepled_fingers
entries.description: Hands held together with only the fingertips touching, forming a [steeple](#steeple) shape, the classic scheming [gesture](#gesture). Different from pressed-together prayer hands.

entries.name: arm_rest
entries.description: An arm laid against a surface, an object, another person or the character's own body, in any posture. When the arm carries the body's [weight](#weight), [arm_support](#arm_support) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: w_arms
entries.description: Elbows tucked down and [forearms](#forearms) raised so both arms together form a W shape. The hands may touch in the middle or be held apart.

entries.name: left-handed
entries.description: The character favours the left hand for [writing](#writing), [eating](#eating), drawing or wielding a [weapon](#weapon). Tag it only where the handedness is plainly shown.

entries.name: hands_in_opposite_sleeves
entries.description: Each hand is tucked right into the wide sleeve on the other side, arms [folded](#folded) across the body, as done with a [kimono](#kimono). Hands hidden inside their own sleeves instead is [sleeves_past_fingers](#sleeves_past_fingers).

entries.name: flexing
entries.description: A pose struck to show off muscle, most often a bent arm raised to [display](#display) the bicep. It usually comes with a [muscular](#muscular) build and a confident face.

entries.name: hands_on_lap
entries.description: A seated or [kneeling](#kneeling) character has at least one hand [resting](#resting) in their [lap](#lap), a composed and demure arrangement. A [standing](#standing) [figure](#figure) with the hands together low in front is [v_arms](#v_arms).

entries.name: shading_eyes
entries.description: A hand or object held above the brow to block the [sun](#sun) while looking out. A cap or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) does not count, and it is unrelated to [shaded_face](#shaded_face).

entries.name: curled_fingers
entries.description: Fingers bent inward so that they look curled, stopping short of a closed fist. Often a relaxed or expressive hand shape rather than a deliberate [sign](#sign).

entries.name: cupping_hands
entries.description: Both hands pressed together [palms](#palms) up to make a [bowl](#bowl), ready to hold [liquid](#liquid) or something small. The [two-handed](#two-handed) counterpart of [cupping_hand](#cupping_hand).

entries.name: arm_between_breasts
entries.description: A hand or forearm lies in the cleft between the [breasts](#breasts), the character's own or another person's. The contact usually pushes the breasts together or apart.

entries.name: hand_on_lap
entries.description: A single hand [resting](#resting) on a [lap](#lap), meaning the upward-facing surface of a seated person's [thighs](#thighs). It may be the character's own lap or somebody else's.

entries.name: hands_on_feet
entries.description: Hands [holding](#holding) or [resting](#resting) on [feet](#feet), which may be the character's own or somebody else's. It covers [sitting](#sitting) with the feet clasped as much as [rubbing](#rubbing) another person's.

entries.name: arms_between_legs
entries.description: Both arms are placed between or inside the [legs](#legs), usually while [sitting](#sitting) or crouching with the [knees](#knees) apart. One arm there is [arm_between_legs](#arm_between_legs).

entries.name: \o/
entries.description: Both arms thrown up and outward in [celebration](#celebration), the stick-figure cheer. The whole body reads as the [emoticon](#emoticon) rather than the hands alone.

entries.name: hand_on_ground
entries.description: One hand touches the ground [outdoors](#outdoors), typically while crouching, [kneeling](#kneeling) or [catching](#catching) a fall. With both [palms](#palms) down the [tag](#tag) is [hands_on_ground](#hands_on_ground).

entries.name: hand_rest
entries.description: A hand allowed to settle against a surface, an object, another person or the character's own body, either to relax or to steady themselves. It applies in any posture, [standing](#standing), seated or [lying](#lying).

entries.name: arm_above_head
entries.description: One arm stretched straight up over the head while the other does something else. With both arms raised, [arms_up](#arms_up) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: elbows_on_table
entries.description: Both elbows propped on a tabletop, usually with the hands [holding](#holding) up the chin or [folded](#folded) together. Only one elbow down is [elbow_on_table](#elbow_on_table), and [forearms](#forearms) laid flat are something else.

entries.name: hands_on_ground
entries.description: Both of a character's hands touch the ground, as when down on all fours, crouching or bracing after a stumble. Only one hand down is [hand_on_ground](#hand_on_ground).

entries.name: hand_on_leg
entries.description: A hand [resting](#resting) on a leg without saying whose leg or whose hand. Where the owner is clear, [hand_on_own_leg](#hand_on_own_leg) or [hand_on_another's_leg](#hand_on_another's_leg) says more.

entries.name: arm_between_legs
entries.description: An arm [reaching](#reaching) down between the [legs](#legs), usually with the [knees](#knees) drawn up or the body tipped forward so the elbow meets the [thighs](#thighs). A hand alone there is [hand_between_legs](#hand_between_legs).

entries.name: arm_on_knee
