entries.description: The forearm or elbow rests on the character's own knee, usually while [sitting](#sitting) or crouching. If it lies further up the leg, [arm_on_thigh](#arm_on_thigh) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hand_on_glass
entries.description: At least one hand presses against a pane of [glass](#glass), and the viewpoint may be from either side of it. Windows, [display](#display) cases and shower screens all qualify.

entries.name: hand_on_wall
entries.description: One hand or both touch a wall, whether [leaning](#leaning) on it, feeling along it or pinning somebody against it. The last of these is the [kabedon](#kabedon) setup.

entries.name: ghost_pose
entries.description: Arms held out in front with elbows bent and the hands [hanging](#hanging) limp [palms](#palms) down, the body tipped forward and the head tilted [back](#back). Curled fingers turned outward make it [claw_pose](#claw_pose), and straight arms make it [zombie_pose](#zombie_pose).

entries.name: reaching_towards_another
entries.description: One character stretches an arm toward someone else without necessarily making contact. Often reads as longing, pleading, or an attempt to hold the other person [back](#back).

entries.name: hand_on_floor
entries.description: A character's hand lies flat on an indoor [floor](#floor). Where the arm is actually [carrying](#carrying) the body's [weight](#weight), [arm_support](#arm_support) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: hand_on_table
entries.description: A character rests a hand on a tabletop, either simply placed there or bearing [weight](#weight) as they lean in. Both [palms](#palms) down is [hands_on_table](#hands_on_table).

entries.name: elbow_on_knee
entries.description: One elbow propped on a knee, usually while [sitting](#sitting) or crouching and often with the chin settled into that hand. Reads as thought, [waiting](#waiting) or weariness.

entries.name: hands_in_pocket
entries.description: Both hands pushed into a single [pocket](#pocket), usually the wide front [pouch](#pouch) of a [hoodie](#hoodie) or sweatshirt that opens at either side. When the pocket count is unclear, the plural [hands_in_pockets](#hands_in_pockets) is the safer [choice](#choice).

entries.name: hand_on_railing
entries.description: A hand laid on the rail of a [balcony](#balcony), [bridge](#bridge), staircase or deck. It frequently accompanies [leaning](#leaning) out over the rail to look down.

entries.name: arm_over_head
entries.description: An arm raised and carried above the head, the hand [hanging](#hanging) loose or [resting](#resting) beyond it. Turns up in [stretching](#stretching), [lounging](#lounging) and [sleeping](#sleeping) [poses](#poses).

entries.name: arm_across_waist
entries.description: An arm held straight across the character's own waist or [stomach](#stomach), the hand near the opposite hip. Often the other arm rests or props on it.

entries.name: elbow_on_table
entries.description: A single elbow [resting](#resting) on a tabletop, commonly with the head [leaning](#leaning) into that hand. Both elbows up is [elbows_on_table](#elbows_on_table).

entries.name: hands_on_shoulders
entries.description: Both hands on shoulders without saying whose hands or whose shoulders. Prefer whichever of the own and another's variants actually applies.

entries.name: cross-body_stretch
entries.description: One arm laid flat over the chest at shoulder level while the other hooks it at the elbow and draws it in. A shoulder-loosening move, generally drawn around exercise or a stretch on waking.

entries.name: arms_on_knees
entries.description: Both [forearms](#forearms) laid across the [knees](#knees) while [sitting](#sitting) or crouching, the [torso](#torso) tipped forward over them. A common way to draw somebody [resting](#resting) or [waiting](#waiting).

entries.name: arm_on_own_head
entries.description: A forearm laid across or [resting](#resting) on top of the character's own head, an idle or weary [gesture](#gesture). Using somebody else's head is [arm_on_another's_head](#arm_on_another's_head).

entries.name: arms_on_table
entries.description: Both arms rest on a [table](#table) top, often [folded](#folded) one over the other. A single arm there is [arm_on_table](#arm_on_table), and elbows alone have their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hands_on_floor
entries.description: Both [palms](#palms) flat on an indoor [floor](#floor), [carrying](#carrying) [weight](#weight) while the character crouches, crawls or breaks a fall. It often goes together with [all_fours](#all_fours).

entries.name: arm_on_table
entries.description: One arm lies on a [table](#table) or [counter](#counter), often with the elbow down and the chin propped on the hand. Both arms up there is [arms_on_table](#arms_on_table).

entries.name: cracking_knuckles
entries.description: A character bends or presses the finger [joints](#joints) until they pop, often as a [threat](#threat) before a fight. Wrists, elbows and [knees](#knees) get the same treatment.

entries.name: surprised_arms
entries.description: Both [forearms](#forearms) snap up in front of the chest in a startled [flinch](#flinch), elbows tucked in, often with the hands balled or splayed. The reflex that accompanies a shocked expression.

entries.name: gunbuster_pose
entries.description: A confident stance with the arms [folded](#folded) across the chest and [feet](#feet) [planted](#planted) wide apart, popularised by [giant](#giant) robots rising into frame. Now used for any character striking that unshakeable attitude.

entries.name: victory_pose
entries.description: The stance struck to celebrate winning, usually with arms flung up or a fist held high. Athletes, fighters and game characters strike it at the end of a match.

entries.name: symmetrical_hand_pose
entries.description: Both hands held in matching, mirrored positions, making the same [gesture](#gesture) on either side of the body. Common in [idol](#idol) [poses](#poses) and spell-casting stances.

entries.name: t-pose
entries.description: Arms held straight out to the sides at shoulder [height](#height) with the [legs](#legs) straight and the face blank, the default rest pose for 3D character rigs. Often used as a joke about [unfinished](#unfinished) or [broken](#broken) animation.

entries.name: crossed_wrists
entries.description: One wrist laid directly over the other, whether raised as the Japanese [sign](#sign) for [no](#no), held up to [guard](#guard) the face, or [bound](#bound) together. Different from [crossed_arms](#crossed_arms), where the [forearms](#forearms) fold flat across the chest.

entries.name: elbows_on_knees
entries.description: Both elbows [planted](#planted) on the [knees](#knees) while seated, the upper body tipped forward over them. A slouched, [waiting](#waiting) or brooding posture.

entries.name: arm_across_chest
entries.description: One arm laid horizontally over the character's own chest, the hand often [reaching](#reaching) toward the far shoulder. A closed, guarded [gesture](#gesture) rather than an embrace.

entries.name: cupping_hand
entries.description: One palm turned upward and curved into a shallow [bowl](#bowl), as though to hold [water](#water) or catch something [falling](#falling). A single hand, not two brought together.

entries.name: double_biceps_pose
entries.description: Both arms raised and bent so the [biceps](#biceps) bunch up on each side, the standard bodybuilding [display](#display). Showing off the arms is the whole point of it.

entries.name: hand_on_window
entries.description: A palm pressed to a windowpane, from inside or outside the room. It carries scenes of longing, rain-streaked [glass](#glass) and being shut out.

entries.name: wrists_extended
entries.description: Both hands are bent [back](#back) at the wrists, [palms](#palms) and fingers angled away from the arms. A paired, deliberate pose rather than a [resting](#resting) hand.

entries.name: ghost_hands
entries.description: An ambiguous name that has been used for several different ideas at once. Prefer the exact alternative: [disembodied_hand](#disembodied_hand) for a hand with [no](#no) body, transparent_hand for one you [can](#can) see through, shadow_hands for hallucinated ones, and [ghost_pose](#ghost_pose) for limp [dangling](#dangling) wrists.

entries.name: hands_on_table
entries.description: Both hands flat on a [table](#table) or [desk](#desk), whether bracing there or [leaning](#leaning) forward over it. Interrogations, negotiations and study scenes all use the pose.

entries.name: thumb_in_pocket
entries.description: A thumb hooked into a trouser or [jacket](#jacket) [pocket](#pocket) while the rest of the hand stays outside. A relaxed, offhand way of [standing](#standing).

entries.name: arm_around_leg
entries.description: An arm wrapped around a leg, either the character's own drawn-up knee or somebody else's. Common in seated, crouching and [clinging](#clinging) [poses](#poses).

entries.name: hand_in_mouth
entries.description: Too vague as it stands, since it never says whose mouth is involved. Use [finger_in_own_mouth](#finger_in_own_mouth) for a character's own and [finger_in_another's_mouth](#finger_in_another's_mouth) when the fingers belong to somebody else.

entries.name: holding_over_opposite_shoulder
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) or long object is carried across the body and rested on the far shoulder, so the arm crosses in front of the [neck](#neck). It reads as a braced, guarded stance; with both hands on the shaft, add a [two-handed](#two-handed) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hand_on_mirror
entries.description: A palm laid flat against the surface of a [mirror](#mirror), frequently meeting its own [reflection](#reflection) at the [glass](#glass). It is a [staple](#staple) of pictures about doubles, doubt and self-regard.

entries.name: arm_on_thigh
entries.description: The length of the forearm lies on the character's own thigh, usually while seated and [leaning](#leaning) forward. More than a hand placed on the leg, the arm itself rests there.

entries.name: hands_under_legs
entries.description: Both hands slipped in beneath the [knees](#knees) or [thighs](#thighs) to hold the [legs](#legs) up. It shows up while [sitting](#sitting) with the legs raised or curled toward the body.

entries.name: carry_me
entries.description: Both arms reach upward toward the viewer with open hands, the way a small [child](#child) asks to be lifted. The appeal is aimed out of the picture rather than at another character.

entries.name: cord_pull
entries.description: A character tugs a [hanging](#hanging) cord, whether a [ceiling](#ceiling) light's, a [window](#window) blind's or a [bus](#bus) stop signal's. The pull itself is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: wrist_extended
entries.description: One hand is bent [back](#back) at the wrist, lifting the palm and fingers away from the natural line of the arm. It is a stylised, often elegant hand position.

entries.name: arms_on_head
entries.description: Both arms raised and [resting](#resting) on top of the character's own head, hands often laced together. An idle, unguarded posture.

entries.name: palmar_flexion
entries.description: The hand hangs loosely forward at the wrist, bent toward the palm side. It reads as anything from a coy 'oh, stop it' or a [beckoning](#beckoning) wave to [disgust](#disgust), showing off a [ring](#ring), or a puppet's slackness.

entries.name: airplane_arms
entries.description: Both arms are stretched straight out to the sides in imitation of a plane, usually while [running](#running) or [leaning](#leaning) into a turn. Children and playful characters do it, and the Japanese name comes from the droning [sound](#sound) effect that goes with it.

entries.name: head_arms
entries.description: An arm lies across the top of a head — the character's own bent up over the [crown](#crown), or somebody else's laid there. The head takes its [weight](#weight).

entries.name: paw_up
entries.description: A four-legged [creature](#creature) holds one front paw clear of the ground while [standing](#standing) or [sitting](#sitting), the way a [pointing](#pointing) [dog](#dog) freezes with a foreleg lifted.

entries.name: hand_on_chair
entries.description: A hand braced on the [back](#back), arm or seat of a [chair](#chair). It shows up when a character leans on the furniture, pulls it out or is about to lower themselves into it.

entries.name: dorsiflexion_(wrist)
entries.description: The hand bent sharply [back](#back) at the wrist, either [hanging](#hanging) loose or pressed against something. Depending on context it reads as refusal, [beckoning](#beckoning), a shrug of confusion, a mannered attitude, or simply shading the eyes.

entries.name: thumb_in_beltline
entries.description: A thumb hooked over the top edge of a waistband and [resting](#resting) at the hip. It reads either as a cocky, [casual](#casual) stance or as the first move in taking the garment off; a thumb dipping lower makes it a pull instead.

entries.name: v
entries.description: The index and middle finger held up in a V, the classic peace [sign](#sign) made when [posing](#posing) for a photo. If the thumb is extended too, [w](#w) is the [tag](#tag) to use instead; the round peace [emblem](#emblem) is a separate symbol entirely.

entries.name: pointing
entries.description: A character extends the index finger to direct attention at something. Add a [target](#target) [tag](#tag) such as [pointing_at_viewer](#pointing_at_viewer) or [pointing_up](#pointing_up); a raised finger that indicates nothing in particular is a different tag.

entries.name: index_finger_raised
entries.description: One index finger held up with the rest of the hand closed, and [no](#no) [pointing](#pointing) involved. It reads as making a point or as an [idea](#idea) arriving.

entries.name: double_v
entries.description: The V or peace [sign](#sign) made with both hands at the same time. A trademark pose for several bright, cheerful characters.

entries.name: paw_pose
entries.description: Hands raised near the chest or face with the wrists bent and the fingers loosely curled to [mimic](#mimic) [animal](#animal) paws, often with a [nyan](#nyan) [sound](#sound) effect beside them. Related hand [shapes](#shapes) are [claw_pose](#claw_pose), [ghost_pose](#ghost_pose) and [zombie_pose](#zombie_pose).

entries.name: waving
entries.description: A hand or arm raised and swung as a greeting or farewell, a hello or a [goodbye](#goodbye). Ocean [waves](#waves) are tagged separately.

entries.name: heart_hands
entries.description: Both hands are brought together so fingers and thumbs [outline](#outline) a [heart](#heart). A heart made with one hand alone is a finger heart.

entries.name: waving_arm
entries.description: One arm swung about to call someone over, wave hello or say [goodbye](#goodbye). Frantic [flailing](#flailing) counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: claw_pose
entries.description: A hand held up, usually near the face, fingers spread and curled like [claws](#claws) with the palm turned outward. Used as a [fighting](#fighting) stance, a [threat](#threat) to grab or a playful cat-like [gesture](#gesture); [paw_pose](#paw_pose) keeps the hands loosely closed instead.

entries.name: w
entries.description: A hand [sign](#sign) with three fingers extended, or two fingers plus the thumb, forming a W. When only the index and middle finger are up it is [v](#v) instead.

entries.name: salute
entries.description: A hand raised in greeting or respect, the [military](#military) hand-to-brow salute or a two-finger, vulcan or straight-arm variant. A [sideways](#sideways) V held by the eye is also tagged as a salute.

entries.name: thumbs_up
entries.description: A raised thumb, with one hand or both, as a [sign](#sign) of approval or a job [well](#well) done. Add [grin](#grin) or [smile](#smile) for the usual accompanying expression.

entries.name: pointing_at_viewer
entries.description: A character's finger is aimed straight at the viewer, often while also [looking_at_viewer](#looking_at_viewer). A [weapon](#weapon) aimed at the viewer instead is [aiming_at_viewer](#aiming_at_viewer).

entries.name: fox_shadow_puppet
entries.description: A hand [sign](#sign) with thumb, middle and [ring](#ring) fingers pinched together and the index and little fingers raised, [throwing](#throwing) a fox-shaped [silhouette](#silhouette). Kitsune characters make it constantly; do not confuse it with the raised [horns](#horns) of the [rock](#rock) [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: pinky_out
entries.description: The little finger held out straight while the others curl around a [cup](#cup) or an object, the stereotyped genteel way of [holding](#holding) a [teacup](#teacup). The same finger position in any other context counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: \m/
entries.description: Thumb, index and little finger extended while the middle two fold to the palm, the sign-language [gesture](#gesture) for love. Tucking the thumb in gives [\n/](#\n/), and [pushing](#pushing) the fingers forward makes a [fox](#fox) [shadow](#shadow) [puppet](#puppet).

entries.name: shushing
entries.description: One index finger held upright against the [lips](#lips) while the rest of the hand curls closed, asking for quiet. Often paired with a knowing look toward the viewer; a spoken "shh" may accompany it.

entries.name: pointing_at_self
entries.description: A character points at their own face or chest, typically a 'who, me?' [gesture](#gesture) or a proud self-introduction. Tag [pointing](#pointing) alongside it.

entries.name: v_over_eye
entries.description: A V [sign](#sign) held up to the face with one eye [peeking](#peeking) through between the two fingers. Most often the ordinary [victory](#victory) [gesture](#gesture), though similar two-finger [shapes](#shapes) count too.

entries.name: pointing_up
entries.description: A finger raised to point at the [sky](#sky) or [ceiling](#ceiling), often with the eyes [following](#following) it. Tag [pointing](#pointing) alongside it; an upright finger making [no](#no) such indication is a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: middle_finger
entries.description: Raising the middle finger with the [back](#back) of the hand toward someone, the Western obscene [gesture](#gesture). Less severe in Japan, though it still reads as open defiance.

entries.name: finger_gun
entries.description: The hand is aimed at someone as a pistol, index finger out and thumb cocked upward; some characters extend two fingers instead. Where the hand genuinely shoots, the [tag](#tag) is [finger_cannon](#finger_cannon).

entries.name: 4-finger_heart_hands
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) shaped with only four fingers, usually the thumbs and index fingers or the index and middle ones, while the rest stay stretched or curled. Judge whether those other fingers are merely relaxed or curving into the shape too.

entries.name: rabbit_pose
entries.description: Both hands held flat on top of the head with fingers together, [imitating](#imitating) a pair of [rabbit](#rabbit) ears, usually as a cute or flirtatious [gesture](#gesture). A V [sign](#sign) held up behind someone else's head instead is [bunny_ears_prank](#bunny_ears_prank).

Middle and [ring](#ring) fingers pressed together while the index and little fingers angle away from them. It is neither the [fox](#fox) [shadow](#shadow) [puppet](#puppet) nor the vulcan [salute](#salute), which parts the hand down the middle.

entries.name: blowing_kiss
entries.description: A [kiss](#kiss) pressed to one's own hand and then blown toward somebody, offered as flirtation or farewell. One_eye_closed and a drawn [heart](#heart) often accompany it.

entries.name: praying
entries.description: A character addresses a deity, hands clasped or [palms](#palms) pressed together, often with closed eyes and a solemn face. Also used for a prayer-like wish or plea.

entries.name: ok_sign
entries.description: Thumb and index finger meet at the tips to form a [ring](#ring) while the remaining fingers stay raised. Do not confuse it with the [money](#money) [gesture](#gesture), where the hand lies flat and the ring faces away from the person making it.

entries.name: four-finger_heart_hands
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) shape formed with both hands using four fingers rather than the thumb-and-forefinger version. Idols and photo [poses](#poses) favour it.

entries.name: heart_hands_duo
entries.description: Two characters each give one hand so that a single [heart](#heart) forms between them. If only one of them plays along, use [heart_hands_failure](#heart_hands_failure).

entries.name: beckoning
entries.description: A hand [gesture](#gesture) inviting somebody nearer: fingers curled toward oneself, the index finger crooked, the hand waved downward knuckles up in the Japanese manner, or a hand [patting](#patting) a seat. It often goes with [looking_at_viewer](#looking_at_viewer).

entries.name: pointing_at_another
entries.description: A character points a finger at another character in the picture, whether accusing, choosing, or [calling](#calling) them out. Tag [pointing](#pointing) alongside it.

entries.name: finger_heart
entries.description: One hand crosses index finger over thumb so their meeting point makes a small [heart](#heart), a [gesture](#gesture) spread by K-pop performers. Only one hand does it; a heart built from two hands is [heart_hands](#heart_hands).

entries.name: index_fingers_together
entries.description: The tips of both index fingers poked together in front of the body, a fidget of nerves or embarrassment, sometimes put on to look sweet. It is neither [heart_hands](#heart_hands) nor the [fusion](#fusion) dance.

entries.name: ily_hand_sign
entries.description: A hand raised with thumb, index and little finger out while the middle two stay [folded](#folded), the sign-language shorthand for "I love you". It is thrown at the viewer or a companion as an [affectionate](#affectionate) flourish.

entries.name: raised_fist
entries.description: A clenched fist is held up in the air, whether as a cheer, a rallying [gesture](#gesture), or a punch thrown skyward. Combine with [arm_up](#arm_up); [hitting](#hitting) an actual [target](#target) is [punching](#punching) instead.

entries.name: double_fox_shadow_puppet
entries.description: The [fox](#fox) hand [sign](#sign), middle and [ring](#ring) fingers meeting the thumb to make a [snout](#snout), formed with both hands at once.

entries.name: double_w
entries.description: The [w](#w) hand [sign](#sign), index and little finger up with the middle fingers [folded](#folded) down, made with both hands. Usually held up beside the face.

entries.name: clapping
entries.description: Palms struck together in applause, in [celebration](#celebration) or to keep a rhythm. Distinct from [own_hands_together](#own_hands_together), where the hands merely rest against each other.

entries.name: v_over_mouth
entries.description: A V [sign](#sign) held against the mouth. When the two fingers instead lie horizontally across the [lips](#lips) with the [tongue](#tongue) out between them, that reads as the separate [cunnilingus_gesture](#cunnilingus_gesture) rather than this.

entries.name: hat_tip
entries.description: The wearer lifts or touches the brim of a [hat](#hat) in greeting or acknowledgement, a courtesy carried over from older manners.

entries.name: akanbe
entries.description: A finger pulls one lower eyelid down while the [tongue](#tongue) sticks out, the childish taunt that means roughly "so there". Both halves belong to the [gesture](#gesture), and it appears in French-speaking countries with its own phrase attached.

entries.name: offering_hand
entries.description: A hand is stretched out toward the viewer, [waiting](#waiting) to be taken for a lift up, a dance or simply to be led away. Two hands held out reads instead as [incoming_hug](#incoming_hug) or [outstretched_arms](#outstretched_arms).

entries.name: heart_in_heart_hands
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) symbol appears within the [space](#space) framed by a [heart_hands](#heart_hands) [gesture](#gesture), so both the hands and the drawn heart are present.

entries.name: \n/
entries.description: Index and little finger raised while the thumb pins the middle two down, the [horns](#horns) thrown at [heavy](#heavy) metal concerts. Extend the thumb and it becomes [\m/](#\m/); push the fingers forward into a muzzle and it is a [fox](#fox) [shadow](#shadow) [puppet](#puppet).

entries.name: finger_frame
entries.description: Thumbs and index fingers of both hands brought together into a [rectangle](#rectangle) and held up to look through. The stock [gesture](#gesture) of photographers, illustrators and painters sizing up a shot.

entries.name: two-finger_salute
entries.description: A [casual](#casual) [salute](#salute) with the index and middle fingers, and often the thumb, raised to the brow, a friendly [gesture](#gesture) common in anime. Not the palm-inward gesture of the same name used elsewhere as an [insult](#insult).

entries.name: gyaru_v
entries.description: An [upside-down](#upside-down) V [sign](#sign) made with the arm extended and the palm turned outward or down, from Japanese gal culture.

entries.name: index_fingers_raised
entries.description: Both index fingers, or several, held up at once with the other fingers [folded](#folded). The [two-handed](#two-handed) form of [index_finger_raised](#index_finger_raised).

entries.name: pointing_forward
entries.description: A character points straight ahead of themselves, from their own [perspective](#perspective), as when [giving](#giving) a direction or ordering a charge. Tag [pointing](#pointing) alongside it.

entries.name: kuji-in
entries.description: Hands held in a [ritual](#ritual) seal, fingers laced together or pointed upward, as [ninja](#ninja), monks and [shrine](#shrine) maidens do when [working](#working) a technique. Chanting or a visible magical effect often goes with it.

entries.name: double_\m/
entries.description: The [horns](#horns) hand [sign](#sign) thrown with both hands at once. Strongly tied to one [idol](#idol) character's [catchphrase](#catchphrase) pose.

entries.name: shrugging
entries.description: Shoulders lifted toward the ears, often with [palms](#palms) turned upward beside them. Reads as not knowing, not caring, or a resigned dismissal of whatever was just said.

entries.name: waving_arms
entries.description: Both arms swung about at once, whether in greeting or in panicked [flapping](#flapping). The two-armed counterpart to a single raised arm.

entries.name: handshake
entries.description: Two [people](#people) [clasp](#clasp) right hands in greeting, agreement or parting, sometimes pumping them up and down. The joined hands are usually what the picture is about.

entries.name: gesture
entries.description: A movement of the hands or body made to express something or to underline speech. It is the [umbrella](#umbrella) term, so the specific [sign](#sign) such as [v](#v) or [pointing](#pointing) is normally tagged as [well](#well).

entries.name: half-heart_hands
entries.description: One hand alone shaping half a [heart](#heart), meant to be completed by a partner or left comically [unfinished](#unfinished). Not for the two-person or three-person versions of the [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: fist_pump
entries.description: A clenched fist driven upward in triumph, either bent at the elbow or thrown straight overhead. The [gesture](#gesture) of a win or of a burst of resolve.

entries.name: thumbs_down
entries.description: A hand held out with the thumb pointed at the ground, the [sign](#sign) for [rejection](#rejection), [failure](#failure) or a bad end coming. It mirrors [thumbs_up](#thumbs_up), and in Japanese works it lands harder than in the West, closer to telling somebody to drop dead.

entries.name: heart_hands_failure
entries.description: Two characters go for a joint [heart](#heart), but one answers with a different [sign](#sign) — a thumbs-up, a peace sign — so the shape never closes. The mismatch is the joke.

entries.name: x_fingers
entries.description: The index fingers of both hands crossed to make an X. In Japanese body language it signals refusal or prohibition, and at a [restaurant](#restaurant) [table](#table) it [can](#can) be used to ask for the bill; fingers merely held side by side is a different [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: pointing_down
entries.description: At least one finger aimed downward, sending attention below: at the ground, at something held, or off the bottom edge of the frame.

entries.name: x_arms
entries.description: Both arms held up and crossed in front of the chest so the [forearms](#forearms) form an X. In Japanese body language the [sign](#sign) reads as [no](#no), wrong or forbidden; because it is a deliberate [gesture](#gesture), the ordinary [crossed_arms](#crossed_arms) [tag](#tag) does not apply.

entries.name: crossed_fingers
entries.description: Index and middle finger twisted over one another on a single hand, the [sign](#sign) for hoping something goes [well](#well). Held behind the [back](#back) it means the opposite: a lie in progress, or a promise the [speaker](#speaker) will not keep.

entries.name: penetration_gesture
entries.description: A hand [sign](#sign) miming [sex](#sex), one index finger pushed in and out of a [ring](#ring) made with the other hand. Made inside the picture as a taunt or a proposition.

entries.name: w_over_eye
entries.description: The hand [shapes](#shapes) a W held up beside or across the eye, a [posing](#posing) [habit](#habit) borrowed from [idol](#idol) photos. The [letter](#letter) shape is what counts, not which fingers form it.

entries.name: heart_arms
entries.description: Both arms are raised and curved over the head so they meet in the [outline](#outline) of a [heart](#heart). The whole-arm version of the small finger heart.

entries.name: finger_counting
entries.description: A number held up on the fingers: one raised digit or a thumb, a V for two, an open palm for five, both hands for ten. Artists use it for countdowns, anniversaries and milestone celebrations.

entries.name: toasting_(gesture)
entries.description: Glasses lifted, and often knocked together, to mark an occasion or honour somebody. Normally paired with a shouted kanpai, prost or cheers.

entries.name: v_over_head
entries.description: The two-finger V [sign](#sign) is made with the arm raised so the hand sits above the head rather than beside the face, a celebratory or [posing](#posing) [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: pinky_swear
entries.description: Two [people](#people) [hook](#hook) their little fingers together to seal a promise. A quiet [gesture](#gesture) of trust, sometimes [standing](#standing) in for a less obvious show of affection.

entries.name: inward_v
entries.description: Two fingers raised in a V with the [back](#back) of the hand turned outward, the [mirror](#mirror) of the ordinary peace [sign](#sign). It reads as an obscenity in Britain, and with the [tongue](#tongue) pushed between the fingers it becomes a sexual one.

entries.name: horns_pose
entries.description: Both hands are raised above the head with the index fingers pointed up, [imitating](#imitating) a pair of [horns](#horns). It is not the two-fingered [sign](#sign) of the horns, which is made at chest [height](#height).

entries.name: snapping_fingers
entries.description: Thumb and middle finger flicked against each other to make a sharp click. It usually marks a command, a sudden [idea](#idea) or a bit of [casual](#casual) style.

entries.name: mudra
entries.description: Ritual hand positions taken from Hindu and Buddhist practice. In manga they most often appear as the nine seals an [onmyouji](#onmyouji) forms while reciting the matching chant.

entries.name: pointing_to_the_side
entries.description: A finger extended [sideways](#sideways), [carrying](#carrying) the viewer's eye left or right across the frame. Often used to single out a companion, an object, or something just out of shot.

entries.name: bed_invitation
entries.description: Someone [lying](#lying) under a [blanket](#blanket) lifts it to one side, offering the empty [space](#space) beside them to another character or to the viewer. The [gesture](#gesture) is the whole of it; nothing need be exposed for the [tag](#tag) to apply.

entries.name: knocking
entries.description: Knuckles rapped against a [door](#door) or another hard surface to announce oneself. It is usually drawn mid-motion, sometimes with small [sound](#sound) marks in the air.

entries.name: fist_in_hand
entries.description: One clenched fist set into the opposite open palm, held about chest [height](#height). It reads as squaring up before a fight; the formal martial-arts [salute](#salute) is a [gesture](#gesture) of its own.

entries.name: money_gesture
entries.description: The Japanese hand [sign](#sign) for cash: thumb and forefinger closed into a coin-sized loop. Reserve it for the flat, palm-down version turned toward the viewer, since held upright and facing inward the same shape reads as the ok sign.

entries.name: ok_sign_over_eye
entries.description: The [ring](#ring) made by thumb and forefinger is held up against an eye, which peers out through the [hole](#hole).

entries.name: middle_w
entries.description: A hand [sign](#sign) with the index, middle and [ring](#ring) fingers raised while the thumb and little finger stay [folded](#folded), read as a W shape or as the number three.

entries.name: double_thumbs_up
entries.description: Both thumbs jabbed upward at once for emphatic approval. Generally paired with a wide [grin](#grin) or a confident stance.

entries.name: double_middle_finger
entries.description: Both middle fingers thrust up at once instead of just one. An emphatic and usually [comic](#comic) obscene [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: shaka_sign
entries.description: Thumb and little finger [stuck](#stuck) out with the middle three fingers curled into the palm. Read as a surfer's greeting, as a mimed telephone when held to the ear, or as the number six in China.

entries.name: bent_v
entries.description: The V [sign](#sign) made with one or both fingers curled or drooping rather than held straight. It reads as bashfulness or low confidence, and sometimes [plain](#plain) exhaustion; in some countries the same shape is a scout [salute](#salute) meant to look like ears.

entries.name: finger_gun_to_head
entries.description: The improvised pistol is turned on oneself, fingertip at the [temple](#temple) or [forehead](#forehead). It reads as exasperation, gallows humour or bravado rather than a real [threat](#threat).

entries.name: calling
entries.description: Getting someone's attention across a distance, [shouting](#shouting) a name or [waving](#waving) them over, usually with the mouth open and one arm raised. Speaking into a telephone is a different matter and takes its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: double_finger_gun
entries.description: One character forms the finger [gun](#gun) shape with both hands at once, often aimed at somebody. Reads as breezy confidence rather than as a [threat](#threat).

entries.name: flick
entries.description: A finger snapped out from under the thumb to strike something in a quick tap. It [can](#can) sting a [forehead](#forehead) as mild [punishment](#punishment), send a small object skidding, or flip a [lid](#lid) open.

entries.name: heart_arms_duo
entries.description: Two characters each raise one arm, and the two curves close into a single [heart](#heart) above them.

entries.name: vitarka_mudra
entries.description: A Buddhist [teaching](#teaching) [gesture](#gesture): thumb and index finger meeting in a [ring](#ring), remaining fingers extended and the palm turned outward. It looks much like the ok [sign](#sign) but carries religious meaning.

entries.name: groping_motion
entries.description: Both hands held up with fingers curled as if [squeezing](#squeezing) something, miming a grope. A [comic](#comic) signal of lecherous intent, often paired with a waki waki [sound](#sound) effect; the claw pose looks similar but reads differently.

entries.name: bunny_ears_prank
entries.description: Two fingers held up in a V behind somebody's head so they appear to [sprout](#sprout) [rabbit](#rabbit) ears. The victim is normally [unaware](#unaware); the same shape raised over one's own head is the rabbit pose.

entries.name: dojikko_pose
entries.description: A wink and a stuck-out [tongue](#tongue) while [rapping](#rapping) oneself lightly on the head, the standard oops [gesture](#gesture). A hand behind the head or a V [sign](#sign) instead makes it [tehepero](#tehepero).

entries.name: taunting
entries.description: A character provokes someone with a deliberate [gesture](#gesture) or expression, such as a stuck-out [tongue](#tongue), a pulled-down eyelid or a [beckoning](#beckoning) hand thrown at an opponent. The needling is aimed either at another character or straight at the viewer.

entries.name: patting_lap
entries.description: A seated character taps their own thigh, inviting somebody to sit there or lay their head down. The offer is what the [tag](#tag) names; whether it is taken up is another matter.

entries.name: vulcan_salute
entries.description: An open palm raised with the fingers [split](#split) between middle and [ring](#ring) finger and the thumb held wide. Known from a science-fiction series and treated as a variant of the [v](#v) [sign](#sign).

entries.name: bras_d'honneur
entries.description: One arm is bent sharply upward while the other hand grips its bicep or is tucked where the arm folds. Most of the world reads the [gesture](#gesture) as an obscenity on a par with the middle finger, but in Japanese work it usually means [flexing](#flexing) and resolve.

entries.name: fig_sign
entries.description: A fist with the thumb pushed out between the index and middle fingers. Its meaning shifts by country, from a luck charm to a crude dismissal; in these pictures it usually reads as a proposition.

entries.name: sign_language
entries.description: Communication through the hand [shapes](#shapes), positions and [facial](#facial) [expressions](#expressions) of an actual signed language, generally shown from a deaf character. Casual hand signs and pop-culture gestures like the [fox](#fox) [shadow](#shadow) [puppet](#puppet) do not count.

entries.name: hands_clasped_in_delight
entries.description: Both hands brought together in front of the chest in a rush of joy, [palms](#palms) pressed or fingers loosely interlaced. A beaming face nearly always comes with it.

entries.name: double_finger_heart
entries.description: The small thumb-and-forefinger [heart](#heart) made with each hand at the same time. Two [people](#people) contributing one hand each does not count.

entries.name: hand_over_heart
entries.description: A flat palm laid on the chest over the [heart](#heart), the [gesture](#gesture) of oaths, anthems and declarations of sincerity. It also serves for a moment of relief.

entries.name: waving_hands
entries.description: Hands raised with fingers spread, moving from side to side. Read as either a greeting or a hurried refusal.

entries.name: raised_fists
entries.description: Both hands are closed and raised, either held level with the chest in a [fighting](#fighting) [guard](#guard) or thrust overhead in triumph or protest. Use the singular [gesture](#gesture) tags when only one arm is lifted.

entries.name: palm-fist_greeting
entries.description: A Chinese [salute](#salute) made by pressing one fist into the opposite open palm at chest or [stomach](#stomach) [height](#height), usually with a [bow](#bow). The everyday form cups the fist with the fingers; the martial-arts version keeps the covering hand flat.

entries.name: dab_(dance)
entries.description: The head dropped into the crook of one raised bent arm while the other arm points away in the same direction. A brief dance fad, now drawn mostly as a [gag](#gag).

entries.name: ganbaru_pose
entries.description: Both fists clenched and raised to chest [height](#height), the standard [sign](#sign) of determination and [cheering](#cheering) someone on. Usually paired with a bright, resolute expression.

entries.name: finger_wagging
entries.description: A raised index finger swung from side to side in refusal or reproach. Motion lines or animation make it [plain](#plain); otherwise look for the two-finger L shape or a thumb [folded](#folded) across the middle finger.

entries.name: double_\n/
entries.description:
Both hands flung up in the [
/](#
/) shape, the arms framing the head in a small burst of [celebration](#celebration). Doing it with a single hand is [plain](#plain) 
/.

entries.name: three-finger_salute
entries.description: A [salute](#salute) given with three fingers raised, most often the thumb, index and middle, the rest [folded](#folded) down. Scouting movements and several national services use the [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: double_ok_sign
entries.description: The thumb-and-forefinger [ring](#ring) formed with both hands at the same time. Often held up beside the face in a bright, approving pose.

entries.name: dog_shadow_puppet
entries.description: Fingers [folded](#folded) so the hand throws a dog-shaped [shadow](#shadow), thumb and fingers making the [snout](#snout) and a flopping ear. Cast against a wall or a lit [screen](#screen).

entries.name: back_turned
entries.description: The character has turned away so that the viewer sees their [back](#back). Add [looking_back](#looking_back) when the head is twisted round toward the [camera](#camera).

entries.name: head_tilt
entries.description: The head leans clearly to one side, the usual inquisitive or cute [gesture](#gesture). Use it only for a noticeable tilt; a head tipped backwards is [head_back](#head_back).

entries.name: facing_viewer
entries.description: The face points at the [camera](#camera) while the eyes are closed, covered or aimed elsewhere. Open eyes meeting the viewer's make it [looking_at_viewer](#looking_at_viewer); this is about the direction of the face, not the gaze.

entries.name: head_rest
entries.description: A character props head or chin against something — their own hands, a companion, a piece of furniture.

entries.name: facing_away
entries.description: The subject is turned a full half [circle](#circle) from the [camera](#camera), so only the [back](#back) of the head shows. It often accompanies [from_behind](#from_behind). A [sideways](#sideways) turn does not count, nor does a background [figure](#figure) who happens to be turned around.

entries.name: facing_another
entries.description: A character is turned toward somebody else with the eyes closed or covered. Once the eyes are open and [resting](#resting) on the other person, use [looking_at_another](#looking_at_another).

entries.name: turning_head
entries.description: The head is rotated to one side or [back](#back) over the shoulder, away from the direction the body faces. Often paired with [looking_back](#looking_back) or a [sideways](#sideways) gaze.

entries.name: facing_to_the_side
entries.description: The head turns to the character's own side with the eyes shut or covered while the body stays put. A whole body turned side-on to the [camera](#camera) is [from_side](#from_side), and the open-eyed version is [looking_to_the_side](#looking_to_the_side).

entries.name: head_back
entries.description: The head is tipped backwards so the underside of the chin faces the viewer. It reads as looking up at the [sky](#sky), or as the [arch](#arch) of a climax.

entries.name: head_down
entries.description: The head is tipped forward, chin toward the chest. It reads as dejection, a [bow](#bow), or simply looking at the ground.

entries.name: head_on_hand
entries.description: A character props their own head on a hand with the arm [carrying](#carrying) the [weight](#weight), the posture of boredom at a [desk](#desk). Not a severed head being held, and not a hand placed under someone else's chin.

entries.name: shoulder_peek
entries.description: A face appears from behind someone's shoulder, only partly visible past the body [standing](#standing) in front. A character simply turning to look [back](#back) over their own shoulder is [looking_back](#looking_back) instead.

entries.name: facing_up
entries.description: The face is tilted upward, the eyes closed or raised with it. Seen when a character gazes at the [sky](#sky), catches [rain](#rain) or is lost in feeling; a far more extreme tilt is [head_back](#head_back).

entries.name: facing_down
entries.description: The face points toward the ground with the eyes closed or unseen. Compare [head_down](#head_down), which is about the tilt of the head itself. Dejection or concentration is the usual [reading](#reading).

entries.name: facing_ahead
entries.description: The face points straight forward from the character's own body while the eyes are shut or blocked. Direction is measured from the character, not the [camera](#camera); turned toward the viewer it becomes [facing_viewer](#facing_viewer).

entries.name: shaking_head
entries.description: The head swings from side to side, usually to say [no](#no) or to shake off disbelief. Motion lines or a doubled [outline](#outline) show that it is moving.

entries.name: cheek_rest
entries.description: A character props a cheek against a hand, an arm or a surface and lets the head lean into the support. The posture reads as boredom, daydreaming or half-hearted attention.

entries.name: head_on_table
entries.description: The head is put down flat on a [table](#table) or [desk](#desk), cheek or [forehead](#forehead) against the surface. Exhaustion, [defeat](#defeat), boredom or sleep, depending on what else is going on.

entries.name: head_on_arm
entries.description: The head is laid down on an arm for support — [folded](#folded) on a [table](#table), on a [pillow](#pillow), or against a companion's arm. Tiredness, dozing or idle rest.

entries.name: three_quarter_profile
entries.description: The head turns nearly to the side, but far enough toward the viewer that a sliver of the far eye and brow still shows. It sits between a full [profile](#profile) and an ordinary three-quarter view.

entries.name: facing_back
entries.description: The head is turned toward what lies behind the character, but the eyes are shut or otherwise blocked. With open eyes the same turn is [looking_back](#looking_back).

entries.name: nodding
entries.description: The head dips up and down in agreement. Motion lines or a small mark beside the head usually convey the movement.

entries.name: head_on_knees
entries.description: The head is lowered onto [knees](#knees), either one's own drawn up and hugged or another person's [lap](#lap). A curled, withdrawn or [sleepy](#sleepy) posture.

entries.name: holding_weapon
entries.description: Any kind of [weapon](#weapon) is held in the hand. Common types have tags of their own such as [holding_sword](#holding_sword), [holding_gun](#holding_gun), [holding_knife](#holding_knife), [holding_axe](#holding_axe) and [holding_polearm](#holding_polearm); for rarer arms, pair this [tag](#tag) with the weapon's own name.

entries.name: holding_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) of any kind is held, [katana](#katana) and [rapier](#rapier) included, drawn or still in its [scabbard](#scabbard). It counts as [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon), and the stance runs from [casual](#casual) to mid-strike.

entries.name: holding_gun
entries.description: A firearm of any size, from a [pocket](#pocket) pistol to a [rifle](#rifle), is held in the hands. Toy [water](#water) guns are excluded and take [holding_water_gun](#holding_water_gun) instead.

entries.name: dual_wielding
entries.description: One [weapon](#weapon) held in each hand, usually two of the same kind. When the two differ, [asymmetrical_dual_wielding](#asymmetrical_dual_wielding) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: holding_staff
entries.description: A [staff](#staff) is held: a wizard's [magic](#magic) staff, a monk's [walking](#walking) staff or a [plain](#plain) bo. A shafted [weapon](#weapon) with a blade on the end is [holding_polearm](#holding_polearm).

entries.name: holding_knife
entries.description: A [knife](#knife) is in the hand, [kitchen](#kitchen) or combat alike, gripped for [cutting](#cutting) or held point-forward as a [threat](#threat). A [dagger](#dagger) meant purely for [fighting](#fighting) has [holding_dagger](#holding_dagger) instead.

entries.name: holding_polearm
entries.description: A [polearm](#polearm) is held: a [spear](#spear), [lance](#lance), [halberd](#halberd) or [naginata](#naginata). It counts as [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon), and the specific arm should be tagged alongside.

entries.name: holding_trident
entries.description: A three-pronged [spear](#spear) is gripped, the arm of sea gods, gladiators and devils alike. Fantasy and mythological scenes, where it doubles as a mark of who the character is.

entries.name: aiming
entries.description: A [gun](#gun), [bow](#bow) or other ranged [weapon](#weapon) is held on a [target](#target), or the stance makes [plain](#plain) that the character has something in their sights. Levelled out of the picture at the reader it becomes [aiming_at_viewer](#aiming_at_viewer).

entries.name: weapon_on_back
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) carried slung or strapped across the [back](#back), most often a [sword](#sword) or [rifle](#rifle); [tag](#tag) that weapon too. When it's held behind the back by hand instead, use [weapon_behind_back](#weapon_behind_back).

entries.name: holding_bow_(weapon)
entries.description: An [archery](#archery) [bow](#bow) is in hand, drawn to shoot or simply carried. It counts as [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon); the bow that plays a [violin](#violin) is [holding_bow_(music)](#holding_bow_(music)).

entries.name: trigger_discipline
entries.description: A character holds a firearm with the index finger [resting](#resting) along the frame or trigger [guard](#guard) instead of on the trigger itself. Does not apply when the finger sits inside the guard, or when the [gun](#gun) is gripped somewhere other than the [handle](#handle).

entries.name: weapon_over_shoulder
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) rested across one or both shoulders while held, such as a [sword](#sword) or bat propped casually. Add the specific weapon [tag](#tag) alongside.

entries.name: holding_shield
entries.description: A [shield](#shield) of any type is visibly held, raised in defence or carried at the side. It pairs naturally with a [weapon](#weapon) in the other hand.

entries.name: holding_axe
entries.description: An [axe](#axe) of any size sits in the hand, from a hatchet to a [two-handed](#two-handed) [battle](#battle) axe. Add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) when it is being wielded as one.

entries.name: reverse_grip
entries.description: A blade held so it points down from the little-finger side of the fist instead of up from the thumb side. A close-quarters knife-fighting grip that reads as aggressive or stealthy.

entries.name: holding_scythe
entries.description: A [scythe](#scythe) is held, from a [farming](#farming) tool to a reaper's curved blade. Add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) when it is being used as one.

entries.name: holding_dagger
entries.description: At least one [dagger](#dagger) is held, a short blade meant as a [weapon](#weapon). Add [reverse_grip](#reverse_grip) when the point runs down out of the fist.

entries.name: finger_on_trigger
entries.description: The shooting hand sits with its finger on the trigger or inside the [guard](#guard) rather than laid along the frame, whether or not a shot is coming. It is the reverse of [trigger_discipline](#trigger_discipline), and someone with two guns may show one hand each way.

entries.name: aiming_at_viewer
entries.description: The muzzle, arrowhead or blade points straight out of the picture at whoever is looking. It is sometimes stretched to a [camera](#camera), [hose](#hose) or other object levelled the same way.

entries.name: holding_sheath
entries.description: A [scabbard](#scabbard) is held, as a rule in the off hand while the blade is being drawn or is already out. It pairs with a drawn-sword pose.

entries.name: holding_arrow
entries.description: An arrow is in the hand, whether nocked against a bowstring or simply carried loose. The [bow](#bow) itself is [holding_bow_(weapon)](#holding_bow_(weapon)).

entries.name: two-handed
entries.description: Both hands grip a single [weapon](#weapon) or object at once, such as a [greatsword](#greatsword) swung with a two-handed hold. Implies [holding](#holding).

entries.name: holding_whip
entries.description: A [whip](#whip) is in hand, as is a related implement such as a [riding](#riding) crop. It need not be in use; simply gripping it is enough.

entries.name: hand_on_hilt
entries.description: One hand rests on the grip or pommel of the character's own [sword](#sword), usually still [sheathed](#sheathed) at the hip or [planted](#planted) point-down in the ground. Actually [pulling](#pulling) the blade free is [unsheathing](#unsheathing).

entries.name: holding_weapon_behind_back
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) stays in the hand but is kept behind the body, out of sight of whoever the character faces. It reads as concealment or an ambush in the making.

entries.name: sword_over_shoulder
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) [resting](#resting) across the shoulder or held there while carried, rather than [hanging](#hanging) at the side.

entries.name: drawing_bow
entries.description: An archer hauls the [string](#string) of a [bow](#bow) [back](#back), ready to loose an arrow at a [target](#target). The moment of full draw and aim rather than the shot leaving.

entries.name: drawing_sword
entries.description: A blade being pulled free, in most cases out of its [sheath](#sheath), which calls for [unsheathing](#unsheathing) as [well](#well). Also covers a [sword](#sword) drawn from somewhere else entirely, or one whose sheath is out of view.

entries.name: ready_to_draw
entries.description: A hand rests on or hovers near a [sheathed](#sheathed) [sword](#sword) or [holstered](#holstered) [gun](#gun), poised to draw it at a moment's notice. Once the [weapon](#weapon) is partway out, [unsheathing](#unsheathing) applies instead.

entries.name: sword_behind_back
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) gripped in the hands and held behind the body. A sword strapped to the [back](#back) and not actively held instead gets [sword_on_back](#sword_on_back).

entries.name: asymmetrical_dual_wielding
entries.description: Each hand carries a different [weapon](#weapon), a [sword](#sword) in one and a pistol in the other for instance. Both are held ready at once, and it is the mismatch between the pair that the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: gun_to_head
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) pressed or pointed directly at a character's head, held either by themselves or by someone else. It need not be suicidal in intent: Persona 3's Evoker [summoning](#summoning) falls under it too.

entries.name: hands_on_hilt
entries.description: Both hands settle on a sword's pommel while the [weapon](#weapon) stands [planted](#planted) upright before the character. Knights and rulers take this stance in formal portraits; one hand is [hand_on_hilt](#hand_on_hilt).

entries.name: weapon_behind_back
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) held in the hands behind the [back](#back), hidden or simply [resting](#resting) there. A weapon strapped or slung across the back without being held by hand is [weapon_on_back](#weapon_on_back) instead.

entries.name: knives_between_fingers
entries.description: Several blades fanned out through the gaps between the fingers of one hand, generally held ready to throw. A [signature](#signature) move for knife-throwing characters.

entries.name: gun_on_back
entries.description: A [rifle](#rifle) or other firearm slung across the [back](#back), usually on a sling, leaving both hands free. Covers [carrying](#carrying) the [weapon](#weapon) that way rather than [holding](#holding) or [firing](#firing) it.

entries.name: holding_crossbow
entries.description: A [crossbow](#crossbow) is carried, lowered at rest or shouldered and aimed. Its stock and horizontal limbs distinguish it from a [plain](#plain) [bow](#bow).

entries.name: reloading
entries.description: Restocking a firearm with [ammunition](#ammunition): swapping a magazine, [feeding](#feeding) cartridges into an internal magazine, or thumbing rounds into a detached magazine. The action mid-motion is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: holding_mace
entries.description: A [mace](#mace) is carried, its weighted or flanged head mounted on a short shaft. Fantasy knights and clerics are the usual bearers.

entries.name: holding_club
entries.description: A blunt club is gripped, anything from a knobbed cudgel to a [spiked](#spiked) bat. Golf clubs are an unrelated object with their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: polearm_behind_back
entries.description: A [spear](#spear), [staff](#staff), [broom](#broom), or similar long shaft carried horizontally behind the body, with the arms hooked over or around it. Only counts while the character actually grips it, not when it is strapped on or [planted](#planted) in the ground.

entries.name: holding_torpedo
entries.description: A [torpedo](#torpedo) is carried in the arms, drawn small enough for one person to lift. Naval-themed art, where crew haul their own ordnance about, supplies most of it.

entries.name: holding_lightsaber
entries.description: An energy-bladed [sword](#sword) is gripped by the [hilt](#hilt), the [glowing](#glowing) beam normally already lit. The stance is almost always a [fighting](#fighting) one.

entries.name: pointing_melee_weapon
entries.description: The dangerous end of a [weapon](#weapon), its blade or point, is levelled at another character or an object. Add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) whenever the weapon is actually gripped rather than mounted on the body.

entries.name: holding_lead_pipe
entries.description: A length of metal pipe is gripped as a blunt [weapon](#weapon) or a work item, shouldered or [caught](#caught) mid-swing. Delinquents and [building](#building) sites both supply it.

entries.name: holding_grenade
entries.description: A [grenade](#grenade) sits in the palm or between the fingers, sometimes with the [pin](#pin) already pulled or gripped in the [teeth](#teeth). Military and action pictures account for nearly all of it.

entries.name: hand_on_weapon
entries.description: A hand [resting](#resting) on a [sheathed](#sheathed) or [holstered](#holstered) [weapon](#weapon), poised to draw without yet wielding it. It signals readiness or a warning rather than a fight in progress.

entries.name: weapon_in_garters
entries.description: A [knife](#knife), pistol or similar [weapon](#weapon) tucked into a [strap](#strap) worn high on the thigh. It stays out of sight under a [skirt](#skirt) until it's needed.

entries.name: holding_rocket_launcher
entries.description: A [rocket](#rocket) or [missile](#missile) launcher is shouldered or braced in both hands, carried or already aimed. Military and action pictures, where the size of the thing is often the point.

entries.name: holding_cannon
entries.description: A [cannon](#cannon) is carried or aimed by hand, its bulk normally [well](#well) past what a person could really lift. Fantasy [artillery](#artillery) and cartoon overkill both qualify.

entries.name: holding_shuriken
entries.description: Throwing stars sit between the fingers, often several fanned out at once and ready to [fly](#fly). Ninja and martial arts scenes account for almost all of it.

entries.name: pointing_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) held out with its point aimed at somebody or something. Reads as a challenge, a [threat](#threat), or the formal [salute](#salute) before a [duel](#duel).

entries.name: holding_bomb
entries.description: An [explosive](#explosive) sits in the hand, whether a round cartoon [bomb](#bomb) with a sputtering [fuse](#fuse) or something more [realistic](#realistic). It is being carried or brandished, not yet going off.

entries.name: battoujutsu_stance
entries.description: A swordsman poised to draw, the drawing hand at or hovering near the [hilt](#hilt) while the other angles the [scabbard](#scabbard) for a rising cut in one motion. It covers the moment before the blade leaves the [sheath](#sheath); once the cut is happening, the drawing-cut [tag](#tag) takes over.

entries.name: triple_wielding
entries.description: A fighter handling three weapons at once, typically swords, with the third gripped somewhere unconventional such as between the [teeth](#teeth). The three-sword [fighting](#fighting) style of a famous [pirate](#pirate) manga popularised the [idea](#idea).

entries.name: holding_flamethrower
entries.description: A [flamethrower](#flamethrower) is carried and usually pointed somewhere, fuel tanks strapped on and a jet of [fire](#fire) at the nozzle. Military and [destruction](#destruction) scenes are where it appears.

entries.name: weapon_in_mouth
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) gripped between the [teeth](#teeth), leaving both hands free. Knives held crosswise this way are by far the most common.

entries.name: holding_magazine_(weapon)
entries.description: An [ammunition](#ammunition) magazine is gripped, on its way into a firearm or freshly ejected from one. Loading and [reloading](#reloading) are what it depicts.

entries.name: sword_between_breasts
entries.description: A blade held upright with its flat pressed into the [cleavage](#cleavage), steadied by the [breasts](#breasts) closing around it rather than by the hands alone.

entries.name: holding_sickle
entries.description: A [sickle](#sickle) is gripped by its short [handle](#handle), the curved blade used for harvesting or turned on somebody. Farm work and horror both fit.

entries.name: sword_in_front_of_face
entries.description: A blade held upright before the face, usually splitting the view between the eyes. Reads as a character steeling themselves or saluting before a [duel](#duel), and turns up often in split-personality compositions.

entries.name: quadruple_wielding
entries.description: Four weapons are handled at once by a single character, usually all of the same type. Extra arms, tails, extra mouths, or [telekinesis](#telekinesis) are what make it possible, extending the [idea](#idea) behind dual wielding.

entries.name: holding_nunchaku
entries.description: Nunchaku are gripped, the pair of sticks and their [chain](#chain) at rest or mid-swing. Martial arts scenes account for nearly all of it.

entries.name: knife_in_mouth
entries.description: A blade gripped crosswise between the [teeth](#teeth), leaving both hands free. It is shorthand for pirates, assassins and [ninja](#ninja) in the middle of action.

entries.name: hand_on_blade
entries.description: A palm or fingers laid along the flat or edge of a blade rather than around its grip. It usually comes with drawing, [wiping](#wiping) down or steadying the [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: holding_turret
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) turret, the sort normally bolted to a vehicle or an emplacement, is carried in the hands. The mismatch between its bulk and the person hefting it is usually the point.

entries.name: hand_on_sheath
entries.description: One hand steadies the [scabbard](#scabbard), normally the off hand while the other reaches for the grip. This is the moment immediately before a draw.

entries.name: gangsta_hold
entries.description: A pistol gripped rotated onto its side, the [barrel](#barrel) still level. Borrowed from action cinema and useless for [aiming](#aiming), it is often combined with a second [gun](#gun) in the other hand.

entries.name: gun_in_mouth
entries.description: The muzzle of a firearm pushed between somebody's [lips](#lips), held either by a threatening attacker or by the character themselves. The [barrel](#barrel) needs to actually be in the mouth, not merely aimed at the face.

entries.name: multiple_wielding
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) gripping five or more weapons at once, held in hands, mouth, [tail](#tail) or extra limbs. Anything under that count is dual wielding or ordinary [holding](#holding).

entries.name: grenade_pin_in_mouth
entries.description: A character grips a grenade's [pin](#pin) [ring](#ring) between the [teeth](#teeth), having just pulled it or about to. It keeps both hands free and reads as pure bravado.

entries.name: weapon_between_legs
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) sits between the character's [legs](#legs), propped upright or laid across them. Often a [sword](#sword) [planted](#planted) point-down while its owner kneels or sits.

entries.name: standing_on_weapon
entries.description: The character carries their [weight](#weight) with their [feet](#feet) on a [weapon](#weapon), perched on a blade, a [spear](#spear) shaft or a hovering [staff](#staff). Merely [resting](#resting) a foot on one is foot_on_weapon, and [lying](#lying) across it is [on_weapon](#on_weapon).

entries.name: aiming_up
entries.description: The [weapon](#weapon) is tilted skyward, tracking something overhead or about to be fired into the air. Barrel and eyeline rise together.

entries.name: holding_food
entries.description: An edible item of any kind is gripped in the hands, from a [snack](#snack) to a full dish. When the [food](#food) is clamped in the mouth with nothing touching it, [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth) is the [tag](#tag); many individual foods also have their own holding_ variants.

entries.name: holding_cup
entries.description: Any kind of [cup](#cup) is held: [teacup](#teacup), [mug](#mug), [drinking](#drinking) [glass](#glass), goblet or [sake](#sake) dish. A stemmed [wine](#wine) glass cradled from under the [bowl](#bowl) is also [cupping_glass](#cupping_glass).

entries.name: holding_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) of any sort is in the hand: a [drink](#drink) bottle, a [sake](#sake) bottle, a perfume or a [potion](#potion). The contents are often visible through the [glass](#glass).

entries.name: holding_tray
entries.description: A [serving](#serving) [tray](#tray) is carried, usually loaded with [food](#food) or drinks. Maids, [waiting](#waiting) [staff](#staff) and anyone bringing something to a [table](#table).

entries.name: holding_plate
entries.description: A [plate](#plate) is held, very often with [food](#food) on it, carried towards a [table](#table) or eaten from where it stands. Serving [staff](#staff) and home [cooking](#cooking) scenes account for much of it.

entries.name: holding_fruit
entries.description: A piece of [fruit](#fruit) rests in the hand, an [apple](#apple), [peach](#peach), [strawberry](#strawberry) or similar; [tag](#tag) the fruit itself as [well](#well). Fruit gripped in the mouth with [no](#no) hands involved is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth) instead.

entries.name: holding_watermelon
entries.description: A [watermelon](#watermelon) is held, whole or cut into a slice, a fixture of [summer](#summer) and [beach](#beach) scenes. A piece gripped in the mouth with [no](#no) hands on it is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth) instead.

entries.name: holding_chopsticks
entries.description: Chopsticks are held in the hand, usually while [eating](#eating) from a [bowl](#bowl) or a [plate](#plate). Eating and [holding_bowl](#holding_bowl) often go with it.

entries.name: holding_spoon
entries.description: A [spoon](#spoon) is held, usually over [soup](#soup), [dessert](#dessert) or [curry](#curry), or raised on its way to the mouth. The long-handled [serving](#serving) kind is [holding_ladle](#holding_ladle) instead.

entries.name: holding_fork
entries.description: A [fork](#fork) is gripped, as a rule at a [table](#table) with a [meal](#meal) or a slice of [cake](#cake) in front of the eater. Tag the dish being eaten alongside it.

entries.name: holding_can
entries.description: A [drink](#drink) [can](#can) is held, [beer](#beer) and [soda](#soda) being the usual contents. A [watering](#watering) can has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: holding_candy
entries.description: A piece of [candy](#candy) is held in the hand. Candy taken in the mouth without hands is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth), and a [lollipop](#lollipop) has [holding_lollipop](#holding_lollipop).

entries.name: holding_lollipop
entries.description: A [lollipop](#lollipop) is held by its [stick](#stick), big swirled ones included. With the sweet in the mouth and [no](#no) hand on it, [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth) applies instead.

entries.name: holding_bowl
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) is held, usually of [rice](#rice), [ramen](#ramen) or [soup](#soup), often with [chopsticks](#chopsticks) in the other hand. Both hands may [cradle](#cradle) it.

entries.name: holding_drink
entries.description: A [drink](#drink) of any kind is held, in a [cup](#cup), [glass](#glass), [bottle](#bottle), [can](#can) or [carton](#carton). The particular [container](#container) may be tagged as [well](#well).

entries.name: holding_popsicle
entries.description: A [popsicle](#popsicle) is held by its [stick](#stick). In the mouth with [no](#no) hand on it, [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold) together with popsicle is the pair to use.

entries.name: holding_ice_cream
entries.description: Ice [cream](#cream) is held in any form: scoops or soft serve on a cone, a [parfait](#parfait) [glass](#glass), or a [frozen](#frozen) bar. A [stick](#stick) lolly [can](#can) carry [holding_popsicle](#holding_popsicle) as [well](#well).

entries.name: drinking_straw_in_mouth
entries.description: A [drinking](#drinking) straw held between the [lips](#lips), whether being sucked on or simply parked there.

entries.name: popsicle_in_mouth
entries.description: A character has an [ice](#ice) pop in their mouth, [licking](#licking) or sucking it. Tag [popsicle](#popsicle) and [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth) alongside it.

entries.name: holding_vegetable
entries.description: A [vegetable](#vegetable) is held in the hand, whether a [carrot](#carrot), a [daikon](#daikon) or a head of [lettuce](#lettuce). Cooking, [shopping](#shopping) and harvest scenes account for most of them.

entries.name: holding_ladle
entries.description: The long-handled [serving](#serving) [spoon](#spoon) is gripped, generally over a pot while [soup](#soup) is stirred or dished into a [bowl](#bowl). Kitchens, canteens and [cooking](#cooking) scenes are where it belongs.

entries.name: holding_chocolate
entries.description: Solid [chocolate](#chocolate) is held, a bar or a heart-shaped Valentine's piece. Chocolate taken in the mouth without hands is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_saucer
entries.description: A [saucer](#saucer) is held, as a rule under a [teacup](#teacup) balanced in the other hand. Tea parties, cafes and polite drawing rooms are where the pairing shows up.

entries.name: pocky_in_mouth
entries.description: A character holds a [pocky](#pocky) [stick](#stick) between the [lips](#lips) or [teeth](#teeth), whether [nibbling](#nibbling) it or simply [posing](#posing) with it. Two characters [sharing](#sharing) one stick from either end is [pocky_kiss](#pocky_kiss) instead.

entries.name: holding_ice_cream_cone
entries.description: A cone is raised in the fingers, and whether [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) still sits on top or it has all been eaten makes [no](#no) difference. Summer and [dessert](#dessert) scenes are its home.

entries.name: holding_cotton_candy
entries.description: Cotton [candy](#candy) on its [stick](#stick) is held, a treat from a [festival](#festival) stall or an amusement [park](#park). Yukata and summer-festival scenes go with it.

entries.name: utensil_in_mouth
entries.description: A [fork](#fork) or [spoon](#spoon) held between the [lips](#lips), usually while [eating](#eating) or lingering over [dessert](#dessert). Chopsticks held the same way take the separate [chopsticks_in_mouth](#chopsticks_in_mouth) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: holding_pizza
entries.description: A slice or a whole [pizza](#pizza) is held in the hands. A slice clamped in the mouth with [no](#no) hands on it is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_burger
entries.description: A [burger](#burger) is held in the hands, about to be eaten or shown off. One gripped in the [teeth](#teeth) with [no](#no) hand on it is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_drink_carton
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [drink](#drink) [carton](#carton) is gripped in the hand, [milk](#milk) and [juice](#juice) being the usual contents. A straw is often already pushed through the top.

entries.name: holding_cake
entries.description: A whole [cake](#cake) or a slice is held, usually on a [plate](#plate). Cake taken in the mouth with [no](#no) hands on it is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_teapot
entries.description: A [teapot](#teapot) is held, generally tilted to pour into a [waiting](#waiting) [cup](#cup). Tea parties, cafes and quiet interiors, frequently alongside a [saucer](#saucer) or a [tray](#tray).

entries.name: holding_frying_pan
entries.description: A frying pan hangs from one hand, whether over a [stove](#stove) during [cooking](#cooking) or swung as an improvised [weapon](#weapon) in a [comic](#comic) scene.

entries.name: holding_crepe
entries.description: A [crepe](#crepe) is held, usually the cone-wrapped street-food kind stuffed with [cream](#cream) and [fruit](#fruit). Festival and shopping-street scenes are typical.

entries.name: toast_in_mouth
entries.description: A slice of [toast](#toast) clamped in the mouth, the classic image of a student [dashing](#dashing) off late to [school](#school).

entries.name: holding_candy_apple
entries.description: A glazed [apple](#apple) on a [stick](#stick) is held up, its [shell](#shell) usually a glossy red. Festival stalls and fairgrounds are where it belongs.

entries.name: holding_spatula
entries.description: A [spatula](#spatula) is held, generally at a [stove](#stove) or a [grill](#grill) while something is turned or lifted. Cooking scenes, often with an [apron](#apron) and a pan alongside.

entries.name: holding_skewer
entries.description: A [skewer](#skewer) of [food](#food) is raised in the hand, [dango](#dango), [yakitori](#yakitori) and kebabs being the usual fare. Festival stalls and [street](#street) food.

entries.name: holding_pocky
entries.description: A chocolate-coated biscuit [stick](#stick) is pinched in the fingers, coated end upward. It frequently sets up the shared-stick game played between two characters.

entries.name: holding_egg
entries.description: An [egg](#egg) rests in the palm or between the fingertips, whether a [kitchen](#kitchen) egg or a creature's. One carried in the mouth is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_milk_carton
entries.description: A [carton](#carton) of [milk](#milk) sits in the hand, at times tipped up and [drunk](#drunk) straight from the spout. Fridges, kitchens and [school](#school) lunches are typical.

entries.name: holding_spring_onion
entries.description: A spring [onion](#onion) is carried like a baton or swung like a [sword](#sword), its long green stalk and pale root plainly drawn. It is a well-worn joke prop.

entries.name: holding_carrot
entries.description: A [carrot](#carrot) is gripped in the hand, often offered to a [rabbit](#rabbit) or a [horse](#horse) or waved about as a joke. The leafy tops may or may not still be attached.

entries.name: holding_cookie
entries.description: A [cookie](#cookie) is pinched in the fingers, about to be eaten or offered to somebody else. One gripped only in the [teeth](#teeth) counts as [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_pumpkin
entries.description: A [pumpkin](#pumpkin) is carried in the arms or raised in the hands, carved jack-o'-lanterns included. Autumn harvests and Halloween scenes.

entries.name: holding_juice_box
entries.description: A small [drink](#drink) [carton](#carton) sits in the hand, generally with a straw pushed through the top. It reads as a [school](#school) or childhood prop.

entries.name: cupping_glass
entries.description: A stemmed [wine](#wine) [glass](#glass) gripped under the [bowl](#bowl) instead of by its stem. It warms the [drink](#drink) and counts as poor manners, which artists sometimes use to say something about the drinker.

entries.name: holding_pastry_bag
entries.description: A piping [bag](#bag) is squeezed between the hands, laying [icing](#icing) onto a [cake](#cake) or a [pastry](#pastry). Baking and confectionery scenes.

entries.name: fish_in_mouth
entries.description: A whole [fish](#fish), or an unmistakable piece of one, gripped in the mouth. Cats, bears and [hungry](#hungry) characters all get drawn this way.

entries.name: holding_tongs
entries.description: Tongs are gripped in the hand, turning [food](#food) over a [grill](#grill) or lifting something out of a pot. Barbecues and kitchens.

entries.name: holding_mushroom
entries.description: A [mushroom](#mushroom) is carried in the hand, freshly foraged, oversized or storybook-bright depending on the picture. Forests and kitchens both fit.

entries.name: holding_doughnut
entries.description: A [doughnut](#doughnut) is pinched in the fingers, whole or with a bite already out of it. Glaze and [sprinkles](#sprinkles) often make it the focus of the frame.

entries.name: holding_gourd
entries.description: A [gourd](#gourd) is carried, most often the dried bottle-shaped sort used as a [sake](#sake) [flask](#flask). Wandering swordsmen, immortals and Chinese-styled settings favour the prop.

entries.name: holding_drinking_straw
entries.description: A straw is pinched between the fingers, being fitted into a [cup](#cup) or just fiddled with. The [drink](#drink) itself may be nowhere in sight.

entries.name: holding_bento
entries.description: A packed Japanese lunch [box](#box) is carried in the hands, [lid](#lid) still on or freshly lifted off. School rooftops, picnics and delivered lunches are the usual settings.

entries.name: holding_sandwich
entries.description: A [sandwich](#sandwich) is gripped in the hands, whole or with a bite already gone. Lunch breaks and picnics are the usual setting.

entries.name: bottle_to_cheek
entries.description: A chilled [bottle](#bottle) or [can](#can) pressed flat against the cheek to cool down, a stock [summer](#summer) [gesture](#gesture). The [drink](#drink) is used against the skin rather than [drunk](#drunk).

entries.name: holding_spork
entries.description: A [spork](#spork) is in the hand, the hybrid [utensil](#utensil) poised over a [tray](#tray) or a lunch [box](#box). Cafeterias and [camping](#camping).

entries.name: holding_candy_cane
entries.description: A striped peppermint [cane](#cane) sits in the fingers, a fixture of Christmas pictures. Clenched in the [teeth](#teeth) with [no](#no) hand on it, it is [food_in_mouth](#food_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_utensil
entries.description: Cutlery or a [kitchen](#kitchen) implement, a [fork](#fork), [spoon](#spoon) or [ladle](#ladle), sits in the hand. More specific implements and [chopsticks](#chopsticks) have tags of their own.

entries.name: holding_kettle
entries.description: A [kettle](#kettle) is carried by its [handle](#handle), at times tilted over a [teapot](#teapot) or a [cup](#cup). Kitchens and [tea](#tea) preparation supply the context.
