entries.name: holding_with_chopsticks
entries.description: Chopsticks grip something, most often a morsel lifted from a [bowl](#bowl) or [plate](#plate). Add [eating](#eating) when the [food](#food) is on its way to the mouth.

entries.name: chopsticks_in_mouth
entries.description: Chopsticks held between the [lips](#lips) or [teeth](#teeth) rather than in a hand, often because both hands are busy. It may happen mid-meal, but [no](#no) [food](#food) needs to be on them.

entries.name: holding_pan
entries.description: A pan is carried by its [handle](#handle), [tossing](#tossing) [food](#food) over a burner or raised as a [comic](#comic) [weapon](#weapon). Kitchens and slapstick share it between them.

entries.name: can_to_cheek
entries.description: A [hot](#hot) [drink](#drink) [can](#can) pressed against the cheek to warm the face in [cold](#cold) weather. A [winter](#winter) [gesture](#gesture), often beside a vending [machine](#machine).

entries.name: holding_coffee_pot
entries.description: A [coffee](#coffee) pot or carafe is carried by its [handle](#handle), often tipped over a [waiting](#waiting) [cup](#cup). Cafes, offices and [breakfast](#breakfast) tables are the natural setting.

entries.name: bottle_between_breasts
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) wedged into [cleavage](#cleavage) and held there by the [breasts](#breasts) alone, both hands free. It is played as a [gag](#gag) or for pin-up effect.

entries.name: holding_snack
entries.description: A small [food](#food) item is in the hand, crisps, [sweets](#sweets) or an unspecified bite of something. Where the food [can](#can) be named, a more exact [tag](#tag) describes the picture better.

entries.name: holding_shaker
entries.description: A shaker is gripped, either a [cocktail](#cocktail) shaker being worked or a small [salt](#salt) or spice shaker at a [table](#table). The surroundings say which is meant.

entries.name: holding
entries.description: Someone has an object in their hands, something that could be picked up and carried. It does not [cover](#cover) body parts, clothing being worn, or things gripped in the mouth, [feet](#feet) or [tail](#tail); the specific holding_ tags name what the object is.

entries.name: mouth_hold
entries.description: Something gripped between the [teeth](#teeth) or [lips](#lips) — a [snack](#snack), a [flower](#flower), a [strap](#strap), a [pen](#pen). Body parts and things merely [resting](#resting) in the mouth do not count as held.

entries.name: holding_phone
entries.description: A [phone](#phone) is held in the hand, looked at, aimed for a photo or raised to the ear. Wedged between cheek and shoulder instead, it is [cradling_phone](#cradling_phone).

entries.name: holding_book
entries.description: One or more books are held, open or shut. Add [reading](#reading) when the character is actually reading from it.

entries.name: holding_unworn_clothes
entries.description: A garment nobody is wearing is held, a [jacket](#jacket), a [hat](#hat) or a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) that has come off. It does not apply while the clothing is still on the body.

entries.name: holding_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol) is held, open against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun), or closed and carried at the side. Two characters [sharing](#sharing) one is a common variation.

entries.name: holding_flower
entries.description: One or more loose flowers are held in the hand. A single stem raised towards the face is the classic framing; a [bound](#bound) arrangement is [holding_bouquet](#holding_bouquet).

entries.name: hugging_object
entries.description: An inanimate thing such as a [pillow](#pillow), [book](#book), [doll](#doll) or stuffed [toy](#toy) is hugged against the body. Do not add [hug](#hug), which covers only embracing [people](#people).

entries.name: holding_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) is carried in the hand: a [handbag](#handbag), [shopping](#shopping) bag, [backpack](#backpack) or purse. One slung on the shoulder with [no](#no) hand on it is just bag.

entries.name: holding_fan
entries.description: A hand fan is held, folding or flat, open or closed. Kimono and [yukata](#yukata) outfits go with it often.

entries.name: holding_microphone
entries.description: A handheld [microphone](#microphone) is gripped, as a rule while [singing](#singing) or speaking to an [audience](#audience). A mic still on its stand is [holding_microphone_stand](#holding_microphone_stand).

entries.name: holding_instrument
entries.description: A musical [instrument](#instrument) is in the hands, as a rule ready to be played. Common instruments have narrower tags such as [holding_guitar](#holding_guitar) and [holding_violin](#holding_violin).

entries.name: holding_bouquet
entries.description: A [bound](#bound) bunch of flowers is carried, at a [wedding](#wedding) or as a [gift](#gift). A single loose stem is [holding_flower](#holding_flower).

entries.name: holding_stuffed_toy
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) is held, hugged to the chest or dangled by a limb. A hard-bodied [doll](#doll) is [holding_doll](#holding_doll), and bedrooms and childlike framing tend to come with it.

entries.name: over_shoulder
entries.description: Something is carried [resting](#resting) on the shoulder: a [sword](#sword), a bat, a [bag](#bag) slung [back](#back). A person or [animal](#animal) perched there is [on_shoulder](#on_shoulder), and a [glance](#glance) back past one's own shoulder is [looking_back](#looking_back).

entries.name: holding_gift
entries.description: A wrapped present, usually tied with a [bow](#bow), is carried or offered to somebody. A [plain](#plain) unwrapped [box](#box) calls for [holding_box](#holding_box).

entries.name: holding_cigarette
entries.description: A [cigarette](#cigarette) is held between the fingers. One [resting](#resting) in the [lips](#lips) instead calls for cigarette with [smoking](#smoking) or [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold).

entries.name: holding_card
entries.description: One or more cards are held in the hand: [playing](#playing) cards, trading cards or [tarot](#tarot). A [card](#card) gripped in the mouth is [card_in_mouth](#card_in_mouth).

entries.name: holding_wand
entries.description: A [magic](#magic) [wand](#wand) is held, from a magical girl's decorated baton to a wizard's slim [stick](#stick). A full-length [staff](#staff) gripped instead belongs to [holding_staff](#holding_staff).

entries.name: holding_paper
entries.description: Loose [paper](#paper) is held, from a single sheet to a [stack](#stack) of documents. Reading it, handing it over and showing a page to the viewer all qualify.

entries.name: object_on_head
entries.description: Something that is not [headgear](#headgear) at all sits on top of the head, seemingly just set down there: a [bucket](#bucket), a [cup](#cup), a [book](#book), a piece of [fruit](#fruit). If it hides the face the matching over-head [tag](#tag) applies, and if it is built into a [hat](#hat) or a hair ornament use those instead.

entries.name: holding_unworn_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) is in the hands rather than on the head, carried, offered or fanned about with. Tipping a hat that stays on the head does not count.

entries.name: holding_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) that has come off the head is held or touched. While it stays on, [hand_on_headwear](#hand_on_headwear) describes the [gesture](#gesture), and the hat itself off the head is [unworn_hat](#unworn_hat).

entries.name: holding_ball
entries.description: A spherical [ball](#ball) is held, a [basketball](#basketball), football or similar. Beachballs and poke balls have tags of their own.

entries.name: holding_pen
entries.description: A [pen](#pen) is held, as a rule while [writing](#writing), signing or pausing in thought over a page. A [pencil](#pencil) instead is [holding_pencil](#holding_pencil) and a tablet [stylus](#stylus) is [holding_stylus](#holding_stylus).

entries.name: between_fingers
entries.description: Something pinched between two fingers rather than gripped in the fist: a [cigarette](#cigarette), a [playing](#playing) [card](#card), a [paper](#paper) charm, or [throwing](#throwing) knives fanned across the hand.

entries.name: pillow_hug
entries.description: Holding a [pillow](#pillow) against the body with the arms, sometimes [wrapping](#wrapping) the [legs](#legs) round it too. Do not add [hug](#hug), which is kept for embracing [people](#people) rather than objects.

entries.name: holding_camera
entries.description: A [camera](#camera) or [camcorder](#camcorder) is in the hands, raised to shoot or simply carried. Add photographing or [selfie](#selfie) when a picture is actually being taken.

entries.name: holding_removed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) have come off and are carried in the hand. While they still sit on the [nose](#nose) or pushed up on the head, [adjusting_eyewear](#adjusting_eyewear) and its neighbours apply.

entries.name: holding_broom
entries.description: A [broom](#broom) is in hand, whether for [sweeping](#sweeping), posed as a witch's prop or ridden through the air. Both hands often grip the shaft.

entries.name: holding_strap
entries.description: The [strap](#strap) of a [bag](#bag), [backpack](#backpack) or similar carrier is gripped, often while [walking](#walking). Straps belonging to clothing take [strap_pull](#strap_pull), [strap_lift](#strap_lift) or [suspenders_pull](#suspenders_pull) instead.

entries.name: holding_towel
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) is held in the hands, after a [bath](#bath), at the [pool](#pool) or handed to somebody. Wrapped around the body instead, it is [naked_towel](#naked_towel).

entries.name: holding_box
entries.description: A [box](#box) of any shape or size is held, heart-shaped boxes, [tissue](#tissue) boxes and [ring](#ring) boxes among them. A wrapped present is [holding_gift](#holding_gift) instead.

entries.name: holding_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) is held rather than worn, a [festival](#festival) [fox](#fox) mask or a masquerade one lifted away from the face. The face itself stays visible.

entries.name: holding_pom_poms
entries.description: Cheerleading pom poms are held, as a rule one in each hand and raised. A [cheerleader](#cheerleader) outfit usually comes with them.

entries.name: holding_controller
entries.description: A [controller](#controller) of some kind is held: a game pad, a remote, a [drone](#drone) controller. A game pad specifically is [holding_game_controller](#holding_game_controller).

entries.name: holding_leash
entries.description: A [leash](#leash) is held, its far end clipped to an animal's [collar](#collar) or, in pet-play pictures, to another person's. Whoever holds it is the handler rather than the one [restrained](#restrained).

entries.name: holding_doll
entries.description: A [doll](#doll) is held, whether a [fashion](#fashion) doll, a ball-jointed doll or a rag doll. A plush [animal](#animal) is [holding_stuffed_toy](#holding_stuffed_toy).

entries.name: holding_flag
entries.description: A [flag](#flag) is held by its [pole](#pole) or by the [cloth](#cloth), waved, [planted](#planted) or carried like a [banner](#banner). National, team and invented flags all count.

entries.name: hair_tie_in_mouth
entries.description: Someone holds a hair tie between their [lips](#lips), typically while both hands are busy gathering their hair to tie it up. Also covers a [scrunchie](#scrunchie) held the same way.

entries.name: clothes_in_mouth
entries.description: Clothing is held between the [teeth](#teeth), most often the hem of a [shirt](#shirt) lifted up so the hands stay free. Generally a form of [clothes_lift](#clothes_lift), and [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: holding_underwear
entries.description: Removed [underwear](#underwear) of any kind, [panties](#panties) and bras alike, is held in the hand. For panties specifically there is [holding_panties](#holding_panties).

entries.name: holding_basket
entries.description: A [basket](#basket) is carried by its [handle](#handle) or braced in the arms, most often a [picnic](#picnic), [flower](#flower) or [shopping](#shopping) basket. It may be full or empty.

entries.name: holding_smoking_pipe
entries.description: A [smoking](#smoking) pipe is held in the hand rather than clenched in the [teeth](#teeth), the long-stemmed [kiseru](#kiseru) included. Smoke and an idle, thoughtful pose usually go with it.

entries.name: holding_hammer
entries.description: A [hammer](#hammer) is gripped, anything from a carpenter's claw hammer to an oversized [war](#war) hammer. Add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) when it is being swung as one.

entries.name: holding_paintbrush
entries.description: A [paintbrush](#paintbrush) is in the hand, painting a picture, a wall or somebody's skin. Other kinds of brush go to [holding_brush](#holding_brush), and a palette often occupies the other hand.

entries.name: holding_baseball_bat
entries.description: A [baseball](#baseball) bat is in hand, cocked for a [swing](#swing) at a game or carried as an improvised [weapon](#weapon). Add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) when it serves as one.

entries.name: holding_behind_back
entries.description: An object is kept behind the character's [back](#back), out of sight of the viewer or of somebody else in the scene. A surprise [gift](#gift) or a concealed [weapon](#weapon) are the usual reasons.

entries.name: holding_sign
entries.description: A [sign](#sign), board or [placard](#placard) is held up, as a rule so a written message faces the viewer. Tag the text on it as [well](#well).

entries.name: hugging_doll
entries.description: A [doll](#doll) or stuffed [animal](#animal) is clutched to the chest rather than merely held in the hands. It often suggests a [child](#child) or somebody looking for comfort.

entries.name: holding_handheld_game_console
entries.description: A portable console is cradled in both hands with the [screen](#screen) towards the player. Playing on the sofa, in [bed](#bed) or on a [train](#train) is the usual scene.

entries.name: holding_clipboard
entries.description: A [clipboard](#clipboard) is held, often in the crook of an arm with a [pen](#pen) in the other hand. Nurses, coaches, inspectors and [office](#office) [staff](#staff) carry them.

entries.name: holding_syringe
entries.description: A [syringe](#syringe) is held, including the oversized cartoon sort. Nurses, doctors and mad scientists are the usual holders, and the [needle](#needle) is often pointed towards the viewer.

entries.name: holding_guitar
entries.description: A [guitar](#guitar) of any sort, acoustic or electric, is held, played, slung on a [strap](#strap) or simply carried. It falls under [holding_instrument](#holding_instrument).

entries.name: holding_lantern
entries.description: A [lantern](#lantern) is held aloft, [paper](#paper), oil-burning or electric, [throwing](#throwing) light into a [night](#night) scene or an [interior](#interior). Festivals and searches through the [dark](#dark) are typical.

entries.name: holding_sack
entries.description: A [sack](#sack) is held, above all the big [cloth](#cloth) kind slung over a shoulder. Santa Claus and Christmas imagery account for much of it.

entries.name: pillow_grab
entries.description: A character clutching or gripping one or more pillows, often with the [fabric](#fabric) bunched up in a fist. Holding one against the body in an embrace is [pillow_hug](#pillow_hug) instead.

entries.name: holding_shoes
entries.description: One or both [shoes](#shoes) are carried in the hands. They may be the character's own, which also makes them [unworn_shoes](#unworn_shoes), or somebody else's being carried for them.

entries.name: holding_gohei
entries.description: The wooden Shinto [wand](#wand) hung with zigzag [paper](#paper) [streamers](#streamers) is carried in the hand. Shrine maidens [waving](#waving) it during purification are the usual subject.

entries.name: holding_panties
entries.description: A removed pair of [panties](#panties) is held in the hand. It is a case of [holding_underwear](#holding_underwear); panties still on the body are not this.

entries.name: holding_swim_ring
entries.description: An inflatable swim [ring](#ring) or inner [tube](#tube) is held, over an arm, around the waist or hoisted overhead. Beaches and pools, with swimwear to match.

entries.name: holding_game_controller
entries.description: A console [gamepad](#gamepad) is held in both hands, thumbs over the sticks or [buttons](#buttons), generally mid-play. It narrows the broader [holding_controller](#holding_controller).

entries.name: holding_pencil
entries.description: A [pencil](#pencil) is in the hand, drawing, [writing](#writing) or [studying](#studying). A [pen](#pen) is [holding_pen](#holding_pen) and a tablet [stylus](#stylus) is [holding_stylus](#holding_stylus).

entries.name: holding_stick
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) [stick](#stick) or branch-like rod is held, picked up [outdoors](#outdoors), used to poke at something or to draw in the [sand](#sand).

entries.name: holding_cane
entries.description: A [cane](#cane) or [walking](#walking) [stick](#stick) is held, as a mobility aid, a gentleman's accessory or a dance prop. It may be [planted](#planted) on the ground or swung about.

entries.name: holding_unworn_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) rests in an arm or a hand instead of on the head. Pilots, knights and riders are drawn this way between rounds, which leaves the face visible.

entries.name: holding_shoe
entries.description: A shoe is carried by hand rather than worn, [dangling](#dangling) by the heel or lifted for a look. The [feet](#feet) are usually bare or in [socks](#socks).

entries.name: elbow_carry
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) or similar item hung from the crook of the arm, the elbow bent and the handles [resting](#resting) along the forearm. The usual way of [carrying](#carrying) a [handbag](#handbag) or [shopping](#shopping) bag, and not a shoulder carry.

entries.name: holding_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) of any kind is carried, often tucked under one arm once it has come off, which conveniently leaves the face visible.

entries.name: incoming_gift
entries.description: A present held out toward the viewer, usually a wrapped [box](#box) or a [bag](#bag) of chocolates. Valentine and Christmas pictures are full of it.

entries.name: holding_pillow
entries.description: A [pillow](#pillow) is held, hugged against the chest, carried from room to room or swung in a pillow fight. Bedrooms and sleepovers are the usual setting.

entries.name: curtain_grab
entries.description: A character gripping a curtain, whether [pulling](#pulling) it aside, [hiding](#hiding) behind it or steadying themselves on it. The curtain itself is tagged as [well](#well).

entries.name: holding_scissors
entries.description: A pair of [scissors](#scissors) is held, [cutting](#cutting) hair, [paper](#paper) or [cloth](#cloth). When they are wielded as a [weapon](#weapon), [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) has to be added by hand.

entries.name: holding_balloon
entries.description: A character holds a [balloon](#balloon), or the [string](#string) or [ribbon](#ribbon) tied to one. A single balloon and a whole bunch both count.

entries.name: holding_leaf
entries.description: A [leaf](#leaf) is held in the hand, an [autumn](#autumn) one turned in the fingers or a large one used as a fan or an [umbrella](#umbrella).

entries.name: holding_brush
entries.description: A brush of some kind is held: a hairbrush, a [makeup](#makeup) brush or a scrubbing brush. A painter's brush is [holding_paintbrush](#holding_paintbrush).

entries.name: holding_water_gun
entries.description: A [toy](#toy) [water](#water) [gun](#gun) is held, typically at a [pool](#pool), a [beach](#beach) or a [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival). Do not add [holding_gun](#holding_gun) unless the toy is [realistic](#realistic) enough to pass for a lethal firearm, since squirt toys are recreation rather than weapons.

entries.name: shared_umbrella
entries.description: Two or more [people](#people) [standing](#standing) under one [umbrella](#umbrella), a classic romantic or intimate scene. The drawn doodle of two names under an umbrella is a separate [tag](#tag), [ai_ai_gasa](#ai_ai_gasa).

entries.name: holding_fireworks
entries.description: A firework is held, lit or not, most often a handheld [sparkler](#sparkler) at a [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival). Night scenes and [yukata](#yukata) go with it.

entries.name: talking_on_phone
entries.description: A character [holding](#holding) a [phone](#phone) to their ear and speaking with someone on the line.

entries.name: carrying_under_arm
entries.description: Something or someone is tucked under one arm and clamped against the side of the [torso](#torso). A [book](#book), a [ball](#ball), a [helmet](#helmet) or a small [struggling](#struggling) companion are the usual load.

entries.name: holding_hose
entries.description: A [hose](#hose) is gripped, the [garden](#garden) sort for [watering](#watering) or [spraying](#spraying) being commonest, though [fire](#fire) hoses appear too. Water is frequently shown coming from the nozzle.

entries.name: holding_fishing_rod
entries.description: A [fishing](#fishing) rod is in the grasp, being [cast](#cast), waited over or reeled in. Add fishing when the activity itself is shown.

entries.name: holding_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) that has come off is carried in the hand or slung across a shoulder. One of the removed-clothing holds.

entries.name: holding_stylus
entries.description: A [stylus](#stylus) is held, the [pen](#pen) used with a drawing tablet or a touchscreen. Digital drawing and note-taking scenes; an ordinary [pencil](#pencil) is [holding_pencil](#holding_pencil).

entries.name: holding_unworn_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) hangs from a hand or is slung over an arm rather than worn. Typical of somebody heading home, or of a character who has just shrugged it off.

entries.name: holding_tablet_pc
entries.description: A tablet [computer](#computer) is held, its [screen](#screen) being read or drawn on. Two hands, or one hand with a [stylus](#stylus) in the other.

entries.name: holding_megaphone
entries.description: A [megaphone](#megaphone) is held, most often raised to shout through. Cheerleaders, event [staff](#staff) and anyone addressing a [crowd](#crowd) use one.

entries.name: ribbon_in_mouth
entries.description: A character [holding](#holding) a [ribbon](#ribbon) between their [lips](#lips) or [teeth](#teeth), often while [tying](#tying) up their hair or just after undoing it. Tagged with [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold) and ribbon.

entries.name: holding_needle
entries.description: A [needle](#needle) is held in the hand, [sewing](#sewing) needles being the ordinary case. Several fanned out between the fingers may add [between_fingers](#between_fingers).

entries.name: holding_notebook
entries.description: A [notebook](#notebook) is held open or closed, frequently while [notes](#notes) are taken or something is sketched. Students, reporters and anyone jotting things down are the usual holders.

entries.name: holding_bucket
entries.description: A [bucket](#bucket) is carried, normally by its [handle](#handle), for [water](#water), [cleaning](#cleaning) or play at the [beach](#beach). It may be full or empty.

entries.name: holding_violin
entries.description: A [violin](#violin) is held, either tucked under the chin to play or carried by its [neck](#neck). Playing it also calls for the [tag](#tag) naming the [instrument](#instrument) itself.

entries.name: holding_beachball
entries.description: An inflatable [beachball](#beachball) is held, normally at the [pool](#pool) or the [seaside](#seaside) in swimwear. A particular case of [holding_ball](#holding_ball).

entries.name: holding_envelope
entries.description: An [envelope](#envelope) is held, a love [letter](#letter), an invitation or a piece of [mail](#mail) about to be opened or delivered. It may be sealed or already [torn](#torn).

entries.name: holding_drumsticks
entries.description: Drumsticks are held, poised to strike or twirled between the fingers. A kit and [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) often go with them.

entries.name: holding_riding_crop
entries.description: A [riding](#riding) crop is held, by an equestrian, as a teacher's [pointer](#pointer) or as a [dominatrix](#dominatrix) prop. It is a short shaft with a small flap at the tip.

entries.name: holding_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) of any kind is held, loose in the fingers, trailing from the hand or mounted on a [stick](#stick) as in rhythmic [gymnastics](#gymnastics). A ribbon worn in the hair is not this.

entries.name: holding_firecrackers
entries.description: A [string](#string) or a handful of [firecrackers](#firecrackers) is carried, the [fuse](#fuse) sometimes already sputtering. Lunar New Year and [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival) scenes are the usual context.

entries.name: holding_jewelry
entries.description: A piece of jewellery, a [ring](#ring), [necklace](#necklace) or earring, rests in the hand instead of on the body, admired or held out to somebody.

entries.name: holding_letter
entries.description: An unfolded sheet of correspondence is held, being read or offered. Love letters and formal notices are the stock cases.

entries.name: between_toes
entries.description: Something is lodged or gripped between someone's [toes](#toes), whether a [pencil](#pencil), a [knife](#knife) or a strand of hair. When the foot is actively gripping and [carrying](#carrying) the item, add [holding_with_feet](#holding_with_feet) as [well](#well).

entries.name: holding_branch
entries.description: A [tree](#tree) [branch](#branch) or [twig](#twig) is held, often with blossom or leaves still on it. Cherry branches are especially common.

entries.name: holding_ofuda
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [talisman](#talisman) is pinched between the fingers, sometimes several fanned at once and raised during an exorcism. Shrine maidens and spirit-hunting scenes.

entries.name: stalk_in_mouth
entries.description: A stalk of [wheat](#wheat), [grass](#grass), straw or a [twig](#twig) held between the [lips](#lips) and chewed on, the classic rustic or [delinquent](#delinquent) look.

entries.name: holding_suitcase
entries.description: A [suitcase](#suitcase) is carried by its [handle](#handle), as a rule while travelling, arriving or leaving. Stations, airports and doorways supply the setting, sometimes with a [coat](#coat) over the arm.

entries.name: holding_money
entries.description: Money is held: banknotes, a fanned-out wad of bills or loose coins. A single [coin](#coin) may also take [holding_coin](#holding_coin), and payment, bribery and gloating scenes all use it.

entries.name: holding_remote_control
entries.description: A remote control is held, for a [television](#television) or, in adult pictures, for a remote-operated [toy](#toy). A thumb [resting](#resting) on a button is the usual detail.

entries.name: giving_to_viewer
entries.description: Something held out towards the [camera](#camera) as though being passed to whoever is looking. Common in Valentine [chocolate](#chocolate) and [gift](#gift) pictures.

entries.name: holding_plectrum
entries.description: A [guitar](#guitar) pick is pinched between the fingers, generally while [playing](#playing) or [posing](#posing) with a guitar. It is small enough that the [tag](#tag) often marks a close view of the hand.

entries.name: holding_microphone_stand
entries.description: A [microphone](#microphone) stand is gripped mid-performance, leaned on, tilted forward or dragged across a [stage](#stage). A [staple](#staple) of [rock](#rock) and [idol](#idol) pictures, generally with [singing](#singing) to match.

entries.name: holding_wrench
entries.description: A [wrench](#wrench) is gripped in the hand, commonly as a mechanic's or engineer's prop. Spanners, [monkey](#monkey) wrenches and pipe wrenches of any size all count.

entries.name: holding_skull
entries.description: A [skull](#skull) is held in the hands, whether in the theatrical contemplative pose or as a necromancer's prop. Gothic and horror imagery.

entries.name: holding_flute
entries.description: A [flute](#flute) or [school](#school) [recorder](#recorder) is carried or lowered from the [lips](#lips) without being played. Actual performance wants a [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: holding_bow_(music)
entries.description: The [bow](#bow) used to play a [string](#string) [instrument](#instrument) such as a [violin](#violin) or [cello](#cello) is in the hand. The [archery](#archery) [weapon](#weapon) is [holding_bow_(weapon)](#holding_bow_(weapon)).

entries.name: holding_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) is cradled in the hands, whether a heart-shaped object, a [floating](#floating) cartoon symbol or an anatomical one. The anatomical case also takes [holding_heart_(organ)](#holding_heart_(organ)).

entries.name: holding_test_tube
entries.description: A test [tube](#tube) is held between the fingers, its coloured contents often the point of the picture. Laboratories, scientists and students at a [bench](#bench), with a lab [coat](#coat) to match.

entries.name: holding_scroll
entries.description: A [scroll](#scroll) is held, rolled shut or unfurled between both hands, whether a [ninja](#ninja) scroll, an [old](#old) [map](#map) or an ancient text. Reading one aloud is a common framing.

entries.name: holding_coin
entries.description: A [coin](#coin) is held, perhaps flipped, offered or examined between the fingertips. Banknotes and cash in general are [holding_money](#holding_money).

entries.name: object_in_pocket
entries.description: Something is stowed in a [pocket](#pocket), on a [shirt](#shirt), a [coat](#coat) or a pair of trousers, generally sticking out far enough to be recognised. Use it for the object being carried there rather than for the pocket itself.

entries.name: holding_quill
entries.description: A feather [pen](#pen) is gripped over [paper](#paper) or an [inkwell](#inkwell), placing the scene in a historical or [fantasy](#fantasy) setting. Letters, contracts and spellbooks accompany it.

entries.name: holding_mop
entries.description: A [mop](#mop) is held, generally while a [floor](#floor) is being cleaned. A [broom](#broom) instead is [holding_broom](#holding_broom), and a [bucket](#bucket) often stands nearby.

entries.name: holding_toy
entries.description: A [toy](#toy) of an unspecified sort is held, a toy [car](#car), a [building](#building) block, a [spinning](#spinning) top. Dolls, plushes and balls have tags of their own.

entries.name: holding_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) that have come off are carried in the hands. It sits under [holding_unworn_clothes](#holding_unworn_clothes), and for ordinary [shoes](#shoes) [holding_shoes](#holding_shoes) is the spelling reached for more often.

entries.name: holding_chain
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) is held in the hand, swung as a [weapon](#weapon), run out as a [leash](#leash) or brandished as a restraint. Loops of it often hang down from the fist.

entries.name: holding_magnifying_glass
entries.description: A magnifying [glass](#glass) is raised in the hand, sometimes with an enlarged eye visible through the lens. Detective work and close inspection are the excuse.

entries.name: holding_scepter
entries.description: A [scepter](#scepter) or ceremonial [staff](#staff) is held upright, marking royalty, regalia or a magical girl's [wand](#wand). An ornament at the tip is typical.

entries.name: skirt_basket
entries.description: The front of a [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) is held up to carry things like [fruit](#fruit), flowers or small animals in the fold.

entries.name: teeth_hold
entries.description: An object gripped between the [teeth](#teeth) rather than [resting](#resting) between the [lips](#lips). A narrower form of [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold), covering things like a bitten [pencil](#pencil), [strap](#strap) or [knife](#knife).

entries.name: holding_lipstick_tube
entries.description: A [tube](#tube) of [lipstick](#lipstick) is held, usually while [makeup](#makeup) is being applied or the colour is shown off to somebody. A [mirror](#mirror) often occupies the other hand.

entries.name: flower_in_mouth
entries.description: A blossom gripped between the [lips](#lips) or [teeth](#teeth), usually by its stem. Add [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold) when nothing but the mouth supports it.

entries.name: holding_briefcase
entries.description: A [briefcase](#briefcase) is carried, usually by its [handle](#handle), the flat hard-sided sort [office](#office) workers use. Salarymen and business scenes are its natural home.

entries.name: holding_swimsuit
entries.description: A removed [swimsuit](#swimsuit) or [bikini](#bikini) piece is held in the hand. One of the removed-clothing holds; the wearer is usually changing or bare.

entries.name: holding_with_feet
entries.description: Something is gripped with the [feet](#feet), sometimes clamped between the [toes](#toes). It does not [cover](#cover) a hand [holding](#holding) a foot, which is [holding_own_foot](#holding_own_foot) or [holding_another's_foot](#holding_another's_foot).

entries.name: holding_shovel
entries.description: A [shovel](#shovel) is held, [digging](#digging), [gardening](#gardening) or brandished as an improvised [weapon](#weapon). Add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) when it is clearly being swung as one.

entries.name: holding_glowstick
entries.description: A [glowstick](#glowstick) or penlight is raised in the hand, its colour [reading](#reading) against a darkened room. Concert crowds and club scenes are where it turns up.

entries.name: holding_cross
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) is held in the hand, a crucifix raised against a [vampire](#vampire) or a religious cross gripped in prayer. It is carried rather than worn on a [chain](#chain).

entries.name: holding_mirror
entries.description: A [mirror](#mirror) is held, usually the hand-held kind, to check an appearance or to apply [makeup](#makeup). One [hanging](#hanging) on a wall or [standing](#standing) on a [table](#table) does not count.

entries.name: holding_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) that has come off is held in the hands. It is a removed-clothing hold; a shirt lifted while still worn is [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift).

entries.name: holding_photo
entries.description: A printed photograph is held, looked at or turned so somebody else [can](#can) see it. Memories and revelations are the usual reason.

entries.name: holding_pole
entries.description: A [pole](#pole) is grabbed and held on to, a grab pole in a [train](#train) or [bus](#bus), a dance pole, or a long staff-like rod. The grip is for support as often as for use.

entries.name: holding_toothbrush
entries.description: A [toothbrush](#toothbrush) is gripped, often mid-brush with [foam](#foam) around the mouth and a [cup](#cup) [standing](#standing) nearby. Bathrooms, [morning](#morning) routines and [sleepy](#sleepy) just-woken framing.

entries.name: hugging_book
entries.description: A [book](#book) is pressed flat against the chest with both arms wrapped around it. A [shy](#shy) or studious pose, common on students [carrying](#carrying) textbooks.

entries.name: holding_necklace
entries.description: A [necklace](#necklace) hangs from the fingers instead of a [neck](#neck), dangled or presented to somebody. Gifts and jewellery boxes accompany it.

entries.name: holding_plant
entries.description: A [plant](#plant) is carried in the hands, roots, cuttings or a leafy sprig, with [no](#no) pot necessarily involved. Gardening and foraging scenes.

entries.name: holding_newspaper
entries.description: A [newspaper](#newspaper) is opened out in both hands or [folded](#folded) under an arm. Breakfast tables, commutes and cafes are the usual company.

entries.name: holding_map
entries.description: A [map](#map) is spread between both hands or carried [folded](#folded) in one, usually while somebody works out the route. Travel and adventure scenes.

entries.name: holding_with_tail
entries.description: An object is carried by the [tail](#tail) rather than the hands, curled around and gripped. This needs a tail [flexible](#flexible) enough to work like a limb.

entries.name: holding_key
entries.description: A [key](#key) is pinched between the fingers or swings from a [ring](#ring), often raised so its shape reads clearly. Doors, locks and symbolic framing accompany it.

entries.name: holding_whisk
entries.description: A [wire](#wire) [whisk](#whisk) is gripped in the hand, usually with a [mixing](#mixing) [bowl](#bowl) close by. Add [cooking](#cooking) when [batter](#batter) or [cream](#cream) is actually being [beaten](#beaten).

entries.name: holding_bra
entries.description: A [bra](#bra) has come off and now hangs from the fingers or lies bunched in the palm. It applies to the garment out of place, never to one still being worn.

entries.name: object_on_breast
entries.description: Something rests or is balanced on the [breasts](#breasts), which serve as a [shelf](#shelf) for it. The object may be set there by the character herself or by somebody else as a joke.

entries.name: holding_surfboard
entries.description: A [surfboard](#surfboard) is carried under an arm or stood on end with a hand steadying it. The water's edge is the usual setting.

entries.name: holding_carton
entries.description: A paperboard [carton](#carton) of the sort [milk](#milk) or [juice](#juice) comes in is held. The name is vague, so [holding_milk_carton](#holding_milk_carton), [holding_juice_box](#holding_juice_box) or a [box](#box) [tag](#tag) usually fits the picture better.

entries.name: holding_torch
entries.description: A [burning](#burning) [torch](#torch) is raised in the hand, [throwing](#throwing) light through a [cave](#cave), a [night](#night) scene or a procession. The flame is what separates it from a [flashlight](#flashlight).

entries.name: holding_gem
entries.description: A cut stone sits between fingertips or in a cupped palm, often [catching](#catching) the light. Treasure piles, jewellery work and [magic](#magic) scenes all produce it.

entries.name: umbrella_over_shoulder
entries.description: An open [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol) rested against the shoulder rather than held overhead, often twirled idly. A relaxed, decorative way of [carrying](#carrying) one.

entries.name: holding_bell
entries.description: A [bell](#bell) rests in the hand, from a small ringing hand bell to the suzu of a [shrine](#shrine). Bells fastened to a [collar](#collar) or tied into the hair are worn rather than held.

entries.name: holding_rope
entries.description: A [rope](#rope) is in the hands, [coiled](#coiled) up, trailing loose or pulled taut. Climbing, hauling and [tying](#tying) scenes all qualify.

entries.name: holding_flask
entries.description: A [flask](#flask) of some kind is held: a conical [laboratory](#laboratory) vessel, a hip flask of spirits, or a [fantasy](#fantasy) [potion](#potion) [bottle](#bottle). The contents are often coloured and clearly visible.

entries.name: holding_lighter
entries.description: A [lighter](#lighter) sits in the hand, flame up or a thumb on the [wheel](#wheel), frequently [reaching](#reaching) towards a [cigarette](#cigarette) or a [candle](#candle).

entries.name: ofuda_between_fingers
entries.description: Paper talismans are fanned out between the fingers of one hand, ready to be thrown or slapped onto a [target](#target).

entries.name: holding_marker
entries.description: A [marker](#marker) [pen](#pen) is in the hand with the cap off, poised over a [whiteboard](#whiteboard), a [sign](#sign) or a sheet of [paper](#paper). Writing and signing scenes.

entries.name: holding_crowbar
entries.description: A [crowbar](#crowbar) is gripped in one or both hands, equally at home prying something open or [serving](#serving) as an improvised [weapon](#weapon). The hooked end usually shows.

entries.name: holding_notepad
entries.description: A small [notepad](#notepad) rests in one hand with a [pen](#pen) ready in the other. Reporters, [waiting](#waiting) [staff](#staff) and detectives are the stock users.

entries.name: holding_calligraphy_brush
entries.description: A brush for [writing](#writing) characters in [ink](#ink) is held, generally upright over [paper](#paper). Its thick soft tuft and long [handle](#handle) set it apart from a painter's brush.

entries.name: holding_candle
entries.description: A [candle](#candle) is carried in the hand or on a small dish, generally lit and lighting the scene by itself. Candlesticks and [candelabra](#candelabra) are tagged separately.

entries.name: holding_watering_can
entries.description: A [watering](#watering) [can](#can) hangs from the hand, usually while plants or a [garden](#garden) are being tended. Add [gardening](#gardening) when the watering is actually under way.

entries.name: holding_handcuffs
entries.description: Handcuffs dangle from a finger or are held out, open or already snapped shut. Nobody's wrists are inside them, which would call for a restraint [tag](#tag).

entries.name: holding_binoculars
entries.description: Field [glasses](#glasses) are in the hands, either raised to the eyes for a distant look or simply carried on their [strap](#strap). Lookouts, birdwatching and [stadium](#stadium) scenes [suit](#suit) it.

entries.name: holding_menu
entries.description: A [restaurant](#restaurant) [menu](#menu) is open in the hands while an order is decided. Cafes and dining rooms provide the setting.

entries.name: holding_feather
entries.description: A single feather is pinched between the fingers, sometimes trailed over skin, sometimes simply admired. A [quill](#quill) used for [writing](#writing) is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: holding_blanket
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) is bunched in the arms or gripped by a [corner](#corner), carried towards a [bed](#bed) or about to be laid over someone. One wrapped around the body is worn, not held.

entries.name: holding_chainsaw
entries.description: A [chainsaw](#chainsaw) is gripped by both handles, often raised and ready. Horror scenes and [comic](#comic) overkill account for most of its use.

entries.name: holding_reins
entries.description: Reins are gripped, steering a [horse](#horse) or another mount from the [saddle](#saddle) or from the ground. Riding and [carriage](#carriage) scenes.

entries.name: object_floating_above_hand
entries.description: An item or a [glowing](#glowing) shape hangs in the air over an open or cupped palm with nothing touching it. It may be a [spell](#spell) taking form, [telekinesis](#telekinesis) at work, or simply a [coin](#coin) at the top of its flip.

entries.name: holding_jar
entries.description: A [jar](#jar) is carried in the hands, [lid](#lid) on or off, its contents often visible through the [glass](#glass). Preserves, specimens and [captured](#captured) creatures all end up inside.

entries.name: holding_pocket_watch
entries.description: A [pocket](#pocket) [watch](#watch) swings from its [chain](#chain) or lies open on the palm, the face angled so the time reads. Period and time-themed pictures.

entries.name: holding_baton
entries.description: A short rod is held in the hand: a conductor's baton, a [police](#police) truncheon, a relay [stick](#stick) or a majorette's twirling baton. It is slim and gripped at one end.

entries.name: holding_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) is gripped in the hand, [hanging](#hanging) loose after being pulled off or held while it is knotted. Tugging at somebody else's tie counts too.

entries.name: holding_comb
entries.description: A [comb](#comb) is in the hand, frequently mid-stroke through hair. A bristled brush belongs to [holding_hair_brush](#holding_hair_brush) instead.

entries.name: holding_flower_pot
entries.description: A potted [plant](#plant) is carried in the hands or braced against the body, generally being moved or handed over. The pot rather than a bare plant is what is gripped.

entries.name: holding_mahjong_tile
entries.description: A [mahjong](#mahjong) tile is pinched between the fingers, generally mid-game beside a wall or a hand of [tiles](#tiles). The face is often turned towards the viewer.

entries.name: holding_whistle
entries.description: A [whistle](#whistle) sits between the fingers or is being blown, sometimes still [hanging](#hanging) on its cord. Coaches, referees and teachers turn up [carrying](#carrying) one.

entries.name: holding_sketchbook
entries.description: A [sketchbook](#sketchbook) is open in the hands or carried shut under an arm, frequently with a [pencil](#pencil) in the other hand. Artists at work.

entries.name: holding_shower_head
entries.description: A detachable shower head is gripped in the hand, [water](#water) usually [running](#running) from it. Bathrooms, [washing](#washing) and [bathing](#bathing) scenes, at times with the spray aimed at somebody else.

entries.name: heavy
entries.description: A character is plainly [struggling](#struggling) with the [weight](#weight) of what they hold or carry: arms [shaking](#shaking), [back](#back) bent, [knees](#knees) [giving](#giving) under it. The strain is the point of the picture.

entries.name: holding_paddle
entries.description: A [paddle](#paddle) is gripped, for propelling a [boat](#boat), for [table](#table) [tennis](#tennis), or as a flat wooden implement. The surroundings say which sort is meant.

entries.name: holding_mallet
entries.description: A [mallet](#mallet) is gripped, from the wooden [kine](#kine) used to pound [mochi](#mochi) to a squeaky [toy](#toy) [hammer](#hammer). Both work and slapstick call for it.

entries.name: holding_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) is carried in the hands rather than wound round a [neck](#neck), just pulled off or about to be draped over somebody.

entries.name: pipe_in_mouth
entries.description: A [smoking](#smoking) pipe held between the [lips](#lips) or clamped in the [teeth](#teeth), lit or not. The [bowl](#bowl) and stem [hanging](#hanging) from the mouth are the [marker](#marker).

entries.name: holding_pregnancy_test
entries.description: A pregnancy test [stick](#stick) is held in the hands, its little result [window](#window) the point of the picture. Shock or joy on the face usually accompanies it.

entries.name: holding_cigar
entries.description: A [cigar](#cigar) sits between the fingers, lit or unlit, generally with a relaxed or self-satisfied air. One clamped in the [teeth](#teeth) with [no](#no) hand on it is tagged differently.

entries.name: instrument_on_back
entries.description: An [instrument](#instrument), or the case [holding](#holding) one, is slung across somebody's [back](#back) on a [strap](#strap). It is being carried rather than played, and guitars are far and away the usual load.

entries.name: holding_palette
entries.description: A painter's palette is balanced on the hand or hooked over the thumb, dabs of colour across its face. A brush usually occupies the other hand.

entries.name: holding_pickaxe
entries.description: A [pickaxe](#pickaxe) is gripped, shouldered while [walking](#walking) or swung down into [rock](#rock). Mines, quarries and [dungeon](#dungeon) corridors supply the setting, and it doubles as a [weapon](#weapon) easily enough.

entries.name: holding_orb
entries.description: A sphere is cradled in the hand, a [crystal](#crystal) [ball](#ball), a [glowing](#glowing) magical [orb](#orb) or a ruler's [globe](#globe) of regalia. Fantasy and fortune-telling settings.

entries.name: holding_barcode_scanner
entries.description: A handheld [barcode](#barcode) reader rests in the hand, the pistol-shaped sort used at a till. Convenience stores, warehouses and [cashier](#cashier) scenes are where it turns up.

entries.name: holding_racket
entries.description: A [racket](#racket) is gripped, [tennis](#tennis) or [badminton](#badminton), poised for a shot or [resting](#resting) on a shoulder. Courts and sports club scenes.

entries.name: holding_flashlight
entries.description: A [torch](#torch) is gripped in the hand, its beam often the only light in the picture. Night, investigation and horror settings favour it.

entries.name: holding_hair_brush
entries.description: A bristled brush is in the hand, commonly mid-stroke through hair, the character's own or somebody else's. A toothed [comb](#comb) belongs to [holding_comb](#holding_comb).

entries.name: carrying_overhead
entries.description: An object or a person is held up above the head on raised arms. The whole [weight](#weight) rests on the hands and outstretched arms.

entries.name: holding_duster
entries.description: A feather [duster](#duster) sits in the hand, usually mid-clean. It is a stock [maid](#maid) prop and tends to arrive with an [apron](#apron).

entries.name: holding_handkerchief
entries.description: A small [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) sits in the hand, offered to somebody, dabbing at [tears](#tears) or [sweat](#sweat), or simply carried.

entries.name: holding_star
entries.description: A star sits in the hand, a solid ornament, a [paper](#paper) cutout or an impossible [glowing](#glowing) one plucked from the [sky](#sky). Whimsical and symbolic framing.

entries.name: object_in_clothes
entries.description: Something with [no](#no) business being there has been pushed into the clothing, down a [collar](#collar), behind a waistband or under a hem, with its shape showing through the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: holding_pendulum
entries.description: A [weight](#weight) on a [string](#string) or [chain](#chain) dangles from the fingers, often drawn mid-swing. It is the standard prop for [hypnosis](#hypnosis) and for dowsing.

entries.name: holding_petal
entries.description: Flower [petals](#petals) rest in the fingers or a cupped palm, at times about to be scattered on the [wind](#wind). Romantic and springtime imagery.

entries.name: holding_pointer
entries.description: A [pointer](#pointer) [stick](#stick) is gripped, tapping at a board, a [chart](#chart) or a [map](#map). Lessons, briefings and presentations are the setting, and teachers are the stock users.

entries.name: holding_butterfly_net
entries.description: An insect [net](#net) on a long [handle](#handle) is carried, typically mid-chase on a [summer](#summer) [day](#day). Bug-catching and countryside scenes go with it.

entries.name: holding_chess_piece
entries.description: A single [chess](#chess) piece is lifted between the fingers, mid-move or held up for effect. A board may sit below it or be absent entirely.

entries.name: glove_in_mouth
entries.description: A glove gripped between the [teeth](#teeth), usually just after being pulled off. When the teeth are doing the [pulling](#pulling), [biting_glove](#biting_glove) is the closer [tag](#tag).

entries.name: holding_bass_guitar
entries.description: A bass [guitar](#guitar) is carried or gripped by the [neck](#neck) without being played. Once the strings are actually being worked, [playing_bass_guitar](#playing_bass_guitar) describes the picture better.

entries.name: holding_cloth
entries.description: A loose piece of [fabric](#fabric) is held in the hands: a [wiping](#wiping) rag, a [wrapping](#wrapping) [cloth](#cloth), or an unidentified swatch. Named garments and towels have tags of their own.

entries.name: bikini_in_mouth
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) held between the [teeth](#teeth), most often the strings of the top while it is being tied or untied. The bottom [can](#can) be carried the same way.

entries.name: holding_bone
entries.description: A [bone](#bone) is gripped in the hand or clamped in the jaws: a comedy drumstick, a dog's treat, a skeletal remain. Playful and grim scenes both use it.

entries.name: holding_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) hangs from the hand rather than the shoulders, carried after removal or swept aside. It must not be worn for the [tag](#tag) to apply.

entries.name: holding_string
entries.description: A length of [string](#string) or [thread](#thread) is pinched in the fingers, pulled taut or [hanging](#hanging) slack. Balloons, kites and [sewing](#sewing) usually explain it.

entries.name: holding_sponge
entries.description: A [sponge](#sponge) is gripped, as a rule soapy, while [dishes](#dishes), a [car](#car) or a body are washed. Bath and chore scenes.

entries.name: holding_clothes_hanger
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) hanger is raised in the hand, frequently with a garment still on it while an outfit is chosen. Wardrobes and [shop](#shop) racks are the usual [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: holding_magazine
entries.description: A magazine lies open across the hands or is carried rolled up, the reader looking down at a page. This is the printed kind; a firearm's is [holding_magazine_(weapon)](#holding_magazine_(weapon)).

entries.name: holding_chalk
entries.description: A stub of [chalk](#chalk) is pinched between the fingers, generally at a blackboard during a lesson. Chalk [dust](#dust) and [writing](#writing) on the board often come with it.

entries.name: holding_party_popper
entries.description: A [party](#party) popper is gripped, its [string](#string) about to be pulled or [streamers](#streamers) already bursting from the end. Birthdays, celebrations and new-year pictures.

entries.name: holding_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) rests in the hands instead of on the head, lifted before a coronation or turned over thoughtfully. It must be off the head to count.

entries.name: holding_paper_airplane
entries.description: A [folded](#folded) [paper](#paper) plane rests in the fingers, commonly wound [back](#back) to throw. Classrooms and idle daydreaming are its setting.

entries.name: tossing
entries.description: Something is thrown lightly into the air with a [flick](#flick) of the wrist, [caught](#caught) again a beat later or left [hanging](#hanging) mid-flight. The motion reads as [casual](#casual) play rather than a forceful throw.

entries.name: holding_headphones
entries.description: Headphones are in the hands, lifted off the ears mid-conversation or [swinging](#swinging) by the band. Small in-ear buds go to [holding_earphones](#holding_earphones).

entries.name: holding_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) is slung over the arm or dangles from the hand instead of being worn. Arriving, leaving and handing a coat over are the usual scenes.

entries.name: holding_earphones
entries.description: Earbuds or [earphones](#earphones) sit in the hand, often with one [bud](#bud) lifted towards or away from an ear. The [cable](#cable) usually runs off to a [phone](#phone) or player.

entries.name: holding_ring
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) is pinched between fingertips rather than worn, very often presented during a proposal. A ring [box](#box) and an engagement scene tend to follow.

entries.name: holding_rod
entries.description: A rod is gripped, whether a [fishing](#fishing) rod, a slender [staff](#staff) or a [plain](#plain) metal bar. The name is vague, so a more exact [tag](#tag) usually serves better.

entries.name: holding_wallet
entries.description: A [wallet](#wallet) or purse rests in the hand, frequently flipped open to pay or to count what is inside. Shopping and [money](#money) scenes are its home.

entries.name: holding_tanzaku
entries.description: The [paper](#paper) strip a wish is written on at Tanabata sits in the hand, usually just before it is tied to a [bamboo](#bamboo) [branch](#branch). Summer [festival](#festival) scenes.

entries.name: holding_tennis_racket
entries.description: A [tennis](#tennis) [racket](#racket) is gripped, poised for a serve or [resting](#resting) on a shoulder between points. Courts and club scenes.

entries.name: holding_hair_dryer
entries.description: A hair dryer is raised in the hand and generally aimed at damp hair. Bathrooms and after-bath routines are the setting.

entries.name: holding_stethoscope
entries.description: A [stethoscope](#stethoscope) is held in the hands, at times with the chest piece pressed against somebody. Doctors, nurses and check-ups.

entries.name: holding_gloves
entries.description: One or both [gloves](#gloves) have been peeled off and dangle from the fingers, leaving the hands themselves bare. It counts among the removed-clothing holds.

entries.name: holding_eyeball
entries.description: A loose [eyeball](#eyeball) sits in the palm or between the fingers, detached from any head. Horror, [surreal](#surreal) and [monster](#monster) imagery make the most of it.

entries.name: holding_cleaver
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) square-bladed chopper is gripped, for [cooking](#cooking) or as a blunt [threat](#threat). The broad rectangular blade sets it apart from an ordinary [kitchen](#kitchen) [knife](#knife).

entries.name: holding_oar
entries.description: An [oar](#oar) or [rowing](#rowing) [paddle](#paddle) is gripped, dipped into [water](#water) from a [boat](#boat) or shouldered on land. Rivers, lakes and boating scenes.

entries.name: holding_cage
entries.description: A [cage](#cage) is carried by its [handle](#handle) or [hoop](#hoop), birdcages being the commonest kind. Whatever sits inside may be an [animal](#animal), a [spirit](#spirit) or a tiny person.

entries.name: holding_goggles
entries.description: Goggles rest in the hand rather than over the eyes or pushed up on the [forehead](#forehead). Swimming, welding, aviation and ski [goggles](#goggles) all qualify.

entries.name: holding_anchor
entries.description: A ship's [anchor](#anchor) is in hand, shouldered, dragged along or swung about as an oversized [weapon](#weapon). Naval-themed characters use one as a prop.

entries.name: holding_skateboard
entries.description: A [skateboard](#skateboard) is tucked under an arm or carried by the deck instead of being ridden. Streets and skate parks.

entries.name: holding_trophy
entries.description: A [trophy](#trophy) or [cup](#cup) is held, frequently lifted overhead in [victory](#victory). Sports finals, award ceremonies and [podium](#podium) pictures, usually with a delighted expression to match.

entries.name: holding_trumpet
entries.description: A [trumpet](#trumpet) sits in the hands, raised to the [lips](#lips) or simply carried at the side. Add [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) only when the horn is actually being blown.

entries.name: holding_cooking_pot
entries.description: A [cooking](#cooking) pot or [saucepan](#saucepan) is carried by its handles, sometimes still steaming. Kitchens and campfires are where it shows up.

entries.name: holding_ticket
entries.description: One or more tickets are pinched between the fingers, frequently turned towards the viewer so the printing reads. Cinemas, concerts and travel scenes.

entries.name: necktie_in_mouth
entries.description: Someone bites the loose end of the tie they are wearing, lifting it away from the chest. The tie has to be worn rather than merely carried.

entries.name: holding_boxcutter
entries.description: A retractable utility [knife](#knife) is in the hand, blade run out or still closed. It reads as an [office](#office) tool or as a [threat](#threat) depending on the scene.

entries.name: holding_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) rests in the hands rather than round a [neck](#neck), sometimes held out towards someone else. Pet collars, [animal](#animal) collars and [fashion](#fashion) pieces all count.

entries.name: holding_id_card
entries.description: An identity [card](#card) is held up, a student pass, [staff](#staff) [badge](#badge) or licence, very often turned to face the viewer. Checkpoints and introductions call for it.

entries.name: holding_unworn_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) that is off the body is held in the hands. While it is still worn the [gesture](#gesture) has its own tags: [clothes_grab](#clothes_grab) for a [plain](#plain) grip, [skirt_hold](#skirt_hold) for a modest one, [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift) for a revealing one and [skirt_tug](#skirt_tug) for [pulling](#pulling) it down.

entries.name: holding_unworn_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) nobody is wearing is held in the hands, just taken off or about to be put on. With the dress still on the body, reach for [clothes_grab](#clothes_grab), dress_hold, [dress_lift](#dress_lift) or [dress_tug](#dress_tug) according to what the hands are doing.

entries.name: holding_screwdriver
entries.description: A [screwdriver](#screwdriver) is gripped, frequently mid-repair beside an opened panel or a [machine](#machine). Workshops, tinkering and [mechanic](#mechanic) scenes, sometimes with other [tools](#tools) laid out nearby.

entries.name: panties_in_mouth
entries.description: A pair of [panties](#panties) gripped in the [teeth](#teeth) and left [hanging](#hanging) from the mouth, often while [undressing](#undressing). Underwear bunched up and pushed inside to silence someone is [panty_gag](#panty_gag).

entries.name: holding_snowball
entries.description: A packed [snowball](#snowball) rests in the hands, very often wound [back](#back) and about to be thrown. Winter play and snowball fights, generally with [heavy](#heavy) coats and [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: holding_walkie-talkie
entries.description: A handheld two-way [radio](#radio) is in the hand, often raised toward the mouth to speak into it. Soldiers, [police](#police) and [rescue](#rescue) workers are its usual carriers.

entries.name: holding_dumbbell
entries.description: A [dumbbell](#dumbbell) is gripped, curled at the side or pressed overhead. Gyms, home workouts and [muscular](#muscular) characters are its home ground.

entries.name: holding_lamp
entries.description: A [lamp](#lamp) is carried by hand, an oil lamp or [lantern](#lantern) most often, lighting the way through a [dark](#dark) scene. It has to be lifted rather than [standing](#standing) on a [table](#table).

entries.name: holding_case
entries.description: A case is carried by hand: a [briefcase](#briefcase), an [instrument](#instrument) case, or a small [container](#container) for [glasses](#glasses) or jewellery. What it holds is often out of sight.

entries.name: holding_hand_grip
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) [strap](#strap) or grab [handle](#handle) is held for balance, the loops in a [train](#train) or [bus](#bus) [carriage](#carriage) being the standard case. The pose puts the subject [standing](#standing) in a moving vehicle.

entries.name: holding_boots
entries.description: Boots dangle from the hand instead of [sitting](#sitting) on the [feet](#feet), generally just pulled off. Bare feet or [socks](#socks) usually show alongside.

entries.name: holding_shell
entries.description: A [seashell](#seashell) rests in the hand or a cupped palm, at times raised to an ear. Beaches and [summer](#summer) scenes.

entries.name: holding_folder
entries.description: A document [folder](#folder) is hugged against the body or flipped open in the hands. School corridors, offices and clinics are typical.

entries.name: holding_golf_club
entries.description: A [golf](#golf) club is gripped, lined up behind a [ball](#ball) or shouldered while [walking](#walking) between shots. Fairways, [driving](#driving) ranges and putting greens supply the [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: holding_sandals
entries.description: Sandals dangle from the hand instead of [sitting](#sitting) on the [feet](#feet), generally slipped off at a [beach](#beach) or a [doorway](#doorway). Bare feet usually follow.

entries.name: card_between_breasts
entries.description: A [card](#card) tucked into the [cleavage](#cleavage) and kept there by the [breasts](#breasts) rather than by a hand. Usually offered out toward the viewer.

entries.name: holding_heart_(organ)
entries.description: The anatomical [heart](#heart), bloody or stylised, is cradled in the hands. It is the organ rather than the rounded symbol used for affection.

entries.name: card_in_mouth
entries.description: A [card](#card) gripped between the [teeth](#teeth) or [lips](#lips), leaving both hands free. Usually a cocky pose during a game or a [duel](#duel).

entries.name: holding_cable
entries.description: A length of [cable](#cable) or [wire](#wire) is gripped, [coiled](#coiled) up or trailing loose across the frame. Electronics, [machinery](#machinery) and repair work supply most of the context.

entries.name: holding_picture_frame
entries.description: A framed picture is carried in the hands, as a rule turned so the [portrait](#portrait) or photograph inside reads. Memory and [mourning](#mourning) scenes use it.

entries.name: holding_crayon
entries.description: A [wax](#wax) [crayon](#crayon) is clutched in the fist or the fingers, generally over a drawing in progress. The prop suggests a [child](#child), or a deliberately childlike scene.

entries.name: eyewear_in_mouth
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) gripped between the [teeth](#teeth) or [lips](#lips) rather than worn. Usually because both hands are busy with something else.

entries.name: holding_drawing
entries.description: A sheet with a picture on it is raised in the hands, often shown proudly to the viewer or to another character. The drawing itself is visible in the frame.

entries.name: holding_bullet
entries.description: A single cartridge is pinched between the fingertips or lies in an open palm, often while a [weapon](#weapon) is loaded or a round inspected. The [bullet](#bullet) is loose rather than chambered.

entries.name: holding_laptop
entries.description: A [laptop](#laptop) is carried in the hands or balanced along one forearm, [lid](#lid) open or shut. It must be off the [desk](#desk) and supported by the person.

entries.name: holding_pitchfork
entries.description: A [pitchfork](#pitchfork) is gripped in one or both hands, as a [farm](#farm) implement or in the hands of an [angry](#angry) mob or a devil. The long shaft and prongs give it away.

entries.name: holding_rattle
entries.description: A baby's [rattle](#rattle) is gripped and usually shaken, by an infant or by an adult entertaining one. Nurseries and pictures of very small children are where it appears.

entries.name: holding_wreath
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of woven leaves, branches or flowers is carried in the hands. It covers both the [door](#door) [wreath](#wreath) of [winter](#winter) scenes and a [flower](#flower) [crown](#crown) not yet placed on anyone's head.

entries.name: holding_scale
entries.description: A set of [scales](#scales) is raised in the hand, the two-pan balance kind most often. It works as a stock [emblem](#emblem) of judgement and fairness.

entries.name: holding_scalpel
entries.description: A [scalpel](#scalpel) is pinched between the fingers, the small blade [catching](#catching) the light. Surgery, dissection and horror scenes use it in equal measure.

entries.name: holding_vial
entries.description: A small stoppered phial sits between the fingers, usually filled with brightly coloured [liquid](#liquid). Alchemists, witches and [laboratory](#laboratory) scenes account for most of them.

entries.name: holding_dice
entries.description: One or more [dice](#dice) sit in the fingers or an open palm, often about to be thrown. Gambling scenes and tabletop games both use it.

entries.name: holding_rock
entries.description: A [rock](#rock) or stone rests in the hand, picked up for a look, weighed thoughtfully or wound [back](#back) to throw. Sizes run from a [pebble](#pebble) to a [boulder](#boulder).

entries.name: holding_legwear
entries.description: Socks, [kneehighs](#kneehighs), [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or tights are carried in the hand after coming off. Add the specific garment [tag](#tag) to say which kind is meant.

entries.name: holding_nail
entries.description: A nail is pinched between the fingertips, as a rule with a [hammer](#hammer) [waiting](#waiting) in the other hand. Building and repair scenes.

entries.name: card_between_fingers
entries.description: A [card](#card) pinched between the index and middle fingers and held up to be seen. A gambler's or duellist's flourish.

entries.name: holding_hair_tie
entries.description: An elastic band or hair tie is pinched in the fingers, at times gripped in the [teeth](#teeth) while both hands gather the hair up. Tying-up [poses](#poses) use it constantly.

entries.name: holding_sheet
entries.description: A [bed](#bed) sheet is gathered into the hands and lifted or carried. Merely clutching at it where it lies is better described as [sheet_grab](#sheet_grab).

entries.name: holding_cue_stick
entries.description: A billiard cue is held, lined up across the [table](#table) for a shot or stood upright against the body. Pool halls and [bars](#bars) are the usual [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: apple_on_head
entries.description: An [apple](#apple) is balanced on top of somebody's head, [resting](#resting) there unheld. The archery-target joke is nearly always the reason.

entries.name: holding_sewing_needle
entries.description: A [sewing](#sewing) [needle](#needle) is pinched between fingertips with [thread](#thread) trailing from the eye, while something is [stitched](#stitched) or mended. Fabric, a [spool](#spool) and a thimble often accompany it.

entries.name: holding_bow_(ornament)
entries.description: A decorative [ribbon](#ribbon) [bow](#bow) is held in the hand, often a [gift](#gift) trimming or a hair bow not yet tied on. It excludes an archer's bow and a [violin](#violin) bow, which have tags of their own.

entries.name: holding_hair_ornament
entries.description: A hair ornament sits in the hand rather than [pinned](#pinned) in place, as a rule about to go in or just taken out.

entries.name: object_behind_ear
entries.description: Something slim such as a [pencil](#pencil), a [cigarette](#cigarette) or a [flower](#flower) is wedged between the ear and the head, staying put with [no](#no) hand on it.

entries.name: holding_snowman
entries.description: A small [snowman](#snowman) is carried in the hands, a [miniature](#miniature) rather than one built on the ground. Winter and holiday scenes.

entries.name: holding_ruler
entries.description: A [ruler](#ruler) is gripped, [measuring](#measuring) something, guiding a drawn line or tapped about like a [pointer](#pointer). Classrooms and drawing desks.

entries.name: flower_to_mouth
entries.description: A blossom raised to the [lips](#lips), kissed or [caught](#caught) in the [teeth](#teeth). The [gesture](#gesture) normally reads as flirtatious or theatrical.

entries.name: holding_mistletoe
entries.description: A sprig of [mistletoe](#mistletoe) is raised, often dangled over another character to invoke the Christmas kissing custom. Winter and holiday pictures.

entries.name: holding_banner
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) [banner](#banner) or [hanging](#hanging) [sign](#sign) is carried, often raised on a [pole](#pole) at a rally, [festival](#festival) or fan event. One person may hold it alone or two may take an end each.

entries.name: holding_charm
entries.description: A small charm or [amulet](#amulet) dangles from the fingers, a keychain trinket or a lucky [omamori](#omamori). The framing usually brings it near enough to read the design.

entries.name: holding_cigarette_pack
entries.description: A [packet](#packet) of cigarettes rests in the hand, sometimes flipped open with one [stick](#stick) drawn out. The pack itself is the object of interest, not a lit [cigarette](#cigarette).

entries.name: holding_crystal
entries.description: A [crystal](#crystal) is cradled in the palm or pinched between the fingertips, frequently [glowing](#glowing) or splitting the light. Fantasy and magical settings favour the prop.

entries.name: holding_maracas
entries.description: Maracas are gripped, as a rule one in each hand and shaken. Music, [party](#party) and [festival](#festival) pictures are where they turn up, often as part of a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: holding_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) is carried in the hand instead of [sitting](#sitting) on the head, freshly slipped off or about to be put on. The hair usually hangs loose.

entries.name: holding_jug
entries.description: A jug or pitcher is carried by its [handle](#handle), at times tipped over to pour. Kitchens, taverns and [market](#market) stalls are the usual company.

entries.name: holding_clover
entries.description: A [clover](#clover) is pinched between the fingers and shown off, most often the four-leaf sort offered as luck. The framing tends to bring it close to the viewer.

entries.name: holding_bandages
entries.description: Rolled or trailing bandage material is in the hand, usually just before a wound gets wrapped. It is the loose [dressing](#dressing), not bandaging already applied to a body.

entries.name: holding_tripod
entries.description: A [camera](#camera) [tripod](#tripod) is carried, [folded](#folded) over a shoulder or steadied by a leg while set up. Photography and filming scenes.

entries.name: holding_razor
entries.description: A [razor](#razor) is in the hand, either a safety razor for [shaving](#shaving) or an open straight razor, which reads as a [threat](#threat) as readily as grooming.

entries.name: holding_telescope
entries.description: A [telescope](#telescope) is carried in the hands, small handheld spyglasses being the common kind, sometimes raised to one eye. Stargazing and seafaring.

entries.name: holding_thermometer
entries.description: A [thermometer](#thermometer) is gripped in the hand, clinical or otherwise, generally being read after a [temperature](#temperature) has been taken. Sickbeds, clinics and check-up scenes.

entries.name: holding_tool
entries.description: A tool of some kind is in the hand, a broad [label](#label) covering hammers, wrenches, screwdrivers and their kin. Where an exact [tag](#tag) exists, prefer it.

entries.name: holding_manga
entries.description: A manga volume or [comic](#comic) [book](#book) is held, open at a page or shut with the [cover](#cover) showing. Reading, bookshops and [school](#school) desks are the settings.

entries.name: object_in_swimsuit
entries.description: An item is slipped inside a [swimsuit](#swimsuit), the tight [fabric](#fabric) pinning it against the body. Beach scenes use it for phones, drinks [money](#money) and stray shells alike.

entries.name: holding_own_leash
entries.description: A [leash](#leash) clipped to the character's own [collar](#collar) is gripped in the hand or the [teeth](#teeth). Held out towards the viewer or another character, [offering_leash](#offering_leash) describes it better.

entries.name: holding_pill
entries.description: A [pill](#pill) or capsule is pinched between fingertips or lies on an open palm, often on its way to the mouth. Sickbeds and [medicine](#medicine) scenes.

entries.name: holding_vase
entries.description: A [vase](#vase) is cradled against the body or carried by its [neck](#neck). It may stand empty or hold an arrangement of flowers.

entries.name: pencil_as_mustache
entries.description: A [pencil](#pencil) or [pen](#pen) balanced between the [nose](#nose) and the upper lip so that it hangs there like a false moustache. An idle [gag](#gag), usually done out of boredom.

entries.name: holding_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) hangs loose from the hand instead of being buckled round a waist. Undressing scenes and strap-swinging threats are where it appears.

entries.name: holding_drawing_tablet
entries.description: A graphics tablet is carried in the hands, lifted rather than [lying](#lying) flat on a [desk](#desk). Artist self-portraits and [studio](#studio) scenes account for most of it.

entries.name: holding_boombox
entries.description: A portable [stereo](#stereo) is carried by its [handle](#handle) or hoisted up onto one shoulder. The prop pulls a picture towards [street](#street), dance and retro settings.

entries.name: holding_pinwheel
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [pinwheel](#pinwheel) on its [stick](#stick) is raised in the hand, the vanes frequently [caught](#caught) [spinning](#spinning). Festivals and childhood scenes are its home.

entries.name: doll_on_head
entries.description: A [doll](#doll) balanced on top of somebody's head, [sitting](#sitting) upright or slumped over to one side. Played for charm, and the character below usually pretends not to notice.

entries.name: holding_saxophone
entries.description: A [saxophone](#saxophone) is held at the body or hangs from its [neck](#neck) [strap](#strap). Actually [blowing](#blowing) it calls for a [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: holding_computer_mouse
entries.description: A [computer](#computer) mouse sits under the hand or has been lifted clear of the [desk](#desk). Desk setups, gaming and [office](#office) work supply the context.

entries.name: holding_water
entries.description: Water is cupped in the [palms](#palms), scooped up from a [stream](#stream), [basin](#basin) or spring. The hands themselves are the vessel, with [no](#no) [cup](#cup) or [bowl](#bowl) involved.

entries.name: holding_compact
entries.description: A powder compact lies open on the palm, its little [mirror](#mirror) often [catching](#catching) the face. This is the [cosmetics](#cosmetics) case, nothing mechanical.

entries.name: holding_veil
entries.description: Fingers grip a [veil](#veil), most often a [bride](#bride) lifting the [fabric](#fabric) away from her face. It also covers a veil carried loose in the hands rather than worn at all.

entries.name: object_in_panties
entries.description: An item is tucked inside the [panties](#panties) and held against the skin by the [fabric](#fabric), its [outline](#outline) usually pressing through. It may be anything from a [phone](#phone) to a keepsake.

entries.name: holding_bandaid
entries.description: An adhesive plaster is pinched between the fingers, generally about to be pressed onto a [scrape](#scrape). It must be loose in the hand rather than [stuck](#stuck) to skin.

entries.name: holding_cd
entries.description: An optical disc or its jewel case is held up, sometimes tilted so the surface throws a [rainbow](#rainbow). It reads as a [music](#music) or software prop.

entries.name: holding_matchstick
entries.description: A match is pinched between the fingers, freshly struck or still unlit. A small flame and [dark](#dark) surroundings usually go with it.

entries.name: pen_to_mouth
entries.description: A [pen](#pen) or [pencil](#pencil) held against the [lips](#lips) or [teeth](#teeth), usually while the character thinks or hesitates over what to write next.

entries.name: money_fan
entries.description: Banknotes held spread apart between the fingers so that they splay out like a folding fan. Almost always a boast about how much the character is [carrying](#carrying).

entries.name: incoming_letter
entries.description: A [letter](#letter) or sealed [envelope](#envelope) held out toward the viewer, often with the [shy](#shy) bearing of a [confession](#confession). The viewer is being asked to take it.

entries.name: bag_on_lap
