entries.description: A seated character rests a [bag](#bag) across their [thighs](#thighs), often steadying it with a hand or both. It is typical of someone [waiting](#waiting) on a [bench](#bench) or [riding](#riding) a [train](#train).

entries.name: holding_dustpan
entries.description: A [dustpan](#dustpan) is carried in one hand, generally with a [broom](#broom) or brush in the other while sweepings are gathered. Housework and [classroom](#classroom) [cleaning](#cleaning) are the settings.

entries.name: holding_digital_media_player
entries.description: A portable [music](#music) player rests in the hand, an earphone [cable](#cable) commonly trailing away from it. The [device](#device) dates a picture to a mid-2000s look.

entries.name: holding_eyepatch
entries.description: An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) is in the hand rather than over an eye, just pulled off or about to be tied on. The face beneath is normally visible.

entries.name: holding_rag
entries.description: A [cleaning](#cleaning) rag sits in the hand, often mid-wipe across a surface. Housework, [maid](#maid) duties and workshops account for it, usually with a [bucket](#bucket) or a soapy [sink](#sink) nearby.

entries.name: holding_shawl
entries.description: A [shawl](#shawl) rests in the hands instead of over the shoulders, gathered up or offered to somebody. The wrap has to be off the body.

entries.name: holding_planet
entries.description: A whole [planet](#planet) sits in the hands, drawn at a scale where a world fits in a palm. Cosmic, divine and symbolic pictures use it.

entries.name: leash_in_mouth
entries.description: The end of a lead is clamped between the [teeth](#teeth), either by the collared character [carrying](#carrying) their own or by a handler keeping both hands free. It reads as playful or as a [pet](#pet) [waiting](#waiting) to be walked.

entries.name: gift_between_breasts
entries.description: A wrapped present held in the [valley](#valley) of the chest with [no](#no) hands on it, the bust alone [pinching](#pinching) it in place. It needs enough volume to grip; a flatter chest needs something else propping the [box](#box) up.

entries.name: holding_candle_stand
entries.description: A candlestick or candelabrum is carried by its base or [ring](#ring) [handle](#handle), often lighting a [dark](#dark) corridor. What is gripped is the stand rather than a bare [candle](#candle).

entries.name: blanket_grab
entries.description: Fingers clutching a [blanket](#blanket), most often [dragging](#dragging) it up around oneself in [bed](#bed). The grip on the [fabric](#fabric) is what is being noted, not merely the blanket's presence.

entries.name: beak_hold
entries.description: A beaked character grips something between the halves of its [beak](#beak), leaving the hands or [claws](#claws) free. The avian counterpart to [carrying](#carrying) an object in the mouth.

entries.name: holding_chair
entries.description: A [chair](#chair) has been lifted clear of the [floor](#floor), carried across a room or swung as a makeshift [weapon](#weapon). Sitting on one is something else entirely.

entries.name: cradling_phone
entries.description: A [phone](#phone) is wedged between ear and shoulder so both hands stay free. Use it in place of [holding_phone](#holding_phone) whenever the phone is carried that way.

entries.name: bullet_in_mouth
entries.description: A cartridge held between the [teeth](#teeth) or [lips](#lips), a piece of gunslinger swagger. The hands are usually busy with the [weapon](#weapon) at the same time.

entries.name: holding_hands
entries.description: Two or more characters have their hands clasped or [resting](#resting) together. Couples, [friends](#friends) and children all qualify, and it has nothing to do with [holding](#holding) an object.

entries.name: carrying
entries.description: A character supports and moves something or someone, in the arms, on the [back](#back) or over a shoulder. Add the specific manner where one applies, such as [princess_carry](#princess_carry) or [piggyback](#piggyback).

entries.name: on_head
entries.description: A living [creature](#creature) or a small character perches on top of somebody's head: a [cat](#cat), a [bird](#bird), a [fairy](#fairy). Lifeless things set there are [object_on_head](#object_on_head).

entries.name: holding_animal
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) such as a [cat](#cat), [bird](#bird) or [rabbit](#rabbit) is carried in the hands or arms. Beings that are not ordinary animals go under [holding_creature](#holding_creature).

entries.name: princess_carry
entries.description: One character carries another cradled in both arms, one arm under the [back](#back) and the other under the [knees](#knees), the way a [groom](#groom) carries a [bride](#bride). Tag [carrying](#carrying) with it.

entries.name: animal_on_head
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) sits on top of somebody's head or [hat](#hat), most often a [cat](#cat) or a [bird](#bird). Stuffed animals count for this as [well](#well).

entries.name: carrying_person
entries.description: One character carries another, most often in the arms or on the [back](#back). Use [princess_carry](#princess_carry) or [piggyback](#piggyback) where the manner is one of those.

entries.name: animal_on_shoulder
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) rides on somebody's shoulder, generally a [bird](#bird) or a small mammal. Narrower tags such as [bird_on_shoulder](#bird_on_shoulder) [can](#can) be added.

entries.name: piggyback
entries.description: One person carried on another's [back](#back), the carrier [holding](#holding) their [legs](#legs) while the rider's arms go round the [neck](#neck) or chest. Riding up on the shoulders instead is [shoulder_carry](#shoulder_carry).

entries.name: bird_on_head
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) perched on top of a character's head or [hat](#hat). One of the [animal_on_head](#animal_on_head) arrangements, and usually played as charming rather than as an [accident](#accident).

entries.name: holding_cat
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) is held in the arms or hands, lifted clear of the ground. A particular case of [holding_animal](#holding_animal).

entries.name: on_shoulder
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) or a small person sits or rides on somebody's shoulder, a [parrot](#parrot), a [cat](#cat), a [child](#child). Objects carried there take [over_shoulder](#over_shoulder) rather than this.

entries.name: on_lap
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) or [creature](#creature) rests on a character's [lap](#lap). When a person is the one on the lap, the tags are [sitting_on_lap](#sitting_on_lap), [lying_on_lap](#lying_on_lap) or [lap_pillow](#lap_pillow).

entries.name: shoulder_carry
entries.description: One person [riding](#riding) on another's shoulders, a leg on each side, often steadying themselves by [holding](#holding) the carrier's head. Implies [carrying](#carrying); someone slung over a shoulder instead is [carrying_over_shoulder](#carrying_over_shoulder).

entries.name: carrying_over_shoulder
entries.description: A person, object or [creature](#creature) is slung over one shoulder, whether a fireman's carry or a [sack](#sack) hauled along. Somebody perched upright there instead is [sitting_on_shoulder](#sitting_on_shoulder).

entries.name: bird_on_hand
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) [resting](#resting) on somebody's hand or finger of its own accord. When the person is actually gripping it, [holding_bird](#holding_bird) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: butterfly_on_hand
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) has settled on a character's hand or fingertip, and they generally hold still to [watch](#watch) it. A quiet moment of contact rather than a catch.

entries.name: animal_hug
entries.description: Someone has their arms around a [creature](#creature), real or invented, [holding](#holding) it against them. Add the species, and a holding [tag](#tag) where the [animal](#animal) is small enough to be carried.

entries.name: bird_on_shoulder
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) perched on a character's shoulder, like a pirate's [parrot](#parrot) or a witch's [familiar](#familiar). One of the [animal_on_shoulder](#animal_on_shoulder) arrangements.

entries.name: cat_on_head
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) is perched on top of a character's head, [sitting](#sitting), [lying](#lying) or draped across it. The person generally holds still and puts up with it.

entries.name: animal_on_lap
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) sits in a seated person's [lap](#lap). It is the [umbrella](#umbrella) over the narrower cases, such as [cat_on_lap](#cat_on_lap) or bird_on_lap.

entries.name: holding_creature
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) that is not an ordinary [animal](#animal) is held: a [mascot](#mascot), a slime, a small [monster](#monster) or a [fantasy](#fantasy) being. Real animals belong to [holding_animal](#holding_animal).

entries.name: animal_on_arm
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) rests along somebody's arm, a [bird](#bird) gripping the forearm or a small mammal [walking](#walking) the sleeve. One gathered up in both arms is [holding_animal](#holding_animal) instead.

entries.name: in_palm
entries.description: A tiny person or [creature](#creature) [standing](#standing) or [sitting](#sitting) in somebody's open hand. It is the usual way to show fairies, minigirls and an extreme [size_difference](#size_difference).

entries.name: holding_fish
entries.description: A [fish](#fish) is held in the hands, live and wriggling or freshly [caught](#caught). A particular case of [holding_animal](#holding_animal).

entries.name: cat_on_shoulder
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) rests on a character's shoulder, balanced there or draped around the [back](#back) of the [neck](#neck). A companion-animal pose.

entries.name: child_carry
entries.description: Someone carries a [child](#child) or small character seated on an arm, fully supported under the bottom. Where the carried person lies cradled across the arms with the [back](#back) supported, use [baby](#baby) carry.

entries.name: animal_on_hand
entries.description: A small [creature](#creature) stands or sits on an open palm or a single outstretched finger. Birds, mice and insects are the usual guests.

entries.name: creature_on_head
entries.description: A small [creature](#creature) sits on top of somebody's head, often without their noticing. Usually a [familiar](#familiar) or a [pet](#pet) [riding](#riding) along.

entries.name: bird_on_arm
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) settled on someone's forearm or wrist. Common in [falconry](#falconry) scenes and with tame songbirds and message-carrying birds.

entries.name: holding_dog
entries.description: A [dog](#dog) has been lifted into the arms or held out towards the viewer, small breeds most often. It must be off the ground and supported by the hands.

entries.name: rabbit_on_head
entries.description: A live [rabbit](#rabbit) sits perched on top of someone's head, a common cute-companion arrangement where the [animal](#animal) rests rather than being held.

entries.name: cat_on_lap
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) has settled on a seated character's [lap](#lap), curled, sprawled or [standing](#standing) across the [thighs](#thighs). The person is necessarily [sitting](#sitting), so a sitting pose comes with it.

entries.name: creature_on_shoulder
entries.description: A small [creature](#creature) perches on a character's shoulder, level with their face. Generally a companion rather than a chance encounter.

entries.name: holding_baby
entries.description: An infant is supported in someone's arms, cradled against the chest or lifted up for a look. What matters is that the [baby](#baby) is off the ground and in their grip.

entries.name: animal_around_neck
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) is slung across the shoulders and around the throat the way a fur [stole](#stole) would be, sometimes alive and [clinging](#clinging), sometimes a [pelt](#pelt) worn as [fashion](#fashion). Snakes, ferrets and foxes are the usual choices.

entries.name: holding_bird
entries.description: A live [bird](#bird) sits in the hands or is cupped between the [palms](#palms). One perched on a shoulder or arm with [no](#no) hands involved does not count.

entries.name: holding_rabbit
entries.description: A live [rabbit](#rabbit) is lifted into the arms or cradled in the hands. A plush bunny is a stuffed [toy](#toy) and belongs to a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: baby_carry
entries.description: One [figure](#figure) lies across another's arms, supported under the [back](#back) so that they rest horizontally. When the [weight](#weight) is taken under the pelvis and the person sits upright in the arms, [child_carry](#child_carry) is the right [tag](#tag).

entries.name: butterfly_on_head
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) rests on somebody's hair or [hat](#hat) with its [wings](#wings) open. One insect at rest, not a swarm.

entries.name: animal_in_clothes
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) is tucked inside somebody's clothing, [poking](#poking) out of a [hood](#hood), a [coat](#coat) front or a [shirt](#shirt). Keep it apart from a clothed [animal](#animal), where the animal is the one wearing the garments.

entries.name: reverse_princess_carry
entries.description: A bridal-style carry with the usual roles swapped, so a woman lifts a man across her arms instead of the other way around. Everything else about the hold [matches](#matches) an ordinary [princess](#princess) carry.

entries.name: holding_chibi
entries.description: A full-sized [figure](#figure) carries a tiny super-deformed character in the palm or the arms. The [chibi](#chibi) is treated as really present in the scene, not as a doodle or a plush.

entries.name: crab_on_head
entries.description: A [crab](#crab) perches on top of somebody's head. Generally a [beach](#beach) [gag](#gag), with the character none the wiser.

entries.name: babywearing
entries.description: An infant is carried against the body in a wrap, a sling or a strapped [harness](#harness), leaving the carrier's hands free. The [child](#child) may ride on the chest, on the hip or on the [back](#back).

entries.name: animal_on_back
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) rides on somebody's [back](#back) or shoulders, [clinging](#clinging) there or perched. It is small enough that the person still stands and moves freely.

entries.name: mouse_on_head
entries.description: A mouse perched on top of somebody's head or tucked into their hair, [riding](#riding) along as they move about. A small [comic](#comic) touch, usually met with an unbothered expression.

entries.name: butterfly_on_nose
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) perches on the very tip of a character's [nose](#nose), who usually goes [cross-eyed](#cross-eyed) trying to see it.

entries.name: animal_between_breasts
entries.description: A small [creature](#creature) sits wedged in a woman's [cleavage](#cleavage), held there by the chest rather than by hands. Cats, birds and rodents are the usual passengers.

entries.name: holding_miniperson
entries.description: A tiny person stands or sits in a cupped hand, a fraction of the holder's size. It is a living [miniature](#miniature) rather than a [doll](#doll) or a figurine.

entries.name: dog_on_head
entries.description: A [dog](#dog) perched on top of somebody's head, [sitting](#sitting) up or draped across it. Small breeds and puppies, played for charm.

entries.name: animal_on_chest
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) settles on top of somebody's chest or [breasts](#breasts), whether they are [lying](#lying) down or upright. A [cat](#cat) parked on a sleeper is the standard case.

entries.name: cat_on_person
entries.description: A [cat](#cat) perches somewhere on a character's body — shoulder, [back](#back), chest or head — while they hold still for it. When it settles specifically on the [lap](#lap), [cat_on_lap](#cat_on_lap) fits better.

entries.name: imminent_hand_holding
entries.description: A hand held out to the viewer or another character so openly that taking it is the obvious next move. The grip has not happened.

entries.name: animal_on_leg
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) is perched on a thigh, a knee or a foot rather than gathered into the arms. Usually a [cat](#cat) or small [dog](#dog) claiming a seated person.

entries.name: snake_on_shoulder
entries.description: A [snake](#snake) draped across a character's shoulders or [coiled](#coiled) around the [neck](#neck) and arm. The person carries it calmly, as a companion rather than a [threat](#threat).

entries.name: insect_on_finger
entries.description: A [bug](#bug) has settled on an outstretched fingertip while the hand is held very still. Ladybirds, butterflies and beetles are the usual visitors, and the moment normally reads as gentle or [curious](#curious).

entries.name: bird_on_leg
entries.description: A [bird](#bird) settled on somebody's leg, knee or foot, generally while they sit still. A quieter counterpart to [bird_on_arm](#bird_on_arm).

entries.name: butterfly_over_eye
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) rests or hovers directly in front of one eye, [hiding](#hiding) it from view.

entries.name: rabbit_on_shoulder
entries.description: A [rabbit](#rabbit) rides on a character's shoulder, balanced against the [neck](#neck) or upper arm. Reads as a [familiar](#familiar) or [pet](#pet) staying close to its owner.

entries.name: hug
entries.description: One character wraps their arms around another person's body in an embrace. It is only for hugging [people](#people); a [pillow](#pillow), [doll](#doll) or other item takes [hugging_object](#hugging_object).

entries.name: hug_from_behind
entries.description: One character embraces another from behind, chest against [back](#back), arms wrapped around them. It differs from [grabbing_from_behind](#grabbing_from_behind), which is a restraint or a grope rather than an embrace.

entries.name: back-to-back
entries.description: Two characters stand, sit or lean with their backs turned toward each other, touching or merely aligned. It reads as partnership, [rivalry](#rivalry), or two [people](#people) covering opposite directions.

entries.name: face-to-face
entries.description: Two characters turned towards each other at close range, noses almost touching. Often the beat before a [kiss](#kiss) or a [confrontation](#confrontation); add [eye_contact](#eye_contact) when their eyes actually meet.

entries.name: heads_together
entries.description: Two or more characters lean in until their heads touch or nearly touch, side by side or [forehead](#forehead) to forehead.

entries.name: lap_pillow
entries.description: One character lies with their head [resting](#resting) in another's [lap](#lap). An offer of the lap is [lap_pillow_invitation](#lap_pillow_invitation), and a body rather than a head laid across it is [lying_on_lap](#lying_on_lap).

entries.name: lying_on_person
entries.description: One character [resting](#resting) their body on top of another who is [lying](#lying) down. Being on someone without lying is [on_person](#on_person), and hovering above them propped on the arms is [yukadon](#yukadon).

entries.name: arms_around_neck
entries.description: Both arms are looped behind another person's [neck](#neck), as in a [hug](#hug) or leading into a [kiss](#kiss). One arm there is [arm_around_neck](#arm_around_neck).

entries.name: leaning_on_person
entries.description: One character rests their [weight](#weight) against another, shoulder to shoulder or slumped onto them. It reads as affection or as tiredness between two subjects.

entries.name: arm_around_shoulder
entries.description: An arm draped over another person's shoulders, friendly or possessive. A hand simply placed there is [hand_on_another's_shoulder](#hand_on_another's_shoulder).

entries.name: leg_lock
entries.description: Legs hooked around another character's [torso](#torso), at the waist or up under the arms. Frequent in [missionary](#missionary) [sex](#sex), where it pulls the partner in close.

entries.name: locked_arms
entries.description: Two characters with an arm hooked through each other's, [walking](#walking) or [standing](#standing) linked at the elbow. The same hold turns up in [back-to-back](#back-to-back) [stretching](#stretching) exercises.

entries.name: arm_hug
entries.description: Clinging to another character's arm with both of one's own, a fond and slightly possessive hold. Simply linking elbows is [locked_arms](#locked_arms).

entries.name: cheek-to-cheek
entries.description: Two or more characters press their cheeks together, heads side by side. The [gesture](#gesture) reads as intimacy, or at the very least [strong](#strong) affection.

entries.name: arm_around_waist
entries.description: One character's arm circles another's waist, as in a [couple](#couple) pose or a dance hold. Both arms doing it is [arms_around_waist](#arms_around_waist).

entries.name: arm_around_another's_waist
entries.description: An arm encircles another character's waist, the hand coming to rest on the hip or the far side. Reads as affection or possessiveness short of a full [hug](#hug).

entries.name: arm_around_neck
entries.description: One person's arm hooks around the [back](#back) of another's [neck](#neck), [pulling](#pulling) them close or [leaning](#leaning) [weight](#weight) on them. With both arms it becomes [arms_around_neck](#arms_around_neck).

entries.name: face_to_breasts
entries.description: One character's face rests against another's [breasts](#breasts), whether in a smothering [hug](#hug), a [comforting](#comforting) embrace or a suggestive moment. The contact is the point, so a hug [tag](#tag) often sits beside it.

entries.name: spooning
entries.description: Two [people](#people) [lying](#lying) on their sides, one's front pressed against the other's [back](#back) like nested spoons. Covers ordinary [cuddling](#cuddling) as [well](#well) as the [sex](#sex) position of the same name.

entries.name: head_between_breasts
entries.description: One character's head is nestled between another's [breasts](#breasts). It covers the gentler cases that [breast_smother](#breast_smother) would overstate; on a male chest the [tag](#tag) is [head_between_pecs](#head_between_pecs).

entries.name: kabedon
entries.description: One person plants a hand flat on a wall beside another whose [back](#back) is against it, [boxing](#boxing) them in. The move usually reads as a romantic advance; a foot used instead is [foot_kabedon](#foot_kabedon), and the lying-down version is [yukadon](#yukadon).

entries.name: hugging_another's_arm
entries.description: Somebody clings to another's arm, [wrapping](#wrapping) both of their own around it and pressing close. An [affectionate](#affectionate), clingy [gesture](#gesture) rather than a full embrace.

entries.name: shared_clothes
entries.description: Two or more characters wear or use one piece of clothing at the same time, such as a [scarf](#scarf) around both necks or one oversized [coat](#coat) shared between them.

entries.name: breast_smother
entries.description: A face is pushed into somebody's [breasts](#breasts) far enough to [cover](#cover) the mouth or [nose](#nose) and block [breathing](#breathing), by [accident](#accident), in a [hug](#hug) or deliberately. If breathing is not obstructed, [face_to_breasts](#face_to_breasts) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: on_person
entries.description: Part of one character's body rests on another person, a hand, a head, a leg thrown over. Someone stretched out at full length on top of another is [lying_on_person](#lying_on_person).

entries.name: cuddling
entries.description: Characters pressed close together for warmth, comfort or [plain](#plain) affection, curled up on a sofa or under a [blanket](#blanket) in [bed](#bed). Rarely sexual in itself; a brief embrace is [hug](#hug).

entries.name: sleeping_on_person
entries.description: Someone sleeps [leaning](#leaning) or [lying](#lying) against another character, such as on a shoulder or in a [lap](#lap). Tag beside [sleeping](#sleeping).

entries.name: head_on_another's_shoulder
entries.description: One character lays their head down on somebody else's shoulder, out of affection, comfort or tiredness.

entries.name: breasts_on_head
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), busty character rests her [breasts](#breasts) on top of a shorter one's head, a [comic](#comic) trope that leans on the [height](#height) gap between them. Add [breast_rest](#breast_rest) and [height_difference](#height_difference); a face [buried](#buried) between the breasts is [face_to_breasts](#face_to_breasts).

entries.name: arms_around_another's_waist
entries.description: Both arms [circle](#circle) another character's waist, from the front or from behind, closing into a hold. A single arm doing it is [arm_around_another's_waist](#arm_around_another's_waist).

entries.name: arms_around_waist
entries.description: Both arms wrap around another person's waist, in a close embrace or a [hug](#hug) from behind. One arm is [arm_around_waist](#arm_around_waist).

entries.name: forehead-to-forehead
entries.description: Two characters press their foreheads together while facing one another, a tender and intimate pose. It is the [face-to-face](#face-to-face) case of [heads_together](#heads_together).

entries.name: cheek_press
entries.description: A character presses or rubs a cheek against a person, an [animal](#animal) or an object, nuzzling into it. Affection is what the [gesture](#gesture) carries.

entries.name: leg_between_thighs
entries.description: One character pushes a leg in between another's [thighs](#thighs), generally as an intimate or [affectionate](#affectionate) move. It [can](#can) [shade](#shade) into [grinding](#grinding), in which case add the act's own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: comforting
entries.description: One character eases another who is visibly upset or in [tears](#tears), by [holding](#holding) them, touching their face, [wiping](#wiping) the tears away or [resting](#resting) a hand on their head or shoulder.

entries.name: glomp
entries.description: An enthusiastic pounce of a [hug](#hug), leaping onto someone and [throwing](#throwing) both arms around them. Also called a [tackle](#tackle) hug.

entries.name: face_between_breasts
entries.description: One character's face is pressed into another's [cleavage](#cleavage) and [buried](#buried) there. Usually the result of a tight [hug](#hug) or of being pulled in.

entries.name: arm_around_another's_back
entries.description: One character reaches behind another and lays an arm along their [back](#back), a loose half-embrace. Usually drawn with the two side by side, [standing](#standing) or seated.

entries.name: lying_on_lap
entries.description: A character stretched across someone else's [lap](#lap) with much of their body, not merely their head. Resting the head alone is [lap_pillow](#lap_pillow).

entries.name: head_on_chest
entries.description: A head rests on another character's chest, [breasts](#breasts) or [pectorals](#pectorals) alike, as when [lying](#lying) together or [holding](#holding) each other. A head wedged in between is [head_between_breasts](#head_between_breasts).

entries.name: pectoral_press
entries.description: Pectorals pushed up against something, be it an object, a pane of [glass](#glass) or another person. The male counterpart of [breast_press](#breast_press); two sets pressed together is [pectoral_docking](#pectoral_docking).

entries.name: group_hug
entries.description: Three or more [people](#people) wrapped together in one [hug](#hug), arms around each other. A hug between only two people is [plain](#plain) hug instead.

entries.name: arm_around_back
entries.description: One character's arm passes around another's [back](#back), as in a side [hug](#hug) or when [helping](#helping) them stand. For tighter holds, [arm_around_waist](#arm_around_waist) and [arm_around_shoulder](#arm_around_shoulder) are more exact.

entries.name: mutual_hug
entries.description: Two or more characters embracing one another at once, each with arms around the other. It is distinct from one [figure](#figure) [holding](#holding) a passive partner.

entries.name: lap_pillow_invitation
entries.description: A seated character, usually in [seiza](#seiza), pats their [thighs](#thighs) and beckons somebody, often the viewer, to lay their head down. An offer of ear [cleaning](#cleaning) sometimes comes with it.

entries.name: noses_touching
entries.description: Two characters press the tips of their noses together, the [affectionate](#affectionate) [gesture](#gesture) often called an Eskimo [kiss](#kiss). The faces are close enough that a kiss looks imminent.

entries.name: head_on_head
entries.description: One character sets their chin, or the whole head, down on top of somebody else's. An [affectionate](#affectionate) [gesture](#gesture), usually with a [height](#height) gap or an embrace from behind.

entries.name: incoming_hug
entries.description: A character opens their arms toward the viewer, about to embrace them. Two characters about to embrace each other is [imminent_hug](#imminent_hug).

entries.name: smother
entries.description: One character pressing another's face into their body, so that it is [buried](#buried) and the view of it blocked. Chest, [thighs](#thighs) and [lap](#lap) are the usual [landing](#landing) places, played as affection as often as dominance.

entries.name: head_between_thighs
entries.description: One character's head sits between another's [thighs](#thighs), held there or simply [resting](#resting). When the [legs](#legs) clamp deliberately to [pin](#pin) or choke, it is also a [scissorhold](#scissorhold).

entries.name: imminent_hug
entries.description: Two characters with arms [opening](#opening) toward each other, a moment short of the embrace. Where the arms open toward the viewer instead, that is [incoming_hug](#incoming_hug).

entries.name: belly-to-belly
entries.description: Two characters pressed together [stomach](#stomach) against stomach, generally while hugging, kissing or curled up close. The contact between the midsections is what is being recorded.

entries.name: clinging
entries.description: One character holds tightly to another, arms wrapped around them and often some of their [weight](#weight) taken. Reads as affection, fear or a refusal to let go.

entries.name: over_the_knee
entries.description: One character sits while a second lies stomach-down across their [thighs](#thighs), arms and [legs](#legs) [hanging](#hanging) loose. The standard arrangement for a [spanking](#spanking), though the pose by itself says nothing about what follows.

entries.name: front-to-back
entries.description: Two characters lined up so that one's chest presses against the other's [back](#back). Turns up in embraces from behind and in tight group arrangements.

entries.name: pectoral_docking
entries.description: Two characters press their bare [pectorals](#pectorals) together chest to chest, the male version of [symmetrical_docking](#symmetrical_docking).

entries.name: breast_pillow
entries.description: One character lays their head on another's [breasts](#breasts) as though on a [cushion](#cushion), at any angle. Burying the face in them belongs to [face_to_breasts](#face_to_breasts) or the smothering tags, and the male counterpart is [pectoral_pillow](#pectoral_pillow).

entries.name: shared_blanket
entries.description: One [blanket](#blanket) is spread over two characters, or over a character and an [animal](#animal), [pulling](#pulling) them close together underneath it.

entries.name: arms_around_back
entries.description: Both arms reach around another character's [back](#back), the hands meeting behind them. Typical of a [face-to-face](#face-to-face) [hug](#hug).

entries.name: hugging_another's_leg
entries.description: One character wraps their arms around another's leg and holds on, usually from a [kneeling](#kneeling) or [sitting](#sitting) position. Children and small characters do it most.

entries.name: nuzzle
entries.description: One character presses or rubs their face against another's cheek, [neck](#neck) or hair out of affection, the way a [cat](#cat) greets someone it likes.

entries.name: waist_hug
entries.description: Arms wrapped around another person's middle instead of their shoulders or [neck](#neck). Works from the front or from behind.

entries.name: person_between_breasts
entries.description: A whole person held in the cleft of another character's [breasts](#breasts), which takes a considerable difference in size between the two.

entries.name: head_hug
entries.description: Arms wrap around another character's head and pull it in against a chest, [stomach](#stomach) or shoulder. Affectionate as a rule, smothering now and then.

entries.name: hugging_another's_tail
entries.description: Someone takes another character's [tail](#tail) in their arms and holds it against their body. When the tail is their own it is [hugging_own_tail](#hugging_own_tail).

entries.name: face_to_pecs
entries.description: A character's face rests against another's chest muscles, usually because a [height](#height) difference puts it there during an embrace. The [muscular](#muscular) counterpart of [face_to_breasts](#face_to_breasts).

entries.name: head_on_ass
entries.description: One character rests their head on another's backside as if on a [cushion](#cushion). The head lies on top of it; a face pushed into the cleft is [face_in_ass](#face_in_ass).

entries.name: whispering_in_ear
entries.description: One character leans in close and speaks quietly directly into another's ear, often with a hand cupped beside the mouth. The listener commonly reacts with a [blush](#blush) or a startled expression.

entries.name: head_between_pecs
entries.description: A head rests between another character's [pectorals](#pectorals). Add [face_to_pecs](#face_to_pecs) when the face itself is turned into them; the counterpart on a female chest is [head_between_breasts](#head_between_breasts).

entries.name: breasts_on_another's_back
entries.description: Breasts are pressed flat against somebody's [back](#back), as happens when hugging or [leaning](#leaning) on them from behind. It is a breast press carried out from the rear.

entries.name: lying_on_another
entries.description: One [figure](#figure) lies stretched out on top of another, chest to chest or sprawled crosswise over them. Nothing sexual is implied; the mood may be [affectionate](#affectionate), [exhausted](#exhausted) or playful.

entries.name: shoulder-to-shoulder
entries.description: Two figures [standing](#standing) or [sitting](#sitting) close enough that their shoulders actually touch, a tighter case than ordinary [side-by-side](#side-by-side) placement where the bodies merely stand near one another.

entries.name: shared_bed
entries.description: Two or more characters occupy one [bed](#bed), whether asleep, [talking](#talking), or wedged in awkwardly beside each other. Nothing sexual is implied by the [tag](#tag) on its own.

entries.name: wing_hug
entries.description: A winged character folds their [wings](#wings) around someone, or is wrapped inside another's. The mood reads as shelter and affection rather than restraint.

entries.name: sharing
entries.description: Two characters make use of one thing at the same moment: an [umbrella](#umbrella), a [book](#book), or a seat. If a handover is still under way rather than mutual use, the [giving](#giving) [tag](#tag) suits better.

entries.name: blowing_in_ear
entries.description: One character [breathing](#breathing) softly into another's ear, close enough that the [lips](#lips) nearly touch it. It reads as [teasing](#teasing) or flirtation and usually draws a startled reaction.

entries.name: kabedon_on_viewer
entries.description: The wall-pinning move aimed straight out of the picture, so the viewer occupies the [trapped](#trapped) position and the hand lands beside their head. Almost always staged as a flirtatious advance.

entries.name: head_under_another's_clothes
entries.description: Someone has pushed their head in under another person's [shirt](#shirt), [coat](#coat) or [skirt](#skirt), so it disappears under the [fabric](#fabric). The shape of it usually bulges through.

entries.name: pectoral_pillow
entries.description: Somebody rests their head on another character's [pectorals](#pectorals) as if on a [cushion](#cushion), facing in any direction. The female equivalent is [breast_pillow](#breast_pillow).

entries.name: double_arm_hug
entries.description: Two characters each cling to one arm of a third, one on either side. Usually shows somebody being fussed over, claimed or squabbled about.

entries.name: hover_hand
entries.description: An arm goes around a companion for a photo but the hand stops short, [floating](#floating) above the shoulder without touching. It reads as awkwardness or nerves.

entries.name: head_on_another's_stomach
entries.description: A head rests against another person's [belly](#belly), ear to the skin. Often the listener is [waiting](#waiting) to feel an unborn [child](#child) move.

entries.name: cheek-to-breast
entries.description: One character rests a cheek against another's breast, or a breast is pressed to a cheek. Only the contact matters, and both may be fully dressed.

entries.name: face_hug
entries.description: A face wrapped up in an embrace, with arms, a body or a [creature](#creature) pulled tight around it so that the face is enclosed. Affectionate or smothering depending on what has hold of it.

entries.name: single_arm_hug
entries.description: An embrace made with just one arm, the other left [hanging](#hanging) free or busy with something else. Reads as more [casual](#casual) than a full two-armed [hug](#hug).

entries.name: kiss
entries.description: Two characters press their [lips](#lips) together, or one kisses another's face or body. Add the placement [tag](#tag) such as [kissing_cheek](#kissing_cheek), and use [imminent_kiss](#imminent_kiss) when the lips have not met yet.

entries.name: french_kiss
entries.description: A [kiss](#kiss) in which the tongues touch or one enters the other's mouth. It is deeper than a [plain](#plain) kiss and is normally drawn with the tongues visible.

entries.name: imminent_kiss
entries.description: Two faces closing on each other with [lips](#lips) about to meet: heads tilting, eyes shutting or locked, sometimes a hand under the chin. A [kiss](#kiss) aimed at the viewer is [incoming_kiss](#incoming_kiss), and an ambiguous frame may equally read as [after_kiss](#after_kiss).

entries.name: kissing_cheek
entries.description: One character kisses another on the cheek, as affection, greeting or thanks. A [kiss](#kiss) on each cheek in turn is [double_cheek_kiss](#double_cheek_kiss).

entries.name: after_kiss
entries.description: The instant two faces part again, often bridged by a [thread](#thread) of [saliva](#saliva) or followed by somebody [wiping](#wiping) their mouth. Lips still touching makes it [kiss](#kiss) instead.

entries.name: kissing_forehead
entries.description: One character kisses another on the [forehead](#forehead), a [gesture](#gesture) of tenderness or protection. A difference in [height](#height) is often played up, with the taller [figure](#figure) [leaning](#leaning) down.

entries.name: surprise_kiss
entries.description: A [kiss](#kiss) that catches its recipient off [guard](#guard), shown through wide eyes or a startled reaction. Implies kiss and [surprised](#surprised).

entries.name: pocky_kiss
entries.description: Two characters eat one [pocky](#pocky) [stick](#stick) from opposite ends, drawing closer as they go until they meet in a [kiss](#kiss). Often shown mid-game, before the kiss itself happens.

entries.name: kissing_hand
entries.description: A character kisses the [back](#back) of another's hand or their fingers, usually as a courtly greeting or a mark of respect. A [bow](#bow) or a bent knee often goes with it.

entries.name: kissing_neck
entries.description: One character presses a [kiss](#kiss) to another's [neck](#neck), often from behind or in the middle of an embrace. The tone is usually intimate.

entries.name: implied_kiss
entries.description: A [kiss](#kiss) strongly suggested but never seen, screened by a hand, a [hat](#hat), an object or the edge of the frame. The [lips](#lips) themselves stay hidden.

entries.name: incoming_kiss
entries.description: A face [leaning](#leaning) toward the [camera](#camera) with [lips](#lips) ready, so the [kiss](#kiss) is meant for the viewer. Two characters leaning toward each other instead is [imminent_kiss](#imminent_kiss).

entries.name: forced_kiss
entries.description: A [kiss](#kiss) taken by force or under coercion, either by the one doing the kissing or by a third [party](#party) [pushing](#pushing) the two together. A struggle or a held head normally makes it [plain](#plain).

entries.name: incoming_pocky_kiss
entries.description: One end of a biscuit [stick](#stick) offered toward the [camera](#camera) while the character bites the other, leaving the viewer to close the gap. It is the viewer-facing form of the shared-stick game.

entries.name: kissing_hair
entries.description: A [kiss](#kiss) that lands on someone's hair rather than their skin, most often on the [crown](#crown) of the head. Hearts, blushing or flowers are commonly drawn alongside it.

entries.name: indirect_kiss
entries.description: Two characters share the same straw, [cup](#cup), [spoon](#spoon) or [snack](#snack), and one of them treats it as a [kiss](#kiss) at one remove. Older or harder-edged work uses a shared [cigarette](#cigarette) the same way.

entries.name: kissing_object
entries.description: Someone kisses a thing rather than a person, or a thing appears to [kiss](#kiss) them. The object is generally humanoid — a plush [toy](#toy), a [puppet](#puppet) or a [figure](#figure).

entries.name: kissing_head
entries.description: One character kisses another on the top or the side of the head. It reads as protective or fond, and usually involves a clear difference in [height](#height).

entries.name: kissing_animal
entries.description: Someone presses their [lips](#lips) to a [creature](#creature), usually a [pet](#pet), as a show of fondness. It may be one-sided or returned; when the [animal](#animal) does the kissing there is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: cigarette_kiss
entries.description: Two characters lean in until the tips of the cigarettes in their mouths touch, one lighting the other. The [gesture](#gesture) mirrors a [kiss](#kiss) without [lips](#lips) meeting; the sweeter version of the same [idea](#idea) uses a [pocky](#pocky) [stick](#stick).

entries.name: double_cheek_kiss
entries.description: One person takes kisses on both cheeks at once from two others, usually while [sandwiched](#sandwiched) between them. Affectionate rather than sexual.

entries.name: kissing_nose
entries.description: A light [kiss](#kiss) placed on the tip of another character's [nose](#nose). It plays as [affectionate](#affectionate) [teasing](#teasing) and is often drawn with a [blush](#blush) or closed eyes.

entries.name: rejected_kiss
entries.description: One character leans in for a [kiss](#kiss) and the other stops it, usually with a palm pressed against the incoming mouth or a turned-away face. The refusal may come from disinterest or [plain](#plain) shyness.

entries.name: tiptoe_kiss
entries.description: The shorter of two characters rises onto the balls of the [feet](#feet) to reach the other's [lips](#lips). The [height](#height) gap between them is the whole point of the composition.

entries.name: upside-down_kiss
entries.description: Two characters [kiss](#kiss) with one of their heads turned fully [upside-down](#upside-down) relative to the other, echoing a famous rain-soaked scene from a well-known film. A composition with [plain](#plain) rotational [symmetry](#symmetry) does not qualify on its own.

entries.name: kissing_shoulder
entries.description: Lips brought to another character's shoulder, bare or clothed. It is often drawn from behind, with the kisser [leaning](#leaning) over the other's [back](#back).

entries.name: waiting_for_kiss
entries.description: Eyes shut and [lips](#lips) pushed forward or slightly parted, the face tilted up for a [kiss](#kiss) that has not landed yet. Works toward another character or straight at the viewer.

entries.name: kissing_ear
entries.description: A character brings their mouth to the side of another's head and kisses the ear. It is usually drawn as an intimate or [teasing](#teasing) move made from behind.

entries.name: kissing_back
entries.description: Lips placed against another character's [back](#back), generally along the [spine](#spine) or a shoulder blade. Read the name as the body part being kissed, not as returning a [kiss](#kiss).

entries.name: kissing_stomach
entries.description: A [kiss](#kiss) placed on someone's [belly](#belly) or [midriff](#midriff). It appears in intimate scenes and in pictures about pregnancy.

entries.name: kissing_foot
entries.description: Lips touching another character's foot. The [gesture](#gesture) reads as devotion or submission and turns up in tender and fetish scenes alike.

entries.name: accidental_kiss
entries.description: Two characters' [lips](#lips) meet by mishap rather than intent, usually after a trip, a shove or a fall. Both parties are generally startled by it.

entries.name: kissing_leg
entries.description: Lips pressed to another character's leg, anywhere between thigh and ankle. It belongs to intimate or worshipful scenes rather than to a [casual](#casual) greeting.

entries.name: groping
entries.description: Touching or fondling another person in a sexual way, most often their [breasts](#breasts) or buttocks. The more specific [grabbing_another's_breast](#grabbing_another's_breast) and [grabbing_another's_ass](#grabbing_another's_ass) imply it; a non-sexual touch does not qualify.

entries.name: hand_on_another's_head
entries.description: One hand settles atop somebody else's head, as when soothing, praising or [holding](#holding) them in place. Two hands there is [hands_on_another's_head](#hands_on_another's_head), while an active [patting](#patting) motion is [headpat](#headpat).

entries.name: grabbing_from_behind
entries.description: One character stands or lies behind another, front to [back](#back), and reaches around to grab them. Frequently paired with [grabbing_another's_breast](#grabbing_another's_breast), though a hold on the waist or shoulders counts just as [well](#well).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_shoulder
entries.description: A single hand placed on another character's shoulder, a touch of encouragement, friendship or restraint. With a hand on each shoulder use [hands_on_another's_shoulders](#hands_on_another's_shoulders).

entries.name: leg_grab
entries.description: A hand closes around a leg, the character's own or somebody else's. Grabbing a [standing](#standing) person's leg usually means a marked [height](#height) difference between the two.

entries.name: hand_on_another's_face
entries.description: The general case of one hand [resting](#resting) anywhere on another character's face. A hand specifically on the cheek also takes [hand_on_another's_cheek](#hand_on_another's_cheek); two hands is [hands_on_another's_face](#hands_on_another's_face).

entries.name: headpat
entries.description: One character pats or strokes another's head, an [affectionate](#affectionate) [gesture](#gesture) toward a [child](#child), a [pet](#pet) or a partner.

entries.name: deep_skin
entries.description: Flesh gripped hard enough that the fingers [sink](#sink) into it as though it were [gelatin](#gelatin), most often a breast, a buttock or a thigh. An emphasis on how soft the body is under a hand.

entries.name: holding_another's_hair
entries.description: A character has someone else's hair in their hands, stroking it gently or hauling on it. Gripping one's own hair is [holding_own_hair](#holding_own_hair).

entries.name: holding_another's_wrist
entries.description: A character grips another's wrist or forearm, often to pull them along or to stop them moving. A hold higher up the arm is [holding_another's_arm](#holding_another's_arm).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_hair
entries.description: One character grabs or pulls another's hair, roughly in a fight or a scene of dominance, or lightly in play. Not to be mixed up with [hair_pulled_back](#hair_pulled_back), which describes a hairstyle.

entries.name: torso_grab
entries.description: Hands gripping another character's body at the waist, hips or chest. Common during a lift, an embrace or a sexual position; add the specific pose alongside it when it applies.

entries.name: thigh_grab
entries.description: One character's hand grips another character's thigh or both [thighs](#thighs). A hand on one's own thigh instead is [hand_on_own_thigh](#hand_on_own_thigh).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_cheek
entries.description: One hand cups or brushes somebody else's cheek, a tender [gesture](#gesture) that often precedes a [kiss](#kiss). With a hand on each cheek use [hands_on_another's_cheeks](#hands_on_another's_cheeks).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_chin
entries.description: A character touches somebody else's chin, commonly a finger placed under it to tilt the face upward. The [gesture](#gesture) reads as flirtatious, appraising or commanding.

entries.name: rubbing
entries.description: Two surfaces moved [back](#back) and forth against each other under pressure, whether a hand over skin, cheeks together or an object against a body. The friction itself is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: grabbing_another's_arm
entries.description: One character grips another's arm, to drag them along, hold them [back](#back) or steady them. Reserve it for a real grab rather than a light touch; a hand on one's own arm is [holding_own_arm](#holding_own_arm).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_back
entries.description: A single hand laid on another person's [back](#back), as when [comforting](#comforting), guiding or [holding](#holding) them during an embrace. Both hands there takes [hands_on_another's_back](#hands_on_another's_back).

entries.name: poking
entries.description: A finger or a blunt object jabbed into something soft, most often another character's cheek or breast. Add the body part involved, or poking_self where relevant.

entries.name: hand_on_another's_thigh
entries.description: A hand laid on another character's thigh, usually an intimate or suggestive touch. Both hands on their [thighs](#thighs) is [hands_on_another's_thighs](#hands_on_another's_thighs).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_chest
entries.description: A single hand rests on another character's chest, male or female. Neither [pectoral_grab](#pectoral_grab) nor [grabbing_another's_breast](#grabbing_another's_breast) is required, though both often appear with it; two hands is [hands_on_another's_chest](#hands_on_another's_chest).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_arm
entries.description: One character's single hand rests on somebody else's arm. Two hands on the same arm is [hands_on_another's_arm](#hands_on_another's_arm), and a hand on each of their arms is [hands_on_another's_arms](#hands_on_another's_arms).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_waist
entries.description: One hand at another character's waist, meaning the flank just above the hip, as in [dancing](#dancing) or drawing them nearer. Two hands there is [hands_on_another's_waist](#hands_on_another's_waist).

entries.name: holding_another's_arm
entries.description: One character grips another's arm above the wrist. Clutching one's own arm is [holding_own_arm](#holding_own_arm), and a grip at the wrist itself is [holding_another's_wrist](#holding_another's_wrist).

entries.name: hands_on_another's_face
entries.description: The general case of both hands placed anywhere on somebody else's face. Should just one hand be doing it, [hand_on_another's_face](#hand_on_another's_face) applies.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_shoulders
entries.description: A character grips or rests both hands on somebody else's two shoulders, from the front or from behind. A single hand is [hand_on_another's_shoulder](#hand_on_another's_shoulder).

entries.name: hand_in_another's_hair
entries.description: One character moves a hand through or across another's hair, stroking it, ruffling it or [sweeping](#sweeping) it aside. The hair belongs to somebody other than the person [reaching](#reaching).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_hip
entries.description: A hand set on somebody else's hip, over the [flare](#flare) of the pelvis. Two hands on both hips takes [hands_on_another's_hips](#hands_on_another's_hips).

entries.name: head_grab
entries.description: One character takes a firm grip on another's head. The hold turns up in fights and, often, in [forced](#forced) [oral](#oral) scenes.

entries.name: tickling
entries.description: Fingers or [feathers](#feathers) stroking a sensitive spot such as the sides, [feet](#feet) or [armpits](#armpits) to force laughter. Combine with [laughing](#laughing), [restrained](#restrained), and the body part being tickled.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_head
entries.description: Both of a character's hands rest on another character's head, as when framing it, ruffling the hair or [holding](#holding) them still. A single hand is [hand_on_another's_head](#hand_on_another's_head).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_shoulders
entries.description: Hands gripping another character's shoulders to shake them, hold them at arm's length or press them still. It reads as urgency far more often than as affection.

entries.name: finger_in_another's_mouth
entries.description: Someone has put at least one finger past another character's [lips](#lips) and inside the mouth. The mood may be playful, intimate or forceful depending on the scene.

entries.name: hand_grab
entries.description: One character takes hold of another's hand while that hand does not grip [back](#back). Mutual, interlocked hand contact belongs to [holding_hands](#holding_hands) instead.

entries.name: hand_on_another's_ass
entries.description: Somebody's hand is placed on another character's buttocks, whether [resting](#resting) there, steadying them or [groping](#groping). Only one hand is involved.

entries.name: arm_held_back
entries.description: One or both of a character's arms are pulled backwards and kept there by somebody else, whether pinning them or [holding](#holding) them during [sex](#sex). Add [restrained](#restrained) where that is what is happening.

entries.name: pinching
entries.description: One character [squeezing](#squeezing) a piece of another's body between thumb and finger, most often a cheek, a [nose](#nose) or a [belly](#belly). It reads as [teasing](#teasing) or [scolding](#scolding); gripping one's own [cuffs](#cuffs) is [pinching_sleeves](#pinching_sleeves).

entries.name: petting
entries.description: Stroking an [animal](#animal) or an animal-like [creature](#creature) by hand, a [cat](#cat), a [dog](#dog) or a [fantasy](#fantasy) beast. Stroking a person is not included; a hand on somebody's head is [headpat](#headpat).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_neck
entries.description: One hand rests on somebody else's [neck](#neck), at the [nape](#nape) behind or at the throat in front. The [reading](#reading) swings from [affectionate](#affectionate) to menacing; both hands is [hands_on_another's_neck](#hands_on_another's_neck).

entries.name: holding_another's_leg
entries.description: One character holds another's leg, lifting it or gripping it at the thigh or calf. Carrying [poses](#poses) and [sex](#sex) positions both produce it.

entries.name: grabbing_another's_leg
entries.description: A hand with a firm hold on another character's leg, raising it, pinning it or [clinging](#clinging) on. A grip on the thigh alone is [grabbing_another's_thighs](#grabbing_another's_thighs).

entries.name: cheek_pinching
entries.description: Fingers pinch a cheek, somebody else's or the character's own. It teases a [child](#child), or checks whether one is [dreaming](#dreaming).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_stomach
entries.description: One hand rests on somebody else's [belly](#belly), common in pregnancy scenes and in intimate holds from behind. Two hands is [hands_on_another's_stomach](#hands_on_another's_stomach); a hand on one's own belly is [hand_on_own_stomach](#hand_on_own_stomach).

entries.name: pulling
entries.description: One character drags another along by the hand, arm, or clothing, or a garment is being tugged off someone. Prefer a more specific [tag](#tag) where one exists, such as [pulling_another's_clothes](#pulling_another's_clothes) or [holding_hands](#holding_hands).

entries.name: cheek_poking
entries.description: A finger or an object presses into a cheek from outside, often as [teasing](#teasing). Something [pushing](#pushing) out from inside the mouth is [cheek_bulge](#cheek_bulge).

entries.name: neckwear_grab
entries.description: A hand closes on somebody else's [collar](#collar), [scarf](#scarf), [ribbon](#ribbon) or other neckwear, usually with a [tug](#tug) to draw them near. When the item is a tie, [necktie_grab](#necktie_grab) is the finer [choice](#choice).

entries.name: pectoral_grab
entries.description: A hand gripping or [squeezing](#squeezing) a male character's [pectorals](#pectorals), whether his own or somebody else's. The male counterpart of breast_grab.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_cheeks
entries.description: A character takes somebody else's face between both hands, one on each cheek, usually to hold their gaze or draw them into a [kiss](#kiss). A single hand is [hand_on_another's_cheek](#hand_on_another's_cheek).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_chin
entries.description: A hand takes hold of another's chin or lower [jaw](#jaw), tilting or [holding](#holding) the face to steer or command it. A gentle [caress](#caress) there is [stroking_another's_chin](#stroking_another's_chin), and touching one's own chin belongs to [hand_on_own_chin](#hand_on_own_chin) or [head_rest](#head_rest).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_leg
entries.description: A single hand rests somewhere on another character's leg. Both hands on one leg is [hands_on_another's_leg](#hands_on_another's_leg), and the thigh specifically has [hand_on_another's_thigh](#hand_on_another's_thigh).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_hips
entries.description: Hands closed on somebody else's hips, [holding](#holding) them steady, [pulling](#pulling) them nearer or keeping them from moving. It turns up in dances, lifts and close embraces.

entries.name: cheek_squash
entries.description: Hands push a character's cheeks inward until the [lips](#lips) pucker, done by the character themself or by another. It differs from [cheek_press](#cheek_press), which is a cheek rubbed against something.

entries.name: guiding_hand
entries.description: A character coaxingly leads another's hand toward a particular spot, including places on their own body. The specifically sexual breast case is [guided_breast_grab](#guided_breast_grab).

entries.name: necktie_grab
entries.description: One person has taken hold of another's tie, usually yanking it to pull them closer or force their attention. It commonly reads as dominance; straightening one's own tie is [adjusting_necktie](#adjusting_necktie) instead.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_hips
entries.description: Both hands grip or settle on somebody else's hips, just above the [thighs](#thighs). It is the standard hold in [dancing](#dancing), in lifting and during [sex](#sex); one hand is [hand_on_another's_hip](#hand_on_another's_hip).

entries.name: leash_pull
entries.description: Someone hauls on a lead, [chain](#chain) or similar tether fastened to another. It [can](#can) be a dominance [gesture](#gesture) in [bdsm](#bdsm) play or simply an [animal](#animal) being brought to heel.

entries.name: shirt_grab
entries.description: Grabbing a fistful of another person's [shirt](#shirt), whether to pull them close or to hold them in place. Implies [clothes_grab](#clothes_grab).

entries.name: hands_on_another's_thighs
entries.description: Both of a character's hands rest on another person's [thighs](#thighs), one to each. A single hand takes [hand_on_another's_thigh](#hand_on_another's_thigh).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_shirt
entries.description: A fist bunched in somebody else's [shirt](#shirt), [dragging](#dragging) them forward, keeping them from [walking](#walking) off, or clutching at the [cloth](#cloth) in anger or grief. It belongs to confrontations and to tearful [clinging](#clinging).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_waist
entries.description: Hands closed around another character's middle, drawing them in or steadying them. Dance holds, lifts and close embraces all involve it.

entries.name: ruffling_hair
entries.description: A hand tousling hair, either one's own or another character's. An [affectionate](#affectionate) or exasperated [gesture](#gesture); done to a [child](#child) by a taller character it overlaps with [headpat](#headpat).

entries.name: ankle_grab
entries.description: A hand closes round an ankle, one's own or somebody else's. It shows up in [stretching](#stretching) [poses](#poses), in falls, and where the [legs](#legs) are held apart during [sex](#sex).

entries.name: squeezing
entries.description: Something soft pressed firmly, usually between the fingers or hands, so it visibly deforms under the grip. Applies equally to objects, animals and body parts.

entries.name: hand_on_another's_hand
entries.description: A character lays one hand over somebody else's, for instance across a [table](#table) or on a shared object. Fingers interlocked or [palms](#palms) clasped together is [holding_hands](#holding_hands) instead.

entries.name: covering_another's_mouth
entries.description: A hand or an object is clamped over somebody else's mouth, to silence them, stop a laugh or hush a secret. Doing it to oneself is [covering_own_mouth](#covering_own_mouth).

entries.name: cheek_pull
entries.description: A character's cheeks are stretched outward, by their own hands or by somebody else's, [pulling](#pulling) the face out of shape. It runs from [affectionate](#affectionate) [teasing](#teasing) to outright [bullying](#bullying).

entries.name: massage
entries.description: One character kneading or [rubbing](#rubbing) another's shoulders, [back](#back) or [feet](#feet), or [working](#working) at their own stiff [neck](#neck). Sexual versions take the relevant explicit tags as [well](#well).

entries.name: tickling_feet
entries.description: The [soles](#soles) or [toes](#toes) are tickled, usually with fingers, a feather or a brush. Very often the [legs](#legs) are tied or held so the [feet](#feet) cannot pull away.

entries.name: dragging
entries.description: One character hauls another along, usually by the hand or wrist, the second trailing behind or [digging](#digging) in their heels. A man in women's [clothes](#clothes) belongs under [crossdressing](#crossdressing) or [otoko_no_ko](#otoko_no_ko) instead.

entries.name: grabbing_another's_twintails
entries.description: A hand catches one or both of another character's [twintails](#twintails), hauling on them like [reins](#reins) or lifting them up. The head comes along with them.

entries.name: hand_on_another's_ear
entries.description: One character reaches out and touches somebody else's ear with a hand. Human ears and [animal](#animal) ears both count, and the latter frequently gets a reaction out of the owner.

entries.name: arm_on_another's_shoulder
entries.description: An arm laid on somebody else's shoulder. Where the hold [can](#can) be [pinned](#pinned) down, [arm_around_shoulder](#arm_around_shoulder) or [arm_around_neck](#arm_around_neck) are better; a hand alone is [hand_on_another's_shoulder](#hand_on_another's_shoulder).

entries.name: hands_on_another's_waist
entries.description: Both hands at another character's sides just above the hips, the usual grip for [dancing](#dancing) or for lifting somebody up. One hand is [hand_on_another's_waist](#hand_on_another's_waist).

entries.name: sleeve_grab
entries.description: One character tugs at another's sleeve, typically to get their attention or hold them [back](#back). A form of [clothes_grab](#clothes_grab).

entries.name: finger_to_another's_mouth
entries.description: A finger laid on another character's [lips](#lips), most often to quiet them. The finger stays outside; pushed past the lips it becomes [finger_in_another's_mouth](#finger_in_another's_mouth).

entries.name: hands_on_another's_chest
entries.description: Both of one character's hands rest on another's chest, a man's [pectorals](#pectorals) or a woman's [breasts](#breasts) alike. It [can](#can) be a push away or a [caress](#caress); one hand is [hand_on_another's_chest](#hand_on_another's_chest).

entries.name: covering_another's_eyes
entries.description: One character blocks somebody else's sight, usually with both hands from behind, as a guess-who game or to keep them from seeing something. Hiding one's own eyes is [covering_own_eyes](#covering_own_eyes).

entries.name: breast_poke
entries.description: A finger, [stick](#stick) or other object presses into a breast hard enough to dent the [flesh](#flesh) inward without [piercing](#piercing) the skin. Once the skin is actually breached it becomes [nipple_penetration](#nipple_penetration).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_thighs
entries.description: Hands wrapped around another character's [thighs](#thighs), hoisting them, forcing them apart or simply [holding](#holding) on. When both are seized at once grabbing_both_thighs applies.

entries.name: horn_grab
entries.description: Somebody takes hold of another character's horn or [horns](#horns), to steer, restrain or tease them. The grip may be playful or forceful.

entries.name: holding_another's_thighs
entries.description: Hands grip another character's [thighs](#thighs), supporting them through a lift or carry or [holding](#holding) the [legs](#legs) in place. The thighs belong to the other person, not to the holder.

entries.name: holding_another's_foot
entries.description: A hand takes hold of somebody else's foot or ankle, lifting it, inspecting it, or steadying it while a shoe goes on. The foot belongs to another character, not to the one [holding](#holding) it.

entries.name: grabbing_another's_ear
entries.description: A hand closes on somebody else's ear, usually [pulling](#pulling) it as a [scolding](#scolding) or a tease. The pull being the point, a pained or [annoyed](#annoyed) face at the other end is standard.

entries.name: flat_chest_grab
entries.description: A hand closes on the chest of a character with [no](#no) bust to speak of. The joke, or the intimacy, is that there is so little there to take hold of.

entries.name: playing_with_another's_hair
entries.description: One character idly toys with someone else's hair, twirling, ruffling, or drawing fingers through it. Reserve it for aimless fiddling; combing, [tying](#tying), or plaiting with a real purpose have their own tags.

entries.name: covering_with_blanket
entries.description: One character lays a [blanket](#blanket) or sheet over another, generally somebody who has fallen asleep uncovered. Using one's own [coat](#coat) for it is [borrowed_clothes](#borrowed_clothes), and [hiding](#hiding) beneath the bedding is [under_covers](#under_covers).

entries.name: hand_over_another's_mouth
entries.description: One character's hand clamped across somebody else's mouth to stop them speaking or [crying](#crying) out. The victim's eyes usually carry the reaction.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_back
entries.description: Both [palms](#palms) laid on somebody else's [back](#back), as in a full embrace or while [pushing](#pushing) them forward. One hand only is [hand_on_another's_back](#hand_on_another's_back).

entries.name: grabbing_another's_stomach
entries.description: A hand laid flat on somebody else's [belly](#belly) and closed on the [flesh](#flesh). Usually a tease about their [weight](#weight) or about how much they have just put away.

entries.name: hand_on_another's_knee
entries.description: One hand placed on another character's knee, a [gesture](#gesture) that [can](#can) read as reassurance or as a pass. Use [hands_on_another's_knees](#hands_on_another's_knees) when both hands are down there.

entries.name: catching
entries.description: Somebody snatches a [falling](#falling) person or object out of the air before it hits the ground. The instant of the grab is what counts, not [carrying](#carrying) something already safely held.

entries.name: hand_on_hand
entries.description: A hand laid on top of another hand, a quiet [gesture](#gesture) of reassurance or affection. It differs from fingers laced together, which is [holding_hands](#holding_hands).

entries.name: holding_another's_tail
entries.description: A character has hold of somebody else's [tail](#tail), gripping it partway along or by the tip. It reads as playful, [teasing](#teasing) or restraining depending on the scene.

entries.name: tickling_sides
entries.description: The flanks between armpit and hip are tickled: [ribs](#ribs) and waist, the stretch where almost nobody [can](#can) hold still.

entries.name: collar_grab
entries.description: One character takes hold of another's [shirt](#shirt) [collar](#collar) and drags them close. It normally reads as [threat](#threat) or aggression, though the same grip precedes a [kiss](#kiss) often enough.

entries.name: neck_grab
entries.description: A hand closed around someone's [neck](#neck). The wording covers far too many different actions — a threatening choke, a pull into a [kiss](#kiss) — so more specific tags are preferred.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_stomach
entries.description: Both hands laid on somebody else's [belly](#belly), often on a [pregnant](#pregnant) partner or as a playful hold from behind. One hand is [hand_on_another's_stomach](#hand_on_another's_stomach).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_wrist
entries.description: Fingers closed around another character's wrist, [holding](#holding) it still or towing them along. It is the standard [gesture](#gesture) for restraint and for leading somebody away.

entries.name: hand_around_waist
entries.description: One hand large enough to close around at least half of a much smaller character's middle. It nearly always comes with a pronounced size difference, as when a [giant](#giant) picks somebody up; a hand merely [resting](#resting) there is [hand_on_another's_waist](#hand_on_another's_waist).

entries.name: drawing_on_another's_face
entries.description: Somebody marks another person's face with [pen](#pen) or [paint](#paint), classically while the victim sleeps. Runs from a [prank](#prank) moustache to careful decorative face paint.

entries.name: ass_smack
entries.description: A hand striking someone's buttocks, drawn at the moment of impact or [resting](#resting) where it landed. Read as [punishment](#punishment), encouragement or arousal depending on the scene.

entries.name: adjusting_another's_clothes
entries.description: One character straightens, tugs or fastens what somebody else is wearing so it sits properly. A small caretaking [gesture](#gesture) between two [people](#people), distinct from fussing with one's own outfit.

entries.name: face_grab
entries.description: One character takes hold of another's face with a hand, gripping the cheeks or the [jaw](#jaw). The mood runs from playful to threatening.

entries.name: grabbing_another's_hand
entries.description: One character closes a hand around another's hand or wrist, usually to tow them along or hold them [back](#back). Firmer and more one-sided than [holding_hands](#holding_hands), where the grip is shared.

entries.name: adjusting_another's_hair
entries.description: One character tends somebody else's hair, [sweeping](#sweeping) the fringe aside, [tying](#tying) it up or smoothing it down. The hands belong to a different person from the hair.

entries.name: shoulder_grab
entries.description: A hand closing on someone's shoulder. Too vague on its own to say much, so a more specific [tag](#tag) naming who grabs whom and why is generally preferred.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_neck
entries.description: Both hands laid gently around somebody else's [neck](#neck), fastening a [necklace](#necklace), settling a [collar](#collar) or simply [holding](#holding) them close. This is the tender version rather than a [strangling](#strangling); one hand is [hand_on_another's_neck](#hand_on_another's_neck).

entries.name: squishing
entries.description: Something soft pressed out of shape by hands, [weight](#weight) or against a surface. Cheeks, plush toys and [flesh](#flesh) are the usual targets.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_shoulder
entries.description: Both hands placed on a single shoulder of another character, [leaning](#leaning) on it or pinning them there. With a hand on each shoulder use [hands_on_another's_shoulders](#hands_on_another's_shoulders).

entries.name: arm_over_shoulder
entries.description: An arm passing over another character's shoulder. Where the hold is clear, [arm_around_shoulder](#arm_around_shoulder), [arm_around_neck](#arm_around_neck) or [arm_on_another's_shoulder](#arm_on_another's_shoulder) describe it better.

entries.name: patting
entries.description: A hand tapped lightly against a person, an [animal](#animal) or an object, once or several times over. Stroking the top of somebody's head is counted separately as [headpat](#headpat).

entries.name: hand_around_neck
entries.description: A hand encircling somebody's [neck](#neck), which on its own says nothing about whether the [gesture](#gesture) is a [caress](#caress), a hold or a [strangling](#strangling). Reach instead for a [tag](#tag) that names what is actually happening.

entries.name: stroking_another's_chin
entries.description: Fingers [scratching](#scratching) or [tickling](#tickling) someone beneath the chin, the way a hand might [pet](#pet) an [animal](#animal). Most often aimed at a pet or at a character with animal ears.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_arms
entries.description: Both hands grip both of another character's arms, one to each. It generally comes with facing them squarely and [holding](#holding) them in place.

entries.name: tickling_legs
entries.description: Fingers [running](#running) over another character's [thighs](#thighs), [calves](#calves) or the backs of the [knees](#knees).

entries.name: tickling_stomach
entries.description: Fingers [working](#working) across somebody's [belly](#belly). Reach for [tickling_navel](#tickling_navel) only when the [navel](#navel) itself is part of it.

entries.name: scarf_grab
entries.description: One character takes hold of another's [scarf](#scarf), hauling them closer or simply demanding attention. Usually reads as impatience or a challenge.

entries.name: yukadon
entries.description: One character pins another to the [floor](#floor), slamming a palm down beside their head while the other lies on their [back](#back). It is the horizontal counterpart to [kabedon](#kabedon); where it cannot be told whether the aggressor is [standing](#standing), kabedon is the safer [choice](#choice).

entries.name: belly_rub
entries.description: A hand laid flat on a [stomach](#stomach) and stroking it, whether another's or the character's own. It reads as affection, comfort, or the contented pat after a large [meal](#meal).

entries.name: hand_on_another's_mouth
entries.description: A hand touching another person's [lips](#lips) or laid lightly across them. Where it is pressed there to silence somebody, [hand_over_another's_mouth](#hand_over_another's_mouth) is the better fit.

entries.name: grabbing_another's_tail
entries.description: One character catches hold of another's [tail](#tail). Since tails count as sensitive in most settings, a yelp, a [blush](#blush) or a swat generally answers it.

entries.name: caress
entries.description: A hand moves gently over another person, stroking a cheek, an arm or the hair. The touch is tender rather than grasping.

entries.name: poking_belly
entries.description: A fingertip pressed into a [stomach](#stomach) or [navel](#navel), either somebody else's or the character's own. Nearly always playful [teasing](#teasing), and often aimed at a soft [belly](#belly).

entries.name: scarf_pull
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) being tugged, dragged down off the mouth and [nose](#nose), or hauled on by somebody else.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_knees
entries.description: Both hands placed on another character's [knees](#knees), frequently while [kneeling](#kneeling) in front of them or [leaning](#leaning) in close. A single hand takes [hand_on_another's_knee](#hand_on_another's_knee).

entries.name: hand_gagged
entries.description: Somebody's mouth is stopped by a palm clamped over it to keep them quiet. It is often drawn from behind, with the other arm pinning them in place.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_leg
entries.description: Both hands [resting](#resting) on one leg of another character, [holding](#holding), stroking or lifting it. One hand alone is [hand_on_another's_leg](#hand_on_another's_leg).

entries.name: tying_another's_hair
entries.description: One character binds somebody else's hair into a [tail](#tail), [braid](#braid) or bun. Usually drawn from behind, with the subject [sitting](#sitting) still while the other works.

entries.name: shoulder_massage
entries.description: One character kneads the shoulders of another, usually [standing](#standing) behind a seated partner who sits slumped or [leaning](#leaning) forward in relaxation.

entries.name: hand_on_animal
entries.description: A hand laid on a [creature](#creature): [patting](#patting) a [dog](#dog), steadying a [horse](#horse), [resting](#resting) on a cat's [back](#back). It is about contact, not about picking the [animal](#animal) up or [carrying](#carrying) it.

entries.name: hands_on_another's_arm
entries.description: Both of one character's hands hold a single arm of somebody else, [clinging](#clinging) to it or steering them by it. A lone hand takes [hand_on_another's_arm](#hand_on_another's_arm).

entries.name: tug
entries.description: A short, light pull at something, most often a piece of clothing on oneself or on someone else. The grip is a pinch or a light fistful rather than a full grasp.

entries.name: holding_another's_wrists
entries.description: One character has both of another's wrists in hand, usually to [pin](#pin) them or tow them along. The plural form is for two wrists taken at once.

entries.name: pushing_face
entries.description: A hand [planted](#planted) flat on someone's face to hold them at arm's length. A specific and often [comic](#comic) form of [pushing_away](#pushing_away).

entries.name: finger_to_another's_cheek
entries.description: A fingertip pressed against or drawn across somebody else's cheek. Teasing or fond, and sometimes a way of turning the other person's face.

entries.name: foot_massage
entries.description: One person works another's foot with their hands, kneading the sole or the [arch](#arch). The scene is normally relaxed and [affectionate](#affectionate).

entries.name: skirt_grab
