entries.description: One character takes hold of another person's [skirt](#skirt) with a hand. Often used to stop them leaving or to get their attention.

entries.name: hand_in_another's_mouth
entries.description: Fingers or a whole hand pushed past another character's [lips](#lips). The mood ranges from playful [feeding](#feeding) and [teasing](#teasing) to a forceful hold on the [jaw](#jaw).

entries.name: arm_on_another's_head
entries.description: One character props a forearm on top of another's head, often [leaning](#leaning) [weight](#weight) onto it. The joke usually turns on the difference in their heights.

entries.name: tickling_breasts
entries.description: Fingers played over somebody's [breasts](#breasts) to tickle them. Add [tickling_nipples](#tickling_nipples) on top only when the [nipples](#nipples) themselves are part of what is being touched.

entries.name: helping
entries.description: One character assists another with a task or a difficulty: steadying them, taking half the load, [pulling](#pulling) them along.

entries.name: holding_finger
entries.description: One character takes hold of another's finger, most often a small [child](#child) [wrapping](#wrapping) a whole fist round an adult's. It reads gentler and more specific than [holding_hands](#holding_hands).

entries.name: forehead_flick
entries.description: A finger snapped against somebody's [forehead](#forehead) for a small stinging tap. Japanese comedy uses it as a mock [punishment](#punishment) or a fond [scolding](#scolding).

entries.name: covering_another's_breasts
entries.description: One character lays their hands over another's bare [breasts](#breasts). A firmer hold counts as [grabbing_another's_breast](#grabbing_another's_breast), a gentler one as [hands_on_another's_chest](#hands_on_another's_chest).

entries.name: squeezing_cheeks
entries.description: Someone's cheeks pinched or pressed between fingers or [palms](#palms), squashing the face out of shape. Usually a [teasing](#teasing) or [affectionate](#affectionate) [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: imminent_breast_grab
entries.description: One hand or both reach toward a woman's chest with the fingers already curling to close, and nothing has been touched yet. By itself it says nothing about whether the grab would be welcome.

entries.name: hand_to_hand
entries.description: Two characters' hands meeting palm against palm, touching without the fingers lacing together. It is often drawn through a pane of [glass](#glass) or as a wordless moment of connection.

entries.name: legs_grab
entries.description: Hands close around both [legs](#legs), whether a character clutching their own [thighs](#thighs) or another person gripping their [calves](#calves).

entries.name: ear_fondling
entries.description: Somebody's ear is stroked, rubbed or played with by another character's fingers. Frequent with [animal](#animal) ears, where it doubles as [petting](#petting).

entries.name: patting_back
entries.description: A hand tapped against another character's [back](#back), usually in the middle of an embrace. It reads as comfort, congratulation, or help for somebody choking or [sobbing](#sobbing).

entries.name: cradling_head
entries.description: One character supports another's head in their hands or the crook of an arm. Gentle or protective, and common in [injury](#injury) and [death](#death) scenes.

entries.name: incoming_headpat
entries.description: A hand [reaching](#reaching) toward the viewer's head, palm down and close to the [camera](#camera), about to pat it. The pat is still to come.

entries.name: covering_another's_crotch
entries.description: One character puts a hand or an object over somebody else's [crotch](#crotch) to keep it out of view. Sometimes protective, sometimes [teasing](#teasing).

entries.name: hand_in_another's_clothes
entries.description: A hand pushed inside a garment somebody else is wearing, in under the hem or through a gap in the front. Whatever it reaches stays hidden behind the [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: foot_kabedon
entries.description: The wall-pinning [gesture](#gesture) performed with a leg: one person [braces](#braces) a foot on the wall beside the other, [boxing](#boxing) them in. The raised leg takes the place of the usual outstretched arm.

entries.name: head_hold
entries.description: Hands take hold of someone's head, cupping it, steadying it or gripping it hard. It covers the tender version and the controlling one alike.

entries.name: grabbing_another's_wing
entries.description: A hand [holding](#holding) a wing that belongs to somebody else, keeping it down, turning it for a look or tugging at it in play. The wing tends to bend awkwardly in the grip.

entries.name: hand_in_another's_pocket
entries.description: Reaching into a [pocket](#pocket) of clothing that another person is wearing. It reads either as familiarity between the two or as pickpocketing, depending on the scene.

entries.name: head_rub
entries.description: A hand moves across someone's head, [rubbing](#rubbing) or ruffling the hair rather than simply [patting](#patting) it. Affectionate, [teasing](#teasing) or consoling by context.

entries.name: tickling_navel
entries.description: The [belly](#belly) button is the spot being poked or teased. Reach for [tickling_stomach](#tickling_stomach) as [well](#well) only when the surrounding belly is worked over too.

entries.name: eye_poke
entries.description: A finger or an object jabbed at somebody's eye, usually [caught](#caught) at the moment of contact with the [target](#target) flinching. Often slapstick.

entries.name: girl_on_top
entries.description: A girl positioned above another character, whether [straddling](#straddling) a partner during [sex](#sex), pinning them in a fight or [landing](#landing) on them in play. Add the specific position [tag](#tag) where one applies.

entries.name: boy_on_top
entries.description: A male lies or kneels over another character, with the one on top plainly in view. It need not be sexual, though in [sex](#sex) it usually means [missionary](#missionary) or [doggystyle](#doggystyle) with the receiving partner beneath; the [mirror](#mirror) case is [girl_on_top](#girl_on_top).

entries.name: lifting_person
entries.description: A character is hoisted clear of the ground by another person, an [animal](#animal) or even an object such as a [hook](#hook). Cheerful lifts and forceful ones both count; a bridal lift is [princess_carry](#princess_carry).

entries.name: held_up
entries.description: A character is lifted clear of the ground in somebody else's hands or arms. It may be [affectionate](#affectionate), playful, or entirely against their will.

entries.name: stepped_on
entries.description: One character has a foot [planted](#planted) on another, usually to show dominance or [victory](#victory). The forceful act of stamping down is [stomping](#stomping) instead.

entries.name: foot_on_head
entries.description: One character plants a foot squarely on another's head, generally while [standing](#standing) over them. An unmistakable [gesture](#gesture) of dominance or mockery.

entries.name: person_on_head
entries.description: A character perched on top of another's head, generally drawn small or in [chibi](#chibi) form so that they fit up there.

entries.name: stacking
entries.description: The act of [building](#building) a [tower](#tower), whether stacking objects one atop another or [people](#people) [climbing](#climbing) onto one another. The piling up itself, not the finished result.

entries.name: chibi_on_head
entries.description: A shrunken, big-headed version of a character or an [animal](#animal) perches on somebody's head. Add person on head or animal on head according to what is [sitting](#sitting) up there.

entries.name: foot_on_another's_face
entries.description: A foot pressed or [resting](#resting) against somebody else's face. Depending on the scene around it, it reads as dominance, [humiliation](#humiliation) or slapstick.

entries.name: stepping
entries.description: A foot [planted](#planted) down on something [lying](#lying) on the ground, often another character and sometimes an object used for support. Where the motion is forceful and marked with speed lines, [stomping](#stomping) fits better; a foot merely [resting](#resting) on someone is [stepped_on](#stepped_on).

entries.name: human_stacking
entries.description: Several [people](#people) lie piled one on top of another, bodies aligned and usually turned toward the viewer. People balanced on each other's shoulders while [standing](#standing) make a [human_tower](#human_tower).

entries.name: standing_on_person
entries.description: One [figure](#figure) stands directly on top of another, [feet](#feet) [planted](#planted) on their [back](#back), chest or shoulders. Reads as triumph, [humiliation](#humiliation) or comedy depending on the scene.

entries.name: human_chair
entries.description: One person kneels on hands and [knees](#knees) while another sits on their [back](#back) as though on furniture. It combines the all-fours posture with [sitting](#sitting) on a person.

entries.name: armpit_carry
entries.description: Somebody is lifted and held up by hands hooked under their arms, [feet](#feet) left [dangling](#dangling). Most often done to a [cat](#cat), sometimes to a small or protesting person.

entries.name: human_tower
entries.description: Two or more [people](#people) stand stacked on one another's shoulders. The Catalan castell is the best-known form of it.

entries.name: chibi_on_shoulder
entries.description: A tiny [deformed](#deformed) version of a character stands or sits on another's shoulder, often piping up like a conscience or a [mascot](#mascot). Speech from the little [figure](#figure) commonly comes with it.

entries.name: dogpile
entries.description: Bodies heaped on top of one another in a tangled mound, everybody piled in at once. Messier and far less deliberate than a human [tower](#tower) or a neatly stacked arrangement.

entries.name: standing_on_another's_head
entries.description: One character plants both [feet](#feet) on someone else's head and stands there, usually as slapstick or a show of dominance over a much smaller [figure](#figure).

entries.name: fireman's_carry
entries.description: One person is slung across another's shoulders and steadied by an arm and a leg, so a single carrier [can](#can) move them unaided. Wrestling and [judo](#judo) use the same lift as the start of a throw.

entries.name: person_on_shoulder
entries.description: A character [riding](#riding) on somebody else's shoulder, small enough to sit or stand there. Familiars and companion characters are often placed this way.

entries.name: standing_on_shoulder
entries.description: A small [figure](#figure), typically a [fairy](#fairy), [familiar](#familiar) or shrunken character, stands balanced on somebody's shoulder, often steadied by a hand.

entries.name: fighting
entries.description: An everyday scuffle rather than [serious](#serious) combat: a heated argument, a childish quarrel, a tussle over something. Real combat with weapons or stakes is [battle](#battle).

entries.name: punching
entries.description: A character strikes out with a fist, whether [landing](#landing) a blow on someone else or [throwing](#throwing) a punch at empty air or an object. A fist simply held up without [swinging](#swinging) is [raised_fist](#raised_fist) instead.

entries.name: teasing
entries.description: One character deliberately provokes another to get a reaction, whether playful, flirtatious, sexual or unkind. Pair it with the target's reaction, such as [embarrassed](#embarrassed) or [annoyed](#annoyed).

entries.name: strangling
entries.description: Squeezing or gripping someone's throat to cut off their [breathing](#breathing), as an [attack](#attack) or as rough play. A total inability to breathe is also [asphyxiation](#asphyxiation); a gentle hand at the throat is [hands_on_another's_neck](#hands_on_another's_neck) instead.

entries.name: chasing
entries.description: One character runs after another, the pursued one out in front, usually in anger. It is frequently played for laughs.

entries.name: struggling
entries.description: A character [fighting](#fighting) against a hold, [hug](#hug), trap or other restraint by thrashing, [pushing](#pushing), [biting](#biting) or [pulling](#pulling) away. Also covers straining against a [heavy](#heavy) object or a stronger opponent.

entries.name: in_the_face
entries.description: Something strikes somebody [square](#square) in the face: a fist, a thrown [pie](#pie), any [flying](#flying) object. Semen to the face takes [facial](#facial) instead.

entries.name: catfight
entries.description: Two women scrapping with each other, almost always unarmed and relying on slaps, hair-pulling and [scratching](#scratching). The undignified, improvised [quality](#quality) sets it apart from a trained fight.

entries.name: slapping
entries.description: An open-handed strike, usually to the face, delivered to punish, wake or shame rather than injure. A closed fist is [punching](#punching).

entries.name: hitting
entries.description: Striking another person with a hand or an object. It usually reads as a light [comic](#comic) blow; a closed fist is [punching](#punching) and an open palm to the face is [slapping](#slapping).

entries.name: pinned
entries.description: One character held firmly against a wall, [floor](#floor) or [bed](#bed) by another so they cannot move away, usually with a wrist or shoulder pressed down. The mood may be playful, threatening or sexual.

entries.name: pushing
entries.description: A character shoves against something, whether straining to move a [heavy](#heavy) object or lightly pushing another person away. Combine with the object involved or with the other character's reaction.

entries.name: fist_bump
entries.description: Two [people](#people) knock their closed fists together at the knuckles as a greeting or a [sign](#sign) of agreement. It stands in for a [handshake](#handshake) or a high five.

entries.name: choke_hold
entries.description: One character locks an arm around another's [neck](#neck) to shut off air or [blood](#blood), the submission grip of [judo](#judo) and other grappling arts. Pressure from outside the neck like this counts as [strangling](#strangling), never as something lodged in the throat.

entries.name: crotch_kick
entries.description: A kick driven up into the [groin](#groin). Usually aimed at a male [target](#target) and drawn for the [pain](#pain) it causes, in earnest fights and in slapstick alike.

entries.name: held_down
entries.description: One character is pressed to the ground, a [bed](#bed) or a wall by another and cannot get up. Hands on the shoulders or the wrists usually do the [holding](#holding).

entries.name: pushing_away
entries.description: One character shoves another [back](#back), [palms](#palms) braced against a chest, shoulder, or face. Refusal, alarm, or annoyance is the usual [reading](#reading).

entries.name: stomping
entries.description: A foot brought down hard on a person or object, the force shown through motion lines and impact marks. Where a foot simply rests on someone with [no](#no) downward drive, [stepped_on](#stepped_on) applies.

entries.name: high_five
entries.description: Two characters [smack](#smack) their raised [palms](#palms) together, arms up, in triumph or agreement. Both hands meeting in the air is what makes it one.

entries.name: face_punch
entries.description: A fist lands on somebody's face, [caught](#caught) at the moment of impact with the head snapping aside. Impact marks, [flying](#flying) spit or [blood](#blood) usually come with it.

entries.name: incoming_punch
entries.description: A fist thrown straight at the [camera](#camera), foreshortened so the knuckles loom in the foreground. One character [punching](#punching) another is [imminent_punch](#imminent_punch).

entries.name: headlock
entries.description: A [wrestling](#wrestling) hold with the opponent's head [trapped](#trapped) in the crook of an arm and clamped to the holder's side. Thighs doing the clamping make it a [scissorhold](#scissorhold) instead.

entries.name: arguing
entries.description: Two or more characters openly at odds, with raised voices, jabbing fingers and faces turned angrily on one another. Sharper than ordinary conversation, which is simply [talking](#talking).

entries.name: scissorhold
entries.description: Thighs locked about somebody's [neck](#neck) or [skull](#skull) and clamped tight, a [headlock](#headlock) built out of the [thighs](#thighs) rather than the arms. It began as a [wrestling](#wrestling) hold and appears mostly in [femdom](#femdom) scenes today.

entries.name: confrontation
entries.description: Two characters [square](#square) off, eyes locked and hostility [hanging](#hanging) between them. It is eye contact with the [threat](#threat) of a fight behind it.

entries.name: uppercut
entries.description: A punch swung upward from below, usually [driving](#driving) into the chin. Not to be [confused](#confused) with [undercut](#undercut), which names a men's hairstyle.

entries.name: stomach_punch
entries.description: A fist driven into someone's midsection, the [target](#target) folding over the blow. Frequent in fight scenes and a fixture of rough combat art.

entries.name: hip_attack
entries.description: A [wrestling](#wrestling) move in which the attacker leaps, turns in mid-air and drives hip or backside into the opponent. A [running](#running) start is usual.

entries.name: suplex
entries.description: A [wrestling](#wrestling) throw in which one fighter hoists an opponent up and over their own body, [driving](#driving) them down back-first. The moment of the [arch](#arch), with both bodies off balance, is what the [tag](#tag) marks.

entries.name: breast_contest
entries.description: Two characters [square](#square) up chest to chest, comparing busts by pressing them together or lining up to be measured. Rivalry and [comic](#comic) indignation are the usual tone.

entries.name: faceoff
entries.description: Two characters, or two groups, stand squared up against each other with hostility in the air. It marks the charged moment before a fight rather than the [fighting](#fighting) itself.

entries.name: headbutt
entries.description: Striking somebody with the [forehead](#forehead) or [crown](#crown) of the head, whether as a blunt [attack](#attack) or as rough affection between [friends](#friends).

entries.name: threat
entries.description: One character menaces another, whether in words, with a raised fist, or with a [weapon](#weapon) held within reach of the [target](#target). Frequently a beat in a [comic](#comic) [gag](#gag).

entries.name: arm_wrestling
entries.description: Two [people](#people) grip hands with their elbows [planted](#planted) on a surface, each straining to force the other's hand flat. The braced elbows and locked [palms](#palms) give it away.

entries.name: constriction
entries.description: A [snake](#snake) or a similar long body is wound tight around a victim and [squeezing](#squeezing). In [nature](#nature) it is how such animals kill, and in art it also serves to [pin](#pin) a character in place.

entries.name: tackle
entries.description: Throwing the whole body at someone to seize or knock them down. Common in rugby and gridiron football, and also used comedically for a [flying](#flying) [hug](#hug).

entries.name: german_suplex
entries.description: A [wrestling](#wrestling) throw where the attacker grips an opponent around the waist from behind, arches backwards and drops them onto their shoulders. Often drawn as a [gag](#gag) finisher.

entries.name: head_pinned_down
entries.description: Someone's head is [forced](#forced) against a surface and held there by a hand, foot or knee. The rest of the body may still be [struggling](#struggling).

entries.name: bearhug
entries.description: One character wraps both arms around another at the waist and squeezes, often lifting them off the [floor](#floor). The grip constricts rather than comforts, so it sits closer to [wrestling](#wrestling) than to a [hug](#hug).

entries.name: mixed-sex_combat
entries.description: A man and a woman [fighting](#fighting) each other, usually framed around [domination](#domination) and [humiliation](#humiliation) rather than an even contest. Once the fight itself turns sexual, sex_battle fits better.

entries.name: following
entries.description: One character walks behind another who leads the way and is aware of them. When the person in front does not know they are being trailed, [stalking](#stalking) is the fitting [tag](#tag).

entries.name: trample
entries.description: One character stands, steps or walks across another [lying](#lying) prone beneath them, most often [barefoot](#barefoot) or in [socks](#socks). Done in [boots](#boots) or heels it edges further into outright dominance play.

entries.name: kanchou
entries.description: A [prank](#prank) in which the hands are clasped with both index fingers [pointing](#pointing) out and jabbed at an unsuspecting person from behind. It is played for shock and laughter rather than as a sexual act.

entries.name: blade_to_throat
entries.description: A [knife](#knife), [sword](#sword) or other edge pressed against somebody's [neck](#neck) as a [threat](#threat). The victim is normally held still and [no](#no) cut has been made, which separates it from an actual wound.

entries.name: bumping
entries.description: Two characters collide by [accident](#accident), usually while [walking](#walking), and one or both is knocked off balance. Frequently the [opening](#opening) beat of a first meeting.

entries.name: pillow_fight
entries.description: People [swinging](#swinging) pillows at one another in play, often with [feathers](#feathers) bursting loose. It also covers the Japanese pillow-throwing game played on [school](#school) trips.

entries.name: pushing_down
entries.description: One character presses another down onto a [bed](#bed), [floor](#floor), or other surface and holds them there. Often the [opening](#opening) beat of a sexual or confrontational scene.

entries.name: elbowing
entries.description: Driving an elbow into somebody, either as a strike in a fight or as a nudge meant to get their attention.

entries.name: bonk
entries.description: A [comic](#comic) clout to the head, often with the [sound](#sound) spelled out in the air beside it. A [baseball](#baseball) bat is the traditional [instrument](#instrument) though anything or a bare hand will serve, and the point is [punishment](#punishment) played for laughs.

entries.name: crosscounter
entries.description: Two fighters [landing](#landing) blows on each other at the same instant, each fist getting past the other's [guard](#guard). Named after the [boxing](#boxing) [counter](#counter) thrown over an opponent's leading hand.

entries.name: throwing_person
entries.description: One character hurling another through the air, by an arm, a leg or a [wrestling](#wrestling) hold. The victim is already airborne or just leaving the thrower's grip.

entries.name: mixed_gender_duel
entries.description: A one-on-one contest between combatants of opposite sexes, squaring off as formal opponents rather than brawling within a [crowd](#crowd).

entries.name: incoming_kick
entries.description: A leg swung toward the [camera](#camera) so the sole fills the foreground, aimed squarely at the viewer. The kick has not landed.

entries.name: pie_in_face
entries.description: A [pie](#pie) or [cake](#cake) lands flat in somebody's face, flung by another character or pushed there by their own hand. Pure slapstick, with [cream](#cream) smeared across the features and the tin often still [stuck](#stuck) in place.

entries.name: kinniku_buster
entries.description: A [wrestling](#wrestling) move in which the opponent is hoisted upside down across the shoulders and then dropped onto a raised knee. English commentary calls it the muscle buster.

entries.name: imminent_punch
entries.description: A fist drawn [back](#back) or already travelling toward another character, impact still to come. Where the [target](#target) is the viewer, use [incoming_punch](#incoming_punch).

entries.name: punched
entries.description: The moment a fist lands and its [target](#target) reacts, the face deforming or the body snapping [back](#back). Covers the receiving end of a blow, where [punching](#punching) covers the [throwing](#throwing) of it.

entries.name: slam
entries.description: A vague [label](#label) for [driving](#driving) something down hard, covering several unrelated actions. Reach for the specific one instead: a body slam, a [desk](#desk) slam, a wall [pin](#pin), a [basketball](#basketball) dunk or a slamming [door](#door).

entries.name: joint_lock
entries.description: A grappling hold that forces an elbow, wrist or shoulder past the range it was built for, to make the other person give in. Judo, jiu-jitsu and their relatives are full of them.

entries.name: armbar
entries.description: A grappling hold in which one arm is [trapped](#trapped) between the attacker's [thighs](#thighs) and levered straight against the elbow, usually from the ground. A standard submission in [judo](#judo) and mixed martial arts.

entries.name: armlock
entries.description: Both of another person's arms are [pinned](#pinned) in place, usually gathered above or behind their head. No grip is taken on the [neck](#neck), which is what separates it from a full nelson.

entries.name: rear_naked_choke
entries.description: A submission hold applied from behind an opponent, one arm wrapped around the [neck](#neck) and the other locking it in place, sometimes with the [legs](#legs) hooked around the [torso](#torso). Known as hadaka-jime in [judo](#judo) and used as a sleeper hold in professional [wrestling](#wrestling).

entries.name: smack
entries.description: An open-handed blow [landing](#landing) on someone, [caught](#caught) at or just after impact. Sound effects, motion lines and a snapped-back head usually sell the hit.

entries.name: slapping_breasts
entries.description: A hand striking somebody's [breasts](#breasts), hard enough to set them moving. Play rather than [injury](#injury) in almost every case.

entries.name: height_difference
entries.description: One character stands conspicuously taller than another beside them. The gap should be striking, not the ordinary variation between [people](#people).

entries.name: side-by-side
entries.description: Two or more characters stand or sit directly beside each other, shoulder to shoulder. The [tag](#tag) describes placement alone; add [holding_hands](#holding_hands) or [arm_around_shoulder](#arm_around_shoulder) for actual contact.

entries.name: sandwiched
entries.description: One person pressed between two others, front and [back](#back). Frequently a sexual arrangement such as a [threesome](#threesome), but the [tag](#tag) covers any close three-person squeeze.

entries.name: take_your_pick
entries.description: Several characters showing off their bodies or a particular body part side by side, posed as an invitation to choose one of them.

entries.name: girl_sandwich
entries.description: A person of any gender pressed between two girls, one on either side. The Japanese idiom for it is [holding](#holding) a [flower](#flower) in each hand.

entries.name: lineup
entries.description: Several characters [standing](#standing) shoulder to shoulder in a row, as in a [cast](#cast) [display](#display) or a [height](#height) [comparison](#comparison). People [waiting](#waiting) one behind another form a [queue](#queue) instead.

entries.name: teamwork
entries.description: Two or more characters cooperate on a shared task, whether one boosts another up, [tools](#tools) pass hand to hand, or a fight is fought in coordination. A sexual counterpart carries its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: behind_another
entries.description: One character is placed behind another, [standing](#standing), [sitting](#sitting) or lurking there, whether looming, [hiding](#hiding) or embracing from the [back](#back). It records only the arrangement; what they are actually doing takes its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: rotational_symmetry
entries.description: Two characters placed head-to-toe and parallel, one [upside-down](#upside-down) relative to the other, so their positions roughly [mirror](#mirror) by rotation. About the pair's arrangement rather than the whole image, and not the [sex](#sex) position [69](#69).

entries.name: odd_one_out
entries.description: A gathering of near-identical figures or things with one blatant exception among them. The break in the pattern is the whole point, which is why it turns up in lineups and in pictures [crowded](#crowded) with copies of something.

entries.name: surrounded
entries.description: One character ringed by others pressing in from every side. Covers being mobbed, cornered or [crowded](#crowded), and in an explicit context a [figure](#figure) encircled by several partners.

entries.name: boy_sandwich
entries.description: Somebody of any gender is pressed between two boys, one on each side. The counterpart with two girls is [girl_sandwich](#girl_sandwich).

entries.name: circle_formation
entries.description: Three or more characters are arranged in a [ring](#ring) with their bodies [pointing](#pointing) inward, often head first. With only two figures it reads as [symmetry](#symmetry) or a rotated pairing instead.

entries.name: symmetrical_pose
entries.description: Two or more figures struck in the same posture, usually mirrored so the group reads as a matched set. Distinct from [symmetrical_docking](#symmetrical_docking), which is specifically about chests pressed together.

entries.name: hiding_behind_another
entries.description: One character shelters behind another's body, [peeking](#peeking) round a shoulder or an arm, generally out of shyness or fright. Using the other person as [cover](#cover) against an [attack](#attack) is human_shield instead.

entries.name: boy_and_girl_sandwich
entries.description: Somebody is squeezed between a male character on one side and a female character on the other. Whoever ends up in the middle may be of any gender.

entries.name: group_pose
entries.description: Several characters striking a coordinated pose together, each taking a different stance that only reads as a whole. Familiar from sentai line-ups and magical-girl finishing [poses](#poses).

entries.name: opposing_sides
entries.description: Two characters or two groups fill the left and right of the frame and size each other up, usually seen from the side in [profile](#profile) as though a fight is about to start. One side alone counts when a companion picture holds the other; two individuals [glaring](#glaring) with real malice [suit](#suit) [confrontation](#confrontation) better.

entries.name: rope_train
entries.description: A group [walking](#walking) in single [file](#file) inside a loose loop of [rope](#rope), each person [holding](#holding) on, in imitation of a [train](#train). A children's game, and the way nursery groups are sometimes led along a [street](#street).

entries.name: cleavage_reach
entries.description: A hand pushed down into a woman's [cleavage](#cleavage), generally [fishing](#fishing) out something stored there. It counts whether she reaches in herself or somebody else does it.

entries.name: own_hands_together
entries.description: One character's hands touch each other, whether clasped, pressed palm to palm, or with only the fingertips meeting. Hands meeting another person's are [holding_hands](#holding_hands).

entries.name: hand_on_own_chest
entries.description: A character lays one hand flat on their own chest, which reads as relief, sincerity or a vow. Both hands there is [hands_on_own_chest](#hands_on_own_chest).

entries.name: hand_on_own_face
entries.description: A hand rests somewhere on the character's own face, without narrowing down where. It overlaps heavily with [hand_on_own_cheek](#hand_on_own_cheek); both hands is [hands_on_own_face](#hands_on_own_face).

entries.name: covering_privates
entries.description: A character hides their private parts out of shyness, embarrassment or [teasing](#teasing). It is the [umbrella](#umbrella) for the specific versions, so add whichever of [breasts](#breasts), [crotch](#crotch), [nipples](#nipples) or backside is being hidden.

entries.name: finger_to_mouth
entries.description: A finger, generally the character's own, held at or against the [lips](#lips) without going in. It stretches from [shushing](#shushing) and cute [posing](#posing) to seduction or pondering; inside the mouth is [finger_in_own_mouth](#finger_in_own_mouth).

entries.name: breasts_squeezed_together
entries.description: Both [breasts](#breasts) are pressed hard against each other, usually by the character's own hands or upper arms, deepening the [cleavage](#cleavage). Merely [holding](#holding) or fondling them is [grabbing_another's_breast](#grabbing_another's_breast), and two girls doing it to one another is [symmetrical_docking](#symmetrical_docking).

entries.name: hand_in_own_hair
entries.description: A character has one hand [buried](#buried) in or drawn through their own hair. When both hands are up there the [tag](#tag) becomes [hands_in_hair](#hands_in_hair).

entries.name: hand_between_legs
entries.description: One or both hands tucked between the character's own [legs](#legs) with nothing further going on, so [no](#no) [masturbation](#masturbation) or [skirt](#skirt) [tug](#tug). It often accompanies [v_arms](#v_arms) and the [wariza](#wariza) [sitting](#sitting) position.

entries.name: adjusting_clothes
entries.description: A character straightens or tugs at a garment they are wearing so it sits comfortably. Reach for the garment-specific [tag](#tag), such as [adjusting_gloves](#adjusting_gloves) or [adjusting_swimsuit](#adjusting_swimsuit), whenever one exists.

entries.name: hand_between_own_legs
entries.description: A hand slipped down between the [thighs](#thighs), usually while seated or [kneeling](#kneeling). The posture reads as closed-in, demure or a little [nervous](#nervous).

entries.name: hand_on_own_cheek
entries.description: One hand rests against the character's own cheek, the classic [thinking](#thinking), bashful or delighted [gesture](#gesture). With a hand on each cheek use [hands_on_own_cheeks](#hands_on_own_cheeks).

entries.name: skirt_hold
entries.description: Holding the hem of a [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) modestly, such as lifting it clear of the [floor](#floor), without exposing anything. Raising it to reveal is [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift); [pulling](#pulling) it down to [cover](#cover) is [skirt_tug](#skirt_tug).

entries.name: covering_own_mouth
entries.description: A character puts their own hand or hands over their mouth, stifling a laugh, gasping, [hiding](#hiding) a [smile](#smile) or [holding](#holding) a [sound](#sound) in. Another person's hand there is [covering_another's_mouth](#covering_another's_mouth).

entries.name: covering_breasts
entries.description: A woman holds her own hands or arms across her chest to hide the [nipples](#nipples) and areolae, the classic hand [bra](#bra). Breast_hold, a different grip on the [breasts](#breasts), is not the same thing.

entries.name: adjusting_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) are pushed up the [nose](#nose), settled into line with the eyes, or lifted onto the head. Add [hand_on_eyewear](#hand_on_eyewear) when two or more fingers do the work and [finger_on_eyewear](#finger_on_eyewear) when only one does.

entries.name: adjusting_hair
entries.description: A character casually fixes, smooths or fiddles with their own hair by hand. Prefer a narrower [tag](#tag) such as hair_tucking or [tying_hair](#tying_hair) whenever one applies.

entries.name: hand_on_headwear
entries.description: One hand touches or grips a [hat](#hat) the character currently has on, whether tipping it, tugging it lower or [holding](#holding) it against [wind](#wind). A hat being carried rather than worn is [holding_hat](#holding_hat).

entries.name: hand_on_own_chin
entries.description: One hand rests at the character's own chin, most often signalling thought, appraisal or boredom. Both hands cradling the chin is [hands_on_own_chin](#hands_on_own_chin).

entries.name: hands_on_own_face
entries.description: Both hands touch the character's own face, covering [despair](#despair), embarrassment or delighted shock. With only one hand use [hand_on_own_face](#hand_on_own_face).

entries.name: hand_to_own_mouth
entries.description: A hand brought up near the character's own mouth without covering it, as when [yawning](#yawning), [giggling](#giggling) behind it or [whispering](#whispering). Once the mouth is actually covered, use [hand_over_own_mouth](#hand_over_own_mouth).

entries.name: breast_grab_(self)
entries.description: A character takes hold of her own [breasts](#breasts), lifting, [squeezing](#squeezing) or offering them with her hands. The [gesture](#gesture) is normally posed and aimed at the viewer.

entries.name: hand_on_own_head
entries.description: A character puts one hand on top of their own head, touching hair rather than face. It covers sheepish [scratching](#scratching), [holding](#holding) hair flat and clutching at the [skull](#skull); both hands is [hands_on_own_head](#hands_on_own_head).

entries.name: hands_on_own_chest
entries.description: A character places both hands on their own chest, as in relief, pleading or clutching something to the [heart](#heart). One hand is [hand_on_own_chest](#hand_on_own_chest).

entries.name: own_hands_clasped
entries.description: A character holds their own two hands together, usually with the fingers laced, as in prayer or entreaty. Two [people](#people) gripping each other's hands are [holding_hands](#holding_hands) with [interlocked_fingers](#interlocked_fingers).

entries.name: covering_crotch
entries.description: A character deliberately shields their own [crotch](#crotch) with hands, clothing or something they are [holding](#holding). It applies whether the crotch is bare or still dressed.

entries.name: holding_own_dress
entries.description: A handful of the character's own [dress](#dress) is gathered up, pinched at the side or lifted clear of the [floor](#floor) as in a [curtsey](#curtsey). The dress stays on throughout.

entries.name: hand_on_own_arm
entries.description: A character grips or touches their own arm with the other hand, a closed-off, self-soothing posture. Both hands on both arms is hands_on_own_arms.

entries.name: holding_own_hair
entries.description: A [lock](#lock) or length of the character's own hair is held in the hand, played with or swept aside. Another person's hair calls for [holding_another's_hair](#holding_another's_hair).

entries.name: hand_on_own_thigh
entries.description: Just one hand lies on the character's own thigh, whether they are seated or [standing](#standing). With a hand on each thigh use [hands_on_own_thighs](#hands_on_own_thighs).

entries.name: hand_on_own_knee
entries.description: One hand rests on one of the character's own [knees](#knees), usually while [sitting](#sitting) or crouching. Keep it apart from [hands_on_own_knee](#hands_on_own_knee) and [hands_on_own_knees](#hands_on_own_knees), which count hands and knees differently.

entries.name: holding_own_arm
entries.description: One hand closes around the character's own arm, a [shy](#shy), [nervous](#nervous) or self-comforting posture. Gripping somebody else's arm is [holding_another's_arm](#holding_another's_arm).

entries.name: clothes_grab
entries.description: A character grips their own or somebody else's clothing without moving it to expose or [cover](#cover) anything, often a light [tug](#tug) at a sleeve to get attention. Moving the garment makes it [shirt_tug](#shirt_tug) or [shirt_pull](#shirt_pull).

entries.name: breast_rest
entries.description: The [breasts](#breasts) take their [weight](#weight) on something: a [table](#table), a [counter](#counter), a carried object or another person's head. Narrower cases have their own tags in [breasts_on_table](#breasts_on_table), [breasts_on_head](#breasts_on_head) and [carried_breast_rest](#carried_breast_rest), while [holding](#holding) them up by hand is [breast_lift](#breast_lift).

entries.name: tying_hair
entries.description: A character [gathers](#gathers) hair into a [ponytail](#ponytail), [twintails](#twintails) or bun, hands [reaching](#reaching) behind the head, often with a hair tie held between the [teeth](#teeth). A common getting-ready moment.

entries.name: hands_on_own_cheeks
entries.description: Both hands pressed to the character's own cheeks, a bashful, thrilled or [horrified](#horrified) reaction. One hand is [hand_on_own_cheek](#hand_on_own_cheek), and doing it to somebody else is [hands_on_another's_cheeks](#hands_on_another's_cheeks).

entries.name: hand_on_own_stomach
entries.description: One hand rests on the character's own [belly](#belly), a common touch in pregnancy, hunger and after-dinner scenes. Both hands is [hands_on_own_stomach](#hands_on_own_stomach); somebody else's belly is [hand_on_another's_stomach](#hand_on_another's_stomach).

entries.name: adjusting_headwear
entries.description: A hand settles a [hat](#hat), cap or other headwear, tipping the brim or [pulling](#pulling) it down snug. The [gesture](#gesture) ranges from tidying to [hiding](#hiding) the eyes.

entries.name: hand_on_own_ass
entries.description: A character rests one hand on their own buttocks. Two hands is [hands_on_own_ass](#hands_on_own_ass), while [pulling](#pulling) the cheeks apart is [ass_support](#ass_support).

entries.name: ass_grab_(self)
entries.description: A character takes hold of one of their own buttocks, [squeezing](#squeezing) it or [pulling](#pulling) it aside. Somebody else's hand doing the same takes a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: covering_face
entries.description: Hands or a held object hide a character's own face, entirely or nearly so. Used for embarrassment, weeping into the [palms](#palms) and [peeking](#peeking) between fingers; [hiding](#hiding) only the mouth or the eyes has its own tags.

entries.name: holding_own_skirt
entries.description: The character takes hold of their own [skirt](#skirt), [pinching](#pinching) or bunching the [cloth](#cloth). Curtseying, keeping the hem down in a breeze and lifting it deliberately are all covered.

entries.name: hands_on_own_knees
entries.description: Both hands rest on the character's own [knees](#knees), one hand per knee. It fits [sitting](#sitting) upright as [well](#well) as [bending](#bending) forward to catch [breath](#breath); compare [hand_on_own_knee](#hand_on_own_knee) and [hands_on_own_knee](#hands_on_own_knee).

entries.name: hands_in_hair
entries.description: A character has both hands, or more than two, in their own hair. It fits gathering it up, [washing](#washing) it and clutching the head; a single hand is [hand_in_own_hair](#hand_in_own_hair).

entries.name: breast_suppress
entries.description: One or both hands press down flat on top of the character's own [breasts](#breasts), [holding](#holding) them still or simply [resting](#resting) there. Lifting from beneath is [breast_lift](#breast_lift), and [hiding](#hiding) the [nipples](#nipples) with the hands is [covering_breasts](#covering_breasts).

entries.name: breast_lift
entries.description: Breasts are pushed or held up by hands, her own or somebody else's. Supporting them on the [forearms](#forearms) is breast_hold, letting them rest on something is [breast_rest](#breast_rest), and pressing them together is [breasts_squeezed_together](#breasts_squeezed_together).

entries.name: hands_in_own_hair
entries.description: Both hands [buried](#buried) in the character's own hair, whether combing through it, gripping it in frustration or lifting it off the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: tucking_hair
entries.description: A hand pushes a stray [lock](#lock) of hair [back](#back) behind the ear or away from the face. A small, often self-conscious [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: finger_to_cheek
entries.description: The character sets a finger, usually the index one, plainly against their own cheek. A cutesy [posing](#posing) [habit](#habit), and sometimes a thoughtful one.

entries.name: hand_over_own_mouth
entries.description: A character covers their own mouth with a hand, out of shock, stifled laughter or an attempt to hide their reaction. A hand held near the mouth without covering it is [hand_to_own_mouth](#hand_to_own_mouth).

entries.name: adjusting_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) is put right by hand, on the wearer or on somebody else, most often tugging the [back](#back) down over the buttocks. Straps being reseated count as [well](#well).

entries.name: twirling_hair
entries.description: A finger winds a [lock](#lock) of hair around itself, a fidget that usually signals nerves or flirtation. Distinct from a [plain](#plain) tuck behind the ear.

entries.name: hand_on_own_leg
entries.description: A character has a single hand on their own leg. Both hands is [hands_on_own_legs](#hands_on_own_legs), and a hand specifically on the thigh is [hand_on_own_thigh](#hand_on_own_thigh).

entries.name: covering_own_eyes
entries.description: A character hides their own eyes, usually behind the hands, to block out a sight, escape embarrassment or keep their face unseen. When somebody else does the covering, use [covering_another's_eyes](#covering_another's_eyes).

entries.name: hands_on_own_head
entries.description: Both hands rest on the character's own head, on the hair rather than the face. It fits clutching the [skull](#skull) in dismay and [holding](#holding) hair down in the [wind](#wind); one hand is [hand_on_own_head](#hand_on_own_head).

entries.name: rubbing_eyes
entries.description: A character [rubbing](#rubbing) one or both eyes with a hand, usually showing sleepiness on waking or before [bed](#bed). Wiping away [tears](#tears) instead is [wiping_tears](#wiping_tears).

entries.name: finger_to_own_chin
entries.description: A finger propped against the character's own chin, the classic pose for weighing something up or being puzzled, occasionally for looking pleased with oneself. Touching another person's chin is its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: playing_with_own_hair
entries.description: A character twirls, twists, or fiddles with a strand of their own hair, often absent-mindedly or flirtatiously. Simply [brushing](#brushing) hair [back](#back) is [adjusting_hair](#adjusting_hair) instead.

entries.name: covering_nipples
entries.description: Only the [nipples](#nipples) are hidden, by a hand or a finger or two, with most of the breast and often the areolae left bare. Arms or whole hands across the chest make it [covering_breasts](#covering_breasts).

entries.name: adjusting_gloves
entries.description: Gloves are pulled or tugged into place for a snug fit, often as a pointed getting-ready [gesture](#gesture). Both hands are typically involved, one [working](#working) the cuff of the other.

entries.name: hands_on_own_thighs
entries.description: Both hands rest on the character's own [thighs](#thighs), frequently taking [weight](#weight) as they lean forward, squat or kneel in [seiza](#seiza). A single hand is [hand_on_own_thigh](#hand_on_own_thigh).

entries.name: finger_in_own_mouth
entries.description: The character's own finger is inside their mouth, held there, bitten or sucked. A finger [resting](#resting) outside the [lips](#lips) is [finger_to_mouth](#finger_to_mouth), and where the two cannot be told apart both [can](#can) be applied.

entries.name: hand_on_eyewear
entries.description: Two fingers or a full hand placed on the [glasses](#glasses) or [goggles](#goggles) a character wears, in order to settle them. A single finger nudging the [bridge](#bridge) upward is [finger_on_eyewear](#finger_on_eyewear).

entries.name: hands_on_headwear
entries.description: A character holds the [hat](#hat) they are wearing with both hands, usually [pulling](#pulling) it down or keeping it from [blowing](#blowing) away. A hat that is not on the head is [holding_hat](#holding_hat).

entries.name: wiping_tears
entries.description: Tears are rubbed away from the eyes or cheeks with a hand, sleeve, or [tissue](#tissue). Tag [tears](#tears) and [crying](#crying) as they apply.

entries.name: palms_together
entries.description: Both hands pressed flat against each other, fingers straight rather than laced. The [praying](#praying) or itadakimasu [gesture](#gesture), also used to plead or to thank; laced fingers make it [own_hands_clasped](#own_hands_clasped).

entries.name: stroking_own_chin
entries.description: A character [rubbing](#rubbing) their own chin, the [familiar](#familiar) [gesture](#gesture) for pondering or for quiet self-satisfaction. For touching someone else's chin use [stroking_another's_chin](#stroking_another's_chin). Implies [hand_on_own_chin](#hand_on_own_chin).

entries.name: hand_on_own_shoulder
entries.description: A character rests one hand on their own shoulder, the arm typically crossed over the chest to reach it. Both hands is [hands_on_own_shoulders](#hands_on_own_shoulders).

entries.name: hair_in_own_mouth
entries.description: A character holds a strand or [lock](#lock) of their own hair in their mouth, a seductive or [nervous](#nervous) [gesture](#gesture). Chewing someone else's hair is [eating_hair](#eating_hair) instead.

entries.name: wiping_face
entries.description: A character wipes their own face with a hand, sleeve, [towel](#towel), or [tissue](#tissue). Use [wiping_sweat](#wiping_sweat) or [wiping_tears](#wiping_tears) instead once it is clear what is being removed.

entries.name: hand_on_own_neck
entries.description: One hand touches the character's own [neck](#neck), [rubbing](#rubbing) the [nape](#nape) behind or clutching at the throat in front. Both hands is [hands_on_own_neck](#hands_on_own_neck).

entries.name: hair_lift
entries.description: Someone lifts their hair up with the hands, arms or an object, for instance to bare the [nape](#nape). Not [floating_hair](#floating_hair), which is hair blown or [drifting](#drifting) by itself.

entries.name: hands_on_own_ass
entries.description: A character has both hands on their own buttocks. One hand is [hand_on_own_ass](#hand_on_own_ass), and [pulling](#pulling) the cheeks apart is [ass_support](#ass_support).

entries.name: holding_own_tail
entries.description: A character with a [tail](#tail) holds it in the hands, hugging it, lifting it or [presenting](#presenting) it. The tail has to be their own.

entries.name: shirt_in_mouth
entries.description: A character [holding](#holding) up the hem of their own [shirt](#shirt) between their [teeth](#teeth), usually to bare the chest or [stomach](#stomach). Implies [clothes_in_mouth](#clothes_in_mouth) and [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold); combine with [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift).

entries.name: wiping_sweat
entries.description: Sweat is brushed off the brow or body with a hand, sleeve, or [cloth](#cloth), usually after exertion or heat. Combine with [sweat](#sweat); a [towel](#towel) takes its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: finger_to_face
entries.description: One extended finger touches the character's own face. Reach for [finger_to_cheek](#finger_to_cheek), [finger_to_mouth](#finger_to_mouth) or [finger_to_own_chin](#finger_to_own_chin) when the spot is covered by one of those.

entries.name: belly_grab
entries.description: A hand takes hold of a fistful of [belly](#belly), either the character's own while lamenting their [weight](#weight) or somebody else's as a taunt. It is a pinch of soft [stomach](#stomach), not an embrace.

entries.name: hand_on_own_forehead
entries.description: A hand placed on or just in front of the character's own [forehead](#forehead). It fits checking a [fever](#fever), shading the eyes against glare, and the slow [gesture](#gesture) of exasperation.

entries.name: eyelid_pull
entries.description: A finger drags down the lower eyelid, usually with the [tongue](#tongue) out in the mocking [akanbe](#akanbe) [gesture](#gesture). It [can](#can) also be a medical check of the eye.

entries.name: hands_on_own_stomach
entries.description: Both of a character's hands rest on their own [belly](#belly), common in pregnancy or after a large [meal](#meal). One hand is [hand_on_own_stomach](#hand_on_own_stomach); another person's belly is [hands_on_another's_stomach](#hands_on_another's_stomach).

entries.name: pinching_sleeves
entries.description: A character [holding](#holding) their own sleeve [cuffs](#cuffs) between the fingers, usually to keep sleeves that hang past the wrists in place. A demure mannerism; tugging somebody else's sleeve is [sleeve_grab](#sleeve_grab).

entries.name: ass_support
entries.description: The underside of the buttocks is held or lifted, by the character's own hands, by another's, or by something propped beneath. The counterpart of [breast_lift](#breast_lift).

entries.name: mouth_pull
entries.description: Fingers hooked into a mouth to drag it open or stretch the cheeks [sideways](#sideways), one's own mouth or somebody else's. Usually a taunt or a piece of clowning.

entries.name: breasts_on_table
entries.description: The [breasts](#breasts) rest on a [table](#table), [desk](#desk) or [counter](#counter) while the character leans or sits at it. Add [breast_rest](#breast_rest), and [breasts_on_glass](#breasts_on_glass) where the surface is [glass](#glass).

entries.name: covering_one_eye
entries.description: A hand or held object rests over one of a character's own eyes while the other stays visible, a favourite dramatic pose. Hair doing the same is [hair_over_one_eye](#hair_over_one_eye), and both eyes hidden is [covering_own_eyes](#covering_own_eyes).

entries.name: hand_on_own_elbow
entries.description: One hand grips or rests on the character's own elbow, usually with that arm [folded](#folded) across the body. The posture reads as guarded or [shy](#shy).

entries.name: ojou-sama_pose
entries.description: The [back](#back) of one hand is raised in front of the mouth in the manner of a haughty rich young lady, generally mid-laugh. Male characters sometimes strike it as a joke.

entries.name: adjusting_legwear
entries.description: Thighhighs, tights or [socks](#socks) are pulled up or straightened by hand, often with the wearer bent over or one leg raised. Tag the legwear itself separately.

entries.name: adjusting_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) is straightened or loosened by hand, usually for comfort or as a bit of swagger. The fingers work at the knot or the length below it.

entries.name: facepalm
entries.description: A hand is [planted](#planted) over one's own face in exasperation at something stupid. Disbelief or weary frustration is the message, usually with the eyes shut.

entries.name: hand_to_head
entries.description: A character raises a hand toward their own head, and it need not actually make contact. The [gesture](#gesture) covers salute-like motions and the pause of somebody [thinking](#thinking).

entries.name: hair_flip
entries.description: A character tosses a [lock](#lock) of hair aside with the hand, an elegant or haughty [gesture](#gesture). Not the hairstyle with curled tips, which is [flipped_hair](#flipped_hair), nor [whipping](#whipping) the whole head of hair.

entries.name: covering_ass
entries.description: A character tries to [shield](#shield) their own backside from view with hands, clothing or an object, whether or not [underwear](#underwear) is worn. Embarrassment or a lifted [skirt](#skirt) is the usual reason.

entries.name: hand_on_own_ear
entries.description: A character touches their own ear, whether cupping it to catch a [sound](#sound) or fiddling with an [animal](#animal) ear. Earrings and earpieces often come into it.

entries.name: hand_on_headphones
entries.description: A character presses or holds the [headphones](#headphones) they are wearing with one hand. It is the standard [listening](#listening) pose, [familiar](#familiar) from disc jockeys and singers in the booth.

entries.name: bunching_hair
entries.description: A character [gathers](#gathers) handfuls of hair and holds them up to [mimic](#mimic) a style they do not actually have, usually fake [twintails](#twintails). Genuinely [tying](#tying) the hair [back](#back) is something else.

entries.name: hugging_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) is held in a [hug](#hug), whether the character's own or somebody else's. When a tail wraps around a character instead, use [tail_wrap](#tail_wrap).

entries.name: hand_over_eye
entries.description: A character holds a hand across one of their own eyes, though the eye need not actually be hidden by it. It is a theatrical [gesture](#gesture), standard in [chuunibyou](#chuunibyou) posturing.

entries.name: clothes_tug
entries.description: A garment is pulled on to adjust its fit or to [cover](#cover) more of the body, such as a [skirt](#skirt) hem tugged down in embarrassment. Pulling in order to expose is [clothes_pull](#clothes_pull).

entries.name: self_hug
entries.description: A character [wrapping](#wrapping) their arms around themselves, hands [resting](#resting) on the opposite arm, shoulder, or hip, sometimes with the arms crossed. A [comforting](#comforting) [gesture](#gesture) when [scared](#scared), [sad](#sad), [embarrassed](#embarrassed), or [cold](#cold).

entries.name: scratching_head
entries.description: A hand up in one's own hair, [working](#working) at the scalp. Reads as puzzlement, sheepishness, or simply having just woken up.

entries.name: adjusting_panties
entries.description: The wearer pulls at their [underwear](#underwear) to seat it comfortably, whether after [dressing](#dressing) or to free a [wedgie](#wedgie). Hands rest at the waistband or the leg [opening](#opening).

entries.name: covering_one_breast
entries.description: One arm or hand hides a single breast while the other is left uncovered. Common in [bathing](#bathing) and [undressing](#undressing) scenes.

entries.name: hands_on_thighs
entries.description: Both hands laid on the [thighs](#thighs), a composed pose common when [kneeling](#kneeling) or [sitting](#sitting) straight-backed. It also shows up while [resting](#resting) after exertion.

entries.name: fingersmile
entries.description: Fingers hooked into the corners of the mouth and pushed upward to force a [grin](#grin). Dragging them down into a [scowl](#scowl) instead falls under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: tying
entries.description: Hands [knotting](#knotting) a piece of clothing together, such as a [bowtie](#bowtie), a uniform [ribbon](#ribbon) or the strings of a side-tie [bikini](#bikini) or pair of [briefs](#briefs). The moment of fastening is what the [tag](#tag) catches.

entries.name: hands_on_own_legs
entries.description: Both hands rest on the character's own [legs](#legs), one to each. A single hand takes [hand_on_own_leg](#hand_on_own_leg).

entries.name: adjusting_scarf
entries.description: Hands [wind](#wind), tighten or straighten a [scarf](#scarf) at the [neck](#neck), on the wearer or on someone else. A [winter](#winter) [gesture](#gesture), often paired with fogged [breath](#breath) or [falling](#falling) [snow](#snow).

entries.name: scratching_cheek
entries.description: A single finger [rubbing](#rubbing) at one's own cheek, the standard [gesture](#gesture) for awkwardness, shyness, or not quite knowing what to say.

entries.name: wiping_mouth
entries.description: A hand, sleeve, or [napkin](#napkin) passes across the mouth after [eating](#eating), [drinking](#drinking), or a [kiss](#kiss). It is often paired with a [blush](#blush) or with the mouth being covered entirely.

entries.name: fingers_to_cheeks
entries.description: More than one finger set against the cheeks, most often an index finger poked into each. A posed, cute [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: sock_pull
entries.description: A sock being tugged at while going on, coming off, or being straightened, or simply [sliding](#sliding) down the leg on its own. A hand gripping the cuff is the usual visual cue.

entries.name: covering_own_ears
entries.description: A character claps both hands over their ears to shut out a noise or refuse to hear something. Embarrassment is another common reason.

entries.name: hands_on_own_chin
entries.description: Both hands [cradle](#cradle) the character's own chin, elbows usually propped on a surface. It is the dreamy, attentive rest; a single hand is [hand_on_own_chin](#hand_on_own_chin).

entries.name: yandere_trance
entries.description: Both hands pressed flat against the cheeks while the character stares out with a fixed, unsettling look. The eyes carry the whole effect and may be drawn [glowing](#glowing) or with unstable pupils.

entries.name: adjusting_buruma
entries.description: A character tugs at the leg [opening](#opening) or waistband of their [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) to make them sit better. It shows up in [school](#school) sports scenes, generally with the rest of the gym kit on.

entries.name: hugging_own_tail
entries.description: A character wraps their arms around their own [tail](#tail) and holds it against themselves, often while curled up. It reads as [shy](#shy) or self-comforting.

entries.name: scratching
entries.description: Fingers or [claws](#claws) raked lightly over one's own skin, usually to relieve an itch. Whatever streaks are left behind afterward are tagged [scratches](#scratches).

entries.name: hand_over_face
entries.description: A hand covering the face without saying which part. Prefer something that names what is hidden, such as covering the eyes or the mouth, or a [facepalm](#facepalm).

entries.name: hands_on_headphones
entries.description: Both hands cupped over [headphones](#headphones) the character wears on the head or has [hanging](#hanging) at the [neck](#neck), pressing them closer. It is the pose of [listening](#listening) hard or of a disc [jockey](#jockey) mid-mix.

entries.name: hand_on_own_hat
entries.description: A hand up at the [crown](#crown) or brim of the [hat](#hat) the character has on, tipping it, tugging it down or [holding](#holding) it against a gust. The hat stays worn rather than carried.

entries.name: adjusting_footwear
entries.description: The wearer reaches down to fix at least one shoe or boot, [pulling](#pulling) it on, straightening the heel or dealing with a fastening. Usually drawn [bending](#bending) over or with one foot lifted.

entries.name: adjusting_leotard
entries.description: The wearer tugs a [leotard](#leotard) [back](#back) into place, most often at the hip or seat where the [fabric](#fabric) has ridden up. Common in [gymnastics](#gymnastics), dance and bunny-suit pictures.

entries.name: covering_chest
entries.description: A character holds an arm or both hands across their own chest to conceal it. It reads as modesty, or as being [caught](#caught) unprepared.

entries.name: fingers_to_mouth
entries.description: Several fingers held at or just before the [lips](#lips), screening a [smile](#smile) or a small [gasp](#gasp). Gentler than [clapping](#clapping) a whole hand over the mouth.

entries.name: holding_own_wrist
entries.description: One hand closes around the character's own wrist or lower arm, a reserved, self-contained [gesture](#gesture). Taking hold of somebody else's wrist has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: gendou_pose
entries.description: Elbows [planted](#planted) and hands [folded](#folded) or fingers laced in front of the mouth so the lower face is hidden, usually while seated. Reads as scheming or unreadable authority, often with light flaring across the [glasses](#glasses).

entries.name: grabbing_own_thigh
entries.description: A hand closed on the character's own thigh, fingers pressing into it or bracing against it. It both draws the eye to the leg and signals tension.

entries.name: peeking_through_fingers
entries.description: Hands held over the face with the fingers parted just enough to see between them. The standard pose for not wanting to look and looking anyway.

entries.name: thumb_sucking
entries.description: A thumb held in the mouth and sucked, the [habit](#habit) of infants and small children. On an older character it reads as regression, comfort-seeking or a deliberately childish affectation.

entries.name: collar_tug
entries.description: Someone pulls their own [shirt](#shirt) [collar](#collar) away from the [neck](#neck), letting air in or [fidgeting](#fidgeting) from nerves. Hauling the neckline down to bare the chest is [shirt_pull](#shirt_pull), tugging the hem is [shirt_tug](#shirt_tug), and another person doing the [pulling](#pulling) is [collar_grab](#collar_grab).

entries.name: adjusting_bra
entries.description: The wearer pulls at their [bra](#bra) to seat it properly, whether just after putting it on or to relieve a [pinching](#pinching) [strap](#strap). Hands rest on the cups, the band or the straps.

entries.name: hands_on_own_knee
entries.description: Both hands rest on one single knee of the character's own, generally with that leg drawn up. Keep it apart from the one-hand and both-knee variants.

entries.name: hand_on_own_foot
entries.description: A character holds one of their own [feet](#feet), as when [rubbing](#rubbing) it, [pulling](#pulling) a sock on or [stretching](#stretching) while seated. The knee is generally drawn up to bring the foot within reach.

entries.name: grabbing_own_hair
entries.description: A character's own fist clenched in their hair, gripping or [dragging](#dragging) at it. It reads as frustration, [pain](#pain) or [despair](#despair); the composed version of touching one's hair is [adjusting_hair](#adjusting_hair).

entries.name: finger_to_eye
entries.description: A finger placed on or beside the character's own eye. Tugging the lower [lid](#lid) down with the [tongue](#tongue) [stuck](#stuck) out makes the mocking [akanbe](#akanbe) face, and [plain](#plain) eye-rubbing counts too.

entries.name: sweater_tug
entries.description: A hand pinches and tugs at part of a [sweater](#sweater) — the hem, [collar](#collar) or a sleeve — without [pulling](#pulling) it out of place. Reads as a small [fidgeting](#fidgeting) [gesture](#gesture) rather than an attempt to undress.

entries.name: breasts_on_tray
entries.description: The [breasts](#breasts) rest on a [tray](#tray), either one carried at chest [height](#height) or one already [standing](#standing) on a [table](#table). Either way the tray is taking their [weight](#weight).

entries.name: hat_tug
entries.description: Gripping a [hat](#hat) by its sides or brim and [dragging](#dragging) it down over the face without taking it off. Hiding is the usual reason.

entries.name: adjusting_goggles
entries.description: Hands settle a pair of [goggles](#goggles), either down over the eyes or pushed up onto the [forehead](#forehead). The [strap](#strap) or rim is being moved rather than simply held.

entries.name: hand_on_own_wrist
entries.description: One hand closed around the opposite wrist, drawing both arms in toward the body. The pose reads as [nervous](#nervous), [restrained](#restrained) or demure.

entries.name: hands_on_legs
entries.description: Both hands [resting](#resting) on the [legs](#legs), most often with the arms straight and the [palms](#palms) flat on the [thighs](#thighs). It is a settled, attentive posture.

entries.name: tying_footwear
entries.description: Hands work the [laces](#laces) of a shoe or boot into a [bow](#bow). Usually shown crouched, or with the foot lifted onto a step.

entries.name: wiping_blood
entries.description: Blood is wiped away from skin, a blade, or a face using a hand, sleeve, or rag. Add whichever [tag](#tag) names where the [blood](#blood) actually sits.

entries.name: pectoral_squeeze
entries.description: Both [pectorals](#pectorals) pushed together, usually by the hands or the upper arms, deepening the groove between them. Pressing them against something is [pectoral_press](#pectoral_press), and merely [holding](#holding) them is [pectoral_grab](#pectoral_grab).

entries.name: apron_hold
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) is gripped at the hem with both hands and held out, the way a [skirt](#skirt) is lifted for a [curtsey](#curtsey). Nothing beneath is shown; the deliberately revealing version is [apron_lift](#apron_lift).

entries.name: clutching_chest
entries.description: Fingers dug into one's own chest, bunching the [fabric](#fabric) over the [heart](#heart). It reads as [pain](#pain), shock or emotion too [strong](#strong) to hold in.

entries.name: breathing_on_hands
entries.description: A character cups both hands near the mouth and blows into them, the usual way of warming [cold](#cold) fingers. Snow, [winter](#winter) clothing or visible [breath](#breath) generally surround it.

entries.name: adjusting_shoe
entries.description: A character works at one of their [shoes](#shoes), [sliding](#sliding) the heel in, tugging the [back](#back) up or seeing to the [laces](#laces). It is usually drawn crouched or with the foot propped on something.

entries.name: stifled_laugh
entries.description: Someone [holding](#holding) laughter [back](#back), usually with a hand clamped over the mouth and the shoulders [shaking](#shaking). It tends to leak out anyway as [giggling](#giggling).

entries.name: hand_to_forehead
entries.description: A palm or the [back](#back) of a hand pressed to the brow. It covers swooning, nursing a [headache](#headache) and shading the eyes to look into the distance.

entries.name: cape_hold
entries.description: A hand grips one's own [cape](#cape), [holding](#holding) an edge out or drawing it across the body. A theatrical flourish for cloaked characters.

entries.name: wiping_forehead
entries.description: The [back](#back) of a hand, a sleeve, or a [towel](#towel) is drawn across the [forehead](#forehead) to clear away [sweat](#sweat). It signals heat, exertion, or relief once work is finished.

entries.name: adjusting_hood
entries.description: Hands pull a [hood](#hood) up, [back](#back) or straight, arranging how it sits on the head. It may be drawn forward to hide the face or pushed off entirely.

entries.name: thumb_to_mouth
entries.description: A thumb [resting](#resting) at or against the [lips](#lips), touching the mouth without being sucked. It usually goes with a thoughtful or coy expression.

entries.name: covering_head
entries.description: A character shields their own head with arms or hands, usually flinching from a blow, a loud noise or [falling](#falling) [debris](#debris).

entries.name: holding_ears
entries.description: Both hands [cup](#cup) or grip the ears, very often [animal](#animal) ears, whether shutting out a noise or fussing with them bashfully. The ears normally belong to the character doing the [holding](#holding).

entries.name: tying_apron
entries.description: A character fastens the strings of an [apron](#apron), [reaching](#reaching) behind the waist or [knotting](#knotting) them at the [neck](#neck). A common [opening](#opening) beat in [cooking](#cooking) and housework scenes.

entries.name: unbuttoning
entries.description: Fingers work [buttons](#buttons) loose in the moment, rather than a garment simply [hanging](#hanging) open already. The hand [caught](#caught) at the button is what separates it from an already-unbuttoned state.

entries.name: shirt_hold
entries.description: A hand gripping a [shirt](#shirt), whether the character's own or someone else's, bunching the [fabric](#fabric) into the fist.

entries.name: finger_to_head
entries.description: A finger raised to one's own head, [resting](#resting) at the [temple](#temple) or [forehead](#forehead). It usually goes with [thinking](#thinking), recalling something, or [driving](#driving) a point home.

entries.name: hand_on_own_ankle
entries.description: Fingers closed around the character's own ankle, usually while seated with the leg drawn up or during a stretch. Both hands there would be the plural form.

entries.name: pectoral_lift
entries.description: A character holds their own [pectorals](#pectorals) up, arms [folded](#folded) beneath them, hands cupping from below, or a [harness](#harness) or [belt](#belt) [pushing](#pushing) them higher. Frequently drawn together with [pectoral_squeeze](#pectoral_squeeze).

entries.name: dress_grab
entries.description: The wearer bunches her [dress](#dress) in one or both fists and holds tight. Read alongside the face it [can](#can) mean nerves, modesty or resolve.

entries.name: nose_picking
entries.description: A finger is pushed up a nostril. It is almost always played for crude comedy or to make a character look coarse.

entries.name: hands_on_own_neck
entries.description: Both hands at the character's own throat, clutching it, cooling off or lifting hair away from the [nape](#nape). A lone hand is [hand_on_own_neck](#hand_on_own_neck).

entries.name: jacket_grab
entries.description: A hand takes hold of a [jacket](#jacket), the wearer's own or somebody else's, often with a small [tug](#tug) for attention. It reads as hesitant or pleading rather than as a struggle.

entries.name: warming_hands
entries.description: Hands cupped and breathed into, or held out toward a [fire](#fire), [heater](#heater) or [hot](#hot) [drink](#drink) to drive off the [cold](#cold). A cold-weather [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: hands_on_own_leg
entries.description: Both of the character's hands rest on one of their own [legs](#legs), hugging or steadying it. Spread across both legs it becomes [hands_on_own_legs](#hands_on_own_legs).

entries.name: dress_in_mouth
entries.description: A hem or fold of a [dress](#dress) gripped between the [teeth](#teeth), keeping the [fabric](#fabric) clear and the hands free.

entries.name: adjusting_headphones
entries.description: One or both hands press against the earcups or the band to settle [headphones](#headphones) on the head. A stock [gesture](#gesture) for [listening](#listening) hard or shutting the world out.

entries.name: playing_with_hair
entries.description: A character fiddles with hair, their own or another's, to [no](#no) particular end: a [lock](#lock) twirled, flipped about, sniffed, or held under the [nose](#nose) like a moustache. When the handling has a clear [goal](#goal), such as [tying](#tying) or [drying](#drying), a matching [tag](#tag) exists instead.

entries.name: hands_on_eyewear
entries.description: Both hands at the frames of [glasses](#glasses) or [goggles](#goggles), settling them, [pushing](#pushing) them up or lifting them off. The dramatic [two-handed](#two-handed) adjustment belongs here.

entries.name: finger_touching
entries.description: Fingertips meet lightly: one character's index fingers poked together in shyness, or two people's hands just [brushing](#brushing). Small and tentative, never a grip.

entries.name: swimsuit_tug
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) being pinched and readjusted rather than pulled aside, with nothing exposed or removed. When it slips or bares something instead, use a lift or aside [tag](#tag).

entries.name: zipping
entries.description: The moment of [pulling](#pulling) a [zipper](#zipper) closed, shown with a hand gripping the tab partway up its track. The reverse motion to [unzipping](#unzipping), and used only for this closing direction.

entries.name: hands_on_own_feet
entries.description: Both hands [holding](#holding) the character's own [feet](#feet), as when [sitting](#sitting) cross-legged, [stretching](#stretching) or curled up tight. The [knees](#knees) are [folded](#folded) in to bring the feet within reach.

entries.name: holding_stomach
entries.description: Hands press against or wrap around the character's own middle. It reads as [pain](#pain), hunger, laughter or pregnancy depending on the face above it.

entries.name: hands_on_own_shoulders
entries.description: The arms [cross](#cross) upward so each hand lands on the opposite shoulder, the posture of hugging oneself. With only one hand use [hand_on_own_shoulder](#hand_on_own_shoulder).

entries.name: adjusting_bow
entries.description: Hands are busy straightening or retying a [fabric](#fabric) [bow](#bow), on the wearer's own outfit or on someone else's. The point is setting the bow right rather than merely touching it.

entries.name: grabbing_own_pectoral
entries.description: A character grips one of their own pectoral muscles, [squeezing](#squeezing) or lifting it to show off the bulk. The male answer to [grabbing_own_breast](#grabbing_own_breast).

entries.name: adjusting_collar
entries.description: Fingers work at a [collar](#collar), straightening the fold, turning it up or tightening a fastening. It covers a [shirt](#shirt) collar as [well](#well) as a band worn round the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: pinky_to_mouth
entries.description: A character holds a little finger at or against their own [lips](#lips), mouth open or closed and sometimes [licking](#licking) it. It reads as coy or thoughtful.

entries.name: nose_pinch
entries.description: Fingers squeeze a [nose](#nose) shut, whether the character's own or somebody else's. It is done against a bad [smell](#smell), to stop a [nosebleed](#nosebleed), or as [teasing](#teasing).

entries.name: rolling_sleeves_up
entries.description: Sleeves being [folded](#folded) [back](#back) toward the elbow to bare the [forearms](#forearms). The [gesture](#gesture) reads as getting down to work or squaring up for a fight.

entries.name: skirt_in_mouth
entries.description: A character holds the hem of their own [skirt](#skirt) between their [teeth](#teeth), keeping it raised and their [underwear](#underwear) on show. Hands are left free, which is often the excuse for the pose.

entries.name: fan_over_face
entries.description: A fan is raised so it screens part of the face, [hiding](#hiding) the mouth or everything below the eyes. It may be spread open or still [folded](#folded) shut.

entries.name: holding_feet
entries.description: Feet are gripped in the hands, whether a character folds up to take hold of their own or somebody else lifts them. Playful [poses](#poses) and foot-focused framing both use it.

entries.name: adjusting_bowtie
entries.description: A character tugs at or squares the [bowtie](#bowtie) at their throat, the stock [gesture](#gesture) of formal confidence or nerves. The hands work at the knot right under the [collar](#collar).

entries.name: face_in_hands
entries.description: Both hands come up over the face, [palms](#palms) against the eyes or cheeks. It reads as [despair](#despair), embarrassment or sheer exhaustion.

entries.name: hand_on_belt
entries.description: A hand [resting](#resting) on the [belt](#belt) at the waist, often with the thumb hooked behind it. The stance reads as relaxed but ready, and turns up on soldiers, [police](#police) and gunslingers.

entries.name: hands_on_stomach
entries.description: Both hands [resting](#resting) on the character's own abdomen, as after [eating](#eating) or over a pregnancy. A single hand there is [hand_on_own_stomach](#hand_on_own_stomach).

entries.name: hand_on_goggles
entries.description: Fingers on a pair of [goggles](#goggles) being worn, [pulling](#pulling) them down over the eyes or shoving them up onto the [forehead](#forehead). The goggles stay on the character throughout.

entries.name: finger_under_clothes
