entries.description: A finger hooked in beneath a [collar](#collar), waistband or hem, lifting the [cloth](#cloth) a little away from the skin. The garment stays on and nothing but the finger goes under.

entries.name: adjusting_mask
entries.description: Fingers reposition a [mask](#mask) on the face or head, whether a surgical mask, a [costume](#costume) piece or a visor. The mask is being worked rather than taken off entirely.

entries.name: three_monkeys
entries.description: The trio covering their eyes, ears and mouth in turn, illustrating the see-no-evil maxim. Drawn with actual monkeys or with characters posed in their places.

entries.name: pulling_own_ear
entries.description: A character takes hold of their own ear and gives it a [tug](#tug), often a sheepish, thoughtful, or [embarrassed](#embarrassed) [gesture](#gesture). On an animal-eared character the whole ear may fold right over.

entries.name: wiping_nose
entries.description: The [nose](#nose) is rubbed or dabbed at with a finger, sleeve, or [tissue](#tissue). Colds, [crying](#crying), and a cocky [gesture](#gesture) [can](#can) all prompt it.

entries.name: tying_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) being knotted, either by its own wearer or by somebody [standing](#standing) close. The second version reads as an intimate or [motherly](#motherly) [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: adjusting_shorts
entries.description: The wearer pulls at the waist or hem of their [shorts](#shorts) to make them sit better. Fingers [hook](#hook) into the [fabric](#fabric) rather than [pulling](#pulling) the garment off.

entries.name: fan_to_mouth
entries.description: A fan is held against or just before the [lips](#lips), a demure [gesture](#gesture) half-hiding a [smile](#smile) or a whisper. Narrower than screening the whole face with it.

entries.name: adjusting_strap
entries.description: Fingers [hook](#hook) under a [strap](#strap) to shift or straighten it, whether on a [bag](#bag), a garment or a piece of gear. The strap itself is what is being handled.

entries.name: twiddling_fingers
entries.description: Both index fingers pressed together and rolled against each other in front of the chest. A shorthand for shyness, hesitation or [working](#working) up the nerve to speak.

entries.name: looking_through_fingers
entries.description: A hand covers the eyes but the fingers are parted enough to peek between them. The classic half-hiding [gesture](#gesture) in a frightening or mortifying moment.

entries.name: adjusting_sleeves
entries.description: A character rolls, tugs or straightens the sleeves of what they have on. Frequently a getting-down-to-work or bracing-for-a-fight [gesture](#gesture).

entries.name: hand_on_knees
entries.description: A hand braced against the [knees](#knees), typically while bent forward to catch [breath](#breath) or to peer at something down low. The arm takes some of the body's [weight](#weight).

entries.name: finger_on_eyewear
entries.description: A single fingertip presses on the frame or [bridge](#bridge) of [glasses](#glasses) to settle them [back](#back) into place. Gripping the arms with two or more fingers calls for [hand_on_eyewear](#hand_on_eyewear) instead.

entries.name: adjusting_skirt
entries.description: Hands smooth or [tug](#tug) a [skirt](#skirt) into place, on the wearer or on someone else. It often covers the hem being pulled down to keep things decent.

entries.name: adjusting_hair_ornament
entries.description: A character reaches up to reseat a clip, [pin](#pin), [flower](#flower) or other ornament in their hair. The fingers are on the ornament itself rather than on the hair around it.

entries.name: hand_on_headset
entries.description: A hand held to a [headset](#headset) or [earpiece](#earpiece), the posture of somebody straining to hear or speaking into the boom [microphone](#microphone). Common on pilots, operators, gamers and idols on [stage](#stage).

entries.name: removing_bandaid
entries.description: A character peels an adhesive plaster off the skin, [pinching](#pinching) one [corner](#corner) and [pulling](#pulling). The [wince](#wince) that goes with it is half the point.

entries.name: adjusting_sock
entries.description: A sock or kneehigh is pulled [back](#back) up the leg, or straightened where it has slipped down. Usually drawn with the wearer stooping and one leg raised.

entries.name: sleeve_pull
entries.description: A hand tugging at the cuff or [opening](#opening) of a sleeve, often to draw it away from the arm and expose the armpit. Grabbing someone else's sleeve to get their attention is [sleeve_grab](#sleeve_grab) instead.

entries.name: rubbing_nose
entries.description: Running a finger under the [nose](#nose), a stock [gesture](#gesture) in anime and older films that reads as pride, bashful confidence or embarrassment, usually given to boys. Older characters tend to stroke their chin or [beard](#beard) instead.

entries.name: holding_ear
entries.description: Fingers take hold of an ear, the character's own or somebody else's. It covers a [scolding](#scolding) ear-pull as much as an idle [tug](#tug) at an [animal](#animal) ear.

entries.name: clutching_head
entries.description: Both hands grip the head hard enough to claw at it, usually with the body hunched over. It signals [despair](#despair), frustration or confusion; a hand simply [resting](#resting) on the head is not this.

entries.name: book_to_mouth
entries.description: A [book](#book) held up against the [lips](#lips) or the lower half of the face. It sits far too close to be read, so it is really [hiding](#hiding) a [smile](#smile) or a reaction.

entries.name: walking
entries.description: A character clearly in the act of walking, shown in a still image by one foot [stepping](#stepping) ahead of the other. Faster movement is [running](#running).

entries.name: wading
entries.description: A character [standing](#standing) or [walking](#walking) in [water](#water) that comes [no](#no) higher than the waist, such as a [stream](#stream), the sea's edge or a [pool](#pool). Deeper immersion is [partially_submerged](#partially_submerged) or [swimming](#swimming).

entries.name: flying
entries.description: Moving through the air under some form of propulsion, whether [wings](#wings), a [broom](#broom), a [machine](#machine), or being thrown or struck a distance. Hovering with nothing [driving](#driving) it is [floating](#floating) instead.

entries.name: running
entries.description: A character in full stride, both [feet](#feet) leaving the ground, [leaning](#leaning) forward with hair and loose clothing streaming [back](#back). Standing on one leg in place does not count as running.

entries.name: jumping
entries.description: A character has pushed off the ground and is in the air, [legs](#legs) bent or thrown out from the leap. Someone merely hovering with [no](#no) push behind it is [floating](#floating).

entries.name: stretching
entries.description: A character extending their arms, [legs](#legs) or whole body to loosen up, as before exercise or right after waking with a yawn. Not for merely raised arms without the stretching intent.

entries.name: falling
entries.description: A character or object drops through the air toward the ground. It covers a plunge from a [height](#height) and a tumble off a [ledge](#ledge); [hitting](#hitting) the ground and staying there is [fallen_down](#fallen_down).

entries.name: ass_shake
entries.description: A character shakes their own buttocks [back](#back) and forth, [twerking](#twerking). Most common in [animated](#animated) pictures, often with motion lines [carrying](#carrying) the movement.

entries.name: throwing
entries.description: A character [launching](#launching) an object by hand, such as a [ball](#ball), a [knife](#knife) or a [snowball](#snowball), [caught](#caught) at the moment of release. Add the object being thrown and [motion_lines](#motion_lines) as fitting.

entries.name: fleeing
entries.description: A character [running](#running) away from someone or something, generally in panic or to escape danger. A particular kind of running.

entries.name: spinning
entries.description: A person or object rotating continuously in place, whether spun like a top in three dimensions or simply turning within the flat plane of the picture. Motion lines or blur often mark the rotation.

entries.name: tripping
entries.description: A character stumbles and falls, or is about to, after [catching](#catching) a foot [mid-stride](#mid-stride). Distinct from [falling](#falling) from a [height](#height) and from being deliberately pushed over.

entries.name: fallen_down
entries.description: A character has lost their balance and hit the ground, shown either in the tumble or picking themselves up afterwards. Often a [comic](#comic) trip; [dropping](#dropping) through the air is [falling](#falling).

entries.name: dropping
entries.description: Something [slipping](#slipping) out of a hand and [falling](#falling), [caught](#caught) partway to the ground. The loss of grip is the point, so the object is usually still in the air.

entries.name: climbing
entries.description: Going up something using hands and [feet](#feet), be it a wall, a [rope](#rope), a [ladder](#ladder), a [tree](#tree) or a [rock](#rock) face. Simply [standing](#standing) somewhere high does not count.

entries.name: levitation
entries.description: A person or object is held up in the air by [magic](#magic) or [psychic](#psychic) force with nothing supporting them. Plain hovering is [floating](#floating); this says the lift is a deliberate power.

entries.name: swinging
entries.description: An ambiguous [tag](#tag) covering a body or object moving in an arc, a character [riding](#riding) a [playground](#playground) [swing](#swing), or a [couple](#couple) exchanging partners. Prefer a more specific tag where one applies.

entries.name: crawling
entries.description: A character moves forward on hands and [knees](#knees), or on all fours. The travelling is what counts; [holding](#holding) still in that position is [all_fours](#all_fours).

entries.name: walking_on_liquid
entries.description: Striding across the surface of [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid) without [sinking](#sinking) into it. Standing or trudging through the liquid instead is [wading](#wading).

entries.name: flapping
entries.description: Wings [beaten](#beaten) up and down to get airborne or to hold a hover. Arms swung the same way count; look for motion lines or blurred wingtips.

entries.name: flailing
entries.description: The arms are thrown about wildly, usually in panic or in a fit of temper. Motion lines and blurred limbs carry the [flapping](#flapping).

entries.name: sinking
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) or object going down into [water](#water), [mud](#mud) or quicksand, with clear signs of descending rather than rising. Also covers a [ship](#ship) going under as its crew abandons it.

entries.name: rolling
entries.description: A body turning over repeatedly as it moves across a surface, whether tumbling downhill, rolling across a [bed](#bed) or evading in combat. The motion is continuous rather than a single flip.

entries.name: walking_away
entries.description: The subject moves off with their [back](#back) to the viewer or to another character. A [staple](#staple) of partings and dramatic exits.

entries.name: sliding
entries.description: A character skidding across a surface, whether because the ground is slick or because it slopes away beneath them. The purpose-built [playground](#playground) ramp is tagged [slide](#slide) instead.

entries.name: faceplant
entries.description: A character meets the ground face first, [caught](#caught) mid-fall or already flat with the [legs](#legs) sprawled behind. Almost always played for laughs.

entries.name: turning_around
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) [caught](#caught) mid-rotation to face a new direction, usually shown across an animation or a short run of drawn frames. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [turnaround](#turnaround), which lays out one character from several fixed angles.

entries.name: landing
entries.description: A [flying](#flying) [figure](#figure) or an [aircraft](#aircraft) comes [back](#back) down and meets the ground under control. It is often [caught](#caught) at the moment of touchdown, with [dust](#dust) [kicking](#kicking) up or the [knees](#knees) braced.

entries.name: slipping
entries.description: A character losing their footing on a slick surface, arms [flailing](#flailing) and body tipping mid-fall. Ice, [wet](#wet) floors and [banana](#banana) peels supply most of the occasions.

entries.name: swaying
entries.description: The body rocking gently from side to side, usually a [happy](#happy), absent-minded motion. Motion lines or a blurred trailing edge often carry the movement.

entries.name: sneaking
entries.description: Moving quietly to avoid being noticed, typically drawn crouched low with careful, exaggerated steps. Often paired with a nearby character who has not spotted them.

entries.name: climbing_ladder
entries.description: A character moves up or down the rungs of a [ladder](#ladder), hands and [feet](#feet) on the steps. Often drawn from directly above or below for the [perspective](#perspective).

entries.name: cat_stretch
entries.description: The body drops onto all fours with the chest low, the rear lifted and the arms [reaching](#reaching) forward, the way a [cat](#cat) unfolds after a nap. It works for animals and for [people](#people) copying the shape.

entries.name: hopping
entries.description: A short bounding jump forward, the [feet](#feet) leaving the ground only briefly. Lighter and smaller in scale than a full jump.

entries.name: pouncing
entries.description: Launching forward through the air onto a [target](#target), arms or forepaws stretched out ahead. Cats, predators and overenthusiastic [friends](#friends) all do it.

entries.name: skipping
entries.description: Moving forward in light hops rather than an even [walking](#walking) stride. Almost always used to show a cheerful, [excited](#excited) mood.

entries.name: running_towards_viewer
entries.description: The subject runs straight at the [camera](#camera), so the body foreshortens and the arms [swing](#swing) toward the front of the frame. It creates a sense of immediacy or of being chased.

entries.name: backflip
entries.description: A jump that carries the body backwards, heels over head, before [landing](#landing) again. It is nearly always [caught](#caught) partway through the rotation.

entries.name: marching
entries.description: Walking with a measured deliberate step, usually in formation and in time with others. Arms [swing](#swing) together and the line keeps its shape.

entries.name: dashing
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) [breaking](#breaking) into a burst of speed, body pitched forward and [legs](#legs) [driving](#driving) hard, usually with speed lines or an [afterimage](#afterimage) trailing behind. Steady ordinary [running](#running) takes running instead.

entries.name: the_monkey
entries.description: A novelty dance from the early 1960s, arms pumping and [knees](#knees) bobbing in imitation of an [ape](#ape). Anime characters occasionally break into it as a [gag](#gag).

entries.name: somersault
entries.description: A full rotation of the body through the air or along the ground, [legs](#legs) [swinging](#swinging) over the head. Caught mid-turn, the [figure](#figure) usually appears upside down or curled tight.

entries.name: girly_running
entries.description: An exaggerated run with the arms flung out to the sides or trailing behind, elbows low and [forearms](#forearms) raised. Drawn for [comic](#comic) effect and usually on female characters.

entries.name: mid-stride
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) [caught](#caught) in the middle of a step, one foot lifted clear of the ground and the [weight](#weight) [carrying](#carrying) forward. Reads as [walking](#walking) [captured](#captured) mid-motion rather than a held pose.

entries.name: launching
entries.description: A character or vehicle begins a takeoff, leaving the ground for the air. It is the counterpart of [landing](#landing), which covers the return.

entries.name: climbing_tree
entries.description: Somebody hauls themselves up a trunk or edges along the branches of a [tree](#tree). Common in [summer](#summer) and childhood scenes, sometimes to reach [fruit](#fruit) or fetch something down.

entries.name: staff_riding
entries.description: Flying while seated or [standing](#standing) on a [staff](#staff), much like a [witch](#witch) [riding](#riding) a [broom](#broom). The rod is usually held between the [legs](#legs) or ridden [sidesaddle](#sidesaddle).

entries.name: running_on_liquid
entries.description: A character [racing](#racing) across the surface of [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid) without [sinking](#sinking), [throwing](#throwing) up spray at each step. It signals supernatural speed or ability.

entries.name: wiggling
entries.description: A part of the body moves [back](#back) and forth in small, rapid motions. A still picture shows it through motion lines, while an [animated](#animated) one plays the loop directly.

entries.name: rappelling
entries.description: A character descends a [cliff](#cliff), wall, or [building](#building) by [feeding](#feeding) a [rope](#rope) through a friction [device](#device) attached to a [harness](#harness). Used by climbers and [rescue](#rescue) teams where [climbing](#climbing) down directly would be too dangerous, and also called abseiling.

entries.name: shared_bathing
entries.description: Two or more [people](#people) [bathing](#bathing) or [showering](#showering) together, innocently or otherwise. Add [same-sex_bathing](#same-sex_bathing) or [mixed-sex_bathing](#mixed-sex_bathing) where it fits, and [nude](#nude) where appropriate.

entries.name: bathing
entries.description: Washing the body while partly [submerged](#submerged), in a tub, a [hot](#hot) spring or a [pool](#pool). A character [cleaning](#cleaning) themselves without [sitting](#sitting) in [water](#water) is [showering](#showering) or simply [wiping](#wiping) down instead.

entries.name: same-sex_bathing
entries.description: Two or more characters of the same [sex](#sex) [sharing](#sharing) a [bath](#bath), [hot](#hot) spring or shower. Tagged with [shared_bathing](#shared_bathing); mixed groups take [mixed-sex_bathing](#mixed-sex_bathing) instead.

entries.name: mixed-sex_bathing
entries.description: Characters of different sexes [sharing](#sharing) a [bath](#bath) or shower together, whether innocently or not, in a [bathtub](#bathtub), [onsen](#onsen) or shower. When [everyone](#everyone) [bathing](#bathing) is the same [sex](#sex), use [same-sex_bathing](#same-sex_bathing) instead.

entries.name: showering
entries.description: A character [washing](#washing) under [running](#running) [water](#water) from a shower head, or occasionally [caught](#caught) [standing](#standing) under a [heavy](#heavy) downpour of [rain](#rain). For the stall or room itself, use [shower_(place)](#shower_(place)) instead.

entries.name: hairdressing
entries.description: Someone is styling, [brushing](#brushing), [cutting](#cutting), braiding or [washing](#washing) hair, their own or another person's. Often seen with a [comb](#comb), hair brush, [scissors](#scissors) or hair dryer in hand.

entries.name: brushing_hair
entries.description: Someone runs a brush or [comb](#comb) through hair, their own or another's, often at a [mirror](#mirror) or [dressing](#dressing) [table](#table). Add whichever of [brushing_own_hair](#brushing_own_hair) and [brushing_another's_hair](#brushing_another's_hair) fits, and name the tool with hairbrush or comb.

entries.name: drying
entries.description: Getting the moisture off a person or an object, usually with a [towel](#towel) but also by [sun](#sun) or hair dryer. Hair in particular is [drying_hair](#drying_hair).

entries.name: brushing_teeth
entries.description: Teeth are being cleaned with a [toothbrush](#toothbrush), either by the character themselves or by another person. In the second case add [brushing_another's_teeth](#brushing_another's_teeth) as [well](#well).

entries.name: applying_makeup
entries.description: Cosmetics are being put on, either by the character on themselves or by one person on another. Add the cosmetic involved, and [mirror](#mirror) where one is used.

entries.name: brushing_another's_hair
entries.description: One character draws a brush or [comb](#comb) through somebody else's hair, as a parent, sibling or attendant would. Where a character grooms their own hair, [brushing_own_hair](#brushing_own_hair) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: drying_hair
entries.description: Wet hair being towelled or blown dry, typically just after a [bath](#bath) or a swim.

entries.name: washing
entries.description: A character scrubbing their body with [soap](#soap) or [water](#water) while [bathing](#bathing). Often shown with a washcloth, [sponge](#sponge) or shower; washing someone else may add the relevant interaction [tag](#tag).

entries.name: cutting_hair
entries.description: Somebody's hair is being shortened, whether by a barber, a friend or the character themselves, and by [scissors](#scissors), [clippers](#clippers) or a blade. Covers a calm salon scene as readily as hair shorn off mid-fight.

entries.name: braiding_hair
entries.description: Somebody is in the middle of plaiting hair, their own or another character's, with the [braid](#braid) only partly finished. The completed style itself is braid.

entries.name: after_bathing
entries.description: Someone who has just come out of a [bath](#bath), shower or [hot](#hot) spring, [drying](#drying) off with a [towel](#towel), wrapped in a [bathrobe](#bathrobe) or half dressed, hair still damp. The [washing](#washing) itself belongs to [bathing](#bathing) or [showering](#showering).

entries.name: washing_hair
entries.description: Hair being lathered with [shampoo](#shampoo), either by its owner or by someone else. Small children are often drawn in a brimmed shampoo [hat](#hat) while it happens.

entries.name: brushing_own_hair
entries.description: A character grooms their own hair with a brush or [comb](#comb) rather than somebody else's. Mirrors and [dressing](#dressing) tables usually come with the scene.

entries.name: toothbrush_in_mouth
entries.description: A [toothbrush](#toothbrush) held between the [lips](#lips) or worked across the [teeth](#teeth), usually with [foam](#foam) at the corners of the mouth. Typical of a [morning](#morning) routine scene.

entries.name: applying_manicure
entries.description: Fingernails are being groomed or painted, at home or in a salon [chair](#chair). It marks the treatment under way; nails already decorated belong with [nail_art](#nail_art).

entries.name: bubble_bath
entries.description: A [bathtub](#bathtub) heaped with [foam](#foam) from [soap](#soap) or a [bath](#bath) [bomb](#bomb). The lather covers the surface and generally hides whatever is beneath it.

entries.name: ear_cleaning
entries.description: One character cleans another's ear, usually with a slender [bamboo](#bamboo) [mimikaki](#mimikaki), while the other lies with their head in their [lap](#lap). The scene reads as quiet trust between the two.

entries.name: shaving
entries.description: Removing body or [facial](#facial) hair with a [razor](#razor), usually shown with [foam](#foam), a [mirror](#mirror) and a [bathroom](#bathroom) setting. Marks the act itself rather than the smooth result afterward.

entries.name: clothed_bath
entries.description: Somebody bathes or showers with their [clothes](#clothes) still on, the [fabric](#fabric) soaked and [clinging](#clinging). Wearing only a [swimsuit](#swimsuit), a [towel](#towel) or [underwear](#underwear) does not count.

entries.name: washing_another
entries.description: One character soaping or scrubbing another's hair or body, generally in a [bath](#bath) or shower and with plenty of lather. Both [people](#people) are usually undressed for it.

entries.name: applying_lipstick
entries.description: A character paints their [lips](#lips), usually with a [mirror](#mirror) to hand and the mouth held slightly open. The moment of putting the colour on is what is shown.

entries.name: applying_pedicure
entries.description: Toenails and [feet](#feet) are being groomed or painted, often with the foot propped up and the [toes](#toes) held apart. The hand equivalent is [applying_manicure](#applying_manicure).

entries.name: applying_sunscreen
entries.description: Lotion is rubbed into the skin against the [sun](#sun), over one's own arms or across somebody else's [back](#back). A fixture of [beach](#beach) and [poolside](#poolside) pictures.

entries.name: washing_back
entries.description: Scrubbing somebody else's [back](#back) for them, a courtesy in [bath](#bath) and [hot](#hot) spring scenes. The one [washing](#washing) usually kneels or sits behind.

entries.name: painting_fingernails
entries.description: Someone is in the middle of [brushing](#brushing) polish onto [fingernails](#fingernails), brush in hand and the [bottle](#bottle) close by. It may be their own hand or somebody else's.

entries.name: cutting_own_hair
entries.description: A character shortening their own hair, [scissors](#scissors) or blade in their own hand and nobody assisting. Usually staged as a moment of resolve rather than as ordinary grooming.

entries.name: foot_bath
entries.description: Feet soaked in a [basin](#basin) or a shallow public [pool](#pool) of [hot](#hot) [water](#water) while the rest of the body stays dressed. Hot-spring towns and quiet moments of rest use it.

entries.name: yuzu_bath
entries.description: A [hot](#hot) [bath](#bath) filled with whole yuzu [fruit](#fruit), a winter-solstice custom meant to warm the body and perfume the [water](#water) with citrus scent. The tub is typically [crowded](#crowded) with [floating](#floating) yellow fruit around the bather.

entries.name: brushing
entries.description: Somebody is [working](#working) a brush — through hair, over [teeth](#teeth), across a surface. It is broad enough that a more precise brushing [tag](#tag) usually serves better.

entries.name: hair_dye
entries.description: Hair whose colour has visibly been changed, or the dyeing itself in progress with bottles, brushes and foil. Roots showing in a different [shade](#shade) are the usual giveaway.

entries.name: washing_hands
entries.description: Hands being soaped and rinsed at a [sink](#sink) or [basin](#basin). A small everyday action that usually sets a quiet [bathroom](#bathroom) or [kitchen](#kitchen) moment.

entries.name: brushing_another's_teeth
entries.description: One character cleans somebody else's [teeth](#teeth) rather than their own, [toothbrush](#toothbrush) in hand while the other holds their mouth open. The one being brushed has to sit still for it.

entries.name: brushing_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) is being groomed with a brush, the character's own or a companion's. Done for somebody else it reads as an intimate favour.

entries.name: drying_body
entries.description: Wiping [water](#water) off the skin after a [bath](#bath), a swim or a soaking, with a [towel](#towel) or a hair dryer. The person is [drying](#drying) themselves rather than any [laundry](#laundry).

entries.name: shaving_another
entries.description: One character works a [razor](#razor) over someone else instead of themselves, often steadying a chin or cheek. Clipping [wool](#wool) from an [animal](#animal) is shearing, not this. Implies [shaving](#shaving).

entries.name: cleaning_eyewear
entries.description: A character wipes their [glasses](#glasses) or [goggles](#goggles), generally with a [cloth](#cloth) or a [shirt](#shirt) hem, lenses held up to the light. Often drawn with the eyes narrowed now that the lenses are off.

entries.name: painting_toenails
entries.description: Polish being brushed onto the [toenails](#toenails), usually with the foot drawn up close or [resting](#resting) on a knee. The pedicure counterpart of [painting_fingernails](#painting_fingernails).

entries.name: drum_bath
entries.description: Bathing in a [barrel](#barrel) or oil [drum](#drum) filled with [water](#water), sometimes with a [fire](#fire) lit underneath. Suggests [camping](#camping), [field](#field) conditions or having [no](#no) proper tub to hand.

entries.name: sleeping
entries.description: A character is asleep, eyes shut and body slack, sometimes with a [nose](#nose) [bubble](#bubble) in cartoon style. Not to be used for [fainting](#fainting).

entries.name: waking_up
entries.description: A character just waking, or awake but still drowsy: [rubbing](#rubbing) eyes, [sitting](#sitting) up in [bed](#bed), [yawning](#yawning). Add bed, [pajamas](#pajamas) or [messy_hair](#messy_hair) as they apply.

entries.name: sleeping_upright
entries.description: Asleep while [sitting](#sitting) or [standing](#standing), often propped against a wall or another person. Tag beside [sleeping](#sleeping).

entries.name: dreaming
entries.description: What a [sleeping](#sleeping) character sees, drawn into the picture as a [bubble](#bubble) or a scene [floating](#floating) above them. Somebody awake and merely picturing something is [imagining](#imagining) instead.

entries.name: nightmare
entries.description: A bad dream, shown either as the frightening scene itself or as the sleeper jolting awake from it. Sweat, wide eyes and twisted bedding mark the waking version.

entries.name: lifting_covers
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) or duvet is held up and drawn [back](#back), either to show what lies beneath or to climb into [bed](#bed).

entries.name: messy_sleeper
entries.description: Someone sprawled and tangled in sleep, limbs flung out, the covers kicked away and hair going every direction. The disorder of the [sleeping](#sleeping) [figure](#figure) is the point of the image.

entries.name: snoring
entries.description: The rasping [sound](#sound) a [sleeping](#sleeping) character makes when [breathing](#breathing) is obstructed, drawn as a [nose](#nose) [bubble](#bubble) or spelled out as a repeated sound effect. It signals unusually deep, undisturbed sleep rather than restlessness.

entries.name: sleeping_animal
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) shown asleep, curled up or sprawled out with its eyes closed. Reserve it for creatures; a [sleeping](#sleeping) person or humanoid takes the [plain](#plain) sleeping [tag](#tag).

entries.name: sleeping_on_desk
entries.description: A character asleep face down over a [desk](#desk), head [resting](#resting) on the surface or on [folded](#folded) arms. Classroom and [office](#office) scenes account for most of it, often with a [book](#book) or [paperwork](#paperwork) still spread out underneath.

entries.name: feigning_sleep
entries.description: A character only pretends to be asleep, eyes shut but plainly awake, often [peeking](#peeking) or [fighting](#fighting) down a [smile](#smile). The picture usually lets the viewer in on the pretence.

entries.name: sleep_talking
entries.description: A [sleeping](#sleeping) character mumbling words aloud, usually shown with a speech [bubble](#bubble) [drifting](#drifting) from their mouth. It commonly accompanies [dreaming](#dreaming), and the spoken line is often the joke of the picture.

entries.name: waking_another
entries.description: One character rousing another out of sleep by [shaking](#shaking), [calling](#calling) or barging in. It makes [no](#no) difference whether the wake-up is gentle or rude.

entries.name: sleeping_with_eyes_open
entries.description: A character who is clearly asleep yet whose eyes remain open, [giving](#giving) a blank or unfocused stare. The mismatch is usually played for comedy or for an unsettling effect.

entries.name: cooking
entries.description: A character preparing [food](#food): [chopping](#chopping), [stirring](#stirring) a pot, frying, plating up, generally in a [kitchen](#kitchen) and often in an [apron](#apron). Baking counts too, and somebody doing it professionally in uniform is also a [chef](#chef).

entries.name: cleaning
entries.description: Somebody is actually cleaning something: [sweeping](#sweeping), mopping, [wiping](#wiping), dusting, [washing](#washing) up or vacuuming. A [broom](#broom) or [bucket](#bucket) merely [standing](#standing) in the scene does not count.

entries.name: laundry
entries.description: Washed [clothes](#clothes) or linen hung out to dry, heaped in a [basket](#basket), or going into a [machine](#machine). Add [clothesline](#clothesline), [laundry_basket](#laundry_basket) or [laundry_pole](#laundry_pole) as the picture calls for.

entries.name: wringing_clothes
entries.description: A character twists [wet](#wet) clothing in their hands to squeeze the [water](#water) out, often after being soaked or while doing [laundry](#laundry). It relates closely to [wet_clothes](#wet_clothes) and to [drying](#drying) [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: sewing
entries.description: Cloth being joined with [needle](#needle) and [thread](#thread), by hand or by [machine](#machine), to make or mend [clothes](#clothes), dolls, and other soft goods. The whole activity counts, from pinning to the last stitch.

entries.name: cutting
entries.description: A blade parting something into portions: vegetables under a [knife](#knife), [rope](#rope), [paper](#paper), [cloth](#cloth). The act is under way rather than the finished pieces being shown.

entries.name: chocolate_making
entries.description: Somebody is preparing [chocolate](#chocolate) by hand, [whisking](#whisking) a [bowl](#bowl) of melted cocoa or [pouring](#pouring) it into moulds. Strongly tied to Valentine's scenes, and the cook usually ends up wearing some of it.

entries.name: baking
entries.description: Making [bread](#bread), [pastry](#pastry) or [sweets](#sweets): [mixing](#mixing) [dough](#dough), [rolling](#rolling) it out, filling tins and [sliding](#sliding) them into the [oven](#oven). It is close to [cooking](#cooking) but far less forgiving of a wrong measurement, and a whole [shop](#shop) given over to it is a [bakery](#bakery).

entries.name: grilling
entries.description: Cooking over a [hot](#hot) [grill](#grill), [meat](#meat) and vegetables laid on the [grate](#grate), usually with [tongs](#tongs), [smoke](#smoke) and rising [steam](#steam) nearby. Covers outdoor barbecues and indoor grill plates alike.

entries.name: wiping
entries.description: A damp or soiled surface is rubbed by hand to clean or dry it, usually with an absorbent [cloth](#cloth) or [tissue](#tissue). Tables, windows, [dishes](#dishes), and skin [can](#can) all be the surface in question.

entries.name: peeling
entries.description: Stripping the skin from [fruit](#fruit) or vegetables with a [knife](#knife) or peeler, in one long [ribbon](#ribbon) or in pieces. It also covers slowly drawing clothing or [pasties](#pasties) away from the skin they cling to.

entries.name: knitting
entries.description: Yarn is worked into [cloth](#cloth) by looping it row after row on a pair of straight needles. The two needles are the giveaway; a single hooked tool means crochet.

entries.name: sweeping
entries.description: Pushing [dust](#dust) and litter along the ground with a [broom](#broom) in a back-and-forth motion, often in a [doorway](#doorway), courtyard or [shrine](#shrine) precinct. The broom must actually be in use, not simply held.

entries.name: watering
entries.description: Sprinkling [water](#water) over plants, usually from a watering [can](#can), and occasionally over a person as a joke. Gardens, [window](#window) boxes and [school](#school) [flower](#flower) beds are the common settings.

entries.name: mochitsuki
entries.description: Steamed [rice](#rice) being pounded into [mochi](#mochi) with a long wooden [mallet](#mallet) in a [heavy](#heavy) tub. A New Year custom, normally drawn as two [people](#people) [working](#working) in rhythm, one striking while the other turns the [dough](#dough).

entries.name: gardening
entries.description: Tending plants: sowing [seed](#seed), [watering](#watering), weeding, pruning or picking from beds and pots. The work itself is what counts, not merely greenery being present.

entries.name: opening
entries.description: A sealed thing is being got into: a [can](#can) pulled, a box's flaps lifted, [wrapping](#wrapping) [torn](#torn) from a [gift](#gift), with the contents about to appear. The act is the point, not the finished open [container](#container).

entries.name: flipping_food
entries.description: Food turned over as it cooks, tossed out of a pan with a snap of the wrist or lifted on a [spatula](#spatula). Pancakes, eggs, [meat](#meat) and stir-fry are the usual candidates, and a botched toss is a [standing](#standing) [gag](#gag).

entries.name: drying_clothes
entries.description: Wet [laundry](#laundry) being dried, pegged out on a line or [pole](#pole) or turning in a [machine](#machine). Also fits somebody [drying](#drying) [clothes](#clothes) still on their body; [squeezing](#squeezing) the [water](#water) out is [wringing_clothes](#wringing_clothes).

entries.name: dishwashing
entries.description: Scrubbing plates and pans at the [sink](#sink), suds up the arms and a [sponge](#sponge) in hand. The chore that comes after a [meal](#meal).

entries.name: chopping
entries.description: Cutting something into pieces with a [knife](#knife), [cleaver](#cleaver) or [axe](#axe), most often vegetables on a board or [firewood](#firewood) on a block. Not the martial arts hand strike, which is [chop](#chop).

entries.name: roasting
entries.description: Cooking [food](#food) slowly in surrounding heat until it tenderises, over an open [fire](#fire) or in an [oven](#oven). Has nothing to do with the sexual position of a similar-sounding name.

entries.name: boiling
entries.description: Liquid heated until it churns and turns to vapour, with bubbles [breaking](#breaking) the surface and [steam](#steam) rising above it. Usually a pot on a [stove](#stove) or a [cauldron](#cauldron) over a [fire](#fire).

entries.name: mixing
entries.description: Stirring or folding ingredients together, typically over a [bowl](#bowl) with a [whisk](#whisk), [spoon](#spoon) or beater. Belongs to [cooking](#cooking) and [baking](#baking) scenes.

entries.name: stitching
entries.description: The passage of a threaded [needle](#needle) in and out of material, whether closing a seam or a wound. The individual [stitches](#stitches) themselves are what is shown.

entries.name: cleaning_windows
entries.description: Somebody wipes down a pane of [glass](#glass) with a [cloth](#cloth), squeegee or spray [bottle](#bottle). Familiar from [classroom](#classroom) [cleaning](#cleaning) duty and from housework scenes.

entries.name: decorating
entries.description: Somebody is putting [decorations](#decorations) up: [hanging](#hanging) baubles on a [tree](#tree), taping [streamers](#streamers) along a wall, [icing](#icing) a [cake](#cake). The act is under way rather than the finished room being shown.

entries.name: wringing
entries.description: Wet [cloth](#cloth) is twisted between both hands to force the [water](#water) out of it. Laundry, [rain](#rain), and scenes right after [swimming](#swimming) all bring it up.

entries.name: whisking
entries.description: A character beats ingredients together in a [mixing](#mixing) [bowl](#bowl) with a [wire](#wire) [whisk](#whisk), [caught](#caught) mid-motion. Belongs to [cooking](#cooking) and [baking](#baking) scenes, distinct from striking someone with a [whip](#whip).

entries.name: reading
entries.description: A character reads a [book](#book), [scroll](#scroll), [newspaper](#newspaper), or other printed text. Combine with book, [holding_book](#holding_book), or the specific material; reading from a [phone](#phone) or [screen](#screen) is usually a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: writing
entries.description: A character is [caught](#caught) in the act of writing on [paper](#paper), a board or another surface. Add [pen](#pen), [pencil](#pencil) or [notebook](#notebook) for the tool in use and paper or the relevant text tags for what is being written.

entries.name: painting_(action)
entries.description: A character is busy painting, brush or roller in hand, [working](#working) on a canvas, a wall or a [model](#model). A finished canvas [hanging](#hanging) in the scene is [painting_(object)](#painting_(object)).

entries.name: math
entries.description: Numbers, equations or formulas as the subject of the picture, chalked on a board, scrawled on [paper](#paper), or [drifting](#drifting) around a character puzzling over them.

entries.name: calligraphy
entries.description: Brushed [writing](#writing) treated as an art, either shown finished on [paper](#paper) or being written by a character at work. Japanese shodou with brush, [ink](#ink) and stone is the usual form.

entries.name: at_computer
entries.description: Someone sits at a desktop [machine](#machine) with the [screen](#screen) and keyboard in front of them, either [working](#working) away or simply settled there ready to. The position counts as much as any actual [typing](#typing).

entries.name: drawing_(action)
entries.description: Somebody in the picture is drawing, [pencil](#pencil), brush or [stylus](#stylus) in hand, [working](#working) on [paper](#paper) or a [screen](#screen). A finished drawing merely [sitting](#sitting) in the scene is [drawing_(object)](#drawing_(object)).

entries.name: studying
entries.description: Working through textbooks, [notes](#notes) or research to learn something, usually at a [desk](#desk) covered in [papers](#papers) with a [pen](#pen) in hand.

entries.name: typing
entries.description: Fingers work a keyboard to enter text, whether on a [computer](#computer), a [phone](#phone) or a [typewriter](#typewriter). Office desks, late-night [writing](#writing) and messaging scenes are the usual settings.

entries.name: chemistry
entries.description: The picture is about doing chemistry: an experiment under way, a reaction, formulae on a board, glassware in use. A [bottle](#bottle) of something merely [standing](#standing) in frame is not enough.

entries.name: turning_page
entries.description: A hand lifts the [corner](#corner) of a page mid-flip to move on to the next one, in a [book](#book), magazine or [sheaf](#sheaf) of [paper](#paper). The half-raised [leaf](#leaf) is what marks the moment.

entries.name: kakizome
entries.description: The first [calligraphy](#calligraphy) of the year, brushed on [paper](#paper) during the [opening](#opening) days of January. It is drawn with an inkstone, a thick brush and a written resolution or lucky word.

entries.name: sand_writing
entries.description: Letters or pictures traced into [sand](#sand) with a fingertip, a [stick](#stick) or a toe, usually on a [beach](#beach). Often a [confession](#confession) or a name that the tide will take.

entries.name: sketching
entries.description: A character shown drawing from something in front of them, [pencil](#pencil) or pad in hand. Not the same as [sketch](#sketch), which describes the finish of the picture itself rather than an action inside it.

entries.name: drawing_on_fourth_wall
entries.description: A character draws, paints or writes on the [invisible](#invisible) surface between the scene and whoever is looking, treating the picture plane as a pane of [glass](#glass). Lettering handled this way normally comes out reversed.

entries.name: finger_writing
entries.description: Letters or [shapes](#shapes) traced with a fingertip on a fogged [window](#window), in [sand](#sand), on skin or in the air. No [pen](#pen) or brush is involved.

entries.name: hacking
entries.description: Breaking into a [computer](#computer), [phone](#phone) or [machine](#machine) without permission, normally drawn as somebody hunched over a keyboard with code streaming down the [screen](#screen). Also covers tampering directly with an [android](#android) or cybernetic body.

entries.name: shopping
entries.description: Browsing and buying goods in a store or [market](#market), grocery shopping being the most commonly depicted form. Tag with [shopping_bag](#shopping_bag), [shopping_cart](#shopping_cart) or a [basket](#basket) where visible.

entries.name: measuring
entries.description: Someone [working](#working) out a size or amount with a [tape](#tape), [ruler](#ruler), scale or calipers. A common [gag](#gag) has one character checking another's bust, waist and hip [measurements](#measurements).

entries.name: groceries
entries.description: Food just bought and carried home, whether in a [paper](#paper) [sack](#sack) with greens or a [baguette](#baguette) [poking](#poking) out, or plastic bags [hanging](#hanging) from both hands. The load being carried is what makes the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: trying_on_clothes
entries.description: Someone [slipping](#slipping) into an outfit to see how it looks on them, typically in front of a [mirror](#mirror). Fitting rooms and [shop](#shop) floors are the usual setting, though a [bedroom](#bedroom) works just as [well](#well).

entries.name: taking_shelter
entries.description: Ducking under something to escape [rain](#rain) or [snow](#snow) — a [tree](#tree), an [awning](#awning), a [bridge](#bridge), a [bus](#bus) stop. About weather rather than danger, which is what taking [cover](#cover) is for.

entries.name: pet_walking
entries.description: Leading an [animal](#animal) along on a [leash](#leash) clipped to its [collar](#collar), most often a [dog](#dog). It covers the walker and the animal together, not a leash worn for other reasons.

entries.name: searching
entries.description: Looking about for something or someone, whether peering under furniture, rummaging through a [bag](#bag), or scanning a [crowd](#crowd) with a hand shading the eyes.

entries.name: queue
entries.description: People stand in a single-file line [waiting](#waiting) their turn for a service or to move ahead. Different from a [lineup](#lineup), where figures are simply arranged side by side for [display](#display).

entries.name: washing_vehicle
entries.description: Scrubbing a [car](#car), [truck](#truck) or other vehicle by hand with [sponge](#sponge), [bucket](#bucket) and [hose](#hose). Charity washes, sometimes staffed in swimwear, are a common excuse for the scene.

entries.name: buying_condoms
entries.description: Somebody at a [shop](#shop) [counter](#counter) or vending [machine](#machine) purchasing condoms, generally played for embarrassment. The scene stops at the transaction itself.

entries.name: pizza_delivery
entries.description: A [pizza](#pizza) being carried to someone's home, [box](#box) in hand at the [door](#door). The handover on the doorstep, often with a uniformed courier, is the usual framing.

entries.name: sale
entries.description: Goods offered at cut prices, shown through banners, slashed [price](#price) tags and picked-over shelves. Often the setting for [shopping](#shopping) and bargain-hunting scenes.

entries.name: walking_bike
entries.description: Pushing a [bicycle](#bicycle) or motorbike along by its handlebars instead of [riding](#riding) it. Common for two [people](#people) [talking](#talking) side by side, or for a [machine](#machine) that has [broken](#broken) down.

entries.name: pressing_button
entries.description: A finger comes down on a button, whether a lift panel, a console, a [doorbell](#doorbell) or a big red [switch](#switch). The moment of contact is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: eating
entries.description: Somebody consuming [food](#food), mid-bite, about to start or just finishing. Meals, snacks and [sweets](#sweets) all count; name whatever is being eaten alongside it.

entries.name: food_in_mouth
entries.description: Food sits inside the mouth or rests on the [tongue](#tongue), whether steadied by a hand or not. Add [mouth_hold](#mouth_hold) when [teeth](#teeth) or [lips](#lips) carry it with [no](#no) hand supporting it.

entries.name: drinking
entries.description: Somebody [swallowing](#swallowing) a [liquid](#liquid), sipping from a [cup](#cup), [bottle](#bottle), [can](#can) or straw. Covers any drinkable liquid, [hot](#hot) or [cold](#cold), alcoholic or not.

entries.name: feeding
entries.description: One character puts or offers [food](#food) into another person's or an animal's mouth. It generally reads as care or affection between the two.

entries.name: pouring
entries.description: A character tips a [container](#container) to let [liquid](#liquid) flow out, into a [cup](#cup), over [food](#food) or onto the ground. Pouring onto one's own body is [pouring_onto_self](#pouring_onto_self).

entries.name: incoming_food
entries.description: A character holds [food](#food) out toward the viewer, offering it or [feeding](#feeding) them directly. The reverse, where the viewer does the feeding, is [fed_by_viewer](#fed_by_viewer).

entries.name: shared_food
entries.description: Two characters [holding](#holding) one item of [food](#food) in their mouths at the same time, classically a [pocky](#pocky) [stick](#stick), hinting at an indirect [kiss](#kiss). Feeding one another mouth to mouth falls here too.

entries.name: chewing
entries.description: A character visibly works [food](#food) between the [teeth](#teeth), cheeks full or [jaw](#jaw) moving, already mid-mouthful rather than about to bite. Pair it with [eating](#eating) and with whatever is being eaten.

entries.name: glutton
entries.description: Somebody [eating](#eating) far more than is normal, or fixated on [food](#food), shown mid-stuffing or ringed by empty plates. Body type does not matter; the excess itself is the point.

entries.name: swallowing
entries.description: The moment of gulping something down, shown by a throat [bulge](#bulge), a gulp [sound](#sound) effect or context. Used for [food](#food) and [drink](#drink) as [well](#well) as for [vore](#vore) scenes.

entries.name: spit_take
entries.description: A character sprays out whatever they were [eating](#eating) or [drinking](#drinking), usually as a startled reaction to something just said or seen. A [staple](#staple) comedic beat.

entries.name: sharing_food
entries.description: Food passes between characters: a bite held out on a [fork](#fork), a [snack](#snack) [broken](#broken) in half, one [plate](#plate) eaten from together. Usually a [sign](#sign) of closeness.

entries.name: full_mouth
entries.description: Cheeks bulging around a mouthful of [food](#food) still being chewed. Narrower than [eating](#eating), which covers the whole business from lifting the food to [swallowing](#swallowing) it.

entries.name: stirring
entries.description: Turning a [spoon](#spoon), [stick](#stick) or straw through a [liquid](#liquid) to mix it or even out its heat. Applies to pots on the [stove](#stove), teacups and mixed drinks alike.

entries.name: incoming_drink
entries.description: A character holds a [drink](#drink) out to the viewer, or pours into a [cup](#cup) the viewer is understood to be [holding](#holding). The offer is aimed out of the frame rather than at another character.

entries.name: tasting
entries.description: A character samples a small portion of [food](#food) or [drink](#drink) to [judge](#judge) its flavour, often with a [spoon](#spoon) halfway to the mouth or a fingertip dipped in a pot. It commonly happens mid-cooking, and the resulting face shows the verdict.

entries.name: force-feeding
entries.description: Food pushed into somebody against their will, often with the [jaw](#jaw) held open and clear [distress](#distress) on their face. Sometimes the point is that far more is going in than could ever be swallowed.

entries.name: imminent_bite
entries.description: Jaws open and closing on their [target](#target), a moment before the [teeth](#teeth) reach it. What is about to be bitten may be [food](#food) or another character.

entries.name: slurping
entries.description: Noisily drawing [food](#food) or [liquid](#liquid) into the mouth along with air, drawn with a trailing noodle or straw and often an onomatopoeia. Ramen and [soup](#soup) scenes account for most of it.

entries.name: eating_hair
entries.description: Hair being chewed on, the character's own or somebody else's. Different from [biting](#biting) a [lock](#lock) and simply [holding](#holding) it there.

entries.name: dinner
entries.description: The [evening](#evening) [meal](#meal), generally the largest of the [day](#day) and often eaten together with [family](#family). Its late hour and its size set it apart from [breakfast](#breakfast) or lunch.

entries.name: serving
entries.description: Food or [drink](#drink) is being carried over and set down for somebody, as a [waiter](#waiter), [maid](#maid), or host would. The [presenting](#presenting) is the action; [eating](#eating) it is a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: shared_drink
entries.description: Two characters [drink](#drink) from one [cup](#cup), [bottle](#bottle), or straw, either passing it [back](#back) and forth or [leaning](#leaning) in together over it.

entries.name: meal
entries.description: A full [sitting](#sitting) of [food](#food) rather than a light [snack](#snack): [breakfast](#breakfast), lunch or [dinner](#dinner), a spread of [dishes](#dishes), or a packed lunch [box](#box) laid out ready to eat.

entries.name: giving_food
entries.description: Handing or [holding](#holding) out something edible to another person. Where a closer [tag](#tag) fits, prefer it: [feeding](#feeding) for putting [food](#food) into someone's mouth, [sharing_food](#sharing_food), or [incoming_food](#incoming_food) for a bite pushed towards the viewer.

entries.name: eating_flower
entries.description: A character [eating](#eating) a blossom, [petals](#petals) and all. Usually played straight as an odd but sincere diet rather than as a [gag](#gag).

entries.name: drinking_blood
entries.description: Blood being [drunk](#drunk), either straight from a bite at the throat or poured out into a [glass](#glass). The mark of vampires and other predatory beings.

entries.name: blowing_on_food
entries.description: Breath aimed at a spoonful or a dish to cool it before [eating](#eating), and equally at a [drink](#drink) that is too [hot](#hot). Steam rising from whatever is held is a common companion.

entries.name: blood_sucking
entries.description: One character [drinking](#drinking) [blood](#blood) straight from another, normally with [fangs](#fangs) set at the [neck](#neck). Vampires and similar beings account for nearly all of it.

entries.name: burger_malfunction
entries.description: The filling of a [burger](#burger) slides out of the bun as somebody bites into it. Usually a joke at the expense of a burger stacked far too high.

entries.name: fed_by_viewer
entries.description: A hand entering from the viewer's side offers [food](#food) to the character, who leans in or opens their mouth for it. The [camera](#camera) stands in for whoever is doing the [feeding](#feeding).

entries.name: playing_games
entries.description: A character [playing](#playing) a game of any kind: [video](#video) games, board games, [dice](#dice), cards, or [carnival](#carnival) and hand games. Organised sports are excluded and take [playing_sports](#playing_sports) instead.

entries.name: swimming
entries.description: A character moving through [water](#water) by stroking with the arms and [kicking](#kicking) with the [legs](#legs), in a [pool](#pool), the sea or a [lake](#lake).

entries.name: exercising
entries.description: Moving the body to keep fit: press-ups, stretches, lifting [weights](#weights), [jogging](#jogging). Often set in a [gym](#gym), with a [dumbbell](#dumbbell) or on a [mat](#mat). Also called [working](#working) out.

entries.name: wrestling
entries.description: One or more characters are shown grappling in a match, or clearly about to be, whatever the style: professional, Olympic, or [street](#street). Individual holds and throws keep their own tags, while the venue is [wrestling_ring](#wrestling_ring) and the gear [wrestling_outfit](#wrestling_outfit).

entries.name: volleyball
entries.description: The sport being played: two teams [knocking](#knocking) a [ball](#ball) over a [net](#net) on a court, [sand](#sand) or [grass](#grass), including two-a-side [beach](#beach) volleyball. The ball itself is [volleyball_(object)](#volleyball_(object)).

entries.name: basketball
entries.description: The team game in play: dribbling, passing and putting the [ball](#ball) through a raised [hoop](#hoop) on a marked court. The ball on its own is [basketball_(object)](#basketball_(object)) and the kit is [basketball_uniform](#basketball_uniform).

entries.name: baseball
entries.description: The bat-and-ball game in play: [pitching](#pitching), batting, fielding, runners rounding the diamond. The [ball](#ball) itself is [baseball_(object)](#baseball_(object)), and the gear has its own tags such as [baseball_bat](#baseball_bat), [baseball_mitt](#baseball_mitt) and [baseball_uniform](#baseball_uniform).

entries.name: basketball_(sport)
entries.description: The game under way: players [driving](#driving), passing and shooting at the [hoop](#hoop). It wants actual play rather than a [ball](#ball) simply [lying](#lying) about somewhere.

entries.name: playing_sports
entries.description: Someone actively engaged in a sport, from [soccer](#soccer) and [tennis](#tennis) to a [swimming](#swimming) race. Add the sport's own [tag](#tag); non-athletic games take [playing_games](#playing_games) instead.

entries.name: mahjong
entries.description: Four players around a [table](#table) [building](#building) hands from [tiles](#tiles), the East Asian [gambling](#gambling) game. The tiles themselves are [mahjong_tile](#mahjong_tile) and the felted table is [mahjong_table](#mahjong_table).

entries.name: volleyball_(sport)
entries.description: Playing [volleyball](#volleyball): [serving](#serving), setting, [digging](#digging) or spiking the [ball](#ball) over a [net](#net). Indoor court and [beach](#beach) versions both belong here.

entries.name: freediving
entries.description: Swimming or [diving](#diving) beneath the surface with [no](#no) [breathing](#breathing) apparatus, whether for pleasure or as the competitive sport. Held [breath](#breath) and an absence of tanks are the tell.

entries.name: soccer
entries.description: Association football being played on a marked pitch, two teams [driving](#driving) a [soccer_ball](#soccer_ball) toward opposing goals. Known simply as football almost everywhere outside a handful of countries.

entries.name: archery
entries.description: Someone actually shooting a [bow](#bow), whether nocking, drawing, [aiming](#aiming) or loosing, in a fight or as a sport such as kyudo. Merely [carrying](#carrying) a bow is not enough.

entries.name: boxing
entries.description: Two fighters trade punches in a [ring](#ring), gloved up, [working](#working) towards a knockout or a decision. Only fists are allowed, so any picture with a kick in it belongs under kickboxing.

entries.name: weightlifting
entries.description: Lifting dumbbells, barbells or other [weights](#weights) as exercise, usually in a [gym](#gym). Specific lifts such as bench_press, deadlift or squat [can](#can) be added alongside.

entries.name: hanetsuki
entries.description: A traditional Japanese New Year game resembling [badminton](#badminton), played with a feathered [shuttlecock](#shuttlecock) and flat wooden paddles. A player who fails to return it gets [ink](#ink) daubed on their face, which is half the fun of drawing it.

entries.name: track_and_field
entries.description: Athletics events such as sprinting, hurdles, long jump, [pole](#pole) vault or shot put, shown in [competition](#competition) or practice. Add [running](#running) and [track_uniform](#track_uniform) for the specific action and outfit.

entries.name: gymnastics
entries.description: Someone performing gymnastics, such as [floor](#floor) routines, balance beam, vaults, splits or rhythmic gymnastics with a [ribbon](#ribbon) or [hoop](#hoop). Often shown in a [leotard](#leotard).

entries.name: surfing
entries.description: Riding a board across a moving wave or over open [water](#water). The board underfoot and the water's surface both need to be part of the picture; simply [carrying](#carrying) a board is not enough.

entries.name: martial_arts
entries.description: Unarmed [fighting](#fighting) technique of [no](#no) clearly named [school](#school), shown as stances, strikes, blocks or throws. Where the discipline [can](#can) actually be told apart, reach for its own [tag](#tag) rather than this catch-all.

entries.name: chess
entries.description: The two-player board game on sixty-four squares, each side moving pieces of differing powers to trap the enemy [king](#king). Games under way, single moves and finished mates all fit.

entries.name: diving
entries.description: Going [underwater](#underwater) deliberately, either with tanks and a regulator or on a single held [breath](#breath). Not the same as plunging headfirst into [water](#water) from above.

entries.name: tennis
entries.description: The [racket](#racket) sport played over a [net](#net) in singles or doubles, players [serving](#serving) and rallying a felt-covered [ball](#ball). Covers the play itself, from a serve toss to a baseline return.

entries.name: kyuudou
entries.description: Japanese [archery](#archery) practised as a formal art, drawing an asymmetric [bow](#bow) gripped [well](#well) below its midpoint that rises far above the archer's head. Hakama are standard, and women often wear a chest [guard](#guard) against the [string](#string).

entries.name: beach_volleyball
entries.description: Volleyball played on [sand](#sand) with a [net](#net) strung between two poles, usually two to a side. Players wear swimwear rather than sports kit, which is a fair part of the appeal in art.

entries.name: skating
entries.description: Gliding along on [skates](#skates), either blades on [ice](#ice) or wheels on [pavement](#pavement). Covers [casual](#casual) rinks and rollerskating as [well](#well) as [figure](#figure) skating routines.

entries.name: yoga
entries.description: Holding a yoga posture: [stretching](#stretching), [balancing](#balancing) or twisting the body, usually on a [mat](#mat). Frequently used to show off a character's suppleness.

entries.name: training
entries.description: A character practising to improve at something, drilling a technique, [working](#working) a routine or [running](#running) through exercises. The effort reads as rehearsal or preparation rather than a real contest.

entries.name: fighting_game
entries.description: The picture borrows the furniture of a versus [fighting](#fighting) game: health [bars](#bars), a round [counter](#counter), a character select [grid](#grid) or a versus [screen](#screen). Simply drawing a character from such a game is not enough.

entries.name: shogi
entries.description: Japanese [chess](#chess), played on a nine-by-nine board with flat, wedge-shaped pieces that all share one colour and point toward the enemy side. A [captured](#captured) piece [can](#can) be dropped [back](#back) into play by its captor. Implies [board_game](#board_game).

entries.name: suikawari
entries.description: The Japanese [beach](#beach) game of splitting a [watermelon](#watermelon): a blindfolded player is spun around and swings a [stick](#stick) at the [fruit](#fruit) on the ground, with [everyone](#everyone) [sharing](#sharing) the pieces afterward. It plays much like a pinata [party](#party) and is strongly tied to [summer](#summer) scenes.

entries.name: cat's_cradle
entries.description: Two or more players pass a closed loop of [string](#string) between their fingers, [building](#building) woven figures as it changes hands. A quiet indoor game, usually a pair [sitting](#sitting) face to face.

entries.name: rhythmic_gymnastics
entries.description: Floor [gymnastics](#gymnastics) performed with a handheld apparatus such as a [ribbon](#ribbon), [hoop](#hoop), [ball](#ball), [rope](#rope) or clubs, danced to [music](#music). Expect a [leotard](#leotard) and a long ribbon trail [sweeping](#sweeping) through the air.

entries.name: racing
entries.description: Characters compete to be first over a finish line, whether on foot, on horseback, or behind the [wheel](#wheel). The point of the [tag](#tag) is the contest itself, so use it whenever someone is clearly striving to outpace a rival.

entries.name: skateboarding
entries.description: Riding a [skateboard](#skateboard), whether cruising along or mid-trick in the air. Ramps, rails and [street](#street) furniture are the usual surroundings.

entries.name: rock_paper_scissors
entries.description: The hand game where two players throw one of three [shapes](#shapes) at once, [rock](#rock) beating [scissors](#scissors), scissors beating [paper](#paper) and paper beating rock. Known in Japan as janken and used to settle small disputes.

entries.name: kung_fu
entries.description: Chinese martial arts being performed: stances, forms and strikes. Apply it only while somebody is actually [carrying](#carrying) out a technique, not merely because a practitioner is in the picture.

entries.name: poker
entries.description: The betting [card](#card) game in play: hands held close to the chest, chips pushed into the middle, faces carefully blank. The [table](#table) and cards involved are tagged separately when shown.

entries.name: push-ups
entries.description: Face-down exercise in which the body is raised and lowered on the arms while held straight. Training and [gym](#gym) scenes are where it turns up.

entries.name: ice_skating
entries.description: Gliding over [ice](#ice) on bladed [boots](#boots), whether fooling about on a [frozen](#frozen) [pond](#pond) or competing in earnest. The blades underfoot are what separate it from roller [skating](#skating).

entries.name: pitching
entries.description: A [baseball](#baseball) pitcher [caught](#caught) mid-windup or at the release, [throwing](#throwing) toward the [batter](#batter) from the mound. The throwing motion itself is the point of the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: figure_skating
entries.description: Choreographed [skating](#skating) on [ice](#ice) with spins, jumps and long glides. The rink, the bladed [boots](#boots) and the extended line of the body identify it.

entries.name: table_tennis
entries.description: The indoor bat-and-ball game played across a low [net](#net) on a [table](#table), in singles or doubles. A frequent fixture of Japanese inn and hot-spring scenes.

entries.name: sumo
entries.description: Japanese [wrestling](#wrestling) in which each fighter tries to push the other out of the [ring](#ring) or down onto the [clay](#clay). Wrestlers are drawn [heavy](#heavy) but solidly muscled, wearing a mawashi [belt](#belt) and a [topknot](#topknot); the [tag](#tag) also covers a character simply striking the stance or wearing the attire.

entries.name: assisted_stretching
entries.description: One person pushes or holds another through a stretch, adding force the person [stretching](#stretching) could not reach alone. Common in [gym](#gym), dance and [training](#training) scenes.

entries.name: billiards
entries.description: Cue sports played on a pocketed [table](#table), covering [pool](#pool), snooker and their relatives. Usually drawn as a player bent over the felt lining up a shot.

entries.name: gacha_(game_mechanic)
entries.description: The randomised pull system of [mobile](#mobile) games, drawn as a [banner](#banner) [screen](#screen), a [spinning](#spinning) summon animation or a player reacting to the result. Physical capsule vending machines are [gashapon](#gashapon), a separate matter.

entries.name: sit-up
entries.description: An abdominal exercise in which someone lies on their [back](#back) and lifts the [torso](#torso) up to [sitting](#sitting), then lowers it again with the [legs](#legs) staying in place. Usually drawn with the [knees](#knees) bent and the hands behind the head.

entries.name: competition
entries.description: Two or more sides set out to outdo each other, usually as an organised event such as a match or a contest. The [rivalry](#rivalry) itself is what the [tag](#tag) records, not the particular sport.

entries.name: goldfish_scooping
entries.description: The [festival](#festival) stall game of lifting [goldfish](#goldfish) out of a shallow [tank](#tank) with a fragile [paper](#paper) scoop before it [tears](#tears). Winners carry the catch home in a water-filled [bag](#bag).

entries.name: karate
entries.description: The striking art of punches, kicks, knee and elbow blows and open-hand strikes, shown in sparring or in [solo](#solo) forms. Characters appear mid-strike, held in a stance, or [working](#working) through a set sequence.

entries.name: card_game
entries.description: A game whose main pieces are cards, from an ordinary deck to a fixed set like UNO or a trading game with an ever-growing [pool](#pool). Characters may be dealing, [holding](#holding) a fan of cards or slamming one down.

entries.name: golf
entries.description: The sport of [driving](#driving) a small [ball](#ball) across an open course into a distant [cup](#cup) in as few strokes as possible. It covers [swinging](#swinging), putting and lining up a shot, along with the caddies and carts around the players.

entries.name: kendo
entries.description: Japanese fencing with [bamboo](#bamboo) swords, fought in a barred [mask](#mask), a [breastplate](#breastplate) and padded [gloves](#gloves). Strikes are called out loudly as they land.

entries.name: jogging
entries.description: Running at an easy, sustained pace for exercise, usually in [sportswear](#sportswear) along a [path](#path), a track or a [street](#street). It is slower and less urgent than a sprint or a chase.

entries.name: old_maid
entries.description: The [card](#card) game in which one unmatchable card is passed along until somebody is left [holding](#holding) it and loses. Play turns on drawing [blind](#blind) from another player's fanned hand.

entries.name: american_football
entries.description: The padded, helmeted [field](#field) game in which two sides carry, throw or kick an oval [ball](#ball) towards the opposing end zone. It also stands for the closely related codes that share the same kit.

entries.name: skiing
entries.description: Travelling downhill or across [snow](#snow) on [skis](#skis), poles in hand. Slopes, lifts and [heavy](#heavy) [winter](#winter) clothing set the scene.

entries.name: snowboarding
entries.description: Riding a [snowboard](#snowboard), or anything [standing](#standing) in for one, across [snow](#snow). A [mountain](#mountain) run isn't required, only that a board is [carrying](#carrying) the rider along.

entries.name: gambling
entries.description: Playing a game of chance with [money](#money) or valuables at [stake](#stake), hoping to come away with more than was risked. Cards, [dice](#dice), [mahjong](#mahjong), slot machines and [casino](#casino) tables are the usual settings.

entries.name: rowing
entries.description: Driving a [boat](#boat) or board forward by [pulling](#pulling) oars or a [paddle](#paddle) through the [water](#water). Covers a leisurely turn on a [lake](#lake) as [well](#well) as competitive sculling.

entries.name: tic-tac-toe
entries.description: The three-by-three [grid](#grid) game in which two players alternate marking X and O and try to complete a line while [blocking](#blocking) the other. Usually drawn on [paper](#paper), a blackboard or a [screen](#screen), often at the moment a row is finished.

entries.name: acrobatics
entries.description: Tumbling, flipping, [balancing](#balancing) or aerial stunts performed with the whole body. The [figure](#figure) is [caught](#caught) mid-manoeuvre rather than simply struck in an athletic pose.

entries.name: target_practice
entries.description: Someone shooting, [firing](#firing) or [throwing](#throwing) at a set [target](#target), with either the act or its result on show: the [weapon](#weapon) in use, arrows [buried](#buried) in the board, holes [torn](#torn) through [paper](#paper). Aiming at a living opponent is a different matter.

entries.name: bread_eating_race
entries.description: A sports-day event in which runners must catch a roll [hanging](#hanging) on a [string](#string) with their [teeth](#teeth) and carry it over the finish line. Melon [bread](#bread) is the usual prize, and stricter versions tie the runners' hands behind their backs.

entries.name: bowling
entries.description: Rolling a [heavy](#heavy) [ball](#ball) down a polished lane to knock over the pins [standing](#standing) at the far end. The word covers the throw itself and the indoor sport around it.

entries.name: squat_(exercise)
entries.description: Squatting performed as a [training](#training) movement, [dropping](#dropping) the hips with a straight [back](#back) and [standing](#standing) back up. A [barbell](#barbell) carried across the shoulders turns it into a [weightlifting](#weightlifting) lift.

entries.name: mixed_martial_arts
entries.description: Full-contact [fighting](#fighting) that blends striking, clinching and ground grappling, typically staged inside an octagonal [cage](#cage). Covers both a match in progress and characters dressed as fighters for the sport.

entries.name: dribbling_(basketball)
entries.description: Bouncing a [basketball](#basketball) off the [floor](#floor) with one hand while moving with it. Shows the [ball](#ball) in play rather than simply carried.

entries.name: taekwondo
entries.description: The Korean martial art built around fast, high, precise [kicking](#kicking). Sparring gear, a white dobok with a colored [belt](#belt), and airborne kicks are the usual visual cues.

entries.name: judo
entries.description: The Japanese grappling art of throws, pins, chokes and joint locks, practised in a [heavy](#heavy) white [jacket](#jacket) and coloured [belt](#belt). Strikes have [no](#no) place in its [matches](#matches).

entries.name: badminton
entries.description: The racquet game in which a [shuttlecock](#shuttlecock) is knocked [back](#back) and forth over a high [net](#net), played one or two to a side. Reserve it for the game actually under way rather than for the equipment [lying](#lying) about.

entries.name: skydive
entries.description: Jumping from an [aircraft](#aircraft) and [falling](#falling) freely before [opening](#opening) a [parachute](#parachute). Not the same as BASE [jumping](#jumping), which starts from a fixed [structure](#structure) or [cliff](#cliff).

entries.name: ragequit
entries.description: A character abandons what they were doing in a fit of temper, storming off, flinging down a [controller](#controller), or slamming a game shut. The anger and the sudden quitting together are the point.

entries.name: slam_dunk_(basketball)
entries.description: A [basketball](#basketball) player leaping to the [hoop](#hoop) and [pushing](#pushing) the [ball](#ball) straight down through it. Usually drawn at the top of the jump with a hand on the rim.

entries.name: dodgeball
entries.description: The gym-class game of [throwing](#throwing) balls at the opposing team to knock its players out, or the equipment in use. A [school](#school) sports scene.

entries.name: lacrosse
entries.description: A contact team sport in which players carry, pass and shoot a rubber [ball](#ball) held in the netted head of a long [stick](#stick). Pictures show the [field](#field), the padding and sticks in play.

entries.name: tug_of_war
entries.description: Two teams hauling on opposite ends of a [rope](#rope), each trying to drag the other side across a line. A sports-day fixture, typically drawn with [everyone](#everyone) [leaning](#leaning) [back](#back) and heels dug in.

entries.name: hide_and_seek
entries.description: The children's game in which one player covers their eyes and counts while the rest scatter for [cover](#cover), then goes [hunting](#hunting) for them. Either half of it fits, the [counting](#counting) or the search.

entries.name: sky_surfing
entries.description: Riding a board through the air as one would ride [waves](#waves), whether on a [surfboard](#surfboard), a [hoverboard](#hoverboard) or something improvised. Usually a [fantasy](#fantasy) or sci-fi means of travel rather than a real sport.

entries.name: esports
entries.description: Competitive [video](#video) gaming staged as a spectacle: team jerseys, gaming chairs, headsets, a tournament [stage](#stage) or a [watching](#watching) [crowd](#crowd). It also fits art referring to a particular professional team or player.

entries.name: music
entries.description: A character [singing](#singing) or [playing](#playing) an [instrument](#instrument) within the picture. Where the [file](#file) itself carries a soundtrack, audible music is the [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: dancing
entries.description: A character moving energetically in time to [music](#music), either improvising or [following](#following) set choreography. Particular styles, moves and routines have tags of their own.

entries.name: playing_instrument
entries.description: A character is shown performing on a musical [instrument](#instrument) of any kind. Add the instrument's own [tag](#tag), and a specific action tag like [playing_guitar](#playing_guitar) or [playing_piano](#playing_piano) where one exists.

entries.name: singing
entries.description: A character producing musical sounds with the voice, usually drawn with the mouth open and musical [notes](#notes) [floating](#floating) nearby. Often paired with [microphone](#microphone) or an [idol](#idol) [stage](#stage).

entries.name: k-pop
entries.description: The picture draws on Korean pop [music](#music) — an [idol](#idol) or group, a [stage](#stage) [costume](#costume), a dance move or a line from a song. Name the specific performer or group as [well](#well) when it [can](#can) be identified.

entries.name: concert
entries.description: A live musical performance in front of an [audience](#audience), given by a band, an [idol](#idol) group or a [solo](#solo) act, generally on a lit [stage](#stage) with a [crowd](#crowd) below.

entries.name: musical_performance
entries.description: Music being played or sung for listeners, from a lone [instrument](#instrument) to a full band on a [stage](#stage). It names the act of performing rather than instruments merely [lying](#lying) about.

entries.name: ballet
entries.description: Classical [stage](#stage) [dancing](#dancing) being practised or performed: [standing](#standing) en pointe, [working](#working) at the [barre](#barre), [dropping](#dropping) into a [split](#split) or lifting one leg high. Tutus and leotards usually come with it, and the [dancer](#dancer) herself is a [ballerina](#ballerina).

entries.name: playing_guitar
entries.description: A character actively strumming or picking a [guitar](#guitar). If the [instrument](#instrument) is merely carried or posed with, use [holding_guitar](#holding_guitar) instead.

entries.name: karaoke
entries.description: Singing along to a backing track while the words [scroll](#scroll) across a [screen](#screen), usually with a [microphone](#microphone) in hand and [friends](#friends) [crowded](#crowded) round. Add [singing](#singing) and microphone where they apply.

entries.name: playing_piano
