entries.description: Fingers [resting](#resting) on or striking the keys of a [piano](#piano), upright or grand, with the player seated or [standing](#standing) at the keyboard. An electric keyboard or synthesiser is tagged separately.

entries.name: playing_flute
entries.description: Someone holds a [flute](#flute) to their [lips](#lips) and blows across or into it. Covers transverse flutes and similar [wind](#wind) pipes played the same way, with the [instrument](#instrument) itself usually tagged alongside.

entries.name: asmr
entries.description: A performance meant to give the listener that tingling scalp-and-spine calm: [whispering](#whispering) into a binaural [microphone](#microphone), ear [cleaning](#cleaning), tapping or [breathing](#breathing) close to the ear. Often framed as a [video](#video), sometimes with the letters lettered on [screen](#screen).

entries.name: marching_band
entries.description: Instrumentalists [playing](#playing) while they walk in formation at a [parade](#parade), ceremony or contest. Military-styled uniforms and plumed caps are what set them apart from an ordinary ensemble.

entries.name: lion_dance
entries.description: The Chinese [festival](#festival) dance in which one or two performers work a [lion](#lion) [puppet](#puppet) to bring luck, seen at new year, weddings and [shop](#shop) openings. A [dragon](#dragon) dance uses a far longer body carried on poles by many [people](#people).

entries.name: magic_trick
entries.description: A staged illusion in progress: a [card](#card) [forced](#forced), a [dove](#dove) produced from nowhere, something made to vanish. Top hats, [playing](#playing) cards and [silk](#silk) handkerchiefs are the usual giveaways.

entries.name: juggling
entries.description: Several objects kept moving through the air in a steady cycle, more of them aloft at any moment than in the hands. Balls, clubs and rings are the usual [choice](#choice).

entries.name: breakdance
entries.description: Acrobatic [street](#street) dance built from footwork, freezes, spins and headstands, danced to hip-hop. It reached the Olympics under the name [breaking](#breaking).

entries.name: playing_bass_guitar
entries.description: A character actually [playing](#playing) a bass [guitar](#guitar), one hand on the strings and the other on the [neck](#neck). Merely [carrying](#carrying) the [instrument](#instrument) without playing it calls for [holding_bass_guitar](#holding_bass_guitar) instead.

entries.name: belly_dancing
entries.description: The Egyptian-rooted dance built on [rolling](#rolling), isolated movements of the hips and [torso](#torso). It is drawn mid-motion with the arms raised and the [midriff](#midriff) [swaying](#swaying), often before an [audience](#audience).

entries.name: drumming
entries.description: Striking a [drum](#drum) with sticks, mallets or bare hands. Covers a full kit, a taiko and a small hand drum alike.

entries.name: waltz_(dance)
entries.description: A [couple](#couple) turning in three-four time, one pair of hands joined and the other hand at the partner's [back](#back). Ballrooms, gowns and formal [dress](#dress) usually come with it.

entries.name: samba
entries.description: The Brazilian dance and its [music](#music), drawn in mid-step with towering feather headdresses, [sequins](#sequins) and very brief [carnival](#carnival) costumes.

entries.name: shishimai
entries.description: The Japanese [lion](#lion) dance, performed under a red lacquered [mask](#mask) with a clacking [jaw](#jaw) and a [patterned](#patterned) [cloth](#cloth) body trailing behind the [dancer](#dancer). Seen at New Year celebrations and [stage](#stage) performances.

entries.name: rapping
entries.description: A character delivers rhymed verse in rhythm, usually [microphone](#microphone) in hand with a pointed [gesture](#gesture) from the free arm. Often paired with speech text or musical [notes](#notes) to make the performance readable.

entries.name: unconventional_guitar
entries.description: Air [guitar](#guitar) mimed on something that merely resembles one, such as a [broom](#broom), a [tennis](#tennis) [racket](#racket) or a [shovel](#shovel). The long [handle](#handle) and broad head sell the illusion of an [instrument](#instrument).

entries.name: para_para
entries.description: A Japanese synchronised dance built almost entirely from arm movements, raised, swept out to the sides, [pointing](#pointing), framing the face, performed to eurobeat and tied to [gyaru](#gyaru) [fashion](#fashion). Each song carries its own fixed routine.

entries.name: wotagei
entries.description: The synchronised fan routine performed at [idol](#idol) concerts: chanting, sharp arm movements, and glowsticks swung in time. It is shown from the [audience](#audience) side of the [stage](#stage) rather than the performers'.

entries.name: tango
entries.description: Two dancers performing the sensual Argentine [ballroom](#ballroom) dance, held close with sharp turns and deep dips. Formal [dress](#dress) and a [rose](#rose) held in the [teeth](#teeth) are the usual visual shorthand.

entries.name: flamenco
entries.description: The Andalusian dance and [music](#music) tradition — heels stamped, hands clapped sharply, arms thrown high, a [guitar](#guitar) behind it all. A [rose](#rose) gripped in the [teeth](#teeth) is the [standing](#standing) cliché.

entries.name: orchestra
entries.description: A large ensemble of musicians arranged in sections of strings, brass, woodwind and percussion. Usually shown mid-performance, often with a [conductor](#conductor) before them.

entries.name: battle
entries.description: A [serious](#serious), large-scale [clash](#clash) between characters or forces: armies meeting, a [party](#party) against a [monster](#monster), fighters in earnest. A minor scuffle or an argument is [fighting](#fighting) instead.

entries.name: kicking
entries.description: A character strikes out with a leg or foot, in a fight, a martial arts move or a playful shove. A leg merely raised is [knee_up](#knee_up) or [leg_lift](#leg_lift).

entries.name: firing
entries.description: A ranged [weapon](#weapon) going off, be it a firearm, a [rocket](#rocket) launcher or a mortar. Muzzle [flash](#flash), [flying](#flying) casings and recoil usually come with it.

entries.name: attack
entries.description: A blow is being delivered against a person, [creature](#creature) or object with intent to do damage. Add the specific action where one exists, such as [punching](#punching), [slashing](#slashing) or shooting.

entries.name: duel
entries.description: A fight between two opponents alone, as opposed to one [figure](#figure) against a [crowd](#crowd) or two armies clashing. Sword duels, gunfights and other single combats all count.

entries.name: incoming_attack
entries.description: A character lunging, [swinging](#swinging) or striking straight at the viewer, as though the viewer were the [target](#target). The blow is aimed out of the picture rather than at anyone in it.

entries.name: stab
entries.description: A blade thrust into someone, or the aftermath of a puncture wound already inflicted by a [knife](#knife) or [sword](#sword). A wound driven all the way through is [impaled](#impaled); a knife left comically [stuck](#stuck) in someone is [knifed](#knifed).

entries.name: psychic
entries.description: A character using mental powers such as [telekinesis](#telekinesis) or [telepathy](#telepathy), often signalled by a [glowing](#glowing) [aura](#aura), objects hovering unsupported, or a hand pressed to the [temple](#temple). Fire manipulation on its own is a separate ability.

entries.name: slashing
entries.description: A bladed [weapon](#weapon) swung through the air at an opponent or as a flourish, usually with an arc trailing the blade.

entries.name: flying_kick
entries.description: A kick thrown while the character is still airborne after leaping. A specific form of [kicking](#kicking), common in action and martial arts scenes.

entries.name: casting_spell
entries.description: A character is actively [working](#working) [magic](#magic), usually with [glowing](#glowing) motes, an [aura](#aura), a rune [circle](#circle) or a [ball](#ball) of [energy](#energy) gathering at the hand or on a [staff](#staff). Chanting counts where magic is real in the setting; the same [gesture](#gesture) in an ordinary one does not.

entries.name: submission_hold
entries.description: A professional [wrestling](#wrestling) [lock](#lock) applied to [pin](#pin) an opponent and force them to give up. Grappling techniques from [judo](#judo) or jiu-jitsu are tagged judo_hold or [joint_lock](#joint_lock) instead. Implies wrestling.

entries.name: dodging
entries.description: Twisting, ducking or springing clear of an incoming [attack](#attack) instead of meeting it with a [guard](#guard). The evasion is [caught](#caught) mid-motion.

entries.name: blocking
entries.description: An incoming [attack](#attack) being stopped, with a [shield](#shield), a [weapon](#weapon), a raised arm or a barrier. It applies equally to swung blades, arrows and beams of [energy](#energy).

entries.name: at_gunpoint
entries.description: One character holds another under the muzzle of a [gun](#gun) to force compliance. When the [weapon](#weapon) is aimed out of the picture at the viewer use [aiming_at_viewer](#aiming_at_viewer), and a gun turned on its own holder is [gun_to_head](#gun_to_head).

entries.name: charging_forward
entries.description: One or more figures rush headlong at a [target](#target), sprinting or leaping into the [attack](#attack). It suits a lone attacker as [well](#well) as an entire formation storming ahead.

entries.name: headshot
entries.description: A [bullet](#bullet), arrow or other projectile strikes somebody in the head, usually fatally unless the [weapon](#weapon) is blunt or the head is armoured. It has nothing to do with the photographic sense of a head-and-shoulders [portrait](#portrait).

entries.name: aerial_battle
entries.description: A fight taking place [well](#well) above the ground, between characters who [can](#can) [fly](#fly), winged creatures or [aircraft](#aircraft). The combatants are genuinely airborne rather than merely leaping.

entries.name: clash
entries.description: Two melee weapons meet in mid-strike, blades locked or ringing off one another. Sparks and impact lines are generally drawn at the point of contact.

entries.name: kneeing
entries.description: Driving a knee into an opponent as a strike during a fight. Do not confuse it with [kneeling](#kneeling), which is a [resting](#resting) posture on the ground.

entries.name: chop
entries.description: A strike delivered with the outer edge of a stiff flat hand, as in [karate](#karate). It is a blow, not the act of [cutting](#cutting) [food](#food) or wood, which is [chopping](#chopping).

entries.name: healing
entries.description: Curative [magic](#magic) at work on a wound: glow, sparkles or a [spell](#spell) [circle](#circle) over the [injury](#injury) while somebody channels it with a hand or a [staff](#staff). The healer is usually a [cleric](#cleric) or white-mage sort.

entries.name: cocking_gun
entries.description: A firearm is being made ready to [fire](#fire): a [hammer](#hammer) thumbed [back](#back), a [slide](#slide) or [pump](#pump) racked, a bolt worked through. It usually marks the beat just before a shot.

entries.name: mexican_standoff
entries.description: Three or more [people](#people) [holding](#holding) weapons on one another at close range, none able to strike without being struck in turn. A deadlock built entirely out of aimed guns.

entries.name: firing_at_viewer
entries.description: The [weapon](#weapon) is discharged straight at the viewer, muzzle [flash](#flash) filling the frame. Merely taking aim without shooting is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: axe_kick
entries.description: A high kick in which the leg swings straight up above the head and then drops heel first onto the [target](#target), [chopping](#chopping) downward. It is tagged mainly for the raised phase; the descent alone counts only when the lift is drawn too.

entries.name: dogfight
entries.description: Fighter [aircraft](#aircraft) turning hard against one another at close range, each trying to get onto the other's [tail](#tail). Both sides know the other is there.

entries.name: rocket_punch
entries.description: A fist that detaches from the arm and flies at the [target](#target) under its own power, usually trailing [exhaust](#exhaust). A [signature](#signature) move of [giant](#giant) robots and of certain game characters.

entries.name: taking_cover
entries.description: Pressing behind something solid to [shield](#shield) oneself from incoming [fire](#fire), such as a wall [corner](#corner), a [trench](#trench) or an overturned vehicle. A [weapon](#weapon) in hand and a peek around the edge are typical.

entries.name: sword_clash
entries.description: Two blades meeting edge to edge, often locked together with [sparks](#sparks) or a shock effect drawn at the point of contact. The moment of impact itself is the subject, not the wider [duel](#duel).

entries.name: at_knifepoint
entries.description: A blade is held close against someone as a [threat](#threat), most often at the throat or pressed into the [back](#back). Any bladed [weapon](#weapon) counts, not only a [knife](#knife).

entries.name: drop_kick
entries.description: A leaping kick landed with both [feet](#feet) at once, the body stretched flat in the air. As much a [wrestling](#wrestling) manoeuvre as a [fighting](#fighting) one.

entries.name: horseback_archery
entries.description: Arrows are loosed from the [back](#back) of a [horse](#horse) or a similar mount. Both halves have to be happening at once; a rider merely [carrying](#carrying) a [bow](#bow) does not qualify.

entries.name: imminent_fight
entries.description: Two or more characters squared off with [violence](#violence) about to break: stances set, weapons drawn, fists raised. No blow has landed yet.

entries.name: fishing
entries.description: Catching [fish](#fish), or trying to: usually a rod and baited line worked from a bank, a [pier](#pier) or a [boat](#boat), though nets, spears and other methods count as [well](#well).

entries.name: interview
entries.description: One person puts questions to another while a [microphone](#microphone), [recorder](#recorder) or [notepad](#notepad) marks the exchange. A press scrum and a quiet sit-down conversation both qualify.

entries.name: teaching
entries.description: One person shows another how something works, whether it is [book](#book) knowledge explained at a blackboard or a physical skill guided hand over hand. Neither a qualified [teacher](#teacher) nor a [school](#school) setting is required.

entries.name: medical_examination
entries.description: A [doctor](#doctor) or [nurse](#nurse) checking a patient over: [listening](#listening) to the chest, taking [height](#height) and [weight](#weight), or inspecting an [injury](#injury). The patient is usually seated or [lying](#lying) on an examination [couch](#couch), partly undressed.

entries.name: digging
entries.description: Breaking ground with a spade, another tool or bare hands to open a [hole](#hole). The loose earth and the growing heap usually show alongside.

entries.name: repairing
entries.description: Somebody mending a [damaged](#damaged) object with [tools](#tools) or materials, whether a [machine](#machine), a piece of furniture, or a [torn](#torn) garment. The work should be in progress rather than finished.

entries.name: working
entries.description: Someone is at their job, typically [grinding](#grinding) through a long shift or a [stack](#stack) of [paperwork](#paperwork). It applies to effort and overtime generally rather than to any one trade.

entries.name: construction
entries.description: A [building](#building) is going up, or the work of putting it up is being shown, with [scaffolding](#scaffolding), cranes and half-finished frames.

entries.name: carving
entries.description: Shaping solid material by [cutting](#cutting) into it — wood, stone, [ice](#ice), [fruit](#fruit) — shown mid-work or finished. Pumpkins cut into lanterns are the seasonal case.

entries.name: paperwork
entries.description: Stacks of forms and documents being filled in, sorted or signed, the shorthand for [office](#office) drudgery. Usually drawn with a cluttered [desk](#desk) and a weary face.

entries.name: polishing
entries.description: Rubbing an object with a [cloth](#cloth) to bring the shine [back](#back): armour, a blade, glassware, or a [car](#car) [bonnet](#bonnet). Both the rag and the resulting [gleam](#gleam) are usually drawn.

entries.name: falconry
entries.description: Hunting with a trained [bird](#bird) of prey, or simply [carrying](#carrying) one perched on a gloved fist. Any [raptor](#raptor) counts, not only falcons, and the thick glove is usually in view.

entries.name: farming
entries.description: The work of tending crops or animals: planting, weeding, harvesting, hauling produce, [feeding](#feeding) stock. About the labour rather than the land itself.

entries.name: surgery
entries.description: An operation in progress, a body opened with instruments to repair damage or remove disease. Expect masks, [gloves](#gloves), an operating [table](#table), drapes and bright overhead light; the [tag](#tag) marks the procedure rather than a general [hospital](#hospital) scene.

entries.name: hunting
entries.description: Game is being tracked, stalked or brought down, with [bow](#bow), [gun](#gun), trap or bare [claws](#claws). The chase, the kill and the carcass carried home all fall under it.

entries.name: cleaning_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) is being maintained rather than used: a blade [oiled](#oiled), a rod run through a [gun](#gun) [barrel](#barrel), parts laid out. A quiet moment, usually with the weapon partly stripped down.

entries.name: rice_planting
entries.description: Setting young [rice](#rice) seedlings into a muddy flooded [field](#field), either bent over doing it by hand or [riding](#riding) a transplanting [machine](#machine). A seasonal [farming](#farming) scene tied to early [summer](#summer).

entries.name: bait
entries.description: Something set out to draw an [animal](#animal) or a [fish](#fish) in, hung from a [hook](#hook) or laid inside a trap. It is usually a scrap of [food](#food) at the end of a line.

entries.name: maintenance
entries.description: Work to keep a [machine](#machine), vehicle or system in order: panels open, [tools](#tools) out, parts spread on the [floor](#floor). Also used when a service has been taken down while it is repaired or updated.

entries.name: riding
entries.description: Sitting astride and travelling on an [animal](#animal) or a vehicle such as a [horse](#horse), [bicycle](#bicycle) or [motorcycle](#motorcycle) for transportation. For the sexual sense of the word, use [cowgirl_position](#cowgirl_position) or [girl_on_top](#girl_on_top) instead.

entries.name: broom_riding
entries.description: Flying while seated on a broomstick, the classic witch's transport. Standing on it instead is [broom_surfing](#broom_surfing), and perching on a [polearm](#polearm) or [scythe](#scythe) is [on_weapon](#on_weapon).

entries.name: driving
entries.description: Somebody at the controls of a vehicle or a mount: steering a [car](#car), [flying](#flying) a [mecha](#mecha), [holding](#holding) the [reins](#reins) of a [cart](#cart) [horse](#horse). Pushing or hauling a vehicle along does not count.

entries.name: horseback_riding
entries.description: Somebody rides on the [back](#back) of a [horse](#horse) or a horse-like [creature](#creature). Donkeys, unicorns, pegasi, centaurs, [carousel](#carousel) horses and even [people](#people) [playing](#playing) at being horses all count.

entries.name: sidesaddle
entries.description: Riding with both [legs](#legs) [hanging](#hanging) on the same side of the mount, traditionally a woman's way of [sitting](#sitting) a [horse](#horse). Applies to brooms and other ridden objects as [well](#well) as animals.

entries.name: saddle
entries.description: A seat strapped to the [back](#back) of a [horse](#horse) or other mount for the rider. Appears with [reins](#reins) and stirrups in [riding](#riding) scenes.

entries.name: riding_bicycle
entries.description: A character pedalling a [bicycle](#bicycle), whether commuting, [racing](#racing) or just cruising.

entries.name: multiple_riders
entries.description: Two or more [people](#people) [riding](#riding) the same [animal](#animal), [bicycle](#bicycle), [motorcycle](#motorcycle) or other mount together. Sharing the one [saddle](#saddle) or seat is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: riding_animal
entries.description: Sitting astride the [back](#back) of a [creature](#creature) that is not a [horse](#horse), including donkeys, unicorns, pegasi, centaurs and mechanical mounts. Riding an actual horse or horse-like beast falls under [horseback_riding](#horseback_riding) instead.

entries.name: camping
entries.description: Staying the [night](#night) [outdoors](#outdoors) under canvas, away from any [house](#house), with [food](#food) cooked over a [fire](#fire) and the [evening](#evening) spent [sitting](#sitting) around it. Woods, lakesides and [mountain](#mountain) clearings are the usual settings.

entries.name: riding_dragon
entries.description: A character seated on a dragon's [back](#back), in flight or on the ground. A [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) illustration, often with [saddle](#saddle) and [reins](#reins) improvised over the [scales](#scales).

entries.name: drifting
entries.description: A [car](#car) steered deliberately [sideways](#sideways) through a [corner](#corner), the rear tyres [spinning](#spinning) free and [smoking](#smoking) while the driver holds the [slide](#slide). Mountain passes and [night](#night) circuits are the usual setting.

entries.name: piloting
entries.description: A character at the controls of an [aircraft](#aircraft), a [spacecraft](#spacecraft) or a [giant](#giant) [robot](#robot), [working](#working) a [stick](#stick), yoke or console. A [cockpit](#cockpit) view with instruments crowding the [figure](#figure) is the usual framing.

entries.name: broom_surfing
entries.description: A character rides a [flying](#flying) [broom](#broom) [standing](#standing) upright, [feet](#feet) [planted](#planted) along the shaft as if on a [surfboard](#surfboard). It is the alternative to [sitting](#sitting) astride the [handle](#handle).

entries.name: hiking
entries.description: Walking a long way through open country for its own [sake](#sake), in [boots](#boots) and [carrying](#carrying) a pack, sometimes with poles. Trails, hills and woodland make up the surroundings.

entries.name: riding_bird
entries.description: A character mounted on a [bird](#bird) large enough to carry them, whether [running](#running) like a chocobo or in flight. Fantasy and game settings supply most examples.

entries.name: hitchhiking
entries.description: Standing at the roadside with a thumb out for a lift, [bag](#bag) at the [feet](#feet). A destination scrawled on [card](#card) sometimes goes with it.

entries.name: umbrella_riding
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol) used as a means of travel: gripped by the [handle](#handle) while [drifting](#drifting) high above the ground, or sat in while the canopy is upturned. A whimsical, often magical way to get about.

entries.name: wheelie
entries.description: A bike, motorbike or [car](#car) accelerating hard enough that its front wheels lift clear of the ground. A show-off move, generally drawn at the point of balance.

entries.name: smoking
entries.description: A character smokes a [cigarette](#cigarette), [cigar](#cigar), pipe, [kiseru](#kiseru), [hookah](#hookah) or similar, [inhaling](#inhaling), exhaling, or simply [holding](#holding) the lit implement. Illegal substances count too.

entries.name: selfie
entries.description: A character photographing themselves with a [phone](#phone) or [camera](#camera), or the picture framed as the photo they took, arm [reaching](#reaching) toward the viewer. The camera may be off-screen but clearly implied.

entries.name: soaking_feet
entries.description: A seated or [resting](#resting) character dips one or both [feet](#feet) into [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid), at a pool's edge, a [stream](#stream), or a footbath. Standing or [walking](#walking) through water instead is [wading](#wading).

entries.name: taking_picture
entries.description: A character photographing something with a [camera](#camera) or a [phone](#phone). Capturing [video](#video) footage instead is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: blowing_bubbles
entries.description: Bubbles made by [blowing](#blowing) through a [wand](#wand) or pipe, by inflating [chewing](#chewing) gum in front of the mouth, or by exhaling [underwater](#underwater). Add [bubble](#bubble) for the bubbles themselves and [chewing_gum](#chewing_gum) for a gum one.

entries.name: giving
entries.description: One character [holding](#holding) something out to another, usually [food](#food) rather than a wrapped present. An offer aimed at the viewer takes [incoming_food](#incoming_food), [incoming_drink](#incoming_drink) or [incoming_gift](#incoming_gift), and an offering laid before a [shrine](#shrine) has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: watching
entries.description: Observing something from a distance without taking part. A character fixed on a [television](#television) [screen](#screen), or trailing somebody obsessively, has a more specific [tag](#tag).

entries.name: mirror_selfie
entries.description: Photographing oneself by [pointing](#pointing) a [phone](#phone) or [camera](#camera) at a [mirror](#mirror), so both the [device](#device) and the reflected pose end up in the frame.

entries.name: blowing_bubble
entries.description: A character sending a [bubble](#bubble) out into the air, blown from soapy [water](#water) through a [wand](#wand) or a [ring](#ring). The bubble in flight is normally visible with them.

entries.name: livestream
entries.description: A character broadcasts themselves live to an online [audience](#audience), usually shown with a [camera](#camera), a chat overlay or a streaming interface.

entries.name: cheering
entries.description: A character shouts encouragement at somebody taking part in something, arms often raised, sometimes with pom-poms or a [banner](#banner). Support is the point rather than the noise.

entries.name: picnic
entries.description: A [meal](#meal) eaten [outdoors](#outdoors) for pleasure, spread on a [blanket](#blanket) in a [park](#park), a [meadow](#meadow) or under trees. Tag the [food](#food) and the outdoor setting as [well](#well), plus [picnic_basket](#picnic_basket) or [picnic_blanket](#picnic_blanket) where they appear.

entries.name: playing
entries.description: Characters engaged in play for its own [sake](#sake), romping with a [pet](#pet), a [toy](#toy), or each other. For an organised game or sport, use [playing_games](#playing_games) or [playing_sports](#playing_sports) instead.

entries.name: fanning_self
entries.description: A character cools themselves with a hand fan, a sheet of [paper](#paper), an electric fan or a bare hand. A [hot](#hot) [summer](#summer) scene as a rule; add [hand_fan](#hand_fan) or [electric_fan](#electric_fan) for the tool.

entries.name: otaku
entries.description: A character shown as an obsessive fan of anime, games or idols, the picture making that visible through [merchandise](#merchandise), posters or a stereotyped look. Only [tag](#tag) it where the enthusiasm is actually on [display](#display).

entries.name: watching_television
entries.description: A character [sitting](#sitting) or [lying](#lying) in front of a [television](#television) [screen](#screen) and [watching](#watching) it. Add the television [tag](#tag) and any furniture like [couch](#couch).

entries.name: prank
entries.description: A trick played on someone for laughs: a tack on the [chair](#chair), scribbles on a [sleeping](#sleeping) face, a [bucket](#bucket) balanced over a [door](#door). Purely verbal wind-ups fall under [trolling](#trolling) instead.

entries.name: listening_to_music
entries.description: Someone is taking in [music](#music) and usually enjoying it, through [headphones](#headphones), [earphones](#earphones) or a [speaker](#speaker) in the room.

entries.name: dating
entries.description: Two characters out together on a romantic outing: [walking](#walking) side by side, [sharing](#sharing) a [meal](#meal), [riding](#riding) a ferris [wheel](#wheel). The romance should be legible from the scene itself.

entries.name: flirting
entries.description: One character making playful romantic advances on another through a look, a lean, a [teasing](#teasing) line or a light touch. Nothing physical need happen; the intent carries it.

entries.name: fanning_face
entries.description: Air is directed at one's own face to cool it, with a fan, a [folded](#folded) [card](#card) or a [flapping](#flapping) hand. Flushed cheeks and [sweat](#sweat) usually go with it.

entries.name: modeling
entries.description: Someone [posing](#posing) as the subject for a [camera](#camera) or for an artist. The [sitting](#sitting) itself is shown, often with the [photographer](#photographer), the [easel](#easel) or the [studio](#studio) lights [sharing](#sharing) the frame.

entries.name: trolling
entries.description: One character deliberately winds another up for laughs, through mockery, misdirection or a [smug](#smug) remark. A physical [prank](#prank) of the thumbtack-on-a-chair sort counts as a prank instead.

entries.name: imitating
entries.description: One character copying another's gestures, voice or bearing, sometimes while wearing their [clothes](#clothes). Where the borrowed outfit is the whole point, [cosplay](#cosplay) belongs alongside.

entries.name: relaxing
entries.description: A character is at ease with nothing to do, stretched out, [leaning](#leaning) [back](#back), or soaking in warmth. The loose posture and untroubled face carry the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: apologizing
entries.description: One character says sorry to another, with a bowed head, clasped hands or a full [kneeling](#kneeling) [prostration](#prostration). The act of contrition is what the picture is built on.

entries.name: smelling_flower
entries.description: A blossom lifted to the [nose](#nose) and breathed in, eyes usually half closed. A quiet, gentle beat that turns up in [garden](#garden) and [field](#field) scenes.

entries.name: lighting_cigarette
entries.description: A [cigarette](#cigarette) is being lit, with a [lighter](#lighter) or match held to the tip and the smoker [leaning](#leaning) into the flame.

entries.name: resting
entries.description: A character pausing to recover after effort, or simply idling with nothing to do. Distinct from [sleeping](#sleeping), since the eyes are usually open and the pose is only relaxed rather than [unconscious](#unconscious).

entries.name: stargazing
entries.description: Watching the [night](#night) [sky](#sky), whether as a hobby, for study, or for astrology. Usually a quiet outdoor scene on a [rooftop](#rooftop) or [lying](#lying) [back](#back) on [grass](#grass), [telescope](#telescope) optional.

entries.name: snowball_fight
entries.description: Characters pelting each other with packed [snow](#snow), [caught](#caught) mid-throw or ducking for [cover](#cover). Improvised barricades and snow-flecked coats often round out the scene.

entries.name: celebration
entries.description: Characters marking a [happy](#happy) occasion together, [cheering](#cheering), raising [glasses](#glasses), [throwing](#throwing) [confetti](#confetti) or applauding. A follower-count post is a milestone celebration and a yearly one an [anniversary](#anniversary).

entries.name: photobomb
entries.description: Someone slips uninvited into a picture as it is taken, popping up in the background or crowding in beside or in front of the intended subject. Usually played for a laugh, with a [grin](#grin) or a [gesture](#gesture) aimed at the lens.

entries.name: sunbathing
entries.description: Lying or [sitting](#sitting) out in direct [sun](#sun), typically to [tan](#tan). Beaches, poolsides, rooftops and balconies are the usual settings, and swimwear or a [towel](#towel) underneath is common.

entries.name: fanning
entries.description: Air is pushed at oneself or at somebody else with a hand fan, an electric fan, a [book](#book) or bare [palms](#palms), nearly always because of the heat. Sweat, thin clothing and open collars come with it.

entries.name: tea_party
entries.description: People gathered around a [table](#table) over [tea](#tea) and [sweets](#sweets), with a pot, cups and tiered plates laid out. It ranges from a polite [garden](#garden) gathering to a child's game staged with dolls.

entries.name: meditation
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) [sitting](#sitting) still with eyes closed and attention turned inward, most often cross-legged with hands [resting](#resting) or [folded](#folded). Frequently set in a [temple](#temple), [garden](#garden) or beside a [waterfall](#waterfall) for quiet emphasis.

entries.name: sleepover
entries.description: Friends spending the [night](#night) together at someone's home, also called a slumber or pyjama [party](#party). Expect pyjamas, futons or a shared [bed](#bed), pillows, snacks and games, usually with several characters awake late into the night.

entries.name: oshi-katsu
entries.description: Devoted fan activity centred on one [idol](#idol) or character: hoarding their [merchandise](#merchandise), [decorating](#decorating) with it and turning out to support them. What sets it apart from broad [otaku](#otaku) interest is the single favourite at the centre.

entries.name: fan_speaking
entries.description: Somebody talks or hums into the blades of an electric fan so the voice comes out chopped and warbling. Usually drawn with stretched-out lettering; without text, look for the open mouth and the lean toward the fan.

entries.name: eavesdropping
entries.description: Somebody [listening](#listening) in on a conversation they are [no](#no) part of, usually flat against a [door](#door) or hidden round a [corner](#corner). Listening rather than [watching](#watching), which would be [voyeurism](#voyeurism).

entries.name: listening
entries.description: A character is attending to a [sound](#sound), often [leaning](#leaning) in, cupping an ear or [holding](#holding) perfectly still.

entries.name: sexting
entries.description: Sexual messages or photographs are being written, sent, or read on a [phone](#phone). The lit [screen](#screen), the [typing](#typing) hand, or the picture being taken carries the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: coin_flip
entries.description: A [coin](#coin) is sent [spinning](#spinning) into the air, generally to settle a [choice](#choice) between two options. Artists draw either the throw or the catch.

entries.name: photo_shoot
entries.description: A staged session in front of a [camera](#camera), with lights, a [backdrop](#backdrop) or a reflector and a subject [posing](#posing) to direction. Use it for the act of shooting pictures rather than for a finished photograph; the person behind the lens is [photographer](#photographer).

entries.name: rock_balancing
entries.description: Stacking stones on top of one another into a [standing](#standing) [tower](#tower) with nothing [holding](#holding) them but their own [weight](#weight). The result reads as meditative, or as a trail [marker](#marker) in the wild.

entries.name: shirt
entries.description: The most general [tag](#tag) for a garment worn on the upper body. Add the specific type where it [can](#can) be told, such as [t-shirt](#t-shirt), [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt) or [dress_shirt](#dress_shirt), along with state tags like [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift) or [open_shirt](#open_shirt).

entries.name: white_shirt
entries.description: Any style of [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) coloured white, from a [dress](#dress) shirt worn under a [blazer](#blazer) to a [casual](#casual) [t-shirt](#t-shirt). It is one of the most heavily used clothing tags, so pair it with shirt and a style [tag](#tag) such as [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt) or t-shirt.

entries.name: collared_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) finished with a [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar), as on [dress](#dress) shirts and [school](#school) uniforms. Do not add collar or any coloured collar [tag](#tag) for it, since those describe bands worn around the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: black_shirt
entries.description: Any [shirt](#shirt) in black, blouses and t-shirts included. Follow it with the cut, such as [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt) or [t-shirt](#t-shirt), since the colour says nothing about the style.

entries.name: sleeveless_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) made without sleeves on the [torso](#torso) piece; [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves), elbow [gloves](#gloves) or a [jacket](#jacket) may go with it. Not a [tank_top](#tank_top), and mutually exclusive with [strapless_shirt](#strapless_shirt) and [off-shoulder_shirt](#off-shoulder_shirt).

entries.name: dress_shirt
entries.description: A collared [shirt](#shirt) fastened by a row of [buttons](#buttons) down the front, the formal shirt worn under suits and with neckties.

entries.name: blue_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) of any style in blue: t-shirts, blouses, [dress](#dress) shirts and collared shirts alike. Add the cut where it matters, such as [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt).

entries.name: tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top with wide shoulder straps, worn by any gender. A version with thin [spaghetti](#spaghetti) straps is a [camisole](#camisole) instead.

entries.name: blouse
entries.description: A loose-fitting [shirt](#shirt), generally cut for women and often left [hanging](#hanging) untucked, with [buttons](#buttons), [frills](#frills) or a soft [collar](#collar). Add the colour variant such as [white_shirt](#white_shirt).

entries.name: red_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) in red, whether a collared button-up, a [t-shirt](#t-shirt), or a [dress](#dress) shirt. Add the shirt style; a red [sweater](#sweater) or [hoodie](#hoodie) carries its own colour [tag](#tag).

entries.name: t-shirt
entries.description: A [casual](#casual), collarless pullover top, classically short-sleeved though other sleeve lengths are common today. A collared pullover of similar cut is a polo [shirt](#shirt) instead.

entries.name: grey_shirt
entries.description: A grey [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) of any style, from a [plain](#plain) T-shirt to a collared shirt. Record the specific type where it matters.

entries.name: pink_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) in pink, of any style from a collared [dress](#dress) shirt to a [plain](#plain) [t-shirt](#t-shirt). Sweaters, [tank](#tank) tops and jackets in pink have tags of their own.

entries.name: camisole
entries.description: A short [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top hung from thin [spaghetti](#spaghetti) straps, worn on its own or as an underlayer. Broad straps make it a [tank_top](#tank_top), and a version [reaching](#reaching) past the waist is a [babydoll](#babydoll) or [chemise](#chemise).

entries.name: yellow_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) of any cut in yellow. Tag shirt as [well](#well).

entries.name: green_shirt
entries.description: A green [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) of any style, from a [plain](#plain) T-shirt to a collared [dress](#dress) shirt. Record the specific type of shirt where it is distinctive.

entries.name: purple_shirt
entries.description: A purple [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse), worn alone or under a [jacket](#jacket). Combine with shirt and the cut, such as [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt) or [t-shirt](#t-shirt).

entries.name: striped_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) [patterned](#patterned) with two or more colours of stripe. A black-and-white horizontal version reads as a burglar's outfit, a vertical one as a referee's. Implies shirt and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: off-shoulder_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) built with a broad neckline that sits under the shoulders, its attached sleeves [resting](#resting) on the upper arms. Open shirts [slipping](#slipping) off the arms, shoulder cutouts, [tube](#tube) tops, camisoles and [tank](#tank) tops all fall outside it.

entries.name: brown_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) in brown, of any cut. Add shirt, and the narrower [tag](#tag) — [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt), [t-shirt](#t-shirt), [dress_shirt](#dress_shirt) — wherever the style is clear.

entries.name: frilled_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) [carrying](#carrying) ruffles, commonly down the front placket, around the [collar](#collar) or at the wrists. The [tag](#tag) covers ruffled blouses as [well](#well) as shirts proper.

entries.name: sailor_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) with a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar), the top half of a [serafuku](#serafuku) or a standalone nautical top. Tagged with shirt and [sailor_collar](#sailor_collar).

entries.name: print_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) with a printed graphic on the front, [back](#back) or both, from a slogan tee to a [patterned](#patterned) [blouse](#blouse). Tag shirt with it; only a shirt with several base colours is also [multicolored_shirt](#multicolored_shirt).

entries.name: black_tank_top
entries.description: A black [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top held up by shoulder straps. It is worn casually, layered under other [clothes](#clothes) or for exercise.

entries.name: wet_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) soaked with [water](#water) or a similar [liquid](#liquid), most striking on white or pale [fabric](#fabric) that turns see-through. Often paired with [wet_hair](#wet_hair) and a [rain](#rain) shower or a swim.

entries.name: undershirt
entries.description: A [plain](#plain), usually white, collarless [shirt](#shirt) or [tank](#tank) top worn beneath other clothing, visible under an open shirt or on its own. Not used for [dress](#dress) shirts; a women's version [can](#can) overlap with [camisole](#camisole).

entries.name: white_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) white top with shoulder straps, worn casually or for exercise. Tag [tank_top](#tank_top) alongside it; thinner straps and a softer cut make it a [camisole](#camisole) instead.

entries.name: orange_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) in orange, of any style from [t-shirt](#t-shirt) to [dress](#dress) shirt. A knitted top is [orange_sweater](#orange_sweater).

entries.name: gym_shirt
entries.description: A short-sleeved [shirt](#shirt) made for exercise, typically the [plain](#plain) white top of a Japanese [gym_uniform](#gym_uniform).

entries.name: torn_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) with ripped [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: two-tone_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) whose design uses exactly two colours, as in raglan [cuts](#cuts) or colour-blocked styles. Add the colour tags as [well](#well).

entries.name: white_camisole
entries.description: A white [camisole](#camisole), the thin-strapped [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top, worn on its own or under an open [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: vertical-striped_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) [patterned](#patterned) with up-and-down stripes, such as a pinstripe [dress](#dress) shirt. Add colour tags for the shirt.

entries.name: plaid_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) in plaid [fabric](#fabric), most often the button-up [flannel](#flannel) of [casual](#casual) or lumberjack wear. Tag [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes) alongside it.

entries.name: turtleneck_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt), often thin and fitted, whose [collar](#collar) rises to wrap the [neck](#neck). Implies shirt and [turtleneck](#turtleneck).

entries.name: taut_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or top stretched tight enough that the [fabric](#fabric) strains and creases between the [breasts](#breasts). A merely snug fit is [tight_shirt](#tight_shirt), and unrealistic [clinging](#clinging) all around is [impossible_shirt](#impossible_shirt).

entries.name: aqua_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) in an aqua [shade](#shade). Combine with the shirt's cut and its sleeve length.

entries.name: black_camisole
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) in black, the thin-strapped [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top worn alone or under a [shirt](#shirt). It falls straight to the waist or hips and is often edged with [lace](#lace).

entries.name: impossible_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) [wrapping](#wrapping) each breast on all sides as if applied with a brush, which real [cloth](#cloth) could not do without [hanging](#hanging) slack between them. It is neither [tight_shirt](#tight_shirt), merely snug, nor [taut_shirt](#taut_shirt), where the [fabric](#fabric) stretches in [ripples](#ripples) across the gap.

entries.name: ribbed_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) in ribbed [fabric](#fabric), [giving](#giving) the look of narrow vertical stripes. Tag shirt too; a knitted pullover with the same texture is [ribbed_sweater](#ribbed_sweater) instead.

entries.name: unworn_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) taken off and visible somewhere in the scene. Add [topless](#topless) or the replacement top as appropriate for what the wearer now has on.

entries.name: strapless_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) with [no](#no) straps, [neck](#neck) or sleeves that bares the shoulders and upper chest. Looser and longer than a [tube](#tube) top, usually covering the [stomach](#stomach); [sleeveless](#sleeveless) and off-shoulder shirts are not [strapless](#strapless).

entries.name: black_undershirt
entries.description: A black [shirt](#shirt) worn beneath an open or [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) outer layer, such as a tee or [tank](#tank) showing under a [jacket](#jacket). It is that visible under-layer being named.

entries.name: multicolored_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) showing at least two clearly separate colours, whether blocked, panelled or [split](#split) down the middle. Neutrals and small trim do not count toward it.

entries.name: untucked_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) whose hem hangs loose outside the [skirt](#skirt) or trousers rather than being tucked in, [giving](#giving) a relaxed or slightly sloppy look.

entries.name: hawaiian_shirt
entries.description: A loose short-sleeved collared [shirt](#shirt) in bright [tropical](#tropical) colours and busy prints, also known as an aloha shirt. Worn open or buttoned, on the [beach](#beach) or off it.

entries.name: long_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) cut long enough to [cover](#cover) the hips and [groin](#groin), sometimes worn as a [dress](#dress) with nothing below it. Sleeve length has [no](#no) bearing on it, and it often overlaps with [naked_shirt](#naked_shirt).

entries.name: no_dickey
entries.description: The false [shirt](#shirt) front or [collar](#collar) insert belonging to an outfit has been left off, so the chest under the [jacket](#jacket) reads differently.

entries.name: polo_shirt
entries.description: A collared [shirt](#shirt) with a short buttoned placket at the [neck](#neck), typically three [buttons](#buttons) and short sleeves, sometimes a breast [pocket](#pocket). It is usually worn with the top button open.

entries.name: blue_tunic
entries.description: A loose blue top [reaching](#reaching) the hip or the knee, belted or [hanging](#hanging) free, and a [staple](#staple) of adventurers and [fantasy](#fantasy) [dress](#dress). Where the garment is clearly two colours, add the second one too.

entries.name: green_tunic
entries.description: A green [tunic](#tunic), the loose garment pulled on over the head and [reaching](#reaching) hip or knee. It is the [familiar](#familiar) [dress](#dress) of [fantasy](#fantasy) heroes, elves and rangers.

entries.name: red_tank_top
entries.description: A red [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [tank](#tank) top, worn alone or under an open [shirt](#shirt). Add [tank_top](#tank_top) and sleeveless where they apply.

entries.name: pinstripe_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) in pinstriped [cloth](#cloth), fine vertical lines over a [plain](#plain) ground. Usually a collared [dress](#dress) shirt; wide bands make it [striped_shirt](#striped_shirt).

entries.name: pink_camisole
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) in mainly pink: the thin-strapped [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top worn as [underwear](#underwear) or as a light layer. Cut and length are unchanged, only the colour.

entries.name: yellow_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) yellow top with straps. Tag [tank_top](#tank_top) alongside.

entries.name: blue_tank_top
entries.description: A blue [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top held up by shoulder straps, leaving the arms bare. It is cut wider and plainer than a [camisole](#camisole).

entries.name: grey_tank_top
entries.description: A grey [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [tank](#tank) top, worn alone or under an open [shirt](#shirt). It leaves the shoulders and arms uncovered.

entries.name: halter_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or top suspended from a [strap](#strap) around the [neck](#neck) with [no](#no) shoulder [fabric](#fabric), also called a halter top.

entries.name: sideless_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) cut open along its sides, baring the flanks and usually the [sideboob](#sideboob), sometimes covering little more than the [nipples](#nipples). A common design trick in gacha art for showing skin without [cleavage](#cleavage).

entries.name: cross-laced_top
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt), [bra](#bra) or similar upper garment laced with crossing cords, most often down the centre of the chest. One of the [cross-laced_clothes](#cross-laced_clothes) [family](#family).

entries.name: shirt_under_shirt
entries.description: One [shirt](#shirt) layered over another, such as a [t-shirt](#t-shirt) showing beneath an open or short-sleeved shirt. Tag both garments where they [can](#can) be identified.

entries.name: frilled_camisole
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) [carrying](#carrying) ruffled trim at the neckline, along the straps or around the hem. Worn as light innerwear under a [blouse](#blouse), or by itself as a [summer](#summer) top.

entries.name: loose_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) [hanging](#hanging) slack on the body without being blatantly too big. An obviously outsized one is [oversized_shirt](#oversized_shirt).

entries.name: green_tank_top
entries.description: A green [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [tank](#tank) top, worn alone or under an open [shirt](#shirt) or [jacket](#jacket). It leaves the shoulders and arms uncovered.

entries.name: polka_dot_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) printed with polka [dots](#dots). Tag shirt and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) alongside; a dotted [dress](#dress) is [polka_dot_dress](#polka_dot_dress).

entries.name: blue_camisole
entries.description: A mostly blue [camisole](#camisole), the thin-strapped [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top worn on its own or layered under something else. Its narrow straps and straight neckline distinguish it from a [tank](#tank) top.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) edged with fur at the [collar](#collar), [cuffs](#cuffs) or hem. Rarer than fur-trimmed outerwear, and usually part of a [costume](#costume) rather than everyday [dress](#dress).

entries.name: shirt_under_dress
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) layered beneath a [dress](#dress), with its [collar](#collar) and sleeves showing past the outer garment. A somewhat vague [label](#label) better replaced by [pinafore_dress](#pinafore_dress) or a skirt-and-vest description.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) finished with [lace](#lace) at the [collar](#collar), [cuffs](#cuffs) or hem. The lace is an edging on otherwise ordinary [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: checkered_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) [patterned](#patterned) in even alternating squares, from tiny [gingham](#gingham) up to broad blocks. Tartan and other crossing-line patterns are plaid instead.

entries.name: pink_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [tank](#tank) top in pink, held up by shoulder straps with [no](#no) sleeves at all. A pink [camisole](#camisole) or crop top takes its own garment [tag](#tag).

entries.name: white_tunic
entries.description: A white [tunic](#tunic), a loose top [falling](#falling) to the hips or [thighs](#thighs) and usually cinched with a [belt](#belt). It is standard [dress](#dress) across ancient, [medieval](#medieval), and [fantasy](#fantasy) settings.

entries.name: yellow_camisole
entries.description: A yellow [camisole](#camisole): a light [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top [hanging](#hanging) from thin shoulder straps. It may be worn as [underwear](#underwear) or on its own in warm weather, with only the colour setting it apart.

entries.name: single-shoulder_shirt
entries.description: A top cut on the diagonal so one shoulder is covered by a [strap](#strap) or sleeve while the other is bare. Not for a normal [shirt](#shirt) tugged off the arm, nor for an off-shoulder cut that exposes both sides.

entries.name: grey_camisole
entries.description: A grey [camisole](#camisole), the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top [hanging](#hanging) from narrow shoulder straps. It serves as [underwear](#underwear) or as a light layer under an open [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: white_undershirt
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) white [shirt](#shirt) worn under the outer clothing, often short-sleeved or [sleeveless](#sleeveless). It becomes visible through an open shirt or once the outer layer comes off.

entries.name: kariyushi_shirt
entries.description: An Okinawan [summer](#summer) [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt): short sleeves, an open [collar](#collar) and a bold local print of [fruit](#fruit), art motifs or guardian [lion](#lion) figures. It fills much the same role as a Hawaiian shirt.

entries.name: side-tie_shirt
entries.description: A top fastened with strings [running](#running) down its sides, so the front and [back](#back) panels join only where they are knotted. Skin shows through the gaps between the ties.

entries.name: shirt_under_sweater
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) layered beneath a [sweater](#sweater), with its [collar](#collar) and [cuffs](#cuffs) left showing at the [neck](#neck) and wrists. A [staple](#staple) of [school](#school) and [office](#office) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: red_camisole
entries.description: A red [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top hung from thin straps, cut straight across the chest. Worn either as an underlayer or on its own in [casual](#casual) and [loungewear](#loungewear) outfits.

entries.name: camouflage_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) of any cut printed in the [familiar](#familiar) mottled greens and browns. Worn buttoned, [hanging](#hanging) open over a tee, or tucked into matching trousers.

entries.name: purple_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) purple top with wide shoulder straps and a scooped [neck](#neck). Worn alone, or layered under an open [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: orange_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) orange [tank](#tank) top, close-fitting or [hanging](#hanging) loose. Worn alone, under an open [shirt](#shirt) or with the straps bare at the shoulders.

entries.name: floral_print_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) cut from flower-patterned [cloth](#cloth), from the loud holiday sort to small repeating sprigs. Printed [fabric](#fabric), not applied trim.

entries.name: hooded_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) with a [hood](#hood) attached, [lighter](#lighter) than a [hoodie](#hoodie) or a hooded [jacket](#jacket). The garment underneath is still an ordinary top.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) with [ribbon](#ribbon) banding along the [collar](#collar), placket, [cuffs](#cuffs) or hem. The band sits flat on the [fabric](#fabric) as a contrasting stripe.

entries.name: pleated_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) [carrying](#carrying) rows of narrow folds, most often as vertical columns flanking the button placket. Formal white shirts and [tuxedo](#tuxedo) fronts show it; a ribbed knit top is a different thing entirely.

entries.name: green_camisole
entries.description: A green [camisole](#camisole): a light [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top [hanging](#hanging) from thin shoulder straps. It may be worn as [underwear](#underwear), as [loungewear](#loungewear), or layered under an open [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: american_flag_shirt
entries.description: A top [patterned](#patterned) after the stars and stripes, whether [t-shirt](#t-shirt), [tank](#tank) or [blouse](#blouse). It often turns up beside matching [shorts](#shorts) or a [bandana](#bandana).

entries.name: backless_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) open right across the [back](#back), held on only by the [collar](#collar) or by straps at the shoulders. Seen from the front it reads as an ordinary top.

entries.name: purple_camisole
entries.description: A purple [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top hung from thin straps and cut straight across the chest. Worn on its own, or layered under something open.

entries.name: black_tunic
entries.description: A black [tunic](#tunic), the loose long-bodied [shirt](#shirt) [falling](#falling) to hip or thigh and often gathered with a [belt](#belt). Fantasy and historical settings account for most of it.

entries.name: purple_tunic
entries.description: A purple long top [reaching](#reaching) to the hip or thigh, often belted at the waist. Common in [fantasy](#fantasy), [medieval](#medieval), and adventurer outfits.

entries.name: polka_dot_camisole
entries.description: A thin strappy [camisole](#camisole) covered in round [dots](#dots), worn as a top or as an underlayer. The [spots](#spots) usually sit on a pale ground.

entries.name: brown_tank_top
entries.description: A brown [tank](#tank) top: [sleeveless](#sleeveless), with wide shoulder straps and a [plain](#plain) scooped [neck](#neck). Worn alone or layered under a [shirt](#shirt) or [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: band_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) printed with a [music](#music) group's [logo](#logo) or album artwork, sold as [merchandise](#merchandise) and worn as a [badge](#badge) of fandom. It is usually a [dark](#dark) tee with the design across the chest.

entries.name: striped_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [tank](#tank) top [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [tank_top](#tank_top).

entries.name: brown_tunic
entries.description: A brown [tunic](#tunic), the loose hip- or thigh-length top usually gathered at the waist with a [belt](#belt). Standard [dress](#dress) in [medieval](#medieval) and [fantasy](#fantasy) settings.

entries.name: print_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [tank](#tank) top [carrying](#carrying) a printed picture, letters or repeating design. The garment shape is unchanged; only the decoration on the [fabric](#fabric) matters here.

entries.name: striped_camisole
entries.description: A thin-strapped [camisole](#camisole) top with stripes across it.

entries.name: gradient_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) of any cut whose [fabric](#fabric) shades gradually from one colour into another, the fade usually [running](#running) from the shoulders down to the hem.

entries.name: diagonal-striped_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) whose stripes run at a slant instead of straight across or straight down. The slant is what sets it apart from an ordinary [striped_shirt](#striped_shirt).

entries.name: bow_camisole
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) [carrying](#carrying) a [bow](#bow), usually set at the middle of the neckline between the two straps. The bow is trim and not a fastening.

entries.name: lace-up_top
entries.description: A top closed with cord pulled through eyelets, usually across the chest or straight down the front. Peasant blouses, corset-styled tops and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume) use it constantly.

entries.name: brown_camisole
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) in brown, the light [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top [hanging](#hanging) from thin shoulder straps. It may sit under a [shirt](#shirt) or be worn alone.

entries.name: fuck-me_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) printed with the phrase fuck me or a variation on it, the wearer crudely advertising an interest in [sex](#sex). A joke garment rather than anything anybody sells as [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: argyle_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) [patterned](#patterned) with argyle diamonds, over the whole body of the garment or on a single panel. Both knitted shirts and printed [casual](#casual) ones count.

entries.name: print_camisole
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) with a printed motif on the front, the [back](#back), or both. The thin strappy cut is unchanged; only the decoration differs.

entries.name: aqua_tunic
entries.description: A loose blue-green top [falling](#falling) to the hips or [thighs](#thighs), often belted at the waist. Fantasy and [medieval](#medieval) designs use it most.

entries.name: orange_tunic
entries.description: An orange [tunic](#tunic), the long loose top [falling](#falling) to the hip or thigh and often belted at the waist.

entries.name: telnyashka
entries.description: The Russian striped [undershirt](#undershirt), white with horizontal bands, worn sleeved or as a [vest](#vest). The stripe colour marks the [branch](#branch): [dark](#dark) blue for the navy, light blue for the airborne, black for the naval infantry.

entries.name: zipper_top
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or crop top closed with a [zipper](#zipper) up the centre front instead of [buttons](#buttons), frequently drawn pulled partway down. The zip itself is the point of interest rather than a hidden fastening.

entries.name: asymmetrical_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) with its two halves cut or trimmed differently, such as a single long sleeve set against a bare arm, or a hem [sitting](#sitting) higher on one side.

entries.name: torn_tank_top
entries.description: A [tank](#tank) top ripped at a [strap](#strap), side seam or hem. Reads as rough wear, a struggle, or a deliberately distressed look.

entries.name: grey_tunic
entries.description: A grey [tunic](#tunic), the loose garment pulled on over the head and [reaching](#reaching) hip or thigh. Medieval and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits usually [belt](#belt) it at the waist.

entries.name: orange_camisole
entries.description: An orange [camisole](#camisole), the thin-strapped [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top, worn on its own, as [underwear](#underwear) or beneath an open [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: lace_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) cut from [lace](#lace), so the [fabric](#fabric) is open and partly sheer. It is commonly layered over a [camisole](#camisole).

entries.name: aqua_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top with shoulder straps in blue-green. Add [midriff](#midriff) or crop tags where the cut is short.

entries.name: pinstripe_camisole
entries.description: A strappy [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [undershirt](#undershirt) [patterned](#patterned) with narrow vertical lines. The stripes are the only thing separating it from a [plain](#plain) [camisole](#camisole).

entries.name: camouflage_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top printed in [camouflage](#camouflage), worn alone or under an open [jacket](#jacket). Bare shoulders and [dog](#dog) tags tend to come with it.

entries.name: blue_undershirt
entries.description: A blue [shirt](#shirt) worn as the layer beneath other clothing, its [collar](#collar), hem or sleeves showing past the outer garment. Only the part that peeks out is usually visible.

entries.name: shirttail
entries.description: The lower hem of a [shirt](#shirt), cut with a rounded dip front and [back](#back) so it sits tucked under a waistband. Comes into view when the shirt is untucked or worn with nothing below.

entries.name: babydoll_t-shirt
entries.description: A close-cut tee, narrow through the body, with a scooped [neck](#neck) and small capped sleeves [sitting](#sitting) high on the arm. It clings and ends near the waist, quite unlike a boxy unisex [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: aqua_camisole
entries.description: A thin strappy [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top in blue-green, worn as [underwear](#underwear) or as a light layer of its own. The colour [reading](#reading) of the [plain](#plain) [camisole](#camisole).

entries.name: grey_undershirt
entries.description: A grey [undershirt](#undershirt) worn beneath the outer layer, showing at the [collar](#collar), at the hem or through an open [shirt](#shirt). It is [plain](#plain) and functional rather than decorative.

entries.name: pink_tunic
entries.description: A pink [tunic](#tunic), the long shirt-like garment [reaching](#reaching) to the hip or thigh and often belted. Looser and longer than a [shirt](#shirt), but not a [dress](#dress).

entries.name: sweater
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) knitted or cotton top covering the [torso](#torso) and arms, sweatshirts included. A front-opening version is a [cardigan](#cardigan), a hooded one a [hoodie](#hoodie); add a colour or pattern [tag](#tag) such as [ribbed_sweater](#ribbed_sweater) alongside it.

entries.name: cardigan
entries.description: A light knitted [sweater](#sweater) open down the front, closed with [buttons](#buttons) or a zip. A [staple](#staple) of [school](#school) uniforms; add the colour variant such as [white_cardigan](#white_cardigan).

entries.name: sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knitted pullover worn over a [shirt](#shirt), closer in cut to a [vest](#vest) than a [sweater](#sweater). Common in [school](#school) uniforms and preppy outfits.

entries.name: ribbed_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) knitted with ribbing, [giving](#giving) fine vertical lines and a close, [clinging](#clinging) fit. The style is popular for showing off a [curvy](#curvy) [figure](#figure), and often appears as a [turtleneck](#turtleneck).

entries.name: turtleneck_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) with a high [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar) covering the [neck](#neck), the classic form of the [turtleneck](#turtleneck) garment. Implies sweater and turtleneck.

entries.name: white_sweater
entries.description: A knitted pullover in white, turtlenecks and ribbed styles included. Combine with [sweater](#sweater); a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) version is a [sweater_vest](#sweater_vest) instead.

entries.name: black_sweater
entries.description: A black knitted pullover with long sleeves, turtlenecked or otherwise. Sleeveless knits belong to [black_sweater_vest](#black_sweater_vest), and a buttoned front makes it a [cardigan](#cardigan) instead.

entries.name: brown_sweater
entries.description: A knitted pullover in brown. Add the shape too where it fits, such as [turtleneck](#turtleneck) or [ribbed_sweater](#ribbed_sweater).

entries.name: brown_cardigan
entries.description: A brown knitted [cardigan](#cardigan), worn open or buttoned over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). It is a [staple](#staple) of school-uniform and [autumn](#autumn) outfits.

entries.name: grey_sweater
entries.description: A knitted grey [sweater](#sweater), pulled on over a [shirt](#shirt) or worn alone. Sleeveless and open-fronted knits take [grey_sweater_vest](#grey_sweater_vest) or [grey_cardigan](#grey_cardigan).

entries.name: blue_sweater
entries.description: A knitted pullover in blue, worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or against the skin. A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knit is a [sweater](#sweater) [vest](#vest) instead.

entries.name: pink_sweater
entries.description: A knitted pullover in pink, worn on its own or over a [shirt](#shirt). Sleeveless knits are a [sweater](#sweater) [vest](#vest) and button-front ones a [cardigan](#cardigan).

entries.name: red_sweater
entries.description: A knitted [sweater](#sweater) in red, pullover or cardigan-style. Typical of [winter](#winter) and Christmas scenes; a red [hoodie](#hoodie) carries its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: off-shoulder_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) whose wide, often thickly banded neckline is meant to sit just under the shoulders, baring them and the upper chest; frequently a ribbed knit. A normal sweater pulled down, a shoulder cutout or a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) one worn with separate sleeves does not count.

entries.name: yellow_sweater
entries.description: A knitted yellow pullover. Tag [sweater](#sweater) alongside.

entries.name: pink_cardigan
entries.description: A knitted button-front [cardigan](#cardigan) in pink, worn open or fastened over a [shirt](#shirt). A [staple](#staple) of school-uniform and soft [casual](#casual) outfits.

entries.name: grey_cardigan
entries.description: A knitted grey [cardigan](#cardigan), generally open at the front over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). It is one of the commonest [school](#school) uniform layers.

entries.name: green_sweater
entries.description: A knitted green [sweater](#sweater), pulled on over a [shirt](#shirt) or worn on its own. Sleeveless and open-fronted knits take [green_sweater_vest](#green_sweater_vest) or [green_cardigan](#green_cardigan).

entries.name: yellow_cardigan
entries.description: A yellow knitted [cardigan](#cardigan), often left open over a [school](#school) [shirt](#shirt). Tag cardigan alongside.

entries.name: blue_cardigan
entries.description: A blue knitted [cardigan](#cardigan), worn open or fastened over a [shirt](#shirt) or a uniform. Its buttoned front separates it from a pullover [sweater](#sweater).

entries.name: black_cardigan
entries.description: A knitted [cardigan](#cardigan) in black, buttoned or [hanging](#hanging) open, often thrown over a [school](#school) uniform or [blouse](#blouse). Its sleeves may be pushed up or left long over the hands.

entries.name: sleeveless_sweater
entries.description: A knit [sweater](#sweater) with [no](#no) sleeves, sometimes worn with [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves) since the [tag](#tag) covers the [torso](#torso) piece only.

entries.name: aran_sweater
entries.description: A bulky fisherman's jumper covered in cable-knit panels across body and sleeves, traditionally in [cream](#cream) or undyed off-white. The [heavy](#heavy) raised texture is what identifies it.

entries.name: brown_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) brown knit worn over a [shirt](#shirt), whose sleeves show beneath it. Standard in [school](#school) uniforms and [office](#office) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: white_cardigan
entries.description: A white knitted [cardigan](#cardigan) worn open or buttoned over a [shirt](#shirt) or [dress](#dress), a common [school](#school) and [casual](#casual) layering piece.

entries.name: purple_sweater
entries.description: A purple knitted pullover, including [turtleneck](#turtleneck) and ribbed styles. Combine with [sweater](#sweater); a buttoned version instead is [purple_cardigan](#purple_cardigan).

entries.name: black_sweater_vest
entries.description: A black [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knit pulled on over a [shirt](#shirt). School and [office](#office) [dress](#dress) use it constantly as a middle layer.

entries.name: open-chest_sweater
entries.description: A ribbed [turtleneck](#turtleneck) [sweater](#sweater) with a large cutout across the chest, from a design that spread as a drawing challenge in [2014](#2014); also called the [keyhole](#keyhole) sweater. Reserve it for that garment or a deliberate reference to it, not for any sweater with a [hole](#hole) at the front.

entries.name: striped_sweater
entries.description: A knitted [sweater](#sweater) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes) and sweater.

entries.name: yellow_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) yellow knit [vest](#vest), commonly worn over a [school](#school) [shirt](#shirt). Tag [sweater_vest](#sweater_vest) as [well](#well).

entries.name: cropped_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) ending between chest and [navel](#navel), leaving the [midriff](#midriff) exposed. Often worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or above high-waisted bottoms.

entries.name: hooded_sweater
entries.description: A knitted [sweater](#sweater) with a [hood](#hood) attached. Close to a [hoodie](#hoodie), which is a hooded sweatshirt; use this one for a plainly knitted garment.

entries.name: orange_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) in orange, from a fine [turtleneck](#turtleneck) to a loose chunky knit. The [sleeveless](#sleeveless) form is [orange_sweater_vest](#orange_sweater_vest).

entries.name: red_cardigan
entries.description: A red knitted [cardigan](#cardigan) worn over a [shirt](#shirt), [blouse](#blouse) or [dress](#dress), buttoned up or [hanging](#hanging) open. Combine with cardigan and [open_cardigan](#open_cardigan) where they apply; a front-closed pullover is [red_sweater](#red_sweater) instead.

entries.name: short-sleeved_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) with short sleeves, typically layered over a [shirt](#shirt). Implies [short_sleeves](#short_sleeves) and sweater.

entries.name: green_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knitted [vest](#vest) in green, normally layered over a collared [shirt](#shirt). It is a [staple](#staple) of [school](#school) uniforms.

entries.name: purple_cardigan
entries.description: A purple knitted [cardigan](#cardigan), buttoned or left open over a [shirt](#shirt) or [dress](#dress). A pullover version with [no](#no) [opening](#opening) is [purple_sweater](#purple_sweater).

entries.name: blue_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) blue knit worn over a collared [shirt](#shirt), a standard layer in [school](#school) uniforms. The shirt sleeves underneath normally stay visible.

entries.name: grey_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knitted [vest](#vest) in grey, usually layered over a collared [shirt](#shirt). It is a [school](#school) uniform [staple](#staple).

entries.name: green_cardigan
entries.description: A knitted green [cardigan](#cardigan), normally open at the front over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). Buttoned or [hanging](#hanging) loose makes [no](#no) difference.

entries.name: two-tone_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) built from two clearly separated colours, [split](#split) by panel, sleeve or a broad band across the chest. Only two shades qualify for this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: argyle_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) knitted or printed with argyle diamonds, a classic preppy pattern. Raised [cable](#cable) [knitting](#knitting) is not argyle.

entries.name: pink_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knitted pullover in pink, worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). Standard in [school](#school) and preppy outfits.

entries.name: cardigan_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [cardigan](#cardigan) that [buttons](#buttons) up the front, cut like a [sweater](#sweater) [vest](#vest) but open down the middle. Frequently layered over a [school](#school) [shirt](#shirt) and tie.

entries.name: print_sweater
entries.description: A knitted [sweater](#sweater) bearing a design, [logo](#logo), or picture across the [fabric](#fabric). The motif [can](#can) be anything at all, and the [tag](#tag) says nothing about the sweater's cut or colour.

entries.name: purple_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) purple knit pulled on over a [shirt](#shirt), leaving the sleeves and [collar](#collar) showing underneath. A [school](#school) and preppy [staple](#staple).

entries.name: sweater_jacket
entries.description: A knitted top cut and closed like a [jacket](#jacket), with a zip or [buttons](#buttons) down the front and a proper [collar](#collar). Sits between a [plain](#plain) [cardigan](#cardigan) and a full [coat](#coat) in [weight](#weight) and [structure](#structure).

entries.name: red_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) red knit worn over a [shirt](#shirt), leaving the shirt's sleeves and [collar](#collar) showing. A common layer in [school](#school) and preppy outfits.

entries.name: impossible_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) moulded to the body the way an impossible [shirt](#shirt) is, [following](#following) every contour beneath. Do not [tag](#tag) the shirt as [well](#well) when the sweater covers its improbable parts.

entries.name: torn_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) with holes [opening](#opening) through the knit or unravelling at the [seams](#seams). Signals wear, hardship, or a rough scene rather than a tidy garment.

entries.name: aqua_sweater
entries.description: A knitted pullover in blue-green worn over the [torso](#torso). Add the knit or the neckline where either is distinctive.

entries.name: orange_cardigan
entries.description: An orange [cardigan](#cardigan), the button-front knit worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). Often [hanging](#hanging) loose or [sliding](#sliding) off one shoulder in [school](#school) scenes.

entries.name: sweater_around_neck
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) left unworn but knotted by its sleeves over the shoulders and across the chest, [hanging](#hanging) down the [back](#back). Reads as a preppy or [casual](#casual) styling [choice](#choice).

entries.name: ribbed_cardigan
entries.description: A button-front knitted [cardigan](#cardigan) whose [fabric](#fabric) is worked in vertical ridges. The ribbing catches the light in narrow stripes down the body and sleeves.

entries.name: christmas_sweater
entries.description: A knitted jumper covered in holiday motifs such as [reindeer](#reindeer), [snowflakes](#snowflakes) or fir trees. The deliberately garish versions worn as a joke belong here too.

entries.name: white_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knitted [vest](#vest) in white, pulled on over a [shirt](#shirt). It is standard issue on [school](#school) uniforms and a fixture of preppy outfits.

entries.name: backwards_virgin_killer_sweater
