entries.description: The backless halter [sweater](#sweater) put on the wrong way round, so the open panel falls down the chest and [stomach](#stomach) while the [neck](#neck) ties hang over the front. Whether the wearer meant to do it is generally the joke.

entries.name: aqua_cardigan
entries.description: A blue-green knitted [jacket](#jacket) fastening down the front, worn open or buttoned over a [shirt](#shirt). Standard over [school](#school) and [office](#office) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: collared_sweater
entries.description: A knitted top with a [collar](#collar) built into the neckline in place of a [plain](#plain) round or V [opening](#opening). The collar may be soft and [folded](#folded) or cut stiff like a shirt's.

entries.name: multicolored_sweater
entries.description: A knitted top [carrying](#carrying) two or more colours, from blocked panels and a [patterned](#patterned) yoke to contrasting [cuffs](#cuffs) and hem. How much second colour is needed follows [multicolored_clothes](#multicolored_clothes).

entries.name: unworn_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) is present in the picture without anyone wearing it, [folded](#folded), hung over a [chair](#chair) or bundled on a [bed](#bed).

entries.name: sweater_under_shirt
entries.description: An unusual layering order where a [sweater](#sweater) sits beneath a [shirt](#shirt) instead of over it, so the shirt becomes the visible outer layer. The knit shows only at the [collar](#collar) and [cuffs](#cuffs).

entries.name: vertical-striped_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) knitted or printed with stripes [running](#running) from shoulder to hem. The lengthwise direction is what marks it out, since knitwear is far more often banded across.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) [carrying](#carrying) fur trim, most often around the neckline or the [cuffs](#cuffs). A cosy, seasonal variation on ordinary knitwear.

entries.name: taut_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) drawn smooth and tight over the body, the strain in the knit most visible across the chest.

entries.name: knit_sweater
entries.description: A pullover with a visible knitted surface — cables, ribbing or chunky [stitches](#stitches) rather than a smooth [jersey](#jersey). It is often drawn oversized and set in cold-weather scenes.

entries.name: orange_sweater_vest
entries.description: An orange [sweater](#sweater) [vest](#vest), the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knitted pullover worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse).

entries.name: argyle_sweater_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knitted [vest](#vest) [patterned](#patterned) in argyle diamonds, usually pulled over a collared [shirt](#shirt) for a [school](#school) or preppy look. The shirt sleeves and [collar](#collar) beneath it are usually visible.

entries.name: unworn_cardigan
entries.description: A [cardigan](#cardigan) appears in the picture without anyone wearing it, tied around a [bag](#bag), laid over a [chair](#chair) or dropped nearby.

entries.name: striped_cardigan
entries.description: An open-front knitted [cardigan](#cardigan) striped, usually in horizontal bands.

entries.name: sweater_under_jacket
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) worn as a middle layer beneath a [jacket](#jacket), its knit [collar](#collar) or [cuffs](#cuffs) [peeking](#peeking) out at the edges. One of the standard cold-weather layering combinations.

entries.name: frilled_sweater
entries.description: A knitted [sweater](#sweater) with ruffles worked into the neckline, the [cuffs](#cuffs) or the hemline. Softens what would otherwise read as a [plain](#plain) [casual](#casual) garment.

entries.name: crop_top
entries.description: A short top, often [sleeveless](#sleeveless), cut to end above the [navel](#navel) so the [midriff](#midriff) is bare, sometimes far enough to show [underboob](#underboob). Add [crop_top_overhang](#crop_top_overhang) when the hem hangs loose off the body.

entries.name: front-tie_top
entries.description: Any top closed by [tying](#tying) its ends together in front of the chest — a [bikini](#bikini) top, a [bra](#bra), or a [shirt](#shirt) knotted up to bare the [midriff](#midriff). Purely ornamental bows and metal loops between the cups fall under it too.

entries.name: cropped_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) whose hem falls between chest and [navel](#navel), leaving the [midriff](#midriff) on show. The shirt version of a crop top; add its colour where that matters.

entries.name: tube_top
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) top made from a single stretchy band of [fabric](#fabric) across the chest, leaving the shoulders and upper chest bare. A narrower version is also a [bandeau](#bandeau), and one made from wrapped [bandages](#bandages) is a [sarashi](#sarashi).

entries.name: bandeau
entries.description: A narrow band of [fabric](#fabric) that covers the [breasts](#breasts) and nothing else, effectively a very short [tube](#tube) top. It turns up as a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) top, an undergarment and [casual](#casual) wear, sometimes [strapless](#strapless), sometimes front-tied or held by a halter [strap](#strap).

entries.name: crop_top_overhang
entries.description: A loose crop top whose hem stands out away from the body over the [midriff](#midriff) or [underboob](#underboob) instead of [clinging](#clinging) to it. Tight-fitting crop tops do not qualify.

entries.name: fishnet_top
entries.description: An upper-body garment made at least in part of [mesh](#mesh), worn on its own, over another top or beneath one. Skin shows through wherever the netting sits.

entries.name: black_tube_top
entries.description: A black [strapless](#strapless) band of stretchy [fabric](#fabric) worn around the chest. Shoulders and [midriff](#midriff) stay bare, since nothing holds it up but the fit.

entries.name: white_tube_top
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) white band of [fabric](#fabric) covering the chest. Tag [tube_top](#tube_top) alongside it; a [bandeau](#bandeau) [bikini](#bikini) top counts as swimwear instead.

entries.name: single_breast_curtain
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) panel of [cloth](#cloth) covering just one breast, leaving the other side of the chest bare or covered by something else. Typical of asymmetric [fantasy](#fantasy) and gacha costumes.

entries.name: black_bandeau
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) black band of [fabric](#fabric) wrapped round the chest, worn as a top on its own or as the upper half of a [swimsuit](#swimsuit). It leaves the shoulders and [midriff](#midriff) bare.

entries.name: white_bandeau
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) band of white [fabric](#fabric) worn across the chest, whether as a [casual](#casual) top or a [bikini](#bikini) top. Add bikini or strapless as fits the context.

entries.name: red_bandeau
entries.description: A red [strapless](#strapless) band of [fabric](#fabric) wrapped across the chest, held up by its own tension. Leaves the shoulders and [midriff](#midriff) bare, and doubles as swimwear in some outfits.

entries.name: yellow_bandeau
entries.description: A yellow strip of [fabric](#fabric) worn straight across the chest, with [no](#no) straps and no shaping. Seen both as a [summer](#summer) top and as part of swimwear.

entries.name: compression_shirt
entries.description: A skin-tight athletic top that presses on the muscles and pulls [sweat](#sweat) away from the skin. Worn under a [jersey](#jersey) or on its own while [training](#training).

entries.name: red_tube_top
entries.description: A red [strapless](#strapless) band covering the chest and [midriff](#midriff), held up without shoulder straps. Leaves the arms and shoulders entirely bare.

entries.name: blue_bandeau
entries.description: A blue band of [fabric](#fabric) wrapped straight across the chest with [no](#no) straps at all. It covers the [breasts](#breasts) alone, leaving the shoulders and [midriff](#midriff) bare.

entries.name: blue_tube_top
entries.description: A blue [strapless](#strapless) top gripping around the chest and leaving the shoulders and [midriff](#midriff) bare. Elastic holds it up, since it has [no](#no) straps at all.

entries.name: pink_tube_top
entries.description: A pink [strapless](#strapless) top [sitting](#sitting) as a band around the chest, leaving the shoulders bare. A colour variant of the ordinary [tube](#tube) top.

entries.name: flapper_shirt
entries.description: A top knotted at the front below the bust, its two halves then [falling](#falling) open to bare the [stomach](#stomach). The [cloth](#cloth) carries on past the knot, which is what tells it from a [cropped](#cropped) top.

entries.name: green_tube_top
entries.description: A green [tube](#tube) top, the [strapless](#strapless) band of stretchy [fabric](#fabric) worn around the chest. Held up by fit alone, it often comes with a shrug or an open [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: striped_bandeau
entries.description: A [bandeau](#bandeau), the [strapless](#strapless) band worn across the chest, [patterned](#patterned) with stripes.

entries.name: green_bandeau
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) green band of [cloth](#cloth) worn across the chest, with [no](#no) cups, straps or shaping. Worn on its own in [summer](#summer) outfits or under an open [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: purple_bandeau
entries.description: A purple strip of [fabric](#fabric) wrapped around the chest with [no](#no) straps or cups [holding](#holding) it up. Worn as a simple top on its own, or under something open.

entries.name: ribbed_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top in ribbed knit, the ridges [running](#running) from hem to shoulder [strap](#strap). The classic [plain](#plain) white version is the everyday [undershirt](#undershirt) cut.

entries.name: grey_tube_top
entries.description: A grey [strapless](#strapless) band of stretchy [fabric](#fabric) worn across the chest. It is held up by fit alone, with nothing crossing the shoulders.

entries.name: heart_ring_top
entries.description: An upper garment held together by a heart-shaped [ring](#ring), usually where the [fabric](#fabric) meets between or below the [breasts](#breasts).

entries.name: pink_bandeau
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) band of pink [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the chest, worn as a [bra](#bra) or as a very brief top. Nothing holds it up but the fit across the ribcage.

entries.name: purple_tube_top
entries.description: A purple [strapless](#strapless) top forming a band around the chest, held up by its own fit. Bares the shoulders and usually the [midriff](#midriff) as [well](#well).

entries.name: two-tone_tank_top
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top in exactly two colours, usually a body in one [shade](#shade) with contrasting straps or trim. Sports vests often follow this scheme.

entries.name: yellow_tube_top
entries.description: A yellow [tube](#tube) top, a [strapless](#strapless) band of [cloth](#cloth) worn across the chest.

entries.name: hooded_top
entries.description: Any upper garment [carrying](#carrying) a [hood](#hood), used where the exact cut is not worth naming. Reach for a narrower [tag](#tag) when the piece is clearly a [hoodie](#hoodie), [shirt](#shirt) or [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: frilled_tube_top
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) [tube](#tube) top finished with ruffles along its top or bottom edge. Summer, [festival](#festival) and [idol](#idol) outfits are where it shows up.

entries.name: brown_bandeau
entries.description: A brown [bandeau](#bandeau): a [strapless](#strapless) band of [fabric](#fabric) worn straight across the chest, without cups or shaping. It serves as either a top or as swimwear.

entries.name: orange_bandeau
entries.description: An orange [bandeau](#bandeau): a [strapless](#strapless) band of [fabric](#fabric) across the chest, worn as a top or as part of a [swimsuit](#swimsuit).

entries.name: grey_bandeau
entries.description: A grey [bandeau](#bandeau): a [strapless](#strapless) band of [cloth](#cloth) across the chest, worn as a top or as the upper half of a [bikini](#bikini). Nothing crosses the shoulders.

entries.name: orange_tube_top
entries.description: An orange [tube](#tube) top, a [strapless](#strapless) band of [fabric](#fabric) worn across the chest.

entries.name: brown_tube_top
entries.description: A brown [tube](#tube) top: a [strapless](#strapless) band of [fabric](#fabric) held up around the chest. Bare shoulders come with it by definition.

entries.name: vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless), collarless garment worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse), common as part of [school](#school) uniforms and [casual](#casual) outfits. The buttoned [suit](#suit) version is [waistcoat](#waistcoat).

entries.name: black_vest
entries.description: A black [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) worn over a [shirt](#shirt). Butler, [bartender](#bartender) and formal outfits rely on it heavily.

entries.name: shrug_(clothing)
entries.description: A garment made of just a pair of sleeves joined across the [back](#back) or by a [turtleneck](#turtleneck), worn over a top or drawn on its own as [lingerie](#lingerie). Differs from [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves), whose sleeves are not connected to each other; add [collared_shrug](#collared_shrug) when it has a [collar](#collar).

entries.name: red_vest
entries.description: A red [vest](#vest), the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) garment worn over a [shirt](#shirt), from a [waistcoat](#waistcoat) to a [casual](#casual) quilted vest. Tag vest as [well](#well).

entries.name: blue_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) blue [vest](#vest) worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse), whether a [school](#school) knit, a [leather](#leather) one or the [waistcoat](#waistcoat) of a formal [suit](#suit).

entries.name: green_vest
entries.description: A green [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) worn over a [shirt](#shirt), whether formal tailoring or a utility vest. It has [no](#no) sleeves, which separates it from a [green_jacket](#green_jacket).

entries.name: brown_vest
entries.description: A brown [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) worn over a [shirt](#shirt), in [leather](#leather), tweed or knit. Buttons down the front are typical.

entries.name: plaid_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) in plaid [fabric](#fabric), often worn over a [shirt](#shirt) as part of a uniform or formal outfit. Tag [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes) alongside it.

entries.name: grey_vest
entries.description: A grey [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) worn over a [shirt](#shirt) as part of a [suit](#suit) or uniform. Having [no](#no) sleeves is what separates it from a [grey_jacket](#grey_jacket).

entries.name: white_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) white [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) worn over a [shirt](#shirt). Tag vest alongside it; a knitted version is a [sweater_vest](#sweater_vest) instead.

entries.name: waistcoat
entries.description: A buttoned [vest](#vest) worn over a [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt) and tie, under a [suit](#suit) [jacket](#jacket) or [coat](#coat). The third piece of a three-piece suit and part of much formal wear; some [school](#school) uniforms include one.

entries.name: layered_clothes
entries.description: An outfit built from several separate garments worn over one another, such as a [jacket](#jacket) over a [cardigan](#cardigan) or a [shirt](#shirt) under a [dress](#dress). Add [layered_sleeves](#layered_sleeves) where more than one sleeve shows, plus the specific combination [tag](#tag).

entries.name: purple_vest
entries.description: A purple [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse), buttoned or left open. Combine with vest; a padded outdoor vest and a [sweater](#sweater) vest each take their own style [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: breast_curtains
entries.description: Two separate loose strips of [fabric](#fabric) hang over the [breasts](#breasts), generally weighted at the ends and ready to [swing](#swing) aside at any movement. The single-flap version is [breast_curtain](#breast_curtain).

entries.name: yellow_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) yellow [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat), including the high-visibility work kind. Tag vest alongside.

entries.name: black_shrug
entries.description: A black shrug, the [cropped](#cropped) bolero-style layer that reaches [no](#no) further than the shoulders and upper arms. Whatever is worn beneath it covers the [torso](#torso).

entries.name: white_shrug
entries.description: A short, open garment in white that covers only the shoulders and upper arms, worn over a [dress](#dress) or top. Tag [shrug_(clothing)](#shrug_(clothing)) alongside it; a bolero is a close relative.

entries.name: cropped_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) cut as short as a [cropped](#cropped) [jacket](#jacket), ending just under the chest and baring the [midriff](#midriff). Common in [dancer](#dancer), [idol](#idol) and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits.

entries.name: pink_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) in pink, generally worn over a [shirt](#shirt). A knitted one is a [sweater](#sweater) vest and takes that [tag](#tag) too.

entries.name: breast_curtain
entries.description: A top made of one loose flap of [cloth](#cloth) [hanging](#hanging) over the [breasts](#breasts) like a very short [tabard](#tabard), [unfastened](#unfastened) at the sides. Some are weighted at the hem so they do not [swing](#swing) open; two separate strips instead of one are [breast_curtains](#breast_curtains).

entries.name: bodice
entries.description: A fitted, often laced or boned garment worn over a [blouse](#blouse) to draw in the waist and support the bust, [familiar](#familiar) from European folk [dress](#dress) and dirndls. It resembles a [corset](#corset) but covers the [breasts](#breasts) as [well](#well).

entries.name: collared_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) or [waistcoat](#waistcoat) [carrying](#carrying) a distinct [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar) around the neckline. When that collar stands upright, [popped_collar](#popped_collar) fits as [well](#well).

entries.name: orange_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) in orange, from a knitted one over a [school](#school) [shirt](#shirt) to a high-visibility work vest. Worn undone it also takes [open_vest](#open_vest).

entries.name: blue_tabard
entries.description: A blue [sleeveless](#sleeveless) overgarment [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) over armour or a [tunic](#tunic) and open at the sides. A [crest](#crest) or [emblem](#emblem) is often [stitched](#stitched) across the chest.

entries.name: layered_shirt
entries.description: One [shirt](#shirt) worn over another, most often a short-sleeved one over a long-sleeved one. Add [short_over_long_sleeves](#short_over_long_sleeves) where that is the arrangement.

entries.name: purple_tabard
entries.description: A purple panel of [cloth](#cloth) [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) from the shoulders, open at the sides and usually belted. Worn over armour or robes in [fantasy](#fantasy) and heraldic [dress](#dress).

entries.name: red_tabard
entries.description: A red [sleeveless](#sleeveless) overgarment [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) from the shoulders, worn over armour or a [robe](#robe) and often bearing a [crest](#crest). Standard [dress](#dress) for knights, crusaders and [fantasy](#fantasy) orders.

entries.name: hooded_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) with a [hood](#hood) attached, sometimes a [hoodie](#hoodie) with the sleeves taken off. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) as [well](#well).

entries.name: striped_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes) and vest.

entries.name: white_tabard
entries.description: A white [tabard](#tabard), the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) overgarment [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) over armour or a [robe](#robe). Knights, crusaders, and clerical orders wear it, usually bearing a [device](#device) on the chest.

entries.name: collared_shrug
entries.description: A [cropped](#cropped) shoulder piece with a [collar](#collar) attached, [sitting](#sitting) somewhere between a detached collar and a short bolero. Coverage runs from the shoulders alone to most of the arms.

entries.name: aqua_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) in pale blue-green, worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or on its own. Only the [shade](#shade) is recorded; the cut and whatever is worn beneath keep their own tags.

entries.name: red_shrug
entries.description: A short red [cropped](#cropped) [jacket](#jacket) or knit that covers only the shoulders and arms, leaving the front open and the [torso](#torso) bare. Worn over dresses and camisoles as an accent layer.

entries.name: hooded_shrug
entries.description: A shrug, the tiny [cropped](#cropped) wrap covering only shoulders and arms, made with a [hood](#hood) on it. Not to be taken for a cropped hooded [jacket](#jacket), which closes over the chest.

entries.name: blue_shrug
entries.description: A [cropped](#cropped) blue [cardigan](#cardigan) covering little beyond the shoulders and arms and left [hanging](#hanging) open. It ends [well](#well) above the waist, which is what separates it from an ordinary cardigan.

entries.name: pinstripe_vest
entries.description: A [waistcoat](#waistcoat) [patterned](#patterned) with thin vertical lines, worn over a [shirt](#shirt). Typically part of a matching striped [suit](#suit).

entries.name: vertical-striped_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) down its length rather than across the chest. Turns up on waistcoats, uniform vests and [stage](#stage) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: two-tone_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) made up of exactly two colours, [split](#split) by panel, lapel or trim. Waistcoats with a contrasting [back](#back) are a typical case.

entries.name: frilled_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) trimmed with ruffles, worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). Often part of a uniform-styled or lolita coordinate.

entries.name: red_tunic
entries.description: A red loose-fitting garment [reaching](#reaching) to the hips or [thighs](#thighs), usually belted at the waist and worn over [leggings](#leggings) or trousers. Fantasy, [medieval](#medieval) and adventurer outfits use it constantly.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) edged with fur along the front [opening](#opening) or the armholes. Fantasy and cold-weather outfits favour it.

entries.name: orange_tabard
entries.description: An orange [tabard](#tabard), the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) panel [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) over the shoulders and often belted at the waist. Worn by heralds, guild members and [fantasy](#fantasy) soldiery.

entries.name: leather_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) hide garment worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or straight against the skin, generally black or brown. Strongly tied to bikers and western looks.

entries.name: torn_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) ripped along a seam or holed through a front panel. Marks the garment as [damaged](#damaged) rather than freshly worn.

entries.name: unworn_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) is present in the picture without being worn, hung on a [chair](#chair), [folded](#folded) or dropped nearby.

entries.name: black_tabard
entries.description: A black [tabard](#tabard), the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) panel [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) over armour or a [robe](#robe) and left open along the sides. Knights, clergy and [fantasy](#fantasy) soldiers wear it most.

entries.name: life_vest
entries.description: A buoyant [vest](#vest) worn on the [water](#water) to keep the wearer [afloat](#afloat), usually bright orange or yellow with webbing straps and buckles. Standard kit on boats and for naval aircrew.

entries.name: print_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) cut from [patterned](#patterned) [cloth](#cloth), floral [fabric](#fabric) being one common example. The pattern rather than the colour is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: orange_shrug
entries.description: An orange shrug, the [cropped](#cropped) open-front knit covering only the shoulders and upper arms, worn over a [dress](#dress) or top.

entries.name: camisole_over_clothes
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) worn on top of another garment instead of underneath it, layered over a [shirt](#shirt) or a [dress](#dress). The reversed order of the layers is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: denim_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [denim](#denim) [jacket](#jacket) worn open or buttoned over a [shirt](#shirt). Often covered in patches, [studs](#studs) or pins.

entries.name: checkered_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) cut from chequered [cloth](#cloth) and worn over a [shirt](#shirt). Uniforms, waiting-staff outfits and semi-formal ensembles all use them.

entries.name: green_tabard
entries.description: A green [tabard](#tabard), the open-sided garment [hanging](#hanging) over the front and [back](#back) of the body. It is usually belted at the waist over other clothing.

entries.name: no_vest
entries.description: The [vest](#vest) that normally goes over a character's [shirt](#shirt) has been dropped from the outfit. Everything worn beneath it stays as usual.

entries.name: impossible_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) curving round and under the [breasts](#breasts) instead of [hanging](#hanging) straight down as gravity would demand. It usually sits over a [shirt](#shirt) drawn just as improbably.

entries.name: cardigan_under_jacket
entries.description: A [cardigan](#cardigan) worn as a middle layer with a [jacket](#jacket) or [coat](#coat) over the top. Its hem and [collar](#collar) show at the edges of the outer garment.

entries.name: multicolored_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) cut in two or more colours, whether the panels differ, a contrasting lining shows, or the edges are picked out in another [shade](#shade). Follow [multicolored_clothes](#multicolored_clothes) for how much is enough.

entries.name: uniform_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) worn as part of an issued uniform, such as those layered over shirts in [school](#school), service or company [dress](#dress). Reads as institutional kit rather than a personal [fashion](#fashion) [choice](#choice).

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) with [ribbon](#ribbon) banding [running](#running) along its edges, usually the front [opening](#opening) and armholes. The trim reads as a contrasting [outline](#outline) of the garment's shape.

entries.name: overshirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) worn open as a light outer layer on top of another top, less structured than a [jacket](#jacket). Usually left [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) so the garment beneath stays fully visible.

entries.name: brown_tabard
entries.description: A brown [tabard](#tabard): a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) panel [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) over other clothing or armour, often belted at the sides. Heraldic and monastic [dress](#dress) both use it.

entries.name: pink_tabard
entries.description: A pink [tabard](#tabard), the panel of [cloth](#cloth) [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back) with the sides left open. Worn over armour or a [robe](#robe) and often [carrying](#carrying) an [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: yellow_tabard
entries.description: A yellow [tabard](#tabard) [hanging](#hanging) over the front and [back](#back) of the body with open sides.

entries.name: grey_tabard
entries.description: A grey [tabard](#tabard) [hanging](#hanging) over the front and [back](#back) of the body with the sides left open. It is normally belted at the waist over other clothing.

entries.name: skirt
entries.description: A separate garment [hanging](#hanging) from the waist over the [legs](#legs). A [dress](#dress) is one piece and is not tagged skirt; lengths are [miniskirt](#miniskirt), [medium_skirt](#medium_skirt) and [long_skirt](#long_skirt).

entries.name: pleated_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) sewn with regular vertical pleats, the standard skirt of Japanese [school](#school) uniforms. Pair it with a colour or pattern [tag](#tag) such as [plaid_skirt](#plaid_skirt) or [blue_skirt](#blue_skirt).

entries.name: black_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) in black, one of the most frequent uniform and [casual](#casual) bottoms. Add the shape with [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt), since the colour says nothing about the cut.

entries.name: miniskirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) ending [well](#well) above the knee, anywhere from mid-thigh to just below the [crotch](#crotch). Shorter still is [microskirt](#microskirt).

entries.name: blue_skirt
entries.description: A blue [skirt](#skirt) of any length, from a [miniskirt](#miniskirt) to a long [pleated](#pleated) one, and a fixture of [school](#school) uniforms. Add the cut as [well](#well), such as [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) or miniskirt.

entries.name: red_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt) in red, [plain](#plain) or [pleated](#pleated). Very common as the bottom half of a [school](#school) uniform; [tag](#tag) the cut too, such as [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt).

entries.name: plaid_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) in plaid or tartan, the [pleated](#pleated) checked skirt of countless [school](#school) uniforms. Tag [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes) alongside it, and [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) when the folds are visible.

entries.name: white_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) of any length in white, miniskirts included. Combine with skirt and add [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt) once the cut is clear.

entries.name: frilled_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) [carrying](#carrying) ruffles, either as a single trimmed hem or as tiers of gathered layers. If the garment is a [dress](#dress) rather than a separate skirt, [frilled_dress](#frilled_dress) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: green_skirt
entries.description: A green [skirt](#skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt), very often part of a [school](#school) uniform. Add [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) or miniskirt where the cut deserves [recording](#recording).

entries.name: pelvic_curtain
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) panel, usually rectangular, that covers the [crotch](#crotch) at the front, the [back](#back) or both while leaving the [thighs](#thighs) bare. Strongly associated with loincloths and with [china](#china) dresses slit high at the sides.

entries.name: grey_skirt
entries.description: A grey [skirt](#skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt), one of the commonest [school](#school) uniform colours. Add [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) or miniskirt where the cut deserves [recording](#recording).

entries.name: skirt_set
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) worn with a top in the same colour, print or pattern, forming a matched set. Many [serafuku](#serafuku) qualify.

entries.name: side_slit
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) or [skirt](#skirt) cut open along the side, on one leg or both, the classic [china_dress](#china_dress) feature. Two high slits on both sides may form a [pelvic_curtain](#pelvic_curtain); a slit that stops short of the hem is a [hip_vent](#hip_vent) instead.

entries.name: pink_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) in pink, miniskirts and [pleated](#pleated) [school](#school) skirts included. Where the pink piece is the lower half of a [dress](#dress), [pink_dress](#pink_dress) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pencil_skirt
entries.description: A narrow straight [skirt](#skirt) fitted closely over the hips and [legs](#legs), usually knee to mini length. Standard [office](#office) wear, and frequently part of a skirt [suit](#suit).

entries.name: high-waist_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose waistband rides high on the [torso](#torso), from [navel](#navel) [height](#height) up to just under the bust. It pairs naturally with tucked-in shirts and with suspender skirts.

entries.name: long_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose hem falls below the knee and [no](#no) higher than three quarters up the calf, sometimes right down to the [floor](#floor). Shorter [cuts](#cuts) are a [plain](#plain) skirt or a [miniskirt](#miniskirt).

entries.name: purple_skirt
entries.description: A purple [skirt](#skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt) in any [shade](#shade) from indigo to violet. Combine with skirt and the cut, such as [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt).

entries.name: brown_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) in brown, at any length. Very common in [school](#school) uniforms and [autumn](#autumn) outfits; add [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt) where they apply.

entries.name: suspender_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) held up by shoulder straps, known as a jumperskirt or JSK in lolita [fashion](#fashion), worn over a [blouse](#blouse) with a [petticoat](#petticoat) beneath. Implies skirt and [suspenders](#suspenders).

entries.name: microskirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) so short it exposes the [thighs](#thighs) and the lower part of the buttocks, along with any [underwear](#underwear) worn beneath. A [miniskirt](#miniskirt) sits above the knee but still covers the thighs.

entries.name: layered_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) made of several tiers of [fabric](#fabric) stacked one over another. The layers usually show at the hem as separate [falling](#falling) edges.

entries.name: yellow_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt) in yellow. Tag skirt and the cut.

entries.name: orange_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt) in orange, [familiar](#familiar) among other things as part of the Anna Miller [waitress](#waitress) outfit.

entries.name: showgirl_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) panel covering only the sides and rear while leaving the front open, usually worn over a [leotard](#leotard) or [swimsuit](#swimsuit) bottom. Worn over another skirt or [shorts](#shorts) it becomes an [overskirt](#overskirt) instead, and one that also covers the front is a [high-low_skirt](#high-low_skirt).

entries.name: unworn_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) present in the picture but not on anyone.

entries.name: medium_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) of roughly knee length, its hem [sitting](#sitting) between mid-thigh and the upper calf when worn normally. The middle point between short and long skirts.

entries.name: bubble_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose hem is turned [back](#back) and sewn underneath so the [fabric](#fabric) balloons out into a rounded puff. A retro [silhouette](#silhouette) tied to the 1950s, the 1980s and mid-2000s [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: striped_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies skirt and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: checkered_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) [patterned](#patterned) in alternating chequerboard squares, whether [pleated](#pleated), straight or flared. Tartan-style patterns of crossing lines belong to [plaid_skirt](#plaid_skirt).

entries.name: print_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) printed with a pattern or images such as leaves or flowers. Tag skirt with it; combine with [multicolored_skirt](#multicolored_skirt) only when the base [fabric](#fabric) has several colours.

entries.name: multicolored_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose [fabric](#fabric) carries two or more colours within a single layer. Where a [layered_skirt](#layered_skirt) has each tier in one flat colour, [tag](#tag) those colours separately instead — that arrangement does not qualify. The threshold for how much second colour is needed follows [multicolored_clothes](#multicolored_clothes).

entries.name: two-tone_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) in exactly two colours. Add the individual colour tags as [well](#well).

entries.name: aqua_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) in aqua, at any length. Add the cut, such as [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) or [miniskirt](#miniskirt).

entries.name: torn_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) with visible rips or a shredded hem.

entries.name: denim_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) made of [denim](#denim), generally short and blue with jeans-style topstitching, rivets and a front [fly](#fly). Reads as everyday [casual](#casual) wear rather than anything formal.

entries.name: overskirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) worn on top of another skirt or over trousers, very often open down the front so the layer beneath shows. It and [showgirl_skirt](#showgirl_skirt) are never used together.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose hem has a [ribbon](#ribbon) woven through slits in the [fabric](#fabric), [reading](#reading) as a line of dashes. Tag with skirt and [ribbon_trim](#ribbon_trim).

entries.name: vertical-striped_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose stripes run from waist to hem rather than around it.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) with a band of fur [running](#running) along its hem. A skirt cut from [pelt](#pelt) throughout is [fur_skirt](#fur_skirt).

entries.name: circle_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) spread flat into a full [circle](#circle) around the wearer like a disc, whether from its cut, a [kneeling](#kneeling) pose, a gust of [wind](#wind) or a view from directly above. It [can](#can) accompany [upskirt](#upskirt) where the [spreading](#spreading) exposes the underside.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) with [lace](#lace) [running](#running) along the hem. One cut entirely from lace is lace_skirt, and [frilled_skirt](#frilled_skirt) is a separate matter since [frills](#frills) need not be lace.

entries.name: polka_dot_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) covered in polka [dots](#dots). Tag skirt and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) with it; a dotted one-piece is [polka_dot_dress](#polka_dot_dress).

entries.name: belt_skirt
entries.description: Several belts strapped around the hips so that together they hang like a short [skirt](#skirt). Showgirl, [fantasy](#fantasy) and armoured designs use it; a [plain](#plain) [belt](#belt) [holding](#holding) up an ordinary skirt does not count.

entries.name: tutu
entries.description: The stiff, layered [ballet](#ballet) [skirt](#skirt) that juts out from the hips, or the softer [hanging](#hanging) version, worn over a [leotard](#leotard). A full ballet_dress with a [bodice](#bodice) attached is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: high-low_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) hem cut short at the front and long at the [back](#back). A front left wholly open makes it a showgirl skirt, and worn over other bottoms it is an [overskirt](#overskirt); a held or lifted hem only imitates the shape.

entries.name: bow_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) with a [bow](#bow) attached at the waist, hip, [back](#back) or hem. A large bow at the small of the back may be [back_bow](#back_bow) instead.

entries.name: half-skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) that covers only one leg, ending near the [crotch](#crotch) in front and [reaching](#reaching) partway down the other thigh, usually worn over [shorts](#shorts) or a shorter skirt. A skirt missing its whole front is [showgirl_skirt](#showgirl_skirt), and one short in front but long behind is [high-low_skirt](#high-low_skirt).

entries.name: skirt_under_dress
entries.description: A separate [skirt](#skirt) worn beneath a [dress](#dress), its hem showing below the dress line. Sometimes a layer of the design rather than two independent garments.

entries.name: two-sided_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose underside or lining is a different colour or pattern, seen when the [fabric](#fabric) flares. Implies [two-sided_fabric](#two-sided_fabric).

entries.name: overall_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) attached to the [bib](#bib) and shoulder straps of [overalls](#overalls), also sold as a salopette skirt. Straps without a bib panel make it a suspender skirt, and a pinafore [dress](#dress) is a third thing again.

entries.name: lowleg_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) worn low around the hips instead of at the waist, showing off the hip bones and usually the [midriff](#midriff), sometimes an edge of [underwear](#underwear) too. If it is short enough it may count as a [microskirt](#microskirt) as [well](#well).

entries.name: cross-laced_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) worked with crossing cords or ribbons, typically along a side seam or up the front panel. One of the [cross-laced_clothes](#cross-laced_clothes) [family](#family).

entries.name: wet_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) soaked with [water](#water) so it hangs [heavy](#heavy), darkens and sticks to the [legs](#legs). It sometimes turns partly [transparent](#transparent) as [well](#well).

entries.name: floral_print_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) made from [cloth](#cloth) [patterned](#patterned) with flowers, told from its [siblings](#siblings) by the motif rather than by the cut.

entries.name: side-tie_skirt
entries.description: A single panel of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the waist and knotted at the hip, often thrown on over a [bikini](#bikini) bottom as a separate piece. If the panel is [stitched](#stitched) to the [swimsuit](#swimsuit) rather than tied on, [bikini_skirt](#bikini_skirt) is the [tag](#tag) to use.

entries.name: pinstripe_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) woven or printed with fine vertical lines. Often worn with a matching striped [jacket](#jacket) as part of a [suit](#suit).

entries.name: gradient_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) whose colour fades from one [shade](#shade) into another down its length. White, grey and black count as parts of the gradient here, which is why it does not entail a multicoloured skirt.

entries.name: zipper_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) closed by a [zipper](#zipper), most often [running](#running) down one side or the front and occasionally all the way to the hem. It leaves a visible seam line down the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: black_overskirt
entries.description: A second [skirt](#skirt) layer in black worn over another skirt or a [dress](#dress), often open at the front or draped at the hips. Only the outer layer is black here; the skirt beneath keeps its own colour.

entries.name: crinoline
entries.description: A stiff hooped [cage](#cage) worn under a [skirt](#skirt) to hold its shape out wide. Sometimes drawn over the [clothes](#clothes) instead, as a decorative frame around a skirt or [leotard](#leotard).

entries.name: camouflage_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) cut from [camouflage](#camouflage) [cloth](#cloth), usually paired with military-styled tops and [boots](#boots). The pattern rather than the skirt's shape is what is recorded.

entries.name: leather_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) of tanned hide, most often black, short and fitted to the hips.

entries.name: blue_overskirt
entries.description: A blue outer [skirt](#skirt) layered above another skirt or a [dress](#dress), frequently open at the front or gathered up at the hips. Whatever it is worn over keeps its own colour [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hoop_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) pushed out into a wide [bell](#bell) by a frame of hoops worn underneath. Farthingales, panniers and crinolines are all versions of the same [construction](#construction) in different centuries.

entries.name: gingham_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) cut from checked [gingham](#gingham) [cloth](#cloth). Frequently paired with a [plain](#plain) [blouse](#blouse) for a [picnic](#picnic) or summer-holiday look.

entries.name: taut_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) pulled tight enough to [crease](#crease) between the [thighs](#thighs) and trace the shape of the hips, most often a [pencil](#pencil) skirt or a snug uniform skirt.

entries.name: rainbow_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) divided into panels or stripes that follow the order of the spectrum. Running the colors in chromatic sequence is what sets it apart from a merely multicolored skirt.

entries.name: grass_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) of dried [grass](#grass) or leaves [hanging](#hanging) in loose strands from a waistband. It belongs to [tropical](#tropical) and [island](#island) settings, and to hula [dancing](#dancing) in particular.

entries.name: flower_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) made of [petals](#petals) or cut so that it reads as a blossom around the hips. Fairy and nature-spirit designs favour it.

entries.name: argyle_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) [carrying](#carrying) crossed argyle diamonds, most often knitted or [pleated](#pleated). A pleated school-style skirt is the usual case.

entries.name: latex_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) of glossy rubber, usually short and tight across the hips. The stiff [shining](#shining) material reads quite differently from [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: diagonal-striped_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) [patterned](#patterned) with slanting bands, the stripes [wrapping](#wrapping) around the [cloth](#cloth) at an angle rather than ringing it horizontally. Any length or cut of skirt may carry it.

entries.name: fur_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) made wholly of fur, standard issue in [barbarian](#barbarian) and [tribal](#tribal) designs. A skirt merely edged with fur is [fur-trimmed_skirt](#fur-trimmed_skirt).

entries.name: asymmetrical_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) with an uneven hem, dipping low on one side and [riding](#riding) up on the other, or assembled from panels of unlike length.

entries.name: leaf_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or hip wrap assembled from leaves. It normally comes with the rest of an outfit of [foliage](#foliage) on [jungle](#jungle) and forest-spirit designs.

entries.name: belted_skirt
entries.description: An ordinary [skirt](#skirt) cinched with a [belt](#belt) at the waist or high on the hips. Here the belt is an accessory, unlike [belt_skirt](#belt_skirt) where the belts are the garment.

entries.name: button_up_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) closed down the front by a row of [buttons](#buttons) rather than a hidden zip.

entries.name: pumpkin_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) shaped like a [pumpkin](#pumpkin), rounding outward before gathering [back](#back) in at the hem, often with vertical ribbing. Common on Halloween and storybook-styled outfits.

entries.name: pants
entries.description: Trousers: a lower-body garment [running](#running) from the waist to about the ankles and covering each leg separately. Shorter [cuts](#cuts) are [shorts](#shorts) or [capri_pants](#capri_pants); add the colour [tag](#tag) and the specific type such as [jeans](#jeans) where they apply.

entries.name: black_pants
entries.description: Trousers in black, from slacks and [jeans](#jeans) to cargo and track styles. Only the leg garment's colour is claimed; short-legged versions take [black_shorts](#black_shorts) instead.

entries.name: white_pants
entries.description: Trousers of any cut colored white, from slacks to [jeans](#jeans). Use it alongside [pants](#pants); other colors have their own tags, such as [black_pants](#black_pants).

entries.name: blue_pants
entries.description: Blue trousers of whatever cut, most often [jeans](#jeans), uniform slacks or work trousers. Legwear ending above the knee takes the [shorts](#shorts) [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: jeans
entries.description: Trousers cut from [denim](#denim), most often blue or grey. Skinny and [torn](#torn) versions have tags of their own, and a denim garment ending above the knee counts as [shorts](#shorts).

entries.name: grey_pants
entries.description: Grey trousers of any style, from [suit](#suit) trousers and slacks to [sweatpants](#sweatpants). Legwear ending above the knee is [grey_shorts](#grey_shorts).

entries.name: overalls
entries.description: A [bib](#bib) with shoulder straps joined to trousers, [shorts](#shorts) or a [skirt](#skirt), classically blue [denim](#denim) and worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or against bare skin. Strapped garments lacking the bib panel are [suspender_shorts](#suspender_shorts) or [suspender_skirt](#suspender_skirt).

entries.name: brown_pants
entries.description: Trousers of any cut coloured brown, from chinos and corduroys to cargo [pants](#pants) and [leather](#leather). The [shade](#shade) runs from pale khaki through to near-black [chocolate](#chocolate).

entries.name: red_pants
entries.description: Long trousers in red, of any cut including [jeans](#jeans), slacks or track [pants](#pants). Short-legged bottoms are [red_shorts](#red_shorts) instead.

entries.name: green_pants
entries.description: Green trousers of any style, from cargo [pants](#pants) and [military](#military) [fatigues](#fatigues) to [plain](#plain) slacks. Legwear that stops above the knee is [green_shorts](#green_shorts).

entries.name: torn_pants
entries.description: Trousers with visible rips, whether by design or from damage.

entries.name: baggy_pants
entries.description: Trousers cut wide enough to billow around the [legs](#legs), from [harem](#harem) and cargo styles to loose [streetwear](#streetwear) [jeans](#jeans). They are often gathered in at the ankle.

entries.name: track_pants
entries.description: Loose athletic trousers worn for [jogging](#jogging) or warming up before exercise. Paired with a matching [jacket](#jacket) they form a [track_suit](#track_suit).

entries.name: blue_overalls
entries.description: Bib-and-strap trousers in blue, the buckled workwear pulled on over a [shirt](#shirt). Denim [farm](#farm) and [mechanic](#mechanic) versions are the usual sight.

entries.name: purple_pants
entries.description: Trousers of any cut in purple. Combine with [pants](#pants) and the style; short [legs](#legs) instead take [purple_shorts](#purple_shorts).

entries.name: high-waist_pants
entries.description: Trousers whose waistband sits high, anywhere from the [navel](#navel) up to just below the bust. The raised waistline is the whole point of the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: yoga_pants
entries.description: Tight, stretchy [pants](#pants) made for [yoga](#yoga) and exercise but often worn casually. Tag pants as [well](#well); [leggings](#leggings) are a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: striped_pants
entries.description: Trousers with a striped pattern. Implies [pants](#pants) and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: pink_pants
entries.description: Trousers of any cut in pink, from [jeans](#jeans) to slacks or track [pants](#pants). Shorter [legs](#legs) make them [pink_shorts](#pink_shorts) instead.

entries.name: capri_pants
entries.description: Cropped trousers finishing anywhere between just under the knee and a little above the ankle. Full-length trousers rolled up the shin are not these.

entries.name: orange_pants
entries.description: Trousers of any cut in orange, from [jeans](#jeans) to track bottoms. Shorter [legs](#legs) take [orange_shorts](#orange_shorts).

entries.name: sweatpants
entries.description: Soft, loose [jersey](#jersey) trousers made for comfort or exercise, usually with an elastic waistband and [cuffed](#cuffed) ankles. Worn [well](#well) beyond athletic settings as everyday [loungewear](#loungewear).

entries.name: yellow_pants
entries.description: Trousers of any style in yellow. Tag [pants](#pants) as [well](#well).

entries.name: puffy_pants
entries.description: Loose trousers that [balloon](#balloon) out along the leg before gathering at the ankle or knee, such as [harem](#harem) [pants](#pants) or a pumpkin-style breech. Short versions of the same cut are [puffy_shorts](#puffy_shorts).

entries.name: chaps
entries.description: Leather leg coverings hung from a [belt](#belt), with [no](#no) seat and no [crotch](#crotch) joining them. Cowboys wear them over trousers and fetish [fashion](#fashion) wears them over nothing, the bare rear being the giveaway.

entries.name: plaid_pants
entries.description: Trousers in plaid or tartan [cloth](#cloth), from punk-style tartan trousers to checked pyjama bottoms. Shorts in the same [fabric](#fabric) are [plaid_shorts](#plaid_shorts).

entries.name: single_pantsleg
entries.description: Trousers that [cover](#cover) one leg while the other side is cut away, sometimes as high as the [bikini](#bikini) line. A deliberate [asymmetrical_clothes](#asymmetrical_clothes) design rather than damage.

entries.name: torn_jeans
entries.description: Denim [jeans](#jeans) with rips, including the deliberately distressed [fashion](#fashion) kind.

entries.name: harem_pants
entries.description: Wide, puffy trousers drawn in tight at the ankle, frequently sheer, worn in bellydancer and storybook [harem](#harem) [dress](#dress). They billow [well](#well) away from the leg, unlike ordinary loose trousers.

entries.name: camouflage_pants
entries.description: Trousers printed with a disruptive [military](#military) pattern, most often in a loose cargo cut with thigh pockets. Any style of trouser in the pattern qualifies.

entries.name: leather_pants
entries.description: Trousers of tanned hide, frequently tight and glossy, at home on bikers and [rock](#rock) musicians. A very shiny skin-tight pair may be [latex](#latex) instead.

entries.name: vertical-striped_pants
entries.description: Trousers with stripes [running](#running) down the leg, from pinstripe [suit](#suit) trousers to bold circus-style patterns.

entries.name: white_leggings
entries.description: White [leggings](#leggings) stretched close over the [legs](#legs) from waist to ankle. Unlike [pantyhose](#pantyhose) they're opaque and worn as an outer garment.

entries.name: two-tone_pants
entries.description: Trousers in exactly two colours, [split](#split) by leg, by panel or by a contrasting side stripe. The colour count, not the pattern, is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: lowleg_pants
entries.description: Trousers made to sit around the hips and [thighs](#thighs) rather than the waist, baring the [midriff](#midriff). They sometimes reveal [underwear](#underwear) or the top of the buttocks.

entries.name: dress_pants
entries.description: Formal trousers of [wool](#wool) or a smooth synthetic, cut straight down the leg with a defined waistband, [belt](#belt) loops and a [fly](#fly). Often the lower half of a [suit](#suit).

entries.name: pants_under_skirt
entries.description: Full-length trousers worn beneath a [skirt](#skirt), so the two are layered. Leggings or [shorts](#shorts) under a skirt have tags of their own.

entries.name: cargo_pants
entries.description: Loose hard-wearing trousers with large [patch](#patch) pockets on the [thighs](#thighs), first made as work and [military](#military) wear. Usually khaki, [olive](#olive) or [camouflage](#camouflage).

entries.name: unworn_pants
entries.description: A pair of trousers present in the picture but not on any [legs](#legs), thrown over furniture, [folded](#folded) or crumpled on the [floor](#floor).

entries.name: pinstripe_pants
entries.description: Trousers with thin vertical lines [running](#running) their whole length, most often the lower half of a striped [suit](#suit). Any cut of trouser qualifies.

entries.name: black_overalls
entries.description: Bib-and-brace [overalls](#overalls) in black, the straps [running](#running) over whatever [shirt](#shirt) is worn beneath. The colour names the overalls only, so [tag](#tag) the top separately.

entries.name: aqua_pants
entries.description: Full-length trousers in blue-green or turquoise. Add the cut, from [jeans](#jeans) through to loose [harem](#harem) [pants](#pants).

entries.name: print_pants
entries.description: Trousers with a design printed over the [fabric](#fabric). Camouflage, florals and repeating graphics are typical.

entries.name: green_overalls
entries.description: Green dungarees: trousers with a [bib](#bib) front held up by two shoulder straps. Worn over a [shirt](#shirt), and associated with plumbers, farmers and manual workers.

entries.name: detached_pants
entries.description: Trouser [legs](#legs) [hanging](#hanging) on their own with [no](#no) waistband joining them, the same [idea](#idea) as detached sleeves worked below the [belt](#belt).

entries.name: asymmetrical_pants
entries.description: Trousers whose [legs](#legs) are deliberately unequal, one [running](#running) the full length while the other is [cropped](#cropped) at the thigh or absent altogether.

entries.name: bell-bottoms
entries.description: Trousers cut close through the thigh and flaring outward from around the knee, most often in [denim](#denim). Also called flares; a [flare](#flare) beginning only at the ankle is a boot cut, and the whole look is [bound](#bound) up with the 1960s and 1970s.

entries.name: multicolored_pants
entries.description: Trousers made up in more than one colour, divided by panels, stripes or contrasting sections down the [legs](#legs). Track and [racing](#racing) wear supplies many of them.

entries.name: pants_under_dress
entries.description: Trousers worn beneath a [dress](#dress) or a long [tunic](#tunic), showing at the hem or through a side slit. A practical layer common in [fantasy](#fantasy) and traditional outfits.

entries.name: brown_overalls
entries.description: Brown bib-and-brace [overalls](#overalls): trousers with a chest panel held up on shoulder straps. Standard workwear, and the stock look for farmers and mechanics.

entries.name: grey_overalls
entries.description: Grey dungarees with a [bib](#bib) front and shoulder straps worn over a [shirt](#shirt). They read as workwear far more often than as [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: yellow_overalls
entries.description: Yellow dungarees: trousers with a [bib](#bib) front held up by shoulder straps. Worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or straight against the skin.

entries.name: latex_pants
entries.description: Trousers cut from shiny rubber, hugging the [legs](#legs) with a near [mirror](#mirror) sheen. They are drawn skin-tight rather than loose.

entries.name: white_overalls
entries.description: White dungarees, trousers with a [bib](#bib) front and shoulder straps. Painters, farmers and mechanics wear them, but they also turn up as [casual](#casual) [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: torn_leggings
entries.description: Leggings laddered, holed or [split](#split) along the leg.

entries.name: red_overalls
entries.description: Red dungarees with a [bib](#bib) front held up by shoulder straps that [buckle](#buckle) at the chest. Worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or on bare skin, in workwear and [casual](#casual) outfits alike.

entries.name: pink_overalls
entries.description: Dungarees in pink: trousers with a [bib](#bib) front held up by shoulder straps. Worn over a [shirt](#shirt), or over very little in [casual](#casual) art.

entries.name: denim_overalls
entries.description: Bib-and-brace trousers in blue [denim](#denim), the straps buckled over the shoulders. Worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or against bare skin, and [reading](#reading) as [farm](#farm), [workshop](#workshop) or easy [casual](#casual) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: pants_under_shorts
entries.description: Full-length trousers worn under a pair of [shorts](#shorts), both garments visible at once. A deliberate layered look rather than an [accident](#accident) of [dressing](#dressing).

entries.name: fur-trimmed_pants
entries.description: Trousers edged with fur, typically at the [cuffs](#cuffs) or around the waistband. Part of [winter](#winter) and [tribal](#tribal) [costume](#costume) designs.

entries.name: red_leggings
entries.description: Stretch trousers in red that cling from waist to ankle. They are opaque, unlike red [pantyhose](#pantyhose), and worn as an outer garment.

entries.name: purple_overalls
entries.description: Purple trousers with a [bib](#bib) front held up by shoulder straps. Work wear, [farm](#farm) wear, and [casual](#casual) outfits all share the cut.

entries.name: orange_overalls
entries.description: Bib-and-brace [overalls](#overalls) in orange, the straps crossing the shoulders and buckling at the chest. Worn over a [shirt](#shirt) or against bare skin.

entries.name: gradient_pants
entries.description: Trousers whose colour shifts gradually down the leg, usually paling toward the ankles rather than changing around the leg.

entries.name: pleated_pants
entries.description: Trousers with folds sewn in below the waistband that open downward over the front of each leg. Standard on [suit](#suit) and uniform trousers, and they drape looser than a flat front.

entries.name: jodhpurs
entries.description: Riding trousers cut wide at hip and thigh and tight from knee to ankle, made to [disappear](#disappear) into [tall](#tall) [boots](#boots). Cavalry and officer [dress](#dress) are their strongest association.

entries.name: american_flag_pants
entries.description: Trousers printed with the stars and stripes, from full-length [jeans](#jeans) to [leggings](#leggings). The pattern may [cover](#cover) both [legs](#legs) or run as bands with a star [field](#field) at the hip.

entries.name: pumpkin-shaped_pants
entries.description: Short trousers that [bulge](#bulge) into a rounded [gourd](#gourd) shape at the thigh, or are simply coloured to suggest one. A [staple](#staple) of Renaissance-style and Halloween outfits.

entries.name: frilled_pants
entries.description: Trousers [carrying](#carrying) ruffled trim, generally at the cuff or [running](#running) down the outer seam. Uncommon enough that the ruffles are clearly the point of the design.

entries.name: cross-laced_pants
entries.description: Trousers closed by [laces](#laces) crossing between eyelets, either at the [fly](#fly) or along the outer seam. A recurring feature of [pirate](#pirate) and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: loose_pants
entries.description: Trousers so baggy and slack at the waist that they look ready to [slide](#slide) off, yet somehow stay put. The slackness is the point, not the length or the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: wet_pants
entries.description: Trousers soaked with [water](#water), darkened and sticking to the [legs](#legs). Read as wetness from outside; an [accident](#accident) has its own separate wording.

entries.name: polka_dot_pants
entries.description: Trousers printed with round [dots](#dots) down the [legs](#legs). Reads either as [loungewear](#loungewear) or as a deliberately loud [fashion](#fashion) [choice](#choice).

entries.name: print_leggings
entries.description: Leggings covered in a printed pattern, hearts, stars and [animal](#animal) [markings](#markings) being the common choices. The design runs over the whole leg rather than [sitting](#sitting) at the cuff.

entries.name: skinny_jeans
entries.description: Denim trousers cut tight all the way down so they trace the shape of the leg. The opposite end of the scale from loose or baggy [pants](#pants).

entries.name: shorts
entries.description: Trousers cut short so part of the [legs](#legs) stays uncovered. State tags include [open_shorts](#open_shorts), [shorts_pull](#shorts_pull), [shorts_aside](#shorts_aside) and [shorts_around_one_leg](#shorts_around_one_leg).

entries.name: short_shorts
entries.description: Shorts with a very short inseam, leaving most of the leg bare, also called [hot](#hot) [pants](#pants). A longer cut is [plain](#plain) [shorts](#shorts), and a shorter one still is [micro_shorts](#micro_shorts). Implies shorts.

entries.name: black_shorts
entries.description: Shorts in black, whether cut-off [denim](#denim), athletic or [dolphin](#dolphin) [shorts](#shorts). Japanese [gym](#gym) shorts carry the [buruma](#buruma) [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: bike_shorts
entries.description: Tight stretch [shorts](#shorts) [reaching](#reaching) about mid-thigh, worn for sport, under a [skirt](#skirt) to keep [underwear](#underwear) hidden, or as everyday wear. Known in Japan as spats; the [old](#old) shoe covering of that name is spats_(footwear).

entries.name: blue_shorts
entries.description: Blue [shorts](#shorts) of any style, from cut-off [denim](#denim) to athletic pairs, ending above the knee. Gym [bloomers](#bloomers) are a garment of their own and take a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: white_shorts
entries.description: Shorts of any cut or length coloured white. Combine with [shorts](#shorts), and add a style [tag](#tag) such as [denim](#denim) or [gym](#gym) shorts once the cut is distinct.

entries.name: denim_shorts
entries.description: Shorts cut from [denim](#denim), frequently [cutoffs](#cutoffs) left with a frayed hem and known as [daisy](#daisy) dukes when very short. A [staple](#staple) of [casual](#casual) [summer](#summer) and pin-up [dress](#dress).

entries.name: red_shorts
entries.description: Shorts of any cut in red, from [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) to [denim](#denim) [cutoffs](#cutoffs). Full-length trousers are [red_pants](#red_pants) instead.

entries.name: grey_shorts
entries.description: Grey [shorts](#shorts) of any style, whether [gym](#gym) shorts or tailored ones. Full-length legwear takes [grey_pants](#grey_pants).

entries.name: brown_shorts
entries.description: Shorts in brown, from khaki cargo [cuts](#cuts) to short [leather](#leather) ones. Neither length nor style matters to the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: micro_shorts
entries.description: Shorts so tiny they could pass for [panties](#panties), worn as outerwear, as [bikini](#bikini) bottoms, or as boyshort-style [underwear](#underwear). Very short but loose [shorts](#shorts) belong under [short_shorts](#short_shorts) instead.

entries.name: green_shorts
entries.description: Green [shorts](#shorts) of any style, whether [gym](#gym) shorts, [denim](#denim) cut-offs or tailored shorts. Full-length legwear takes [green_pants](#green_pants).

entries.name: cutoffs
entries.description: Shorts of [denim](#denim) whose bottom edge is [unfinished](#unfinished) and often fraying, whether the [legs](#legs) were really cut from [jeans](#jeans) or the garment was made to look that way. The same ragged edge on other denim pieces, such as single-leg trousers, is tagged here too.

entries.name: shorts_under_skirt
entries.description: Shorts worn beneath a [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress), now common with Japanese [school](#school) uniforms: knee-length [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) or shorter sport shorts, with a tomboyish variant called [bike_shorts_under_skirt](#bike_shorts_under_skirt). Implies shorts.

entries.name: dolphin_shorts
entries.description: Very short athletic [shorts](#shorts) with notched side [seams](#seams), normally one flat colour with contrasting trim and a [drawstring](#drawstring) at the waist. A distinct cut from [gym_shorts](#gym_shorts).

entries.name: white_bloomers
entries.description: Bloomers in white, whether the puffy Victorian [underwear](#underwear) style [peeking](#peeking) under a [skirt](#skirt) or the athletic [buruma](#buruma).

entries.name: red_buruma
entries.description: Tight red [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of the Japanese [buruma](#buruma) cut, usually worn with a gym uniform top. Pair with buruma and [gym_uniform](#gym_uniform); the loose Victorian-style [bloomers](#bloomers) are a different garment entirely.

entries.name: yellow_shorts
entries.description: Shorts in yellow, of any length. Tag [shorts](#shorts) alongside.

entries.name: pink_shorts
entries.description: Shorts in pink at any length or cut, from athletic [shorts](#shorts) to [denim](#denim) cut-offs. Full-length trousers are [pink_pants](#pink_pants).

entries.name: bike_shorts_under_skirt
entries.description: Bike [shorts](#shorts) worn beneath a [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress), coming into view when the hem lifts or rides up. The modest answer to a [pantyshot](#pantyshot).

entries.name: high-waist_shorts
entries.description: Shorts cut with the waistband up at the [navel](#navel), sometimes as far as the [ribs](#ribs). A tucked-in or [cropped](#cropped) top usually goes with them.

entries.name: gym_shorts
entries.description: Loose exercise [shorts](#shorts) with straight waist and hem lines, [plain](#plain) or with side stripes, as worn in a [gym](#gym) uniform. Not [dolphin_shorts](#dolphin_shorts), which are a different cut.

entries.name: purple_shorts
entries.description: Shorts of any cut in purple, from [denim](#denim) [cutoffs](#cutoffs) to athletic [shorts](#shorts). Combine with shorts and the style, such as [short_shorts](#short_shorts) or [bike_shorts](#bike_shorts); full-length trousers instead are [purple_pants](#purple_pants).

entries.name: suspender_shorts
entries.description: Shorts fitted with suspender straps attached to the waistband. Implies [shorts](#shorts) and [suspenders](#suspenders).

entries.name: orange_shorts
entries.description: Shorts in orange, whether athletic, [denim](#denim) cut-offs or tailored. Full-length [legs](#legs) take [orange_pants](#orange_pants).

entries.name: torn_shorts
entries.description: Shorts with visible rips, by design or from damage.

entries.name: shorts_over_leggings
entries.description: Shorts worn over a pair of [leggings](#leggings), so the tight leg covering continues on below the hem. A common [casual](#casual) or sporty layering [choice](#choice).

entries.name: shorts_over_legwear
entries.description: The general term for any legwear worn beneath a pair of [shorts](#shorts), whether tights, [leggings](#leggings) or stockings. Where the layer is specifically sheer hosiery, the narrower [shorts_over_pantyhose](#shorts_over_pantyhose) applies.

entries.name: shorts_over_pantyhose
entries.description: Sheer hosiery worn beneath a pair of [shorts](#shorts), leaving the [legs](#legs) covered from the hem downward, distinct from thicker, opaque [leggings](#leggings) worn the same way.

entries.name: puffy_shorts
entries.description: Shorts that [balloon](#balloon) out from the waist more than an ordinary pair, often gathered at the hem in the manner of [bloomers](#bloomers) or [pumpkin](#pumpkin) [pants](#pants). Full-length versions of the same cut are [puffy_pants](#puffy_pants).

entries.name: striped_shorts
entries.description: Shorts marked with a striped pattern. Implies [shorts](#shorts) and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: black_buruma
entries.description: Buruma in black, the tight Japanese [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) worn with a gym [shirt](#shirt). Not the same thing as Western [bloomers](#bloomers), which are loose and gathered.

entries.name: frilled_shorts
entries.description: Shorts of any cut decorated with ruffles, most often along the hem. Keep apart from [frilled_skirt](#frilled_skirt) and from [bloomers](#bloomers), which are separate garments.

entries.name: overall_shorts
entries.description: Overalls whose [legs](#legs) stop above the knee, keeping the [bib](#bib) and shoulder straps of the full-length garment. Warm-weather wear, often drawn on children and on workers.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_shorts
entries.description: Shorts edged with fur around the waistband or the leg hems. Christmas and [winter](#winter) costumes account for most of them.

entries.name: shorts_under_dress
entries.description: Shorts worn underneath a [dress](#dress). Implies dress; the [skirt](#skirt) version of the same layering is [shorts_under_skirt](#shorts_under_skirt).

entries.name: vertical-striped_shorts
entries.description: Shorts with stripes [running](#running) top to bottom. Add the [shorts](#shorts)' colour tags.

entries.name: side_slit_shorts
entries.description: Shorts with a slit cut into the side seam, whether tiny or [reaching](#reaching) the waistband. Tagged alongside [shorts](#shorts) and [side_slit](#side_slit).

entries.name: exposed_pocket
entries.description: Cutoffs or [denim](#denim) [shorts](#shorts) cut so short that the pale [pocket](#pocket) linings hang out below the hem. A detail of very short shorts, and usually seen together with them.

entries.name: print_shorts
entries.description: Shorts of any style [carrying](#carrying) a printed design anywhere on the [fabric](#fabric). Tag [shorts](#shorts) alongside.

entries.name: bike_shorts_under_shorts
entries.description: Tight bike [shorts](#shorts) worn beneath a looser pair, the stretch [fabric](#fabric) showing below the outer hem. A sporty layering seen on [gym](#gym) and [casual](#casual) outfits.

entries.name: pleated_shorts
entries.description: Short trousers whose [fabric](#fabric) is [folded](#folded) into creases, so the leg flares out like a small [skirt](#skirt). Frequently part of [school](#school), cheer, or sports outfits.

entries.name: unworn_shorts
entries.description: A pair of [shorts](#shorts) visible in the picture but not being worn, dropped on the [floor](#floor), [folded](#folded) or slung over something.

entries.name: aqua_shorts
entries.description: Short trousers in blue-green, in any cut from [denim](#denim) to athletic. Add [short_shorts](#short_shorts) or [bike_shorts](#bike_shorts) where they apply.

entries.name: two-tone_shorts
entries.description: Shorts made up of exactly two colours, [split](#split) by panel, leg or waistband. Sports [shorts](#shorts) with a contrasting side stripe are a common example.

entries.name: plaid_shorts
entries.description: Shorts of any cut made from tartan [cloth](#cloth). Both [casual](#casual) [summer](#summer) wear and [school](#school) uniforms use them.

entries.name: torn_bike_shorts
entries.description: Bike [shorts](#shorts) [split](#split) or shredded, whether cut that way by design or [damaged](#damaged) in the scene.

entries.name: lowleg_shorts
entries.description: Shorts with a very low waistline [resting](#resting) on the hips, baring much of the lower [belly](#belly) and the top of the [groin](#groin). It is the rise that the [tag](#tag) records, not the leg length.

entries.name: multicolored_shorts
entries.description: Shorts made up in two or more colours, whether panelled, striped or trimmed in a contrasting [shade](#shade). Sportswear supplies most examples.

entries.name: cargo_shorts
entries.description: Loose [shorts](#shorts) [reaching](#reaching) to just above the knee, with big [patch](#patch) pockets down the outside of each leg. Summer [casual](#casual) wear with an outdoor look.

entries.name: shorts_under_shorts
entries.description: Two pairs of [shorts](#shorts) worn at once, most often snug cycling shorts [peeking](#peeking) out beneath a looser outer pair, usually showing only at the hem.

entries.name: cutoff_jeans
entries.description: Denim [shorts](#shorts) made by [cutting](#cutting) the [legs](#legs) off a pair of [jeans](#jeans), so the hem is left raw and fraying on purpose. The length varies; a short enough pair also counts as [short_shorts](#short_shorts).

entries.name: camouflage_shorts
entries.description: Shorts printed in a disruptive [military](#military) pattern, frequently with cargo pockets down the leg. Summer wear for a soldierly look.

entries.name: black_bloomers
entries.description: Loose gathered [shorts](#shorts) in black, [cuffed](#cuffed) at the thigh. Worn as [gym](#gym) wear or as a covering layer beneath a [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: cross-laced_shorts
entries.description: Shorts laced with cords or ribbons crossing over the front, the hip or the leg [opening](#opening). The lacing may tighten the fit or serve purely as trim.

entries.name: pink_bloomers
entries.description: Loose gathered [shorts](#shorts) drawn in at the thigh, here in pink. Worn as period [underwear](#underwear) or as part of an old-fashioned [gym](#gym) kit.

entries.name: culottes
entries.description: Wide-legged trousers tailored to hang like a [skirt](#skirt), also called a divided skirt. The [split](#split) between the [legs](#legs) stays visible, unlike a skort, where an outer panel hides it.

entries.name: baggy_shorts
entries.description: Shorts cut wide and loose, the [fabric](#fabric) [standing](#standing) away from the [thighs](#thighs) rather than [following](#following) them. Skate and [streetwear](#streetwear) styling favours the shape.

entries.name: wet_shorts
entries.description: Shorts soaked with [water](#water) or a similar [liquid](#liquid), darkened and [clinging](#clinging) to the [legs](#legs). Beaches, pools and downpours provide the soaking.

entries.name: leather_shorts
entries.description: Short trousers cut from hide, usually [dark](#dark) and close over the hips.

entries.name: polka_dot_shorts
entries.description: Short trousers covered in round [dots](#dots). Most often part of a [summer](#summer) outfit or a [sleepwear](#sleepwear) set.

entries.name: striped_bike_shorts
entries.description: Tight thigh-length cycling [shorts](#shorts) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes, worn alone or under a [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: orange_buruma
entries.description: Orange [buruma](#buruma), the snug [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of Japanese [school](#school) sports kit. Usually seen with a gym [shirt](#shirt) and indoor [shoes](#shoes).

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_shorts
entries.description: Shorts of any cut with a [ribbon](#ribbon) band around the waist, along the leg openings, or both. The trim is what sets them apart from [plain](#plain) [shorts](#shorts).

entries.name: highleg_buruma
entries.description: Gym [shorts](#shorts) of the [buruma](#buruma) cut with the leg openings raised [well](#well) above the [crease](#crease) of the hip, so hip and thigh are largely uncovered. The exaggerated cut is all that separates them from ordinary buruma.

entries.name: taut_shorts
entries.description: Shorts plainly too small for the wearer, [seams](#seams) straining across the hips and seat. They often overlap with very short [shorts](#shorts).

entries.name: bow_bloomers
entries.description: Loose gathered [bloomers](#bloomers) trimmed with a [bow](#bow), at the waistband or at the cuff of each leg. The bow is decoration rather than a [working](#working) tie.

entries.name: white_buruma
entries.description: White [gym](#gym) [bloomers](#bloomers), the tight elasticated [shorts](#shorts) of an older Japanese PE kit. Almost always paired with a matching gym [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: side-tie_shorts
