entries.description: Shorts closed with [laces](#laces) or ribbons at the hips instead of a [stitched](#stitched) seam. The knots sit high on the sides and the [fabric](#fabric) gaps slightly between them.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_shorts
entries.description: Shorts edged with [lace](#lace) at the leg openings or the waistband. They show up on frilly [loungewear](#loungewear) and on drawers worn beneath skirts.

entries.name: yellow_buruma
entries.description: Yellow [buruma](#buruma), the tight [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of Japanese [school](#school) [sportswear](#sportswear).

entries.name: brown_buruma
entries.description: Buruma in brown, the tight high-cut [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of Japanese [school](#school) [sportswear](#sportswear). Colour variant of the standard pair.

entries.name: dress
entries.description: One garment joining [bodice](#bodice) and [skirt](#skirt), with a top edge rising far enough to hide most of the chest. A separate top worn over a skirt, or a piece that begins below the [breasts](#breasts), is a skirt instead.

entries.name: white_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is mostly white in color, from sundresses to gowns. Add the specific style, such as [sundress](#sundress) or [wedding_dress](#wedding_dress), and any pattern.

entries.name: black_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is chiefly black, from a small [cocktail](#cocktail) dress to a gothic [gown](#gown) or a maid's frock. Add the style, such as [sundress](#sundress) or gown, wherever it is clear.

entries.name: sleeveless_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with [no](#no) attached sleeves, though [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves) may be worn with it. A wide neckline with sleeves on the arms is an [off-shoulder_dress](#off-shoulder_dress) and no shoulder support at all a [strapless_dress](#strapless_dress); the three exclude each other.

entries.name: blue_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that reads mainly blue, anywhere from a pale [sundress](#sundress) to a navy [evening](#evening) [gown](#gown). Its cut and length are recorded by separate tags.

entries.name: frilled_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) decorated with ruffles, whether a single trimmed hem or layer upon layer of them. Central to lolita, [maid](#maid) and doll-styled designs.

entries.name: red_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is mostly red. Combine with dress and the cut, such as [china_dress](#china_dress) or [gown](#gown).

entries.name: short_dress
entries.description: A one-piece [dress](#dress) whose hem ends between mid-thigh and just below the [crotch](#crotch). An even shorter cut is [microdress](#microdress). Implies dress.

entries.name: pink_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose main colour is pink, at any length and in any cut. Where the pink is only a trim or a single panel the [tag](#tag) does not apply.

entries.name: strapless_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with nothing over the shoulders [holding](#holding) it up, [no](#no) straps, sleeves or halter, so shoulders and upper chest are bare. Detached sleeves or [gloves](#gloves) may be worn with it; [strapless](#strapless), [sleeveless](#sleeveless) and off-shoulder dresses are mutually exclusive.

entries.name: purple_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is mostly purple. Combine with dress and the cut, such as [sundress](#sundress) or [gown](#gown); a dress [split](#split) between two colours takes both colour tags.

entries.name: green_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is predominantly green, of any length or cut. Where the shape is distinctive, [tag](#tag) the dress style as [well](#well).

entries.name: sailor_dress
entries.description: A one-piece [dress](#dress) with [sailor](#sailor) details such as a sailor [collar](#collar) and [neckerchief](#neckerchief), worn as [school](#school) uniform or [casual](#casual) wear. Differs from [serafuku](#serafuku), which is a separate top and [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: lolita_fashion
entries.description: A Japanese [fashion](#fashion) built on a knee-length frilled [dress](#dress) or [skirt](#skirt) over a [petticoat](#petticoat), worn with a [blouse](#blouse), [headdress](#headdress), knee [socks](#socks) and [platform](#platform) or heeled [shoes](#shoes). Dolls and teddy bears often complete the childlike look, a goth-tinged version is [gothic_lolita](#gothic_lolita), and it has nothing to do with the loli [tag](#tag).

entries.name: collared_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose neckline is finished with a [folded](#folded) shirt-style [collar](#collar), as on [shirt](#shirt) dresses and a great many uniform dresses. The collar is sewn to the dress, so a separate band worn at the [neck](#neck) does not count.

entries.name: long_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose hem passes the knee and sits [no](#no) higher than three quarters up the calf, often [reaching](#reaching) right to the [floor](#floor). Gowns and most formal dresses qualify.

entries.name: off-shoulder_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose wide, low neckline is meant to rest below the shoulders, its attached sleeves [sitting](#sitting) on the upper arms so [neck](#neck) and [collarbone](#collarbone) stay bare. Strapless, [sleeveless](#sleeveless) and single-shoulder dresses are not this, nor is one with detached sleeves or a garment simply tugged down.

entries.name: brown_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) mainly in brown, from a [plain](#plain) peasant frock to an elegant [evening](#evening) [gown](#gown). Add dress.

entries.name: wedding_dress
entries.description: A bridal [gown](#gown), typically white with [frills](#frills), [lace](#lace) and a [veil](#veil). A gown in another color keeps this [tag](#tag) alongside the color tag, for instance wedding_dress with [pink_dress](#pink_dress).

entries.name: pleated_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with pressed vertical pleats, usually in the [skirt](#skirt) portion. When only a separate skirt is [pleated](#pleated), use [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt) instead.

entries.name: pinafore_dress
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless), collarless [dress](#dress) meant to be worn over a [blouse](#blouse), [shirt](#shirt) or [sweater](#sweater), known as a jumper in American usage. It is not an [apron](#apron), which has [no](#no) [back](#back), nor a [suspender_skirt](#suspender_skirt) or [overall_skirt](#overall_skirt).

entries.name: two-tone_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) in exactly two colours, such as a white [bodice](#bodice) paired with a black [skirt](#skirt). Add the individual colour tags as [well](#well).

entries.name: grey_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose dominant colour is grey, of any cut or length. Add the dress style where the shape is distinctive.

entries.name: yellow_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is mostly yellow. Tag dress and the style such as [sundress](#sundress).

entries.name: sundress
entries.description: A light, informal [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [dress](#dress) for warm weather, frequently white. Implies dress.

entries.name: layered_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose body or [skirt](#skirt) is made up of several layers of [fabric](#fabric) [falling](#falling) over one another. Each layer usually shows separately at the hem or the neckline.

entries.name: backless_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) open at the [back](#back), whether by a modest [keyhole](#keyhole) or by an expanse [running](#running) down to the waist. Evening gowns and [halterneck](#halterneck) designs account for most of them; add [bare_back](#bare_back) when the skin is broadly on show.

entries.name: striped_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes.

entries.name: multicolored_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) [carrying](#carrying) at least two clearly different colours in its design. Neutral shades and simple trim do not count toward it.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with fur trim at the neckline, hem or sleeve ends. Typical of santa dresses and other [winter](#winter) designs.

entries.name: plaid_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) in plaid or tartan [fabric](#fabric), the checked crossbarred pattern [familiar](#familiar) from Scottish dress. Tag [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes) alongside it; a plaid [skirt](#skirt) on its own is [plaid_skirt](#plaid_skirt).

entries.name: sweater_dress
entries.description: A knitted [sweater](#sweater) cut long enough to fall past the hips so it reads as a [dress](#dress) rather than a top. Warm and [casual](#casual), usually worn with [leggings](#leggings) or [thighhighs](#thighhighs) underneath.

entries.name: print_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) printed with images, [shapes](#shapes) or a pattern such as flowers or leaves. Can be combined with [multicolored_dress](#multicolored_dress) only when the base [fabric](#fabric) itself has several colours.

entries.name: halter_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose top is held up by a [strap](#strap) around the [neck](#neck), leaving the shoulders and upper [back](#back) bare.

entries.name: orange_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose main colour is orange, at any length or cut. A dress merely trimmed or [patterned](#patterned) in orange does not qualify.

entries.name: medium_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) ending around knee length, its hem [falling](#falling) between mid-thigh and the upper calf when worn normally. Sits between short and long dresses on the length scale.

entries.name: torn_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with visible rips or shredded hems.

entries.name: santa_dress
entries.description: A Christmas-themed [dress](#dress) in red with white fur edging, often [strapless](#strapless) or short and paired with a matching fur-trimmed [capelet](#capelet). Use [santa_costume](#santa_costume) for the complete outfit and [santa_hat](#santa_hat) for the [hat](#hat) alone.

entries.name: vertical-striped_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) from top to hem. Pair it with the dress's colour tags.

entries.name: aqua_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is mostly aqua or turquoise. Combine it with the dress's cut and with any pattern printed on it.

entries.name: microdress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) so short it bares the [thighs](#thighs) and lower buttocks, along with any [underwear](#underwear) worn beneath. A [short_dress](#short_dress) ends above the knee without exposing that much.

entries.name: turtleneck_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with a high neck-covering [collar](#collar), typically knit or closely fitted through the [bodice](#bodice). The collar reads as a [turtleneck](#turtleneck) grafted onto an ordinary dress.

entries.name: evening_gown
entries.description: A long, flowing formal [dress](#dress) for a [ball](#ball), gala or [evening](#evening) [party](#party), usually in a rich [fabric](#fabric) such as [satin](#satin), [silk](#silk) or velvet. Lengths run from mid-calf to the [floor](#floor).

entries.name: cross-laced_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) worked with cords or ribbons crossing over each other, most often up the [bodice](#bodice) or down the [back](#back). One of the [cross-laced_clothes](#cross-laced_clothes) [family](#family).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) [carrying](#carrying) [lace](#lace) along the hem, neckline or sleeves. Keep it apart from [frilled_dress](#frilled_dress), since a frill is not necessarily made of lace.

entries.name: romper
entries.description: A one-piece garment like a [dress](#dress) but ending in [shorts](#shorts) rather than a [skirt](#skirt). Once children's playwear, now women's [summer](#summer) [fashion](#fashion) too; a long-legged version instead is a [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit).

entries.name: american_flag_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) [carrying](#carrying) the stars and stripes, typically a blue starred [bodice](#bodice) above a red and white striped [skirt](#skirt). The print may also run over the whole garment.

entries.name: ribbed_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) in ribbed knit [fabric](#fabric), showing fine vertical lines. If it resembles a long ribbed [sweater](#sweater) it may also be a [sweater_dress](#sweater_dress); a smooth [turtleneck](#turtleneck) dress without ribbing does not count.

entries.name: gown
entries.description: A long, elaborate [dress](#dress) [reaching](#reaching) the ankles or trailing on the [floor](#floor) and flaring at the sides, worn to balls, weddings and formal evenings. An everyday dress is not a gown.

entries.name: white_romper
entries.description: A one-piece garment that joins a fitted top to a pair of [shorts](#shorts), coloured white. It reads as breezy [summer](#summer) or [beach](#beach) wear, so [tag](#tag) [romper](#romper) for the base garment alongside the colour.

entries.name: impossible_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that clings the way [no](#no) [cloth](#cloth) could, [following](#following) each breast separately or outlining a [navel](#navel) it supposedly covers. Another member of the [impossible_clothes](#impossible_clothes) [family](#family).

entries.name: pencil_dress
entries.description: A close-fitting [dress](#dress) whose lower half runs straight and narrow over the hips and [legs](#legs), from knee to mini length, with straps, sleeves or a [halterneck](#halterneck). The [strapless](#strapless) version is a [tube_dress](#tube_dress).

entries.name: polka_dot_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) covered in polka [dots](#dots), a classic retro and [summer](#summer) look. Tag dress and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) alongside it.

entries.name: gradient_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose colour shifts gradually from one tone into another, typically darkening or paling toward the hem.

entries.name: taut_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) pulled taut enough that the [fabric](#fabric) creases across the chest, hips or [thighs](#thighs).

entries.name: cocktail_dress
entries.description: A sleek [dress](#dress) cut at or above the knee for semi-formal [evening](#evening) wear, generally in a single colour. Something floor-length and grander is an evening [gown](#gown).

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose hem or [cuffs](#cuffs) carry a [ribbon](#ribbon) laced in and out of slits in the [fabric](#fabric), forming a dashed line. Tag with dress and [ribbon_trim](#ribbon_trim).

entries.name: tube_dress
entries.description: A snug, [strapless](#strapless) [dress](#dress) shaped like an elongated [tube_top](#tube_top), typically [reaching](#reaching) to around the [knees](#knees) and hugging the [legs](#legs). Shoulder straps or a halter neckline instead make it a [pencil_dress](#pencil_dress).

entries.name: unworn_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) lies or hangs in view with nobody wearing it.

entries.name: two-sided_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) made of [fabric](#fabric) with a contrasting inner face, seen at a lifted hem or a flared [skirt](#skirt). Implies dress and [two-sided_fabric](#two-sided_fabric).

entries.name: sideless_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that leaves the sides of the [torso](#torso) open, baring skin from the underarm toward the hip and often the [sideboob](#sideboob). The dress-specific form of a [sideless_outfit](#sideless_outfit).

entries.name: floral_print_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) made from flower-patterned [cloth](#cloth), whether small scattered sprigs or big [tropical](#tropical) blooms. The pattern is in the material, not sewn on afterwards.

entries.name: wet_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that is visibly drenched, [clinging](#clinging) or turning [translucent](#translucent), its wearer sometimes shown [wringing](#wringing) it out. Add see-through when the [fabric](#fabric) reveals what's underneath.

entries.name: hooded_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with a [hood](#hood) built into it, seen on [fantasy](#fantasy), [witch](#witch) and [casual](#casual) designs alike. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) depending on how it is worn.

entries.name: coat_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) tailored on the lines of a [coat](#coat), fastening down the front and finished with [lapels](#lapels) or a [collar](#collar). It is worn as the outfit itself, not thrown over another garment.

entries.name: pinstripe_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) woven or printed with fine evenly spaced vertical lines. The pattern lends it a tailored, business-like look.

entries.name: checkered_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) cut from chequered [cloth](#cloth), whether fine [gingham](#gingham) or large colour blocks. The pattern runs over the whole garment rather than edging it.

entries.name: silver_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) in a metallic silver-grey, typically drawn with hard sheen where the [fabric](#fabric) catches light. Common on [evening](#evening) and gala wear.

entries.name: single-shoulder_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with a slanted neckline that rises over one shoulder and passes under the opposite armpit, baring that shoulder and part of the chest. Supported by a single [strap](#strap) or sleeve; an ordinary dress [slipping](#slipping) off the arm does not count.

entries.name: empire_waist
entries.description: A cut, usually on a [dress](#dress), whose seam sits directly under the bust rather than at the natural waist, so the [fabric](#fabric) falls straight from the chest. It draws the eye upward and makes the [figure](#figure) read as longer.

entries.name: funeral_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) worn to a memorial service, almost always black and plainly cut so as not to draw attention. The occasion matters as much as the shape of the garment.

entries.name: zipper_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) closed by a conspicuous [zipper](#zipper) down the front, [back](#back) or side, drawn as a visible design feature rather than a closure hidden in a seam.

entries.name: feather_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose [skirt](#skirt) or [bodice](#bodice) is built from layered [feathers](#feathers). Showgirl, [swan](#swan) and bird-maiden designs favour it.

entries.name: latex_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) cut from shiny rubber, gripping the [figure](#figure) with bright highlights along its curves. It is usually drawn in black or in one [saturated](#saturated) colour.

entries.name: flower_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose [bodice](#bodice) and [skirt](#skirt) are built from [petals](#petals), stems and leaves rather than [cloth](#cloth). Fairies, [nature](#nature) spirits and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume) designs wear it most often.

entries.name: side-tie_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) held together by ties knotted along one or both sides rather than sewn shut. The open seam usually leaves a strip of hip visible between the knots.

entries.name: argyle_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) [carrying](#carrying) argyle's crossed diamonds, often on a knitted [bodice](#bodice) or [running](#running) down the [skirt](#skirt). It reads as preppy or academic dress more often than as [evening](#evening) wear.

entries.name: bodycon
entries.description: Japanese body-conscious [fashion](#fashion): a short, tight minidress that follows every line of the [figure](#figure). It carries a [strong](#strong) late-1980s club flavour, and a folding hand fan often comes with it.

entries.name: asymmetrical_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose two halves are deliberately unlike each other: a hem cut on the slant, one shoulder covered and the other bare, or panels of differing length. The imbalance is built into the garment rather than being a matter of it [slipping](#slipping) out of place.

entries.name: gold_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) of [gold](#gold) [fabric](#fabric), from a softly shimmering [gown](#gown) to a hard metallic [sheath](#sheath). It reads as wealth and formality.

entries.name: highleg_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) slit as far up as the hip at the side or the [back](#back), so the leg is bare to the top of the thigh as the wearer moves. The [opening](#opening) reaches over the [crotch](#crotch) line rather than stopping mid-thigh.

entries.name: o-ring_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) held together or trimmed with rings, often bridging a cut-out at the chest or joining the two sides of a slit.

entries.name: glitter_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) covered in glittering flecks or sequinned [cloth](#cloth) that catches the light as it moves. Belongs to [stage](#stage), [party](#party) and [idol](#idol) wardrobes.

entries.name: feather-trimmed_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) edged with [feathers](#feathers) along the hem, neckline or shoulders. The body of the garment is ordinary [cloth](#cloth) and only its [border](#border) is plumed.

entries.name: sleeveless_turtleneck_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that climbs into a high [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar) at the [neck](#neck) while leaving the shoulders and arms uncovered. The [contrast](#contrast) between the closed neckline and the bare arms is the look this [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: gingham_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) made from evenly checked [gingham](#gingham) [cloth](#cloth), usually one colour against white. Reads as summery and countrified.

entries.name: puffy_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that balloons outward and then curves [back](#back) in, rounded like a [bubble](#bubble) around the hem. A [skirt](#skirt) that only flares wider without tucking back under is a [circle](#circle) skirt instead.

entries.name: train_(clothing)
entries.description: The length of [fabric](#fabric) that trails along the [floor](#floor) behind the wearer, traditional on [wedding](#wedding) dresses and formal court gowns. Reserve it for a hem that genuinely reaches the ground; a merely longer [back](#back) is a high-low [skirt](#skirt) or [overskirt](#overskirt) instead.

entries.name: floral_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) shaped to look like a [flower](#flower) itself, with petal-like panels making up the [skirt](#skirt) or [bodice](#bodice). Not a dress printed with flowers, and not one [pinned](#pinned) with a single [bloom](#bloom).

entries.name: lace_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) whose [fabric](#fabric) is [lace](#lace) all over, letting skin or a lining show through the openwork. It is distinct from a solid dress [carrying](#carrying) lace only at its edges.

entries.name: mermaid_dress
entries.description: A long [gown](#gown) fitted close to the body down to the knee or calf before flaring out sharply like a fin. Longer and more dramatic in its [flare](#flare) than a [hobble](#hobble) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: hobble_dress
entries.description: A long [dress](#dress) tapering to a hem so narrow at the ankles that the wearer [can](#can) only take small steps. The restricted stride gives it both its name and its vampish [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: satin_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) in glossy [satin](#satin), the [cloth](#cloth) pooling into bright highlights and deep folds over the body. Common on [evening](#evening) and slip dresses.

entries.name: nontraditional_wedding_dress
entries.description: A bridal outfit that departs from the [plain](#plain) white [gown](#gown), whether in colour, in a short cut, or by borrowing from armour, a [kimono](#kimono) or the character's own [costume](#costume).

entries.name: liquid_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) made of flowing fluid rather than [cloth](#cloth), keeping a dress [silhouette](#silhouette) as it pours down the body.

entries.name: formal_clothes
entries.description: Dressy attire for a formal occasion, covering suits, tuxedos and [evening](#evening) gowns alike. It is the [umbrella](#umbrella); [tag](#tag) the individual garments alongside it.

entries.name: suit
entries.description: A matching set of formal Western [clothes](#clothes), a [jacket](#jacket) plus trousers or a [skirt](#skirt) in the same [fabric](#fabric), worn over a collared [shirt](#shirt). Only applies while the jacket is worn; add a colour [tag](#tag) such as [black_suit](#black_suit) alongside it.

entries.name: black_suit
entries.description: A matching black [jacket](#jacket) and trousers worn as one ensemble, the standard [dress](#dress) of businessmen, agents and mourners. Only the suit's colour is claimed, not its cut.

entries.name: suit_jacket
entries.description: The tailored [jacket](#jacket) of a [suit](#suit), usually cut with [lapels](#lapels) and buttoned down the front. Implies jacket.

entries.name: tailcoat
entries.description: A formal [coat](#coat) cut short in front with two long tails [hanging](#hanging) at the [back](#back), usually with [lapels](#lapels). Worn by butlers, [orchestra](#orchestra) conductors and at white-tie events.

entries.name: business_suit
entries.description: A matching [jacket](#jacket) with trousers or a [skirt](#skirt), cut from one sober [cloth](#cloth) — the standard [office](#office) outfit. A [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt) and usually a [necktie](#necktie) go beneath it.

entries.name: white_suit
entries.description: A matching white [jacket](#jacket) and trousers, a flashy or summery take on formal wear. Tag [suit](#suit) alongside it; a white [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt) or a white [tuxedo](#tuxedo) jacket alone does not earn the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: skirt_suit
entries.description: A woman's business [suit](#suit) pairing a [skirt](#skirt) with a matching [jacket](#jacket). Office-lady and [teacher](#teacher) characters wear it often.

entries.name: tuxedo
entries.description: Formal [evening](#evening) wear built around a [dinner](#dinner) [jacket](#jacket), trousers, white [shirt](#shirt) and [bow](#bow) tie, sometimes with a [waistcoat](#waistcoat) added. A woman may wear one as tailored or paired with a [skirt](#skirt), [shorts](#shorts) or [leotard](#leotard) instead of trousers.

entries.name: pant_suit
entries.description: A woman's matching [suit](#suit) whose lower half is trousers rather than a [skirt](#skirt), the businesswoman look. The skirted version is [skirt_suit](#skirt_suit).

entries.name: grey_suit
entries.description: A grey [suit](#suit), [jacket](#jacket) and trousers or [skirt](#skirt) together, worn as business or formal [dress](#dress). It is the most ordinary colour the garment takes.

entries.name: blue_suit
entries.description: A matching [jacket](#jacket) and trousers in blue, navy most of the time, worn by businessmen and at formal occasions. Mark the [shirt](#shirt) and tie underneath separately.

entries.name: red_suit
entries.description: A matching [suit](#suit) of [jacket](#jacket) and trousers in red, as a flashy formal outfit or villain look. Add formal and jacket tags as applicable; a red [blazer](#blazer) alone is [red_jacket](#red_jacket).

entries.name: pinstripe_suit
entries.description: A matching [suit](#suit) cut from pinstriped [cloth](#cloth), the fine-lined [fabric](#fabric) associated with bankers and gangsters. Jacket and trousers share the pattern.

entries.name: aristocratic_clothes
entries.description: Rich early-modern European [dress](#dress), or fiction's version of it: tailcoats, waistcoats, ruffled shirts, corseted gowns and layered skirts. Modern styles that merely borrow the look, such as lolita [fashion](#fashion), take their own tags.

entries.name: brown_suit
entries.description: A tailored [suit](#suit) in brown — matching [jacket](#jacket) with trousers or a [skirt](#skirt), generally over a [shirt](#shirt). It reads warmer and less formal than the black or navy equivalent.

entries.name: green_suit
entries.description: A tailored green [suit](#suit), the [jacket](#jacket) matching trousers or a [skirt](#skirt). Business suits rarely come in this colour, so it reads as flashy rather than sober.

entries.name: purple_suit
entries.description: A matching purple [jacket](#jacket) and trousers or [skirt](#skirt) worn as formal or business [dress](#dress). Showy on a performer, [sinister](#sinister) on a villain.

entries.name: striped_suit
entries.description: A tailored [suit](#suit) cut from pinstriped or more broadly striped [cloth](#cloth). Implies suit.

entries.name: pocket_square
entries.description: A small [handkerchief](#handkerchief) [folded](#folded) into the breast [pocket](#pocket) of a [jacket](#jacket), showing only its top edge or points. Purely ornamental, and a [marker](#marker) of careful formal [dress](#dress).

entries.name: business_casual
entries.description: Office [dress](#dress) pitched between a full [suit](#suit) and [street](#street) [clothes](#clothes): a [blazer](#blazer) over a [shirt](#shirt), a [turtleneck](#turtleneck), or knitwear above trousers or a [skirt](#skirt). The [jacket](#jacket) need not match the bottoms and a tie is optional.

entries.name: tuxedo_shirt
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt) built for formal occasions, marked by a [pleated](#pleated) or ruffled front panel, French [cuffs](#cuffs) and a wing or spread [collar](#collar). Butlers and upper-class characters wear it beneath a [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: shawl_lapels
entries.description: Jacket [lapels](#lapels) that run in one unbroken curve from the [collar](#collar) down to the front edge, without the notch or point cut into a standard lapel. Typical of [dinner](#dinner) jackets and [smoking](#smoking) robes.

entries.name: pink_suit
entries.description: A tailored two- or three-piece [suit](#suit) in pink, the [jacket](#jacket) matching the trousers or [skirt](#skirt). Only the colour separates it from any other suit.

entries.name: yellow_suit
entries.description: A tailored [suit](#suit) in yellow, [jacket](#jacket) with matching trousers or [skirt](#skirt). A loud [choice](#choice) usually reserved for showy or [comic](#comic) characters.

entries.name: unworn_blazer
entries.description: A [blazer](#blazer) is present in the scene without anyone wearing it, slung over a [chair](#chair), carried over an arm or dropped on a [bed](#bed). Typical of [school](#school) and [office](#office) scenes at the end of the [day](#day).

entries.name: sleeveless_blazer
entries.description: A tailored [blazer](#blazer) whose sleeves have been removed, leaving the shoulders and arms bare while the [lapels](#lapels) and front closure stay intact. It reads as a smart [jacket](#jacket) restyled for a [lighter](#lighter) or sharper [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: orange_suit
entries.description: A matching [jacket](#jacket) and trousers in orange worn as a [suit](#suit). The [shirt](#shirt) beneath keeps its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: school_uniform
entries.description: Any uniform worn by students, in Japan mostly by middle and high schoolers. The usual designs are the [serafuku](#serafuku) and the [blazer](#blazer), boys often in a [gakuran](#gakuran), with sweaters, cardigans, [kneehighs](#kneehighs) or [thighhighs](#thighhighs) as [accessories](#accessories).

entries.name: serafuku
entries.description: The sailor-collared Japanese girls' [school](#school) uniform: a [blouse](#blouse) with a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar), a [pleated](#pleated) [skirt](#skirt), and a [neckerchief](#neckerchief) or [bow](#bow), in countless [variations](#variations). A skirt is required; a sailor top worn with [shorts](#shorts) is [sailor_shirt](#sailor_shirt) and a one-piece is [sailor_dress](#sailor_dress).

entries.name: black_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad flat [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style top, squared off across the [back](#back), rendered in black. Its colour is counted on its own and never feeds into [black_serafuku](#black_serafuku).

entries.name: winter_uniform
entries.description: A [school](#school) uniform in its cold-season form, such as a long-sleeved [dark](#dark) [serafuku](#serafuku) or a [blazer](#blazer) worn over a [cardigan](#cardigan). It is not used for a [military](#military) uniform meant for [cold](#cold) climates; [summer_uniform](#summer_uniform) is its warm-weather counterpart.

entries.name: black_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose top and [skirt](#skirt) are both black, typical of the [winter](#winter) version. The [collar](#collar) and [neckerchief](#neckerchief) are judged on their own and never count toward this.

entries.name: summer_uniform
entries.description: The warm-weather version of a [school](#school) uniform, typically a short-sleeved white [shirt](#shirt) or white [serafuku](#serafuku), sometimes worn with a [sweater](#sweater) [vest](#vest). Not used for hot-climate [military](#military) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: gakuran
entries.description: The military-cut Japanese [school](#school) uniform for boys: a black or navy [jacket](#jacket) with a [standing](#standing) [collar](#collar) buttoned from top to bottom, worn with straight trousers and a [dark](#dark) [belt](#belt). The default look for male students in school settings.

entries.name: blue_buruma
entries.description: Buruma in blue, the tight Japanese [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) worn with a gym [shirt](#shirt) for [school](#school) sports. They are not the loose Western [bloomers](#bloomers).

entries.name: grey_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad flat [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style uniform, coloured grey and often edged with contrasting stripes. The collar's colour is judged apart from [grey_serafuku](#grey_serafuku).

entries.name: green_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad flat [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style uniform, coloured green. Teal shades leave some overlap with [blue_sailor_collar](#blue_sailor_collar), so [judge](#judge) by which reads closer.

entries.name: blue_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose [shirt](#shirt) and [skirt](#skirt) are both blue. The [collar](#collar) and the [neckerchief](#neckerchief) are judged separately and do not decide the colour here.

entries.name: white_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose top and [skirt](#skirt) are both white. The colour of the [collar](#collar) or [neckerchief](#neckerchief) plays [no](#no) part in this, so a white [serafuku](#serafuku) [can](#can) still carry a differently coloured [sailor](#sailor) collar.

entries.name: kindergarten_uniform
entries.description: A preschooler's outfit: a [plain](#plain) [smock](#smock) or long-sleeved blue top with a yellow [hat](#hat), worn with [shorts](#shorts) or a [pleated](#pleated) [skirt](#skirt). A name [tag](#tag) and a small shoulder [bag](#bag) usually go with it.

entries.name: purple_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose top and [skirt](#skirt) are both purple. The [collar](#collar) and [neckerchief](#neckerchief) do not count toward the colour; combine with [serafuku](#serafuku) and [school_uniform](#school_uniform).

entries.name: orange_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) of a [school](#school) uniform in orange. Shade overlap with the brown, red and yellow versions is common.

entries.name: grey_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose [shirt](#shirt) and [skirt](#skirt) are both grey. The [collar](#collar) and [neckerchief](#neckerchief) colours do not count towards it and are tagged on their own.

entries.name: amesuku_gyaru
entries.description: A [school](#school) uniform worn in the loudest possible way: the [shirt](#shirt) knotted open to show the [bra](#bra) or [bikini](#bikini) beneath, the [skirt](#skirt) short enough to [flash](#flash), plus [heavy](#heavy) make-up and piled-on [accessories](#accessories). It is the extreme end of the [gyaru](#gyaru) schoolgirl look.

entries.name: yellow_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad flap [collar](#collar) of a [sailor](#sailor) [blouse](#blouse) rendered in yellow. It lies over the shoulders and squares off across the [back](#back).

entries.name: brown_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose [blouse](#blouse) and [skirt](#skirt) are both brown. The [collar](#collar) and [neckerchief](#neckerchief) are counted separately, so their colour makes [no](#no) difference here.

entries.name: pink_buruma
entries.description: The tight elasticated [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of Japanese [school](#school) PE kit, here in pink. Worn with a gym [shirt](#shirt) for athletics class, cut high on the hip.

entries.name: pink_serafuku
entries.description: A Japanese sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose [blouse](#blouse) and [skirt](#skirt) are both pink. The [collar](#collar) and the [neckerchief](#neckerchief) may be any colour without affecting it.

entries.name: green_serafuku
entries.description: A Japanese sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose [shirt](#shirt) and [skirt](#skirt) are both green. The [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) and [neckerchief](#neckerchief) are judged on their own and do not decide this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: serasuku
entries.description: A sailor-collar top worn directly over a [school](#school) [swimsuit](#swimsuit), the two garments combined into one look. Do not confuse it with an ordinary [serafuku](#serafuku) and [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: red_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose [blouse](#blouse) and [skirt](#skirt) are both red. The colours of the [neckerchief](#neckerchief) and the [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) are ignored when deciding whether the [tag](#tag) applies.

entries.name: green_buruma
entries.description: Green [buruma](#buruma), the tight [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of a Japanese [school](#school) sports kit. They nearly always appear with a gym [shirt](#shirt) in a gymnasium or on a sports [field](#field).

entries.name: plaid_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad squared-off [collar](#collar) of a [sailor](#sailor) uniform, cut from tartan [cloth](#cloth). The [blouse](#blouse) underneath it may still be [plain](#plain).

entries.name: soviet_school_uniform
entries.description: The brown [dress](#dress) with a white or black pinafore worn by Soviet schoolgirls until the early 1990s, usually paired with large white hair bows and a Pioneer [neckerchief](#neckerchief). Often mistaken by outsiders for a [maid](#maid) outfit.

entries.name: indonesian_high_school_uniform
entries.description: The Indonesian secondary-school kit: a white collared [shirt](#shirt) with a pale blue-grey tie, worn with a matching [skirt](#skirt) or trousers. A student-council [badge](#badge) sits on the left breast [pocket](#pocket).

entries.name: yellow_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) outfit whose [blouse](#blouse) and [skirt](#skirt) are both yellow. The [neckerchief](#neckerchief) and the [collar](#collar) are judged on their own and do not decide this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: white_gakuran
entries.description: A Japanese boys' [school](#school) [jacket](#jacket) in white rather than the usual black or navy, with a stand-up [collar](#collar) and metal [buttons](#buttons). Marks a particular school or an alternate colorway.

entries.name: blue_gakuran
entries.description: The Japanese boys' [school](#school) [jacket](#jacket) with its [standing](#standing) [collar](#collar), made up in blue rather than the usual black or white. Buttons run straight up the front to the throat.

entries.name: thai_school_uniform
entries.description: The Thai [school](#school) outfit: a white collared [shirt](#shirt) with a long [dark](#dark) [skirt](#skirt) and a small [ribbon](#ribbon) for girls, short dark [shorts](#shorts) for boys. It descends from the Japanese uniform, but the longer skirt and the shorts set it apart.

entries.name: orange_serafuku
entries.description: A sailor-style [school](#school) uniform whose [blouse](#blouse) and [skirt](#skirt) are both orange. The [neckerchief](#neckerchief) and the [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) are judged separately and have [no](#no) bearing on it.

entries.name: grey_buruma
entries.description: Grey [buruma](#buruma), the close-fitting [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of Japanese [school](#school) [sportswear](#sportswear). They appear with a gym [shirt](#shirt) in physical education scenes.

entries.name: military_uniform
entries.description: The formal [dress](#dress) of a real or fictional armed force, marked with [insignia](#insignia), [epaulettes](#epaulettes), medals and similar trim. Requires the uniform top itself to be worn, not just [accessories](#accessories) associated with it.

entries.name: epaulettes
entries.description: Ornamental shoulder pieces on [military](#military) and [dress](#dress) uniforms, usually finished with a fringe of tassels. Seen on imperial-era officers and on elaborate [stage](#stage) costumes. Flat rank strips without fringe are [shoulder_boards](#shoulder_boards).

entries.name: naval_uniform
entries.description: A navy's [dress](#dress), typically white for [summer](#summer) and the tropics and black or [dark](#dark) blue for colder [seasons](#seasons). Officers tend toward a peaked cap and [epaulettes](#epaulettes), while enlisted sailors wear a [sailor_collar](#sailor_collar) and [sailor](#sailor) [hat](#hat).

entries.name: police_uniform
entries.description: The uniform of a [police](#police) officer: collared [shirt](#shirt), peaked cap, [badge](#badge), and [necktie](#necktie), often with a [holster](#holster), utility [belt](#belt), or high-visibility [vest](#vest). Tag [policewoman](#policewoman) or [policeman](#policeman) for the person wearing it.

entries.name: aiguillette
entries.description: A braided ornamental cord, usually [gold](#gold), looped from the shoulder of a [dress](#dress) or [military](#military) uniform. It is a detail added to a uniform rather than a garment in itself.

entries.name: shoulder_boards
entries.description: Flat rank [insignia](#insignia) fastened onto the shoulder straps of a [military](#military) or [police](#police) uniform, smaller than [epaulettes](#epaulettes) and without their fringe trim.

entries.name: tactical_clothes
entries.description: Gear worn by [police](#police), SWAT teams and special operators: body [armor](#armor), combat [boots](#boots), pouches, holsters, headsets and helmets, with little or [no](#no) [camouflage](#camouflage). Camouflaged [army](#army) [dress](#dress) is a separate [military_uniform](#military_uniform) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: load_bearing_vest
entries.description: A [military](#military) or [police](#police) [vest](#vest) with [ammunition](#ammunition) pouches, [grenade](#grenade) slots and sometimes a [holster](#holster) built into the garment itself. It overlaps with a bulletproof vest where armour plates [can](#can) be slid in, while pouches carried separately on the chest make a chest rig.

entries.name: single_epaulette
entries.description: One shoulder ornament of the [military](#military) kind, worn instead of the usual matched pair on both shoulders.

entries.name: military_combat_uniform
entries.description: Battle [dress](#dress) loaded with [fighting](#fighting) gear: [fatigues](#fatigues) worn under a bulletproof [vest](#vest), [ammunition](#ammunition) pouches, [goggles](#goggles) and a [helmet](#helmet). Police and SWAT equipment instead falls under [tactical_clothes](#tactical_clothes).

entries.name: military_dress_uniform
entries.description: A formal service uniform meant for parades and ceremonies rather than the [field](#field), hung with medals, [ribbon](#ribbon) [bars](#bars) and [braid](#braid). Frequently drawn on senior officers.

entries.name: fatigues
entries.description: Working [military](#military) [dress](#dress) for the [field](#field): a matching [jacket](#jacket) or [shirt](#shirt) with trousers, generally in [camouflage](#camouflage) or [olive](#olive) drab. A character who merely looks worn out takes an exhaustion [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: flight_suit
entries.description: The one-piece coverall a [pilot](#pilot) wears in the [cockpit](#cockpit), zipped up the front and covered in patches, straps and pockets. Military aviators and racing-style crews both wear them.

entries.name: united_states_navy
entries.description: The naval [branch](#branch) of the American armed forces is shown or referenced through its ships, [aircraft](#aircraft), uniforms or [insignia](#insignia), its air arm included under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: united_states_army
entries.description: The land [branch](#branch) of the American armed forces is shown or referenced by uniform, vehicle, [insignia](#insignia) or explicit mention, including historical formations such as the wartime Army Air Corps.

entries.name: waffen-ss
entries.description: Uniforms and [insignia](#insignia) of the combat [branch](#branch) of a historical German paramilitary organisation, identified by particular [collar](#collar) [runes](#runes) and rank patches. Fictional outfits merely styled after them do not belong here.

entries.name: g-suit
entries.description: A jet pilot's pressure garment, its inflatable bladders over [legs](#legs) and abdomen keeping the wearer conscious under [heavy](#heavy) acceleration. The skin-tight suits worn by fictional [mecha](#mecha) pilots are pilot_suit instead.

entries.name: royal_navy
entries.description: The naval forces of the United Kingdom, whose ships carry the prefix HMS. Reserve it for references to the real service rather than to same-named in-game factions that merely borrow the name.

entries.name: ss_insignia
entries.description: Insignia of the German Waffen-SS: paired lightning-bolt [runes](#runes), [collar](#collar) tabs, cuff titles and death's-head badges worn on wartime uniforms. Appears in genuine historical settings and alternate-history fiction alike.

entries.name: ribbon_bar
entries.description: The block of small coloured stripes [pinned](#pinned) above a breast [pocket](#pocket) on a [military](#military) or [police](#police) uniform, each stripe [standing](#standing) for an award or campaign. Also called a service [ribbon](#ribbon) or [medal](#medal) ribbon.

entries.name: luftwaffe
entries.description: The German air force, present through its uniforms, [insignia](#insignia) and [aircraft](#aircraft). Most often the wartime service of the 1930s and 40s, though the modern German air arm inherited the name.

entries.name: united_states_marine_corps
entries.description: The American Marine Corps is depicted or referenced through its [dress](#dress) uniform, [camouflage](#camouflage), [insignia](#insignia) or amphibious operations. Best known for its Pacific campaigns and its duty guarding embassies abroad.

entries.name: scout_uniform
entries.description: Scouting [dress](#dress): a [shirt](#shirt) covered in sewn-on badges, a rolled [neckerchief](#neckerchief) through a woggle, [shorts](#shorts) or a [skirt](#skirt), and frequently a broad-brimmed [hat](#hat).

entries.name: fourragere
entries.description: A braided cord looped over one shoulder and [pinned](#pinned) at the chest, awarded to a [military](#military) unit and worn with [dress](#dress) uniform. The decoration began with the French [army](#army).

entries.name: united_states_air_force
entries.description: The air arm of the American [military](#military) appears or is named, through its [aircraft](#aircraft), [insignia](#insignia), uniforms or personnel. It [split](#split) from the wartime Army Air Corps and today handles fixed-wing combat [flying](#flying).

entries.name: apron
entries.description: A protective garment covering the front of the body, tied on over other [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking), [cleaning](#cleaning) or work, and part of [maid](#maid), [nurse](#nurse) and [waitress](#waitress) [dress](#dress). A frilly one is [frilled_apron](#frilled_apron), and one worn with nothing underneath [naked_apron](#naked_apron).

entries.name: white_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) colored white, the standard piece of a [maid](#maid) outfit and many [cooking](#cooking) or [waitress](#waitress) ensembles. Add the shape too, such as [waist_apron](#waist_apron) or [frilled_apron](#frilled_apron).

entries.name: maid_apron
entries.description: The white frilled [apron](#apron) of a maid's uniform, [reaching](#reaching) from the chest down to the [thighs](#thighs) or [knees](#knees) and tied at the [back](#back). Implies apron.

entries.name: waist_apron
entries.description: A half [apron](#apron) tied at the waist and [hanging](#hanging) over the front of the [lap](#lap), without a [bib](#bib). A [staple](#staple) of [waitress](#waitress) uniforms and some [maid](#maid) outfits.

entries.name: frilled_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) trimmed with ruffles along its edges, the classic [maid](#maid) apron worn over a [dark](#dark) [dress](#dress). Waitress and [cooking](#cooking) outfits use it too; add [maid_apron](#maid_apron) when it belongs to that uniform.

entries.name: lab_coat
entries.description: A knee-length white [coat](#coat) with deep pockets, worn by scientists, doctors and researchers. It is often draped loose over the shoulders or left [hanging](#hanging) open over ordinary [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: jumpsuit
entries.description: A loose one-piece garment covering arms and [legs](#legs), like the coveralls worn by mechanics, pilots and skydivers. Unlike a [bodysuit](#bodysuit) it does not cling; when the legs end like [shorts](#shorts) use [short_jumpsuit](#short_jumpsuit).

entries.name: unconventional_maid
entries.description: A [maid](#maid) outfit that departs from the standard [dress](#dress) and [apron](#apron), such as a maid [bikini](#bikini), maid [leotard](#leotard), tracksuit maid or armed tactical maid. Implies maid.

entries.name: employee_uniform
entries.description: What a [shop](#shop), convenience store or [restaurant](#restaurant) worker wears on shift: a [logo](#logo) [shirt](#shirt) or [dress](#dress) shirt with [plain](#plain) trousers, sometimes an [apron](#apron) or a visor cap. Waitress and [maid](#maid) outfits have tags of their own.

entries.name: wa_maid
entries.description: A Japanese take on the [maid](#maid) outfit: a [yukata](#yukata) or [plain](#plain) [kimono](#kimono) worn with a maid [apron](#apron) and often a maid [headdress](#headdress). If a Western maid outfit appears in the same picture, add [mixed_maids](#mixed_maids).

entries.name: pink_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in pink rather than the usual white, tied over [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking) or housework or worn as part of a cute uniform. Cut and coverage are unchanged; only the colour differs.

entries.name: black_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in black, tied over other [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking), [serving](#serving) or work, and standard on [cafe](#cafe) and [butler](#butler) outfits. Tag the garment worn beneath it separately.

entries.name: blue_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in blue tied on over the [clothes](#clothes). Housework, [cooking](#cooking) and [shop](#shop) uniforms account for most of its appearances.

entries.name: traditional_nun
entries.description: A modest, historically accurate nun's [habit](#habit): a long [dark](#dark) [dress](#dress) with a white [guimpe](#guimpe), and the [coif](#coif) and [veil](#veil), without the cutouts and skin-tight fit typical of [costume](#costume) versions. Distinguishes a properly modest habit from a more revealing anime take.

entries.name: green_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in green worn over the [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking), [cleaning](#cleaning) or [shop](#shop) and [cafe](#cafe) work.

entries.name: brown_apron
entries.description: A brown [apron](#apron) tied over ordinary [clothes](#clothes), as worn by a cook, [barista](#barista), shopkeeper or craftsman. Add apron.

entries.name: red_apron
entries.description: A red [apron](#apron) worn over clothing for [cooking](#cooking) or [serving](#serving). Combine with [naked_apron](#naked_apron) when nothing is worn underneath it.

entries.name: yellow_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in yellow, worn for [cooking](#cooking), [cleaning](#cleaning) or as part of a work outfit. Tag apron as [well](#well).

entries.name: jersey_maid
entries.description: A [maid](#maid) outfit built on a track [suit](#suit) or track [jacket](#jacket) instead of a [dress](#dress), whether a long jacket worn as one or a jacket with a [skirt](#skirt) or trousers. Some maid element such as an [apron](#apron) or [headdress](#headdress) has to be there.

entries.name: orange_jumpsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit) in orange, the colour associated with [prison](#prison) issue and high-visibility work clothing.

entries.name: grey_apron
entries.description: A grey [apron](#apron) tied over other [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking), [cleaning](#cleaning) or [shop](#shop) work. The outfit underneath, such as a [maid](#maid) uniform, is tagged separately.

entries.name: fast_food_uniform
entries.description: Staff clothing from a [burger](#burger) or [chicken](#chicken) [counter](#counter): a [logo](#logo) [shirt](#shirt) or polo, a visor or cap, an [apron](#apron), with a [skirt](#skirt) or [shorts](#shorts) below. The [branded](#branded) cap and shirt together set it apart from other service wear.

entries.name: cassock
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) floor-length [robe](#robe) buttoned down the front, worn by Catholic clergy as everyday [dress](#dress). The embroidered vestments layered over it for services are a separate matter.

entries.name: purple_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in a purple [shade](#shade), tied on over other clothing at the front. Colour is the only thing separating it from the [plain](#plain) apron [tag](#tag).

entries.name: orange_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in orange tied over the rest of the outfit. Kitchen, [serving](#serving) and [workshop](#workshop) aprons all count.

entries.name: high-visibility_clothing
entries.description: Workwear in fluorescent yellow or orange, banded with reflective strips so the wearer stands out in [traffic](#traffic) or poor light. Road and rail crews, [airport](#airport) [staff](#staff) and emergency services are the [people](#people) who wear it.

entries.name: high-visibility_vest
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) fluorescent [tabard](#tabard) pulled on over ordinary [clothes](#clothes), normally crossed with reflective [tape](#tape). It is the commonest piece of [high-visibility_clothing](#high-visibility_clothing).

entries.name: print_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) [carrying](#carrying) a printed design of any kind, from a small motif on the [bib](#bib) to a pattern across the whole [cloth](#cloth). What the print depicts makes [no](#no) difference to the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: plaid_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) cut from tartan [cloth](#cloth) and tied over other [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking) or work. The pattern is what separates it from a [plain](#plain) apron.

entries.name: smock
entries.description: A loose lightweight overgarment pulled on to keep [clothes](#clothes) clean while [working](#working) or painting. In Japanese contexts the word [can](#can) stand for a [kindergarten](#kindergarten) outfit as a whole.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) finished with a decorative [lace](#lace) [border](#border) along the hem, [bib](#bib) or straps. It is standard issue on frilly [maid](#maid) outfits.

entries.name: hazmat_suit
entries.description: A sealed full-body [suit](#suit) with [hood](#hood) and faceplate worn against chemical, biological or radiological hazards. A [respirator](#respirator) usually goes with it, and a pressurised one looks inflated. Outbreaks, cleanups and ruined-world scenes are where it appears.

entries.name: gingham_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) cut from checked [gingham](#gingham) [cloth](#cloth), tied over a [dress](#dress) or a [shop](#shop) uniform. A [signature](#signature) piece of [bakery](#bakery) and [cafe](#cafe) outfits.

entries.name: firefighter_jacket
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy) protective [coat](#coat) of firefighting kit, marked with reflective bands across chest, sleeves and hem. Also called a turnout or bunker coat.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) finished at its edges or straps with a decorative [ribbon](#ribbon) band. Frequently part of a [maid](#maid) or [cafe](#cafe) outfit rather than [plain](#plain) [working](#working) [kitchen](#kitchen) wear.

entries.name: striped_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes, tied over other [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking) or work.

entries.name: heart_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) whose [bib](#bib) is cut as a [heart](#heart) or built around one. An ordinary apron [carrying](#carrying) a heart print does not count.

entries.name: medical_scrubs
entries.description: The loose shirt-and-trouser set worn by [hospital](#hospital) and surgical [staff](#staff), typically in [mint](#mint) green, blue or pink. Distinct from a nurse's [dress](#dress) uniform or a doctor's lab [coat](#coat).

entries.name: mixed_maids
entries.description: Maid outfits from different cultural traditions appearing together in one picture - a Western frilled [maid](#maid) beside a [wa_maid](#wa_maid) or qi maid, for instance. The [contrast](#contrast) between the styles is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: polka_dot_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) scattered with evenly spaced round [dots](#dots). The [spots](#spots) may [cover](#cover) the whole [cloth](#cloth) or sit as a band along the hem or [pocket](#pocket).

entries.name: qi_maid
entries.description: A [maid](#maid) uniform reworked with Chinese [dress](#dress) elements, such as a mandarin [collar](#collar), [frog](#frog) fastenings, and a qipao-style cut with side slits. It stands as the Chinese counterpart to the standard maid outfit.

entries.name: brown_jumpsuit
entries.description: A one-piece garment joining top and trousers, coloured brown. It covers work coveralls, flight suits and [casual](#casual) jumpsuits alike.

entries.name: aqua_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) in a blue-green [shade](#shade), tied over other [clothes](#clothes) for [cooking](#cooking), [waiting](#waiting) tables or housework. Only the colour is recorded; the apron's cut and trim keep their own tags.

entries.name: checkered_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) cut from [cloth](#cloth) [patterned](#patterned) in alternating squares, from fine [gingham](#gingham) to bold blocks. Kitchens, cafes and [maid](#maid) outfits are where it shows up.

entries.name: torn_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) ripped or shredded, its [bib](#bib) or ties [hanging](#hanging) loose.

entries.name: unworn_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) lies in the scene with nobody wearing it, hung on a [hook](#hook), draped over furniture or left in a heap. The garment must actually be visible rather than merely implied.

entries.name: collared_jumpsuit
entries.description: A full-length one-piece [suit](#suit) finished with a proper [shirt](#shirt) [collar](#collar) at the [neck](#neck). Typical of workwear, flight suits and uniform-styled outfits.

entries.name: vertical-striped_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) whose stripes run up and down its length rather than banding across it, common on [cafe](#cafe), [bakery](#bakery) and [kitchen](#kitchen) outfits, where the pattern reads as a uniform touch.

entries.name: closed_lab_coat
entries.description: A lab [coat](#coat) worn properly buttoned up rather than [hanging](#hanging) open. Much rarer in pictures than the usual [flapping](#flapping) version.

entries.name: tactical_maid
entries.description: A [maid](#maid) uniform crossed with modern combat gear — a [plate](#plate) carrier, pouches, holsters and [headset](#headset) worn over the [apron](#apron) and [frills](#frills). The [clash](#clash) between the two registers is the point of the design.

entries.name: gym_uniform
entries.description: The [clothes](#clothes) worn for physical education class: a white [gym_shirt](#gym_shirt) with [gym_shorts](#gym_shorts) for boys, or with [buruma](#buruma), [bike_shorts](#bike_shorts) or track [pants](#pants) for girls. Tag the individual pieces too.

entries.name: buruma
entries.description: Snug, underwear-like [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) worn with a gym [shirt](#shirt) as Japanese [school](#school) [sportswear](#sportswear). Long out of real use but a fixture in illustration; the looser boxer-cut [bloomers](#bloomers) are a different garment.

entries.name: sportswear
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) term for clothing worn to play sport, covering jerseys, [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts), tracksuits, [tennis](#tennis) dresses and cycling kit among others. Add the more specific garment [tag](#tag) alongside it where possible.

entries.name: dougi
entries.description: The [training](#training) uniform of [karate](#karate), [judo](#judo) and related arts: a wrap [jacket](#jacket) tied with a coloured [belt](#belt) over loose trousers. The Korean dobok is tagged here as [well](#well).

entries.name: track_suit
entries.description: A matched set of athletic [jacket](#jacket) and trousers worn for sports and warm-ups, a common look for [gym](#gym) teachers and [delinquent](#delinquent) characters alike.

entries.name: soccer_uniform
entries.description: A football kit of [jersey](#jersey), [shorts](#shorts), and long [socks](#socks) in team colors, worn on the pitch or as fan gear.

entries.name: wrestling_outfit
entries.description: Attire made for [wrestling](#wrestling), from a [realistic](#realistic) [singlet](#singlet) with pads to the flamboyant costumes of professional wrestling. Tag wrestling when the characters are actually competing, and [wrestling_ring](#wrestling_ring) for the venue.

entries.name: baseball_uniform
entries.description: The full kit of a [baseball](#baseball) player: buttoned [jersey](#jersey), belted trousers, cap and often stirrup [socks](#socks). Worn on the [field](#field) or as fan and [cheering](#cheering) wear.

entries.name: jersey
entries.description: A sports [shirt](#shirt), usually [carrying](#carrying) a number or a team [badge](#badge), as worn by players. It does not mean a track [jacket](#jacket) or track [suit](#suit), even though the Japanese word covers those.

entries.name: tennis_uniform
entries.description: Light [sportswear](#sportswear) for [tennis](#tennis): a [shirt](#shirt) with [shorts](#shorts) on men, a shirt with a short [skirt](#skirt) or shorts on women, often finished with a visor cap.

entries.name: volleyball_uniform
entries.description: Sportswear for [volleyball](#volleyball): a tight [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [jersey](#jersey) with short [shorts](#shorts), bike shorts or [buruma](#buruma), often finished with knee pads, elbow pads or sleeves.

entries.name: biker_clothes
entries.description: The [riding](#riding) kit of a motorcyclist: [leather](#leather) [jacket](#jacket), sturdy trousers, [gloves](#gloves) and [boots](#boots), often with a [helmet](#helmet). Occasionally used for a [racing](#racing) cyclist's gear as [well](#well).

entries.name: basketball_uniform
entries.description: A [basketball](#basketball) player's kit, generally a loose [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top with a number and long matching [shorts](#shorts). Worn on court and, in [fashion](#fashion) pictures, as [street](#street) clothing.

entries.name: martial_arts_belt
entries.description: The coloured [cloth](#cloth) [belt](#belt) knotted over a [dougi](#dougi) or similar [training](#training) outfit, which also states the wearer's rank. Normally seen with the uniform rather than by itself.

entries.name: karate_gi
entries.description: The white cotton [training](#training) [suit](#suit) for [karate](#karate): a wrap [jacket](#jacket) over loose trousers, closed with a coloured [belt](#belt). It is cut [lighter](#lighter) and looser than the [heavy](#heavy) jacket [judo](#judo) requires.

entries.name: hooded_track_jacket
entries.description: A zip-up sports track [jacket](#jacket) with a [hood](#hood) built in. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) depending on how it is worn.

entries.name: track_uniform
entries.description: Competition wear for athletics, ranging from a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top and [shorts](#shorts) to a [gym](#gym) uniform or sports [bikini](#bikini) depending on the wearer. Add [track_and_field](#track_and_field) for the event itself.

entries.name: red_track_suit
entries.description: A red track [suit](#suit), the zip-up [jacket](#jacket) and matching [pants](#pants) worn for sport or as [casual](#casual) [gym](#gym) wear. Tag [track_suit](#track_suit) too; a red track jacket alone may be [red_jacket](#red_jacket).

entries.name: band_uniform
entries.description: The bright, heavily trimmed [dress](#dress) of a [marching](#marching) band: a [tall](#tall) shako cap, a braided [jacket](#jacket), and for women a short [pleated](#pleated) [skirt](#skirt). A baton or a brass [instrument](#instrument) generally comes with it.

entries.name: pink_track_suit
entries.description: A matching pink [jacket](#jacket) and trousers of the zip-up sporting kind. Worn for [training](#training) or as [casual](#casual) [streetwear](#streetwear).

entries.name: racing_suit
entries.description: The one-piece fireproof overall worn by [racing](#racing) drivers and pit crew, usually padded, zipped up the front, and covered in sponsor patches. Built for protection from flame and heat rather than for [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: basketball_jersey
entries.description: The [sleeveless](#sleeveless) team top worn for [basketball](#basketball), cut with deep armholes and a number front and [back](#back). It hangs loose over [shorts](#shorts) in the same colours.

entries.name: baseball_jersey
entries.description: The buttoned [shirt](#shirt) of a [baseball](#baseball) kit, usually with a team name across the chest and a number on the [back](#back). It goes with the trousers and cap to make the full uniform.

entries.name: workout_clothes
entries.description: Clothing made for exercise: fitted tops, [shorts](#shorts), [leggings](#leggings), and sports bras. It is worn for personal [training](#training) rather than as an issued [school](#school) [gym](#gym) uniform.

entries.name: bike_jersey
entries.description: A close-cut cycling top with a short [neck](#neck) zip, pockets across the [back](#back) and loud sponsor-style printing. Usually worn with bike [shorts](#shorts) on [racing](#racing) and touring designs.

entries.name: cycling_uniform
entries.description: Road-racing kit: a tight [jersey](#jersey), padded [shorts](#shorts), [gloves](#gloves), a hard [shell](#shell) [helmet](#helmet) and stiff [shoes](#shoes). Purpose-built [racing](#racing) clothing rather than everyday [sportswear](#sportswear).

entries.name: american_football_uniform
entries.description: The kit of a gridiron player: a [numbered](#numbered) short-sleeved [jersey](#jersey) over bulky shoulder padding, tight trousers, [gloves](#gloves) and a [helmet](#helmet). Fanservice versions tend to leave the padding out.

entries.name: boxing_shorts
entries.description: Wide loose [shorts](#shorts) cut to about mid-thigh with a broad elastic waistband, worn in the [ring](#ring). They generally turn up alongside [gloves](#gloves) and high laced [boots](#boots).

entries.name: purple_buruma
entries.description: The tight, high-cut [gym](#gym) [shorts](#shorts) of Japanese [school](#school) PE kit, here in purple. Usually paired with a gym [shirt](#shirt) and indoor [shoes](#shoes).

entries.name: figure_skating_dress
entries.description: Competition wear for the [ice](#ice): a fitted [leotard](#leotard) with a very short attached [skirt](#skirt), often sequinned and with sheer sleeves. Cut to leave the [legs](#legs) free for jumps.

entries.name: blue_track_suit
entries.description: A blue athletic set of zip-fronted [jacket](#jacket) and matching trousers, often with a contrasting stripe down the sleeve and leg. Worn for [training](#training) and just as readily as everyday clothing.

entries.name: rugby_uniform
entries.description: The rugby kit of a [heavy](#heavy) collared [jersey](#jersey) with broad hoops or a club [crest](#crest), short [shorts](#shorts) and long [socks](#socks) over [studded](#studded) [boots](#boots). Often shown muddied after play.

entries.name: green_track_suit
entries.description: A green tracksuit: the zip-up [jacket](#jacket) with matching trousers of a sports kit. Beyond athletics it is standard wear for delinquents and [gym](#gym) teachers.

entries.name: black_track_suit
entries.description: A black athletic two-piece of zip-up [jacket](#jacket) and matching trousers, often with a contrasting stripe down the arm or leg. Worn for [training](#training) or as everyday [casual](#casual) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: bougu
entries.description: The protective kit worn for [kendo](#kendo): a grilled face [mask](#mask) with shoulder flaps, padded forearm [gauntlets](#gauntlets), a lacquered chest [cuirass](#cuirass) and an [apron](#apron) of [heavy](#heavy) [cloth](#cloth) flaps at the waist. Naginata practice adds shin guards.

entries.name: buruma_under_skirt
entries.description: Gym [bloomers](#bloomers) worn beneath a [skirt](#skirt) and showing under its hem, as when a uniform is only half changed.

entries.name: racing_colors
entries.description: The bright, [patterned](#patterned) silks a [jockey](#jockey) wears during a [horse](#horse) race, registered to identify the horse's owner. In horse-racing-themed art the outfits often echo the colors carried by each character's real-world counterpart.

entries.name: cosplay
entries.description: A character dressed as a different fictional character, from their own series or another one. Name who is being imitated with the matching xxx_(cosplay) [tag](#tag); photographs of real [people](#people) in [costume](#costume) are [cosplay_photo](#cosplay_photo).

entries.name: playboy_bunny
entries.description: The classic bunny-girl outfit: a [strapless](#strapless) [leotard](#leotard), fake [rabbit](#rabbit) ears and [tail](#tail), wrist [cuffs](#cuffs), a [collar](#collar) with [bowtie](#bowtie), [fishnets](#fishnets) or [thighhighs](#thighhighs), and heels. Colour changes and missing [accessories](#accessories) still count; a real rabbit-eared character without this [costume](#costume) does not.

entries.name: magical_girl
entries.description: The frilled [transformation](#transformation) outfit of the mahou shoujo heroine: short [skirt](#skirt), ribbons, [gloves](#gloves) and a decorative [brooch](#brooch) or [wand](#wand). Applied for the [costume](#costume) rather than the story role, so a character simply dressed that way counts.

entries.name: fake_tail
entries.description: An artificial [tail](#tail) worn as an accessory, glued on, sewn to clothing or fixed to a plug. The bunny-girl cottontail is the standard case.

entries.name: santa_costume
entries.description: Clothing styled after Santa Claus, red [fabric](#fabric) with white fur edges, in any form from a full [suit](#suit) to a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) or [lingerie](#lingerie), often with a wide black [belt](#belt). If only the [hat](#hat) is Santa-themed use [santa_hat](#santa_hat) alone.

entries.name: enmaided
entries.description: A character who is not a [maid](#maid) put into a western maid outfit. Only the western style counts; the Japanese wa maid version simply takes [alternate_costume](#alternate_costume).

entries.name: meme_attire
entries.description: An outfit that became a [running](#running) joke among artists and gets [redrawn](#redrawn) on many different characters, [spreading](#spreading) [well](#well) beyond its original design. Tag the specific garment itself alongside this one.

entries.name: gyaru
entries.description: A girl in Japanese gal [fashion](#fashion): dyed or bleached hair, [heavy](#heavy) [makeup](#makeup) with false lashes and [circle](#circle) lenses, trendy revealing [clothes](#clothes) and often a [tan](#tan). Tan skin and blonde hair alone do not make a gyaru; the whole look and attitude does.

entries.name: halloween_costume
entries.description: A character wears an outfit or [accessories](#accessories) made for Halloween: orange and black [clothes](#clothes), [skeleton](#skeleton) or [skull](#skull) prints, [jack-o'-lantern](#jack-o'-lantern) motifs, [demon](#demon) [horns](#horns) and [tail](#tail), and [candy](#candy) hair ornaments among them.

entries.name: habit
entries.description: The religious garb of a [nun](#nun) or [priest](#priest), usually a black [dress](#dress) with a [veil](#veil) over a white [coif](#coif). Covers the whole outfit rather than only the [headdress](#headdress); colours and lengths vary in fiction.

entries.name: gothic_lolita
entries.description: Lolita [dress](#dress) in a [dark](#dark) [key](#key): black or deep-toned frilled dresses, [lace](#lace), petticoats and Victorian [doll](#doll) styling. Use it when the outfit reads gothic rather than sweet or classic; [lolita_fashion](#lolita_fashion) is implied.

entries.name: animal_costume
entries.description: Someone is dressed as a recognisable [creature](#creature), usually in a full-body [suit](#suit) with head and paws. Wearing nothing but an [animal_hat](#animal_hat) does not qualify.

entries.name: fox_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) shaped like a fox's face, most often the painted white [kitsune](#kitsune) mask of Japanese festivals. It is worn over the face or pushed up to the side of the head.

entries.name: superhero_costume
entries.description: A Western-style superhero outfit: [bodysuit](#bodysuit), [cape](#cape), a domino or full [mask](#mask), an [emblem](#emblem) on the chest. A purely visual [tag](#tag) that applies just as [well](#well) to a villain dressed the same way.

entries.name: reverse_outfit
entries.description: An outfit built as the [negative](#negative) of a [familiar](#familiar) garment: [cloth](#cloth) covers only where the original had none, so a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top becomes only detached sleeves. Usually done to turn a well-known design into revealing [clothes](#clothes); the [reverse_bunnysuit](#reverse_bunnysuit) is the best-known case.

entries.name: costume_switch
entries.description: Two or more characters wearing each other's usual outfits in one picture. Both sides must have traded; one character in another's [clothes](#clothes), or only one of a pair swapped, is [plain](#plain) [cosplay](#cosplay).

entries.name: idol_clothes
entries.description: Stage [costume](#costume) for a pop performer: frilled and sparkling dresses for girls, sharp accessorised suits for boys, often matched across a whole group. It is too elaborate to wear anywhere but a performance.

entries.name: goth_fashion
entries.description: Dark, sometimes morbid [dress](#dress) drawing on Elizabethan and Victorian lines: stark black clothing, [lace](#lace) and [silk](#silk), high heels, with deep red, purple or green as accents. It covers western and Japanese gothic styles alike.

entries.name: reverse_bunnysuit
entries.description: A [meme](#meme) outfit that inverts the Playboy bunny [suit](#suit): the [leotard](#leotard) is missing and the [torso](#torso) is bare, while the arms and [legs](#legs) keep their coverings in a [cropped](#cropped) [jacket](#jacket) or shrug, legwear, [cuffs](#cuffs), and [collar](#collar). Bunny ears, a [tail](#tail), and often [pasties](#pasties) complete it.

entries.name: unworn_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) has been pulled off the face and left visible in the scene, held, pushed up or set aside.

entries.name: pirate_costume
entries.description: Pirate [dress](#dress) worn as an outfit: [tricorne](#tricorne) or [bandana](#bandana), frock [coat](#coat), [sash](#sash), high [boots](#boots) and a [cutlass](#cutlass) at the hip. Use it for the [clothes](#clothes), on a real [pirate](#pirate) or on somebody in fancy dress.

entries.name: kogal
entries.description: A schoolgirl take on [gyaru](#gyaru) [fashion](#fashion): [heavy](#heavy) eye [makeup](#makeup), dyed or bleached hair, sometimes a [tan](#tan), and a uniform worn with a very short [skirt](#skirt) and loose [socks](#socks). Without the school-uniform cues, [plain](#plain) gyaru is the better [tag](#tag).

entries.name: virgin_killer_sweater
entries.description: A backless, [halterneck](#halterneck) [turtleneck](#turtleneck) [sweater](#sweater) [dress](#dress) with a [drawstring](#drawstring) at the neckband, made famous online. Usually worn with nothing underneath, exposing [sideboob](#sideboob), the whole [back](#back) and often the top of the buttocks; distinct from the [virgin_killer_outfit](#virgin_killer_outfit).

entries.name: harem_outfit
entries.description: Bellydancer-style [dress](#dress): a bare [midriff](#midriff) between a [bra](#bra) or [bustier](#bustier) and either baggy trousers, a [loincloth](#loincloth) or a long [skirt](#skirt), finished with a [veil](#veil) or [headdress](#headdress), loose sleeves and a good deal of jewellery. Individual pieces are often sheer. Dunhuang-style robes are easily mistaken for it.

entries.name: jirai_kei
entries.description: A Japanese [street](#street) style built on short [twintails](#twintails) or two side-up hair, a mouth [mask](#mask), a frilled collared [shirt](#shirt), a high-waisted suspender [skirt](#skirt), [fishnets](#fishnets) and a [heavy](#heavy) pink-and-black palette. Variations abound, but they hold to that recipe.

entries.name: costume
entries.description: Clothing that makes the wearer look like something they are not: an [animal](#animal), a [monster](#monster), a [mascot](#mascot), a holiday [figure](#figure). Reach for a specific [tag](#tag) such as [santa_costume](#santa_costume) or [animal_costume](#animal_costume) when one fits.

entries.name: matching_outfits
entries.description: Two or more characters dressed alike, or in outfits that plainly share theme and detail, sometimes with the colours swapped between them. Uniforms and [idol](#idol) [stage](#stage) [clothes](#clothes) are excluded, since matching is their design.

entries.name: nontraditional_playboy_bunny
entries.description: A bunny-girl [costume](#costume) that departs from the [plain](#plain) [rabbit](#rabbit) ears and [leotard](#leotard), such as a cat-eared [suit](#suit), [fox](#fox) ears, or a variant themed on some other [creature](#creature).

entries.name: fake_wings
