entries.description: Pretend [wings](#wings) that are [no](#no) part of the body: [costume](#costume) add-ons, objects arranged into wing [shapes](#shapes), or wings painted on a wall behind the character. Real wings hovering unattached are [detached_wings](#detached_wings).

entries.name: ouji_fashion
entries.description: The princely counterpart to lolita [fashion](#fashion): short trousers, waistcoats, ascots, [epaulettes](#epaulettes), capes and top hats drawn from Victorian boys' [dress](#dress). Worn by [bishounen](#bishounen), [crossdressing](#crossdressing) girls and [androgynous](#androgynous) characters.

entries.name: mummy_costume
entries.description: An outfit of wound [bandages](#bandages) made to look like a [mummy](#mummy), worn by a living character. A standard Halloween [choice](#choice), and distinct from an actual [undead](#undead) mummy.

entries.name: fake_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard) or moustache that is plainly not growing there, worn for a [disguise](#disguise) or a [costume](#costume) such as Santa. Common on female characters; a woman whose [facial](#facial) hair looks real is bearded_girl.

entries.name: male_playboy_bunny
entries.description: A male character in bunny-suit [dress](#dress), often an [otoko_no_ko](#otoko_no_ko). Some versions swap the [leotard](#leotard) for a tuxedo-like cut, since the original [costume](#costume) was built on [evening](#evening) dress.

entries.name: fake_mustache
entries.description: A false moustache of loose hair or felt worn on the upper lip, usually for a joke or a [disguise](#disguise). Especially noticeable on a female character.

entries.name: ghost_costume
entries.description: An outfit made to look like a [ghost](#ghost): a white sheet with eye holes, a white hooded [cloak](#cloak), or the [plain](#plain) white burial [kimono](#kimono) and triangular [headpiece](#headpiece) of Japanese tradition. Often shown with [floating](#floating) soul flames and a limp-wristed [ghost_pose](#ghost_pose).

entries.name: kigurumi
entries.description: Full-body [costume](#costume) in which a [mask](#mask) and [suit](#suit) hide the wearer completely, [giving](#giving) a living-doll or [mascot](#mascot) look. It is not the animal-print [onesie](#onesie) worn as pyjamas.

entries.name: reindeer_costume
entries.description: An outfit styled after a [reindeer](#reindeer), with brown fur, [antlers](#antlers), and often a red [nose](#nose), as seen in Christmas pictures. Tagged as an [animal](#animal) [costume](#costume); describes the outfit, not the animal.

entries.name: tribal
entries.description: Characters styled after an [indigenous](#indigenous) or pre-modern tribal [people](#people): sparse clothing, face or body [paint](#paint), [bone](#bone) or feather ornaments, and simple weapons such as spears. Also covers tribal-pattern designs printed on clothing or drawn on skin.

entries.name: shark_costume
entries.description: A full-body [costume](#costume) shaped like a [shark](#shark), the wearer's face showing at its mouth.

entries.name: food-themed_clothes
entries.description: Clothing built around a [food](#food) or [drink](#drink) theme, whether printed with it, cut into its shape or finished with edible-looking [accessories](#accessories). The food is understood to be fake, unlike [food_as_clothes](#food_as_clothes).

entries.name: vampire_costume
entries.description: Dressing up as a stock Western [vampire](#vampire), a Halloween favourite built from a black [cape](#cape) with a high [collar](#collar), an [ascot](#ascot), fake [fangs](#fangs) and [blood](#blood) smears, sometimes with bat [wings](#wings) or a bat-shaped hair ornament. The wearer is not actually a vampire.

entries.name: prison_clothes
entries.description: Inmate garb: either a [shirt](#shirt) and trousers in black-and-white stripes or an orange [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit). Often paired with [handcuffs](#handcuffs), a cell setting, or a [prisoner](#prisoner) number. Applies to the outfit whether or not the wearer is actually imprisoned.

entries.name: sweet_lolita
entries.description: The pastel [branch](#branch) of lolita [fashion](#fashion), drawing on rococo and Victorian children's wear: soft pinks, [baby](#baby) blue, white and [mint](#mint), with the heaviest use of [frills](#frills), bows and [lace](#lace) among the style's variants.

entries.name: streetwear
entries.description: Trendy [urban](#urban) [fashion](#fashion) [mixing](#mixing) [casual](#casual) and athletic pieces with designer brands: hoodies, [sneakers](#sneakers), caps, oversized jackets. Draws on hip hop, skate and [punk](#punk) subcultures rather than formal or traditional [dress](#dress).

entries.name: no_mask
entries.description: A character usually seen [masked](#masked) appears with the face uncovered. The [mask](#mask) is absent from the picture; one held or [hanging](#hanging) is [unworn_mask](#unworn_mask).

entries.name: jiangshi_costume
entries.description: A character who is not [undead](#undead) wears the trappings of a [hopping](#hopping) [vampire](#vampire): the [forehead](#forehead) charm, the round rimmed cap and often a [china](#china) [dress](#dress). Use [jiangshi](#jiangshi) for the real thing.

entries.name: dracula_costume
entries.description: The theatrical vampire-lord outfit: a high-collared [cape](#cape), a formal black [suit](#suit), a [medallion](#medallion) and usually false [fangs](#fangs). The wearer is dressed up rather than actually [undead](#undead).

entries.name: noh_mask
entries.description: A carved wooden [mask](#mask) from classical Japanese theatre, painted or lacquered and tied on with red cord. Human ones have pale calm faces whose mood shifts with the angle, while [demon](#demon) and [spirit](#spirit) masks carry huge eyes, [horns](#horns), [fangs](#fangs) and [gold](#gold) highlights.

entries.name: bear_costume
entries.description: A full-body outfit or [kigurumi](#kigurumi) built to look like a [bear](#bear), [hood](#hood) and ears included. It is something the character has put on, not their real body.

entries.name: punk
entries.description: Punk [fashion](#fashion): bold hair such as a [mohawk](#mohawk) or [spikes](#spikes), [torn](#torn) [casual](#casual) [clothes](#clothes), [leather](#leather), [studs](#studs), and safety pins, weighted toward black, red, and white. Tag the look as a whole and add the individual garments alongside it.

entries.name: horned_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) with [horns](#horns) attached to it, worn over the face or pushed up onto the head. Horned helmets and other horned [headgear](#headgear) have tags of their own.

entries.name: red_nose
entries.description: A round red [ball](#ball) worn over the [nose](#nose), the mark of a [clown](#clown) or of Rudolph the [reindeer](#reindeer). Typically appears with a clown outfit or a Christmas reindeer [costume](#costume).

entries.name: virgin_destroyer_sweater
entries.description: A [meme](#meme) outfit: a variant of the [virgin_killer_sweater](#virgin_killer_sweater) with detached sleeves and a chest panel that splits below the bust into garter-like straps joined to [sweater](#sweater) [thighhighs](#thighhighs), usually worn with a matching [thong](#thong). Went viral in a fan art challenge around a Christmas season.

entries.name: cat_costume
entries.description: An outfit for [dressing](#dressing) as a [cat](#cat), with fake ears, a [tail](#tail), paws or a whole fur [suit](#suit). Not the same thing as a [catsuit](#catsuit), the zip-fronted skin-tight [bodysuit](#bodysuit), though both [can](#can) apply at once.

entries.name: wolf_costume
entries.description: A [wolf](#wolf) outfit worn over ordinary [clothes](#clothes), complete with ears, a [tail](#tail), and sometimes a full head covering. Halloween scenes account for most examples, though [cosplay](#cosplay) counts too.

entries.name: tengu_mask
entries.description: The long-nosed folk [mask](#mask) of the [tengu](#tengu), usually painted bright red with fierce brows and a stern mouth. Worn over the face, pushed up onto the head, or hung on a wall as decoration.

entries.name: werewolf_costume
entries.description: A dress-up [wolf](#wolf) outfit, whether a [furry](#furry) [suit](#suit), a fanged [mask](#mask), or clip-on ears and [claws](#claws), worn by someone who plainly hasn't transformed. Halloween scenes are its usual home.

entries.name: rabbit_costume
entries.description: A full-body [rabbit](#rabbit) [suit](#suit) worn as a [mascot](#mascot) or [kigurumi](#kigurumi) [costume](#costume). Not the same as the [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny) [leotard](#leotard) outfit, and not for a character with genuine rabbit features.

entries.name: virgin_killer_outfit
entries.description: A viral Japanese look: a [dark](#dark) high-waisted [skirt](#skirt), suspender skirt or [underbust](#underbust) [corset](#corset) over a white [blouse](#blouse), cut to emphasise the chest. Resembles some [waitress](#waitress) uniforms, and is not the same as the [virgin_killer_sweater](#virgin_killer_sweater).

entries.name: magical_boy
entries.description: The masculine version of the [transformation](#transformation) [costume](#costume) worn by magical girls, with the same ornament and flourish cut for a boyish [silhouette](#silhouette). It describes the outfit, so a character of any [sex](#sex) wearing one qualifies.

entries.name: clown_nose
entries.description: The round [foam](#foam) or rubber [ball](#ball), usually red, slipped over the [nose](#nose) as part of a clown's [makeup](#makeup). One accessory is enough to read a face as a clown's.

entries.name: cat_mask
entries.description: A face covering built to look like a [cat](#cat), from a flat painted [festival](#festival) [mask](#mask) to a full moulded head. Often worn pushed up on the [forehead](#forehead) rather than over the eyes.

entries.name: decora
entries.description: A Harajuku [street](#street) look piled high with plastic clips, stacked bracelets and clashing sweet colours. The sheer quantity of [accessories](#accessories) defines it rather than any one garment.

entries.name: emo_fashion
entries.description: A [dark](#dark) teenage look from the 2000s, part [punk](#punk) and part gothic lolita: black clothing, [studded](#studded) belts, piercings and [heavy](#heavy) [eyeliner](#eyeliner). Its brighter relative is scene [fashion](#fashion), and the two often blur together.

entries.name: cyber_fashion
entries.description: A Harajuku [street](#street) look built on nineties retrofuturism: shiny vinyl, faux fur, holographic and [transparent](#transparent) [fabric](#fabric), visor caps, [goggles](#goggles), masks and plastic jewellery. Colours run loud, motifs favour aliens, planets and computers, and synthetic [dreadlocks](#dreadlocks) often finish it.

entries.name: self_cosplay
entries.description: One version of a character dressed in the [clothes](#clothes) belonging to another version of herself, such as a heroine's everyday identity wearing her transformed outfit. The hair usually reveals which form the body actually is.

entries.name: cow_costume
entries.description: A full-body [cow](#cow) outfit, generally a hooded [onesie](#onesie) in [patch](#patch) print with ears and [horns](#horns) attached. Plain cow-print [clothes](#clothes), or a cow girl without the [suit](#suit), do not count.

entries.name: kittysuit
entries.description: A bunny-suit [leotard](#leotard) worn with [cat](#cat) ears and a cat [tail](#tail) in place of the [rabbit](#rabbit) set. Japanese fandom calls the look a nekomimi bunny.

entries.name: translucent_bunnysuit
entries.description: A black plastic bunnysuit with a clear panel cut down the centre, based on a real garment sold online. The design spread widely after one artist invited others to draw it on their own characters.

entries.name: penguin_costume
entries.description: An outfit built to look like a [penguin](#penguin), a white front on a black body with a [hood](#hood) or [headpiece](#headpiece) [carrying](#carrying) the [beak](#beak), often finished with flipper sleeves.

entries.name: yellow_mask
entries.description: A yellow [mask](#mask) over part or all of the face, of any design.

entries.name: plague_doctor_mask
entries.description: The long beaked [mask](#mask) of the plague physician, its hollow bill once stuffed with herbs against foul air. Worn alone it still reads as the whole [costume](#costume).

entries.name: wrestling_mask
entries.description: The close-fitting [fabric](#fabric) [hood](#hood) of a lucha libre [wrestler](#wrestler), cut open at the eyes and mouth and boldly decorated. It carries the wearer's [ring](#ring) identity as part of the persona.

entries.name: sheep_costume
entries.description: A full woolly outfit made to resemble a [sheep](#sheep), typically a fleecy body [suit](#suit) with a [hood](#hood) [carrying](#carrying) ears and curled [horns](#horns), worn as one whole piece. Implies [animal_costume](#animal_costume).

entries.name: fake_claws
entries.description: Claw-shaped pieces worn over the fingers or nails as part of a [costume](#costume). They only look the part and serve [no](#no) purpose.

entries.name: gyaruo
entries.description: The male side of [gyaru](#gyaru) [fashion](#fashion): deep tans or [dark](#dark) skin, bleached hair and loose showy [streetwear](#streetwear). Characters wearing it are typically drawn as brash, flirtatious young men.

entries.name: tiger_costume
entries.description: A full outfit made to look like a [tiger](#tiger), striped [fabric](#fabric) with a [hood](#hood) [carrying](#carrying) ears on top. Worn as [party](#party) or [kigurumi](#kigurumi) [dress](#dress), not the body of an actual tiger character.

entries.name: classic_lolita
entries.description: The [restrained](#restrained), historically minded [branch](#branch) of lolita [fashion](#fashion): longer skirts, muted colours and Victorian motifs such as florals, crowns and fine art prints. More sober in look than the pastel sweet style.

entries.name: character_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) made to look like one specific character, worn over the face or pushed up onto the head. Party masks, [festival](#festival) masks and full [mascot](#mascot) heads all count.

entries.name: mascot_costume
entries.description: A full-body character [suit](#suit) with an oversized head that hides the wearer completely, of the sort worn at parks, [matches](#matches) and conventions. Add [mascot_head](#mascot_head) only once the head has come off and shows separately.

entries.name: dinosaur_costume
entries.description: A padded [suit](#suit) shaped like a [dinosaur](#dinosaur), with a toothy [hood](#hood) and a stuffed [tail](#tail) [dragging](#dragging) behind. Party and [mascot](#mascot) wear rather than a real body.

entries.name: hannya
entries.description: A horned theatre [mask](#mask) with bared [teeth](#teeth) and a twisted, grieving glare, representing a woman consumed by jealousy. It is more angular and more anguished than the plainer [oni](#oni) mask it is often [confused](#confused) with.

entries.name: jester_costume
entries.description: A fool's outfit sewn in blocks of contrasting colour, worn with a limp many-pointed cap hung with bells. A ruffled [collar](#collar) and [shoes](#shoes) that curl at the toe often complete it.

entries.name: cracked_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) [damaged](#damaged) so that cracks run across it, or with pieces [broken](#broken) away entirely. It still has to be recognisable as a mask.

entries.name: dog_costume
entries.description: A [suit](#suit) made to look like a [dog](#dog), ears and [tail](#tail) attached, pulled on over the [clothes](#clothes). Party and [mascot](#mascot) wear rather than an actual [animal](#animal) body.

entries.name: headwear_switch
entries.description: A character wears headwear belonging to somebody else, usually a [hat](#hat) recognisable as another's. When the whole outfit is swapped as [well](#well), it becomes [cosplay](#cosplay).

entries.name: fake_beard
entries.description: A false [beard](#beard) held on by straps, [glue](#glue) or elastic for a [costume](#costume) or a [disguise](#disguise). Santa suits and [stage](#stage) roles are the usual reason for one.

entries.name: tenshi_kaiwai
entries.description: A Japanese [fashion](#fashion) aesthetic built on pale blue and white, [blending](#blending) cute subculture pieces with motifs of angels, [water](#water) and technology. Track jackets and jersey-fabric [maid](#maid) outfits are typical, and the look shades into yume kawaii and Y2K styling.

entries.name: panda_costume
entries.description: A dress-up outfit made to look like a [giant](#giant) [panda](#panda), usually black ears and limbs against a white body. The colour [split](#split) varies, and long sleeves are part of the effect.

entries.name: tailcoat_playboy_bunny
entries.description: A playboy bunny [leotard](#leotard) worn together with a formal [tailcoat](#tailcoat) over it, [blending](#blending) cabaret [costume](#costume) with [evening](#evening) [dress](#dress). Ears and [cuffs](#cuffs) usually complete the look.

entries.name: frog_costume
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) [costume](#costume) shaped as a [frog](#frog), typically a green hooded [suit](#suit) with eyes perched on the [crown](#crown). Worn as a whole outfit rather than as a [hood](#hood) on its own.

entries.name: rabbit_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) [carrying](#carrying) [rabbit](#rabbit) features, from a stylized [festival](#festival) piece to a full [animal](#animal) head. It covers the face while the wearer's own head remains underneath.

entries.name: dragon_costume
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) [suit](#suit) or [kigurumi](#kigurumi) pulled on over ordinary [clothes](#clothes), with a hooded head, a stuffed [tail](#tail) and often small [wings](#wings). Dressing up rather than actually draconic.

entries.name: pumpkin_costume
entries.description: An oversized [pumpkin](#pumpkin) worn as a Halloween outfit, the wearer's body [sitting](#sitting) inside the round [shell](#shell) with the limbs [poking](#poking) out. A [hat](#hat) or [mask](#mask) alone is not enough to qualify.

entries.name: food_as_clothes
entries.description: Real [food](#food) worn in place of clothing, usually swollen far past its natural size: an aubergine [suit](#suit), a [mushroom](#mushroom) cap for a [hat](#hat), [cream](#cream) laid on skin in the shape of a garment. Spilled food and merely food-patterned [clothes](#clothes) are separate matters.

entries.name: mermaid_costume
entries.description: A [fish](#fish) [tail](#tail) worn as a removable [costume](#costume) piece rather than grown as [anatomy](#anatomy), easy to step [back](#back) out of. The more practical [swimming](#swimming) version is a monofin.

entries.name: oni_costume
entries.description: A dress-up [demon](#demon) outfit, usually a tiger-skin wrap with a horned [headband](#headband) and a [toy](#toy) club, worn for Setsubun or a [festival](#festival).

entries.name: demon_costume
entries.description: Horns, a spade-tipped [tail](#tail) and usually red or black clothing worn as an outfit rather than being the body itself. Party and Halloween [dress](#dress); a genuine [demon](#demon) takes the species [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bee_costume
entries.description: An outfit built to look like a [bee](#bee): yellow and black bands, attached [antennae](#antennae), small round [wings](#wings) and often a [stinger](#stinger). It is worn, unlike a bee girl's own body.

entries.name: boar_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) shaped as a boar's face, [snout](#snout) and [tusks](#tusks) included, worn over the face or pushed up onto the [forehead](#forehead). Festival and [tribal](#tribal) scenes are where it usually turns up.

entries.name: black_santa_costume
entries.description: The fur-trimmed Christmas [suit](#suit) made up in black instead of the usual red. Coat, trim and [hat](#hat) keep their [familiar](#familiar) shape; only the [fabric](#fabric) colour changes.

entries.name: french_girly
entries.description: A soft girlish coordinate built from pastel colours, ribbons, [lace](#lace) and vintage-cut blouses and skirts. It names a Japanese [fashion](#fashion) style rather than any one garment.

entries.name: christmas_tree_costume
entries.description: An outfit built to look like a decorated fir, usually a cone-shaped green [dress](#dress) hung with baubles and topped with a star. Worn by a character, as opposed to the decoration itself.

entries.name: chicken_costume
entries.description: A full-body [chicken](#chicken) [suit](#suit) with [feathers](#feathers), stubby [wings](#wings) and a floppy [comb](#comb), worn as a [mascot](#mascot) outfit or a [party](#party) joke. The wearer's face usually shows through an [opening](#opening) at the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: playboy_bunny_swimsuit
entries.description: A bunny-girl outfit built on a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) rather than the usual [leotard](#leotard), worn with the ears, [collar](#collar) and [cuffs](#cuffs) intact. The cut of the body garment is the whole difference.

entries.name: lion_costume
entries.description: An outfit made to look like a [lion](#lion), from a full plush [suit](#suit) to a maned [hood](#hood) pulled over the head.

entries.name: skinsuit
entries.description: A full [bodysuit](#bodysuit) made of skin, worn to [disguise](#disguise) the wearer as someone or something else. The [idea](#idea) shades into [transformation](#transformation) stories and a fetish about wearing another body.

entries.name: bird_costume
entries.description: An outfit made to look like a [bird](#bird), with attached [wings](#wings), a feathered body and often a beaked [hood](#hood). It is clothing put on rather than the character's own [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: harlequin
entries.description: The motley of the pantomime [clown](#clown): brightly checkered or diamond-patterned clothing, usually with tights, a small [mask](#mask) and a wooden slapstick. The [costume](#costume) alone is enough to use this, without the shaved head or any other trapping.

entries.name: swimsuit_costume
entries.description: An outfit built around a [swimsuit](#swimsuit), usually a one-piece, dressed up with extra pieces so it reads as a character or [stage](#stage) [costume](#costume) rather than [plain](#plain) beachwear.

entries.name: mascot_head
entries.description: The huge [headpiece](#headpiece) of a character [suit](#suit), built to [chibi](#chibi) proportions. Use it where the head stands alone in frame or has been pulled off the rest of the [costume](#costume).

entries.name: animegao
entries.description: A smooth full-head [mask](#mask) sculpted into an anime character's face, worn by a costumed performer whose own features vanish behind it. The fixed, doll-like expression is the whole point.

entries.name: fox_costume
entries.description: An outfit made to look like a [fox](#fox), whether a full furred [suit](#suit) or a set of ears, [tail](#tail) and russet colouring. It is worn rather than being the character's own body.

entries.name: hamster_costume
entries.description: An outfit built to make the wearer look like a [hamster](#hamster), with rounded ears, puffed cheeks and a stub [tail](#tail). It runs from a full plush [bodysuit](#bodysuit) to a [hood](#hood) or [cape](#cape) with ears attached.

entries.name: food_costume
entries.description: A whole outfit made to resemble a recognisable dish or ingredient, in most cases a full-body [suit](#suit). Clothing merely themed after [food](#food) is [food-themed_clothes](#food-themed_clothes).

entries.name: clown_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) painted as a clown's face, with a wide [grin](#grin), a bulbous [nose](#nose) and often tufts of hair. Used for performers and, just as often, for horror.

entries.name: pig_costume
entries.description: A full-body outfit made to look like a [pig](#pig), [snout](#snout) [hood](#hood) and curled [tail](#tail) included. It is fancy [dress](#dress) or a [mascot](#mascot) [suit](#suit) worn over the character, never their actual body.

entries.name: palette_suit
entries.description: An outfit built from blocks of colour laid out like a painter's palette or a colour [chart](#chart). Worn as a themed [costume](#costume) rather than as ordinary [dress](#dress).

entries.name: horse_mask
entries.description: A rubber [mask](#mask) of a horse's head pulled down over the face. Online it is worn to keep the wearer anonymous, much as a Guy Fawkes mask is elsewhere.

entries.name: anglerfish_costume
entries.description: An outfit built to look like a deep-sea [anglerfish](#anglerfish), usually a [hood](#hood) or [headpiece](#headpiece) with the [dangling](#dangling) lure and a wide toothy mouth. It is worn as a novelty rather than as swimwear.

entries.name: yuru-chara
entries.description: A simply designed, huggable [mascot](#mascot) character built to promote a [town](#town), region, business or event, usually centred on a local [animal](#animal) or specialty. It often appears as a costumed performer greeting visitors at festivals and promotional events.

entries.name: fake_whiskers
entries.description: Whiskers worn or painted on as part of a [costume](#costume), glued to the face or fixed to a [mask](#mask), rather than growing there.

entries.name: scene_fashion
entries.description: A louder, more colourful cousin of emo [dress](#dress): teased two-tone hair, cartoon-print tops, tutus and plaid, [studded](#studded) belts, chunky-framed [glasses](#glasses) and [heavy](#heavy) black [eyeliner](#eyeliner). Rainbows, skulls and [animal](#animal) prints are its stock motifs.

entries.name: fake_nose
entries.description: A false [nose](#nose) worn on the face, from a clown's red [ball](#ball) to the nose-and-glasses [disguise](#disguise). It is held on by elastic or a frame and belongs to a [costume](#costume) rather than the character.

entries.name: fish_costume
entries.description: An outfit built in the shape of a [fish](#fish), from a padded full-body [suit](#suit) to a hooded [shark](#shark) or [carp](#carp) getup. Worn for fun or [mascot](#mascot) work rather than being real [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: himekaji
entries.description: A Japanese [fashion](#fashion) look [mixing](#mixing) [princess](#princess) prettiness with everyday [clothes](#clothes): pastel knits, [lace](#lace) trim, soft curls and small jewellery. Sweet but wearable, [well](#well) short of full lolita [dress](#dress).

entries.name: blue_santa_costume
entries.description: The Christmas [suit](#suit) with its [coat](#coat), [hat](#hat) and white fur trim rendered in blue instead of red. Only the colour changes; the cut of the outfit is the [familiar](#familiar) one.

entries.name: tactical_playboy_bunny
entries.description: A playboy bunny outfit fitted out with [military](#military) gear such as thigh holsters, magazine pouches and a [headset](#headset). Ears and a [leotard](#leotard) alone are not enough; the load-bearing equipment needs to be visible.

entries.name: mori_kei
entries.description: The forest-girl look: loose layered natural fabrics in [cream](#cream) and earth tones, cardigans, knitted shawls, [lace](#lace) and [embroidery](#embroidery), all [hiding](#hiding) the line of the body. Handmade or vintage trinkets and soft minimal [makeup](#makeup) finish it.

entries.name: mouse_costume
entries.description: A mouse outfit pulled on over ordinary [clothes](#clothes), generally with a [hood](#hood) of round ears and a [string](#string) [tail](#tail) [hanging](#hanging) behind. The wearer stays plainly human underneath.

entries.name: torn_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) cracked or ripped apart, sometimes [hanging](#hanging) in pieces and leaving part of the face uncovered.

entries.name: techwear
entries.description: A near-future [streetwear](#streetwear) look built from technical fabrics: black or grey layers, hoods, harnesses and an abundance of straps, buckles and pockets. It reads [urban](#urban) and functional rather than [military](#military).

entries.name: tempura_costume
entries.description: A full-body outfit shaped like a piece of battered, deep-fried [food](#food), most often a prawn, with the wearer's face [poking](#poking) out of the coating. A [gag](#gag) [costume](#costume) rather than real clothing.

entries.name: wolf_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) shaped into a wolf's face, covering part or all of the wearer's own. Festival, [tribal](#tribal), and horror scenes all make use of it.

entries.name: constellation_costume
entries.description: An outfit [patterned](#patterned) with stars and the lines joining them, usually deep blue with points of [gold](#gold). A favourite for celestial and astrology designs.

entries.name: monkey_costume
entries.description: A [monkey](#monkey) [suit](#suit) pulled on over ordinary [clothes](#clothes), usually with a [hood](#hood) of round ears and a [tail](#tail) trailing behind. The wearer stays plainly human underneath.

entries.name: unworn_wig
entries.description: A [wig](#wig) appears in the picture off a head, held out, [sitting](#sitting) on a stand or [lying](#lying) discarded, often showing a character's own hair alongside it.

entries.name: tomato_costume
entries.description: A round red outfit that turns the wearer into an upright [tomato](#tomato), usually with a [hood](#hood) [carrying](#carrying) a green stem.

entries.name: jacket
entries.description: A sleeved outer garment ending at the hip or waist, cut from [lighter](#lighter) [cloth](#cloth) than a [coat](#coat). Related states have tags of their own: [open_jacket](#open_jacket), [jacket_on_shoulders](#jacket_on_shoulders), [jacket_around_waist](#jacket_around_waist), [jacket_over_hoodie](#jacket_over_hoodie).

entries.name: black_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) in black, taking in blazers, bombers, [leather](#leather) jackets and uniform jackets. A longer garment [falling](#falling) past the hips is [black_coat](#black_coat).

entries.name: coat
entries.description: A long, weighty outer garment [reaching](#reaching) the thigh or below, frequently with [lapels](#lapels), worn against the [cold](#cold) or for the look of it. Something ending at the waist or hip is a [jacket](#jacket), and one worn [hanging](#hanging) open is [open_coat](#open_coat).

entries.name: white_jacket
entries.description: A white [jacket](#jacket) of any cut worn as an outer layer, from blazers to [bomber](#bomber) jackets.

entries.name: blue_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) in blue, taking in [school](#school) blazers, [denim](#denim) jackets and track tops alike. Longer garments [reaching](#reaching) past the hip are [blue_coat](#blue_coat).

entries.name: blazer
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) cut along [suit](#suit) lines but worn more casually, with [lapels](#lapels) and [buttons](#buttons), most often as the top half of a [school](#school) uniform. Add the colour variant such as [black_jacket](#black_jacket).

entries.name: hooded_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) with an attached [hood](#hood), often [zipping](#zipping) up the front and finished with a [drawstring](#drawstring). It is distinct from a [hoodie](#hoodie), which is a pullover sweatshirt; a hooded garment that zips open is this one.

entries.name: red_jacket
entries.description: A red [jacket](#jacket) or [blazer](#blazer) worn as an outer layer over another top. Covers [bomber](#bomber) jackets, track jackets, blazers and similar; a red garment [reaching](#reaching) past the hips is a [coat](#coat) instead.

entries.name: black_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) in black, from a [trench](#trench) coat to an [overcoat](#overcoat) or a long [military](#military) one, worn properly or slung over the shoulders. A shorter garment stopping at the hips is [black_jacket](#black_jacket).

entries.name: cropped_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) shortened to end just under the [breasts](#breasts), often called a bolero. Stopping above the breasts instead makes it a shrug; it may be worn open or fastened over a top or [dress](#dress).

entries.name: white_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) of any cut colored white, worn as outerwear. A doctor's or scientist's coat is the separate labcoat [tag](#tag) and doesn't need this one.

entries.name: robe
entries.description: A loose full-length outer garment with sleeves, [reaching](#reaching) the [knees](#knees) or [feet](#feet). Worn by wizards, priests, angels and graduates; a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) wrap belongs under [cape](#cape) or [cloak](#cloak) instead.

entries.name: track_jacket
entries.description: A zip-up athletic [jacket](#jacket), often striped lengthwise with a ribbed [collar](#collar) and [cuffs](#cuffs). Paired with matching trousers it becomes a full [track_suit](#track_suit).

entries.name: grey_jacket
entries.description: A grey or silver [jacket](#jacket) of any cut, from a [blazer](#blazer) to a hooded or [leather](#leather) jacket. Longer outerwear takes [grey_coat](#grey_coat).

entries.name: green_jacket
entries.description: A green [jacket](#jacket) of any cut, from a [bomber](#bomber) or [blazer](#blazer) to a [military](#military) [field](#field) jacket. Anything long enough to read as an [overcoat](#overcoat) is a [green_coat](#green_coat).

entries.name: brown_jacket
entries.description: A brown [jacket](#jacket), taking in [leather](#leather), [bomber](#bomber), [denim](#denim) and [blazer](#blazer) [cuts](#cuts). Warm lighting makes it overlap with [red_jacket](#red_jacket) and [orange_jacket](#orange_jacket); add jacket.

entries.name: pink_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) whose main colour is pink, in any cut from a [blazer](#blazer) to a [bomber](#bomber) or track jacket. A longer, heavier garment reads as a [coat](#coat) and a knitted one as a [cardigan](#cardigan).

entries.name: fur-trimmed_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) with fur [running](#running) along its [collar](#collar), [hood](#hood) or hem. A jacket cut from [pelt](#pelt) throughout is [fur_jacket](#fur_jacket).

entries.name: yellow_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) in yellow, whether a track jacket, [bomber](#bomber) or [blazer](#blazer). Tag jacket and the type.

entries.name: purple_jacket
entries.description: A purple [jacket](#jacket), worn closed or left open. Combine with jacket and the style, such as [blazer](#blazer) or [track_jacket](#track_jacket).

entries.name: winter_clothes
entries.description: Cold-weather clothing in general: coats, parkas, sweaters, knit hats, [earmuffs](#earmuffs), scarves, [mittens](#mittens), and [snow](#snow) [boots](#boots). It works as a catch-all alongside whichever specific garment tags apply.

entries.name: multicolored_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) [carrying](#carrying) at least two distinct colours in its design. Small trim, piping or [buttons](#buttons) on their own are not enough to qualify.

entries.name: brown_coat
entries.description: A brown [coat](#coat): a [trench](#trench) coat, [overcoat](#overcoat), duffel or fur-collared [winter](#winter) coat. Add coat; a shorter garment is [brown_jacket](#brown_jacket).

entries.name: red_coat
entries.description: A red [coat](#coat), worn or draped over the shoulders. Combine with coat and whatever style [tag](#tag) fits the cut.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) with fur [running](#running) along its [collar](#collar), [cuffs](#cuffs) or hem. A coat made of [pelt](#pelt) throughout is [fur_coat](#fur_coat).

entries.name: collared_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) with a pronounced [standing](#standing) or [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar). Jackets that carry only [lapels](#lapels), blazers and [suit](#suit) jackets among them, do not count.

entries.name: blue_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) in blue, such as a naval greatcoat, a [trench](#trench) coat or a [winter](#winter) [overcoat](#overcoat). Shorter garments ending at the hip are [blue_jacket](#blue_jacket).

entries.name: two-tone_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) whose design uses exactly two colours. Implies [multicolored_jacket](#multicolored_jacket).

entries.name: hooded_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) with a [hood](#hood) attached, such as a [parka](#parka) or a hooded [winter](#winter) coat. It runs longer than a [hooded_jacket](#hooded_jacket); add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) as [well](#well).

entries.name: sleeveless_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) without sleeves, told apart from a [vest](#vest) by its [collar](#collar), heavier weatherproof build and sometimes a [hood](#hood).

entries.name: long_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) whose hem falls below the [knees](#knees), such as a [trench](#trench) coat or a greatcoat. Shorter ones take the [plain](#plain) coat [tag](#tag).

entries.name: orange_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) in orange, whether [bomber](#bomber), [blazer](#blazer), track or high-visibility. Add [open_jacket](#open_jacket) when it is worn undone.

entries.name: grey_coat
entries.description: A grey [coat](#coat), whether a long [overcoat](#overcoat), a [trench](#trench) coat or a [military](#military) greatcoat. Shorter outerwear is a [grey_jacket](#grey_jacket).

entries.name: military_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) taken from a [military](#military) uniform, or civilian wear cut to imitate one, whether combat-styled or dressed up for formal wear.

entries.name: leather_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) of tanned hide, most often the biker or [bomber](#bomber) cut. It carries [rock](#rock) and rebellious associations.

entries.name: unworn_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) taken off entirely or slipped most of the way off, further than merely [resting](#resting) on the shoulders.

entries.name: striped_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) woven or printed with a striped pattern. Implies jacket and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: winter_coat
entries.description: A thick, insulated [coat](#coat) resembling a down [jacket](#jacket), visibly warmer than an ordinary coat. Tag coat and [winter_clothes](#winter_clothes) alongside it.

entries.name: coattails
entries.description: The [split](#split) panels at the [back](#back) of a [tailcoat](#tailcoat) or long [coat](#coat), [hanging](#hanging) free below the waist. Standard on tuxedos, [butler](#butler) [dress](#dress) and formal [military](#military) uniforms.

entries.name: purple_coat
entries.description: A purple [coat](#coat), worn closed or draped open over the shoulders. Combine with coat and the length or style, such as [long_coat](#long_coat) or [trench_coat](#trench_coat).

entries.name: trench_coat
entries.description: A long belted [raincoat](#raincoat) in black, brown or [tan](#tan), classic wear for detectives and spies and, in comedy, for a flasher about to fling it open. Tag ordinary [coat](#coat) conventions alongside it.

entries.name: green_coat
entries.description: A green [coat](#coat) of any cut, from a long [overcoat](#overcoat) to a [trench](#trench) coat or a [military](#military) greatcoat. Shorter and [lighter](#lighter) outerwear is a [green_jacket](#green_jacket).

entries.name: collared_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) whose neckline carries a [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar), whether laid flat or turned up. It describes the cut of the coat itself, so the [plain](#plain) coat [tag](#tag) goes on beside it and [neck](#neck) collars are unrelated.

entries.name: two-sided_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) whose lining shows a contrasting colour or pattern wherever it opens or folds [back](#back). Implies jacket and [two-sided_fabric](#two-sided_fabric).

entries.name: off-shoulder_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) cut so that its neckline sits below the shoulders as intended. Very often mistagged for an ordinary open jacket [slipping](#slipping) down the arms; where the design is uncertain, use [off_shoulder](#off_shoulder).

entries.name: letterman_jacket
entries.description: An American varsity [jacket](#jacket) with a large [initial](#initial) on the chest, sleeves in a contrasting colour and striped knit [collar](#collar) and [cuffs](#cuffs). Worn by high [school](#school) and college athletes.

entries.name: raincoat
entries.description: A waterproof [coat](#coat) with sleeves, often yellow or [transparent](#transparent), worn against [rain](#rain) along with rubber [boots](#boots) and an [umbrella](#umbrella). A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) rain covering instead is a [rain_poncho](#rain_poncho).

entries.name: fur_coat
entries.description: A sleeved [coat](#coat) made entirely of fur. A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) fur garment is [fur_cloak](#fur_cloak), while a [cloth](#cloth) coat that merely carries fur trim at its borders is [fur-trimmed_coat](#fur-trimmed_coat).

entries.name: aqua_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) in an aqua [shade](#shade). Combine with the jacket's style, and with [open_clothes](#open_clothes) when it hangs open.

entries.name: pink_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) in pink, of any length or cut, worn over the rest of the outfit. Shorter, [lighter](#lighter) outerwear reads as a [jacket](#jacket) instead.

entries.name: yellow_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) in yellow, from [trench](#trench) coats to duffels. Tag coat as [well](#well); a rubber [rain](#rain) coat is [yellow_raincoat](#yellow_raincoat) instead.

entries.name: bomber_jacket
entries.description: A short sturdy [jacket](#jacket) with elasticated waist and [cuffs](#cuffs), zipped or buttoned up the front, often collared in fur, fleece or knit. It began as the [leather](#leather) flight jacket, and modern [fabric](#fabric) and letterman versions count too.

entries.name: short-sleeved_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) cut with short sleeves. Implies jacket and [short_sleeves](#short_sleeves).

entries.name: multicolored_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) cut or finished in two or more distinct colours, whether panelled, blocked or lined in a contrasting [shade](#shade). Trim and [buttons](#buttons) alone are not enough to earn it.

entries.name: plaid_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) in plaid or tartan [cloth](#cloth), ranging from a lumberjack [flannel](#flannel) to a checked [blazer](#blazer). Tag [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes) alongside it.

entries.name: two-sided_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) whose inner surface differs in colour or pattern from the outside, visible whenever it hangs open. Implies coat and [two-sided_fabric](#two-sided_fabric).

entries.name: vertical-striped_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) with an up-and-down stripe pattern, as on some [baseball](#baseball) and pinstripe styles. Tag the jacket's colours separately.

entries.name: no_jacket
entries.description: A character officially drawn in a [jacket](#jacket) appears without it, showing whatever is worn underneath. A jacket [lying](#lying) nearby or draped over something is [unworn_jacket](#unworn_jacket).

entries.name: print_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) printed with a design, from a [logo](#logo) on the [back](#back) to an all-over pattern. Tag jacket with it; a print alone does not make it [multicolored_jacket](#multicolored_jacket).

entries.name: pinstripe_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) [patterned](#patterned) with thin vertical stripes, generally a [suit](#suit) [coat](#coat) or a [blazer](#blazer). Add [pinstripe_suit](#pinstripe_suit) when trousers of the same [cloth](#cloth) are worn with it.

entries.name: sleeveless_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) with [no](#no) sleeves, worn over other [clothes](#clothes) like a long [vest](#vest). Tag beside coat and [sleeveless](#sleeveless).

entries.name: denim_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) cut from [denim](#denim), usually blue with metal [buttons](#buttons), a pointed [collar](#collar) and chest pockets. Worn open or fastened over whatever is underneath.

entries.name: camouflage_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) of any cut printed in disruptive greens and browns, from a [military](#military) [field](#field) jacket to a [fashion](#fashion) piece. Often worn open over an ordinary top.

entries.name: transparent_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) cut from clear or heavily sheer material, so whatever is worn underneath and the wearer's own shape stay visible through it. Vinyl raincoats and plastic windbreakers are typical examples.

entries.name: overcoat
entries.description: A long, [heavy](#heavy) [coat](#coat) of thick [wool](#wool) or fur, put on over a [jacket](#jacket) against the [cold](#cold). Bulkier and longer than an ordinary coat.

entries.name: duffel_coat
entries.description: A thick woollen [winter](#winter) [coat](#coat) closed by cone-shaped [toggles](#toggles) pushed through [rope](#rope) loops instead of [buttons](#buttons), usually hooded. The toggles let it be worked with [gloves](#gloves) on.

entries.name: torn_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) with rips in it.

entries.name: yellow_raincoat
entries.description: A bright yellow rubberised [rain](#rain) [coat](#coat) in the fisherman's oilskin style, often paired with a matching [hat](#hat). A rain-and-puddles [staple](#staple); [tag](#tag) [raincoat](#raincoat).

entries.name: unworn_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) is present in the picture, draped over a [chair](#chair) or held in hand, but not on anyone's body.

entries.name: frilled_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) [carrying](#carrying) ruffles at the [collar](#collar), front, [cuffs](#cuffs) or hem. Common on lolita, gothic and [stage](#stage) [costume](#costume) designs.

entries.name: two-tone_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) whose design uses exactly two colours. Implies [multicolored_coat](#multicolored_coat).

entries.name: turtleneck_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) whose own [collar](#collar) rises to wrap the [neck](#neck) rather than [lying](#lying) flat or open. The [turtleneck](#turtleneck) effect is built into the jacket itself, not a separate layer underneath.

entries.name: jacket_over_hoodie
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) worn on top of a [hoodie](#hoodie), so the [hood](#hood) and its drawstrings sit outside the [collar](#collar). It is a layered [casual](#casual) look.

entries.name: striped_coat
entries.description: A long [coat](#coat) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes, worn over the rest of the outfit.

entries.name: sukajan
entries.description: A Japanese souvenir [jacket](#jacket) cut like a [bomber](#bomber) jacket, with embroidered dragons, tigers or [cherry](#cherry) blossoms across the [back](#back) and chest. Associated with [delinquent](#delinquent) and [yakuza](#yakuza) characters. Implies jacket.

entries.name: parka
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) hooded [winter](#winter) [coat](#coat), often with fur around the [hood](#hood), made for [cold](#cold) climates. The Japanese word that sounds the same simply means [hoodie](#hoodie), and that garment takes the hoodie [tag](#tag).

entries.name: fur_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) cut from fur throughout, sleeves included. One made of ordinary [fabric](#fabric) that carries fur only along its edges is [fur-trimmed_jacket](#fur-trimmed_jacket).

entries.name: down_jacket
entries.description: A puffy quilted [jacket](#jacket) stuffed with [duck](#duck) or [goose](#goose) down for warmth, the [winter](#winter) puffer. Its sewn tubes and stubby padded sleeves are the giveaway.

entries.name: torn_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) visibly ripped, with [split](#split) sleeves, shredded tails or holes through the body.

entries.name: off-shoulder_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) whose neckline is cut wide and low enough that it sits under the shoulders by design. Badly mistagged in practice: a normal coat [hanging](#hanging) off the arms does not qualify, and [off_shoulder](#off_shoulder) is the safe [choice](#choice) when the design is unclear.

entries.name: spiked_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) [studded](#studded) with metal points, usually across the shoulders and [collar](#collar). The [leather](#leather) [punk](#punk) jacket is the classic example.

entries.name: orange_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) in orange, in any cut from a hip-length [jacket](#jacket) to a long [overcoat](#overcoat), worn open or fastened.

entries.name: vertical-striped_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) [carrying](#carrying) stripes that run from shoulder to hem rather than across the body. Often chosen for showy [stage](#stage) [costume](#costume), [circus](#circus) [dress](#dress) or period looks, since the lines lengthen the [figure](#figure).

entries.name: aqua_coat
entries.description: An outer [coat](#coat) in blue-green, anywhere from a short [jacket](#jacket) length to a full [overcoat](#overcoat). Add the coat's cut where it [can](#can) be named.

entries.name: gradient_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) coloured with a smooth fade between shades, frequently [lighter](#lighter) at the shoulders and deeper at the hem, with the sleeves [following](#following) the body.

entries.name: padded_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) stuffed with down or a similar filling and quilted into puffed panels for warmth. The shorter relative of the padded [coat](#coat), with the same swollen [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: royal_robe
entries.description: A long ceremonial [robe](#robe) of state, typically [heavy](#heavy) velvet with a fur-trimmed edge and a trailing hem. Worn over other clothing by monarchs and nobles at formal occasions.

entries.name: padded_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) filled with down or synthetic wadding and quilted into puffed bands. Made for [cold](#cold) weather and drawn with a bulky, rounded [outline](#outline).

entries.name: sleeveless_duster
entries.description: A [duster](#duster) is a long, loose [coat](#coat) that falls near the ankles; this version has [no](#no) sleeves at all, so the arms stay bare inside the open drape of the garment. Nothing to do with the [cleaning](#cleaning) implement of the same name.

entries.name: quilted_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) whose [shell](#shell) or lining is [stitched](#stitched) into padded panels, producing the characteristic ridged squares or diamonds. Warm outerwear suited to cold-weather scenes.

entries.name: plaid_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) cut from tartan [cloth](#cloth), whether a long [overcoat](#overcoat) or a shorter jacket-length piece. The check runs across the whole garment.

entries.name: frilled_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) [carrying](#carrying) ruffled trim, usually down the front [opening](#opening), around the [cuffs](#cuffs) or along the hem. The effect is [ornate](#ornate) and period rather than practical.

entries.name: no_coat
entries.description: A character normally shown in a [coat](#coat) appears without one, revealing what is worn underneath. When the coat is still somewhere in the frame, [unworn_coat](#unworn_coat) is the right [tag](#tag).

entries.name: military_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) cut as part of a [military](#military) uniform, often [double-breasted](#double-breasted) and marked with [collar](#collar) tabs, shoulder boards, [braid](#braid) or an [aiguillette](#aiguillette).

entries.name: feather_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) feathered over its whole surface rather than merely trimmed at the edges. The plumage reads as the material of the garment itself.

entries.name: asymmetrical_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) whose halves are cut differently, with one sleeve shortened or missing, a hem [running](#running) on a diagonal, or the two sides finished in unlike ways.

entries.name: safari_jacket
entries.description: A lightweight buttoned [jacket](#jacket) in the bush-expedition style, cut with [patch](#patch) pockets and often a waist [belt](#belt). Almost always drawn in khaki, beige or another dusty earth tone.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_robe
entries.description: A long [robe](#robe) bordered with fur at the [collar](#collar), [cuffs](#cuffs) or hem. Depending on the rest of the outfit it reads as royal, wizardly or simply wintry.

entries.name: feather-trimmed_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) bordered with [feathers](#feathers), most often at the [collar](#collar) or down the front [opening](#opening). Showy [stage](#stage) and [idol](#idol) costumes use it constantly.

entries.name: white_raincoat
entries.description: A white waterproof [coat](#coat), usually hooded and glossy. Belongs to [rain](#rain), [storm](#storm) and [seaside](#seaside) scenes.

entries.name: print_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) with a printed design on it. The print by itself does not make the coat multicoloured, which is recorded separately.

entries.name: studded_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) covered in metal [studs](#studs), typically [leather](#leather) and associated with [punk](#punk) and biker [fashion](#fashion). Implies jacket.

entries.name: checkered_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) cut from chequered material and worn over other [clothes](#clothes). The squares may be small or large so long as they stay regular across the garment.

entries.name: impossible_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) gripping the body far more closely than the material would allow, tracing curves and even the [navel](#navel) beneath. The fit rather than the garment is what is being tagged.

entries.name: tokkoufuku
entries.description: A long stiff [coat](#coat) covered in embroidered slogans and kanji, the uniform of biker gangs and delinquents. The lettering across the [back](#back) is the point of the garment.

entries.name: shared_coat
entries.description: Two [people](#people) wear or huddle inside the same [coat](#coat) at once, one garment stretched across both. A cold-weather intimacy [gag](#gag).

entries.name: wet_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) soaked through, darkened by [water](#water) and either [clinging](#clinging) or [dripping](#dripping). Rain and unplanned swims account for most cases.

entries.name: cross-laced_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) drawn shut with [laces](#laces) crossing over the front rather than [buttons](#buttons) or a zip. Turns up constantly on folk [costume](#costume) and [fantasy](#fantasy) outerwear.

entries.name: argyle_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) [carrying](#carrying) the argyle diamond pattern, either across the whole garment or kept to panels, lining and trim. The base colour and the coat's own cut stay on other tags.

entries.name: feather-trimmed_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) finished with a band of [feathers](#feathers), usually at the [collar](#collar), [cuffs](#cuffs) or hem. The feathers are edging on an otherwise ordinary coat.

entries.name: duffel_jacket
entries.description: A short hooded [wool](#wool) [coat](#coat) fastened with [toggles](#toggles) through [rope](#rope) loops and hung with big [patch](#patch) pockets. Bulky [winter](#winter) wear with a schoolboy flavour.

entries.name: polka_dot_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) printed with round [dots](#dots) across its panels. The [spots](#spots) may sit in a regular [grid](#grid) or be scattered at random.

entries.name: frog_raincoat
entries.description: A [raincoat](#raincoat), almost always green, whose [hood](#hood) is shaped as a frog's head. Children's wear by origin, and often put on adult characters for the joke.

entries.name: blue_raincoat
entries.description: A blue waterproof [coat](#coat), usually glossy and often with a [hood](#hood) attached. Rain, puddles or [wet](#wet) streets tend to come with it.

entries.name: cape
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) outer garment fastened at the [neck](#neck) and [hanging](#hanging) down the [back](#back). It leaves the front and sides open, unlike a [cloak](#cloak) that wraps the whole body; a shoulder-length one is a [capelet](#capelet).

entries.name: capelet
entries.description: A short [cape](#cape) [falling](#falling) [no](#no) further than the shoulders, also called a mantle. Common on [winter](#winter) outfits and worn with Santa costumes.

entries.name: cloak
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) outer garment [wrapping](#wrapping) the whole body or at least the upper half, with an [opening](#opening) or slit down the front. Worn against [cold](#cold) and [wind](#wind) or as [fantasy](#fantasy) attire; a [cape](#cape) covers only the [back](#back).

entries.name: red_cape
entries.description: A red [cape](#cape), the classic hero and superhero garment, fastened at the [neck](#neck) and left to hang or billow. Combine with cape; a short version cut to the shoulders is [red_capelet](#red_capelet).

entries.name: shawl
entries.description: A [square](#square), oblong or triangular [cloth](#cloth) draped loosely over the shoulders and upper body. Unlike a [sash](#sash), it is not wrapped or tied around the [torso](#torso).

entries.name: black_cape
entries.description: A black [cape](#cape) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders, the standard [dress](#dress) of vampires, villains and brooding heroes. A short one [reaching](#reaching) only the shoulders is [black_capelet](#black_capelet).

entries.name: white_capelet
entries.description: A short white shoulder [cape](#cape) [reaching](#reaching) only to the upper arms, common on [winter](#winter) outfits and [fantasy](#fantasy) costumes.

entries.name: white_cape
entries.description: A white [cape](#cape) draped from the shoulders, typical of paladins, princes and magical girls.

entries.name: blue_cape
entries.description: A blue [cape](#cape) [falling](#falling) from the shoulders down the [back](#back). Heroes and royalty wear it most; a short one covering only the shoulders is [blue_capelet](#blue_capelet).

entries.name: black_capelet
entries.description: A short black [cape](#cape) covering only the shoulders and upper [back](#back), often part of a [witch](#witch), gothic or uniform outfit. It fastens at the throat and stops [well](#well) above the waist.

entries.name: hooded_cloak
entries.description: A long [cloak](#cloak) with a [hood](#hood) that [can](#can) be drawn over the head, worn by travellers, rogues and mages. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) as appropriate.

entries.name: red_capelet
entries.description: A short red [cape](#cape) covering only the shoulders, as on Little Red Riding Hood-style outfits. Combine with [capelet](#capelet).

entries.name: fur-trimmed_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) of ordinary [fabric](#fabric) with fur [running](#running) along its edges. One made wholly of [pelt](#pelt) is [fur_cape](#fur_cape).

entries.name: fur-trimmed_capelet
entries.description: A short [capelet](#capelet) covering the shoulders, edged with a band of fur around its [border](#border). Winter [dress](#dress) and Christmas costumes use it constantly.

entries.name: waist_cape
entries.description: A cape-like drape fastened around the waist instead of the shoulders, [hanging](#hanging) over the hips and [legs](#legs). Common on [fantasy](#fantasy), [idol](#idol) and military-styled costumes.

entries.name: black_cloak
entries.description: A long black [cloak](#cloak) wrapped about the body, frequently hooded, worn by mages, assassins and travellers. It falls to the [calves](#calves) or the ground and hides the [figure](#figure) beneath.

entries.name: blue_capelet
entries.description: A short blue [cape](#cape) [reaching](#reaching) [no](#no) further than the shoulders. Uniforms and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits use it as a layer over the top half.

entries.name: green_cape
entries.description: A green [cape](#cape) [falling](#falling) from the shoulders down the [back](#back). The shoulder-length version is a [green_capelet](#green_capelet).

entries.name: hooded_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) with a [hood](#hood) attached, a [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) and storybook outfits. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) as [well](#well).

entries.name: two-sided_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) whose lining shows a different colour or pattern from its outer face. The [contrast](#contrast) appears wherever the [fabric](#fabric) folds [back](#back) or catches the [wind](#wind).

entries.name: purple_cape
entries.description: A purple [cape](#cape) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders. Combine with cape; a shorter shoulder-length version is [purple_capelet](#purple_capelet) and a hooded wrap is [purple_cloak](#purple_cloak).

entries.name: white_cloak
entries.description: A white full-length [cloak](#cloak), frequently hooded, as worn by assassins, priests or travelers.

entries.name: red_cloak
entries.description: A red [cloak](#cloak), often hooded, wrapped around the body. Combine with cloak and [hood_up](#hood_up) where the [hood](#hood) is shown raised.

entries.name: hagoromo
entries.description: A long thin celestial [shawl](#shawl) [drifting](#drifting) around the arms and shoulders, associated with tennin, deities and Chinese-style heavenly beings; it often floats unaided. Buddhist tian_yi shawls are tagged with this as [well](#well).

entries.name: hooded_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) with a [hood](#hood) joined at the [collar](#collar), shorter than a full [cloak](#cloak). Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) as the picture calls for.

entries.name: torn_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) with holes, rips or ragged edges.

entries.name: brown_capelet
entries.description: A short brown [cape](#cape) covering the shoulders and upper arms, often with a [hood](#hood) attached. It turns up on rangers, villagers and lolita outfits alike.

entries.name: frilled_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) trimmed with ruffles around its edge. A [staple](#staple) piece of lolita, gothic and magical girl outfits.

entries.name: brown_cape
entries.description: A brown [cape](#cape) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders, generally in a rustic or travel-worn style. Add cape; a short one [reaching](#reaching) only the shoulders is [brown_capelet](#brown_capelet).

entries.name: collared_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) whose [neck](#neck) is finished with a [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar), [standing](#standing) or turned down over the shoulders. The collar is part of the cape rather than a separate band, and the [plain](#plain) cape [tag](#tag) goes on beside it.

entries.name: side_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) clasped at the [neck](#neck) but draped over only one shoulder, leaving the other arm free. Common on [fantasy](#fantasy) and military-styled designs.

entries.name: purple_capelet
entries.description: A short purple [cape](#cape) ending around the shoulders or upper arms. A longer version of the same garment is [purple_cape](#purple_cape).

entries.name: poncho
entries.description: A blanket-like [cloak](#cloak) with a [hole](#hole) for the head, [hanging](#hanging) over the shoulders to the chest or hips with [no](#no) sleeves. Distinct from a [cape](#cape), which fastens at the front.

entries.name: stole
entries.description: A band of [fabric](#fabric) or fur draped over the shoulders or around the [neck](#neck) with the ends [hanging](#hanging) loose, either a formal wrap or a priest's vestment.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_cloak
entries.description: A long [cloak](#cloak) of ordinary [cloth](#cloth) lined or bordered with fur, usually at the [hood](#hood) and the front [opening](#opening). A cloak cut from [pelt](#pelt) throughout is [fur_cloak](#fur_cloak).

entries.name: blue_cloak
entries.description: A long blue [cloak](#cloak) wrapped about the body and often hooded. Mages and travellers wear it; a shorter shoulder piece is [blue_capelet](#blue_capelet).

entries.name: yellow_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) in yellow [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders. Tag cape as [well](#well).

entries.name: brown_cloak
entries.description: A brown [cloak](#cloak), the long draped wrap of travellers, rangers and monks, frequently hooded. Add cloak.

entries.name: green_capelet
entries.description: A short green [cape](#cape) [reaching](#reaching) [no](#no) further than the shoulders and upper arms. Anything longer is a [green_cape](#green_cape).

entries.name: floating_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape), [cloak](#cloak) or [capelet](#capelet) streaming out behind the wearer, lifted by [wind](#wind) or by movement. It adds drama to a [standing](#standing) or a [running](#running) [figure](#figure).

entries.name: half_cape
entries.description: A short [cape](#cape) covering only one shoulder and part of the chest or [back](#back) rather than [hanging](#hanging) around the whole body. A [staple](#staple) of uniforms and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits.

entries.name: pink_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) in pink, ending around the upper arm or the chest. Longer versions [reaching](#reaching) down the [back](#back) are a cape or a [cloak](#cloak).

entries.name: pink_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) in pink [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders, at any length from a short [flare](#flare) to a floor-sweeping sweep. One covering only the shoulders is a [capelet](#capelet).

entries.name: two-tone_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) coloured in exactly two tones on its visible surface. Compare [two-sided_cape](#two-sided_cape), where the difference is between the inside and outside rather than a surface [split](#split).

entries.name: fur_cape
entries.description: A short [cape](#cape) of [animal](#animal) fur covering the shoulders and upper [back](#back). A longer fur garment is [fur_cloak](#fur_cloak), and [fabric](#fabric) with fur edging is [fur-trimmed_cape](#fur-trimmed_cape).

entries.name: green_cloak
entries.description: A green [cloak](#cloak) wrapped around the body, frequently hooded. It is the stock garment of travellers, rangers and [fantasy](#fantasy) wanderers.

entries.name: grey_capelet
entries.description: A short grey [cape](#cape) covering only the shoulders and upper arms. Anything [reaching](#reaching) further down the [back](#back) is a [grey_cape](#grey_cape).

entries.name: grey_cape
entries.description: A grey [cape](#cape) [falling](#falling) from the shoulders down the [back](#back). A short one [reaching](#reaching) only the shoulders is a [grey_capelet](#grey_capelet).

entries.name: collared_capelet
entries.description: A short [cape](#cape) [reaching](#reaching) [no](#no) further than the shoulders, cut with a [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar) at the throat. Common over uniforms and formal coats, and tagged together with [capelet](#capelet).

entries.name: white_shawl
entries.description: A white [shawl](#shawl) draped across the shoulders and upper arms, whether knitted, [lace](#lace), or [plain](#plain) [cloth](#cloth). It appears both as warm layering and as part of [evening](#evening) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: multicolored_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) in two or more colours, which includes a lining cut from [fabric](#fabric) different from the outer face. The second colour often shows only as the cape turns.

entries.name: blue_shawl
entries.description: A blue length of [cloth](#cloth) draped over the shoulders and upper arms, [hanging](#hanging) open at the front. Broader and heavier than a [scarf](#scarf), and nothing fastens it.

entries.name: fur_cloak
entries.description: A long [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [cloak](#cloak) made of fur. With sleeves it becomes [fur_coat](#fur_coat), shorter and covering only the [back](#back) it is [fur_cape](#fur_cape), and [fabric](#fabric) with furred edges is [fur-trimmed_cloak](#fur-trimmed_cloak).

entries.name: orange_cape
entries.description: An orange [cape](#cape) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders, a [staple](#staple) of heroic and [fantasy](#fantasy) [dress](#dress). One with a [hood](#hood) attached may count as a [cloak](#cloak) too.

entries.name: grey_cloak
entries.description: A grey [cloak](#cloak) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders, frequently hooded. It is the default travelling and mercenary wear of [fantasy](#fantasy) settings.

entries.name: fur_shawl
entries.description: A wrap of [animal](#animal) [pelt](#pelt) draped over the shoulders. It reads as wealth and aristocracy as readily as it reads as [cold](#cold) weather.

entries.name: purple_cloak
entries.description: A purple [sleeveless](#sleeveless) outer garment [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders over the [back](#back), often hooded. Typical of [fantasy](#fantasy) adventurers and royal [dress](#dress) alike.

entries.name: yellow_cloak
entries.description: A long yellow [cloak](#cloak) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders, sometimes with a [hood](#hood) attached. Short shoulder pieces are capelets rather than cloaks.

entries.name: two-sided_cloak
entries.description: A [cloak](#cloak) lined in a contrasting colour or pattern, black outside and red inside being the classic combination. Implies cloak and [two-sided_fabric](#two-sided_fabric).

entries.name: torn_cloak
entries.description: A [cloak](#cloak) frayed and holed, its hem [hanging](#hanging) in strips. Standard shorthand for a long or hard journey.

entries.name: unworn_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) that a character usually wears is somewhere in the scene but off their shoulders, hung up, [folded](#folded) or spread out flat. The cape must actually be visible for the [tag](#tag) to apply.

entries.name: red_shawl
entries.description: A red wrap draped over the shoulders and upper arms, held closed by hand or [pinned](#pinned). Worn for warmth or as a decorative layer over a [dress](#dress).

entries.name: yellow_capelet
entries.description: A short yellow [cape](#cape) covering just the shoulders and upper [back](#back), generally fastened at the throat. Longer versions belong under cape or [cloak](#cloak) instead.

entries.name: brown_shawl
entries.description: A brown [shawl](#shawl) draped across the shoulders or wound round the upper body. It is loose [cloth](#cloth) rather than a tailored garment, and easily let slip.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) finished with a [ribbon](#ribbon) band around its hem or [opening](#opening). Typical of gothic lolita and magical girl outfits.

entries.name: frilled_shawl
entries.description: A [shawl](#shawl) draped over the shoulders whose [border](#border) is gathered into ruffles. Lends a period or purely ornamental [note](#note) to whatever is worn beneath it.

entries.name: pink_shawl
entries.description: A pink wrap draped over the shoulders and upper arms, knitted or woven. It hangs loose rather than being fastened like a [cape](#cape).

entries.name: black_shawl
entries.description: A black piece of [cloth](#cloth) draped over the shoulders or across the arms. It hangs free rather than fastening shut, which sets it apart from a [capelet](#capelet) or a [cape](#cape).

entries.name: wolf_pelt
entries.description: The skin and fur of a [wolf](#wolf) worn as clothing, usually draped over the shoulders with the head [serving](#serving) as a [hood](#hood). Warriors and hunters wear it as a mark of strength.

entries.name: no_cape
entries.description: Somebody known for a [cape](#cape), [cloak](#cloak) or [capelet](#capelet) is drawn without it, so the shoulders and [back](#back) carry [no](#no) drapery.

entries.name: fur_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [capelet](#capelet) made entirely of fur rather than merely edged with it. Winter [dress](#dress) and aristocratic designs both reach for it.

entries.name: plaid_shawl
entries.description: A tartan wrap draped over the shoulders. Highland and [autumn](#autumn) outfits both reach for it.

entries.name: cowl
entries.description: A hooded [cloak](#cloak), or a close-fitting [hood](#hood) that covers head and shoulders in one piece. Superhero masks cut to that shape count as [well](#well).

entries.name: orange_capelet
entries.description: A short orange [cape](#cape) covering the shoulders and [no](#no) more than the upper arms. Length is what separates it from a full [cloak](#cloak).

entries.name: aqua_cape
entries.description: A blue-green [cape](#cape) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders down the [back](#back). The shorter version, stopping at the upper arms, is a [capelet](#capelet).

entries.name: multicolored_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) in two or more colours, most often a contrasting lining or a band around the hem. The second colour usually picks up something else in the outfit.

entries.name: torn_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) ripped along the hem or holed through the [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: plaid_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) in tartan, [reaching](#reaching) about to the elbow. Frequently seen as part of a [winter](#winter) [school](#school) outfit.

entries.name: two-tone_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) in exactly two colours, commonly divided by panel or set off by a contrasting hem. It is the colour count that matters, not the arrangement.

entries.name: print_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) bearing a printed design, whether a heraldic [device](#device), a repeating pattern or a picture spread across the [cloth](#cloth). Best seen when the cape swings open.

entries.name: yellow_shawl
entries.description: A yellow [shawl](#shawl) draped across the shoulders or over the arms, sometimes [pinned](#pinned) at the front. Worn for warmth or as an accent to a [dress](#dress).

entries.name: purple_shawl
entries.description: A purple wrap laid across the shoulders and upper arms, often draped rather than fastened. Lighter than a [cloak](#cloak) and shorter than a [cape](#cape).

entries.name: two-tone_cloak
entries.description: A full-length [cloak](#cloak) in exactly two colours, [split](#split) along its panels or set off by a contrasting [border](#border). Distinct from a lined cloak, where the difference is between the inside and out.

entries.name: two-sided_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) lined in a colour or pattern different from its outer face. The [contrast](#contrast) shows wherever the [fabric](#fabric) folds [back](#back) or lifts.

entries.name: green_shawl
entries.description: A green [shawl](#shawl) draped over the shoulders and upper arms, often gathered closed at the front. It is worn for warmth or as a formal covering.

entries.name: collared_cloak
entries.description: A [cloak](#cloak) made with a [standing](#standing) or [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar) at the [neck](#neck). The collar is sewn to the cloak rather than being a separate neck piece.

entries.name: pink_cloak
entries.description: A pink full-length wrap fastened at the [neck](#neck) and [hanging](#hanging) loose over the shoulders, sometimes hooded. It falls further and hangs heavier than a [cape](#cape).

entries.name: wing_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) cut and shaped to resemble a pair of [wings](#wings) [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders. Because it is a garment, actual wings on the same character are tagged separately.

entries.name: detached_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) held in the air near its wearer without being fastened to anything. The gap has to read clearly, and the piece may float at the waist as readily as at the shoulders.

entries.name: santa_capelet
entries.description: A short red shoulder [cape](#cape) edged in white fur, worn as part of a Christmas outfit. Usually paired with a matching [hat](#hat) and [dress](#dress).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) finished with a [lace](#lace) [border](#border) along its rim. It turns up constantly in gothic and lolita styling.

entries.name: grey_shawl
entries.description: A grey [shawl](#shawl) draped over the shoulders and arms, sometimes gathered closed at the front. It is worn for warmth or as a formal covering.

entries.name: multicolored_cloak
entries.description: A full-length [cloak](#cloak) [carrying](#carrying) more than one colour, commonly a contrasting inner face that shows as it swings open. Otherwise the second colour may never appear at all.

entries.name: frilled_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) whose edges are gathered into ruffles rather than hemmed flat. It turns up constantly on magical girl designs and gothic lolita coordinates.

entries.name: aqua_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) in blue-green, [reaching](#reaching) [no](#no) lower than the upper arms. Smaller than a full cape, and often hooded.

entries.name: orange_cloak
entries.description: A full-length orange [cloak](#cloak) fastened at the [neck](#neck) and [falling](#falling) across the [back](#back) and shoulders. Any cut qualifies so long as the colour is orange.

entries.name: gradient_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) whose colour drifts from one [shade](#shade) to another down its length, as a rule deepening at the hem. Magical and heroic costumes favour the finish.

entries.name: striped_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes, [hanging](#hanging) from the shoulders.

entries.name: unworn_cloak
entries.description: A [cloak](#cloak) is shown in the picture but not worn, hung from a peg, spread on the ground or bundled up. Often seen in [resting](#resting) or [camping](#camping) scenes.

entries.name: print_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) [carrying](#carrying) a printed pattern. Its length, [no](#no) further than the upper arms, is what separates it from a full cape.

entries.name: spiked_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) or mantle whose shoulders or hem bristle with points. Usually part of an imposing villain or warlord [costume](#costume), the [spikes](#spikes) sewn in or growing from [armor](#armor) worn beneath.

entries.name: rain_poncho
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) waterproof sheet worn over the shoulders, usually with a [hood](#hood), that sheds [rain](#rain) off the body. The lack of sleeves is what separates it from a [raincoat](#raincoat).

entries.name: gold_cape
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) of [gold](#gold) [cloth](#cloth) [falling](#falling) from the shoulders, often lined in another colour. It suits royal, divine and ceremonial [dress](#dress).

entries.name: striped_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) with a striped pattern, [falling](#falling) [no](#no) lower than the upper arms.

entries.name: padded_cloak
entries.description: A [cloak](#cloak) thickened with insulating filling and quilted into puffy sections. Winter and expedition wear rather than a light travelling cloak.

entries.name: red_poncho
