entries.description: A red sheet of [cloth](#cloth) with a head [opening](#opening), [hanging](#hanging) loose over the shoulders and arms. It reads as western or south-american [dress](#dress) and as [rain](#rain) gear depending on the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: layered_capelet
entries.description: A short shoulder [cape](#cape) built from two or more tiers [falling](#falling) over one another. Ornate [fantasy](#fantasy) and military-styled coats use it often.

entries.name: orange_shawl
entries.description: An orange [shawl](#shawl) draped over the shoulders or carried across the arms.

entries.name: hoodie
entries.description: A pullover sweatshirt with an attached [hood](#hood) and usually a [drawstring](#drawstring), pulled on over the head. If it zips open at the front it is a [hooded_jacket](#hooded_jacket); related states include [hoodie_lift](#hoodie_lift), [open_hoodie](#open_hoodie) and [naked_hoodie](#naked_hoodie).

entries.name: black_hoodie
entries.description: A black hooded sweatshirt, zipped or pullover, one of the commonest [casual](#casual) tops. Its [hood](#hood) may be up or down, often with a [drawstring](#drawstring) [hanging](#hanging) at the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: white_hoodie
entries.description: A white hooded sweatshirt worn as a [casual](#casual) top.

entries.name: blue_hoodie
entries.description: A blue hooded sweatshirt, pullover or zip-up, worn as [casual](#casual) [dress](#dress). Whether the [hood](#hood) is up or down is recorded separately.

entries.name: grey_hoodie
entries.description: A grey hooded sweatshirt, the plainest and most everyday version of the garment. It may be zipped or pulled on over the head.

entries.name: pink_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded sweatshirt in pink, zipped or pulled on over the head. Its [hood](#hood) is part of the garment rather than a separate piece.

entries.name: red_hoodie
entries.description: A red hooded sweatshirt, worn zipped, pulled over, or tied around the waist. The [hood](#hood) may be up or down; the [tag](#tag) is about the garment's colour.

entries.name: green_hoodie
entries.description: A green hooded sweatshirt, zipped or pulled on over the head, worn as [casual](#casual) [streetwear](#streetwear). The [hood](#hood) may be up or [hanging](#hanging) behind.

entries.name: yellow_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded sweatshirt in yellow. Tag [hoodie](#hoodie) as [well](#well) and [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) for the hood's state.

entries.name: cropped_hoodie
entries.description: A [hoodie](#hoodie) cut short to finish just below the [breasts](#breasts), leaving the [midriff](#midriff) bare. The hooded counterpart to a [cropped](#cropped) [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: orange_hoodie
entries.description: A [hoodie](#hoodie) in orange, worn zipped, open or pulled on over the head. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) for the state of the [hood](#hood).

entries.name: purple_hoodie
entries.description: A purple hooded sweatshirt, worn as a top on its own or open over a [shirt](#shirt). Combine with [hoodie](#hoodie) and [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down).

entries.name: sleeveless_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded top with the sleeves cut away, baring the arms, a sporty or [streetwear](#streetwear) look. Tag beside [hoodie](#hoodie) and [sleeveless](#sleeveless).

entries.name: brown_hoodie
entries.description: A brown hooded sweatshirt, worn as a top on its own or thrown over a [shirt](#shirt). Add [hoodie](#hoodie).

entries.name: two-tone_hoodie
entries.description: A [hoodie](#hoodie) in exactly two colours, such as contrasting sleeves or [hood](#hood). Add the colour tags as [well](#well).

entries.name: hooded_cardigan
entries.description: A knitted open-front [cardigan](#cardigan) with a [hood](#hood) sewn on. Say how the hood sits with [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down).

entries.name: print_hoodie
entries.description: A [hoodie](#hoodie) with a printed graphic, [logo](#logo) or pattern on it. Tag hoodie alongside.

entries.name: striped_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded pullover top [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [hoodie](#hoodie) and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: multicolored_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded top made up in two or more colours — contrasting sleeves, a differently coloured [hood](#hood) lining, or panels across the body. Sports and [streetwear](#streetwear) designs account for most of them.

entries.name: long_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded sweatshirt cut long enough to fall past the hips, sometimes worn on its own like a short [dress](#dress) with bare [legs](#legs) beneath. Keep it for hoodies that clearly hang below the waistline.

entries.name: aqua_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded sweatshirt in blue-green, pulled over the head or zipped at the front. The [hood](#hood) may be up or down.

entries.name: two-sided_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded top lined in a different colour from its outer [shell](#shell). The [contrast](#contrast) typically shows inside the [hood](#hood) and along the opened front.

entries.name: unworn_hoodie
entries.description: A [hoodie](#hoodie) is present in the picture without anyone wearing it, tied round the waist, tossed onto a [bed](#bed) or draped over the [back](#back) of a [chair](#chair).

entries.name: torn_hoodie
entries.description: A [hoodie](#hoodie) ripped at the sleeve, the [hood](#hood) or the body.

entries.name: polka_dot_hoodie
entries.description: A hooded sweatshirt printed all over with round [dots](#dots). The pattern normally runs across the body and sleeves alike.

entries.name: bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) with a bra-like top and a brief bottom, leaving the [midriff](#midriff) bare. Where only half is worn use [bikini_top_only](#bikini_top_only) or [bikini_bottom_only](#bikini_bottom_only), and [mismatched_bikini](#mismatched_bikini) when the two pieces do not match.

entries.name: black_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) in black, top and bottom alike; the separate colour tags for the two halves fold into this one. Add the cut, such as [micro_bikini](#micro_bikini) or [string_bikini](#string_bikini), on top of it.

entries.name: side-tie_bikini_bottom
entries.description: Bikini bottoms fastened with a [string](#string) [bow](#bow) at each hip, the swimwear equivalent of side-tie [panties](#panties). Frequently paired with a matching front-tie [bikini](#bikini) top.

entries.name: white_bikini
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) white [bikini](#bikini) top and/or bottom without stripes. A white one-piece [suit](#suit) is tagged [white_one-piece_swimsuit](#white_one-piece_swimsuit) instead, never this.

entries.name: black_bikini_bottom
entries.description: The lower half of a [bikini](#bikini) in black, worn alone or with a matching top. A colour [tag](#tag) only, so the cut may be anything from full [briefs](#briefs) to strings.

entries.name: string_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose top or bottom is tied together with thin cords instead of wide straps. Not the same as [micro_bikini](#micro_bikini) or [thong_bikini](#thong_bikini), although those may also be tied with strings.

entries.name: micro_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) cut so small it barely covers the [nipples](#nipples) and [crotch](#crotch).

entries.name: blue_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) in blue, top and bottom counted together. Where only one piece is blue, [judge](#judge) which colour dominates the [swimsuit](#swimsuit) as a whole.

entries.name: bikini_top_only
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top worn with [no](#no) bikini bottom, whether with [shorts](#shorts), trousers or nothing at all. Only where the lower body is visible and plainly without one; a bikini [skirt](#skirt), bikini shorts or [sarong](#sarong) rules it out.

entries.name: frilled_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) finished with ruffles on the top, the bottom or both. A cute rather than sporty swimwear style.

entries.name: red_bikini
entries.description: A red [bikini](#bikini), whether the top, the bottom, or both pieces are red. Combine with the specific style, such as [string_bikini](#string_bikini) or [micro_bikini](#micro_bikini); a one-piece [suit](#suit) instead is [red_one-piece_swimsuit](#red_one-piece_swimsuit).

entries.name: striped_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) on which both the top and the bottom carry a striped pattern.

entries.name: front-tie_bikini_top
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top fastened by [knotting](#knotting) its ends together between the [breasts](#breasts). Keep it apart from [front-tie_bra](#front-tie_bra), which is [underwear](#underwear) rather than swimwear.

entries.name: print_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) bearing a printed motif such as flowers, animals, flags or hearts. The print alone does not make it [multicolored_bikini](#multicolored_bikini); that needs distinct base colours.

entries.name: pink_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in pink, whether both halves match or only the top or the bottom is shown. Cut and style do not matter here, only the colour.

entries.name: bikini_under_clothes
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) worn beneath everyday clothing, its straps or edges showing at a neckline or through an open [jacket](#jacket). Typical of a character on the way to the [beach](#beach) or [pool](#pool).

entries.name: purple_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) in purple, covering the top piece, the bottom piece, or both. Combine with bikini and the specific style, such as [string_bikini](#string_bikini) or [micro_bikini](#micro_bikini).

entries.name: yellow_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in yellow, covering both halves or only one when mismatched. Tag [bikini](#bikini) alongside.

entries.name: highleg_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) bottom whose legline is cut far higher than usual, leaving much more of the hip bare. The top is an ordinary bikini top.

entries.name: slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) that runs from the [crotch](#crotch) up over the [nipples](#nipples) and shoulders and down the [back](#back), a [thong](#thong) with shoulder straps; the mankini on men. Not tagged [one-piece_swimsuit](#one-piece_swimsuit) despite being one piece.

entries.name: green_bikini
entries.description: A green two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit), the top, the bottoms or both pieces. Where the two halves differ in colour, [tag](#tag) each of them for what it actually is.

entries.name: frilled_bikini_bottom
entries.description: The lower half of a [bikini](#bikini) edged with ruffles along the waistband or the leg openings. When the top is ruffled as [well](#well), [tag](#tag) [frilled_bikini_top](#frilled_bikini_top) beside it.

entries.name: bikini_skirt
entries.description: A short [skirt](#skirt) [serving](#serving) as the lower half of a [bikini](#bikini), with a bottom built into it and colours matching the top. A [sarong](#sarong) is a separate wrap and does not count.

entries.name: thong_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose bottom is a thin strip that leaves the buttocks bare. Tag only when the bare cheeks are actually visible; most micro bikinis qualify, but not every [string](#string) bikini does.

entries.name: o-ring_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose cups or straps are linked by rings, at the chest, at the hips, or in both places.

entries.name: o-ring_top
entries.description: A top, very often a [bikini](#bikini) top, in which a [ring](#ring) is a conspicuous feature, such as cups meeting at one large [circle](#circle) in front. Ovals, hearts and other pierced [shapes](#shapes) are covered as [well](#well).

entries.name: gold_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in [gold](#gold), frequently with a metallic sheen to the [fabric](#fabric). It reads as showy rather than practical, and turns up in [treasure](#treasure), [dancer](#dancer) and [summer](#summer) settings.

entries.name: bikini_bottom_only
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) bottom worn with [no](#no) bikini top, whether [topless](#topless) or under a [shirt](#shirt) or [jacket](#jacket). Use it only when the upper body is in view and clearly bare of one; a [bandeau](#bandeau) or [tankini](#tankini) top rules it out.

entries.name: untied_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose ties have come loose at the side, front or [back](#back), so the [fabric](#fabric) hangs slack or is on the verge of [falling](#falling) away entirely.

entries.name: cow_print_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) printed in black-and-white [cow](#cow) patches, the centrepiece of most cow girl outfits. Usually worn with matching [gloves](#gloves) and stockings, plus ears and [horns](#horns).

entries.name: multicolored_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) worked in two or more clearly different colours, or blended between them. The threshold for what counts as multicoloured is the one set by [multicolored_clothes](#multicolored_clothes).

entries.name: orange_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) in orange, [counting](#counting) whether only the top, only the bottom or both pieces carry the colour. Add the cut, such as [string_bikini](#string_bikini), where it matters.

entries.name: strapless_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top with [no](#no) shoulder straps or halter, held up only by its snug fit, like a [bandeau](#bandeau). Most bandeau and [eyepatch](#eyepatch) bikinis qualify.

entries.name: lowleg_bikini
entries.description: Bikini bottoms cut low across the hips in a nearly horizontal line, baring more of the hip than a normal cut. The waistband is generally narrow.

entries.name: two-tone_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) in exactly two colours, whether top and bottom differ from each other or each piece is [split](#split). Implies bikini.

entries.name: polka_dot_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) printed with polka [dots](#dots), on either piece or both. Tag bikini and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) alongside it.

entries.name: flag_print_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut from [cloth](#cloth) printed with a [flag](#flag), rather than shaped to a flag's own proportions. The design sits in the [fabric](#fabric) like any other print.

entries.name: eyepatch_bikini
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) [bikini](#bikini) whose top is two small [square](#square) patches, like medical eyepatches, joined by parallel straps. Usually cut small enough to barely [cover](#cover) the [nipples](#nipples).

entries.name: maid_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) trimmed with [maid](#maid) motifs: [frills](#frills), a small [apron](#apron) panel, [cuffs](#cuffs) and a [headdress](#headdress). Counts among the unconventional maid outfits.

entries.name: multi-strapped_bikini_bottom
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) bottom held at the hips by several straps rather than one band, sometimes worn under a strapped bikini [skirt](#skirt). Two separate bottoms pulled on one over the other are a layered bikini.

entries.name: o-ring_bottom
entries.description: Swimwear or [underwear](#underwear) bottoms in which a [ring](#ring) is a conspicuous part of the design, typically joining the front and [back](#back) panels at each hip. Ovals, hearts and other pierced [shapes](#shapes) count too.

entries.name: layered_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) worn in two or more visible layers, for instance a [highleg](#highleg) bottom beneath a [lowleg](#lowleg) one so both edges show at the hip. When one layer is a one-piece, add [layered_swimsuit](#layered_swimsuit).

entries.name: low-rise_bikini
entries.description: Bikini bottoms whose waistband rides low across the hips, [well](#well) below the [navel](#navel). The whole lower [belly](#belly) is left bare above them.

entries.name: american_flag_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) printed in the stars and stripes, often with the star [field](#field) on the top and the [bars](#bars) on the bottom. It belongs to patriotic and midsummer pin-ups.

entries.name: bow_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) with a [bow](#bow) worked into it, knotted at the centre of the top, tied at the hips of the bottom, or [stitched](#stitched) on as trim. Mark the bikini and the bow as [well](#well).

entries.name: mismatched_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose top and bottom differ from each other in color or pattern.

entries.name: sailor_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose top features a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar), often with a [pleated](#pleated) bikini [skirt](#skirt) or a sailor [hat](#hat) to echo a [serafuku](#serafuku). Tagged with bikini and [sailor_collar](#sailor_collar).

entries.name: aqua_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) in a blue-green [shade](#shade). Add the cut where it is distinctive, such as a [string](#string) or side-tie style.

entries.name: santa_bikini
entries.description: A red [bikini](#bikini) with white fur trim styled after a Santa [costume](#costume), a Christmas pin-up [staple](#staple). Tagged with bikini and often [santa_hat](#santa_hat).

entries.name: plaid_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in plaid or tartan [fabric](#fabric), on the top, the bottom, or both. Pair it with [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes), since the [bikini](#bikini) is clothing [carrying](#carrying) the pattern.

entries.name: sports_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) with a sports-bra-style top, or the sports-bra-and-buruma combination worn for [running](#running) and [beach](#beach) [volleyball](#volleyball). Athletic rather than fashion-driven swimwear.

entries.name: tankini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) pairing a tank-style or crop top with [bikini](#bikini) bottoms.

entries.name: unworn_bikini_top
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top is visible in the picture but taken off, held or set aside nearby. Where [no](#no) top appears at all, [topless](#topless) is the [tag](#tag) for the bare state.

entries.name: grey_bikini
entries.description: A grey [bikini](#bikini), [counting](#counting) the top, the bottom or the pair together. A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) made in a single piece is [grey_one-piece_swimsuit](#grey_one-piece_swimsuit).

entries.name: off-shoulder_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) cut to sit below the shoulders, normally with short sleeves [resting](#resting) on the upper arms and a wide neckline baring the [collarbone](#collarbone). An ordinary bikini whose [strap](#strap) has slid down is not this.

entries.name: brown_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) in brown, [plain](#plain) or in animal-print and leather-look styles. Add bikini.

entries.name: shell_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top made from seashells, the classic [mermaid](#mermaid) outfit. Implies [shell](#shell); add bikini when the bottom half is also shown.

entries.name: floral_print_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut from flower-patterned [cloth](#cloth). The blooms are in the [fabric](#fabric) rather than attached as ornaments.

entries.name: vertical-striped_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose top, bottom or both carry stripes [running](#running) up and down. Combine with the matching bikini colour tags to give the stripes their colour.

entries.name: untied_bikini_top
entries.description: The strings of a [bikini](#bikini) top have released at the [neck](#neck) or [back](#back), leaving the cups [hanging](#hanging) loose against the chest rather than supported.

entries.name: multi-strapped_bikini_top
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top with more than one pair of shoulder straps, or a [halterneck](#halterneck) combined with shoulder straps. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a layered or an [eyepatch](#eyepatch) bikini.

entries.name: sling_bikini_top
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top of two straight bands crossing the [breasts](#breasts) diagonally to [cover](#cover) the [nipples](#nipples). If the bands run down to join the bottom it is a [slingshot_swimsuit](#slingshot_swimsuit).

entries.name: unworn_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) is visible in the scene but nobody has it on, whether [folded](#folded), held up, [hanging](#hanging) to dry or [lying](#lying) beside its owner. Either piece alone or the set as a whole [can](#can) qualify.

entries.name: bikini_shorts
entries.description: Swim [shorts](#shorts) matched to a [bikini](#bikini) top in colour and pattern, [standing](#standing) in for the usual brief bottom. They [cover](#cover) more than [briefs](#briefs) while still [reading](#reading) as part of the [swimsuit](#swimsuit).

entries.name: unworn_bikini_bottom
entries.description: The lower half of a [bikini](#bikini) appears in the picture off the body. Where [no](#no) bikini bottom [can](#can) be seen anywhere, [bottomless](#bottomless) covers the bare state instead.

entries.name: german_flag_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) printed with the black, red and [gold](#gold) bands of the German [flag](#flag). One of the national-flag swimwear designs used in sports and [summer](#summer) artwork.

entries.name: bikini_under_shorts
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) worn under a pair of [shorts](#shorts), showing at the waistband, through the [cloth](#cloth) or where the shorts ride up. Standard beach-bound and [poolside](#poolside) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: fur-trimmed_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) with fur [running](#running) along its edges, [giving](#giving) swimwear a wintry or [tribal](#tribal) [note](#note). A two-piece cut from [pelt](#pelt) throughout is [fur_bikini](#fur_bikini) instead.

entries.name: leopard_print_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) [patterned](#patterned) with a leopard's [dark](#dark) rosettes, usually on a [tan](#tan) ground.

entries.name: fur_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece cut from [animal](#animal) [pelt](#pelt) rather than [fabric](#fabric), the standard cavewoman and [barbarian](#barbarian) garment. A [bikini](#bikini) merely edged with fur is [fur-trimmed_bikini](#fur-trimmed_bikini).

entries.name: cross-laced_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top whose cups or centre panel are joined by cords or ribbons crossing into an X. The lacing may genuinely hold the piece shut or sit there as pure decoration.

entries.name: torn_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) [torn](#torn) at [cup](#cup) or tie, the garment barely [holding](#holding) together.

entries.name: untied_bikini_bottom
entries.description: The side ties of a [bikini](#bikini) bottom have come undone, so the panel of [fabric](#fabric) [no](#no) longer holds itself against the hips. It still rests on the wearer's body rather than having been taken off.

entries.name: white_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A white slingshot [swimsuit](#swimsuit), two narrow straps rising from the [crotch](#crotch) over the shoulders and leaving the sides of the [torso](#torso) bare. It covers little beyond the [nipples](#nipples) and [groin](#groin).

entries.name: frilled_bikini_top
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top edged with ruffles, sometimes layered in tiers across the bust. Its counterpart below is [frilled_bikini_bottom](#frilled_bikini_bottom).

entries.name: camouflage_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut from camouflage-patterned [cloth](#cloth), top and bottom alike. It generally turns up on military-flavoured characters, often beside [dog](#dog) tags, [boots](#boots) or a [rifle](#rifle) propped in the [sand](#sand).

entries.name: loose_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) that is oversized or badly tied, so the cups gape away from the body and the [fabric](#fabric) threatens to slip. It is not the same as a small [suit](#suit) that merely fits tightly.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose top, bottom or both are edged with a [ribbon](#ribbon) band. The trim usually runs along the cups or the waistband.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose edges are finished with [lace](#lace). The garment itself is solid [fabric](#fabric), unlike a [suit](#suit) cut entirely from openwork lace.

entries.name: checkered_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) printed in squares, top and bottoms matching. Small [gingham](#gingham) is the usual [choice](#choice), though larger blocks appear too.

entries.name: red_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A red [swimsuit](#swimsuit) reduced to two narrow straps that run from the [crotch](#crotch) over the shoulders, barely covering the [nipples](#nipples) and leaving the sides of the body open. Worn as [display](#display) rather than for [swimming](#swimming).

entries.name: leaf_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) improvised from [foliage](#foliage), leaves covering chest and hips in place of [fabric](#fabric). Jungle, castaway and nature-spirit pictures use it, and it overlaps with [leaf_clothing](#leaf_clothing).

entries.name: silver_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) rendered in a shiny silver-grey. The metallic sheen is usually painted in with [strong](#strong) highlights against the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: zipper_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) with zippers built into the [fabric](#fabric), usually crossing the cups or [running](#running) down the front of the bottoms. It may be shown partly undone to expose what lies beneath, often with a prominent pull tab drawn in.

entries.name: rainbow_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) whose [fabric](#fabric) runs through the colors of the spectrum, either in stripes or as a smooth blend. Both pieces usually share the same pattern.

entries.name: bikini_over_clothes
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) put on over ordinary clothing instead of against the skin. The reverse of wearing one underneath, and usually either a joke or a deliberately odd outfit.

entries.name: metal_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece cut from rigid metal plates, closer to ornament or light [armor](#armor) than to [cloth](#cloth). A [staple](#staple) of sword-and-sorcery [costume](#costume) design.

entries.name: gradient_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) whose [fabric](#fabric) shades gradually from one colour into another rather than being flat or [patterned](#patterned). Top and bottoms normally carry the same fade.

entries.name: heart_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose cups or bottoms are cut as hearts rather than printed with them. It stands in for heart-shaped [underwear](#underwear) generally, since bras and [panties](#panties) have [no](#no) shaped-cut tags of their own.

entries.name: latex_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut from glossy rubber rather than [cloth](#cloth), [clinging](#clinging) with a wet-looking sheen. It is worn for the look far more often than for [swimming](#swimming).

entries.name: flower_bikini
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) whose cups and [briefs](#briefs) are made from flowers, or cut in their shape, instead of ordinary [cloth](#cloth). Fantasy and nature-spirit designs favour it.

entries.name: pretzel_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top whose straps rise behind the [neck](#neck), [cross](#cross) down over the chest and join again at the [back](#back), tracing a looping [path](#path). A bridging [strap](#strap) between the cups rules the [tag](#tag) out.

entries.name: wet_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) soaked through so it clings to the body and sometimes turns partly see-through. Pools, [rain](#rain) and the sea are the usual causes.

entries.name: leather_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece cut from hide rather than swim [fabric](#fabric), mostly black or brown. It appears as [barbarian](#barbarian) gear or fetish wear far more often than as anything worn to a [beach](#beach).

entries.name: horizontal-striped_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) banded with stripes [running](#running) across the body rather than up and down. Both pieces normally carry the same banding.

entries.name: double_bikini
entries.description: Two bikinis worn at the same time, one layered over the other. Usually a [gag](#gag), or a way of setting two colour schemes against each other.

entries.name: satin_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut from glossy [satin](#satin), the [fabric](#fabric) [catching](#catching) hard highlights across the cups and hips.

entries.name: union_jack_bikini
entries.description: A two-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut from the pattern of the British [flag](#flag), dominated by the blue ground behind its crossed red and white [bars](#bars). Often given to characters marked out as British.

entries.name: starfish_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) whose cups are [starfish](#starfish), or one printed with them. A [beach](#beach) and [mermaid](#mermaid) [staple](#staple), often worn with [shell](#shell) jewellery.

entries.name: swimsuit
entries.description: Any garment made for [swimming](#swimming), [bathing](#bathing) or the [beach](#beach). Women's versions are stretchy one- or two-piece suits, men's are trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or [jammers](#jammers); add the specific type such as [bikini](#bikini) or [one-piece_swimsuit](#one-piece_swimsuit) where it applies.

entries.name: one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) made as a single garment covering [torso](#torso) and [crotch](#crotch), [giving](#giving) more coverage than a [bikini](#bikini). A slingshot swimsuit is excluded despite being one piece of [cloth](#cloth); [school](#school) and [competition](#competition) suits are common kinds.

entries.name: school_swimsuit
entries.description: The standard one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) issued by Japanese schools, usually navy, black, white or grey, often with a white name [tag](#tag) across the chest. Old, new and [competition](#competition) variants differ in [strap](#strap) width, [seams](#seams) and the [groin](#groin) flap.

entries.name: competition_swimsuit
entries.description: A sleek one-piece [racing](#racing) [suit](#suit) with a [racerback](#racerback), made for swim meets, sometimes extended over the [thighs](#thighs) like a [bodysuit](#bodysuit). It plays down [cleavage](#cleavage) and often carries [sportswear](#sportswear) branding.

entries.name: blue_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) of a single piece in blue, covering the [torso](#torso) between shoulders and hips. The navy [school](#school) swimsuit normally carries this as [well](#well).

entries.name: black_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in black. A [competition](#competition) or [school](#school) cut [can](#can) be tagged on top, since this records only the colour.

entries.name: white_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A single-piece [bathing](#bathing) [suit](#suit) in white, covering the [torso](#torso) as one garment rather than a two-piece [bikini](#bikini). A [staple](#staple) of [summer](#summer) and [pool](#pool) illustrations, and pairs with [school_swimsuit](#school_swimsuit) when it's that particular style.

entries.name: highleg_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) with an exaggerated legline that bares much more of the hips. Everything else about it is an ordinary one-piece.

entries.name: sarong
entries.description: A big sheet of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the hips as a [skirt](#skirt), most often over a [bikini](#bikini) and knotted at one side. A pareo is treated as the same garment here, though the two have different origins.

entries.name: casual_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: An everyday [fashion](#fashion) one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit), as opposed to a [school](#school) or a [competition](#competition) [suit](#suit). It covers most [beach](#beach) and holiday one-pieces.

entries.name: male_swimwear
entries.description: Trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or [jammers](#jammers) worn by a male character for [swimming](#swimming) or the [beach](#beach). Displaced versions are male_swimwear_aside and [male_swimwear_pull](#male_swimwear_pull).

entries.name: competition_school_swimsuit
entries.description: A [school](#school) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut on [racing](#racing) lines, with thin separate shoulder straps and [no](#no) visible [seams](#seams) across the body. It sits between [school_swimsuit](#school_swimsuit) and [competition_swimsuit](#competition_swimsuit).

entries.name: old_school_swimsuit
entries.description: The classic Japanese [school](#school) [swimsuit](#swimsuit): a [dark](#dark) blue or black one-piece with wide straps, [seams](#seams) [running](#running) down the [torso](#torso) and a skirt-like flap over the [groin](#groin), sometimes with a white name [patch](#patch) across the chest. Drop the flap and it becomes [new_school_swimsuit](#new_school_swimsuit); thin straps and [no](#no) seams make it [competition_school_swimsuit](#competition_school_swimsuit).

entries.name: frilled_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) [carrying](#carrying) ruffles, typically around the hips, across the bust or on the straps. The two-piece equivalent is [frilled_bikini](#frilled_bikini).

entries.name: swim_trunks
entries.description: Loose swim [shorts](#shorts) with a [drawstring](#drawstring) waist, most often worn by men though women wear them too. The tight, brief-cut style is a separate garment.

entries.name: two-tone_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) of any style in exactly two colours. Add the colour tags too.

entries.name: wet_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) [wet](#wet) from the [water](#water), shown by droplets on the [fabric](#fabric), a [dripping](#dripping) wearer, or a white one-piece gone [translucent](#translucent).

entries.name: multicolored_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) worked in two or more colours, whether panelled, trimmed or printed in blocks. The general rule for what counts as multicoloured is set out under [multicolored_clothes](#multicolored_clothes).

entries.name: red_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A red one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit), the single-garment cut covering [torso](#torso) and [crotch](#crotch). A red two-piece is [red_bikini](#red_bikini) instead.

entries.name: white_school_swimsuit
entries.description: The Japanese [school](#school) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) rendered in white rather than its usual navy, a one-piece with a chest name [tag](#tag). Since white is not the issued colour, the tag usually signals a stylised alternate or a soaked, see-through effect.

entries.name: swim_briefs
entries.description: Tight, brief-cut men's swimwear in the style popularized by a well-known [sportswear](#sportswear) brand. Never use it for that brand's own [logo](#logo) or products, which get a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pink_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in pink, the single garment covering [torso](#torso) and [crotch](#crotch). School and [competition](#competition) swimsuits in pink take it as [well](#well); a two-piece is [pink_bikini](#pink_bikini).

entries.name: black_male_swimwear
entries.description: Swim trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or [jammers](#jammers) in black worn by a male character. Only the colour and the wearer are recorded, so the cut is left to other tags.

entries.name: blue_male_swimwear
entries.description: Blue [swimming](#swimming) garments cut for men, trunks, [briefs](#briefs) and [jammers](#jammers) among them. Add the particular style where the cut [can](#can) be told apart.

entries.name: diving_suit
entries.description: A full-body [suit](#suit) for staying in the [water](#water), whether a [wetsuit](#wetsuit), a drysuit or the [old](#old) brass-helmeted rig. Usually paired with a [snorkel](#snorkel), a regulator or a [helmet](#helmet).

entries.name: polka_dot_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) printed with polka [dots](#dots), usually a one-piece; a dotted two-piece is [polka_dot_bikini](#polka_dot_bikini). Tag swimsuit and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) alongside.

entries.name: purple_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A purple one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit). Combine with [one-piece_swimsuit](#one-piece_swimsuit) and the cut, such as [school_swimsuit](#school_swimsuit) or [competition_swimsuit](#competition_swimsuit); a two-piece is [purple_bikini](#purple_bikini).

entries.name: wetsuit
entries.description: A protective neoprene [suit](#suit) for [surfing](#surfing) or [diving](#diving), told apart from a [plain](#plain) [unitard](#unitard) by its [collar](#collar), visible [seams](#seams) and sportier cut. Add [male_swimwear](#male_swimwear) when worn by a male character.

entries.name: two-tone_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) coloured in exactly two tones, such as a [dark](#dark) body with contrasting side panels. Add the colour tags too.

entries.name: new_school_swimsuit
entries.description: The Japanese [school](#school) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) as cut since the 1980s, lacking the horizontal seam above the [crotch](#crotch) that the [old_school_swimsuit](#old_school_swimsuit) carries. Competition-style suits and skirted variants have tags of their own.

entries.name: impossible_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit), usually a one-piece, gripping the [breasts](#breasts) and body like [paint](#paint) instead of [fabric](#fabric). The [leotard](#leotard) equivalent is [impossible_leotard](#impossible_leotard).

entries.name: green_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A green [swimsuit](#swimsuit) made as a single garment, whether a [school](#school) swimsuit, a [competition](#competition) cut or a [casual](#casual) style. A two-piece is a [green_bikini](#green_bikini).

entries.name: unworn_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) is visible in the picture but nobody has it on, [hanging](#hanging) to dry, [folded](#folded) on a [towel](#towel) or held up for inspection.

entries.name: swimsuit_cover-up
entries.description: A light, often sheer garment thrown over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) to [cover](#cover) the arms or upper body. A wrap tied around the waist instead is a [sarong](#sarong).

entries.name: blue_swim_trunks
entries.description: Loose blue [swimming](#swimming) [shorts](#shorts) of the kind cut for men, ending on the upper thigh. Baggier than [briefs](#briefs), and generally gathered at the waist with a [drawstring](#drawstring).

entries.name: yellow_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in yellow, covering the [torso](#torso) without splitting into top and bottom. School and [competition](#competition) [cuts](#cuts) count as long as they are yellow.

entries.name: black_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A black slingshot [swimsuit](#swimsuit), the V-shaped one-piece whose narrow straps pass over the shoulders. It covers little beyond the [crotch](#crotch) and the [nipples](#nipples).

entries.name: torn_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) ripped somewhere on the body while it is still being worn, rather than removed. The tear reads as damage or a rough moment rather than deliberate [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: white_sarong
entries.description: A length of white [cloth](#cloth) wound around the hips like a [skirt](#skirt), typically layered over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) at the [beach](#beach). Tag [sarong](#sarong) for the garment itself and [note](#note) whatever swimwear lies underneath.

entries.name: off-shoulder_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) with a wide low neckline and sleeves [sitting](#sitting) on the upper arms, so shoulders and upper chest stay uncovered. The two-piece equivalent is [off-shoulder_bikini](#off-shoulder_bikini).

entries.name: strapless_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) with [no](#no) straps, halter or sleeves, relying on [fabric](#fabric) tension, so it looks much like a [strapless](#strapless) [leotard](#leotard).

entries.name: dress_swimsuit
entries.description: Swimwear cut to look like a [dress](#dress) or [sundress](#sundress), with a flared [skirt](#skirt) [falling](#falling) over the brief beneath. Chosen where a [plain](#plain) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) would be too bare.

entries.name: print_swimsuit
entries.description: Swimwear [carrying](#carrying) a [patterned](#patterned) design that [no](#no) more specific [tag](#tag) already covers. Plaid, polka-dot and striped swimsuits have dedicated tags and should use those. A printed design does not by itself make the [swimsuit](#swimsuit) multicoloured.

entries.name: blue_sarong
entries.description: A blue wrap of [cloth](#cloth) knotted around the hips or the chest, most often thrown over swimwear at the [beach](#beach). It hangs loose and open rather than being sewn into a [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: striped_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [one-piece_swimsuit](#one-piece_swimsuit) and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: red_male_swimwear
entries.description: Swim trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or [shorts](#shorts) in red worn by a male character. Covers everything from loose [beach](#beach) shorts to [competition](#competition) briefs.

entries.name: o-ring_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) with rings on show, commonly bridging a gap at the chest or the hips. Two-piece swimwear takes [o-ring_top](#o-ring_top) and [o-ring_bottom](#o-ring_bottom), or [o-ring_bikini](#o-ring_bikini) when both halves have them.

entries.name: one-piece_thong
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) or [leotard](#leotard) cut so narrowly at the [back](#back) that the buttocks are left bare the way a [thong](#thong) would leave them.

entries.name: print_sarong
entries.description: A [sarong](#sarong) with a printed design, wrapped round the hips over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit). Tropical florals are the standard motif.

entries.name: taut_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) too small or tight for the body wearing it, the [fabric](#fabric) drawn taut and [biting](#biting) slightly into the skin. When the cups cannot really contain the [breasts](#breasts), [impossible_swimsuit](#impossible_swimsuit) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: rash_guard
entries.description: A close-fitting athletic [shirt](#shirt) worn for [surfing](#surfing) and other watersports, [giving](#giving) more coverage than a [plain](#plain) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) without the bulk of a [wetsuit](#wetsuit). Most have long sleeves; a visible seam where top meets bottom marks it apart from a full wetsuit.

entries.name: backless_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) left open down the [back](#back) toward the waist, carried by a halter [neck](#neck) or by thin crossing straps. The front is cut like any other one-piece.

entries.name: grey_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A grey [swimsuit](#swimsuit) covering the [torso](#torso) as a single garment. School and [competition](#competition) [cuts](#cuts) count whenever they are this colour.

entries.name: side-tie_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece or other non-bikini [swimsuit](#swimsuit) whose sides are laced or knotted rather than closed. The ties leave open gaps along the flanks.

entries.name: pink_sarong
entries.description: A pink length of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped round the hips over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) and knotted at one side. A [beach](#beach) cover-up rather than a proper [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: print_male_swimwear
entries.description: Men's trunks or swim [shorts](#shorts) [carrying](#carrying) a printed design, from florals and stripes to cartoon motifs. Worn at the [beach](#beach) or the [pool](#pool).

entries.name: white_male_swimwear
entries.description: Trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or swim [shorts](#shorts) for men in white. Artists often play on how the white [fabric](#fabric) turns [translucent](#translucent) once it's [wet](#wet).

entries.name: front_zipper_swimsuit
entries.description: A racing-cut one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) whose chest zip is drawn down to open a wedge of bare skin. It [caught](#caught) on as an online fad in the same [spirit](#spirit) as the open-chest [sweater](#sweater).

entries.name: green_male_swimwear
entries.description: Swim trunks, [shorts](#shorts) or [briefs](#briefs) cut for men and coloured green. It belongs with [beach](#beach), [poolside](#poolside) and [swimming](#swimming) scenes.

entries.name: swimsuit_skirt
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) whose lower half is cut into a small attached [skirt](#skirt). When the skirt belongs to the bottom half of a two-piece, use [bikini_skirt](#bikini_skirt) instead.

entries.name: black_sarong
entries.description: A black length of [cloth](#cloth) knotted around the hips or waist, most often over swimwear at a [pool](#pool) or [beach](#beach). It works as a cover-up rather than as a [skirt](#skirt) in its own right.

entries.name: jammers
entries.description: Close-fitting competitive swim [shorts](#shorts) for men, [running](#running) from the waist to just above the knee. They are cut like cycling shorts rather than loose trunks.

entries.name: yellow_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A yellow slingshot [swimsuit](#swimsuit): two narrow strips [running](#running) from the [crotch](#crotch) over the shoulders, leaving the sides of the chest and the hips bare. It covers little beyond the [nipples](#nipples) and [groin](#groin).

entries.name: school_swimsuit_flap
entries.description: The drainage flap on the front of a [school](#school) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) pulled open or made the focus of the picture. Pulling the [crotch](#crotch) of the [suit](#suit) aside to expose instead takes [swimsuit_aside](#swimsuit_aside).

entries.name: red_sarong
entries.description: A red length of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the hips and knotted at the side, worn over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) at the [beach](#beach). It drapes rather than being tailored, so it reads as a cover-up rather than a [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: orange_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: An orange [swimsuit](#swimsuit) made as a single garment rather than as separate top and bottom. Any neckline or [back](#back) cut counts.

entries.name: purple_sarong
entries.description: A purple length of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the hips over swimwear and knotted at the side. A [beach](#beach) and [poolside](#poolside) cover-up.

entries.name: aqua_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A single-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in blue-green covering the [torso](#torso). School and [competition](#competition) [cuts](#cuts) each have a [tag](#tag) of their own to add.

entries.name: nontraditional_school_swimsuit
entries.description: A [school](#school) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) altered from the [plain](#plain) standard cut, with [frills](#frills), a [skirt](#skirt) or bike [shorts](#shorts) added, or a customary element such as the name panel dropped.

entries.name: green_sarong
entries.description: A green [sarong](#sarong), the length of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the hips and knotted at one side. It is normally worn over swimwear at a [beach](#beach) or [poolside](#poolside).

entries.name: blue_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A blue [swimsuit](#swimsuit) made of two narrow straps that run over the shoulders and meet between the [breasts](#breasts) before continuing to the [crotch](#crotch). The sides and much of the chest stay bare.

entries.name: yellow_male_swimwear
entries.description: Men's swimwear in yellow, whether trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or [shorts](#shorts). Colour is the only thing separating it from the general swimwear [tag](#tag).

entries.name: vertical-striped_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) down the body from shoulder to hip. The lengthwise direction distinguishes it from a horizontally banded [suit](#suit).

entries.name: purple_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A purple [swimsuit](#swimsuit) reduced to two narrow straps [running](#running) from the [crotch](#crotch) over the shoulders, leaving the sides of the [torso](#torso) and most of the [breasts](#breasts) bare.

entries.name: cross-laced_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) laced with cords crossing over the chest or along the sides. Two-piece versions carry [cross-laced_bikini](#cross-laced_bikini) instead.

entries.name: ribbed_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut from ribbed [fabric](#fabric), [giving](#giving) it fine vertical lines across the body. The texture reads most clearly where the [cloth](#cloth) stretches over the chest and hips.

entries.name: legskin
entries.description: Skin-tight [racing](#racing) swimwear for men [running](#running) from the waist down to the ankles, cut to reduce drag in the [water](#water). It looks much like a glossy pair of [leggings](#leggings).

entries.name: brown_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in brown built as one garment over the [torso](#torso). Two separate pieces in the same [shade](#shade) make a [bikini](#bikini) instead.

entries.name: orange_male_swimwear
entries.description: Trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or [jammers](#jammers) cut for men in orange, from loose [beach](#beach) [shorts](#shorts) to [competition](#competition) swimwear.

entries.name: yellow_sarong
entries.description: A yellow length of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the hips over swimwear and knotted at the waist or side. It usually falls somewhere between knee and ankle.

entries.name: orange_sarong
entries.description: An orange [sarong](#sarong), the length of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped about the hips over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit). Beach and resort wear.

entries.name: pink_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A pink [swimsuit](#swimsuit) reduced to narrow bands [running](#running) from the [crotch](#crotch) up over the shoulders, leaving the sides of the [torso](#torso) bare. Made for [display](#display) rather than for [swimming](#swimming).

entries.name: black_wetsuit
entries.description: A black [diving](#diving) or [surfing](#surfing) [suit](#suit) of thick rubbery material clamped tight to the body. Its bulk and visible [seams](#seams) distinguish it from a [plain](#plain) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) or a [bodysuit](#bodysuit).

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) edged with a [ribbon](#ribbon) band, in the manner of the banding seen on [miko](#miko) sleeves. The trim commonly outlines the neckline and leg openings.

entries.name: bow_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) decorated with a [bow](#bow), on a one-piece or on a [bikini](#bikini) alike. It may sit at the chest, on a hip, or where the ties meet at the [back](#back).

entries.name: grey_male_swimwear
entries.description: Men's swimwear in grey, whether trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or board [shorts](#shorts). It belongs with [beach](#beach), [poolside](#poolside) and [swimming](#swimming) scenes.

entries.name: purple_male_swimwear
entries.description: Men's swimwear, whether trunks, [briefs](#briefs), or [shorts](#shorts), in purple.

entries.name: aqua_sarong
entries.description: A length of blue-green [cloth](#cloth) wrapped round the hips over swimwear. Standard on [beach](#beach) and [poolside](#poolside) designs.

entries.name: turtleneck_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) that closes high around the [neck](#neck) in a rolled [collar](#collar) instead of [opening](#opening) at the chest. The covered throat gives it an unusually sporty, modest [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: gold_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in [gold](#gold) [fabric](#fabric), usually with a metallic finish. One of the colour variants of the garment.

entries.name: unworn_sarong
entries.description: A [sarong](#sarong) appears in the picture but is not wrapped around anyone, spread on the [sand](#sand), draped over a [chair](#chair) or carried.

entries.name: sailor_one-piece_swimsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) with a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) built into the garment itself. It does not apply when a separate school-uniform top is worn over a [plain](#plain) swimsuit.

entries.name: monokini
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) cut wide open at the sides, so that a narrow front panel is all that joins the top to the bottom, with little left at the [back](#back). It sits halfway between a [bikini](#bikini) and a full one-piece.

entries.name: green_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A green [swimsuit](#swimsuit) built from two narrow straps that run from the [crotch](#crotch) up over the shoulders, leaving the sides of the [torso](#torso) bare. It exposes far more than an ordinary one-piece.

entries.name: layered_swimsuit
entries.description: Two swimsuits worn at once, whole or in part, one showing beneath the other. When a [bikini](#bikini) is one of the layers, add the layered bikini [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: brown_male_swimwear
entries.description: Swimwear cut for men in brown, whether trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or board [shorts](#shorts). The colour applies to the garment itself, whatever its style.

entries.name: pink_male_swimwear
entries.description: Men's swimwear in pink, whether trunks, [briefs](#briefs) or swim [shorts](#shorts). Only the colour and the cut for men set it apart.

entries.name: springsuit
entries.description: A short [wetsuit](#wetsuit) that leaves either the arms or the [legs](#legs) bare instead of covering the whole body. Its cut varies as leotards do, with long-sleeve, short-sleeve, [highleg](#highleg) and [thong](#thong) versions.

entries.name: brown_sarong
entries.description: A brown length of [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the hips, most often pulled on over swimwear at the [beach](#beach) or [poolside](#poolside).

entries.name: orange_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: An orange slingshot [swimsuit](#swimsuit): two narrow straps run over the shoulders and down between the [breasts](#breasts), leaving the flanks bare.

entries.name: grey_sarong
entries.description: A grey [sarong](#sarong) wrapped around the hips and knotted at one side. It is normally worn over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) at a [beach](#beach) or [poolside](#poolside).

entries.name: grey_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A grey slingshot [swimsuit](#swimsuit), its two narrow straps [running](#running) over the shoulders and between the [breasts](#breasts) with the sides left bare. It exposes far more than an ordinary one-piece.

entries.name: brown_slingshot_swimsuit
entries.description: A brown slingshot [swimsuit](#swimsuit): two narrow straps passing over the shoulders and down between the [breasts](#breasts), leaving the flanks bare.

entries.name: brown_swimwear
entries.description: Swimwear in brown with [no](#no) cut specified — the general colour [tag](#tag), used where no narrower swimwear tag applies.

entries.name: grey_swimwear
entries.description: Swimwear of any cut in grey. It serves as the general colour variant where [no](#no) more specific swimwear [tag](#tag) fits.

entries.name: orange_swimwear
entries.description: Swimwear in orange of any cut. The general colour [tag](#tag), used where [no](#no) narrower swimwear tag fits.

entries.name: leotard
entries.description: A skin-tight one-piece covering the [torso](#torso) and leaving the [legs](#legs) bare, in any sleeve length, worn by gymnasts, dancers and [circus](#circus) performers. If it also covers the upper legs it is a [bodysuit](#bodysuit), and a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) is never one of these. Colour variants such as [black_leotard](#black_leotard) exist.

entries.name: sleeveless_leotard
entries.description: A close-fitting one-piece that covers the [torso](#torso) and stops at the hips, cut without sleeves so the arms are entirely bare. Common on dancers, gymnasts, idols and superhero-style outfits.

entries.name: bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight single garment [running](#running) from the [neck](#neck) down over at least the upper [legs](#legs), as in plugsuits and superhero costumes. A single piece of [cloth](#cloth) is required: a [leotard](#leotard) above [pantyhose](#pantyhose) does not qualify, a version stopping at the hips is a leotard, and sheer [fabric](#fabric) makes it a [bodystocking](#bodystocking).

entries.name: black_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) in black, cut high on the hips so the [legs](#legs) stay bare, worn for [gymnastics](#gymnastics), dance and bunny suits. One that covers the legs too is [black_bodysuit](#black_bodysuit).

entries.name: strapless_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with [no](#no) shoulder straps, held on the upper body only by its tight fit.

entries.name: highleg_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) whose leg openings sweep up over the hips, showing the [thighs](#thighs) and the sides of the waist. Eighties aerobics looks and [fantasy](#fantasy) costumes lean on it heavily.

entries.name: black_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight black [suit](#suit) covering the [torso](#torso) and limbs, common on [ninja](#ninja), [pilot](#pilot) and hero designs. A garment that leaves the [legs](#legs) bare is [black_leotard](#black_leotard) instead.

entries.name: white_leotard
entries.description: A white [leotard](#leotard), the [sleeveless](#sleeveless) swimsuit-cut garment worn by gymnasts and magical girls. A full-length version is [white_bodysuit](#white_bodysuit) instead.

entries.name: blue_leotard
entries.description: A blue [leotard](#leotard), the high-cut one-piece that leaves the [legs](#legs) bare, worn for [gymnastics](#gymnastics), dance or as a bunny [suit](#suit). A version covering the legs is [blue_bodysuit](#blue_bodysuit).

entries.name: black_bikesuit
entries.description: A one-piece [riding](#riding) [suit](#suit) in black, sealed at the wrists and ankles and closed by a front zip. Worn with [motorcycle](#motorcycle) and track gear, often panelled or with contrasting [seams](#seams).

entries.name: mecha_pilot_suit
entries.description: The skin-tight flight [suit](#suit) worn by a [mecha](#mecha) [pilot](#pilot), often paired with a [helmet](#helmet), hard plating and [glowing](#glowing) [seams](#seams) along the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: bodystocking
entries.description: A one-piece garment of sheer or soft [fabric](#fabric) sheathing the whole body, essentially full-length hosiery. The thin see-through [cloth](#cloth) is what separates it from a [bodysuit](#bodysuit), and it is regularly worn under a [dress](#dress) or [leotard](#leotard).

entries.name: red_leotard
entries.description: A red [leotard](#leotard), the one-piece cut that leaves arms and [legs](#legs) bare. A full-length skin-tight garment covering the limbs is a red [bodysuit](#bodysuit), not this.

entries.name: thong_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) cut so high at the hips that most of the buttocks are exposed, in the style worn by Cammy from Street Fighter.

entries.name: plugsuit
entries.description: A tight full-body [pilot](#pilot) [suit](#suit) with a distinctive [collar](#collar), hip pads, and interface clips, first worn by the pilots of one famous [mecha](#mecha) series. Used both for those original characters and for others drawn in the same style of outfit.

entries.name: white_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight full [bodysuit](#bodysuit) in white, as seen on plugsuits and sci-fi [pilot](#pilot) uniforms. A leotard-cut version is [white_leotard](#white_leotard) instead.

entries.name: red_bodysuit
entries.description: A red, skin-tight [suit](#suit) covering the whole body including the [legs](#legs). A shorter, hip-length one-piece instead is [red_leotard](#red_leotard).

entries.name: blue_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight blue [suit](#suit) covering [torso](#torso), arms and [legs](#legs), [familiar](#familiar) from pilots and superheroes. A one-piece that leaves the legs bare is [blue_leotard](#blue_leotard).

entries.name: leotard_under_clothes
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) worn as a base layer with a [shirt](#shirt), [skirt](#skirt), trousers or other garments over it. Distinct from [leotard_peek](#leotard_peek), where only a glimpse of it shows.

entries.name: purple_leotard
entries.description: A purple [leotard](#leotard), a one-piece that ends at the hips and leaves the [legs](#legs) bare. A [suit](#suit) that covers the legs as [well](#well) is [purple_bodysuit](#purple_bodysuit).

entries.name: multicolored_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) whose design carries at least two distinct colours, most often as panels [running](#running) down the limbs and [torso](#torso). Racing suits and hero outfits supply most examples.

entries.name: torn_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) ripped open to show the skin underneath, often after a [battle](#battle).

entries.name: pink_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) in pink, the one-piece garment cut high on the hip that leaves the [legs](#legs) bare. A pink [bodysuit](#bodysuit) covers the legs too, so the two are not interchangeable.

entries.name: spacesuit
entries.description: A full-body protective [suit](#suit) for surviving in [space](#space), usually paired with a [helmet](#helmet) and life-support fittings. Science-fiction versions tend to look far sleeker than real ones.

entries.name: latex_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight [suit](#suit) covering the whole body in glossy [latex](#latex) or PVC, usually black and highlighted to look [wet](#wet). Zips and [seams](#seams) are often the only break in the surface.

entries.name: bodysuit_under_clothes
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) worn as a base layer with a [jacket](#jacket), armour, a [skirt](#skirt) or [shorts](#shorts) over it, parts of the [suit](#suit) still showing. Mark both the suit and whatever goes on top.

entries.name: green_leotard
entries.description: A green one-piece [leotard](#leotard) that covers the [torso](#torso) and leaves the [legs](#legs) bare. Where the legs are covered too, the garment is a [green_bodysuit](#green_bodysuit).

entries.name: purple_bodysuit
entries.description: A full-body skin-tight [suit](#suit) in purple that covers the [legs](#legs). A version ending at the hips instead is [purple_leotard](#purple_leotard).

entries.name: two-tone_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) whose design uses exactly two colours. Add the individual colour tags alongside it.

entries.name: impossible_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) that sinks into the gap between the [breasts](#breasts) and grips every curve in a way [fabric](#fabric) cannot manage. It belongs to the [impossible_clothes](#impossible_clothes) [family](#family).

entries.name: orange_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) in orange covering the [torso](#torso) and limbs. Warm lighting on pale skin is easily mistaken for one, so look for [seams](#seams) and edges before tagging.

entries.name: pink_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight one-piece garment covering [torso](#torso) and [legs](#legs), coloured pink. A version that leaves the legs bare is a [leotard](#leotard) rather than a [bodysuit](#bodysuit).

entries.name: multicolored_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) [carrying](#carrying) at least two colours, [split](#split) into panels or edged in a contrasting [shade](#shade). Gymnastic, [idol](#idol) and hero outfits are where it appears most.

entries.name: backless_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) cut open at the [back](#back) so that part or all of it is left bare. Dancers, gymnasts and race-queen or [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits wear them.

entries.name: impossible_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) drawn so tight over the [breasts](#breasts) and body that it reads as [paint](#paint) rather than [cloth](#cloth). Compare [impossible_swimsuit](#impossible_swimsuit) for the same trick on swimwear.

entries.name: torn_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) shredded to the point of barely staying on.

entries.name: side-tie_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) whose hips are closed with strings tied into bows at the sides, like side-tie [panties](#panties) built into the garment.

entries.name: two-tone_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) in exactly two colours. Tag each colour separately as [well](#well).

entries.name: grey_bodysuit
entries.description: A close-fitting grey [suit](#suit) covering [torso](#torso) and limbs, as in [pilot](#pilot) suits and hero costumes. Leaving the [legs](#legs) bare makes it a [grey_leotard](#grey_leotard).

entries.name: sleeveless_turtleneck_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with a high [turtleneck](#turtleneck) [collar](#collar) and [no](#no) sleeves, a common base layer for [battle](#battle) outfits and magical girl designs. Detached sleeves or [gloves](#gloves) often complete it.

entries.name: turtleneck_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with a high [collar](#collar) covering the [neck](#neck), a design popularised by a specific [branded](#branded) piece but now used for the shape generally. Implies leotard and [turtleneck](#turtleneck).

entries.name: green_bodysuit
entries.description: A close-fitting one-piece [suit](#suit) in green, covering the [torso](#torso) and the limbs. Where the [legs](#legs) are left bare the garment is a [green_leotard](#green_leotard) instead.

entries.name: yellow_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight full-body [suit](#suit) in yellow, the Bruce Lee [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit) being the famous real-world example. Tag [bodysuit](#bodysuit); a [leotard](#leotard) cut is [yellow_leotard](#yellow_leotard) instead.

entries.name: bikesuit
entries.description: A one-piece [motorcycle](#motorcycle) [suit](#suit) fitted close to the body, covering everything but the head and closed by a long front zip. Worn with [boots](#boots), [gloves](#gloves) and a [helmet](#helmet), and frequently drawn [unzipped](#unzipped) part way down.

entries.name: frilled_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with ruffles attached to it, most commonly framing the leg openings. Magical girl, [idol](#idol) and [stage](#stage) designs favour the look.

entries.name: short_jumpsuit
entries.description: A one-piece [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit) whose [legs](#legs) end short, like a pair of [shorts](#shorts), also known as a [romper](#romper).

entries.name: unitard
entries.description: A skin-tight one-piece covering the [legs](#legs) and usually the arms down to wrist and ankle, essentially a [leotard](#leotard) extended over the limbs. The [lingerie](#lingerie) version of the same cut is a [bodystocking](#bodystocking), and a [catsuit](#catsuit) is made of heavier material.

entries.name: yellow_leotard
entries.description: A yellow [leotard](#leotard), cut high at the hips with the [legs](#legs) left bare. Not a full-leg [yellow_bodysuit](#yellow_bodysuit); [tag](#tag) leotard.

entries.name: athletic_leotard
entries.description: The kind of [leotard](#leotard) worn for [ballet](#ballet), [gymnastics](#gymnastics) or dance, cut with sleeves or firm straps that will not slip during movement. Dance versions are usually flat-coloured and worn with tights, while gymnastics ones are bare-legged and often have a sheen.

entries.name: ribbed_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) knitted with a ribbed pattern of fine vertical lines. Tagged with bodysuit; the pattern is what sets it apart from a [plain](#plain) one.

entries.name: ribbed_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) in ribbed knit with vertical lines, the kind sold in shops as a knit [bodysuit](#bodysuit) worn instead of a [shirt](#shirt). It counts as a leotard here; the bodysuit [tag](#tag) is reserved for garments covering the full limbs.

entries.name: brown_leotard
entries.description: A brown [leotard](#leotard), the one-piece garment covering the [torso](#torso) and finishing at the hips with the [legs](#legs) bare. A [suit](#suit) that carries on down the legs is [brown_bodysuit](#brown_bodysuit).

entries.name: grey_leotard
entries.description: A grey [leotard](#leotard) covering the [torso](#torso) and leaving the [legs](#legs) bare. With the legs covered as [well](#well) the garment is a [grey_bodysuit](#grey_bodysuit).

entries.name: sleeved_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with sleeves of its own, short or long, instead of the usual [sleeveless](#sleeveless) cut.

entries.name: hooded_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight one-piece [suit](#suit) with a [hood](#hood) built into it, as Spider-Gwen wears. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) for how the hood sits.

entries.name: sleeveless_bodysuit
entries.description: A skin-tight [bodysuit](#bodysuit) cut without sleeves, leaving the arms bare from the shoulder. Tag beside bodysuit and [sleeveless](#sleeveless); [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves) may still be worn with it.

entries.name: torn_bodystocking
entries.description: A sheer [bodystocking](#bodystocking) with rips in it.

entries.name: brown_bodysuit
entries.description: A one-piece garment covering the whole body in brown, cut close to the skin. It is not [brown_leotard](#brown_leotard), which leaves the [legs](#legs) bare.

entries.name: catsuit
entries.description: A single garment sheathing the [legs](#legs) and generally the arms too, fastened by a zip and often cut from [latex](#latex) or [leather](#leather). That zip and the tougher material separate it from a [plain](#plain) [unitard](#unitard).

entries.name: blue_jumpsuit
entries.description: A blue one-piece garment joining top and trousers. Mechanics, prisoners and pilots wear it, and it also appears cut as [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: turtleneck_bodysuit
entries.description: A one-piece skin-tight garment whose neckline rises into a rolled high [collar](#collar). The unbroken line from throat to hip is what marks it apart from other bodysuits.

entries.name: leotard_peek
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) glimpsed under other clothing, showing at a neckline, a hem or a gap. Where the layered outfit itself is the point, [leotard_under_clothes](#leotard_under_clothes) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: aqua_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) in aqua, cut high at the hip and leaving the [legs](#legs) bare. Once the garment covers the upper legs as [well](#well) it is an [aqua_bodysuit](#aqua_bodysuit).

entries.name: orange_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) in orange, cut high at the leg and leaving the limbs bare. An orange garment that also sheathes the arms and [legs](#legs) is an [orange_bodysuit](#orange_bodysuit).

entries.name: white_jumpsuit
entries.description: A one-piece garment joining a top and trousers, colored white. Covers work coveralls, [racing](#racing) suits and [fashion](#fashion) pieces alike.

entries.name: latex_leotard
entries.description: A one-piece [leotard](#leotard) cut from glossy rubber, moulded tight over the [torso](#torso). Dominatrix and superheroine designs use it constantly.

entries.name: black_jumpsuit
entries.description: A one-piece garment joining top and trousers, in black. It spans loose work coveralls through to sleek fitted flight suits.

entries.name: taut_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) fitted so tightly that the [fabric](#fabric) lies smooth and even across the chest and hips. Where the [cloth](#cloth) could not actually [cover](#cover) what it covers, the picture is an [impossible_leotard](#impossible_leotard) instead.

entries.name: fishnet_bodysuit
entries.description: A one-piece of open [mesh](#mesh) covering [torso](#torso) and [legs](#legs) together. With nothing worn under it the whole body reads through the netting; a version ending at the hip is a [fishnet_leotard](#fishnet_leotard).

entries.name: fur-trimmed_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) bordered with fur, usually at the neckline, shoulders or leg openings. Common on festive and [winter](#winter) [costume](#costume) designs.

entries.name: green_jumpsuit
entries.description: A green one-piece garment joining top and trousers, ranging from loose work coveralls to a fitted flight [suit](#suit). The body of the suit is green whatever colour its trim takes.

entries.name: singlet
entries.description: A one-piece stretch garment joining [shirt](#shirt) and [shorts](#shorts), cut close to the body in [spandex](#spandex) or nylon. Standard kit for amateur [wrestling](#wrestling) and [weightlifting](#weightlifting).

entries.name: black_unitard
entries.description: A close-fitting black one-piece covering the [torso](#torso) and [legs](#legs) while leaving the [feet](#feet) or lower legs free. A [leotard](#leotard) stops at the hips, which is the difference.

entries.name: collared_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) whose neckline carries a folded-down [collar](#collar) of its own. A [plain](#plain) leotard worn with a separate detached collar is not this.

entries.name: yellow_jumpsuit
entries.description: A yellow one-piece garment joining top and trousers, from baggy work coveralls to a fitted [pilot](#pilot) or [racing](#racing) [suit](#suit). The colour is all the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: red_jumpsuit
entries.description: A one-piece red garment joining top and trousers, usually zipped up the front. Worn by pilots, mechanics, racers and prisoners depending on the cut.

entries.name: print_bodysuit
entries.description: A one-piece skin-tight [suit](#suit) with a design printed across it. The print may be an allover pattern, a [logo](#logo), or a picture spanning the [torso](#torso).

entries.name: print_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with a stylised print across it, most often floral or [animal](#animal) patterning. Frequent on [gymnastics](#gymnastics) and [stage](#stage) outfits.

entries.name: halter_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) whose straps run up around the [neck](#neck) instead of over the shoulders, leaving the upper [back](#back) open. Do not mistake the high neck [strap](#strap) for a [turtleneck](#turtleneck).

entries.name: hooded_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with a [hood](#hood) built onto it, so the head covering and the body-hugging one-piece form a single garment. Ears worked into the hood are a common addition.

entries.name: zipper_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) closed by a [zipper](#zipper) [running](#running) up the front or [back](#back), often left partway open across the chest. Common on [stage](#stage) costumes, [sportswear](#sportswear) and superhero designs alike.

entries.name: gold_leotard
entries.description: A [gold](#gold) one-piece stretch garment covering the [torso](#torso) and [crotch](#crotch) and leaving the [legs](#legs) bare. Gymnasts, dancers and [stage](#stage) performers wear it.

entries.name: off-shoulder_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) whose neckline runs beneath the shoulders, with attached sleeves on the upper arms and the [collarbone](#collarbone) left bare. Where the sleeves are separate pieces, the garment is [strapless](#strapless) and takes [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves) instead.

entries.name: backless_bodysuit
entries.description: A one-piece [bodysuit](#bodysuit) cut away across the [back](#back), leaving the shoulder blades and [spine](#spine) bare while the front stays closed. A halter [neck](#neck) or crossing straps hold up whatever [fabric](#fabric) remains.

entries.name: striped_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) covering the [torso](#torso) and leaving the [legs](#legs) bare, [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies leotard and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: fishnet_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) cut wholly or partly from [mesh](#mesh), ending high on the hip. Once the [thighs](#thighs) are covered as [well](#well) it counts as a [fishnet_bodysuit](#fishnet_bodysuit).

entries.name: maid_leotard
entries.description: A [maid](#maid) [costume](#costume) built on a [leotard](#leotard) instead of a [skirt](#skirt), keeping the [apron](#apron), [cuffs](#cuffs) and [headdress](#headdress) while leaving the hips and [legs](#legs) bare. One of the unconventional maid variants.

entries.name: vertical-striped_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) lengthwise down the body rather than around it. The direction of the stripe is what separates it from the horizontally banded version.

entries.name: collared_bodysuit
entries.description: A one-piece [bodysuit](#bodysuit) finished at the [neck](#neck) with a turned-down [collar](#collar). The collar belongs to the garment, not to a separate band worn over it.

entries.name: asymmetrical_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) cut differently on each side, one sleeve and not the other, mismatched [legs](#legs), or panels that do not [mirror](#mirror). Common on fighting-game and hero designs.

entries.name: grey_jumpsuit
entries.description: A grey one-piece garment joining top and [legs](#legs), from utility coveralls to a fitted flight [suit](#suit). Prison and [laboratory](#laboratory) settings favour it.

entries.name: leather_suit
entries.description: A full outfit of hide covering most of the body, anywhere from padded [motorcycle](#motorcycle) leathers to a sleek one-piece that clings throughout.

entries.name: sleeveless_jumpsuit
entries.description: A one-piece garment joining top and trousers that leaves the shoulders and arms uncovered. The cut may be fitted or loose; what matters is the single continuous body and the absent sleeves.

entries.name: cross-laced_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) with cords or ribbons crossing over part of it, usually over the chest, across the [back](#back) or around the hips. The lacing is decorative as often as it is structural.

entries.name: bodystocking_only
entries.description: A sheer full-body stocking worn with nothing over it. Gloves, detached sleeves and [accessories](#accessories) are allowed; anything covering the [torso](#torso) disqualifies it.

entries.name: striped_bodysuit
