entries.description: Purple [pleated](#pleated) Japanese trousers or a [skirt](#skirt) worn over a [kimono](#kimono), as in [miko](#miko) or [kendo](#kendo) [dress](#dress). Combine with [hakama](#hakama).

entries.name: two-tone_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) made up of exactly two colours, typically [split](#split) by panel, sleeve or hem. Patterned [fabric](#fabric) [carrying](#carrying) several shades falls outside this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: han'eri
entries.description: A decorative band of [cloth](#cloth) laid along the [collar](#collar) of the juban worn under a [kimono](#kimono), showing colour or [embroidery](#embroidery) at the throat. Because it detaches for [washing](#washing), its [fabric](#fabric) and motifs vary widely from one outfit to the next.

entries.name: wa_lolita
entries.description: Lolita [fashion](#fashion) fused with Japanese [dress](#dress): a [yukata](#yukata) or kimono-style top over a lolita [skirt](#skirt), or a [kimono](#kimono) reshaped into a frilly lolita [silhouette](#silhouette). The Chinese-inspired version is [qi_lolita](#qi_lolita); a Japanese-style [maid](#maid) is [wa_maid](#wa_maid).

entries.name: haramaki
entries.description: A wide band of knitted or woven [cloth](#cloth) worn wrapped around the middle to keep the [belly](#belly) warm. It is associated with [old](#old) men, delinquents and anybody [lounging](#lounging) at home in [winter](#winter).

entries.name: midriff_sarashi
entries.description: Sarashi [cloth](#cloth) wound around the [stomach](#stomach), the historical way it was worn by both sexes, often paired with [festival](#festival) [dress](#dress) like [happi](#happi), [hachimaki](#hachimaki) or [fundoshi](#fundoshi). Use only when the wrapped [midriff](#midriff) itself is clearly shown; unwrapped cloth is [undone_sarashi](#undone_sarashi), and covering the chest as [well](#well) calls for [chest_sarashi](#chest_sarashi) too.

entries.name: vertical-striped_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono), [yukata](#yukata) or [furisode](#furisode) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) lengthwise, a very traditional Japanese textile design. Yukata with such stripes count here too.

entries.name: chihaya_(clothing)
entries.description: A sheer white ceremonial overrobe a [shrine](#shrine) maiden puts on over her usual red and white [dress](#dress). It is kept for rituals rather than everyday shrine work.

entries.name: mizu_happi
entries.description: Shinto [festival](#festival) [dress](#dress) worn by the men who carry a yamakasa float: a short [cloth](#cloth) [jacket](#jacket) knotted at the front over a [fundoshi](#fundoshi). It bares most of the body, which is why artists sometimes put women in it as [well](#well).

entries.name: right-over-left_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) closed with the right panel laid over the left, the reverse of ordinary wear. Custom reserves this fold for [dressing](#dressing) the dead, so fiction uses it to mark ghosts and beings tied to [death](#death).

entries.name: blue_haori
entries.description: A blue [haori](#haori), the hip-length Japanese [jacket](#jacket) worn open over a [kimono](#kimono). It hangs loose rather than being tied shut at the front.

entries.name: black_haori
entries.description: The hip-length Japanese [jacket](#jacket) worn open over a [kimono](#kimono), in black. Worn by men and women alike, and common on [samurai](#samurai) and [shrine](#shrine) designs.

entries.name: white_hakama
entries.description: White [hakama](#hakama), the wide [pleated](#pleated) trousers worn over a [kimono](#kimono). This white version belongs to [shrine](#shrine) [dress](#dress), kyudo and formal ceremony.

entries.name: kataginu
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [vest](#vest) whose shoulders [flare](#flare) stiffly outward into [wings](#wings), worn over a [kimono](#kimono) with [hakama](#hakama) as the upper half of a samurai's formal [dress](#dress). It is not a [haori](#haori), nor the [jinbaori](#jinbaori) that goes over armour.

entries.name: obidome
entries.description: A small [brooch](#brooch) slid onto the cord that crosses the front of the [obi](#obi), made of lacquer, [shell](#shell), ceramic or precious metal. It is one of the very few ornaments worn with a [kimono](#kimono), and apprentice [geisha](#geisha) wear an outsized, lavish version.

entries.name: gradient_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) dyed so its colour moves gradually from one [shade](#shade) into another across the [cloth](#cloth), an effect with a long history in Japanese dyeing. Printed patterns and blocks of flat colour do not count.

entries.name: white_haori
entries.description: A white [haori](#haori), the hip-length [jacket](#jacket) worn open over a [kimono](#kimono). It adds a layer without changing the garment underneath.

entries.name: short_yukata
entries.description: A [yukata](#yukata) cut so its hem falls above the knee rather than [reaching](#reaching) the ankle, the [summer](#summer) counterpart of a short [kimono](#kimono). Implies [short_kimono](#short_kimono) and yukata.

entries.name: brown_hakama
entries.description: Hakama in brown, the [pleated](#pleated) wide-legged trousers tied at the waist over a [kimono](#kimono). They are worn for martial arts, [shrine](#shrine) duties and formal [dress](#dress).

entries.name: grey_hakama
entries.description: Grey [hakama](#hakama), the wide [pleated](#pleated) trousers tied at the waist over a [kimono](#kimono). They are standard [dress](#dress) for martial arts and formal traditional occasions.

entries.name: torn_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) cut or ripped open, sleeves and [skirt](#skirt) [hanging](#hanging) in strips. Yukata and [furisode](#furisode) count under it as [well](#well).

entries.name: jinbei_(clothes)
entries.description: A light two-piece Japanese set of a short wrap top and matching [shorts](#shorts), cut from thin cotton or hemp. It is worn at home or to a [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival), and is [cooler](#cooler) and plainer than a [yukata](#yukata).

entries.name: checkered_haori
entries.description: A [haori](#haori) [jacket](#jacket) woven in squares and worn open over a [kimono](#kimono). The bold check reads as Taisho-era [fashion](#fashion) and suits period designs.

entries.name: kosode
entries.description: The short-sleeved [robe](#robe) from which the modern [kimono](#kimono) developed. Its body is cut wider, the [collar](#collar) runs longer, and the narrow sleeves are heavily rounded at the outer edge and [stitched](#stitched) shut down the side.

entries.name: unworn_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) appears in the picture off the body, hung on a rack, [folded](#folded) neatly or slipped from the shoulders onto the [floor](#floor).

entries.name: jinbaori
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [surcoat](#surcoat) worn by ranking [samurai](#samurai) over their armour, cut wide across the [back](#back) and often boldly decorated there. It should not be mistaken for the shoulder-flared [kataginu](#kataginu).

entries.name: tenugui
entries.description: A thin [rectangle](#rectangle) of woven cotton used in Japan as a [towel](#towel), a head wrap or a decorative [cloth](#cloth). Tied round the head or [neck](#neck) at festivals and while [working](#working), or hung up for its printed pattern.

entries.name: shiromuku
entries.description: The bridal [uchikake](#uchikake) worn in unbroken white over the [wedding](#wedding) [kimono](#kimono) at a Shinto ceremony. Newer versions edge the hem and sleeves in red. Implies uchikake.

entries.name: kimono_dress
entries.description: A garment that crosses a [kimono](#kimono) with a western [dress](#dress) — wide sleeves, a crossed front and a [sash](#sash), cut short and shaped like a frock. It is neither a proper kimono nor a [plain](#plain) dress.

entries.name: plaid_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) woven in a checked, tartan-like pattern rather than a traditional print. Taisho-era and modern styling both favour it.

entries.name: red_fundoshi
entries.description: The traditional Japanese [loincloth](#loincloth) in red, a long strip of [cloth](#cloth) wound around the hips and between the [legs](#legs). Red ones appear in [festival](#festival) scenes and shrine-themed designs.

entries.name: chanchanko_(clothes)
entries.description: A padded Japanese [jacket](#jacket) worn over other [clothes](#clothes), told apart from the hanten, dotera and tanzen by having [no](#no) sleeves at all. Children wear them, and a red one traditionally marks a sixtieth [birthday](#birthday).

entries.name: haori_himo
entries.description: The braided cord that holds a [haori](#haori) closed across the chest, usually finished with a soft pom-pom at each end. It is frequently white and [can](#can) be quite ornamental in its own right.

entries.name: shiroshouzoku
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) white [robe](#robe) used in Shinto [ritual](#ritual) and, far more often, as burial [dress](#dress) for the dead, which is why Japanese ghosts are almost always drawn wearing one. Implies [kimono](#kimono).

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) with [ribbon](#ribbon) banding added along the [collar](#collar), sleeve edges or hem. The trim reads as a modern decorative touch rather than traditional [construction](#construction).

entries.name: yellow_haori
entries.description: A yellow [haori](#haori), the hip-length open [jacket](#jacket) worn over a [kimono](#kimono). It hangs loose at the front and is held, if at all, by a short cord across the chest.

entries.name: print_hakama
entries.description: Wide [pleated](#pleated) [hakama](#hakama) trousers or [skirt](#skirt) [carrying](#carrying) a printed design. Usually worn with a [kimono](#kimono) top for festivals and [graduation](#graduation) portraits.

entries.name: karaginu_mo
entries.description: The full formal [dress](#dress) of a Heian court lady: many layered robes finished with a short waist-length [jacket](#jacket) and a [pleated](#pleated) [train](#train) trailing behind. Also called juunihitoe, it is usually drawn in loud, contrasting colours.

entries.name: wet_fundoshi
entries.description: A Japanese [loincloth](#loincloth) soaked through, [clinging](#clinging) and sometimes turning [translucent](#translucent). Festivals, waterfalls and trips to the sea supply the [water](#water).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) given [lace](#lace) edging at the sleeve openings, [collar](#collar) or hem. The trim is a modern decorative twist on the traditional cut.

entries.name: yellow_happi
entries.description: A yellow [happi](#happi), the straight-cut [festival](#festival) [coat](#coat) worn over other [clothes](#clothes) and belted with a [sash](#sash). Common at [summer](#summer) festivals and outside shops.

entries.name: hooded_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) cut or worn with a [hood](#hood), [mixing](#mixing) Japanese [dress](#dress) with a cowled [outline](#outline). Wandering swordsmen and [fantasy](#fantasy) travellers wear it most.

entries.name: skirt_under_kimono
entries.description: A western [skirt](#skirt) worn beneath a [kimono](#kimono), showing at the hem where the wrap opens. A mixed-dress look associated with Taisho-era and modern-fusion outfits.

entries.name: polka_dot_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono), [yukata](#yukata), or [furisode](#furisode) strewn with round [dots](#dots). Beside the usual florals, it reads as [casual](#casual) and modern-leaning.

entries.name: dotera_(clothes)
entries.description: A long padded housecoat cut like a [kimono](#kimono), worn [indoors](#indoors) for warmth and at [hot](#hot) spring inns; also called tanzen. Its hem falls lower than a hanten's, which it is often mistaken for.

entries.name: strapless_kimono
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) reworked to bare the shoulders, [dropping](#dropping) the usual overlapping [collar](#collar) and wide sleeves. A [fashion](#fashion) variation rather than real traditional [dress](#dress).

entries.name: torn_hakama
entries.description: A [hakama](#hakama) [split](#split) or shredded, its pleats cut through.

entries.name: yellow_hakama
entries.description: Yellow [hakama](#hakama), the [pleated](#pleated) Japanese trousers or [skirt](#skirt) worn over a [kimono](#kimono).

entries.name: orange_hakama
entries.description: Orange [hakama](#hakama), the [pleated](#pleated) trousers or divided [skirt](#skirt) worn over a [kimono](#kimono). The upper garment keeps its own colour [tag](#tag).

entries.name: chinese_clothes
entries.description: Any garment of Chinese cut, from historical [hanfu](#hanfu), [changpao](#changpao) and Manchu [dress](#dress) to martial-arts wear, Mao suits and modern [tangzhuang](#tangzhuang). A qipao-style dress takes [china_dress](#china_dress) in addition, while qipao-styled tops and vests take this [tag](#tag) alone.

entries.name: china_dress
entries.description: A close-fitting Chinese [dress](#dress) with a mandarin [collar](#collar), an asymmetric front closure held by [frog](#frog) fasteners, and slits [running](#running) up the sides. Drawn versions often shorten it or cut the slits far higher than the traditional garment. Reserve it for actual dresses; qipao-styled shirts and vests take [chinese_clothes](#chinese_clothes) alone.

entries.name: hanfu
entries.description: Historical [dress](#dress) of the Han Chinese, generally closing in a crossed Y at the [collar](#collar) though rounded collars exist, in styles such as ruqun, [aoqun](#aoqun) and [yuanlingpao](#yuanlingpao). It is easy to mistake for a [kimono](#kimono), so check the hairstyle, headwear and [forehead](#forehead) mark; Manchu [frog](#frog) [buttons](#buttons) and mandarin collars are [chinese_clothes](#chinese_clothes) rather than hanfu.

entries.name: black_hanfu
entries.description: Chinese [hanfu](#hanfu) robes in black, with crossed collars, wide sleeves and a [sash](#sash) at the waist. Often layered over [lighter](#lighter) under-robes.

entries.name: white_hanfu
entries.description: Chinese [hanfu](#hanfu) in white, with crossed collars, long flowing sleeves and a [sash](#sash) at the waist. Favored for immortals, [mourning](#mourning) scenes and wuxia settings.

entries.name: korean_clothes
entries.description: Traditional Korean [dress](#dress) of any period, most often a [hanbok](#hanbok) made up of the short jeogori [jacket](#jacket) with a chima [skirt](#skirt) or baji trousers. Hats such as the gat and the various undergarments count too; add the specific garment where it is known.

entries.name: tangzhuang
entries.description: A Chinese [jacket](#jacket) with a mandarin [collar](#collar) and knotted [buttons](#buttons), descended from a late-Qing garment once reserved for nobility and officials. Worn today as men's formal national [dress](#dress), and by women as [well](#well).

entries.name: hanbok
entries.description: Traditional Korean [dress](#dress) in [strong](#strong) flat colours with clean uninterrupted lines and [no](#no) pockets. Women wear a short bolero-like jeogori [jacket](#jacket) over the high-waisted chima [skirt](#skirt), men a jeogori with roomy baji trousers gathered at the ankle, sometimes topped by a gat [hat](#hat).

entries.name: dudou
entries.description: A traditional Chinese top cut as a diamond of [cloth](#cloth), tied behind the [neck](#neck) and around the waist and leaving the [back](#back) bare. Originally an undergarment, it appears in art as a revealing standalone top.

entries.name: red_hanfu
entries.description: The historical Chinese [robe](#robe) in red, with wide crossed [lapels](#lapels), long flowing sleeves and a [sash](#sash) at the waist. Red is the [wedding](#wedding) and [celebration](#celebration) colour, so it often marks a [bride](#bride) or a festive scene.

entries.name: changpao
entries.description: A long straight men's [robe](#robe) [reaching](#reaching) the ankles, the male counterpart to the qipao worn by women. A short [jacket](#jacket) is often layered over it.

entries.name: qixiong_ruqun
entries.description: Chinese [hanfu](#hanfu) made from a long-sleeved [jacket](#jacket) worn over a [skirt](#skirt) tied high, just under the [armpits](#armpits), most associated with the Tang dynasty. Other ruqun styles tie the skirt at the waist instead, and the outfit is the direct ancestor of the Korean [hanbok](#hanbok).

entries.name: qi_lolita
entries.description: Lolita [fashion](#fashion) styled after Chinese rather than Japanese tradition, drawing on garments like the qipao and [hanfu](#hanfu). Mandarin collars, knotted [frog](#frog) fastenings, tassels, and side slits worn over a [petticoat](#petticoat) mark it out; the Japanese-inspired counterpart is [wa_lolita](#wa_lolita).

entries.name: blue_hanfu
entries.description: Chinese [hanfu](#hanfu) robes in blue, with their wide crossed front and long flowing sleeves. Layers and sashes belong to the outfit and may carry colours of their own.

entries.name: green_hanfu
entries.description: Green [hanfu](#hanfu), the layered traditional Chinese [dress](#dress) with a wrapped front and long wide sleeves. The colour may fall on the outer [robe](#robe), the [skirt](#skirt) or both.

entries.name: duijin_ruqun
entries.description: A [hanfu](#hanfu) set whose [jacket](#jacket) meets in two straight parallel edges down the front and tucks into a long [skirt](#skirt). One of the standard Chinese historical outfits.

entries.name: aoqun
entries.description: A form of Chinese [hanfu](#hanfu) in which the upper garment hangs loose over the [skirt](#skirt) instead of being tucked in. The reverse arrangement, top worn inside the skirt, is ruqun.

entries.name: zhijupao
entries.description: A long Chinese wrap-around [robe](#robe) with a crossing y-shaped [collar](#collar), a [sash](#sash) at the waist and a straight hem, worn informally in antiquity by [people](#people) of any gender. That straight hem is what separates it from the curved-hem qujupao, and together the two styles are known as shenyi.

entries.name: jiaoling_ruqun
entries.description: An upper garment whose front panels [cross](#cross) into a Y at the [neck](#neck), tucked into a long [skirt](#skirt): one of the standard [hanfu](#hanfu) sets. The crossed [collar](#collar) is what tells it from the parallel-collar and chest-high forms.

entries.name: white_hanbok
entries.description: Korean [hanbok](#hanbok) in white, a short [jacket](#jacket) worn over a full high-waisted [skirt](#skirt) or wide trousers. The color carries associations of [mourning](#mourning) as [well](#well) as purity.

entries.name: yuanlingpao
entries.description: A Chinese round-collared [robe](#robe) belonging to the [hanfu](#hanfu) tradition, closing across the chest and belted at the waist. Worn by officials and commoners alike in historical settings.

entries.name: yunjian
entries.description: An [ornate](#ornate) Chinese shoulder [collar](#collar) with a scalloped, cloud-shaped edge, often heavily [patterned](#patterned) and hung with tassels. Traditionally worn over formal or bridal [dress](#dress), especially during the Ming and Qing periods.

entries.name: mamianqun
entries.description: A Chinese wrap [skirt](#skirt) of two overlapping [pleated](#pleated) panels on a waistband, with broad flat pleats front and [back](#back) and finer ones down the sides. Traditionally worn with a matching [jacket](#jacket), though modern outfits set it against everyday tops.

entries.name: futou
entries.description: A black Chinese official's cap with two flat [wings](#wings) projecting from the [back](#back), seen in historical and wuxia settings. The Korean samo is its close relative, worn in white for [mourning](#mourning).

entries.name: daxiushan
entries.description: A Chinese formal [robe](#robe) with enormously wide, draping sleeves, worn over layered inner garments in Han-style [dress](#dress). The sleeve [silhouette](#silhouette) alone identifies it.

entries.name: banbi
entries.description: A short-sleeved Chinese overgarment cut like a [waistcoat](#waistcoat), worn over or under a long-sleeved [robe](#robe) as part of [hanfu](#hanfu) [dress](#dress). Its [collar](#collar) varies, and it fastens at the front with ties or a small metal [clasp](#clasp).

entries.name: tunic
entries.description: A loose, simple garment [falling](#falling) from the shoulders to about knee length, often [sleeveless](#sleeveless) and belted at the waist, in the manner of ancient Greek or Roman [dress](#dress). A common look for [fantasy](#fantasy) adventurers and elves.

entries.name: ainu_clothes
entries.description: Robes of the [indigenous](#indigenous) [people](#people) of Hokkaido and Sakhalin, cut differently from a [kimono](#kimono) and covered in bold appliqued swirling borders. A matching [headband](#headband) and beaded [necklace](#necklace) usually come with them.

entries.name: greco-roman_clothes
entries.description: Dress styled after ancient Greece or Rome: a draped [chiton](#chiton) or [tunic](#tunic), a [peplos](#peplos), a [toga](#toga), [sandals](#sandals) and laurel crowns. An [umbrella](#umbrella) term, so [tag](#tag) the individual pieces as [well](#well).

entries.name: ancient_egyptian_clothes
entries.description: Dress styled after ancient Egypt: [pleated](#pleated) linen wraps, broad [gold](#gold) collars, striped headdresses and [heavy](#heavy) jewellery [carrying](#carrying) [ankh](#ankh), [scarab](#scarab) and serpent motifs. Much of the effect comes from the gold rather than the [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: arabian_clothes
entries.description: Dress based on Arabian and Middle Eastern tradition, real or invented: veils, wide sashes, baggy trousers, [harem](#harem) outfits. Name the individual garments as [well](#well) where they [can](#can) be identified.

entries.name: ancient_greek_clothes
entries.description: Garments of classical Greece or copies of them: the [chiton](#chiton), [peplos](#peplos) and [himation](#himation), often with a laurel [crown](#crown) above. The short [cloak](#cloak) is tagged as a cloak and the footwear as [sandals](#sandals), while later Greek [dress](#dress) belongs to traditional_greek_clothes.

entries.name: german_clothes
entries.description: Dress from Germany or made to evoke German culture, such as a [dirndl](#dirndl) or lederhosen. Tag the specific garment alongside it.

entries.name: dirndl
entries.description: The Alpine folk [dress](#dress) of Bavaria and Austria: a fitted [bodice](#bodice) with a full [skirt](#skirt), a [low-cut](#low-cut) [blouse](#blouse) with puffed sleeves, and an [apron](#apron) tied at the waist. Standard wear for beer-festival scenes, and the side the apron [bow](#bow) sits on traditionally announces marital status.

entries.name: indigenous
entries.description: Native peoples and their traditional [dress](#dress) and ornament, from any part of the world. Feathers, beadwork, woven [cloth](#cloth) and painted skin are the usual markers.

entries.name: native_american
entries.description: A character dressed and styled after the [indigenous](#indigenous) nations of North America. Feathered headdresses, fringed [leather](#leather) and beadwork are the usual markers.

entries.name: toga
entries.description: A loose [sleeveless](#sleeveless) wrap of white [cloth](#cloth) in the ancient Roman style, draped over the body and leaving the right arm free. Add [greco-roman_clothes](#greco-roman_clothes) and [laurel_crown](#laurel_crown) as fitting.

entries.name: ao_dai
entries.description: The Vietnamese national [dress](#dress): a long fitted [tunic](#tunic) slit high at both sides and worn over loose trousers. Often paired with the conical non_la [hat](#hat).

entries.name: indian_clothes
entries.description: Garments of the Indian subcontinent such as the [sari](#sari), salwar kameez, sherwani and dhoti, often in [strong](#strong) colours with [heavy](#heavy) [embroidery](#embroidery). Not to be [confused](#confused) with Native American [dress](#dress).

entries.name: mexico
entries.description: Mexican places, culture and iconography in general - Day of the Dead skulls, Aztec [ruins](#ruins), [street](#street) scenes, [food](#food) and the national colors. Used broadly rather than for one specific detail.

entries.name: chiton
entries.description: The draped Greco-Roman [tunic](#tunic), a loose length of [wool](#wool) [pinned](#pinned) at the shoulders and belted, worn knee-length by men and full-length by women. Not to be [confused](#confused) with chitin, the hard [shell](#shell) of insects.

entries.name: roman_clothes
entries.description: Dress of ancient Rome or garments styled after it: draped togas, tunics, stolas, cloaks [pinned](#pinned) at the shoulder. Easily mistaken for Greek [dress](#dress), since Roman [fashion](#fashion) borrowed and reworked much of it.

entries.name: indian
entries.description: People, [dress](#dress) and settings from India and the wider South Asian region. The native peoples of the Americas are covered by [native_american](#native_american) instead.

entries.name: russian_clothes
entries.description: Traditional Russian [dress](#dress): the sarafan, embroidered blouses, [ushanka](#ushanka) fur hats and [heavy](#heavy) [patterned](#patterned) shawls. It marks a character's origin or a folk-styled [costume](#costume).

entries.name: peplos
entries.description: A draped ancient Greek garment: a [rectangle](#rectangle) of [cloth](#cloth) [pinned](#pinned) at the shoulders and belted, [falling](#falling) in vertical folds with an overfold across the chest. Standard [dress](#dress) for goddesses and classical scenes.

entries.name: himation
entries.description: A large [rectangle](#rectangle) of [cloth](#cloth) draped over one shoulder and wound round the body, the outer wrap of ancient Greek [dress](#dress). It goes over a [tunic](#tunic) with its ends trailing [well](#well) past the waist.

entries.name: white_loincloth
entries.description: A white [cloth](#cloth) [hanging](#hanging) from a [belt](#belt) over the hips, covering the front and sometimes the [back](#back) as [well](#well). Suits [tribal](#tribal), mythological and [fantasy](#fantasy) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: vietnamese_clothes
entries.description: Traditional garments of Vietnam, above all the long split-panel ao dai and its relatives, frequently worn with a conical straw [hat](#hat). Many of the styles trace [back](#back) to the Nguyen court.

entries.name: slavic_clothes
entries.description: Folk [dress](#dress) from Slavic countries, or outfits styled after it: embroidered linen shirts, headscarves, sashes and floral crowns. Where the [costume](#costume) clearly belongs to one nation, the country-specific [tag](#tag) such as [russian_clothes](#russian_clothes) or polish_clothes is the better fit.

entries.name: flamenco_dress
entries.description: The Spanish dancer's [gown](#gown), close through the body and [breaking](#breaking) into tiers of ruffles at hem and sleeve. Usually spotted or in [strong](#strong) red, cut to [swirl](#swirl) when the [skirt](#skirt) is swept up.

entries.name: mongolian_clothes
entries.description: Mongolian [dress](#dress), above all the [deel](#deel): a long [robe](#robe) wrapped across the front and held with a wide [sash](#sash). Usually worn with [boots](#boots) and a brimmed or fur-edged [hat](#hat).

entries.name: sari
entries.description: A long uncut length of [cloth](#cloth) wound about the waist, [pleated](#pleated) at the front and carried up over one shoulder, worn above a [blouse](#blouse) and [petticoat](#petticoat). The loose end [can](#can) be drawn over the head as a covering.

entries.name: mexican_clothes
entries.description: Mexican [dress](#dress) in general: embroidered blouses, sarapes and ponchos, wide-brimmed sombreros and the ornamented [charro](#charro) [suit](#suit).

entries.name: mexican_dress
entries.description: A loose folk [dress](#dress) in the Mexican style, flowers embroidered around a wide gathered neckline above a full, flaring [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: kilt
entries.description: A knee-length wrapped [skirt](#skirt) with deep pleats at the [back](#back), usually woollen tartan and buckled at the side. It belongs to Scottish men's [dress](#dress) and often comes with a sporran and knee [socks](#socks).

entries.name: indonesian_clothes
entries.description: Traditional Indonesian [dress](#dress) such as the kebaya, batik [cloth](#cloth), the songkok cap and wrapped headcloths. Several of these pieces are shared with neighbouring cultures or trace [back](#back) to Javanese and Balinese roots.

entries.name: mayan_clothes
entries.description: Traditional Maya [dress](#dress): woven wraps and tunics in banded geometric patterns, jade ornaments and [tall](#tall) feathered headpieces. Used for Mesoamerican settings and characters.

entries.name: deel
entries.description: A long Mongolian wrapped [coat](#coat) [reaching](#reaching) [well](#well) below the knee, fastened down one side and belted with a [sash](#sash). The side closure recalls a qipao, though a crossed Y-collar is common too.

entries.name: shendyt
entries.description: The wrapped linen [kilt](#kilt) of ancient Egypt, gathered at the waist and [falling](#falling) to about the knee. Worn by pharaohs, gods and commoners alike in Egyptian-themed art.

entries.name: hawaiian_clothes
entries.description: Island resort [dress](#dress): loud floral shirts, [grass](#grass) or [leaf](#leaf) skirts, [flower](#flower) garlands and a blossom worn at the ear. Beach and luau surroundings usually come with it.

entries.name: miao_clothes
entries.description: Dress of the Miao and Hmong peoples: indigo [pleated](#pleated) skirts, dense [embroidery](#embroidery), and [heavy](#heavy) silver [neck](#neck) rings and headpieces.

entries.name: armor
entries.description: Protective gear of metal, [leather](#leather) or hardened material worn into a fight, from a single [breastplate](#breastplate) up to full [plate](#plate). A complete [suit](#suit) is [full_armor](#full_armor); name the individual pieces as [well](#well).

entries.name: shoulder_armor
entries.description: Armor plates fitted over the shoulders, ranging from small caps to large [pauldrons](#pauldrons). Implies [armor](#armor).

entries.name: gauntlets
entries.description: Armoured [gloves](#gloves) or mitts, padded or plated, usually with a cuff that runs partway up the forearm. If it looks like a metal glove it belongs here; [bridal_gauntlets](#bridal_gauntlets) are a separate [fashion](#fashion) piece.

entries.name: pauldrons
entries.description: Plate armour covering the shoulders, generally metal and sometimes [reaching](#reaching) over the armpit, upper chest and [back](#back). Spaulders, the smaller overlapping-plate version, are tagged with this name too.

entries.name: breastplate
entries.description: A solid [plate](#plate), usually metal, guarding the chest and often the upper [torso](#torso), as worn by knights and [fantasy](#fantasy) warriors. Add [armor](#armor); a plate moulded into cups is [boobplate](#boobplate), and a small pad over the sternum is [chest_guard](#chest_guard).

entries.name: tabard
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) or short-sleeved [cloth](#cloth) panel worn over clothing or [armor](#armor), [hanging](#hanging) down the front or front and [back](#back), often bearing a [coat](#coat) of arms or [emblem](#emblem). Purely decorative, unlike a [surcoat](#surcoat), which is meant to [shield](#shield) the wearer from the weather.

entries.name: rigging
entries.description: The ship-part equipment strapped to the backs and limbs of shipgirl characters in settings like Kantai Collection and Azur Lane, [standing](#standing) in for the vessel they personify. Worn like armour rather than carried like a [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: japanese_armor
entries.description: Traditional Japanese armour of the sort [samurai](#samurai) wore: laced lamellar plates, a boxy [cuirass](#cuirass), wide shoulder guards and a kabuto [helmet](#helmet). A [jinbaori](#jinbaori) is often worn over it.

entries.name: vambraces
entries.description: Armoured [cuffs](#cuffs) [protecting](#protecting) the forearm, frequently worn together with [gauntlets](#gauntlets). Tag them when the forearm piece appears on its own without gauntlets covering the hands.

entries.name: armored_boots
entries.description: Metal [boots](#boots) forming the foot and shin of a [suit](#suit) of armour, plated and often jointed at the ankle. Worn by knights, [fantasy](#fantasy) fighters and armoured heroines.

entries.name: armored_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) fitted with combat plating, or a [suit](#suit) of armour shaped into a dress, elegant but built for [fighting](#fighting). Where the plating sits on a [skirt](#skirt) alone, [armored_skirt](#armored_skirt) fits better.

entries.name: knee_pads
entries.description: Padded protection strapped over the [knees](#knees) against impact or for long spells of [kneeling](#kneeling). They are standard on sports kit, work [clothes](#clothes) and tactical outfits.

entries.name: greaves
entries.description: Plates of armour strapped over the shins in [medieval](#medieval) or [fantasy](#fantasy) [harness](#harness). Where the foot is enclosed as [well](#well), [armored_boots](#armored_boots) may be the better [tag](#tag).

entries.name: arm_guards
entries.description: Protective pieces strapped over the [forearms](#forearms), such as bracers or [vambraces](#vambraces). Worn by fighters, archers and armoured characters alike.

entries.name: bikini_armor
entries.description: Fantasy armour cut like a [bikini](#bikini): metal-edged cups and a small bottom piece, with [midriff](#midriff), hips and [legs](#legs) left bare. Pauldrons, [gauntlets](#gauntlets) and a [cape](#cape) usually complete it, and the opposite coverage is reverse_bikini_armor.

entries.name: shoulder_pads
entries.description: Padding built into or worn on the shoulders of a garment, ranging from 1980s [fashion](#fashion) jackets to sports equipment. An armored version instead takes [shoulder_armor](#shoulder_armor).

entries.name: white_robe
entries.description: A loose, flowing white [robe](#robe) such as those worn by priests, mages or angels. Also covers a white [bathrobe](#bathrobe) or ceremonial garment; add robe plus the specific kind when it's known.

entries.name: faulds
entries.description: Bands of [plate](#plate) armour [hanging](#hanging) from the bottom edge of a [breastplate](#breastplate) to [cover](#cover) waist and hips like a steel [skirt](#skirt). Longer pieces [reaching](#reaching) over the [thighs](#thighs) are called [tassets](#tassets).

entries.name: full_armor
entries.description: A complete [suit](#suit) of armour covering head, [torso](#torso), arms and [legs](#legs). It also counts when the set stands empty on a [display](#display) stand, or when the [helmet](#helmet) is carried rather than worn.

entries.name: black_robe
entries.description: A long black [robe](#robe) of the sort worn by mages, clergy or judges, or a [dark](#dark) ceremonial garment. A soft [bathrobe](#bathrobe) belongs with the [sleepwear](#sleepwear) tags rather than here.

entries.name: kote
entries.description: Japanese armoured sleeves built from many small plates sewn onto padded [cloth](#cloth), [reaching](#reaching) from forearm to shoulder or only as far as the elbow. Ones made of black iron [plate](#plate) are [kurokote](#kurokote).

entries.name: black_armor
entries.description: Plate, [mail](#mail) or [fantasy](#fantasy) armour that is largely black, the [signature](#signature) of the [dark](#dark) [knight](#knight) archetype. Add the individual pieces, such as [pauldrons](#pauldrons) or a [breastplate](#breastplate), when they stand out.

entries.name: single_pauldron
entries.description: Shoulder [armor](#armor) worn on one side only, a [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) [warrior](#warrior) designs. Tag alongside [pauldrons](#pauldrons).

entries.name: power_armor
entries.description: Full-body [armor](#armor) with a powered [exoskeleton](#exoskeleton) that boosts the wearer's strength as [well](#well) as [protecting](#protecting) them, in the style of famous sci-fi power suits. A [lighter](#lighter) [suit](#suit) that leaves parts uncovered is [power_suit](#power_suit).

entries.name: red_armor
entries.description: A [suit](#suit) of [armor](#armor), or individual pieces of it, colored red. Combine with the specific part shown.

entries.name: sode
entries.description: The large, rectangular shoulder guards of [samurai](#samurai) [armor](#armor), built from laced iron or [leather](#leather) plates and sometimes [reaching](#reaching) down to the elbow. The Japanese counterpart to [pauldrons](#pauldrons).

entries.name: shoulder_spikes
entries.description: Spikes protruding from one or both shoulders, typical of villain [armor](#armor) and [mecha](#mecha) design. Implies [spikes](#spikes).

entries.name: kurokote
entries.description: Armoured Japanese sleeves whose plates are black iron, which is where the name comes from. They are otherwise built like any other [kote](#kote), laced over a padded [cloth](#cloth) sleeve.

entries.name: bulletproof_vest
entries.description: A [torso](#torso) [vest](#vest) of Kevlar or hard plates worn to stop bullets and fragments, often webbed for pouches and magazines. Soldiers, [police](#police) and tactical characters wear it over their other clothing.

entries.name: blue_armor
entries.description: Armour that reads mostly blue, from lacquered [samurai](#samurai) plates to a [fantasy](#fantasy) knight's [suit](#suit). Individual pieces such as [pauldrons](#pauldrons) or [greaves](#greaves) keep their own tags.

entries.name: gold_armor
entries.description: Armour that reads as [gold](#gold), be it [cast](#cast) from the metal, gilded or simply painted. Ceremonial knights, divine warriors and [ornate](#ornate) machines wear it.

entries.name: white_armor
entries.description: Armor plated or painted white, from a holy knight's [suit](#suit) to a sci-fi hardsuit. Add the specific [armor](#armor) pieces alongside.

entries.name: helm
entries.description: A one-piece [medieval](#medieval) [helmet](#helmet) enclosing the whole head, the classic knight's protection, [heavy](#heavy) and hard to see out of. A helmet with a face [mask](#mask) added on is not the same thing, and a ship's steering [wheel](#wheel) is [ship's_wheel](#ship's_wheel).

entries.name: gorget
entries.description: An armoured [collar](#collar) guarding the throat, sometimes strapped straight onto a [breastplate](#breastplate). It sits between the [helmet](#helmet) and the body armour, and often carries a [crest](#crest) or decorative edge.

entries.name: single_gauntlet
entries.description: An armored gauntlet covers one arm while the other stays unarmored. Common on fighters whose [weapon](#weapon) hand carries the extra protection.

entries.name: crotch_plate
entries.description: A stiff, generally metal panel worn over the [crotch](#crotch) as protection, fixed to clothing or set straight against the skin. A recurring piece on armoured and mechanical designs.

entries.name: blue_robe
entries.description: A long flowing [robe](#robe) in blue, the sort worn by mages, priests and scholars. It reaches at least the [knees](#knees) and hangs loose rather than [following](#following) the body.

entries.name: arm_armor
entries.description: Plating covering the arm: [vambraces](#vambraces) on the forearm, rerebraces above the elbow, couters at the joint. Armoured hands are [gauntlets](#gauntlets) and take their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hooded_robe
entries.description: A long [robe](#robe) with an attached [hood](#hood), worn by monks, mages, cultists and anonymous figures. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) for how it sits.

entries.name: plate_armor
entries.description: Armor built from solid metal plates, from a single [breastplate](#breastplate) to a full knight's [suit](#suit). Mail made of interlocking rings is [chainmail](#chainmail) instead; [tag](#tag) individual pieces like [pauldrons](#pauldrons) or [gauntlets](#gauntlets) when they stand out.

entries.name: chainmail
entries.description: Armour of small metal rings interlocked into a [flexible](#flexible) [mesh](#mesh), made up as a [shirt](#shirt), [hood](#hood), [leggings](#leggings) or [collar](#collar). Japanese kusari counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: leg_armor
entries.description: Plating on the [legs](#legs) that [no](#no) narrower term such as [greaves](#greaves) or [faulds](#faulds) covers. Use it for the catch-all pieces of a leg [harness](#harness).

entries.name: kusazuri
entries.description: The [skirt](#skirt) of [hanging](#hanging) plated panels fixed under the chest piece of [samurai](#samurai) armour, guarding waist and upper [thighs](#thighs) while still allowing movement. It answers to the [faulds](#faulds) and [tassets](#tassets) of European [harness](#harness).

entries.name: armored_gloves
entries.description: Gloves reinforced with metal plates over the [back](#back) of the hand and fingers, [lighter](#lighter) than full [gauntlets](#gauntlets). The [leather](#leather) or [fabric](#fabric) underneath stays visible.

entries.name: shin_guards
entries.description: Protective plates worn over the lower leg from knee to ankle, standard equipment in sports such as football and hockey, and reused as light leg [armor](#armor) in [fantasy](#fantasy) settings.

entries.name: visor_(armor)
entries.description: The hinged front [plate](#plate) of a [helmet](#helmet) that covers the face and [can](#can) be raised, typical of [medieval](#medieval) and [fantasy](#fantasy) knights. The shaded eyeshade of a cap is [visor_cap](#visor_cap).

entries.name: boobplate
entries.description: A [breastplate](#breastplate) moulded with a separate [cup](#cup) over each breast while still covering most of the [torso](#torso). Armour shielding the [breasts](#breasts) alone and leaving the rest of the chest bare is [bikini_armor](#bikini_armor) or a chest [guard](#guard).

entries.name: power_suit
entries.description: An exoskeletal [suit](#suit) that protects the wearer and enhances their abilities without encasing them fully in [armor](#armor). When the body is completely armored, use [power_armor](#power_armor).

entries.name: red_robe
entries.description: A loose, sleeved, full-length [robe](#robe) in red, as worn by mages, priests or nobles. Tagged alongside robe; a [bathrobe](#bathrobe) of the same colour is usually not what is meant.

entries.name: exoskeleton
entries.description: A mechanical frame worn over the body, strapped on or bolted into it, adding armour and strength. Bulky enough versions also read as [mecha](#mecha), while a [shell](#shell) grown by the body is [carapace](#carapace).

entries.name: single_shoulder_pad
entries.description: A padded shoulder piece on one side only, as on a sports uniform or a stylized [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: body_armor
entries.description: Modern protective gear: a bulletproof [vest](#vest), [plate](#plate) carrier, flak [jacket](#jacket) or [bomb](#bomb) [suit](#suit), worn by soldiers, [police](#police), guards and [war](#war) correspondents. Plate and [mail](#mail) of a [medieval](#medieval) or [fantasy](#fantasy) look are [armor](#armor) instead.

entries.name: purple_robe
entries.description: A long purple [robe](#robe) of the [wizard](#wizard), [priest](#priest), or scholar kind, often with wide sleeves. Combine with robe; a [bathrobe](#bathrobe) is a different garment entirely.

entries.name: kabuto_(helmet)
entries.description: The [samurai](#samurai) [helmet](#helmet): a hard metal [bowl](#bowl) over the [skull](#skull) with jointed plates [hanging](#hanging) down to [shield](#shield) the [neck](#neck). Ornate examples carry a [crest](#crest) at the brow and fasten to a face [mask](#mask) rather than a chin [strap](#strap).

entries.name: green_armor
entries.description: Armour that is mostly green, whether steel [plate](#plate), layered scale or a moulded science-fiction [shell](#shell). Only the colour is at [stake](#stake), so the style and period are tagged separately.

entries.name: leather_armor
entries.description: Protective gear cut from hide instead of [plate](#plate) or [mail](#mail), trading coverage for lightness and freedom of movement. Common on rangers, scouts and rogues.

entries.name: green_robe
entries.description: A long, loose green [robe](#robe), anything from a mage's [habit](#habit) to a draped ceremonial overgarment. A green [bathrobe](#bathrobe) counts as [sleepwear](#sleepwear) rather than this.

entries.name: armored_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) fitted with armour plates, or [plate](#plate) cut to a leotard's high-legged shape. A [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) and [mecha](#mecha) character design.

entries.name: surcoat
entries.description: A loose over-garment worn by [medieval](#medieval) knights on top of their [armor](#armor), often [carrying](#carrying) a [coat](#coat) of arms and shielding the metal from [sun](#sun) and [rain](#rain). Similar to a [tabard](#tabard), which is decorative rather than protective.

entries.name: couter
entries.description: The elbow piece of [plate](#plate) armour, a cupped [guard](#guard) over the front and [back](#back) of the joint. Normally part of a full arm [harness](#harness) beside [vambraces](#vambraces) and [pauldrons](#pauldrons).

entries.name: purple_armor
entries.description: Armor whose plates or main body are purple, from a full [suit](#suit) down to a single shoulder [guard](#guard). Combine with [armor](#armor) and the specific piece, such as [breastplate](#breastplate) or [pauldrons](#pauldrons).

entries.name: cuirass
entries.description: Torso armour made of a [breastplate](#breastplate) and a matching backplate strapped together, enclosing chest and [back](#back) in one rigid [shell](#shell). The [core](#core) piece of a full [harness](#harness).

entries.name: spiked_pauldrons
entries.description: Shoulder plates with points growing out of them, often oversized and asymmetrical. A quick way to make [fantasy](#fantasy) [armor](#armor) read as menacing.

entries.name: broken_armor
entries.description: Worn armour that has been cracked, dented or [torn](#torn) open, with plates missing and edges [split](#split). It is nearly always the aftermath of a fight.

entries.name: grey_armor
entries.description: Body armour in grey, [plate](#plate) or segmented, without the bright shine of polished steel. It is the standard issue of soldiers, knights and rank-and-file [fantasy](#fantasy) troops.

entries.name: shoulder_plates
entries.description: Broad, often layered [armor](#armor) panels capping the shoulders, typical of [fantasy](#fantasy) knights and [heavy](#heavy) sci-fi suits, larger and more sculptural than a [plain](#plain) shoulder pad.

entries.name: flak_jacket
entries.description: Soft quilted body armour built to stop [shell](#shell) splinters and [grenade](#grenade) fragments rather than [rifle](#rifle) rounds. Its buttoned or zipped front, [collar](#collar) and many pouches set it apart from a rigid modern [plate](#plate) carrier.

entries.name: armored_bodysuit
entries.description: A close-fitting full-body [suit](#suit) with armour plates fixed over it. Standard [dress](#dress) for pilots, agents and science-fiction soldiers.

entries.name: shoulder_guard
entries.description: A rigid protective [plate](#plate) strapped over the shoulder on its own, frequently the only piece of [armor](#armor) on an otherwise ordinary [cloth](#cloth) outfit.

entries.name: rerebrace
entries.description: The armour [plate](#plate) strapped over the upper arm, between the shoulder defence and the elbow. Appears as a curved metal band above the [couter](#couter) on a full [harness](#harness).

entries.name: yellow_armor
entries.description: Plate, scale or [fantasy](#fantasy) armour coloured yellow or [gold](#gold), whether a full [harness](#harness) or just a few separate pieces. Only the colour is being recorded, not the style of the plating.

entries.name: scale_armor
entries.description: Armour built from a mass of small overlapping plates, each [stitched](#stitched) to a [cloth](#cloth) or [leather](#leather) backing and laid out like [fish](#fish) [scales](#scales). Japanese-style plates perforated and laced into straight ridged rows are lamellar, not this.

entries.name: poleyn
entries.description: The [plate](#plate) knee defence of [medieval](#medieval) armour, a shaped [cup](#cup) strapped over the joint. Often drawn with a fluted or [spiked](#spiked) wing guarding the outer side.

entries.name: brown_robe
entries.description: A long loose [robe](#robe) in brown, worn over whatever else the character has on. Monks, mages and travellers are its usual wearers.

entries.name: sabaton
entries.description: The armoured shoe of a [plate](#plate) [harness](#harness), built from overlapping metal lames across the top of the foot. It is also called a solleret, and shares its name with a metal band that has nothing to do with armour.

entries.name: chest_guard
entries.description: A [plate](#plate) or padded panel covering only the upper chest, of the kind archers and fencers [strap](#strap) on. Fuller [torso](#torso) padding worn by catchers and goalkeepers is a chest protector.

entries.name: spiked_armor
entries.description: Armor with [spikes](#spikes) growing out of its plates, most often at the shoulders, [gauntlets](#gauntlets), and [helm](#helm). Shorthand for a villain or a [heavy](#heavy) [fantasy](#fantasy) fighter.

entries.name: armored_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) made of, or plated with, metal panels [hanging](#hanging) from the waist. Where the whole [dress](#dress) is armoured, [armored_dress](#armored_dress) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: grey_robe
entries.description: A long grey [robe](#robe) [falling](#falling) to the ankles, monastic or magical in flavour. A grey [bathrobe](#bathrobe) counts as [sleepwear](#sleepwear) rather than this.

entries.name: gambeson
entries.description: A thickly quilted [cloth](#cloth) [jacket](#jacket) that served as basic [medieval](#medieval) protection, worn either by itself or as padding under [mail](#mail) or [plate](#plate). Rivets studding the surface mean it is a brigandine rather than this.

entries.name: plackart
entries.description: A [plate](#plate) of armour guarding the lower [belly](#belly), fitted over the bottom edge of a [breastplate](#breastplate) or [cuirass](#cuirass). One of the smaller components of a full plate [harness](#harness).

entries.name: suneate
entries.description: Japanese shin guards from [samurai](#samurai) armour: iron plates or splints backed with [mail](#mail), sewn to [cloth](#cloth) and laced around the lower leg to [cover](#cover) the front of the shin below the knee. Implies [japanese_armor](#japanese_armor).

entries.name: cuisses
entries.description: Plate armour strapped over the [thighs](#thighs), [sitting](#sitting) between the hip [faulds](#faulds) and the knee. Worn as part of a full [suit](#suit) rather than by itself.

entries.name: hip_armor
entries.description: Plates guarding the hips and upper [thighs](#thighs), hung from a [belt](#belt) or from the [skirt](#skirt) of a [cuirass](#cuirass). Historical [plate](#plate) [harness](#harness) and invented [fantasy](#fantasy) armour both use them.

entries.name: barding
entries.description: Armour made for a [horse](#horse) or another mount, plating the head, chest and flanks. Even a lone face [guard](#guard) or chest piece qualifies, and the plates are often worked with [heraldry](#heraldry).

entries.name: dou
entries.description: The chest piece of a [samurai](#samurai) armour set, built up from iron or [leather](#leather) plates with [skirt](#skirt) panels [hanging](#hanging) front and [back](#back). Roughly the Japanese counterpart to a European [cuirass](#cuirass).

entries.name: asymmetrical_armor
entries.description: Armour that differs from one side of the body to the other: a single pauldron, one gauntlet, plating down only one leg. A favourite way to keep an armoured design from looking stiff.

entries.name: ornate_armor
entries.description: Armour covered in elaborate decoration: etched plates, scrollwork, gilded edges and heraldic detail. Favoured by ceremonial and heroic designs.

entries.name: multicolored_armor
entries.description: Armour built up from plates finished in several different colours rather than in one throughout. The colours mark out separate pieces of the [suit](#suit), not just its trim.

entries.name: pink_armor
entries.description: Protective [plate](#plate) or [mail](#mail) in pink, from a full [harness](#harness) down to a single [breastplate](#breastplate) or pauldron. Only the colour sets it apart from any other armour.

entries.name: spiked_gauntlets
entries.description: Armored [gloves](#gloves) with points [running](#running) along the knuckles, wrist, or forearm [plate](#plate), turning the hand itself into a [weapon](#weapon). Worn by knights, brawlers, and dark-fantasy fighters alike.

entries.name: knee_guards
entries.description: Rigid plates or hard caps strapped over the [knees](#knees) as protection. They turn up on armour sets, tactical gear and sports outfits alike.

entries.name: single_sode
entries.description: The broad, laced shoulder [plate](#plate) of Japanese [armor](#armor) worn on one side only. Leaves the opposite shoulder in [cloth](#cloth) or bare.

entries.name: single_vambrace
entries.description: Plate [armor](#armor) covering the forearm of one arm alone. Part of the half-armored look where the other arm stays in sleeve or bare skin.

entries.name: shin_strap
entries.description: A band buckled or wound around the shin, over bare skin, a boot or legwear. Purely decorative on some outfits, part of [armor](#armor) or sports kit on others.

entries.name: yellow_robe
entries.description: A long yellow [robe](#robe) [falling](#falling) loosely from the shoulders, of the kind worn by monks, mages or as a housecoat. Only the colour distinguishes it from any other robe.

entries.name: menpoo
entries.description: A Japanese [armor](#armor) [mask](#mask) guarding the chin, cheeks and [nose](#nose), often molded into a fierce [grimace](#grimace) and hung with a throat [guard](#guard). Part of a samurai's [war](#war) [harness](#harness) rather than modern [kendo](#kendo) gear.

entries.name: armored_legwear
entries.description: Legwear shaped like [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or stockings but built up with plating, [reading](#reading) as hosiery and [greaves](#greaves) at once. Common on [fantasy](#fantasy) and mecha-flavoured designs.

entries.name: unworn_armor
entries.description: Pieces of armour rest in the scene apart from any body, stacked on a stand, propped against a wall or scattered on the ground. Common in [resting](#resting) and after-battle pictures.

entries.name: brown_armor
entries.description: Armour in brown, whether tanned [leather](#leather), painted [plate](#plate) or rusted metal. The colour applies to the armour pieces, not to any [cloth](#cloth) worn beneath them.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_armor
entries.description: Armour edged with fur, most often at the [pauldrons](#pauldrons), [collar](#collar) or waist. It signals a northern, [barbarian](#barbarian) or high-ranking design.

entries.name: chinese_armor
entries.description: Traditional Chinese [battle](#battle) gear: small lamellar or scale plates laced into panels, broad shoulder guards and a [hanging](#hanging) [skirt](#skirt) of [tassets](#tassets). The shape differs sharply by dynasty, and generals get elaborate versions with beast-head [pauldrons](#pauldrons).

entries.name: elbow_spikes
entries.description: Spikes [standing](#standing) out from the elbows, either growing from the body or set into armour worn there. A frequent touch on aggressive character designs.

entries.name: orange_armor
entries.description: Plate, [mail](#mail) or [fantasy](#fantasy) armour finished in orange, whether by [paint](#paint), enamel or the material itself.

entries.name: no_armor
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) who normally wears [plate](#plate) or [mail](#mail) appears in the clothing worn beneath it, the armour set aside. The rest of the outfit is unchanged, so this is not an alternate [costume](#costume).

entries.name: yellow_tunic
entries.description: A yellow [tunic](#tunic), the loose shirt-like garment [reaching](#reaching) to the hip or thigh and often belted. Fantasy and [medieval](#medieval) settings account for many of them.

entries.name: codpiece
entries.description: A [pouch](#pouch) or moulded flap fastened over the [crotch](#crotch) of [hose](#hose), trousers or armour to [cover](#cover) the male genitals. Made in [cloth](#cloth), [leather](#leather) or shaped metal, and standard in Renaissance and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: armored_shoes
entries.description: Shoes or low [boots](#boots) plated in metal, the foot's share of a [suit](#suit) of armour. Worn with [knight](#knight) and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits where [heavy](#heavy) sabatons would be too much.

entries.name: tassets
entries.description: Overlapping [armor](#armor) plates [hanging](#hanging) from a [breastplate](#breastplate) or [faulds](#faulds) to [shield](#shield) the upper [thighs](#thighs), one panel over each leg. They [swing](#swing) as the wearer walks and are a fixture of knightly and [fantasy](#fantasy) [plate](#plate) armor.

entries.name: orange_robe
entries.description: A long loose [robe](#robe) in orange, worn over other [clothes](#clothes) or on its own. Covers monastic, ceremonial and wizardly robes alike.

entries.name: torn_robe
entries.description: A [robe](#robe) visibly ripped, hems shredded and holes through the [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: lamellar_armor
entries.description: Armour built from small pierced rectangular plates of metal, [leather](#leather) or [bone](#bone) laced into overlapping rows. Unlike scale armour the plates hang from each other rather than from a backing hide.

entries.name: rondel
entries.description: A small round armour [plate](#plate) hung to [cover](#cover) a joint left open by a plate [harness](#harness), most often the armpit or the inside of the elbow. Also known as a besagew.

entries.name: hip_gear
entries.description: Equipment mounted at the hips like a [belt](#belt) rig: armour plates, [thrusters](#thrusters), [weapon](#weapon) mounts or [machinery](#machinery) [hanging](#hanging) at either side. Mechanised-girl designs are full of it.

entries.name: knee_spikes
entries.description: Pointed [studs](#studs) or short blades projecting forward from armour at the knee. A [staple](#staple) of aggressive [fantasy](#fantasy) and villain designs.

entries.name: kettle_helm
entries.description: A [medieval](#medieval) [war](#war) [hat](#hat): a shallow iron [bowl](#bowl) with a broad brim [running](#running) all the way round to [shade](#shade) the face and turn blows from above. It was infantry equipment rather than a knight's closed [helmet](#helmet).

entries.name: shikoro
entries.description: The layered [neck](#neck) [guard](#guard) [hanging](#hanging) from the [back](#back) and sides of a Japanese [helmet](#helmet), built from laced plates to [shield](#shield) the [nape](#nape) and throat. Implies [japanese_armor](#japanese_armor).

entries.name: sallet
entries.description: A rounded fifteenth-century European [helmet](#helmet) with a [tail](#tail) flaring [back](#back) over the [neck](#neck). Some have a visor, hinged or forged as one piece with the [bowl](#bowl), and some leave the face open.

entries.name: bevor
entries.description: Plate armour shielding the chin, throat and lower [jaw](#jaw), buckled on beneath a [helmet](#helmet). It is usually paired with a [sallet](#sallet), the two closing the head off between them.

entries.name: armored_animal
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) or beast fitted with armour, such as [barding](#barding) on a [horse](#horse) or plates strapped to a [wolf](#wolf) or [dragon](#dragon), rather than a person in a [suit](#suit). Warhorses and [war](#war) beasts are the usual wearers.

entries.name: armor_under_clothes
entries.description: Plate or [mail](#mail) worn as an inner layer with ordinary clothing pulled over it, so only a [collar](#collar) or an edge betrays the protection. Common on characters who need to look unarmed.

entries.name: boots
entries.description: Hard-wearing footwear enclosing the whole foot and the ankle, sometimes the shin or even the thigh, in [leather](#leather), rubber or metal. Add the [height](#height) and material where they [can](#can) be seen: [knee_boots](#knee_boots), [thigh_boots](#thigh_boots), [ankle_boots](#ankle_boots), [rubber_boots](#rubber_boots).

entries.name: thigh_boots
entries.description: Boots [reaching](#reaching) past the knee to mid-thigh or higher. When stockings show above them, add [thighhighs_under_boots](#thighhighs_under_boots).

entries.name: knee_boots
entries.description: Boots [reaching](#reaching) roughly to the knee. They may stop a little below it but never rise above; taller ones are [thigh_boots](#thigh_boots).

entries.name: high_heel_boots
entries.description: Boots built on a raised heel, at any [height](#height) from the ankle to the thigh. Tag [boots](#boots) and [high_heels](#high_heels) alongside it.

entries.name: lace-up_boots
entries.description: Boots closed with [laces](#laces) criss-crossing up the front, the way [tall](#tall) [sneakers](#sneakers) are. The lacing runs over the instep and often the whole shaft.

entries.name: ankle_boots
entries.description: Short [boots](#boots) ending at or just above the ankle, never [climbing](#climbing) the calf. Taller [cuts](#cuts) are [knee_boots](#knee_boots) or [thigh_boots](#thigh_boots).

entries.name: cross-laced_boots
entries.description: Boots fastened by [laces](#laces) zigzagging between eyelets or hooks up the shaft. Standard on combat and [hiking](#hiking) styles, and a favourite flourish on lolita and [fantasy](#fantasy) designs.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_boots
entries.description: Boots with a band of fur around the top [opening](#opening). Other footwear edged in fur is [fur-trimmed_footwear](#fur-trimmed_footwear), and [boots](#boots) made of [pelt](#pelt) throughout are [fur_boots](#fur_boots).

entries.name: rudder_footwear
entries.description: Footwear built with [ship](#ship) rudders attached, as worn by shipgirl characters in settings like Kantai Collection and Azur Lane. Covers [boots](#boots), [geta](#geta), heels or ordinary [shoes](#shoes) fitted with the rudder detail.

entries.name: rubber_boots
entries.description: Waterproof rubber [boots](#boots), also called wellingtons or galoshes, worn against [rain](#rain), [mud](#mud) or [snow](#snow).

entries.name: roller_skates
entries.description: Boots with wheels on the sole, either four wheels in a [square](#square) or a single inline row. Worn for [skating](#skating) on any hard surface; [ice_skates](#ice_skates) have blades instead.

entries.name: platform_boots
entries.description: Boots built with thick, raised [platform](#platform) [soles](#soles). Common in gothic, [punk](#punk) and [idol](#idol) [fashion](#fashion); [tag](#tag) [boots](#boots) and [platform_footwear](#platform_footwear) alongside them.

entries.name: unworn_boots
entries.description: Boots taken off and left visible in the scene, as at a [doorway](#doorway) or beside a [bed](#bed). Do not use the [tag](#tag) when the [boots](#boots) are not actually shown.

entries.name: fold-over_boots
entries.description: Boots with a cuff at the top turned down over the shaft. Pirate and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits favour them, as do a good many [idol](#idol) character designs.

entries.name: leather_boots
entries.description: Boots of tanned hide, drawn with a dull sheen and visible [stitching](#stitching) or creasing around the ankle.

entries.name: santa_boots
entries.description: Boots worn as part of a Santa Claus look, usually red with white fur trim, though black is possible. Tagged with [boots](#boots) and often [santa_costume](#santa_costume) or [santa_hat](#santa_hat).

entries.name: single_thigh_boot
entries.description: A thigh-high boot worn on one leg while the other is bare or wears a shorter boot. Tag alongside [thigh_boots](#thigh_boots).

entries.name: combat_boots
entries.description: Sturdy [lace-up](#lace-up) [boots](#boots) on a [military](#military) pattern, generally black or brown, worn with uniforms and with [punk](#punk) or tactical outfits.

entries.name: cowboy_boots
entries.description: Leather [riding](#riding) [boots](#boots) with a high shaft, a pointed or rounded toe and [no](#no) lacing. Usually seen with a brimmed [hat](#hat), [chaps](#chaps) and the rest of the Western outfit.

entries.name: belt_boots
entries.description: Boots with one or more buckled straps wrapped around them, [holding](#holding) them up or simply there for looks. A [staple](#staple) of [punk](#punk), gothic and [fantasy](#fantasy) footwear.

entries.name: single_boot
entries.description: A boot worn on one foot only, the other bare or in different footwear. Add [single_shoe](#single_shoe) if the other foot has a shoe on it.

entries.name: fur_boots
entries.description: Boots made of [animal](#animal) fur throughout or lined with it inside, santa [boots](#boots) being the [familiar](#familiar) case. Boots [carrying](#carrying) only a band of fur at the top are [fur-trimmed_boots](#fur-trimmed_boots).

entries.name: latex_boots
entries.description: Boots cut from shiny rubber, tight to the leg with a hard highlight along the curves. They are frequently thigh-length and worn with other rubber pieces.

entries.name: single_knee_boot
entries.description: A boot [reaching](#reaching) the knee worn on one leg, while the other leg is bare or wears footwear of a different [height](#height). Part of the deliberately mismatched [costume](#costume) look.

entries.name: spurs
entries.description: Metal wheels or blunt points strapped to the heels of [riding](#riding) or [cowboy](#cowboy) [boots](#boots) to urge a [horse](#horse) on, worn in pairs and often shown jingling as the wearer walks.

entries.name: spiked_footwear
entries.description: Any shoe or boot with at least one spike sticking out of it, wherever the point sits. An [umbrella](#umbrella) [tag](#tag) spanning [spiked_boots](#spiked_boots) and [spiked_shoes](#spiked_shoes).

entries.name: spiked_boots
entries.description: Boots [carrying](#carrying) [spikes](#spikes) on the shaft, toe, or heel. When the points sit underneath for grip instead, the correct [tag](#tag) is [cleats](#cleats).

entries.name: frilled_boots
entries.description: Boots decorated with ruffled trim, most often around the cuff at the top. Magical girl and lolita footwear reach for them.

entries.name: torn_boots
entries.description: Boots [split](#split) at the [seams](#seams) or worn through, [leather](#leather) [gaping](#gaping) and the sole coming away.

entries.name: zipper_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) fastened with a [zipper](#zipper), typically [running](#running) up the inner side of the shaft or along the [back](#back). Usually finished with a visible pull tab.

entries.name: snow_boots
entries.description: Insulated, water-resistant [boots](#boots) built for [walking](#walking) through [snow](#snow), sometimes with [cleats](#cleats) for grip. Softer and bulkier than rigid ski boots, which they are easily [confused](#confused) with.

entries.name: mechanical_boots
entries.description: Footwear built out of visible [machinery](#machinery), with plating, [joints](#joints) and sometimes powered components, rather than [leather](#leather) or [cloth](#cloth). Common on cyborgs and characters in powered armour.

entries.name: ballet_boots
entries.description: Boots built on a heel so extreme that the foot is [forced](#forced) vertical, [standing](#standing) the wearer permanently on her [toes](#toes) and limiting how she [can](#can) move. They are mostly [bondage](#bondage) gear, though [mecha](#mecha) musume and power-armour designs borrow the [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: clawed_boots
entries.description: Footwear ending in sharp talon-like points at the [toes](#toes), either sculpted into the boot or fitted as metal caps. Standard on monstrous, demonic and [fantasy](#fantasy) armour designs.

entries.name: riding_boots
entries.description: Boots cut for horseback [riding](#riding): usually knee-high, close-fitting in the shaft and set on a low heel. They read as equestrian, [military](#military) or aristocratic [dress](#dress).

entries.name: steel-toe_boots
entries.description: Heavy work [boots](#boots) with a reinforced cap [protecting](#protecting) the [toes](#toes), often visible as a [bulge](#bulge) or a bare metal [plate](#plate) at the front. Thick treaded [soles](#soles) and sturdy [leather](#leather) complete the look. Worn by labourers, soldiers and punk-styled characters.

entries.name: rocket_boots
entries.description: Boots fitted with [thrusters](#thrusters) at the [soles](#soles) or heels, [firing](#firing) to lift the wearer off the ground. A [staple](#staple) of superhero and [science](#science) fiction outfits.

entries.name: shoes
entries.description: The most generic footwear [tag](#tag). Some specific types such as [mary_janes](#mary_janes) imply it while others such as [boots](#boots) do not; state tags [cover](#cover) [unworn_shoes](#unworn_shoes), [shoe_dangle](#shoe_dangle) and putting on or [tying](#tying) footwear.

entries.name: black_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots), [sneakers](#sneakers) or any other footwear in black; the separate colour tags for [shoes](#shoes) and boots fold into this one. Add the kind of footwear as [well](#well), since the colour [tag](#tag) does not name it.

entries.name: high_heels
entries.description: Shoes that lift the heel [well](#well) above the [toes](#toes): stilettos, wedges and platforms all belong here. Any footwear built on a high heel qualifies, [boots](#boots) included.

entries.name: brown_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots), [sandals](#sandals) or any other footwear in brown, frequently [leather](#leather). Add the specific type as [well](#well), such as boots, [loafers](#loafers) or sandals.

entries.name: white_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sneakers](#sneakers) of any style in white. Add the specific footwear type alongside.

entries.name: no_shoes
entries.description: Feet in [socks](#socks), [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or [pantyhose](#pantyhose) with the [shoes](#shoes) off, often [indoors](#indoors) or on a [bed](#bed). Entirely bare [feet](#feet) are [barefoot](#barefoot).

entries.name: sneakers
entries.description: Athletic [shoes](#shoes) worn as everyday footwear, trainers in British usage. Brand tags like converse or nike may accompany them.

entries.name: red_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots), [sandals](#sandals) or any other footwear in red. The [tag](#tag) records the colour alone, so pair it with the specific type such as boots or [high_heels](#high_heels).

entries.name: loafers
entries.description: Flat slip-on [dress](#dress) [shoes](#shoes) with a broad low heel, usually brown or black, worn with [school](#school) uniforms, suits and [casual](#casual) [clothes](#clothes) alike. A [strap](#strap) across an open top makes them [mary_janes](#mary_janes), and soft Japanese indoor school shoes are [uwabaki](#uwabaki).

entries.name: mary_janes
entries.description: Low or flat women's [shoes](#shoes) held on by a single buckled [strap](#strap) over the instep, usually black and [plain](#plain). Common with [school](#school) [dress](#dress) and lolita [fashion](#fashion); [loafers](#loafers) and indoor [uwabaki](#uwabaki) are different shoes.

entries.name: blue_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sneakers](#sneakers) in blue. Tag the kind of footwear separately, since the colour says nothing about the shape.

entries.name: cross-laced_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) laced with cords crossing over one another, either across the instep or spiralling up around the ankle and shin in [gladiator](#gladiator) [fashion](#fashion). Applies regardless of the wearer's [sex](#sex).

entries.name: pink_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots), [sandals](#sandals) or any other footwear in pink. Add the style [tag](#tag) as [well](#well), such as [sneakers](#sneakers), [high_heels](#high_heels) or boots.

entries.name: unworn_shoes
entries.description: Shoes removed but visible, at an entryway or beside the character. Distinct from [no_shoes](#no_shoes), though both tags [can](#can) apply to the same picture.

entries.name: grey_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) coloured grey, whatever the style. Tag the kind of footwear as [well](#well).

entries.name: purple_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots), or [sandals](#sandals) of any style in purple. Combine with the specific kind of footwear, such as boots or [high_heels](#high_heels).

entries.name: platform_footwear
entries.description: Any shoe, boot or sandal with a very thick sole, roughly two inches or more. Tag the specific footwear type as [well](#well), such as [platform_heels](#platform_heels) or [platform_boots](#platform_boots).

entries.name: shoe_soles
entries.description: The underside of a shoe or boot visible in the picture, as when a foot is raised toward the viewer. Tag with the specific footwear type.

entries.name: green_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots), [sneakers](#sneakers) or [sandals](#sandals) coloured green, whatever the style. Tag the kind of footwear as [well](#well) so the shape is recorded too.

entries.name: yellow_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) in yellow. Tag the specific footwear type as [well](#well).

entries.name: single_shoe
entries.description: One shoe is worn while the other foot is bare or socked, whether the shoe was lost or removed. If the missing shoe lies nearby, also [tag](#tag) [unworn_shoes](#unworn_shoes).

entries.name: uwabaki
entries.description: Japanese indoor [shoes](#shoes) worn at [school](#school), in gyms or in offices where [street](#street) shoes are not allowed. Usually white [cloth](#cloth) slip-ons in a mary-jane style with a coloured rubber toe and sole, distinct from the [loafers](#loafers) sometimes worn with a uniform [outdoors](#outdoors).

entries.name: toeless_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) with the toe section cut away so the [toes](#toes) show. Add toes and the footwear type such as boots.

entries.name: high_heel_sandals
entries.description: Open [sandals](#sandals) set on a raised heel, so the foot arches while [toes](#toes) and instep stay bare. Strappy [evening](#evening) and [summer](#summer) pairs are the usual kind.

entries.name: pumps
entries.description: Dressy high heels with a [low-cut](#low-cut) front and [no](#no) straps or fastenings [holding](#holding) them on. Strapped or [platform](#platform) heels take their own tags instead.

entries.name: asymmetrical_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) made unlike each other by design, differing in cut or [construction](#construction) from one foot to the other. Where the difference is only how far up the leg each reaches, use [uneven_footwear](#uneven_footwear); where it is colour or pattern, [mismatched_footwear](#mismatched_footwear).

entries.name: orange_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) of any style in orange. The general [tag](#tag), used where the colour matters more than the exact kind of footwear.

entries.name: stiletto_heels
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) with a very long, thin heel. Tag beside [high_heels](#high_heels) when the heel is clearly needle-thin.

entries.name: strappy_heels
entries.description: High-heeled [shoes](#shoes) or [sandals](#sandals) with straps, ties or ribbons [wrapping](#wrapping) the ankle or calf. The raised heel must be visible; ankle-strapped [flats](#flats) and [mary_janes](#mary_janes) do not count.

entries.name: flats
entries.description: Heelless [shoes](#shoes) with a thin sole, [ballet](#ballet) flats and the like, worn with Chinese [dress](#dress) and with [casual](#casual) outfits.

entries.name: paw_shoes
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) made to look like [animal](#animal) paws, with pads, [claws](#claws) or [fluffy](#fluffy) [toes](#toes), worn with a [costume](#costume) or a kemonomimi outfit. The hand equivalent is [paw_gloves](#paw_gloves).

entries.name: mismatched_footwear
entries.description: The left and right [shoes](#shoes) differ from each other in color or pattern. A difference in length instead is [uneven_footwear](#uneven_footwear).

entries.name: two-tone_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) coloured in exactly two tones, like [saddle](#saddle) [shoes](#shoes) or a classic two-colour sneaker. Add the specific footwear and colour tags as [well](#well).

entries.name: platform_heels
entries.description: High heels whose front sole is also raised on a [platform](#platform) of around two inches, keeping the foot less steeply angled than [plain](#plain) heels. Tag [high_heels](#high_heels) and [platform_footwear](#platform_footwear) alongside them.

entries.name: shoelaces
entries.description: The [laces](#laces) of a shoe shown as a visible detail, whether tied, loose or in the process of being tied. Untied laces may also carry [untied_footwear](#untied_footwear).

entries.name: colored_shoe_soles
entries.description: Outsoles in a colour that stands apart from the rest of the shoe, such as white [soles](#soles) beneath [dark](#dark) uppers. The soles have to be meaningfully visible, and [uwabaki](#uwabaki) are excluded since their two-tone build is standard.

entries.name: ankle_strap
entries.description: A single band fastened round the ankle, normally part of a shoe or sandal. Jewelry worn there is an [anklet](#anklet), and [laces](#laces) winding round it are [ankle_lace-up](#ankle_lace-up).

entries.name: ankle_lace-up
entries.description: Footwear whose [laces](#laces) [cross](#cross) over and wrap round the ankle, sometimes [carrying](#carrying) on up the shin or as far as the knee. A shoe held by one [plain](#plain) band at the ankle is [ankle_strap](#ankle_strap).

entries.name: multicolored_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) of any style finished in several colours rather than one, contrasting panels and [soles](#soles) included. Where the left and right differ from each other, that is a separate [idea](#idea).

entries.name: pointy_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) whose toe extends into a sharp point, sometimes curling up like an elf's or a jester's. Footwear with actual [spikes](#spikes) is a different, related [tag](#tag).

entries.name: ballet_slippers
entries.description: Soft flat [shoes](#shoes) with thin [soles](#soles) worn for [ballet](#ballet), usually tied around the ankle with ribbons. Stiffened pointe shoes, worn to protect the foot en pointe, fall under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: winged_footwear
