entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) fitted with a pair of small [wings](#wings), usually at the heel, in the style of Hermes' [sandals](#sandals). Tag the footwear type and its colour separately.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_footwear
entries.description: Footwear other than [boots](#boots) edged with fur — [slippers](#slippers), [sandals](#sandals), [shoes](#shoes). Boots go to [fur-trimmed_boots](#fur-trimmed_boots), and footwear cut from [pelt](#pelt) is fur_footwear.

entries.name: dress_shoes
entries.description: Smart [leather](#leather) [shoes](#shoes) such as [oxfords](#oxfords) or [loafers](#loafers), worn with suits, uniforms and formal wear. Polished and [plain](#plain) rather than sporty.

entries.name: aqua_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) in a blue-green [shade](#shade). Add the kind of footwear as [well](#well).

entries.name: gold_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) finished in metallic [gold](#gold), with more shine and less brightness than [plain](#plain) [yellow_footwear](#yellow_footwear).

entries.name: two-tone_shoes
entries.description: Shoes in exactly two colours, commonly an upper in one [shade](#shade) with the sole, toe cap or [laces](#laces) in the other. Saddle [shoes](#shoes) and classic [sneakers](#sneakers) are typical cases.

entries.name: high_tops
entries.description: Sneakers whose [collar](#collar) rises above the ankle. Mid-tops that only reach the ankle do not count, and other ankle-high [shoes](#shoes) or [boots](#boots) use their own tags.

entries.name: untied_footwear
entries.description: Laced [shoes](#shoes) or [sneakers](#sneakers) whose [laces](#laces) have been left undone and trailing, [giving](#giving) a [casual](#casual) or careless look.

entries.name: toe_cleavage
entries.description: The line where the [toes](#toes) meet the [low-cut](#low-cut) top edge of a shoe, leaving their base on show. A fit detail of heels and [flats](#flats) rather than of the foot itself.

entries.name: wedge_heels
entries.description: Shoes whose heel and sole form one solid tapering block, so [no](#no) gap opens beneath the [arch](#arch). Espadrilles are the classic [summer](#summer) version.

entries.name: unworn_footwear
entries.description: A vague catch-all for [shoes](#shoes) off the [feet](#feet), better avoided in favour of a specific [tag](#tag). Legwear worn with nothing over it takes [no_shoes](#no_shoes), and a particular pair left [lying](#lying) about takes its own name, such as [unworn_boots](#unworn_boots) or [unworn_sandals](#unworn_sandals).

entries.name: print_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) [carrying](#carrying) a printed design across the upper. Graphic trainers and [patterned](#patterned) [rain](#rain) boots are the usual examples.

entries.name: uneven_footwear
entries.description: The two [shoes](#shoes) or [boots](#boots) being worn differ in [height](#height) or length, for instance a knee-high boot on one leg and an ankle boot on the other. Where the pair differs only in colour or pattern, [mismatched_footwear](#mismatched_footwear) applies instead.

entries.name: unworn_shoe
entries.description: A vague [tag](#tag) better replaced by something more specific: [single_shoe](#single_shoe) fits when a character wears only one shoe, and [unworn_shoes](#unworn_shoes) fits when [shoes](#shoes) are left [lying](#lying) about with nobody in them.

entries.name: glass_slipper
entries.description: A [transparent](#transparent) shoe from the Cinderella story, drawn in practice as a heel rather than a soft slipper. Signals a [ball](#ball), a fairy-tale role, or the moment one is left behind on the [stairs](#stairs).

entries.name: white_sneakers
entries.description: White trainers on a rubber sole, laced or slip-on. They are the default [casual](#casual) shoe for [school](#school) and [street](#street) outfits alike.

entries.name: paw_print_soles
entries.description: Normal [shoes](#shoes) or [boots](#boots) with a paw mark set into the sole, usually one per foot. Footwear moulded into a paw shape with built-in pads is [paw_shoes](#paw_shoes).

entries.name: shiny_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) with a high gloss, as in patent [leather](#leather), [latex](#latex) or polished lacquer, [throwing](#throwing) hard bright highlights.

entries.name: frilled_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [sandals](#sandals) or similar footwear [carrying](#carrying) ruffled trim. When the piece is plainly a boot, reach for the boot-specific [tag](#tag) instead of this general one.

entries.name: oxfords
entries.description: Lace-up [shoes](#shoes) whose eyelet flaps are [stitched](#stitched) underneath the front, [giving](#giving) a closed, neat line that reads as formal. Once [plain](#plain) [leather](#leather) [dress](#dress) shoes, they are now made in suede, patent and canvas for uniforms and [casual](#casual) outfits as [well](#well).

entries.name: silver_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) in a metallic silver tone, whether armored [greaves](#greaves), heels or [sneakers](#sneakers). Usually rendered with sharp specular highlights.

entries.name: cleats
entries.description: Sports [shoes](#shoes) with [studs](#studs) or [spikes](#spikes) set into the sole for grip, worn for football, [baseball](#baseball) or track [running](#running). The projections underneath are the identifying feature.

entries.name: heel-less_heels
entries.description: Shoes that [arch](#arch) the foot as a high heel does but have [no](#no) heel [column](#column) under them, so the wearer appears to balance on nothing. Hoof-styled [shoes](#shoes) are often built this way.

entries.name: striped_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) of any style [carrying](#carrying) a striped pattern.

entries.name: block_heels
entries.description: Heeled [shoes](#shoes) whose heel is a thick [column](#column) rather than a thin spike, [holding](#holding) its width all the way down or even widening. The broad base makes them far steadier than a stiletto.

entries.name: shoe_belt
entries.description: A [strap](#strap) crossing the top of a shoe and fastening at the side, as seen on mary janes and many [sandals](#sandals).

entries.name: spiked_shoes
entries.description: Shoes [carrying](#carrying) [spikes](#spikes) anywhere on them, including the sole, toe, or heel. Can overlap with [pointy_footwear](#pointy_footwear) when the toe itself is drawn to a point.

entries.name: extreme_dangling
entries.description: A shoe hangs off the [toes](#toes) right at the point of [dropping](#dropping), held on by almost nothing. The exaggerated far end of shoe [dangling](#dangling).

entries.name: polished_shoes
entries.description: Leather [shoes](#shoes) buffed to a [mirror](#mirror) finish, [catching](#catching) a hard highlight across the toe. Goes with formal [dress](#dress), uniforms, and [butler](#butler) outfits.

entries.name: pointed_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) whose [toes](#toes) taper to a sharp point, sometimes curling upward at the tip. A [staple](#staple) of [witch](#witch), [jester](#jester) and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits as [well](#well) as of [fashion](#fashion) heels.

entries.name: gradient_footwear
entries.description: Shoes or [boots](#boots) whose colour fades smoothly between two shades instead of [holding](#holding) one flat tone. The change usually climbs from the sole upward.

entries.name: transparent_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) made of clear plastic or vinyl, leaving the foot inside visible. An unusual material [choice](#choice) that stands out against ordinary opaque footwear.

entries.name: argyle_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [slippers](#slippers) whose uppers carry the argyle diamond pattern, usually knitted or printed on canvas. The pattern sits on the upper rather than the sole.

entries.name: hoof_shoes
entries.description: Footwear moulded into the shape of a [horse](#horse) or cloven hoof, usually built without a heel. Pony play accounts for most of them, though they also appear as pure [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: half-soles
entries.description: Slip-on covers used in rhythmic [gymnastics](#gymnastics) and dance that sheathe the front of the foot and leave the heel bare, held on by an ankle [strap](#strap). Also called toe [shoes](#shoes).

entries.name: torn_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) coming apart, with [toes](#toes) or heels showing through the damage.

entries.name: polka_dot_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots), or [sandals](#sandals) [patterned](#patterned) with round [dots](#dots). The [spots](#spots) may run over the whole upper or appear only as a trim.

entries.name: shoe_print
entries.description: The tread pattern a shoe leaves pressed into [snow](#snow), [mud](#mud), [sand](#sand) or [dust](#dust), or stamped across a surface.

entries.name: sandals
entries.description: Open footwear with a sole held on by straps across the foot and ankle. Covers [flip-flops](#flip-flops) and strappy sandals; wooden [geta](#geta) are tagged separately.

entries.name: geta
entries.description: Traditional Japanese wooden [sandals](#sandals) lifted off the ground on two crosswise [teeth](#teeth) and held on by a [fabric](#fabric) [thong](#thong), the single-peg [tengu](#tengu) version included. Okobo stand on one solid [platform](#platform) and are tagged separately.

entries.name: slippers
entries.description: Soft, flat, closed-toe indoor [shoes](#shoes). Seen with [pajamas](#pajamas) at home or as [school](#school) [hallway](#hallway) footwear.

entries.name: zouri
entries.description: Flat Japanese thonged [sandals](#sandals) resembling [flip-flops](#flip-flops), commonly worn with a [kimono](#kimono) or [yukata](#yukata). Platform versions are called [okobo](#okobo), and the wooden slat-soled kind is [geta](#geta).

entries.name: flip-flops
entries.description: Light flat [sandals](#sandals) held on by a Y-shaped [thong](#thong) [running](#running) between the first two [toes](#toes). Casual [beach](#beach) and [summer](#summer) footwear.

entries.name: tengu-geta
entries.description: Wooden [geta](#geta) [sandals](#sandals) raised on a single [tall](#tall) central [tooth](#tooth) rather than the usual pair. Associated with [tengu](#tengu) and [mountain](#mountain) ascetics, and worn by several characters in the Touhou series.

entries.name: okobo
entries.description: Tall Japanese [platform](#platform) [sandals](#sandals) worn by apprentice [geisha](#geisha), most often drawn black-lacquered with red thongs. They are one solid block, unlike the two [teeth](#teeth) of [geta](#geta), and far from flat, unlike [zouri](#zouri).

entries.name: unworn_sandals
entries.description: A pair of [sandals](#sandals) in the picture with nobody wearing them, kicked off at the [beach](#beach) or by a [doorway](#doorway).

entries.name: gladiator_sandals
entries.description: Sandals held on by many straps, often winding up past the ankle. Tag by the [strap](#strap) arrangement even on pairs that stop below the ankle.

entries.name: animal_slippers
entries.description: Slippers shaped as a [creature](#creature), bunny [slippers](#slippers) being the obvious example. Pair them with the [animal](#animal) and with [sleepwear](#sleepwear) where that is what is worn.

entries.name: single_sandal
entries.description: A sandal worn on one foot with the other foot bare. Often shown with the missing sandal [lying](#lying) nearby.

entries.name: waraji
entries.description: Flat [sandals](#sandals) plaited from straw and lashed on with cords that [wind](#wind) up the ankle. Once everyday footwear in Japan, now mostly seen on monks and in period settings.

entries.name: unworn_slippers
entries.description: Slippers [can](#can) be seen in the picture but nobody has them on, usually set neatly by a [bed](#bed), a [doorway](#doorway) or the edge of a [tatami](#tatami) [mat](#mat).

entries.name: bunny_slippers
entries.description: Plush indoor [slippers](#slippers) moulded into a rabbit's face and ears, most often in pink. The archetypal [animal](#animal) slipper.

entries.name: sports_sandals
entries.description: Rugged [strap](#strap) [sandals](#sandals) built for [hiking](#hiking) and [water](#water) sports, with a chunky sole and wide straps often secured by velcro. Mostly open-toed, though closed-toe versions exist.

entries.name: cross-laced_sandals
entries.description: Sandals held on by straps that [cross](#cross) the foot and [wind](#wind) up around the ankle or calf before being tied off. The [gladiator](#gladiator) style is the obvious example.

entries.name: cat_slippers
entries.description: House [slippers](#slippers) built to look like cats, ears [standing](#standing) up and a face across each toe. They mark an at-home indoor scene.

entries.name: jika-tabi
entries.description: Split-toe [boots](#boots) with a rubber sole, built to be worn straight onto the ground instead of inside [sandals](#sandals). Builders, gardeners and ninja-styled outfits all wear them.

entries.name: thighhighs
entries.description: Stockings that run from the foot up to the thigh, held by an elastic band or garter straps. Pantyhose reach the waist instead, and [over-kneehighs](#over-kneehighs) stop just above the knee.

entries.name: black_thighhighs
entries.description: Stockings in black stopping somewhere on the thigh instead of continuing to the waist. Legwear joined at the waist is [black_pantyhose](#black_pantyhose).

entries.name: white_thighhighs
entries.description: Legwear ending above the knee in white, a classic pairing with skirts, [maid](#maid) outfits, and [nurse](#nurse) costumes. Tag [thighhighs](#thighhighs) alongside it; legwear that stops at the knee is [white_socks](#white_socks) instead.

entries.name: garter_straps
entries.description: The straps [running](#running) down from a waist [belt](#belt) or thigh [strap](#strap) to grip the top of [thighhighs](#thighhighs). Use this when the straps show but the belt does not, and [garter_belt](#garter_belt) when both are in view.

entries.name: single_thighhigh
entries.description: A thigh-high stocking worn on one leg only, the other bare. A very common asymmetric legwear design; [tag](#tag) with [thighhighs](#thighhighs).

entries.name: striped_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs or over-the-knee [socks](#socks) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes) and [thighhighs](#thighhighs).

entries.name: asymmetrical_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [socks](#socks) or tights that differ from leg to leg by design, so that each foot is dressed unlike the other. A length difference alone is [uneven_legwear](#uneven_legwear), a colour or pattern difference [mismatched_legwear](#mismatched_legwear), and trousers with a single leg are [single_pantsleg](#single_pantsleg).

entries.name: toeless_legwear
entries.description: Socks or stockings that [cover](#cover) the foot but leave the [toes](#toes) bare. If the whole foot is uncovered, use [leggings](#leggings) instead.

entries.name: brown_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs or over-the-knee stockings in brown, ending above the knee and held there by elastic or garters.

entries.name: purple_thighhighs
entries.description: Purple stockings that stop at the thigh or just over the knee. Combine with [thighhighs](#thighhighs); tights [reaching](#reaching) the waist are [purple_pantyhose](#purple_pantyhose).

entries.name: blue_thighhighs
entries.description: Blue stockings ending somewhere on the thigh, over-the-knee versions included. Hosiery continuing to the waist is [blue_pantyhose](#blue_pantyhose).

entries.name: red_thighhighs
entries.description: Red [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or over-the-knee [socks](#socks), ending on the thigh. Legwear stopping at or below the knee is [red_socks](#red_socks).

entries.name: fishnet_thighhighs
entries.description: Mesh stockings ending on the thigh, over-the-knee styles included. A [staple](#staple) of showgirl, [punk](#punk) and gothic looks.

entries.name: torn_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs or [over-kneehighs](#over-kneehighs) with rips, runs or holes [torn](#torn) into the [fabric](#fabric). A common way to show wear, a fight, or a deliberately dishevelled look.

entries.name: mismatched_legwear
entries.description: Socks or stockings that differ in color or pattern between the two [legs](#legs). A difference in length instead is [uneven_legwear](#uneven_legwear).

entries.name: uneven_legwear
entries.description: Legwear that does not match on the two [legs](#legs), such as one thighhigh paired with a bare leg or a kneehigh. Differences of color or pattern rather than length belong under mismatched legwear instead.

entries.name: pink_thighhighs
entries.description: Pink [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or over-the-knee stockings, ending on the upper leg. Shorter legwear is [pink_socks](#pink_socks) and hosiery joined at the waist is [pink_pantyhose](#pink_pantyhose).

entries.name: stirrup_legwear
entries.description: Thighhighs, [socks](#socks) or [pantyhose](#pantyhose) with a [strap](#strap) under the [arch](#arch) that leaves both heel and [toes](#toes) bare. A type of [toeless_legwear](#toeless_legwear).

entries.name: print_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs decorated with a distinctive repeating motif such as hearts, stars, or an [animal](#animal) print. Plain striped or single-colour legwear belongs under its own [tag](#tag) instead; combine with the specific pattern tag when one exists.

entries.name: grey_thighhighs
entries.description: Grey [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or over-the-knee [socks](#socks) ending high on the thigh. Legwear stopping below the knee is [grey_socks](#grey_socks).

entries.name: vertical-striped_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-high stockings with stripes [running](#running) up the leg, a common look on pop-idol and [witch](#witch) outfits. Horizontal rings are [striped_thighhighs](#striped_thighhighs) without this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: frilled_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs whose upper band is gathered into ruffles. A ruffled band worn on bare skin is a bridal garter, and legwear edged in flat [lace](#lace) is lace-trimmed rather than frilled.

entries.name: over-kneehighs
entries.description: Legwear that ends a short way above the knee, [sitting](#sitting) lower than ordinary [thighhighs](#thighhighs) and leaving more of the thigh bare. Judge it by how far the top rises above the knee, not by the size of the gap up to the [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: thighhighs_under_boots
entries.description: Thighhigh stockings worn beneath [boots](#boots), with the top of the stocking showing above the boot line.

entries.name: cow_print_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-high stockings printed in black-and-white [cow](#cow) patches, completing the cow-themed set with the matching [bikini](#bikini) and [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: green_thighhighs
entries.description: Green [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or over-the-knee [socks](#socks) ending high on the thigh. Legwear stopping below the knee is [green_socks](#green_socks).

entries.name: black_garter_straps
entries.description: Black straps [running](#running) from a [belt](#belt) or waistband down to grip stockings or [thighhighs](#thighhighs). They usually run in pairs down each thigh and show below a short hem.

entries.name: american_flag_legwear
entries.description: Socks, [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or [pantyhose](#pantyhose) printed with the stars and stripes, stars at the top and [bars](#bars) down the leg. The print is what the [tag](#tag) names, whatever the length.

entries.name: legwear_garter
entries.description: A band round the leg with straps clipping onto [socks](#socks) or [thighhighs](#thighhighs) to hold them up, also called sock [suspenders](#suspenders). A waist version is [garter_belt](#garter_belt), an unattached [plain](#plain) band is [thigh_strap](#thigh_strap), a lacy one [bridal_garter](#bridal_garter), and the straps alone are [garter_straps](#garter_straps).

entries.name: multicolored_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs worked in two or more distinct colours. Both [legs](#legs) have to share the same design — where the two differ, the pair is mismatched legwear instead.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs finished with a [ribbon](#ribbon) trim around the top hem.

entries.name: bow_legwear
entries.description: Socks, stockings or [thighhighs](#thighhighs) decorated with a [bow](#bow), most often at the top band or at the [back](#back) of the ankle. Name the kind of legwear as [well](#well).

entries.name: horizontal-striped_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs banded with stripes [running](#running) around the leg. Stripes running lengthwise belong to [vertical-striped_thighhighs](#vertical-striped_thighhighs) instead.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs with a [lace](#lace) band worked around the top. When the stocking is mostly or wholly lace, [lace_thighhighs](#lace_thighhighs) applies instead.

entries.name: seamed_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [pantyhose](#pantyhose), [thighhighs](#thighhighs), or similar legwear with a visible seam line [running](#running) up the leg, not a printed stripe. Prefer the more specific back-seamed, front-seamed, or side-seamed [tag](#tag) over this [umbrella](#umbrella) term.

entries.name: yellow_thighhighs
entries.description: Above-the-knee legwear in yellow. Tag [thighhighs](#thighhighs) as [well](#well).

entries.name: ribbed_legwear
entries.description: Socks, [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or [pantyhose](#pantyhose) worked in a ribbed pattern of vertical lines. Add the specific legwear type; [ribbed_socks](#ribbed_socks) and [ribbed_sweater](#ribbed_sweater) are sibling tags for other garments.

entries.name: white_garter_straps
entries.description: White straps [running](#running) from a garter [belt](#belt) down to hold up stockings, a common bridal and [maid](#maid) detail.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_legwear
entries.description: Socks, [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or other legwear with a band of fur at the top. Legwear made of [pelt](#pelt) throughout uses its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: missing_legwear
entries.description: A character whose usual outfit includes [socks](#socks), stockings or tights instead appears with bare [legs](#legs).

entries.name: orange_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs or [over-kneehighs](#over-kneehighs) in orange, ending somewhere on the thigh. The waist-high version is [orange_pantyhose](#orange_pantyhose).

entries.name: two-tone_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-high legwear with exactly two basic colours, for example a black stocking with a white band. Add the colour tags too.

entries.name: animal_ear_legwear
entries.description: Legwear, usually [thighhighs](#thighhighs), whose upper band carries a creature's face and ears, so a small [animal](#animal) seems to peer over each thigh. Tag the legwear type alongside it.

entries.name: gradient_legwear
entries.description: Socks, [thighhighs](#thighhighs), [pantyhose](#pantyhose) or [leggings](#leggings) whose colour fades from one tone into another along the leg. Tag the specific kind of legwear as [well](#well).

entries.name: single_garter_strap
entries.description: A garter [strap](#strap) holds up legwear on one leg only, often beside a [thigh_strap](#thigh_strap). Like [garter_straps](#garter_straps) it is not used when a garter [belt](#belt) is visible.

entries.name: thighhighs_over_pantyhose
entries.description: Thighhigh stockings worn on top of [pantyhose](#pantyhose), so both layers show on the [legs](#legs) at once.

entries.name: argyle_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs [carrying](#carrying) the argyle diamond pattern up the leg. Knitted ones are usual, though the pattern also appears printed on sheer [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: hiphighs
entries.description: Stockings drawn all the way up to the hip, so the top band sits at the hip [bone](#bone) rather than mid-thigh. They run longer than [thighhighs](#thighhighs) and are often held up by straps.

entries.name: two-tone_legwear
entries.description: Socks, stockings or [pantyhose](#pantyhose) in exactly two colours. Add the specific legwear item and the colour tags.

entries.name: cat_ear_legwear
entries.description: Thighhighs or [socks](#socks) whose upper band is styled with [cat](#cat) ears or a cat's face. The feline case of animal-eared legwear.

entries.name: polka_dot_legwear
entries.description: Socks, [thighhighs](#thighhighs), or [pantyhose](#pantyhose) printed with round [dots](#dots). Tag the specific legwear type and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) alongside it.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs finished with a band of fur around the upper edge, where the legwear meets bare thigh. A [winter](#winter) and Christmas [costume](#costume) [staple](#staple).

entries.name: bridal_legwear
entries.description: Stockings or [thighhighs](#thighhighs) cut to bare the heel and [toes](#toes), finishing in a loop around one toe, the leg counterpart of [bridal_gauntlets](#bridal_gauntlets). Some versions run the [fabric](#fabric) between two toes instead of ending in a [ring](#ring).

entries.name: cross-laced_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or other legwear laced with crossing cords or ribbons, commonly [running](#running) up the outside or the [back](#back) of the leg. One of the [cross-laced_clothes](#cross-laced_clothes) [family](#family).

entries.name: ribbed_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-length stockings knitted with vertical ridges rather than a flat weave. The ribbing reads as thicker and more [casual](#casual) than sheer [thighhighs](#thighhighs).

entries.name: aqua_thighhighs
entries.description: Stockings in blue-green [reaching](#reaching) up the thigh, over-knee lengths included. Shorter legwear in the same [shade](#shade) is [aqua_socks](#aqua_socks).

entries.name: detached_leggings
entries.description: Leg coverings that stop at the ankle and leave the foot bare, the lower-body answer to detached sleeves. Thighhighs by [contrast](#contrast) enclose the foot.

entries.name: stirrup_footwear
entries.description: Legwear held in place by a band passing under the [arch](#arch) of the foot, leaving heel and [toes](#toes) uncovered. That [strap](#strap) beneath the sole is the identifying detail.

entries.name: latex_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-high stockings of [latex](#latex), or of any material given the same [mirror](#mirror) shine. The gloss [running](#running) up the leg is what identifies them.

entries.name: mismatched_thighhighs
entries.description: A pair of thigh-high stockings that differ from each other in color, pattern, or how far up the leg they reach.

entries.name: unworn_thighhighs
entries.description: Thighhighs appear in the picture off the [legs](#legs), rolled down beside the wearer, draped over furniture or held in a hand.

entries.name: checkered_legwear
entries.description: Thighhighs, [socks](#socks) or tights printed in squares [running](#running) around the leg. Harlequin diamonds are a different pattern and belong elsewhere.

entries.name: single_legwear_garter
entries.description: One decorative band worn over a stocking on a single leg. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a lone garter [strap](#strap), a thigh strap, or a bride's garter.

entries.name: side-seamed_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, tights or a [bodysuit](#bodysuit) [carrying](#carrying) a thin seam line [running](#running) vertically up the outside of the leg. Different from printed vertical stripes, which are part of the pattern rather than the garment's [construction](#construction).

entries.name: loose_thighhigh
entries.description: One of a pair of [thighhighs](#thighhighs) has slipped or been rolled down the leg while the other stays up, by [accident](#accident) or as a deliberate quirk. Do not confuse it with [loose_socks](#loose_socks), which are a garment in their own right.

entries.name: unworn_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [socks](#socks) or tights are visible in the picture without being on anyone's [legs](#legs). The more specific [tag](#tag) applies when the type is clear, such as [unworn_thighhighs](#unworn_thighhighs) or [unworn_pantyhose](#unworn_pantyhose).

entries.name: frilled_garter
entries.description: A ruffled band worn around the bare thigh purely for decoration, [holding](#holding) nothing up. Garter straps, by [contrast](#contrast), actually fasten to legwear and take their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: lace_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-high stockings knitted entirely from [lace](#lace). When only the thigh band carries lace, the lace-trimmed spelling applies.

entries.name: red_garter_straps
entries.description: The red suspender straps [running](#running) from a [belt](#belt) at the hips down to the tops of stockings. Covers the straps themselves rather than the belt they hang from.

entries.name: toe_seam
entries.description: A [stitched](#stitched) line visible across the toe end of [socks](#socks), tights or [thighhighs](#thighhighs), a small [realistic](#realistic) touch on drawn legwear.

entries.name: single_over-kneehigh
entries.description: One stocking pulled above the knee while the other leg is bare or wears something shorter. The over-the-knee counterpart of a single thighhigh.

entries.name: layered_legwear
entries.description: Two or more pieces of legwear stacked on the same [legs](#legs), such as [thighhighs](#thighhighs) over tights or [socks](#socks) pulled up over stockings. Leg warmers over socks count too.

entries.name: wet_legwear
entries.description: Socks, stockings or tights soaked with [water](#water), gone darker and sticking to the leg. Puddles, [rain](#rain) and the sea are the common sources.

entries.name: purple_garter_straps
entries.description: Purple elastic straps [running](#running) from a [belt](#belt) at the hips down to the top of a stocking. They may actually hold the legwear up, or serve a purely decorative role.

entries.name: o-ring_legwear
entries.description: Stockings or [thighhighs](#thighhighs) that hang from a [ring](#ring) or carry one as trim. Keep it apart from [o-ring_thigh_strap](#o-ring_thigh_strap), which is a separate band worn against bare skin.

entries.name: wet_thighhighs
entries.description: Over-the-knee stockings soaked with [water](#water), [clinging](#clinging) tighter and turning several shades darker. Usually paired with [rain](#rain) or a dip in water.

entries.name: rabbit_ear_legwear
entries.description: Legwear, most often [thighhighs](#thighhighs), with a [rabbit](#rabbit) design worked into the band at the top. One member of the wider [animal](#animal) ear legwear [family](#family).

entries.name: pink_garter_straps
entries.description: Pink straps [running](#running) from a garter [belt](#belt) or [corset](#corset) down to the top of a stocking to hold it up. The straps themselves are tagged, not the belt they hang from.

entries.name: blue_garter_straps
entries.description: Blue elastic straps [running](#running) from a [belt](#belt) or [corset](#corset) down to the tops of stockings to hold them up. Only the straps are blue; the legwear itself may be any colour.

entries.name: thighhigh_gaiters
entries.description: Fitted leg coverings [reaching](#reaching) up to the thigh, cut like sports [gaiters](#gaiters) or spats rather than knitted stockings. Uniform and combat-styled designs favour them.

entries.name: pinstripe_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-high stockings [patterned](#patterned) with narrow parallel lines, usually [running](#running) the length of the leg. The stripes are the whole of the difference.

entries.name: polka_dot_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-length stockings [patterned](#patterned) with round [dots](#dots). The [spots](#spots) run over the leg itself rather than [sitting](#sitting) only on the band.

entries.name: lace-up_thighhighs
entries.description: Thigh-high stockings fastened with cord drawn through eyelets, most often up the [back](#back) of the leg. The visible lacing is what sets them apart.

entries.name: aran_legwear
entries.description: Legwear knitted with the raised [cable](#cable) texture of an Aran [sweater](#sweater). Usually drawn as half of a matching knit set alongside a [virgin_killer_sweater](#virgin_killer_sweater).

entries.name: white_garter
entries.description: A white band worn snug around the thigh, either purely decorative or [holding](#holding) a stocking in place. Bridal outfits use it more than anything else.

entries.name: brown_garter_straps
entries.description: Brown straps [running](#running) from a garter [belt](#belt) down to the tops of the stockings. The legwear they hold up may be any colour at all.

entries.name: grey_garter_straps
entries.description: Grey straps joining a garter [belt](#belt) to the tops of the stockings. The stockings themselves may be any colour.

entries.name: green_garter_straps
entries.description: Green straps [running](#running) from a garter [belt](#belt) down to the tops of the stockings. The legwear they hold up may be any colour at all.

entries.name: yellow_garter_straps
entries.description: Yellow straps [running](#running) from a garter [belt](#belt) down to the tops of stockings.

entries.name: orange_garter_straps
entries.description: Orange straps [running](#running) from a garter [belt](#belt) down to the tops of the stockings.

entries.name: pantyhose
entries.description: Sheer or skintight hosiery worn from the waist all the way down over the [feet](#feet), tights included. Thighhighs stop on the thigh and [leggings](#leggings) leave the feet bare; add colour and pattern tags as they apply.

entries.name: black_pantyhose
entries.description: Legwear in black [running](#running) from the waist all the way down over the [feet](#feet), sheer or fully opaque. Shading blurs the line with grey and brown [pantyhose](#pantyhose), so go by whichever colour reads strongest.

entries.name: white_pantyhose
entries.description: Sheer or opaque hosiery covering the [legs](#legs) and hips in white. Distinct from [white_thighhighs](#white_thighhighs), which stop at the thigh; a garment [reaching](#reaching) the waist counts as [pantyhose](#pantyhose).

entries.name: brown_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose in a brown [shade](#shade), from sheer [nude](#nude) tones to [dark](#dark) [coffee](#coffee). The boundary with [black_pantyhose](#black_pantyhose) and [grey_pantyhose](#grey_pantyhose) is fuzzy, so expect the three to overlap.

entries.name: thighband_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose printed with a band around each thigh so they resemble [thighhighs](#thighhighs) from a distance.

entries.name: torn_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose with holes or ladders in them.

entries.name: fishnet_pantyhose
entries.description: Mesh hosiery covering [legs](#legs) and hips in one piece, most often in black. The open diamond weave shows skin all the way up.

entries.name: leggings
entries.description: Close-fitting leg coverings that stop at the ankle, like [pantyhose](#pantyhose) without [feet](#feet). Coverage over the sole alone is [stirrup_legwear](#stirrup_legwear), and a pair ending at the thigh is [detached_leggings](#detached_leggings).

entries.name: pantyhose_under_shorts
entries.description: Pantyhose worn as a layer under [shorts](#shorts), so the [legs](#legs) stay covered while the shorts sit on top. A common cold-weather and [fashion](#fashion) pairing; [tag](#tag) [pantyhose](#pantyhose) as [well](#well).

entries.name: striped_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [pantyhose](#pantyhose) and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: single_leg_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose that sheathes one leg only, the other leg bare or wearing a different piece such as a [single_thighhigh](#single_thighhigh). A deliberate asymmetric design.

entries.name: grey_pantyhose
entries.description: Grey [pantyhose](#pantyhose) covering the [legs](#legs) from waist to toe. Sheer hosiery sits awkwardly between black, brown and grey, so expect overlap with those tags.

entries.name: print_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose printed with [shapes](#shapes) or images such as hearts, stars or [animal](#animal) prints, as opposed to [plain](#plain) or fishnet. Tag [pantyhose](#pantyhose) alongside.

entries.name: purple_pantyhose
entries.description: Purple sheer or opaque tights covering the [legs](#legs) up to the waist. Combine with [pantyhose](#pantyhose); stockings stopping at the thigh are [purple_thighhighs](#purple_thighhighs) instead.

entries.name: black_leggings
entries.description: Leggings in black, the opaque stretch trousers worn under skirts or [shorts](#shorts) or on their own. Sheer ones are [black_pantyhose](#black_pantyhose).

entries.name: blue_pantyhose
entries.description: Sheer or opaque hosiery in blue [running](#running) from the waist over both [legs](#legs) and [feet](#feet) in one piece. Where the legwear stops on the thigh it is [blue_thighhighs](#blue_thighhighs).

entries.name: no_legwear
entries.description: Bare [legs](#legs) on a character whose standard outfit includes [pantyhose](#pantyhose) or [thighhighs](#thighhighs). It does not apply to non-canon outfits, swimsuits or underwear-only scenes.

entries.name: red_pantyhose
entries.description: Red [pantyhose](#pantyhose), the sheer or opaque [hose](#hose) that runs from [toes](#toes) to waist. Legwear that stops at the thigh is [red_thighhighs](#red_thighhighs), not this.

entries.name: vertical-striped_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose with stripes [running](#running) lengthwise along the [legs](#legs). Horizontal bands are [striped_pantyhose](#striped_pantyhose) alone.

entries.name: pink_pantyhose
entries.description: Pink [pantyhose](#pantyhose), the hosiery covering both [legs](#legs) and joining at the waist, sheer or opaque. Separate stockings ending at the thigh are [pink_thighhighs](#pink_thighhighs).

entries.name: gusset
entries.description: The [inset](#inset) panel reinforcing the [crotch](#crotch) of [pantyhose](#pantyhose) or [leggings](#leggings), visible when the crotch area is shown.

entries.name: patterned_legwear
entries.description: Socks, stockings or tights [carrying](#carrying) a repeated design over the leg rather than one flat colour: [dots](#dots), stripes, small motifs or worked [lace](#lace) figures.

entries.name: orange_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose in orange covering the [legs](#legs) up to the waist. Separate stockings ending on the thigh are [orange_thighhighs](#orange_thighhighs).

entries.name: argyle_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose [patterned](#patterned) with argyle diamonds along the [legs](#legs), knitted in or printed on sheer [fabric](#fabric). The diamonds stretch and distort over the shape of the leg.

entries.name: back-seamed_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [thighhighs](#thighhighs), [pantyhose](#pantyhose) or a [bodysuit](#bodysuit) with a single seam [running](#running) straight up the [back](#back) of each leg. The line is [stitching](#stitching) in the [fabric](#fabric), not a printed stripe.

entries.name: shiny_legwear
entries.description: Legwear with a visible glossy sheen, typical of nylon or [latex](#latex) stockings. Implies [shiny_clothes](#shiny_clothes).

entries.name: green_pantyhose
entries.description: Green [pantyhose](#pantyhose), sheer or opaque, covering the [legs](#legs) from waist to toe. Legwear that ends on the thigh is [green_thighhighs](#green_thighhighs).

entries.name: high-waist_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose [reaching](#reaching) [well](#well) above the hips, with the waistband at [navel](#navel) [height](#height) or higher. It only shows when the top is short, lifted or absent.

entries.name: yellow_pantyhose
entries.description: Waist-high hosiery in yellow. Tag [pantyhose](#pantyhose) alongside.

entries.name: leggings_under_shorts
entries.description: Leggings worn as an underlayer with [shorts](#shorts) over them, so the [fabric](#fabric) carries on down the [legs](#legs) past the hem. A sporty or cold-weather pairing.

entries.name: single_fishnet_legwear
entries.description: Netted hosiery on one leg while the other is bare or wearing something else. A deliberate mismatch typical of [punk](#punk) and burlesque styling.

entries.name: pantyhose_under_swimsuit
entries.description: Pantyhose worn beneath a [swimsuit](#swimsuit), the sheer [legs](#legs) [running](#running) out from under the swimwear. A styled or [school](#school) look rather than anything meant for actual [swimming](#swimming).

entries.name: front-seamed_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [pantyhose](#pantyhose), [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or a [bodysuit](#bodysuit) marked by a line of [stitching](#stitching) [climbing](#climbing) the front of each leg — a seam, not a printed stripe. Tag whichever side is actually visible; the rear version has its own name.

entries.name: multicolored_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose worked in more than one colour, whether graded along the leg or [split](#split) into bands. One leg differing from the other is a separate [idea](#idea) from this.

entries.name: aqua_pantyhose
entries.description: Tights in blue-green covering [legs](#legs) and hips in one piece, sheer or opaque. Thigh-length stockings in the same [shade](#shade) are [aqua_thighhighs](#aqua_thighhighs).

entries.name: lace_pantyhose
entries.description: Tights of [lace](#lace) over the whole leg, [patterned](#patterned) and half [transparent](#transparent). Plain hosiery finished with a lace top band is a different thing.

entries.name: two-tone_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose in exactly two colours, whether divided leg from leg or banded at the thigh. The join is usually a clean line rather than a gradient.

entries.name: lowleg_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose whose waistband sits low on the hips, so the upper part of the buttocks is left uncovered. The [legs](#legs) are covered as usual; only the rise is cut down.

entries.name: blue_leggings
entries.description: Close-fitting blue trousers of stretchy [fabric](#fabric) [running](#running) down to the ankle. Thicker and more opaque than [pantyhose](#pantyhose), and worn as clothing in their own right.

entries.name: unworn_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose visible in the picture yet nobody is wearing them, [lying](#lying) rolled up, [hanging](#hanging) to dry or held in a hand.

entries.name: striped_leggings
entries.description: Close-fitting [leggings](#leggings) that [cover](#cover) the [legs](#legs), [patterned](#patterned) with stripes.

entries.name: wet_pantyhose
entries.description: Tights soaked through, going darker and more [transparent](#transparent) wherever the [water](#water) [gathers](#gathers). Rain and pools are the usual reasons.

entries.name: grey_leggings
entries.description: Grey [leggings](#leggings), the stretchy trousers fitted close from waist to ankle. They may be worn alone or under a [skirt](#skirt) or [shorts](#shorts).

entries.name: purple_leggings
entries.description: Purple stretch trousers fitted close to the leg, worn as legwear rather than as trousers proper. Thicker and less sheer than [pantyhose](#pantyhose).

entries.name: pink_leggings
entries.description: Close-fitting pink legwear of stretch [fabric](#fabric) covering the [legs](#legs) down to the ankle. Sheerer hosiery joined at the waist is [pantyhose](#pantyhose) instead.

entries.name: brown_leggings
entries.description: Close-fitting leg coverings in brown, [running](#running) from the waist to the ankle. They are thicker and more opaque than [pantyhose](#pantyhose) and count as a garment in their own right.

entries.name: shiny_pantyhose
entries.description: Pantyhose with a [wet](#wet), glossy sheen rather than a matte weave, the way [latex](#latex) or [leather](#leather) reflects light down the [legs](#legs).

entries.name: orange_leggings
entries.description: Orange [leggings](#leggings) fitting close from waist to ankle.

entries.name: green_leggings
entries.description: Green [leggings](#leggings) hugging the [legs](#legs) from waist to ankle. They may be worn alone or under a [skirt](#skirt) or [shorts](#shorts).

entries.name: yellow_leggings
entries.description: Yellow [leggings](#leggings) fitted closely along the [legs](#legs).

entries.name: socks
entries.description: Foot coverings worn under [shoes](#shoes), ranging from ankle length up to the knee. Kneehighs, [loose_socks](#loose_socks), [tabi](#tabi), and toe_socks name the more specific kinds.

entries.name: kneehighs
entries.description: Socks ending just below the knee, at about three-quarter calf [height](#height). Shorter ones are ankle [socks](#socks); anything rising above the knee is [over-kneehighs](#over-kneehighs) or [thighhighs](#thighhighs).

entries.name: white_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) in white, the standard legwear under a [school](#school) uniform. Combine with [socks](#socks); a pair [reaching](#reaching) above the knee is [white_thighhighs](#white_thighhighs) instead.

entries.name: black_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) in black, ending at or below the knee. Legwear [reaching](#reaching) up the thigh is [black_thighhighs](#black_thighhighs).

entries.name: tabi
entries.description: Traditional Japanese [socks](#socks) [split](#split) between the big toe and the rest of the foot, worn with [sandals](#sandals). Socks dividing every toe are a separate [tag](#tag), as is the rubber-soled outdoor version.

entries.name: leg_warmers
entries.description: Thick footless tubes pulled over the lower [legs](#legs) from ankle to knee, worn on top of [socks](#socks) and [shoes](#shoes). Loose_socks [cover](#cover) the [feet](#feet), while [detached_leggings](#detached_leggings) are thinner and reach the thigh.

entries.name: loose_socks
entries.description: Baggy [socks](#socks), usually white, slouched down and bunched below the knee, a [staple](#staple) of [gyaru](#gyaru) and [kogal](#kogal) [school](#school) [fashion](#fashion). Leg warmers look similar but leave the [feet](#feet) bare.

entries.name: baggy_socks
entries.description: Thick slouch [socks](#socks) that bunch and sag around the ankle and calf instead of gripping the leg. They are a [signature](#signature) of 1990s Japanese schoolgirl [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: bobby_socks
entries.description: Ankle [socks](#socks) with a thick cuff turned down over the ankle, either flaring out or [lying](#lying) snug, in mid-century style. Kneehighs pushed down do not count.

entries.name: single_sock
entries.description: A sock worn on one foot only, the other bare. Use [single_kneehigh](#single_kneehigh) or [single_thighhigh](#single_thighhigh) when the length is known.

entries.name: striped_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [socks](#socks) and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: no_socks
entries.description: Shoes worn straight on bare skin, with [no](#no) [socks](#socks) or other legwear showing. Bare [feet](#feet), [pantyhose](#pantyhose) and [thighhighs](#thighhighs) do not count.

entries.name: blue_socks
entries.description: Blue [socks](#socks) [reaching](#reaching) the ankle, the calf or the knee. Legwear ending above the knee is [blue_thighhighs](#blue_thighhighs).

entries.name: ankle_socks
entries.description: Short [socks](#socks) rising a little above the ankle [bone](#bone) and stopping below the shin. Anything that reaches up the shin counts as [kneehighs](#kneehighs), and the sock-like booties have a [tag](#tag) of their own.

entries.name: grey_socks
entries.description: Grey [socks](#socks) or [kneehighs](#kneehighs), at any length that stops below the knee. Legwear [reaching](#reaching) over the knee is [grey_thighhighs](#grey_thighhighs) instead, whatever its length above that point.

entries.name: red_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) in red. Legwear [reaching](#reaching) above the knee is [red_thighhighs](#red_thighhighs); [hose](#hose) to the waist is [red_pantyhose](#red_pantyhose).

entries.name: single_kneehigh
entries.description: One knee-high sock on one leg, the other leg bare or wearing something else. Tagged alongside [kneehighs](#kneehighs) and [single_sock](#single_sock).

entries.name: frilled_socks
entries.description: Socks with ruffles gathered around the top edge, classically short white pairs worn with [mary_janes](#mary_janes) or a [school](#school) outfit. Ruffled hosiery [reaching](#reaching) the thigh is [frilled_thighhighs](#frilled_thighhighs).

entries.name: pink_socks
entries.description: Pink [socks](#socks) or [kneehighs](#kneehighs), ending below the knee or just above it. Legwear [reaching](#reaching) the thigh is [pink_thighhighs](#pink_thighhighs) and full hosiery is [pink_pantyhose](#pink_pantyhose).

entries.name: short_socks
entries.description: Socks ending at or just above the ankle, [well](#well) below the calf, covering both visible ankle [socks](#socks) and hidden no-show socks.

entries.name: anklehighs
entries.description: Very short [socks](#socks) stopping at or barely above the ankle, leaving the whole calf bare. Shorter than [kneehighs](#kneehighs), and often only just visible above a shoe.

entries.name: white_leg_warmers
entries.description: Loose white knitted tubes worn over the lower [legs](#legs), typical of the 1980s dance look and some [school](#school) uniforms.

entries.name: brown_socks
entries.description: Socks in brown, anywhere from ankle length up to the knee. Add [kneehighs](#kneehighs) as [well](#well) when they reach that far.

entries.name: unworn_socks
entries.description: Socks taken off and left visible in the picture, often [lying](#lying) beside bare [feet](#feet) or held in hand.

entries.name: green_socks
entries.description: Green [socks](#socks) or [kneehighs](#kneehighs), at any length that stops below the knee. Legwear [reaching](#reaching) over the knee is [green_thighhighs](#green_thighhighs).

entries.name: yellow_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) in yellow. Tag [socks](#socks) as [well](#well).

entries.name: purple_socks
entries.description: Purple [socks](#socks) of any length up to the knee, ankle socks and [kneehighs](#kneehighs) included. Combine with socks and the length; legwear [reaching](#reaching) the thigh is [purple_thighhighs](#purple_thighhighs) and full tights are [purple_pantyhose](#purple_pantyhose).

entries.name: ribbed_socks
entries.description: Socks knitted with vertical ribbing, from ankle [socks](#socks) to [kneehighs](#kneehighs). Tag with socks; ribbed [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or [pantyhose](#pantyhose) belong under [ribbed_legwear](#ribbed_legwear) instead.

entries.name: leg_wrap
entries.description: A strip of [cloth](#cloth) or bandage wound round the leg, common on [ninja](#ninja) and martial designs. A decorative [ribbon](#ribbon) is [leg_ribbon](#leg_ribbon), and [wrapping](#wrapping) one's [legs](#legs) around a person is [leg_lock](#leg_lock).

entries.name: orange_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) in orange, ending at or below the knee. Anything [reaching](#reaching) the thigh is [orange_thighhighs](#orange_thighhighs).

entries.name: fishnet_socks
entries.description: Mesh [socks](#socks), kneehigh lengths that stop below the knee included. Reaching the thigh makes them [fishnet_thighhighs](#fishnet_thighhighs), and a full pair is [fishnet_pantyhose](#fishnet_pantyhose).

entries.name: black_leg_warmers
entries.description: Loose knitted tubes pulled over the lower [legs](#legs) in black, often bunched down at the ankle. Part of dance, retro and [idol](#idol) outfits.

entries.name: vertical-striped_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) with lengthwise stripes. Ringed [socks](#socks) are just [striped_socks](#striped_socks).

entries.name: ankle_wrap
entries.description: A strip of [cloth](#cloth) or bandage wound round the ankle, standard on martial artists and [fantasy](#fantasy) fighters. Add [bandages](#bandages) where the [wrapping](#wrapping) is plainly medical.

entries.name: print_socks
entries.description: Socks decorated with a repeating motif rather than left [plain](#plain) or simply striped. Hearts, stars and [animal](#animal) designs turn up most often.

entries.name: pink_leg_warmers
entries.description: Knitted pink tubes pulled over the [calves](#calves), leaving the [feet](#feet) bare or ending above the shoe. Associated with dance practice and eighties [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: torn_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) with rips or holes worn through at the toe, heel, or [split](#split) along the leg. Marks legwear as [damaged](#damaged) or worn out rather than a pristine pair.

entries.name: socks_over_pantyhose
entries.description: Ordinary [socks](#socks) pulled on over a pair of [pantyhose](#pantyhose), so two layers of legwear show at once with the sheer [fabric](#fabric) continuing above the sock cuff. A common part of schoolgirl styling.

entries.name: gaiters
entries.description: Coverings worn over the top of the shoe and the lower leg to keep [rain](#rain), [snow](#snow) and [mud](#mud) out, sometimes strapped beneath the sole. They run from ankle [height](#height) to the thigh, and are not the bands that hold stockings up.

entries.name: two-tone_socks
entries.description: Socks in exactly two colours, typically a body in one [shade](#shade) with cuff, heel or toe in another. Anything busier than that counts as multicoloured.

entries.name: aqua_socks
entries.description: Socks in blue-green, anywhere from ankle length up to [kneehighs](#kneehighs). Longer legwear in the same [shade](#shade) is [aqua_thighhighs](#aqua_thighhighs).

entries.name: argyle_socks
entries.description: Socks knitted in argyle, diamonds set on the diagonal with fine lines crossing them. Ankle [socks](#socks) and [kneehighs](#kneehighs) alike carry it.

entries.name: mismatched_socks
entries.description: The two [socks](#socks) don't agree in color, pattern or length - one case of the broader [mismatched_legwear](#mismatched_legwear) [idea](#idea).

entries.name: plaid_socks
entries.description: Socks [patterned](#patterned) in tartan, at any length up to the knee. Only the check separates them from [plain](#plain) [socks](#socks).

entries.name: single_leg_warmer
entries.description: A loose knitted [tube](#tube) pulled up one calf while the other leg wears nothing. The lopsided version of the dancewear [staple](#staple).

entries.name: blue_leg_warmers
entries.description: Blue knitted tubes drawn over the lower [legs](#legs) with the [feet](#feet) left uncovered. They bunch loosely at the ankle rather than fitting like [socks](#socks).

entries.name: sock_dangle
entries.description: A sock [slipping](#slipping) loose from the foot and [hanging](#hanging) off the [toes](#toes). Reads as relaxed or careless, and often turns up alongside [lounging](#lounging) or [dangling](#dangling) [legs](#legs).

entries.name: grey_leg_warmers
entries.description: Grey knitted tubes pulled up over the lower [legs](#legs), worn over [socks](#socks) or on bare skin. They are common in dance, exercise and [casual](#casual) [winter](#winter) outfits.

entries.name: socks_over_thighhighs
entries.description: Shorter [socks](#socks) worn on top of [thighhighs](#thighhighs), layering two separate pieces of legwear on the same leg. The thighhigh's band still shows higher up.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_socks
entries.description: Socks finished with a [ribbon](#ribbon) band around the cuff. The trim usually sits at the top edge where the sock folds over.

entries.name: red_leg_warmers
entries.description: Loose red knitted tubes worn over the lower [legs](#legs), usually bunched around the ankle. Unlike stockings they leave the foot uncovered.

entries.name: tube_socks
entries.description: Straight-cut [socks](#socks) [reaching](#reaching) the calf or knee with [no](#no) shaped heel, so a single style fits any foot. A [sportswear](#sportswear) [staple](#staple), usually marked by coloured bands circling the top.

entries.name: polka_dot_socks
entries.description: Socks or [kneehighs](#kneehighs) printed with round [dots](#dots) up the leg. The [spots](#spots) may be a single colour or several.

entries.name: puttee
entries.description: A long strip of [cloth](#cloth) spiral-wound up the lower leg for support during [marching](#marching) or [standing](#standing). Adopted into Western uniforms from British Indian troops, it was standard kit through both world wars.

entries.name: foot_wraps
entries.description: Strips of [cloth](#cloth) wound around the foot and ankle in place of [socks](#socks) or [shoes](#shoes). Martial arts, [ninja](#ninja) and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits use them.

entries.name: purple_leg_warmers
entries.description: Purple knitted tubes worn over the lower [legs](#legs), usually bunched at the ankle and leaving the foot bare. Common on dance and [casual](#casual) outfits.

entries.name: single_loose_sock
entries.description: One slouchy, baggy sock bunched around the ankle while the other leg wears something else or nothing. A deliberately untidy schoolwear look.

entries.name: yellow_leg_warmers
entries.description: Yellow leg warmers pulled over the [calves](#calves).

entries.name: no-show_socks
entries.description: Very short [socks](#socks) cut below the ankle so that they vanish inside the shoe. The foot looks bare while still being covered.

entries.name: brown_leg_warmers
entries.description: Brown leg warmers pulled up over the [calves](#calves), worn straight or bunched down. Colour variant of the usual knitted pair.

entries.name: fluffy_legwear
entries.description: Socks, stockings or leg covers with a plush furred surface made to resemble an animal's [coat](#coat). Winter outfits and [animal](#animal) costumes both use them.

entries.name: green_leg_warmers
entries.description: Green leg warmers pulled over the [calves](#calves), leaving the foot uncovered. They are worn over [socks](#socks) or straight on bare skin.

entries.name: orange_leg_warmers
entries.description: Orange leg warmers pulled up over the [calves](#calves), worn smooth or bunched down.

entries.name: hat
entries.description: Headwear of any kind worn on the head, brimmed or not — caps, beanies, berets, top hats, straw hats, [witch](#witch) hats and the rest. Where a more exact kind has its own [tag](#tag), use that as [well](#well).

entries.name: black_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) in black, of any shape from a witch's cone or a top hat to a [beret](#beret) or cap. Add the specific hat [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: beret
entries.description: A soft cap, round and flat across the top, its band [running](#running) underneath the [crown](#crown), usually worn tilted. It is [fashion](#fashion) wear for both men and women and also part of many [military](#military) and [police](#police) uniforms.

entries.name: witch_hat
entries.description: A pointed, wide-brimmed [hat](#hat), typically black, worn by witches. Kirisame Marisa is the character most associated with it, while a [tall](#tall) cone without a brim counts as a [wizard_hat](#wizard_hat) instead; [tag](#tag) hat as [well](#well).

entries.name: wizard_hat_with_brim
entries.description: The classic pointed [magic](#magic) [hat](#hat) with a brim circling the [crown](#crown), often [slouching](#slouching) over at the tip. Witches, wizards, and Halloween costumes all wear it.

entries.name: brimmed_wizard_hat
entries.description: The classic [tall](#tall) conical [hat](#hat) of [magic](#magic) users, with a wide brim circling its base and often a slouched or bent tip. Stars, buckles and a broad band are the usual trimmings.

entries.name: white_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) of any style in white, from [sun](#sun) hats to [sailor](#sailor) caps, [nurse](#nurse) caps and berets. Add the specific hat type alongside.

entries.name: mob_cap
entries.description: A soft round indoor cap gathered into a frilled brim, usually held on by a [ribbon](#ribbon) band. Worn by women of the eighteenth century and by servants in place of a [headdress](#headdress); prefer it to the [plain](#plain) [hat](#hat) tags whenever the shape fits.

entries.name: hat_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around or onto headwear of any sort, such as the band of a straw [hat](#hat). It often appears together with a [hat_bow](#hat_bow).

entries.name: hat_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) fastened to a [hat](#hat) as decoration, frequently [sitting](#sitting) alongside a [ribbon](#ribbon) band around the [crown](#crown).

entries.name: red_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) of any shape in red, from caps and berets to wide-brimmed styles. Add the specific hat [tag](#tag) as [well](#well); a [santa_hat](#santa_hat) usually carries its own tag rather than this one.

entries.name: no_headwear
entries.description: Someone usually seen in a [hat](#hat), [helmet](#helmet) or [bandana](#bandana) appears bareheaded. The item is absent altogether rather than merely taken off and held.

entries.name: tokin_hat
entries.description: A tiny black box-shaped cap worn on the [forehead](#forehead), part of the [mountain](#mountain) ascetic's outfit and the standard [headgear](#headgear) of [tengu](#tengu).

entries.name: blue_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) in blue of any shape, from a [beret](#beret) or a cap to a [witch](#witch) hat. Add the specific hat [tag](#tag), since this names only the colour.

entries.name: santa_hat
entries.description: The soft, floppy red cone [hat](#hat) of Santa Claus, edged in white fur and finished with a white pom-pom at its tip. Common on Christmas pictures of any character and does not require the rest of the [costume](#costume).

entries.name: unworn_headwear
entries.description: Any [hat](#hat), cap, [helmet](#helmet), [headdress](#headdress) or similar item is present in the scene beside someone who could wear it, but nobody has it on. Add the more specific [tag](#tag) as [well](#well), such as [unworn_hat](#unworn_hat) or [unworn_helmet](#unworn_helmet).

entries.name: top_hat
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), flat-topped Victorian [hat](#hat) worn by gentlemen, magicians and ringmasters. A tiny one on a [hairband](#hairband) is [mini_top_hat](#mini_top_hat).

entries.name: hat_ornament
entries.description: Any decorative piece fixed to a [hat](#hat): a [badge](#badge), a [pin](#pin), a [brooch](#brooch), a charm. Bows, ribbons, [feathers](#feathers) and flowers each have a [tag](#tag) of their own.

entries.name: sun_hat
entries.description: A wide-brimmed [hat](#hat) that shades the face from the [sun](#sun), often made of straw and worn at the [beach](#beach) or in [summer](#summer) scenes. Implies hat.

entries.name: mini_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) too small to actually fit the head, worn clipped into the hair as decoration instead.

entries.name: missing_headwear
entries.description: A character usually seen in a [hat](#hat), cap or [headdress](#headdress) is drawn bare-headed instead. Their hair often falls differently as a result.

entries.name: unworn_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) that belongs to a character is off the head and visible somewhere in the picture, held or [resting](#resting) nearby. If the hat is absent entirely, [no_headwear](#no_headwear) is the [tag](#tag) to use instead.

entries.name: hat_flower
entries.description: Flowers fixed to a [hat](#hat) as decoration, one or several. Straw hats and [sun](#sun) hats carry them most often.

entries.name: straw_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) woven from straw, from wide-brimmed [sun](#sun) hats to Asian conical kasa such as amigasa or [sandogasa](#sandogasa).

entries.name: brown_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) of any style coloured brown, be it a [fedora](#fedora), [cowboy](#cowboy) hat, [beret](#beret) or [witch](#witch) hat. Add hat and the particular kind.

entries.name: green_hat
entries.description: A green [hat](#hat) of any shape, from a [beret](#beret) to a wide-brimmed [sun](#sun) hat or a [witch](#witch) hat. Tag the specific style of hat wherever it is identifiable.

entries.name: pink_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) in pink of any style, from a [beret](#beret) to a wide-brimmed [sun](#sun) hat. Add the shape [tag](#tag) as [well](#well) so the style is recorded.

entries.name: animal_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) shaped after a creature's head, with ears and often a printed face, [cat](#cat) and bunny hats being the standard pair. Once the whole body is dressed as the [animal](#animal), use [animal_costume](#animal_costume).

entries.name: hat_feather
entries.description: A feather tucked into a hatband for show, as on musketeer and Tyrolean styles. One [plume](#plume) or several.

entries.name: tilted_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), cap, [crown](#crown) or [helmet](#helmet) worn askew, sloping to one side of the head. Mini top hats on a [hairband](#hairband) are a common case.

entries.name: tate_eboshi
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), upright black cap worn by court nobles from the Heian period onward. A closely related ceremonial cap, the kanmuri, is generally filed under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: purple_hat
entries.description: A purple [hat](#hat) of any style, from a [witch_hat](#witch_hat) to a [beret](#beret). Combine with hat and the specific kind.

entries.name: bonnet
entries.description: A soft head covering without a brim, tied under the chin with strings and leaving the [forehead](#forehead) clear. Babies, dolls, period ladies and lolita outfits wear them; a [hat](#hat) with a brim is something else.

entries.name: crescent_hat_ornament
entries.description: A crescent-shaped decoration fixed to a [hat](#hat), such as a [moon](#moon) on a witch's brim or on a [night](#night) cap. Tag the hat itself as [well](#well).

entries.name: mini_top_hat
entries.description: A small, dainty top [hat](#hat) worn tilted on the head, popular in Victorian and gothic lolita [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: star_hat_ornament
entries.description: A star-shaped decoration attached to a [hat](#hat), such as a [witch](#witch) hat or a cap.

entries.name: cowboy_hat
entries.description: A wide-brimmed [hat](#hat) with a [tall](#tall) [crown](#crown), worn by herders and ranchers of the American West and Mexico. The [signature](#signature) piece of any Western outfit.

entries.name: jester_cap
entries.description: A floppy [hat](#hat) with several points, each usually tipped with a [bell](#bell) or a bauble, the fool's headwear. Do not confuse it with a two-pointed [witch](#witch) hat.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_headwear
entries.description: Headwear of any shape with fur lining its edges, the santa [hat](#hat) being the obvious case. Headwear made of [pelt](#pelt) throughout is [fur_hat](#fur_hat).

entries.name: tilted_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) worn at an angle instead of [square](#square) on the head, tipped forward, [back](#back) or over one ear.

entries.name: grey_hat
entries.description: A grey [hat](#hat) of any shape, from a [beret](#beret) to a [fedora](#fedora) or a peaked cap. Record the specific style of hat where it is identifiable.

entries.name: frilled_hat
entries.description: Any [hat](#hat) [carrying](#carrying) ruffled trim or decoration — bonnets, [sun](#sun) hats, berets and the rest. The visible gathered edge is all that is required.

entries.name: fur_hat
entries.description: A thick padded [hat](#hat) of fur or [heavy](#heavy) fur trim, the Russian [ushanka](#ushanka) being the [model](#model). Beanies and santa hats are not this, and headwear with a mere fur edge is [fur-trimmed_headwear](#fur-trimmed_headwear).

entries.name: fedora
entries.description: A soft felt [hat](#hat) whose [crown](#crown) carries a lengthways dent and is pinched at the front, usually with a band around it. The classic detective-film hat; a much shorter brim makes it a trilby.

entries.name: yellow_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) of any style in yellow, from a [rain](#rain) hat to a [beret](#beret). Tag hat and the type.

entries.name: pirate_hat
entries.description: A [tricorne](#tricorne) or [bicorne](#bicorne) associated with pirates, often bearing a [skull](#skull) and crossbones on the front. The wearer need not be a [pirate](#pirate); costumes and mascots wear it too.

entries.name: wizard_hat
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), narrow, conical [hat](#hat) worn by wizards and other mages. The wide-brimmed version of the shape is a [witch_hat](#witch_hat) instead; [tag](#tag) hat alongside it.

entries.name: brimless_witch_hat
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) pointed witch's [hat](#hat) rising straight off the head with [no](#no) brim at its base. Without the brim it reads closer to a hennin or a [plain](#plain) cone than to the usual pointed hat.

entries.name: witch_hat_without_brim
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) pointed [hat](#hat) that tapers straight up from the head with [no](#no) brim circling the [crown](#crown). The missing brim is what sets it apart from an ordinary [witch](#witch) hat.

entries.name: large_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) markedly bigger than the wearer's head, or than a normal hat of the same design would be. Enormous [witch](#witch) hats and [sun](#sun) hats are the usual cases.

entries.name: chef_hat
entries.description: Any of the hats cooks wear: the [tall](#tall) [pleated](#pleated) toque above all, but also the low pillbox or [skull](#skull) cap of a line cook. It applies to the [hat](#hat) alone, whether or not the wearer is otherwise dressed for a [kitchen](#kitchen).

entries.name: qingdai_guanmao
entries.description: The round official [hat](#hat) worn during China's Qing dynasty, with a [dark](#dark) velvet brim and a bright conical [crown](#crown) finished by a small button. It is worn heavily by [jiangshi](#jiangshi) characters, usually paired with an [ofuda](#ofuda) [stuck](#stuck) to the front.

entries.name: winged_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) with a pair of [wings](#wings) fixed to it, worn by characters such as Mystia Lorelei and Blue Archive's Koharu. Tag hat alongside it.

entries.name: cat_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) with [cat](#cat) ears on it, or one styled as a whole cat [sitting](#sitting) on the head. One of the [animal](#animal) hats.

entries.name: porkpie_hat
entries.description: A short [hat](#hat) with a flat [crown](#crown) and a stiff brim all the way round, lower than a [fedora](#fedora) and without its pinched front. Popular with jazz, blues and ska styles.

entries.name: jingasa
entries.description: A soldier's [hat](#hat) from [old](#old) Japan, a broad conical or flat dish often [beaten](#beaten) from metal or lacquered. Foot soldiers and travellers wear it in period scenes.

entries.name: jiangshi_hat
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) round black cap of a Qing official, worn by [hopping](#hopping) vampires and usually hung with a [paper](#paper) [talisman](#talisman) from the brim. It marks the wearer out at a [glance](#glance).

entries.name: orange_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) in orange, of any shape from a [beret](#beret) to a witch's point. Add the specific hat [tag](#tag) where one exists.

entries.name: party_hat
entries.description: A small cone of stiff [paper](#paper) worn on the head with an elastic [strap](#strap), the sort handed round at birthdays, often striped or topped with a pompom. It usually turns up beside [cake](#cake), [streamers](#streamers) and other [celebration](#celebration) tags.

entries.name: pith_helmet
entries.description: A rounded, cloth-covered [sun](#sun) [helmet](#helmet) with a brim [running](#running) all the way round, the classic gear of the safari-going explorer. It marks [jungle](#jungle) and expedition outfits at a [glance](#glance).

entries.name: bucket_hat
entries.description: A soft [cloth](#cloth) [hat](#hat) whose brim slopes down all the way round, the sort anglers favour. An actual pail worn on the head is [bucket_on_head](#bucket_on_head), and the stiffer safari shape is a [pith_helmet](#pith_helmet).

entries.name: school_hat
entries.description: The [hat](#hat) worn by Japanese [kindergarten](#kindergarten) and elementary pupils, most often yellow and shaped like a pith [helmet](#helmet), though other colours and [cuts](#cuts) exist.

entries.name: tam_o'_shanter
entries.description: A flat, round Scottish [bonnet](#bonnet), usually topped with a pom-pom.

entries.name: tricorne
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) with its brim [folded](#folded) up on three sides to form a triangular [outline](#outline), worn by pirates, admirals and eighteenth-century soldiers alike.

entries.name: ushanka
entries.description: The Russian fur cap with ear flaps that [can](#can) be tied up over the [crown](#crown) or down under the chin to [guard](#guard) against the [cold](#cold).

entries.name: pillbox_hat
entries.description: A small round [hat](#hat) with a flat top, straight sides and [no](#no) brim, perched on the head rather than pulled down over it. Worn mostly by women in vintage and formal styles, and the shape of a bellhop's cap.

entries.name: striped_headwear
entries.description: Any [hat](#hat), cap or other [headpiece](#headpiece) marked with a striped pattern; add the specific piece of headwear alongside it. Implies [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: bowl_hat
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) worn upside down as a [hat](#hat), [sitting](#sitting) on the head like a [dome](#dome). The round-crowned felt [bowler_hat](#bowler_hat) is an entirely different thing despite the name.

entries.name: frilled_headwear
entries.description: Head pieces of any shape edged with ruffles, such as a [fascinator](#fascinator), [bonnet](#bonnet) or small perched ornament. Use [frilled_hat](#frilled_hat) where the piece is clearly a [hat](#hat); this covers the wider range.

entries.name: two-tone_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), cap or other headwear item in exactly two colours. Add the specific headwear [tag](#tag) and the colours.

entries.name: deerstalker
entries.description: A checked tweed cap with a brim front and [back](#back) and ear flaps that tie up over the [crown](#crown). Born in [rural](#rural) nineteenth-century England and long attached to the famous consulting [detective](#detective).

entries.name: floating_headgear
entries.description: Headgear hovering around or above the head with nothing visibly [holding](#holding) it, common on ship-girl and [idol](#idol) designs. It reads as worn even though it never touches the hair.

entries.name: plume
entries.description: An upright [crest](#crest) of [feathers](#feathers) or horsehair fixed to a [hat](#hat) or [helmet](#helmet), as on [cavalry](#cavalry) helmets and marching-band caps. Tag the hat or helmet it decorates alongside it.

entries.name: ajirogasa
entries.description: A wide conical [hat](#hat) woven from [bamboo](#bamboo) or wicker, worn by monks, travellers and farmers. Tilted forward it shades the whole face.

entries.name: print_headwear
entries.description: Headwear with a printed design. The [tag](#tag) is generic; prefer the specific form such as print_hat, print_helmet or print_veil when it exists.

entries.name: polka_dot_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) or other headwear printed with polka [dots](#dots), such as a dotted [jester](#jester) cap, [bandana](#bandana), or [beanie](#beanie). Tag the headwear type alongside [polka_dot](#polka_dot).

entries.name: tulip_hat
entries.description: A soft [cloth](#cloth) [hat](#hat) whose [crown](#crown) is made of petal-like panels flaring out toward the brim, resembling an [upside-down](#upside-down) [tulip](#tulip). Common on toddlers and in playful sun-hat designs.

entries.name: two-tone_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) built from two colours, commonly a [crown](#crown) in one [shade](#shade) with a brim or band in the other. Any further colour takes it out of this category.

entries.name: plaid_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) in plaid [fabric](#fabric), such as a flat cap, [deerstalker](#deerstalker), or [bucket](#bucket) hat. Tag the specific hat type alongside [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes).

entries.name: bicorne
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) whose brim is [folded](#folded) up on two sides into a pair of points, the Napoleonic officer's [headgear](#headgear). Worn by [pirate](#pirate) captains, admirals and other historical [military](#military) characters.

entries.name: hat_over_one_eye
entries.description: The [hat](#hat) is tilted so its brim covers a single eye, leaving the other clear. Add [one_eye_covered](#one_eye_covered) where that fits too.

entries.name: aqua_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) in an aqua [shade](#shade). Name the kind as [well](#well), such as [beret](#beret), cap or [sun_hat](#sun_hat).

entries.name: papakha
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) cylindrical [hat](#hat) of [wool](#wool) or astrakhan fleece, worn by men across the Caucasus and by regional and Cossack [military](#military) units. Usually black or grey and shaggy.

entries.name: sideways_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) of any kind is worn turned to the side rather than facing forward. Not the same as [tilted_headwear](#tilted_headwear), where the hat perches off to one side of the head instead of [sitting](#sitting) on top.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), [bonnet](#bonnet) or [fascinator](#fascinator) edged with a [ribbon](#ribbon) trim. Tag the specific headwear type as [well](#well).

entries.name: two-sided_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), [hood](#hood) or cap whose lining differs in colour or pattern from its outer surface. A turned-up brim or flipped-back flap puts both faces on show at once.

entries.name: boater_hat
entries.description: A stiff straw [hat](#hat) with a flat [crown](#crown), a flat brim and a [ribbon](#ribbon) band, in the turn-of-the-century style. Worn by either [sex](#sex), generally with [summer](#summer) or period outfits.

entries.name: pom_pom_beanie
entries.description: A knitted [beanie](#beanie) topped with a [fluffy](#fluffy) pom pom, [sitting](#sitting) upright or flopping to one side like a santa [hat](#hat). Tag beanie and [pom_pom_(clothes)](#pom_pom_(clothes)) with it; [earflap_beanie](#earflap_beanie) [can](#can) apply too.

entries.name: pointy_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) rising to a point. The [idea](#idea) is vague on its own, so prefer the specific kind where it [can](#can) be told, such as [witch_hat](#witch_hat), [wizard_hat](#wizard_hat), or [santa_hat](#santa_hat).

entries.name: multicolored_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) whose design sets two or more clearly separate colours against each other. Where one colour dominates and the rest is only trim, a [plain](#plain) colour [tag](#tag) serves better.

entries.name: rabbit_hat
