entries.description: A [hat](#hat) styled to look like a [rabbit](#rabbit), typically finished with floppy ears and a small face. A [hood](#hood) with ears attached is [rabbit_hood](#rabbit_hood) instead.

entries.name: bowler_hat
entries.description: A hard felt [hat](#hat) with a rounded [crown](#crown) and a short brim curled at the edge, the classic derby of gentlemen and silent-film comedians. A [bowl](#bowl) set on the head is [bowl_hat](#bowl_hat).

entries.name: hat_tassel
entries.description: A [tassel](#tassel) [hanging](#hanging) from headwear — off a fez, a [graduation](#graduation) cap or the tip of a knitted [hat](#hat).

entries.name: fascinator
entries.description: A small ornamental [headpiece](#headpiece) of [feathers](#feathers), netting, [beads](#beads) or [silk](#silk) flowers on a [comb](#comb) or clip, worn tilted to one side. Cocktail hats count too, and it [can](#can) sit beside a proper [hat](#hat).

entries.name: mitre
entries.description: The [tall](#tall), pointed ceremonial [hat](#hat) worn by bishops, abbots and cardinals in the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

entries.name: camouflage_headwear
entries.description: Any head covering in a [camouflage](#camouflage) pattern, whether a soft [hat](#hat), a cap or a [helmet](#helmet). Reach for camouflage_hat or camouflage_helmet when the kind is clear.

entries.name: hat_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt), [buckle](#buckle) and all, worn around the [crown](#crown) of a [hat](#hat) as its band. It takes the place of the usual [ribbon](#ribbon).

entries.name: wide_brim
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) whose brim reaches out far past the [crown](#crown), shading the face and shoulders below it. Sun hats, [witch](#witch) hats, and [cowboy](#cowboy) hats are its usual carriers.

entries.name: skull_on_head
entries.description: A real [skull](#skull), often an [animal](#animal) one, worn over the head like a [helmet](#helmet) or cap. Distinct from a [hat](#hat) merely built in a skull shape.

entries.name: pumpkin_hat
entries.description: Headwear built to look like a [pumpkin](#pumpkin): a whole [gourd](#gourd), a carved [jack-o'-lantern](#jack-o'-lantern), a cap in that shape, or just the stalk perched on top. It may sit lightly on the [crown](#crown) or swallow the whole head like a [mask](#mask).

entries.name: fruit_hat_ornament
entries.description: A fruit-shaped decoration mounted on a [hat](#hat), whether a single piece or a heaped arrangement. Several Touhou designs are the best-known examples.

entries.name: rice_hat
entries.description: The wide conical [hat](#hat) woven from straw or [reeds](#reeds), worn against [sun](#sun) and [rain](#rain) by farmers and travellers. A stiffer version made of metal, wood or hardened [leather](#leather) worn by soldiers is a [jingasa](#jingasa) instead.

entries.name: vertical-striped_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), cap or other head covering striped from [crown](#crown) to brim. Common on [circus](#circus), [clown](#clown) and holiday designs.

entries.name: mini_witch_hat
entries.description: A small, pointed witch's [hat](#hat) perched in the hair rather than covering the whole head, usually clipped on at a tilt.

entries.name: hat_over_eyes
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) is worn low enough to hide both eyes while the [nose](#nose) and mouth stay in view. It makes the face unreadable, and often reads as sleep or [sulking](#sulking).

entries.name: hat_bell
entries.description: A [bell](#bell) fixed to a [hat](#hat) or [hood](#hood), most often a small round jingle bell [swinging](#swinging) from the point or the brim. Jester caps and knitted [winter](#winter) hats carry them.

entries.name: horned_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) built with [horns](#horns) as part of its design. Where a character's own horns pass through or around the hat instead, [horns_through_headwear](#horns_through_headwear) applies.

entries.name: black_bonnet
entries.description: A brimmed [hat](#hat) tied under the chin, in black. The brim frames the face, and it is standard on [maid](#maid), gothic lolita and period outfits.

entries.name: torn_hat
entries.description: Headwear frayed, holed or ripped along the brim or the [crown](#crown).

entries.name: frilled_bonnet
entries.description: A soft [bonnet](#bonnet) tied under the chin whose brim is gathered into ruffles framing the face. Maid, lolita and infant-styled outfits wear it.

entries.name: mortarboard
entries.description: The flat [square](#square) academic cap with a [tassel](#tassel) [swinging](#swinging) from the button at its centre. Worn with a [gown](#gown) at [graduation](#graduation) ceremonies.

entries.name: mini_chef_hat
entries.description: A doll-sized version of the [tall](#tall), [pleated](#pleated) cook's [hat](#hat), clipped into the hair rather than worn over the whole head.

entries.name: skull_hat_ornament
entries.description: A [skull](#skull), sometimes with crossed bones, fixed to a [hat](#hat) as decoration. Sits on the brim or band rather than being the shape of the hat itself.

entries.name: heart_hat_ornament
entries.description: A heart-shaped decoration [pinned](#pinned) or sewn to a [hat](#hat), on the brim, the [crown](#crown) or the band.

entries.name: whale_hat
entries.description: A soft [animal](#animal) [hat](#hat) modeled on a [whale](#whale), complete with [tail](#tail) flukes or a spout on top, pulled down over the head like a [hood](#hood).

entries.name: hat_pin
entries.description: A long [pin](#pin) pushed through a [hat](#hat) and into the hair to hold it on, its ornamental head left showing. Wide-brimmed and period hats need one.

entries.name: headwear_with_attached_mittens
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) or [hood](#hood) with [gloves](#gloves) or [mittens](#mittens) joined to it by cords or built-in sleeves, so the hand covers dangle from the headwear. A children's [winter](#winter) design.

entries.name: sombrero
entries.description: A Mexican [hat](#hat) with a very wide, upturned brim and a [tall](#tall), often embroidered [crown](#crown). Best known as the mariachi hat, and reads instantly as Mexican [dress](#dress).

entries.name: toque_blanche
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) [pleated](#pleated) chef's [hat](#hat), brimless and straight-sided, almost always white. A flat-topped cook's cap has a [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: gold_headwear
entries.description: Any gold-coloured [hat](#hat), cap or head covering. Vague as it stands: name the specific piece and pair it with [gold](#gold) or yellow where you [can](#can).

entries.name: eel_hat
entries.description: A soft puffy cap shaped and marked like an eel's face, [sitting](#sitting) over the head. More a [costume](#costume) [signature](#signature) than practical headwear.

entries.name: fox_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) built to resemble a fox's head, ears [standing](#standing) up on the [crown](#crown) and often a [snout](#snout) over the brow. One of the animal-hat [family](#family).

entries.name: hat_horns
entries.description: Horn [shapes](#shapes) built into a [hat](#hat) or [helmet](#helmet) rather than growing from the head. Viking-style helms, [jester](#jester) caps and [demon](#demon) [costume](#costume) headwear all use them.

entries.name: sandogasa
entries.description: A broad woven travelling [hat](#hat) whose brim slopes down all the way round, sometimes drawn nearly flat across the top. Worn by pilgrims, wandering swordsmen and [field](#field) workers.

entries.name: butterfly_hat_ornament
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) fixed to a [hat](#hat) as decoration, perched on the brim or the [crown](#crown).

entries.name: mushroom_hat
entries.description: Headwear modelled on a [mushroom](#mushroom) cap, a domed and often spotted [crown](#crown) [sitting](#sitting) over the head. It appears on [forest](#forest) spirits, fairy-tale designs and game characters.

entries.name: pom_pom_hat_ornament
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) finished with a [fluffy](#fluffy) [ball](#ball), usually at the [crown](#crown) of a knit [beanie](#beanie) or on the drooping tip of a [nightcap](#nightcap). The pom may also hang from a cord.

entries.name: cow_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) made to look like a [cow](#cow), with ears, small [horns](#horns) and [patch](#patch) [markings](#markings). Worn as a novelty rather than as part of a whole [costume](#costume).

entries.name: paper_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) [folded](#folded) from a sheet of [paper](#paper) or [newspaper](#newspaper), usually the simple [boat](#boat) shape worn by children and decorators. Improvised [headgear](#headgear) rather than a real hat.

entries.name: guan_hat
entries.description: A formal Chinese cap covering the whole top of the head, worn with court [dress](#dress) and once a [badge](#badge) of official rank. A smaller cap covering only the [topknot](#topknot) is a different garment.

entries.name: ichimegasa
entries.description: A woven straw [hat](#hat) with a blunt knob rising from its centre, worn by noblewomen in [old](#old) Japan. A [veil](#veil) hung from the whole brim and fell about as far as the waist.

entries.name: gat_(hat)
entries.description: A Korean [hat](#hat) of black horsehair [gauze](#gauze) stretched over a [bamboo](#bamboo) frame, cylindrical with a wide flat brim and worn by noblemen in historical settings. Colour carried meaning: white for [mourning](#mourning), red for [military](#military) officials.

entries.name: bear_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) built to look like a bear's head, small rounded ears [standing](#standing) on top and sometimes a muzzle across the brow. It is usually soft and plush.

entries.name: conical_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) that narrows to a point, whether a witch's [tall](#tall) cone or a wide woven [farming](#farming) hat. The [silhouette](#silhouette) is what counts, not the material.

entries.name: red_bonnet
entries.description: A red brimmed cap tied under the chin with a [ribbon](#ribbon), [sitting](#sitting) close around the face. Carries a period or doll-like flavor, common in lolita and Christmas outfits.

entries.name: phrygian_cap
entries.description: A soft conical cap whose peak flops forward over the [crown](#crown), made of [cloth](#cloth) rather than anything stiff. Long a symbol of liberty and a [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits; a [nightcap](#nightcap) hangs longer and ends in a [tassel](#tassel).

entries.name: cavalier_hat
entries.description: A broad-brimmed seventeenth-century [hat](#hat), usually [carrying](#carrying) an oversized [plume](#plume), with one side of the brim often [pinned](#pinned) up to the [crown](#crown). Known too as a musketeer hat; the [tricorne](#tricorne) eventually replaced it.

entries.name: frog_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) shaped as a [frog](#frog) or bearing its face and bulging eyes. Worn as a cute accessory on its own, not as part of a full [animal](#animal) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: flat_top_chef_hat
entries.description: A cook's toque whose puffed [crown](#crown) has been squared off level, [giving](#giving) it a boxy [outline](#outline). Otherwise the same [tall](#tall) white [kitchen](#kitchen) [hat](#hat).

entries.name: pot_on_head
entries.description: A [cooking](#cooking) pot worn upside down over the [skull](#skull) like a makeshift [helmet](#helmet). Usually [comic](#comic), or part of a scrappy improvised outfit.

entries.name: skull-shaped_hat
entries.description: Headgear moulded to look like a [skull](#skull), made of [cloth](#cloth), plastic or [leather](#leather). An actual [bone](#bone) skull worn on the head is [skull_on_head](#skull_on_head) instead.

entries.name: mini_santa_hat
entries.description: A doll-sized red and white Christmas [hat](#hat), [pinned](#pinned) or clipped into the hair rather than pulled down over the head.

entries.name: food-themed_hat
entries.description: Headwear cut into the shape of something edible, from a [burger](#burger) cap to a [mushroom](#mushroom) [crown](#crown). The whole [hat](#hat) takes the form rather than [carrying](#carrying) a small charm.

entries.name: flower_hat
entries.description: An outsized blossom worn on the head in place of a [hat](#hat), its [petals](#petals) doing the work of a brim. An ordinary hat with a [flower](#flower) [pinned](#pinned) to it does not qualify.

entries.name: penguin_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) shaped like a [penguin](#penguin) or its head, the [beak](#beak) [sitting](#sitting) over the [forehead](#forehead) and flipper flaps often [hanging](#hanging) beside the ears.

entries.name: bird_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) modelled on a [bird](#bird), with a [beak](#beak), eyes or [wings](#wings) built into its shape. It sits somewhere between [costume](#costume) piece and novelty accessory.

entries.name: multiple_hats
entries.description: Two or more pieces of headwear on one character at once, stacked on the [crown](#crown) or perched separately about the head. A [hat](#hat) paired with a [hood](#hood), [helmet](#helmet) or [headdress](#headdress) qualifies.

entries.name: panda_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) built to look like a [panda](#panda), with round black ears [standing](#standing) up from a white [crown](#crown). The relative with an attached [cowl](#cowl) is [panda_hood](#panda_hood).

entries.name: pinstripe_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) covered in narrow parallel stripes, usually a [fedora](#fedora) or trilby matching a striped [suit](#suit). Gangster and jazz-age outfits reach for it.

entries.name: squid_hat
entries.description: Headwear shaped like a [squid](#squid), its mantle covering the [crown](#crown) with [tentacles](#tentacles) [hanging](#hanging) down the sides. A novelty piece rather than genuine clothing.

entries.name: character_hat
entries.description: Headwear modelled on a particular character, with its face, ears or colours worked into the shape. Theme parks and [mascot](#mascot) [merchandise](#merchandise) supply most of them.

entries.name: jack-o'-lantern_hat_ornament
entries.description: A carved [pumpkin](#pumpkin) fixed to a [hat](#hat) as decoration, [pinned](#pinned) to the brim or tucked into the band. Witch hats carry it most often.

entries.name: picture_hat
entries.description: An elaborate wide-brimmed [hat](#hat) for women, worn with a [gown](#gown) or at formal occasions and usually loaded with flowers, [feathers](#feathers) or [ribbon](#ribbon). Its [outline](#outline) resembles a [sun](#sun) hat, but it is ornamental rather than practical.

entries.name: floating_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) suspended in the air instead of [resting](#resting) on the head. It may hover by design, or simply have lifted off because the wearer is [falling](#falling), leaping or hovering.

entries.name: oversized_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) far too big for the head under it, often [sliding](#sliding) down over the eyes. Common on witches and on small characters wearing something borrowed.

entries.name: boonie_hat
entries.description: A soft wide-brimmed [field](#field) [hat](#hat) worn by troops in [hot](#hot) climates. It resembles a [bucket](#bucket) hat, but the brim is broader and holds a stiffer, flatter shape.

entries.name: food-themed_hat_ornament
entries.description: A small food-shaped decoration fixed onto a [hat](#hat). It stands in for the many [fruit](#fruit) and sweet ornaments that have [no](#no) [tag](#tag) of their own.

entries.name: hat_bobbles
entries.description: Round pom-poms or [hanging](#hanging) balls attached to headwear, usually on cords at the sides of a knitted cap or [hood](#hood). They [swing](#swing) about when the wearer moves.

entries.name: pumpkin_on_head
entries.description: A [pumpkin](#pumpkin) [resting](#resting) on top of a character's head while the head itself stays visible underneath. When the [gourd](#gourd) replaces the head entirely, pumpkin_head is the [tag](#tag) to use instead.

entries.name: fez_hat
entries.description: A short brimless felt cylinder, most often red, with a [tassel](#tassel) [swinging](#swinging) from the flat top. Associated with the Ottoman world and still worn around the Mediterranean.

entries.name: snowflake_hat_ornament
entries.description: A snowflake-shaped decoration fixed to a [hat](#hat), whether [pinned](#pinned) to the band or set at the front. Common on [winter](#winter) caps and [witch](#witch) hats alike.

entries.name: pumpkin_hat_ornament
entries.description: A small pumpkin-shaped decoration fixed to a [hat](#hat) rather than worn loose in the hair. Where the shape is carved into a face instead, use the [jack-o'-lantern](#jack-o'-lantern) version.

entries.name: zhuang_hat
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) [headdress](#headdress) worn by an ethnic minority group of southern China, commonly [folded](#folded) over on itself and finished with a [tassel](#tassel) or [hanging](#hanging) strips of [fabric](#fabric). Its [outline](#outline) ranges from arched to triangular or horned.

entries.name: eggshell_hat
entries.description: Half an [eggshell](#eggshell) worn as a cap, its jagged rim [resting](#resting) around the head. A cartoon look, often on somebody freshly hatched.

entries.name: eye_on_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) [carrying](#carrying) an eye: printed, [stitched](#stitched), or set in as an actual [eyeball](#eyeball) looking out from the headwear. Common on [witch](#witch) hats and other odd or occult designs.

entries.name: chaperon_hat
entries.description: Medieval European headwear wrapped around a stuffed [fabric](#fabric) [ring](#ring), from which a thick floppy drape hangs down one side. Shapes range from a small cap to something close to a [turban](#turban), and a feather is a common addition.

entries.name: chinese_hat
entries.description: The conical straw or [bamboo](#bamboo) [hat](#hat) of East Asia, tied under the chin and [shedding](#shedding) both [sun](#sun) and [rain](#rain). Worn by farmers and travellers, and used to finish Chinese-styled [fantasy](#fantasy) costumes.

entries.name: tall_hat
entries.description: Headwear with an unusually high [crown](#crown), such as a stovepipe [hat](#hat), a [tall](#tall) chef's toque or an exaggerated wizard's cone. The [height](#height) itself is the point, whatever the shape.

entries.name: dog_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) made to look like a [dog](#dog), ears drooping at the sides and often a [snout](#snout) over the brow. Novelty headwear rather than real ears.

entries.name: helmet
entries.description: Protective [headgear](#headgear) covering the [skull](#skull), in any style: combat, [motorcycle](#motorcycle), [construction](#construction), sports or [science](#science) fiction. Shape follows era and purpose.

entries.name: baseball_cap
entries.description: A soft-crowned cap fronted by a long stiff bill, curved or flat, usually with an adjustable [strap](#strap) at the [back](#back). Worn bill-forward against the [sun](#sun), but just as often turned around or cocked [sideways](#sideways); add [backwards_hat](#backwards_hat) for the reversed wear.

entries.name: peaked_cap
entries.description: A stiff uniform cap with a flat [crown](#crown), a band and a short visor, worn by armed forces, [police](#police), pilots and other uniformed [staff](#staff), usually with a [badge](#badge) at the front.

entries.name: military_hat
entries.description: Any cap belonging to a [military](#military) uniform, such as a peaked cap, [field](#field) cap, Mao cap or sailor's dixie-cup [hat](#hat). Helmets are excluded from this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: nurse_cap
entries.description: The small [folded](#folded) white cap that went with the [old](#old) nursing [dress](#dress), sometimes bearing a [cross](#cross). It was meant to hold the hair [back](#back) and disappeared from real wards once scrubs took over, but it remains the quickest way to signal a [nurse](#nurse).

entries.name: visor_cap
entries.description: A brim without a [crown](#crown), held on by a band or elastic [strap](#strap), as worn for [tennis](#tennis) or [golf](#golf). The stiff-brimmed [peaked_cap](#peaked_cap) of [police](#police) and [military](#military) uniforms is a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: beanie
entries.description: A snug knitted cap that hugs the [skull](#skull), worn either [cuffed](#cuffed) up at the brim or with the [crown](#crown) left slack to flop over. Some have a pom pom on top or flaps over the ears; also called a tuque.

entries.name: cabbie_hat
entries.description: A rounded, full-bodied cap with a stiff front peak, panelled and buttoned at the [crown](#crown) — also called a newsboy cap. Fuller than a flat cap, and unlike a [beret](#beret) it has a visor.

entries.name: sailor_hat
entries.description: The round, flat, brimless cap of a navy [sailor](#sailor), often with a [ribbon](#ribbon) naming the [ship](#ship). Tagged with [hat](#hat).

entries.name: flat_cap
entries.description: A soft cap with a short stiff brim and a low [crown](#crown) pressed flat on top. Easy to confuse with the cabbie [hat](#hat), [beret](#beret), peaked cap and [baseball](#baseball) cap.

entries.name: garrison_cap
entries.description: A soft foldable cap with flat sides and a creased [crown](#crown) that slopes [back](#back) to a parting, [reading](#reading) as a [triangle](#triangle) from the front. A standard piece of many [military](#military) and service uniforms.

entries.name: backwards_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), usually a [baseball](#baseball) cap, worn with the peak [pointing](#pointing) behind. Tag the particular hat alongside it.

entries.name: assault_visor
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) or plated visor built into a [helmet](#helmet) or a mecha's head, a science-fiction [staple](#staple). It is part of the helmet rather than eyewear; a [screen](#screen) worn over the eyes is [head-mounted_display](#head-mounted_display).

entries.name: unworn_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) recently removed sits visible in the scene, tucked under an arm or set on the ground. A helmet-wearing character shown with [no](#no) helmet anywhere in view is [no_headwear](#no_headwear) instead.

entries.name: horned_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) decorated with [horns](#horns), the stereotypical [viking](#viking) or [barbarian](#barbarian) shape. Other horned head coverings take [horned_headwear](#horned_headwear) instead.

entries.name: gas_mask
entries.description: A sealed full-face covering with filters that shields the [nose](#nose), mouth and eyes from fumes and airborne [poison](#poison). A version leaving the eyes bare is a [respirator](#respirator) instead.

entries.name: police_hat
entries.description: The peaked cap of a [police](#police) uniform, usually [dark](#dark) blue with a [badge](#badge) on the front. Tag [hat](#hat) and police alongside it.

entries.name: nightcap
entries.description: A soft [cloth](#cloth) cap worn in [bed](#bed), generally along with pyjamas. Its long floppy point [can](#can) look much like a [santa_hat](#santa_hat).

entries.name: shako_cap
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), cylindrical [military](#military) cap with a visor, a [badge](#badge) or [plate](#plate) at the front, and often a [plume](#plume) or pompom on top, as worn by [marching](#marching) bands. Do not confuse it with a [top_hat](#top_hat).

entries.name: space_helmet
entries.description: A rounded, [transparent](#transparent) [helmet](#helmet) of the kind astronauts wear, typically sealed to a [spacesuit](#spacesuit). Tag it whether worn or simply carried.

entries.name: winged_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) with [wings](#wings) mounted on both sides, an image tracing [back](#back) to depictions of the Greek god Mercury and later applied to Vikings and Norse gods. Valkyries and other Norse-themed characters wear it often; [tag](#tag) helmet as [well](#well).

entries.name: combat_helmet
entries.description: A modern [helmet](#helmet) built to stop bullets and fragments, as worn by soldiers, [police](#police) units and reporters in [war](#war) zones, usually with a chin [strap](#strap) and a [cloth](#cloth) [cover](#cover). Historical and [fantasy](#fantasy) [headgear](#headgear) is just helmet.

entries.name: dixie_cup_hat
entries.description: The white sailor's cap of a naval enlisted uniform, its brim turned up all round so it sits like an upended [paper](#paper) [cup](#cup). Some versions carry a stripe along the brim.

entries.name: xiao_guan_(headdress)
entries.description: A small Chinese cap for men that fits over a [topknot](#topknot), secured by a [hairpin](#hairpin) through it or a cord under the chin. Its shape varies widely, but it never covers more than the knot of hair itself.

entries.name: red_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) in red, whether [military](#military), sports, [motorcycle](#motorcycle) or [fantasy](#fantasy) armour. Tag the helmet type alongside the colour.

entries.name: blue_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) in blue, for sport, motorcycling, the [military](#military) or [fantasy](#fantasy) armour. Which kind it is must be tagged separately.

entries.name: motorcycle_helmet
entries.description: A rider's [helmet](#helmet), full-face or open-faced with a visor. Even where it wraps the whole head it is protective gear rather than a piece of armour.

entries.name: black_helmet
entries.description: A protective [helmet](#helmet) in black, covering anything from [medieval](#medieval) [plate](#plate) to a [motorcycle](#motorcycle) [shell](#shell) or modern combat gear. Only the colour is recorded; the shape is left to other tags.

entries.name: kepi
entries.description: A [military](#military) cap with a flat circular top, straight sides and a short stiff peak. It is most closely tied to French forces and to armies of the later nineteenth century.

entries.name: chin_strap
entries.description: A [strap](#strap), or a pair of ties, fastened under the chin to hold a [hat](#hat), [bonnet](#bonnet) or [helmet](#helmet) in place. Tag it beside whatever headwear it secures.

entries.name: hard_hat
entries.description: A rigid safety [helmet](#helmet) of reinforced plastic, most often yellow, worn on [building](#building) sites. Japanese ones are usually drawn [carrying](#carrying) a green band and a [cross](#cross) on the front.

entries.name: swim_cap
entries.description: A snug rubber or [fabric](#fabric) cap that covers the hair for [swimming](#swimming), keeping it dry and [cutting](#cutting) drag through the [water](#water).

entries.name: chinstrap
entries.description: The [strap](#strap) [running](#running) under the [jaw](#jaw) that keeps a [helmet](#helmet), cap or [hat](#hat) from [sliding](#sliding) off. Common on [military](#military) helmets, [riding](#riding) hats and sports gear, and often still visible when the headwear itself is [cropped](#cropped) out.

entries.name: helmet_over_eyes
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) has slipped or been pushed down far enough to hide the eyes while mouth and chin stay clear. Often a joke with an oversized [helm](#helm).

entries.name: white_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) colored white, whether for [construction](#construction), motorcycling, the [military](#military) or [fantasy](#fantasy) [armor](#armor). Only the color is asserted here, not the type.

entries.name: aviator_cap
entries.description: A close-fitting [leather](#leather) [flying](#flying) [helmet](#helmet) with ear flaps and a chin [strap](#strap), worn against [cold](#cold) and [wind](#wind) in open cockpits and [racing](#racing) cars. Enclosed cockpits ended its practical life and hard helmets replaced it.

entries.name: animal_helmet
entries.description: Headgear built as a creature's head, or at least fitted with false ears on the [crown](#crown). It ranges from soft cartoonish shells to fully sculpted [animal](#animal) heads.

entries.name: stahlhelm
entries.description: The flared German steel combat [helmet](#helmet) of both world wars, its [skirt](#skirt) [sweeping](#sweeping) down over the ears and [neck](#neck). It replaced the earlier [spiked](#spiked) [pickelhaube](#pickelhaube) and was later adopted by several other armies.

entries.name: female_service_cap
entries.description: The women's answer to a peaked uniform cap, its sides or [back](#back) [folded](#folded) up so the brim reads flat and wide. Worn by flight attendants, [train](#train) [staff](#staff) and servicewomen.

entries.name: green_helmet
entries.description: A green [helmet](#helmet), whether [military](#military), sporting or part of a [suit](#suit) of armour. The shell's colour decides the [tag](#tag), regardless of visor or [crest](#crest).

entries.name: baseball_helmet
entries.description: The hard cap worn by batters and base runners against a [ball](#ball) travelling fast, moulded with a flap over one ear or both. It carries the team's colours and mark.

entries.name: knit_hat
entries.description: A soft cap knitted from [wool](#wool) or synthetic [yarn](#yarn) to keep the head warm, tapering over the [crown](#crown). Cuffed beanies and pompom-topped versions both count.

entries.name: hockey_mask
entries.description: The flat white face [guard](#guard) pierced with round and triangular holes once worn by ice-hockey goalkeepers. Caged helmets replaced it in the sport, but it survives as the face of a slasher-film killer.

entries.name: tank_helmet
entries.description: The padded [headgear](#headgear) worn by armored vehicle crews, meant to [cushion](#cushion) the [skull](#skull) against a [cramped](#cramped) steel [interior](#interior) rather than stop a [bullet](#bullet). Shape and padding vary by country and era.

entries.name: spiked_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) [carrying](#carrying) one or more [spikes](#spikes), ranging from the single point of the historical German [pickelhaube](#pickelhaube) to [fantasy](#fantasy) helms bristling all over.

entries.name: pilot_helmet
entries.description: The hard flight [helmet](#helmet) worn by aircrew, generally fitted with a visor, a [headset](#headset) and mountings for a [mask](#mask) or night-vision gear. It replaced the soft [leather](#leather) [flying](#flying) cap of earlier decades.

entries.name: pickelhaube
entries.description: A [spiked](#spiked) [leather](#leather) [helmet](#helmet) with a metal point rising from the [crown](#crown), worn by Prussian and Imperial German troops and still used ceremonially in a few countries. The spike is what identifies it.

entries.name: pink_helmet
entries.description: A protective [helmet](#helmet) in pink, whether for [riding](#riding), [construction](#construction), sport or combat. Nothing but the colour distinguishes it.

entries.name: grey_helmet
entries.description: A grey [helmet](#helmet), [military](#military), sporting or fantastical. The colour of the [shell](#shell) decides it, whatever visor or [crest](#crest) it carries.

entries.name: bicycle_helmet
entries.description: A light vented [shell](#shell) strapped under the chin and shaped for cycling, sometimes with a small visor. It turns up with sports and commuting outfits, usually near a [bicycle](#bicycle).

entries.name: unworn_swim_cap
entries.description: A swim cap appears in the picture off the head, held in a hand, [resting](#resting) on a [poolside](#poolside) [bench](#bench) or [hanging](#hanging) from a pair of [goggles](#goggles).

entries.name: no_headgear
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet), [hat](#hat) or [headpiece](#headpiece) belonging to a character's usual look has been left off, leaving the head bare. It marks a departure from the standard design.

entries.name: brodie_helmet
entries.description: A shallow steel [helmet](#helmet) with a domed [crown](#crown) and a broad flat brim, worn by British and Commonwealth troops through both world wars. Its [silhouette](#silhouette) borrows from the [medieval](#medieval) [kettle](#kettle) [hat](#hat).

entries.name: field_cap
entries.description: A soft [military](#military) cap with a flat top and a stiff rounded bill, somewhere between a [baseball](#baseball) cap and a [kepi](#kepi). Worn on duty when [no](#no) [helmet](#helmet) is called for.

entries.name: unworn_headgear
entries.description: Head equipment a character habitually wears is off their head but still shown in the picture. Covers rigs and pieces that fall outside ordinary hats or hair ornaments.

entries.name: purple_helmet
entries.description: A purple hard [helmet](#helmet), whether [military](#military), sporting, [riding](#riding), or part of a [suit](#suit) of armour. Colour is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: earflap_beanie
entries.description: A knitted cap with long flaps [hanging](#hanging) down over the ears, sometimes finished with ties or a pom pom. Warmer than a [plain](#plain) [beanie](#beanie) and firmly [winter](#winter) wear.

entries.name: fishbowl_helmet
entries.description: A clear rounded [dome](#dome) enclosing the whole head like an upturned [glass](#glass) [bowl](#bowl). The standard look for retro [space](#space) suits and [old](#old) [diving](#diving) rigs.

entries.name: gold_helmet
entries.description: A [helm](#helm) of [gold](#gold) or gilded metal, closed or open-faced. Mythic warriors, ceremonial guards and ornately built machines wear one.

entries.name: yellow_helmet
entries.description: A yellow [helmet](#helmet) of any sort, whether for [construction](#construction) work, sport, [riding](#riding) or armour. Only the colour is being noted.

entries.name: mining_helmet
entries.description: A hard [hat](#hat) fitted with a [lamp](#lamp) on the front for [working](#working) [underground](#underground). That [headlamp](#headlamp) is what sets it apart from an ordinary hard hat.

entries.name: paper_kabuto
entries.description: A [samurai](#samurai) [helmet](#helmet) [folded](#folded) from a single [square](#square) of [paper](#paper), with two [horns](#horns) [sweeping](#sweeping) up at the front. Tied to Children's Day and generally worn by a small [child](#child).

entries.name: animal_ears_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) with false [creature](#creature) ears rising from the [shell](#shell). The ears belong to the [headgear](#headgear) rather than growing from the wearer, which is what separates it from real [animal_ears](#animal_ears).

entries.name: gakuseibou
entries.description: An old-fashioned peaked cap for Japanese schoolboys, cut much like a [military](#military) [hat](#hat). Normally worn as part of a [gakuran](#gakuran) outfit.

entries.name: diving_helmet
entries.description: A sealed [helmet](#helmet) worn with a [diving](#diving) [suit](#suit) and fed air down a [hose](#hose). The [old](#old) rounded brass sort belongs under standard_diving_dress.

entries.name: brown_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) in brown, of any kind: combat, sports or [fantasy](#fantasy). The colour describes the [shell](#shell) rather than any attached decoration.

entries.name: broken_helmet
entries.description: A [helmet](#helmet) cracked, dented or partly [torn](#torn) away. The wearer's face often shows through the damage.

entries.name: woollen_cap
entries.description: A knitted cap pulled down over the head, sometimes with a [folded](#folded) brim or a bobble on top. It belongs to [winter](#winter) outfits and [casual](#casual) wear alike.

entries.name: fire_helmet
entries.description: A firefighter's hard [helmet](#helmet), often with a long rear brim or a [hanging](#hanging) flap shielding the [neck](#neck) from heat. A [badge](#badge) or crew number frequently sits at the front.

entries.name: american_football_helmet
entries.description: The hard [shell](#shell) worn by gridiron players, fronted by a metal face [cage](#cage) and sometimes a tinted visor. Older [leather](#leather) versions appear in period pictures.

entries.name: chullo
entries.description: A pointed Andean knitted cap with long earflaps that tie under the chin, worked in [alpaca](#alpaca) or [llama](#llama) [wool](#wool). Usually [patterned](#patterned) in bright geometric bands.

entries.name: mini_shako_cap
entries.description: A tiny copy of the [tall](#tall), cylindrical military-band cap, worn tilted in the hair as an ornament. Common on [idol](#idol) and marching-band [costume](#costume) designs.

entries.name: m1_helmet
entries.description: The domed steel combat [helmet](#helmet) worn by American forces from the Second World War until the mid-1980s. It is usually drawn under a [cloth](#cloth) [cover](#cover) or wrapped in netting.

entries.name: orange_helmet
entries.description: An orange [helmet](#helmet) on the head, covering sports gear, [construction](#construction) hard hats and armour alike.

entries.name: chajinbou
entries.description: A brimless cylindrical cap with a flat [crown](#crown), worn by the host at an Edo-period [tea](#tea) ceremony. It also goes by rikyubou, after the tea master who made it famous.

entries.name: biretta
entries.description: A stiff [square](#square) cap with three ridges rising from the [crown](#crown), worn by Catholic clergy. Its colour marks rank: scarlet for cardinals, red for bishops, black for priests and seminarians.

entries.name: hair_net
entries.description: A fine [mesh](#mesh) cap [holding](#holding) the hair flat and contained, worn in kitchens, canteens and factories. Functional headwear with [no](#no) decorative purpose.

entries.name: hood
entries.description: A covering for the head and [neck](#neck), either a separate piece or sewn onto a [cloak](#cloak), [coat](#coat) or top. Add [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) to say whether it is actually over the head.

entries.name: mask
entries.description: Any covering worn over the face, from surgical and [cloth](#cloth) mouth masks to [festival](#festival), [gas](#gas) and [carnival](#carnival) masks. Paper held over the head is [paper_on_head](#paper_on_head), and where a mask rests off the face there are tags such as [mask_on_head](#mask_on_head).

entries.name: hood_down
entries.description: A hooded garment is worn with the [hood](#hood) [lying](#lying) [back](#back) on the shoulders instead of over the head, and the hood itself must be visible. If a character normally drawn hooded has none at all, [no_headwear](#no_headwear) may fit better; a hood in the act of being thrown back is removing_hood.

entries.name: veil
entries.description: A sheer piece of [fabric](#fabric) worn over the head or face, as in bridal wear, [mourning](#mourning) [dress](#dress) or certain religious and [fantasy](#fantasy) costumes. Add the more specific kind such as [bridal_veil](#bridal_veil) where it applies.

entries.name: hood_up
entries.description: The [hood](#hood) is pulled over the head, frequently shadowing the face. It may belong to a [hoodie](#hoodie), [cloak](#cloak), [cape](#cape) or [coat](#coat), and is the counterpart of [hood_down](#hood_down).

entries.name: mouth_mask
entries.description: A covering over the lower face alone: a surgical [mask](#mask), a [cloth](#cloth) pandemic mask, the wrapped lower face of a [ninja](#ninja). Skincare sheet masks belong to a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: animal_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) made to look like a [creature](#creature), normally with a face on the [crown](#crown) and ears attached. One that carries ears and nothing more is [animal_ear_hood](#animal_ear_hood).

entries.name: bandana
entries.description: A [square](#square) or strip of [cloth](#cloth) tied over the hair, across the lower face, or knotted at the [neck](#neck), worn for protection or as decoration. Cooks, delinquents and bikers wear one, as do students psyching themselves up for exams.

entries.name: mask_on_head
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) [resting](#resting) on the [forehead](#forehead) or the top of the head with the face left bare. Common with [fox](#fox) and [festival](#festival) masks worn as decoration. Implies mask.

entries.name: bridal_veil
entries.description: The sheer [veil](#veil) a [bride](#bride) wears with her [dress](#dress), hung from a [tiara](#tiara), [comb](#comb) or [flower](#flower) [crown](#crown) over the hair or across the face. Add veil, and [wedding_dress](#wedding_dress) or bride where they apply.

entries.name: headscarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) worn over the head and knotted under the chin or behind, in the manner of a babushka, a [kerchief](#kerchief) or a [hijab](#hijab).

entries.name: nun_headdress
entries.description: The veiled [coif](#coif) of a nun's [habit](#habit), [wrapping](#wrapping) the hair and closing around the face. Frequently drawn on its own above clothing that has nothing else religious about it.

entries.name: white_veil
entries.description: A sheer white [cloth](#cloth) worn over the head or face. Reserve [bridal_veil](#bridal_veil) for a [bride](#bride) or [wedding](#wedding) scene; this [tag](#tag) covers nuns, priestesses, dancers, and any other white [veil](#veil).

entries.name: black_mask
entries.description: A black [mask](#mask) over part or all of the face, whether a domino mask, a [fabric](#fabric) mouth mask, a ninja's wrap or a masquerade piece. Add the specific kind alongside it.

entries.name: surgical_mask
entries.description: A [pleated](#pleated) [cloth](#cloth) or [paper](#paper) [mask](#mask) covering the mouth and [nose](#nose), the type worn in hospitals and commonly in Japan when someone is ill. Also a [delinquent](#delinquent) and [yakuza](#yakuza) look. Implies [mouth_mask](#mouth_mask).

entries.name: white_headdress
entries.description: A white [headdress](#headdress), most often referring to the frilled [maid](#maid) headdress. Add [maid_headdress](#maid_headdress) specifically when that's what it is.

entries.name: cat_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) on a [hoodie](#hoodie), [cloak](#cloak) or [jacket](#jacket) with fake [cat](#cat) ears sewn onto it. The feline case of the [animal](#animal) hood.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) with fur lining its [opening](#opening), as on parkas and [heavy](#heavy) [winter](#winter) coats. Whether the hood is up or down is worth tagging separately.

entries.name: rabbit_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) with fake [rabbit](#rabbit) ears sewn onto it, attached to a [hoodie](#hoodie), [cloak](#cloak), or [onesie](#onesie). Combine with [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) depending on how it is worn.

entries.name: black_veil
entries.description: A black [veil](#veil) [hanging](#hanging) over the head or the face. Mourning is the usual occasion, though a gothic bridal look uses it too.

entries.name: mouth_veil
entries.description: A [veil](#veil) hung across the mouth and sometimes the [nose](#nose), leaving the eyes clear. Common on [dancer](#dancer) and [desert](#desert) outfits.

entries.name: red_bandana
entries.description: A red [bandana](#bandana), tied over the hair, worn as a [headband](#headband), or knotted around the [neck](#neck). Where it also covers the lower face, combine with [mouth_mask](#mouth_mask) or [bandana_over_mouth](#bandana_over_mouth).

entries.name: turban
entries.description: Headwear made by winding a long strip of [cloth](#cloth) around the head, worn traditionally by Sikh men and women and across parts of the Middle East and South Asia. Also appears as an improvised [towel](#towel) wrap after [bathing](#bathing).

entries.name: oni_mask
entries.description: A horned [demon](#demon) face carved or moulded as a [mask](#mask), worn over the face or pushed up onto the head. Common on [ninja](#ninja), [festival](#festival) and Setsubun characters.

entries.name: red_hood
entries.description: A red [hood](#hood) over the head, most often as an allusion to Little Red Riding Hood. Applies to the hood of a [cloak](#cloak) or [cape](#cape) as [well](#well) as to a standalone hood.

entries.name: shark_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) shaped like a shark's head, with the wearer's face framed inside the open jaws. Best known from the Bape [shark](#shark) [hoodie](#hoodie) and closely tied to Gawr Gura's look.

entries.name: skull_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) modelled on a [skull](#skull), human or [animal](#animal), worn over the face. Tag beside mask.

entries.name: black_hood
entries.description: A black [hood](#hood) covering or framing the head, attached to a [cloak](#cloak) or [hoodie](#hoodie) or worn on its own. Note whether it is up or down with the matching [tag](#tag).

entries.name: respirator
entries.description: A half-face filter [mask](#mask) covering the [nose](#nose) and mouth against [dust](#dust) or fumes, as worn by painters or in [industrial](#industrial) scenes. If the mask also shields the eyes it is a [gas_mask](#gas_mask) instead.

entries.name: red_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) in red covering all or part of the face, from [festival](#festival) and [demon](#demon) masks to surgical-style ones. Tag the mask's kind as [well](#well) where a [tag](#tag) for it exists.

entries.name: white_hood
entries.description: A white [hood](#hood), attached to a [cloak](#cloak), [robe](#robe) or [hoodie](#hoodie), worn up over the head or left [hanging](#hanging) [back](#back).

entries.name: mask_around_neck
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) [hanging](#hanging) at the [neck](#neck) instead of over the face, as when a mouth mask has been dragged all the way down. Implies mask.

entries.name: half_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) covering roughly half the face, typically the upper half around the eyes, as in a masquerade mask. A mask over the mouth and [jaw](#jaw) is [mouth_mask](#mouth_mask) instead.

entries.name: coif
entries.description: A close cap of [medieval](#medieval) cut covering the [crown](#crown), [back](#back) and sides of the head, worn by men and women alike and sometimes hung with lappets. The padded cap under [mail](#mail) and the white piece beneath a nun's [veil](#veil) are both this.

entries.name: animal_ear_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) with false [creature](#creature) ears [standing](#standing) up from the [crown](#crown), common on hoodies and [kigurumi](#kigurumi). Where the whole hood is shaped as an animal's head, use [animal_hood](#animal_hood).

entries.name: transparent_veil
entries.description: A [veil](#veil) of [gauze](#gauze) or fine netting worn over the head or face, thin enough that the features behind it stay readable. Turns up on brides, dancers and [mourning](#mourning) outfits alike.

entries.name: purple_veil
entries.description: A purple [veil](#veil) worn over the head or face, as on a [bride](#bride), [dancer](#dancer), or [priestess](#priestess). Combine with veil.

entries.name: ninja_mask
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) [mask](#mask) covering the mouth and [jaw](#jaw) in the manner of a shinobi. A mask [hiding](#hiding) one side of the face is [half_mask](#half_mask) instead.

entries.name: blue_veil
entries.description: A blue [veil](#veil) [hanging](#hanging) from the head or from a [headdress](#headdress) across the face, hair or shoulders, usually of thin [fabric](#fabric). Dancers, priestesses and bridal [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits wear them most.

entries.name: bird_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) with [bird](#bird) features worn over the face, from a long-beaked plague doctor's to a [festival](#festival) or [tribal](#tribal) design. Add mask alongside it.

entries.name: blue_hood
entries.description: A blue [hood](#hood) framing or covering the head, attached to a [cloak](#cloak) or [hoodie](#hoodie) or worn by itself. Note [hood_up](#hood_up) or [hood_down](#hood_down) alongside it.

entries.name: masked
entries.description: A person or [animal](#animal) actually wearing a [mask](#mask) over the face. It holds only while the mask is on, so one taken off or pushed aside takes the placement tags instead.

entries.name: blue_bandana
entries.description: A blue [bandana](#bandana) knotted around the head, the [neck](#neck) or an arm. Its [folded](#folded) [triangle](#triangle) of [cloth](#cloth) sets it apart from a [hat](#hat) or a [scarf](#scarf).

entries.name: penguin_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) made to look like a penguin's head, generally with a [beak](#beak) and a pair of eyes on top.

entries.name: two-tone_veil
entries.description: A [veil](#veil) in exactly two colours, commonly a sheer body with a contrasting edge or a layered pair of shades. Bridal and ceremonial headwear both take this form.

entries.name: bear_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) with rounded [bear](#bear) ears sewn onto it, pulled up over the head. Hoodies, coats and [kigurumi](#kigurumi) all come in this form.

entries.name: wataboushi
entries.description: The white [hood](#hood) a [bride](#bride) wears over her hair at a traditional Japanese [wedding](#wedding). It swallows the hairstyle far more completely than the flatter tsunokakushi band.

entries.name: green_bandana
entries.description: A green [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) [folded](#folded) and knotted over the hair, round the [neck](#neck) or across the brow. Cooks, delinquents and outdoor workers wear one.

entries.name: panda_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) shaped like a panda's head, ears and [dark](#dark) eye patches included. One of the animal-hood [family](#family), usually attached to a [jacket](#jacket) or a [onesie](#onesie).

entries.name: black_bandana
entries.description: A black [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) knotted over the head or worn as a band across the brow. It [can](#can) also sit round the [neck](#neck) or be pulled up over the lower face.

entries.name: broken_mask
entries.description: A worn [mask](#mask) that is cracked or has pieces missing from it. Part of the face beneath is generally revealed through the break.

entries.name: mask_over_one_eye
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) covering half the face, [hiding](#hiding) one eye while the other stays clear. Common on half-masks and lopsided villain designs.

entries.name: white_bandana
entries.description: A white [bandana](#bandana) tied over the hair, wrapped around the [forehead](#forehead), or knotted at the [neck](#neck). Cooks, athletes and rough-edged characters wear them most.

entries.name: detached_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) worn as a piece of its own, with [no](#no) [jacket](#jacket), [cloak](#cloak) or [shirt](#shirt) attached behind it. It covers head and shoulders and stops there.

entries.name: orange_bandana
entries.description: An orange [bandana](#bandana), most often knotted over the hair or across the [forehead](#forehead), sometimes worn at the throat instead.

entries.name: masquerade_mask
entries.description: A decorative half [mask](#mask) over the eyes and [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose), tied on or held up on a [stick](#stick). Belongs to [ball](#ball) and [carnival](#carnival) scenes and is often trimmed with [feathers](#feathers), [lace](#lace) or gilt. Implies mask.

entries.name: bag_over_head
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) has been pulled right down over the head so that the face is hidden entirely. It is not to be mixed up with [bag_on_head](#bag_on_head), where the bag merely perches on top.

entries.name: balaclava
entries.description: A knitted [hood](#hood) covering the whole head and [neck](#neck), leaving only the eyes, or the eyes and mouth, uncovered. Soldiers, tactical [police](#police) and [masked](#masked) criminals all wear one.

entries.name: character_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) cut to resemble a character, with ears, [horns](#horns) or a printed face across the [crown](#crown). It normally comes attached to a [jacket](#jacket) or a kigurumi-style garment.

entries.name: blue_mask
entries.description: A face covering in blue, whether a half [mask](#mask), a full one or a themed piece. Only the colour is claimed, not what the mask depicts.

entries.name: green_hood
entries.description: A green [hood](#hood), drawn up over the head or fallen [back](#back) onto the shoulders. It may belong to a [cloak](#cloak), a [coat](#coat) or a hooded top.

entries.name: horned_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) shaped with [horns](#horns) worked into it, [giving](#giving) a demonic or beastly [outline](#outline). The wearer need not be horned themselves.

entries.name: yellow_bandana
entries.description: A yellow [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) worn as a [bandana](#bandana), knotted over the hair, across the [forehead](#forehead) or around the [neck](#neck). Nothing but the colour sets it apart from any other bandana.

entries.name: hijab
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) wrapped over the hair, ears and [neck](#neck) with the face left open, worn by Muslim women. A burqa covers the whole body instead, and the thick Japanese [winter](#winter) [hood](#hood) is a different garment again.

entries.name: orca_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) cut and coloured to look like an orca's head, with the white eye patches and often a dorsal fin on top. One of the [animal](#animal) hoods.

entries.name: white_bonnet
entries.description: A white [bonnet](#bonnet), a soft cap with a front brim tied under the chin. Worn by maids, nurses, babies and lolita-fashion characters.

entries.name: purple_hood
entries.description: A purple [hood](#hood) drawn up over the head, whether attached to a [cloak](#cloak) or a hooded top, or worn on its own. It may [shadow](#shadow) the face or sit [back](#back) on the shoulders.

entries.name: yellow_hood
entries.description: A yellow [hood](#hood) pulled up over the head, either attached to a garment or worn as a separate piece. The colour applies to the hood, not necessarily to the rest of the outfit.

entries.name: bandana_over_mouth
entries.description: A [bandana](#bandana) drawn up across the [nose](#nose) and mouth and knotted behind the head. Bandits, delinquents and anyone [working](#working) in [dust](#dust) are drawn wearing one this way.

entries.name: dog_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) with false [dog](#dog) ears sewn on, either part of a [jacket](#jacket) or a separate piece pulled over the head. The ears belong to the garment, not the wearer.

entries.name: red_veil
entries.description: A red length of sheer or opaque [cloth](#cloth) draped over the head and face. If it is the cloth worn by a [bride](#bride) at a Chinese [wedding](#wedding), the honggaitou [tag](#tag) belongs alongside it.

entries.name: pink_mask
entries.description: A face covering in pink, be it a masquerade piece, a surgical [mask](#mask) or part of a [costume](#costume). Only the colour distinguishes it from any other mask.

entries.name: pink_hood
entries.description: A pink [hood](#hood), sewn onto a garment or worn on its own over the head. Whether it is up or [hanging](#hanging) behind the shoulders does not change the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: wolf_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) cut with [wolf](#wolf) ears and often a muzzle shape across the brow, attached to a [coat](#coat) or [costume](#costume). The wearer's own face still shows through underneath it.

entries.name: brown_hood
entries.description: A brown [hood](#hood), attached to a [cloak](#cloak), [coat](#coat) or [robe](#robe), or worn as a separate piece. Pulled up it usually throws the face into [shadow](#shadow).

entries.name: cow_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) [carrying](#carrying) [cow](#cow) ears, [horns](#horns) or both, often in patched hide colours. Usually the head end of a cow-themed outfit.

entries.name: grey_hood
entries.description: A grey [hood](#hood), raised over the head or [lying](#lying) [back](#back) across the shoulders. It may belong to a [cloak](#cloak), a [coat](#coat) or a hooded top.

entries.name: print_bandana
entries.description: A [square](#square) [cloth](#cloth) [carrying](#carrying) a printed pattern, tied over the head or knotted at the [neck](#neck). Paisley is the classic [choice](#choice), but any motif counts.

entries.name: luchador_mask
entries.description: The close-fitting [hood](#hood) a [wrestler](#wrestler) wears to hide his identity, cut with openings for the eyes and mouth and [patterned](#patterned) in bold colours. It may be worn with the rest of the [costume](#costume) or on its own.

entries.name: purple_mask
entries.description: A face covering in purple, whether a small domino [mask](#mask), a full helm-like piece, or a [festival](#festival) mask. Colour alone is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: grey_veil
entries.description: A grey [veil](#veil) covering the head or face. Check that the [cloth](#cloth) is genuinely grey and not a white or black veil pushed off-colour by the lighting.

entries.name: lappet
entries.description: Long decorative flaps of [cloth](#cloth) [hanging](#hanging) from a [headpiece](#headpiece), singly or one at each side, like tails. Coverings that only wrap the ears belong to [hat](#hat) tags such as [ushanka](#ushanka).

entries.name: grey_mask
entries.description: A grey [mask](#mask) worn over part or all of the face. Only the mask's own colour is being recorded.

entries.name: keffiyeh
entries.description: A [square](#square) Middle Eastern [cloth](#cloth), usually white with a black or red check, [folded](#folded) over the head or wound round the [neck](#neck) like a [scarf](#scarf). It may hang loose or be held down by a cord.

entries.name: tiger_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) with fake [tiger](#tiger) ears sewn on and stripe [markings](#markings) across it, part of a [jacket](#jacket), [onesie](#onesie) or [costume](#costume).

entries.name: hat_under_hood
entries.description: Two layers of headwear at once: a [hat](#hat) on the head with a [hood](#hood) drawn up over it. Typical of [winter](#winter) [dress](#dress) and cloaked travellers.

entries.name: hyottoko_mask
entries.description: A [comic](#comic) Japanese [mask](#mask) with a lopsided face and [lips](#lips) puckered to one side, tied in folklore to [fire](#fire) and its god. It is worn or carried at festivals, often beside the smiling female mask that partners it.

entries.name: frog_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) cut as a frog's head, with eyes on the [crown](#crown) and a wide mouth framing the wearer's face. Either sewn to a [jacket](#jacket) or worn as a standalone [animal](#animal) hood.

entries.name: purple_bandana
entries.description: A purple [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) tied over the head or knotted around the [neck](#neck). How it is worn is a separate detail from the [tag](#tag) itself.

entries.name: pink_bandana
entries.description: A [square](#square) of pink [cloth](#cloth) [folded](#folded) and knotted over the head, round the [neck](#neck) or on the arm. The same garment as any other [bandana](#bandana), differing only in colour.

entries.name: green_mask
entries.description: A green [mask](#mask) covering part or all of the face, from a surgical mask to a full [costume](#costume) piece. Only the mask's own colour is being recorded.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_veil
entries.description: A [veil](#veil) finished with [lace](#lace) around its [border](#border). It appears in bridal, [mourning](#mourning) and gothic [dress](#dress) alike.

entries.name: raccoon_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) cut and colored to look like a [raccoon](#raccoon) or [tanuki](#tanuki), usually with sewn-on ears and the animal's [dark](#dark) [facial](#facial) [mask](#mask). It sits over the wearer's own head, so the ears belong to the garment rather than the character.

entries.name: wimple
entries.description: Cloth wound snugly over the head and beneath the chin, covering the [neck](#neck), [jaw](#jaw), and ears while leaving the face open. Nuns wear it under a [veil](#veil), and it also suits [medieval](#medieval) [dress](#dress) generally.

entries.name: veil_lift
entries.description: A [veil](#veil) is being raised away from the face, whether by the wearer or by someone else, most often as part of a [wedding](#wedding) scene.

entries.name: monkey_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) moulded or painted into a monkey's face, from [festival](#festival) papier-mâché to a rubber novelty. It covers the face alone, unlike a full [monkey](#monkey) [suit](#suit).

entries.name: orange_hood
entries.description: An orange [hood](#hood), attached to a garment or worn as a separate piece, pulled up over the head or [lying](#lying) [back](#back) on the shoulders.

entries.name: scarf_on_head
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) worn over the hair and knotted under the chin or at the [nape](#nape), used as a [headscarf](#headscarf) rather than around the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: dinosaur_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) shaped as a dinosaur's head, usually with a [spiked](#spiked) [crest](#crest) [running](#running) along the top. Sewn onto a [jacket](#jacket) or a [onesie](#onesie) rather than worn on its own.

entries.name: white_coif
entries.description: A white [coif](#coif), the close-fitting cap that covers the hair and fastens under the chin. Worn by nuns, [medieval](#medieval) commoners and some [maid](#maid) uniforms.

entries.name: brown_bandana
entries.description: A brown [bandana](#bandana), the [square](#square) [cloth](#cloth) [folded](#folded) and knotted over the hair, across the [forehead](#forehead) or round the [neck](#neck). It is a piece of cloth rather than a shaped [hat](#hat).

entries.name: hood_basket
entries.description: The [hood](#hood) [hanging](#hanging) down the [back](#back) is being used as a [container](#container), with an [animal](#animal), [food](#food) or small object [riding](#riding) inside it. The wearer often has [no](#no) [idea](#idea) it is there.

entries.name: print_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) [carrying](#carrying) a printed design, whether a soft face covering or a moulded [shell](#shell). The motif is printed on rather than sculpted into the shape.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) finished with a [ribbon](#ribbon) band around its [opening](#opening) or along its [seams](#seams). Seen on cloaks, capelets and [fantasy](#fantasy) costumes.

entries.name: nemes
entries.description: The striped [cloth](#cloth) [headdress](#headdress) of the Egyptian pharaohs, covering the [crown](#crown) and the [back](#back) of the [neck](#neck). Two wide lappets fall forward over the shoulders on either side of the face.

entries.name: butterfly_mask
entries.description: A face [mask](#mask) cut or painted as a [butterfly](#butterfly), its [wings](#wings) [spreading](#spreading) over cheeks and brow. Masquerade eye masks are the usual form.

entries.name: reindeer_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) made to look like a reindeer's head, with [stitched](#stitched) [antlers](#antlers) and ears attached. A garment worn over the hair, so the antlers do not belong to the character.

entries.name: boar_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) built to look like a boar's head, with moulded ears and a [snout](#snout) [sitting](#sitting) above the wearer's face. It is a piece of clothing, not the [animal](#animal) features of the character underneath.

entries.name: brown_mask
entries.description: A brown [mask](#mask) covering part or all of the face. Half masks, full face coverings and [creature](#creature) masks all qualify so long as the mask reads brown.

entries.name: fox_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) with fake [fox](#fox) ears sewn on, so that [pulling](#pulling) it up gives the wearer a fox's head. It usually comes as part of a hooded [coat](#coat) or a [kigurumi](#kigurumi).

entries.name: pink_veil
entries.description: A pink [veil](#veil) covering the head or the face, of sheer or opaque [cloth](#cloth). Bridal, religious and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits alike use one.

entries.name: two-sided_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) lined in a contrasting colour or pattern, so the inside reads differently from the outside. Most visible when the hood hangs [back](#back) off the head.

entries.name: pumpkin_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) or [helmet](#helmet) cut or moulded into a [pumpkin](#pumpkin) face, sometimes an actual hollowed [gourd](#gourd) and sometimes a manufactured piece. The wearer's own head stays underneath it.

entries.name: veil_over_eyes
entries.description: A [veil](#veil) hangs across the upper face, covering the eyes while leaving the mouth and chin visible. Used for bridal, [mourning](#mourning) and mysterious looks alike.

entries.name: bird_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) shaped like a bird's head, with a [beak](#beak) over the brow and often eyes above the face. Part of [animal](#animal) hoodies and [kigurumi](#kigurumi).

entries.name: blanket_veil
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) draped over the head so that it hangs down at the sides like a [veil](#veil), with the face still showing. Lying face down under a blanket or [hiding](#hiding) completely beneath one is something else.

entries.name: green_veil
entries.description: A green [veil](#veil) covering the head or face, sheer or opaque. Only the cloth's own colour is being recorded.

entries.name: sheep_hood
entries.description: A [hood](#hood) trimmed with fake [sheep](#sheep) ears, curled [horns](#horns) or fleece, worn as a [lighter](#lighter) accessory rather than a full [costume](#costume). Implies [animal_hood](#animal_hood).

entries.name: grey_bandana
entries.description: A grey [bandana](#bandana), tied over the hair or knotted around the [neck](#neck). Only the cloth's colour decides the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: yellow_veil
entries.description: A yellow [veil](#veil) draped over the head or face.

entries.name: orange_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) in orange covering part or all of the face, of any shape from a small domino to a full face-piece.

entries.name: brown_veil
entries.description: A brown [veil](#veil) [hanging](#hanging) over the head or face. Bridal, [mourning](#mourning) and purely decorative veils all count.

entries.name: orange_veil
entries.description: An orange [veil](#veil) [hanging](#hanging) over the head or across the face.

entries.name: headgear
entries.description: Specialised head [accessories](#accessories) that are neither hats and hoods nor hair ornaments, such as the sensor arrays and [antennae](#antennae) of machine-girl designs. They often float beside the head rather than [resting](#resting) on it.

entries.name: crown
entries.description: The ceremonial [headpiece](#headpiece) of royalty, worn squarely on the head, from a full jewelled monarch's crown down to a small token one. Add the colour or material [tag](#tag) such as [gold_crown](#gold_crown) or paper_crown where it applies.

entries.name: tiara
entries.description: A slim metal band, often set with gems, worn on top of the head by princesses, idols and [fantasy](#fantasy) heroines. Narrower than a [crown](#crown) and worn higher than a [circlet](#circlet); a tiny clip-on belongs under [hairclip](#hairclip) instead.

entries.name: circlet
entries.description: An open-topped band worn around the head, usually across the [forehead](#forehead), with [no](#no) arches or cap over the [crown](#crown). A [tiara](#tiara) sits higher, on top of the hair, and is not this.

entries.name: headpiece
entries.description: Decorative headwear fitted round the head, usually low on the [forehead](#forehead), that is not a [crown](#crown), [tiara](#tiara) or [hairband](#hairband). Most are jewellery-like, though [cloth](#cloth) and [machinery](#machinery) versions exist, and it is generally worn on its own.

entries.name: headdress
entries.description: Ornamental or ceremonial covering for the head — a feathered [war](#war) [bonnet](#bonnet), a stiff decorated band, a bonnet reduced to its middle strip. It also serves as the fallback for decorative [headgear](#headgear) that is not a [hat](#hat), a [helmet](#helmet), a hair ornament, fake ears or a [plain](#plain) [ribbon](#ribbon).

entries.name: mini_crown
entries.description: A tiny [crown](#crown) perched on the head as an ornament rather than sized to actually fit around it.

entries.name: head_wreath
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of flowers, leaves or other ornament worn on the head, also called a [flower](#flower) [crown](#crown).

entries.name: green_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) hovering above or behind the head that glows or is drawn green. The [ring](#ring) itself carries the colour, whatever the character's other trappings.

entries.name: grey_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) above or behind the head that is grey rather than [gold](#gold) or white. It is a common [choice](#choice) for fallen angels and for muted character palettes.

entries.name: laurel_crown
entries.description: A [wreath](#wreath) of laurel leaves worn round the head in the ancient Greek and Roman manner. A [hairpin](#hairpin) cut in the shape of a [leaf](#leaf) is [leaf_hair_ornament](#leaf_hair_ornament) instead.

entries.name: diadem
entries.description: An ornamental [headband](#headband) worn as a [badge](#badge) of royalty, most often by women. Lighter and plainer than a full [crown](#crown) and close kin to a [tiara](#tiara).

entries.name: dalachi_(headdress)
entries.description: The broad wing-shaped [headdress](#headdress) worn by noble Manchu women late in the Qing dynasty, its name meaning big wing. A dianzi cap is sometimes set over it, and the earlier, smaller form is liangbatou.

entries.name: black_tiara
entries.description: A small ornamental [crown](#crown) in black, [resting](#resting) on top of the hair rather than closing around the head. A full band or a heavier [headpiece](#headpiece) is a crown.

entries.name: no_halo
entries.description: A character who normally has a [ring](#ring) of light above the head is drawn without one, as happens when such a [figure](#figure) is asleep or [unconscious](#unconscious). Where the [halo](#halo) is in the picture but off the head, halo_removed is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: gold_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) of [gold](#gold), or coloured to pass for it. The default royal [headpiece](#headpiece), taller and heavier than a [tiara](#tiara) or [circlet](#circlet).

entries.name: arched_crown
entries.description: A closed royal [crown](#crown) whose metal bands rise from the rim and meet at the top under an [orb](#orb) and [cross](#cross), often [studded](#studded) with gems. The cap inside is usually red velvet with white fur; an open [ring](#ring) with [no](#no) bands is a [circlet](#circlet).

entries.name: pointed_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) with [spikes](#spikes) or [fleur-de-lis](#fleur-de-lis) points rising from its rim, either a full [circlet](#circlet) or a tiara-like front piece. Tag crown alongside it.

entries.name: red_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) that is red, most often the velvet cap set inside an arched metal frame. Combine with crown.

entries.name: gold_tiara
entries.description: A [gold](#gold) band with raised points [sitting](#sitting) on the head, smaller and [lighter](#lighter) than a [crown](#crown). It marks princesses, magical girls and formal occasions.

entries.name: gold_circlet
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) [gold](#gold) band [resting](#resting) around the head, without the raised points of a [tiara](#tiara) or the [height](#height) of a [crown](#crown). Elves, priestesses and royalty wear one.

entries.name: black_headdress
entries.description: An ornamental head covering in black, from a maid's frilled band to a [veil](#veil), [coif](#coif) or ceremonial piece. It sits on or over the hair rather than enclosing the whole head.

entries.name: crown_of_thorns
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of thorny branches twisted together and worn on the head, taken from the imagery of Christ's [crucifixion](#crucifixion). Used for martyrdom and suffering as readily as for outright religious subjects.

entries.name: pink_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) in pink, whether a jewelled [circlet](#circlet) or a small toy-like ornament perched on the hair. A colour variant of the ordinary crown.

entries.name: unworn_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) appears in the picture off the head, [resting](#resting) on a [cushion](#cushion), held, or set on a [table](#table). Distinct from [floating_crown](#floating_crown), where it hovers above the head as though still worn.

entries.name: black_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) of black metal, set on the head or laid aside. A favourite for villains, [dark](#dark) royalty and gothic designs.

entries.name: floating_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) hovering a little above the head rather than [sitting](#sitting) on it, and still counted as being worn. A crown set down on a [table](#table) or held in the hand is unworn instead.

entries.name: hirabitai
entries.description: A flat golden [headpiece](#headpiece) with three upright prongs, worn at the front of the hair and held by a [comb](#comb) and pins. It belongs to Heian women's court [dress](#dress) and to the empress [doll](#doll) of the Girls' Day set.

entries.name: crown_bow
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) with a [bow](#bow) fixed onto it as part of the piece. The bow belongs to the crown itself, not to the hair underneath.

entries.name: blue_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) in blue, whether from its metal, its enamel or its stones. It closes around the head as a full [circlet](#circlet) rather than perching like a small [tiara](#tiara).

entries.name: native_american_headdress
entries.description: A [crest](#crest) of long [feathers](#feathers) rising over the head in the manner of the Plains nations, built onto a [leather](#leather) [headband](#headband). The most elaborate versions are known as [war](#war) bonnets.

entries.name: saishi
entries.description: A three-pointed metal ornament worn flat across the [forehead](#forehead) by the empress [figure](#figure) of a hina [doll](#doll) set, [sitting](#sitting) like a small [tiara](#tiara). A similarly named Heian-era [hairpin](#hairpin) is tagged separately as [kanzashi](#kanzashi).

entries.name: ribboned_xiao_guan
entries.description: A small Chinese hair [crown](#crown) fastened over a [topknot](#topknot) and tied with ribbons that hang down. Worn in historical Chinese [dress](#dress) and in [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume) styled after it.

entries.name: uraeus
entries.description: The [rearing](#rearing) cobra worn at the brow of ancient Egyptian headdresses, a mark of kingship and divine authority. Appears on crowns, circlets and [nemes](#nemes) headcloths.

entries.name: mian_guan
entries.description: A Chinese imperial [crown](#crown) topped with a flat lacquered board, strands of jade [beads](#beads) [hanging](#hanging) from its front and [back](#back) edges to mark rank. Worn by emperors and high nobility at ceremonies, and echoed in Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese royal headwear.

entries.name: yellow_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) rendered in yellow, which in practice usually reads as [gold](#gold). Where the metal itself is clearly the point, [gold_crown](#gold_crown) is the better fit.

entries.name: white_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) rendered in white or a very pale metal. Shading decides whether it reads as white or silver, so it overlaps heavily with [grey_crown](#grey_crown).

entries.name: jeweled_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) set with gemstones around its band or its points. The stones catch the light against the metal and say royalty far more loudly than a [plain](#plain) [circlet](#circlet).

entries.name: multiple_halos
entries.description: More than one [halo](#halo) about a figure's head, stacked in a [column](#column), orbiting, or set at odd angles. Common on angelic and divine designs where a single [ring](#ring) would look too [plain](#plain).

entries.name: grey_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) rendered grey. Together with [white_crown](#white_crown) it is how a silver crown is usually recorded, the shading deciding which of the two reads better.

entries.name: green_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) in green worn on the head. The colour covers metal, jewelled and purely fanciful designs alike.

entries.name: purple_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) in purple worn on the head.

entries.name: orange_crown
entries.description: A [crown](#crown) in orange [resting](#resting) on the head, whether metal, gemmed or wholly fantastical.

entries.name: hairband
entries.description: A band of plastic, metal or [fabric](#fabric) worn over the top of the head to keep hair [back](#back) and hold a style in place; it may also carry fake [animal](#animal) ears. A strip tied across the [forehead](#forehead) for sport is [headband](#headband) instead.

entries.name: fake_animal_ears
entries.description: Animal ears that are not part of the body, worn on a [hairband](#hairband), a [hood](#hood) or a [hat](#hat). The everyday bunny-girl and cat-ear-headband case. A character who has grown real [animal](#animal) features is [kemonomimi_mode](#kemonomimi_mode).

entries.name: maid_headdress
entries.description: The frilled white band or small cap worn at the [crown](#crown) with [maid](#maid) [dress](#dress), often [standing](#standing) up in a single ruffle. Wearing one alone does not make a character a maid; other parts of the uniform must be there for that.

entries.name: headband
entries.description: A strip tied across the [forehead](#forehead): a [sweatband](#sweatband), a martial-arts or sports band, a ninja's forehead [plate](#plate), often with tails trailing behind. The hair usually covers some of it; a band arching over the [crown](#crown) to hold a hairstyle is [hairband](#hairband).

entries.name: black_hairband
entries.description: A black [hairband](#hairband), the rigid or elastic band arching over the top of the head to hold hair [back](#back). A strip worn round the [forehead](#forehead) instead is [black_headband](#black_headband).

entries.name: ear_covers
entries.description: Decorative pieces worn over pointed or [animal](#animal) ears, from a full [sheath](#sheath) to a small clipped-on [plate](#plate). They sit over the ear rather than [piercing](#piercing) it, and are common on elves and horse-girl designs.

entries.name: fake_horns
entries.description: Horns worn as an accessory, on a [hairband](#hairband) or as a removable [costume](#costume) piece. Oni and [demon](#demon) outfits use them constantly.

entries.name: animal_ear_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) with false [creature](#creature) ears mounted on it, the standard way [cat](#cat) or bunny ears are worn as an accessory. Add the specific ear type, such as fake_cat_ears.

entries.name: triangular_headpiece
entries.description: The small white [triangle](#triangle) worn on the [forehead](#forehead) by ghosts in Japanese folklore, held on with a band. It descends from Edo-period burial [dress](#dress) and marks a character as a yuurei or as someone costumed like one.

entries.name: earmuffs
entries.description: Two padded cups joined by a band and worn over the ears against the [cold](#cold). They resemble [headphones](#headphones) but carry [no](#no) [sound](#sound), and usually come with a [winter](#winter) outfit.

entries.name: lolita_hairband
