entries.description: A broad [hairband](#hairband), sometimes padded or made of [lace](#lace), trimmed with [pleated](#pleated) [frills](#frills) or [flower](#flower) motifs and typical of lolita [fashion](#fashion). Where the trim is frilled it is also a [frilled_hairband](#frilled_hairband), and unlike a [bonnet](#bonnet) it never overhangs the head.

entries.name: frilled_hairband
entries.description: A band worn over the [crown](#crown) trimmed with ruffles, sometimes [no](#no) more than a [ribbon](#ribbon) with gathered edging on either side. A band bearing one upright ruffle is a [maid_headdress](#maid_headdress) whatever the wearer does for a living, and extra [embroidery](#embroidery) or [lace](#lace) pushes it toward [lolita_hairband](#lolita_hairband).

entries.name: animal_ear_headphones
entries.description: Headphones with [creature](#creature) ears built onto the band, sometimes doubling as mechanical ears. Different from an [animal_ear_hairband](#animal_ear_hairband), and from [plain](#plain) [headphones](#headphones) worn over ears the character actually has.

entries.name: hachimaki
entries.description: A Japanese [cloth](#cloth) [headband](#headband) tied around the [forehead](#forehead) to show effort or [spirit](#spirit), [plain](#plain) in team colours at sports days or printed with a red [sun](#sun) or slogan. A twisted one is [nejiri_hachimaki](#nejiri_hachimaki), worn at festivals.

entries.name: rabbit_ear_hairband
entries.description: A [headband](#headband) fitted with fake [rabbit](#rabbit) ears [standing](#standing) up from it, the standard ears seen on a [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny) [costume](#costume). Combine with [fake_animal_ears](#fake_animal_ears) and [rabbit_ears](#rabbit_ears).

entries.name: forehead_protector
entries.description: Protective [headgear](#headgear) covering the [forehead](#forehead), most familiarly a metal [plate](#plate) riveted to a [cloth](#cloth) [headband](#headband) and stamped with an [emblem](#emblem). An all-metal band, or a plate seemingly held by nothing at all, counts too.

entries.name: red_headband
entries.description: A red strip of [cloth](#cloth) tied around the [forehead](#forehead), in the style of a martial artist or athlete. Not the same as [red_hairband](#red_hairband), the rigid [arch](#arch) worn over the top of the head.

entries.name: single_ear_cover
entries.description: An ear [cover](#cover), often the flap-style piece over an [animal](#animal) ear or a headphone-like [cup](#cup), is worn on one ear only.

entries.name: black_headband
entries.description: A black band worn round the [forehead](#forehead) or over the hair, like a [sweatband](#sweatband) or a ninja's. A band arching over the top of the head to push hair [back](#back) is [black_hairband](#black_hairband).

entries.name: orange_hairband
entries.description: An orange [hairband](#hairband) arcing over the top of the head to hold the hair [back](#back). A soft strip tied round the head is a [headband](#headband) instead.

entries.name: green_hairband
entries.description: A rigid green band worn over the [crown](#crown) of the head to hold the hair [back](#back). A strip of [cloth](#cloth) tied around the [forehead](#forehead) is [green_headband](#green_headband) instead.

entries.name: horned_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), [hood](#hood), cap or other head covering with fake [horns](#horns) built into it for effect. A [helmet](#helmet) with horns is [horned_helmet](#horned_helmet), and real horns [poking](#poking) through a hat are [horns_through_headwear](#horns_through_headwear).

entries.name: animal_ear_headwear
entries.description: A cap, [helmet](#helmet) or other piece of [headgear](#headgear) with false [creature](#creature) ears fixed to it. A [hairband](#hairband) with ears is [animal_ear_hairband](#animal_ear_hairband) and a [hood](#hood) with ears [animal_ear_hood](#animal_ear_hood).

entries.name: blue_headband
entries.description: A blue band worn around the [forehead](#forehead) or pushed [back](#back) over the hair like a [sweatband](#sweatband). A band arching over the top of the head is [blue_hairband](#blue_hairband).

entries.name: fake_antlers
entries.description: Antlers worn as an accessory, usually on a [headband](#headband) as part of a [reindeer](#reindeer) [costume](#costume). Unlike real [antlers](#antlers) they [can](#can) be taken off.

entries.name: cat_ear_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) with fake [cat](#cat) ears fixed to it, an accessory rather than ears growing from the head. The wearer keeps their human ears.

entries.name: grey_hairband
entries.description: A rigid grey band arching over the top of the head to hold the hair [back](#back). Cloth tied around the [forehead](#forehead) is [grey_headband](#grey_headband).

entries.name: green_headband
entries.description: A green strip of [cloth](#cloth) or elastic tied around the [forehead](#forehead). It should not be mixed up with [green_hairband](#green_hairband), which arches over the top of the head.

entries.name: horn_hairband
entries.description: A [headband](#headband) [carrying](#carrying) fake [horns](#horns), worn as [costume](#costume) or [party](#party) [dress](#dress). The horns leave with the band, unlike real ones growing from the head.

entries.name: striped_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) showing several stripes rather than just two colour blocks; when only two bands of colour show, use [two-tone_hairband](#two-tone_hairband) instead. Implies hairband and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: hat_with_ears
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) with [animal](#animal) ears sewn onto its [crown](#crown), such as a cat-ear [beanie](#beanie). Ears growing from the wearer's own head are something else entirely.

entries.name: ear_protection
entries.description: Heavy padded defenders worn over the ears to shut out loud noise on a [firing](#firing) range or a [building](#building) site. They look like [earmuffs](#earmuffs) or [headphones](#headphones) but carry [no](#no) [sound](#sound) and give no warmth.

entries.name: yellow_headband
entries.description: A yellow band worn around the head and crossing the [forehead](#forehead). Do not confuse it with a [hairband](#hairband), which arcs over the top of the head instead.

entries.name: nejiri_hachimaki
entries.description: A [headband](#headband) made from [cloth](#cloth) twisted into a [rope](#rope) and knotted round the head, worn by [festival](#festival) float bearers and taiko drummers and sometimes by cooks. Like any [hachimaki](#hachimaki) it has to sit across the [forehead](#forehead).

entries.name: chain_headband
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) worn across the head as a band, or a rigid metal band shaped to imitate one. Fine [gold](#gold) strands draped over the [forehead](#forehead) are [head_chain](#head_chain) instead.

entries.name: orange_headband
entries.description: A strip of orange [cloth](#cloth) tied round the head, in the athletic or [festival](#festival) manner. Not the same as a rigid orange [hairband](#hairband) [sitting](#sitting) in the hair like an alice band.

entries.name: fake_halo
entries.description: A [costume](#costume) [halo](#halo) held over the head on a [wire](#wire) or rod rising from a [headband](#headband), instead of [floating](#floating) there by itself.

entries.name: purple_headband
entries.description: A purple strip of [cloth](#cloth) tied around the head across the brow. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [hairband](#hairband), the rigid arc worn over the top of the head.

entries.name: unworn_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) is present in the picture but off the head of the character who usually wears it. Where the band does not appear anywhere in the image, [no_hairband](#no_hairband) is the [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: brown_headband
entries.description: A brown band worn round the head, crossing the [forehead](#forehead). A [hairband](#hairband), which arcs over the [crown](#crown) instead, is a separate item.

entries.name: frog_headband
entries.description: A band across the head [carrying](#carrying) a [frog](#frog) motif, often with a pair of eyes [standing](#standing) upright on it. When the piece actually covers the [skull](#skull) it is a [frog_hat](#frog_hat) instead.

entries.name: fake_antennae
entries.description: Insect or [alien](#alien) [antennae](#antennae) worn as an accessory, generally bobbing on springs or [wire](#wire) from a [headband](#headband). They are [costume](#costume), not part of the character.

entries.name: striped_headband
entries.description: A band worn across the top of the head, [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) along its length. Implies [headband](#headband).

entries.name: earmuffs_around_neck
entries.description: Earmuffs pushed off the head and left [hanging](#hanging) around the [neck](#neck). Reads as somebody [stepping](#stepping) [indoors](#indoors) or into warmth.

entries.name: shampoo_hat
entries.description: A wide-brimmed [ring](#ring) worn during a [bath](#bath) so suds and rinse [water](#water) run clear of the eyes while the hair is washed. Made for small children, so it reads as childish on an adult.

entries.name: rabbit_earmuffs
entries.description: Ear warmers shaped like a [rabbit](#rabbit) or [carrying](#carrying) rabbit ears and features. Common in [winter](#winter) and festive scenes.

entries.name: grey_headband
entries.description: A grey band worn across the [forehead](#forehead). It should not be mixed up with a grey [hairband](#hairband), which sits over the [crown](#crown) and sweeps the hair [back](#back).

entries.name: unworn_headband
entries.description: A [headband](#headband) is visible somewhere in the picture without being tied around a head, often held, [hanging](#hanging) or [lying](#lying) loose.

entries.name: necktie_on_head
entries.description: A tie knotted around the brow in place of a [headband](#headband). In Japanese comedy this is the standard look for a drunken [office](#office) worker.

entries.name: animal_earmuffs
entries.description: Ear warmers built to look like a creature's ears, so the wearer seems to have grown a pair while bundled up. Winter and Christmas pictures lean on them heavily.

entries.name: glasses
entries.description: Spectacles worn to correct sight or to [shield](#shield) the eyes, including lightly tinted lenses that fall short of [sunglasses](#sunglasses). Monocles and [goggles](#goggles) have their own tags, and a [drinking](#drinking) vessel is [glass_(cup)](#glass_(cup)).

entries.name: sunglasses
entries.description: Dark-lensed [glasses](#glasses) worn to cut glare or simply to hide the eyes. Do not also [tag](#tag) glasses or [bespectacled](#bespectacled) alongside them.

entries.name: eyepatch
entries.description: A flap of [cloth](#cloth) or [leather](#leather) worn over one eye, whether to [cover](#cover) an [injury](#injury) or purely for the look of it. A fixture of pirates, assassins and [chuunibyou](#chuunibyou) characters; lifting or tugging it aside have tags of their own.

entries.name: eyewear_on_head
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) parked on top of the head rather than [sitting](#sitting) over the eyes, the everyday way sunglasses are carried. Resting on a [hat](#hat), they are [eyewear_on_headwear](#eyewear_on_headwear).

entries.name: goggles
entries.description: Eyewear sealing around the eyes against [dust](#dust), [water](#water), [wind](#wind) or glare, covering ski, swim, welding and [diving](#diving) types. Where they are not over the eyes the position takes its own [tag](#tag), such as [goggles_on_head](#goggles_on_head).

entries.name: semi-rimless_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses whose frame runs only along the top or bottom of the lenses, or only down the sides, leaving the rest rimless. Tag with [glasses](#glasses) or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) as appropriate.

entries.name: round_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses with clearly circular or oval lenses.

entries.name: black-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or a [monocle](#monocle) whose frames are black, much the commonest frame colour. Tag the kind of eyewear as [well](#well), since the colour alone says nothing about how it is worn.

entries.name: goggles_on_head
entries.description: Goggles pushed up onto the [crown](#crown) rather than worn over the eyes. If they rest on a [hat](#hat) or [helmet](#helmet) the [tag](#tag) is [goggles_on_headwear](#goggles_on_headwear).

entries.name: red-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, [sunglasses](#sunglasses), or a [monocle](#monocle) with red-colored frames. Combine with [glasses](#glasses) or sunglasses; red-tinted lenses instead take the [red-tinted_eyewear](#red-tinted_eyewear) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: under-rim_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses whose frame runs only beneath the lenses, leaving the top edge bare. Implies [semi-rimless_eyewear](#semi-rimless_eyewear).

entries.name: blindfold
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) or band tied across the eyes so the wearer cannot see, used in games, in restraint, at an [execution](#execution) or as a permanent part of a design. A padded [mask](#mask) for [sleeping](#sleeping) is [sleep_mask](#sleep_mask).

entries.name: tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) with coloured lenses, such as red, blue or yellow. Ordinary [dark](#dark) [sunglasses](#sunglasses) are excluded; lightly tinted spectacles still count as [glasses](#glasses).

entries.name: bespectacled
entries.description: A character who normally goes without [glasses](#glasses) is drawn wearing a pair. Sunglasses do not count, and the reverse case, a habitual wearer without them, is [no_eyewear](#no_eyewear).

entries.name: eye_mask
entries.description: A strip of [cloth](#cloth) or a domino [mask](#mask) worn across the eyes with the eyes themselves left showing, the kind worn by [masked](#masked) heroes and bandits. Not a sleep mask, and not a [blindfold](#blindfold).

entries.name: unworn_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) taken off and held, hung on a [collar](#collar) or set down. Not to be [confused](#confused) with [no_eyewear](#no_eyewear), used for a normally [bespectacled](#bespectacled) character shown without them at all.

entries.name: monocle
entries.description: A single framed lens held in front of one eye, correcting the sight of that eye alone. It normally hangs from a cord or [chain](#chain) fastened to the wearer's [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: rimless_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses with [no](#no) frame around the lenses, only the [bridge](#bridge) and temples [holding](#holding) them. A faint line tracing the lens edge still counts unless it is clearly thick and coloured.

entries.name: black_blindfold
entries.description: A black strip of [cloth](#cloth) tied across the eyes, taking the wearer's sight. The colour is all this adds, so pair it with whatever the scene calls for.

entries.name: domino_mask
entries.description: A small rounded [mask](#mask) covering just the eyes and the [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose). The superhero and masquerade kind, held on by ties or simply staying put.

entries.name: heart-shaped_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) whose frames are shaped as hearts. An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) in that shape is [heart_eyepatch](#heart_eyepatch).

entries.name: rectangular_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) built with squared-off rectangular frames rather than round or oval ones. Combine with [glasses](#glasses) and the frame color.

entries.name: pince-nez
entries.description: Spectacles with [no](#no) arms, staying on by gripping the [bridge](#bridge) of the [nose](#nose). A nineteenth-century style, usually given to scholarly, aristocratic or villainous characters.

entries.name: opaque_glasses
entries.description: Spectacles whose lenses give nothing away, filled with white glare so the eyes cannot be seen. It usually marks a character as bookish or as [hiding](#hiding) something. Sunglasses and lenses that are opaque by [nature](#nature) are not this.

entries.name: goggles_on_headwear
entries.description: Goggles [resting](#resting) on a [hat](#hat), [helmet](#helmet), swim cap or any other head covering rather than on the eyes or on bare hair.

entries.name: orange-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or [goggles](#goggles) with orange lenses, warming everything seen through them. The tint decides the [tag](#tag); the frame colour is recorded separately.

entries.name: goggles_around_neck
entries.description: Goggles [hanging](#hanging) at the [neck](#neck) rather than covering the eyes, the [strap](#strap) [resting](#resting) on the shoulders.

entries.name: red-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Lenses tinted red, worn on [glasses](#glasses) or [sunglasses](#sunglasses). The color describes the lens rather than the frame.

entries.name: white-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) whose frames are colored white. Add [glasses](#glasses) or sunglasses and any specific frame style alongside.

entries.name: blue-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or a [monocle](#monocle) whose frames are blue. Tag the type of eyewear too, since nothing is claimed here about the lenses.

entries.name: white_mask
entries.description: A white [mask](#mask) covering part or all of the face, from a surgical mask to a masquerade or [fox](#fox) mask. Add the specific mask type alongside.

entries.name: head-mounted_display
entries.description: An opaque visor covering both eyes and showing the wearer an image, whether a virtual-reality set, a pilot's [display](#display) or a science-fiction tactical band. Transparent [goggles](#goggles) and [glasses](#glasses) are not this.

entries.name: yellow-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) whose frames are yellow or [gold](#gold). Tag [glasses](#glasses) or the eyewear type alongside.

entries.name: over-rim_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses framed along the top of the lenses only, with nothing [running](#running) underneath them. The [mirror](#mirror) image, framed below and open above, is [under-rim_eyewear](#under-rim_eyewear).

entries.name: pink-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or other eyewear whose frames are pink. Combine it with the eyewear [tag](#tag) itself, such as [glasses](#glasses) or [sunglasses](#sunglasses); a pink lens is [pink-tinted_eyewear](#pink-tinted_eyewear) instead.

entries.name: grey-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or other eyewear whose frames are grey or silver. Record the kind of eyewear as [well](#well), such as [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or [goggles](#goggles).

entries.name: pink-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Lenses coloured pink, so the eyes read through a rosy film. The tint is what matters here, and the colour of the frames is recorded separately.

entries.name: no_eyewear
entries.description: A character who normally wears [glasses](#glasses) or similar appears without them, the reverse of [bespectacled](#bespectacled). Eyewear present but not on the face is [unworn_eyewear](#unworn_eyewear).

entries.name: purple-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) with lenses tinted purple. The tint colours the lens rather than the frame; add [purple-framed_eyewear](#purple-framed_eyewear) as [well](#well) when the frame is purple too.

entries.name: diving_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) sealing over both eyes and the [nose](#nose) for snorkelling or [diving](#diving). Eyewear that covers the eyes alone is [swim_goggles](#swim_goggles).

entries.name: blue-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Lenses tinted blue, as on blue [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or [goggles](#goggles). The frames are described separately and may be any colour at all.

entries.name: eyewear_strap
entries.description: A [strap](#strap), cord or [chain](#chain) fixed to [glasses](#glasses) to stop them [falling](#falling) off or to let them hang at the [neck](#neck). Eyepatches and monocles come with their own strings and are not counted.

entries.name: eyewear_on_headwear
entries.description: Glasses, [goggles](#goggles) or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) [sitting](#sitting) on a [hat](#hat) or other headwear instead of over the eyes — aviator goggles on a cap, for instance. Directly on the hair it is [eyewear_on_head](#eyewear_on_head).

entries.name: brown-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) whose frames are brown, in plastic, tortoiseshell or wood tones. Add [glasses](#glasses) or whichever eyewear type applies.

entries.name: green-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or other eyewear with green frames. Tag the type of eyewear too; a green lens is a separate matter, see [green-tinted_eyewear](#green-tinted_eyewear).

entries.name: yellow-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Eyewear whose lenses carry a yellow tint, like shooting [glasses](#glasses) or [fashion](#fashion) [sunglasses](#sunglasses). Tag [tinted_eyewear](#tinted_eyewear) alongside.

entries.name: eyewear_hang
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) hooked onto a garment while not being worn, most often at the neckline of a [shirt](#shirt). Any piece of clothing will do.

entries.name: blindfold_mask
entries.description: A shaped, rigid covering across the eyes that works as a [mask](#mask) rather than a strip of [cloth](#cloth). It blocks sight while the rest of the face stays open.

entries.name: aviator_sunglasses
entries.description: Sunglasses with big [teardrop](#teardrop) lenses, slightly domed rather than flat, set in thin [wire](#wire) frames and often mirrored. They are not [goggles](#goggles), and the clear-lensed version of the same shape is aviator_glasses.

entries.name: diving_mask_on_head
entries.description: A [diving](#diving) [mask](#mask) shoved up onto the [forehead](#forehead) or hair rather than worn over the face. The between-dives look, and a [signature](#signature) of certain naval-themed characters.

entries.name: no_blindfold
entries.description: A character usually drawn blindfolded appears with the [cloth](#cloth) gone and the eyes visible. It marks a departure from the standard design rather than a scene of removal.

entries.name: green-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or [goggles](#goggles) whose lenses are tinted green, so the eyes show through coloured [glass](#glass). Green frames with clear lenses are [green-framed_eyewear](#green-framed_eyewear) instead.

entries.name: no_eyepatch
entries.description: A character usually wearing an [eyepatch](#eyepatch) appears without it, both eyes on show. If the [patch](#patch) is in the picture but not worn, [unworn_eyepatch](#unworn_eyepatch) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: coke-bottle_glasses
entries.description: Round [glasses](#glasses) whose lenses are drawn as thick spirals that hide the eyes behind them. They are the stock shorthand for a nerd or [otaku](#otaku), named for lenses as deep as the base of a [glass](#glass) [bottle](#bottle).

entries.name: green_visor
entries.description: A green visor, either a brimmed visor cap or a [translucent](#translucent) band shielding the eyes. Tag the general visor [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: purple-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) whose frames are purple. Combine with [glasses](#glasses) or sunglasses and the frame style; [purple-tinted_eyewear](#purple-tinted_eyewear) covers lenses in that colour instead.

entries.name: star-shaped_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) whose lenses are cut in the shape of stars. When the entire frame is one large star, use simon_shades instead.

entries.name: scouter
entries.description: A single-lens eyepiece worn wrapped around the side of the head, projecting a heads-up [display](#display) of information about the wearer's surroundings. Its [signature](#signature) use is [reading](#reading) out the power level of whoever it targets. A [monocle](#monocle), worn only to correct vision, is a different thing.

entries.name: unworn_eyepatch
entries.description: Somebody whose usual look includes an [eyepatch](#eyepatch) has it off, with the [patch](#patch) itself still shown somewhere in the frame. Where [no](#no) patch appears at all, [no_eyepatch](#no_eyepatch) is the [tag](#tag) for the bare eye instead.

entries.name: cracked_glass
entries.description: Glass fractured into [spreading](#spreading) lines, most often the lens of a pair of spectacles, [binoculars](#binoculars) or a [telescope](#telescope). Windows and [display](#display) covers count as [well](#well).

entries.name: yellow_visor
entries.description: A yellow visor: either the tinted [shield](#shield) across the eyes on a [helmet](#helmet), or the brimmed band worn to [shade](#shade) the face. The colour is what is recorded.

entries.name: ski_goggles
entries.description: Wide-lensed [goggles](#goggles) strapped over the eyes against [cold](#cold), [wind](#wind) and glare on the slopes. The single large lens spans both eyes and is usually tinted or mirrored.

entries.name: safety_glasses
entries.description: Protective spectacles with tough lenses, worn in workshops, laboratories or on a shooting range. Usually recognisable by side shields or a wrap-around frame rather than an ordinary spectacle shape.

entries.name: blue_visor
entries.description: A blue [shield](#shield) across the eyes, either the faceplate of a [helmet](#helmet) or a curved band strapped over the face. On [machine](#machine) characters it is regularly tinted or lit from within.

entries.name: triangular_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or shades whose lenses come to points, [giving](#giving) the whole frame a triangular [outline](#outline). The pointed wraparound shades associated with a famous hot-blooded anime character are the best-known example.

entries.name: orange_goggles
entries.description: Goggles with orange lenses, worn over the eyes or pushed up on the [forehead](#forehead). The [glass](#glass) carries the colour, not the [strap](#strap).

entries.name: unworn_goggles
entries.description: Goggles [can](#can) be seen in the picture but nobody has them on their eyes or [forehead](#forehead), often set beside the character after [swimming](#swimming), welding or [flying](#flying).

entries.name: night_vision_device
entries.description: An optical rig that renders near-darkness visible, usually a cluster of tubes on a [helmet](#helmet) mount swung down over the eyes. Its eyepieces glow green while it is [running](#running).

entries.name: broken_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) visibly [damaged](#damaged), with a cracked or [shattered](#shattered) lens, a snapped arm or a bent frame. The damage has to be drawn, not merely implied.

entries.name: swim_goggles
entries.description: Small sealed lenses strapped over the eyes for [swimming](#swimming), keeping [water](#water) out while letting the wearer see clearly [underwater](#underwater). Eyewear that also covers the [nose](#nose) is a [diving](#diving) [mask](#mask) instead.

entries.name: flower_eyepatch
entries.description: An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) [carrying](#carrying) a [flower](#flower), where the [cloth](#cloth) pad or the [strap](#strap) [holding](#holding) it on [can](#can) actually be seen. If a [bloom](#bloom) simply sits over the eye with nothing supporting it, [flower_over_eye](#flower_over_eye) is the right [tag](#tag).

entries.name: brown-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Lenses [carrying](#carrying) a brown tint, on [glasses](#glasses), [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or [goggles](#goggles). The eyes stay visible through the warm [shade](#shade).

entries.name: colored_eyepatch
entries.description: An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) in some colour besides [plain](#plain) black or white, red, blue and pink among the usual choices. It covers dressings worn over a hurt eye and purely decorative patches alike.

entries.name: orange-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or similar eyewear whose rims and arms are orange. It records the frame, not any tint in the lenses.

entries.name: gradient-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Lenses whose tint fades smoothly from one [shade](#shade) into another, as a rule darkest at the top and clearing toward the bottom. Where several distinct hues appear it overlaps with multicolour-tinted eyewear.

entries.name: red_blindfold
entries.description: A red strip of [cloth](#cloth) tied over the eyes so the wearer cannot see. Shows up in [ritual](#ritual) scenes, combat [training](#training), and [bondage](#bondage) contexts, as [well](#well) as being a permanent part of some character designs.

entries.name: monocle_chain
entries.description: The cord or fine [chain](#chain) [running](#running) from a [monocle](#monocle) to a lapel or [pocket](#pocket) so that a slip cannot send the lens to the [floor](#floor). Artists usually draw it [swinging](#swinging) free with a charm on the loose end.

entries.name: heart_eyepatch
entries.description: An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) cut as a [heart](#heart), covering one eye. A [costume](#costume) piece rather than a [dressing](#dressing) over an [injury](#injury).

entries.name: white_blindfold
entries.description: A white strip of [cloth](#cloth) [bound](#bound) over the eyes so the wearer can't see. Appears in [bondage](#bondage) scenes, [ritual](#ritual) imagery and [blind](#blind) guessing games alike.

entries.name: heterochromatic_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) whose two lenses are tinted different colours, as with [old](#old) red-and-blue 3D specs. Several colours within one lens is multicolor-tinted eyewear; differing frame [shapes](#shapes) is asymmetrical eyewear.

entries.name: teardrop-framed_glasses
entries.description: Spectacles whose frame carries a drop-shaped flourish beside one lens, [hanging](#hanging) off the rim like a [falling](#falling) tear. When both lenses are themselves teardrop-shaped, the picture is cat_eye-framed_eyewear instead.

entries.name: aqua-framed_eyewear
entries.description: Spectacles or other eyewear with blue-green rims. The colour belongs to the frame, not to the lenses.

entries.name: print_eyepatch
entries.description: An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) decorated with a printed motif such as a [heart](#heart), a [skull](#skull) or a character's mark. Worn as an accessory rather than as a [dressing](#dressing).

entries.name: eyewear_lift
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) pushed up off the eyes onto the brow, while still being worn. Caught in the act of shifting them rather than parked there, which is [eyewear_on_head](#eyewear_on_head).

entries.name: welding_mask
entries.description: The full face [shield](#shield) a welder wears, with a darkened viewing [window](#window) across the eyes and a hinged front panel. Worn down while [working](#working) or flipped up to talk.

entries.name: groucho_glasses
entries.description: The novelty [disguise](#disguise) of [heavy](#heavy) black frames [carrying](#carrying) attached bushy eyebrows, a large plastic [nose](#nose) and a moustache. Worn purely for slapstick.

entries.name: 3d_glasses
entries.description: The cheap [glasses](#glasses) handed out at a three-dimensional film screening, classically a [cardboard](#cardboard) frame with one red lens and one blue-green one. The modern kind look like [plain](#plain) grey-tinted [sunglasses](#sunglasses) and count as [well](#well).

entries.name: crooked_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) [sitting](#sitting) askew, tilted off level or slid down the [nose](#nose) instead of [resting](#resting) straight. Often drawn on a startled or dishevelled character.

entries.name: eyes_visible_through_eyewear
entries.description: The eyes [can](#can) be made out through [dark](#dark) lenses, tinted [goggles](#goggles) or a [blindfold](#blindfold) that would normally hide them. A drawing [convention](#convention) that keeps the gaze readable.

entries.name: partially_opaque_glasses
entries.description: Lenses that hide the eyes only in part: one blank while the other shows through, or both obscuring without concealing entirely.

entries.name: red_goggles
entries.description: Goggles whose lenses are tinted red, worn over the eyes or pushed up onto the [forehead](#forehead). Common on [pilot](#pilot), [mechanic](#mechanic) and adventurer designs.

entries.name: aviator_goggles
entries.description: Round-lensed [goggles](#goggles) on a broad [strap](#strap), the sort worn in an open [cockpit](#cockpit) or on a [motorcycle](#motorcycle). They are as often pushed up on the [forehead](#forehead) or worn over a [leather](#leather) cap as actually covering the eyes.

entries.name: x-ray_glasses
entries.description: Novelty spectacles that let whoever looks through them see past clothing or solid objects. They are often drawn together with an eyewear-view framing, so the lenses fill most of the picture.

entries.name: orange_visor
entries.description: An orange visor: either the brimmed crownless cap or the tinted [shield](#shield) [sweeping](#sweeping) across the eyes on a [helmet](#helmet).

entries.name: black_visor
entries.description: A black [shield](#shield) worn across the eyes, either the hinged brow-piece of a [helmet](#helmet) or a wraparound band. It conceals the eyes without covering the whole face.

entries.name: red_visor
entries.description: A red [transparent](#transparent) or tinted [shield](#shield) covering the eyes, either a brimless cap visor or the faceplate of a [helmet](#helmet). Frequent on sports, cyber and mecha-pilot designs.

entries.name: eyewear_around_neck
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) hang round the [neck](#neck) instead of [sitting](#sitting) on the face, often on a cord or a [chain](#chain). Eyewear hooked onto clothing is [eyewear_hang](#eyewear_hang).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_eyepatch
entries.description: An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) bordered with [lace](#lace) rather than left as [plain](#plain) [dressing](#dressing). The trim makes it read as an ornament of a gothic or elaborate outfit.

entries.name: metal_eyepatch
entries.description: An eye covering shaped from a [plate](#plate) of metal, strapped or bolted into place rather than sewn from [cloth](#cloth). Reads as [armor](#armor) or [prosthesis](#prosthesis) rather than an ordinary [patch](#patch).

entries.name: nose_pads
entries.description: The small plastic or silicone pads on a spectacle frame that rest against either side of the [nose](#nose) [bridge](#bridge), drawn as a visible part of the [glasses](#glasses).

entries.name: novelty_glasses
entries.description: Spectacles or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) with a joke or decorative frame, cut as hearts, stars, flowers or animals, or simply oversized and gaudy. It is a catch-all for [shapes](#shapes) with [no](#no) [tag](#tag) of their own.

entries.name: semi-circular_eyewear
entries.description: Lenses cut as half circles, so the frames have one straight edge and one curve instead of a closed oval. Often used on scholarly or severe character designs.

entries.name: face_shield
entries.description: A [transparent](#transparent) visor covering the whole face, mounted on a [headband](#headband) or fixed to a [helmet](#helmet). Worn against splashes, [flying](#flying) [debris](#debris) or infection by medics, riot [police](#police) and workers.

entries.name: x-shaped_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, [goggles](#goggles) or a visor whose lenses or frame form an X across the face. A design gimmick found on costumes, robots and stylised characters rather than ordinary spectacles.

entries.name: sports_sunglasses
entries.description: Wraparound shades shaped for movement, with narrow oval or rectangular lenses that sometimes merge into a single visor. Worn for cycling, [running](#running) and [skiing](#skiing).

entries.name: shutter_shades
entries.description: Novelty [sunglasses](#sunglasses) whose frames carry horizontal slats instead of solid lenses, so the face looks barred by [window](#window) blinds. Strongly tied to late-2000s pop and [party](#party) [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: flight_goggles
entries.description: Aviator [goggles](#goggles) with a metal or [leather](#leather) frame and tinted lenses, worn over the eyes or pushed up onto a [flying](#flying) cap. Wartime pilots wear them most often.

entries.name: eyewear_switch
entries.description: Characters trade eyewear: one tries on another's [glasses](#glasses) with the owner [standing](#standing) right there, or the two wear each other's. Both parties have to be in the picture.

entries.name: asymmetrical_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [goggles](#goggles) whose two lenses are not alike, differing in shape, size or frame design. Where the only difference between them is the tint, a separate heterochromatic [tag](#tag) covers it.

entries.name: goggles_around_breasts
entries.description: Goggles pushed down the body to rest on the chest instead of [sitting](#sitting) over the eyes or on the [forehead](#forehead). One of the displaced-eyewear tags.

entries.name: multicolor-tinted_eyewear
entries.description: Tinted lenses that [shade](#shade) through two or more colours within one single lens. Where each lens instead carries its own flat tint, the heterochromatic eyewear [tag](#tag) is the right one.

entries.name: eyewear_pull
entries.description: The frames are tugged down the [nose](#nose) or away from the face, to take them off, to settle them, or to peer over the top. Frequently paired with [looking_over_eyewear](#looking_over_eyewear).

entries.name: grey_visor
entries.description: A grey visor shielding the eyes, whether a sports brim or a band across the face. Tag the general visor [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: white_visor
entries.description: A white visor shielding the eyes, whether the brim of a cap or a band worn across the face.

entries.name: pink_visor
entries.description: A pink visor shading the eyes, whether a brimmed band worn on the head or a tinted [screen](#screen) across the face. It leaves the [crown](#crown) open, unlike a cap.

entries.name: purple_visor
entries.description: A purple visor worn over the eyes, from a sports brim to a solid face band.

entries.name: necktie
entries.description: A long strip of [cloth](#cloth) knotted around the [neck](#neck), the usual companion to a [suit](#suit) or a [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt). A [tuxedo](#tuxedo) generally takes a [bowtie](#bowtie) instead, and further tags [cover](#cover) a tie being grabbed, adjusted or worn on the head.

entries.name: bowtie
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) knotted at the throat, whether the soft [ribbon](#ribbon) bow of a girls' [school](#school) uniform or the stiff formal kind worn with a [tuxedo](#tuxedo) or on a [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny) [collar](#collar). Volume is what separates it from [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon), which lies flat.

entries.name: ascot
entries.description: A broad [neck](#neck) [scarf](#scarf) knotted so it finishes in a wide, flat [tail](#tail) over the chest, also called a cravat. Usually worn tucked into a collared [shirt](#shirt), [waistcoat](#waistcoat) or [jacket](#jacket).

entries.name: neck_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied at the [neck](#neck) where a [necktie](#necktie) would sit. A fuller [bow](#bow) is a [bowtie](#bowtie), and a ribbon wound around the neck like a band is [ribbon_choker](#ribbon_choker).

entries.name: red_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in red, knotted at the [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt). Applies to solid red ties and mostly red [patterned](#patterned) ones; a small [bow](#bow) is a [bowtie](#bowtie), not a necktie.

entries.name: red_bowtie
entries.description: A red [bowtie](#bowtie) worn at the [collar](#collar), a fixture of both [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny) outfits and formal wear. A loose [ribbon](#ribbon) tied in a [bow](#bow) instead is [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon).

entries.name: black_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in black worn with a collared [shirt](#shirt), common in suits, [school](#school) uniforms and [funeral](#funeral) [dress](#dress). It may be knotted tight to the [collar](#collar) or [hanging](#hanging) loose.

entries.name: blue_necktie
entries.description: A blue [necktie](#necktie) worn with a collared [shirt](#shirt), in business suits and [school](#school) uniforms alike. Its width and pattern are not part of the claim.

entries.name: black_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) in black, the formal [neck](#neck) [bow](#bow) of tuxedos, [butler](#butler) suits and bunny outfits. It may be a stiff self-tie or a band clipped at the [collar](#collar).

entries.name: blue_bowtie
entries.description: A blue [bowtie](#bowtie) fastened at the [collar](#collar). Formal [dress](#dress), [butler](#butler) and host outfits and [school](#school) uniforms all use it as an accent.

entries.name: yellow_ascot
entries.description: A yellow [ascot](#ascot) or jabot at the [collar](#collar), a look shared by several Touhou characters. Tag ascot as [well](#well).

entries.name: red_ascot
entries.description: A red [ascot](#ascot) or jabot filling the neckline of a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse), a common accent on Gothic and Victorian-styled outfits. A loose [ribbon](#ribbon) tied in a [bow](#bow) at the [neck](#neck) instead is [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon).

entries.name: white_ascot
entries.description: A white [ascot](#ascot) or jabot worn at the [collar](#collar), the ruffled [neck](#neck) [scarf](#scarf) commonly seen on butlers, vampires and many gothic-styled outfits.

entries.name: pink_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) in pink, knotted at the [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt), [blouse](#blouse) or uniform. A long tie of the same colour is [pink_necktie](#pink_necktie).

entries.name: striped_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes, the diagonal kind common on [school](#school) and business ties in particular. Implies necktie.

entries.name: green_necktie
entries.description: A green [necktie](#necktie) worn with a collared [shirt](#shirt), as part of a [school](#school) uniform, [suit](#suit) or [office](#office) outfit. A bow-shaped tie is a [green_bowtie](#green_bowtie).

entries.name: aqua_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in aqua, knotted at the [collar](#collar). Add [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt), or the [school](#school) or [office](#office) uniform the tie belongs to.

entries.name: yellow_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in yellow or [gold](#gold). Tag necktie as [well](#well).

entries.name: white_bowtie
entries.description: A white [bow](#bow) tie worn at the [collar](#collar), the formal white-tie look or a [staple](#staple) for butlers and [stage](#stage) magicians.

entries.name: purple_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) in purple worn at the [collar](#collar). A loose [neck](#neck) [ribbon](#ribbon) tied in a [bow](#bow) shape instead is [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon).

entries.name: yellow_bowtie
entries.description: A yellow [bowtie](#bowtie) worn at the [collar](#collar). Tag bowtie and [yellow_bow](#yellow_bow) alongside.

entries.name: necktie_between_breasts
entries.description: The [tail](#tail) of a [necktie](#necktie) lies down the [cleavage](#cleavage) instead of over the front of the chest, held in place by the [breasts](#breasts) on either side. It is usually drawn on characters of at least medium bust size.

entries.name: striped_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) with stripes on it.

entries.name: traditional_bowtie
entries.description: The classic butterfly-shaped [bow](#bow) tie associated with formal menswear, commonly worn with a [tuxedo](#tuxedo) or attached to a detached [collar](#collar) on a playboy bunny outfit.

entries.name: white_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in white, worn with [dress](#dress) shirts and some [school](#school) or [stage](#stage) uniforms.

entries.name: purple_necktie
entries.description: A purple [necktie](#necktie) worn with a collared [shirt](#shirt). Combine with necktie and the knot or style, if it is notable.

entries.name: green_bowtie
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tie in green, [sitting](#sitting) at the [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt) or uniform. It counts as a green bow as [well](#well), so both tags apply.

entries.name: short_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) noticeably shorter than usual, ending [well](#well) above the waist. Implies necktie.

entries.name: pink_necktie
entries.description: A pink [necktie](#necktie) knotted at the [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt), long and [hanging](#hanging) down the chest. A bow-shaped one is [pink_bowtie](#pink_bowtie).

entries.name: black_ascot
entries.description: An [ascot](#ascot) or jabot in black, the broad [neck](#neck) [cloth](#cloth) tucked into a [collar](#collar) or [spilling](#spilling) down a [shirt](#shirt) front. Not the same as a black [necktie](#necktie) or [bowtie](#bowtie).

entries.name: blue_ascot
entries.description: A blue [ascot](#ascot) or jabot filling the open neckline of a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). It sits in a soft knot rather than [hanging](#hanging) long like a [necktie](#necktie).

entries.name: loose_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) still knotted but [hanging](#hanging) slack away from the [collar](#collar). Where the knot is undone and the tie simply drapes round the [neck](#neck), use [undone_necktie](#undone_necktie).

entries.name: diagonal-striped_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) at a slant, the classic regimental or school-tie design. One of the most common uniform details there is.

entries.name: orange_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) in orange, whether the [ribbon](#ribbon) type on a [school](#school) uniform or a formal one at a [collar](#collar).

entries.name: orange_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in orange worn with a collared [shirt](#shirt) or a uniform. A bow-shaped one is [orange_bowtie](#orange_bowtie).

entries.name: aqua_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) in blue-green, worn at the [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt) or uniform. Add the outfit it belongs to.

entries.name: plaid_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) cut from plaid or tartan [cloth](#cloth), the usual neckwear on many [school](#school) uniforms. A plaid [ribbon](#ribbon) merely tied into a [bow](#bow) shape elsewhere is [plaid_bow](#plaid_bow).

entries.name: print_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) [carrying](#carrying) a printed pattern or motif. Tag bowtie and [print_bow](#print_bow) alongside it.

entries.name: plaid_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in plaid [fabric](#fabric), often paired with a plaid [skirt](#skirt) on a [school](#school) uniform. A bow-shaped version in the same fabric is [plaid_bowtie](#plaid_bowtie).

entries.name: grey_necktie
entries.description: A grey [necktie](#necktie) worn with a collared [shirt](#shirt) in a [suit](#suit), [school](#school) or [office](#office) outfit. A bow-shaped tie is a [grey_bowtie](#grey_bowtie).

entries.name: brown_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in brown, [plain](#plain) or [patterned](#patterned), knotted at the [collar](#collar). Pair it with necktie and with whatever [shirt](#shirt) or uniform carries it.

entries.name: diagonal-striped_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) at a slant across the [fabric](#fabric). A common detail on [school](#school) uniforms and on formal [dress](#dress).

entries.name: checkered_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) [patterned](#patterned) in even alternating squares, worn at a [shirt](#shirt) [collar](#collar). School and [office](#office) outfits carry them most often.

entries.name: loose_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) still tied but pulled distinctly slack around the [neck](#neck), a favourite touch on [gyaru](#gyaru) [school](#school) uniforms. Fully untied it becomes [undone_bowtie](#undone_bowtie).

entries.name: square-end_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) whose bottom edge is cut straight across instead of coming to a point, a more modern and less common style than the classic pointed tie.

entries.name: two-tone_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) in exactly two colours. Implies bowtie and [two-tone_bow](#two-tone_bow).

entries.name: brown_bowtie
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) knotted at the [neck](#neck) in brown, from a school-uniform [ribbon](#ribbon) to a formal bow tie. Add [bowtie](#bowtie) and [brown_bow](#brown_bow).

entries.name: bolo_tie
entries.description: A slim cord, or a braided [leather](#leather) [strap](#strap), worn in place of a [necktie](#necktie) and drawn together at the [collar](#collar) by an ornamented [clasp](#clasp), in American western style. A [cross](#cross) tie is a short broad piece of [fabric](#fabric) and a [neck](#neck) [ribbon](#ribbon) is simply knotted, so neither counts.

entries.name: purple_ascot
entries.description: A purple [ascot](#ascot) or jabot tied at the [neck](#neck). A loose tie in a [bow](#bow) shape instead would be [purple_bowtie](#purple_bowtie).

entries.name: cross_tie
entries.description: A narrow strip of [cloth](#cloth) worn at the [collar](#collar) whose two ends lie across one another in front, also called a continental tie. A neat formal alternative to a knotted [necktie](#necktie).

entries.name: frilled_ascot
entries.description: An [ascot](#ascot) whose edges are finished with ruffles, worn at the throat of a [blouse](#blouse) or [dress](#dress) [shirt](#shirt). Lolita and fantasy-uniform designs favour it.

entries.name: orange_ascot
entries.description: An orange [ascot](#ascot) tucked into the [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse). The ascot itself must carry the colour, not merely the garment around it.

entries.name: pink_ascot
entries.description: The loose [folded](#folded) [neck](#neck) [scarf](#scarf) tucked into a [collar](#collar), here in pink; a jabot of the same colour folds in too. A long tie is a [necktie](#necktie) and a knotted one a [bowtie](#bowtie).

entries.name: print_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) [carrying](#carrying) a printed pattern or picture rather than a [plain](#plain) or striped design. Tag necktie with it.

entries.name: grey_bowtie
entries.description: A grey [bow](#bow) tie at the [collar](#collar), worn with formal or uniform [dress](#dress). It counts as a grey bow as [well](#well), so both tags apply.

entries.name: two-tone_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) in exactly two colours, whether striped, halved or tipped in a contrasting [shade](#shade). School and club ties often take this form.

entries.name: green_ascot
entries.description: A green [ascot](#ascot), the wide [neck](#neck) [cloth](#cloth) [folded](#folded) and tucked into an open [collar](#collar). Formal and gothic outfits favour it, and a green jabot is filed here too.

entries.name: unworn_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) [can](#can) be seen in the picture together with someone who might wear it, but it sits on nobody's [collar](#collar), often draped over a [chair](#chair) or clutched in a hand.

entries.name: brown_ascot
entries.description: A brown [ascot](#ascot), the wide soft [neck](#neck) [cloth](#cloth) tucked into an open [collar](#collar). It fills the neckline where a tie would otherwise sit.

entries.name: grey_ascot
entries.description: A grey [ascot](#ascot) knotted at the throat and tucked into the [collar](#collar). Grey jabots are filed under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: multicolored_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) made up of at least two colours, whether [split](#split) between the two halves or [patterned](#patterned) all over. Stripes and blocked halves are the usual arrangements.

entries.name: floating_neckwear
entries.description: A tie, [bow](#bow) or [neck](#neck) [ribbon](#ribbon) [hanging](#hanging) in the air at the throat instead of being fastened to a [collar](#collar). Shorthand in game and [idol](#idol) character design.

entries.name: ascot_between_breasts
entries.description: The [hanging](#hanging) end of an [ascot](#ascot) drops into the cleft between the [breasts](#breasts) instead of [lying](#lying) flat on the chest. It needs a full enough bust for the [cloth](#cloth) to settle there.

entries.name: multicolored_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) with two or more distinct colours worked into it, such as diagonal stripes or a contrasting tip. School and club ties are the usual carriers.

entries.name: polka_dot_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) printed with round [dots](#dots), worn at the [collar](#collar). A playful break from [plain](#plain) formal neckwear, and a favourite for clowns and waiters.

entries.name: unworn_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) is visible in the picture, but nobody has it fastened around their [neck](#neck). It may be draped over furniture, held out or [lying](#lying) loose.

entries.name: loose_neck_ribbon
entries.description: The [ribbon](#ribbon) at the [collar](#collar) has been slackened, so its knot rides low and the two ends hang open. A stock signal of a schoolgirl [relaxing](#relaxing) or [dressing](#dressing) carelessly.

entries.name: gradient_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) whose colour fades along its length, as a rule with the darkest tone at the point.

entries.name: vertical-striped_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) [carrying](#carrying) stripes that run straight down its length rather than the diagonal bands ties usually wear. Common on [school](#school) and [office](#office) uniforms drawn with a simplified pattern.

entries.name: necktie_between_pectorals
entries.description: A man's tie runs down the groove between [heavy](#heavy) [pectorals](#pectorals), which press in on the [fabric](#fabric) from both sides. It is the male counterpart to a tie [resting](#resting) in [cleavage](#cleavage).

entries.name: polka_dot_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) sprinkled with round [dots](#dots), worn over a collared [shirt](#shirt). One of the standard tie patterns beside stripes and plaid.

entries.name: aqua_ascot
entries.description: A broad, softly knotted [neck](#neck) [cloth](#cloth) in blue-green, tucked into the [collar](#collar). Formal and uniform designs use it in place of a tie.

entries.name: checkered_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) printed in squares and worn at the [collar](#collar). School uniforms and [cafe](#cafe) outfits use them, generally matched to another chequered piece.

entries.name: frilled_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) cut from ruffled [fabric](#fabric), or a [plain](#plain) one with ruffles [stitched](#stitched) along its length. The result reads somewhere between a cravat and a jabot.

entries.name: torn_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) [damaged](#damaged), shredded down the blade or cut away so only the knot and a stub are left.

entries.name: gold_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) of [gold](#gold) [cloth](#cloth) or worked metal [sitting](#sitting) at the throat. It goes with formal [dress](#dress), [stage](#stage) [costume](#costume) and bunny suits.

entries.name: american_flag_neckwear
entries.description: A tie, [bow](#bow), [scarf](#scarf) or similar [neck](#neck) piece [patterned](#patterned) after the stars and stripes. The print matters, not the shape of the garment.

entries.name: no_neckwear
entries.description: The tie, [bowtie](#bowtie) or similar throat piece belonging to the usual outfit is missing. Where a different one is worn in its place, alternate_neckwear applies.

entries.name: string_tie
entries.description: A narrow cord worn in place of a [necktie](#necktie), knotted or held with a [clasp](#clasp) at the throat. Includes bolo-style ties and thin [ribbon](#ribbon) ties on a [collar](#collar).

entries.name: frilled_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) cut from ruffled [fabric](#fabric) or edged with ruffles, tied at the throat. Maid outfits, frilly blouses and lolita coordinates use it in place of a flat bowtie.

entries.name: long_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) whose blade hangs unusually far down the body, sometimes past the waist. It reads as an exaggeration of ordinary neckwear rather than a garment of its own.

entries.name: argyle_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) knitted or printed with argyle diamonds. A tie in [plain](#plain) squares is checkered, which is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: plaid_ascot
entries.description: A wide [neck](#neck) [scarf](#scarf) tucked into the [collar](#collar), cut from tartan [cloth](#cloth). School and formal outfits reach for it often.

entries.name: choker
entries.description: A narrow band fitted snugly high on the [neck](#neck), of [ribbon](#ribbon), [lace](#lace), [leather](#leather) or metal. It is a kind of [necklace](#necklace) but is not tagged as one, it is not the thicker [collar](#collar), and it has nothing to do with choking.

entries.name: sailor_collar
entries.description: The wide two-tone [collar](#collar) with stripes along its edge, the hallmark of a [serafuku](#serafuku) or naval uniform. Usually blue or black on white and worn with a [neckerchief](#neckerchief).

entries.name: collar
entries.description: A band worn around the [neck](#neck) on its own, thicker and looser than a [choker](#choker), often [carrying](#carrying) a [ring](#ring) or a [bell](#bell). It never means the collar of a [shirt](#shirt), [coat](#coat) or [dress](#dress), which take [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt) and its relatives.

entries.name: black_choker
entries.description: A black [choker](#choker) fitted close around the [neck](#neck), one of the most common [accessories](#accessories) in gothic and [casual](#casual) designs alike. It may be [plain](#plain) [ribbon](#ribbon) or [leather](#leather), sometimes hung with a small charm.

entries.name: detached_collar
entries.description: A [folded](#folded) [shirt](#shirt) [collar](#collar) worn on its own with [no](#no) shirt behind it, commonly paired with a [necktie](#necktie) or [bowtie](#bowtie). A fixture of bunny suits and revealing costumes.

entries.name: blue_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad flat [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style uniform in blue, commonly navy edged with white lines. It hangs [square](#square) across the [back](#back) and tapers to a point at the front, and does not make the uniform itself count as blue.

entries.name: wing_collar
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) [collar](#collar) whose front corners fold down into small points, typical of formal [dress](#dress) shirts. It may be large-winged or only tipped at the corners; combine with [collared_shirt](#collared_shirt).

entries.name: white_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad, [square](#square) [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) of a [serafuku](#serafuku) rendered in white, tagged separately from the [shirt](#shirt) beneath it. A navy uniform with this collar still takes the [tag](#tag), while the neckerchief's colour is recorded on its own.

entries.name: neck_bell
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) or [choker](#choker) hung with one or more bells, of the kind put on a [house](#house) [cat](#cat) so it [can](#can) be heard. Common on catgirls and pet-themed outfits.

entries.name: fur_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) or detached collar built completely of fur. Fur only along the edge is [fur-trimmed_collar](#fur-trimmed_collar), the [choker](#choker) version is [fur_choker](#fur_choker), and a character's own ruff of body fur is [neck_fur](#neck_fur).

entries.name: black_collar
entries.description: A black [collar](#collar) worn round the [neck](#neck) as its own piece, such as a buckled [pet](#pet) or [slave](#slave) collar with a [ring](#ring). Not for the collar of a [shirt](#shirt) or for a black [sailor](#sailor) collar.

entries.name: white_collar
entries.description: A standalone white [collar](#collar) worn around the [neck](#neck), detached from any [shirt](#shirt). Not for a collared shirt, a [sailor](#sailor) collar or a wing collar that's part of a garment.

entries.name: red_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting red band worn around the [neck](#neck). Combine with [choker](#choker); borderline shades [can](#can) drift toward [pink_choker](#pink_choker) or [orange_choker](#orange_choker).

entries.name: white_choker
entries.description: A white band worn snugly around the [neck](#neck), often [lace](#lace) or [ribbon](#ribbon), common on lolita and [idol](#idol) outfits.

entries.name: cowbell
entries.description: The squat rectangular [bell](#bell) hung round the [neck](#neck) of grazing livestock, most often drawn on the [collar](#collar) of a cow-themed character. Real cattle wear them too, and they serve as a percussion [instrument](#instrument).

entries.name: ribbon_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) made of [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around the [neck](#neck) and finished with a [bow](#bow) at the front or [back](#back). Distinct from [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon), which stands in for a [necktie](#necktie) or [bowtie](#bowtie) at a [collar](#collar).

entries.name: spiked_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) ringed with [spikes](#spikes), worn as [punk](#punk) [fashion](#fashion) or fitted to an unusually aggressive [dog](#dog). Applies to both [people](#people) and animals alike.

entries.name: animal_collar
entries.description: A pet-style [collar](#collar) buckled round a person's [neck](#neck), typically a broad red [leather](#leather) band, sometimes with a name [tag](#tag) or [leash](#leash) attached. Frequent on characters with [animal_ears](#animal_ears), and it often hints at [pet_play](#pet_play) or [bdsm](#bdsm).

entries.name: belt_collar
entries.description: A [neck](#neck) [collar](#collar) made like a [belt](#belt), complete with [buckle](#buckle) and [punched](#punched) holes. Gothic, [punk](#punk) and pet-play designs favour it.

entries.name: blue_choker
entries.description: A blue band fastened snugly around the [neck](#neck). It sits high on the throat rather than [hanging](#hanging) loose like a [necklace](#necklace).

entries.name: red_collar
entries.description: A standalone red [collar](#collar) of the [pet](#pet) or accessory kind, worn around the [neck](#neck). Not for [shirt](#shirt) collars or a [red_sailor_collar](#red_sailor_collar); combine with collar.

entries.name: frilled_collar
entries.description: A ruffled [collar](#collar) that stands on its own, [wrapping](#wrapping) the [neck](#neck) as a separate piece rather than belonging to a garment. When the frilly collar is sewn onto a [shirt](#shirt), [blouse](#blouse) or [dress](#dress), use [frilled_shirt_collar](#frilled_shirt_collar) instead.

entries.name: popped_collar
entries.description: The [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt), [jacket](#jacket) or [coat](#coat) is turned up rather than [folded](#folded) flat. A styling [choice](#choice) often drawn on cool or arrogant characters.

entries.name: frilled_choker
entries.description: A neckband worn snug at the throat with ruffles [running](#running) along its edges. If the frilled band sits loosely rather than tight to the [neck](#neck), [frilled_collar](#frilled_collar) is the right [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pink_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting pink band worn tight around the [neck](#neck). The [shade](#shade) [can](#can) shade into [red_choker](#red_choker) or [purple_choker](#purple_choker), and a broader buckled band reads as a [collar](#collar).

entries.name: metal_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) made of metal, ranging from a slave-style [ring](#ring) to a decorative steel band.

entries.name: heart_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) [carrying](#carrying) at least one [heart](#heart), as a [dangling](#dangling) charm or worked into the band itself. A wider band with a heart ornament or [lock](#lock) at the front is [heart_collar](#heart_collar).

entries.name: red_sailor_collar
entries.description: A [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) in red on a [serafuku](#serafuku), sailor [dress](#dress) or sailor [shirt](#shirt). Colour judgement [can](#can) drift toward pink, orange or purple sailor collars in some lighting; pick the closest.

entries.name: o-ring_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) with a [ring](#ring) set into the band, generally [sitting](#sitting) at the hollow of the throat or at the [nape](#nape).

entries.name: purple_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting purple band worn around the [neck](#neck). A wider band with a [ring](#ring) or [buckle](#buckle) may instead be [purple_collar](#purple_collar).

entries.name: pendant_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) with a small ornament [dangling](#dangling) from it, free to [swing](#swing). A decoration fixed flat against the band does not count; [tag](#tag) what the ornament is as [well](#well).

entries.name: gold_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) of [gold](#gold) or gold-coloured material fitted snugly at the [neck](#neck), from a [plain](#plain) band to a worked [collar](#collar).

entries.name: purple_sailor_collar
entries.description: The wide flap [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style top in purple. Combine with [sailor_collar](#sailor_collar) and [serafuku](#serafuku); [shade](#shade) judgement overlaps with [blue_sailor_collar](#blue_sailor_collar) and [red_sailor_collar](#red_sailor_collar).

entries.name: neck_ruff
entries.description: The [pleated](#pleated) frill worn about the [neck](#neck) in European [fashion](#fashion) of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. It turns up on period [dress](#dress) and on [clown](#clown) costumes.

entries.name: green_choker
entries.description: A narrow green band fitted snugly around the throat, [plain](#plain) or [carrying](#carrying) a [pendant](#pendant) or [bell](#bell). A broad [strap](#strap) with a [buckle](#buckle) or [ring](#ring) is a [green_collar](#green_collar).

entries.name: bow_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband decorated with a [bow](#bow), often a [ribbon](#ribbon) knotted at the front or a [dark](#dark) band with a small bow sewn on. A bow worn at the throat in place of a tie is a [bowtie](#bowtie).

entries.name: star_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) [carrying](#carrying) at least one star, whether built into the band itself or hung from it as a charm. Any star shape counts.

entries.name: blue_collar
entries.description: A blue [collar](#collar) worn around the [neck](#neck) as a piece in its own right, like a [pet](#pet) or accessory collar. Shirt collars and a blue [sailor_collar](#sailor_collar) are something else.

entries.name: orange_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) in orange fastened close around the throat. Shading [can](#can) put it near [brown_choker](#brown_choker) or [yellow_choker](#yellow_choker), so judgement decides.

entries.name: yellow_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting yellow band worn around the [neck](#neck). Tag [choker](#choker) as [well](#well).

entries.name: spiked_choker
entries.description: A tight neckband [carrying](#carrying) at least one small spike. A close-fitting counterpart to [spiked_collar](#spiked_collar).

entries.name: pink_collar
entries.description: A standalone pink [collar](#collar) buckled around the [neck](#neck), of the pet-style or decorative sort. Not for the collar of a [shirt](#shirt), nor for a pink [sailor](#sailor) collar.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) finished with a [ribbon](#ribbon) threaded along its edge. Common on lolita [fashion](#fashion) and frilly dresses; [tag](#tag) the collar type as [well](#well).

entries.name: lace_choker
entries.description: A neckband that is a strip of [lace](#lace), with gaps visible through the middle rather than a solid backing. A solid band with lace edging is [lace-trimmed_choker](#lace-trimmed_choker).

entries.name: usekh_collar
entries.description: The broad, flat beaded [collar](#collar) of ancient Egyptian nobility, [spreading](#spreading) over the shoulders and chest. Common on [pharaoh](#pharaoh) and Egyptian-themed costumes.

entries.name: heart_collar
entries.description: A heart-shaped ornament sits at the front of a [collar](#collar), frequently a small [padlock](#padlock). Broader and more collar-like than a [heart_choker](#heart_choker).

entries.name: neck_tassel
entries.description: A decorative [tassel](#tassel) [hanging](#hanging) from a cord tied at the [neck](#neck), often on Chinese-styled or [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits. A tassel worn elsewhere uses tassel alone.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_collar
entries.description: A standalone or detached [collar](#collar) lined with fur along its edge. Made entirely of fur it is [fur_collar](#fur_collar), the [choker](#choker) version is [fur-trimmed_choker](#fur-trimmed_choker), and fur on a garment's own collar is tagged with that garment's name.

entries.name: brown_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting brown band round the [neck](#neck), often [leather](#leather) or [ribbon](#ribbon). A yellow one in dim light [can](#can) read as this; add [choker](#choker).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_choker
entries.description: A solid neckband with [lace](#lace) [running](#running) along its edges. The other case, a strip of openwork lace with [no](#no) solid centre, is [lace_choker](#lace_choker).

entries.name: cross_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband [carrying](#carrying) a [cross](#cross) charm or [pendant](#pendant). Reads as gothic or devotional depending on the rest of the outfit.

entries.name: purple_collar
entries.description: A standalone purple [collar](#collar) of the [pet](#pet) or accessory kind, worn around the [neck](#neck). Not for the collar built into a [shirt](#shirt) or a [purple_sailor_collar](#purple_sailor_collar).

entries.name: flower_choker
entries.description: A band worn snugly at the throat with a [bloom](#bloom) set on it, or plaited together from flowers outright. The blossom usually sits at the front of the [neck](#neck) as the centrepiece.

entries.name: anchor_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband [carrying](#carrying) an [anchor](#anchor), hung as a [pendant](#pendant), worked into the band or set as one large piece. It belongs to the nautical [wardrobe](#wardrobe).

entries.name: brown_collar
entries.description: A brown [collar](#collar) worn round the [neck](#neck) as its own item, such as a [leather](#leather) [pet](#pet) collar or a buckled band. It is not for a collared [shirt](#shirt) or a [brown_sailor_collar](#brown_sailor_collar), which are parts of a garment.

entries.name: green_collar
entries.description: A green [collar](#collar) of the strap-and-buckle sort worn by pets and pet-play designs, fastened around the [neck](#neck). The green collar of a [shirt](#shirt) is an entirely different thing.

entries.name: studded_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) set with metal [studs](#studs), worn tight around the [neck](#neck) in [punk](#punk) or gothic styling.

entries.name: grey_choker
entries.description: A grey band worn snug around the throat, in [ribbon](#ribbon), [leather](#leather) or [fabric](#fabric). It sits narrower and higher on the [neck](#neck) than a [collar](#collar).

entries.name: neck_flower
entries.description: A single [flower](#flower) or small spray worn at the throat, tucked into a [collar](#collar) or tied onto a [ribbon](#ribbon). It sits where a [choker](#choker) or [corsage](#corsage) would.

entries.name: studded_collar
entries.description: A [neck](#neck) [collar](#collar) reinforced with rows of metal [studs](#studs), worn as [fashion](#fashion) or as protection for an animal's throat. A [spiked](#spiked) collar, with long sharp points, is a separate thing. Implies collar.

entries.name: fur_choker
entries.description: A neckband made wholly of fur rather than [fabric](#fabric) or [leather](#leather). Fur-trimmed_choker carries fur only along its edge.

entries.name: pendant_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) with something [hanging](#hanging) from it that swings freely, a [tag](#tag), a [ring](#ring) or a jewel. Decorations [lying](#lying) flat on the band are not pendants.

entries.name: neck_garter
entries.description: A narrow band worn snug about the throat in the manner of a garter, often with a small [buckle](#buckle), [strap](#strap) or frill. It reads as [lingerie](#lingerie) moved up to the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: cat_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband [carrying](#carrying) a [cat](#cat) motif: a face, a pair of ears or a small [bell](#bell). Cat girl designs pair with it constantly, though any character may wear one.

entries.name: gold_collar
entries.description: A broad stiff [gold](#gold) band closed around the [neck](#neck), more rigid than a [choker](#choker). It appears on Egyptian-styled [dress](#dress), [ornate](#ornate) armour and imagery of ownership.

entries.name: padlocked_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) closed at the throat with a [padlock](#padlock), which may really [lock](#lock) or be there purely for looks. Reads as a mark of ownership and turns up throughout [bondage](#bondage) and pet-play pictures.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) edged with [lace](#lace), whether it belongs to a [blouse](#blouse) or is worn as a band of its own. The body of the piece stays solid [cloth](#cloth), with lace only at the rim.

entries.name: collar_jewel
entries.description: A gemstone mounted on a worn [neck](#neck) [collar](#collar), [sitting](#sitting) flat against the band. Where the stone swings loose from it instead, the picture also fits [pendant_collar](#pendant_collar).

entries.name: bead_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband built from [beads](#beads) threaded on a cord, [sitting](#sitting) snug at the throat. It reads as jewellery rather than as a [collar](#collar).

entries.name: aqua_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting band round the throat in a blue-green [shade](#shade). Wider buckled versions belong with the [collar](#collar) tags.

entries.name: yellow_collar
entries.description: A yellow band worn snugly around the [neck](#neck), from a buckled pet-style [collar](#collar) to a [plain](#plain) [strap](#strap). Colour is the only distinction from any other collar.

entries.name: grey_collar
entries.description: A standalone grey [collar](#collar) buckled around the [neck](#neck), separate from any garment. Shirt collars and [sailor](#sailor) collars that happen to be grey belong to other tags.

entries.name: o-ring_collar
entries.description: A band worn round the [neck](#neck) with a [ring](#ring) fixed at the front, the point where a lead would clip on.

entries.name: lace_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) made of [lace](#lace) throughout, sheer and open rather than solid [cloth](#cloth) trimmed at the rim. Blouses and gothic dresses carry it most often.

entries.name: bib_collar
entries.description: A wide flat [collar](#collar) in a rounded, [square](#square) or oval shape that lies over the upper chest like a child's [bib](#bib). Common on doll-like, gothic lolita and nursery-themed outfits.

entries.name: tassel_choker
entries.description: A narrow band worn tight at the throat with one or more tassels or [hanging](#hanging) cords [dropping](#dropping) from it. The [tassel](#tassel) is what distinguishes it; without one it is simply a [choker](#choker).

entries.name: mystical_high_collar
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [collar](#collar) that flares up and outward behind the head, generally built onto a [cloak](#cloak) rather than a [shirt](#shirt). Standard issue for wizards, psychics and vampires, often lined in a contrasting colour or marked with occult symbols.

entries.name: puritan_collar
entries.description: A wide flat [collar](#collar) that lies over the upper chest and hangs down, stopping at the shoulder rather than draping over it. Comes in rounded, pointed, or squared [shapes](#shapes) and is common in Lolita [fashion](#fashion), echoing historical pilgrim [dress](#dress); a [capelet](#capelet) is the version that does [cover](#cover) the shoulder.

entries.name: heart_ring_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) whose two ends meet at a heart-shaped [ring](#ring) [sitting](#sitting) at the throat.

entries.name: striped_choker
entries.description: A band worn close around the [neck](#neck) with stripes on it.

entries.name: butterfly_choker
entries.description: A close band around the throat [carrying](#carrying) a [butterfly](#butterfly) as its centrepiece. The [wings](#wings) may be metal, enamel or [lace](#lace), and the band itself is often [ribbon](#ribbon) or velvet.

entries.name: skull_choker
entries.description: A neckband bearing at least one [skull](#skull), either built into the band or hung from it as a charm. A gothic and [punk](#punk) [fashion](#fashion) [staple](#staple).

entries.name: guimpe
entries.description: A white [collar](#collar) piece covering the [neck](#neck) and shoulders, sometimes [reaching](#reaching) down over the chest, worn over a [dress](#dress). Historically a mark of modesty and [standing](#standing), best known today as part of a nun's [habit](#habit).

entries.name: orange_collar
entries.description: A separate orange [collar](#collar) buckled or tied round the [neck](#neck), of the band or [choker](#choker) sort. Shirt collars and [sailor](#sailor) collars are parts of a garment and do not count.

entries.name: crescent_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband with a [crescent](#crescent) [moon](#moon) at its front, worked in metal or [cloth](#cloth). Common on lunar and magical-girl designs.

entries.name: pearl_choker
entries.description: A short strand of pearls [sitting](#sitting) snug at the throat instead of [hanging](#hanging) down the chest. A classic formal piece, usually worn with an [evening](#evening) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: skull_collar
entries.description: A broad [collar](#collar) decorated with skulls, worn snug at the throat. Heavier and more strap-like than a [choker](#choker) of the same design.

entries.name: two-tone_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband in exactly two colours, often a band with contrasting trim or an [inset](#inset) stripe. A third colour takes it out of this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: feather_collar
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of [feathers](#feathers) worn about the [neck](#neck), either a separate band or a plumed [collar](#collar) built into a [costume](#costume). Common on bird-themed and burlesque outfits.

entries.name: no_choker
