entries.description: The [choker](#choker) belonging to a character's usual design is missing from the [neck](#neck). Use it only where the whole throat is visible, since a chin or a raised [collar](#collar) [can](#can) hide one.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) with fur lining its edge. One made entirely of fur is [fur_choker](#fur_choker), and furred collars attached to a [jacket](#jacket) or [kimono](#kimono) are [fur_collar](#fur_collar).

entries.name: aqua_collar
entries.description: A blue-green band buckled or clasped round the [neck](#neck), of the sort worn by pets and pet-play designs. Not the [folded](#folded) [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt), which is tagged separately.

entries.name: silver_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband in a silvery metallic finish. Recorded as [grey_choker](#grey_choker) or [white_choker](#white_choker) instead, since the sheen is treated as a [shade](#shade) of one of those colors rather than its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: leather_choker
entries.description: A snug band of hide worn around the throat, [plain](#plain), buckled or set with [studs](#studs). An accessory rather than a restraint.

entries.name: neck_bobbles
entries.description: Small round [beads](#beads) or pom-poms strung at the throat as an ornament, [hanging](#hanging) just under the chin. They sit on a cord or band rather than a [chain](#chain).

entries.name: unworn_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) is present in the picture but not fastened around anyone's [neck](#neck), held in a hand, [lying](#lying) on a surface or [dangling](#dangling) by its [ring](#ring).

entries.name: scarf_choker
entries.description: A small [scarf](#scarf) or strip of [cloth](#cloth) wound tight around the [neck](#neck) so that it sits snug like a [choker](#choker). A scarf [hanging](#hanging) loose at the throat does not qualify.

entries.name: chain_around_neck
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) looped plainly about the throat, [reading](#reading) as a chain rather than as a finished piece of jewellery. A proper [necklace](#necklace) built out of links is [chain_necklace](#chain_necklace).

entries.name: striped_collar
entries.description: A [neck](#neck) [collar](#collar) marked with stripes, whether a [fashion](#fashion) band or a pet-style one.

entries.name: snowflake_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband built around a snowflake as its centerpiece, or with [snowflakes](#snowflakes) repeated along its length. A constant on winter- and ice-themed outfits.

entries.name: clerical_collar
entries.description: The stiff white band at the throat of a black clergy [shirt](#shirt), marking the wearer as a [priest](#priest) or pastor. A small detail that identifies the whole outfit.

entries.name: supportasse
entries.description: A stiffened frame worn under a ruff or a [standing](#standing) [collar](#collar) to hold it out from the [neck](#neck), part of European court [dress](#dress) around 1600. It props the [lace](#lace) or linen collar into its wide shape.

entries.name: diamond_choker
entries.description: A close-fitting neckband set with diamonds or diamond-cut stones, [sitting](#sitting) tight against the throat. Worn with [evening](#evening) [dress](#dress) and other formal wear.

entries.name: string_choker
entries.description: A [choker](#choker) made from [plain](#plain) cord or thin [string](#string) knotted at the throat, with [no](#no) band, [plate](#plate) or [pendant](#pendant). Minimal by design.

entries.name: scarf
entries.description: A long, narrow strip of [cloth](#cloth) wound around the [neck](#neck), typically in [cold](#cold) weather and a trademark of [ninja](#ninja) characters. Related tags [cover](#cover) [scarf_over_mouth](#scarf_over_mouth), [shared_scarf](#shared_scarf) and [holding](#holding) a scarf.

entries.name: neckerchief
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the [neck](#neck) so that two loose ends hang down like a tie. It most often belongs to a [serafuku](#serafuku) or another outfit with a [sailor_collar](#sailor_collar).

entries.name: red_neckerchief
entries.description: A red [neckerchief](#neckerchief), the triangular [scarf](#scarf) knotted at the front of a [serafuku](#serafuku) or scout uniform. One of the most common school-uniform accents; a long wrapped scarf is [red_scarf](#red_scarf) instead.

entries.name: red_scarf
entries.description: A long red [scarf](#scarf) wrapped around the [neck](#neck), often trailing in the [wind](#wind) on heroic or [winter](#winter) designs. A small knotted [triangle](#triangle) at the [collar](#collar) is [red_neckerchief](#red_neckerchief) instead.

entries.name: white_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) in white, wound at the [neck](#neck) or streaming out behind the wearer. It turns up constantly on [winter](#winter) outfits and on ninja- or pilot-styled designs; use alongside scarf.

entries.name: yellow_neckerchief
entries.description: A yellow [kerchief](#kerchief) knotted at the front of a [serafuku](#serafuku) or scout uniform. Tag [neckerchief](#neckerchief) alongside.

entries.name: blue_neckerchief
entries.description: A blue [neckerchief](#neckerchief) knotted at the front of a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) or a uniform. It is a small [folded](#folded) [triangle](#triangle) rather than a wrapped [scarf](#scarf).

entries.name: blue_scarf
entries.description: A blue [scarf](#scarf) wound around the [neck](#neck), whether a thick [winter](#winter) knit or a long one streaming out behind. It sits at the neck, unlike a [shawl](#shawl) draped over the shoulders.

entries.name: black_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) in black wound around the [neck](#neck), from a bulky [winter](#winter) knit to a long trailing one. Neither length nor material is part of the claim.

entries.name: black_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) in black, the triangular [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the front of a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) or uniform. It lies flat over the chest rather than [wrapping](#wrapping) the throat.

entries.name: white_neckerchief
entries.description: A white [neckerchief](#neckerchief) knotted at the front of the [collar](#collar), usually part of a sailor-style [school](#school) uniform or scout [dress](#dress).

entries.name: plaid_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) in plaid or tartan, usually a [winter](#winter) scarf wrapped around the [neck](#neck). Tag [plaid_clothes](#plaid_clothes) alongside it.

entries.name: pink_neckerchief
entries.description: A pink [neckerchief](#neckerchief), the small [folded](#folded) [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the front of a sailor-style [collar](#collar). School [serafuku](#serafuku) wear it most; other neckwear [shapes](#shapes) have their own tags.

entries.name: striped_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes, often a knitted [winter](#winter) piece in alternating bands. Implies scarf and [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: pink_scarf
entries.description: A pink [scarf](#scarf) wound round the [neck](#neck) or draped over the shoulders, knitted for [winter](#winter) or light for [fashion](#fashion). A small knotted [cloth](#cloth) on a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) is a [neckerchief](#neckerchief).

entries.name: yellow_scarf
entries.description: A yellow [scarf](#scarf) worn around the [neck](#neck). Tag scarf alongside.

entries.name: brown_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) in brown, wound round the [neck](#neck) or [hanging](#hanging) loose over the shoulders. Autumn and [winter](#winter) scenes carry it most often.

entries.name: green_scarf
entries.description: A green [scarf](#scarf) wound around the [neck](#neck) or trailing in the [wind](#wind). It is a [staple](#staple) of [winter](#winter) and [autumn](#autumn) outfits.

entries.name: feather_boa
entries.description: A long [fluffy](#fluffy) [rope](#rope) of [feathers](#feathers) or fur draped round the [neck](#neck) or over the upper arms like a [scarf](#scarf). A showgirl and glamour accessory, often in a bright colour.

entries.name: checkered_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) [carrying](#carrying) a clear chequerboard pattern, wound around the [neck](#neck) or [hanging](#hanging) loose over the shoulders. The check has to be [plain](#plain) enough to read at a [glance](#glance).

entries.name: purple_scarf
entries.description: A purple [scarf](#scarf) wound around the [neck](#neck), draped over the shoulders, or trailing loose in the [wind](#wind). Combine with scarf; a small knotted [square](#square) instead is a [purple_neckerchief](#purple_neckerchief).

entries.name: fur_scarf
entries.description: A length of fur worn wrapped around the [neck](#neck). Distinct from a [fur_collar](#fur_collar) belonging to a garment and from a character's own neck fur.

entries.name: aqua_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) in aqua, knotted at the throat as on a sailor-style [school](#school) top. Add [serafuku](#serafuku) where that is the outfit.

entries.name: orange_neckerchief
entries.description: An orange [neckerchief](#neckerchief), most often the triangular [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the front of a [sailor](#sailor) uniform. A long wound one is [orange_scarf](#orange_scarf).

entries.name: grey_neckerchief
entries.description: A grey [neckerchief](#neckerchief), such as the small [scarf](#scarf) knotted at the front of a [serafuku](#serafuku) or a scout uniform. It sits at the throat rather than [wrapping](#wrapping) the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: green_neckerchief
entries.description: A green [neckerchief](#neckerchief), such as the small [scarf](#scarf) knotted at the front of a [serafuku](#serafuku). It sits at the throat rather than [wrapping](#wrapping) the [neck](#neck) for warmth.

entries.name: orange_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) in orange wound round the [neck](#neck), from a [heavy](#heavy) [winter](#winter) knit to a long trailing one. A small triangular [cloth](#cloth) is [orange_neckerchief](#orange_neckerchief).

entries.name: grey_scarf
entries.description: A grey [scarf](#scarf) wound around the [neck](#neck) or trailing loose. It is a [staple](#staple) of [winter](#winter) and [autumn](#autumn) outfits.

entries.name: shared_scarf
entries.description: One [scarf](#scarf) wrapped around two or more [people](#people) at once, a [familiar](#familiar) [sign](#sign) of closeness and a romantic [winter](#winter) motif.

entries.name: purple_neckerchief
entries.description: A purple [neckerchief](#neckerchief) knotted at the front of a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar) or [shirt](#shirt). On a [serafuku](#serafuku) it does not make the whole uniform count as purple.

entries.name: torn_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) with ragged, ripped ends.

entries.name: scarf_over_mouth
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) pulled up so it hides the wearer's mouth, either for warmth or to conceal the face. Implies scarf.

entries.name: two-tone_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) made in two basic colours, striped or [split](#split) down its length. Implies scarf.

entries.name: bandana_around_neck
entries.description: A [bandana](#bandana) tied at the throat with most of the [cloth](#cloth) [hanging](#hanging) down over the chest. It [can](#can) be pulled up to serve as a [mask](#mask) when needed.

entries.name: floating_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) trailing or fluttering in the air, generally [caught](#caught) by [wind](#wind). A dramatic accent on a [standing](#standing) or [running](#running) [figure](#figure).

entries.name: multicolored_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) with two or more distinct colours in it, bold stripes in contrasting hues being the usual case. Knitted [winter](#winter) scarves are the commonest carriers.

entries.name: bib
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) or plastic [square](#square) tied under the chin to catch [food](#food), worn mainly by babies and small children. Adults wear one in [comic](#comic) scenes or in age-play pictures.

entries.name: kerchief
entries.description: A [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) tied at the [neck](#neck) or over the head, or carried [folded](#folded) as a [handkerchief](#handkerchief). Where the placement is obvious, [neckerchief](#neckerchief), [headscarf](#headscarf) or handkerchief says more.

entries.name: brown_neckerchief
entries.description: A small brown [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the throat. It shows up most on [school](#school) uniforms, scouting outfits and [cowboy](#cowboy) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: unworn_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) is visible in the picture without being wound around a [neck](#neck), hung up, [folded](#folded) or fallen across a surface.

entries.name: long_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) longer than its wearer is [tall](#tall), trailing behind them or streaming through the air. Artists lean on it to give a still picture a sense of [wind](#wind) and movement.

entries.name: print_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) with a design printed across it. The print alone does not make it multicoloured, which is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: aqua_scarf
entries.description: A blue-green [scarf](#scarf) wound round the [neck](#neck) or trailing loose behind. Winter scenes and long flowing hero scarves both use it.

entries.name: striped_neckerchief
entries.description: A small [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the throat, [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [neckerchief](#neckerchief).

entries.name: neck_warmer
entries.description: A closed [tube](#tube) of knit or fleece pulled over the [neck](#neck), sometimes drawn up over the lower face. It gives a scarf's warmth without the trailing ends.

entries.name: scarf_bow
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) knotted so that its ends stand out as a [bow](#bow) at the throat or across the chest.

entries.name: polka_dot_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) [patterned](#patterned) with round [dots](#dots), wound at the [neck](#neck) or draped over the shoulders. Works as a [winter](#winter) wrap and as a light accessory alike.

entries.name: vertical-striped_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) whose stripes run along its length rather than banding across it at intervals. Less usual than the crosswise pattern most knitted scarves carry.

entries.name: polka_dot_neckerchief
entries.description: A [square](#square) of dotted [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the throat. Turns up on [sailor](#sailor) uniforms, scout outfits, and rockabilly styling.

entries.name: neckerchief_between_breasts
entries.description: The [tail](#tail) of a [neckerchief](#neckerchief) [hanging](#hanging) down into the [cleavage](#cleavage) rather than [lying](#lying) flat across the chest. The [breasts](#breasts) frame the strip of [cloth](#cloth) either side of it.

entries.name: multicolored_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) [carrying](#carrying) at least two colours, whether [patterned](#patterned) or divided plainly between them. Sailor-collar uniforms supply most of the examples.

entries.name: gradient_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) whose [cloth](#cloth) shades from one colour into another, most often knotted at the [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style uniform.

entries.name: checkered_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) [patterned](#patterned) in alternating squares, knotted or clipped at the throat. School and scouting uniforms are its usual home.

entries.name: argyle_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) [carrying](#carrying) the argyle diamond [lattice](#lattice), usually a [heavy](#heavy) knitted one worn for warmth. The pattern usually runs the length of the scarf and ends at a fringe.

entries.name: plaid_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) in tartan, knotted at the throat or tucked under a [sailor](#sailor) [collar](#collar). Common on [school](#school) uniforms.

entries.name: torn_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) frayed or ripped through.

entries.name: two-tone_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) [carrying](#carrying) exactly two colours, often a [field](#field) with a contrasting edge or stripe. Anything richer counts as multicoloured.

entries.name: no_scarf
entries.description: Somebody whose [signature](#signature) look includes a [scarf](#scarf) is drawn without one, and [no](#no) scarf appears anywhere in the picture. Where it is visible but taken off, [unworn_scarf](#unworn_scarf) fits.

entries.name: unworn_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) is in the picture but off the wearer's [neck](#neck). Where the [cloth](#cloth) is untied yet still [hanging](#hanging) on the character, [undone_neckerchief](#undone_neckerchief) is the correct [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: camouflage_scarf
entries.description: A [neck](#neck) [scarf](#scarf) printed in a [camouflage](#camouflage) pattern, wrapped close or [hanging](#hanging) loose. Usually part of a military-flavoured outfit.

entries.name: print_neckerchief
entries.description: A [neckerchief](#neckerchief) [carrying](#carrying) a printed motif, knotted at the throat. The pattern takes the place of the usual single-colour [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: gradient_scarf
entries.description: A [scarf](#scarf) whose colour passes smoothly from one [shade](#shade) to another along its length, the shift clearest where the ends hang loose.

entries.name: gloves
entries.description: Coverings for the hands with a separate [opening](#opening) or [sheath](#sheath) for at least one finger besides the thumb. Material, colour and state tags such as [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves), [white_gloves](#white_gloves) or [single_glove](#single_glove) are added on top.

entries.name: black_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in black, whether short, elbow-length, fingerless or [leather](#leather). Add the length or style [tag](#tag) wherever it matters.

entries.name: elbow_gloves
entries.description: Long [gloves](#gloves) [reaching](#reaching) to the elbow or past it, also called opera or [evening](#evening) gloves. They go with gowns, bunny suits and magical girl outfits.

entries.name: white_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in white, the standard for butlers, [military](#military) [dress](#dress) uniforms, brides and [stage](#stage) magicians. Add the length, such as [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves).

entries.name: fingerless_gloves
entries.description: Gloves cut off so the fingers stay bare, guarding the palm while leaving a skin-on grip. Fighters, bikers and action characters wear them constantly.

entries.name: wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Detached [cuffs](#cuffs) worn around the wrists that look like the end of a [shirt](#shirt) sleeve, complete with [frills](#frills), [buttons](#buttons), or similar detail, in [fabric](#fabric), [leather](#leather), fur, or metal. A [plain](#plain) band without that cuff shape is a [wristband](#wristband) instead, and actual [restraints](#restraints) are cuffs, [handcuffs](#handcuffs), or [shackles](#shackles).

entries.name: armband
entries.description: A band of [cloth](#cloth) worn around the upper arm over a sleeve, marking rank, group or duty, or worn simply for looks. An elastic band on the bare arm is [arm_garter](#arm_garter).

entries.name: wristband
entries.description: One of any number of bands worn around the wrist, made of [cloth](#cloth), rubber, [leather](#leather) or metal depending on its purpose, from sweatbands to [festival](#festival) wristbands. A frilled or cuff-like version is called [wrist_cuffs](#wrist_cuffs) instead.

entries.name: bridal_gauntlets
entries.description: Close-fitting, usually elbow-length handwear held on by a loop around one finger instead of separate finger holes, in the style worn at weddings. It names that particular shape only: any other glove paired with a [wedding_dress](#wedding_dress) is simply [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: brown_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in brown, whether [leather](#leather), [wool](#wool) or fingerless. Add [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: red_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in red, of any length or style, from short hand [gloves](#gloves) to elbow-length ones. Combine with the matching cut [tag](#tag) such as [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) or [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves) where it applies.

entries.name: single_glove
entries.description: A glove worn on one hand only. Use [single_fingerless_glove](#single_fingerless_glove) or [single_elbow_glove](#single_elbow_glove) for those particular variants.

entries.name: partially_fingerless_gloves
entries.description: Gloves where some fingers are cut off and others stay covered, for instance a bare thumb and index finger with the rest enclosed. A variant of [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves).

entries.name: blue_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in blue, of any length from short to elbow-high. The style is a separate matter, so add [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) or [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves) where they apply.

entries.name: arm_warmers
entries.description: Loose tubes of [fabric](#fabric) pulled over the arms, separate from the top and [running](#running) past the wrist, with [no](#no) holes for the fingers. Sleeves that match the outfit are [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves).

entries.name: wrist_scrunchie
entries.description: A [scrunchie](#scrunchie) worn on the wrist like a [bracelet](#bracelet) rather than in the hair. It is not the same thing as [wrist_cuffs](#wrist_cuffs); [tag](#tag) scrunchie alongside it.

entries.name: half_gloves
entries.description: Gloves that [cover](#cover) only the fingers or stop [well](#well) short of the wrist. Gloves with the fingertips cut off are [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves), not this.

entries.name: purple_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in purple of any length. Combine with [gloves](#gloves) and the style, such as [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) or [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves).

entries.name: mittens
entries.description: Hand coverings with one [pocket](#pocket) for the thumb and another shared pocket for the remaining four fingers, usually knitted [winter](#winter) wear. Not counted as [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: paw_gloves
entries.description: Gloves shaped like [animal](#animal) paws, generally [furry](#furry) with pads or [claws](#claws) at the tips, worn with animal ears or as part of a full [costume](#costume). The matching footwear is [paw_shoes](#paw_shoes).

entries.name: asymmetrical_gloves
entries.description: Gloves built to differ between the hands, one cut or shaped unlike the other. A difference of length alone belongs to [uneven_gloves](#uneven_gloves), and one of colour or pattern to [mismatched_gloves](#mismatched_gloves).

entries.name: white_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Detached white [cuffs](#cuffs) worn at the wrists in the shape of a [shirt](#shirt) sleeve's end, common on [maid](#maid) and bunny outfits. Tag [wrist_cuffs](#wrist_cuffs) alongside it.

entries.name: bracer
entries.description: A rigid [guard](#guard) of [leather](#leather) or metal strapped over the wrist and forearm, worn by archers and as light armour. It is bulkier and sturdier than a [bracelet](#bracelet), while a full articulated [plate](#plate) piece is [vambraces](#vambraces).

entries.name: pink_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in pink at any length, from short wrist [gloves](#gloves) to elbow-length ones. Fingerless and elbow versions carry their own tags alongside.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_gloves
entries.description: Gloves finished with a band of fur at the wrist or cuff. Usually part of a matching set of fur-trimmed [winter](#winter) clothing.

entries.name: grey_gloves
entries.description: Grey [gloves](#gloves), at any length from the wrist to the elbow. Add [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves) or [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) where the cut is worth [recording](#recording).

entries.name: yellow_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in yellow, from rubber [cleaning](#cleaning) [gloves](#gloves) to formal [dress](#dress) gloves. Tag gloves alongside.

entries.name: arm_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around the upper arm, worn as an ornament or used to hold up a loose glove or arm warmer. Tag its colour alongside.

entries.name: green_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in green, at any length from the wrist to the elbow. Add [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves) or [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) where the cut is worth [recording](#recording).

entries.name: arm_garter
entries.description: An elastic band worn around the bare upper arm, in most art purely as an ornament. Worn over a sleeve instead, it becomes a [sleeve_garter](#sleeve_garter).

entries.name: print_gloves
entries.description: Gloves [carrying](#carrying) a printed pattern or motif. Tag [gloves](#gloves) with them; a print does not by itself make them [multicolored_gloves](#multicolored_gloves).

entries.name: mismatched_gloves
entries.description: A pair of [gloves](#gloves) with different colors or patterns on each hand. Different lengths are [uneven_gloves](#uneven_gloves), and a single glove worn alone is [single_glove](#single_glove).

entries.name: two-tone_gloves
entries.description: Gloves made in exactly two colours, whether [split](#split) by panel or between finger and palm. Add the colour tags too.

entries.name: frilled_gloves
entries.description: Gloves [carrying](#carrying) ruffles anywhere on them, most often bunched at the cuff. The same picture may [well](#well) need [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) or [frilled_sleeves](#frilled_sleeves) alongside it.

entries.name: single_elbow_glove
entries.description: An elbow-length glove worn on one arm only. Tag with [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves); if the glove lacks fingers add [single_fingerless_glove](#single_fingerless_glove).

entries.name: elbow_pads
entries.description: Padding strapped round the elbows to take the shock of falls and knocks. Worn by skaters, cyclists, athletes and soldiers, generally alongside knee pads.

entries.name: red_armband
entries.description: A red band worn around the upper arm. In Japanese [school](#school) settings it commonly marks a student council member or event leader, while in political contexts it [can](#can) evoke Nazi or communist imagery.

entries.name: wrist_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around the wrist purely as decoration. Tag ribbon alongside it, and add [wrist_bow](#wrist_bow) too if it is tied into a [bow](#bow) shape.

entries.name: latex_gloves
entries.description: Gloves of glossy [latex](#latex), from long opera-length fetish pairs to thin surgical ones. The sheen along the fingers is what separates them from [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: cow_print_gloves
entries.description: Gloves, often [reaching](#reaching) to the elbow, printed in black-and-white [cow](#cow) patches. Part of the standard cow-themed set beside the [bikini](#bikini) and the stockings.

entries.name: orange_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in orange, from short [dress](#dress) [gloves](#gloves) to long ones [reaching](#reaching) the elbow. Add the length [tag](#tag) where one applies.

entries.name: black_bridal_gauntlets
entries.description: Bridal [gauntlets](#gauntlets) in black: fingerless arm coverings that [hook](#hook) over the middle finger and run up the forearm. They belong to [fantasy](#fantasy) and bridal-styled designs rather than to armour.

entries.name: single_fingerless_glove
entries.description: A fingerless glove worn on one hand alone, the [single_glove](#single_glove) pattern with the fingers cut away.

entries.name: multicolored_gloves
entries.description: A single glove worked in several colours. Where the two [gloves](#gloves) of a pair differ from each other, the uneven gloves [tag](#tag) fits better.

entries.name: frilled_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Separate bands worn at the wrists, made of or edged with ruffles. Maid and lolita outfits favour them; ruffles belonging to a sleeve are [frilled_sleeves](#frilled_sleeves) instead.

entries.name: uneven_gloves
entries.description: A pair of [gloves](#gloves) of unequal length, such as one wrist-length and one elbow-length. Different colours or patterns instead is [mismatched_gloves](#mismatched_gloves), and a single glove alone is [single_glove](#single_glove).

entries.name: yugake
entries.description: The single [leather](#leather) glove of Japanese [archery](#archery), worn on the right hand and covering only three or four fingers. Seen on [kyuudou](#kyuudou) practitioners; [tag](#tag) [partially_fingerless_gloves](#partially_fingerless_gloves) as [well](#well).

entries.name: sleeve_garter
entries.description: A band worn around the upper arm over a [shirt](#shirt) sleeve to hold it up, a look tied to old-time bartenders and barbershop quartets. Around a bare arm it is [arm_garter](#arm_garter).

entries.name: blue_armband
entries.description: A blue band worn around the upper arm. It often marks a committee, a team or a rank rather than [serving](#serving) purely as decoration.

entries.name: sweatband
entries.description: A [fluffy](#fluffy), absorbent band worn on the wrist or around the [forehead](#forehead) to soak up [sweat](#sweat) during sport.

entries.name: arm_wrap
entries.description: Strips of [cloth](#cloth) wound around the arm from wrist to elbow, as fighters wear them to [guard](#guard) the hands and [forearms](#forearms). Dressings applied to a wound are [bandages](#bandages) instead.

entries.name: fishnet_gloves
entries.description: Gloves made of open [mesh](#mesh), so the hands show through. Often worn with other mesh pieces in [punk](#punk) and gothic outfits.

entries.name: yellow_armband
entries.description: A yellow band worn around the upper arm, often marking a role such as class representative or committee member. Tag [armband](#armband) alongside.

entries.name: wrist_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied directly around the wrist as an accessory. A bow attached to a glove instead is [glove_bow](#glove_bow); [tag](#tag) bow alongside it.

entries.name: black_armband
entries.description: A black band worn around the upper arm or over a sleeve, sometimes signalling [mourning](#mourning), rank or a duty role. It is a narrow strip rather than a full sleeve.

entries.name: striped_arm_warmers
entries.description: Arm warmers banded with stripes, covering the [forearms](#forearms) while leaving the hands free.

entries.name: striped_gloves
entries.description: Gloves with a striped pattern.

entries.name: wrist_guards
entries.description: Protective gear strapped over the wrists for sport or combat, such as [skating](#skating) guards or [archery](#archery) bracers. Tag whichever sport is shown alongside it.

entries.name: leather_gloves
entries.description: Gloves of tanned hide, from thin [driving](#driving) [gloves](#gloves) to [heavy](#heavy) work or combat pairs.

entries.name: black_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Black bands worn around the wrists as separate pieces, as on a bunny [suit](#suit) or a dance [costume](#costume). They belong to [no](#no) sleeve and [cover](#cover) nothing else.

entries.name: clawed_gauntlets
entries.description: Armoured [gauntlets](#gauntlets) fitted with claw-like blades or [talons](#talons) at the fingertips. Part of the armour or [costume](#costume) rather than a [weapon](#weapon) carried on its own.

entries.name: black_arm_warmers
entries.description: Tubes of knit or stretch [fabric](#fabric) worn on the [forearms](#forearms) in black, leaving the hands free. Distinct from [gloves](#gloves), which [cover](#cover) the hand, and from sleeves attached to a garment.

entries.name: unworn_gloves
entries.description: One or both [gloves](#gloves) have been removed and are visible in the scene, held in hand or set aside.

entries.name: lace_gloves
entries.description: Gloves made throughout of [lace](#lace), so the hand shows through the openwork. Gloves with only a lace cuff are [lace-trimmed_gloves](#lace-trimmed_gloves).

entries.name: pink_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Pink [cuffs](#cuffs) worn around the wrists with [no](#no) glove attached to them. Bunny suits, [idol](#idol) costumes and [maid](#maid) outfits use them most.

entries.name: no_gloves
entries.description: A character usually drawn gloved appears bare-handed, a departure from the standard design. The [gloves](#gloves) are absent from the picture rather than set aside.

entries.name: oven_mitts
entries.description: Thickly padded [mittens](#mittens) worn to grip [hot](#hot) trays and pans without [burning](#burning) the hands. Kitchen and [baking](#baking) scenes are where they appear, frequently together with an [apron](#apron).

entries.name: wrist_wrap
entries.description: A strip of [cloth](#cloth) or bandage wound around the wrist alone, leaving the hand and most of the forearm bare. It is common on martial artists and adventurers.

entries.name: torn_gloves
entries.description: Gloves with rips or holes in them.

entries.name: single_wrist_cuff
entries.description: A detached shirt-style cuff worn on one wrist only, the other wrist bare. An asymmetric accessory detail; [tag](#tag) alongside [wrist_cuffs](#wrist_cuffs).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_gloves
entries.description: Gloves finished with a band of [lace](#lace) at the cuff. Gloves cut entirely from lace are [lace_gloves](#lace_gloves).

entries.name: aqua_gloves
entries.description: Gloves in a blue-green [shade](#shade). Add the length or style, such as [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) or [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves).

entries.name: pink_arm_warmers
entries.description: Tubes of knitted or stretch [fabric](#fabric) pulled over the [forearms](#forearms) in pink, leaving the hands entirely free. That open end is what separates them from [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: green_armband
entries.description: A green band worn round the upper arm, often part of a uniform or marking somebody out as a committee member or team official.

entries.name: white_mittens
entries.description: White [mittens](#mittens) covering the hands without separate fingers, a [winter](#winter) outfit [staple](#staple).

entries.name: santa_gloves
entries.description: Red [gloves](#gloves) with white trim in the style of Santa Claus's, usually worn as part of a Christmas outfit. Tag alongside [santa_costume](#santa_costume) or [santa_dress](#santa_dress) when the rest of the clothing [matches](#matches).

entries.name: red_mittens
entries.description: Red [mittens](#mittens), the handwear with one [pocket](#pocket) for the fingers and a separate thumb. Typical of [winter](#winter) and Christmas scenes; [gloves](#gloves) with separated fingers take [red_gloves](#red_gloves).

entries.name: arm_cuffs
entries.description: Decorative [cuffs](#cuffs) worn on the arms above the wrist, matching the wrist and ankle cuffs of a bunny [suit](#suit) or dancer's [costume](#costume). Restraints locked onto the arms are a different matter.

entries.name: white_arm_warmers
entries.description: Tube-shaped sleeves worn over the [forearms](#forearms) in white, separate from any top. They leave the hands and fingers bare, which sets them apart from [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: white_bridal_gauntlets
entries.description: Long white sleeves [running](#running) from above the elbow across the [back](#back) of the hand, leaving the fingers free. Named for bridal wear but just as common on priestesses and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits.

entries.name: single_arm_warmer
entries.description: An arm warmer worn on one arm only, the other left bare or dressed differently. Tag alongside [arm_warmers](#arm_warmers).

entries.name: blue_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Blue bands fastened around the wrists as ornament, covering nothing of the hand. They are worn on their own rather than as the cuff of a glove.

entries.name: rubber_gloves
entries.description: Thick rubber [gloves](#gloves) worn for [cleaning](#cleaning), [dishwashing](#dishwashing) or handling [chemicals](#chemicals). Thin medical gloves are made from a different material and are tagged separately.

entries.name: single_bridal_gauntlet
entries.description: A fingerless, over-the-hand sleeve of the [bridal_gauntlets](#bridal_gauntlets) kind is worn on one arm alone. Not the same as [single_sleeve](#single_sleeve) or an ordinary detached sleeve.

entries.name: frilled_armband
entries.description: A band worn around the upper arm, gathered or edged with ruffles. It is a standard piece of [maid](#maid), [idol](#idol) and lolita coordinates.

entries.name: glove_bow
entries.description: A small [bow](#bow) fixed to a glove, usually at the cuff or on the [back](#back) of the hand. A bow tied around a bare wrist is [wrist_bow](#wrist_bow).

entries.name: hand_wraps
entries.description: Strips of [cloth](#cloth) or bandage wound tightly around the hands and knuckles. They mark out [boxers](#boxers), martial artists and anyone about to throw a punch.

entries.name: two-sided_gloves
entries.description: Gloves lined on the inside in a different colour from the outside. The difference shows at the cuff or wherever the [fabric](#fabric) turns over.

entries.name: frilled_wristband
entries.description: A band of gathered ruffled [fabric](#fabric) worn at the wrist, generally as a matching pair. Maid, [idol](#idol) and [stage](#stage) costumes rely on them heavily.

entries.name: brown_mittens
entries.description: Brown [mittens](#mittens), the [winter](#winter) hand covering that [gathers](#gathers) all four fingers into a single [pocket](#pocket) and gives the thumb its own. Warmer than [gloves](#gloves) and much clumsier for handling anything.

entries.name: elbow_sleeve
entries.description: A short band of stretchy [fabric](#fabric) wrapped tight round the elbow alone, worn for support in sport. Anything [carrying](#carrying) on to the wrist or shoulder is [arm_warmers](#arm_warmers), [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves) or [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves).

entries.name: igote
entries.description: A sleeve-shaped [guard](#guard) covering one arm and its shoulder, traditionally the left, worn by Japanese archers so the bowstring cannot snag on [cloth](#cloth). It also goes by the name yugote.

entries.name: fur_cuffs
entries.description: Bands of fur worn around the wrists or the ankles. Tribal, animal-themed and [winter](#winter) costumes use them, usually in matching pairs.

entries.name: red_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Red bands worn snugly around the wrists, sometimes with a frilled or buckled edge. An accessory rather than [restraints](#restraints), unlike the [cuffs](#cuffs) used in [bondage](#bondage).

entries.name: glove_cutout
entries.description: A glove with an [opening](#opening) cut into it, most often on the [back](#back) of the hand, baring skin while the fingers stay covered. Different from [fingerless_gloves](#fingerless_gloves), where the fingertips are missing.

entries.name: blue_mittens
entries.description: Blue handwear gathering the fingers into a single [pocket](#pocket) with the thumb kept apart. Warmer and clumsier than [gloves](#gloves), which sleeve each finger.

entries.name: metal_gloves
entries.description: Gauntlet-style [gloves](#gloves) formed from metal plates, worn with [armor](#armor) or [heavy](#heavy) [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: wrist_straps
entries.description: Straps buckled or wound around the wrist, whether decorative or [holding](#holding) something else in place. They read narrower than a full gauntlet and plainer than a [bracelet](#bracelet).

entries.name: purple_armband
entries.description: A purple band worn around the upper arm, whether decorative, part of a uniform, or marking a role. Narrower than an arm warmer, and worn higher on the arm.

entries.name: purple_arm_warmers
entries.description: Purple tubes of [fabric](#fabric) covering the [forearms](#forearms) without enclosing the hands. Distinct from [gloves](#gloves), which have separate sections for the fingers and thumb.

entries.name: wrist_flower
entries.description: One or more blossoms worn around the wrist as a [corsage](#corsage). Weddings, dances, and other formal occasions call for it.

entries.name: studded_gloves
entries.description: Gloves set with metal [studs](#studs), most often across the knuckles or the [back](#back) of the hand.

entries.name: single_half_glove
entries.description: One short glove ending before the wrist, worn on a single hand while the other stays bare. The stubby variant of wearing just one glove.

entries.name: layered_gloves
entries.description: Two or more pairs of [gloves](#gloves) worn one over the other on the same hands. The cuff of the inner pair usually shows at the wrist.

entries.name: single_elbow_pad
entries.description: Padding strapped over one elbow only, the other arm left unprotected. Turns up on skaters, athletes and casually equipped fighters.

entries.name: bandana_around_arm
entries.description: A [bandana](#bandana) knotted around the upper arm or [biceps](#biceps), its ends left [hanging](#hanging) loose. It often serves as the mark of a gang, team or squad.

entries.name: purple_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Purple bands worn snug around the wrists, decorative rather than restraining. Frequently part of a matching [costume](#costume) set.

entries.name: gold_gloves
entries.description: Hand coverings in [gold](#gold), from soft gilt [cloth](#cloth) to jointed metal [plate](#plate). They belong to ceremonial [dress](#dress), magical-girl [costume](#costume) and gilded armour.

entries.name: arm_scrunchie
entries.description: A [fabric](#fabric) [scrunchie](#scrunchie) pushed up the arm and worn like an [armlet](#armlet). The narrower elastic band in the same place is an arm garter.

entries.name: fold-over_gloves
entries.description: Gloves with a soft upper turned [back](#back) at the end, leaving a [folded](#folded) cuff at the wrist or forearm. That doubled band is the visual [marker](#marker).

entries.name: archery_shooting_glove
entries.description: A [leather](#leather) glove covering only the three fingers that draw a bowstring, worn in Western [archery](#archery) to save them from the [string](#string). The Japanese equivalent, the [yugake](#yugake), protects thumb, index and middle finger instead.

entries.name: fur_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Bands of fur worn at the wrists, generally as a matching pair. Winter, [tribal](#tribal) and bunny-suit costumes all use them.

entries.name: chain_around_arm
entries.description: A length of [chain](#chain) wound round a character's arm, worn for looks or held ready to [swing](#swing). It circles the limb itself, unlike a [bracelet](#bracelet) [dangling](#dangling) at the wrist.

entries.name: spiked_gloves
entries.description: Gloves set with [studs](#studs) or points, ranging from fingerless [leather](#leather) pairs to ones capped in metal. Equally at home in [punk](#punk) [fashion](#fashion) and street-fighting gear.

entries.name: blue_arm_warmers
entries.description: Blue tubes of [fabric](#fabric) covering the [forearms](#forearms) and leaving the hands free. They stand apart from the sleeves of anything worn on the [torso](#torso).

entries.name: vertical-striped_gloves
entries.description: Gloves [patterned](#patterned) with stripes that run along the arm rather than ringing it. Applies to short [gloves](#gloves) and elbow-length ones alike, so long as the lines follow the arm's length.

entries.name: gold_bracer
entries.description: A rigid [gold](#gold) [guard](#guard) strapped over the forearm, worn singly or as a pair. Warriors, divine figures and [fantasy](#fantasy) armour designs all use them.

entries.name: arm_scarf
entries.description: A length of [cloth](#cloth) wound or knotted around the forearm with the ends left [hanging](#hanging). Decoration rather than protection, common on [dancer](#dancer) and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits.

entries.name: silver_armlet
entries.description: A metal band in a silvery finish worn high on the upper arm. Frequent on [fantasy](#fantasy), [dancer](#dancer) and ancient-world outfits, often as part of a matched set.

entries.name: gradient_gloves
entries.description: Gloves whose colour moves smoothly between the fingertips and the cuff. The effect shows best on elbow [gloves](#gloves), which have the most length to fade over.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_gloves
entries.description: Gloves with a [ribbon](#ribbon) band worked along the cuff, often dotted or scalloped. The trim marks where the glove ends against the arm.

entries.name: pink_armband
entries.description: A band worn around the upper arm in pink, either an [insignia](#insignia) band or a purely decorative [strap](#strap). It may mark rank or team, or simply finish off the outfit.

entries.name: single_arm_guard
entries.description: A protective forearm piece worn on one arm only, the other left bare or sleeved. A [staple](#staple) of asymmetric adventurer and archer outfits.

entries.name: pink_mittens
entries.description: Pink handwear enclosing the four fingers together with a separate thumb. Warmer and clumsier than [gloves](#gloves), and usually part of [winter](#winter) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: fur-trimmed_mittens
entries.description: Mittens finished with a band of fur around the wrist [opening](#opening). Winter and Christmas outfits reach for them, generally alongside other fur-trimmed pieces.

entries.name: black_mittens
entries.description: Handwear in black [holding](#holding) the four fingers together in one [pouch](#pouch) with the thumb kept separate. Winter gear, and usually knitted.

entries.name: orange_armband
entries.description: A band of orange [cloth](#cloth) or elastic worn round the upper arm or sleeve, of the sort marking stewards, team members and pupils on duty.

entries.name: nagatekkou
entries.description: A Japanese arm covering [running](#running) from the shoulder down over the arm to the wrist, worn on both sides. It often forms part of traditional or [festival](#festival) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: compression_sleeve
entries.description: A tight [fabric](#fabric) [tube](#tube) pulled over an arm or a leg for support and warmth. Lengths run from a short band over the elbow to a full-limb sleeve, and it appears in sport and in recovery alike.

entries.name: yellow_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Yellow bands fitted closely around the wrists, generally as a matching pair. Wider and stiffer than a [bracelet](#bracelet), and often part of a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: purple_bridal_gauntlets
entries.description: Long purple sleeves covering the forearm and [reaching](#reaching) over the [back](#back) of the hand, hooked around a finger to stay on. Decorative rather than protective, despite the armour-sounding name.

entries.name: red_arm_warmers
entries.description: Tubes of red knitted or stretch [fabric](#fabric) covering the [forearms](#forearms) while leaving the hands bare. Worn for warmth or as a design accent, unlike [gloves](#gloves), which enclose the fingers.

entries.name: fur_gloves
entries.description: Gloves made entirely of fur, covering the hands in [pelt](#pelt) rather than [cloth](#cloth) or [leather](#leather). Gloves [carrying](#carrying) fur only at the cuff are [fur-trimmed_gloves](#fur-trimmed_gloves) instead.

entries.name: brown_arm_warmers
entries.description: Brown tubes of [fabric](#fabric) drawn up over the [forearms](#forearms), leaving the hands free. They are worn for warmth or purely as part of an outfit.

entries.name: single_bracer
entries.description: A stiff forearm sleeve worn on one arm alone. Common on archers, where it guards the [bow](#bow) arm, and on lopsided [fantasy](#fantasy) costumes.

entries.name: finger_cots
entries.description: Short sheaths pulled over single fingers, covering the tips where a whole glove would be too much. Worn for medical work, electronics assembly and watchmaking; picture a glove with only the finger parts kept.

entries.name: artist_glove
entries.description: A glove covering only the little and [ring](#ring) fingers, leaving thumb, index and middle free to hold a [pen](#pen) or [stylus](#stylus). It keeps the hand from smudging graphite and from [dragging](#dragging) across a tablet, and is worn on the drawing hand alone.

entries.name: grey_arm_warmers
entries.description: Grey arm warmers pulled over the [forearms](#forearms) with the hands left free. They may be worn with or without [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: red_bridal_gauntlets
entries.description: Long red sleeves worn on the [forearms](#forearms) and looped over the middle finger, leaving the fingers and upper arm bare. A [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) [priestess](#priestess) and bridal character designs.

entries.name: winter_gloves
entries.description: Thick, padded or knitted [gloves](#gloves) made for [cold](#cold) weather, often with a cuff [riding](#riding) over the sleeve. They pair naturally with coats, scarves, and snowy scenes.

entries.name: green_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Green bands closed around the wrists as ornament, part of an outfit rather than a restraint. They are normally worn as a matching pair.

entries.name: green_arm_warmers
entries.description: Green tubes of [cloth](#cloth) drawn over the [forearms](#forearms) with the hands left free. They are worn apart from the sleeves, so the arm [can](#can) be bare above and below them.

entries.name: yellow_mittens
entries.description: Yellow [mittens](#mittens), the handwear that keeps all four fingers in one compartment with the thumb apart. Winter scenes account for most sightings.

entries.name: cross-laced_gloves
entries.description: Gloves closed or trimmed with cords crossing into an X, along the [back](#back) of the hand or [running](#running) the length of the forearm. The lacing may be functional or purely ornamental.

entries.name: striped_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Bands worn around the wrists, [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes) and [wrist_cuffs](#wrist_cuffs).

entries.name: striped_wristband
entries.description: A [wristband](#wristband) marked with a striped pattern.

entries.name: ribbed_gloves
entries.description: Gloves knitted or moulded with raised parallel ridges [running](#running) along the hand and cuff. The texture is what sets them apart from [plain](#plain) [gloves](#gloves) of the same cut.

entries.name: paw_print_palms
entries.description: Ordinary [gloves](#gloves) or [mittens](#mittens) printed with a paw mark on the palm, typically one to a hand. Paw gloves are excluded, since their pads are moulded into the design.

entries.name: mechanical_gloves
entries.description: Gloves built from [machine](#machine) parts, with plated fingers and articulated knuckles, sometimes housing a built-in [device](#device). Worn over the hand rather than replacing it.

entries.name: work_gloves
entries.description: Sturdy [fabric](#fabric) or [leather](#leather) [gloves](#gloves) worn to protect the hands during manual labour. Construction, [gardening](#gardening), and moving scenes are where they show up.

entries.name: purple_mittens
entries.description: Purple handwear that [gathers](#gathers) all four fingers into one [pouch](#pouch) with a separate thumb. Warmer, and less dexterous, than [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: fur_armlet
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of fur worn around the upper arm. Generally part of a [tribal](#tribal), [barbarian](#barbarian) or [fantasy](#fantasy) outfit rather than everyday [dress](#dress).

entries.name: yellow_arm_warmers
entries.description: Yellow arm warmers covering the [forearms](#forearms) while leaving the hands free.

entries.name: orange_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Orange bands worn snugly around the wrists as an accessory.

entries.name: grey_mittens
entries.description: Grey [mittens](#mittens), the [winter](#winter) handwear that keeps the four fingers in a single compartment. Handwear separating every finger is [gloves](#gloves).

entries.name: grey_armband
entries.description: A grey band worn around the upper arm, [plain](#plain) or [carrying](#carrying) an [emblem](#emblem). It sits above the elbow rather than at the wrist.

entries.name: unworn_armband
entries.description: An [armband](#armband) that belongs on a character's sleeve appears in the picture off the arm, held, set down or simply missing from where it should be worn.

entries.name: leather_wrist_straps
entries.description: Narrow bands of hide buckled around one or both wrists, worn as ornament rather than restraint.

entries.name: sheer_gloves
entries.description: Gloves woven from [thread](#thread) fine enough that the skin shows faintly through, [giving](#giving) a delicate, half-transparent look rather than a [lace](#lace) pattern.

entries.name: green_mittens
entries.description: Green [mittens](#mittens), which keep the four fingers together in a single compartment. Handwear that separates each finger is [green_gloves](#green_gloves).

entries.name: brown_armband
entries.description: A brown band worn round the upper arm. It covers [plain](#plain) bands as [well](#well) as those bearing [insignia](#insignia) or lettering.

entries.name: grey_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Bands worn around the wrists that are coloured grey, whether purely decorative or part of a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: orange_mittens
entries.description: Orange [mittens](#mittens), which enclose the four fingers together and leave the thumb its own [pocket](#pocket).

entries.name: brown_wrist_cuffs
entries.description: Brown bands worn snugly around the wrists. They are decorative rather than restraining, and often belong to a [fantasy](#fantasy) or [tribal](#tribal) outfit.

entries.name: orange_arm_warmers
entries.description: Orange tubes of [fabric](#fabric) covering the [forearms](#forearms) while leaving the hands free.

entries.name: ribbon
entries.description: A thin [flexible](#flexible) band of [cloth](#cloth) or similar material, longer than it is wide, tied into hair or onto clothing. Use either ribbon or [bow](#bow) for a single knot, never both; a ribbon tied into a bow shape is a bow instead.

entries.name: hair_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) worn tied in the hair. Hair that is itself made of ribbon is ribbon_hair instead.

entries.name: hair_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied into the hair, whether [holding](#holding) [back](#back) a [ponytail](#ponytail) or [twintails](#twintails) or worn purely as decoration.

entries.name: hairbows
entries.description: Bows tied into the hair, whether one large one or several small. Counts as a hair accessory rather than trim on the clothing.

entries.name: red_bow
entries.description: A red [ribbon](#ribbon) [bow](#bow) worn in the hair, on clothing, or at the [neck](#neck). Combine with the specific placement, such as [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [back_bow](#back_bow).

entries.name: red_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in red, tied in the hair, at the [collar](#collar), around the waist, or on clothing. Add the placement [tag](#tag) too, such as [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon).

entries.name: black_ribbon
entries.description: A length of black [ribbon](#ribbon), tied into the hair, knotted at the throat, sewn onto a garment or wrapped around an object. Add [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon) so the placement is recorded too.

entries.name: blue_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) in blue, tied into the hair, sewn onto clothing or fastened to an object. Add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [bowtie](#bowtie) so that the placement is recorded.

entries.name: blue_ribbon
entries.description: A length of blue [ribbon](#ribbon) tied in the hair, at the throat, on a garment or around an object. Add the placement as [well](#well), such as [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon).

entries.name: pink_bow
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied into a pink [bow](#bow), worn in the hair, at the [collar](#collar), on a [dress](#dress) or on [shoes](#shoes). The [shade](#shade) [can](#can) shade into [red_bow](#red_bow) or [purple_bow](#purple_bow); add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) when it sits in the hair.

entries.name: yellow_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) in yellow worn in the hair, at the [neck](#neck) or on clothing. Add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or the placement [tag](#tag); a yellow [bowtie](#bowtie) is tagged separately.

entries.name: pink_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in pink tied in the hair, at the [neck](#neck), round the waist or onto a garment. When it is tied into a [bow](#bow), [pink_bow](#pink_bow) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: purple_bow
entries.description: A purple [ribbon](#ribbon) [bow](#bow) worn anywhere on a character, from the hair to a [collar](#collar), a [dress](#dress), or a shoe. Combine with bow and a placement [tag](#tag) such as [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [back_bow](#back_bow).

entries.name: yellow_ribbon
entries.description: A yellow [ribbon](#ribbon) worn in the hair, at the [neck](#neck) or on clothing. Tag ribbon and the placement such as [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon).

entries.name: striped_bow
entries.description: A decorative [bow](#bow), worn in the hair or on clothing, whose [fabric](#fabric) shows a striped pattern.

entries.name: purple_ribbon
entries.description: A purple [ribbon](#ribbon) worn on the hair, on clothing, or at the [neck](#neck), or simply held loose. Combine with ribbon and a placement [tag](#tag) such as [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon).

entries.name: tress_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around a single [lock](#lock) of hair rather than around a [tail](#tail) or the whole head. The word tress refers to one long strand, and the ribbon typically hangs at a sidelock.

entries.name: ear_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied around an ear, nearly always an [animal](#animal) ear on a kemonomimi or anthro character. An accessory rather than part of the body.

entries.name: aqua_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) in blue-green, tied in the hair, at the [collar](#collar) or on a garment. Add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [bowtie](#bowtie) to say where it sits.

entries.name: polka_dot_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) of polka-dotted [fabric](#fabric) worn in the hair, at the [neck](#neck), or on clothing. Tag bow and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) alongside it.

entries.name: multiple_hair_bows
entries.description: Three or more bows tied into the hair. Two is common enough to go untagged, and bows fixed to a [hat](#hat) or [hood](#hood) belong with [multiple_hat_bows](#multiple_hat_bows) instead.

entries.name: plaid_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) made of plaid [fabric](#fabric), worn in the hair, at the [neck](#neck), or on a garment. Common on [school](#school) uniforms; a plaid bow tied specifically as a [bowtie](#bowtie) is [plaid_bowtie](#plaid_bowtie) instead.

entries.name: brown_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) of brown [ribbon](#ribbon) or [fabric](#fabric), tied in the hair, on clothing, on [shoes](#shoes) or around a [gift](#gift). Add bow and where it sits, such as [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [brown_bowtie](#brown_bowtie).

entries.name: horn_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) wound or tied around a character's or an animal's [horns](#horns) or [antlers](#antlers). A ribbon tied there into a [bow](#bow) is also [horn_bow](#horn_bow).

entries.name: ear_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied round an ear, nearly always an [animal](#animal) one, its ends left trailing rather than knotted into a [bow](#bow). Worn decoration, not a body feature.

entries.name: striped_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon), worn in the hair or elsewhere as trim, [patterned](#patterned) with stripes. Implies ribbon.

entries.name: diagonal-striped_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) whose [fabric](#fabric) carries stripes [running](#running) at a slant, worn in the hair or set on clothing. The pattern is the point; the bow itself may be any size.

entries.name: print_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) decorated with a printed design rather than a [plain](#plain) colour. Tag bow with it, and [print_bowtie](#print_bowtie) when it is tied as a [bowtie](#bowtie).

entries.name: two-tone_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) made from [fabric](#fabric) in exactly two colours. Applies equally to hair bows and to bows sewn onto clothing.

entries.name: aqua_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in aqua, worn in the hair, at the [neck](#neck) or on clothing. Add [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon) to place it.

entries.name: brown_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in brown, tied in the hair, at the throat or trimming a garment. Add the placement as [well](#well), such as [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon).

entries.name: horn_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied onto a character's [horns](#horns) or [antlers](#antlers) rather than into their hair. Suika and EX-Keine made the look [familiar](#familiar); add horns as [well](#well).

entries.name: frilled_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) whose long edges are gathered into ruffles instead of [lying](#lying) flat. It may be worn in the hair, tied at the [neck](#neck), or used as decoration on a garment.

entries.name: two-tone_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in exactly two colours, worn either in the hair or on clothing. Implies ribbon.

entries.name: long_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) with very long trailing ends, worn in the hair or on a [dress](#dress), [hat](#hat) or [weapon](#weapon) and often streaming out in the [wind](#wind). Add [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon) to say where it sits.

entries.name: polka_dot_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in dotted [fabric](#fabric), worn in the hair or on a garment. When tied into a [bow](#bow), [polka_dot_bow](#polka_dot_bow) fits better.

entries.name: plaid_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in plaid [fabric](#fabric), worn in the hair or on clothing. Once tied into a [bow](#bow) shape, [plaid_bow](#plaid_bow) becomes the closer [tag](#tag).

entries.name: print_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) [carrying](#carrying) a printed pattern rather than a flat colour. Tied into the hair, at the [collar](#collar), or onto a garment.

entries.name: gradient_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) whose colour changes noticeably from one end or edge to the other, in the hair or on clothing alike.

entries.name: checkered_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) [patterned](#patterned) in alternating squares, tied into the hair or used to trim a garment. Gingham versions carry a country or [cafe](#cafe) flavour.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) whose loops or tails carry a [ribbon](#ribbon) band along their edges. The trim gives the bow a second colour outlining its shape.

entries.name: no_hair_bow
entries.description: A character normally drawn with a [bow](#bow) in the hair appears without it, the hairstyle otherwise unchanged. The bow does not appear anywhere else in the picture either.

entries.name: torn_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) frayed or [torn](#torn), whether worn in the hair or on clothing.

entries.name: gold_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) of [gold](#gold) tied into the hair, sewn onto a garment or wrapped round a [gift](#gift). What it records is the ribbon's colour, not where it sits.

entries.name: unworn_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) that plainly belongs on hair, [neck](#neck) or clothing is present in the picture without being worn, whether held, laid down or [drifting](#drifting) loose.

entries.name: unworn_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) appears somewhere in the picture without being worn by anyone, whether held, set down or [hanging](#hanging) loose off the hair, [neck](#neck) or clothing it belongs to.

entries.name: torn_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) frayed or ripped, whether tied in the hair or fixed to clothing.

entries.name: untied_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) that had been tied has come apart, its ends left [hanging](#hanging) loose wherever it was worn, whether in the hair, at the [collar](#collar) or wrapped around a [gift](#gift).

entries.name: antler_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) knotted round an antler, or strung between a pair of them. A festive touch on [deer](#deer) and [reindeer](#reindeer) characters.

entries.name: pinstripe_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied from [cloth](#cloth) [carrying](#carrying) fine parallel stripes. Worn in the hair, at the throat or as trim on a garment.

entries.name: hairclip
entries.description: A clip or [clasp](#clasp) that snaps onto the hair to hold it in place or simply decorate it, also called a barrette or hair [slide](#slide). Unlike a [hairpin](#hairpin) it has a spring or clasp mechanism.

entries.name: hairpin
entries.description: A [pin](#pin) that simply slides into the hair to hold it, with [no](#no) [clasp](#clasp), shaped like a U or a [stick](#stick) and sometimes decorated at one end. The [plain](#plain) bobby pin, often drawn as a short line on a [lock](#lock), is the most common form.

entries.name: hair_stick
entries.description: A long narrow [stick](#stick) pushed through wrapped hair to hold it up, or worn simply as decoration, ranging from a [plain](#plain) [twig](#twig) to an [ornate](#ornate) piece. Chinese-style sticks with [dangling](#dangling) parts also take [chinese_hairpin](#chinese_hairpin).

entries.name: parallel_hairclips
entries.description: Two or more hairclips worn side by side in a row, their [bars](#bars) all [running](#running) the same way. A tidy schoolgirl look, usually pinning [back](#back) a fringe or a sidelock.

entries.name: kanzashi
entries.description: Ornaments worn in a traditional Japanese [updo](#updo), from [plain](#plain) sticks to elaborate [dangling](#dangling) [flower](#flower) pieces. Brides, [geisha](#geisha) and characters in [kimono](#kimono) are the usual wearers.

entries.name: multiple_hairclips
entries.description: Three or more clips fastened in the hair at once, often lined up along a fringe or clustered above one ear. The sheer number of clips is the notable thing rather than any single one.

entries.name: multiple_hairpins
entries.description: A character wearing more than one [hairpin](#hairpin), whether a row down one side or pins scattered through the style. A lone [pin](#pin) uses hairpin by itself.

entries.name: chinese_hairpin
entries.description: An [ornate](#ornate) Chinese hair [stick](#stick) or [pin](#pin), frequently hung with [dangling](#dangling) drops, used to hold up a historical Chinese hairstyle. Made from [bone](#bone), jade, wood or metal; a [plain](#plain) modern pin is just [hairpin](#hairpin).

entries.name: flower_hairpin
entries.description: A [pin](#pin) or clip whose decoration is a [flower](#flower), pushed into the hair to hold or [dress](#dress) it. Kimono, [festival](#festival) and traditional coordinates use it constantly.

entries.name: shuriken_hair_ornament
entries.description: A [hairpin](#hairpin) or clip shaped like a [throwing](#throwing) star. A stock accessory for ninja-themed characters and school-festival costumes.

entries.name: arrow_hair_ornament
entries.description: A [pin](#pin) or clip shaped like an arrow, pushed through the hair so the shaft appears to run right across it. Sometimes worn as a pair.

entries.name: scissors_hair_ornament
entries.description: A [hairpin](#hairpin) or clip made in the shape of a pair of [scissors](#scissors). Often worn by hairdresser characters or as one piece of a themed set.

entries.name: unworn_hairclip
entries.description: A [hairclip](#hairclip) appears in the picture while nobody has it in their hair, held in a hand or set down on a surface nearby.

entries.name: bobby_pin
entries.description: A small flat [wire](#wire) clip pushed into the hair to hold loose strands in place. Plainer and far less conspicuous than a decorative [hairclip](#hairclip).

entries.name: claw_hair_clip
entries.description: A hinged plastic clip with interlocking [teeth](#teeth) that bites down on gathered hair, [holding](#holding) a twist or a half-updo. Everyday rather than decorative.

entries.name: spoon_hair_ornament
entries.description: A [hairpin](#hairpin) or clip shaped like a [spoon](#spoon), one of several cutlery- and food-themed hair ornaments.

entries.name: scrunchie
entries.description: A cloth-covered elastic band, most often [tying](#tying) up the hair but also worn around a wrist, arm, or ankle as an accessory. Not to be [confused](#confused) with [wrist_cuffs](#wrist_cuffs) or an arm garter.

entries.name: hair_bobbles
entries.description: An elastic hair tie with one or two large balls that fastens a [ponytail](#ponytail) or [twintails](#twintails), stereotypically worn by young girls. Many smaller [beads](#beads) strung together are [hair_beads](#hair_beads) instead.

entries.name: hair_scrunchie
entries.description: A [scrunchie](#scrunchie) worn in the hair, usually fastening a [ponytail](#ponytail) or [twintails](#twintails).

entries.name: white_hairband
entries.description: A white band worn over the top of the head to hold hair [back](#back), as on Alice-style outfits. Not the same placement as a [white_headband](#white_headband).

entries.name: red_hairband
entries.description: A red [hairband](#hairband), the arch-shaped band worn over the top of the head to hold hair [back](#back). Distinct from [red_headband](#red_headband), a strip tied around the [forehead](#forehead).

entries.name: hair_tie
entries.description: A small elastic band that [gathers](#gathers) hair into a [ponytail](#ponytail) or another tied style. Comes in many colours and patterns; a thicker fabric-covered band is a [scrunchie](#scrunchie) instead.

entries.name: blue_hairband
entries.description: A blue band arching over the top of the head to keep the hair [back](#back). A band worn around the [forehead](#forehead) is [blue_headband](#blue_headband).

entries.name: bow_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) [carrying](#carrying) a [bow](#bow) or a [ribbon](#ribbon) fixed to it, worn across the [crown](#crown) of the head. The bow must genuinely be attached to the band; one tied into the hair itself is [hair_bow](#hair_bow).

entries.name: yellow_hairband
entries.description: A rigid yellow band worn over the top of the head to hold hair [back](#back). Tag [hairband](#hairband) as [well](#well).

entries.name: pink_hairband
entries.description: A pink [hairband](#hairband), the curved band slipped over the top of the head to hold hair [back](#back) off the face. It sits towards the [crown](#crown) rather than across the brow.

entries.name: purple_hairband
entries.description: A purple band worn over the top of the head to hold the hair [back](#back). A band worn around the [forehead](#forehead) instead is a [headband](#headband).

entries.name: white_headband
entries.description: A white band tied around the [forehead](#forehead), sporty or martial in style. A band worn over the top of the head instead is [white_hairband](#white_hairband).

entries.name: red_scrunchie
entries.description: A red [scrunchie](#scrunchie), the fabric-covered elastic that ties a [ponytail](#ponytail) or [twintails](#twintails). Sometimes worn on the wrist instead; [tag](#tag) scrunchie as [well](#well).

entries.name: blue_scrunchie
entries.description: A blue fabric-covered elastic gathering a [ponytail](#ponytail) or bun, or slipped over the wrist when it is not in use. Its bunched [ring](#ring) of [cloth](#cloth) sets it apart from a [plain](#plain) hair tie.

entries.name: black_scrunchie
entries.description: A black fabric-covered elastic gathering a [ponytail](#ponytail), or slipped over the wrist when it is not in the hair. The soft sleeve of [cloth](#cloth) is what separates it from a [plain](#plain) hair tie.

entries.name: white_scrunchie
entries.description: A cloth-covered elastic tie in white, gathering a [ponytail](#ponytail) or bun. Worn around the wrist instead, the matching [tag](#tag) is [wrist_scrunchie](#wrist_scrunchie); combine with [scrunchie](#scrunchie).

entries.name: pink_scrunchie
entries.description: A fabric-covered elastic hair tie in pink, [holding](#holding) a [ponytail](#ponytail) or bun or slipped over the wrist. Its gathered [cloth](#cloth) sets it apart from a [plain](#plain) elastic.

entries.name: yellow_scrunchie
entries.description: A yellow [fabric](#fabric) hair tie. Tag [scrunchie](#scrunchie); worn on the wrist it is also [wrist_scrunchie](#wrist_scrunchie).

entries.name: multicolored_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) made up of several distinct colours rather than a single one, usually as stripes or blocks [running](#running) around the band. Tag the individual colours as [well](#well) where they [can](#can) be named.

entries.name: orange_scrunchie
entries.description: An orange [scrunchie](#scrunchie), [fabric](#fabric) gathered on an elastic, [holding](#holding) a [ponytail](#ponytail) or slipped over the wrist. Add [wrist_scrunchie](#wrist_scrunchie) for the latter.

entries.name: brown_hairband
entries.description: A brown [hairband](#hairband) arcing over the top of the head to hold the hair [back](#back). A band crossing the [forehead](#forehead) instead is [brown_headband](#brown_headband).

entries.name: gold_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) of [gold](#gold) or a gold-coloured material [holding](#holding) the hair [back](#back). Not a [circlet](#circlet) or [diadem](#diadem) worn across the brow, and not an ornamental [tiara](#tiara).

entries.name: metal_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) made of metal [holding](#holding) the hair [back](#back). Distinct from a diadem-style [headband](#headband) and from a [circlet](#circlet); a [tiara](#tiara) is a decorative piece rather than a [plain](#plain) hairband.

entries.name: two-tone_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) combining exactly two colours. Implies hairband.

entries.name: diamond_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) built from a row of linked diamond [shapes](#shapes) [running](#running) across the head. The repeated lozenges are what distinguish it from a [plain](#plain) band.

entries.name: purple_scrunchie
entries.description: A purple fabric-covered elastic [holding](#holding) a [ponytail](#ponytail) or a set of [twintails](#twintails), or worn loose around the wrist. Combine with [scrunchie](#scrunchie) and the hairstyle.

entries.name: spiked_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) with [spikes](#spikes) of any length rising from it, a [punk](#punk) or demonic twist on the ordinary hairband.

entries.name: pink_headband
entries.description: A pink band worn across the top of the head, of the sporty or soft-fabric kind. The rigid [hoop](#hoop) slipped over the [crown](#crown) is a [hairband](#hairband) instead.

entries.name: green_scrunchie
entries.description: A green fabric-covered elastic hair tie, gathering the hair or slipped around a wrist. It usually holds a [ponytail](#ponytail) or a bun.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) decorated with [lace](#lace) along its edge, as on a [maid](#maid) [headdress](#headdress). A band that is nothing but a strip of lace is [lace_hairband](#lace_hairband).

entries.name: aqua_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) in blue-green, [sitting](#sitting) [back](#back) over the [crown](#crown) to hold the hair off the face. A band worn across the [forehead](#forehead) is a [headband](#headband) instead.

entries.name: polka_dot_scrunchie
entries.description: A [fabric](#fabric) hair [scrunchie](#scrunchie) printed with polka [dots](#dots), [holding](#holding) a [ponytail](#ponytail) or worn on the wrist. Tag scrunchie and [polka_dot](#polka_dot) with it.

entries.name: ear_scrunchie
entries.description: A [fabric](#fabric) [scrunchie](#scrunchie) slipped over an [animal](#animal) ear instead of gathering a [ponytail](#ponytail), usually bunching a tuft of ear fur.

entries.name: checkered_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) [patterned](#patterned) in alternating squares, [holding](#holding) the hair [back](#back) off the face. Maid and [cafe](#cafe) outfits often pair one with a matching [apron](#apron).

entries.name: motoyui
entries.description: The cord or [folded](#folded) [paper](#paper) strip used to bind traditional Japanese hairstyles at the base of a [topknot](#topknot) or [tail](#tail), usually white and looking like wrapped [cloth](#cloth). A notably long one overlaps with the hair [tube](#tube) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: aqua_scrunchie
entries.description: A gathered [fabric](#fabric) hair tie in blue-green, round a [ponytail](#ponytail) or slipped over the wrist. Add the hairstyle it holds.

entries.name: spiked_headband
entries.description: A band worn around the head with [studs](#studs) or [spikes](#spikes) set along it. Punk styling that, at a [glance](#glance), [can](#can) double as a crude [crown](#crown).

entries.name: flower_hairband
entries.description: A band across the top of the head [carrying](#carrying) one or more blossoms. The band itself is what separates it from a single [bloom](#bloom) simply tucked into the hair.

entries.name: print_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) with a printed pattern [running](#running) along its length. Sits over the [crown](#crown), [holding](#holding) the hair [back](#back) from the face.

entries.name: metal_hair_tubes
entries.description: Metal cylinders threaded over lengths of hair to bind and shape them, taking the place a [ribbon](#ribbon) or tie would otherwise hold.

entries.name: silver_hairband
entries.description: A band worn over the top of the head in a silvery metallic finish. Holds the hair [back](#back) from the face and often reads as a thin [circlet](#circlet).

entries.name: ponytail_holder
entries.description: The elastic band or [clasp](#clasp) gathering hair into a [ponytail](#ponytail), visible at the base of the [tail](#tail). Covers [plain](#plain) ties as [well](#well) as decorated clips made for the job.

entries.name: polka_dot_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) [carrying](#carrying) a pattern of round [dots](#dots). Often matched with a [ribbon](#ribbon) or [apron](#apron) in the same spotted [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: brown_scrunchie
entries.description: A brown [scrunchie](#scrunchie): an elastic hair tie sleeved in gathered [fabric](#fabric). Shown [holding](#holding) a [ponytail](#ponytail) or parked around the wrist for later.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_hairband
entries.description: A [hairband](#hairband) edged or wrapped with a decorative [ribbon](#ribbon) band. The trim runs along the [arch](#arch) and is usually a contrasting colour.

entries.name: print_scrunchie
