entries.description: A [bloom](#bloom) or small posy worn for an occasion, [pinned](#pinned) at the [dress](#dress) or strapped to the wrist. Worn on a lapel instead, it becomes a [boutonniere](#boutonniere).

entries.name: boutonniere
entries.description: A single [flower](#flower) or [bud](#bud) pushed through the buttonhole of a [jacket](#jacket) lapel, worn at weddings, formals and ceremonies. Anyone may wear one, but a [bloom](#bloom) [pinned](#pinned) anywhere else counts as a [corsage](#corsage).

entries.name: green_brooch
entries.description: A green [brooch](#brooch) [pinned](#pinned) at the [collar](#collar), chest or waist. Whatever metal frames it, the stone or enamel carries the colour.

entries.name: accessories
entries.description: Small worn extras such as jewellery, clips, bands and trinkets shown as a set. It often applies where the pieces are laid out for [display](#display) rather than being worn by anyone.

entries.name: purple_brooch
entries.description: A purple ornamental [pin](#pin) fastened at the [collar](#collar), chest, or [cloak](#cloak). Whether the stone or the setting carries the colour, the [tag](#tag) reads the same.

entries.name: nipple_bells
entries.description: Small bells hang at the [nipples](#nipples), fixed through piercings or held by clamps or cord. They [ring](#ring) at any movement, which is generally the whole [idea](#idea).

entries.name: collar_chain_(jewelry)
entries.description: A short decorative [chain](#chain) worn across a [shirt](#shirt) [collar](#collar), usually linking its two points. It is [dress](#dress) [jewelry](#jewelry) rather than restraint hardware; a chain [running](#running) off a worn [neck](#neck) collar is [chain_leash](#chain_leash).

entries.name: hand_jewel
entries.description: A gemstone seated on the [back](#back) of the hand, either fixed to bare skin or mounted in a glove or bridal gauntlet. It reads as worn ornament rather than as part of the body.

entries.name: skull_brooch
entries.description: A [pin](#pin) worn at the [collar](#collar) or chest shaped as a [skull](#skull). Common on gothic and pirate-flavoured costumes.

entries.name: quimbaya_airplane
entries.description: A small [gold](#gold) artifact from Colombia's ancient Quimbaya culture, often claimed as an out-of-place depiction of an [aircraft](#aircraft) though it is most likely a stylized [bird](#bird). One character in a doujin franchise wears one as a [cloak](#cloak) [clasp](#clasp).

entries.name: coin_(ornament)
entries.description: Coins used as decoration rather than as [money](#money): strung across a [headdress](#headdress), sewn along a hem or hung from a [belt](#belt). Typical of [dancer](#dancer) and traveller [costume](#costume).

entries.name: food-themed_ornament
entries.description: A food-shaped decoration worn anywhere other than the hair or ears, [pinned](#pinned) to a [sash](#sash), a glove, a garter or even a [tail](#tail). Hair and earring versions have their own tags but often appear together with it.

entries.name: body_jewelry
entries.description: Chains, [beads](#beads) and gems arranged across the body as an outfit in their own right, usually tracing the chest, waist and hips. They may lie against skin or be worn over [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: face_jewel
entries.description: A [gem](#gem) sits on the skin of the face, on the [forehead](#forehead), a cheek or below an eye. It is [stuck](#stuck) or set in place as ornament rather than pierced through the [flesh](#flesh).

entries.name: nipple_tassels
entries.description: Small tassels hang at the [nipples](#nipples), [stuck](#stuck) to the skin or [dangling](#dangling) from [pasties](#pasties). The rest of the breast is left bare, in burlesque [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: pink_brooch
entries.description: A pink ornamental [pin](#pin) fastened at a [collar](#collar), chest or [sash](#sash). It clasps onto the [cloth](#cloth) itself, unlike a [pendant](#pendant) [hanging](#hanging) from a [chain](#chain).

entries.name: pussy_jewelry
entries.description: Chains, gems, or ornaments hung on or attached to the vulva, often anchored to a [piercing](#piercing). A [plain](#plain), undecorated piercing does not need this [tag](#tag) unless the metalwork itself is elaborate.

entries.name: cross_ornament
entries.description: A decorative [cross](#cross) attached to clothing, hair or a [chain](#chain) as a trinket. Worn for the shape rather than handled as a devotional implement.

entries.name: yellow_brooch
entries.description: A yellow [pin](#pin) or [clasp](#clasp) worn as an ornament, usually fastened at the [collar](#collar), chest or waist. The stone, enamel or metal is what gives it the colour.

entries.name: carrot_pin
entries.description: A [pin](#pin) or [brooch](#brooch) shaped like a [carrot](#carrot), fastened to clothing or fixed in the hair. Another piece of rabbit-themed [dress](#dress).

entries.name: chain_between_breasts
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) lies down the [cleavage](#cleavage), whether a [necklace](#necklace) fallen between the [breasts](#breasts) or a strand of a [harness](#harness) routed that way. What gets recorded is the placement rather than the chain.

entries.name: waist_brooch
entries.description: An ornamental [pin](#pin) or [clasp](#clasp) fastened at the waist rather than at the chest. It frequently holds a [sash](#sash) or a drape of [fabric](#fabric) in place.

entries.name: star_pin
entries.description: A star-shaped [pin](#pin) or [badge](#badge) fastened to clothing, a [hat](#hat) or a [bag](#bag). A small metal or enamel accessory.

entries.name: bat_brooch
entries.description: A [brooch](#brooch) [cast](#cast) in the shape of a bat, [pinned](#pinned) to a [collar](#collar), [cape](#cape) or [hat](#hat). It suits gothic and [vampire](#vampire) outfits.

entries.name: body_chain
entries.description: Fine chains worn over the [torso](#torso), looping around the chest, waist or hips. They are ornament rather than clothing, and sit against bare skin or thin [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: stomach_jewel
entries.description: A gemstone set at or near the [navel](#navel), either mounted in an ornament worn on the [belly](#belly) or embedded in the body itself. Common on dancers and on [fantasy](#fantasy) beings built around a [gem](#gem).

entries.name: character_pin
entries.description: An enamel [badge](#badge) [carrying](#carrying) a character, fastened to a [bag](#bag), lapel or [hat](#hat). Collectors [cover](#cover) entire straps in rows of them.

entries.name: bird_pin
entries.description: A [brooch](#brooch) or lapel [pin](#pin) shaped like a [bird](#bird), fastened to a [coat](#coat), [collar](#collar) or [hat](#hat). Small enough to read as jewellery rather than as an [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: nipple_sleeves
entries.description: Rings or short collars that [slide](#slide) over the [nipples](#nipples) and grip around them as jewellery. Nothing passes through the [flesh](#flesh), which sets them apart from a [piercing](#piercing).

entries.name: diamond-shaped_brooch
entries.description: A [pin](#pin) whose body is cut as a rhombus. The shape is what earns the [tag](#tag); a [brooch](#brooch) set with an actual diamond stone is a different thing.

entries.name: orange_brooch
entries.description: An ornamental [pin](#pin) in orange fastened to clothing. Only the [brooch](#brooch) carries the colour.

entries.name: black_brooch
entries.description: A decorative [pin](#pin) fastened to clothing whose ornament is black. The colour describes the [brooch](#brooch) itself, not the garment it rests on.

entries.name: brown_brooch
entries.description: An ornamental [pin](#pin) or [clasp](#clasp) fastened to clothing, brown in colour. Only the [brooch](#brooch) itself needs to be brown for it to count.

entries.name: grey_brooch
entries.description: A grey ornamental [pin](#pin) fastened to clothing. Grey and white brooches often stand in for silver, depending on how the artist has shaded them.

entries.name: white_brooch
entries.description: A white ornamental [pin](#pin) worn on clothing. Depending on the shading it [can](#can) just as easily read as a silver piece.

entries.name: belt
entries.description: A strip of [leather](#leather), [rope](#rope) or similar material worn around the waist of trousers, [shorts](#shorts) or a [skirt](#skirt), whether it holds anything up or is purely decorative. A [fabric](#fabric) one is a [sash](#sash), and variants such as [chest_belt](#chest_belt), [multiple_belts](#multiple_belts) and [belt_pouch](#belt_pouch) have tags of their own.

entries.name: bag
entries.description: Any bag in the picture, whether a [handbag](#handbag), a tote, a shoulder bag, a [paper](#paper) bag or a [plain](#plain) [sack](#sack), and whether carried, worn or set down. Reach for the specific type when it is clear, such as [backpack](#backpack) or [plastic_bag](#plastic_bag).

entries.name: thigh_strap
entries.description: A band of [fabric](#fabric), [leather](#leather) or a [belt](#belt) worn around the thigh. A metal band is [thighlet](#thighlet), a frilly elastic one is [bridal_garter](#bridal_garter), and a single garter [strap](#strap) may attach to it.

entries.name: sash
entries.description: A broad band of [fabric](#fabric) worn around the body, either diagonally from shoulder to opposite hip or horizontally at the waist. The waist form is everyday [dress](#dress) while the shoulder form is ceremonial; an [obi](#obi) counts as a waist sash.

entries.name: backpack
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) worn on the [back](#back) on two shoulder straps, from a [school](#school) [randoseru](#randoseru) to a [hiking](#hiking) pack. Tag it whether worn, slung from a single [strap](#strap), or set down beside the character.

entries.name: suspenders
entries.description: Elastic straps worn over the shoulders that hold up trousers or a [skirt](#skirt), clipped or buttoned to the waistband in an X or Y shape at the [back](#back). Not the British sense of the term, which means a garter [belt](#belt).

entries.name: black_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) in black worn at the waist or hips, over trousers, a [skirt](#skirt) or a [dress](#dress). This is the garment; a martial arts rank is something else entirely.

entries.name: pouch
entries.description: A small soft [container](#container) of [leather](#leather), [cloth](#cloth) or plastic: a [drawstring](#drawstring) [bag](#bag), a zipped case or a flap-closed [pocket](#pocket). One worn on a [belt](#belt) is [belt_pouch](#belt_pouch).

entries.name: school_bag
entries.description: The [bag](#bag) Japanese students carry, in one of two styles: a rigid briefcase-like case with a top [handle](#handle) and flap, or a small blue duffel-style bag with shoulder straps. A [randoseru](#randoseru), the elementary [school](#school) [backpack](#backpack), has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: shoulder_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) carried on one shoulder by its [strap](#strap). On a student it may specifically be a [school_bag](#school_bag). Implies bag.

entries.name: watch
entries.description: A timepiece worn on the body, nearly always a [wristwatch](#wristwatch) on the wrist. A watch on a [chain](#chain) is [pocket_watch](#pocket_watch).

entries.name: brown_belt
entries.description: A brown [belt](#belt), usually [leather](#leather), worn at the waist or across the hips over trousers, a [skirt](#skirt) or a [dress](#dress). Add belt.

entries.name: handbag
entries.description: A small [bag](#bag) carried by the handles or over the forearm, [holding](#holding) [money](#money) and personal odds and ends. Also called a purse, and often decorated on the outside.

entries.name: wristwatch
entries.description: A [watch](#watch) strapped to the wrist rather than worn as a [pendant](#pendant) or carried loose. Some watch brands commission art specifically to show off a [model](#model), so [tag](#tag) watch alongside it.

entries.name: harness
entries.description: Straps buckled across the body, whether the tack that hitches a [horse](#horse) to a [cart](#cart) or the [fashion](#fashion) and fetish sort that frames the shoulders and chest. Leather is common but not required. Add [chest_harness](#chest_harness) when the straps [cross](#cross) the [breasts](#breasts) or [pectorals](#pectorals).

entries.name: randoseru
entries.description: The stiff [leather](#leather) [school](#school) [backpack](#backpack) with a curved top flap carried by Japanese elementary pupils, traditionally red for girls and black for boys though now made in many colors. Often marks a character as a young [child](#child).

entries.name: white_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) that is white, worn at the waist or hips. In martial-arts contexts the same color also marks a beginner's rank.

entries.name: holster
entries.description: A worn carrier for a [handgun](#handgun), strapped at the thigh, on the hip or under the arm as a shoulder rig. Blades carried this way take [sheath](#sheath) or [scabbard](#scabbard) instead.

entries.name: arm_strap
entries.description: A band of [fabric](#fabric) or [leather](#leather) worn around the arm. A buckled one is [arm_belt](#arm_belt) and an elastic one is [arm_garter](#arm_garter).

entries.name: frilled_thigh_strap
entries.description: A decorative [strap](#strap) circling the thigh, finished with ruffles and supporting nothing. Sits in the same place as [frilled_garter](#frilled_garter) and is easily mistaken for it.

entries.name: belt_pouch
entries.description: A small [pouch](#pouch) [hanging](#hanging) from a [belt](#belt) or strapped around the waist, for coins, potions or [tools](#tools). Adventurers and soldiers carry them.

entries.name: strap
entries.description: A narrow band of [fabric](#fabric) or [leather](#leather) that is part of clothing, a [bag](#bag) or bedding, as opposed to a separate [belt](#belt). Shoulder straps and [spaghetti](#spaghetti) straps are specific cases.

entries.name: chest_harness
entries.description: Straps worn around the chest, framing the [breasts](#breasts) or [pectorals](#pectorals), as [fashion](#fashion) or fetish wear. A [harness](#harness) covering the whole body is a [bondage](#bondage) outfit, and [underbust](#underbust) is worth adding when a [strap](#strap) runs directly beneath.

entries.name: red_sash
entries.description: A red [sash](#sash) worn around the waist or over the shoulder, as a belt-like band or ceremonial band. Tagged with sash; a stiff [belt](#belt) with a [buckle](#buckle) is a belt instead.

entries.name: black_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) in black, whether [backpack](#backpack), [handbag](#handbag), [satchel](#satchel) or shoulder bag, carried or set down in the scene. Add the [tag](#tag) for the kind of bag as [well](#well).

entries.name: lanyard
entries.description: A cord worn round the [neck](#neck), wrist or [belt](#belt) [holding](#holding) something that must not be dropped, such as an ID [card](#card), [whistle](#whistle), [camera](#camera) or [phone](#phone). It is neither an eyewear [strap](#strap) nor the braided [aiguillette](#aiguillette) of a [dress](#dress) uniform.

entries.name: brown_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) of any sort in brown, from a [backpack](#backpack) to a [handbag](#handbag), [satchel](#satchel) or shoulder bag, most often [leather](#leather). Add bag and the type; a brown [paper](#paper) grocery [sack](#sack) is [paper_bag](#paper_bag).

entries.name: shopping_bag
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) or plastic [bag](#bag) for [carrying](#carrying) purchases, often printed with a store's [logo](#logo), which may call for a separate copyright [tag](#tag). Implies bag.

entries.name: thigh_holster
entries.description: A [holster](#holster) strapped to the thigh, [holding](#holding) a [knife](#knife), pistol or other small [weapon](#weapon). A non-weapon [container](#container) worn the same way is [thigh_pouch](#thigh_pouch).

entries.name: arm_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) buckled around the arm as decoration, sometimes several stacked along a sleeve. A [plain](#plain) unbuckled band in the same place is [arm_strap](#arm_strap).

entries.name: multiple_belts
entries.description: One character wearing two or more belts at once, around the waist, hips, chest or [thighs](#thighs). Several characters with a single [belt](#belt) each is not enough.

entries.name: blue_belt
entries.description: A blue [belt](#belt) at the waist or across the hips, worn over trousers, a [skirt](#skirt) or a [dress](#dress). Buckles and [studs](#studs) are described by their own tags.

entries.name: red_belt
entries.description: A red [belt](#belt) worn at the waist or slung on the hips, whether [leather](#leather) or [fabric](#fabric). A wide tied [cloth](#cloth) band instead is [red_sash](#red_sash).

entries.name: pocket_watch
entries.description: A round [watch](#watch) on a [chain](#chain) meant to be carried in a [pocket](#pocket), often shown open in the hand. Use it for any such watch that is not worn hung around the [neck](#neck).

entries.name: thigh_belt
entries.description: A buckled [belt](#belt) fastened around the thigh, a specific kind of [thigh_strap](#thigh_strap). Often anchors a [thigh_holster](#thigh_holster) or a [pouch](#pouch).

entries.name: black_sash
entries.description: A black band of [cloth](#cloth) tied at the waist or worn diagonally across the chest, as on a [kimono](#kimono), a martial arts uniform or ceremonial [dress](#dress). It is soft cloth rather than a buckled [belt](#belt).

entries.name: blue_sash
entries.description: A blue band of [cloth](#cloth) knotted at the waist or worn diagonally across the chest, seen on [kimono](#kimono), martial arts [dress](#dress) and ceremonial outfits. Wider and softer than a [belt](#belt), and it ties rather than buckles.

entries.name: o-ring_thigh_strap
entries.description: A band worn around the thigh with a [ring](#ring) fitted to it, heart-shaped rings included. A ringed garter fastened to legwear is o-ring_legwear_garter, and ringed stockings are [o-ring_legwear](#o-ring_legwear).

entries.name: pink_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) of any kind in pink, from a [handbag](#handbag) or tote to a [backpack](#backpack) or shoulder bag, carried, slung or set down. Only the colour distinguishes it.

entries.name: briefcase
entries.description: A flat hard-sided case with a [handle](#handle), carried for documents and files by [office](#office) workers and businessmen. A larger travelling case is [suitcase](#suitcase), and a soft shoulder [bag](#bag) is bag.

entries.name: chest_belt
entries.description: A buckled [belt](#belt) crossing the chest, worn over clothing or built into it. Without a [buckle](#buckle) it is a [chest_strap](#chest_strap), a diagonal run from shoulder to waist is a shoulder belt, and when it sits right beneath the [breasts](#breasts) or [pectorals](#pectorals) consider [underbust](#underbust) as [well](#well).

entries.name: red_bag
entries.description: A red [bag](#bag) of any kind, [handbag](#handbag), [backpack](#backpack), or shoulder bag, carried or set down nearby. Combine with the specific type of bag.

entries.name: bag_charm
entries.description: A small ornament [dangling](#dangling) from a [bag](#bag) or [backpack](#backpack): a plush [mascot](#mascot), a [keyring](#keyring) [figure](#figure), a little [bell](#bell). It covers the trinket alone, with the bag itself tagged separately.

entries.name: purple_sash
entries.description: A purple [sash](#sash) or [obi](#obi) tied around the waist or worn across the body. Combine with sash, and with [kimono](#kimono) when it functions as an obi.

entries.name: white_sash
entries.description: A wide white band of [fabric](#fabric) worn across the chest or cinched at the waist. It shows up on ceremonial [dress](#dress), martial-arts uniforms, and traditional outfits alike; combine with [sash](#sash).

entries.name: blue_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) in blue of any kind, a [backpack](#backpack), [handbag](#handbag) or [school](#school) [satchel](#satchel) among them. Add the type of bag as [well](#well), since the colour says nothing about the shape.

entries.name: thigh_pouch
entries.description: A closed [pouch](#pouch) strapped to the thigh for [carrying](#carrying) small items, usually held by a [thigh_strap](#thigh_strap). When it carries a [weapon](#weapon) such as a [gun](#gun), use [thigh_holster](#thigh_holster) instead.

entries.name: loose_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) worn slack as an ornament rather than to hold anything up, sagging across the hips. An unbuckled one is [open_belt](#open_belt).

entries.name: white_bag
entries.description: A white [bag](#bag) of any kind, carried or worn, including backpacks and handbags. Add the specific bag style alongside.

entries.name: pink_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) in pink, buckled at the waist or slung across the hips. A wider band of [cloth](#cloth) tied round the waist reads as a [sash](#sash) instead.

entries.name: yellow_sash
entries.description: A yellow band of [cloth](#cloth) worn around the waist or across the body. Tag [sash](#sash) as [well](#well).

entries.name: chest_strap
entries.description: A buckle-less [strap](#strap) crossing the chest, worn over the clothing or part of it. With a [buckle](#buckle) it becomes a [chest_belt](#chest_belt), a diagonal run from shoulder to waist is a shoulder strap, and [underbust](#underbust) applies when it lies directly beneath the [breasts](#breasts).

entries.name: duffel_bag
entries.description: A large cylindrical [bag](#bag) of canvas or similar tough [cloth](#cloth), slung by a shoulder [strap](#strap) and shut with a zip or [drawstring](#drawstring). Hauls sports kit, or stands in for a [suitcase](#suitcase).

entries.name: fanny_pack
entries.description: A small zipped [pouch](#pouch) on a [strap](#strap) worn round the waist or hips, sometimes slung across the chest instead. A [casual](#casual), sporty accessory, called a bum [bag](#bag) in Britain.

entries.name: yellow_belt
entries.description: A yellow [belt](#belt) worn at the waist or hips. Tag belt as [well](#well); in martial arts it may indicate a rank.

entries.name: purple_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) in purple worn at the waist or hips. A wide tied [sash](#sash) instead is [purple_sash](#purple_sash).

entries.name: studded_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) covered in rows of metal [studs](#studs), a [staple](#staple) of [punk](#punk) and [rock](#rock) [fashion](#fashion). If the belt is made from gems rather than studs, [tag](#tag) gem_belt instead. Implies belt.

entries.name: yellow_bag
entries.description: A yellow [bag](#bag) of any kind, including backpacks and handbags. Tag bag and the type such as [backpack](#backpack).

entries.name: grey_belt
entries.description: A grey [belt](#belt) worn at the waist or hips over trousers, a [skirt](#skirt) or a [dress](#dress). Whether it fastens with a [buckle](#buckle) or a [clasp](#clasp) makes [no](#no) difference.

entries.name: holstered
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon), nearly always a [handgun](#handgun), sits inside its [holster](#holster) rather than being drawn. The weapon itself has to be visible; an empty carrier is only holster.

entries.name: satchel
entries.description: A flat [bag](#bag) with a long [strap](#strap) slung across the body, the bag [hanging](#hanging) at one side while the strap loops over the opposite shoulder. Carried mostly by students for books, also by [office](#office) workers.

entries.name: leg_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) buckled around a thigh or calf, worn for decoration or to carry a [holster](#holster) or [pouch](#pouch).

entries.name: shoulder_strap
entries.description: Any [strap](#strap) that hangs from or loops around a shoulder without a [buckle](#buckle). A buckled diagonal strap is [shoulder_belt](#shoulder_belt) instead; [spaghetti](#spaghetti) straps, [bra](#bra) straps, [strap_slip](#strap_slip) and [epaulettes](#epaulettes) are excluded.

entries.name: animal_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) or [backpack](#backpack) made in the likeness of a [creature](#creature), complete with ears, a face or a [dangling](#dangling) [tail](#tail). Add the ordinary bag type alongside where it is clear.

entries.name: utility_belt
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [belt](#belt) fitted with attached pouches and holsters for [carrying](#carrying) gear, as worn by [police](#police) officers, soldiers and superheroes.

entries.name: leather_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) of tanned hide, worn at the waist or strapped elsewhere on the body, generally closed with a metal [buckle](#buckle).

entries.name: ammunition_pouch
entries.description: A [pouch](#pouch) made to hold magazines or loose rounds, worn on a [belt](#belt) or a [vest](#vest), open-topped or flapped. It is part of the carried gear rather than of the [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: shoulder_belt
entries.description: A buckled [belt](#belt) [running](#running) over one shoulder and across the chest, most often part of a [military](#military) uniform. Joined to a waist belt it becomes a Sam Browne belt; a [strap](#strap) without a [buckle](#buckle) is [shoulder_strap](#shoulder_strap), and a belt worn around the upper arm is [arm_belt](#arm_belt) instead.

entries.name: green_bag
entries.description: A green [bag](#bag) of any kind, [backpack](#backpack), [handbag](#handbag) or shoulder bag alike. Tag the sort of bag as [well](#well).

entries.name: unworn_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) of any kind is present next to someone who could carry it, but nobody is [holding](#holding) or wearing it on the body.

entries.name: rope_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) or [sash](#sash) made from [rope](#rope), knotted at the waist. Common on monks, martial artists and rustic or [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits.

entries.name: orange_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) in orange, buckled at the waist or slung on the hips over trousers, a [skirt](#skirt) or a [dress](#dress). Cloth tied rather than buckled is a [sash](#sash).

entries.name: o-ring_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) whose two ends meet at a prominent [ring](#ring) instead of a [buckle](#buckle). A frequent detail on [fantasy](#fantasy) armour and [stage](#stage) costumes.

entries.name: green_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) in green worn at the waist or the hips. It records the colour of the [strap](#strap) and says nothing about martial-arts rank.

entries.name: waist_sash
entries.description: A broad band of [cloth](#cloth) wound around the waist and knotted or tucked in. A Japanese [obi](#obi) technically qualifies but is tagged separately so other styles stay findable.

entries.name: shoulder_sash
entries.description: A [sash](#sash) draped diagonally from one shoulder down to the opposite hip, the ceremonial form of the garment. Implies sash.

entries.name: school_briefcase
entries.description: A stiff, boxy [briefcase](#briefcase) carried by students, with a top [handle](#handle) and sometimes straps so it [can](#can) be worn on the [back](#back). More rigid than the general [school_bag](#school_bag).

entries.name: messenger_bag
entries.description: A shoulder [bag](#bag) closed by one large flap over the front, worn slung across the body.

entries.name: high-waist_belt
entries.description: A wide [belt](#belt) fastened up under the bust rather than around the hips, drawing in the waist of a [dress](#dress) or [skirt](#skirt). Sitting [well](#well) above the natural waistline, it [shapes](#shapes) the whole [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: bandolier
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) of [ammunition](#ammunition) loops or magazine pouches worn as a [sash](#sash) across the chest or over one shoulder, a look tied to gunslingers and soldiers. A linked belt [feeding](#feeding) a [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) is an [ammunition_belt](#ammunition_belt), and a [plain](#plain) diagonal [dress](#dress) [strap](#strap) is a [sam_browne_belt](#sam_browne_belt).

entries.name: grocery_bag
entries.description: A [paper](#paper), plastic or reusable [bag](#bag) [carrying](#carrying) [groceries](#groceries), often with a leek or [baguette](#baguette) [poking](#poking) out the top.

entries.name: pink_sash
entries.description: A broad pink band worn round the waist or across the body, a [kimono](#kimono) [obi](#obi) included. A narrow band closed with a [buckle](#buckle) is a [belt](#belt) instead.

entries.name: high_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) worn high on the body, at the natural waist or above it, instead of down on the hips. Position alone is what separates it from an ordinary belt.

entries.name: unworn_backpack
entries.description: A [backpack](#backpack) sits in the picture with nobody [carrying](#carrying) it, set down on the [floor](#floor) or beside its owner.

entries.name: white_armband
entries.description: A white band worn around the upper arm, over a sleeve or on bare skin. It [can](#can) serve as a uniform [marker](#marker), a [mourning](#mourning) band or a [costume](#costume) detail.

entries.name: cat_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) or [backpack](#backpack) shaped like a [cat](#cat) or printed with a cat's face, ears and [whiskers](#whiskers). One of the animal-shaped bags.

entries.name: kinchaku
entries.description: A small [cloth](#cloth) [drawstring](#drawstring) [pouch](#pouch), sometimes with a woven base, carried to match a [kimono](#kimono) or [yukata](#yukata) and seen especially at [summer](#summer) festivals. The stewed [tofu](#tofu) parcel of the same name is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: green_sash
entries.description: A green [sash](#sash), worn across one shoulder or knotted at the waist with the ends left [hanging](#hanging). It suits uniforms, pageant outfits and traditional [dress](#dress).

entries.name: sam_browne_belt
entries.description: A waist [belt](#belt) with a [strap](#strap) [running](#running) diagonally over the right shoulder, typical of [military](#military) and [police](#police) [dress](#dress) uniforms. A diagonal strap with [no](#no) waist belt is [shoulder_belt](#shoulder_belt) instead.

entries.name: seatbelt
entries.description: The safety [belt](#belt) strapped across a passenger or driver in a [car](#car) or plane seat. Tag it when the belt is visibly worn.

entries.name: brown_sash
entries.description: A brown [sash](#sash) tied at the waist or worn across the chest, as on a [kimono](#kimono), a martial-arts uniform or a [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: checkered_sash
entries.description: A [sash](#sash) or [obi](#obi) [patterned](#patterned) in squares, generally wrapped and tied at the waist over a [kimono](#kimono). It also appears on uniforms and costumes as a broad band of pattern.

entries.name: gold_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) in [gold](#gold), whether linked plates, gilt [leather](#leather) or a [chain](#chain) slung about the waist. Armour, dancewear and [ornate](#ornate) [fantasy](#fantasy) [dress](#dress) all use one.

entries.name: arm_pouch
entries.description: A small [pouch](#pouch) or case strapped to the upper arm or forearm. Standard kit on [military](#military), adventuring and other practical outfits.

entries.name: grey_bag
entries.description: A grey [bag](#bag) of any shape, held in the hand, slung from a shoulder or set down beside the character. What the bag is meant to carry makes [no](#no) difference.

entries.name: weapon_case
entries.description: A rigid or padded case built to carry arms out of sight, frequently lined inside with [foam](#foam). Shapes range from briefcases and backpacks to ones disguised as [instrument](#instrument) cases.

entries.name: purple_bag
entries.description: Any carried [bag](#bag) in purple, from a [school](#school) [backpack](#backpack) to a [handbag](#handbag) or shoulder [satchel](#satchel). Colour is the only thing the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: muzzle_(mask)
entries.description: A [cage](#cage) or [strap](#strap) [harness](#harness) buckled over the mouth and [nose](#nose) to hold the jaws shut. It turns up on [working](#working) animals, on feral characters kept in check, and as part of restraint gear.

entries.name: bridle
entries.description: Horse [headgear](#headgear) made of buckled straps [carrying](#carrying) a bit and a pair of [reins](#reins), used to steer the [animal](#animal). Fitted to a character instead of a [horse](#horse) it reads as pony play.

entries.name: coin_purse
entries.description: A small [pouch](#pouch) with [no](#no) shoulder [strap](#strap), meant for coins and other odds and ends. Often shut with a metal snap frame and carried in one hand.

entries.name: belt_chain
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) [hanging](#hanging) from a [belt](#belt) or looped along it, [swinging](#swinging) at the hip. Keep it apart from a chain belt, where the chain takes the belt's place rather than [decorating](#decorating) it.

entries.name: weapon_bag
entries.description: A long soft [bag](#bag) for [carrying](#carrying) a [sword](#sword) or a bundle of [bamboo](#bamboo) practice blades, usually slung from a shoulder [strap](#strap). Made of [cloth](#cloth), nylon or imitation [leather](#leather).

entries.name: breast_strap
entries.description: A band runs horizontally across the top of the chest, [holding](#holding) a garment up, flattening the [breasts](#breasts) or [serving](#serving) purely as decoration. It is the [mirror](#mirror) of a cord passed underneath them instead.

entries.name: load_bearing_equipment
entries.description: A webbing rig of [belt](#belt) and [suspenders](#suspenders) that spreads the [weight](#weight) of pouches, [canteen](#canteen), [knife](#knife) and [ammunition](#ammunition) around a soldier's waist. Pouches sewn into a [vest](#vest), or a rig [sitting](#sitting) up on the chest, are separate items.

entries.name: spiked_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) set with metal [studs](#studs) or points along its length, often slung loosely across the hips. Punk and [rock](#rock) styling, sometimes worn two at once.

entries.name: o-ring_harness
entries.description: Straps crossing the body that converge on one or more rings, the [ring](#ring) [sitting](#sitting) at the visible centre of the arrangement.

entries.name: multiple_thigh_straps
entries.description: Two or more bands buckled around the same thigh, stacked one above another. Popular on [military](#military) and gunslinger designs, where the straps double as mounts for a [holster](#holster) or [pouch](#pouch).

entries.name: orange_sash
entries.description: A broad orange band worn round the waist or across the chest, tied or knotted rather than fastened with a [buckle](#buckle).

entries.name: heart_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) whose [buckle](#buckle) or centre [clasp](#clasp) is a [heart](#heart), sometimes with a heart-shaped stone set into it.

entries.name: winged_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) or [backpack](#backpack) with decorative [wings](#wings) fixed to its sides. The wings are purely ornamental, part of the outfit's design rather than any means of flight.

entries.name: striped_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) with stripes [running](#running) along its length, worn at the waist or slung on the hips.

entries.name: black_pouch
entries.description: A small black carrier fastened to a [belt](#belt), a thigh [strap](#strap) or a [harness](#harness). It counts as worn gear, unlike a [bag](#bag) carried in the hand.

entries.name: hair_belt
entries.description: A length of the character's own hair wrapped around the waist in place of a [belt](#belt), or a belt-like band cinching a long fall of hair. The hair is doing the work of an accessory.

entries.name: black_straps
entries.description: Black bands crossing the body or a garment, [holding](#holding) something in place or added purely for looks. It is the straps that are black, not necessarily the outfit they run over.

entries.name: belt_bag
entries.description: A small [pouch](#pouch) or purse hung on a [belt](#belt) at the waist or hip. It covers fanny packs and utility pouches alike, and turns up on adventurer and courier designs.

entries.name: crotch_strap
entries.description: A [strap](#strap) [running](#running) front to [back](#back) between the [legs](#legs) to keep a [harness](#harness), [swimsuit](#swimsuit) or piece of armour [sitting](#sitting) where it should. Structural webbing rather than a revealing cut.

entries.name: aqua_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) in blue-green worn at the waist or across the hips. The [shade](#shade) is all this records; buckles, holsters and pouches keep their own tags.

entries.name: frilled_sash
entries.description: A wide [cloth](#cloth) [sash](#sash) tied at the waist with ruffled edging worked along it. Often the finishing touch on a [dress](#dress) or a [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: tote_bag
entries.description: A roomy, open-topped [bag](#bag) with two handles, carried by hand or slung over one shoulder. Frequently printed with a design, [logo](#logo) or slogan across the side.

entries.name: kindergarten_bag
entries.description: A small shoulder [bag](#bag), usually yellow, worn across the body by preschool children along with the matching [hat](#hat). Part of the standard nursery kit.

entries.name: chain_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) made of linked metal rings, worn at the waist or slung low across the hips. Keep it apart from a [chain](#chain) that merely dangles from an ordinary [leather](#leather) belt.

entries.name: skull_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) [carrying](#carrying) a [skull](#skull) motif, either worked into the [buckle](#buckle) or repeated along the [strap](#strap). Standard on [punk](#punk), biker and villain outfits.

entries.name: backpack_basket
entries.description: A woven [basket](#basket) carried on the [back](#back) with shoulder straps, worn exactly as a rucksack is. It is the traditional way of hauling crops, herbs or [firewood](#firewood).

entries.name: suspenders_hanging
entries.description: The straps are off the shoulders entirely and left [dangling](#dangling) loose at the hips. The trousers or [skirt](#skirt) still stay in place; only the [braces](#braces) have been dropped.

entries.name: crossed_belts
entries.description: Two belts worn together so that they meet in an X over the hips or across the chest. A stock finishing touch on adventurer and military-flavoured outfits.

entries.name: open_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag), [satchel](#satchel) or [backpack](#backpack) with the flap thrown [back](#back) or the zip run open, so what is inside [can](#can) be seen, or that nothing is.

entries.name: heart-shaped_bag
entries.description: A [handbag](#handbag) or purse cut to the [outline](#outline) of a [heart](#heart), carried by a [handle](#handle) or a [strap](#strap). A [staple](#staple) of sweet and Valentine-themed outfits.

entries.name: orange_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag), [handbag](#handbag) or [backpack](#backpack) in orange, carried in the hand, slung over a shoulder or [resting](#resting) nearby.

entries.name: suspenders_gap
entries.description: Suspender straps stand away from the [torso](#torso), leaving daylight between the [strap](#strap) and the body. A large chest is the usual reason a strap cannot lie flat.

entries.name: book_holster
entries.description: A carrier fixed to a [belt](#belt) or to a shoulder [strap](#strap), [holding](#holding) a [book](#book) so it rides along hands-free. A strap wound around the book alone, attached to nothing, is a book strap.

entries.name: birthday_sash
entries.description: A broad [sash](#sash) worn across the chest announcing whose [birthday](#birthday) it is, printed with a greeting or with the Japanese phrase for today's guest of honour.

entries.name: unworn_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) appears in the picture without being worn, [lying](#lying) on furniture, [dangling](#dangling) from a hand or dropped on the [floor](#floor), separated from any waistband.

entries.name: furoshiki_around_neck
entries.description: A wrapped [furoshiki](#furoshiki) bundle knotted over the [neck](#neck) or shoulders so it rides on the [back](#back) like a small pack. The stock image of a [thief](#thief) or a runaway [carrying](#carrying) everything they own.

entries.name: waist_bag
entries.description: A small [pouch](#pouch) worn on a [strap](#strap) around the waist, [riding](#riding) at the hip or the small of the [back](#back). Practical gear for travel, sport and [casual](#casual) outfits.

entries.name: metal_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) made of linked plates or a solid metal band rather than [leather](#leather) or [fabric](#fabric). Common on [armor](#armor) and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume) designs.

entries.name: print_sash
entries.description: A [sash](#sash) or [obi](#obi) [carrying](#carrying) a printed pattern, tied at the waist. The decoration belongs to the band itself, not to the garment beneath it.

entries.name: chest_rig
entries.description: A [harness](#harness) of pouches worn across the [torso](#torso) [carrying](#carrying) magazines, a [radio](#radio), a [knife](#knife) and other kit, [sitting](#sitting) over the clothing rather than sewn into it. Vests with the pouches built in are load-bearing vests.

entries.name: grey_sash
entries.description: A grey [sash](#sash) tied at the waist or worn diagonally across the chest. It is more at home on uniforms and traditional [dress](#dress) than on [casual](#casual) [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: tool_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) hung with loops and pouches so [tools](#tools) ride at the waist, worn by builders, engineers and repair workers.

entries.name: o-ring_strap
entries.description: A narrow [strap](#strap) threaded through a [ring](#ring), worn on the body or fitted somewhere among an outfit's buckles and straps.

entries.name: floral_print_sash
entries.description: A wide band worn at the waist or over one shoulder, its [cloth](#cloth) [patterned](#patterned) with flowers. Kimono [obi](#obi) and [dress](#dress) sashes both turn up this way.

entries.name: thigh_sheath
entries.description: A [knife](#knife) or blade holder strapped to the thigh with one or two bands round the leg. Standard kit for assassins, [ninja](#ninja) and action heroines.

entries.name: aqua_sash
entries.description: A wide band of blue-green [cloth](#cloth) tied at the waist or worn across the chest. Military [dress](#dress), [festival](#festival) wear and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume) all use one.

entries.name: knee_strap
entries.description: A band fastened round the knee itself, of [cloth](#cloth), [leather](#leather) or buckled belting. A bridal garter, worn higher on the thigh, is a different thing with its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bear_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) made in the shape of a bear's head or whole body, slung from a [strap](#strap) or worn on the [back](#back). Its face forms the front of the bag.

entries.name: green_suspenders
entries.description: Green [braces](#braces) [running](#running) over the shoulders and clipped to trousers or a [skirt](#skirt) to hold them up. They are usually shown over a [shirt](#shirt) with the [jacket](#jacket) off.

entries.name: smartwatch
entries.description: A wrist-worn [watch](#watch) with a lit rectangular [screen](#screen) and phone-like functions, replacing a [dial](#dial) with an interface. Modern-day and near-future settings use it as shorthand for a connected character.

entries.name: leather_strap
entries.description: One or more narrow bands of hide [running](#running) across a body, an outfit or a piece of kit. They may hold armour or gear together, or lie over bare skin purely for effect.

entries.name: transparent_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) made of clear plastic or vinyl, its contents visible from outside. Ranges from a [school](#school) [satchel](#satchel) to a [shopping](#shopping) carrier bag.

entries.name: insulated_delivery_bag
entries.description: The padded [square](#square) [backpack](#backpack) or [box](#box) a courier uses to keep [food](#food) [hot](#hot) on the way to a customer. Pizza runs and app couriers on bicycles are its natural setting.

entries.name: heart_pouch
entries.description: A small [pouch](#pouch) or [belt](#belt) [bag](#bag) made to a [heart](#heart) [outline](#outline), worn at the hip or on a [strap](#strap).

entries.name: rabbit_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) shaped like a rabbit's face or like the whole [animal](#animal), ears included. Carried or worn the same way as any other bag.

entries.name: too_many_belts
entries.description: An outfit strung with belts and straps [well](#well) past any use, buckled around waist, [thighs](#thighs), arms and chest. A [staple](#staple) of certain [fantasy](#fantasy) and [rock](#rock) designs.

entries.name: striped_sash
entries.description: A wide band of striped [cloth](#cloth) worn across the shoulder or wound around the waist.

entries.name: ankle_belt
entries.description: A buckled [strap](#strap) fastened round the ankle, over bare skin, [boots](#boots) or legwear. Almost always decorative, echoing belts used elsewhere on the outfit.

entries.name: leg_holster
entries.description: A [holster](#holster) strapped down the leg to carry a pistol or [knife](#knife), [sitting](#sitting) low toward the shin or calf. One [riding](#riding) high on the thigh is a thigh holster instead.

entries.name: large_belt
entries.description: An unusually wide or bulky [belt](#belt), frequently with an outsized [buckle](#buckle). It is normally a design accent rather than anything [holding](#holding) clothing up.

entries.name: red_suspenders
entries.description: Red [braces](#braces) [running](#running) over the shoulders and clipped or buttoned to the waistband to hold up trousers or a [skirt](#skirt). They [cross](#cross) or run parallel down the [back](#back).

entries.name: itabag
entries.description: A shoulder [bag](#bag) or [backpack](#backpack) so thickly covered in badges, acrylic charms and character goods that the bag beneath barely shows. It is carried to [display](#display) a fandom in public.

entries.name: baby_carrier
entries.description: Any contraption made for [carrying](#carrying) an infant about: a pram, a [cloth](#cloth) sling, or a strapped pack worn on the chest or the [back](#back). Fan art frequently puts a small [creature](#creature) in one instead of a [child](#child).

entries.name: print_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) or [backpack](#backpack) decorated with a printed design, be it characters, a slogan or a repeating pattern. The design sits on the [fabric](#fabric) rather than [hanging](#hanging) off it as a charm.

entries.name: spiked_thigh_strap
entries.description: A [studded](#studded) [strap](#strap) buckled around the thigh, over bare skin or legwear. Purely decorative, part of [punk](#punk) and battle-fashion outfits.

entries.name: card_holster
entries.description: A rectangular [holster](#holster) for [carrying](#carrying) [playing](#playing) or duelling cards, worn at the hip the way a weapon's would be. It marks its wearer out as a [card](#card) duellist.

entries.name: in_pocket
entries.description: A small character or [animal](#animal) [riding](#riding) inside a [pocket](#pocket) or [pouch](#pouch), head and arms over the rim. Chest pockets and [apron](#apron) pouches are the usual [spots](#spots).

entries.name: round_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) whose body is a [circle](#circle) or [drum](#drum) rather than a [rectangle](#rectangle), carried by a [strap](#strap) or a short [handle](#handle). Its shape is what sets it apart from an ordinary [handbag](#handbag).

entries.name: food-themed_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag), purse or [backpack](#backpack) shaped or decorated to look like something edible, from a bread-loaf clutch to a [strawberry](#strawberry) rucksack. A novelty design rather than a lunch [container](#container).

entries.name: drawstring_bag
entries.description: A soft [sack](#sack) shut by [pulling](#pulling) a cord through its top, usually carried on the [back](#back) by the two loops of that cord. Light kit for [gym](#gym) [clothes](#clothes) or [school](#school) things.

entries.name: recorder_case
entries.description: The slim zip or hard case a [school](#school) [recorder](#recorder) is carried in, usually slung from a [strap](#strap). A [familiar](#familiar) prop in Japanese [classroom](#classroom) and commuting scenes.

entries.name: medicine_box
entries.description: A wicker or wooden chest of remedies carried on the [back](#back) like a pack, as travelling apothecaries do in period or folklore settings.

entries.name: syringe_holster
entries.description: A strapped carrier, often worn on the thigh, [holding](#holding) one or more syringes in loops or pockets. Mirrors the cut and placement of a [gun](#gun) [holster](#holster).

entries.name: long_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves covering the arm at least as far as the wrist. Detached sleeves count when they begin at the middle of the upper arm or above.

entries.name: bare_shoulders
entries.description: The shoulders are uncovered, by way of a [sleeveless](#sleeveless), [strapless](#strapless) or wide-necked design or [clothes](#clothes) that have slipped down. Not for [nude](#nude) or [topless](#topless) characters; when only one shoulder shows, use [single_bare_shoulder](#single_bare_shoulder).

entries.name: short_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves ending at or above the elbow, leaving the [forearms](#forearms) bare. Sleeveless tops and long sleeves each have their own separate tags.

entries.name: sleeveless
entries.description: A top or [dress](#dress) with a neckline but [no](#no) sleeves, baring the arms. May be combined with [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves); not for [strapless](#strapless), [halterneck](#halterneck), [off_shoulder](#off_shoulder) or spaghetti-strap garments.

entries.name: detached_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves worn separately from the upper garment, leaving the shoulders or upper arms bare between them. They sit happily with [sleeveless](#sleeveless) or [strapless](#strapless), since those describe only the [torso](#torso) piece.

entries.name: puffy_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that [balloon](#balloon) outward instead of [lying](#lying) flat against the arm, whether at the shoulder or along their whole length. The general [tag](#tag); use [puffy_short_sleeves](#puffy_short_sleeves), [puffy_long_sleeves](#puffy_long_sleeves), or [puffy_detached_sleeves](#puffy_detached_sleeves) for the specific form.

entries.name: wide_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that [flare](#flare) open widely at the cuff, as on a [kimono](#kimono), a mage's [robe](#robe), or certain [fantasy](#fantasy) dresses. When they hang [well](#well) past the hands, [sleeves_past_fingers](#sleeves_past_fingers) applies too.

entries.name: off_shoulder
entries.description: A sleeved garment sits below the shoulders at about the level of the upper arms, whether cut that way or merely slipped down. Once it has fallen much further the [tag](#tag) is [clothes_down](#clothes_down), and strapped garments pulled off the shoulder take [strap_slip](#strap_slip).

entries.name: puffy_short_sleeves
entries.description: Short sleeves that [balloon](#balloon) out from the shoulder before gathering above the elbow, a [staple](#staple) of blouses, dresses, and [maid](#maid) outfits alike.

entries.name: clothing_cutout
entries.description: A gap cut into a garment on purpose so a [patch](#patch) of skin shows through, at the chest, waist, [back](#back) or elsewhere, sometimes shaped as a [heart](#heart) or an [animal](#animal) head. Pair it with the [tag](#tag) naming where the [opening](#opening) sits.

entries.name: sleeves_past_wrists
entries.description: Sleeves that extend beyond the wrist to [cover](#cover) part of the hand, usually from baggy or oversized [clothes](#clothes). It includes the longer [sleeves_past_fingers](#sleeves_past_fingers).

entries.name: strapless
entries.description: A top or [dress](#dress) with [no](#no) straps, neckline or sleeves, leaving shoulders and [neck](#neck) bare; detached sleeves are allowed. A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top still has a neck and an [off_shoulder](#off_shoulder) top still has sleeves, so neither counts as strapless.

entries.name: bare_arms
entries.description: The arms are left uncovered from the shoulder down to at least mid-forearm, as [sleeveless](#sleeveless) tops leave them. It records a clothing [choice](#choice), so it does not apply to a [nude](#nude) or [topless](#topless) character.

entries.name: turtleneck
entries.description: A high, close-fitting [collar](#collar) that wraps the [neck](#neck), most often on a [sweater](#sweater) but seen on shirts, dresses and leotards too. Pair with the garment's own [tag](#tag), such as [turtleneck_sweater](#turtleneck_sweater).

entries.name: halterneck
entries.description: A neckline where the garment is held up by a single [strap](#strap) [running](#running) around the [back](#back) of the [neck](#neck), leaving the shoulders bare. Found on dresses, shirts, leotards, one-piece swimsuits and bikinis alike.

entries.name: cleavage_cutout
entries.description: A [hole](#hole) in the chest of a garment, closed at both top and bottom within the same layer, showing the [breasts](#breasts), [pectorals](#pectorals) or the [space](#space) between them. The wearer need not have any [cleavage](#cleavage) for it to apply.

entries.name: frilled_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that finish in ruffles at their ends, whether sewn to a garment or worn as [detached_sleeves](#detached_sleeves). Sleeve length is tagged separately.

entries.name: juliet_sleeves
entries.description: Long, close-fitting sleeves that swell into a puff at the shoulder, a shape taken from Renaissance [dress](#dress). It adds to both [puffy_sleeves](#puffy_sleeves) and [long_sleeves](#long_sleeves); a short sleeve that puffs is not this.

entries.name: puffy_long_sleeves
entries.description: Full-length sleeves that billow loosely from shoulder to wrist, sometimes called bishop sleeves. Sleeves that puff only at the shoulder and then [hug](#hug) the arm are [juliet_sleeves](#juliet_sleeves) instead.

entries.name: white_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves coloured white that read as distinct from the rest of the outfit, either because they are detached or because they [contrast](#contrast) with a differently coloured body, as with raglan styling. A [shirt](#shirt) that is simply white all over is [white_shirt](#white_shirt) instead.

entries.name: sleeves_past_fingers
entries.description: Sleeves so long the whole hand disappears inside them, typical of oversized [clothes](#clothes). Sleeves that [cover](#cover) only part of the hand are [sleeves_past_wrists](#sleeves_past_wrists).

entries.name: high_collar
entries.description: A garment finished with a [tall](#tall) [standing](#standing) [collar](#collar) that rises up the [neck](#neck). Military coats, [china](#china) dresses and a great many [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits use one.

entries.name: frilled_shirt_collar
entries.description: The ruffled [collar](#collar) of a [shirt](#shirt), [blouse](#blouse) or [dress](#dress), attached to the garment itself. A ruffled band that wraps the [neck](#neck) as a separate piece is [frilled_collar](#frilled_collar).

entries.name: black_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves in black that stand apart from the rest of the outfit, either detached or contrasting like raglan sleeves. A [plain](#plain) black top with matching sleeves does not need it.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves with a [ribbon](#ribbon) laced through slits near the cuff, leaving a dashed line. Seen on [miko](#miko) outfits and other traditional Japanese wear as [well](#well) as lolita [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: moe_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves long enough to swallow the hands, leaving only the fingertips showing. The bundled look reads as small and [shy](#shy), and the [cuffs](#cuffs) are often gripped shut from inside.

entries.name: layered_sleeves
entries.description: More than one sleeve shows on the same arm, from garments worn over each other, as when a short sleeve reveals a long one beneath. It usually accompanies [layered_clothes](#layered_clothes).

entries.name: backless_outfit
entries.description: Any outfit leaving the [back](#back) partly or wholly uncovered, from an open-backed [dress](#dress) or [leotard](#leotard) to a [sweater](#sweater) with nothing behind it at all. Tag the specific garment as [well](#well), and [bare_back](#bare_back) where most of the skin there is visible.

entries.name: criss-cross_halter
entries.description: A halter whose straps [cross](#cross) over the chest in an X before winding up around the [neck](#neck). Found on dresses, swimsuits and tops alike, so [tag](#tag) the garment too.

entries.name: spaghetti_strap
entries.description: A very thin shoulder [strap](#strap) [holding](#holding) up a [camisole](#camisole), [dress](#dress), or similar top. Describes the strap style only, not the garment itself, so the top still needs its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: lapels
entries.description: The flaps of [cloth](#cloth) [folded](#folded) [back](#back) down the front of a [blazer](#blazer), [suit](#suit) [jacket](#jacket) or [coat](#coat), [running](#running) out of the [collar](#collar). The [tag](#tag) is for when they are a visible feature of the garment.

entries.name: shoulder_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) cut into a top or [dress](#dress) that bares the shoulders, the classic cold-shoulder style. Implies [clothing_cutout](#clothing_cutout).

entries.name: center_opening
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit), [catsuit](#catsuit) or top is [unzipped](#unzipped) or cut open down the middle, showing a long strip of bare skin and [cleavage](#cleavage) while the [breasts](#breasts) themselves stay covered. The look also goes by the name absolute cleavage.

entries.name: single_bare_shoulder
entries.description: An outfit covers one shoulder by design while the other stays exposed, or a loose top has simply slipped off one side. Compare [single_off_shoulder](#single_off_shoulder) and [single_strap](#single_strap).

entries.name: bare_back
entries.description: Three quarters or more of the [back](#back) is exposed, generally through a backless design. A [nude](#nude) or [topless](#topless) character's back is bare by default and takes those tags instead.

entries.name: sleeve_cuffs
entries.description: Distinct [cuffs](#cuffs) at the wrist end of a sleeve, in a contrasting colour or with visible detail. Plain cuffs go untagged; detached ones are [wrist_cuffs](#wrist_cuffs), and [restraints](#restraints) are [handcuffs](#handcuffs) or cuffs.

entries.name: sleeveless_turtleneck
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top with a high [turtleneck](#turtleneck) [collar](#collar), the combination popular in gacha designs. Tag beside sleeveless and turtleneck.

entries.name: hip_vent
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) cut at the hip of a garment, like the side gaps in a [hakama](#hakama) waistband. Where the cut runs all the way down to the hem it is a [side_slit](#side_slit), sometimes with [pelvic_curtain](#pelvic_curtain).

entries.name: navel_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) cut into the front of a garment that leaves the [navel](#navel) bare, sometimes shaped as a [heart](#heart). It is a designed feature rather than clothing come undone.

entries.name: short_over_long_sleeves
entries.description: A short-sleeved garment worn over a long-sleeved one for a deliberate colour or pattern [contrast](#contrast), a layering look especially popular in the 1990s. Implies [layered_sleeves](#layered_sleeves), [long_sleeves](#long_sleeves) and [short_sleeves](#short_sleeves).

entries.name: raglan_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves joined to the body by a diagonal seam [running](#running) from armpit to neckline instead of a simple circular shoulder seam, often in a contrasting color. Common on [baseball](#baseball) shirts and [sportswear](#sportswear) for the extra freedom of movement they give.

entries.name: fur-trimmed_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves finished with a band of fur at their ends, whether attached to a garment or detached. Sleeves made of [pelt](#pelt) from shoulder to wrist are [fur_sleeves](#fur_sleeves).

entries.name: three-quarter_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves ending partway down the forearm, between the elbow and the wrist. Blouses, knitwear and [casual](#casual) jackets are commonly cut this way.

entries.name: heart_cutout
entries.description: A heart-shaped [opening](#opening) cut into a garment, most often over the [cleavage](#cleavage) but valid anywhere on the body.

entries.name: notched_lapels
entries.description: The commonest lapel style on a [jacket](#jacket), where the lapel meets the [collar](#collar) at an angle and leaves a visible step.

entries.name: sleeves_past_elbows
entries.description: Three-quarter sleeves: they [cover](#cover) the elbow and end somewhere on the forearm, short of the wrist.

entries.name: v-neck
entries.description: A top such as a [shirt](#shirt) or [sweater](#sweater) whose neckline dips to a V-shaped point. Where the V runs low enough to reveal the inner curve of the chest, [plunging_neckline](#plunging_neckline) is the [tag](#tag) to use instead.

entries.name: blue_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves in blue that differ from the garment they belong to, either detached entirely or set in a contrasting colour as with raglan [cuts](#cuts). A [plain](#plain) blue [shirt](#shirt) with matching sleeves does not need it.

entries.name: mandarin_collar
entries.description: A short [collar](#collar) that stands up at the [neck](#neck) without folding over, on a [shirt](#shirt), [jacket](#jacket) or [dress](#dress). Standard on the [china_dress](#china_dress) and [changpao](#changpao), and also called a band or [standing](#standing) collar.

entries.name: asymmetrical_sleeves
entries.description: The two sleeves of a garment are built differently, one long and one short or one missing entirely. A difference only of length is [uneven_sleeves](#uneven_sleeves) and one of colour or pattern [mismatched_sleeves](#mismatched_sleeves), while a lone detached sleeve has a [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: red_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that are red while the rest of the garment is not, or detached red sleeves worn on their own. A red [shirt](#shirt) with matching sleeves is just [red_shirt](#red_shirt).

entries.name: back_cutout
entries.description: A [hole](#hole) cut into the [back](#back) of a garment that leaves a [patch](#patch) of skin showing, often a [keyhole](#keyhole) or a [heart](#heart). A [competition](#competition) [swimsuit](#swimsuit) with an [opening](#opening) there is a [racerback](#racerback), and a back left open altogether is [backless_outfit](#backless_outfit).

entries.name: single_sleeve
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [jacket](#jacket) is made with one sleeve attached and none on the other side. Sleeves of differing length are [uneven_sleeves](#uneven_sleeves); a lone glove, gauntlet or detached sleeve does not qualify.

entries.name: single_off_shoulder
entries.description: A top slides off one arm to bare a single shoulder while staying in place on the other. Once the arm is fully out of the sleeve, use [arm_out_of_sleeve](#arm_out_of_sleeve) instead.

entries.name: purple_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that are purple and stand apart from the rest of the garment, either detached entirely or a different colour from the body of the top, as with raglan sleeves. A [shirt](#shirt) that is purple all over is simply [purple_shirt](#purple_shirt).

entries.name: side_cutout
entries.description: A deliberate [opening](#opening) cut into the side of a garment, baring skin between the armpit and the hip. If the gap is a rip rather than a design [choice](#choice), [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes) is the [tag](#tag) to use.

entries.name: single_detached_sleeve
entries.description: Only one detached sleeve is worn. Do not add [single_sleeve](#single_sleeve) or [uneven_sleeves](#uneven_sleeves) for this, since those describe sleeves attached to the garment; single_sleeve may join it only when the other sleeve is attached.

entries.name: cat_cutout
entries.description: A cat-shaped [hole](#hole) cut into a garment, most often over the [cleavage](#cleavage) and now and then over the rear. The shape may be a cat's face or a whole [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: sideless_outfit
entries.description: Clothing that exposes the sides of the body, either the full length from shoulder to leg or at least the flank from armpit to hip. The [umbrella](#umbrella) [tag](#tag) behind [sideless_shirt](#sideless_shirt), [sideless_dress](#sideless_dress) and [sideless_kimono](#sideless_kimono).

entries.name: framed_breasts
entries.description: The garment surrounds the [breasts](#breasts) in a different material or cut from the [cloth](#cloth) around them, visually outlining the chest. It [can](#can) overlap with [breastless_clothes](#breastless_clothes) when the framed area is left open.

entries.name: green_sleeves
entries.description: Green sleeves that read as separate from the garment they belong to, either detached altogether or coloured differently from the body of the top, as on a raglan [shirt](#shirt). A green shirt with sleeves to match does not qualify.

entries.name: stomach_cutout
entries.description: A gap cut into a garment that bares the [stomach](#stomach) or [midriff](#midriff) area.

entries.name: plunging_neckline
entries.description: A deep V neckline that dives between the [breasts](#breasts) toward the [stomach](#stomach). Reserve it for garments designed to sit open this low, or an [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) [shirt](#shirt) a character habitually wears that way.

entries.name: pink_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves in pink that stand apart from the rest of the outfit, either detached or cut in a different colour from the garment's body. A top that is pink all over does not count.

entries.name: torn_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that are ripped, whether styled that way or [damaged](#damaged).

entries.name: bare_hips
entries.description: The outfit leaves the hips uncovered, as a high-cut [leotard](#leotard) or [swimsuit](#swimsuit) does, or a [skirt](#skirt) or [hakama](#hakama) slit open down the side. The character is still dressed; it is the skin at the hip that shows.

entries.name: puffy_detached_sleeves
entries.description: Balloon-shaped sleeves worn on the upper arms with [no](#no) connection to the top underneath, leaving the shoulders themselves bare. Common on [idol](#idol) and magical-girl outfits.

entries.name: very_long_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that hang far beyond the hands, an exaggerated step past [sleeves_past_fingers](#sleeves_past_fingers). Often the result of oversized or ceremonial clothing.

entries.name: brown_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad [square](#square) [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style top rendered in brown, [lying](#lying) over the shoulders and down the [back](#back). It normally comes with [serafuku](#serafuku) or [school_uniform](#school_uniform).

entries.name: striped_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves [carrying](#carrying) stripes that the rest of the garment does not, whether detached or cut in a different [fabric](#fabric) such as a raglan style. For striped arm warmers use [striped_arm_warmers](#striped_arm_warmers) instead.

entries.name: ass_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) in a garment leaving the buttocks bare, heart-shaped ones being a favourite. The rest of the garment stays on around it.

entries.name: uneven_sleeves
entries.description: A single garment whose two sleeves run to different lengths, such as one long sleeve paired with a short one. Colour or pattern mismatches between sleeves are tagged separately as mismatched sleeves.

entries.name: grey_sleeves
entries.description: Grey sleeves that stand apart from the garment, either detached or in a different colour from the body of the top, as on raglan sleeves. A grey top with matching sleeves does not qualify.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves finished with a [lace](#lace) edge at the cuff. Sleeves made throughout of lace are [lace_sleeves](#lace_sleeves).

entries.name: feather-trimmed_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves edged with a band of [feathers](#feathers), generally at the cuff. A glamorous detail on gowns and [stage](#stage) outfits.

entries.name: diamond_cutout
entries.description: A rhombus-shaped [opening](#opening) cut into a garment, often at the chest, [back](#back) or hip, showing skin through it.

entries.name: pink_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad flap [collar](#collar) of a sailor-style uniform or [dress](#dress), here in pink. Pale or reddish shades [can](#can) [slide](#slide) into [purple_sailor_collar](#purple_sailor_collar) or [red_sailor_collar](#red_sailor_collar), so [judge](#judge) the dominant hue.

entries.name: frilled_cuffs
entries.description: Ruffles gathered at the wrist end of a sleeve, as on a [blouse](#blouse), [maid](#maid) [dress](#dress) or lolita outfit. Detached ruffled wrist bands count too; ruffles [running](#running) the length of the sleeve are [frilled_sleeves](#frilled_sleeves).

entries.name: yellow_sleeves
entries.description: Yellow sleeves that are detached or [contrast](#contrast) with the rest of the garment, as on raglan shirts. A fully yellow [shirt](#shirt) is simply [yellow_shirt](#yellow_shirt).

entries.name: cutout_above_navel
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) in the front of a garment placed between the [underbust](#underbust) and the [belly](#belly) button, baring a strip of [midriff](#midriff). Higher up is [underboob_cutout](#underboob_cutout), and one centred on the [navel](#navel) is [navel_cutout](#navel_cutout).

entries.name: low_neckline
entries.description: A neckline cut so low that the garment seems held up only by the [breasts](#breasts) or pecs, generally on [strapless](#strapless) or off-shoulder clothing and showing [cleavage](#cleavage). A neckline that scoops down between the breasts instead is [plunging_neckline](#plunging_neckline).

entries.name: arm_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) in the sleeve or arm of a garment leaving a [patch](#patch) of skin bare. The rest of the sleeve stays in place around it.

entries.name: breast_cutouts
entries.description: Openings cut into the chest of a garment, so the [breasts](#breasts) appear through the [fabric](#fabric) rather than under it. The gap is part of the tailoring, not clothing that has been pulled aside.

entries.name: single_strap
entries.description: A top or [dress](#dress) designed with one shoulder [strap](#strap) instead of two. A two-strap garment with one strap fallen is [strap_slip](#strap_slip) instead.

entries.name: breast_cutout
entries.description: A garment with holes cut over or around the [breasts](#breasts), letting skin or [underwear](#underwear) show while the rest stays covered. Where the openings leave the breasts entirely bare it is [breastless_clothes](#breastless_clothes); add cutouts.

entries.name: ribbed_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves with a ribbed pattern while the rest of the garment differs, or detached sleeves that are ribbed. A ribbed [sweater](#sweater) whose sleeves match the body is simply [ribbed_sweater](#ribbed_sweater).

entries.name: argyle_cutout
entries.description: Openings cut through a garment and laid out in the diamond [lattice](#lattice) of argyle, showing skin through them. The shape of the holes is what counts, not a printed design.

entries.name: mismatched_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves in two different colors or patterns on one garment. Differing lengths are [uneven_sleeves](#uneven_sleeves), and a garment with only one sleeve at all is [single_sleeve](#single_sleeve).

entries.name: frilled_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad flat [collar](#collar) of a [sailor](#sailor) top, here finished with ruffles along its [border](#border). Normally part of a [serafuku](#serafuku) or a sailor-styled [dress](#dress), so the [school](#school) uniform tags usually belong with it.

entries.name: brown_sleeves
entries.description: Brown sleeves that stand apart from the rest of the outfit, either detached altogether or cut in a different colour from the body of the top, as on a raglan [shirt](#shirt). A garment that is brown throughout does not count.

entries.name: cross-laced_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves threaded with cords or ribbons that [cross](#cross) over each other, sometimes spanning cutouts along the arm. One of the [cross-laced_clothes](#cross-laced_clothes) [family](#family).

entries.name: armpit_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) in a garment that leaves the armpit bare, usually cut down the side of the [bodice](#bodice). Sleeves may still [cover](#cover) the rest of the arm.

entries.name: crew_neck
entries.description: A round neckline [sitting](#sitting) close at the base of the throat, with [no](#no) [collar](#collar) and no plunge. The default shape for t-shirts and sweatshirts.

entries.name: orange_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that are orange and set apart from the rest of the garment, either detached entirely or contrasting as raglan sleeves do. A top that is orange throughout does not qualify.

entries.name: low-cut_neckline
entries.description: The neckline plunges [well](#well) down the chest, [opening](#opening) a broad V or scoop of bare skin. It describes the cut of the garment rather than how much is actually revealed.

entries.name: front_slit
entries.description: A [dress](#dress), [skirt](#skirt), [nightgown](#nightgown) or [shirt](#shirt) cut with a long [opening](#opening) down the centre front, usually beginning below the bust or [stomach](#stomach) and occasionally from the throat or [groin](#groin). Not the same as a showgirl skirt, which hangs open along its whole length.

entries.name: lace-up_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves held together by cord threaded criss-cross along their length, usually leaving strips of skin showing between. A [staple](#staple) detail of [fantasy](#fantasy) and gothic [costume](#costume).

entries.name: fishnet_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves of open [mesh](#mesh), whether part of a garment or separate detached pieces. The arm reads plainly through them.

entries.name: square_neckline
entries.description: A top or [dress](#dress) cut with a straight horizontal neckline and [square](#square) corners at the shoulders.

entries.name: print_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves [carrying](#carrying) a printed design, either detached from the top or [patterned](#patterned) differently from the body of the garment, as with raglan [cuts](#cuts). Sleeves that simply share the shirt's overall print do not qualify; add the matching print [tag](#tag) for the motif.

entries.name: puff_and_slash_sleeves
entries.description: Puffy sleeves cut with narrow slits so a contrasting layer underneath shows through the gaps, a [fashion](#fashion) that dates to Renaissance Europe and is also called paned sleeves.

entries.name: racerback
entries.description: A top or [swimsuit](#swimsuit) whose [back](#back) narrows into an inverted T shape between the shoulder blades, leaving the shoulders free to move. Typical of [sportswear](#sportswear) and [competition](#competition) swimsuits; a rounded X-shaped cut counts too, but crossed straps do not.

entries.name: lace_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves made throughout of [lace](#lace), sheer down the length of the arms. Solid sleeves finished with a lace [border](#border) are [lace-trimmed_sleeves](#lace-trimmed_sleeves).

entries.name: vertical-striped_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) down the arm, whether the rest of the garment is striped or not.

entries.name: low-cut_armhole
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) top whose armholes are cut so deep that their lower edge falls beneath the [underbust](#underbust) or the pectoral. The side of the chest is easily seen through the [opening](#opening).

entries.name: scoop_neck
entries.description: A broad, deeply curved neckline that bares the collarbones and the top of the chest while leaving the shoulders covered. It stops short of dipping below the bust.

entries.name: aqua_sleeves
entries.description: The sleeves of a garment are blue-green, matching the rest of it or set against it. Detached sleeves in that [shade](#shade) count too.

entries.name: two-tone_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves [carrying](#carrying) exactly two colours, whether one per arm or [split](#split) along the length. Raglan tops with contrasting arms are the everyday example.

entries.name: frilled_straps
entries.description: Shoulder or [bodice](#bodice) straps made from gathered ruffled [fabric](#fabric). Camisoles, sundresses and swimsuits use them where the straps are meant to be decoration in their own right.

entries.name: aqua_sailor_collar
entries.description: The broad squared-off [collar](#collar) of a [sailor](#sailor) top in blue-green, [lying](#lying) over the shoulders and [back](#back). Add [serafuku](#serafuku) or the [school](#school) uniform it belongs to.

entries.name: plaid_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves in tartan that stand apart from the rest of the outfit, either detached entirely or [patterned](#patterned) differently from the garment's body. Matching sleeves on an all-plaid garment do not count.

entries.name: leg_cutout
entries.description: Openings worked into the leg of a garment so bare skin shows through, whether on [leggings](#leggings), a [bodysuit](#bodysuit) or a long [skirt](#skirt). The gaps belong to the design rather than being damage.

entries.name: single_bare_arm
entries.description: One arm is left uncovered while the other stays clothed for most of its length. Produced by asymmetric sleeves, a single glove, or an outfit built around one bare side.

entries.name: low-cut
entries.description: A garment cut open far down the chest, leaving the sternum and the upper swell of the [breasts](#breasts) bare. It describes how the garment is made rather than any one neckline shape.

entries.name: furisode_sleeves
entries.description: Long deep sleeves [hanging](#hanging) in the manner of a [furisode](#furisode) [kimono](#kimono) but attached to some other garment. Dresses, coats and [fantasy](#fantasy) outfits use them for a Japanese flavour.

entries.name: white_sleeve_cuffs
entries.description: White bands finishing the ends of the sleeves, [standing](#standing) apart from the rest of the garment's colour. It marks a detail of the sleeve itself, not a separate [bracelet](#bracelet) or [wristband](#wristband).

entries.name: single_sleeve_past_fingers
entries.description: One sleeve runs long enough to swallow the hand entirely while the other stops at a normal length. Produces the sweater-paw look on one side only.

entries.name: pleated_sleeves
