entries.description: Sleeves gathered into regular folds along their length or at the cuff, so the [cloth](#cloth) fans open. A decorative touch on blouses, dresses and [stage](#stage) costumes.

entries.name: black_sleeve_cuffs
entries.description: Black bands closing the ends of the sleeves, usually set against a [lighter](#lighter) sleeve. Only that trim at the wrist is described, not the garment behind it.

entries.name: gradient_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that [shade](#shade) from one colour into another, often darkening at the wrist while the rest of the garment stays flat. Detached sleeves show it off particularly [well](#well).

entries.name: torn_sleeve
entries.description: Only one sleeve of the garment is ripped while the other stays whole.

entries.name: criss-cross_back-straps
entries.description: Straps that pass over one another across the wearer's [back](#back), meeting in an X between the shoulder blades. Seen on swimwear, halter tops and dresses cut open behind.

entries.name: plaid_collar
entries.description: A garment [collar](#collar) [patterned](#patterned) in tartan, often matched to a [skirt](#skirt) or tie in the same [fabric](#fabric). The check stays confined to the collar itself.

entries.name: cowl_neck
entries.description: A neckline that falls in soft draped folds of [cloth](#cloth) across the chest. Common on loose sweaters and [evening](#evening) dresses.

entries.name: multicolored_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves worked in more than one colour, whether they differ from the body of the garment or from one another. Colour blocks, gradients and contrasting [cuffs](#cuffs) all count.

entries.name: no_detached_sleeves
entries.description: A design that normally carries separate sleeves on the arms is drawn without them, leaving the arms bare or in ordinary sleeves.

entries.name: bell_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that follow the arm and then widen suddenly near the wrist into a [bell](#bell), sometimes finished with [frills](#frills). Compare [wide_sleeves](#wide_sleeves), which are broad along their whole length.

entries.name: fur_sleeves
entries.description: Detached sleeves made entirely of fur, worn on the arms apart from the rest of the outfit. Sleeves only bordered with fur do not count.

entries.name: single_sleeve_past_wrist
entries.description: One sleeve reaches past the wrist onto the hand while the other ends where a sleeve normally would. A milder version of the one-long-sleeve look.

entries.name: peaked_lapels
entries.description: Jacket [lapels](#lapels) whose points angle sharply upward toward the shoulders, [giving](#giving) a formal, broad-chested line. The rounded, softer alternative is notched lapels.

entries.name: single_wide_sleeve
entries.description: An asymmetric cut in which one sleeve flares wide while the other is narrow or missing entirely. Frequent on eastern-styled robes and mage outfits.

entries.name: star_cutout
entries.description: A star-shaped [opening](#opening) cut into a garment so skin shows through it, usually set on the chest, [back](#back) or hip.

entries.name: floral_print_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves [patterned](#patterned) with flowers while the rest of the garment stays [plain](#plain), or detached sleeves [carrying](#carrying) the print. The motif belongs to the sleeve [fabric](#fabric) itself.

entries.name: two-sided_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves lined in a colour or pattern unlike their outer face. Wide or rolled [cuffs](#cuffs) put both surfaces on view.

entries.name: gloved_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that carry on over the hands as part of the garment. Unlike [elbow_gloves](#elbow_gloves) they are not separate pieces but grow straight out of the top.

entries.name: circle_cutout
entries.description: A garment with a round [hole](#hole) cut into it, baring a disc of skin at the chest, [back](#back) or [stomach](#stomach). The shape of the [opening](#opening) is what this records.

entries.name: peter_pan_collar
entries.description: A flat [collar](#collar) with rounded ends that lies down over the shoulders instead of [standing](#standing) up. It dates from early twentieth-century [fashion](#fashion) and suits schoolgirl blouses, dolly dresses and classic lolita outfits.

entries.name: checkered_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves carry a squared pattern the rest of the outfit lacks, either detached altogether or set into a [plain](#plain) garment as contrasting panels. Where the whole garment is chequered, [tag](#tag) the garment.

entries.name: fold-over_collar
entries.description: A [collar](#collar) whose two sides [lap](#lap) across one another at the chest. Kimono, [hanbok](#hanbok) and similar wrap garments are excluded, since the overlap is simply how they are cut, though [fusion](#fusion) designs may qualify.

entries.name: shanghai_neckline
entries.description: A neckline in the Chinese manner, where a short [standing](#standing) band at the throat sits above an [opening](#opening) cut low or wide across the chest. Seen on qipao-influenced dresses.

entries.name: polka_dot_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves dotted with circles while the rest of the outfit is not, whether detached or set in as a contrasting panel. The mismatch with the body of the garment is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: cross_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) shaped like a [cross](#cross) cut through a garment, baring the skin behind it. Usually placed over the chest or the [stomach](#stomach).

entries.name: elbow_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) cut into a sleeve that bares the elbow while the rest of the arm stays covered. One of the many clothing cutouts.

entries.name: paw_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves that close over the hands and end in soft paw [shapes](#shapes), [hiding](#hiding) the fingers inside. They are part of the garment rather than [gloves](#gloves) worn separately.

entries.name: knee_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) deliberately cut into trousers, tights or a [bodysuit](#bodysuit) so the knee shows through. Ragged holes left by wear or damage are [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes) instead.

entries.name: feather_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves formed from [feathers](#feathers) or heavily plumed along their length. Bird costumes and [stage](#stage) wear use them to suggest [wings](#wings) on the arms.

entries.name: unworn_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves, usually detachable ones, appear in the picture while off the arms. Where a character who normally wears detached sleeves is simply drawn without them, [no_detached_sleeves](#no_detached_sleeves) is the [tag](#tag) to use.

entries.name: argyle_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves [carrying](#carrying) argyle. The pattern may run their whole length, sit only on the cuff, or appear as a single [column](#column) of triangles down the arm.

entries.name: cutout_below_navel
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) in the front of a garment [sitting](#sitting) under the [belly](#belly) button and above the [crotch](#crotch), showing the lower belly. It fills the gap between [navel_cutout](#navel_cutout) and [crotch_cutout](#crotch_cutout).

entries.name: animal_cutout
entries.description: A creature's [silhouette](#silhouette) appears as a [hole](#hole) cut through something, an [opening](#opening) shaped into a garment or a flat standee trimmed to the [outline](#outline). What matters is that the missing material makes the shape.

entries.name: dress_straps
entries.description: The narrow shoulder straps [holding](#holding) up a [sleeveless](#sleeveless) [dress](#dress). Worth naming when they read as a visible part of the design.

entries.name: back_slit
entries.description: A vertical [opening](#opening) cut up the rear of a narrow [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) so that the wearer [can](#can) walk in it at all. Pencil skirts are where it turns up most.

entries.name: floppy_sleeves
entries.description: Loose sleeves [hanging](#hanging) slack and drooping past the hands or elbows, with nothing [giving](#giving) them shape. Limp rather than merely wide.

entries.name: abs_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) cut into the front of a garment that bares the [stomach](#stomach) while the rest of the [torso](#torso) stays covered. The gap is part of the design, not [torn](#torn) [cloth](#cloth) or [fabric](#fabric) pulled aside.

entries.name: striped_clothes
entries.description: Any garment printed with stripes, usually broad bands of alternating colour of equal width. Add the specific piece too, such as [striped_shirt](#striped_shirt), [striped_panties](#striped_panties) or [striped_thighhighs](#striped_thighhighs).

entries.name: plaid_clothes
entries.description: Any garment showing a plaid or tartan pattern of crossing coloured bands. This is the [umbrella](#umbrella) [tag](#tag); add the specific piece as [well](#well), such as [plaid_skirt](#plaid_skirt), [plaid_shirt](#plaid_shirt), or [plaid_scarf](#plaid_scarf).

entries.name: floral_print
entries.description: Flowers printed on a piece of clothing, stylised or [realistic](#realistic). Particular blooms have tags of their own, such as [rose_print](#rose_print) or [cherry_blossom_print](#cherry_blossom_print).

entries.name: animal_print
entries.description: Cloth or an object printed with a creature's [coat](#coat) pattern, or with pictures of the [animal](#animal) itself: [leopard](#leopard) [spots](#spots), [zebra](#zebra) stripes, [cow](#cow) patches. Add the specific print where it [can](#can) be named.

entries.name: polka_dot
entries.description: A pattern of evenly spaced circles of the same size, on [fabric](#fabric), a background, or an object. Add the item [carrying](#carrying) it, such as [polka_dot_dress](#polka_dot_dress); the fine dot [screen](#screen) used in printing is a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: multicolored_clothes
entries.description: Clothing [carrying](#carrying) two or more clearly different colours, a [dress](#dress) [split](#split) between red and blue for instance. White, black and grey do not count, nor do shades of one colour, trim and bows, or patterns such as plaid and stripes that have tags of their own.

entries.name: vertical-striped_clothes
entries.description: Any garment [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) up and down rather than across. Tag the specific piece too, such as [vertical-striped_shirt](#vertical-striped_shirt) or [vertical-striped_thighhighs](#vertical-striped_thighhighs).

entries.name: text_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) [patterned](#patterned) with printed lettering that works as decoration rather than as a message meant to be read. Scattered words, repeated slogans and blocks of pseudo-English all qualify.

entries.name: cow_print
entries.description: The black-and-white [patch](#patch) pattern of a dairy [cow](#cow) on clothing or [fabric](#fabric), the [staple](#staple) of cow-themed outfits. Add the specific garment [tag](#tag) wherever one exists.

entries.name: checkered_clothes
entries.description: Clothing [patterned](#patterned) in even alternating squares of two colours, like a chequerboard. It is not the same as plaid, whose crossing lines vary in width and colour.

entries.name: star_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) printed with a pattern of star symbols.

entries.name: argyle_clothes
entries.description: Garments [patterned](#patterned) with argyle: rows of diamonds crossed by thin diagonal lines, most [familiar](#familiar) on knitwear, vests and legwear. Raised [cable](#cable) [knitting](#knitting) is a different thing entirely.

entries.name: tiger_print
entries.description: Clothing [patterned](#patterned) with black stripes on orange or yellow like a tiger's [coat](#coat). Classic on [oni](#oni) characters and worn as a [bikini](#bikini) print.

entries.name: camouflage
entries.description: A mottled disruptive pattern in greens, browns or greys meant to break up an [outline](#outline) against terrain. It appears on clothing, gear and equipment; add the specific garment [tag](#tag) such as [camouflage_jacket](#camouflage_jacket).

entries.name: pinstripe_pattern
entries.description: Very narrow lines [running](#running) parallel over a wider [plain](#plain) ground, the classic [cloth](#cloth) of business suits and [baseball](#baseball) kit. Broader, evenly weighted bands are striped instead.

entries.name: diagonal-striped_clothes
entries.description: Clothing [patterned](#patterned) with stripes [running](#running) at a slant rather than straight up and down or straight across. A sub-type of [striped_clothes](#striped_clothes).

entries.name: heart_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object printed with hearts, whether a repeated pattern or a single [heart](#heart) across a [shirt](#shirt) or [bag](#bag).

entries.name: flag_print
entries.description: A garment or object printed with a national flag's design, such as a Union Jack [shirt](#shirt) or a flag-patterned [swimsuit](#swimsuit).

entries.name: leopard_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [patterned](#patterned) with a leopard's [dark](#dark) rosettes, or bearing the animal's face or body. In anime it works as shorthand for the flashy, sexually forward older woman.

entries.name: argyle_print
entries.description: The argyle motif itself: overlapping diamonds crossed by fine diagonal lines. It may sit on [cloth](#cloth), on an object, or fill a flat background.

entries.name: food_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) printed with pictures of [food](#food), carrots, cherries, mushrooms and strawberries being the commonest. It covers any food that has [no](#no) print [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: unmoving_pattern
entries.description: A repeating print such as plaid or checks that stays flat and fixed instead of [following](#following) the folds of the [cloth](#cloth) or the curve of the body beneath it. A cheap animation shortcut; where nothing repeats at all, [double_exposure](#double_exposure) is the [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: gradient_clothes
entries.description: A visible garment fades from one colour into another across its surface, whether a [skirt](#skirt), [shirt](#shirt), [dress](#dress) or legwear. Use it with the specific garment [tag](#tag); [gradient_dress](#gradient_dress) covers a dress on its own.

entries.name: leaf_print
entries.description: Clothing or swimwear printed with a [leaf](#leaf) pattern, from [tropical](#tropical) fronds to maple leaves. The pattern is printed into the [fabric](#fabric) rather than made of real [foliage](#foliage).

entries.name: serval_print
entries.description: Clothing [patterned](#patterned) after a serval's [coat](#coat), tawny with black [spots](#spots) and stripes, strongly associated with Kemono Friends' Serval. Tag the print wherever it appears.

entries.name: dragon_print
entries.description: A [dragon](#dragon) motif printed or embroidered onto clothing or an object, such as a [kimono](#kimono), a [jacket](#jacket) or a [banner](#banner). Often an eastern serpent coiling across the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: american_flag_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [carrying](#carrying) the stars-and-stripes design. Garment tags such as [american_flag_bikini](#american_flag_bikini) narrow it to whatever is wearing the print.

entries.name: rose_print
entries.description: Roses printed as a repeating pattern on clothing or an object. A specific kind of [floral_print](#floral_print).

entries.name: bat_print
entries.description: Clothing [patterned](#patterned) with bat [shapes](#shapes), most famously the legwear of certain succubus characters. It counts as a kind of [animal_print](#animal_print).

entries.name: cheetah_print
entries.description: Tan [cloth](#cloth) or objects scattered with small black [spots](#spots), each mark a solid dot rather than an outlined shape. Leopard print differs, its marks clustering into [broken](#broken) rosettes.

entries.name: fruit_print
entries.description: Fabric [patterned](#patterned) with [fruit](#fruit) motifs such as cherries, strawberries or lemons. Applies to any garment, from sundresses to swimwear.

entries.name: jaguar_print
entries.description: Cloth [patterned](#patterned) with a jaguar's rosettes, black rings over a tawny ground. The rings run larger than a leopard's and carry a dot in the middle.

entries.name: spider_web_print
entries.description: A spider-web design printed onto clothing or an object, popular on gothic and Halloween outfits. For an actual web, use [spider_web](#spider_web) instead.

entries.name: rabbit_print
entries.description: A [rabbit](#rabbit) [figure](#figure) or face printed on clothing or an object, whether as a single motif or a repeating pattern.

entries.name: patterned_clothing
entries.description: A garment covered in a repeating design of any sort. It is a general [tag](#tag), so add the more exact one, [striped_shirt](#striped_shirt) or [floral_print](#floral_print) for instance, whenever it applies.

entries.name: snowflake_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object printed with one or more snowflake motifs, typical of winter-themed outfits.

entries.name: character_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object carries a print of one specific character. When the printed character is the same one wearing it, use [self_character_print](#self_character_print).

entries.name: cat_print
entries.description: A cat's body or face printed as a motif on clothing or an object. One of the [animal](#animal) prints.

entries.name: skull_print
entries.description: A [skull](#skull) motif printed onto clothing or an object, such as a skull [t-shirt](#t-shirt) or a skull-patterned [scarf](#scarf). A whole [skeleton](#skeleton) design is [skeleton_print](#skeleton_print) instead.

entries.name: starry_sky_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) printed to look like a [night](#night) [sky](#sky) full of stars, a popular motif for dresses and coats.

entries.name: butterfly_print
entries.description: Cloth or clothing [carrying](#carrying) a printed [butterfly](#butterfly) design, whether a repeating pattern or one large motif.

entries.name: constellation_print
entries.description: Cloth [patterned](#patterned) with stars joined by lines into constellations, on a garment or on any other [fabric](#fabric). It makes [no](#no) difference whether the figures are real ones or invented for the design.

entries.name: cloud_print
entries.description: Cloth [carrying](#carrying) a printed [cloud](#cloud) motif, on clothing or on any other [fabric](#fabric) in the picture. Where the pattern is the curling East-Asian auspicious cloud, add [xiangyun](#xiangyun).

entries.name: cherry_blossom_print
entries.description: Fabric or an object printed with a [cherry](#cherry) blossom motif, typically pink five-petalled flowers scattered over a [kimono](#kimono), [dress](#dress) or accessory. Real blossom in the scene is [cherry_blossoms](#cherry_blossoms).

entries.name: single_vertical_stripe
entries.description: A narrow vertical stripe down skin-tight wear such as a [bodysuit](#bodysuit), [swimsuit](#swimsuit) or [gym](#gym) uniform, prominent enough to accentuate the body's contours. Seams and highlights do not count as stripes.

entries.name: seigaiha
entries.description: A traditional Japanese motif of overlapping fan-shaped [waves](#waves), used on [kimono](#kimono) [fabric](#fabric), backgrounds, and decor. Tag the pattern wherever it appears.

entries.name: flame_print
entries.description: A printed motif of flames on clothing or an object, in the manner of hot-rod paintwork. Pattern only; nothing is actually [burning](#burning).

entries.name: strawberry_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [patterned](#patterned) with printed strawberries.

entries.name: cross_print
entries.description: Crosses printed onto clothing or an object, whether simple plus signs or crucifix [shapes](#shapes). Add the garment's own [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: meandros
entries.description: A continuous line [folded](#folded) into a repeating right-angled [border](#border), known as the Greek [key](#key) elsewhere but most often seen here [running](#running) around the rim of a [ramen](#ramen) [bowl](#bowl).

entries.name: clover_print
entries.description: A pattern of [clover](#clover) leaves repeated across [cloth](#cloth), on clothing or on any other [fabric](#fabric) in the picture. It is frequently green, and tends to be tied to luck, spring or springtime holiday themes.

entries.name: crescent_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) printed with crescents, generally meant as moons, whether repeated as a pattern or used as a single motif.

entries.name: yagasuri
entries.description: A traditional Japanese arrow-fletching pattern of repeating feather [shapes](#shapes), usually rendered in one colour on a [plain](#plain) ground. A classic on [kimono](#kimono) and [hakama](#hakama), especially in Meiji-era schoolgirl outfits.

entries.name: bear_print
entries.description: Clothing [carrying](#carrying) one or more bears as a print, from a single face on a [shirt](#shirt) to a repeating pattern across pyjamas. A kind of [animal_print](#animal_print).

entries.name: greek_key
entries.description: The meander: a band of interlocking right-angled lines [running](#running) unbroken along an edge, taken from classical Greek [pottery](#pottery). It trims clothing, floors, frames and [architecture](#architecture).

entries.name: triangle_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) decorated with a repeated [triangle](#triangle) pattern. Solid geometric prints built from other [shapes](#shapes) carry their own separate tags.

entries.name: single_stripe
entries.description: One lone stripe runs across a garment or object, rather than a repeating striped pattern. Direction-specific versions are [single_horizontal_stripe](#single_horizontal_stripe) and [single_vertical_stripe](#single_vertical_stripe).

entries.name: fish_print
entries.description: Fish worked into the pattern of a garment, from [goldfish](#goldfish) scattered over a [yukata](#yukata) to one printed across a [shirt](#shirt). Tag the garment itself alongside it.

entries.name: single_horizontal_stripe
entries.description: Exactly one horizontal stripe runs across a garment, such as a band across a [sweater](#sweater). Several stripes together is just striped.

entries.name: asa_no_ha_(pattern)
entries.description: The traditional Japanese hemp-leaf pattern, a [lattice](#lattice) of overlapping six-pointed stars. Common on [kimono](#kimono), [yukata](#yukata) and [paper](#paper) goods; [tag](#tag) the garment as [well](#well).

entries.name: sparkle_print
entries.description: A [sparkle](#sparkle) or [glint](#glint) motif printed onto clothing or [fabric](#fabric). Tag the printed pattern, not a drawn light effect elsewhere in the picture.

entries.name: anchor_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [patterned](#patterned) with anchors, repeated across the [fabric](#fabric). A single [insignia](#insignia) rather than a pattern is [anchor_symbol](#anchor_symbol).

entries.name: honeycomb_(pattern)
entries.description: A tiling of hexagons packed edge to edge as in a beehive, printed on clothing or objects or [floating](#floating) free as a design. A single [hexagon](#hexagon) [standing](#standing) alone does not count; the cells have to join up.

entries.name: frog_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [carrying](#carrying) a printed [frog](#frog) design, whether the whole [animal](#animal) or just its face. Tag the garment or item bearing the print as [well](#well).

entries.name: double_vertical_stripe
entries.description: Two parallel stripes [running](#running) down a garment, as along the outer seam of track trousers or down the front of a [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: musical_note_print
entries.description: Musical [notes](#notes) printed across clothing or another item, as a repeating pattern or as a single motif. A note-covered [skirt](#skirt) or [bag](#bag) is the usual case.

entries.name: houndstooth
entries.description: A two-tone textile pattern of jagged [broken](#broken) checks, classically black and white. Coats, skirts and scarves carry it most.

entries.name: hitodama_print
entries.description: Clothing [patterned](#patterned) with [hitodama](#hitodama), the little tailed [spirit](#spirit) flames. The [shapes](#shapes) are printed into the [fabric](#fabric) rather than [drifting](#drifting) loose in the scene.

entries.name: bird_print
entries.description: Clothing printed with birds, whether a single motif or a pattern repeating across the [fabric](#fabric). One of the [animal_print](#animal_print) [family](#family), so add that [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: skeleton_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) printed with a [skeleton](#skeleton) motif, like a ribcage [shirt](#shirt) or bone-patterned tights. A Halloween and [punk](#punk) [staple](#staple); a [skull](#skull) alone is [skull_print](#skull_print).

entries.name: maple_leaf_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [patterned](#patterned) with maple leaves, common on [kimono](#kimono) and on autumn-themed [dress](#dress). Implies [leaf_print](#leaf_print).

entries.name: hexagon_print
entries.description: Clothing or [fabric](#fabric) printed with hexagons, often a honeycomb-like repeat. Hexagons on a hard surface are just [hexagon](#hexagon).

entries.name: double_horizontal_stripe
entries.description: Two parallel horizontal lines forming an equals [sign](#sign) on a garment. Commonly across a sleeve, a sock or a [skirt](#skirt) hem.

entries.name: lightning_bolt_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object decorated with bolt [shapes](#shapes), whether one large bolt or a repeating pattern.

entries.name: white_stripes
entries.description: A striped pattern whose stripes are white against a differently coloured ground, seen on clothing, fur, flags, and objects alike. Combine with striped and, where useful, the colour of the other stripe.

entries.name: patterned
entries.description: Clothing [carrying](#carrying) a distinct design woven or printed into the [cloth](#cloth) that [matches](#matches) none of the named pattern tags such as striped or plaid. It is the fallback for odd or unnamed designs.

entries.name: sayagata
entries.description: A traditional Japanese interlocking pattern built from linked manji [shapes](#shapes), often seen on [kimono](#kimono) [fabric](#fabric) and backgrounds. Tag the pattern wherever it appears on [cloth](#cloth) or decor.

entries.name: eye_print
entries.description: Cloth printed with the design of an open eye, on a [shirt](#shirt), [dress](#dress), [bag](#bag) or similar. The eye is part of the pattern, not part of a face.

entries.name: kikkoumon
entries.description: A traditional [hexagon](#hexagon) pattern named for a [tortoise](#tortoise) [shell](#shell), tiled across [cloth](#cloth), armour and crests. Thick multiple outlines and flowers set inside the cells tell it from a [plain](#plain) honeycomb.

entries.name: number_print
entries.description: Numerals printed across a garment or object, the way a sports [jersey](#jersey), a tee [shirt](#shirt) or a [bag](#bag) carries them. The [figure](#figure) is part of the design rather than lettering added over the picture.

entries.name: yin_yang_print
entries.description: The yin yang disc used as a printed motif on clothing or an object, whether once or repeated. It sits on the surface as a pattern, unlike a charm [hanging](#hanging) free.

entries.name: paw_print_pattern
entries.description: Paw prints repeated as a decorative pattern across [cloth](#cloth), an object or a surface, rather than a single trail of tracks left in the scene.

entries.name: shippou_(pattern)
entries.description: A traditional Japanese design of overlapping circles arranged in a [grid](#grid), so that four-petal [shapes](#shapes) appear in the gaps between them. Its name literally means seven treasures.

entries.name: sky_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object printed with a picture of the [sky](#sky). Clouds, a [moon](#moon) or birds in the pattern are what make it read as sky rather than [plain](#plain) blue.

entries.name: gingham
entries.description: A check woven from coloured stripes crossing white ones, [giving](#giving) three tones where the bands overlap. Common on [summer](#summer) dresses, aprons and tablecloths; plaid differs by [mixing](#mixing) several widths and colours.

entries.name: space_print
entries.description: A pattern [imitating](#imitating) outer [space](#space), with planets, nebulae, or galaxies among the stars, usually printed on clothing. A design showing only stars belongs under [starry_sky_print](#starry_sky_print) instead.

entries.name: brazilian_flag_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [patterned](#patterned) after Brazil's [flag](#flag), green with a yellow diamond and the blue banded [globe](#globe). The design may [cover](#cover) a whole garment or sit on it as a small [patch](#patch).

entries.name: cherry_print
entries.description: Cherries repeated as a motif across clothing or objects, usually red pairs scattered on a pale ground. Retro and pin-up styling reaches for it constantly.

entries.name: peony_print
entries.description: Peonies printed on [cloth](#cloth) or an object, generally with their broad leaves, as a single motif or repeated over the surface. A traditional Chinese and Japanese decoration.

entries.name: multicolored_stripes
entries.description: Striping that runs in three or more colours rather than alternating between two. Cloth is the usual carrier, though any striped surface qualifies.

entries.name: snake_print
entries.description: A scale pattern [imitating](#imitating) snakeskin printed on clothing or an object. The repeating diamond or hexagonal cells are what mark it out from other [animal](#animal) prints.

entries.name: spider_print
entries.description: A [spider](#spider) used as a printed motif on clothing or an object, appearing mostly on Halloween wear and gothic outfits.

entries.name: shark_print
entries.description: Clothing textured or printed with a [shark](#shark) motif, whether [fins](#fins) and [teeth](#teeth) printed on the [cloth](#cloth) or the [fabric](#fabric) itself [patterned](#patterned) to suggest shark skin.

entries.name: xiangyun
entries.description: The curling, scroll-like clouds of Chinese decorative art, drawn as tight spirals with trailing tails and read as an auspicious motif. Different from the stepped, blocky Japanese [cloud](#cloud) pattern known as [egasumi](#egasumi).

entries.name: colored_stripes
entries.description: A striped pattern made of two colours with neither of them white. Three or more colours in the stripes call for [multicolored_stripes](#multicolored_stripes).

entries.name: pink_stripes
entries.description: Pink stripes [running](#running) across a surface, whether [cloth](#cloth), fur or an object. The stripes are the point; the colour of the ground beneath them is tagged separately.

entries.name: blue_stripes
entries.description: Blue stripes patterning a garment, an object or part of the [scenery](#scenery). Only the colour of the striping is stated, so pair it with whatever carries the pattern.

entries.name: chrysanthemum_print
entries.description: A pattern of [chrysanthemum](#chrysanthemum) blooms, often with their leaves, printed on [fabric](#fabric) or an object. A favourite motif on [kimono](#kimono) and on other Japanese and Chinese garments.

entries.name: morning_glory_print
entries.description: Trumpet-shaped [morning](#morning) glory blooms printed or dyed onto [cloth](#cloth) or an object. A [summer](#summer) motif much used on [yukata](#yukata), fans and [paper](#paper) goods.

entries.name: red_stripes
entries.description: Red bands [running](#running) across [fabric](#fabric), walls, or other surfaces in the picture. Covers striped garments as [well](#well) as striped elements of the setting.

entries.name: zebra_print
entries.description: A black-and-white striped pattern copying a zebra's [coat](#coat), printed on clothing or an object. The bands taper and wander irregularly, unlike evenly ruled stripes.

entries.name: black_stripes
entries.description: Striping in black on clothing, an object or the surroundings. Since it describes the pattern's colour, pair it with whatever carries the stripes.

entries.name: piano_print
entries.description: Cloth or an object [carrying](#carrying) the repeating black-and-white pattern of a keyboard. Music-themed ties, dresses and [accessories](#accessories) favour it; a real [instrument](#instrument) in the scene is [piano](#piano).

entries.name: carrot_print
entries.description: Carrots repeated as a pattern on [cloth](#cloth) or an object, drawn whole with their green tops. It turns up on aprons, [panties](#panties) and rabbit-themed outfits.

entries.name: lemon_print
entries.description: A [lemon](#lemon) motif printed onto clothing or an object, either repeated across the surface or placed as a single decorative image.

entries.name: onigiri_print
entries.description: Rice balls used as a printed motif, repeating across a garment or some other object. It describes the pattern, not an actual [rice](#rice) [ball](#ball) in the scene.

entries.name: sun_print
entries.description: A [sun](#sun) motif printed onto [fabric](#fabric), whether a [shirt](#shirt), a [dress](#dress), a [bag](#bag) or any other [cloth](#cloth) object. The sun is part of the material's pattern, not a piece of [jewelry](#jewelry) or a [floating](#floating) symbol.

entries.name: arrow_print
entries.description: Arrows used as a repeating decoration on [cloth](#cloth) or objects, printed or woven rather than shown as real missiles. Common on [casual](#casual) clothing and banners.

entries.name: bone_print
entries.description: Cloth [patterned](#patterned) with bones or a [skeleton](#skeleton), on clothing, bedding or anything else made of [fabric](#fabric). The bones are printed into the material rather than real ones.

entries.name: ghost_print
entries.description: Little [ghost](#ghost) figures repeated across [cloth](#cloth) or over an object's surface. Sits with the seasonal novelty prints used on Halloween clothing.

entries.name: split-color_clothes
entries.description: A garment divided into two or more colour blocks, typically [split](#split) down the centre or on a diagonal so each half reads differently. The classic [jester](#jester) or [harlequin](#harlequin) look.

entries.name: hibiscus_print
entries.description: Large [tropical](#tropical) [hibiscus](#hibiscus) blooms, usually with [foliage](#foliage), repeated across [fabric](#fabric) or an object. It is the pattern that defines aloha shirts and [beach](#beach) gear.

entries.name: playing_card_theme
entries.description: Card suits, pips or a whole deck used as a decorative motif [running](#running) through the artwork or across an object. Use it for the design theme; a deck actually being handled is [playing_card](#playing_card) instead.

entries.name: wave_print
entries.description: Fabric or an object [patterned](#patterned) with crashing [water](#water), drawn as curling crests and [flying](#flying) spray. Kept apart from the stacked-arc [seigaiha](#seigaiha) motif, which is its own pattern.

entries.name: kanoko_(pattern)
entries.description: A tie-dyed [cloth](#cloth) pattern of small diamond-shaped [spots](#spots), each with a dot at its centre, ranked in even rows. The name comes from the dappling on a fawn's [coat](#coat).

entries.name: watermelon_print
entries.description: Watermelons printed across [fabric](#fabric) or an object, shown whole or cut into wedges. Common on [summer](#summer) dresses, swimwear and towels.

entries.name: vine_print
entries.description: Cloth or an object [patterned](#patterned) with [climbing](#climbing) [vines](#vines) and their leaves. Popular on [summer](#summer) dresses, [curtains](#curtains) and decorative borders.

entries.name: woodland_camouflage
entries.description: The green, brown, [tan](#tan), and black splotch pattern of American woodland [camouflage](#camouflage), printed across uniforms and gear. It reads instantly as late twentieth-century [military](#military) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: sunflower_print
entries.description: Sunflowers printed onto clothing or another [fabric](#fabric) object. One [flower](#flower) is enough to earn the [tag](#tag); it marks a pattern on the material, not an actual [bloom](#bloom) in the scene.

entries.name: square_print
entries.description: Squares used as a clothing or object pattern, whether scattered loosely or arranged in a [grid](#grid). Different from plaid, which is built from crossing stripes.

entries.name: rainbow_print
entries.description: Fabric or an object [patterned](#patterned) with [rainbow](#rainbow) motifs or spectrum bands as a printed design. The pattern sits on the surface rather than being the object's own inherent color.

entries.name: moon_print
entries.description: A [moon](#moon) motif printed, dyed or [stitched](#stitched) onto [cloth](#cloth) or an object, from a scatter of small discs to one large moon across the [back](#back). Stars and other night-sky motifs often keep it company.

entries.name: abbreviated_karakusa
entries.description: A shorthand version of the traditional curling vine motif, reduced to rows of small spirals resembling at signs. It appears on [cloth](#cloth), [wrapping](#wrapping) and [carrying](#carrying) squares in place of the fully drawn pattern.

entries.name: wing_print
entries.description: A wing motif printed, embroidered, or stamped onto clothing or an object. The wearer need not have [wings](#wings) of their own for the [tag](#tag) to apply.

entries.name: giraffe_print
entries.description: Cloth [patterned](#patterned) with the irregular brown patches and pale channels of a giraffe's [coat](#coat). One of the animal-print [family](#family) used on [clothes](#clothes) and [accessories](#accessories).

entries.name: crown_print
entries.description: Crowns repeated as a printed motif across [fabric](#fabric), on a [shirt](#shirt), a [dress](#dress) or [underwear](#underwear). Worked into the [cloth](#cloth) rather than worn on the head.

entries.name: spider_lily_print
entries.description: Red [spider](#spider) lilies worked into the pattern of clothing or an object, their long curled stamens [spraying](#spraying) outward. Some [chrysanthemum](#chrysanthemum) prints have similarly thin [petals](#petals) and get [confused](#confused) with it.

entries.name: camellia_print
entries.description: Camellia blossoms printed across [fabric](#fabric) or an object, each drawn as layered round [petals](#petals) about a yellow centre. Frequent on [kimono](#kimono) and other traditional [dress](#dress).

entries.name: musical_staff_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [patterned](#patterned) with [staff](#staff) lines and [notes](#notes), as though a page of score had been printed onto it. The pattern may run over the whole surface or sit as a band.

entries.name: plum_blossom_print
entries.description: Plum blossoms printed or woven onto [cloth](#cloth) or an object, a favourite motif on [kimono](#kimono) and East Asian decor. A single [flower](#flower) on the item is enough to qualify.

entries.name: digital_camouflage
entries.description: Camouflage built from small squared blocks, the [pixelated](#pixelated) patterns issued by many modern armies. The colour scheme and the service it belongs to make [no](#no) difference.

entries.name: sword_print
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) motif printed onto [fabric](#fabric) or another surface as decoration. The blade is part of the pattern rather than an actual [weapon](#weapon) present in the scene.

entries.name: shield_print
entries.description: A [shield](#shield) or heraldic [crest](#crest) printed, embroidered or appliqued onto a garment.

entries.name: dog_print
entries.description: A repeating pattern of dogs, [dog](#dog) faces or paw marks [running](#running) across [fabric](#fabric) or another surface. Found on shirts, bags, cushions and [wrapping](#wrapping) alike.

entries.name: phoenix_print
entries.description: Stylised phoenixes repeated across [cloth](#cloth) or another surface, common on [kimono](#kimono) and Chinese-styled robes. Tag the item [carrying](#carrying) the design rather than an actual [bird](#bird) in the scene.

entries.name: jack-o'-lantern_print
entries.description: Carved [pumpkin](#pumpkin) faces repeated as a printed motif across [fabric](#fabric) or another surface. It applies to clothing, bedding and [wrapping](#wrapping) alike.

entries.name: whale_print
entries.description: A [whale](#whale) motif printed on [cloth](#cloth) or an object, from a [plain](#plain) [silhouette](#silhouette) to a cartoon one spouting [water](#water). Popular on children's and [summer](#summer) wear.

entries.name: diamond_print
entries.description: A repeating rhombus pattern across [cloth](#cloth), wallpaper, upholstery or a [backdrop](#backdrop). Argyle and [harlequin](#harlequin) layouts fall under it.

entries.name: scale_print
entries.description: Cloth printed with a repeating pattern of overlapping [fish](#fish) or [dragon](#dragon) [scales](#scales). Common on swimwear, bodysuits and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume) where a reptilian look is wanted without real scales.

entries.name: multicolored_polka_dots
entries.description: Dots scattered across [cloth](#cloth) in several colours rather than one. Whether the garment then counts as multicoloured clothing as [well](#well) depends on how much of the ground the [dots](#dots) take up.

entries.name: bow_print
entries.description: Fabric [patterned](#patterned) with rows of small bows, printed over a [shirt](#shirt), [skirt](#skirt), [underwear](#underwear) or anything else. The bows are part of the print and could not be untied.

entries.name: african_wild_dog_print
entries.description: Fabric [carrying](#carrying) the irregular blotched [coat](#coat) of an African wild [dog](#dog). The pattern is printed on the garment, so the wearer needs [no](#no) [animal](#animal) traits of their own.

entries.name: bamboo_print
entries.description: Fabric [patterned](#patterned) with [bamboo](#bamboo) stalks and leaves, whether printed, woven or dyed in. It turns up on [kimono](#kimono) and [yukata](#yukata) and on household [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: panda_print
entries.description: A [panda](#panda) motif repeated across [fabric](#fabric) or an object, either the face alone or the whole [animal](#animal). It is a pattern printed on the thing, not its colouring.

entries.name: orange_print
entries.description: The orange [fruit](#fruit) repeated as a printed motif on [fabric](#fabric) or clothing. It describes the pattern, not the colour of the garment.

entries.name: apple_print
entries.description: Apples repeated across [fabric](#fabric), on a [dress](#dress), an [apron](#apron), [curtains](#curtains) or bedding. Here the [fruit](#fruit) is a pattern rather than an object in the scene.

entries.name: uroko_(pattern)
entries.description: A Japanese design of interlocking triangles meant to suggest [fish](#fish) or [snake](#snake) [scales](#scales), common on [kimono](#kimono), [obi](#obi) and [stage](#stage) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: white_tiger_print
entries.description: Dark stripes of varying length scattered over a white or silvery ground, copying a white tiger's [coat](#coat) as a printed pattern. It applies to clothing and objects; an actually furred character with this colouring takes a [markings](#markings) [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: grape_print
entries.description: Grapes used as a repeating motif printed or woven into a surface. The pattern is the point, not actual [fruit](#fruit) [sitting](#sitting) in the scene.

entries.name: karakusa_(pattern)
entries.description: A traditional Japanese design of curling [vines](#vines) that interlock and run over the whole surface. It is best known in white on the green [cloth](#cloth) used for [wrapping](#wrapping) bundles.

entries.name: lily_print
entries.description: A lily motif printed on clothing or an object, whether a single [bloom](#bloom) or a repeating pattern.

entries.name: mushroom_print
entries.description: A [mushroom](#mushroom) motif printed or [stitched](#stitched) onto clothing or an object. It may repeat across the [fabric](#fabric) or stand alone as a single [figure](#figure).

entries.name: aardwolf_print
entries.description: Fabric [carrying](#carrying) the vertically striped [coat](#coat) of an aardwolf, most often on legwear. The pattern lives in the [cloth](#cloth), so the wearer needs [no](#no) [animal](#animal) features of their own.

entries.name: horizontal-striped_clothes
entries.description: Garments printed or knitted with bands [running](#running) side to side across the body. Where the stripes run lengthwise instead, use [vertical-striped_clothes](#vertical-striped_clothes).

entries.name: goldfish_print
entries.description: Goldfish repeated as a woven or printed motif across [cloth](#cloth) or an object. A [summer](#summer) pattern, seen on [yukata](#yukata), folding fans and glassware.

entries.name: desert_camouflage
entries.description: The [tan](#tan) pattern of brown blotches and speckled [rock](#rock) [shapes](#shapes) issued for arid ground, nicknamed [chocolate](#chocolate) chip. Painted onto [fatigues](#fatigues), webbing and equipment in [military](#military) subjects.

entries.name: goshoguruma
entries.description: A traditional Japanese motif of an ox-drawn court [carriage](#carriage), reduced to its great spoked [wheel](#wheel) and decorated body. It ornaments [kimono](#kimono), fans and screens; the pattern is what is tagged, not a [cart](#cart) [standing](#standing) in the scene.

entries.name: gear_print
entries.description: Cogwheels repeated as a printed or woven motif across [fabric](#fabric) or an object's surface. Pairs naturally with [steampunk](#steampunk), [engineer](#engineer) and [clockwork](#clockwork) outfits.

entries.name: lotus_print
entries.description: Lotus blossoms printed or woven into the [fabric](#fabric) of a garment. The motif turns up most often on [kimono](#kimono) and other East Asian [dress](#dress).

entries.name: petal_print
entries.description: Cloth or a surface [patterned](#patterned) with repeated [flower](#flower) [petals](#petals). It belongs on the item [carrying](#carrying) the design, not on loose petals [drifting](#drifting) through a scene.

entries.name: fox_print
entries.description: Fabric [patterned](#patterned) with foxes or fox-like [markings](#markings), printed across a garment. The [animal](#animal) is on the [cloth](#cloth) rather than part of the wearer.

entries.name: hazard_stripes
entries.description: Diagonal warning bands in yellow and black or red and white, the marking that flags danger or a closed-off edge. They turn up on barriers, [machinery](#machinery) and industrial-styled clothing.

entries.name: pineapple_print
entries.description: A repeating [pineapple](#pineapple) motif across [cloth](#cloth) or an object, the mark of [summer](#summer) and [tropical](#tropical) shirts. Tag the item [carrying](#carrying) the pattern; real [fruit](#fruit) in the scene is pineapple.

entries.name: italian_flag_print
entries.description: The green, white and red bands of the Italian [flag](#flag) used as a printed motif on [cloth](#cloth) or an object. It covers a whole flag reproduced on a garment as [well](#well) as small repeated flag marks.

entries.name: horse_print
entries.description: Horses appear as a repeating printed motif on [fabric](#fabric) or an object. The [animal](#animal) itself is shown, not a [horseshoe](#horseshoe) or another equestrian symbol.

entries.name: tree_print
entries.description: Trees printed or woven onto [fabric](#fabric), whether as a single motif or a repeating woodland pattern. Applies to clothing, [curtains](#curtains), bedding and similar printed surfaces.

entries.name: sand_cat_print
entries.description: Cloth printed with the sandy, faintly barred [coat](#coat) of a [sand](#sand) [cat](#cat). Used on swimwear and [lingerie](#lingerie) the way [leopard](#leopard) and [tiger](#tiger) prints are.

entries.name: broken_heart_print
entries.description: A pattern of [split](#split) or cracked hearts printed across clothing or an object. It works as a statement of mood rather than [plain](#plain) decoration.

entries.name: candy_print
entries.description: Sweets repeated as a pattern across [cloth](#cloth) or an object: wrapped drops, lollipops and similar [shapes](#shapes). Common on pastel and childlike outfits.

entries.name: mustache_print
entries.description: A stylised curling [mustache](#mustache) printed on clothing or an accessory. It is a joke motif, most often placed on a tie, a [shirt](#shirt) or a [mug](#mug).

entries.name: white_polka_dots
entries.description: A pattern of evenly spaced white [dots](#dots), normally printed on [fabric](#fabric) over a darker ground. Dresses, umbrellas and swimwear carry it most often.

entries.name: circuit_board_print
entries.description: Fabric or an object [patterned](#patterned) with the branching traces and pads of a printed circuit board. A [staple](#staple) of [cyberpunk](#cyberpunk) and technology-themed outfits.

entries.name: union_jack_print
entries.description: Clothing bearing the British [flag](#flag) as its print, whether spread across the whole garment or confined to one panel. A common shorthand for marking a character as British.

entries.name: splatter_print
entries.description: A clothing or object design [imitating](#imitating) flung [paint](#paint) or [ink](#ink) spatters. A common motif in [streetwear](#streetwear) graphics.

entries.name: horseshoe_print
entries.description: A repeating pattern of [horseshoe](#horseshoe) [shapes](#shapes) across [fabric](#fabric) or an object. It reads as a luck charm as often as an equestrian reference.

entries.name: triple_horizontal_stripe
entries.description: Three parallel bands [running](#running) side by side across a garment, most often circling a sleeve, cuff or hem. A [sportswear](#sportswear) [staple](#staple) seen on track jackets and [tube](#tube) [socks](#socks) alike.

entries.name: no_print
entries.description: Clothing that normally carries printed lettering or a design appears [plain](#plain), the print left off. The cut and colour of the garment are otherwise unaltered.

entries.name: pumpkin_print
entries.description: Pumpkins repeated as a printed motif across [fabric](#fabric), most often on [autumn](#autumn) or Halloween clothing. The shape works purely as decoration here, not as an actual [gourd](#gourd) in the scene.

entries.name: genjiguruma
entries.description: A traditional Japanese motif of spoked ox-cart wheels, often drawn half-sunk as though [rolling](#rolling) through [water](#water). Printed on [kimono](#kimono), fans and lacquerware.

entries.name: chocolate_print
entries.description: Clothing or an object [patterned](#patterned) with [chocolate](#chocolate) motifs such as [bars](#bars), hearts or cocoa [beans](#beans). The printed design is what counts; real chocolate in the scene is tagged separately.

entries.name: dazzle_paint
entries.description: Bold irregular bands and angular blocks, usually black against white, painted across a [ship](#ship), a vehicle or a [gun](#gun) turret. It hid nothing; the point was to wreck an observer's read on speed and heading.

entries.name: duck_print
entries.description: A repeating pattern of small ducks across a garment or object. Reads as cosy or childish, and lands on pyjamas, towels and swim gear.

entries.name: horizontal-striped_sleeves
entries.description: The sleeves are banded with stripes [running](#running) around the arm. The body of the garment may match or be left [plain](#plain).

entries.name: fireworks_print
entries.description: Bursting [fireworks](#fireworks) printed across [cloth](#cloth) as a motif, a favourite on [summer](#summer) [yukata](#yukata). The pattern is in the [fabric](#fabric) and nothing is actually going off.

entries.name: feather_print
entries.description: Feather [shapes](#shapes) printed or woven across a [fabric](#fabric) or surface as a repeating motif. Decoration on the material, not real plumage.

entries.name: matsu_symbol
entries.description: A stylised pine [crest](#crest) used as a traditional Japanese [family](#family) [emblem](#emblem), drawn as a round cluster of [needle](#needle) [shapes](#shapes). Appears on banners, formal garments and decorative backgrounds.

entries.name: shima_(pattern)
entries.description: A traditional Japanese pattern whose name literally means stripe, applied here to a run of interlocking, chain-like links across the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: yellow_stripes
entries.description: Yellow bands [running](#running) as a pattern across clothing, an object or a body. They may stand alone or alternate with black in a hazard-style scheme.

entries.name: horizontal-striped_sleeve_cuffs
entries.description: Only the [cuffs](#cuffs) at the ends of the sleeves carry crosswise banding, while the rest of the garment stays [plain](#plain). A small detail rather than a description of the whole outfit.

entries.name: wisteria_print
entries.description: Hanging clusters of [wisteria](#wisteria) blossom printed onto [fabric](#fabric), typically trailing down a [kimono](#kimono) or [dress](#dress). It is a common spring motif in Japanese textile design.

entries.name: snowman_print
entries.description: A [snowman](#snowman) motif printed onto clothing or an object, whether as a single large [figure](#figure) or a repeating [winter](#winter) pattern.

entries.name: fur_trim
entries.description: A strip of fur [running](#running) along a garment's [collar](#collar), hem, [cuffs](#cuffs) or other edges. Most often white fur on Christmas clothing, and the base [tag](#tag) beneath every fur-trimmed_ garment.

entries.name: ribbon_trim
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) threaded along the edge of a garment, for decoration or to hold the [fabric](#fabric) in place. The base [tag](#tag) for the ribbon-trimmed [family](#family); add the garment-specific tag too.

entries.name: lace_trim
entries.description: Any garment finished with [lace](#lace) along its hems, [cuffs](#cuffs) or neckline. Add the garment-specific spelling such as [lace-trimmed_skirt](#lace-trimmed_skirt); something made wholly of lace is lace instead.

entries.name: gold_trim
entries.description: Gold edging along at least one hem, [collar](#collar), cuff or seam of a garment or a [suit](#suit) of armour. Uniforms, formal wear and [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume) are full of it.

entries.name: ribbon-trimmed_clothes
entries.description: Clothing edged with a threaded [ribbon](#ribbon) trim. A general catch-all [tag](#tag); prefer a garment-specific version such as [ribbon-trimmed_sleeves](#ribbon-trimmed_sleeves) or [ribbon-trimmed_skirt](#ribbon-trimmed_skirt) where one applies.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_legwear
entries.description: Socks, stockings or [thighhighs](#thighhighs) with a band of [lace](#lace) worked around the top edge. Legwear woven throughout from lace is [lace_legwear](#lace_legwear).

entries.name: fringe_trim
entries.description: Hanging strips of [fabric](#fabric) or lengths of cord attached along the edge of clothing or an object as decoration. Western wear, scarves and Native American styled outfits use it constantly.

entries.name: red_trim
entries.description: A garment edged in red along a hem, cuff, [collar](#collar) or seam, while the body of the garment is another colour. Describes the trim only; a fully red garment takes its own colour [tag](#tag).

entries.name: studs
entries.description: Small metal or plastic knobs pushed through holes in [fabric](#fabric) for decoration, round or pointed and in a range of sizes. Longer sharp points count as [spikes](#spikes) instead.

entries.name: white_trim
entries.description: A garment or object edged in white along its hems, [cuffs](#cuffs), or [seams](#seams) while the main colour is something else. Furry white edging is white fur trim specifically; combine with the item's own base colour.

entries.name: feather_trim
entries.description: A [border](#border) of [feathers](#feathers) along the edge of a garment, most often at sleeves, collars or hems. The feathered answer to [fur_trim](#fur_trim).

entries.name: blue_trim
entries.description: A garment edged in blue along at least one hem, cuff, [collar](#collar) or seam, [standing](#standing) out against the main colour of the [cloth](#cloth). Only the edging is blue, not the garment itself.

entries.name: yellow_trim
entries.description: Yellow edging along the hems, [cuffs](#cuffs) or [seams](#seams) of clothing or an object whose main colour is different. Combine with the garment's own colour [tag](#tag).

entries.name: aqua_trim
entries.description: A garment is edged with blue-green along at least one hem, cuff or seam. The trim stands out against the main body of the [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: sleeve_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around a sleeve as decoration, often at the shoulder or the cuff. When it is knotted into a [bow](#bow), [sleeve_bow](#sleeve_bow) is the closer [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pink_trim
entries.description: Pink edging, piping or borders along the hems, [cuffs](#cuffs) and [seams](#seams) of a garment whose body is another colour. Only the trim is pink.

entries.name: silver_trim
entries.description: A garment edged with silver along at least one hem, [collar](#collar) or cuff. The metallic counterpart of [gold_trim](#gold_trim).

entries.name: black_trim
entries.description: Black edging [running](#running) along the borders of a garment, at hems, collars or [cuffs](#cuffs). The body of the clothing keeps whatever colour it has; only the outlining band is described.

entries.name: green_trim
entries.description: Green edging, piping or banding along the hems, [cuffs](#cuffs) and [seams](#seams) of a garment that is otherwise another colour. It marks a detail rather than the main colour of the [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: purple_trim
entries.description: Purple edging along the hems, [cuffs](#cuffs), [collar](#collar), or [seams](#seams) of a garment that is mainly another colour. A finishing detail, not the garment's main [shade](#shade).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_headwear
entries.description: Any [hat](#hat), [bonnet](#bonnet), [headdress](#headdress) or band finished with a [lace](#lace) edging. Maid headpieces and lolita bonnets account for most of it.

entries.name: orange_trim
entries.description: Orange edging, piping or banding along the hems, [cuffs](#cuffs) or [seams](#seams) of a garment whose body is another colour.

entries.name: flower_trim
entries.description: Blossoms or flower-shaped ornaments [running](#running) along the [border](#border) of a garment, at a hem, cuff or neckline. The decoration follows an edge rather than covering the whole [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: plaid_trim
entries.description: Tartan edging along the [cuffs](#cuffs), hems, or borders of a garment that is otherwise [plain](#plain). Only the trim itself carries the check.

entries.name: grey_trim
entries.description: A garment finished with grey edging along at least one of its borders, be it hem, cuff, [collar](#collar) or placket. The garment's own colour is recorded separately.

entries.name: edging_underwear
entries.description: Underwear finished with contrasting trim along its borders, a band of [lace](#lace) or piping [running](#running) round the waist and leg openings. A detail of how the garment is made.

entries.name: polka_dot_trim
entries.description: A dotted [border](#border) along the edge of a garment, at hem, cuff, [collar](#collar) or waistband, while the main [fabric](#fabric) stays [plain](#plain). The pattern is confined to that trim.

entries.name: brown_trim
entries.description: Brown edging on a garment — piping, [cuffs](#cuffs), hems or borders picked out against a main colour that is something else. Only the trim is brown, not the item as a whole.

entries.name: flower-trimmed_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) edged with flowers or flower-shaped decoration along the hem, neckline or straps. The blooms run along a [border](#border) rather than covering the [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: studded
entries.description: Small metal knobs set through [fabric](#fabric) or [leather](#leather) as decoration, the treatment itself rather than any one garment.

entries.name: checkered_trim
entries.description: A band of check runs along a garment's edge, at the hem, cuff, [collar](#collar) or front [opening](#opening), while the body of it stays [plain](#plain). The pattern works as a [border](#border) rather than as the main [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: buttons
entries.description: Buttons on clothing, fastening a [shirt](#shirt), [coat](#coat), trousers or cuff, or sewn on purely for looks. A pressable [switch](#switch) is [push-button](#push-button), and one [pinned](#pinned) to the chest is a [button_badge](#button_badge).

entries.name: buckle
entries.description: The fastener that joins two loose ends, most often the metal [clasp](#clasp) on a [belt](#belt) or [strap](#strap). Reserve it for clothing and [accessories](#accessories) rather than [machinery](#machinery).

entries.name: o-ring
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) set into a garment or accessory with straps or panels threaded through it so they join together. Ovals, rectangles and any other pierced shape count as [well](#well), while a heart-shaped one is [heart_o-ring](#heart_o-ring). Use it wherever [no](#no) more specific ringed-garment [tag](#tag) exists.

entries.name: zipper
entries.description: A toothed fastener joining two edges of [fabric](#fabric), tagged when the artist draws it as a deliberate, visible detail rather than an incidental closure. An opened one pairs with [open_clothes](#open_clothes), and the tab alone has its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pocket
entries.description: A visible pocket sewn into a garment, on trousers, [shorts](#shorts), a [jacket](#jacket), or a [shirt](#shirt). Tag [hand_in_pocket](#hand_in_pocket) when a hand is tucked inside one.

entries.name: belt_buckle
entries.description: The [clasp](#clasp) that fastens a [belt](#belt), prominent enough to be worth noting, from a [plain](#plain) metal frame to a broad decorative [plate](#plate). Tag belt as [well](#well).

entries.name: double-breasted
entries.description: A front closing with two rows of [buttons](#buttons) and overlapping flaps rather than edges that meet in the middle. Usually seen on coats, jackets and uniform tunics.

entries.name: drawstring
entries.description: A cord run through a channel of [fabric](#fabric) that [gathers](#gathers) and tightens it when pulled. Seen on hoods, sweatpant waistbands, [bloomers](#bloomers) and the mouths of bags, often left [dangling](#dangling) as two loose ends.

entries.name: cross-laced_clothes
entries.description: Any garment threaded with cords, strings or ribbons that [cross](#cross) over each other, as on a laced [bodice](#bodice) or a [corset](#corset) front. Use the narrower [tag](#tag) where one exists, such as [cross-laced_dress](#cross-laced_dress), [cross-laced_top](#cross-laced_top) or [cross-laced_legwear](#cross-laced_legwear).

entries.name: zipper_pull_tab
entries.description: The small tab used to grip and [slide](#slide) a [zipper](#zipper) closed or open, often drawn as a prominent detail on jackets and bodysuits. Tag zipper alongside it.

entries.name: diamond_button
entries.description: One or more [buttons](#buttons) on a garment cut as diamonds rather than as discs. A small design detail, and the shape alone earns the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: heart_o-ring
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) shaped as a [heart](#heart) used as hardware — joining the ends of a [bikini](#bikini) top, a [collar](#collar) or a [strap](#strap) — or worn as a [plain](#plain) ornament.

entries.name: safety_pin
entries.description: A small clasped [pin](#pin) used to fasten [fabric](#fabric) together, often seen on [punk](#punk) outfits, [torn](#torn) clothing or as an improvised accessory.

entries.name: heart_button
entries.description: Clothing [buttons](#buttons) cut as hearts, fastening a [coat](#coat), [blouse](#blouse) or [dress](#dress). One or a whole row.

entries.name: buttoned_cuffs
entries.description: Visible [buttons](#buttons) at the wrist end of the sleeve, as on [dress](#dress) shirts and [suit](#suit) jackets. Plain [sleeve_cuffs](#sleeve_cuffs) without fastenings, of the kind sweaters have, are a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: snap-fit_buckle
entries.description: The plastic side-release [buckle](#buckle) of [backpack](#backpack) and utility straps, three prongs clicking into a [shell](#shell). Tag beside buckle.

entries.name: full-length_zipper
entries.description: A one-piece garment closed by a [zipper](#zipper) that runs from the throat down past the [navel](#navel). Bodysuits, plugsuits and [racing](#racing) outfits are built this way.

entries.name: gold_buttons
entries.description: Buttons of [gold](#gold) set down a garment's front or along the [cuffs](#cuffs). Military coats, blazers and [dress](#dress) uniforms are full of them.

entries.name: cross-laced_slit
entries.description: A slit in a garment bridged by cords or ribbons crossing over it instead of [hanging](#hanging) open, as up the side of a [skirt](#skirt) or the front of a top. The cords span the gap rather than closing the garment.

entries.name: cuff_links
entries.description: Small decorative fasteners pushed through both sides of a [shirt](#shirt) cuff in place of a button. A mark of formal [dress](#dress), on shirts made with buttonholes but [no](#no) [buttons](#buttons) there.

entries.name: toggles
entries.description: Barrel-shaped wooden pegs pushed through cord loops to fasten a [coat](#coat), the classic duffel-coat closure. The knotted [frog](#frog) fastenings on qipao and [tangzhuang](#tangzhuang) fall under it as [well](#well).

entries.name: heart-shaped_buckle
entries.description: The fastening of a [belt](#belt) or [strap](#strap) is formed as a [heart](#heart). Frequent on magical-girl, [idol](#idol) and gothic-sweet costumes.

entries.name: cross-laced_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) cut through a garment with cords or ribbons crossing over it, skin showing in the gaps. The [hole](#hole) is closed at top and bottom within a single layer, which separates it from [cross-laced_slit](#cross-laced_slit).

entries.name: flying_button
entries.description: One or more [buttons](#buttons) [caught](#caught) in mid-air, usually after bursting off a garment stretched past its limit. Motion lines or blur normally sell the pop.

entries.name: cross-laced_corset
entries.description: Lacing crossed over the waist to pull a garment in tight, [giving](#giving) the classic corseted [silhouette](#silhouette). It counts on a real [corset](#corset) and on a laced panel built into a [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress). Where the lacing runs higher or lower, the garment belongs to [cross-laced_skirt](#cross-laced_skirt), [cross-laced_top](#cross-laced_top) or [cross-laced_dress](#cross-laced_dress).

entries.name: tied_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeves fastened shut or [bound](#bound) together. The [label](#label) is vague, so prefer the precise version: a sleeve sewn or tied closed at the cuff, or both sleeves lashed to each other.

entries.name: gold_buckle
entries.description: The [buckle](#buckle) closing a [belt](#belt), [strap](#strap) or shoe rendered in [gold](#gold). Worth noting apart from the strap it holds, since the metal catches the eye.

entries.name: pankou
entries.description: The knotted [fabric](#fabric) toggle-and-loop fastenings of Chinese [dress](#dress), [running](#running) down the front of a [tangzhuang](#tangzhuang) or a [china](#china) dress. Also called [frog](#frog) [buttons](#buttons), and often as decorative as they are functional.

entries.name: multicolored_buttons
entries.description: The [buttons](#buttons) [running](#running) down a garment come in different colours from one another instead of matching as a set. A playful detail, common on handmade-looking [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: breast_zipper
entries.description: A zip runs across the breast of an outfit, placed there so the chest [can](#can) be opened up or closed off rather than to fasten the garment on. A matching zip at the [crotch](#crotch) usually comes with it.

entries.name: sweater_guard
entries.description: A short [chain](#chain) or cord strung between two clips across the chest, either keeping a garment closed or purely decorative. Despite the name it is not limited to sweaters, and differs from a [haori](#haori) himo, which is worn hidden under the [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: laces
entries.description: The cords themselves, threaded through eyelets on [boots](#boots), corsets or garments. They are often drawn [hanging](#hanging) undone or trailing loose.

entries.name: front_zipper
entries.description: A [zipper](#zipper) [running](#running) down the front of a garment, drawn prominently and frequently left part way open. Jackets, bodysuits and dresses all carry one.

entries.name: lace-up
entries.description: A closure in which cord is threaded to and fro through paired eyelets and pulled tight, as on a [corset](#corset) or a boot. The criss-crossing lacing is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: large_buttons
entries.description: Oversized [buttons](#buttons) on a garment, far bigger than the fastening needs. They serve as a decorative accent in cute and cartoonish [costume](#costume) design.

entries.name: oversized_zipper
entries.description: A [zipper](#zipper) with [teeth](#teeth) and a pull much larger than any [working](#working) fastener needs, there as a design flourish. Common on stylised jackets and on [costume](#costume) pieces.

entries.name: center_cross_lace
entries.description: A cord zigzags [back](#back) and forth across an [opening](#opening) down the front of a garment, drawing its two edges together over bare skin or a contrasting panel. Fantasy bodices, swimsuits and [idol](#idol) costumes lean on it heavily.

entries.name: bow_button
entries.description: A garment fastening moulded into the shape of a small [bow](#bow), or a [stitched](#stitched) bow [standing](#standing) in for a button. It is a fixed detail rather than a length of [ribbon](#ribbon) that could be undone.

entries.name: tied_drawstring
entries.description: The cord of a [hood](#hood), waistband or [pouch](#pouch) drawn closed and knotted, usually finished as a [bow](#bow) with the ends [hanging](#hanging) free.

entries.name: seams
entries.description: Visible joining lines of either kind: [stitching](#stitching) on a garment, or the panel gaps where two mechanical parts meet on armour or a [machine](#machine).

entries.name: sleeve_tied_shut
entries.description: A sleeve knotted closed at its end so nothing [can](#can) pass through it. Artists use it to signal a missing arm and keep the empty [fabric](#fabric) from [flapping](#flapping), though [bullying](#bullying) or a joke can explain it too. Two sleeves knotted to each other is sleeves_tied_together.

entries.name: star_button
entries.description: The fasteners on a garment cut in the shape of stars instead of [plain](#plain) discs, a small decorative touch on jackets and coats.

entries.name: cat_o-ring
entries.description: A metal [ring](#ring) bent into the shape of a [cat](#cat) and set into a garment or accessory, usually at a neckline, [strap](#strap) or waistband. It reads as decoration rather than as a [working](#working) fastener.

entries.name: clasp
entries.description: A metal fastener that hooks two ends together to close a [cloak](#cloak), [necklace](#necklace), [bag](#bag) or [belt](#belt). A small piece of hardware on a garment or accessory rather than a garment of its own.

entries.name: raise_buckle
entries.description: A fastening [buckle](#buckle) designed to let a [strap](#strap) be raised or adjusted along its length, most often seen on [boots](#boots), harnesses, or [costume](#costume) pieces where the fit needs tightening.

entries.name: bow
entries.description: A knot of two loops and a pair of loose ends, tied on clothing, in hair, on [shoes](#shoes), on [underwear](#underwear) or around a [gift](#gift). When the tails run far longer than the loops it is a [ribbon](#ribbon) rather than a bow; add the placement, and [bowtie](#bowtie) when it sits at the throat in place of a tie.

entries.name: frills
entries.description: Strips of [cloth](#cloth) or [lace](#lace) gathered along one edge and left loose along the other, applied as decorative trim. Also called ruffles, and the base [tag](#tag) every frilled_ garment sits under.

entries.name: black_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) in black, wherever it happens to sit: on clothing, in the hair, on a [gift](#gift). Add [hair_bow](#hair_bow), [bowtie](#bowtie) or the like once its placement is known.

entries.name: white_bow
entries.description: A white [ribbon](#ribbon) [bow](#bow) worn anywhere on the character, in the hair, at the [neck](#neck), on a [dress](#dress) or on [shoes](#shoes). Add a placement [tag](#tag) such as [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [bowtie](#bowtie).

entries.name: tassel
entries.description: A bundle of [hanging](#hanging) threads [bound](#bound) at the top, [dangling](#dangling) from a cord on [curtains](#curtains), hats, weapons or worn [decorations](#decorations).

entries.name: white_ribbon
entries.description: A strip of white [ribbon](#ribbon) worn or tied somewhere on the character, in the hair, at the [neck](#neck) or on clothing. Add [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon) for the placement; a [bow](#bow) shape instead is [white_bow](#white_bow).

entries.name: lace
entries.description: A garment made throughout of lace, the fine openwork [fabric](#fabric) with web-like patterning, most often white. It is not a word for [frills](#frills), and [clothes](#clothes) [carrying](#carrying) only a lace edging take [lace_trim](#lace_trim) instead.

entries.name: pom_pom_(clothes)
entries.description: A small [fluffy](#fluffy) [ball](#ball) attached to clothing as decoration, on a [hat](#hat), a [hood](#hood) [string](#string), a [scarf](#scarf) or a shoe. The cheerleader's large shaker is [pom_pom_(cheerleading)](#pom_pom_(cheerleading)).

entries.name: clothes_writing
entries.description: Letters or words printed across a garment, in any language, from a slogan on a [t-shirt](#t-shirt) to characters [running](#running) down a sleeve. A worn name [badge](#badge) is [name_tag](#name_tag) rather than this.

entries.name: green_bow
entries.description: A decorative [bow](#bow) in green, tied on clothing, in the hair or on an accessory. Add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [green_bowtie](#green_bowtie) where the placement is more specific.

entries.name: back_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied at the wearer's rear, most often at the waist of a [dress](#dress), an [apron](#apron) or a [sash](#sash), and occasionally at the [nape](#nape) behind a [choker](#choker). It records where the bow sits; the garment it decorates is tagged separately.

entries.name: center_frills
entries.description: A vertical band of [frills](#frills) runs down the middle of a [shirt](#shirt) or [dress](#dress) front. It generally starts near the [collar](#collar) and ends somewhere around the lower chest or [navel](#navel).

entries.name: green_ribbon
entries.description: A green [ribbon](#ribbon) on clothing, in the hair or tied around something. Add [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon) where the placement is worth [recording](#recording).

entries.name: orange_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) of orange [ribbon](#ribbon) anywhere on the outfit. One worn in the hair also takes orange_hair_bow, and one at the throat [orange_bowtie](#orange_bowtie).

entries.name: breast_pocket
entries.description: A [pocket](#pocket) sewn to the chest of a [shirt](#shirt), [jacket](#jacket) or similar top, sometimes with a flap or button and sometimes [holding](#holding) a [pen](#pen) or [handkerchief](#handkerchief). Add pocket.

entries.name: name_tag
entries.description: A small [label](#label) sewn or [pinned](#pinned) onto clothing [carrying](#carrying) the wearer's name, typical of [gym](#gym) uniforms and [school](#school) swimsuits. It is distinct from other [clothes_writing](#clothes_writing) and from an id [card](#card) on a [lanyard](#lanyard); where the name is part of the composition, use character name.

entries.name: emblem
entries.description: A heraldic [device](#device) or symbolic [badge](#badge) [standing](#standing) for a nation, an order, a clan or a [family](#family), carried on clothing, banners or walls. Recurring named ones get their own qualified tags; a Japanese family mon is [family_crest](#family_crest).

entries.name: anchor_symbol
entries.description: An anchor-shaped [insignia](#insignia) worn on clothing, most often on a [sailor](#sailor) cap or [collar](#collar). A real [anchor](#anchor) is anchor, and a repeating pattern is [anchor_print](#anchor_print).

entries.name: frilled_bow
entries.description: A tied [bow](#bow) whose [ribbon](#ribbon) ends are finished with gathered ruffles rather than a [plain](#plain) cut edge. It [can](#can) sit in the hair, at the [neck](#neck) or anywhere on a garment, so add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or the [tag](#tag) for the piece it decorates.

entries.name: leg_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around some part of a leg, on one side or on both. Cloth or bandage winding is [leg_wrap](#leg_wrap) instead.

entries.name: badge
entries.description: A small [emblem](#emblem) worn on clothing to declare rank, membership or allegiance, such as a [police](#police) [shield](#shield) or a [school](#school) [crest](#crest), made of metal, plastic or [cloth](#cloth). Pin-back [buttons](#buttons) worn for [fashion](#fashion) or campaigning count too; name the specific badge where it [can](#can) be read.

entries.name: dress_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) belonging to a dress's design, sewn or tied on as decoration. Where the bow actually holds the [dress](#dress) up at the waist, [waist_bow](#waist_bow) is the right name.

entries.name: flower_knot
entries.description: Cord, [rope](#rope) or thin [ribbon](#ribbon) wound into several loops and [bound](#bound) at the middle so the loops splay out like [petals](#petals). It turns up most often as trim on Chinese-styled clothing.

entries.name: pleated
entries.description: Fabric [folded](#folded) into regular creases that hang in narrow columns. Describes any garment or accessory made this way; the specific item usually carries its own pleated [tag](#tag) as [well](#well), such as [pleated_skirt](#pleated_skirt).

entries.name: waist_bow
