entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied at the front of the waist that works like a [belt](#belt) [holding](#holding) a [dress](#dress) or [skirt](#skirt) in place. A purely decorative bow sewn onto the garment is [dress_bow](#dress_bow), and one tied at the [back](#back) is [back_bow](#back_bow).

entries.name: footwear_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied onto a shoe or boot as decoration. Mary janes and lolita footwear carry them almost as standard.

entries.name: large_bow
entries.description: An oversized [bow](#bow), worn in the hair or on an outfit and big enough to dominate it. Add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or the relevant garment bow [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: orange_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) in orange tied onto clothing, at the throat or in the hair. Where it is knotted into a [bow](#bow), [orange_bow](#orange_bow) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: button_badge
entries.description: A round pin-backed [badge](#badge) with a printed face, fastened to a [shirt](#shirt), [bag](#bag) or [jacket](#jacket). Fandom, campaigns and souvenirs all use them.

entries.name: grey_bow
entries.description: A decorative grey [bow](#bow), tied on clothing or worn in the hair. Add [hair_bow](#hair_bow) or [grey_bowtie](#grey_bowtie) where the placement is more specific.

entries.name: sleeve_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied around a sleeve, usually at the cuff or upper arm, as decoration.

entries.name: dress_flower
entries.description: One or more flowers [decorating](#decorating) a [dress](#dress) or [skirt](#skirt), [stitched](#stitched) on or [pinned](#pinned) into place.

entries.name: patch
entries.description: Either a [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) [stitched](#stitched) over a tear to mend a garment, or an embroidered [badge](#badge) or [crest](#crest) sewn or [stuck](#stuck) onto one. An [eyepatch](#eyepatch) is something else entirely, and a sticking plaster is [bandaid](#bandaid).

entries.name: insignia
entries.description: A symbol [standing](#standing) for rank or for membership of a body, worn on a uniform or displayed on equipment. The design is usually plainer than an [emblem](#emblem) or a [badge](#badge), though the outer shape [can](#can) be intricate.

entries.name: thigh_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around the thigh, often as a [bow](#bow) or [lace-up](#lace-up). Add [thigh_strap](#thigh_strap) where it also functions as one.

entries.name: multicolored_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied in two or more colours, in the hair or on clothing. A bow is not always made from a [ribbon](#ribbon), so do not swap it for the multicoloured ribbon [tag](#tag).

entries.name: grey_ribbon
entries.description: A grey [ribbon](#ribbon) on clothing, in the hair or tied around an object. Add [hair_ribbon](#hair_ribbon) or [neck_ribbon](#neck_ribbon) where the placement is worth [recording](#recording).

entries.name: chest_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) tied at the middle of the chest, [sitting](#sitting) on a [dress](#dress) front, [blouse](#blouse) or uniform. It is larger and more decorative than a [bowtie](#bowtie) worn at the [collar](#collar).

entries.name: huge_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) so large it could not realistically be worn, whether set in the hair or on a garment. A bow that is big but still plausible is [large_bow](#large_bow).

entries.name: skirt_bow
entries.description: A tied [bow](#bow) attached to a [skirt](#skirt), at the waist, hip or hem. Decorative rather than structural, and often oversized on frilly outfits.

entries.name: footwear_ribbon
entries.description: Ribbons that [wind](#wind) around the ankle or calf to keep a shoe on, most [familiar](#familiar) from [ballet](#ballet) [slippers](#slippers). In some designs it is hard to tell apart from a separate ankle [ribbon](#ribbon) or a [plain](#plain) [strap](#strap).

entries.name: expressive_clothes
entries.description: A garment or worn object that changes with the character's mood: lettering on a [shirt](#shirt) that rewrites itself, an accessory that droops when they are [sad](#sad). The clothing behaves like part of the body.

entries.name: criss-cross_straps
entries.description: Two or more straps laid over each other in an X, either as part of a garment or wound directly around an arm or a leg. It is the crossing itself that is being recorded.

entries.name: legwear_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) fixed to [socks](#socks), stockings or [thighhighs](#thighhighs), usually at the top band or beside the ankle.

entries.name: patchwork_clothes
entries.description: Clothes pieced together from many mismatched scraps of [fabric](#fabric), so the garment reads as a [quilt](#quilt) of clashing colours and textures. Common on scarecrows, ragdolls and homemade or ragged outfits.

entries.name: gathers
entries.description: Cloth pulled into small even puckers by drawing a line of [stitching](#stitching) tight. A [sewing](#sewing) detail found at waistbands, yokes and the tops of sleeves.

entries.name: kikumon
entries.description: A stylised sixteen-petal [chrysanthemum](#chrysanthemum) [crest](#crest) belonging to the Japanese imperial [house](#house), seen on passports, [warship](#warship) bows and formal [kimono](#kimono). Do not mistake it for the five-petalled cherry-blossom crest.

entries.name: embroidery
entries.description: Decorative designs worked in [thread](#thread) on [cloth](#cloth), [leather](#leather) or [paper](#paper), such as flowers [stitched](#stitched) into a [kimono](#kimono) or a [jacket](#jacket). Use it for the visible needlework, or for somebody doing the [sewing](#sewing).

entries.name: waist_ribbon
entries.description: A slim [ribbon](#ribbon) tied around the waist to cinch a [dress](#dress) or [blouse](#blouse), often finished with a [bow](#bow). Decorative rather than load-bearing, unlike a [belt](#belt).

entries.name: peach_hat_ornament
entries.description: A peach-shaped decoration fixed to a [hat](#hat), [sitting](#sitting) on the brim or on the [crown](#crown).

entries.name: checkered_bow
entries.description: A [fabric](#fabric) [bow](#bow) [patterned](#patterned) in alternating squares, tied into the hair or fixed to a garment. The pattern belongs to the bow, not to whatever it sits on.

entries.name: dress_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) sewn or tied onto a [dress](#dress) as trim, at the waist, chest or neckline. Decoration on the garment, not something worn in the hair.

entries.name: leaf_hat_ornament
entries.description: A [leaf](#leaf) [pinned](#pinned) to, tucked into or sprouting from a [hat](#hat) as decoration. Straw hats, [witch](#witch) hats and woodland costumes all carry it.

entries.name: ankle_bow
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied into a [bow](#bow) at one or both ankles, often finishing an ankle [strap](#strap). A frilly flourish on lolita, [idol](#idol) and [dancer](#dancer) outfits.

entries.name: lifebuoy_ornament
entries.description: A decorative [ring](#ring) copying a ship's life buoy, banded in red and white, worn or carried as part of a nautical design.

entries.name: back_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) fastened at the [back](#back) of a garment, its [bow](#bow) and long ends trailing down behind. Dresses, aprons and [sailor](#sailor) collars carry one most often.

entries.name: multicolored_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) [carrying](#carrying) two or more distinct colours. Keep it apart from a multicoloured [bow](#bow): a ribbon here is a loose trailing strand, not something tied into loops.

entries.name: anchor_ornament
entries.description: A decorative [anchor](#anchor) attached to an outfit or accessory, [hanging](#hanging) as a charm or fixed as a [badge](#badge). Where it sits somewhere specific, the narrower [tag](#tag) such as [anchor_hat_ornament](#anchor_hat_ornament) is better.

entries.name: shirt_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) fixed to a [shirt](#shirt), at the [collar](#collar), the front placket or the chest, sewn on as part of the garment rather than a loose [ribbon](#ribbon). Implies bow.

entries.name: footwear_flower
entries.description: A blossom fixed to a shoe, boot or sandal as ornament. It sits on the footwear rather than being held or worn elsewhere.

entries.name: thigh_bow
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) tied into a [bow](#bow) on the thigh, usually fixed to a [strap](#strap) or the top of a stocking. Purely ornamental, and a frequent piece of [idol](#idol) and magical-girl trim.

entries.name: too_many_frills
entries.description: Frills layered on [frills](#frills) until the outfit is more ruffle than [cloth](#cloth), with trim on sleeves, [collar](#collar), [gloves](#gloves) and [hat](#hat) as [well](#well) as the [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: ribbon_between_breasts
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) [running](#running) down the chest and tucked into the [cleavage](#cleavage) rather than [lying](#lying) flat on top of the garment. Often part of an outfit's lacing or a decorative [strap](#strap).

entries.name: shoulder_patch
entries.description: An [emblem](#emblem) sewn or [stuck](#stuck) onto the upper sleeve of a garment, common on uniforms and flight jackets, [carrying](#carrying) a unit [crest](#crest), [logo](#logo) or slogan. Implies [patch](#patch).

entries.name: grape_hat_ornament
entries.description: A decoration in the shape of [grapes](#grapes) fastened to a [hat](#hat), [dangling](#dangling) from the brim or tucked into the band. Any style of hat [can](#can) carry one.

entries.name: sheriff_badge
entries.description: The metal star [pinned](#pinned) to a lawman's chest, usually with five or six points. A modern [police](#police) [badge](#badge) is shield-shaped instead and does not count.

entries.name: military_rank_insignia
entries.description: Badges, stripes, stars or shoulder boards fixed to a uniform to declare the wearer's rank.

entries.name: multiple_hat_bows
entries.description: Headwear [carrying](#carrying) three or more bows, piled on the [crown](#crown) or spaced around the brim. Only bows attached to the [hat](#hat) count; ribbons tied into the hair belong with the hair [accessories](#accessories).

entries.name: large_ribbon
entries.description: An oversized [ribbon](#ribbon) or [bow](#bow), wide enough to be a focal point of the outfit. It is worn in the hair, at the waist or across the chest.

entries.name: lace-trimmed_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) whose [ribbon](#ribbon) carries [lace](#lace) along its edges. It may be tied in the hair, worn at the [neck](#neck) or sewn onto a garment.

entries.name: ornate_clothes
entries.description: Garments loaded with rich detail: [embroidery](#embroidery), brocade, layered trims and applied ornament. Usual on nobility, priesthoods and high [fantasy](#fantasy) [costume](#costume).

entries.name: anchor_hat_ornament
entries.description: A small [anchor](#anchor) [pinned](#pinned) or [stitched](#stitched) onto a [hat](#hat) as decoration. It goes with the rest of the nautical kit, from [sailor](#sailor) collars to captain's caps.

entries.name: no_emblem
entries.description: The [crest](#crest), [badge](#badge) or [insignia](#insignia) normally carried on a character's clothing or [machine](#machine) has been left out of the drawing.

entries.name: collar_tabs
entries.description: Paired patches of [cloth](#cloth) or metal fixed to the [collar](#collar) points of a uniform. In real services they mark rank, [branch](#branch) or unit; in art they are quick shorthand for [military](#military) or official [dress](#dress).

entries.name: ornate
entries.description: An object worked over with intricate decoration such as engraving, filigree, inlay or [carving](#carving), [plain](#plain) enough to read at a [glance](#glance). It suits weapons, armour, clothing and vehicles, and elaborate need not mean impractical, since the patterning may be [runes](#runes).

entries.name: sequins
entries.description: Small, reflective discs [stitched](#stitched) over [fabric](#fabric) so a garment glitters as it moves. Typical of [stage](#stage) costumes, [evening](#evening) gowns, and [idol](#idol) [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: lace-trimmed_ribbon
entries.description: A [ribbon](#ribbon) whose long edges are finished with [lace](#lace). It appears tied in the hair, sewn onto clothing or knotted at the throat.

entries.name: skirt_cutout
entries.description: One or more openings cut into the [fabric](#fabric) of a [skirt](#skirt) or the lower part of a [dress](#dress), often near the hem. Not the same as a slit, which is a single cut [running](#running) up from the edge.

entries.name: totenkopf
entries.description: A skull-and-crossbones [insignia](#insignia) showing a jawless [skull](#skull) at a three-quarter angle over crossed bones. Worn historically by German [cavalry](#cavalry) and later by armoured and SS units as a cap or [collar](#collar) [badge](#badge).

entries.name: criss-cross_strings
entries.description: Thin cords crossed in an X, worked into an outfit or laid bare across the skin as decoration. Slimmer than [criss-cross_straps](#criss-cross_straps), which covers broader bands.

entries.name: argyle_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow), in the hair or fastened to a garment, [patterned](#patterned) with argyle diamonds. Where it sits and what colour it is are left to other tags.

entries.name: unit_patch
entries.description: A sewn or fastened [cloth](#cloth) [badge](#badge) marking the specific [military](#military) or [police](#police) unit someone belongs to, [carrying](#carrying) its own [insignia](#insignia). Usually seen [stitched](#stitched) to a sleeve, chest or cap.

entries.name: self_character_print
entries.description: Clothing or a held item printed with a picture of the very character wearing or [carrying](#carrying) it. The joke lies in someone [walking](#walking) around in their own [merchandise](#merchandise).

entries.name: thigh_scrunchie
entries.description: A soft fabric-covered elastic band worn around the thigh, gathered like a hair tie. Distinct from a [bridal_garter](#bridal_garter), which is frilled and made of [lace](#lace).

entries.name: gradient_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) or [bowtie](#bowtie) whose [ribbon](#ribbon) visibly changes colour across the [fabric](#fabric), either along the loops or outward from the knot.

entries.name: belt_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) [sitting](#sitting) on a [belt](#belt), either tied from the belt itself or fixed onto it as an ornament. A soft touch on an otherwise [plain](#plain) waistline.

entries.name: panty_tag
entries.description: The little sewn-in [label](#label) of a pair of [panties](#panties) drawn as a visible detail, often [standing](#standing) up at the waistband. A close-focus flourish rather than a kind of garment.

entries.name: vertical-striped_bow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) whose [ribbon](#ribbon) carries stripes [running](#running) along its length rather than across it. Worn in hair, at the [neck](#neck) or sewn onto a garment as decoration.

entries.name: flower_underskirt
entries.description: Blossoms packed beneath a [skirt](#skirt) or the lower half of a [dress](#dress), [pushing](#pushing) the [fabric](#fabric) out the way a [petticoat](#petticoat) would. The flowers show below the hem.

entries.name: ornamental_weight
entries.description: A small [weight](#weight) hung on a garment to govern how the [fabric](#fabric) falls, left in view as a decoration in its own right. Most often on breast [curtains](#curtains) and on the long skirts of dancers.

entries.name: denim
entries.description: The sturdy cotton twill with diagonal ribbing that [jeans](#jeans) are cut from, most often blue but woven in any colour. Used together with the garment [tag](#tag), as in [denim_shorts](#denim_shorts) or [denim_jacket](#denim_jacket).

entries.name: fishnets
entries.description: The open diamond-knit [mesh](#mesh) itself, generally black, used for stockings, tights and bodystockings. Nothing to do with the [net](#net) used to catch [fish](#fish).

entries.name: shiny_clothes
entries.description: Clothing with a visible gloss, typical of [spandex](#spandex), nylon, [latex](#latex), [leather](#leather), [silk](#silk), metal or simply soaked [fabric](#fabric). Add the specific material [tag](#tag) where it [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: latex
entries.description: Clothing of shiny, smooth, skin-tight rubber, drawn with hard highlights; PVC counts as the same thing. Add the garment [tag](#tag) such as [latex_bodysuit](#latex_bodysuit) alongside it.

entries.name: two-sided_fabric
entries.description: Any garment whose inside shows a different colour or pattern from its outside, whether from a separate lining, a reversible cut, or [fabric](#fabric) printed differently on both faces. Prefer a specific [tag](#tag) such as [two-sided_cape](#two-sided_cape) when the garment is known.

entries.name: leather
entries.description: Tanned hide as a garment material, with a softer and more diffuse shine than [latex](#latex) and sometimes a faint grain. It usually sits looser on the body too, though in drawn work the two are often hard to separate; name the garment as [well](#well), such as [leather_jacket](#leather_jacket).

entries.name: cable_knit
entries.description: Knitwear with raised rope-like twists, braids or lattices worked into the [fabric](#fabric), as on an Aran [sweater](#sweater). It is also the usual texture of the [virgin_killer_sweater](#virgin_killer_sweater).

entries.name: silk
entries.description: Fine fiber strands spun by insects, spiders or monsters, seen as cocoons, webs or threads. Also covers the smooth [fabric](#fabric) woven from them.

entries.name: spandex
entries.description: A highly stretchy synthetic [fabric](#fabric) used for [sportswear](#sportswear) and other skin-tight clothing. Tag the material when a garment visibly reads as glossy and elastic.

entries.name: fine_fabric_emphasis
entries.description: Sheer legwear drawn so the weave itself reads, as fine parallel lines or a soft sheen [running](#running) over the leg. Pantyhose and [thighhighs](#thighhighs) are the usual carriers; what matters is that the texture of the material is rendered rather than simplified away.

entries.name: latex_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [thighhighs](#thighhighs) or [leggings](#leggings) made of shiny [latex](#latex), most often black and drawn with [strong](#strong) highlights. Add the type of legwear itself as [well](#well).

entries.name: satin
entries.description: Fabric with a smooth, glossy weave that catches the light, typical of [lingerie](#lingerie) and [bed](#bed) sheets. Apply when a textile has a clearly lustrous surface rather than a matte one.

entries.name: shiny_swimsuit
entries.description: A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) in high-gloss [fabric](#fabric) that bounces bright highlights off the body, common on [competition](#competition) suits and latex-look designs.

entries.name: holographic_clothing
entries.description: Garments cut from [iridescent](#iridescent) material that shifts colour as the light moves across it. The [rainbow](#rainbow) sheen is the point, whatever the shape of the garment.

entries.name: wool
entries.description: Wool as a material, the soft curled fibre sheared from [sheep](#sheep) and similar animals and spun into [yarn](#yarn) or knitted [cloth](#cloth). Balls of yarn and [heavy](#heavy) knitwear both bring the [tag](#tag) up.

entries.name: liquid_clothes
entries.description: Clothing formed out of a fluid such as [water](#water) or [ink](#ink), [holding](#holding) a garment's shape while it visibly flows and drips.

entries.name: lace_legwear
entries.description: Socks, stockings or tights knitted throughout from [lace](#lace), skin visible through the pattern. Legwear that only carries a lace band at the top does not qualify.

entries.name: fur_(clothing)
entries.description: Garments made from [animal](#animal) [pelt](#pelt) — coats, stoles, hats and wraps. It describes the material being worn, never fur growing on a character's own body.

entries.name: flannel
entries.description: Soft brushed [cloth](#cloth), usually woven in a check and most often seen as a loose button-up [shirt](#shirt). Tag it where the napped, plaid look of the material identifies the garment.

entries.name: fishnet_fabric
entries.description: The open diamond-grid [mesh](#mesh) named as a material, wherever a garment happens to use it. It names the [cloth](#cloth) rather than any one piece of clothing.

entries.name: quilted_clothes
entries.description: Garments made from layered [fabric](#fabric) [stitched](#stitched) into a [grid](#grid) or diamond pattern with padding [sandwiched](#sandwiched) inside, [giving](#giving) the surface a raised, puffy texture. Used for warmth, for protective padding beneath [armor](#armor), or purely for its look.

entries.name: leaf_clothing
entries.description: Garments made from [foliage](#foliage) instead of [cloth](#cloth), with leaves layered, [stitched](#stitched) or simply draped over the body. Forest spirits, [plant](#plant) creatures and characters living wild wear it.

entries.name: reflective_clothes
entries.description: Garments made from a material that bounces light [back](#back) sharply: high-visibility strips, mirrored panels, or a glossy coated [fabric](#fabric). The bright catch of light is the point.

entries.name: mesh
entries.description: An interlaced diamond-shaped weave, as seen in netting, screens and open [summer](#summer) fabrics. Treated as a pattern of [fabric](#fabric) rather than a specific garment.

entries.name: red_leather
entries.description: Garments or [accessories](#accessories) made of [leather](#leather) dyed red, recognisable by the hard specular highlights along the folds. Used for jackets, [boots](#boots), harnesses and [bondage](#bondage) gear.

entries.name: clothes_lift
entries.description: Clothing hitched upward to reveal the [breasts](#breasts) or the [crotch](#crotch), such as a [shirt](#shirt) or [skirt](#skirt) raised by hand. Pulled down instead is [clothes_pull](#clothes_pull); add the specific [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift) or [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift).

entries.name: shirt_lift
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt), [tank](#tank) top or similar garment raised to reveal the [bra](#bra), [breasts](#breasts), chest or [stomach](#stomach) beneath. Tag the exposed [underwear](#underwear) or swimwear separately, and use [shirt_pull](#shirt_pull) instead for a [collar](#collar) pulled down. Implies [clothes_lift](#clothes_lift).

entries.name: skirt_lift
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) raised high enough to expose the [crotch](#crotch), whether by the wearer, another person or something passive like [wind](#wind). A modest hold is [skirt_hold](#skirt_hold); the same on a [dress](#dress) is [dress_lift](#dress_lift).

entries.name: clothes_pull
entries.description: Clothing dragged downward to reveal the [breasts](#breasts) or the [crotch](#crotch). Lifted upward is [clothes_lift](#clothes_lift), tugged down to [cover](#cover) oneself is [clothes_tug](#clothes_tug), and merely held is [clothes_grab](#clothes_grab).

entries.name: lifting_own_clothes
entries.description: A character raises their own garment, teasingly or to show something underneath. Combine it with the specific lift [tag](#tag) such as [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift), [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift) or [bra_lift](#bra_lift).

entries.name: panty_pull
entries.description: Panties lowered from where they normally sit but not taken off, [resting](#resting) on the hips, [thighs](#thighs) or [knees](#knees). Nobody has to be actively [pulling](#pulling) them; they only have to be lower than they belong.

entries.name: dress_lift
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) raised to show the [underwear](#underwear) or bare skin below, by the wearer, by somebody else, or by an object [catching](#catching) the [cloth](#cloth). Merely [holding](#holding) a dress without revealing anything is [skirt_hold](#skirt_hold).

entries.name: pulling_own_clothes
entries.description: A character tugs their own garment downward, such as [panties](#panties), a [skirt](#skirt), or a [shirt](#shirt). Always paired with the specific clothes-pull [tag](#tag) rather than [standing](#standing) alone; lifting or moving a garment aside uses a different pair of tags.

entries.name: wind_lift
entries.description: A gust of [wind](#wind) lifts a piece of clothing, most often a [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress), or another light [article](#article) such as a [parasol](#parasol). Combine it with [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift), [dress_lift](#dress_lift), or [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift) as fits; the effect is the classic Marilyn Monroe subway-grate moment.

entries.name: pants_pull
entries.description: Trousers pulled down from where they normally sit, whether just off the hips or as far as the [thighs](#thighs) or [knees](#knees). Frequently paired with [panty_pull](#panty_pull) or with exposed [underwear](#underwear).

entries.name: tied_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) knotted at the front or hem to expose the [midriff](#midriff), as with a button-up's tails tied under the bust. Knotted sleeves belong to [sleeve_tied_shut](#sleeve_tied_shut) or [clothes_around_waist](#clothes_around_waist) instead.

entries.name: pantyhose_pull
entries.description: Pantyhose pulled down from the waist, usually bunched around mid-thigh, without being taken off entirely. Often seen alongside [panty_pull](#panty_pull) while [undressing](#undressing) or during [sex](#sex).

entries.name: skirt_pull
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) tugged down from the waist so it sits lower than it should, exposing hip or [underwear](#underwear). Pulling it down to hide the [legs](#legs) is [skirt_tug](#skirt_tug) instead.

entries.name: shirt_pull
entries.description: A shirt's [collar](#collar) pulled downward, typically to show the [breasts](#breasts). Lifting the hem instead is [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift), tugging the hem down is [shirt_tug](#shirt_tug), and [pulling](#pulling) the collar outward for air or nerves is [collar_tug](#collar_tug). Implies [clothes_pull](#clothes_pull).

entries.name: shorts_pull
entries.description: Shorts tugged down from the waist, whether by the wearer or by someone else. Implies [clothes_pull](#clothes_pull) and [shorts](#shorts).

entries.name: sweater_lift
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) pulled upward to bare the [breasts](#breasts) or chest beneath it. The garment stays worn, only hiked out of its normal position.

entries.name: strap_pull
entries.description: Tugging or [pulling](#pulling) at the [strap](#strap) of a [swimsuit](#swimsuit), [bra](#bra), [panties](#panties) or similar garment, by oneself or by someone else.

entries.name: dress_pull
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) dragged down to bare skin, most often the [bra](#bra) or the [breasts](#breasts). Pulling the hem down to [cover](#cover) up instead is [dress_tug](#dress_tug).

entries.name: one-piece_swimsuit_pull
entries.description: The shoulder straps of a one-piece are dragged down so that some or all of the chest is bared. Tugging the [crotch](#crotch) aside is [swimsuit_aside](#swimsuit_aside), a mere adjustment is [adjusting_swimsuit](#adjusting_swimsuit), and the two-piece case is [bikini_pull](#bikini_pull).

entries.name: mask_pull
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) being tugged out of place, most often a mouth mask dragged down to bare the mouth. The act of [pulling](#pulling) is the point; one simply [resting](#resting) elsewhere is [mask_around_neck](#mask_around_neck) or [mask_on_head](#mask_on_head).

entries.name: lifting_another's_clothes
entries.description: One character raises somebody else's garment. Always pair it with the garment's own lift [tag](#tag) such as [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift) or [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift), and add [assisted_exposure](#assisted_exposure) when [breasts](#breasts) or genitals come into view; doing it to oneself is [lifting_own_clothes](#lifting_own_clothes).

entries.name: shirt_tug
entries.description: Pulling the hem of one's own [shirt](#shirt) downward to adjust the fit or [cover](#cover) the [crotch](#crotch) or [underwear](#underwear). Not the same as [shirt_pull](#shirt_pull), which is a [collar](#collar) pulled down, or [sleeve_grab](#sleeve_grab), which tugs someone else's sleeve.

entries.name: skirt_tug
entries.description: Pulling one's own [skirt](#skirt) hem downward to [cover](#cover) the [crotch](#crotch) or [thighs](#thighs), the defensive opposite of a [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift). Pulling it down to expose is [skirt_pull](#skirt_pull) instead.

entries.name: pulling_another's_clothes
entries.description: Someone tugs another person's garment downward, always paired with the specific [tag](#tag) for what is being pulled, such as [panty_pull](#panty_pull) or [skirt_pull](#skirt_pull). Lifting or moving clothing to the side is a different set of tags, and add [assisted_exposure](#assisted_exposure) where it bares something intimate.

entries.name: leotard_pull
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) is tugged or dragged down, by the wearer or by somebody else, often baring the chest or hips. Moving only the [crotch](#crotch) panel [sideways](#sideways) is [leotard_aside](#leotard_aside).

entries.name: clothes_down
entries.description: A top is pulled far down or nearly off, baring a lot of skin while still being worn. Down only as far as the [breasts](#breasts) is [shirt_pull](#shirt_pull), simply opened is [open_clothes](#open_clothes), exposed breasts take [breasts_out](#breasts_out), and a missing top is [topless](#topless).

entries.name: dress_tug
entries.description: The hem of a [dress](#dress) pulled downward, generally to keep the [crotch](#crotch) or [thighs](#thighs) covered. The opposite intent to [dress_pull](#dress_pull), which bares skin.

entries.name: thighhighs_pull
entries.description: A character tugs on one or both [thighhighs](#thighhighs), either putting them on or hitching them [back](#back) up. Add [adjusting_legwear](#adjusting_legwear) and thighhighs alongside it.

entries.name: hoodie_lift
entries.description: The hem of a [hoodie](#hoodie) is pulled upward, baring the [stomach](#stomach) or chest. The garment stays on and is only raised, by the wearer or by somebody else.

entries.name: kimono_pull
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) is being tugged down at the [collar](#collar) or off a shoulder, which may or may not bare the chest. It is the kimono counterpart of [shirt_pull](#shirt_pull).

entries.name: tied_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) knotted at its bottom hem to bare the [midriff](#midriff), either modified or [cropped](#cropped) by design. Sleeves knotted together belong to sleeves_tied_together or [clothes_around_waist](#clothes_around_waist) instead.

entries.name: skirt_around_belly
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) that has ridden up or been pushed up to sit bunched around the waist and [stomach](#stomach). The waistband ends up [well](#well) above where it should rest.

entries.name: strap_lift
entries.description: A character lifts the shoulder [strap](#strap) of a top, [bra](#bra) or [swimsuit](#swimsuit) away from the body.

entries.name: buruma_pull
entries.description: Gym [shorts](#shorts) pulled down from the waist, usually to around mid-thigh, by the wearer or by somebody else. Merely tugging them straight does not count.

entries.name: male_underwear_pull
entries.description: Men's [underwear](#underwear) pulled down from the waist without being taken off, by the wearer or by another person. Pushed aside rather than down is [male_underwear_aside](#male_underwear_aside).

entries.name: jacket_pull
entries.description: The [collar](#collar) of a [jacket](#jacket) is dragged down, usually to bare the chest. Lifting the hem is [jacket_lift](#jacket_lift), [pulling](#pulling) it down over the [crotch](#crotch) is [jacket_tug](#jacket_tug), and tugging a collar merely for air is [collar_tug](#collar_tug).

entries.name: kimono_lift
entries.description: The lower hem of a [kimono](#kimono) is raised, generally to show [underwear](#underwear) or bare skin beneath. It is the kimono's version of [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift).

entries.name: apron_lift
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) is raised, generally far enough to show the hips, [groin](#groin) or genitals beneath. Usually seen where the apron is the only thing being worn.

entries.name: sports_bra_lift
entries.description: A sports [bra](#bra) pushed or pulled upward to expose what it normally covers. Pair with [breasts](#breasts) or [nipples](#nipples) tags as appropriate.

entries.name: skirt_flip
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) blown or flipped up unexpectedly, by [wind](#wind) or a prankster, rather than lifted on purpose. A deliberate raise is [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift).

entries.name: camisole_lift
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) pulled up the body, baring the [stomach](#stomach) and often the [bra](#bra) or [breasts](#breasts) beneath. The garment stays on; it is only raised.

entries.name: pelvic_curtain_lift
entries.description: The [hanging](#hanging) front or [back](#back) panel of a garment raised, by the wearer or by somebody else, so that what lies beneath is shown.

entries.name: panty_lift
entries.description: Panties stretched away from the body or hauled up tight into the [crotch](#crotch), generally by tugging the waistband, which tends to produce a [cameltoe](#cameltoe) or expose more. The wearer or someone else may be doing it.

entries.name: jacket_lift
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) is pulled upward to bare what lies under it, a [shirt](#shirt), [underwear](#underwear) or skin. The garment stays on the body, which is what separates this from [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: shorts_aside
entries.description: Shorts pulled [sideways](#sideways) out of the way at the [crotch](#crotch) so what is underneath is exposed, while the garment stays on the hips. Implies [clothing_aside](#clothing_aside) and [shorts](#shorts).

entries.name: sweater_pull
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) dragged down and off the chest so the [breasts](#breasts) show, rather than lifted upward. The garment remains on the body, simply hauled out of place.

entries.name: mask_lift
entries.description: A worn [mask](#mask) pushed up out of place, usually onto the [forehead](#forehead), so the face beneath shows. The mask stays with the character rather than being taken away.

entries.name: sailor_collar_lift
entries.description: The broad flat [collar](#collar) of a [sailor](#sailor) top raised away from the shoulders or [back](#back). It may be held up by the wearer, tugged by somebody else, or [caught](#caught) by the [wind](#wind).

entries.name: lifted_by_tail
entries.description: A [tail](#tail) hooks under a [skirt](#skirt), [dress](#dress) or other garment and raises it, uncovering what is below. Not the same as a tail simply held upright.

entries.name: bike_shorts_pull
entries.description: Bike [shorts](#shorts) tugged down or stretched away from the body, often by a thumb hooked into the waistband. The [pulling](#pulling) is what is recorded; whether anything is uncovered depends on how far they go.

entries.name: vest_lift
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) is pulled or held upward, baring what lies beneath it. Part of the [family](#family) of garment-lifting tags alongside [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift) and [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift).

entries.name: self_wedgie
entries.description: The character hauls their own [panties](#panties) or [briefs](#briefs) upward until the [fabric](#fabric) pulls tight between the buttocks, leaving a thong-like line. It [can](#can) be tugged to the front instead.

entries.name: suspenders_pull
entries.description: A [strap](#strap) is grabbed and drawn away from its usual seat, whether stretched outward or tugged down. Someone else's hand may be doing the [pulling](#pulling).

entries.name: skirt_caught_on_object
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) or [dress](#dress) snagged on something so that it is held up and the [underwear](#underwear) shows. The wearer is usually [flustered](#flustered) and trying to free it.

entries.name: bikini_tug
entries.description: Fingers hooked under a [bikini](#bikini) [strap](#strap) or waistband, [pulling](#pulling) it away from the skin without taking it off. A [teasing](#teasing) [gesture](#gesture) that need not uncover anything.

entries.name: bloomers_pull
entries.description: Bloomers tugged by the wearer or by somebody else, stretched away from the body or drawn downward. Whether anything is exposed is a separate question.

entries.name: pelvic_curtain_aside
entries.description: The [hanging](#hanging) [crotch](#crotch) panel of a garment pushed to one side, uncovering what it normally hides.

entries.name: shirt_slip
entries.description: The [shirt](#shirt) has shifted out of place on its own, [sliding](#sliding) off a shoulder or [gaping](#gaping) open so skin or [underwear](#underwear) underneath comes into view without anyone tugging at it.

entries.name: male_swimwear_pull
entries.description: Men's trunks or [briefs](#briefs) tugged down or held open, by the wearer or by somebody else, so what is under them shows. The [gesture](#gesture) is the point rather than the garment.

entries.name: top_pull
entries.description: The upper garment is grabbed and dragged out of place, hauled up, down or aside, without being taken off.

entries.name: pajamas_pull
entries.description: Pajamas tugged down, up or aside while still worn, the [fabric](#fabric) held out of the way. Common in just-woken and half-dressed scenes.

entries.name: swimsuit_lift
entries.description: The lower part of a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) pulled upward to show or emphasize what lies beneath it. The garment stays on, only raised out of position.

entries.name: blindfold_lift
entries.description: A worn [blindfold](#blindfold) pushed or pulled upward so the eye beneath comes into view, by the wearer or by somebody else. What shows may be an ordinary eye or an empty socket.

entries.name: visor_lift
entries.description: The wearer pushes a helmet's visor up out of the way, uncovering the face. Knights, pilots and racers do it when they stop to speak or catch their [breath](#breath).

entries.name: cape_lift
entries.description: A [cape](#cape) swept up and spread out behind or to one side of the wearer. Often [caught](#caught) mid-motion for a dramatic [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: jacket_tug
entries.description: The wearer pulls their own [jacket](#jacket) downward, [stretching](#stretching) the hem over the hips or [crotch](#crotch). It is a self-conscious [gesture](#gesture), and distinct from tugging at somebody else's [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: shirt_behind_neck
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) pulled up over the chest and bunched at the throat, baring the [torso](#torso) while the garment stays on the body. Implies [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift).

entries.name: eyepatch_lift
entries.description: A worn [eyepatch](#eyepatch) is tipped or pulled up to show what sits underneath: an eye, a [scar](#scar), or nothing at all. The [patch](#patch) stays on the character throughout.

entries.name: panty_tug
entries.description: A finger or hand hooked into the waistband of [panties](#panties), [pulling](#pulling) them out or partway down without taking them off. Once they are actually lowered it becomes [panty_pull](#panty_pull).

entries.name: pants_lift
entries.description: A trouser leg or waistband pulled up to show what is underneath: an ankle, a sock, legwear or bare skin. The [skirt](#skirt) equivalent is [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift).

entries.name: shirt_down
entries.description: An older way of tagging a [shirt](#shirt) [slipping](#slipping) off the shoulders. Current practice tags the shirt together with off-shoulder or clothes-down instead, so this survives mostly on older posts.

entries.name: sarong_lift
entries.description: The wrap tied over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) held up by its wearer, baring the hip and leg beneath it.

entries.name: bodysuit_pull
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) peeled partway off, the freed portion still [hanging](#hanging) from what remains worn. It also covers the [suit](#suit) simply being tugged, by the wearer or by somebody else.

entries.name: breast_curtain_lift
entries.description: The [hanging](#hanging) panel of [cloth](#cloth) that covers the [breasts](#breasts) is being raised, uncovering what it hung over. It belongs to outfits where a loose flap does the work a top otherwise would.

entries.name: hakama_lift
entries.description: The wide [pleated](#pleated) [skirt](#skirt) of a [hakama](#hakama) raised to bare what is underneath, whether by the wearer, by somebody else, or by the [wind](#wind). Follows the same pattern as [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift).

entries.name: cardigan_lift
entries.description: A [cardigan](#cardigan) raised up the body, uncovering the [stomach](#stomach) or whatever is worn beneath it. The garment is not taken off, only pulled upward.

entries.name: skirt_around_ankles
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) pulled right down past the [knees](#knees) so it hangs around the lower shins or pools on the [floor](#floor) at the [feet](#feet). A further [stage](#stage) than a skirt merely pushed down to the [thighs](#thighs).

entries.name: coat_lift
entries.description: The hem of a [coat](#coat) is raised, by the wearer's own hands or by a gust of [wind](#wind). What it uncovers depends on what is worn beneath.

entries.name: camisole_pull
entries.description: A [camisole](#camisole) dragged down off the chest so the [breasts](#breasts) are uncovered. Where the garment is raised upward instead, [camisole_lift](#camisole_lift) is the one to use.

entries.name: sweater_vest_lift
entries.description: A [sleeveless](#sleeveless) knit [vest](#vest) raised to show the [stomach](#stomach) or whatever is worn underneath it. The lifting hand or the raised hem should be visible.

entries.name: dress_flip
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) blown or knocked upward and turned inside out without the wearer meaning it to happen. Somebody deliberately raising the hem is a [dress_lift](#dress_lift).

entries.name: apron_tug
entries.description: Fingers pull lightly at an [apron](#apron), shifting the [cloth](#cloth) a little without stripping anything. A small [nervous](#nervous) or [teasing](#teasing) [gesture](#gesture) rather than an act of [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: tube_top_lift
entries.description: A [strapless](#strapless) [tube](#tube) top pulled upward so the chest beneath comes into view. The garment stays on the body, bunched above the [breasts](#breasts) rather than removed entirely.

entries.name: leggings_pull
entries.description: Leggings are dragged down or hauled away from the waist, by the wearer or by another hand.

entries.name: apron_pull
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) is drawn aside or down, uncovering the chest or whatever it had been [hiding](#hiding). Raising it instead is [clothes_lift](#clothes_lift), and merely [holding](#holding) on to the [cloth](#cloth) is [clothes_grab](#clothes_grab).

entries.name: shirt_aside
entries.description: The [shirt](#shirt) is dragged [sideways](#sideways) out of the way so that what it covered is exposed, rather than being lifted, opened or removed entirely.

entries.name: tied_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) knotted up out of the way, the [skirt](#skirt) gathered at the hip or the front so the hem rides higher. Done to keep it clean and dry, or simply to free the [legs](#legs).

entries.name: leotard_lift
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) is hauled up into the [crotch](#crotch) or stretched [sideways](#sideways) off the body, usually by the edges of the leg openings. The result exposes far more of the hips and [groin](#groin) than the cut intends.

entries.name: sports_bra_pull
entries.description: A sports [bra](#bra) tugged out of place, most often dragged down off the chest though sometimes shoved up, while the garment stays on the body.

entries.name: bikini_bottom_lift
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) bottom hauled upward or stretched [sideways](#sideways) by the waistband so the [fabric](#fabric) bites into the [crotch](#crotch). Cameltoe usually follows, and sometimes outright exposure.

entries.name: robe_lift
entries.description: A [robe](#robe) raised by its wearer or by someone else, exposing what lies underneath. Follows the same pattern as [skirt_lift](#skirt_lift) and [dress_lift](#dress_lift).

entries.name: shorts_lift
entries.description: Shorts raised or tugged upward by the wearer, [riding](#riding) higher on the thigh or hip than they were originally cut to sit.

entries.name: hakama_pull
entries.description: A [hakama](#hakama) tugged down or dragged aside by a hand. Which companion [tag](#tag) fits depends on whether the garment is the skirted, trousered or short kind.

entries.name: crop_top_lift
entries.description: A crop top pulled or held upward, baring more of the [midriff](#midriff) or the chest beneath. A full-length [shirt](#shirt) raised the same way is [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift).

entries.name: fundoshi_pull
entries.description: A [fundoshi](#fundoshi) hauled down from the waist without being taken off, or [caught](#caught) mid-tug by the wearer or somebody else. Shifting it to the side rather than down is [fundoshi_aside](#fundoshi_aside).

entries.name: babydoll_lift
entries.description: The flared hem of a [babydoll](#babydoll) is drawn upward, uncovering the hips and [stomach](#stomach) beneath it. The garment stays on the shoulders, and it is generally the wearer raising it herself.

entries.name: bandeau_lift
entries.description: A [bandeau](#bandeau) top pulled upward so the band rides above what it covered while staying on the body. The garment is shifted rather than taken off.

entries.name: tied_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) knotted at the side or in front so the hem lifts and the [fabric](#fabric) bunches around the knot.

entries.name: leotard_tug
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) is pulled out of place, hauled down or dragged aside by the wearer or another hand.

entries.name: kneehighs_pull
entries.description: A hand tugs knee-high [socks](#socks) up the calf or draws them down. The [pulling](#pulling) [gesture](#gesture) is what the [tag](#tag) records, not simply wearing them.

entries.name: open_clothes
entries.description: Any garment left [unfastened](#unfastened) and [hanging](#hanging) open: a [shirt](#shirt), a [jacket](#jacket), a [coat](#coat), a [robe](#robe), a [gown](#gown). The specific open_* tags name the garment and all lead [back](#back) here.

entries.name: open_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) of any style, [blazer](#blazer) and track jacket included, left [unzipped](#unzipped) or [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned). Add [naked_jacket](#naked_jacket) when the wearer has nothing on underneath.

entries.name: open_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [blouse](#blouse) [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) in part or completely and left [hanging](#hanging) open. Add [naked_shirt](#naked_shirt) when nothing is worn beneath it.

entries.name: open_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) worn [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) so the [clothes](#clothes) or skin beneath show down the front. A lab coat hangs open as a matter of course and is not tagged this way unless nothing is worn under it, where [naked_coat](#naked_coat) fits as [well](#well).

entries.name: strap_slip
entries.description: One or both straps of a [tank](#tank) top, [bra](#bra), [camisole](#camisole) or [bikini](#bikini) have slid down off the shoulder. Do not add [off_shoulder](#off_shoulder) unless a second garment such as a [jacket](#jacket) is also worn off the shoulder.

entries.name: open_fly
entries.description: The [crotch](#crotch) of a pair of trousers or [shorts](#shorts) is [unzipped](#unzipped) or [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned). Often drawn with a loosened [belt](#belt), and [open_pants](#open_pants) or [open_shorts](#open_shorts) frequently apply beside it.

entries.name: unbuttoned
entries.description: A garment's [buttons](#buttons) are undone, leaving it [hanging](#hanging) open or loose. Combine with the specific garment [tag](#tag), such as [unbuttoned_shirt](#unbuttoned_shirt), and add [open_clothes](#open_clothes) when it gapes fully.

entries.name: open_cardigan
entries.description: A [cardigan](#cardigan) worn [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) or [unzipped](#unzipped) so it hangs open down the front. Add [naked_cardigan](#naked_cardigan) when there is nothing underneath it.

entries.name: unzipped
entries.description: A [zipper](#zipper) on a garment or [bag](#bag) has been left open. If the zip is still in the process of being pulled, [unzipping](#unzipping) is the [tag](#tag) to use instead.

entries.name: partially_unbuttoned
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) or [jacket](#jacket) with only some of its [buttons](#buttons) undone and the rest still fastened, usually opened at the top to show [cleavage](#cleavage) or [pectoral_cleavage](#pectoral_cleavage). Add [button_gap](#button_gap) when an open button sits between two closed ones. Every button undone is [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) or [open_shirt](#open_shirt).

entries.name: open_kimono
entries.description: The front of a [kimono](#kimono) or [yukata](#yukata) is parted, showing whatever lies beneath. Where there is nothing underneath, [naked_kimono](#naked_kimono) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: open_vest
entries.description: A [vest](#vest) whose [buttons](#buttons) or straps are undone, showing the [shirt](#shirt) or the skin behind it.

entries.name: jacket_partially_removed
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) has slid down to hang at the elbows with the arms still through the sleeves, baring the shoulders. A jacket cut low and wide by design is [off-shoulder_jacket](#off-shoulder_jacket) and never this.

entries.name: open_hoodie
entries.description: A [hoodie](#hoodie) worn with the zip or [buttons](#buttons) undone, [hanging](#hanging) loose at the front. Where nothing is worn beneath it, [naked_hoodie](#naked_hoodie) applies too.

entries.name: partially_unzipped
entries.description: A zip closed along only part of its run, so the garment gapes above or below the slider, as on a [jacket](#jacket) or [bodysuit](#bodysuit) opened halfway down. Once the zip is fully open, [unzipped](#unzipped) or [open_clothes](#open_clothes) applies instead.

entries.name: open_collar
entries.description: The top of a collared [shirt](#shirt) is left [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned), or a wing [collar](#collar) hangs [unfastened](#unfastened), so the throat is bare. Milder than [open_shirt](#open_shirt), where the whole front of the garment falls open.

entries.name: button_gap
entries.description: A button-up [shirt](#shirt) gapes open between two of its [buttons](#buttons) over the chest, showing a strip of skin or [cleavage](#cleavage). The shirt stays fastened above and below, and the [breasts](#breasts) are not fully out.

entries.name: open_bikini
entries.description: A [bikini](#bikini) top or bottom has come undone at its ties, so the piece hangs slack instead of [sitting](#sitting) in place. The cause may be a slipped knot, [sunbathing](#sunbathing) without [tan](#tan) lines, or the start of [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: unbuttoned_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) worn with some or all of its [buttons](#buttons) undone. Add [open_shirt](#open_shirt) on top of this if it hangs fully open.

entries.name: open_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) of any cut hangs open after being [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned), [unzipped](#unzipped) or untied. What shows beneath may be [underwear](#underwear), another garment or bare skin.

entries.name: open_shorts
entries.description: Shorts with the [fly](#fly) [unzipped](#unzipped) or [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned), the waistband [gaping](#gaping) at the front. The full-length equivalent is [open_pants](#open_pants).

entries.name: hadanugi_dousa
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) with one side of its upper half slipped off and [hanging](#hanging) at the waist, baring that shoulder and part of the chest, as archers do in [kyuudou](#kyuudou). Seen on characters such as Shouhou, Hanzo and Yoimiya.

entries.name: open_robe
entries.description: A [robe](#robe) left [unfastened](#unfastened) so the body inside is visible. Where nothing is worn under it, [naked_robe](#naked_robe) applies too.

entries.name: open_skirt
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) [unfastened](#unfastened) at its side zip or [buttons](#buttons), frequently while [undressing](#undressing) or as it slips down the hips.

entries.name: open_pants
entries.description: Trousers with the [fly](#fly) undone, usually with the waistband loosened as [well](#well). Do not confuse them with [chaps](#chaps), which have [no](#no) [crotch](#crotch) to begin with.

entries.name: open_bra
entries.description: A [bra](#bra) unhooked or untied at the [clasp](#clasp), front or [back](#back), [hanging](#hanging) slack on the body. Frequently drawn with the [breasts](#breasts) already [slipping](#slipping) free.

entries.name: thigh_cutout
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) cut into [pants](#pants) or legwear at the thigh, leaving bare skin visible. A kind of [clothing_cutout](#clothing_cutout), seen on characters such as Skadi from Arknights.

entries.name: undone_bra
entries.description: The [clasp](#clasp) of a [bra](#bra) has been opened, leaving the cups loose against the chest while the garment still hangs on the body. Often part of an [undressing](#undressing) scene, before the bra comes off entirely.

entries.name: undone_necktie
entries.description: A [necktie](#necktie) that has been loosened or untied yet still hangs around the [neck](#neck), its ends [dangling](#dangling) down the chest. One taken off entirely instead is [unworn_necktie](#unworn_necktie).

entries.name: open_belt
entries.description: A [belt](#belt) worn unbuckled, its end [hanging](#hanging) loose down the front. It turns up beside [undressing](#undressing), open trousers and clothing being [shed](#shed), and says nothing about the belt's own design.

entries.name: untying
entries.description: A character [caught](#caught) in the act of undoing a [bow](#bow), [ribbon](#ribbon) or [string](#string) fastening, whether a uniform tie, a hair ribbon, or side-tie swimwear or [panties](#panties). Add the matching untied [tag](#tag) too if the knot ends up fully loose within the same picture.

entries.name: unzipping
entries.description: A character [pulling](#pulling) a [zipper](#zipper) down to open a garment. Once it sits fully open with [no](#no) further motion, [unzipped](#unzipped) is the correct [tag](#tag), and pulling it [back](#back) up is [zipping](#zipping).

entries.name: open_bodysuit
entries.description: A [bodysuit](#bodysuit) [unzipped](#unzipped) or peeled open down the front, showing skin or [underwear](#underwear) beneath. A [plugsuit](#plugsuit) stripped halfway counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: opened_by_self
entries.description: The character pulls their own clothing open with their hands rather than letting it simply hang. Always used beside the [tag](#tag) for the garment concerned, such as [open_shirt](#open_shirt) or [open_coat](#open_coat).

entries.name: coat_partially_removed
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) shrugged only halfway off, [caught](#caught) at the elbows or [slipping](#slipping) from one shoulder rather than worn properly or taken off.

entries.name: male_underwear_peek
entries.description: A glimpse of a man's [underwear](#underwear) past his outer [clothes](#clothes), through an open [fly](#fly), over a sagging waistband, or through [fabric](#fabric) gone [wet](#wet) and see-through. Only the partial view counts.

entries.name: unfastened
entries.description: A garment's [clasp](#clasp) or [hook](#hook) has come loose so it hangs slack rather than fitting snugly, most often a [bra](#bra) [caught](#caught) mid-undress. Clothing opened at [buttons](#buttons), a [zipper](#zipper) or a tied knot has its own separate tags instead.

entries.name: undone_neck_ribbon
entries.description: A [neck](#neck) [ribbon](#ribbon) has been unknotted and now hangs in two loose ends around the [collar](#collar). If it is still tied but [sitting](#sitting) slackly against the chest, [loose_neck_ribbon](#loose_neck_ribbon) fits better.

entries.name: suspenders_slip
entries.description: One [strap](#strap) has slid down off the shoulder to rest on the upper arm, the [braces](#braces) equivalent of a slipped [bra](#bra) or [dress](#dress) strap. Implies [suspenders](#suspenders).

entries.name: double_strap_slip
entries.description: Both shoulder straps of a garment have slid down the arms, leaving the top [hanging](#hanging) loose across the chest. Where only one side has fallen, [strap_slip](#strap_slip) applies.

entries.name: cardigan_partially_removed
entries.description: A [cardigan](#cardigan) slipped half off: one arm free of its sleeve, or the whole thing pushed down to the elbows. It is still on the body.

entries.name: undone_neckerchief
entries.description: The knot of a [neckerchief](#neckerchief) has been released and the [cloth](#cloth) hangs open around the [neck](#neck) or shoulders. It stays on the wearer, unlike [unworn_neckerchief](#unworn_neckerchief) where the cloth is off the body entirely.

entries.name: open_jumpsuit
entries.description: A [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit) or coverall [unfastened](#unfastened) down the chest, the upper half loose while the [legs](#legs) stay on. The empty sleeves are often knotted around the waist.

entries.name: undone_sarashi
entries.description: The long [cloth](#cloth) wrapped around the chest or [torso](#torso) has come untied or slackened, so the [wrapping](#wrapping) trails loose instead of binding. Frequently shown mid-unwinding.

entries.name: open_pajamas
entries.description: A pajama top hangs [unbuttoned](#unbuttoned) or loose, baring the chest or the [shirt](#shirt) underneath. Suits both [sleepy](#sleepy) [morning](#morning) scenes and getting ready for [bed](#bed).

entries.name: partially_open_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) with the zip run partway down or only some [buttons](#buttons) done up, so it gapes across the chest while still being worn.

entries.name: open_cloak
entries.description: A [cloak](#cloak) worn [unfastened](#unfastened) at the throat, [falling](#falling) away to either side so the clothing beneath is on show. Used for dramatic reveals as much as for a cloak simply thrown on without clasping it.

entries.name: undone_bowtie
entries.description: A [bowtie](#bowtie) has been pulled apart [back](#back) into a flat length of [ribbon](#ribbon) while remaining draped around the [neck](#neck). One still knotted but [sitting](#sitting) slack is [loose_bowtie](#loose_bowtie), and a [hanging](#hanging) ribbon with [no](#no) [sign](#sign) it was ever a [bow](#bow) is [undone_neck_ribbon](#undone_neck_ribbon).

entries.name: undone_bikini
entries.description: The strings of a [bikini](#bikini) have been pulled loose at the front of the top or the hip of the bottom, yet the [swimsuit](#swimsuit) still rests on the wearer. Nothing has actually been removed; the piece merely [no](#no) longer holds itself in place.

entries.name: unbuttoned_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) left [unfastened](#unfastened) so the front hangs loose over whatever is worn beneath. A [casual](#casual) look, and a way of showing off the layer underneath.

entries.name: unbuttoned_sleeves
entries.description: Sleeve [cuffs](#cuffs) left undone, so the [fabric](#fabric) falls open around the wrist. Often paired with rolled-up or pushed-back sleeves.

entries.name: open_happi
entries.description: A [happi](#happi), the short [festival](#festival) [coat](#coat), hangs loose at the front instead of being closed with a [sash](#sash). Whatever is underneath, clothing or bare skin, shows down the middle.

entries.name: blindfold_slip
entries.description: A [blindfold](#blindfold) still in place but [sitting](#sitting) badly, so that one eye or both look out from beneath it. Nobody need be lifting it; the covering has simply shifted.

entries.name: undone_duijin
entries.description: The front-fastening Chinese duijin [jacket](#jacket) is worn open or with its knot fastenings released, so the panels hang apart. The garment stays on the shoulders rather than being removed.

entries.name: open_leotard
entries.description: A [leotard](#leotard) undone at the front by zip, [buttons](#buttons) or ties, so it gapes instead of fitting close. The garment stays on the body rather than being taken off.

entries.name: opening_another's_clothes
entries.description: One character undoes or spreads apart somebody else's clothing instead of their own. Pair it with the garment [tag](#tag), such as [open_shirt](#open_shirt) or [open_jacket](#open_jacket), so the picture records which piece was opened.

entries.name: wings_through_clothes
entries.description: The clothing is slit, [torn](#torn), or purpose-cut at the [back](#back) so a pair of [wings](#wings) [can](#can) pass through it. Both an open-backed design and a specially made [hole](#hole) count.

entries.name: unbuttoned_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) with its [buttons](#buttons) undone, [hanging](#hanging) open at the front or [slipping](#slipping) off the shoulders. Covers both a partial and a full unfastening.

entries.name: coat_stash
entries.description: One side of a [coat](#coat), [cloak](#cloak) or [jacket](#jacket) is held open to [display](#display) what is hidden in the lining: weapons, [tools](#tools), goods for [sale](#sale) or contraband. The reveal is the point of the picture.

entries.name: torn_clothes
entries.description: Any garment that is ripped, shredded or [hanging](#hanging) in tatters. Add the specific piece such as [torn_shirt](#torn_shirt) or [torn_pantyhose](#torn_pantyhose); the act of [ripping](#ripping) is [tearing_clothes](#tearing_clothes).

entries.name: wet_clothes
entries.description: Clothing soaked through, [clinging](#clinging) to the body and sometimes turning see-through, especially when white. Clothes damp from perspiration instead are [sweaty_clothes](#sweaty_clothes).

entries.name: ripped_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, tights or [socks](#socks) with holes, runs and [tears](#tears) in the [fabric](#fabric). It may be damage from a fight or a deliberate distressed look.

entries.name: dirty_clothes
entries.description: Clothing marked with [mud](#mud), [soil](#soil) or grime. Stains left by other substances have their own names, [blood_on_clothes](#blood_on_clothes) and [food_on_clothes](#food_on_clothes).

entries.name: torn
entries.description: Something ripped apart and left in tatters, whether [paper](#paper), a [flag](#flag) or [fabric](#fabric). For garments in that state prefer [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes).

entries.name: stain
entries.description: A [patch](#patch) of discolouration left where a [liquid](#liquid) or chemical has soaked in, whether on [fabric](#fabric), [paper](#paper) or metal. The mark itself is what is tagged, distinct from [stained_panties](#stained_panties) which names the specific garment.

entries.name: sweaty_clothes
entries.description: Clothing soaked through with perspiration, darkened in patches or turned see-through where the [fabric](#fabric) clings. A [sign](#sign) of heat, exertion or a stressful moment.

entries.name: burnt_clothes
entries.description: Clothing scorched by [fire](#fire), showing blackened edges, holes and singe marks. It often follows an [explosion](#explosion) or a fight.

entries.name: tearing_clothes
entries.description: Someone is [caught](#caught) in the act of [ripping](#ripping) a garment apart, whether their own [clothes](#clothes) or another person's. The aftermath of the act is [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes); this [tag](#tag) covers the action itself.

entries.name: popped_button
entries.description: A button has burst off a garment, usually a [shirt](#shirt) straining over the chest, and is missing or [flying](#flying) through the air. Common with large [breasts](#breasts) or [clothes](#clothes) that are too small.

entries.name: dissolving_clothes
entries.description: Garments [melting](#melting) or [crumbling](#crumbling) away on the body, baring skin as they go. Magic or some unexplained force is the usual cause.

entries.name: stained_clothes
entries.description: Clothing darkened where a [liquid](#liquid), such as [wine](#wine), [paint](#paint) or [food](#food), has soaked into the [fabric](#fabric). Darkening and see-through fabric from [sweat](#sweat) alone is tagged [sweaty_clothes](#sweaty_clothes) instead.

entries.name: paint_on_clothes
entries.description: Paint spattered and streaked over someone's clothing, the mark of [messy](#messy) work in progress. Read it as a [working](#working) artist or decorator, not as a pattern woven into the [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: exploding_clothes
entries.description: Clothing bursts off the body all at once, [fabric](#fabric) [flying](#flying) apart in shreds. Usually caused by a blast, a [transformation](#transformation) or a sudden change of size, with the wearer left unhurt.

entries.name: food_on_clothes
entries.description: Something edible [resting](#resting) on or spilled down a garment, from a crumb in a [lap](#lap) to [sauce](#sauce) [running](#running) over a [shirt](#shirt) front. The [food](#food) touches the [cloth](#cloth) rather than being printed on it.

entries.name: wringing_skirt
entries.description: The hem of a [skirt](#skirt) is gathered and twisted in both hands to squeeze out [water](#water). It follows a soaking, so [wet_clothes](#wet_clothes) usually applies alongside it.

entries.name: ripping
entries.description: Cloth or [paper](#paper) being [torn](#torn) apart in the moment shown, hands [pulling](#pulling) in opposite directions. An item that is merely already ripped does not qualify; the tearing has to be happening on [screen](#screen).

entries.name: paint_stains
entries.description: Blotches and dried smears left on [clothes](#clothes) or skin by [working](#working) with [paint](#paint), almost always unintentional. Small and scattered rather than covering the garment.

entries.name: strap_break
entries.description: A shoulder or [bikini](#bikini) [strap](#strap) snapping under load, usually because the garment is far too small for what is inside it. If the break makes the whole garment give way, pair it with [wardrobe_malfunction](#wardrobe_malfunction).

entries.name: rags
entries.description: Worn-out, shredded garments with [no](#no) ornament and a washed-out brown or grey color, the standard [costume](#costume) of beggars, captives, and humanoid monsters. Distinct from a [cleaning](#cleaning) rag, which is a [cloth](#cloth) used for [wiping](#wiping) surfaces.

entries.name: unraveling
entries.description: Fabric or [wrapping](#wrapping) coming apart [thread](#thread) by thread or turn by turn, whether a knit [pulling](#pulling) loose into [yarn](#yarn) or [bandages](#bandages) spooling away. The act of undoing itself, rather than the finished damage, is what the picture shows.

entries.name: burning_clothes
entries.description: Garments alight, still worn or [lying](#lying) discarded, scorching and [falling](#falling) apart. Smoke and blackened edges usually come with them.

entries.name: chocolate_on_clothes
entries.description: Melted [chocolate](#chocolate) has landed on what somebody is wearing, leaving brown streaks or [spots](#spots) in the [fabric](#fabric). Frequently a by-product of a Valentine's [baking](#baking) scene.

entries.name: frayed_clothes
entries.description: Garments whose edges have worn into loose straggling threads and ragged hems. It suggests age and hard use; outright rips and holes are [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes).

entries.name: skindentation
entries.description: Tight clothing presses into the [flesh](#flesh) so the skin bulges around it, typically [thighs](#thighs) swelling over thighhigh tops. When fingers do the pressing it is [deep_skin](#deep_skin).

entries.name: highleg
entries.description: A garment cut so its leg openings or side straps ride high on the hips, baring more of hip and thigh. It covers swimsuits, leotards and [panties](#panties) alike, and the specific highleg_ tags say which garment it is.

entries.name: skin_tight
entries.description: Clothing that clings to the body with [no](#no) gap, as with bodysuits, leotards, swimsuits and [spandex](#spandex) [sportswear](#sportswear); contours like [covered_nipples](#covered_nipples) or [covered_navel](#covered_navel) often show through. Ordinary snug [clothes](#clothes) are [tight_clothes](#tight_clothes); unrealistically clingy ones [impossible_clothes](#impossible_clothes).

entries.name: sleeves_rolled_up
entries.description: One or both sleeves [folded](#folded) up the arm in neat turns, even a single fold. Sleeves merely shoved up without folding are [sleeves_pushed_up](#sleeves_pushed_up).

entries.name: impossible_clothes
entries.description: Clothing that fits like [paint](#paint), [wrapping](#wrapping) each breast on every side and underneath, which [no](#no) real garment does. Merely snug wear is [tight_clothes](#tight_clothes) or [skin_tight](#skin_tight); Japanese calls the effect chichi-bukuro.

entries.name: underbust
entries.description: A garment whose upper edge sits right beneath the [breasts](#breasts), lifting or framing them, as on corsets, dirndls and some [maid](#maid) and [waitress](#waitress) outfits. Fabric enclosing the bust on all sides instead is [framed_breasts](#framed_breasts), and the exposed lower breast itself is [underboob](#underboob).

entries.name: tight_clothes
entries.description: Garments that fit very snugly and show the body's shape without being skin-tight. Use [skin_tight](#skin_tight) instead for [fabric](#fabric) that clings like a second skin.

entries.name: lowleg
entries.description: Any garment cut low on the hips with a thin waistband, from [panties](#panties) and [bikini](#bikini) bottoms to trousers, [shorts](#shorts), skirts and [pantyhose](#pantyhose). Add the [tag](#tag) for the particular garment as [well](#well).

entries.name: taut_clothes
entries.description: Fabric stretched so tight it visibly [ripples](#ripples), most often across the bust. Distinct from [tight_clothes](#tight_clothes), which is merely snug, and from [impossible_clothes](#impossible_clothes), which clings unrealistically to every curve.

entries.name: clothes_between_breasts
entries.description: A piece of clothing, typically a tie, [ribbon](#ribbon) or [strap](#strap), sits nudged into the gap between the [breasts](#breasts). A particular case of [between_breasts](#between_breasts).

entries.name: oversized_clothes
entries.description: Garments obviously too big for the person in them, with sleeves [swallowing](#swallowing) the hands and hems [dragging](#dragging). Often a borrowed or swapped outfit; the reverse is [undersized_clothes](#undersized_clothes).

entries.name: asymmetrical_clothes
entries.description: An outfit that differs markedly from one side of the body to the other, by cut or by the way it is worn. Mismatched [socks](#socks), and lopsidedness caused by [undressing](#undressing), [bandages](#bandages) or strapped-on gear, do not count.

entries.name: low-rise
entries.description: Bottoms cut to sit below the natural waist, [riding](#riding) on the hips and leaving the [navel](#navel) and hip bones uncovered. It applies to trousers, skirts, swimwear and [underwear](#underwear) alike.

entries.name: clothes_too_big
entries.description: The garment swamps its wearer, sleeves [swallowing](#swallowing) the hands and hems pooling on the [floor](#floor). Usually a borrowed [shirt](#shirt) or a deliberately oversized look.

entries.name: floating_clothes
entries.description: Clothing lifted by [wind](#wind) or [drifting](#drifting) in the air instead of [hanging](#hanging) under its own [weight](#weight). Use the specific tags where hair, a [cape](#cape) or a [scarf](#scarf) is what is moving.

entries.name: tight_pants
entries.description: Trousers that fit snugly against the [legs](#legs) without being skin-tight.

entries.name: sleeves_pushed_up
entries.description: One or both sleeves shoved up the arm in a loose bunch, to cool off, keep them clean, or get ready for a task. Neatly [folded](#folded) sleeves are [sleeves_rolled_up](#sleeves_rolled_up).

entries.name: undersized_clothes
entries.description: Clothing plainly too small for the wearer, straining or [riding](#riding) up, often after a [costume](#costume) swap between characters. The reverse of [oversized_clothes](#oversized_clothes).

entries.name: oversized_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) clearly too big for the wearer, often [reaching](#reaching) the [thighs](#thighs) and [swallowing](#swallowing) the hands. Long sleeves [hanging](#hanging) past the fingers also take [sleeves_past_wrists](#sleeves_past_wrists).

entries.name: loose_clothes
entries.description: Garments [hanging](#hanging) slack and draped over the body without being obviously the wrong size. Clothing plainly too large is [oversized_clothes](#oversized_clothes).

entries.name: clothes_too_small
entries.description: The garment is visibly undersized, straining at the [seams](#seams) and [riding](#riding) up to leave skin bare. Fabric pulled tight across the chest and hips is the usual cue.

entries.name: tight_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) that is too small for its wearer and strains against the body. The reverse is [oversized_shirt](#oversized_shirt).

entries.name: tight_dress
entries.description: A [dress](#dress) that hugs the [figure](#figure) closely without being skin-tight.

entries.name: pants_rolled_up
entries.description: Trouser [legs](#legs) [folded](#folded) or rolled upward so they finish somewhere between the ankle and the knee, for [wading](#wading), [working](#working), or as a style. Trousers cut to that length instead are [capri_pants](#capri_pants).

entries.name: baggy_clothes
entries.description: Clothing that hangs loose and voluminous instead of [following](#following) the body, such as an oversized [hoodie](#hoodie) or slack [overalls](#overalls). Trousers cut that way have their own [tag](#tag), [baggy_pants](#baggy_pants).

entries.name: pants_tucked_in
entries.description: Trouser [legs](#legs) pushed into the tops of [boots](#boots) or other [tall](#tall) footwear rather than [hanging](#hanging) over them. Common on [military](#military) and adventuring outfits, and on the baggy [hakama](#hakama) worn under armour.

entries.name: tented_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) pulled taut over large [breasts](#breasts) so the [cloth](#cloth) hangs away from the body underneath them like a [tent](#tent), usually because it is tucked in tightly. Never combined with [underbust](#underbust).

entries.name: clothes_between_thighs
entries.description: Fabric is [caught](#caught) between the [legs](#legs) at the [crotch](#crotch), usually a [skirt](#skirt), [dress](#dress) or pelvic curtain bunched there by the pose. Sometimes it doubles as [convenient_censoring](#convenient_censoring).

entries.name: oversized_breast_cup
entries.description: The cups of a [bra](#bra), [leotard](#leotard) or bunnysuit are plainly too big for the [breasts](#breasts) and hang slack off the chest. Tight fabrics such as bikinis and [spandex](#spandex) do not qualify, and the garment must be worn more or less properly for the mismatch to read.

entries.name: sweater_tucked_in
entries.description: The whole hem of a [sweater](#sweater) is pushed under a [skirt](#skirt), trousers or other bottomwear for a clean waistline. When only part of the hem is tucked, use the partially-tucked variant instead.

entries.name: shirt_overhang
entries.description: A full-length [shirt](#shirt) [hanging](#hanging) loosely off the bust and away from the [stomach](#stomach) instead of fitting close to the body. The crop-top equivalent is [crop_top_overhang](#crop_top_overhang).

entries.name: sleeve_rolled_up
entries.description: One sleeve pushed or [folded](#folded) [back](#back) up the arm while the other stays down or out of view. Use the plural [sleeves_rolled_up](#sleeves_rolled_up) when both arms are bared this way.

entries.name: tight_top
entries.description: An upper garment stretched close across chest and [torso](#torso), the body's [outline](#outline) readable straight through the [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: skirt_rolled_up
entries.description: The waistband of a [skirt](#skirt) has been [folded](#folded) over several times to shorten the hem. On a [pleated](#pleated) skirt the folded pleats show as a thick band at the waist.

entries.name: wrinkled_fabric
entries.description: Cloth drawn with pronounced creases and folds rather than a smooth surface. It suggests [weight](#weight), wear, or a garment that has recently been crumpled.

entries.name: impossible_towel
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) wrapped so that it hugs the body like a tailored garment, dipping in under each breast. Not strictly impossible, but [no](#no) [plain](#plain) [rectangle](#rectangle) of [cloth](#cloth) falls that way by itself.

entries.name: swaddled
entries.description: A body wrapped snugly in [cloth](#cloth) or a [blanket](#blanket) so the arms are [pinned](#pinned) inside, the way an infant is bundled. Larger characters get the same treatment either as a joke or for warmth.

entries.name: back_peek
entries.description: A narrow band of [back](#back), usually low down, is uncovered where clothing has ridden up or falls short of [reaching](#reaching). Bending forward, reaching up or a gust [catching](#catching) an untucked [shirt](#shirt) is what exposes it, the way [midriff_peek](#midriff_peek) works at the front.

entries.name: shirt_rolled_up
entries.description: Sleeves or hem [folded](#folded) [back](#back) on themselves so the [shirt](#shirt) sits shorter, baring the [forearms](#forearms) or [midriff](#midriff).

entries.name: bikini_bridge
entries.description: The gap that opens between the hip bones when a taut waistband stretches across a [lying](#lying) figure's [stomach](#stomach). Panties and low-slung trousers make one as readily as a [bikini](#bikini) bottom does.

entries.name: shorts_rolled_up
entries.description: The hems of a pair of [shorts](#shorts) [folded](#folded) upward one or more times, shortening the [legs](#legs) and leaving a visible cuff, often done to wade into [water](#water) or simply to show more thigh.

entries.name: undressing
entries.description: A character in the act of removing clothing. Use it when it is unclear whether [clothes](#clothes) are coming off or going on; a clear put-on is [dressing](#dressing), an accidental slip is [wardrobe_malfunction](#wardrobe_malfunction), and already-removed items are [unworn_clothes](#unworn_clothes).

entries.name: no_pants
entries.description: A top and [underwear](#underwear) with nothing over the underwear, as in a [shirt](#shirt) above bare [panties](#panties). Being wholly bare below the waist is [bottomless](#bottomless), and a character with [no](#no) top does not qualify.

entries.name: shirt_tucked_in
