entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) tucked fully into a [skirt](#skirt), trousers or other bottoms. Only partly tucked is [shirt_partially_tucked_in](#shirt_partially_tucked_in) instead.

entries.name: jacket_on_shoulders
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) or [coat](#coat) hangs over the shoulders with the arms out of the sleeves, worn like a short [cape](#cape). It may be for warmth, for [cover](#cover), or purely for the look.

entries.name: swimsuit_under_clothes
entries.description: A one-piece [swimsuit](#swimsuit) worn beneath ordinary clothing, showing at the neckline or through an open [shirt](#shirt). For a two-piece worn the same way, use [bikini_under_clothes](#bikini_under_clothes).

entries.name: clothes_around_waist
entries.description: A long-sleeved garment such as a [jacket](#jacket), [hoodie](#hoodie) or [shirt](#shirt) is knotted by its sleeves around the waist instead of worn. Common on [casual](#casual) outfits and [gym](#gym) uniforms.

entries.name: coat_on_shoulders
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) hung over the shoulders with both arms out of the sleeves, worn like a [cape](#cape). It reads either as an imposing pose or as a borrowed coat used for warmth.

entries.name: clothes
entries.description: Garments are visible but nobody is wearing them: [hanging](#hanging) in a [closet](#closet), draped over a [chair](#chair), strewn about the room. Prefer [unworn_clothes](#unworn_clothes) or [clothes_in_front](#clothes_in_front) where they fit, and footwear may fall outside it.

entries.name: no_shirt
entries.description: Bottoms plus a [bra](#bra) or [bikini](#bikini) top, with [no](#no) [shirt](#shirt) over them. Not for [nude](#nude), [topless](#topless), [bottomless](#bottomless) or underwear-only figures; both a bra-like top and proper bottoms have to be present.

entries.name: partially_undressed
entries.description: Part of what a character was wearing has come off: a [shirt](#shirt) pushed down to bare a [bra](#bra), a bra half removed, or a top or bottom simply absent. It overlaps with [topless](#topless), [bottomless](#bottomless), [undressing](#undressing) and [clothes_pull](#clothes_pull).

entries.name: unworn_clothes
entries.description: A character is partly or fully undressed and the [shed](#shed) garments remain visible somewhere in the picture. Use [undressing](#undressing) instead while the [clothes](#clothes) are still coming off.

entries.name: dressing
entries.description: Somebody in the middle of putting [clothes](#clothes) on. Only use it where the picture settles which way the clothes are going; if it could be either, [undressing](#undressing) is the fallback.

entries.name: jacket_around_waist
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) is knotted by its sleeves around the waist instead of being worn. It belongs to the [clothes_around_waist](#clothes_around_waist) [family](#family).

entries.name: skirt_around_one_leg
entries.description: A [skirt](#skirt) pulled partly off so it hangs bunched around one leg only, the underwear-removal shape applied to a skirt.

entries.name: sweater_around_waist
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) tied by its sleeves around the hips rather than worn over the [torso](#torso), [hanging](#hanging) like a loose [belt](#belt). Common in [casual](#casual), preppy or gym-adjacent outfits.

entries.name: undressing_another
entries.description: One character removes another's clothing, whether teasingly, helpfully or forcibly. Usually a prelude in an adult scene.

entries.name: cardigan_around_waist
entries.description: A [cardigan](#cardigan) tied by its sleeves around the hips rather than worn on the body. One case of [clothes_around_waist](#clothes_around_waist).

entries.name: jacket_over_swimsuit
entries.description: An open light [jacket](#jacket) or [shirt](#shirt) worn over a [swimsuit](#swimsuit), the usual [beach](#beach) layer. When more [clothes](#clothes) are on, or the garment is fully done up, [swimsuit_under_clothes](#swimsuit_under_clothes) fits better.

entries.name: shorts_around_one_leg
entries.description: Shorts pulled off partway and left [hanging](#hanging) around a single leg. Implies [shorts](#shorts); the [panties](#panties) equivalent is [panties_around_one_leg](#panties_around_one_leg).

entries.name: panties_on_head
entries.description: Panties worn on top of the head like a [hat](#hat), as a joke or as a mark of perversion. Pulled down over the face instead, they are [panty_mask](#panty_mask).

entries.name: hat_on_back
entries.description: The [hat](#hat) is not on the head but hangs behind the wearer, tied at the [neck](#neck) or slung on the [back](#back) by its cord. Sun hats and [cowboy](#cowboy) hats are worn this way often.

entries.name: dressing_another
entries.description: One character puts a garment on somebody else, or ties and straightens it for them. Roughly the [mirror](#mirror) of [assisted_exposure](#assisted_exposure).

entries.name: removing_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) is coming off, [sliding](#sliding) from the shoulders or being drawn down one arm. Also used when one character strips it off another.

entries.name: shirt_partially_tucked_in
entries.description: Only part of a shirt's hem sits inside the [skirt](#skirt) or trousers, with the rest left [hanging](#hanging) out for a deliberately scruffy look.

entries.name: shirt_around_waist
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) removed and knotted by its sleeves around the hips, [hanging](#hanging) as a loose wrap instead of being worn on the [torso](#torso). Implies [clothes_around_waist](#clothes_around_waist) and shirt.

entries.name: arm_out_of_sleeve
entries.description: A sleeved garment is worn with one or both arms slipped free, the empty sleeve [hanging](#hanging) loose. A [kimono](#kimono) knotted at the waist instead takes [hadanugi_dousa](#hadanugi_dousa).

entries.name: wardrobe_error
entries.description: A garment put on wrongly: a [shirt](#shirt) [back](#back) to front, a [bikini](#bikini) top upside down, [buttons](#buttons) out of line. Different from clothing worn correctly that happens to expose the wearer.

entries.name: shirt_partially_removed
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) taken half off: one arm free while the garment still hangs from the other shoulder or catches at the waist, somewhere between worn and removed.

entries.name: clothes_on_floor
entries.description: Discarded garments lie scattered on the ground with nobody in them. Often a trail leading off somewhere, suggesting a hurried [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: folded_clothes
entries.description: Garments squared away into a neat [stack](#stack), set on a [bench](#bench), a [bed](#bed) or in a [basket](#basket). They are typically [waiting](#waiting) beside a [bath](#bath), in a changing room, or on a made-up [futon](#futon).

entries.name: jacket_over_shoulder
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) taken off and slung over one shoulder, usually hooked on a finger. It is being carried, not worn.

entries.name: glove_pull
entries.description: A glove being drawn on or peeled off, the free hand tugging at the cuff. A [staple](#staple) of elegant and villainous character moments.

entries.name: removing_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses or [sunglasses](#sunglasses) are being lifted away from the face, held in the fingers close to the eyes. The eyewear has to be visibly in hand rather than already set aside.

entries.name: undersuit
entries.description: A character appears without several of the outer layers they normally wear, so an inner garment that is usually hidden shows instead. Not the same as being down to [underwear](#underwear) only; if just one covering piece is missing, prefer the matching [no_jacket](#no_jacket) or [no_cape](#no_cape) style [tag](#tag) instead, unless that piece would ordinarily hide most of what now shows.

entries.name: clothes_in_front
entries.description: A character holds a garment up against their body to see how it would [suit](#suit) them, without putting it on. Typical of [shopping](#shopping) scenes and of getting dressed.

entries.name: removing_bra
entries.description: A [bra](#bra) is being unhooked or slipped off, hands [reaching](#reaching) behind the [back](#back) or drawing a [strap](#strap) down the arm. Fastening one counts here as [well](#well).

entries.name: changing_clothes
entries.description: A character is [caught](#caught) between outfits, partly out of one garment and partly into the next. The swap is what distinguishes it from simply [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: putting_on_footwear
entries.description: A character is [caught](#caught) mid-motion getting a shoe, boot, or sandal onto their foot, whether tugging a heel into place or lacing it up. Applies just as much to [boots](#boots) as to ordinary [shoes](#shoes).

entries.name: putting_on_gloves
entries.description: Gloves being drawn onto the hands, fingers only half seated or a cuff being pulled up the wrist. Once they are simply worn with [no](#no) motion implied, the [plain](#plain) [gloves](#gloves) [tag](#tag) covers it.

entries.name: jumpsuit_around_waist
entries.description: A [jumpsuit](#jumpsuit) undone and pushed down so its top half bunches round the hips, showing whatever is worn beneath. Mechanics' coveralls and [racing](#racing) suits do this most.

entries.name: putting_on_jewelry
entries.description: A [necklace](#necklace), [ring](#ring), [bracelet](#bracelet), or earring is being fastened or slipped into place, often in front of a [mirror](#mirror) or by another character's hands. Combine with [jewelry](#jewelry) and the specific piece.

entries.name: hat_loss
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) has just come off by [accident](#accident) — snatched by [wind](#wind), knocked away, or [slipping](#slipping) as the wearer turns. It is generally still in shot, in the air or on the ground.

entries.name: strip_game
entries.description: A group [playing](#playing) a game where the loser of each round takes off a piece of clothing, usually until somebody is bare. Poker, [mahjong](#mahjong) and even rock-paper-scissors get played this way, and it [can](#can) also grow out of a [gambling](#gambling) game once a player runs out of [money](#money).

entries.name: putting_on_headwear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), [crown](#crown), [helmet](#helmet), or [headdress](#headdress) is being lowered onto a head, whether the wearer's own or someone else's. Any kind of headwear qualifies, not only hats.

entries.name: pantyhose_around_one_leg
entries.description: Pantyhose peeled off and left gathered around one leg while the other is bare. A half-undressed state rather than a way of wearing them.

entries.name: removing_mask
entries.description: A [mask](#mask) is being lifted away from the face, revealing what was behind it. The [gesture](#gesture) is usually the point of the picture rather than incidental.

entries.name: removing_glove
entries.description: A glove is being peeled off, often gripped at the fingertip and drawn away, or pulled down from the wrist. A stock [gesture](#gesture) for challenges and for changing register.

entries.name: removing_shoes
entries.description: One or both [shoes](#shoes) are being taken off, the heel eased out or the shoe pulled from the foot. A routine [gesture](#gesture) in genkan and indoor scenes.

entries.name: removing_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [socks](#socks) or tights are being rolled or peeled down the leg. Fingers hooked at the top edge and [fabric](#fabric) bunched at the ankle are the usual cues.

entries.name: shirt_on_shoulders
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) draped over the shoulders with the arms left out of the sleeves, [hanging](#hanging) loose like a short [cape](#cape).

entries.name: shoe_loss
entries.description: A shoe has come off by [accident](#accident) and lies visible in the scene, typically shaken loose by [running](#running) or [kicking](#kicking). A shoe removed on purpose is [unworn_shoes](#unworn_shoes), and one [hanging](#hanging) from the [toes](#toes) is [shoe_dangle](#shoe_dangle).

entries.name: tied_sweater
entries.description: A [sweater](#sweater) carried rather than worn, knotted around the waist or draped over the shoulders with the arms tied at the chest. A [casual](#casual) styling detail rather than a way of [dressing](#dressing).

entries.name: panty_mask
entries.description: Panties pulled over the head so they [cover](#cover) the face, the [crotch](#crotch) panel across the [nose](#nose) and mouth and the ears [poking](#poking) through the leg openings. A stock joke for perverts and [underwear](#underwear) thieves; simply [resting](#resting) on top of the head they are [panties_on_head](#panties_on_head).

entries.name: bra_over_clothes
entries.description: The [bra](#bra) has been strapped on outside a [shirt](#shirt) or [dress](#dress) instead of underneath it. It reads as a joke, a deliberate [costume](#costume) [choice](#choice), or somebody who dressed in a great hurry.

entries.name: removing_pasties
entries.description: The adhesive covers over the [nipples](#nipples) are being peeled away, exposing what they hid. One may already be off while the other is still in place.

entries.name: kimono_on_shoulders
entries.description: A [kimono](#kimono) hangs over the shoulders like a [cape](#cape) with the arms out of the sleeves, worn loose over whatever is underneath. It is often drawn [sliding](#sliding) down the [back](#back).

entries.name: putting_on_legwear
entries.description: Stockings, [socks](#socks), or tights are being rolled or pulled up the leg, [caught](#caught) at the half-dressed moment rather than the finished look.

entries.name: bloomers_around_one_leg
entries.description: Bloomers pulled off one leg completely and left [dangling](#dangling) from the other. The wearer is uncovered below while the garment technically stays on.

entries.name: removing_sock
entries.description: A character [caught](#caught) in the act of [pulling](#pulling) a sock off one or both [feet](#feet). The motion has to be visible; [socks](#socks) already discarded on the [floor](#floor) do not count.

entries.name: buttoning
entries.description: Fingers work a button through its [hole](#hole), closing a [shirt](#shirt), [coat](#coat) or cuff. It catches the moment of [dressing](#dressing) or straightening up rather than the finished garment.

entries.name: clothes_on_bed
entries.description: Garments lie unworn across a [bed](#bed), dropped there or laid out ready. Usually implies somebody has just undressed or is choosing what to put on.

entries.name: removing_hat
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) is being lifted from the head, held by the brim or the [crown](#crown). It reads as greeting, respect, or simply settling in.

entries.name: swimsuit_over_clothes
entries.description: Swimwear pulled on over ordinary clothing rather than worn against the skin. A [swimsuit](#swimsuit) worn over another swimsuit instead is a layered swimsuit.

entries.name: removing_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) is in the act of coming off, shrugged from the shoulders or pulled down the arms. Also covers a coat being taken off someone else.

entries.name: removing_bra_under_shirt
entries.description: A [bra](#bra) is unhooked and worked out from beneath a [shirt](#shirt) that stays on, arms pulled inside the sleeves to do it. Adjusting the bra the same way counts too.

entries.name: cardigan_on_shoulders
entries.description: A [cardigan](#cardigan) draped over both shoulders with the arms out of the sleeves, worn like a short [cape](#cape). Often thrown on against a chill [indoors](#indoors).

entries.name: headband_around_neck
entries.description: A [headband](#headband) has come off the [forehead](#forehead) and is worn round the [neck](#neck) instead, [sitting](#sitting) there like a loose band or a narrow [scarf](#scarf).

entries.name: strip_mahjong
entries.description: Mahjong played with clothing as the forfeit: whoever loses a hand removes something, round after round.

entries.name: panties_around_one_finger
entries.description: A pair of [panties](#panties) hooked over one finger and held clear of the body. Usually a tease after [undressing](#undressing), or a [trophy](#trophy) waved about in a [comic](#comic) scene.

entries.name: panty_dangle
entries.description: Panties [hanging](#hanging) loose from a foot, an ankle or a finger rather than being worn, usually mid-undress. Nothing further about the wearer's state is implied.

entries.name: sword
entries.description: A bladed [weapon](#weapon) with a [hilt](#hilt) and a straight or curved blade meant for [cutting](#cutting) or thrusting, ranging from a knight's longsword to a [katana](#katana). Add the specific type and any relevant pose [tag](#tag) such as [holding_sword](#holding_sword).

entries.name: katana
entries.description: The curved, single-edged Japanese [sword](#sword) with a round or squared [guard](#guard) and a grip long enough for both hands, carried thrust through the [belt](#belt) edge upward. A longer, deeper-curved blade slung edge-down is a tachi.

entries.name: knife
entries.description: A short-bladed [cutting](#cutting) tool or [weapon](#weapon) with a [handle](#handle), taking in daggers and combat knives as [well](#well) as [kitchen](#kitchen) and [pocket](#pocket) knives. Add the specific type, and [holding_knife](#holding_knife) where somebody has one in hand.

entries.name: sheath
entries.description: The case that holds a [sword](#sword) or other large blade, typically hung at the hip or slung across the [back](#back). Tag [sheathed](#sheathed) when the [weapon](#weapon) is inside, [unsheathing](#unsheathing) when partway drawn and [unsheathed](#unsheathed) once it is fully out; a gun's equivalent case is a [holster](#holster), and a cloth-wrapped weapon takes [weapon_bag](#weapon_bag) instead.

entries.name: sheathed
entries.description: A [sword](#sword), [dagger](#dagger) or similar blade [sitting](#sitting) inside its case, usually [hanging](#hanging) at the hip or across the [back](#back). Implies [sheath](#sheath).

entries.name: scythe
entries.description: A long-handled harvesting blade, drawn in anime and [fantasy](#fantasy) as the [weapon](#weapon) of [choice](#choice) for grim reapers and [dark](#dark) characters. The real [battlefield](#battlefield) [polearm](#polearm) called a [war](#war) scythe is a different weapon, closer to a glaive.

entries.name: axe
entries.description: A wedge-shaped head on a haft, either the tool for splitting wood or the longer, keener [weapon](#weapon) version made to hack at [people](#people). Add [holding_axe](#holding_axe) when it is carried and [battle_axe](#battle_axe) for the double-edged [war](#war) type.

entries.name: dagger
entries.description: A short blade sharpened on both edges, or on none, built for thrusting rather than slicing and often carried as a backup arm. A [knife](#knife) by [contrast](#contrast) carries one edge and is meant for [cutting](#cutting).

entries.name: scabbard
entries.description: The [sheath](#sheath) of a bladed [weapon](#weapon) such as a [sword](#sword), [dagger](#dagger) or [bayonet](#bayonet). Narrower than the general sheath [tag](#tag), which also covers holders for axes and other weapons.

entries.name: planted
entries.description: An object, most often a [weapon](#weapon), driven point-first into the ground so it stands upright on its own. A [sword](#sword) left [standing](#standing) this way also takes [planted_sword](#planted_sword).

entries.name: sheath_(sword)
entries.description: The [scabbard](#scabbard) a blade slides into, whether hung at the [belt](#belt), gripped in the free hand or slung across the [back](#back). Applies whether the [sword](#sword) is stowed inside it or already drawn. Implies [sheath](#sheath).

entries.name: unsheathing
entries.description: A character [caught](#caught) in the act of drawing a [sword](#sword) or similar bladed [weapon](#weapon) out of its [scabbard](#scabbard). If the hand rests on the [hilt](#hilt) but the blade has not begun to move, [ready_to_draw](#ready_to_draw) is the [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: energy_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) whose blade is light or [plasma](#plasma) rather than metal, the lightsaber being the version [everyone](#everyone) knows. Also called a beam saber, and very common in science-fiction anime.

entries.name: planted_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) [standing](#standing) with its blade driven into the ground, often beside a [resting](#resting) or victorious character. Tag [planted](#planted) alongside it.

entries.name: unsheathed
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) drawn fully out of its [sheath](#sheath), blade bare. A [weapon](#weapon) still [resting](#resting) inside its sheath is tagged [sheathed](#sheathed), and one only part way out is [unsheathing](#unsheathing).

entries.name: rapier
entries.description: A slim, sharp-pointed thrusting [sword](#sword) with an elaborate [guard](#guard) [protecting](#protecting) the grip, the classic blade of the fencer and duelist. Combine with sword and [holding_sword](#holding_sword).

entries.name: sword_on_back
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) carried strapped or slung across the [back](#back) rather than worn at the hip or gripped in the hands.

entries.name: sword_stuck_in_ground
entries.description: A blade driven point-first into earth, [sand](#sand), stone or a [floor](#floor) and left [standing](#standing) upright. A common shorthand for a [grave](#grave) [marker](#marker), a pause between fights, or a [waiting](#waiting) challenge.

entries.name: greatsword
entries.description: A very large [two-handed](#two-handed) [sword](#sword) with a long or broad double-edged blade, often as [tall](#tall) as the person [carrying](#carrying) it. A [katana](#katana) or a one-handed blade is not one.

entries.name: short_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) short enough to be used comfortably with one hand, longer than a [dagger](#dagger). A full-length one-handed sword such as an arming sword is tagged plainly as sword. Implies sword.

entries.name: arm_blade
entries.description: A blade fixed to the forearm: a wrist blade, a claw [weapon](#weapon), or an edge built into a mechanical limb. It stays attached rather than being gripped.

entries.name: battle_axe
entries.description: An [axe](#axe) built for combat, its head thinner and [lighter](#lighter) than a woodcutter's since it is meant for limbs rather than logs. Oversized [fantasy](#fantasy) versions fall here too; add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) when one is being wielded.

entries.name: multiple_swords
entries.description: More than one [sword](#sword) in the picture, whether carried by a single [figure](#figure), held by several, or [lying](#lying) about the scene. The count matters rather than who owns them.

entries.name: wooden_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) carved from wood, such as a [bokken](#bokken) used in [kendo](#kendo) practice or a child's [toy](#toy) blade. Tag sword as [well](#well).

entries.name: ootachi
entries.description: An outsize Japanese [sword](#sword), a [katana](#katana) whose blade [can](#can) run longer than the person [carrying](#carrying) it. Also called a nodachi, it was difficult to forge and served as much as a mark of [standing](#standing) as a [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: shinai
entries.description: The [bamboo](#bamboo) practice [sword](#sword) used in [kendo](#kendo), built from [bound](#bound) slats so sparring does [no](#no) real harm. Usually seen with kendo [armor](#armor) or a [hakama](#hakama). Implies sword.

entries.name: wakizashi
entries.description: A short Japanese [sword](#sword) with a blade of roughly 30 to 60 centimetres, worn as the companion to a [katana](#katana). Shorter than a katana and usually shorter than a [kodachi](#kodachi).

entries.name: bayonet
entries.description: A [knife](#knife), [dagger](#dagger) or spike mounted at the muzzle of a [gun](#gun) so it [can](#can) be used at close quarters or on [parade](#parade). Keep it apart from a [gunblade](#gunblade), where [sword](#sword) and firearm are one [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: tantou
entries.description: A Japanese short [sword](#sword) or [dagger](#dagger) with a nearly flat blade, carried by [samurai](#samurai) and, for self-defense, by noblewomen as [well](#well).

entries.name: saber_(weapon)
entries.description: A curved single-edged [sword](#sword) with a large handguard, the [cavalry](#cavalry) and officer's blade. The Fate character of the same name is tagged separately.

entries.name: gunblade
entries.description: A hybrid of [sword](#sword) and [gun](#gun), most famously the weapons of Final Fantasy VIII. A blade simply fixed onto a gun is a [bayonet](#bayonet) instead.

entries.name: bokken
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) wooden practice [sword](#sword) shaped and weighted like a [katana](#katana), used for [solo](#solo) [training](#training) rather than for sparring. The [split](#split) [bamboo](#bamboo) [shinai](#shinai) [people](#people) actually [fence](#fence) with is a separate [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: knife_sheath
entries.description: The [cover](#cover) or [holster](#holster) for a [knife](#knife) or another short blade, worn on a [belt](#belt) or strapped to the body. A cover made for a sword-length blade is a [scabbard](#scabbard).

entries.name: hatchet_(axe)
entries.description: A short [axe](#axe) swung in one hand, its broad blade meant for [chopping](#chopping) and splitting wood and readily turned on a person. Larger [two-handed](#two-handed) versions are simply axe.

entries.name: stiletto_(weapon)
entries.description: A slim [dagger](#dagger) made purely for thrusting, its blade a long needle-like spike with little or [no](#no) edge. The narrow point pushes through [heavy](#heavy) [cloth](#cloth) and [mail](#mail) while leaving a small wound, and it hides easily, which made it a favoured tool for secretive killings.

entries.name: combat_knife
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [fighting](#fighting) [knife](#knife) built for rough use, normally full-tang with a durable blade and a grip in [leather](#leather) or composite. Some bayonets serve the same purpose once off the [rifle](#rifle).

entries.name: jian_(weapon)
entries.description: A straight Chinese [sword](#sword) with two edges, a slim tapering blade and a small [guard](#guard), often finished with a [tassel](#tassel) at the pommel. One hand or two [can](#can) hold it, and it still features in martial arts forms.

entries.name: broken_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) whose blade has snapped, leaving a stub in the [hilt](#hilt). The severed length often lies nearby on the ground.

entries.name: whip_sword
entries.description: A blade that breaks into linked segments on an internal [cable](#cable), or one [flexible](#flexible) enough to lash out like a [whip](#whip). Only apply it when the whip form is actually shown, and keep it apart from chainsaw-edged swords.

entries.name: hashitsuki_nata
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) splitting blade with a rectangular head and a small [nose](#nose) at the tip, gripped in both hands to cut [firewood](#firewood). It looks like an outsized [cleaver](#cleaver) and has become stock equipment for the unhinged-lover character. A billhook is a different tool.

entries.name: cutlass
entries.description: A short broad [sword](#sword) with a single [cutting](#cutting) edge, straight or gently curved, generally fitted with a [guard](#guard) over the knuckles. Firmly associated with sailors and Caribbean pirates.

entries.name: claymore_(sword)
entries.description: A large Scottish [two-handed](#two-handed) [sword](#sword) whose crossguard slopes forward and ends in small four-leaf terminals. Carried by Highlanders between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries.

entries.name: floating_sword
entries.description: A blade [hanging](#hanging) in the air beside its owner, [no](#no) hand on the grip and nothing [holding](#holding) it up. Typical of mages and [psychic](#psychic) fighters, who often command several at once.

entries.name: field_of_blades
entries.description: A [landscape](#landscape) [planted](#planted) with weapons, usually swords driven point-down into the ground in great numbers. It reads as the aftermath of a [battle](#battle) or an [emblem](#emblem) of endless [war](#war).

entries.name: pommel_tassel
entries.description: A cord and [hanging](#hanging) tuft fixed to the butt of a [sword](#sword) [hilt](#hilt), standard on Chinese jian and [dao](#dao). It swings with the blade and is usually coloured to match the wielder's outfit.

entries.name: long_sword
entries.description: A straight European blade with a cross-shaped [hilt](#hilt) and a grip made for two hands, [standing](#standing) roughly from the [belly](#belly) to the armpit of its owner. A blade as [tall](#tall) as the wielder is a [greatsword](#greatsword), and the same shape shortened for one hand is an arming [sword](#sword).

entries.name: double-blade
entries.description: A single haft with a [sword](#sword) blade fixed at each end, gripped in the middle and swung like a [staff](#staff). Not the same as [carrying](#carrying) two separate swords.

entries.name: machete
entries.description: A broad cleaver-like blade a foot or two long, made for [hacking](#hacking) through undergrowth and readily turned on [people](#people). The blade is thin for its width and the [handle](#handle) [plain](#plain).

entries.name: crystal_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) whose blade is cut from [crystal](#crystal) or [ice](#ice), [translucent](#translucent) and often faintly lit. A [fantasy](#fantasy) [weapon](#weapon) rather than a historical one.

entries.name: sword_writing
entries.description: Letters, [runes](#runes) or an inscription cut or painted directly onto a blade. The text must be visible on the [sword](#sword) itself, not on a [scabbard](#scabbard) or a [tag](#tag) [hanging](#hanging) from it.

entries.name: tachi_(weapon)
entries.description: A Japanese [sword](#sword) slung from the [belt](#belt) with its edge facing downward, the style that preceded the [katana](#katana). Generally longer and more strongly curved, and made for use on horseback.

entries.name: ninjatou
entries.description: The straight-bladed short [sword](#sword) with a [square](#square) [guard](#guard) that fiction puts in a ninja's hands. No such [weapon](#weapon) is attested historically; the design descends from mid-century films.

entries.name: scimitar
entries.description: A single-edged [sword](#sword) with a strongly curved blade that broadens toward the tip, associated with the Middle East and North Africa.

entries.name: crossed_swords
entries.description: Two blades laid or held over one another in an X. Common where duellists [lock](#lock) weapons, and just as common as a fixed [emblem](#emblem) on a [banner](#banner) or a [crest](#crest).

entries.name: tsuba_(guard)
entries.description: The hand [guard](#guard) fitted between blade and grip on a Japanese [sword](#sword) or [polearm](#polearm), most often a disc but sometimes squared or four-lobed. It shields the hand and gives the fingers a fixed reference point on the [hilt](#hilt).

entries.name: two-handed_sword
entries.description: A long, [heavy](#heavy) blade with a grip sized for both hands, such as a [greatsword](#greatsword) or [zweihander](#zweihander). Its bulk usually shows in how the wielder [braces](#braces) before [swinging](#swinging) it.

entries.name: butterfly_swords
entries.description: A matched pair of short, broad, single-edged Chinese blades, fought with one in each hand. The wide blade and small knuckle [guard](#guard) identify them.

entries.name: zweihander
entries.description: A very large European [two-handed](#two-handed) [sword](#sword) with a long grip and small parrying hooks set above the blunt base of the blade. Swung much like a [polearm](#polearm), and closely associated with Renaissance-era mercenary soldiers.

entries.name: chainsword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) whose [cutting](#cutting) edge is a [running](#running) [chainsaw](#chainsaw), the [teeth](#teeth) travelling around the blade. Do not confuse it with a [whip](#whip) sword, whose segments are threaded on a cord.

entries.name: saya_(scabbard)
entries.description: The Japanese [scabbard](#scabbard), traditionally lacquered wood, with a knob on the side for the cord that ties it to the [belt](#belt). Tagged when the [sheath](#sheath) is on show, whether [holding](#holding) a blade or empty.

entries.name: chokutou
entries.description: An [old](#old) straight-bladed Japanese [sword](#sword) with a single [cutting](#cutting) edge, older than the curved [katana](#katana) and modelled on continental Chinese swords. The dead-straight blade is the giveaway.

entries.name: kukri
entries.description: A Nepalese [knife](#knife) whose [spine](#spine) kinks forward, [giving](#giving) an inward-curving edge that puts [weight](#weight) behind every [chop](#chop). It serves as a [working](#working) tool and as a [fighting](#fighting) blade alike.

entries.name: needle_sword
entries.description: An outsized [sewing](#sewing) [needle](#needle) wielded as a blade, its eye [standing](#standing) in for the pommel. It marks a fighter whose [weapon](#weapon) comes out of a sewing [box](#box) rather than an armoury.

entries.name: kama_(weapon)
entries.description: A short [sickle](#sickle) with a stubby [handle](#handle) and a curved blade set almost [square](#square) to it, used as a [weapon](#weapon) rather than for [cutting](#cutting) grain. It looks like a [scythe](#scythe) in [miniature](#miniature) and is often carried in pairs or fixed to a [chain](#chain).

entries.name: jamadhar
entries.description: An Indian push [dagger](#dagger) whose grip runs crosswise between two side [bars](#bars), so the blade juts straight out from a closed fist. It is commonly called a katar.

entries.name: kodachi
entries.description: A short Japanese [sword](#sword), close to a [wakizashi](#wakizashi) in length but meant as a main [weapon](#weapon) in its own right, with a longer grip and a deeper curve. It let [people](#people) barred from [carrying](#carrying) a [katana](#katana) go armed.

entries.name: planted_knife
entries.description: A [knife](#knife) driven point-down into the ground, a [table](#table), or another surface so it stands upright. The blade is embedded there, not held in hand.

entries.name: hand_guard
entries.description: The part of a [weapon](#weapon) that protects the gripping hand: the [cross](#cross), [cup](#cup) or [basket](#basket) above a sword's grip, or the shroud a [rifle](#rifle) is held by. It counts as part of the weapon rather than as worn equipment.

entries.name: double-sided_axe
entries.description: An [axe](#axe) whose head carries a [cutting](#cutting) edge on both sides instead of one edge and a blunt [back](#back). A favourite shape for [barbarian](#barbarian) and [fantasy](#fantasy) designs.

entries.name: hilt
entries.description: The [handle](#handle) end of a bladed [weapon](#weapon), grip and [guard](#guard) and pommel, made the point of interest. It suits a [sword](#sword) still [sheathed](#sheathed) or a hand [resting](#resting) ready to draw.

entries.name: tsuka-ito
entries.description: The cord wrapped in a criss-cross pattern around the grip of a Japanese [sword](#sword). Traditionally [silk](#silk), though cotton and [leather](#leather) are common on more modern pieces.

entries.name: sword_hilt
entries.description: Only the grip, [guard](#guard) and pommel are shown, with [no](#no) blade present or conjured. Do not add the [plain](#plain) [sword](#sword) [tag](#tag) or [holding_sword](#holding_sword) here; a [broken](#broken) blade or a [sheathed](#sheathed) [weapon](#weapon) still counts as a whole sword.

entries.name: fire_axe
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [axe](#axe) with a pick spike opposite the [cutting](#cutting) edge, standard firefighting kit. The spike levers doors and windows open and helps work the blade free again.

entries.name: golden_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) with a [gold](#gold) blade or gold fittings, made more for [display](#display) than for use. Ceremonial, divine and game-item weapons take this form.

entries.name: tsuka_(handle)
entries.description: The [hilt](#hilt) of a Japanese [sword](#sword), a wooden [core](#core) covered in rayskin and [bound](#bound) with cord. Sits behind the [guard](#guard) and, on a [katana](#katana), takes both hands.

entries.name: balisong
entries.description: A folding [knife](#knife) whose two handles [swing](#swing) apart around the tang, the blade tucked into grooves in them when it is shut. Named for its Philippine origin, it is usually drawn mid-flip.

entries.name: too_many_knives
entries.description: A character [carrying](#carrying) or [throwing](#throwing) knives by the dozen, fanned between the fingers or [hanging](#hanging) in the air around them.

entries.name: epee
entries.description: A fencing [sword](#sword) with a stiff blade of triangular section and a large [bell](#bell) [guard](#guard), heavier in the hand than a foil. It comes with the white [jacket](#jacket), glove and [mesh](#mesh) [mask](#mask) of the sport.

entries.name: winged_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) decorated with [wings](#wings), usually flaring out from the crossguard. It is ornamental rather than functional, a [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) and game [weapon](#weapon) design.

entries.name: dao
entries.description: A Chinese single-edged sabre, most often the gently curved willow-leaf form. Its straight, double-edged counterpart is the jian.

entries.name: gun
entries.description: Any firearm that fires bullets by [explosive](#explosive) propellant, from pistols and rifles to shotguns, [machine](#machine) guns and antique flintlocks. Sci-fi [energy](#energy) weapons that [fire](#fire) [no](#no) bullets are excluded; pair it with a specific type and an action like [holding_gun](#holding_gun) or [aiming](#aiming).

entries.name: rifle
entries.description: A long [gun](#gun) fired from the shoulder, including carbines and every subtype from bolt-action to assault and sniper rifles. Tag the specific subtype or [model](#model) too; a short [handgun](#handgun) does not count.

entries.name: handgun
entries.description: A short-barrelled firearm meant to be fired from the hand at close range, covering semi-automatic pistols, revolvers, flintlocks, derringers and [machine](#machine) pistols. The hand shape that mimics one is [finger_gun](#finger_gun).

entries.name: assault_rifle
entries.description: A [military](#military) [rifle](#rifle) [firing](#firing) an intermediate cartridge from a detachable magazine, switchable between single shots and automatic [fire](#fire). Name the [model](#model), AK, M16, FAMAS or AUG, where it [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: submachine_gun
entries.description: A compact, fully automatic firearm chambered for pistol rounds, such as the MP5, the Uzi or the Thompson. Machine pistols and personal defence weapons like the P90 also fall under it. Implies [gun](#gun).

entries.name: sniper_rifle
entries.description: A precision [rifle](#rifle) built to hit targets at long range, almost always fitted with a telescopic sight and often a folding [bipod](#bipod) for a steady rest. Covers everything from World War II bolt-actions with a [scope](#scope) bolted on to purpose-built modern designs. Tag it alongside rifle.

entries.name: revolver
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) with a rotating cylinder [holding](#holding) several rounds that turns with each shot. Almost always also a [handgun](#handgun), though rare revolver rifles and shotguns exist; [tag](#tag) the specific [model](#model) when it is recognisable.

entries.name: machine_gun
entries.description: A firearm built for sustained automatic [fire](#fire), covering light models one person [can](#can) carry as [well](#well) as crew-served medium and [heavy](#heavy) guns. It is bigger and holds more [ammunition](#ammunition) than an assault or [battle](#battle) [rifle](#rifle).

entries.name: bullet
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) projectile, or the whole cartridge with its casing, shown loaded, held, scattered or in flight. Most drawings show the complete cartridge even where only the projectile is meant.

entries.name: shotgun
entries.description: A smoothbore [gun](#gun) that fires shells of pellets or a solid [slug](#slug), devastating at close range but short in reach. Types include double-barrelled, pump-action, lever-action and sawn-off. Implies gun.

entries.name: bolt_action
entries.description: A firearm whose action the shooter works by hand, [pulling](#pulling) a bolt [handle](#handle) [back](#back) and forward to chamber each round. Nearly always a [rifle](#rifle), so name the [weapon](#weapon) type as [well](#well).

entries.name: scope
entries.description: The telescopic sight mounted on a [rifle](#rifle) or other [gun](#gun) to magnify the [target](#target). Also covers bulkier electronic sights with [night](#night) or thermal modes.

entries.name: magazine_(weapon)
entries.description: The spring-loaded [container](#container) that holds cartridges and feeds them into a repeating firearm, whether seated in the [gun](#gun), held for a reload or stowed spare in a [pouch](#pouch). A [clip_(weapon)](#clip_(weapon)) is the flat strip used to charge a fixed magazine, and is a different thing.

entries.name: bullpup
entries.description: A [rifle](#rifle) or [shotgun](#shotgun) laid out with its action and magazine behind the trigger, beside the shooter's cheek, keeping the [weapon](#weapon) short for its [barrel](#barrel) length. The FAMAS, AUG, P90 and Tavor are the [familiar](#familiar) [shapes](#shapes).

entries.name: ammunition
entries.description: Bullets, shells or cartridges for a [gun](#gun) or similar [weapon](#weapon), loose, boxed, in a magazine or [lying](#lying) spent. Rounds joined into a [chain](#chain) are [ammunition_belt](#ammunition_belt).

entries.name: shell_casing
entries.description: The empty metal or plastic cartridge case ejected from a [gun](#gun) after [firing](#firing), often drawn [flying](#flying) from a semiautomatic [weapon](#weapon) or scattered on the ground. A loaded round is [bullet](#bullet) or cartridge instead.

entries.name: suppressor
entries.description: A [tube](#tube) attached to a gun's muzzle that quiets the shot and hides the [flash](#flash), popularly called a silencer. Tag it whenever one is fitted to a visible firearm.

entries.name: kalashnikov_rifle
entries.description: Any self-loading [rifle](#rifle) built on the AK-47 pattern, licensed copies included, and the fallback for an AK whose exact [model](#model) cannot be [pinned](#pinned) down. Similar-looking rifles of other designs, and unlicensed imitations, have tags of their own.

entries.name: anti-materiel_rifle
entries.description: An oversized [rifle](#rifle) of .50 calibre or larger, built to wreck vehicles, [aircraft](#aircraft) and equipment rather than [people](#people). Its length, [heavy](#heavy) muzzle brake and [bipod](#bipod) give it away.

entries.name: gatling_gun
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [gun](#gun) with a cluster of barrels that rotate as it fires, from the hand-cranked original to modern rotary [cannon](#cannon). One small enough for a person to carry is a [minigun](#minigun).

entries.name: gun_sling
entries.description: A [strap](#strap) fixed to a firearm for [carrying](#carrying) it over the shoulder. Not a stone-throwing sling_(weapon), nor an [arm_sling](#arm_sling) for an injured limb.

entries.name: ammunition_belt
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) of cartridges linked together to feed a [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) or [minigun](#minigun). A [sash](#sash) of rounds worn across the chest is a [bandolier](#bandolier), and a carried case is an [ammunition_pouch](#ammunition_pouch).

entries.name: shoulder_holster
entries.description: A [handgun](#handgun) [holster](#holster) worn on the chest, its straps crossing over the shoulders with the [gun](#gun) [sitting](#sitting) under the armpit, often hidden beneath a [jacket](#jacket). Implies holster.

entries.name: battle_rifle
entries.description: A select-fire [rifle](#rifle) [firing](#firing) full-power [ammunition](#ammunition) from a detachable magazine, the class [standing](#standing) between semi-automatic rifles and [lighter](#lighter) assault rifles. Largely replaced in front-line service, it lingers in marksman and [police](#police) roles; [tag](#tag) the exact [model](#model) when it [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: antique_firearm
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) shaped like the firearms of the early nineteenth century or earlier: [flintlock](#flintlock) pistols, muskets, blunderbusses. The mechanism need not actually be [old](#old), since the old look is enough.

entries.name: shoulder_cannon
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) or [cannon](#cannon) mounted directly on a character's or a mecha's shoulder, as on the Guncannon or the Doom Slayer. Tag the type of gun where it [can](#can) be identified.

entries.name: smoking_barrel
entries.description: Wisps of [smoke](#smoke) rise from the muzzle of a [gun](#gun) that was just fired. Tag beside smoke; often paired with [firing](#firing) or [aiming](#aiming).

entries.name: light_machine_gun
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) light enough for one [soldier](#soldier) to carry and [fire](#fire), fed by [belt](#belt) or magazine, such as the Bren, M249 or RPK. Heavier crew-served weapons take [machine_gun](#machine_gun) or [heavy_machine_gun](#heavy_machine_gun).

entries.name: m1911
entries.description: The classic American .45 semi-automatic pistol, with an exposed [hammer](#hammer), a beavertail behind the grip and a thumb safety, fed from a seven-round magazine. The [tag](#tag) covers any [handgun](#handgun) built to that pattern, the revised M1911A1 included.

entries.name: ar-15
entries.description: The civilian semi-automatic [rifle](#rifle) of that design, or any similar rifle whose exact [model](#model) cannot be named, in a non-military setting. Its [military](#military) relatives such as the M16, M4 carbine and HK416 have tags of their own.

entries.name: pump_action
entries.description: A firearm cycled by [sliding](#sliding) its fore-grip [back](#back) and forth, most [familiar](#familiar) on shotguns. Tag it when the mechanism itself is visible or being worked.

entries.name: grenade_launcher
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) that throws [grenade](#grenade) rounds further and more accurately than an arm could, either standalone or slung under a [rifle](#rifle); crew-served and vehicle-mounted automatics count too. A rocket-propelled grenade launcher is a separate weapon and must not be tagged as this.

entries.name: shotgun_shell
entries.description: A [shotgun](#shotgun) cartridge, a coloured plastic [tube](#tube) on a brass base. Tag whenever one is visible, often tucked into a [bandolier](#bandolier); an empty fired one is [shell_casing](#shell_casing), and one [flying](#flying) out of the [gun](#gun) is [casing_ejection](#casing_ejection).

entries.name: p90
entries.description: A compact [bullpup](#bullpup) submachine [gun](#gun) with its magazine [lying](#lying) flat along the top of the receiver and a smooth, futuristic [outline](#outline). Spent cases drop out of the bottom and the sight sits in the carry [handle](#handle).

entries.name: firelock
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) from before cartridges, where an external mechanism sets loose powder alight: a smouldering cord, [sparks](#sparks) struck from flint or pyrite, or a percussion cap. Use it when the mechanism cannot be made out, and the specific [tag](#tag) when it [can](#can).

entries.name: musket
entries.description: A long smooth-bored [gun](#gun) loaded down the [barrel](#barrel) and fired from the shoulder, recognisable by the [lock](#lock) [plate](#plate) on its side. It was the standard arm of soldiers, hunters and pirates before repeating firearms.

entries.name: bipod
entries.description: A folding two-legged rest clamped near the muzzle of a [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) or sniper [rifle](#rifle), propping it up so the shooter [can](#can) hold a position without tiring. Usually shown deployed on the ground or a [ledge](#ledge).

entries.name: vertical_foregrip
entries.description: An upright [handle](#handle) fitted beneath the [barrel](#barrel) of a [rifle](#rifle) or submachine [gun](#gun) so the shooter [can](#can) steady it with the second hand. Usually a solid bar [hanging](#hanging) from the handguard, though some weapons use a [strap](#strap) instead.

entries.name: casing_ejection
entries.description: Spent cases [fly](#fly) clear of a firearm, thrown out as it fires or worked loose by hand with a [slide](#slide), a [pump](#pump) or an opened [revolver](#revolver) cylinder. The brass is [caught](#caught) in mid-air.

entries.name: drum_magazine
entries.description: A wide cylindrical magazine that coils its cartridges around a central spindle, [carrying](#carrying) far more rounds than a [box](#box). Goes with submachine guns and light [machine](#machine) guns.

entries.name: optical_sight
entries.description: A non-magnifying [aiming](#aiming) [device](#device) on a firearm that lays a dot or reticle over the [target](#target), such as a red dot or holographic unit; a few [rifle](#rifle) designs carry one built in. Long magnifying tubes for precision shooting are a [scope](#scope) instead.

entries.name: mg42
entries.description: A German wartime [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) with a squared-off, more heavily perforated [barrel](#barrel) shroud and a fearsome rate of [fire](#fire). Stamped from sheet metal for cheap production, and fed by [belt](#belt) or [drum](#drum) magazine.

entries.name: minigun
entries.description: A motor-driven rotary [gun](#gun) with a [spinning](#spinning) cluster of barrels, carried by hand in defiance of how [heavy](#heavy) it actually is.

entries.name: anti-aircraft_gun
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) mounted so it [can](#can) [swing](#swing) steeply upward at [aircraft](#aircraft), from multi-barrelled [machine](#machine) guns to [heavy](#heavy) [cannon](#cannon). Wartime and [mecha](#mecha) settings are where it appears.

entries.name: flintlock
entries.description: An early [gun](#gun) fired by a spring-driven cock that scrapes flint on steel, [dropping](#dropping) [sparks](#sparks) into a powder pan beside the [barrel](#barrel). Standard for pirates and eighteenth-century soldiers, later displaced by percussion locks.

entries.name: mosin-nagant
entries.description: The Russian bolt-action [rifle](#rifle) adopted in the 1890s and carried through both world wars. Its straight bolt [handle](#handle), slotted sling mounts and the five-round magazine bulging ahead of the trigger [guard](#guard) identify it.

entries.name: rifle_cartridge
entries.description: Ammunition sized for rifles, longer and heavier than pistol rounds but smaller than [cannon](#cannon) shells. Typically bottlenecked and rimless, covering everything from intermediate calibres up to [heavy](#heavy) [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) rounds.

entries.name: laser_sight
entries.description: A small module clamped to a firearm that throws a coloured beam at the [target](#target) to help the shooter aim. It is neither a handheld presentation [pointer](#pointer) nor a beam fired from a character's eyes.

entries.name: kriss_vector
entries.description: A modern submachine [gun](#gun) with a boxy angular receiver and a magazine [running](#running) down through the grip. Its unusual bolt travel pushes recoil downward so the muzzle stays level on automatic [fire](#fire).

entries.name: eotech
entries.description: A boxy holographic [gun](#gun) sight with an open rectangular [window](#window), clamped to a rifle's top rail for quick [aiming](#aiming) at close range. Drawn on modern [military](#military) and [police](#police) weapons rather than on older rifles.

entries.name: heavy_machine_gun
entries.description: A large-calibre belt-fed [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) built for sustained suppressing [fire](#fire) and for [punching](#punching) through light [cover](#cover). Too [heavy](#heavy) to carry, it is set on a [tripod](#tripod), a vehicle or an emplacement.

entries.name: tank_shell
entries.description: A large-caliber [cannon](#cannon) round for an armored vehicle, drawn either as a brass case topped by a pointed projectile or as the projectile alone. Often shown held by a loader, stacked in a rack, or [streaking](#streaking) through the air.

entries.name: ammunition_box
entries.description: A metal or plastic case [holding](#holding) cartridges, sometimes clipped under a [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) to feed a [belt](#belt). Unlike a magazine it has [no](#no) spring, so it only stores and guides the rounds.

entries.name: m16a1
entries.description: An early [model](#model) of the American M16 [rifle](#rifle), told apart by its triangular handguard and its twenty-round magazine. It is the pattern most associated with the Vietnam [war](#war).

entries.name: foregrip
entries.description: A grip jutting from the front of a [gun](#gun) for the support hand to hold, steadying the [weapon](#weapon) as it fires. Some designs build it in permanently, others let it fold away.

entries.name: sig_556
entries.description: A SIG Sauer assault [rifle](#rifle) made from [2007](#2007) to [2016](#2016), derived from the earlier SG550 but fitted with an AR-15-style lower receiver and magazine [well](#well). Produced in both 5.56 NATO and 7.62x39 chamberings, with Picatinny rails along the top.

entries.name: arisaka
entries.description: The Japanese bolt-action service [rifle](#rifle) [family](#family) carried from the late 1890s until 1945, fed from a five-round internal magazine by a [stripper](#stripper) clip. The long Type 38 and shorter Type 99 are the ones usually drawn, their receivers stamped with an imperial [chrysanthemum](#chrysanthemum).

entries.name: thompson_submachine_gun
entries.description: The American .45 submachine [gun](#gun) of the interwar years, known for its finned [barrel](#barrel), vertical [foregrip](#foregrip) and [drum](#drum) or [stick](#stick) magazine. Associated equally with Prohibition-era gangsters and Second World War infantry.

entries.name: sig_mpx
entries.description: A compact SIG Sauer submachine [gun](#gun) introduced in [2015](#2015), built with a gas-piston action and [heavy](#heavy) rail coverage. Rare in real service but a regular sight in fan art of certain gacha games.

entries.name: muzzle_device
entries.description: A fitting screwed onto the end of a [gun](#gun) [barrel](#barrel) to tame recoil and muzzle rise, such as a brake, compensator or [flash](#flash) hider. A small detail that says how the [weapon](#weapon) has been set up.

entries.name: dragunov_svd
entries.description: A Soviet semi-automatic marksman's [rifle](#rifle) with a thumbhole stock, long slotted handguards and a [scope](#scope) mounted off the left of the receiver. Its resemblance to a Kalashnikov is only skin deep.

entries.name: walther_wa_2000
entries.description: A rare [bullpup](#bullpup) marksman's [rifle](#rifle) with wooden furniture and a [barrel](#barrel) clamped at both ends. Barely more than a hundred and seventy were built, which is part of its appeal in fiction.

entries.name: luger_p08
entries.description: A German semi-automatic pistol carried through both World Wars, unmistakable for the toggle-lock action that hinges up above the grip. Long-barrelled versions with a [drum](#drum) magazine and a shoulder stock belong here too.

entries.name: underbarrel_grenade_launcher
entries.description: A short launcher mounted beneath the [barrel](#barrel) of a [rifle](#rifle), letting the same [weapon](#weapon) [fire](#fire) grenades. It sits forward of the magazine with its own trigger and grip.

entries.name: m14
entries.description: An American 7.62mm [battle](#battle) [rifle](#rifle) built along the lines of the M1 Garand but fed from a detachable twenty-round magazine and able to [fire](#fire) automatically. Replaced as a service rifle in the 1960s, it stayed on for marksman work thanks to its reach and accuracy.

entries.name: mp40
entries.description: The German submachine [gun](#gun) of the Second World War, chambered in 9mm and built largely from stamped steel. Its under-folding stock and long straight magazine make it easy to pick out.

entries.name: sig_p220/p226
entries.description: The SIG Sauer P220 semi-automatic pistol and its double-stack successor the P226, which share a decocking [lever](#lever) and a squared trigger [guard](#guard). The compact P225 variant is filed under this [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: m1903_springfield
entries.description: An American bolt-action [rifle](#rifle) built on the Mauser action with a five-round internal magazine, carried through both World Wars and kept afterwards for sniping. Recognise it by the straight-grip stock, the bent bolt [handle](#handle) and the flip-up rear sight.

entries.name: lever_action
entries.description: A [rifle](#rifle) or [shotgun](#shotgun) cycled by [swinging](#swinging) a loop under the grip, which throws out the spent case and chambers the next round. The loop around the trigger gives it away, and the type is a [staple](#staple) of western settings.

entries.name: mac-10/11
entries.description: A blocky American [machine](#machine) pistol with its charging [handle](#handle) on top of the receiver, a retractable [wire](#wire) stock and a short [strap](#strap) at the front used as a [foregrip](#foregrip). The MAC-11 is the smaller version of the same design, and a threaded [barrel](#barrel) for a [suppressor](#suppressor) is common.

entries.name: folding_stock
entries.description: A [rifle](#rifle) butt hinged so it [can](#can) [swing](#swing) against the receiver, shortening the [weapon](#weapon) for [carrying](#carrying) or storage. Most swing to the side, a few over the top or beneath.

entries.name: lee-enfield
entries.description: A British bolt-action [rifle](#rifle) in .303, [feeding](#feeding) from a detachable ten-round magazine usually topped up with [stripper](#stripper) clips. It armed British and Commonwealth troops through both world wars and is known by its blunt [nose](#nose) cap and sharply bent bolt [handle](#handle).

entries.name: uzi
entries.description: The blocky Israeli submachine [gun](#gun) of the 1950s, known by its [square](#square) receiver, angular trigger [guard](#guard) and magazine loaded through the grip. The [tag](#tag) covers the full-size version, usually drawn with its folding metal stock.

entries.name: double-barreled_shotgun
entries.description: A [shotgun](#shotgun) with two barrels, either side by side or stacked one over the other, usually hinged open at the breech to load. Frequently drawn sawn short in western, [wasteland](#wasteland) and horror scenes.

entries.name: l85
entries.description: The standard British assault [rifle](#rifle), a [bullpup](#bullpup) with its magazine behind the trigger, a stubby [outline](#outline) and a broad handguard. Early production earned a poor reputation for reliability that a later [factory](#factory) rebuild largely repaired.

entries.name: thompson/center_contender
entries.description: A break-action single-shot firearm made in both pistol and [rifle](#rifle) lengths. Its angular grip, wide trigger [guard](#guard) and stubby forend beneath the [barrel](#barrel) give it an unmistakable [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: lanchester_smg
entries.description: A British submachine [gun](#gun) of the Second World War, copied from a German design and issued mostly to naval crews. A [heavy](#heavy) wooden stock, brass magazine housing and a [bayonet](#bayonet) lug mark it out.

entries.name: sig_mcx
entries.description: A modular SIG Sauer [rifle](#rifle) [family](#family) whose upper receiver mates to standard AR-15 lowers with an adapter. Covers the original [model](#model) along with its Virtus, short-barreled Rattler and larger-caliber Spear variants.

entries.name: sig_516
entries.description: A gas-piston assault [rifle](#rifle) built on the AR-15 pattern by SIG Sauer. Recognizable by its rail-covered handguard alongside a [familiar](#familiar) magazine [well](#well) and pistol grip.

entries.name: manually-operated_mounted_gun
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) fixed to a vehicle mount and worked by hand rather than from inside, such as the [machine](#machine) gun over a [tank](#tank) [hatch](#hatch) or the [cannon](#cannon) bolted to a pickup [bed](#bed). Anything from a light machine gun to an [autocannon](#autocannon) may sit on one.

entries.name: walther_ppk
entries.description: A compact blowback pistol of German design, famous as a spy's sidearm. Short [barrel](#barrel), rounded [slide](#slide) and a small finger-rest magazine identify it.

entries.name: iwi_tavor
entries.description: An Israeli assault [rifle](#rifle) of [bullpup](#bullpup) layout, the magazine [sitting](#sitting) behind the trigger so the [weapon](#weapon) looks short and blocky with the grip [well](#well) forward. It is chambered in 5.56 and built in several [barrel](#barrel) lengths.

entries.name: p14_enfield
entries.description: A British bolt-action service [rifle](#rifle) of the First World War, chambered in .303 with a five-round magazine built into the stock. Most were made under contract by American factories.

entries.name: stg44
entries.description: The German wartime [rifle](#rifle) that gave the assault rifle its name, [firing](#firing) a shortened 7.92mm cartridge. Its curved magazine, stamped receiver and long handguard set the pattern that postwar designs followed.

entries.name: welrod
entries.description: A wartime assassination pistol built around a [fat](#fat) [suppressor](#suppressor) [tube](#tube) and worked by hand between shots. Its rear bolt knob and rod-like body make it hard to mistake for anything else.

entries.name: em-2
entries.description: A short British [rifle](#rifle) trialled in the early 1950s, with the magazine set behind the trigger and the sight built into the carry [handle](#handle). Wooden furniture and a bulged handguard mark it out, and its layout was later echoed in the SA80.

entries.name: qbz-95
entries.description: A Chinese-made assault [rifle](#rifle) built in [bullpup](#bullpup) configuration, with the action and magazine positioned behind the trigger grip and a [carrying](#carrying) [handle](#handle) along the top. The stubby, compact [profile](#profile) is what makes it recognizable.

entries.name: m1_garand
entries.description: The American semi-automatic service [rifle](#rifle) of the Second World War and Korea, loaded from an eight-round en-bloc clip. The clip springs free with a distinctive ping once the last shot is fired.

entries.name: m249_saw
entries.description: A gas-operated 5.56mm light [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) issued at squad level, with a quick-change [barrel](#barrel) and a folding [bipod](#bipod). It feeds from linked belts or, at need, from [rifle](#rifle) [box](#box) magazines.

entries.name: winchester_model_1887
entries.description: A lever-action [shotgun](#shotgun) from the late nineteenth century, recognisable by the large loop [lever](#lever) beneath its receiver. Western scenes favour it, along with characters who spin it one-handed to reload.

entries.name: steyr_aug
entries.description: An Austrian [bullpup](#bullpup) [rifle](#rifle) with the magazine set behind the trigger, a wraparound trigger [guard](#guard), a folding vertical [foregrip](#foregrip) and an optic built into the carry [handle](#handle). The green polymer [shell](#shell) makes it unmistakable. The HBAR variant adds a long [heavy](#heavy) [barrel](#barrel) and a [bipod](#bipod).

entries.name: acog
entries.description: A compact telescopic [gun](#gun) sight at fixed low magnification, its reticle lit by fibre optics and tritium instead of batteries. It sits on the top rail of rifles in modern [military](#military) art.

entries.name: ankle_gun
entries.description: A compact firearm carried low on the leg, strapped just above the shoe and usually hidden by a trouser cuff. A concealed-carry detail in spy and crime pictures.

entries.name: m1918_bar
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) American selective-fire [rifle](#rifle) in .30-06, in practice a light [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun), with a [bipod](#bipod) folding down near the muzzle and a one-piece wooden forearm. Foreign-built copies of the same design count as [well](#well).

entries.name: m60_(machine_gun)
entries.description: A belt-fed American 7.62mm general-purpose [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) adopted in 1957 and carried heavily in Vietnam. Its bulk and its appetite for [ammunition](#ammunition) earned it the nickname the Pig.

entries.name: locked_slide
entries.description: The [slide](#slide) of a semi-automatic pistol held [back](#back) in the open position, leaving the breech exposed. It happens once the last round is fired and the magazine runs dry, and again during a reload.

entries.name: mg34
entries.description: A German belt-fed [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) from the 1930s, recognizable by its round-perforated tubular [barrel](#barrel) [jacket](#jacket) and quick-change barrel. Costly to manufacture, which is why the [mg42](#mg42) eventually took over from it.

entries.name: reflex_sight
entries.description: A compact sight mounted on a firearm that projects an illuminated dot onto a small [glass](#glass) [window](#window), letting the shooter aim with both eyes open. Its open squared frame distinguishes it from a [tube](#tube) [scope](#scope).

entries.name: snubnosed_revolver
entries.description: A [revolver](#revolver) built with a very short [barrel](#barrel) on a small frame, sometimes with the [hammer](#hammer) shrouded or removed for a smoother draw. The Smith & Wesson Model 36 is the classic example.

entries.name: walther_p38
entries.description: A German service pistol of the Second World War whose open-topped [slide](#slide) leaves the [barrel](#barrel) exposed. It replaced an older toggle-locked design and shaped many later handguns.

entries.name: m203
entries.description: A single-shot 40mm [grenade](#grenade) launcher clamped beneath a rifle's [barrel](#barrel), letting one [soldier](#soldier) [switch](#switch) instantly between the two. Designed for the M16 [family](#family), it has been fitted to plenty of other rifles.

entries.name: m16a2
entries.description: A revised M16 with a reworked [barrel](#barrel) able to carry a launcher slung beneath it, along with changes to the sights, handguard and stock. It fires single shots or three-round bursts rather than fully automatic.

entries.name: winchester_model_1897
entries.description: An early pump-action [shotgun](#shotgun) with an exposed [hammer](#hammer) and a [tube](#tube) magazine beneath the [barrel](#barrel). Its trench-gun version made it a fixture of First World War imagery.

entries.name: cocked_hammer
entries.description: The [hammer](#hammer) of a [revolver](#revolver) or pistol is drawn [back](#back) and [waiting](#waiting), so the [weapon](#weapon) fires at a touch of the trigger. A small detail that sharpens the tension of a standoff.

entries.name: aa-12
entries.description: A fully automatic combat [shotgun](#shotgun) with a squared, bulky body, fed from a [box](#box) magazine or a large [drum](#drum). Its distinctive [silhouette](#silhouette) makes it a favourite in action and [military](#military) art.

entries.name: type_100_smg
entries.description: A Japanese submachine [gun](#gun) of the Second World War, chambered for a small pistol round. It carries a full wooden [rifle](#rifle) stock with [no](#no) separate pistol grip, and the magazine feeds in from the left side.

entries.name: fabarm_fp6
entries.description: An Italian 12-gauge pump-action [shotgun](#shotgun) with a ribbed handguard, sold for [police](#police) and civilian use. Often fitted with a pistol grip or a folding stock.

entries.name: m134_minigun
entries.description: A six-barrelled rotary [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) spun by an external motor, [firing](#firing) thousands of rounds a minute. Spot it by the [handlebar](#handlebar) above the [barrel](#barrel) cluster, the cylindrical feed at the side and the [stick](#stick) grip with its firing button; unnamed rotary guns go under [minigun](#minigun).

entries.name: finger_cannon
entries.description: The fingers themselves are [gun](#gun) barrels, so the hand shoots without [holding](#holding) anything. Standard equipment for androids and cyborgs. A hand merely shaped like a pistol is [finger_gun](#finger_gun).

entries.name: airsoft
entries.description: Replica guns that [fire](#fire) small plastic pellets while copying real firearms as closely as they [can](#can). They stand in for real weapons in settings where those are tightly restricted.

entries.name: rpk-16
entries.description: A Russian squad automatic [weapon](#weapon) of [2016](#2016) in 5.45mm, built on the long-stroke [piston](#piston) action of the AK [family](#family) with rails, a folding stock and a detachable [bipod](#bipod). It feeds from a [drum](#drum) magazine and takes interchangeable barrels.

entries.name: lahti-saloranta_m/26
entries.description: A Finnish light [machine](#machine) [gun](#gun) of the years between the wars, fed from a [box](#box) magazine and rested on a [bipod](#bipod). Its vented [barrel](#barrel) shroud and pistol grip give it away.

entries.name: nagant_m1895
entries.description: A seven-shot Russian service [revolver](#revolver) whose gas-sealing cylinder lets it take a silencer, rare among revolvers. Reloading is slow, one round at a time through a [gate](#gate), and the cylinder does not [swing](#swing) out.

entries.name: 9a-91
entries.description: A stubby Russian assault [rifle](#rifle) [firing](#firing) a [heavy](#heavy) subsonic round, built in the early 1990s as a cheap compact [weapon](#weapon). Its short body, top-folding stock and screw-on [suppressor](#suppressor) make it easy to recognise.

entries.name: ptrd-41
entries.description: A Soviet anti-tank [rifle](#rifle) from the Second World War: enormous, single-shot, bolt-operated, and typically fired from a [bipod](#bipod). Its extreme length and [heavy](#heavy) muzzle brake make it recognisable at a [glance](#glance).

entries.name: pepperbox_revolver
entries.description: An early multi-barrelled [handgun](#handgun) in which the whole cluster of barrels turns, instead of a cylinder [feeding](#feeding) one fixed [barrel](#barrel). Stubby and nose-heavy, and firmly nineteenth-century.

entries.name: clip_(weapon)
entries.description: A metal strip [holding](#holding) cartridges together so a firearm [can](#can) be loaded in one motion, in [stripper](#stripper), [moon](#moon) or en bloc form. A magazine is the box-shaped [container](#container) the rounds sit inside and is not this.

entries.name: micro_uzi
entries.description: The smallest of the Uzi [machine](#machine) pistols, barely longer than a hand, with [no](#no) forearm and a very short [barrel](#barrel). Fired one-handed or wielded as a pair.

entries.name: m16a4
entries.description: The last of the M16 service rifles, a light gas-operated [weapon](#weapon) fed from a magazine and [firing](#firing) single shots or three-round bursts. It usually carries a flat-top rail on the receiver in place of a fixed [carrying](#carrying) [handle](#handle).

entries.name: matchlock
entries.description: The earliest firearm [lock](#lock), in which a [lever](#lever) lowers a smouldering cord into a pan of priming powder. Found on arquebuses and on the Japanese tanegashima, and later displaced by the [flintlock](#flintlock).

entries.name: derringer
entries.description: A tiny [pocket](#pocket) pistol with a stubby [barrel](#barrel) [holding](#holding) only one or two rounds, sometimes four. Fiction reaches for it as a concealed or last-resort [weapon](#weapon) rather than a [serious](#serious) sidearm.

entries.name: sawed-off_shotgun
entries.description: A [shotgun](#shotgun) with its [barrel](#barrel) and stock cut down so it [can](#can) be hidden under a [coat](#coat). Most are double-barrelled guns cut [back](#back) until they are barely longer than a [heavy](#heavy) [handgun](#handgun), which puts them outside the law in many places.

entries.name: nambu_type_14
entries.description: The standard Japanese [army](#army) sidearm of the world [war](#war) years, a slim pistol with a narrow grip. Its [outline](#outline) invites [comparison](#comparison) with the German Luger, though the mechanism differs.

entries.name: dual_drum_magazine
entries.description: Two [drum](#drum) magazines paired side by side on one [weapon](#weapon) for twice the [ammunition](#ammunition). Bulky, and typical of [machine](#machine) guns.

entries.name: adaptive_combat_rifle
entries.description: A modular American assault [rifle](#rifle) whose [barrel](#barrel), bolt and magazine [can](#can) be swapped to change calibre. Its lines recall the SCAR, with features borrowed from the AR-15 and G36.

entries.name: vsk-94
entries.description: A Russian suppressed marksman's [rifle](#rifle) [firing](#firing) [heavy](#heavy) subsonic rounds, with a [fat](#fat) [tube](#tube) [running](#running) the length of the [barrel](#barrel). Its blocky polymer body sets it apart from other quiet designs.

entries.name: arquebus
entries.description: An early long [gun](#gun) of the fifteenth century onward, set off by a [matchlock](#matchlock) or wheellock and steadied against the shoulder. The version that reached Japan through Portuguese traders is the tanegashima.

entries.name: steyr_iws_2000
entries.description: A bulky Austrian single-shot anti-materiel [rifle](#rifle) [firing](#firing) fin-stabilised sabot rounds from a smoothbore [barrel](#barrel). Despite its size it is carried and fired by one [soldier](#soldier), [resting](#resting) on a [bipod](#bipod) behind a large muzzle brake.

entries.name: angled_foregrip
entries.description: A grip fitted under a rifle's handguard at a slant rather than straight down, so the supporting hand rests forward along it. It is a detail for firearm pictures, set against the vertical kind.

entries.name: staff
entries.description: A long [stick](#stick) carried for casting [magic](#magic) or for [fighting](#fighting), taller than a [wand](#wand) and plainer than a [scepter](#scepter). Not used for a simple [cane](#cane).

entries.name: polearm
entries.description: A melee [weapon](#weapon) whose blade, point or head sits at the end of a long shaft: spears, halberds, [naginata](#naginata), glaives and the like. Add the specific type where it [can](#can) be identified.

entries.name: spear
entries.description: A long shaft tipped with a sharp point or blade, meant for thrusting. The most common form of [polearm](#polearm); a specifically named spear may carry its own dedicated [tag](#tag).

entries.name: lance
entries.description: A long [cavalry](#cavalry) [spear](#spear) with a broad conical head, the jousting [weapon](#weapon) of a mounted [knight](#knight) and a stock symbol for one. The generic spears some games call lances do not qualify.

entries.name: trident
entries.description: A three-pronged [spear](#spear), the [signature](#signature) [weapon](#weapon) of sea gods, merfolk and demons alike. Unbarbed or blunt prongs make it a [pitchfork](#pitchfork) instead, and it still counts as a [polearm](#polearm).

entries.name: mage_staff
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [ornate](#ornate) [staff](#staff) carried by spellcasters as a focus for their [magic](#magic), its head set with a [gem](#gem) or [crystal](#crystal) or twisted into gnarled wood. Keep it apart from a [wand](#wand), a [scepter](#scepter) or a [crosier](#crosier).

entries.name: naginata
entries.description: A Japanese [polearm](#polearm) with a curved blade mounted on a long shaft, cousin to the glaive and the guan [dao](#dao). It is frequently given to female characters, [following](#following) its historical use by women fighters.

entries.name: halberd
entries.description: A [polearm](#polearm) whose head combines an [axe](#axe) blade, a [spear](#spear) point and a [hook](#hook) or spike on the [back](#back). The [tag](#tag) also covers close relatives such as the poleaxe and the Chinese ji.

entries.name: glaive_(polearm)
entries.description: A European [polearm](#polearm) [carrying](#carrying) a single-edged blade on a long shaft, a cousin of the [naginata](#naginata) and the guan [dao](#dao). Reach for a closer polearm [tag](#tag) when one fits, and never use it for the thrown [fantasy](#fantasy) weapons that borrow the name.

entries.name: bo_staff
entries.description: A long straight wooden [fighting](#fighting) [staff](#staff) from the Japanese martial arts, [standing](#standing) about as [tall](#tall) as the person wielding it and used to strike and to block. A staff crowned with a [gem](#gem) or ornament is a different [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: bident
entries.description: A two-pronged [spear](#spear) like a [pitchfork](#pitchfork), used both as a [weapon](#weapon) and for spearing [fish](#fish). Folklore hands it to demons and lords of the underworld; the three-pronged version is a [trident](#trident).

entries.name: paw_stick
entries.description: A long [staff](#staff) topped with an oversized paw and swung as a blunt [weapon](#weapon). Usually carried by cat-themed characters who fight hand to hand.

entries.name: harpoon
entries.description: A shafted [spear](#spear) with a barbed head, thrown or fired to strike [fish](#fish) and sea mammals and hold them on a line. Designs run from a [plain](#plain) hand-thrown shaft to a deck-mounted [gun](#gun).

entries.name: guan_dao
entries.description: A Chinese [polearm](#polearm) [carrying](#carrying) a [heavy](#heavy) curved blade on a long shaft, often with a spike at the butt end. Tied to a famous Three Kingdoms general and to characters modelled after him.

entries.name: wooden_staff
entries.description: A long wooden [pole](#pole) carried as a [walking](#walking) [stick](#stick), a [fighting](#fighting) [weapon](#weapon), or a magical focus. It is [plain](#plain) and unshod, unlike a metal-tipped [spear](#spear).

entries.name: yari
entries.description: The straight-bladed Japanese [spear](#spear) carried by [samurai](#samurai) and foot soldiers, made either with a single point or with side prongs in the cross-shaped form used by [cavalry](#cavalry). Older polearms and spears in general take the [plain](#plain) spear [tag](#tag).

entries.name: planted_spear
entries.description: A [spear](#spear) [stuck](#stuck) point-first into the ground or another surface and left [standing](#standing). Often left beside a [resting](#resting) [warrior](#warrior) or marking a spot.

entries.name: energy_spear
entries.description: A [spear](#spear) whose head is a spike of [glowing](#glowing) power on a shaft, or one formed whole out of light. Braced for a charge or thrown, and common in magical and futuristic fights.

entries.name: gunlance
entries.description: A [polearm](#polearm) combining a [lance](#lance) with an [explosive](#explosive) [barrel](#barrel), letting the wielder [stab](#stab) and then [fire](#fire) shells. Recognisable by its [heavy](#heavy) shield-like [guard](#guard) and bulky [shell](#shell) magazine.

entries.name: double-sided_polearm
