entries.description: A long shaft with a blade or striking head mounted at each end, thrust and spun from either side. Common in stylised martial arts and [fantasy](#fantasy) designs.

entries.name: bow_(weapon)
entries.description: A hand-drawn [bow](#bow) that shoots arrows, used for [hunting](#hunting), sport or [war](#war), from a [plain](#plain) longbow to a Japanese yumi. Add [arrow_(projectile)](#arrow_(projectile)) and the [holding](#holding) [tag](#tag) where they fit; a mechanically drawn [crossbow](#crossbow) is separate.

entries.name: arrow_(projectile)
entries.description: The shaft loosed from a [bow](#bow) or [crossbow](#crossbow), with a head at one end and fletching at the other. The [pointing](#pointing) mark is [arrow_(symbol)](#arrow_(symbol)).

entries.name: explosive
entries.description: Anything built to blow up: grenades, bombs, mines, [dynamite](#dynamite). Use it for the [device](#device) itself, held, thrown or [planted](#planted); the blast it makes is [explosion](#explosion).

entries.name: quiver
entries.description: A case for [carrying](#carrying) arrows, worn on the [back](#back) or hip alongside a [bow](#bow). For a character [shaking](#shaking) or [trembling](#trembling), a different [tag](#tag) applies instead.

entries.name: kunai
entries.description: A leaf-shaped iron blade with a [ring](#ring) at the butt, thrown or used for stabbing and firmly tied to [ninja](#ninja). Add [holding_weapon](#holding_weapon) or a [throwing](#throwing) [tag](#tag) as the picture requires.

entries.name: grenade
entries.description: A lethal hand-thrown [explosive](#explosive), whether a pineapple-shaped fragmentation grenade or a [stick](#stick) grenade, held or in flight. Flashbangs and [smoke](#smoke) grenades are their own tags, and rounds fired from a launcher are 40mm_grenade.

entries.name: shuriken
entries.description: Flat bladed [throwing](#throwing) stars, the concealed [weapon](#weapon) most associated with ninjas. Usually drawn with three or four points around a central [hole](#hole), either held in the hand or [spinning](#spinning) through the air.

entries.name: throwing_knife
entries.description: A slim, balanced blade meant to be thrown rather than held, usually carried as a set. Drawn in flight, fanned between the fingers, or [stuck](#stuck) quivering in a [target](#target).

entries.name: bomb
entries.description: An [explosive](#explosive) that does not propel itself, from the cartoon black sphere with a [burning](#burning) [fuse](#fuse) to timed charges and aerial ordnance. Missiles and shells are separate; add [explosion](#explosion) once it goes off.

entries.name: crossbow
entries.description: A [bow](#bow) fixed crosswise on a stock, its [string](#string) drawn [back](#back) by a [lever](#lever) or crank and released to shoot bolts. Heavier [hitting](#hitting) and simpler to aim than [bow_(weapon)](#bow_(weapon)), but slow between shots.

entries.name: grenade_pin
entries.description: The safety [pin](#pin) and its [ring](#ring) pulled clear of a [grenade](#grenade) and shown apart from the [weapon](#weapon) body. Its presence says the grenade has been armed.

entries.name: chakram
entries.description: An Indian [throwing](#throwing) [ring](#ring) sharpened around its outer rim, which [can](#can) be hurled or gripped and swung in close. Game and [fantasy](#fantasy) characters often carry a matched pair.

entries.name: yumi_(bow)
entries.description: The traditional Japanese longbow, gripped [well](#well) below its centre so the upper limb towers over the lower one. Used in traditional Japanese [archery](#archery), distinct from generic or western [bow](#bow) designs.

entries.name: depth_charge
entries.description: A drum-shaped [underwater](#underwater) [bomb](#bomb) rolled or thrown from a [ship](#ship) to burst at a set depth against submarines. A regular fixture in naval and warship-girl subjects.

entries.name: dynamite
entries.description: Sticks of high [explosive](#explosive), singly or [bound](#bound) into a bundle with a [fuse](#fuse). The cartoon version is a red [tube](#tube) with a [burning](#burning) wick.

entries.name: boomerang
entries.description: A flat curved [throwing](#throwing) [stick](#stick), traditionally cut from wood, best known in the Australian form that comes [back](#back) to the thrower. It appears as a [hunting](#hunting) tool, a [toy](#toy) and a [fantasy](#fantasy) [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: throwing_needles
entries.description: Long thin metal [spikes](#spikes) thrown as weapons, sharpened at one end and held fanned between the fingers. A [ninja](#ninja) [staple](#staple), and unrelated to [sewing](#sewing) despite the shape.

entries.name: smoke_grenade
entries.description: A [canister](#canister) that pours out coloured [smoke](#smoke) instead of exploding, used to signal, mark a position or [screen](#screen) movement. It produces far more smoke than a small smoke [bomb](#bomb).

entries.name: slingshot_(weapon)
entries.description: A Y-shaped frame strung with elastic, drawn [back](#back) to fling pebbles or other small projectiles. It reads as a child's [toy](#toy) far more often than as a [serious](#serious) [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: compound_bow
entries.description: A modern [bow](#bow) whose limbs are drawn through cams and cables, [giving](#giving) it a boxy mechanical look beside a [plain](#plain) wooden one. Usually shown with a sight and an arrow rest.

entries.name: energy_arrow
entries.description: An arrow made of [glowing](#glowing) power instead of wood and steel, either nocked on a [bow](#bow) or already in flight. The shaft trails light and carries [no](#no) real fletching.

entries.name: bola_(weapon)
entries.description: A [throwing](#throwing) [weapon](#weapon) of two or more [weights](#weights) joined by cords, whirled and let go so it wraps around a target's [legs](#legs). It is meant to trip and tangle rather than to cut.

entries.name: flashbang
entries.description: A stun [grenade](#grenade) that puts out a blinding burst and a deafening [crack](#crack) instead of fragments. Usually the cylindrical [military](#military) type, held, thrown, or going off in someone's face.

entries.name: stielhandgranate
entries.description: The German potato-masher [grenade](#grenade): a metal charge [can](#can) fixed to a long wooden [handle](#handle). It served as the army's standard grenade from the first [war](#war) through the second, and its [outline](#outline) is instantly recognisable.

entries.name: heart_arrow
entries.description: An arrow whose head or fletching is a [heart](#heart), the sort [cupid](#cupid) shoots. A [bow](#bow) and a [lovestruck](#lovestruck) [target](#target) usually come with it.

entries.name: repeating_crossbow
entries.description: A [crossbow](#crossbow) fitted with a magazine and [lever](#lever) so that bolts [can](#can) be loaded and loosed in quick succession without [reloading](#reloading) by hand. The Chinese chu-ko-nu is the classic example and the shape most often drawn.

entries.name: javelin_(spear)
entries.description: A slender [throwing](#throwing) [spear](#spear), light enough to be hurled yet still usable in the hand. The [tag](#tag) covers both the ancient [weapon](#weapon) and the modern athletics implement.

entries.name: stick_grenade
entries.description: A hand [grenade](#grenade) with the [explosive](#explosive) head mounted on a wooden [throwing](#throwing) [handle](#handle) for extra leverage. A cord in the base of the shaft is yanked to start the [fuse](#fuse) [burning](#burning).

entries.name: planted_arrow
entries.description: An arrow or [crossbow](#crossbow) bolt [stuck](#stuck) head-first into the ground and left [standing](#standing). It suggests a fight just finished, or a shot that went wide.

entries.name: bowgun
entries.description: A ranged [weapon](#weapon) marrying a gun's stock and [barrel](#barrel) to [crossbow](#crossbow) limbs. Largely a fictional design, and [familiar](#familiar) from monster-hunting games.

entries.name: pipe_bomb
entries.description: An improvised [bomb](#bomb) built from a capped length of pipe packed with [explosive](#explosive). The casing itself bursts into shrapnel, which is what makes so crude a [device](#device) deadly.

entries.name: fuuma_shuriken
entries.description: An oversized [throwing](#throwing) star, anywhere from plate-sized to taller than the person [swinging](#swinging) it, usually built from four broad folding blades. Wielded in the hand as often as thrown.

entries.name: shield
entries.description: A broad, flat piece of [armor](#armor) held in the hand or strapped to the forearm to block attacks. Tag whether it is carried, raised or slung on the [back](#back).

entries.name: shield_on_back
entries.description: A [shield](#shield) slung across the [back](#back) instead of held on the forearm, commonly alongside a [sheathed](#sheathed) [weapon](#weapon). Marks a fighter [resting](#resting) or on the move. Implies shield.

entries.name: ballistic_shield
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) opaque slab of metal or composite carried by [police](#police) and soldiers to stop bullets, generally pierced by a narrow viewing slot. The see-through polymer sort is a riot [shield](#shield) and stops far less.

entries.name: arm_shield
entries.description: A [shield](#shield) strapped along the forearm rather than gripped by a [handle](#handle), which leaves the hand free for something else. Small bucklers and long [bracer](#bracer) shields both count.

entries.name: riot_shield
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [transparent](#transparent) [shield](#shield) carried by [police](#police) for [crowd](#crowd) control, [shrugging](#shrugging) off thrown objects and blows but not bullets. It comes in a one-handed version that leaves an arm free for a baton and a larger [two-handed](#two-handed) one.

entries.name: shield_module
entries.description: An extra mechanical arm [carrying](#carrying) a [shield](#shield), bolted onto a [robot](#robot), [mecha](#mecha) or armored [figure](#figure), so the shield is built-in hardware rather than something merely held.

entries.name: buckler
entries.description: A small round [shield](#shield), sometimes domed at the centre, used to turn blows aside rather than to hide behind. It is often drawn strapped to the forearm instead of gripped.

entries.name: energy_shield
entries.description: A [shield](#shield) of projected light, strapped to the arm or [floating](#floating) in front of it, often a flat [hexagon](#hexagon) or disc that flares where a blow lands. A smaller, carried form of an [energy_barrier](#energy_barrier).

entries.name: wooden_shield
entries.description: A [shield](#shield) built primarily from planks, sometimes banded in iron or painted with a heraldic [device](#device). Early [medieval](#medieval) and [fantasy](#fantasy) fighters both carry it.

entries.name: weapon
entries.description: A handheld weapon of any kind appears in the picture, covering swords, guns, knives, bows and similar [tools](#tools) grasped or wielded by hand. Fixed or vehicle-mounted arms such as [artillery](#artillery), turrets or torpedoes don't count; add the specific weapon and any [holding](#holding) [tag](#tag) alongside.

entries.name: spikes
entries.description: Sharp, pointed [studs](#studs) or protrusions on an object, garment, or surface, whether on [armor](#armor), a [collar](#collar), a wall, or a [weapon](#weapon). Use the body-specific tags instead for spikes that are [anatomy](#anatomy) rather than an accessory.

entries.name: ship_turret
entries.description: A rotating [gun](#gun) turret from a [warship](#warship), whether mounted on the vessel itself or carried as part of a [ship](#ship) girl's [rigging](#rigging). Tag with turret or [cannon](#cannon) where it fits.

entries.name: cannon
entries.description: A large mounted [tube](#tube) that fires shells or balls, from [ship](#ship) and [castle](#castle) guns to a modern tank's [barrel](#barrel). It also covers the oversized versions characters lug about as personal weapons.

entries.name: arm_cannon
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) that sheathes the whole arm or takes its place, muzzle where the hand would be. Standard equipment for cyborgs, androids and armoured heroes.

entries.name: huge_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) at least as large as the character wielding it, such as an oversized [sword](#sword) or [gun](#gun). Add the weapon's own type as [well](#well); an outsized item that is not a weapon is [oversized_object](#oversized_object).

entries.name: torpedo
entries.description: A self-propelled [underwater](#underwater) [weapon](#weapon) fired from a [ship](#ship) or [submarine](#submarine) toward a [target](#target), detonating on contact or close proximity. Often carried by warships and personified ship characters alike.

entries.name: whip
entries.description: A long [flexible](#flexible) lash on a [handle](#handle), used to strike or control, common in [bondage](#bondage) scenes and as a [signature](#signature) [weapon](#weapon) for some [fantasy](#fantasy) heroes. A stiff rod without a lash is [riding_crop](#riding_crop) instead.

entries.name: energy_gun
entries.description: A handheld [weapon](#weapon) that sends out a bolt or beam instead of a [bullet](#bullet) — a ray [gun](#gun) or [laser](#laser) pistol. Standard issue in science-fiction settings.

entries.name: riding_crop
entries.description: A short stiff [whip](#whip) with a flap at the end, made for [horse](#horse) [riding](#riding). In art it appears as often in a dominatrix's hand as in a rider's.

entries.name: club_(weapon)
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) blunt [stick](#stick) swung as a [weapon](#weapon), from a [plain](#plain) cudgel to a [studded](#studded) [oni](#oni) kanabo. A bat meant for sport is [baseball_bat](#baseball_bat).

entries.name: rocket_launcher
entries.description: A shoulder-fired [weapon](#weapon) that launches a [rocket](#rocket) or [missile](#missile), including anti-tank tubes, MANPADS and recoilless rifles, grouped here for their identical look. A vehicle-mounted system instead is [missile_pod](#missile_pod).

entries.name: claw_(weapon)
entries.description: Blades arranged in the shape of [claws](#claws) and worn over the hand or forearm as a [weapon](#weapon). Natural [animal](#animal) claws are claws, and the empty-handed [gesture](#gesture) is [claw_pose](#claw_pose).

entries.name: beam_rifle
entries.description: A rifle-shaped [energy](#energy) [weapon](#weapon) that fires a beam, the standard armament of [giant](#giant) robots in [mecha](#mecha) [science](#science) fiction. It is usually scaled to the [machine](#machine) rather than to a person.

entries.name: missile
entries.description: A self-propelled [explosive](#explosive) [weapon](#weapon), guided or not, covering both true guided missiles and unguided [military](#military) rockets. Non-weapon civilian [rocket](#rocket) engines are tagged as rocket instead.

entries.name: mace
entries.description: A blunt [weapon](#weapon) with a [heavy](#heavy) head, often flanged or [spiked](#spiked), mounted on a [handle](#handle) and swung to crush. Clerics and armoured knights carry it in [fantasy](#fantasy) art.

entries.name: multiple_weapons
entries.description: Two or more kinds of [weapon](#weapon) in one picture, or more than three of a single kind, carried by one [figure](#figure) or strewn about the scene. Several characters each [holding](#holding) one weapon does not qualify.

entries.name: torpedo_tubes
entries.description: The tube-shaped launchers built into a warship's hull, or worn on a ship-girl's [rigging](#rigging), for [firing](#firing) torpedoes. Add [torpedo](#torpedo) when one is actually loaded or in flight.

entries.name: spiked_club
entries.description: A club with [spikes](#spikes) protruding from its head, such as the Japanese [kanabou](#kanabou) favored by [oni](#oni). Tag the [weapon](#weapon) whether carried or simply [lying](#lying) about.

entries.name: torpedo_launcher
entries.description: A cylindrical mount used to [fire](#fire) torpedoes, whether on a real [warship](#warship) or worn as [rigging](#rigging) by a personified [ship](#ship) character. Add [torpedo](#torpedo) when one is shown loaded or launched.

entries.name: kanabou
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) Japanese club of oak or iron, [studded](#studded) along its length with iron [spikes](#spikes). Its [weight](#weight) suits enormously [strong](#strong) figures, and [oni](#oni) are the classic wielders.

entries.name: floating_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) suspended in the air on its own, usually hovering at its owner's side rather than being held. Swords specifically are [floating_sword](#floating_sword).

entries.name: broken_weapon
entries.description: Any [weapon](#weapon) that has been snapped, [shattered](#shattered) or otherwise wrecked, from a [sword](#sword) [broken](#broken) at the blade to a splintered [spear](#spear) shaft. Add weapon and broken, plus the weapon type where it [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: energy_cannon
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [gun](#gun) that throws [energy](#energy) rather than shells, mounted on the ships, [mecha](#mecha) and fortifications of [science](#science) fiction. It names the [weapon](#weapon); what leaves the muzzle is an [energy_beam](#energy_beam).

entries.name: energy_weapon
entries.description: A ranged [weapon](#weapon) that fires focused [energy](#energy) rather than a projectile, [glowing](#glowing) at the muzzle and along its vents. A [staple](#staple) of science-fiction arsenals at any size.

entries.name: missile_pod
entries.description: A launcher cluster mounted on a vehicle or [mecha](#mecha) that stores and fires a volley of missiles or rockets.

entries.name: tonfa
entries.description: A short baton with a side [handle](#handle) from Okinawan martial arts, usually wielded as a pair. The modern [police](#police) baton is derived from it.

entries.name: nail_bat
entries.description: A wooden [baseball](#baseball) bat with nails hammered part-way through its business end. The protruding points turn a piece of sports equipment into a crude [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: hook
entries.description: A curved barbed point on the end of a [rope](#rope) or [chain](#chain), thrown so that it catches a [target](#target) and drags them [back](#back). It is wielded as a [weapon](#weapon) rather than used for [fishing](#fishing) or for [hanging](#hanging) things up.

entries.name: ball_and_chain_(weapon)
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy), often [spiked](#spiked) [ball](#ball) swung at the end of a long [chain](#chain), with or without a [handle](#handle) at the other end. Where the chain is short and fixed to a haft, the [weapon](#weapon) is a [flail](#flail).

entries.name: baton_(weapon)
entries.description: A short rigid club carried by [police](#police), sometimes telescoping out of its [handle](#handle). Martial artists [swing](#swing) the same sort of [stick](#stick) in [training](#training) and in fights.

entries.name: war_hammer
entries.description: A blunt-headed [weapon](#weapon) built to crush through armour, often with a spike opposite the head and sometimes a long haft. It also covers the oversized [fantasy](#fantasy) sledgehammers characters [swing](#swing) [two-handed](#two-handed).

entries.name: beam_cannon
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [weapon](#weapon) that fires a sustained beam of [energy](#energy) instead of shells, mounted on a [mecha](#mecha), a [warship](#warship) or a fortification. The shot is drawn as a bright [column](#column) with glare blooming at the muzzle.

entries.name: ray_gun
entries.description: A pulp science-fiction sidearm with a bulbous [barrel](#barrel), coils, and [fins](#fins), the kind a 1950s [space](#space) hero would carry. The retro styling matters more here than whatever beam it actually fires.

entries.name: flamethrower
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) [throwing](#throwing) a [clinging](#clinging) [stream](#stream) of [burning](#burning) fuel from a nozzle, fed from tanks worn on the [back](#back). The jet of flame is what identifies it.

entries.name: lead_pipe
entries.description: A length of metal pipe swung as an improvised blunt [weapon](#weapon). Pipework drawn as part of plumbing or [industrial](#industrial) fittings takes a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: brass_knuckles
entries.description: A shaped metal grip with holes for the fingers, worn across the knuckles so that a punch lands with far more force. It also goes by knuckle [duster](#duster).

entries.name: flail
entries.description: A [handle](#handle) joined by a hinge, [rope](#rope) or short [chain](#chain) to one or more striking [weights](#weights), descended from the threshing tool of the same name. A chain longer than an arm points to a [ball](#ball) and chain instead.

entries.name: energy_blade
entries.description: A [cutting](#cutting) edge of [glowing](#glowing) power in any shape but a [plain](#plain) [sword](#sword): [claws](#claws), discs, or [spurs](#spurs) projecting from a [hilt](#hilt) or an arm. A straight blade of light is [energy_sword](#energy_sword).

entries.name: railgun
entries.description: An electromagnetic launcher that drives a conductive projectile down a pair of charged rails at enormous speed. Science fiction favors them, usually as oversized [artillery](#artillery), and the concept is distinct from a railway [gun](#gun), which is simply a [cannon](#cannon) mounted on a [train](#train).

entries.name: artillery
entries.description: Heavy ordnance [throwing](#throwing) shells far beyond the reach of personal weapons: [field](#field) guns, howitzers, mortars and [rocket](#rocket) launchers, wheeled or dug in. Crews and emplacements often appear with them.

entries.name: spiked_ball_and_chain
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [spiked](#spiked) [ball](#ball) swung on the end of a [chain](#chain). The [spikes](#spikes) are what separate it from a [plain](#plain) [ball_and_chain_(weapon)](#ball_and_chain_(weapon)).

entries.name: nunchaku
entries.description: Two short batons joined end to end by a [chain](#chain) or a cord, whirled and struck with in martial arts. Their small size makes them easy to hide and quick to [swing](#swing); a three-section [staff](#staff) has one [stick](#stick) more and takes its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: autocannon
entries.description: A [cannon](#cannon) fed from a [belt](#belt) or a magazine, so that it keeps [firing](#firing) for as long as the trigger is held. Too [heavy](#heavy) to carry, it is normally bolted to a vehicle, an [aircraft](#aircraft) or a [mecha](#mecha).

entries.name: rpg_(weapon)
entries.description: A shoulder-fired anti-tank [grenade](#grenade) launcher named after the Russian abbreviation for the [family](#family), of which the RPG-7 is only the best-known member. Use it for launchers resembling that pattern, and never for role-playing games.

entries.name: concealed_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) carried out of sight, such as a blade hidden inside a [cane](#cane) or a pistol strapped under a [skirt](#skirt). The point is that it stays unseen until it is wanted.

entries.name: gunpod
entries.description: A detachable [weapon](#weapon) pack of cannons or [machine](#machine) guns carried outside an [aircraft](#aircraft) or [mecha](#mecha), bolted on for a mission and left off to save [weight](#weight). Often drawn as a bulky rifle-shaped unit gripped by a fighter craft.

entries.name: spiked_mace
entries.description: A club-type [weapon](#weapon) topped with a [spiked](#spiked) [ball](#ball) head, usually called a [morning](#morning) star after the shape. The head is fixed to the haft rather than [hanging](#hanging) on a [chain](#chain).

entries.name: detonator
entries.description: The trigger for an [explosive](#explosive) charge: a [plunger](#plunger) [box](#box), a keypad, a [radio](#radio) handset with a [switch](#switch). Almost always shown mid-threat with wires or a [countdown](#countdown) attached.

entries.name: spiked_knuckles
entries.description: Points [sitting](#sitting) over the knuckles, whether from brass knuckles, an armored glove, or [spurs](#spurs) that appear to grow straight from the hand. Marks a character who fights by striking.

entries.name: cat_o'_nine_tails
entries.description: A [whip](#whip) whose [handle](#handle) splits into a bundle of knotted cords, built historically for flogging. It serves as a [punishment](#punishment) implement in period scenes and as a [bondage](#bondage) prop elsewhere.

entries.name: harisen
entries.description: A flat fan [folded](#folded) from stiff [paper](#paper), swung to [smack](#smack) somebody with a loud [crack](#crack) rather than to move air. It is standard slapstick equipment, and several comedy heroines carry one as their [signature](#signature) [weapon](#weapon). Ordinary folding and round fans belong under [paper_fan](#paper_fan).

entries.name: pink_weapon
entries.description: A [sword](#sword), [gun](#gun) or other [weapon](#weapon) coloured pink. Frequent on magical-girl gear and on joke armaments; the kind of weapon is tagged separately.

entries.name: bear_trap
entries.description: Two spring-loaded metal jaws on a pressure [plate](#plate) that snap shut around whatever steps on them. Toothed versions bite into the leg, smooth ones simply clamp, and either is usually drawn closed on a victim rather than [lying](#lying) open.

entries.name: power_fist
entries.description: An oversized armoured glove built to amplify a punch, [humming](#humming) with its own [energy](#energy) source. An unpowered metal glove is a gauntlet instead.

entries.name: nuclear_weapon
entries.description: The [bomb](#bomb), warhead or [missile](#missile) itself, shown as an object. Where only a [mushroom](#mushroom) [cloud](#cloud) appears use nuclear_explosion, and nuclear-powered vehicles do not count.

entries.name: spike_ball
entries.description: A [ball](#ball) [studded](#studded) all over with [spikes](#spikes), appearing as the head of a [morning](#morning) star, on the end of a [swinging](#swinging) [chain](#chain), or occasionally as a standalone hazard.

entries.name: rpg-7
entries.description: The Soviet shoulder-fired [rocket](#rocket) launcher of 1958, a [plain](#plain) [tube](#tube) with an optical sight and a conical [grenade](#grenade) sticking out of the muzzle when loaded. The most widespread launcher of its kind in the world, and its foreign copies count too.

entries.name: mine_(weapon)
entries.description: An [explosive](#explosive) charge laid on or [buried](#buried) in the ground, set off by pressure, proximity or a remote trigger.

entries.name: spacecraft_turret
entries.description: A rotating [gun](#gun) mount fixed to the hull of a [spacecraft](#spacecraft), either manned from a [bubble](#bubble) canopy or operated remotely. Common in [dogfight](#dogfight) and boarding scenes.

entries.name: stake
entries.description: A pointed length of wood or metal driven into the ground or into something else. Appears in [vampire](#vampire) [hunting](#hunting), [tent](#tent) lines, fences and executions.

entries.name: pile_bunker
entries.description: A [mecha](#mecha) melee [weapon](#weapon) that drives a [heavy](#heavy) spike through armour with an [explosive](#explosive) or electric charge, sometimes ejecting a spent casing afterwards. Standard equipment in real-robot fiction.

entries.name: stun_gun
entries.description: A small handheld [device](#device) that delivers a high-voltage shock through contact prongs, usually drawn with a crackling arc between them. A [taser](#taser), which fires darts on wires from a distance, is a separate device.

entries.name: fuse
entries.description: The [burning](#burning) cord of a [bomb](#bomb) or firework, drawn as a short twist of [rope](#rope) sparking at its tip. Not the electrical component of the same name, which this [tag](#tag) never covers.

entries.name: taser
entries.description: A handheld electroshock [weapon](#weapon) that fires barbed darts on trailing wires to drop a [target](#target) from a few paces away. A contact stun [gun](#gun) that must be pressed against the body is a separate thing.

entries.name: umbrella_gun
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) that doubles as a firearm, with a [barrel](#barrel) hidden inside the shaft or [handle](#handle). A [staple](#staple) of spy fiction and eccentric villain designs.

entries.name: self-propelled_artillery
entries.description: A [gun](#gun) or howitzer carried on its own tracked or wheeled chassis so it [can](#can) drive into [firing](#firing) position. Unlike a [tank](#tank) it exists to shoot in one direction, often from a fixed or open mount; [mobile](#mobile) [rocket](#rocket) launchers are not covered by the term.

entries.name: wrist_blades
entries.description: Blades mounted along the forearm that project past the wrist, either fixed in place or spring-loaded. Assassin characters and [mecha](#mecha) alike carry them.

entries.name: kusarigama
entries.description: A short [sickle](#sickle) joined to a length of [chain](#chain) that ends in an iron [weight](#weight). The chain snares or strikes at a distance while the blade handles anything close.

entries.name: ornate_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) decorated far beyond its [plain](#plain) counterpart, with [patterned](#patterned) blades, chased fittings or sculpted hilts. Careful rendering or complicated mechanics alone do not make one [ornate](#ornate).

entries.name: broken_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) with its base or [neck](#neck) smashed away, leaving a [ring](#ring) of jagged [glass](#glass). In practice it is almost always clutched in a fist as an improvised stabbing [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: red_lightsaber
entries.description: The [plasma](#plasma) blade of Star Wars [glowing](#glowing) red, projected from a metal [hilt](#hilt). Red blades belong to the Sith and their allies, so the colour itself carries the allegiance.

entries.name: tnt
entries.description: Blocky charges or bundled sticks marked TNT, drawn as the cartoon standard for explosives with a [fuse](#fuse) on top. Keep it for material actually labelled that way; unlabelled sticks belong to [dynamite](#dynamite).

entries.name: sai_(weapon)
entries.description: A short metal truncheon with two curved prongs flanking the central shaft, from Okinawan martial arts. Carried in pairs and used for stabbing or for trapping an opponent's blade.

entries.name: arm_mounted_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) fixed along the forearm rather than carried: blades, launchers and [gun](#gun) mounts strapped or built into the limb. A [barrel](#barrel) [pointing](#pointing) forward from the arm is better called an arm [cannon](#cannon).

entries.name: panzerfaust
entries.description: A German single-shot anti-tank [weapon](#weapon) of the Second World War: a slim disposable [tube](#tube) with an oversized shaped-charge head on the [nose](#nose), fired from the shoulder by one [soldier](#soldier).

entries.name: weapon_formation
entries.description: Three or more weapons arranged in a deliberate pattern, such as a fan, arc or [ring](#ring), usually hovering in the air around their owner. A [display](#display) of arsenal rather than of use.

entries.name: war_fan
entries.description: A Japanese [battle](#battle) fan, either a folding one with metal [ribs](#ribs) or a solid [paddle](#paddle) carried by commanders. Used to signal troops, to turn a blade aside and sometimes as a club.

entries.name: spiked
entries.description: Something in the picture, whether clothing, an accessory, [armor](#armor), or an object, carries protruding [spikes](#spikes). A general [marker](#marker) used when [no](#no) more specific spiked_ [tag](#tag) applies.

entries.name: molotov_cocktail
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) [bottle](#bottle) of fuel stoppered with a rag that is lit before it is thrown, [spreading](#spreading) [burning](#burning) [liquid](#liquid) where it breaks. Standard equipment in riot and street-fighting scenes.

entries.name: multishot_rocket_launcher
entries.description: A launcher carried on the shoulder that holds several rockets and [can](#can) send off more than one before it is reloaded or discarded. Pods of missiles bolted onto a vehicle or [mecha](#mecha) do not count.

entries.name: three_section_staff
entries.description: A Chinese [weapon](#weapon) of three wooden rods joined end to end by short chains, swung and [folded](#folded) like an elongated [nunchaku](#nunchaku). Held closed, it [can](#can) pass for an ordinary [staff](#staff).

entries.name: cross_(weapon)
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) built to fight with, swung as a blunt [instrument](#instrument) or unfolded as a housing for blades and guns. Standard equipment in gothic and religion-flavoured action art.

entries.name: improvised_weapon
entries.description: An object swung, thrown or brandished as a [weapon](#weapon) although it was never meant to be one, from a frying pan to a [chair](#chair) leg. It also covers a genuine weapon used in some wholly unintended way.

entries.name: expandable_baton
entries.description: A telescoping metal baton that flicks out to full length from a short grip, carried by [police](#police) and security. Drawn either [collapsed](#collapsed) or extended for a blow.

entries.name: flanged_mace
entries.description: A blunt club whose head carries raised ridges [standing](#standing) out around the shaft. Use it for that [medieval](#medieval) design rather than for a [plain](#plain) ball-headed or [spiked](#spiked) [mace](#mace).

entries.name: hair_weapon
entries.description: Hair ending in a blade, spike or other dangerous fitting, or acting as a [weapon](#weapon) in its own right. Common on characters who fight with their hair.

entries.name: bladed_tonfa
entries.description: A [tonfa](#tonfa), the baton gripped by a [handle](#handle) set into its side, given a [cutting](#cutting) edge or fitted with blades instead of staying blunt. It is usually carried as a pair.

entries.name: jitte
entries.description: A short iron truncheon with a single [hook](#hook) beside the shaft, carried by Edo-period constables. The hook catches a [sword](#sword) blade so the wielder [can](#can) twist it aside or disarm the attacker.

entries.name: laser_rifle
entries.description: A long arm that fires a beam of concentrated light instead of a [bullet](#bullet), [burning](#burning) or [cutting](#cutting) whatever it strikes. It is a fixture of [science](#science) fiction arsenals.

entries.name: garrote
entries.description: A length of [wire](#wire) or cord, often with a grip at each end, used to strangle someone from behind. An assassin's quiet tool, occasionally drawn slicing rather than choking.

entries.name: syringe_gun
entries.description: A firearm shaped like an oversized [syringe](#syringe), or one built to [fire](#fire) syringes as its [ammunition](#ammunition). A recurring prop on mad-scientist and medic character designs.

entries.name: liquid_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) shaped from [water](#water) or another fluid, [holding](#holding) a blade or [spear](#spear) form while staying visibly [liquid](#liquid) at the edges.

entries.name: dual_arm_cannons
entries.description: Cannons mounted on both arms rather than only one. Standard fitting for heavily armed [mecha](#mecha) and [cyborg](#cyborg) designs.

entries.name: mortar_(weapon)
entries.description: A short, steeply angled [tube](#tube) that lobs shells in a high arc onto targets sheltering behind [cover](#cover). Loaded down the muzzle and set on a baseplate, with a [barrel](#barrel) only a few calibres long.

entries.name: weapon_on_floor
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) lies on the ground rather than being held. It suggests a fight that has ended, a surrender, or a quiet moment of rest.

entries.name: weapon_background
entries.description: Weapons fill the [space](#space) behind the subject as decoration, arranged rather than wielded. Common on character showcase illustrations.

entries.name: chain_blades
entries.description: Two or more blades joined by chains, either to each other or [back](#back) to the wielder's grip. Flinging them out to reach and hauling them back is the whole [idea](#idea) of the design.

entries.name: chain_whip
entries.description: A [flexible](#flexible) [weapon](#weapon) of linked metal segments swung like a lash, sometimes weighted or edged at the far end. Martial arts and [fantasy](#fantasy) characters carry them.

entries.name: phone
entries.description: Any telephone in the picture, from a [mobile](#mobile) to an [old](#old) landline or a [payphone](#payphone). Add [cellphone](#cellphone) or [smartphone](#smartphone) for the handheld sort, and [holding_phone](#holding_phone) or [talking_on_phone](#talking_on_phone) for what is being done with it.

entries.name: cellphone
entries.description: A handheld [mobile](#mobile) [phone](#phone), whether a modern flat-screened one or an older flip [model](#model), held, used or [lying](#lying) within reach. Often shown lit up in a darkened room.

entries.name: smartphone
entries.description: A flat touch-screen [phone](#phone), the modern [pocket](#pocket) [computer](#computer). Tagged under [cellphone](#cellphone); add [holding_phone](#holding_phone) or phone [screen](#screen) tags as relevant.

entries.name: controller
entries.description: A [gamepad](#gamepad) or [joystick](#joystick) with [buttons](#buttons) for [driving](#driving) a console or another electronic [device](#device), held in the hands or [lying](#lying) about. Add a [tag](#tag) for [playing](#playing) games when it is actually in use.

entries.name: computer
entries.description: A desktop or [laptop](#laptop) [machine](#machine) in the scene, generally with [monitor](#monitor), keyboard and mouse. Add the peripheral tags, and laptop where that applies.

entries.name: monitor
entries.description: The [display](#display) [screen](#screen) of a [computer](#computer), either a flat panel or a deep [old](#old) cathode-ray set, [standing](#standing) on a [desk](#desk) or fixed to a wall. A flat-screen [television](#television) is a different [tag](#tag) despite the similar look.

entries.name: game_controller
entries.description: An input [device](#device) held apart from the [machine](#machine) and linked by [cable](#cable) or [wireless](#wireless): [gamepad](#gamepad), [joystick](#joystick), [arcade](#arcade) [stick](#stick), steering [wheel](#wheel), light [gun](#gun). The built-in [buttons](#buttons) of a handheld are excluded; add the specific [model](#model) [tag](#tag) when it is recognisable.

entries.name: handheld_game_console
entries.description: A portable game system played in both hands, [screen](#screen) and [buttons](#buttons) in one [shell](#shell). It covers everything from a Game Boy or DS to a modern hybrid console held undocked.

entries.name: gamepad
entries.description: A [controller](#controller) made to sit comfortably in two hands, with a direction pad, start and select, several face [buttons](#buttons) and often thumbsticks. Kept apart from the [joystick](#joystick), which is mounted and gripped upright.

entries.name: laptop
entries.description: A folding portable [computer](#computer), open on a [desk](#desk), a [lap](#lap) or a [bed](#bed), or carried shut. Add a using or [typing](#typing) [tag](#tag) when somebody is [working](#working) at it.

entries.name: computer_keyboard
entries.description: The [typing](#typing) keyboard of a [computer](#computer), [standing](#standing) separate on a [desk](#desk) or built into a [laptop](#laptop). A musical keyboard is [keyboard_(instrument)](#keyboard_(instrument)).

entries.name: tablet_pc
entries.description: A handheld touchscreen [computer](#computer) with [no](#no) attached keyboard, like an iPad. Distinct from a [convertible](#convertible) [laptop](#laptop) and from a drawing tablet used for [pen](#pen) input.

entries.name: game_console
entries.description: A home [machine](#machine) for [playing](#playing) [video](#video) games, hooked up to a [television](#television). Portable machines and separate controllers have tags of their own.

entries.name: stylus
entries.description: A pen-shaped [pointer](#pointer) used to draw or write on a tablet or touchscreen. Do not also [tag](#tag) [pen](#pen); the two are treated as mutually exclusive.

entries.name: computer_mouse
entries.description: The physical [pointing](#pointing) [device](#device) that sits beside a keyboard, often on a mousepad. The arrow it moves on [screen](#screen) is [cursor](#cursor), and the [animal](#animal) is mouse.

entries.name: cellphone_photo
entries.description: A photograph is displayed on a phone's [screen](#screen) inside the picture, usually as one character photographs another or shows a shot off. A whole image drawn as a [phone](#phone) [display](#display) is [fake_phone_screenshot](#fake_phone_screenshot).

entries.name: user_interface
entries.description: The picture shows software UI, real or mocked up: [buttons](#buttons), menus, health [bars](#bars), text boxes or an entire game [screen](#screen). Physical controls with [no](#no) visible screen do not count on their own.

entries.name: drawing_tablet
entries.description: A flat rectangular pad used with a [stylus](#stylus) to draw into a [computer](#computer), [standing](#standing) in for [pen](#pen) and brush. A touchscreen computer is [tablet_pc](#tablet_pc), and a stone tablet is unrelated.

entries.name: video_game
entries.description: A [video](#video) game is present in the picture, on a [screen](#screen), console or handheld. The [tag](#tag) is about the game as an object or activity, not about characters who come from games.

entries.name: d-pad
entries.description: The cross-shaped directional control found on game controllers and on some remote units, with a button at each point. Appears as an object in hand or as a [floating](#floating) graphic motif; a hair clip in that shape is [d-pad_hair_ornament](#d-pad_hair_ornament).

entries.name: health_bar
entries.description: A [gauge](#gauge) drawn into the picture showing how much life a character has left, as in a [fighting](#fighting) or adventure game. Similar meters for special moves count as [well](#well).

entries.name: flip_phone
entries.description: A clamshell [mobile](#mobile) that folds open, the ordinary [phone](#phone) before smartphones took over. Modern folding handsets with the same shape count too.

entries.name: screen
entries.description: A [display](#display) surface of any kind: a [monitor](#monitor), [television](#television), [phone](#phone) screen, or the image shown on one. Tag the specific [device](#device), such as monitor or television, alongside it.

entries.name: game_interface
entries.description: On-screen furniture from a [video](#video) game laid over the scene: health [bars](#bars), menus, [buttons](#buttons) and status readouts. It frames the image as a moment of play.

entries.name: holographic_interface
entries.description: A control surface projected into the air, such as a [floating](#floating) keyboard, [screen](#screen) or panel, that somebody reads or operates. Standard science-fiction furniture; pair it with [hologram](#hologram) when other projections share the scene.

entries.name: cursor
entries.description: A [computer](#computer) mouse [pointer](#pointer) drawn into the image, as in a mocked-up screenshot or a joke about clicking on the character. It sits over the artwork as an interface element rather than belonging to the scene.

entries.name: corded_phone
entries.description: A landline telephone whose handset hangs off its base by a cord, rotary or [push-button](#push-button). Payphones, [office](#office) [desk](#desk) sets and [old](#old) household phones all count; handheld mobiles are [cellphone](#cellphone) or [smartphone](#smartphone).

entries.name: window_(computing)
entries.description: A software [window](#window) or pop-up dialog appearing somewhere in the picture, whether as an interface element or a drawn joke. It is not used for an architectural window, which is simply window.

entries.name: text_messaging
entries.description: Two characters exchange messages on their phones, usually shown [typing](#typing) or [reading](#reading) a chat. A fake screenshot of a whole chat [window](#window) is [chat_log](#chat_log) instead.

entries.name: heads-up_display
entries.description: A game-style interface laid over the picture, with health [bars](#bars), minimaps and similar readouts. It appears in screenshots and in drawings that imitate a game [screen](#screen).

entries.name: antique_phone
entries.description: A telephone from before this century, whether a rotary [desk](#desk) set, a candlestick [model](#model) or a corded wall unit. Name the specific type where you [can](#can), since the general [tag](#tag) says very little.

entries.name: cellphone_charm
entries.description: A small decorative charm or [toy](#toy) [dangling](#dangling) from a [phone](#phone) on a short [strap](#strap). The phone-specific use of the wider charm accessory.

entries.name: camera_phone
entries.description: An older [mobile](#mobile) handset whose one extra trick is a built-in [camera](#camera), without the rest of a smartphone's abilities; the body may be a bar, a flip or a slider. Different from a whole picture drawn as a [phone](#phone) [display](#display), and from a photo shown on a [screen](#screen) inside the scene.

entries.name: joystick
entries.description: A control [stick](#stick) with a visible upright [lever](#lever) and [handle](#handle): an [arcade](#arcade) stick, a fight stick, a flight stick, or the thumbsticks [standing](#standing) up from a console pad. A pad with [no](#no) such lever is a [gamepad](#gamepad).

entries.name: smartphone_case
entries.description: A protective [shell](#shell) fitted around a [phone](#phone), often decorated with charms, prints or character motifs. It is visible whenever the handset is held up or set down in view.

entries.name: holographic_monitor
entries.description: A [display](#display) made of projected light rather than a solid panel, [hanging](#hanging) in mid-air. Cockpits, laboratories and control rooms are full of them.

entries.name: arcade_cabinet
entries.description: An upright coin-fed [video](#video) game [machine](#machine) with a [screen](#screen), a control panel and a painted marquee overhead. One [can](#can) stand anywhere; a whole room of them also takes [arcade](#arcade).

entries.name: rotary_phone
entries.description: A telephone dialled by turning a finger [wheel](#wheel) against a stop, with a corded handset [resting](#resting) in a [cradle](#cradle). It marks a scene as older, since keypad phones later replaced it.

entries.name: usb
entries.description: The [familiar](#familiar) connector and [cable](#cable) standard used for linking devices and [carrying](#carrying) power, along with the [flash](#flash) drives built around it. Recognisable by its rectangular plug and trident-shaped [logo](#logo).

entries.name: mousepad_(object)
entries.description: The flat pad a [computer](#computer) mouse slides across, [lying](#lying) on a [desk](#desk) somewhere in the scene. Where the artwork itself takes that shape, the medium [tag](#tag) applies instead.

entries.name: minimap
entries.description: A small overhead [map](#map) tucked into a [corner](#corner) of the frame the way a [video](#video) game interface places one, showing position and nearby surroundings.

entries.name: multiple_monitors
entries.description: Two or more [display](#display) screens set side by side or stacked into a rig, usually over a [desk](#desk). The number of screens is what counts, not what is shown on them.

entries.name: breast_mousepad
entries.description: A [computer](#computer) mousepad whose gel wrist rest is moulded into the shape of a pair of [breasts](#breasts). Versions shaped as a male chest exist as [well](#well).

entries.name: computer_tower
entries.description: The boxy case [holding](#holding) a desktop computer's internals, apart from its [monitor](#monitor), keyboard and mouse. Glowing fans behind a [glass](#glass) side panel are common in recent art.

entries.name: cracked_screen
entries.description: The [display](#display) of a [device](#device) has been cracked, whether a [phone](#phone), [monitor](#monitor), [laptop](#laptop) or handheld console. Damage worse than cracking is [broken_screen](#broken_screen).

entries.name: icon_(computing)
entries.description: A small pictogram of the sort that stands for a [file](#file), an app or a command on a [screen](#screen). It counts whether it sits on a depicted [device](#device) or floats over the picture as an interface element.

entries.name: loading_screen
entries.description: The [screen](#screen) a game or program puts up while it prepares itself, generally [carrying](#carrying) a progress bar or a percentage [figure](#figure). Artwork often fills the [space](#space) behind the bar.

entries.name: charging_device
entries.description: A [phone](#phone), handheld console or tablet is plugged in and taking power, usually with the lead in [plain](#plain) view. When it is the character themself being topped up, [recharging](#recharging) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: video_call
entries.description: People speaking to each other over live [video](#video) on a [phone](#phone), tablet or [computer](#computer). The [screen](#screen) showing the person on the other end is the giveaway.

entries.name: arcade_stick
entries.description: A boxed [controller](#controller) [carrying](#carrying) a ball-topped [lever](#lever) and a cluster of large [buttons](#buttons), copying an [arcade](#arcade) panel for play at home. Fighting game players call it a fightstick.

entries.name: blue_screen_of_death
entries.description: The blue [crash](#crash) [screen](#screen) a Windows [machine](#machine) shows after a fatal error, covered in white error text. It appears on a [monitor](#monitor), [laptop](#laptop) or [phone](#phone) inside the picture, usually as a joke about something going badly wrong.

entries.name: payphone
entries.description: A coin-fed public telephone on a wall or [standing](#standing) free; Japanese ones are squat and green with a [card](#card) slot beside the [coin](#coin) slot. Where only the surrounding kiosk shows, [phone_booth](#phone_booth) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: desktop_(computing)
entries.description: A computer's home [screen](#screen) on show, icons scattered over a wallpaper with a task bar along one edge. A maximised or full-screen [window](#window) does not count even when the bar is still visible.

entries.name: game_cartridge
entries.description: A hard plastic [shell](#shell) [holding](#holding) the chips of a console or handheld game. Drawn loose in a hand, being blown into, or half pushed into a slot.

entries.name: floppy_disk
entries.description: A [square](#square) plastic sleeve [holding](#holding) a magnetic disc, read through a slot on older computers. Now mostly a retro prop or the save icon on a [screen](#screen).

entries.name: phone_with_ears
entries.description: A [smartphone](#smartphone) in a case with [animal](#animal) ears rising from its top corners. The ears belong to the case, not to whoever is [holding](#holding) it.

entries.name: wii_remote
entries.description: A wand-shaped motion [controller](#controller) held upright in one hand, with a wrist [strap](#strap) looped through the base. Its shape sets it apart from the [two-handed](#two-handed) pads used by other consoles.

entries.name: virtual_reality
entries.description: Headsets, tracked controllers and the simulated worlds seen through them. Covers both someone wearing the gear and the digital [space](#space) they are experiencing.

entries.name: cellphone_strap
entries.description: A cord or loop [hanging](#hanging) from a [phone](#phone) to keep hold of it, which in Japan grew into a whole culture of [dangling](#dangling) charms and character figures. The phone itself may be out of frame.

entries.name: incoming_call
entries.description: A [phone](#phone) or other [device](#device) signalling that somebody is [calling](#calling): a lit [screen](#screen), [ring](#ring) marks, a vibration effect. Nobody has answered yet.

entries.name: calculator
entries.description: A small keypad [device](#device) for [working](#working) out sums, from a [pocket](#pocket) [model](#model) to a scientific one. It turns up on desks in study and [office](#office) scenes.

entries.name: printer
entries.description: The [office](#office) [machine](#machine) that puts text or images onto [paper](#paper). Usually shown beside a [desk](#desk) or [computer](#computer), sometimes with a sheet emerging from it.

entries.name: painttool_sai
entries.description: The drawing program itself appears in the picture, whether its canvas [window](#window), its toolbars or its [logo](#logo). Artwork merely made with it takes [painttool_sai_(medium)](#painttool_sai_(medium)) instead.

entries.name: broken_screen
entries.description: A [display](#display), whether [phone](#phone), [monitor](#monitor) or [television](#television), with its panel cracked or [shattered](#shattered). It may still be lit up behind the damage.

entries.name: holographic_touchscreen
entries.description: A projected light [display](#display) that also answers to touch, with fingers pressing controls [floating](#floating) in the air. A narrower case of [holographic_monitor](#holographic_monitor).

entries.name: internet
entries.description: Being online shown in a general way: browser windows, feeds, chat threads or a stylised web of connections. Reach for it when the network itself is the subject and [no](#no) particular named service is.

entries.name: progress_bar
entries.description: The on-screen strip that fills up to show how far along something is, such as playback, a download, or a loading [screen](#screen). Timestamps or a percentage [figure](#figure) may sit beside it.

entries.name: abacus
entries.description: The bead-and-rod [counting](#counting) frame still in daily use across East Asia, known in Japan as a soroban. It appears in shops, classrooms and period scenes, usually being worked by hand.

entries.name: floating_screen
entries.description: A [monitor](#monitor) or [display](#display) panel [hanging](#hanging) unsupported in the air, standard furniture for science-fiction interfaces. A [transparent](#transparent) projected image is a holographic monitor, and one [cast](#cast) onto a surface is a monitor projection.

entries.name: graphics_card
entries.description: The [computer](#computer) expansion [card](#card) that drives [video](#video) output, known by its long board, fan shroud and row of [display](#display) sockets. Turns up as loot, as a status symbol and in jokes about prices.

entries.name: cracked_phone
entries.description: A [phone](#phone) whose [display](#display) has [shattered](#shattered) into a web of cracks. Usually a small disaster inside the story of the picture.

entries.name: wii_u
entries.description: A home game console from the early 2010s, a small rounded [box](#box) paired with a screened handheld [controller](#controller). It is shown as hardware [sitting](#sitting) in the scene rather than as gameplay.

entries.name: cpu
entries.description: The [tower](#tower) or case of a desktop [computer](#computer), the [box](#box) everything else plugs into. Usually drawn beside a [monitor](#monitor) and a keyboard.

entries.name: wii_u_gamepad
entries.description: The tablet-like [controller](#controller) belonging to the Wii U, a [screen](#screen) framed by sticks and [buttons](#buttons) held in both hands. It is often drawn in use while its owner sits and plays.

entries.name: headphones
entries.description: Two speakers joined by a band over or behind the head, generally covering the whole ear, worn or carried. Small pieces [sitting](#sitting) in the ear without a band are [earphones](#earphones) or [earbuds](#earbuds).

entries.name: microphone
entries.description: A [device](#device) for [singing](#singing) or speaking into, held by hand, mounted on a stand, or worn as a [headset](#headset), including the boom mics used by film crews. Add [holding_microphone](#holding_microphone) or [microphone_stand](#microphone_stand) depending on how it's used.

entries.name: headset
entries.description: Headphones with a [microphone](#microphone) on a boom in front of the mouth, often covering only one ear. Stage idols, call-centre [staff](#staff) and [military](#military) operators wear them.

entries.name: camera
entries.description: A [device](#device) for taking still photographs, raised to the eye, hung on a [strap](#strap) or [standing](#standing) on a [tripod](#tripod). Anything that records moving pictures takes [video_camera](#video_camera) or [camcorder](#camcorder).

entries.name: headphones_around_neck
entries.description: Headphones hang at the throat like a [collar](#collar) instead of [sitting](#sitting) over the ears.

entries.name: television
entries.description: A TV set present in the scene, whether an [old](#old) boxy [model](#model) or a modern flat [screen](#screen). A real capture from a broadcast is [anime_screenshot](#anime_screenshot), and an invented broadcast is [fake_screenshot](#fake_screenshot).

entries.name: recording
entries.description: Audio or [video](#video) is being recorded within the scene, shown through a [viewfinder](#viewfinder) frame, a REC [marker](#marker) in a [corner](#corner), or a [camera](#camera) aimed at the subject. Combine with [video_camera](#video_camera) or viewfinder depending on what is drawn.

entries.name: earphones
entries.description: Small speakers worn in or on the ears with [no](#no) band over the head. Takes in [earbuds](#earbuds) and clip-on types; a [device](#device) with only one [speaker](#speaker) is an [earpiece](#earpiece).

entries.name: microphone_stand
entries.description: An adjustable stand that holds a [microphone](#microphone) upright, freeing the performer's or speaker's hands. Typical of [concert](#concert) and [idol](#idol) [stage](#stage) scenes.

entries.name: cat_ear_headphones
entries.description: Headphones with [cat](#cat) ears built into the [headband](#headband), gadget and accessory at once. The best-known real version lights up and carries speakers inside the ears.

entries.name: earpiece
entries.description: A single small earphone worn in one ear, the sort agents, guards and [stage](#stage) performers use. It carries [no](#no) [microphone](#microphone), which is what separates it from a [headset](#headset).

entries.name: megaphone
entries.description: A cone-shaped [device](#device) held to the mouth to project the voice, or its electric cousin the bullhorn, which pairs a [microphone](#microphone) with a horn [speaker](#speaker). Common at sports days, protests and cheer scenes.

entries.name: digital_media_player
entries.description: A [pocket](#pocket) [device](#device) that stores, sorts and plays audio files, the sort carried on a [strap](#strap) or in a pocket with [earphones](#earphones) [running](#running) from it.

entries.name: speaker
entries.description: A loudspeaker [cabinet](#cabinet) converting a signal into [sound](#sound), [standing](#standing) on the [floor](#floor), a [desk](#desk), or mounted to a wall. Part of [stereo](#stereo), PA, [computer](#computer), or [concert](#concert) setups.

entries.name: binoculars
entries.description: Two small telescopes joined side by side for looking at distant things, held up to the eyes or hung round the [neck](#neck). Handed to scouts, lookouts and birdwatchers.

entries.name: earbuds
entries.description: Small [earphones](#earphones) that rest in the [bowl](#bowl) of the outer ear rather than over it, corded or [wireless](#wireless). Drawn in the ears of somebody [listening](#listening) to [music](#music).

entries.name: walkie-talkie
entries.description: A handheld two-way [radio](#radio) held to the mouth or clipped to gear, typical of soldiers, [police](#police) and security characters. Backpack radios are [field_radio](#field_radio).

entries.name: video_camera
entries.description: A physical [camera](#camera) that records moving pictures, from a handheld [camcorder](#camcorder) to a [studio](#studio) TV or film camera. A scene framed as seen through one is [viewfinder](#viewfinder) or [recording](#recording), not this.

entries.name: phonograph
entries.description: A [record](#record) player, especially the [old](#old) gramophone with a wide horn and a hand crank, though modern turntables count as [well](#well). The disc itself is tagged separately.

entries.name: crt
entries.description: A boxy cathode-ray-tube [television](#television) or [monitor](#monitor) [standing](#standing) in the scene, deep at the [back](#back) and [heavy](#heavy), the kind flat panels replaced. Sets a retro room or an [old](#old) [arcade](#arcade).

entries.name: radio
entries.description: A radio set, from a compact tabletop receiver with dials to a handheld transceiver, shown either as a prop or in active use. Combine with whatever activity is happening around it, such as [listening](#listening) or transmitting.

entries.name: camcorder
entries.description: A handheld [video](#video) [camera](#camera) with a flip-out [screen](#screen) or an eyepiece, held up to [record](#record), pointed at somebody or set down [running](#running). The still-photo kind is a camera instead.

entries.name: telescope
entries.description: An optical [instrument](#instrument) for viewing distant things, whether a [tube](#tube) fixed on a stand and aimed skyward or a hand-held [spyglass](#spyglass). Often paired with [stargazing](#stargazing) and a [night](#night) [sky](#sky).

entries.name: cd
entries.description: A compact disc, the shiny optical disc [holding](#holding) [music](#music) or data, held up, [spinning](#spinning) in a player or [lying](#lying) beside its case. It also turns up as a prop or a [hanging](#hanging) decoration.

entries.name: behind-the-head_headphones
entries.description: Headphones whose band curves around the [back](#back) of the [skull](#skull) instead of arching over the top. Tag [headphones](#headphones) as [well](#well).

entries.name: record
entries.description: A flat vinyl disc, usually black, [carrying](#carrying) a [spiral](#spiral) groove that a [stylus](#stylus) tracks to play [music](#music). Shown [spinning](#spinning) on a [turntable](#turntable), held by the edges, or stacked in a [crate](#crate).

entries.name: tripod
entries.description: A three-legged stand that holds something steady, most often a [camera](#camera). Also used to support telescopes, lights and surveying equipment.

entries.name: shared_earphones
entries.description: A wired pair of [earphones](#earphones) [split](#split) between two characters, one [bud](#bud) each, so both hear the same track. The short [cable](#cable) keeps their heads close together.

entries.name: audio_jack
entries.description: The plug ending an audio [cable](#cable), a slim metal prong banded into tip, [ring](#ring) and sleeve, or the socket it pushes into. Headphones, microphones and electric guitars all finish in one.

entries.name: throat_microphone
entries.description: A [microphone](#microphone) worn snug against the [neck](#neck) like a [choker](#choker), picking up speech through the skin rather than through the air. A standard fitting on [military](#military) and tactical character designs.

entries.name: flat_screen_tv
entries.description: A slim [television](#television) only a few centimetres deep, hung on a wall or [standing](#standing) on a [cabinet](#cabinet). Bulky [tube](#tube) sets and rear-projection boxes are something else.

entries.name: selfie_stick
entries.description: An extendable [pole](#pole) with a [phone](#phone) or [camera](#camera) clamped at the far end, held out so the [photographer](#photographer) fits into the frame. Usually paired with a [selfie](#selfie) or a group shot.

entries.name: camera_around_neck
entries.description: A [camera](#camera) hangs at the chest from a [strap](#strap) looped over the [neck](#neck), leaving both hands free. It marks its owner out as a [photographer](#photographer), tourist or [reporter](#reporter).

entries.name: film_strip
entries.description: A length of film showing a run of small frames with sprocket holes down both edges. It may carry motion picture frames or stills from a [camera](#camera).

entries.name: headphones_removed
entries.description: Headphones are in the picture but nobody has them on — [hanging](#hanging) from a hand, [lying](#lying) on a [desk](#desk), set down beside the character.

entries.name: satellite_dish
entries.description: A parabolic antenna aimed at the [sky](#sky) to pick up broadcast or [radio](#radio) signals, mounted on a roof or wall. A single huge dish, or a line of them all facing one way, is a radio [telescope](#telescope) instead.

entries.name: black_headphones
entries.description: Over-ear or on-ear [headphones](#headphones) in black, worn on the head, hung round the [neck](#neck) or [resting](#resting) nearby. Only the colour is recorded, not whether anything is [playing](#playing).

entries.name: wireless_earphones
entries.description: Small [earbuds](#earbuds) [sitting](#sitting) in the ears with [no](#no) [cable](#cable) [running](#running) down to a [device](#device). They are frequently drawn with a stem below each [bud](#bud), sometimes shown beside their charging case.

entries.name: cd_case
entries.description: The hinged plastic sleeve a compact disc lives in, [cover](#cover) art slipped behind the front panel. Found stacked on desks, filed on shelves and [lying](#lying) open beside a player.

entries.name: boombox
entries.description: A big portable [stereo](#stereo) with a [carrying](#carrying) [handle](#handle), built-in speakers and a cassette deck, disc [tray](#tray) or [radio](#radio). It runs from batteries or the mains, and the loudest models grew nearly as large as a [suitcase](#suitcase).

entries.name: earphones_removed
entries.description: A pair of [earphones](#earphones) is in the picture but in nobody's ears, held, [hanging](#hanging) loose or laid aside. Where only one [bud](#bud) has come out, [single_earphone_removed](#single_earphone_removed) is the name.

entries.name: single_earphone_removed
entries.description: One earbud stays in place while the other has been pulled out and hangs free. Done to hear what is going on nearby, or to hold the loose side out for somebody else to listen.

entries.name: turntable
entries.description: A [record](#record) player with a flat rotating platter, tonearm and electrical pickup, distinct from older crank or horn phonographs. Heavily associated with DJ setups.

entries.name: pink_headphones
entries.description: Over-ear or on-ear [headphones](#headphones) in pink, worn on the head or slung round the [neck](#neck). Earbuds and in-ear sets take their own tags.

entries.name: cassette_player
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) that plays cassette tapes, from a [pocket](#pocket) personal player to a large home deck with speakers. A [staple](#staple) of nostalgic and 1980s-flavoured scenes.

entries.name: rabbit_ear_headphones
entries.description: Headphones fitted with false [rabbit](#rabbit) ears positioned as though they were the wearer's own. Headphones simply decorated with a rabbit pattern instead take the [bunny_headphones](#bunny_headphones) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: cassette_tape
entries.description: A small plastic [shell](#shell) [holding](#holding) magnetic [tape](#tape) wound between two reels, openings along the bottom edge for the player's heads. Often drawn with a hand-written [label](#label).

entries.name: vintage_microphone
entries.description: The bulky chrome [studio](#studio) [microphone](#microphone) of mid-century [radio](#radio) and rockabilly stages, [standing](#standing) on a round base or slung in a [ring](#ring). Chosen for period flavour rather than as modern performance gear.

entries.name: studio_microphone
entries.description: A large condenser [microphone](#microphone) of the kind slung on a boom arm in a [recording](#recording) booth, usually shown with a round pop [screen](#screen) in front of it. Implies microphone.

entries.name: white_headphones
entries.description: Over-ear [headphones](#headphones) in white, worn on the head or slung around the [neck](#neck). In-ear buds fall under a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pop_filter
entries.description: A fabric-covered [hoop](#hoop) mounted in front of a [studio](#studio) [microphone](#microphone) to soften bursts of [breath](#breath) and keep spit off the capsule. A fixture of [recording](#recording) booths and streamer desks.

entries.name: stereo
entries.description: A home audio system with a receiver [feeding](#feeding) two or more separate speakers, [playing](#playing) from CD, cassette or a [record](#record) deck. Sits in the room as furniture rather than being carried around.

entries.name: headphones_over_headwear
entries.description: Headphones sit on top of a [hat](#hat), [hood](#hood) or [helmet](#helmet) rather than on the hair, the band crossing over the headwear.

entries.name: wireless
entries.description: A [device](#device) that would ordinarily trail a [cable](#cable), such as [headphones](#headphones), a [microphone](#microphone), or a game [controller](#controller), is drawn without one. The missing cord is the whole point of the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: dvd_case
entries.description: The flat plastic clamshell a [video](#video) disc is sold in, printed [cover](#cover) art slipped under its sleeve. Shown as [merchandise](#merchandise) or lined up along a [shelf](#shelf).

entries.name: videocassette
entries.description: The flat plastic [shell](#shell) [holding](#holding) magnetic [tape](#tape) that a VCR plays. Usually shows up in retro rooms, beside a player, or as shorthand for the pre-disc era.

entries.name: hidden_camera
entries.description: A [camera](#camera) placed to [record](#record) somebody who has [no](#no) [idea](#idea) it is there, tucked into a [shelf](#shelf), a vent or an ordinary object. The picture may show the [device](#device) itself or be framed as the footage it captures.

entries.name: single-lens_reflex_camera
entries.description: A [camera](#camera) whose [viewfinder](#viewfinder) looks through the taking lens by way of a [mirror](#mirror) and prism, so the framing [matches](#matches) the photograph exactly. Recognizable by the boxy body with a raised hump above the lens mount.

entries.name: webcam
entries.description: A small [camera](#camera) clipped to the top of a [monitor](#monitor), used for [video](#video) calls and livestreaming. Its presence usually signals that the scene is a call or a broadcast.

entries.name: film_reel
entries.description: A [spool](#spool) with movie film wound between two rimmed sides, ready to go on a [projector](#projector). Not the similar-looking reel of magnetic [tape](#tape).

entries.name: binaural_microphone
entries.description: A [stereo](#stereo) [microphone](#microphone) built as a pair of artificial ears with a capsule inside each [canal](#canal), sometimes mounted on a [dummy](#dummy) head. Strongly tied to ASMR [recording](#recording).

entries.name: cd_player
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) that spins and reads audio compact discs, from a hi-fi deck to a [boombox](#boombox) or a [car](#car) unit. The pocket-sized battery-powered kind is a [cd_walkman](#cd_walkman).

entries.name: security_camera
entries.description: A fixed or panning [camera](#camera) mounted to keep [watch](#watch) over a place, usually set high on a wall or [ceiling](#ceiling) in a small housing. Its feed appears as evidence or as a voyeuristic framing [device](#device).

entries.name: unworn_headphones
entries.description: Headphones appear in the picture but are not over anyone's ears or [resting](#resting) on a [neck](#neck), whether [hanging](#hanging) from a [hook](#hook), [sitting](#sitting) on a [desk](#desk) or held in hand.

entries.name: projector
entries.description: A [device](#device) that throws a picture onto a wall, [screen](#screen), or other surface, usually shown with a visible cone of light. Common in classrooms, cinemas, and darkened presentation rooms.

entries.name: clapperboard
entries.description: The hinged slate snapped shut at the start of a film take to line up [sound](#sound) and picture, its face chalked with scene and take numbers. Usually held by a director or crew member.

entries.name: digital_camera
entries.description: A modern [camera](#camera) with a [screen](#screen) on the [back](#back) in place of a film advance, compact or SLR. Held up to shoot, checked afterwards, or [hanging](#hanging) on a [neck](#neck) [strap](#strap).

entries.name: microphone_wand
entries.description: A slim rod or [staff](#staff) with a [microphone](#microphone) fixed at its tip, carried by idols and [stage](#stage) performers as much for the [silhouette](#silhouette) it creates as for its [sound](#sound) function.

entries.name: red_headphones
entries.description: Over-ear [headphones](#headphones) coloured red, worn on the head or [hanging](#hanging) around the [neck](#neck). They also work as a design accent on music-themed characters.

entries.name: mixing_console
entries.description: A [desk](#desk) of faders, knobs and meters used to balance [sound](#sound) coming from microphones and instruments. Found in [recording](#recording) studios, live venues and DJ booths alike.

entries.name: bunny_headphones
entries.description: Headphones built around a [rabbit](#rabbit) motif, worked into the cups or the band. Sets with upright fake ears rising above the head are [rabbit_ear_headphones](#rabbit_ear_headphones), and neither counts as real [animal](#animal) ears.

entries.name: tv_show
entries.description: A [television](#television) programme visible within the picture, [playing](#playing) on a set or presented as its own broadcast scene. News desks, panel shows and drama playing in the background all qualify.

entries.name: facial_recognition
entries.description: Camera software picks out faces, drawn as brackets or boxes around each head, sometimes with readouts beside them. Distinct from a [plain](#plain) [viewfinder](#viewfinder), whose marks sit in the middle of the frame.

entries.name: jukebox
entries.description: A coin-operated [cabinet](#cabinet) that plays a [record](#record) picked from the stock inside it, its front lined with lettered and [numbered](#numbered) [buttons](#buttons) and edged in [glowing](#glowing) coloured tubes. Diners and [bars](#bars) are where it stands.

entries.name: boom_microphone
entries.description: A [microphone](#microphone) mounted on the end of a long [pole](#pole), either lifted by a crew member or clamped to a weighted stand. It belongs to filming, [catching](#catching) speech from just outside the shot; a microphone [standing](#standing) on a [desk](#desk) is not one.

entries.name: cd_walkman
entries.description: A palm-sized portable CD player carried about with [headphones](#headphones) plugged into it. Only name a maker when the branding is actually visible on the body.

entries.name: twin-lens_reflex_camera
entries.description: A boxy [camera](#camera) [carrying](#carrying) two stacked lenses of matching focal length, one exposing the film and one [feeding](#feeding) a waist-level [viewfinder](#viewfinder) looked down into. Classic Rolleiflex-style bodies are the best-known example.

entries.name: dvd_(object)
entries.description: A shiny optical disc [holding](#holding) [video](#video), shown bare in a hand or [sliding](#sliding) into a player. The format that sat between videotape and Blu-ray.

entries.name: dial_television
entries.description: An older cathode-ray set worked by rotary knobs, one for channel and one for volume, sometimes with smaller trim dials below. Reads instantly as furniture from before the eighties.

entries.name: field_radio
entries.description: A backpack-sized transceiver carried by one operator, with a handset on a cord and a [whip](#whip) antenna. Standard kit in [military](#military) and expedition scenes.

entries.name: record_jacket
entries.description: The [square](#square) [cardboard](#cardboard) sleeve a vinyl [record](#record) is sold and stored in, [protecting](#protecting) the disc while [carrying](#carrying) the [cover](#cover) art. Appears in music-themed scenes as [well](#well) as parodying real album covers.

entries.name: horn_speaker
entries.description: A flared metal [speaker](#speaker) that throws [sound](#sound) through an acoustic cone. Public address poles, megaphones and antique phonographs carry them.

entries.name: microphone_cord
entries.description: The lead trailing from a handheld [microphone](#microphone), looped in the hand, [coiled](#coiled) at the [feet](#feet) or snaking across a [stage](#stage). Marks a wired mic rather than a [wireless](#wireless) one.

entries.name: polaroid_camera
entries.description: A boxy instant [camera](#camera) that pushes a developing print out through a slot in its front. The print it produces is tagged [polaroid_photo](#polaroid_photo).

entries.name: tape_recorder
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) for [playing](#playing) or [recording](#recording) cassette [tape](#tape), with spools, chunky [buttons](#buttons) and usually a small [speaker](#speaker) grille. Appears as a [desk](#desk) prop, a portable unit slung over a shoulder, or held out to catch someone's words.

entries.name: hammer
entries.description: A tool for striking, whether [driving](#driving) nails, forging metal or [breaking](#breaking) things apart. A large one, such as a [sledgehammer](#sledgehammer), may be wielded as a [crushing](#crushing) [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: scissors
entries.description: A pair of pivoted metal blades that [slide](#slide) past each other to cut [paper](#paper), [cloth](#cloth), hair or [wire](#wire). Tag whenever scissors are shown, held or in use.

entries.name: ladle
entries.description: A long-handled scoop for [serving](#serving) [soup](#soup) and other liquids. It is usually in the hand of somebody [stirring](#stirring) a pot or dishing out of one.

entries.name: wrench
entries.description: A hand tool for gripping and turning nuts and bolts, also called a spanner. It is often held by a [mechanic](#mechanic) character; add [holding](#holding) when it sits in someone's hand.

entries.name: needle
entries.description: A slim pointed shaft used for [sewing](#sewing), [knitting](#knitting), pinning things together or thrown as a [weapon](#weapon). Medical [injection](#injection) needles belong to [syringe](#syringe) instead.

entries.name: shovel
entries.description: The [familiar](#familiar) [digging](#digging) tool with a broad blade on a long [handle](#handle), spades included. The [card](#card) [suit](#suit) is [spade_(shape)](#spade_(shape)), and the small [gardening](#gardening) hand tool is [trowel](#trowel).

entries.name: chainsaw
entries.description: A motorised [saw](#saw) with a toothed loop [running](#running) around its bar. It appears far more often as a gruesome [weapon](#weapon) in horror-flavoured scenes than as a tool for [cutting](#cutting) timber.

entries.name: spatula
