entries.description: A flat-bladed [kitchen](#kitchen) tool used to flip, lift, or [scrape](#scrape) [food](#food), or a soft rubber version for [spreading](#spreading) [icing](#icing). A common sight in [cooking](#cooking) scenes.

entries.name: mallet
entries.description: A [hammer](#hammer) with a broad flat-faced head, in wood or rubber, for [driving](#driving) pegs, striking at games or [swinging](#swinging) as a cartoon [weapon](#weapon). Much bulkier in the head than an ordinary hammer.

entries.name: whisk
entries.description: A [kitchen](#kitchen) [utensil](#utensil) of looped [wire](#wire) on a [handle](#handle), used for beating eggs or [cream](#cream) in a [bowl](#bowl). Add [whisking](#whisking) when a character is actively using it.

entries.name: watering_can
entries.description: A portable [can](#can) with a long spout and top [handle](#handle) for [watering](#watering) plants by hand. Typical of [gardening](#gardening) scenes.

entries.name: pointer
entries.description: A slim rod of wood, metal or plastic used by a [teacher](#teacher) or officer to indicate something on a board or [map](#map). A [laser](#laser) pointer, a mouse [cursor](#cursor), and an arrow symbol are all separate tags.

entries.name: drill
entries.description: The tool for boring holes, from a handheld power drill to an oversized one swung as a [weapon](#weapon). Mecha and [fantasy](#fantasy) designs often build one into an arm.

entries.name: kitchen_knife
entries.description: A [knife](#knife) of the sort used to prepare [food](#food), with a broad blade and a [plain](#plain) [handle](#handle). It is tagged as [well](#well) when one is brandished as a [threat](#threat).

entries.name: hand_net
entries.description: A [mesh](#mesh) [bag](#bag) stretched on a rigid [hoop](#hoop) and fitted to a [handle](#handle), used for [catching](#catching) things. Butterfly nets are by far the most common, but the same [tag](#tag) covers nets for [fish](#fish), small animals or skimming a [pool](#pool).

entries.name: saw
entries.description: A [cutting](#cutting) tool with a toothed blade, [wire](#wire) or [chain](#chain), pushed and pulled through wood or other hard material. Covers hand saws and larger types.

entries.name: butterfly_net
entries.description: A long-handled [net](#net) of fine [mesh](#mesh), swung to catch butterflies without damaging their [wings](#wings). It serves for any insect-catching net, sturdier sweep nets included.

entries.name: screwdriver
entries.description: A hand tool with a flat, [cross](#cross), or star-shaped tip used to turn screws. Not the [cocktail](#cocktail) of the same name.

entries.name: pickaxe
entries.description: A mining tool with a curved steel head set crosswise on a long [handle](#handle), pointed for [breaking](#breaking) [rock](#rock). Carried by miners, dwarves and block-world adventurers, and sometimes swung as an improvised [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: kine
entries.description: The big wooden [mallet](#mallet) swung to pound steamed [rice](#rice) into [mochi](#mochi), usually over a [heavy](#heavy) mortar. It turns up in New Year scenes and in pictures of the [rabbit](#rabbit) in the [moon](#moon).

entries.name: tools
entries.description: Hand tools such as a [hammer](#hammer), [wrench](#wrench) or [screwdriver](#screwdriver) present in the scene, whether in use, carried or [lying](#lying) in a [workshop](#workshop). Add the specific tool's own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: tongs
entries.description: A two-armed gripping tool for picking up [food](#food) or [hot](#hot) items, most often in a [kitchen](#kitchen) or at a barbecue. Add [cooking](#cooking) when in use.

entries.name: cleaver
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) one-handed butcher's [knife](#knife) with a [square](#square) blade, roughly 18 to 25 cm long. A bigger or [two-handed](#two-handed) blade of the same shape is a nata; a favourite prop for unhinged characters.

entries.name: boxcutter
entries.description: A slim-handled utility [knife](#knife) with a blade that slides in and out, used to slit boxes open. The segmented snap-off type is the one usually drawn, and the object turns up often in pictures about [self-harm](#self-harm).

entries.name: nata_(tool)
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) Japanese hatchet with a rectangular blade, close to an oversized [cleaver](#cleaver), used for splitting wood and [bamboo](#bamboo). It doubles as a stock [weapon](#weapon) for [yandere](#yandere) characters.

entries.name: tape_measure
entries.description: A [flexible](#flexible) marked strip used for [measuring](#measuring): a tailor's [cloth](#cloth) or plastic one for taking body [measurements](#measurements), or a builder's metal one housed in a small case. Often seen during a bust-measuring scene.

entries.name: crowbar
entries.description: An L-shaped steel pry bar with flattened [claws](#claws), used to [lever](#lever) crates and doors open or swung as an improvised [weapon](#weapon). The notch in the hooked end pulls nails.

entries.name: sickle
entries.description: A short-handled [farming](#farming) tool with a curved blade, used for [cutting](#cutting) [grass](#grass) or grain. Also drawn as a [weapon](#weapon) in [fantasy](#fantasy) art, and paired with a [hammer](#hammer) it forms the communist [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: pastry_bag
entries.description: The cone-shaped [bag](#bag) squeezed to pipe [icing](#icing) or soft [food](#food) through a nozzle, filled at its wide end and twisted shut. It turns up in [baking](#baking) and cake-decorating scenes; also called a piping bag.

entries.name: shamoji
entries.description: The broad, flat [paddle](#paddle) used to scoop and turn cooked [rice](#rice), traditionally wood or [bamboo](#bamboo) and nowadays often moulded plastic. Also used to fold vinegar through [sushi](#sushi) rice.

entries.name: sewing_needle
entries.description: A slim steel [needle](#needle) with an eye at the blunt end to carry [thread](#thread), pushed through [fabric](#fabric) to stitch it. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [syringe](#syringe) or a [knitting](#knitting) needle.

entries.name: circular_saw
entries.description: A powered [saw](#saw) that [cuts](#cuts) with a [spinning](#spinning) toothed disc rather than a pushed blade. At home in workshops, and a favourite prop for horror scenes.

entries.name: trowel
entries.description: A small one-handed blade on a short [handle](#handle), used to dig, scoop or spread material. A [gardening](#gardening) version ends in a scooped point, while a plastering version has a flat rectangular face.

entries.name: pitchfork
entries.description: A long-handled [farm](#farm) [fork](#fork) with several tines, used for lifting [hay](#hay), straw or manure. Sharpened, barbed points turn the same [silhouette](#silhouette) into a [trident](#trident) instead.

entries.name: chisel
entries.description: A hand tool with a wedged blade ground to a [cutting](#cutting) edge, pushed by hand or struck with a [mallet](#mallet) to cut wood, stone or metal. Turns up in [carving](#carving), sculpting and carpentry scenes.

entries.name: traffic_baton
entries.description: A [wand](#wand) that glows along its length, waved by [police](#police) to direct [traffic](#traffic) or by ground crews to marshal [aircraft](#aircraft). In its simplest form it is a [torch](#torch) wrapped in a coloured plastic [tube](#tube).

entries.name: pliers
entries.description: A hinged hand tool with two jaws for gripping, [bending](#bending), or snipping. Covers needle-nose types and [wire](#wire) cutters, whether in use or [lying](#lying) among other [tools](#tools).

entries.name: sledgehammer
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [two-handed](#two-handed) [hammer](#hammer) with a long shaft and a broad flat metal head. Its wide striking face spreads force rather than [concentrating](#concentrating) it, which suits demolition, [driving](#driving) [spikes](#spikes) and forcing doors, and makes it look close to a [mallet](#mallet).

entries.name: knitting_needle
entries.description: A long, blunt-tipped rod used in pairs to loop [yarn](#yarn) into [fabric](#fabric). Unlike a crochet [hook](#hook) it keeps an even thickness the whole way along and has [no](#no) hook at the tip.

entries.name: mortar_(bowl)
entries.description: A thick-walled [bowl](#bowl) in which things are [crushed](#crushed) and ground against the sides with a [pestle](#pestle). The oversized wooden tub used for pounding [mochi](#mochi) is one; the [artillery](#artillery) piece of the same name is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: paint_roller
entries.description: A sleeve of absorbent nap on a frame and [handle](#handle), run across a wall to spread [paint](#paint) quickly. Usually drawn with a [tray](#tray) or an open [can](#can) nearby.

entries.name: utensil
entries.description: A household implement, most often from the [kitchen](#kitchen). Use it as the fallback when the exact tool cannot be identified because its end runs off the edge of the picture and nothing else names it.

entries.name: ice_cream_spoon
entries.description: A stubby little [spoon](#spoon), flatter and shorter than ordinary [cutlery](#cutlery), meant for [eating](#eating) [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream). It is generally the one handed over with a [cup](#cup) or a [sundae](#sundae).

entries.name: pincushion
entries.description: A small stuffed [cushion](#cushion), classically shaped like a [tomato](#tomato), that needles and pins are [stuck](#stuck) into so they stay together and out of the way. Sewing and tailoring scenes use it.

entries.name: sewing_pin
entries.description: A short, straight [pin](#pin) with a head at one end, [stuck](#stuck) through [cloth](#cloth) to hold pattern pieces, [seams](#seams), or trims in place before anything is [stitched](#stitched). A temporary fastener, not the [stitching](#stitching) itself.

entries.name: hoe
entries.description: A long-handled [garden](#garden) tool with a flat blade set crosswise, used to break [soil](#soil) and cut [weeds](#weeds). It is often carried over the shoulder in [farming](#farming) scenes.

entries.name: rolling_pin
entries.description: The cylindrical [kitchen](#kitchen) tool used to flatten [dough](#dough), either a [plain](#plain) rod or one with handles at each end. In comedy it doubles as a blunt [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: claw_hammer
entries.description: The common carpentry [hammer](#hammer), flat on one face for [driving](#driving) nails and [split](#split) into a curved [fork](#fork) on the other for prying them out. The forked head is the giveaway.

entries.name: rake
entries.description: A long-handled [garden](#garden) tool ending in a row of [teeth](#teeth), swept across the ground to gather leaves and [grass](#grass) or dragged through [soil](#soil) to break it up.

entries.name: butter_knife
entries.description: A blunt, flat-bladed [knife](#knife) made for [spreading](#spreading) rather than [cutting](#cutting). It turns up at the [table](#table) beside [bread](#bread) and [jam](#jam).

entries.name: power_tool
entries.description: Any tool driven by a motor rather than by hand: drills, saws, sanders, nailers and the like. An [umbrella](#umbrella) [tag](#tag), so use the specific one when the tool [can](#can) be made out.

entries.name: pestle
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy) club-shaped tool used to crush and grind material against a mortar or a slab. Made of stone, wood or metal; in Japan often the long wooden one for pounding [rice](#rice) cakes.

entries.name: tweezers
entries.description: A pair of thin metal arms joined at one end and squeezed together to grip something tiny. Used for plucking hairs, handling small parts or picking out splinters.

entries.name: wood_carving_tool
entries.description: A short, chisel-like tool with a rounded grip and a small shaped blade, used for [cutting](#cutting) wood by hand. It is usually shown as part of a set laid out on a workbench.

entries.name: adjustable_wrench
entries.description: A spanner whose lower [jaw](#jaw) slides along a [worm](#worm) [screw](#screw) so the [opening](#opening) [can](#can) be [resized](#resized). The detached jaw and the visible [thread](#thread) beside it set it apart from a fixed [wrench](#wrench).

entries.name: gavel
entries.description: The short ceremonial [mallet](#mallet) a [judge](#judge) or auctioneer knocks against a block to call order or settle a matter. Appears in [courtroom](#courtroom) scenes, verdict jokes and auctions.

entries.name: shears
entries.description: Large two-bladed cutters worked with both hands, used on hedges, [wool](#wool) or [heavy](#heavy) [fabric](#fabric). Bulkier and blunter than an ordinary pair of [scissors](#scissors).

entries.name: set_square
entries.description: A flat triangular drawing aid used against a straightedge to rule lines at fixed angles. Belongs on desks in drafting, [architecture](#architecture), and maths-class scenes.

entries.name: hacksaw
entries.description: A metal-cutting [saw](#saw) whose thin blade is stretched taut inside a C-shaped frame with a pistol grip. Quite unlike a wood saw, whose broad blade stands free.

entries.name: power_drill
entries.description: A pistol-gripped electric tool with a trigger and a chuck that takes interchangeable bits. Bores holes and drives screws; the similar-looking impact [wrench](#wrench) is a different tool.

entries.name: japanese_saw
entries.description: A [saw](#saw) that [cuts](#cuts) on the pull stroke rather than the push, with a thin springy blade on a straight wooden [handle](#handle). The common ryoba carries [teeth](#teeth) on both edges, one set for [ripping](#ripping) and one across the grain.

entries.name: anvil
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) iron block with a flat [working](#working) face, a pointed horn at one end and [square](#square) holes in the top, on which a smith beats [hot](#hot) metal into shape. Forge scenes use it, and so do falling-anvil gags.

entries.name: gardening_shears
entries.description: Heavy-bladed cutters for stems and branches, from small one-handed secateurs to long [hedge](#hedge) [clippers](#clippers). Sometimes picked up as an improvised [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: measuring_cup
entries.description: A clear [cup](#cup) or jug marked with graduated lines for portioning ingredients, in metric or cup units. A [staple](#staple) prop in [baking](#baking) and [cooking](#cooking) scenes.

entries.name: soup_ladle
entries.description: A deep, half-round scoop on a short [handle](#handle) used to move [liquid](#liquid) between pots while [cooking](#cooking). The shallower, wider [sauce](#sauce) [ladle](#ladle) used at the [table](#table) is a separate implement.

entries.name: cutlery
entries.description: The handheld implements laid out at a [table](#table) for [eating](#eating): knives, forks, spoons and hybrids such as sporks. Narrower than utensils, which take in [cooking](#cooking) gear like ladles.

entries.name: snow_shovel
entries.description: A wide, flat-bladed [shovel](#shovel) made for clearing [snow](#snow), usually of ribbed plastic or light metal in a bright color. It lacks the raised sides of a [digging](#digging) spade.

entries.name: table_knife
entries.description: A blunt-tipped [knife](#knife) with a single dull [cutting](#cutting) edge, meant for cutting cooked [food](#food) at the [table](#table). Everyday [cutlery](#cutlery) rather than a [kitchen](#kitchen) or combat blade.

entries.name: shepherd's_crook
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [staff](#staff) topped with a curved [hook](#hook), used to steer and sometimes catch [sheep](#sheep). Carried by shepherds and by pastoral or religious figures in art.

entries.name: honey_dipper
entries.description: A grooved wooden [stick](#stick) used to lift [honey](#honey) out of a [jar](#jar) and let it run onto [food](#food). It is almost always drawn mid-drip.

entries.name: protractor
entries.description: The flat half-disc or full-disc tool marked out in degrees, used to measure and draw angles. Turns up in [classroom](#classroom) and study scenes alongside rulers and compasses.

entries.name: cutting_mat
entries.description: A tough self-healing plastic sheet, generally green or black and printed with a [measuring](#measuring) [grid](#grid), laid under work so that blades spare both the [table](#table) and their own edge. Craft, [sewing](#sewing) and model-making equipment, unlike the wooden board used for [food](#food).

entries.name: cookie_cutter
entries.description: A shaped metal or plastic form pressed into rolled [dough](#dough) so biscuits come out in a pattern. Usually drawn beside a [rolling](#rolling) [pin](#pin) and a dusting of [flour](#flour).

entries.name: ice_cream_scoop
entries.description: The [serving](#serving) [utensil](#utensil) with a half-round [bowl](#bowl), sometimes fitted with a sweep [lever](#lever), used to shape and lift balls of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream). It is not the [ball](#ball) itself, which other tags count.

entries.name: sewing_kit
entries.description: A boxed or bundled set [holding](#holding) [thread](#thread), needles, pins, and [fabric](#fabric) for a project. Usually drawn open with its contents on show.

entries.name: ice_pick
entries.description: A slim steel spike on a short [handle](#handle), made for chipping and splitting blocks of [ice](#ice). Anime hands it almost exclusively to unhinged characters, which is why it reads as a [weapon](#weapon); the mountaineer's ice [axe](#axe) is a different tool.

entries.name: soldering_iron
entries.description: A pen-shaped heated tool for [melting](#melting) solder to join electrical parts, often shown trailing a wisp of [smoke](#smoke) with a [coiled](#coiled) stand nearby. A fixture of electronics and repair scenes.

entries.name: clippers
entries.description: A small short-bladed [cutting](#cutting) tool worked in one hand, for trimming plants, snipping [thread](#thread) or tidying [model](#model) parts. Longer-bladed [garden](#garden) [tools](#tools) are [shears](#shears).

entries.name: compass_(instrument)
entries.description: A hinged two-legged drafting tool with a [pencil](#pencil) or nib in one leg, used to scribe circles and arcs. The navigation [device](#device) belongs under [compass](#compass).

entries.name: hand_saw
entries.description: The western style of [saw](#saw): a broad stiff toothed blade fixed into a wooden or plastic grip, [cutting](#cutting) on both push and pull. Japanese saws, thin and knife-like on a long straight [handle](#handle), look quite different.

entries.name: grater
entries.description: A [kitchen](#kitchen) implement with a [punched](#punched) metal face for shredding [food](#food), either a flat handheld blade or a four-sided [box](#box). Cheese, ginger and [daikon](#daikon) are what it usually meets.

entries.name: machinery
entries.description: Detailed [heavy](#heavy) mechanical equipment given visual [weight](#weight) in the picture: engines, hydraulics, vehicle innards, [mecha](#mecha) parts, and the armament rigs worn by [ship](#ship) girls. A generic unremarkable [device](#device) is [machine](#machine).

entries.name: cable
entries.description: Any [sheathed](#sheathed) cord, cable or [tube](#tube) — headphone leads, power cords, data lines, the thick conduits of science-fiction [machinery](#machinery). Bare metal strands with [no](#no) covering are [wire](#wire) instead.

entries.name: wire_(electrical)
entries.description: Cables and wires [running](#running) through a scene, [hanging](#hanging) loose, bundled together, or plugged into equipment. Cyberpunk interiors and [machine](#machine) rooms are typically full of them.

entries.name: radio_antenna
entries.description: A metal aerial for picking up [radio](#radio) signals, mounted on a [building](#building), a vehicle, a handset, or a robot's head. Combine with whatever it is attached to.

entries.name: gears
entries.description: Toothed wheels that [mesh](#mesh) and turn together, as inside [clockwork](#clockwork). A [staple](#staple) of [steampunk](#steampunk) imagery and machine-filled backgrounds.

entries.name: remote_control
entries.description: A handheld remote for a [television](#television), player, or air conditioner, pointed at the [device](#device) or [lying](#lying) around. Wireless game controllers and [computer](#computer) peripherals are tagged as their own things rather than this.

entries.name: electric_fan
entries.description: Spinning blades behind a [wire](#wire) [cage](#cage), [standing](#standing) on the [floor](#floor) or a [desk](#desk) to push air around a room. A [summer](#summer) prop, often [blowing](#blowing) hair and clothing about. One fixed overhead is [ceiling_fan](#ceiling_fan) instead.

entries.name: machine
entries.description: A mechanical [device](#device) of [no](#no) more particular kind, from [factory](#factory) apparatus to strange contraptions. Heavy equipment drawn in detail and given visual [weight](#weight) is [machinery](#machinery) instead.

entries.name: steering_wheel
entries.description: The round [wheel](#wheel) used to steer a [car](#car) or similar vehicle. A spoked ship's [helm](#helm) is tagged [ship's_wheel](#ship's_wheel) instead.

entries.name: caterpillar_tracks
entries.description: Continuous treads [running](#running) around drive wheels to spread a vehicle's [weight](#weight) over rough ground. Seen on tanks, half-tracks, bulldozers, excavators and some tractors.

entries.name: industrial_pipe
entries.description: Metal or plastic piping for [water](#water), [gas](#gas) or [steam](#steam), [running](#running) along walls and ceilings or through [factory](#factory) and [sewer](#sewer) scenes. Something smoked is a [smoking](#smoking) pipe, and a length swung as a [weapon](#weapon) is [lead_pipe](#lead_pipe).

entries.name: thrusters
entries.description: Rocket or jet propulsion nozzles on an [aircraft](#aircraft), [spacecraft](#spacecraft) or [mecha](#mecha), often shown [firing](#firing). Commonly paired with mecha, spacecraft or [flying](#flying).

entries.name: air_conditioner
entries.description: The boxed cooling unit mounted high on a wall or set into a [window](#window). It is a stock fixture of apartments and classrooms in [summer](#summer) scenes.

entries.name: wheel
entries.description: A standalone wheel, or one made prominent in the picture, whether from a vehicle, a [cart](#cart), a mill or a piece of [machinery](#machinery). An ordinary vehicle's own wheels don't need this [tag](#tag).

entries.name: jet_booster
entries.description: Thrusters mounted on a [machine](#machine) or a powered [suit](#suit), [throwing](#throwing) out flame and [exhaust](#exhaust) to drive it forward or hold it aloft. Mecha and armoured suits carry them as standard.

entries.name: rocket_booster
entries.description: The thrust unit strapped to a craft or [suit](#suit) to push it upward, drawn as a nozzle trailing flame and [exhaust](#exhaust). It may be a launch [stage](#stage) on a [rocket](#rocket) or a [backpack](#backpack) thruster on a character.

entries.name: winding_key
entries.description: A wind-up [key](#key) like those found on [clockwork](#clockwork) toys, often shown sticking out of a character's [back](#back) to mark them as a [robot](#robot) or living [doll](#doll). Shinonome Nano of Nichijou is the character best known for wearing one.

entries.name: crane_(machine)
entries.description: A large lifting [machine](#machine) with a boom and [cable](#cable), [standing](#standing) over [building](#building) sites, docks and [industrial](#industrial) skylines. Not the [bird](#bird), and not the [arcade](#arcade) claw machine.

entries.name: screw
entries.description: A threaded metal fastener with a slotted or cross-shaped head, turned by hand or with a [screwdriver](#screwdriver) to join parts together. Shown driven into a surface, [lying](#lying) loose as a small detail, or studding a robot's plating.

entries.name: propeller
entries.description: A [spinning](#spinning) multi-bladed rotor that drives an [aircraft](#aircraft) or [boat](#boat) through air or [water](#water). Covers propellers on planes, ships, and [toy](#toy) or [fantasy](#fantasy) contraptions alike; add the vehicle's own [tag](#tag) when the whole craft is shown.

entries.name: electric_plug
entries.description: The moulded end of a power cord, with pins that go into a socket. Drawn on appliances, trailing from a [cable](#cable), or used for a visual [pun](#pun). The socket it fits is [electrical_outlet](#electrical_outlet).

entries.name: electrical_outlet
entries.description: A socket set into a wall with slots for a plug, usually a small piece of [interior](#interior) detail. Sometimes it carries a joke together with an [electric_plug](#electric_plug). Also called a power outlet or power socket.

entries.name: jetpack
entries.description: A thrust unit worn on the [back](#back) that carries its wearer into the air, a science-fiction [staple](#staple). Flame or vapour trailing from the nozzles usually marks it in flight.

entries.name: battle_damage
entries.description: Fighting has left visible marks on a [machine](#machine), vehicle or [mecha](#mecha): dented plating, scorch streaks, [torn](#torn) armour, missing parts. Androids, cyborgs and robots count as [well](#well); damage to a living body takes the [injury](#injury) tags.

entries.name: cash_register
entries.description: The till on a [shop](#shop) [counter](#counter), with its keypad, [display](#display) and [money](#money) [drawer](#drawer). Its presence marks the spot as a checkout.

entries.name: bolt_(hardware)
entries.description: A straight metal fastener with a head, held by a nut and turned with a spanner. A [screw](#screw) tapers and [cuts](#cuts) its own [thread](#thread) into the material, which a bolt does not.

entries.name: magnet
entries.description: An object that pulls iron to itself, drawn as a [horseshoe](#horseshoe) or a bar with one end red and the other blue. Novelty [shapes](#shapes) [stuck](#stuck) to a [refrigerator](#refrigerator) [door](#door) count too.

entries.name: barcode_scanner
entries.description: A [device](#device) that reads a printed [barcode](#barcode) and passes what it finds to a till or [computer](#computer). It comes as a gun-shaped handheld unit or as a [glass](#glass) [plate](#plate) set into a [shop](#shop) [counter](#counter).

entries.name: radar
entries.description: Equipment or a [display](#display) used to locate objects by [bouncing](#bouncing) [radio](#radio) [waves](#waves) off them, often shown as a [screen](#screen) with blips [sweeping](#sweeping) across a [circle](#circle). Common in [military](#military), aviation, and naval settings.

entries.name: battery
entries.description: A cell or pack that stores chemical [energy](#energy) and gives it [back](#back) as [electricity](#electricity). It is drawn as a cylinder with a raised terminal or as a flat rectangular block.

entries.name: engine
entries.description: A motor treated as an object in its own right, with cylinders, pistons and pipework on show. Covers one [sitting](#sitting) in an open bay, stripped out onto a stand, or being worked on.

entries.name: push-button
entries.description: A physical button pressed with a finger to work a [device](#device), on a console, remote, or [machine](#machine). Not the fastening kind sewn onto clothing.

entries.name: stasis_tank
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [transparent](#transparent) [tank](#tank) or [tube](#tube) filled with fluid, with a body suspended inside. Science fiction uses them for cloning, accelerated growth, [healing](#healing), and keeping [people](#people) asleep between voyages.

entries.name: gauge
entries.description: An [instrument](#instrument) [reading](#reading) out pressure, [temperature](#temperature) or a similar value with a [needle](#needle) [sweeping](#sweeping) a [dial](#dial) or a marked bar. Energy meters in game overlays are [health_bar](#health_bar), and wide-bore ear piercings are plug.

entries.name: satellite
entries.description: A body circling a [planet](#planet), most often an artificial one, panelled with solar [wings](#wings) and [studded](#studded) with dish antennas, drawn against the curve of the Earth.

entries.name: seven-segment_display
entries.description: Digits built from seven [bars](#bars) lit in different combinations, as on [clock](#clock) radios, calculators, and meters. The blocky, angular numerals give it away.

entries.name: charger
entries.description: The plug and lead that feed power into a device's [battery](#battery). It lies [coiled](#coiled) on a [desk](#desk), runs from a wall socket, or dangles from a hand.

entries.name: transformer
entries.description: An electrical [device](#device) for changing voltage, most often seen as the grey cylinder strapped to a utility [pole](#pole) or a green [cabinet](#cabinet) at the kerbside. Unrelated to any franchise about transforming robots.

entries.name: handle
entries.description: The gripping part fitted to an object so that it [can](#can) be held, turned or carried. Everything from a mug's loop to a [suitcase](#suitcase) grip or a [door](#door) [lever](#lever) counts.

entries.name: sewing_machine
entries.description: A [machine](#machine) that drives a [needle](#needle) up and down to stitch [cloth](#cloth) fed under its foot. Both treadle-worked and electric models count.

entries.name: clockwork
entries.description: Exposed mechanical gearing, cogs and springs of the sort that drives a wind-up mechanism. Turns up in [steampunk](#steampunk) designs and inside opened-up automatons.

entries.name: piston
entries.description: A cylinder and [sliding](#sliding) rod that drives or is driven, the kind of part seen inside engines, hydraulics and [machinery](#machinery) generally. Mecha art often leaves them exposed at a joint or limb.

entries.name: circuit_board
entries.description: The printed board inside an electronic [device](#device), [crowded](#crowded) with soldered components and branching conductive traces. Decorative line patterns [imitating](#imitating) that layout count too.

entries.name: power_strip
entries.description: A block of electrical sockets on a lead, plugged into one wall outlet to feed several devices. A fixture of cluttered desks and games setups.

entries.name: exhaust_pipe
entries.description: The tailpipe or muffler at the [back](#back) of a [car](#car) or [motorcycle](#motorcycle), often chromed and flared. Shown close up on a bike, or with [smoke](#smoke) curling out of it.

entries.name: riding_machine
entries.description: An exercise [machine](#machine) that imitates the motion of horseback [riding](#riding), [working](#working) the [back](#back) and abdominal muscles while the user straddles the seat. It is not a mechanical [bull](#bull), which bucks far harder, nor a [sybian](#sybian), which shares only the [straddling](#straddling) posture.

entries.name: valve
entries.description: A fitting that opens, closes or throttles the flow through a pipe or duct, often turned by a [wheel](#wheel) or [lever](#lever) [handle](#handle). Common in [industrial](#industrial), [bathroom](#bathroom) and [machinery](#machinery) settings.

entries.name: spring_(object)
entries.description: A [coiled](#coiled) length of metal that stores tension when compressed or stretched. Found in [machinery](#machinery), mattresses and [bouncing](#bouncing) toys, and used in cartoons to launch something skyward.

entries.name: conveyor_belt
entries.description: A moving band that carries goods along, as on a production line, in a [factory](#factory) or at a checkout. Characters sometimes ride it rather than work beside it.

entries.name: nut_(hardware)
entries.description: The six-sided metal fastener that threads onto a bolt, its [flats](#flats) sized for a spanner. Shows up in workshops, in repair scenes and loose among [machine](#machine) parts.

entries.name: computer_chip
entries.description: An integrated circuit: a small [dark](#dark) [rectangle](#rectangle) with metal [legs](#legs) or contact pads. Usually shown mounted on a board or held up close to the viewer.

entries.name: pantograph
entries.description: A hinged, spring-loaded arm on the roof of an electric [train](#train), tram or trolleybus, pressed up against the overhead [wire](#wire) to draw current. Not the drafting linkage that shares the name.

entries.name: rebreather
entries.description: A closed [breathing](#breathing) set that scrubs carbon dioxide out of exhaled air and recycles the remaining oxygen, so almost [no](#no) bubbles escape. Worn by divers and by soldiers operating in sealed environments.

entries.name: alarm_siren
entries.description: A [device](#device) that blares or flashes to warn of danger, from a rotating red beacon to a horn bolted to a wall. Its presence says an emergency is under way.

entries.name: switch
entries.description: A physical toggle or button that turns a [device](#device) on and off — a wall switch, a [lever](#lever), a rocker control. Not to be [confused](#confused) with the handheld game console of the same name.

entries.name: jet_engine
entries.description: A turbine [engine](#engine) on its own, drawn as a cylindrical nacelle with the fan blades showing in the intake. It hangs beneath a wing or sits opened up for work in a [hangar](#hangar).

entries.name: solar_panel
entries.description: A flat, [dark](#dark) [grid](#grid) of photovoltaic cells converting [sunlight](#sunlight) into power, mounted on a roof, a vehicle, or a standalone frame. A quick way to signal a modern or off-grid setting.

entries.name: pump
entries.description: A mechanical [device](#device) that moves or pressurises [liquid](#liquid) or air, from a simple hand bulb to [industrial](#industrial) [machinery](#machinery). Prefer a narrower [tag](#tag) where one exists, since the shoe called a pump and a push-top [soap](#soap) [bottle](#bottle) each have their own.

entries.name: aircraft_catapult
entries.description: The [launching](#launching) gear that throws an [aircraft](#aircraft) up to [flying](#flying) speed within a very short run, most [familiar](#familiar) from carrier decks. Older warships and some land bases carry them too.

entries.name: countdown_timer
entries.description: A [display](#display) [running](#running) down towards zero a second at a time. Almost always a warning that something is about to happen.

entries.name: segment_display
entries.description: A digital readout that builds numbers and letters from a set of lit [bars](#bars). Seven segments is the usual arrangement, though displays with more exist for letters.

entries.name: range_finder
entries.description: An optical or [laser](#laser) [instrument](#instrument) used to measure the distance to a [target](#target), either held up to the eye or mounted alongside a [weapon](#weapon). Common in [military](#military) and [hunting](#hunting) scenes.

entries.name: dial
entries.description: A round face marked with numbers or graduations, as on a [clock](#clock), a [gauge](#gauge), a speedometer or a safe. Older designs often carry roman numerals.

entries.name: landing_gear
entries.description: The wheels, struts and skids an [aircraft](#aircraft) rests on, either lowered for touchdown or [folded](#folded) away into the airframe. It shows up on planes, helicopters and [spacecraft](#spacecraft).

entries.name: radar_dish
entries.description: The broad, concave antenna mounted outside a [radar](#radar) installation, aimed skyward and often shown rotating on a [mast](#mast). The visible collector attached to the equipment rather than its [display](#display).

entries.name: photocopier
entries.description: An [office](#office) [machine](#machine) that reproduces [pages](#pages) onto [paper](#paper), with a [glass](#glass) [plate](#plate) under a hinged [lid](#lid). Modern ones print, [scan](#scan) and fax as [well](#well), and they turn up in workplace, [school](#school) and archive scenes.

entries.name: lever
entries.description: A pivoted [handle](#handle) pushed or pulled to work a mechanism, from a [switch](#switch) bolted to a wall to a control [stick](#stick) in a [cockpit](#cockpit).

entries.name: device
entries.description: An unnamed piece of equipment or gadget whose purpose is left open. Reach for a specific [tag](#tag) whenever the object [can](#can) actually be identified.

entries.name: open_hatch
entries.description: An access [hatch](#hatch) on a [tank](#tank), [submarine](#submarine), [spacecraft](#spacecraft) or similar [machine](#machine) is swung open. Usually somebody is [climbing](#climbing) out of it or [leaning](#leaning) from the [opening](#opening).

entries.name: reactive_armor
entries.description: Modular [armor](#armor) [tiles](#tiles) bolted onto the outside of tanks and other [military](#military) vehicles, designed to detonate outward when struck and deflect the incoming round rather than simply absorbing it. Drawn as a [grid](#grid) of blocks over the hull and turret.

entries.name: bladeless_fan
entries.description: An electric fan that drives air through a hollow [ring](#ring), its impeller hidden away in the base. The open loop makes it easy to spot in modern interiors.

entries.name: disassembly
entries.description: A manufactured thing taken apart into its separate components, laid out in rows or [drifting](#drifting) apart in the air. Machines, dolls and androids are the usual subjects.

entries.name: gas_pump
entries.description: The filling-station [machine](#machine) that measures fuel into a vehicle, with its readout, [hose](#hose) and nozzle. Usually paired with a [car](#car) being filled up.

entries.name: gas_pump_nozzle
entries.description: The handled spout at the end of a fuel [hose](#hose), gripped while a [tank](#tank) is filled. Sometimes used as a prop and levelled like a pistol.

entries.name: fruit
entries.description: Sweet edible [plant](#plant) produce of any sort — apples, berries, [grapes](#grapes) and the rest. Also serves as a catch-all when many kinds appear at once; name the specific fruit where one dominates.

entries.name: strawberry
entries.description: The red, seed-dotted [fruit](#fruit), whole, [sliced](#sliced) or perched on a [cake](#cake). Tag it on its own or as a topping.

entries.name: apple
entries.description: An apple, whole, cut or bitten into, in red, green or yellow. The [fruit](#fruit) often carries a meaning of its own, temptation above all.

entries.name: carrot
entries.description: The orange root [vegetable](#vegetable), whole with its leafy top or cut into pieces, held or served on a [plate](#plate). Stereotypically paired with rabbits and bunny girls.

entries.name: pumpkin
entries.description: A large orange [squash](#squash), whole or carved. Strongly associated with Halloween, where it becomes a [jack-o'-lantern](#jack-o'-lantern), and equally at home in an [autumn](#autumn) harvest scene or as the shape behind a themed [hat](#hat) or [costume](#costume).

entries.name: peach
entries.description: A soft fuzzy [fruit](#fruit) with yellow-orange skin and a stone at its centre, shown whole, cut open or used as a motif.

entries.name: mushroom
entries.description: A capped fungus on a stem, growing wild, gathered for the pot, or used as a motif. It covers everything from edible varieties to lethal spotted toadstools.

entries.name: cherry
entries.description: The small round [fruit](#fruit) on a slender stalk, red, black or yellow, whole, paired on a shared stem, or perched on a [dessert](#dessert) or [drink](#drink). Cherry blossom is an entirely separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: watermelon
entries.description: The large green-striped [melon](#melon) with red watery [flesh](#flesh), a classic [summer](#summer) treat. Japanese-grown ones are drawn almost perfectly round; a cut piece is [watermelon_slice](#watermelon_slice).

entries.name: grapes
entries.description: Small round berries in a [hanging](#hanging) bunch, purple, red or green, whether still on the vine, heaped on a [plate](#plate) or being eaten.

entries.name: orange_(fruit)
entries.description: The round citrus [fruit](#fruit), whole, halved or peeled. Where orange is meant as the dominant colour of a picture, [orange_theme](#orange_theme) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: spring_onion
entries.description: A long Japanese [onion](#onion) with a white stalk forking into green leaves, often drawn as a Y shape. Also called a leek or negi, and famous as Hatsune Miku's prop.

entries.name: lemon
entries.description: The yellow oval citrus with sharp, juicy [flesh](#flesh), shown whole, halved or heaped in a [bowl](#bowl). A single cut round is [lemon_slice](#lemon_slice).

entries.name: tomato
entries.description: The red [fruit](#fruit) eaten as a [vegetable](#vegetable), whole, [sliced](#sliced) or on the vine. A [cherry](#cherry) tomato in a [bento](#bento) counts too.

entries.name: mandarin_orange
entries.description: A small loose-skinned citrus, the Japanese mikan, eaten through the [winter](#winter) and a fixture of the [kotatsu](#kotatsu). Larger [fruit](#fruit) of the kind is [orange_(fruit)](#orange_(fruit)).

entries.name: vegetable
entries.description: Edible roots, leaves, stems or savoury fruits such as carrots, [cabbage](#cabbage) or tomatoes appear in the picture. Use the general [tag](#tag) when several kinds are shown together, otherwise the specific vegetable's own tag is preferred.

entries.name: banana
entries.description: The long curved [fruit](#fruit), peeled or still in its skin, in a bunch or held singly, most often yellow but sometimes green or red. It doubles as a phallic joke often enough; add [eating](#eating) when someone is eating one.

entries.name: lemon_slice
entries.description: A round or wedge cut from a [lemon](#lemon), usually perched on a [glass](#glass) rim or [floating](#floating) in a [cold](#cold) [drink](#drink). It also covers wedges served beside [food](#food).

entries.name: blueberry
entries.description: Small round dark-blue berries, one alone or a handful, on the [bush](#bush), in a [bowl](#bowl) or set on a [cake](#cake). Blueberry-flavoured [food](#food) with [no](#no) [berry](#berry) in sight does not qualify.

entries.name: sweet_potato
entries.description: An orange-fleshed tuber with a sweeter taste than a regular [potato](#potato), most often shown roasted in its skin as a Japanese [autumn](#autumn) [snack](#snack). Frequently mislabeled as a yam, though the two are unrelated botanically.

entries.name: orange_slice
entries.description: A [wheel](#wheel) cut across an orange or one of the segments from inside the rind, often garnishing a [drink](#drink) or laid out on a [plate](#plate).

entries.name: lettuce
entries.description: The leafy green [salad](#salad) [vegetable](#vegetable), eaten raw in salads, sandwiches and burgers. Shown as a whole head or as loose leaves.

entries.name: berry
entries.description: A small [fruit](#fruit) that cannot be [pinned](#pinned) to a particular kind. If it is plainly a [strawberry](#strawberry), [blueberry](#blueberry), [raspberry](#raspberry) or the like, use that [tag](#tag); if it is simply unrecognisable, fruit is the safer [choice](#choice).

entries.name: cucumber
entries.description: A long green cucumber, whole or [sliced](#sliced), appearing as [food](#food) or as a prop. Kappa are fond of them and cats are famously alarmed by them.

entries.name: eggplant
entries.description: The glossy purple [vegetable](#vegetable), sometimes white or orange, also called an aubergine. Drawn as an ingredient, on a [plate](#plate), or held up as a suggestive prop.

entries.name: potato
entries.description: The starchy tuber as [food](#food), raw or cooked, mashed or in a [sack](#sack). French fries and chips have their own tags.

entries.name: watermelon_slice
entries.description: A cut wedge of [watermelon](#watermelon), held, eaten or served on a [plate](#plate), rind and seeds typically visible. The uncut [fruit](#fruit) is the [plain](#plain) watermelon [tag](#tag).

entries.name: corn
entries.description: Maize as crop or [food](#food): a cob [crowded](#crowded) with yellow kernels, raw, boiled, grilled or still [standing](#standing) in a [field](#field). Eating straight off the cob is included, as are the multicoloured decorative kinds.

entries.name: kiwi_(fruit)
entries.description: The fuzzy brown-skinned [fruit](#fruit), usually shown cut open to reveal green [flesh](#flesh) ringed with tiny black seeds. The [bird](#bird) of the same name has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: coconut
entries.description: The [fruit](#fruit) of the coconut palm, whether as a hard [hairy](#hairy) brown [shell](#shell), a smooth green or yellow husked one, or [split](#split) open and [drunk](#drunk) from. A [staple](#staple) [beach](#beach) and [tropical](#tropical) prop.

entries.name: beans
entries.description: Legumes grown in a pod, such as soybeans, chickpeas or kidney beans, shown in the pod, in a [bowl](#bowl), cooked in a dish or scattered loose. The roasted soybeans thrown at [setsubun](#setsubun) count as [well](#well).

entries.name: melon
entries.description: A gourd-family [fruit](#fruit) with a tough rind and sweet, watery [flesh](#flesh), such as [cantaloupe](#cantaloupe) or honeydew, whole or [sliced](#sliced). Watermelon is tagged on its own.

entries.name: onion
entries.description: The layered bulb [vegetable](#vegetable), whole, [sliced](#sliced) or going into the pan. Chopping one is a [standing](#standing) joke for streaming eyes.

entries.name: radish
entries.description: The root [vegetable](#vegetable) radish, whether the small red variety or the long white [daikon](#daikon), shown whole, held, or being eaten.

entries.name: pineapple
entries.description: The [tropical](#tropical) [fruit](#fruit) with a spiky armoured skin and a [crown](#crown) of stiff leaves, whole or cut open to the yellow [flesh](#flesh). A stock [summer](#summer) and [beach](#beach) accent.

entries.name: broccoli
entries.description: The green [vegetable](#vegetable) with a thick stalk and a head of tight florets, raw, cooked or served on a [plate](#plate). Add vegetable and [food](#food); the company [sharing](#sharing) the name is broccoli_(company).

entries.name: cabbage
entries.description: A [leaf](#leaf) [vegetable](#vegetable) that grows as a dense round head of tightly packed leaves on a thick stalk. Shown whole, halved or being shredded for [cooking](#cooking).

entries.name: lime_(fruit)
entries.description: The small green citrus, shown whole, halved or heaped in a [bowl](#bowl).

entries.name: raspberry
entries.description: A small clustered [berry](#berry), red or occasionally black, made up of many tiny [beads](#beads) around a hollow [core](#core). Appears on cakes, in bowls, and held up to the mouth.

entries.name: chili_pepper
entries.description: A [hot](#hot) pepper pod, usually drawn slim and red, fresh or dried on a [string](#string). It stands in for spice and runs through Mexican and Sichuan [cooking](#cooking).

entries.name: bamboo_shoot
entries.description: The young edible [sprout](#sprout) of a [bamboo](#bamboo) [plant](#plant), a pale cone wrapped in overlapping husks. Sliced, it is a [staple](#staple) of Japanese and Chinese [cooking](#cooking).

entries.name: golden_apple
entries.description: An [apple](#apple) coloured [gold](#gold) or a bright yellow, generally [carrying](#carrying) mythic or magical [weight](#weight). It shows up in [fairy](#fairy) tales, stories of temptation and game item art.

entries.name: banana_peel
entries.description: The soft yellow skin stripped off a [banana](#banana), its ends splayed outward. One dropped on the ground is a stock slapstick hazard.

entries.name: fruit_on_head
entries.description: A piece of [fruit](#fruit) balanced on top of somebody's head. Generally played as a visual [gag](#gag), or as a nod to a character's own motif.

entries.name: lime_slice
entries.description: A lime cut into thin rounds or wedges, often set on a [glass](#glass) as a [garnish](#garnish) for a [summer](#summer) [drink](#drink).

entries.name: strawberry_slice
entries.description: A [strawberry](#strawberry) cut open, showing the pale [core](#core) and seeded [flesh](#flesh) of the cut face. Common as decoration on cakes and desserts.

entries.name: persimmon
entries.description: An orange [autumn](#autumn) [fruit](#fruit), squat and tomato-like, with a four-lobed leafy cap at the stem. Easily mistaken for a [tomato](#tomato) or an orange, but the cap and the season give it away.

entries.name: daikon
entries.description: A long, blunt-ended white [radish](#radish) of East Asia with a mild taste. Turns up whole [poking](#poking) out of a [shopping](#shopping) [bag](#bag), or cut into rounds for a simmered dish.

entries.name: kiwi_slice
entries.description: A round slice cut across a kiwifruit, its pale [core](#core) circled by black seeds against green [flesh](#flesh). It is a common [garnish](#garnish) on desserts and drinks.

entries.name: cherry_tomato
entries.description: A small round [tomato](#tomato) a [couple](#couple) of centimetres across, eaten whole or halved into a [salad](#salad). Bento boxes use it as a spot of red beside the [rice](#rice).

entries.name: tomato_slice
entries.description: A round cut disc of [tomato](#tomato) with the seeds and pulp showing, laid on a [burger](#burger), tossed in a [salad](#salad) or left on a [chopping](#chopping) board.

entries.name: pear
entries.description: The bell-shaped [fruit](#fruit), narrow at the stem and swelling toward the base, with faintly grainy [flesh](#flesh). Green, yellow or russet, and often drawn beside apples.

entries.name: bell_pepper
entries.description: A blocky sweet pepper, hollow inside with a cluster of small seeds, in green, red, yellow or orange. Mild rather than [hot](#hot), and green ones are the standard shorthand for the [vegetable](#vegetable) a childish character refuses to eat.

entries.name: apple_slice
entries.description: A cut piece of [apple](#apple), wedge or [ring](#ring), its pale [flesh](#flesh) set against the coloured skin. Normally one of several on a [plate](#plate), or held out to somebody.

entries.name: pomegranate
entries.description: A round deep-red [fruit](#fruit) whose leathery rind hides packed clusters of glassy seeds. Shown whole, [split](#split) open, or as a heap of loose arils.

entries.name: pea_pod
entries.description: The green case that grows around [peas](#peas), drawn closed or [split](#split) open to show the row of seeds [sitting](#sitting) inside.

entries.name: corn_cob
entries.description: An ear of maize on its cob, husked or half stripped. Shown raw, boiled or grilled at a [festival](#festival) stall.

entries.name: turnip
entries.description: A round white root [vegetable](#vegetable) with a leafy green top, grown in cool climates. Japanese [cooking](#cooking) serves it raw, marinated or pickled, and it is part of the seven-herb New Year tradition.

entries.name: green_pepper
entries.description: A green [bell](#bell) pepper or chilli, shown whole, halved or [sliced](#sliced). In Japanese scenes it is the standard [vegetable](#vegetable) a [child](#child) refuses to eat.

entries.name: banana_slice
entries.description: A [banana](#banana) cut crosswise into rounds, scattered over [cereal](#cereal), [cake](#cake) or a [bowl](#bowl) of [fruit](#fruit). The pale discs show the little [seed](#seed) pattern at their centres.

entries.name: garlic
entries.description: A papery white bulb of the [onion](#onion) [family](#family), or the loose cloves [broken](#broken) off it. Appears in [cooking](#cooking) scenes and as a charm held up against vampires.

entries.name: fly_agaric
entries.description: The storybook toadstool: a broad scarlet cap flecked with white warts on a pale stalk. It stands in for mushrooms generally in [fantasy](#fantasy) and game art, and is poisonous in life.

entries.name: fruit_bowl
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) [holding](#holding) a mixture of different [fruit](#fruit). Usually sits on a [table](#table) as a [kitchen](#kitchen) or still-life prop.

entries.name: yuzu_(fruit)
entries.description: A knobbly yellow citrus roughly the size of a small [grapefruit](#grapefruit), grown across East Asia and prized for its fragrant peel. Pictured whole or halved in [kitchen](#kitchen) scenes, or [floating](#floating) in a [hot](#hot) [bath](#bath).

entries.name: green_apple
entries.description: An [apple](#apple) with green skin, tarter than the red kind. Drawn whole, [sliced](#sliced), bitten into or held out to somebody.

entries.name: orange_peel
entries.description: The rind taken off an orange, curling away in a strip or [lying](#lying) discarded beside the [fruit](#fruit). Usually part of a scene of [eating](#eating) or preparing it.

entries.name: bitten_apple
entries.description: An [apple](#apple) with a chunk eaten out of it, the pale [flesh](#flesh) showing inside the [tooth](#tooth) marks. Held up mid-bite or left half-finished somewhere in the scene.

entries.name: olive
entries.description: The stone [fruit](#fruit) of the olive [tree](#tree), a small oval in green, black or brown. Frequently speared on a [stick](#stick) and dropped into a [cocktail](#cocktail) [glass](#glass).

entries.name: pineapple_slice
entries.description: A cut piece of [pineapple](#pineapple), either a cored [ring](#ring) or a wedge with the spiny rind still on. Found on plates, perched on the rim of a [drink](#drink), and on [pizza](#pizza).

entries.name: myouga_(plant)
entries.description: A Japanese ginger grown for its pale [flower](#flower) buds, which are [sliced](#sliced) thin as a seasoning. It shows up as a growing [plant](#plant), held in the hand, or served as a [garnish](#garnish).

entries.name: apple_rabbit
entries.description: An [apple](#apple) wedge with the skin cut [back](#back) on one side into two [standing](#standing) points, so the piece reads as a [rabbit](#rabbit) with raised ears. A standard flourish in packed lunches.

entries.name: shiitake
entries.description: A brown-capped East Asian [mushroom](#mushroom) heavily used in [cooking](#cooking), usually drawn with a [cross](#cross) cut into the top. Turns up in stews, grills and [hotpot](#hotpot).

entries.name: pickle
entries.description: A [cucumber](#cucumber) preserved in brine or vinegar, shown whole, halved or in slices, and called a gherkin in some places. Appears in burgers, on plates and as a joke object.

entries.name: watermelon_seeds
entries.description: The small black seeds of a [watermelon](#watermelon), scattered over a cut slice, spat out or held in the hand. Usually part of a [summer](#summer) [eating](#eating) scene.

entries.name: cucumber_slice
entries.description: A [cucumber](#cucumber) cut into thin rounds. Shows up in a [salad](#salad) or a [sandwich](#sandwich), and laid over the eyes during a spa or [facial](#facial) scene.

entries.name: mango
entries.description: A sweet [tropical](#tropical) [fruit](#fruit) with orange [flesh](#flesh) [clinging](#clinging) to a large flat stone, the skin peeled away before [eating](#eating). Shown whole, halved and scored, or in slices.

entries.name: cantaloupe
entries.description: An orange-fleshed [melon](#melon) under a netted rind. Japanese work usually draws the prized Yubari King with its T-shaped length of stem left on top.

entries.name: hanging_food
entries.description: Fruit, vegetables or mushrooms strung up on cord, usually to dry out or to keep them from spoiling. Rows of persimmons [drying](#drying) under the eaves are the classic sight.

entries.name: fruit_basket
entries.description: A woven [basket](#basket) [holding](#holding) an assortment of [fruit](#fruit). Turns up in still lifes, [picnic](#picnic) scenes and as a [gift](#gift) being carried or handed over.

entries.name: apple_core
entries.description: What is left of an [apple](#apple) once the [flesh](#flesh) is gone, a narrow [spine](#spine) with the stalk still on top. Usually drawn tossed aside or [dangling](#dangling) from somebody's fingers.

entries.name: blackberry_(fruit)
entries.description: The [dark](#dark) bramble [berry](#berry) built from many small globes packed into a cluster, ranging from deep red to nearly black. The [phone](#phone) brand of the same name is something else entirely.

entries.name: avocado
entries.description: A thick-skinned green [fruit](#fruit) with one large stone, drawn whole, [split](#split) around the pit, or mashed. It is treated as savoury [food](#food) and is the basis of guacamole.

entries.name: blue_apple
entries.description: An [apple](#apple) painted blue rather than red, green or yellow. Since the colour cannot occur naturally, it usually signals that something is wrong.

entries.name: red_pepper
entries.description: A red capsicum or chilli, shown whole, [sliced](#sliced), or strung up to dry. Cooking scenes and spicy-food gags are the usual settings.

entries.name: plum
entries.description: A small round stone [fruit](#fruit) with smooth purple or red skin, close kin to cherries and peaches. Drawn whole, halved around the pit, or dried into a wrinkled prune.

entries.name: lotus_root
entries.description: The pale rhizome of the [lotus](#lotus), eaten raw or cooked and usually shown cut into rounds. Each slice is pierced by a [ring](#ring) of holes, which makes it instantly recognisable.

entries.name: melon_slice
entries.description: A wedge cut from a [melon](#melon), its pale [flesh](#flesh) exposed along the curving rind. A [summer](#summer) prop, often held up as if about to be bitten.

entries.name: carrot_slice
entries.description: Carrot cut crossways into thin rounds, showing the pale [ring](#ring) inside. Pieces cut the long way into batons are carrot_sticks.

entries.name: grapefruit
entries.description: The big sour citrus with thick yellow-pink peel, shown whole or halved to bare its segments. Often served cut open at [breakfast](#breakfast).

entries.name: peas
entries.description: Small round green seeds shelled from their pod and eaten as a [vegetable](#vegetable), shown loose, heaped in a [bowl](#bowl) or scattered over a [plate](#plate).

entries.name: asparagus
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) green spears of the asparagus [plant](#plant), drawn bundled raw or served on a [plate](#plate). Its feathery [foliage](#foliage) sometimes appears with them.

entries.name: squash
entries.description: The edible [gourd](#gourd) in any of its forms, from [pumpkin](#pumpkin) to zucchini to butternut. Shown whole in a [kitchen](#kitchen) or [market](#market), or cut open ready for [cooking](#cooking).

entries.name: habanero_pepper
entries.description: A small wrinkled lantern-shaped chilli, drawn most often in orange or red and understood to be searingly [hot](#hot). Use it for the pepper itself, whole or [crushed](#crushed) into flakes.

entries.name: carrot_in_pocket
entries.description: A [carrot](#carrot) pushed into a [pocket](#pocket) with its green top sticking out. A rabbit-themed touch on an otherwise ordinary outfit.

entries.name: bell_pepper_slice
entries.description: A [bell](#bell) pepper cut into strips or rings, the pieces curving because the [vegetable](#vegetable) is hollow and bulbous. Pizza toppings and stir fries are where they usually land.

entries.name: apple_peel
entries.description: The skin taken off an [apple](#apple) in one unbroken [spiral](#spiral), [hanging](#hanging) as a long curling [ribbon](#ribbon). It shows the [peeling](#peeling) was done carefully, often as a small kindness for somebody else.

entries.name: fruit_on_liquid
entries.description: Fruit [floating](#floating) on [water](#water) — in a [bathtub](#bathtub), an [onsen](#onsen), a [pool](#pool), the sea or a [drink](#drink). Yuzu bobbing in a [hot](#hot) [winter](#winter) [bath](#bath) is the classic instance.

entries.name: arrow_through_apple
entries.description: An [apple](#apple) pierced by an arrow, usually while balanced on somebody's head after the William Tell story. The shot itself may be shown or only its result.

entries.name: candy
entries.description: Sugar confectionery of any kind: boiled [sweets](#sweets), wrapped drops, gummies, lollipops. Add the [tag](#tag) for the particular sweet wherever one exists.

entries.name: cake
entries.description: A sweet baked [dessert](#dessert), usually iced and dressed with [fruit](#fruit), [cream](#cream) or sugar figures. It is the centrepiece of [birthday](#birthday) and [wedding](#wedding) scenes.

entries.name: lollipop
entries.description: Hard [candy](#candy) on a [stick](#stick), usually a small sphere but sometimes a flat disc, held in the hand or in the mouth. It serves as a prop for a childish look as readily as for a suggestive one.

entries.name: popsicle
entries.description: A [frozen](#frozen) flavoured [ice](#ice) on a [stick](#stick), whatever the brand. Often shown [melting](#melting) in [summer](#summer) heat; [eating](#eating) one [can](#can) be drawn suggestively. Add [popsicle_in_mouth](#popsicle_in_mouth) when it is between the [lips](#lips).

entries.name: ice_cream
entries.description: Frozen dairy [dessert](#dessert) in any form: scoops in a cone or dish, soft serve, a bar on a [stick](#stick), a [sundae](#sundae). Colour variants are deliberately not given tags of their own.

entries.name: chocolate
entries.description: Chocolate in any form: [bars](#bars), truffles, coated [sweets](#sweets), melted in a [bowl](#bowl), or moulded into hearts and figures. A [staple](#staple) of Valentine's and White Day art, and particular forms such as [chocolate_bar](#chocolate_bar) carry their own tags.

entries.name: pocky
entries.description: Thin biscuit sticks coated in [chocolate](#chocolate) or another flavour, a Japanese [snack](#snack) sold elsewhere under other names. Add [pocky_in_mouth](#pocky_in_mouth) when a character has one between the [lips](#lips), and [pocky_kiss](#pocky_kiss) for the shared-stick game.

entries.name: wagashi
entries.description: Traditional Japanese [sweets](#sweets) served with [tea](#tea), made from [mochi](#mochi), red bean paste, adzuki or [fruit](#fruit): [daifuku](#daifuku), [dango](#dango), sakura mochi, youkan and the like. Tag the specific sweet too when it is identifiable.

entries.name: doughnut
entries.description: A fried [pastry](#pastry), glazed or frosted and most recognisably ring-shaped, though round filled ones, crullers and knobbly [chained](#chained) varieties count too.

entries.name: cookie
entries.description: Small flat baked [sweets](#sweets): [chocolate](#chocolate) chip, gingerbread, [sandwich](#sandwich) biscuits, wafers and the like. Shown on a [plate](#plate), in a [jar](#jar) or halfway to somebody's mouth.

entries.name: cake_slice
entries.description: A single wedge cut from a [cake](#cake) and served on a [plate](#plate), frequently with a [fork](#fork) alongside or already in it.

entries.name: dango
entries.description: Japanese dumplings of [rice](#rice) [flour](#flour), generally three or four to a [skewer](#skewer) and served with green [tea](#tea). Grilled mitarashi, tricolour sanshoku and [plain](#plain) white [tsukimi](#tsukimi) are the usual kinds; the Chinese candied [fruit](#fruit) on a [stick](#stick) is [tanghulu](#tanghulu), not this.

entries.name: ice_cream_cone
entries.description: The crisp [wafer](#wafer) or [waffle](#waffle) cone that carries scoops so they [can](#can) be eaten without a dish. It shows up held aloft, being licked, or [standing](#standing) empty.

entries.name: heart-shaped_chocolate
entries.description: A piece of [chocolate](#chocolate) moulded as a [heart](#heart), a Valentine [staple](#staple). A closed heart-shaped [box](#box) is not enough on its own — the chocolate has to be visible.

entries.name: macaron
entries.description: A small French confection of two round [almond](#almond) shells sandwiching a layer of [cream](#cream), made in bright pastel colours. They are usually drawn in neat stacks or rows.

entries.name: chewing_gum
entries.description: Gum in any form: in its [packet](#packet) or wrapper, as a strip, being chewed, or [stuck](#stuck) to something. When a character blows a [bubble](#bubble) with it, add [blowing_bubbles](#blowing_bubbles) as [well](#well).

entries.name: parfait
entries.description: A layered [dessert](#dessert) of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) or cream with [fruit](#fruit), jelly, [cereal](#cereal) or [sauce](#sauce), built up in a [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass) so every layer shows. Nearly always the sundae-style version rather than the French [frozen](#frozen) custard.

entries.name: candy_apple
entries.description: A whole [apple](#apple) on a [stick](#stick) under a hard [shell](#shell) of red sugar, [caramel](#caramel) or [chocolate](#chocolate), sold at [autumn](#autumn) festivals. Easy to mistake for a big [lollipop](#lollipop), so look for the flat top and the size.

entries.name: cream
entries.description: Dairy cream as [food](#food): whipped onto a [cake](#cake) or a [drink](#drink), piped into a [pastry](#pastry), poured from a jug. Cream left on somebody's face has a [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: cupcake
entries.description: A small individual [cake](#cake) baked in a [paper](#paper) case and finished with frosting and [decorations](#decorations). Shown as a [party](#party) treat or lined up on a [bakery](#bakery) [display](#display).

entries.name: birthday_cake
entries.description: A [cake](#cake) made for a [birthday](#birthday), commonly iced with a greeting and a name and topped with candles to blow out. Add birthday for the occasion and [candle](#candle) when they are lit.

entries.name: pudding
entries.description: A wobbly milk-based [dessert](#dessert), in most anime art the crème [caramel](#caramel) style served in a small [cup](#cup) or turned out onto a [plate](#plate) with caramel [sauce](#sauce) on top. Also called flan, a name artists like to [pun](#pun) on with certain characters.

entries.name: mochi
entries.description: Japanese [rice](#rice) [cake](#cake), glutinous rice pounded to a [sticky](#sticky) paste and shaped into rounds. Eaten above all at New Year, and the base of many [sweets](#sweets) such as [daifuku](#daifuku) and sakura mochi.

entries.name: candy_cane
entries.description: A hard striped [stick](#stick) of sugar bent into a [hook](#hook) at the top, almost always red and white and tied to Christmas. It is not a [walking](#walking) [cane](#cane).

entries.name: shaved_ice
entries.description: Kakigori, the Japanese [summer](#summer) [dessert](#dessert) of finely shaved [ice](#ice) piled in a [cup](#cup) and drizzled with flavoured [syrup](#syrup), often condensed [milk](#milk), eaten with a [spoon](#spoon). Implies [food](#food).

entries.name: dessert
entries.description: Sweet [food](#food) served at the end of a [meal](#meal), such as [cake](#cake), [parfait](#parfait) or [pudding](#pudding), often crowned with [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream), whipped cream or [fruit](#fruit). The sandy [wasteland](#wasteland) is [desert](#desert), with one s.

entries.name: swirl_lollipop
entries.description: A flat, round [lollipop](#lollipop) [patterned](#patterned) with a [colorful](#colorful) [spiral](#spiral) [swirl](#swirl).

entries.name: sweets
entries.description: Sugary treats in general — [candy](#candy), confectionery and small desserts. Prefer a more specific [tag](#tag) such as candy or [cake](#cake) when the item is identifiable.

entries.name: strawberry_shortcake
entries.description: Layered [cake](#cake) filled with whipped [cream](#cream) and strawberries, usually topped with more berries. In Japan the layers are [sponge](#sponge) rather than true [shortcake](#shortcake). Tag the cake itself, and add [personification](#personification) when a character is dressed as one.

entries.name: whipped_cream
entries.description: Cream [beaten](#beaten) into soft [fluffy](#fluffy) peaks, piled on drinks, cakes and pies. Sometimes applied directly to a body in food-play scenes.

entries.name: crepe
entries.description: A very thin [pancake](#pancake), in Japan usually rolled into a [paper](#paper) cone around [fruit](#fruit), [cream](#cream) or [syrup](#syrup) and eaten in the hand. Street [food](#food), carried on a date or around a [festival](#festival).

entries.name: taiyaki
entries.description: A Japanese fish-shaped [pastry](#pastry), usually filled with sweetened red bean paste.

entries.name: sanshoku_dango
entries.description: Three [dango](#dango) on one [skewer](#skewer) in pink, white and green, the [hanami](#hanami) dango eaten during [cherry](#cherry) blossom viewing. Not bocchan_dango, which is green, yellow and brown.

entries.name: chocolate_bar
entries.description: A flat slab of [chocolate](#chocolate) scored so it [can](#can) be snapped into pieces, often still half inside its wrapper. Smaller log-shaped confections belong to [candy_bar](#candy_bar) instead.

entries.name: checkerboard_cookie
entries.description: A [square](#square) biscuit baked from [chocolate](#chocolate) and [plain](#plain) [dough](#dough) laid in alternating blocks, so the cut face reads as a chequerboard.

entries.name: cotton_candy
entries.description: Sugar spun into threads and gathered into a [fluffy](#fluffy) pink or pastel [cloud](#cloud) on a [stick](#stick) or in a [bag](#bag). The classic fairground and [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival) treat, also called [candy](#candy) floss.

entries.name: bungeoppang
entries.description: A Korean [street](#street) [pastry](#pastry) baked in a fish-shaped mould and filled with sweet red bean. Very close to [taiyaki](#taiyaki) and drawn much the same way.

entries.name: icing
entries.description: The sweet glaze spread or piped over cakes, cupcakes and biscuits, thin enough to set hard or thick enough to hold a shape. It also covers icing smeared over a character rather than a [cake](#cake).

entries.name: box_of_chocolates
entries.description: An opened [gift](#gift) [box](#box) with a [tray](#tray) of assorted chocolates inside, the classic Valentine's present. The [sweets](#sweets) themselves must be visible; if only the closed [lid](#lid) shows, the picture calls for [gift_box](#gift_box) instead.

entries.name: sundae
entries.description: Ice [cream](#cream) served in a [glass](#glass) with toppings such as whipped cream, [syrup](#syrup), cherries, wafers or [sprinkles](#sprinkles). Implies [ice_cream](#ice_cream).

entries.name: watermelon_bar
entries.description: A wedge-shaped [ice](#ice) pop flavored and colored to resemble a slice of [watermelon](#watermelon), complete with chocolate-chip seeds. A [familiar](#familiar) Japanese [summer](#summer) treat.

entries.name: mochi_trail
entries.description: A piece of [mochi](#mochi) drawn out into a long sagging strand as someone bites or pulls at it, the [dough](#dough) too stretchy to part cleanly. Nearly always shown mid-mouthful.

entries.name: swiss_roll
entries.description: A [sponge](#sponge) [cake](#cake) baked flat, spread with [cream](#cream) or [jam](#jam), and rolled up into a [spiral](#spiral).

entries.name: wrapped_candy
entries.description: Sweets still sealed in their twisted or wrapped packaging. Tag [candy](#candy) alongside it; an unwrapped piece is simply candy on its own.

entries.name: chocolate_cake
entries.description: A [cake](#cake) made from or flavoured with [chocolate](#chocolate), whole or cut into slices and often under [dark](#dark) frosting. The [plain](#plain) cake [tag](#tag) applies alongside it.

entries.name: marshmallow
entries.description: Soft spongy sugar confection, bobbing in [hot](#hot) [chocolate](#chocolate), pressed into s'mores or browning on a [stick](#stick) over a [fire](#fire). Implies [food](#food).

entries.name: sprinkles
entries.description: Tiny coloured sugar pieces scattered as a topping over [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream), [cake](#cake), cupcakes or doughnuts.

entries.name: kagami_mochi
entries.description: Two round [rice](#rice) cakes stacked with the smaller on top and crowned by a bitter orange with its [leaf](#leaf) still attached. It is set out as a New Year offering, generally on a small stand over [folded](#folded) [paper](#paper).

entries.name: soft_serve
entries.description: Machine-churned [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) pumped into a [tall](#tall) [swirl](#swirl) onto a cone or into a [cup](#cup). The ridged, spiraled shape is what sets it apart from ice cream that has been scooped.

entries.name: wafer_stick
entries.description: A rolled [tube](#tube) of [wafer](#wafer), typically striped with a brown [spiral](#spiral), eaten as a [snack](#snack) or [stuck](#stuck) into a scoop of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream). Different from the flat biscuit sort.

entries.name: strawberry_cake
entries.description: A [sponge](#sponge) or [shortcake](#shortcake) built around strawberries, layered with [cream](#cream) and topped with whole or halved berries. The Japanese Christmas [cake](#cake) is this cake.

entries.name: tart_(food)
entries.description: An open-faced [pastry](#pastry) case filled with [fruit](#fruit), custard or [jam](#jam), with nothing laid over the top. That missing [lid](#lid) is exactly what separates it from a [pie](#pie).

entries.name: gingerbread_man
entries.description: A spiced biscuit cut into a stubby human shape and piped with [icing](#icing) for eyes, [buttons](#buttons) and a [smile](#smile). Strongly tied to Christmas, though not only to it.

entries.name: popsicle_stick
entries.description: The flat wooden [stick](#stick) left over from an [ice](#ice) lolly, held in the fingers or clamped in the mouth. Often shown bare after the ice is gone, sometimes with a printed prize on it.

entries.name: character-themed_food
entries.description: Food shaped, iced or printed to look like a character: pancakes, biscuits, [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) [bars](#bars), [sweets](#sweets). It has to stay an inanimate object, since a living [food](#food) [creature](#creature) is [foodification](#foodification).

entries.name: chocolate_banana
entries.description: A [banana](#banana) on a [stick](#stick) dipped in a hard [chocolate](#chocolate) [shell](#shell) and usually finished with coloured [sprinkles](#sprinkles). A fixture of Japanese [festival](#festival) stalls, so it tends to appear beside [summer](#summer) festival imagery.

entries.name: cream_puff
entries.description: A light hollow [pastry](#pastry) filled with sweetened [cream](#cream), round and sometimes dusted with sugar. Usually shown by the plateful.

entries.name: chocolate_chip_cookie
entries.description: A baked [cookie](#cookie) with chunks of [chocolate](#chocolate) [studded](#studded) through the [dough](#dough). Use it where the chips [can](#can) actually be seen, not for any brown biscuit.

entries.name: double_scoop
entries.description: Two balls of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) stacked on a cone or set side by side in a dish. A larger [serving](#serving), still an ordinary [dessert](#dessert).

entries.name: ice_cream_cup
entries.description: Ice [cream](#cream) served in a small tub or [glass](#glass) rather than a cone, disposable [paper](#paper) at a stall and glass in a parlour. A short flat [spoon](#spoon) usually comes tucked in with it.

entries.name: gelatin
entries.description: A wobbling [translucent](#translucent) [dessert](#dessert) set with [animal](#animal) collagen, usually moulded and brightly coloured. Covers jelly cups and moulded puddings as [well](#well) as savoury aspic; the seaweed-based version is agar.

entries.name: tanghulu
entries.description: Skewered [fruit](#fruit) dipped in hardened sugar [syrup](#syrup), a traditional Chinese [street](#street) [snack](#snack). Hawthorn berries are the classic filling, though [strawberry](#strawberry), kiwi and citrus versions are common too.

entries.name: cheesecake
entries.description: A [dessert](#dessert) of sweetened soft [cheese](#cheese) set over a biscuit, [sponge](#sponge) or [pastry](#pastry) base, often finished with [fruit](#fruit), [chocolate](#chocolate) or [coffee](#coffee). Whole cakes and single slices both count.

entries.name: shaped_lollipop
entries.description: A [lollipop](#lollipop) moulded into a recognisable [outline](#outline), such as a [heart](#heart), a star, or a [jack-o'-lantern](#jack-o'-lantern), instead of the usual disc or [spiral](#spiral).

entries.name: sakura_mochi
entries.description: A pink [rice](#rice) [cake](#cake) filled with sweet red bean paste and wrapped in a salt-pickled [cherry](#cherry) [leaf](#leaf). One of the standard springtime [wagashi](#wagashi), usually served two or three to a [plate](#plate).

entries.name: mint_chocolate
entries.description: Chocolate flavored with [mint](#mint), tinted pale green or aqua in the West and sometimes blue in Japan. Appears as [bars](#bars), chip-studded [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) and layered desserts.

entries.name: konpeitou
entries.description: Tiny hard sugar [sweets](#sweets) covered in knobbly points, made in soft pastel colours. They are usually shown heaped in a [glass](#glass) [jar](#jar) or scattered loose in a handful.

entries.name: strawberry_parfait
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) layered [dessert](#dessert) in a footed [glass](#glass) built on strawberries and their [syrup](#syrup), with [cream](#cream), [ice](#ice) cream and [sponge](#sponge) stacked between.

entries.name: jelly_bean
entries.description: Little bean-shaped [sweets](#sweets) with a hard sugar [shell](#shell) over a chewy centre, made in a spread of bright colours. They are usually drawn loose in a [jar](#jar), a [bowl](#bowl) or a cupped palm.

entries.name: apple_pie
entries.description: A baked [pie](#pie) with [apple](#apple) filling on show, whole beneath a [lattice](#lattice) crust or cut into a slice. Steam and a scoop of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) often come with it.

entries.name: triple_scoop
entries.description: Three balls of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) stacked one above the next, whether piled on a cone or heaped in a dish. The precarious [tower](#tower) is the whole point of the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: thumbprint_cookie
entries.description: A round shortbread biscuit with a dent pressed into the top and filled with [jam](#jam) or preserves. That pressed hollow is what separates it from a [plain](#plain) round [cookie](#cookie).

entries.name: mitarashi_dango
entries.description: A [skewer](#skewer) of grilled [rice](#rice) dumplings glazed in a sweet, savory soy [syrup](#syrup), usually three or four to a [stick](#stick).

entries.name: heart-shaped_lollipop
entries.description: A boiled-sugar sweet on a [stick](#stick) shaped as a [heart](#heart), often swirled red and white. Held at the mouth in cute or flirtatious [poses](#poses).

entries.name: fruit_tart
entries.description: A baked [pastry](#pastry) [shell](#shell) filled with [cream](#cream) and covered in neatly arranged pieces of [fruit](#fruit). A [staple](#staple) of [dessert](#dessert) tables, [cafe](#cafe) counters and [picnic](#picnic) scenes.

entries.name: mont_blanc_(food)
entries.description: A [dessert](#dessert) of sweetened [chestnut](#chestnut) purée piped in fine threads over [cream](#cream), built on a meringue or tart base. The dusting over the top is meant to read as a snow-covered peak.

entries.name: tsukimi_dango
entries.description: Plain white [rice](#rice) dumplings piled into a small pyramid on a wooden stand. Prepared as an offering for the Japanese [autumn](#autumn) moon-viewing [festival](#festival).

entries.name: mooncake
