entries.description: A dense round Chinese [pastry](#pastry) with a pattern stamped into the [lid](#lid) and a rich paste filling, sometimes [hiding](#hiding) a salted [egg](#egg) yolk. Eaten at the Mid-Autumn Festival.

entries.name: waffle_cone
entries.description: An [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) cone rolled from a thin [waffle](#waffle), its [grid](#grid) pattern still visible on the outside. Browner and crisper than the pale [cake](#cake) sort.

entries.name: wafer
entries.description: A thin, crisp, dry biscuit, usually with a fine [grid](#grid) texture and sometimes layered with [cream](#cream). Often [planted](#planted) in [ice](#ice) cream or used as decoration on a [dessert](#dessert).

entries.name: ice_cream_bar
entries.description: A moulded block of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) on a [stick](#stick), sometimes jacketed in a [chocolate](#chocolate) [shell](#shell). It is softer than a [water](#water) ice, though sold in much the same [shapes](#shapes).

entries.name: french_cruller
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) [doughnut](#doughnut) of choux [pastry](#pastry) with deep grooves twisting around its surface, [lighter](#lighter) and airier than a [cake](#cake) doughnut. Pon_de_ring has rounded bumps set further apart, so keep the two apart.

entries.name: chocolate_doughnut
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) [doughnut](#doughnut) either glazed with [chocolate](#chocolate) on top or baked from cocoa [dough](#dough). Sprinkles and drizzled lines are common but not required.

entries.name: daifuku
entries.description: A round [mochi](#mochi) [cake](#cake) wrapped around a sweet filling, most often red bean paste and sometimes a whole [strawberry](#strawberry) inside it. Dusted pale with starch, eaten in a bite or two, and counted among the [wagashi](#wagashi).

entries.name: hishimochi
entries.description: Diamond-shaped [rice](#rice) cakes stacked in three coloured layers, pink over white over green. They are set out for the Girls' Day [festival](#festival).

entries.name: churro
entries.description: A ridged [stick](#stick) of fried [dough](#dough) dusted with sugar, eaten with thick [chocolate](#chocolate) to dip it in. Spanish in origin and hugely popular as [street](#street) [food](#food) across Latin America.

entries.name: dorayaki
entries.description: Sweet red bean paste [sandwiched](#sandwiched) between two small castella pancakes. A classic Japanese confection and a constant [snack](#snack) in everyday scenes.

entries.name: shiruko_(food)
entries.description: A sweet Japanese [soup](#soup) of [crushed](#crushed) red [beans](#beans), served [hot](#hot) with grilled [mochi](#mochi) or rice-flour dumplings [floating](#floating) in it. A [winter](#winter) dish, also sold canned.

entries.name: candy_bar
entries.description: A moulded bar of [sweets](#sweets), usually chocolate-coated and sold in a printed wrapper. Often drawn half unwrapped with a bite gone from one end.

entries.name: ice_cream_cone_spill
entries.description: The scoop has come off its cone, [caught](#caught) in the air or already splattered on the ground. The small disaster is played for sympathy or for a laugh.

entries.name: white_chocolate
entries.description: Pale ivory [chocolate](#chocolate) made from cocoa [butter](#butter) without cocoa solids, shown as [bars](#bars), hearts or a coating on [sweets](#sweets). Appears most around Valentine's Day and White Day.

entries.name: layer_cake
entries.description: A [cake](#cake) built from several rounds of [sponge](#sponge) stacked with [cream](#cream) or [icing](#icing) between them. A cut slice shows the alternating bands clearly.

entries.name: chocolate_covered
entries.description: An item has been dipped in a [coat](#coat) of [chocolate](#chocolate), whether [fruit](#fruit), biscuits or [snack](#snack) sticks. It describes the coating on the [food](#food), not chocolate smeared over a person.

entries.name: kashiwa_mochi_(food)
entries.description: A [rice](#rice) [cake](#cake) filled with sweet bean paste and wrapped in an oak [leaf](#leaf), eaten for the children's [festival](#festival) in early May. The leaf is a wrapper and is not meant to be eaten with it.

entries.name: red_bean_paste
entries.description: A sweet [dark](#dark) paste ground from adzuki [beans](#beans), known as anko in Japan and used to fill buns, [mochi](#mochi), and [dorayaki](#dorayaki). Appears as a glossy dark-red filling or as a spoonful set beside a [dessert](#dessert).

entries.name: gummy_bear
entries.description: The small bear-shaped chewy sweet sold in bags of mixed colours. Covers the [candy](#candy) at any scale, from a handful of them to one blown up as a prop.

entries.name: christmas_cake
entries.description: A [cake](#cake) baked for Christmas, iced and dressed with [holly](#holly), a small Santa [figure](#figure) or a written greeting. In Japan the standard form is a [strawberry](#strawberry) [sponge](#sponge).

entries.name: sandwich_cookie
entries.description: Two flat biscuits with a layer of [cream](#cream) or [jam](#jam) pressed between them, the shape of an Oreo. Often shown being twisted apart.

entries.name: youkan_(food)
entries.description: A firm Japanese sweet of bean paste set with agar and cut into glossy blocks in black, brown, green or yellow. Easily mistaken for uirou, which comes in much the same shape.

entries.name: zunda_mochi
entries.description: Soft [rice](#rice) cakes topped with a bright green paste of mashed young soybeans, a regional specialty of northern Japan. Usually served a few pieces to a [plate](#plate).

entries.name: ice_cream_crepe
entries.description: Ice [cream](#cream) rolled into a thin [pancake](#pancake) wrapped to a point, usually dressed with [fruit](#fruit), cream, [chocolate](#chocolate) or biscuit. Stall counters and [street](#street) scenes are its setting.

entries.name: shortcake
entries.description: A [dessert](#dessert) of crumbly biscuit-style [cake](#cake) layered with [fruit](#fruit) and whipped [cream](#cream). Not the same dish as [strawberry](#strawberry) shortcake, which in Japan is built on [sponge](#sponge) instead.

entries.name: malasada
entries.description: A Portuguese [ball](#ball) of fried [dough](#dough) rolled in sugar, popular in Hawaii and, through it, a regional sweet in [tropical](#tropical) [island](#island) settings. Shown warm and sugar-dusted, often held in one hand.

entries.name: too_many_scoops
entries.description: An [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) cone stacked with an implausible [tower](#tower) of scoops, teetering as it goes. Four is roughly where it starts to qualify.

entries.name: eclair_(food)
entries.description: A finger of choux [pastry](#pastry) piped full of [cream](#cream) or custard and iced along the top, most often with [chocolate](#chocolate). A patisserie [staple](#staple).

entries.name: star-shaped_food
entries.description: Food cut or moulded into a star shape, from [carrot](#carrot) slices in a lunch [box](#box) to cookies and [sweets](#sweets). A standard trick for making a [bento](#bento) look cheerful.

entries.name: heart-shaped_cake
entries.description: A [cake](#cake) baked or cut to a [heart](#heart) [outline](#outline), usually iced and given as a Valentine or [birthday](#birthday) present.

entries.name: heart-shaped_cookie
entries.description: A biscuit cut to a [heart](#heart) [outline](#outline), often iced or filled with [jam](#jam). Usually part of a [gift](#gift) [box](#box) or a [baking](#baking) scene.

entries.name: baumkuchen
entries.description: A German [cake](#cake) baked layer on layer over a turning spit, so a slice shows concentric rings around a hollow middle. Its [ring](#ring) shape made it a favourite [wedding](#wedding) return [gift](#gift) in Japan.

entries.name: ichigo_daifuku
entries.description: A soft [mochi](#mochi) [cake](#cake) wrapped around bean paste with a whole [strawberry](#strawberry) set inside. Cut open, the red [fruit](#fruit) against the white [shell](#shell) is how it is nearly always drawn.

entries.name: caramel
entries.description: Sugar cooked until it melts and browns, then softened with [butter](#butter), [milk](#milk) or [cream](#cream). It appears as chewy [sweets](#sweets), as a [sauce](#sauce), or poured over a [dessert](#dessert).

entries.name: wedding_cake
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) tiered [cake](#cake) served at a [wedding](#wedding), usually white and elaborately decorated, often topped with a small [figure](#figure) of the [couple](#couple). Cutting the first slice together is the standard scene.

entries.name: anmitsu_(dessert)
entries.description: A Japanese sweet of cubed agar jelly served in a [bowl](#bowl) with red bean paste, boiled [peas](#peas) and pieces of [fruit](#fruit). A small pot of [dark](#dark) [syrup](#syrup) comes alongside and is poured over just before [eating](#eating).

entries.name: mousse_(food)
entries.description: An airy dish set with whipped [cream](#cream) or [beaten](#beaten) [egg](#egg) white, sweet or savoury according to what is [folded](#folded) through it. Served [cold](#cold) in a [glass](#glass) or turned out of a mould.

entries.name: strawberry_pocky
entries.description: Biscuit sticks coated in pink [strawberry](#strawberry) [cream](#cream), sold in a red [box](#box). Frequently used for the shared-stick game between two characters.

entries.name: gingerbread_house
entries.description: A [miniature](#miniature) [house](#house) built from slabs of spiced biscuit, cemented with [icing](#icing) and [studded](#studded) with [sweets](#sweets). Belongs to Christmas scenes and to retellings of Hansel and Gretel.

entries.name: old-fashioned_doughnut
entries.description: A [cake](#cake) [doughnut](#doughnut) with a craggy ridged surface and [split](#split), crisp edges, denser and heavier than a raised [ring](#ring).

entries.name: strawberry_tart
entries.description: A [pastry](#pastry) case filled with [cream](#cream) and covered in strawberries laid out across the top.

entries.name: roasted_marshmallow
entries.description: A [marshmallow](#marshmallow) browned over a flame, usually still speared on a [stick](#stick). Belongs to [campfire](#campfire) and [bonfire](#bonfire) scenes.

entries.name: chocolate_icing
entries.description: A cocoa glaze spread or poured over a [cake](#cake), [doughnut](#doughnut) or [pastry](#pastry) as a set topping. Runny [sauce](#sauce) poured across a [dessert](#dessert) is [chocolate_syrup](#chocolate_syrup) instead.

entries.name: double_popsicle
entries.description: A twin [ice](#ice) lolly moulded so it [can](#can) be snapped down the middle and shared. A recurring [gag](#gag) has the break go crooked, leaving one person with a stub.

entries.name: tiramisu
entries.description: An Italian layered [dessert](#dessert) of coffee-soaked [sponge](#sponge) fingers under sweetened mascarpone, finished with a dusting of cocoa. Served as a [square](#square) slice or spooned into a [glass](#glass).

entries.name: pudding_a_la_mode
entries.description: A custard [pudding](#pudding) plated with a scoop of [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) and pieces of [fruit](#fruit), often finished with whipped cream. A café [dessert](#dessert) [staple](#staple), usually served in a [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass) or shallow dish.

entries.name: yule_log_(cake)
entries.description: A rolled [sponge](#sponge) [cake](#cake) iced to look like a [log](#log), complete with a bark-textured surface and small sugar or meringue [decorations](#decorations) on top. A traditional Christmas [dessert](#dessert), also known by its French name.

entries.name: bread
entries.description: Baked bread in any form: a loaf, a [baguette](#baguette), rolls, [toast](#toast) or a sweet bun, on a [plate](#plate), in a [bag](#bag) or halfway to somebody's mouth. Add [food](#food), and the specific kind where it is clear, such as [bread_slice](#bread_slice) or [melon_bread](#melon_bread).

entries.name: burger
entries.description: A ground-meat patty served in a [split](#split) bun, often with [cheese](#cheese), [sauce](#sauce) and vegetables. A patty melt counts; the Japanese hamburger [steak](#steak) served without [bread](#bread) does not.

entries.name: pizza
entries.description: A round flat baked [bread](#bread) topped with [sauce](#sauce), [cheese](#cheese) and other toppings, shown whole or cut into wedges. Sweet [dessert](#dessert) versions count too; a single wedge on its own is better tagged [pizza_slice](#pizza_slice).

entries.name: sandwich
entries.description: Two slices of [bread](#bread) with a filling between them. Not a [burger](#burger), which has a [beef](#beef) patty; sandwiches use [cold](#cold) [cuts](#cuts) or other fillings.

entries.name: pancake
entries.description: A round flat [cake](#cake) of sweet [batter](#batter) cooked on a [griddle](#griddle) or in a pan, often served with [syrup](#syrup), [butter](#butter) or [fruit](#fruit). Several piled up additionally take [pancake_stack](#pancake_stack).

entries.name: baozi
entries.description: A round white steamed bun with a filling of [meat](#meat) or sweet paste, called nikuman or manjuu in Japanese. It is usually drawn steaming in a [bamboo](#bamboo) [basket](#basket) or cupped in both hands on a [cold](#cold) [day](#day).

entries.name: bread_slice
entries.description: A single slice cut from a loaf, most often [toast](#toast), on a [plate](#plate), in a hand or clamped between somebody's [teeth](#teeth). Where a character is [running](#running) with it in their mouth, [toast_in_mouth](#toast_in_mouth) applies too.

entries.name: siopao
entries.description: A Filipino steamed bun with a soft white [dough](#dough) [shell](#shell) and a savory filling, usually [pork](#pork). Served in a round [dome](#dome) shape, often carried in a [bamboo](#bamboo) [basket](#basket).

entries.name: pastry
entries.description: A baked item such as a [croissant](#croissant), danish or tart. It serves as the catch-all when the exact kind of baked good cannot be made out or has [no](#no) [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: toast
entries.description: A toasted slice of [bread](#bread), frequently spread with [butter](#butter) or [jam](#jam) and served at [breakfast](#breakfast). A slice carried in the mouth is [toast_in_mouth](#toast_in_mouth).

entries.name: bean_bun
entries.description: A soft steamed or baked bun filled with sweet red bean paste, the [dark](#dark) filling showing when it is [torn](#torn) open. A [staple](#staple) of Japanese and Chinese confectionery.

entries.name: baguette
entries.description: A long, slim French loaf slashed diagonally across the crust, those [cuts](#cuts) being part of how it bakes. It gets carried home in a [bag](#bag), eaten, or swung about like a [sword](#sword) for comedy.

entries.name: pie
entries.description: A baked dish whose [pastry](#pastry) crust encloses [fruit](#fruit), [cream](#cream), [chocolate](#chocolate), [meat](#meat) or vegetables, shown whole or already cut. An open-topped one is [tart_(food)](#tart_(food)), and a single wedge is [pie_slice](#pie_slice).

entries.name: pizza_slice
entries.description: A single wedge cut from a whole [pizza](#pizza), held, plated, or being eaten. The whole [pie](#pie) or several slices together should be tagged pizza instead.

entries.name: hot_dog
entries.description: A [sausage](#sausage) served in a [split](#split) bun, usually striped with [ketchup](#ketchup), [mustard](#mustard) or relish. The sausage on its own counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: pancake_stack
entries.description: Pancakes piled one on another into a little [tower](#tower), the classic [breakfast](#breakfast) presentation with [butter](#butter) [melting](#melting) on top. Use [pancake](#pancake) alongside it.

entries.name: melon_bread
entries.description: A sweet bun with a crackled, cookie-like crust [patterned](#patterned) after a melon's rind, traditionally baked without any [melon](#melon) flavoring. A [signature](#signature) [snack](#snack) of the character Shana.

entries.name: croissant
entries.description: A flaky buttery [pastry](#pastry) curved into a [crescent](#crescent), on a [breakfast](#breakfast) [plate](#plate) or in a [bakery](#bakery) [window](#window). Hair or a [costume](#costume) merely shaped like one is a different matter.

entries.name: muffin
entries.description: A small domed [cake](#cake) baked in a [paper](#paper) case, often [studded](#studded) with berries, bran or [chocolate](#chocolate). Unlike a [cupcake](#cupcake) it carries [no](#no) [icing](#icing) on top.

entries.name: waffle
entries.description: A [pastry](#pastry) pressed in an iron so it carries a deep [grid](#grid) pattern. Usually served stacked with [syrup](#syrup), [cream](#cream) or [fruit](#fruit) at [breakfast](#breakfast) or as a [dessert](#dessert).

entries.name: chocolate_cornet
entries.description: A Japanese sweet [bread](#bread) wound into a tapering horn and piped full of [chocolate](#chocolate) [cream](#cream). Its [spiral](#spiral) [shell](#shell) shape makes it easy to pick out on a [plate](#plate) or in somebody's hand.

entries.name: pie_slice
entries.description: A wedge cut from a whole [pie](#pie), [resting](#resting) on a [plate](#plate) or lifted on a [fork](#fork). The exposed face showing the filling is what sets it apart from an uncut pie.

entries.name: pretzel
entries.description: A baked [snack](#snack) of salted [dough](#dough), twisted into the [familiar](#familiar) loose knot or rolled out as a straight [stick](#stick). Comes both soft and doughy and hard and brittle.

entries.name: loaf_of_bread
entries.description: A whole loaf of [bread](#bread) with its crust intact and not yet cut. Use it for the entire loaf rather than for a slice or a roll.

entries.name: bread_bun
entries.description: A soft round [bread](#bread) roll, [plain](#plain) or with something baked inside it. The [tag](#tag) is a catch-all and takes in the [sliced](#sliced) kind used for burgers and [submarine](#submarine) sandwiches.

entries.name: margherita_pizza
entries.description: The [plain](#plain) Neapolitan [pizza](#pizza) of [tomato](#tomato), mozzarella and fresh basil with [salt](#salt) and oil, so red, white and green show in patches. Served whole on a board or cut into wedges.

entries.name: scone
entries.description: A small crumbly baked [cake](#cake) of [flour](#flour), [fat](#fat) and [milk](#milk), sometimes [studded](#studded) with raisins. Served [split](#split), often with [cream](#cream) and [jam](#jam) beside a pot of [tea](#tea).

entries.name: souffle_pancake
entries.description: A Japanese [pancake](#pancake) made unusually thick and airy by folding [beaten](#beaten) [egg](#egg) whites into the [batter](#batter), so it stands [tall](#tall) and jiggles. Cooked in a [ring](#ring) [mold](#mold), it comes out neater and denser.

entries.name: yakisobapan
entries.description: A soft [split](#split) roll stuffed with sauced fried [noodles](#noodles), usually sold tightly wrapped in plastic because the filling tends to [slide](#slide) out. Cheap school-canteen fare, so it turns up often in student settings.

entries.name: anpan
entries.description: A soft round Japanese bun filled with sweet red bean paste, often sprinkled with black sesame or topped with a single poppy [seed](#seed). A [staple](#staple) of lunchboxes and [street](#street) snacks.

entries.name: biscuit_(bread)
entries.description: The American quickbread: a small round roll with a golden crust, a soft crumbly inside and [no](#no) sweetness at all. Eaten at [breakfast](#breakfast) or beside a main course, unlike the sweet British biscuit.

entries.name: cinnamon_roll
entries.description: A [spiral](#spiral) [pastry](#pastry) rolled around cinnamon sugar, baked and finished with glaze or [cream](#cream) [cheese](#cheese) frosting. The visible coil is what identifies it.

entries.name: bagel
entries.description: A dense [ring](#ring) of [bread](#bread), boiled before it goes into the [oven](#oven), which is what gives it a chewy crust. It is bigger than a [doughnut](#doughnut) and finished with seeds or [salt](#salt) rather than sugar.

entries.name: submarine_sandwich
entries.description: A long roll [split](#split) lengthwise and packed with layers of [meat](#meat), [cheese](#cheese) and vegetables, named for its resemblance to the boat's shape. Implies [sandwich](#sandwich).

entries.name: fruit_sandwich
entries.description: A Japanese [sandwich](#sandwich) of whipped [cream](#cream) and cut [fruit](#fruit), [sliced](#sliced) so the pieces show as a [cross-section](#cross-section). Sold in convenience stores and drawn constantly in [cafe](#cafe) scenes.

entries.name: hot_dog_bun
entries.description: The long roll [split](#split) along the top that a [sausage](#sausage) sits in. It covers the [bread](#bread) itself, whether filled, empty or held out to be filled.

entries.name: bun_(food)
entries.description: A soft round [bread](#bread) roll, [plain](#plain) or with something baked inside. Shown on a [plate](#plate), in a hand or as part of a larger [meal](#meal).

entries.name: food
entries.description: Something edible is present in the picture, on a [plate](#plate), in a hand or spread across a [table](#table). It is the catch-all; add the specific dish or ingredient wherever it [can](#can) be named.

entries.name: rice
entries.description: Cooked rice on view, in a [bowl](#bowl), on a [plate](#plate) or as part of a larger [meal](#meal). Shaped rice has its own tags such as [onigiri](#onigiri); a bowl on its own is [rice_bowl](#rice_bowl).

entries.name: noodles
entries.description: Long strips of boiled [dough](#dough), covering [pasta](#pasta) such as [spaghetti](#spaghetti) as [well](#well) as [ramen](#ramen), [udon](#udon) and [soba](#soba). They may sit in a [bowl](#bowl), be lifted on [chopsticks](#chopsticks) or hang from the mouth.

entries.name: onigiri
entries.description: A [ball](#ball) of Japanese [rice](#rice) pressed into a [triangle](#triangle) or an oval, usually banded with a strip of [seaweed](#seaweed) and filled with pickled [plum](#plum) or [fish](#fish). Grilled ones count as [well](#well).

entries.name: sushi
entries.description: Japanese seasoned [rice](#rice) served with [fish](#fish) or other toppings, whether as nigiri, rolls or presented in a [box](#box). Implies [food](#food).

entries.name: ramen
entries.description: Japanese [wheat](#wheat) [noodles](#noodles) served in a flavored broth, topped with items like chashu [pork](#pork), [seaweed](#seaweed), a soft [egg](#egg), or spring [onion](#onion). Combine with [bowl](#bowl) and either [eating](#eating) or [chopsticks](#chopsticks) when it is being eaten.

entries.name: omelet
entries.description: Beaten eggs cooked flat and [folded](#folded) over, often with vegetables, [cheese](#cheese) or [rice](#rice) inside. The Japanese rice-stuffed version has its own [tag](#tag), [omurice](#omurice).

entries.name: bento
entries.description: A Japanese packed lunch: [rice](#rice) with [fish](#fish) or [meat](#meat), rolled omelette and pickled or cooked vegetables arranged in a compartmented [box](#box), sometimes tied up in a [cloth](#cloth). Rooftops and picnics are where it gets opened.

entries.name: egg_(food)
entries.description: An [egg](#egg) in its role as something to eat: fried, boiled, scrambled, [folded](#folded) into an omelette or laid over [rice](#rice). Use it where the egg is prepared or served rather than [sitting](#sitting) raw in a [nest](#nest).

entries.name: fried_egg
entries.description: An [egg](#egg) fried with its yolk left whole, a [breakfast](#breakfast) [staple](#staple) eaten alone, on [toast](#toast) or in a [burger](#burger). A yolk still runny makes it sunny side up.

entries.name: curry
entries.description: A spiced [sauce](#sauce) dish of South Asian origin, in anime almost always the Japanese kind. Add [curry_rice](#curry_rice) for the usual [serving](#serving) with [rice](#rice) underneath.

entries.name: chicken_(food)
entries.description: Chicken served as a dish: fried, roasted, grilled, or in pieces such as [wings](#wings) and [drumsticks](#drumsticks). The living [bird](#bird) takes [chicken](#chicken).

entries.name: omurice
entries.description: Fried [rice](#rice) wrapped in a thin sheet of [egg](#egg) and topped with [ketchup](#ketchup), which is usually squeezed out to write a name or a message. A [staple](#staple) of [maid](#maid) [cafe](#cafe) scenes.

entries.name: in_food
entries.description: A character [sitting](#sitting) in a single dish or among a spread of them. The [food](#food) may be [scenery](#scenery), a playful [screen](#screen) over a bare body, or a design the character has been built to blend into.

entries.name: takoyaki
entries.description: Japanese [batter](#batter) balls cooked with a piece of [octopus](#octopus) inside, topped with [sauce](#sauce), [seaweed](#seaweed) and scallions. A classic [festival](#festival) [food](#food) stall item.

entries.name: cup_ramen
entries.description: Instant [noodles](#noodles) sold in a [foam](#foam) or plastic [cup](#cup), ready three minutes after [hot](#hot) [water](#water) goes in. The [branded](#branded) product is nissin_cup_noodle, and a [bowl](#bowl) served in a [shop](#shop) is [ramen](#ramen).

entries.name: tempura
entries.description: Japanese deep-fried [food](#food) in a light, crisp [batter](#batter), most often [shrimp](#shrimp), [fish](#fish) or vegetables, served on its own or over [rice](#rice) and [noodles](#noodles).

entries.name: fast_food
entries.description: Quick-service [food](#food) such as burgers, fries, [hot](#hot) dogs, [pizza](#pizza) and fried [chicken](#chicken), often in printed wrappers and [paper](#paper) cups. It covers the [meal](#meal) and the [counter](#counter) it came from; add the specific food [tag](#tag) too.

entries.name: soup
entries.description: A [hot](#hot), broth-based dish, often [carrying](#carrying) [noodles](#noodles), vegetables, or [meat](#meat). Covers Western-style soups as [well](#well) as ramen-type bowls where the [liquid](#liquid) itself is the point.

entries.name: pasta
entries.description: Italian [noodles](#noodles) of [wheat](#wheat) [dough](#dough) in any shape, from [spaghetti](#spaghetti) to penne to sheets of lasagne, generally served with [sauce](#sauce). Where the shape is [plain](#plain) to see, use the specific [tag](#tag) such as spaghetti instead.

entries.name: instant_cup_noodles
entries.description: Dried [noodles](#noodles) packed in their own [paper](#paper) or [foam](#foam) [cup](#cup), wanting nothing but [hot](#hot) [water](#water) and a folded-back [lid](#lid). Convenience stores, late nights and cluttered desks are where they turn up.

entries.name: makizushi
entries.description: Cylindrical [sushi](#sushi) rolled in a sheet of nori, thick or thin, normally [sliced](#sliced) into rounds. Rolls with the [seaweed](#seaweed) on the inside are uramaki and whole uncut ones are [ehoumaki](#ehoumaki); it is also a stock phallic prop.

entries.name: curry_rice
entries.description: A [plate](#plate) of [rice](#rice) with Japanese-style [curry](#curry) ladled over it, a household [staple](#staple) that arrived by way of the navy. Frequently topped with katsu, fried prawn or a boiled [egg](#egg).

entries.name: dumpling
entries.description: Small parcels of [dough](#dough) wrapped round a savoury or sweet filling, such as gyoza, [jiaozi](#jiaozi) or [baozi](#baozi). Served alone, [floating](#floating) in [soup](#soup), or stacked in a steamer [basket](#basket).

entries.name: bad_food
entries.description: A dish meant to be appetising that has come out looking lethal, [glowing](#glowing) an impossible colour, bubbling, or blacked out entirely. It is a [comic](#comic) [staple](#staple), with a well-meaning cook and [horrified](#horrified) onlookers around it.

entries.name: spaghetti
entries.description: Long, thin, round strands of [pasta](#pasta), typically served with [sauce](#sauce) on a [plate](#plate) or twirled around a [fork](#fork). The most recognizable pasta shape.

entries.name: shrimp_tempura
entries.description: Shrimp deep-fried in a light [tempura](#tempura) [batter](#batter), a Japanese dish eaten on its own or over [rice](#rice) or [noodles](#noodles). Implies [shrimp](#shrimp) and tempura.

entries.name: steak
entries.description: A thick cut of [meat](#meat), usually [beef](#beef), grilled or pan-seared and served on a [plate](#plate). Fish or venison steaks count too.

entries.name: salad
entries.description: A dish of cut raw vegetables tossed in a [bowl](#bowl), usually with [dressing](#dressing). Tag alongside [food](#food).

entries.name: fried_chicken
entries.description: Chicken pieces seasoned, breaded and fried, served in a [bucket](#bucket), a [basket](#basket) or on a [plate](#plate). Japanese karaage counts as its local form.

entries.name: food_art
entries.description: Food deliberately sculpted or arranged into a recognisable shape, like a character-shaped [bento](#bento) or a design poured into [coffee](#coffee) [foam](#foam). The presentation is the point.

entries.name: tamagoyaki
entries.description: A Japanese rolled [omelet](#omelet), [sliced](#sliced) into blocks and often served on [sushi](#sushi) or packed into a [bento](#bento).

entries.name: ehoumaki
entries.description: A thick [sushi](#sushi) roll left uncut and eaten whole on the [night](#night) of Setsubun while facing the lucky direction of that year. A Kansai custom that convenience stores later spread across the country.

entries.name: fried_rice
entries.description: Cooked [rice](#rice) tossed in a [hot](#hot) [wok](#wok) or pan with [egg](#egg), vegetables and scraps of [meat](#meat). A [staple](#staple) of Chinese and other Asian kitchens, heaped on a [plate](#plate) or served straight from the pan.

entries.name: yakisoba
entries.description: Wheat [noodles](#noodles) fried with [meat](#meat) and vegetables under a sweet-savoury [sauce](#sauce), often heaped on a [paper](#paper) [tray](#tray). A [staple](#staple) of [festival](#festival) stalls and [seaside](#seaside) [food](#food) shacks; the instant [cup](#cup) version is tagged separately.

entries.name: chicken_leg
entries.description: A cooked drumstick, [meat](#meat) wrapped round a [bone](#bone) that sticks out like a [handle](#handle). Cartoon feasts use it as shorthand for a hearty [meal](#meal).

entries.name: udon
entries.description: Thick white Japanese [wheat](#wheat) [noodles](#noodles), usually served [hot](#hot) in broth. Noticeably fatter and softer than the noodles used for [ramen](#ramen).

entries.name: hotpot
entries.description: A pot of broth simmers on the [table](#table) while [meat](#meat), vegetables and [noodles](#noodles) are cooked in it as the [meal](#meal) goes on. A communal [winter](#winter) dish in Chinese and Japanese scenes.

entries.name: jiaozi
entries.description: Half-moon dumplings of thin [dough](#dough) wrapped round minced [meat](#meat) and vegetables, then boiled, steamed or fried. Japan calls them gyoza, and browning one side makes potstickers.

entries.name: turkey_(food)
entries.description: Roast turkey on the [table](#table), whether whole and browned or already carved. Belongs with Thanksgiving and Christmas spreads and other large feasts; the live [bird](#bird) itself is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: kebab
entries.description: Cubes of marinated [meat](#meat) threaded onto a [skewer](#skewer) with vegetables and grilled. Meat carved off a vertical spit and rolled in flatbread is shawarma rather than this.

entries.name: nigirizushi
entries.description: Hand-pressed [sushi](#sushi): a slice of raw [fish](#fish) laid across a small oblong of vinegared [rice](#rice). It is the commonest form served over a sushi [counter](#counter).

entries.name: oden
entries.description: A [winter](#winter) [stew](#stew) of boiled [egg](#egg), [daikon](#daikon), konnyaku and [fish](#fish) cakes left to simmer in a pale soy broth, ladled out of a partitioned pot. What goes into it varies by region and by cook.

entries.name: hamburger_steak
entries.description: A patty of seasoned minced [meat](#meat) shaped by hand and fried, served on a [plate](#plate) under [sauce](#sauce) rather than in a bun. A fixture of Japanese [family](#family) restaurants and [school](#school) lunches.

entries.name: ikayaki
entries.description: Whole [squid](#squid) grilled and brushed with a soy-based [sauce](#sauce), usually served on a [skewer](#skewer). It is stall [food](#food) at [summer](#summer) festivals and [beach](#beach) shops, so it dates the scene as much as feeds it.

entries.name: miso_soup
entries.description: Japanese broth seasoned with fermented [soybean](#soybean) paste, served in a lacquer [bowl](#bowl) with [tofu](#tofu), [seaweed](#seaweed) or spring [onion](#onion) [floating](#floating) in it.

entries.name: zouni_soup
entries.description: The New Year [soup](#soup) eaten in Japan: a clear or miso broth with vegetables and soft [mochi](#mochi) cakes that stretch into long threads when lifted from the [bowl](#bowl). Not to be [confused](#confused) with shiruko, a sweet red-bean soup.

entries.name: nabe
entries.description: A Japanese [hot](#hot) pot simmered at the [table](#table) in a [clay](#clay) or iron vessel, diners [fishing](#fishing) pieces out as they cook. Oden and [sukiyaki](#sukiyaki) are the best-known versions, usually eaten with a dipping [sauce](#sauce).

entries.name: sashimi
entries.description: Raw [fish](#fish) cut into thin slices and arranged on a [plate](#plate) or a [bed](#bed) of shredded [radish](#radish), eaten with soy [sauce](#sauce) and [wasabi](#wasabi). Unlike [sushi](#sushi) it comes without [rice](#rice).

entries.name: soba
entries.description: Thin, greyish-brown buckwheat [noodles](#noodles), served chilled with a dipping [sauce](#sauce) or [hot](#hot) in broth. Eating them on New Year's Eve is a custom, since the easily severed strands are meant to cut off the year's troubles.

entries.name: croquette
entries.description: Minced [meat](#meat), [potato](#potato) or [vegetable](#vegetable) filling wrapped in breadcrumbs and deep-fried, served as a flattened oval patty. A [familiar](#familiar) side dish and [lunchbox](#lunchbox) filler across East Asia and [well](#well) beyond it.

entries.name: breakfast
entries.description: The [morning](#morning) [meal](#meal) set out: [toast](#toast), eggs, [cereal](#cereal) and pancakes, or [rice](#rice) and [soup](#soup), usually with [coffee](#coffee) or [tea](#tea) beside it. Use it for the meal as a whole rather than for any single dish on the [table](#table).

entries.name: fried_egg_on_toast
entries.description: A sunny-side-up [egg](#egg) [resting](#resting) on a slice of [toast](#toast), sometimes with [bacon](#bacon) alongside. Japanese art often nods to the version eaten in a well-known Ghibli film, where it goes by the name Laputa [bread](#bread).

entries.name: stew
entries.description: Meat and vegetables simmered together and served in the thick broth they cooked in. Shown in a pot on the [stove](#stove) or ladled into a deep [bowl](#bowl).

entries.name: instant_ramen
entries.description: Ramen sold as a dried precooked block, either in a flat [packet](#packet) or in a bowl-shaped [cup](#cup). Cheap and quick, it stands in for a student or bachelor [meal](#meal).

entries.name: yakitori
entries.description: Small pieces of [chicken](#chicken) threaded onto [bamboo](#bamboo) skewers and grilled, seasoned with [salt](#salt) or a sweet glaze. Usually shown a few skewers at a time, often alongside drinks.

entries.name: instant_soba
entries.description: Buckwheat [noodles](#noodles) dried into a precooked block, most often packed in a [cup](#cup) and sometimes in flat packets. Cup versions are generally sold as [yakisoba](#yakisoba).

entries.name: meatball
entries.description: A [ball](#ball) of seasoned minced [meat](#meat), usually [beef](#beef), served in [sauce](#sauce), threaded on a [skewer](#skewer), or piled over [noodles](#noodles) or [pasta](#pasta).

entries.name: taco
entries.description: A [folded](#folded) [corn](#corn) or [wheat](#wheat) tortilla [holding](#holding) a filling of [meat](#meat), vegetables or [cheese](#cheese). Usually drawn as a half-moon shape with the filling [spilling](#spilling) over the top edge.

entries.name: nattou
entries.description: Fermented soybeans eaten at Japanese breakfasts, usually over [rice](#rice) with [mustard](#mustard) and soy. Stirring draws out long [sticky](#sticky) threads, and the [smell](#smell) divides opinion sharply.

entries.name: instant_udon
entries.description: Thick [wheat](#wheat) [noodles](#noodles) sold dried and precooked, usually in a bowl-shaped [cup](#cup) that needs only [hot](#hot) [water](#water). Flat packets of it exist as [well](#well).

entries.name: yakiniku
entries.description: Bite-sized [cuts](#cuts) of [meat](#meat) grilled by the diners themselves on a [griddle](#griddle) built into the [table](#table). Tongs, a [smoking](#smoking) [grill](#grill) and small dipping bowls usually complete the scene.

entries.name: wrapped_bento
entries.description: A lunch [box](#box) bundled in [cloth](#cloth), usually a [furoshiki](#furoshiki) knotted over the [lid](#lid). It is carried to [school](#school), work, or a [picnic](#picnic) before anyone opens it.

entries.name: mapo_tofu
entries.description: A Sichuan dish of [tofu](#tofu) cubes in a fiery red chilli and bean [sauce](#sauce), served in a [bowl](#bowl) under minced [meat](#meat) and spring [onion](#onion). The Japanese version leaves out the numbing pepper of the original.

entries.name: grilled_eel
entries.description: Eel [split](#split), skewered and grilled with a sweet soy glaze, usually laid over a [bowl](#bowl) of [rice](#rice). A dish strongly tied to midsummer in Japan.

entries.name: okonomiyaki
entries.description: A thick savoury [pancake](#pancake) of [batter](#batter) and shredded [cabbage](#cabbage) cooked on a [griddle](#griddle), finished with brown [sauce](#sauce), [mayonnaise](#mayonnaise) and curling flakes of dried [fish](#fish). Kansai and Hiroshima each assemble it their own way.

entries.name: burnt_food
entries.description: A dish cooked far past done, blackened and often still [smoking](#smoking). The standard joke about a character who cannot cook.

entries.name: gyuudon
entries.description: A deep [bowl](#bowl) of [rice](#rice) heaped with thin [beef](#beef) and [onion](#onion) stewed in a sweet-savoury broth. Often topped with a raw [egg](#egg) or served beside pickled ginger.

entries.name: grilled_fish
entries.description: A whole [fish](#fish) cooked over heat, identified by char marks or a [skewer](#skewer) run through it. A [staple](#staple) of [campfire](#campfire) meals and [plain](#plain) home [cooking](#cooking).

entries.name: osechi
entries.description: The Japanese New Year spread: small symbolic [dishes](#dishes) packed into stacked lacquer boxes, each [carrying](#carrying) a wish for the year ahead.

entries.name: kiritanpo_(food)
entries.description: Freshly cooked [rice](#rice) pressed around a [skewer](#skewer) into a cylinder and toasted over heat. It is eaten straight off the [stick](#stick) or simmered in [hot](#hot) pot, and is a speciality of northern Japan.

entries.name: creature_as_food
entries.description: A non-human [creature](#creature) or [monster](#monster) is being eaten as a [meal](#meal), cooked and served like ordinary fare. Food merely moulded into such a shape is [character-themed_food](#character-themed_food).

entries.name: char-siu
entries.description: Cantonese barbecued [pork](#pork), glazed deep red and carved into thin slices for [rice](#rice) and noodle [dishes](#dishes). The Japanese version is rolled into a [log](#log) and braised gently before being laid over [ramen](#ramen).

entries.name: too_much_food
entries.description: A character hemmed in by more [food](#food) than any one person could eat, spread across a [table](#table) or heaped in bowls. Sometimes a whole banquet, sometimes one dish repeated absurdly.

entries.name: cereal
entries.description: Grain flakes, rings or puffs in a [bowl](#bowl), usually with [milk](#milk) poured over and sometimes [fruit](#fruit) on top. Breakfast scenes are its home, often in the bright sugary kind made for children.

entries.name: gunkanmaki
entries.description: Sushi built as an oval of [rice](#rice) ringed by a band of [seaweed](#seaweed), forming a little [cup](#cup) for a loose topping such as [roe](#roe). Use it for that specific shape, not for flat rolls or [plain](#plain) nigiri.

entries.name: bucket_of_chicken
entries.description: Fried [chicken](#chicken) served in a [paper](#paper) [bucket](#bucket), the takeaway format of fast-food chains. In Japanese settings it doubles as a [party](#party) and Christmas [dinner](#dinner) prop.

entries.name: katsudon_(food)
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) of [rice](#rice) topped with a fried cutlet simmered with [onion](#onion) and set in [beaten](#beaten) [egg](#egg). A second version dips the cutlet in [sauce](#sauce) and lays it over shredded [cabbage](#cabbage) instead.

entries.name: zongzi
entries.description: Glutinous [rice](#rice) steamed inside a [folded](#folded) bamboo-leaf wrapper into a pyramid shape, filled sweet or savoury depending on the region. Traditionally eaten at the Dragon Boat Festival, and known under a different name for a similar Japanese holiday.

entries.name: dropped_food
entries.description: Food [lying](#lying) on the [floor](#floor) or spilled out of whatever held it, generally by [accident](#accident). The dismay of the moment is usually the point of the picture.

entries.name: inarizushi
entries.description: Sushi [rice](#rice) packed into a [pouch](#pouch) of sweet fried [tofu](#tofu), so the parcel is golden-brown instead of seaweed-wrapped. Its name comes from the [fox](#fox) deity said to be fond of fried tofu.

entries.name: napolitan
entries.description: A Japanese [spaghetti](#spaghetti) dish dressed with [tomato](#tomato) [ketchup](#ketchup) and fried up with [onion](#onion), green pepper, [mushroom](#mushroom) and [sausage](#sausage). It is a [diner](#diner) [staple](#staple) rather than anything Italian.

entries.name: katsu_(food)
entries.description: A [meat](#meat) cutlet coated in breadcrumbs, deep-fried and cut into strips. Pork is standard, [chicken](#chicken) and [beef](#beef) appear too, and shredded [cabbage](#cabbage) with a thick brown [sauce](#sauce) comes alongside.

entries.name: dim_sum
entries.description: Small Cantonese portions served in stacked [bamboo](#bamboo) steamers or on little plates: dumplings, buns, rolls and [rice](#rice) parcels, normally with [tea](#tea). Best used when a spread of the small [dishes](#dishes) covers the [table](#table).

entries.name: kitsune_udon
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) of thick [udon](#udon) [noodles](#noodles) in broth topped with sweetened fried [tofu](#tofu) pouches. The name comes from the belief that foxes love that tofu, so it often turns up with [fox](#fox) characters.

entries.name: field_ration
entries.description: Packaged [military](#military) [food](#food) meant to be eaten away from any [kitchen](#kitchen), in foil pouches, tins or a printed [carton](#carton). The American MRE is one particular kind.

entries.name: sushi_geta
entries.description: A flat wooden [serving](#serving) board raised on two small [feet](#feet), used to present [sushi](#sushi). The name comes from its likeness to the traditional raised sandal.

entries.name: spaghetti_and_meatballs
entries.description: Long [pasta](#pasta) under [tomato](#tomato) [sauce](#sauce) topped with meatballs, served in a [bowl](#bowl) or on a [plate](#plate). Its Western-diner look sets it apart from most Japanese pasta [dishes](#dishes).

entries.name: tamagokake_gohan
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) of white [rice](#rice) with a raw or lightly cooked [egg](#egg) [broken](#broken) over it, often finished with a splash of soy [sauce](#sauce). A [plain](#plain), everyday Japanese [breakfast](#breakfast) dish.

entries.name: feast
entries.description: A [table](#table) loaded with far more [dishes](#dishes) or [sweets](#sweets) than one [meal](#meal) needs. The sheer spread is the subject, whether in a banquet hall or at a holiday [dinner](#dinner).

entries.name: nagashi_soumen
entries.description: Thin [wheat](#wheat) [noodles](#noodles) sent down a [split](#split) [bamboo](#bamboo) flume in [cold](#cold) [running](#running) [water](#water) and snatched out with [chopsticks](#chopsticks) as they pass. It is as much a [summer](#summer) game as a [meal](#meal).

entries.name: donburi
entries.description: A deep [bowl](#bowl) of [rice](#rice) topped with [meat](#meat), [fish](#fish) or vegetables that have been simmered together and spooned over. The word covers the dish and the bowl it arrives in alike.

entries.name: stargazy_pie
entries.description: A Cornish [pie](#pie) baked with whole [fish](#fish) [poking](#poking) head-first through the crust so they seem to look upward. Sardines are the usual filling.

entries.name: sukiyaki
entries.description: A hot-pot dish simmered at the [table](#table): thin [beef](#beef) with [tofu](#tofu), mushrooms, greens, spring [onion](#onion) and [noodles](#noodles) in a sweetened soy broth. Diners usually dip each piece in raw [beaten](#beaten) [egg](#egg) before [eating](#eating). Implies [food](#food).

entries.name: chinese_food
entries.description: Dishes from the Chinese [kitchen](#kitchen) such as dim sum, [baozi](#baozi), [jiaozi](#jiaozi), mooncakes, tangyuan and [zongzi](#zongzi). They usually arrive in [bamboo](#bamboo) steamers or on shared plates around a round [table](#table).

entries.name: jirou_(ramen)
entries.description: A [ramen](#ramen) style served under a heap of bean sprouts with thick slabs of fatty [pork](#pork) and raw [garlic](#garlic) in a rich pork-and-soy broth. Finishing a [bowl](#bowl) is famously hard.

entries.name: soumen
entries.description: Extremely thin [wheat](#wheat) [noodles](#noodles), roughly a millimeter across, eaten chilled in [summer](#summer) to cool off. Their fineness sets them apart from thicker [udon](#udon), and served [hot](#hot) in broth they take the name nyumen.

entries.name: okosama_lunch
entries.description: The Japanese children's [plate](#plate): a moulded mound of [rice](#rice), a hamburger [steak](#steak), [spaghetti](#spaghetti), [shrimp](#shrimp) and fried odds and ends set out together, with a small [paper](#paper) [flag](#flag) [stuck](#stuck) in the top.

entries.name: egg
entries.description: An egg of any sort, most often the white or brown [chicken](#chicken) kind but also those of reptiles, [fish](#fish) or invented creatures. Use it for the object in any role; where it is clearly served up, add [egg_(food)](#egg_(food)).

entries.name: meat
entries.description: Cooked or raw meat left unidentified as to type or cut. When the specific cut or dish [can](#can) be named instead, such as [steak](#steak) or [sausage](#sausage), use that [tag](#tag); the cartoonish [ham](#ham) on a [bone](#bone) is [boned_meat](#boned_meat).

entries.name: heart-shaped_food
entries.description: Any [food](#food) item made in the [outline](#outline) of a [heart](#heart): biscuits, cakes, a fried [egg](#egg), [rice](#rice) pressed into shape.

entries.name: chips_(food)
entries.description: Thin fried slices of [potato](#potato), [corn](#corn) tortilla or similar, salted or seasoned, in a [bag](#bag), tipped into a [bowl](#bowl) or being eaten. British-style fried potato sticks are [french_fries](#french_fries) and do not belong here.

entries.name: cheese
entries.description: A block, slice or wedge of cheese, or cheese melted over a [burger](#burger) or [pizza](#pizza). It has to read as a distinct [food](#food) item.

entries.name: french_fries
entries.description: Long strips of deep-fried [potato](#potato), called chips in British English. They usually arrive in a fast-food [carton](#carton), and [cheese](#cheese) fries and poutine are variants of them.

entries.name: skewer
entries.description: A thin [stick](#stick) threaded with pieces of grilled [meat](#meat), vegetables or [dango](#dango). Covers both the stick and the skewered [food](#food).

entries.name: potato_chips
entries.description: Thin fried [potato](#potato) slices eaten as a [snack](#snack), called crisps in Britain, usually in a [bag](#bag) or [bowl](#bowl). Includes stacked-dough versions like Pringles; fried potato sticks are [french_fries](#french_fries).

entries.name: fish_(food)
entries.description: Fish prepared or served as a [meal](#meal), grilled whole on a [plate](#plate) or cut into fillets. Distinct from a live [fish](#fish) in the [water](#water).

entries.name: ketchup
entries.description: Thick red [tomato](#tomato) [sauce](#sauce) used as a condiment, squeezed onto [food](#food) or drawn into words and pictures on an omelette. Tag the [bottle](#bottle) separately if one is shown.

entries.name: boned_meat
entries.description: The cartoon joint of [meat](#meat): a [fat](#fat) rounded cut with a length of [bone](#bone) [poking](#poking) out at each end. It stands in for hunger or for [food](#food) in general and looks like nothing a butcher would sell.

entries.name: sausage
entries.description: Ground [meat](#meat) packed into a casing, shown whole, [sliced](#sliced) or on a [plate](#plate). Distinct from [hot_dog](#hot_dog), which is a sausage served in a bun.

entries.name: syrup
entries.description: A thick, sweet [liquid](#liquid), typically golden brown, poured over pancakes or waffles as a topping.

entries.name: popcorn
entries.description: Puffed maize kernels, usually in a [bucket](#bucket) or [bag](#bag), the [snack](#snack) of cinemas and spectators. Often shown eaten while [watching](#watching) something.

entries.name: honey
entries.description: Thick golden [syrup](#syrup) made by bees, shown [dripping](#dripping) from a dipper or [spoon](#spoon), pooling in a [jar](#jar), or poured over [food](#food). Bees, honeycomb and [bear](#bear) characters keep it company.

entries.name: wheat
entries.description: The [staple](#staple) [cereal](#cereal) crop, most often shown as a golden [field](#field) of ripe stalks [swaying](#swaying) before harvest, or as a few ears held or chewed on.

entries.name: snack
entries.description: Light finger [food](#food) between meals like chips, [popcorn](#popcorn), pretzels or crackers, or any unidentifiable nibble. Sugary ones fall under [sweets](#sweets) and after-dinner ones under [dessert](#dessert).

entries.name: butter
entries.description: A pat, block or dish of butter, often [melting](#melting) over [toast](#toast), pancakes or waffles. It is churned from [cream](#cream), unlike the plant-oil margarine it resembles.

entries.name: crumbs
entries.description: Small scattered fragments of [bread](#bread), biscuit, [cake](#cake) or crisps, left on a [plate](#plate), a [table](#table) or a character's face. Usually the leftovers of [eating](#eating).

entries.name: bag_of_chips
entries.description: A [snack](#snack) [packet](#packet) of [potato](#potato) crisps or similar, sealed or [torn](#torn) open, being eaten from or simply [lying](#lying) about. Add [eating](#eating) when somebody is [working](#working) through it.

entries.name: food_bite
entries.description: A chunk is missing where [teeth](#teeth) went in, and the [tag](#tag) records that notch rather than the act of [biting](#biting). Someone [caught](#caught) mid-bite belongs to biting, and what was bitten need not even be edible.

entries.name: sauce
entries.description: A [liquid](#liquid) or creamy condiment poured over or mixed into [food](#food), such as [ketchup](#ketchup), soy sauce, pesto or a white sauce. Tag when the sauce itself is visibly present in the picture.

entries.name: roasted_sweet_potato
entries.description: A sweet [potato](#potato) baked whole until the skin darkens and the [flesh](#flesh) turns golden, [split](#split) open and eaten [hot](#hot). In Japan it is a [winter](#winter) [street](#street) [food](#food) sold from carts.

entries.name: kamaboko
entries.description: Fish paste steamed into a firm loaf and cut into thin slices, laid over [noodles](#noodles) or floated in [soup](#soup). A slice with a pink [spiral](#spiral) [running](#running) through it is [narutomaki](#narutomaki).

entries.name: jam
entries.description: Fruit boiled with sugar until it sets into a thick sweet spread, shown in a [jar](#jar) or spread over [bread](#bread). It ranges from a clear jelly to a chunky preserve full of pieces.

entries.name: bacon
entries.description: Strips of cured [pork](#pork) from the [belly](#belly) or the [back](#back), fried until the [fat](#fat) crisps and the edges curl. It shows up at [breakfast](#breakfast), stacked into burgers and sandwiches, or wrapped around something else.

entries.name: pet_food
entries.description: Kibble, tinned [meat](#meat) or similar [food](#food) meant for an [animal](#animal), most often served in a [bowl](#bowl) on the [floor](#floor). Tag it for the food itself rather than for the animal [eating](#eating) it.

entries.name: narutomaki
entries.description: A slice of steamed [fish](#fish) [cake](#cake) with a pink [spiral](#spiral) [coiled](#coiled) at its centre. It is laid on a [bowl](#bowl) of [ramen](#ramen) as [garnish](#garnish) rather than eaten on its own.

entries.name: senbei
entries.description: Crisp Japanese [rice](#rice) crackers, usually round and glazed with soy [sauce](#sauce), sometimes banded with a strip of dried [seaweed](#seaweed). Snack [food](#food), generally eaten with [tea](#tea).

entries.name: tofu
entries.description: Soft white blocks of pressed soy curd, served cubed in [soup](#soup), [sliced](#sliced) on a [plate](#plate) or [sitting](#sitting) in a [bowl](#bowl) of [water](#water).

entries.name: soy_sauce
entries.description: A thin, [dark](#dark) brown seasoning brewed from fermented soybeans, poured over [food](#food) or served in a small dish for dipping.

entries.name: seed
entries.description: A [plant](#plant) seed, held, sown into [soil](#soil), or eaten. Frequently used where a character nibbles at seeds hamster-fashion.

entries.name: chocolate_syrup
entries.description: Chocolate thinned to a pourable [sauce](#sauce), drizzling over [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream), pancakes or another [dessert](#dessert). The [running](#running) [stream](#stream) is what separates it from a set glaze.

entries.name: eggshell
entries.description: The hard outer casing of an [egg](#egg), cracked open, [split](#split) in halves or [lying](#lying) in fragments. Scattered across a [counter](#counter), or worn on a head as a joke.

entries.name: mint
entries.description: The [herb](#herb) and the flavor drawn from it: sprigs of toothed green leaves, and the pale green candies, ices and drinks scented with it.

entries.name: cheese_trail
entries.description: Melted [cheese](#cheese) pulls into strings between a bite and the rest of the dish, most often a slice being lifted off a [pizza](#pizza). It signals that the [food](#food) is [hot](#hot) and freshly made.

entries.name: egg_yolk
entries.description: The yellow [heart](#heart) of an [egg](#egg), [sitting](#sitting) domed on a fried egg or [broken](#broken) and [running](#running) loose. Beaten into the white it becomes an omelette or scrambled egg instead.

entries.name: aburaage
entries.description: Thin slabs of [tofu](#tofu) fried twice until golden and puffed, a [staple](#staple) of Japanese [cooking](#cooking). Its association with a certain noodle dish makes it a recurring prop in fox-spirit pictures.

entries.name: animal-themed_food
entries.description: Something edible cut, moulded or decorated into a [creature](#creature): bunny-eared [apple](#apple) wedges, bear-faced buns, [cat](#cat) pancakes. The reverse arrangement, a creature built to look like [food](#food), has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: nori_(seaweed)
entries.description: Dried sheets of edible [seaweed](#seaweed), nearly black in colour, wrapped around [rice](#rice) balls and [sushi](#sushi) or shredded over [noodles](#noodles) and [soup](#soup).

entries.name: tako-san_wiener
entries.description: A small [sausage](#sausage) [sliced](#sliced) at one end so it splays into octopus-like [legs](#legs) once cooked, a standard decoration in packed lunch boxes. The crab-shaped version of the same trick has its own name.

entries.name: mayonnaise
entries.description: A thick pale condiment whipped from oil and [egg](#egg) yolk, squeezed over [food](#food) in neat lines or piled on far past what is reasonable for [comic](#comic) effect.

entries.name: coffee_beans
entries.description: The roasted seeds [coffee](#coffee) is brewed from, shown loose in a [sack](#sack), a [jar](#jar), a scoop or a grinder. Despite the name they are seeds rather than [beans](#beans).

entries.name: canned_food
entries.description: Food sealed in a steel or tin-plated [can](#can), usually cylindrical and needing an opener. Found in kitchens, on [shop](#shop) shelves and in stockpiles.

entries.name: chestnut
entries.description: The glossy brown nut that grows inside a spiky green husk, eaten roasted or candied. Autumn scenes and Japanese [sweets](#sweets) both make [heavy](#heavy) use of it.

entries.name: corn_dog
entries.description: A [sausage](#sausage) on a wooden [stick](#stick), coated in cornmeal [batter](#batter) and deep fried. Festival and [street](#street) [food](#food), sold in Japan under the name American [dog](#dog).

entries.name: salmon
entries.description: The orange-pink [flesh](#flesh) of the [fish](#fish) prepared to eat: raw slices for [sashimi](#sashimi), a topping on [sushi](#sushi), or a grilled fillet on a [plate](#plate).

entries.name: garnish
entries.description: A small decorative addition to a dish or a [drink](#drink): a [herb](#herb) sprig, a [mint](#mint) [leaf](#leaf), a twist of citrus. Put there for looks rather than to add substance.

entries.name: chikuwa
entries.description: A Japanese fish-paste [stick](#stick), browned outside and hollow down the middle from the rod it was formed around. It goes into [oden](#oden) pots and noodle bowls.

entries.name: hardboiled_egg
entries.description: An [egg](#egg) cooked in its [shell](#shell) until both white and yolk have set firm. It appears whole, peeled, or halved to show the yolk, and often [sliced](#sliced) onto [ramen](#ramen) or into a [salad](#salad).

entries.name: mustard
entries.description: The yellow condiment ground from mustard [seed](#seed), squeezed over [hot](#hot) dogs and burgers or set out in a small dish. Ketchup is its usual companion at the [table](#table).

entries.name: nut_(food)
entries.description: Tree nuts as something to eat: acorns, chestnuts, peanuts and the like, shelled or still whole. Often heaped in a [bowl](#bowl) or clutched in the paws of a [squirrel](#squirrel).

entries.name: ikura_(food)
entries.description: Salmon [roe](#roe): glossy orange [beads](#beads) served loose over [rice](#rice) or heaped on a seaweed-walled [sushi](#sushi) roll. Those [translucent](#translucent) spheres [catching](#catching) the light are how it reads at a [glance](#glance).

entries.name: salt
entries.description: White crystalline seasoning, shown heaped in a dish, poured from a cellar or scattered over [food](#food). In Japanese scenes it also appears as small cones piled at a [doorway](#doorway) for purification.

entries.name: spicy
entries.description: The reaction to [eating](#eating) something too [hot](#hot) to [handle](#handle) comfortably: [fire](#fire) breathed out, [sweat](#sweat), a wide open mouth with the [tongue](#tongue) out, streaming eyes, and a reddened face. Can also just [tag](#tag) the fiery dish being shown.

entries.name: matcha_(food)
entries.description: Sweets and [dishes](#dishes) flavoured and dyed with powdered green [tea](#tea), recognisable by their deep green colour. Brewed and [drunk](#drunk) it is [green_tea](#green_tea) instead.

entries.name: cracker
entries.description: A thin baked biscuit, usually salted or savoury, eaten by the handful or with something spread on top. Sweet and chocolate-coated kinds exist too.

entries.name: chicken_nuggets
entries.description: Small pieces of boneless [chicken](#chicken) in [batter](#batter) or crumb, fried or baked and served in a [box](#box) with a dip. Fast [food](#food) scenes are where they belong.

entries.name: beef
entries.description: Meat from cattle, drawn raw as steaks and [cuts](#cuts) or [cooking](#cooking) on a [grill](#grill) or [plate](#plate). Barbecue, [yakiniku](#yakiniku) and [kitchen](#kitchen) scenes account for most of it.

entries.name: peanut
entries.description: The legume eaten roasted, ground into [butter](#butter) or pressed for oil, drawn in its wrinkled [tan](#tan) [shell](#shell) or as bare kernels in their papery skins.

entries.name: raw_meat
entries.description: Uncooked [flesh](#flesh), whether whole [cuts](#cuts), chops, or slabs, shown before any heat has touched it. Butcher shops, [kitchen](#kitchen) prep, and feral [feeding](#feeding) scenes are the usual contexts, with [sashimi](#sashimi) [standing](#standing) as the exception [people](#people) eat as is.

entries.name: softboiled_egg
entries.description: An [egg](#egg) boiled only until the white sets, leaving the yolk still [liquid](#liquid). Halved over [ramen](#ramen) or served in a [cup](#cup), the [running](#running) yolk is what identifies it.

entries.name: sesame_seeds
entries.description: Tiny flat seeds scattered over buns, [rice](#rice) balls, [noodles](#noodles), or dressings, drawn as pale or black specks. A [garnish](#garnish) rather than a dish in its own right.

entries.name: ham
entries.description: Cured or smoked [meat](#meat) from the leg of a [pig](#pig), shown as a whole joint or as thin slices. Covers the roast on a platter and the filling in a [sandwich](#sandwich) alike.

entries.name: pepperoni
entries.description: The spiced red [sausage](#sausage) cut into discs, best known as a [pizza](#pizza) topping though it is also stacked into sandwiches.

entries.name: sunflower_seed
entries.description: The striped teardrop-shaped seeds of a [sunflower](#sunflower), shown loose, in a [packet](#packet) or being eaten. They also turn up as [bird](#bird) or [hamster](#hamster) feed.

entries.name: herb
entries.description: Leaves, seeds or flowers of a [plant](#plant) kept for flavour, scent or [medicine](#medicine): sprigs on a [chopping](#chopping) board, in a mortar, or among a healer's stores.

entries.name: maple_syrup
entries.description: Thick amber [syrup](#syrup) boiled down from maple sap, usually shown [pouring](#pouring) over pancakes or waffles. Strongly tied to Canada, where the trees grow [cold](#cold) enough to run.

entries.name: flour
entries.description: Finely ground grain, white and powdery, in a [bag](#bag) or a [bowl](#bowl), dusting a work surface, or smudged over a baker's face and [apron](#apron). A baking-scene [staple](#staple).

entries.name: roe
entries.description: Fish eggs, whether loose orange [beads](#beads) or still held in the ovarian membrane. Served on [sushi](#sushi) and [rice](#rice) bowls, or shown at the fishmonger's.

entries.name: pork
entries.description: Meat cut from a [pig](#pig): chops, [belly](#belly) slices, [bacon](#bacon), [ham](#ham) and [sausage](#sausage). Shown raw on a board, sizzling on a [grill](#grill), or plated as part of a [meal](#meal).

entries.name: oyster
entries.description: A bivalve shellfish, drawn open on the half [shell](#shell) as [food](#food) or closed on the [shore](#shore). Sometimes shown with a pearl [sitting](#sitting) inside.

entries.name: batter
entries.description: The loose pourable mixture of [flour](#flour), [egg](#egg) and [liquid](#liquid) that becomes [cake](#cake) or pancakes. It is shown being [beaten](#beaten) in a [bowl](#bowl) or poured into a tin or pan.

entries.name: cracked_egg
entries.description: An [egg](#egg) [broken](#broken) open, its [shell](#shell) [split](#split) and the contents [spilling](#spilling) out or already [sitting](#sitting) in a [bowl](#bowl). Usually part of a [cooking](#cooking) scene.

entries.name: dough
entries.description: A soft elastic mass of [flour](#flour) and [liquid](#liquid), kneaded and [waiting](#waiting) to be shaped. Applies while it is still raw; once baked, [tag](#tag) the [bread](#bread), [pastry](#pastry) or [pizza](#pizza) it became.

entries.name: wasabi
entries.description: The pale green Japanese condiment served as a small mound beside [sushi](#sushi). Its heat hits the [nose](#nose) rather than the [tongue](#tongue), which is often the joke when somebody takes too much.

entries.name: yogurt
entries.description: Thick, tangy fermented [milk](#milk), served [plain](#plain) or stirred through with [fruit](#fruit), usually in a pot or [bowl](#bowl) with a [spoon](#spoon). Drinkable versions come in small bottles.

entries.name: umaibou
entries.description: A cheap cylindrical [corn](#corn) puff [snack](#snack) sold in Japan, wrapped in colourful packaging with its own [mascot](#mascot) character on the front.

entries.name: chopped_spring_onion
entries.description: Green [onion](#onion) [sliced](#sliced) into fine rings and scattered as a [garnish](#garnish) over [ramen](#ramen), [rice](#rice) bowls and other East Asian [dishes](#dishes). It reads as small green flecks across the surface of a [meal](#meal).

entries.name: swiss_cheese
entries.description: A pale, firm [cheese](#cheese) riddled with round holes. Illustrations often push its color toward a deep yellow or orange [well](#well) past the pale [shade](#shade) of the real thing.

entries.name: broken_egg
entries.description: An [egg](#egg) cracked open so that the yolk and white [spill](#spill) out. Half shells and a [spreading](#spreading) white in a pan or [bowl](#bowl) come with it.

entries.name: edamame
entries.description: Green soybeans steamed in the pod and salted, eaten by [squeezing](#squeezing) the [beans](#beans) straight into the mouth. A standard [snack](#snack) alongside drinks.

entries.name: konnyaku_(food)
entries.description: A firm grey block of jelly pressed from konjac starch, nearly tasteless and eaten as part of a dish rather than on its own. It turns up in simmered pots and, [forced](#forced) through a [mesh](#mesh), as thread-like shirataki [noodles](#noodles).

entries.name: soybean
entries.description: Small pale [beans](#beans) underpinning a huge share of East Asian [cooking](#cooking), turning up as [tofu](#tofu), miso, soy [sauce](#sauce), natto, and [edamame](#edamame). Buddhist vegetarian practice helped spread their use across the region.

entries.name: hot_sauce
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) of pungent chilli condiment, or the [sauce](#sauce) itself poured over [food](#food). It is generally there to say that something is painfully [spicy](#spicy).

entries.name: umeboshi
entries.description: Salt-pickled Japanese plums, wrinkled and deep red, intensely sour and salty. Most [familiar](#familiar) as the single red dot in the middle of a [rice](#rice) [ball](#ball) or [lunchbox](#lunchbox).

entries.name: cinnamon_stick
entries.description: A short [quill](#quill) of dried cinnamon bark curled in on itself, used to flavour [hot](#hot) drinks or set on a dish as a [garnish](#garnish). Often propped in a [mug](#mug) of mulled [wine](#wine) or cocoa.

entries.name: pepper_(spice)
entries.description: Dried peppercorns and the ground spice made from them, whole in a mill or shaken out of a pot. Black is the usual kind, though white, green and pink varieties exist.

entries.name: takuan
entries.description: Bright yellow pickled [daikon](#daikon) [radish](#radish), [sliced](#sliced) into thick discs and served alongside [rice](#rice), one of the most common Japanese pickles at a [meal](#meal).

entries.name: seafood
entries.description: Fish and shellfish prepared to eat, from a heaped platter of prawns and [crab](#crab) to a [market](#market) slab laid out on [ice](#ice).

entries.name: strawberry_syrup
entries.description: A thick red [sauce](#sauce) boiled down from strawberries, drizzled over [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream), pancakes and other desserts.

entries.name: sugar_(food)
entries.description: Granulated sugar, loose in a [bowl](#bowl), a [jar](#jar) or on a [spoon](#spoon), distinct from pressed cubes.

entries.name: onion_rings
entries.description: Rings cut from an [onion](#onion), coated in [batter](#batter) or [crumbs](#crumbs) and deep fried, usually heaped up as a side dish.

entries.name: sardine
entries.description: A small silvery schooling [fish](#fish). Drawn [swimming](#swimming) in a tight shoal, or laid out packed in oil in a flat tin.

entries.name: almond
entries.description: The pale teardrop-shaped nut, shown whole, [split](#split) or scattered over a [dessert](#dessert). It also turns up as an ingredient in [baking](#baking) and confectionery scenes.

entries.name: walnut
entries.description: The wrinkled edible kernel of the walnut [tree](#tree), shown shelled or still closed in its hard round [shell](#shell). Appears in [baking](#baking), [snack](#snack) bowls and [autumn](#autumn) arrangements.

entries.name: fukujinzuke
entries.description: A sweet Japanese [pickle](#pickle) of [daikon](#daikon), [lotus](#lotus) root, [cucumber](#cucumber) and other vegetables steeped in soy [sauce](#sauce) and dyed a bright red-brown. Served as a small heap beside a [plate](#plate) of [curry](#curry) [rice](#rice).

entries.name: sliced_meat
entries.description: Thin [cuts](#cuts) of cured or cooked [meat](#meat), the kind laid over [ramen](#ramen) or stacked in sandwiches. Deli-counter slices and chashu rounds both belong here.

entries.name: potato_wedges
entries.description: Thick chunks of [potato](#potato) cut lengthways and then fried or roasted, skin generally left on. Chunkier and softer inside than french fries, and often served with a dip.

entries.name: cheese_wheel
entries.description: A whole round of aged [cheese](#cheese) in the [drum](#drum) shape it matures in, rind and all. Sometimes a wedge has already been cut out of it.

entries.name: drink
entries.description: Any beverage present in the picture, [alcohol](#alcohol), [coffee](#coffee), [tea](#tea), [juice](#juice), [soda](#soda) and [milk](#milk) alike. Specific drinks have names of their own, so reach for those when you [can](#can) tell what it is.

entries.name: tea
entries.description: The brewed [drink](#drink) made from tea leaves, held in a [cup](#cup), pot or [glass](#glass), and by extension the [plant](#plant) or plantation it comes from. Pair it with the vessel [tag](#tag), such as [teacup](#teacup) or [teapot](#teapot).

entries.name: milk
entries.description: Cow's or other [animal](#animal) milk served as a [drink](#drink), in cartons, bottles, jugs or a [glass](#glass). Human breast milk from [lactation](#lactation) is tagged separately.

entries.name: coffee
entries.description: The [dark](#dark) brewed [drink](#drink) itself, visible in a [mug](#mug), a [cup](#cup) or a takeaway [carton](#carton). A ceramic cup on a [saucer](#saucer) counts as [teacup](#teacup) whatever is in it, and the thick handled sort takes [coffee_mug](#coffee_mug).

entries.name: bubble_tea
entries.description: Tea mixed with [milk](#milk) or [fruit](#fruit) flavouring and served over chewy tapioca pearls, [drunk](#drunk) through an extra-wide straw. It became a stock illustration prop after its popularity surged in Japan.

entries.name: juice
entries.description: A [drink](#drink) pressed from [fruit](#fruit) or vegetables, in a [glass](#glass), a [bottle](#bottle) or a [carton](#carton). Use [juice_box](#juice_box) when it is [drunk](#drunk) from a small carton through a straw.

entries.name: ramune
entries.description: A Japanese carbonated soft [drink](#drink) sold in a distinctive Codd-neck [bottle](#bottle) sealed by a [glass](#glass) marble, a [staple](#staple) of [summer](#summer) festivals. The original flavor is lemon-lime, though many others exist.

entries.name: soda
entries.description: A flavored carbonated soft [drink](#drink), shown in a [bottle](#bottle), [can](#can), or [glass](#glass). The specific containers are [soda_bottle](#soda_bottle) and [soda_can](#soda_can).

entries.name: energy_drink
entries.description: A canned or bottled stimulant [drink](#drink) [heavy](#heavy) on caffeine and sugar. Coffee and [tea](#tea), caffeinated by [nature](#nature), are not included. A stock prop in gaming and all-nighter scenes.

entries.name: ice_cream_float
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass) of fizzy [drink](#drink) with scoops dropped in, foaming where the two meet. Vanilla on green [melon](#melon) [soda](#soda) and the root [beer](#beer) version are the ones drawn most.

entries.name: green_tea
entries.description: Green [tea](#tea) served as a [drink](#drink), frequently in a [yunomi](#yunomi), the handleless Japanese [teacup](#teacup). The powder it is brewed from is [matcha_(food)](#matcha_(food)).

entries.name: cola
entries.description: The brown fizzy soft [drink](#drink), in a [bottle](#bottle), a [can](#can) or a [glass](#glass) over [ice](#ice), shown without naming a maker. Named products carry their own brand tags.

entries.name: canned_coffee
entries.description: Brewed [coffee](#coffee) sold ready to [drink](#drink) in a slim steel or aluminium [can](#can), a [staple](#staple) of Japanese vending machines. Bought warm in [winter](#winter) and chilled in [summer](#summer).

entries.name: orange_juice
entries.description: Juice pressed from oranges, poured into a [glass](#glass) or still in its [carton](#carton) or [bottle](#bottle). Turns up at [breakfast](#breakfast) tables, picnics and [summer](#summer) scenes.

entries.name: melon_soda
entries.description: A vividly green, melon-flavored [soda](#soda) popular in Japan, served fizzing in a [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass). Often crowned with a scoop of vanilla [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) to make a float.

entries.name: milkshake
entries.description: A thick, [cold](#cold) [drink](#drink) made by [blending](#blending) [milk](#milk) and [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) together, served in a [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass) with a straw and often a [swirl](#swirl) of cream on top.

entries.name: hot_chocolate
entries.description: A warm cocoa [drink](#drink) served in a [mug](#mug), often topped with marshmallows or [cream](#cream). Winter and Christmas scenes are its home.

entries.name: black_tea
entries.description: Fully oxidised [tea](#tea), amber to deep red once brewed and usually poured western-style with [cup](#cup) and [saucer](#saucer). Japanese names it red tea, so a reddish brew in a [teacup](#teacup) often belongs here rather than with green tea.

entries.name: lemonade
entries.description: A cool [drink](#drink) of pressed [lemon](#lemon) [juice](#juice) with sugar, generally served in a [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass) over [ice](#ice). A fixture of [summer](#summer), [beach](#beach) and [festival](#festival) scenes.

entries.name: teabag
entries.description: A small porous [pouch](#pouch) of [tea](#tea) leaves with a [string](#string) and [paper](#paper) tab, steeping in a [cup](#cup) or [dangling](#dangling) from a hand. Usually drawn next to a [mug](#mug) with a curl of [steam](#steam).

entries.name: latte_art
entries.description: A pattern poured into the [foam](#foam) on a [coffee](#coffee), from a simple [heart](#heart) or [leaf](#leaf) to a detailed [portrait](#portrait). The [cup](#cup) is usually shown from straight above so the design reads.

entries.name: spilled_milk
entries.description: Milk tipped out of its [glass](#glass), [carton](#carton), or [bottle](#bottle) and [spreading](#spreading) across a surface, usually a small mishap in an everyday scene.

entries.name: strawberry_milk
entries.description: Milk flavoured with [strawberry](#strawberry), pink in the [glass](#glass), [bottle](#bottle) or [carton](#carton). Often [drunk](#drunk) through a straw.

entries.name: iced_coffee
entries.description: Coffee served [cold](#cold) over cubes, usually in a [tall](#tall) clear [glass](#glass) so the [ice](#ice) and any curl of [milk](#milk) show through. It is a fixture of hot-weather scenes.

entries.name: iced_tea
entries.description: Brewed [tea](#tea) chilled and poured over [ice](#ice), [drunk](#drunk) [cold](#cold). It arrives in a [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass), often with a [lemon](#lemon) slice or a straw, in [summer](#summer) settings.

entries.name: apple_juice
entries.description: Pale golden [juice](#juice) pressed from apples, poured into a [glass](#glass) or served in a [carton](#carton) or [bottle](#bottle). Cafe and lunch scenes usually give it a straw.

entries.name: smoothie
entries.description: A thick blended [drink](#drink) of [fruit](#fruit) or vegetables with [milk](#milk), yoghurt or [ice](#ice), usually served in a [tall](#tall) [glass](#glass) with a straw. Its opaque, creamy colour distinguishes it from [juice](#juice).

entries.name: hot_drink
entries.description: Any [hot](#hot) beverage, given away by the [steam](#steam) rising off the [cup](#cup). Use it where the [drink](#drink) cannot be identified as [tea](#tea), [coffee](#coffee) or anything more specific.

entries.name: milk_tea
entries.description: Tea served with [milk](#milk) stirred through it, ranging from British-style brews to sweetened Asian versions and [bubble](#bubble) [tea](#tea). Often served in a sealed plastic [cup](#cup) with a wide straw.

entries.name: chocolate_milk
entries.description: Milk flavoured with cocoa, served in a [glass](#glass), [carton](#carton) or [bottle](#bottle) and known by its light brown colour. It covers the [drink](#drink) itself, not [chocolate](#chocolate) spilled over somebody.

entries.name: amazake_(drink)
entries.description: A cloudy white Japanese [drink](#drink) brewed from fermented [rice](#rice), sweet and with little or [no](#no) [alcohol](#alcohol) in it. It is served warm in a [cup](#cup) at New Year and at [shrine](#shrine) festivals.

entries.name: tomato_juice
entries.description: Thick red [juice](#juice) pressed from tomatoes, poured into a [glass](#glass) or [drunk](#drunk) from a [carton](#carton). Occasionally used for a [gag](#gag) where it reads as [blood](#blood).

entries.name: alcohol
entries.description: Any [drink](#drink) containing alcohol, from [beer](#beer) and [wine](#wine) to [sake](#sake), spirits and cocktails, whether in a [bottle](#bottle), [glass](#glass) or [cup](#cup). Add [drinking](#drinking) or [drunk](#drunk) for the act and its effect. Note that the Japanese word read as sake covers every such drink, not only the [rice](#rice) wine.

entries.name: beer
entries.description: The hopped, brewed [drink](#drink) itself, served in a [mug](#mug), [glass](#glass), [bottle](#bottle) or [can](#can) with its head of [foam](#foam). Add the vessel, such as [beer_mug](#beer_mug) or [beer_can](#beer_can), and [drinking](#drinking) or [drunk](#drunk) where they apply.

entries.name: wine
entries.description: Fermented grape [drink](#drink), shown in a [glass](#glass), a [bottle](#bottle), or mid-pour. Tag [alcohol](#alcohol) alongside it, and add [wine_glass](#wine_glass) or [wine_bottle](#wine_bottle) for whichever vessel appears.

entries.name: sake
entries.description: Japanese [rice](#rice) [wine](#wine), poured from a [tokkuri](#tokkuri) or [bottle](#bottle) into a small [cup](#cup). Tagged with [alcohol](#alcohol); the Japanese word [can](#can) also [cover](#cover) alcohol in general, so translated tags need care.
