entries.name: champagne
entries.description: Sparkling [wine](#wine), in the [glass](#glass) or the [bottle](#bottle), at toasts, parties and celebrations. It is often shown mid-pour or with the [cork](#cork) just gone.

entries.name: tropical_drink
entries.description: A [cocktail](#cocktail) or [fruit](#fruit) [drink](#drink) served in a [glass](#glass) dressed up with [sliced](#sliced) fruit, flowers or a [paper](#paper) [umbrella](#umbrella). A [beach](#beach) or [poolside](#poolside) setting usually accompanies it.

entries.name: cocktail
entries.description: A mixed alcoholic [drink](#drink), often brightly coloured and finished with [fruit](#fruit), a [cherry](#cherry) or a [paper](#paper) [parasol](#parasol). The stemmed cone-shaped [glass](#glass) has its own [tag](#tag), [cocktail_glass](#cocktail_glass).

entries.name: red_wine
entries.description: Red [wine](#wine) in a [glass](#glass), [bottle](#bottle) or decanter, the dark-grape variety. Usually paired with [wine_glass](#wine_glass) or bottle and often with [alcohol](#alcohol).

entries.name: whiskey
entries.description: A distilled grain [spirit](#spirit), shown as a [bottle](#bottle) or a small measure in a tumbler, often over [ice](#ice). Covers bourbon, Scotch and similar styles.

entries.name: vodka
entries.description: A clear distilled [spirit](#spirit), usually shown in a labelled [bottle](#bottle) or a small shot [glass](#glass). Often works as shorthand for Eastern European or Nordic characters and for [heavy](#heavy) [drinking](#drinking).

entries.name: alcohol_carton
entries.description: Sake, [wine](#wine) or another [drink](#drink) sold in a [paper](#paper) [carton](#carton) or [box](#box) instead of a [bottle](#bottle). Cheap and everyday, so it belongs to [casual](#casual) or shabby [drinking](#drinking) scenes.

entries.name: liquor
entries.description: Distilled spirits such as whisky, [vodka](#vodka) or shochu, in the [bottle](#bottle) or poured into a [glass](#glass). Separate from fermented drinks like [beer](#beer) and [wine](#wine).

entries.name: blue_hawaii
entries.description: A bright blue [tropical](#tropical) [cocktail](#cocktail) of rum, [pineapple](#pineapple) [juice](#juice) and blue curacao, poured [tall](#tall) and dressed with [fruit](#fruit) and a [paper](#paper) [umbrella](#umbrella). An alcohol-free version is a popular [dessert](#dessert) [drink](#drink) in Japanese [family](#family) restaurants.

entries.name: martini
entries.description: A [cocktail](#cocktail) of gin or [vodka](#vodka) with a splash of vermouth, served in the wide conical stemmed [glass](#glass) that took its name. Garnished with an [olive](#olive) or a twist of peel.

entries.name: froth
entries.description: A head of [foam](#foam) [sitting](#sitting) on top of a [drink](#drink), most often a [mug](#mug) of [beer](#beer). Whipped or shaken liquids and [coffee](#coffee) [can](#can) carry it too.

entries.name: cup
entries.description: Any vessel [drunk](#drunk) from: a [mug](#mug), a tumbler, a [teacup](#teacup), a [sake](#sake) cup, a disposable [coffee](#coffee) cup. Add the narrower [tag](#tag) such as teacup, mug or [shot_glass](#shot_glass) where one fits.

entries.name: bottle
entries.description: A narrow-necked [container](#container) for [liquid](#liquid) in [glass](#glass) or plastic: [water](#water), [wine](#wine), [sake](#sake), [beer](#beer), perfume or a [potion](#potion). Add [holding_bottle](#holding_bottle) when it is carried, and the specific kind where it is clear.

entries.name: drinking_glass
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) vessel meant for [cold](#cold) drinks, from a [plain](#plain) tumbler to a [tall](#tall) highball. A stemmed one may want [wine_glass](#wine_glass) as [well](#well).

entries.name: glass_(cup)
entries.description: A clear [drinking](#drinking) vessel without a [handle](#handle), from a [plain](#plain) tumbler to a [tall](#tall) highball. Stemmed ones belong with [wine_glass](#wine_glass) and handled ones with [mug](#mug).

entries.name: teacup
entries.description: A small handled [cup](#cup) for [tea](#tea) or another [hot](#hot) [drink](#drink), usually shown with a [saucer](#saucer) or as part of a full [tea_set](#tea_set). Handleless Japanese [yunomi](#yunomi) and bowl-shaped chawan fall under this [tag](#tag) too.

entries.name: drinking_straw
entries.description: A thin [tube](#tube) for drawing a [drink](#drink) up to the mouth, [standing](#standing) in a [glass](#glass), [carton](#carton) or [cup](#cup). When it sits between somebody's [lips](#lips), add [drinking_straw_in_mouth](#drinking_straw_in_mouth).

entries.name: mug
entries.description: A sturdy cylindrical [drinking](#drinking) vessel with a [handle](#handle), made for [coffee](#coffee), cocoa or [tea](#tea). Heavier and larger than a [cup](#cup) [sitting](#sitting) on a [saucer](#saucer).

entries.name: can
entries.description: A cylindrical metal [container](#container) for drinks such as [soda](#soda), [beer](#beer) or [coffee](#coffee), or for preserved [food](#food). Shown held, [drunk](#drunk) from, stacked on a [shelf](#shelf) or dropped as litter.

entries.name: chopsticks
entries.description: A pair of [eating](#eating) sticks, [lying](#lying) on the [table](#table), gripped between the fingers or pushed through the hair as an ornament. What is being done with them takes [holding_chopsticks](#holding_chopsticks), [holding_with_chopsticks](#holding_with_chopsticks) or [chopsticks_in_mouth](#chopsticks_in_mouth).

entries.name: disposable_cup
entries.description: A single-use [paper](#paper) or plastic [cup](#cup), the [soda](#soda) or [party](#party) sort. The lidded takeaway kind is [disposable_coffee_cup](#disposable_coffee_cup).

entries.name: wine_glass
entries.description: A stemmed [glass](#glass) with a rounded [bowl](#bowl), made for [drinking](#drinking) [wine](#wine). A metal equivalent is a [chalice](#chalice), and a [tall](#tall) narrow bowl belongs to a [champagne](#champagne) [flute](#flute) instead; [tag](#tag) [drinking_glass](#drinking_glass) alongside it.

entries.name: teapot
entries.description: A lidded pot with a spout and a [handle](#handle) for steeping and [pouring](#pouring) [tea](#tea), often part of a full [tea_set](#tea_set). It reads rounder and squatter than a [coffee](#coffee) pot, which carries its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: water_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) for [carrying](#carrying) [water](#water) or another [drink](#drink), from a disposable plastic one to a reusable sports [flask](#flask). Common in exercise and outdoor scenes.

entries.name: drink_can
entries.description: A metal [can](#can) [holding](#holding) a fixed portion of beverage, whether [soda](#soda), [beer](#beer), an [energy](#energy) [drink](#drink), [juice](#juice) or [tea](#tea).

entries.name: saucer
entries.description: The small [plate](#plate) placed under a [cup](#cup), usually a [teacup](#teacup), to catch drips and protect the [table](#table). Commonly drawn as part of a [tea](#tea) set when tea is being served.

entries.name: sakazuki
entries.description: A flat, shallow saucer-like [cup](#cup) for [drinking](#drinking) [sake](#sake), held in the fingers. Tagged with cup and usually sake.

entries.name: beer_mug
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [heavy](#heavy) [mug](#mug) of [glass](#glass) or metal filled with [beer](#beer), frequently raised in a [toast](#toast). Add beer alongside it.

entries.name: coffee_mug
entries.description: A thick ceramic or [glass](#glass) [mug](#mug) with a [handle](#handle), built [heavy](#heavy) enough to hold while what is in it is [hot](#hot). Add [coffee](#coffee) when the [liquid](#liquid) itself [can](#can) be seen.

entries.name: wine_bottle
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), narrow-necked [glass](#glass) [bottle](#bottle) [holding](#holding) [wine](#wine), often still corked. Tag bottle alongside it; the [drink](#drink) itself is wine.

entries.name: drink_carton
entries.description: A waxed [paper](#paper) [carton](#carton) of [milk](#milk), [juice](#juice) or [tea](#tea), usually with a straw [punched](#punched) through the top. The standard [lunchbox](#lunchbox) and convenience-store [drink](#drink).

entries.name: beer_can
entries.description: An aluminium [can](#can) of [beer](#beer), unopened, cracked open or [crushed](#crushed) flat. It belongs to relaxed [drinking](#drinking) at home.

entries.name: soda_can
entries.description: An aluminum [can](#can) of [soda](#soda) or, in some cases, an [energy](#energy) [drink](#drink), held or set down on a surface. A specific kind of [drink_can](#drink_can).

entries.name: sake_bottle
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) [bottle](#bottle) of [sake](#sake), taller-necked than a [wine](#wine) bottle. The ceramic [serving](#serving) [flask](#flask) is [tokkuri](#tokkuri) instead.

entries.name: ice_cube
entries.description: Small blocks of [frozen](#frozen) [water](#water), clinking in a [glass](#glass), [sitting](#sitting) in a [tray](#tray) or heaped in a pail. They also appear pressed against skin to cool somebody down.

entries.name: disposable_coffee_cup
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) takeaway [cup](#cup) closed by a snap-on [lid](#lid), with a [cardboard](#cardboard) sleeve around it against the heat. A ceramic [coffee_mug](#coffee_mug) or a saucered [teacup](#teacup) are separate tags.

entries.name: yunomi
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), handleless Japanese [cup](#cup) used for everyday [tea](#tea) [drinking](#drinking), straighter and narrower than the wide, bowl-shaped chawan. Tag cup alongside it.

entries.name: milk_bottle
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) or plastic [bottle](#bottle) of [milk](#milk), the traditional doorstep-delivery kind.

entries.name: cocktail_glass
entries.description: The stemmed [glass](#glass) with a wide conical [bowl](#bowl) that a [martini](#martini) is served in. Judge by that shape alone, since a [cocktail](#cocktail) poured into any other glass does not qualify.

entries.name: champagne_flute
entries.description: A stemmed [glass](#glass) with a [tall](#tall) narrow [bowl](#bowl), made for sparkling [wine](#wine) so the hand does not warm it. A stemmed glass whose bowl is wide and round is a [wine_glass](#wine_glass).

entries.name: tokkuri
entries.description: A narrow-necked ceramic [flask](#flask) for [pouring](#pouring) [sake](#sake), usually served warm alongside small cups. Add sake and choko or [cup](#cup).

entries.name: milk_carton
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [carton](#carton) with a gabled, triangular top, the kind [school](#school) lunches often serve [plain](#plain), [chocolate](#chocolate) or [strawberry](#strawberry) [milk](#milk) in.

entries.name: juice_box
entries.description: A small rectangular [carton](#carton) of [drink](#drink), sipped through a straw pushed into the top. It often marks a [child](#child) character or a [casual](#casual) break.

entries.name: choko_(cup)
entries.description: A small cylindrical ceramic [cup](#cup) for [drinking](#drinking) [sake](#sake), held in the fingers or set beside a [flask](#flask). The shallow dish-shaped sake cup is a [sakazuki](#sakazuki).

entries.name: kettle
entries.description: A metal pot with a [lid](#lid), a spout and a [handle](#handle) over the top, used to boil [water](#water) on a [stove](#stove) or over a [fire](#fire). A wide open [cooking](#cooking) pot hung above flames is a [cauldron](#cauldron).

entries.name: bendy_straw
entries.description: A straw for [drinking](#drinking) with a concertina hinge near the top, so it [can](#can) be angled. Add drinking or the [drink](#drink) itself as they apply.

entries.name: soda_bottle
entries.description: A narrow-necked [glass](#glass) or plastic [bottle](#bottle) of [soda](#soda) in the classic [cola](#cola) shape, held or [standing](#standing) on a [table](#table). The same [drink](#drink) in a [can](#can) is [soda_can](#soda_can).

entries.name: chalice
entries.description: A metal [drinking](#drinking) [cup](#cup) with a footed stem and a rounded [bowl](#bowl), the [outline](#outline) of a [wine](#wine) [glass](#glass) rendered in [gold](#gold), silver or brass. Ceremonial grails fall under it too.

entries.name: glass_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) made of [glass](#glass), whether it holds a [drink](#drink), a [potion](#potion) or nothing at all.

entries.name: thermos
entries.description: An insulated [flask](#flask) that keeps drinks [hot](#hot) or [cold](#cold), carried on trips or set beside a [bento](#bento). Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [laboratory](#laboratory) vacuum flask.

entries.name: sugar_cube
entries.description: A small pressed block of sugar for sweetening [tea](#tea) or [coffee](#coffee), shown on a [saucer](#saucer), in a [bowl](#bowl) or lifted with [tongs](#tongs).

entries.name: plastic_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) made of clear or coloured plastic, usually [holding](#holding) [water](#water) or a soft [drink](#drink). A bottle made of [glass](#glass) takes the [plain](#plain) bottle [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: baby_bottle
entries.description: A [feeding](#feeding) [bottle](#bottle) fitted with a rubber teat, used to give [milk](#milk) to an infant. It may be gripped by the [baby](#baby), offered by an adult, or serve as a prop in babysitting and age-play scenes.

entries.name: beer_bottle
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) [bottle](#bottle) of [beer](#beer), capped or open, held in the hand or [standing](#standing) on a [table](#table). Add beer for the [drink](#drink) itself.

entries.name: tea_set
entries.description: A matched service for [tea](#tea): a [teapot](#teapot), cups on saucers and typically a [tray](#tray), sometimes joined by a sugar [bowl](#bowl), creamer or tiered stand. Tag the individual pieces, such as teapot and [teacup](#teacup), alongside it.

entries.name: crazy_straw
entries.description: A [drinking](#drinking) straw bent into loops and spirals along its length while still [working](#working) as a straw. Novelty glassware and children's drinks are the usual setting.

entries.name: coffee_pot
entries.description: A vessel for [serving](#serving) [coffee](#coffee): either the [glass](#glass) carafe that stands under a brewer, or a [tall](#tall) slim metal or ceramic pot with a long spout. Shown [pouring](#pouring), or [waiting](#waiting) on the warmer.

entries.name: masu
entries.description: A [square](#square) wooden [cup](#cup), once a measure for [rice](#rice) and now used for [drinking](#drinking) [sake](#sake) and for [holding](#holding) [beans](#beans) at Setsubun. Its [box](#box) shape and visible [corner](#corner) [joints](#joints) identify it.

entries.name: cork
entries.description: A tapered stopper pushed into the [neck](#neck) of a [bottle](#bottle) or [jar](#jar). Often drawn in mid-air just after a bottle has been opened.

entries.name: canteen
entries.description: A small [flask](#flask) for [carrying](#carrying) [drinking](#drinking) [water](#water), slung from a [strap](#strap) or clipped to a [belt](#belt). Standard kit for soldiers, hikers and campers.

entries.name: pitcher_(container)
entries.description: A wide-mouthed handled vessel for [pouring](#pouring) [water](#water), [juice](#juice) or [beer](#beer) at the [table](#table). Distinct from a narrow-necked jug bought full from a [shop](#shop), and unrelated to the [baseball](#baseball) sense of the word.

entries.name: print_mug
entries.description: A [mug](#mug) with a picture, pattern or slogan printed around its side. Held while [drinking](#drinking) or parked on a [desk](#desk).

entries.name: jug_(bottle)
entries.description: A big [bottle](#bottle) with a narrow [neck](#neck) and a moulded [handle](#handle), the sort [milk](#milk) or cider is sold in, tipped to fill a smaller [glass](#glass). A pitcher is a different thing: open-mouthed [serving](#serving) ware rather than a [container](#container) bought full.

entries.name: fruit_cup
entries.description: A hollowed-out [coconut](#coconut), [pineapple](#pineapple), [watermelon](#watermelon) or similar [fruit](#fruit) pressed into use as a [cup](#cup) or [bowl](#bowl). A [drinking](#drinking) straw sticking out of it is the usual giveaway.

entries.name: champagne_bottle
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy) [dark](#dark) [bottle](#bottle) sparkling [wine](#wine) comes in, capped with a wired [cork](#cork) under foil. Celebration scenes show one erupting in [foam](#foam).

entries.name: heart_straw
entries.description: A [drinking](#drinking) straw bent into a [heart](#heart) along its length, or a joined pair whose twist makes one between two [people](#people) [sharing](#sharing) a single [glass](#glass).

entries.name: cocktail_shaker
entries.description: The metal tumbler a [bartender](#bartender) loads with [ice](#ice) and spirits and shakes to chill and mix a [drink](#drink). Shown mid-shake, or [standing](#standing) beside the finished [glasses](#glasses).

entries.name: shot_glass
entries.description: A very small, thick-walled [glass](#glass) [holding](#holding) a single measure of spirits, much shorter than an ordinary tumbler and often shown lined up in rows on a bar or [table](#table). Implies [drinking_glass](#drinking_glass).

entries.name: cocktail_umbrella
entries.description: A tiny [paper](#paper) [parasol](#parasol) on a wooden [stick](#stick), [planted](#planted) in a [glass](#glass) as decoration. It turns almost any [drink](#drink) into a holiday or [beach](#beach) one.

entries.name: tankard
entries.description: A large handled [drinking](#drinking) [mug](#mug), often staved like a [miniature](#miniature) [barrel](#barrel) and sometimes fitted with a hinged [lid](#lid), though metal and ceramic versions exist too. A common prop in taverns and pseudo-medieval [fantasy](#fantasy) settings.

entries.name: creamer_(vessel)
entries.description: A small jug for [milk](#milk) or [cream](#cream), poured out into [tea](#tea) or [coffee](#coffee). Usually [porcelain](#porcelain) and part of a matching service.

entries.name: bottle_cap
entries.description: The cap sealing a bottle's mouth, crimped metal over a liner for [glass](#glass) or a threaded plastic [screw](#screw) top. Most carry a brand mark, and one is often drawn [lying](#lying) loose beside the [bottle](#bottle) it came off.

entries.name: coconut_cup
entries.description: Half a [coconut](#coconut) [shell](#shell) pressed into service as a [drinking](#drinking) vessel, usually with a straw and a [paper](#paper) [parasol](#parasol) [standing](#standing) out of it. A fixture of [beach](#beach) and [island](#island) scenes.

entries.name: teaspoon
entries.description: A small [spoon](#spoon) for [stirring](#stirring) a [cup](#cup) or [measuring](#measuring) sugar, [resting](#resting) on a [saucer](#saucer) or [standing](#standing) in a [drink](#drink). It appears wherever [tea](#tea) or [coffee](#coffee) is being served.

entries.name: corked_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) still sealed with its stopper in place, nothing poured from it yet. Covers [wine](#wine), potions and messages set adrift alike.

entries.name: hurricane_glass
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), vase-shaped [drinking](#drinking) [glass](#glass) on a short stem. Cocktails and elaborate iced drinks are served in it.

entries.name: glass_teapot
entries.description: A see-through pot for brewing [tea](#tea), with the leaves or an [opening](#opening) [flower](#flower) visible inside. Turns up in tea-ceremony and [cafe](#cafe) pictures.

entries.name: broken_cup
entries.description: A [cup](#cup) or [mug](#mug) cracked or smashed. It may lie in pieces on the [floor](#floor) or still stand upright with a chip out of the rim.

entries.name: sugar_bowl
entries.description: A small lidded [bowl](#bowl) for granulated sugar or cubes, usually part of a [tea](#tea) set. The [lid](#lid) often has a notch cut so the [spoon](#spoon) [can](#can) rest inside while it is closed.

entries.name: chopstick_rest
entries.description: A small ceramic or wooden stand that keeps the tips of [chopsticks](#chopsticks) off the [table](#table) between bites. A quiet [marker](#marker) of a properly laid Japanese place setting.

entries.name: coaster
entries.description: A small flat [mat](#mat) of [cork](#cork), [card](#card) or plastic that a [glass](#glass) or [cup](#cup) stands on to keep rings off the [table](#table). A minor prop in bar, [cafe](#cafe) and living-room scenes.

entries.name: wooden_cup
entries.description: A [cup](#cup) turned or carved from wood, thick-walled and usually left unglazed. It suits rustic, [fantasy](#fantasy), and [camping](#camping) scenes alike.

entries.name: hip_flask
entries.description: A slim flattened metal [bottle](#bottle) for spirits, shaped to lie against the body and carried in a [pocket](#pocket). It is usually shown being unscrewed or tipped [back](#back).

entries.name: crushed_can
entries.description: A [drink](#drink) [can](#can) dented or flattened, stamped underfoot or squeezed shut in a fist. Turns up as litter and as quick shorthand for temper.

entries.name: chinese_spoon
entries.description: The deep, flat-bowled [soup](#soup) [spoon](#spoon) of East Asian tableware, its short thick [handle](#handle) [running](#running) straight out of the [bowl](#bowl). Usually shown [resting](#resting) in a bowl of [ramen](#ramen) or held while [eating](#eating).

entries.name: glass_teacup
entries.description: A [cup](#cup) of clear [glass](#glass) for [tea](#tea), letting the colour of the brew show through. Often paired with a matching [transparent](#transparent) pot.

entries.name: cup_on_head
entries.description: A [cup](#cup) or [drinking](#drinking) [glass](#glass) balanced on top of a character's head. Generally played for laughs or shown off as a [party](#party) trick.

entries.name: skull_cup
entries.description: A [drinking](#drinking) vessel shaped as a cranium, or an actual [skull](#skull) used as one. Turns up with pirates, demons and villains raising a [toast](#toast).

entries.name: chair
entries.description: A raised seat [standing](#standing) on [legs](#legs), covering everything from a dining chair to an [office](#office) chair or a [throne](#throne). Benches, stools and couches take their own tags.

entries.name: table
entries.description: A piece of furniture with a flat, raised surface for [eating](#eating), [working](#working) or setting things on. Pairs naturally with pose tags like [hand_on_table](#hand_on_table) or [sitting_on_table](#sitting_on_table).

entries.name: couch
entries.description: An upholstered seat built for several [people](#people), including two-seat loveseats, sectionals and chaise longues. When a large [armchair](#armchair) and a small couch are hard to tell apart, this is the default.

entries.name: desk
entries.description: A piece of furniture with a flat [writing](#writing) or [working](#working) surface, usually over drawers or compartments. Belongs to offices, classrooms and studies.

entries.name: school_desk
entries.description: The small individual [desk](#desk) found in a [classroom](#classroom), typically a wooden top on tubular metal [legs](#legs) with a [shelf](#shelf) underneath.

entries.name: bench
entries.description: A long seat meant for several [people](#people) at once, a continuous [plank](#plank) or divided into places, with or without a [back](#back). It is made for public and outdoor use; an indoor seat of that length is more likely a [couch](#couch).

entries.name: stool
entries.description: A simple seat with [no](#no) [back](#back) or armrests, from a bar stool to a wooden step stool.

entries.name: swivel_chair
entries.description: A rotating [chair](#chair) mounted on wheeled casters, such as an [office](#office) chair or a gaming chair.

entries.name: school_chair
entries.description: The [plain](#plain) [classroom](#classroom) [chair](#chair) a student sits on, usually a wooden seat on a metal frame. Often drawn beside a [school_desk](#school_desk).

entries.name: kotatsu
entries.description: A low [table](#table) with a [heater](#heater) slung beneath it and a [quilt](#quilt) [trapped](#trapped) between frame and tabletop, so [everyone](#everyone) [sitting](#sitting) round [can](#can) tuck their [legs](#legs) into the warmth. A [winter](#winter) fixture, often with a [bowl](#bowl) of mandarins on top.

entries.name: throne
entries.description: An [ornate](#ornate), often cushioned seat reserved for a [ruler](#ruler) or someone of high [standing](#standing). Add [sitting](#sitting) or the [throne_room](#throne_room) setting where relevant.

entries.name: armchair
entries.description: A padded [chair](#chair) with a support on each side for the arms, generally upholstered. Comfortable seating for a [lounging](#lounging) or [reading](#reading) pose.

entries.name: office_chair
entries.description: The wheeled swivelling [chair](#chair) used at a [desk](#desk), generally with a padded [back](#back), armrests and an adjustable [column](#column). A racing-seat [gaming_chair](#gaming_chair) has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: counter
entries.description: The long [table](#table) of a [shop](#shop), bar or [cafe](#cafe) across which goods are sold, drinks are served or payment is handed over. Only this piece of furniture; a numerical [tally](#tally) and the [fighting](#fighting) move are other tags.

entries.name: wooden_table
entries.description: A [table](#table) built from wood, whether a rustic [tavern](#tavern) table or a polished dining one. Tag table alongside it.

entries.name: beach_chair
entries.description: Outdoor seating at the [beach](#beach) or [pool](#pool), and an ambiguous [label](#label). One whose seat and [back](#back) are a single sheet of [fabric](#fabric) is a [deck_chair](#deck_chair), and one that folds down flat like a [bed](#bed) is a [lounge_chair](#lounge_chair).

entries.name: lounge_chair
entries.description: A [reclining](#reclining) outdoor [chair](#chair) for [sunbathing](#sunbathing), found beside pools and on beaches and often set under a [parasol](#parasol). A folding deck chair with a [fabric](#fabric) sling is a different item, its [back](#back) longer than its seat.

entries.name: bar_stool
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) seat made for raised counters, usually with a [ring](#ring) near the base to rest the [feet](#feet) on and sometimes a small [back](#back). Bars and [kitchen](#kitchen) counters are where it stands.

entries.name: folding_chair
entries.description: A light portable [chair](#chair) that collapses flat for [stacking](#stacking) or storage. It is also the classic improvised [weapon](#weapon) of professional [wrestling](#wrestling).

entries.name: wooden_chair
entries.description: A [chair](#chair) made of wood, from a [plain](#plain) [kitchen](#kitchen) seat to an ornately carved one. Add chair and [sitting](#sitting) when someone occupies it.

entries.name: under_kotatsu
entries.description: A character sits or lies with [legs](#legs) beneath the [quilt](#quilt) of a heated [kotatsu](#kotatsu) [table](#table), sometimes with the whole view taken from underneath it. Implies kotatsu and [under_table](#under_table).

entries.name: gaming_chair
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) swivel [chair](#chair) shaped like a [racing](#racing) seat, with a headrest and a high winged [back](#back). Close to an [office](#office) chair but with a look all of its own.

entries.name: bean_bag_chair
entries.description: A large [fabric](#fabric) [sack](#sack) of [foam](#foam) pellets that slumps into whatever shape the person on it takes, so it [can](#can) be sat in or sprawled across. The small [tossing](#tossing) [bag](#bag) used in games is bean_bag.

entries.name: bath_stool
entries.description: The low [stool](#stool), these days almost always plastic, that Japanese bathrooms keep for [sitting](#sitting) on while [washing](#washing) before getting into the tub. A [basin](#basin) and a shower head are usually beside it.

entries.name: booth_seating
entries.description: Fixed padded benches facing each other across a [table](#table), the seating of diners and [family](#family) restaurants. A row of them puts guests [back](#back) to back; telephone booths and [market](#market) stalls share the word but not the meaning.

entries.name: round_table
entries.description: A [table](#table) with a circular top, so [everyone](#everyone) seated faces the middle. Common in cafes, dining rooms and council scenes.

entries.name: poker_table
entries.description: The baize-topped [table](#table) built for [card](#card) play, with a padded rail and chip trays set into the edge. Usually shown mid-game with cards dealt and chips heaped up.

entries.name: wooden_bench
entries.description: A [bench](#bench) made from wooden slats, or a [plank](#plank) set on [legs](#legs), with or without a [back](#back). Parks, stations, and changing rooms are full of them.

entries.name: glass_table
entries.description: A [table](#table) topped with a sheet of [glass](#glass) over a metal or wooden frame, so whatever sits beneath shows through. Frequent in modern living rooms and cafes.

entries.name: nightstand
entries.description: The small [table](#table) or low [cabinet](#cabinet) [standing](#standing) beside a [bed](#bed). A [lamp](#lamp), an alarm [clock](#clock) or a [glass](#glass) of [water](#water) is usually [sitting](#sitting) on top of it.

entries.name: pool_table
entries.description: The cloth-topped [table](#table) for [billiards](#billiards) or snooker, ringed by cushioned rails with pockets at the corners and sides. Usually shown mid-game, balls racked or scattered.

entries.name: coffee_table
entries.description: A low [table](#table) set in front of a sofa, [carrying](#carrying) cups, magazines or a remote. A standard fitting of living-room scenes.

entries.name: piano_bench
entries.description: The low seat that belongs with a [piano](#piano), wooden and sometimes padded, occasionally short enough to read as a [stool](#stool). Usually shown with a player at the keyboard, sometimes [standing](#standing) empty beside it.

entries.name: casino_card_table
entries.description: The gaming [table](#table) of a [gambling](#gambling) hall: green felt inside a raised rim, printed with betting areas for cards and chips. Blackjack and baccarat are played across it.

entries.name: gynecology_chair
entries.description: An examination [chair](#chair) fitted with raised stirrups that hold the [legs](#legs) apart, found in clinics. Shows up in medical scenes and in art that borrows the setting.

entries.name: car_seat
entries.description: A seat inside a [car](#car), occupied or shown as bare upholstery. The separate padded seat strapped in for a small [child](#child) is not this.

entries.name: easy_chair
entries.description: A big upholstered [chair](#chair) built for [lounging](#lounging) in, generally with arms. Where a wide one is hard to tell from a small sofa, call it a [couch](#couch).

entries.name: chaise_longue
entries.description: An upholstered seat drawn out long enough to take the sitter's [legs](#legs) as [well](#well), half [armchair](#armchair) and half sofa. Only the indoor piece counts; the [garden](#garden) [sun](#sun) lounger that shares the name does not.

entries.name: roulette_table
entries.description: The long [casino](#casino) [table](#table) with the [spinning](#spinning) [wheel](#wheel) set into one end and the [numbered](#numbered) betting layout printed across the felt. Chips, a [rake](#rake) and a [croupier](#croupier) usually complete the scene.

entries.name: chabudai_(table)
entries.description: A low Japanese [table](#table) on stubby [legs](#legs), [no](#no) taller than roughly thirty centimetres, meant for use while [sitting](#sitting) on the [floor](#floor). Meals, [tea](#tea) and [homework](#homework) all happen around one.

entries.name: vanity_table
entries.description: A [dressing](#dressing) [table](#table) fitted with drawers and a fixed [mirror](#mirror), often paired with a [stool](#stool). Its top is typically strewn with [makeup](#makeup), brushes, jewellery and hair ornaments.

entries.name: mahjong_table
entries.description: A [square](#square) [table](#table) made for the game, its top felted in green and edged with a raised wooden rim that stops [tiles](#tiles) [sliding](#sliding) off. Automatic ones shuffle and [stack](#stack) the wall by themselves.

entries.name: rocking_chair
entries.description: A [chair](#chair) set on curved rockers or springs so it tips gently [back](#back) and forth. It carries connotations of [old](#old) age, porches and quiet evenings.

entries.name: sanbou
entries.description: A low wooden offering stand with cut-out panels in its sides. Mirror [mochi](#mochi) at New Year and [dango](#dango) for moon-viewing are set out on one.

entries.name: deck_chair
entries.description: A folding wooden frame slung with a strip of [fabric](#fabric) or vinyl that forms both seat and [back](#back), set out on beaches, decks and poolsides. British usage stretches the word to lounge chairs generally.

entries.name: lectern
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) stand with a sloped top that a [speaker](#speaker) stands behind to read from. It shows up in lectures, sermons, speeches and press conferences; the raised [platform](#platform) itself is a [podium](#podium), which is a separate thing.

entries.name: lifeguard_chair
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) raised seat a [lifeguard](#lifeguard) watches from, [giving](#giving) a view across a whole [beach](#beach) or [pool](#pool) and reached by a short [ladder](#ladder).

entries.name: pew
entries.description: A long backed wooden [bench](#bench) of the kind lined up in rows for a congregation. It turns up in chapel, [cathedral](#cathedral) and [funeral](#funeral) interiors.

entries.name: wooden_stool
entries.description: A backless wooden seat set on three or four [legs](#legs). Bathrooms, workshops, and [bars](#bars) are where it typically turns up.

entries.name: lotus_pedestal
entries.description: A seat or [platform](#platform) shaped from stylised [lotus](#lotus) [petals](#petals), the traditional stand on which Buddhist and Hindu divinities sit or stand. It marks the [figure](#figure) above it as sacred.

entries.name: bleachers
entries.description: Tiered rows of open seating stepped up beside a sports [field](#field) or along a gymnasium wall. They usually serve as the [backdrop](#backdrop) to a match or a place for characters to sit and talk.

entries.name: camping_chair
entries.description: A folding [chair](#chair) made to pack down small, its seat and [back](#back) one panel of weatherproof [cloth](#cloth) slung on a scissor frame. Better ones carry armrests, a [cup](#cup) holder and side pockets.

entries.name: zaisu
entries.description: A legless Japanese [chair](#chair) made of a flat seat and backrest set straight onto a [tatami](#tatami) [floor](#floor), sometimes drawn up to a low [table](#table). Often paired with a [kotatsu](#kotatsu).

entries.name: footstool
entries.description: A low padded seat or block for [resting](#resting) the [feet](#feet) on while [sitting](#sitting). It gets pressed into service as a small [stool](#stool) to perch on as [well](#well).

entries.name: transparent_seat
entries.description: A [chair](#chair), [stool](#stool) or [bench](#bench) made of clear material, letting the sitter's body be seen straight through the seat. Often paired with a low [camera](#camera) angle looking up from beneath.

entries.name: massage_chair
entries.description: A deeply padded [reclining](#reclining) [chair](#chair) fitted with motors that knead the sitter's [back](#back) and [legs](#legs). Turns up in living rooms, salons and relaxation scenes.

entries.name: armrest
entries.description: The padded side support of a [chair](#chair), sofa or vehicle seat. Usually noticed because an elbow or forearm is propped on it.

entries.name: monobloc_(chair)
entries.description: The plastic [chair](#chair) moulded in one piece, cheap and stackable. Its best-known form is the white [armchair](#armchair) with a spindled [back](#back), found [outdoors](#outdoors) almost everywhere in the world.

entries.name: bed
entries.description: A bed shown outright, with its frame, [headboard](#headboard), edge or [pillow](#pillow) in view. When only the sheet fills the frame and the bed is merely implied, [tag](#tag) [bed_sheet](#bed_sheet) and leave this one off; the Japanese [floor](#floor) equivalent is the [futon](#futon).

entries.name: pillow
entries.description: A soft [cushion](#cushion) supporting the head or body on a [bed](#bed), a [couch](#couch) or the [floor](#floor). Colour variants fold into this [tag](#tag); related actions are [pillow_hug](#pillow_hug), [pillow_grab](#pillow_grab) and [pillow_fight](#pillow_fight).

entries.name: bed_sheet
entries.description: The [cloth](#cloth) sheet of a [bed](#bed), lain on or under, often filling the entire background behind a [reclining](#reclining) character. Use it alone when the bed is only implied, and add bed only if the frame or [pillow](#pillow) is actually in view.

entries.name: blanket
entries.description: A large [cloth](#cloth) used for warmth, spread over a [bed](#bed), wrapped around somebody, hung over a [kotatsu](#kotatsu) or laid out for a [picnic](#picnic). Use [under_covers](#under_covers) where a character is tucked beneath one.

entries.name: futon
entries.description: The Japanese [bed](#bed): a [mattress](#mattress) spread straight onto the [floor](#floor), with [pillow](#pillow) and covers laid over it. Neither a [sleeping](#sleeping) [bag](#bag) nor the Western fold-out [couch](#couch) that borrowed the name.

entries.name: cushion
entries.description: A padded [square](#square) for [sitting](#sitting) on or for decoration, found on couches, chairs and floors, [zabuton](#zabuton) included. One meant for [sleeping](#sleeping) on is a [pillow](#pillow).

entries.name: frilled_pillow
entries.description: A [pillow](#pillow) or [cushion](#cushion) with a gathered ruffle [running](#running) right around its edge. Usually a prop on a [bed](#bed), sofa or dressing-table [chair](#chair).

entries.name: heart-shaped_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) or [pillow](#pillow) cut to a [heart](#heart). An ordinary pillow printed with hearts is [heart_print](#heart_print) together with [print_pillow](#print_pillow).

entries.name: yes-no_pillow
entries.description: A matched pair of pillows, one blue and one pink, printed with '[yes](#yes)' on one side and '[no](#no)' on the other, from a Japanese newlywed talk show where couples hinted at their willingness for [sex](#sex). Add the yes or no [tag](#tag) for the side shown.

entries.name: dakimakura_(object)
entries.description: A printed body [pillow](#pillow) appearing inside the picture, hugged, propped against a [bed](#bed) or carried about. When the image is itself the pillow's printed design, use [dakimakura_(medium)](#dakimakura_(medium)).

entries.name: hospital_bed
entries.description: A [bed](#bed) of the kind used in hospitals, with a metal frame, side rails, wheels and a backrest that raises. It normally appears with a [hospital](#hospital) or [infirmary](#infirmary) setting.

entries.name: zabuton
entries.description: A flat, [square](#square) [cushion](#cushion) used for [sitting](#sitting) directly on a [tatami](#tatami) [floor](#floor), often placed under someone [kneeling](#kneeling) in [seiza](#seiza). Tag cushion alongside it.

entries.name: hammock
entries.description: A slung [bed](#bed) of [cloth](#cloth), netting or knotted [rope](#rope) strung between two fixed points such as trees, posts or a ship's beams. It sags under the sleeper's [weight](#weight) and swings, so it usually signals [lounging](#lounging) or a nap [outdoors](#outdoors).

entries.name: canopy_bed
entries.description: A [bed](#bed) with a post at each [corner](#corner) [holding](#holding) up a frame and [curtains](#curtains) overhead, often richly carved and draped. It signals a princess's or noble's [bedroom](#bedroom).

entries.name: stained_sheets
entries.description: Bedding marked with patches where a [liquid](#liquid) has soaked in, usually shown as the aftermath of whatever caused it rather than the event itself.

entries.name: bed_frame
entries.description: The wooden or metal [structure](#structure) of a [bed](#bed), [headboard](#headboard), footboard and posts, clear enough to be worth noting. It is often what rises behind or above a character [lying](#lying) down.

entries.name: mattress
entries.description: The padded [sleeping](#sleeping) pad of a [bed](#bed), shown bare on a frame or set directly on the [floor](#floor) without one. A bed that is fully made up with sheets and covers takes the separate bed [tag](#tag).

entries.name: sleeping_bag
entries.description: A padded [fabric](#fabric) [tube](#tube) that zips shut around a person, used as portable bedding when [sleeping](#sleeping) away from a [bed](#bed). It turns up in [camping](#camping) scenes, on floors during overnight stays, and sometimes worn upright as a joke.

entries.name: body_pillow
entries.description: A long [pillow](#pillow) to [hug](#hug) or lean on while [sleeping](#sleeping), [running](#running) most of a person's [height](#height). Once its [cover](#cover) carries a printed character, the dakimakura [tag](#tag) takes over.

entries.name: air_mattress
entries.description: An inflatable [bed](#bed) or [mat](#mat) used for [sleeping](#sleeping) where [no](#no) proper [mattress](#mattress) is at hand, light enough to pack away. Setting decides whether it is this or a [pool](#pool) float, which looks much the same.

entries.name: bunk_bed
entries.description: Two or more beds stacked on one frame with a short [ladder](#ladder) between them, fitting more sleepers into the same [floor](#floor) [space](#space). Dormitories, barracks, ships and shared children's rooms use them.

entries.name: star-shaped_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) sewn in the [outline](#outline) of a five-pointed star, common [bedroom](#bedroom) or sofa clutter and often clutched by a character.

entries.name: polka_dot_pillow
entries.description: A [pillow](#pillow) or [cushion](#cushion) whose [cover](#cover) is dotted with evenly spaced circles. Usually part of a [bedroom](#bedroom) or sofa arrangement.

entries.name: striped_pillow
entries.description: A [pillow](#pillow) or [cushion](#cushion) covered in [fabric](#fabric) [patterned](#patterned) with stripes.

entries.name: cat-shaped_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) sewn in the [outline](#outline) of a [cat](#cat), ears and [stitched](#stitched) face included. It sits on beds and sofas or gets hugged, and stays an object rather than a live [animal](#animal).

entries.name: headboard
entries.description: The upright panel at the head end of a [bed](#bed), [plain](#plain) wood, padded or barred metal. Characters lean [back](#back) against it.

entries.name: print_pillow
entries.description: A [pillow](#pillow) or [cushion](#cushion) whose [cover](#cover) carries a printed design. Character-printed body pillows are the best-known kind.

entries.name: carrot-shaped_pillow
entries.description: A long [cushion](#cushion) sewn as a [carrot](#carrot), orange with a green leafy [crown](#crown). Hugged, leaned against or hauled about the [house](#house).

entries.name: character_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) sewn into the shape of a character, body and all. Contrast the long body [pillow](#pillow), which carries a character printed flat across its [cover](#cover).

entries.name: pink_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) or [bed](#bed) [pillow](#pillow) in pink, propped up, hugged or [lying](#lying) on a bed. A colour variant of the ordinary pillow.

entries.name: quilt
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) made of [fabric](#fabric) patches [stitched](#stitched) into a [patterned](#patterned) top, quilted over a padded inner layer. The visible patchwork [grid](#grid) is what sets it apart from a [plain](#plain) blanket.

entries.name: neck_pillow
entries.description: The horseshoe-shaped [cushion](#cushion) worn around the [neck](#neck) to prop the head while [sleeping](#sleeping) upright. It goes with planes, trains and long journeys.

entries.name: bedroll
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) or padded [mat](#mat) rolled up for [carrying](#carrying) and spread out to sleep on. It belongs to [camping](#camping), travelling and adventuring scenes where [no](#no) real [bed](#bed) is at hand.

entries.name: food-themed_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) moulded or printed to resemble an edible item, such as a [sushi](#sushi) bolster or a fried-egg cushion. It is furnishing rather than [costume](#costume).

entries.name: plaid_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) or [bed](#bed) [pillow](#pillow) with a tartan [cover](#cover). A common sight in cosy domestic interiors.

entries.name: animal-shaped_pillow
entries.description: A [cushion](#cushion) sewn in the shape of a [creature](#creature), a [fish](#fish), a [cat](#cat), a [bear](#bear), meant to be rested on rather than played with. Bedrooms and [lounging](#lounging) scenes are where it turns up.

entries.name: red_sheet
entries.description: Red bedding, the sheet under a [figure](#figure) or the [cloth](#cloth) spread across a [bed](#bed) or [floor](#floor). It often serves as a flat [field](#field) of colour behind the subject.

entries.name: crib
entries.description: A baby's [bed](#bed) with high barred sides so the [child](#child) cannot climb out. Furnishes nursery and [bedroom](#bedroom) scenes.

entries.name: wrapped_in_blanket
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) pulled all the way around a character, leaving little more than the head showing. It suits [cold](#cold) weather, comfort, and the moments right after a [bath](#bath).

entries.name: cradle
entries.description: A small [bed](#bed) for an infant, generally set on rockers so it [can](#can) be swayed. A fixed-frame [baby](#baby) bed is a [crib](#crib).

entries.name: bookshelf
entries.description: Furniture with rows of shelves [carrying](#carrying) books, in a study, [library](#library) or [bedroom](#bedroom). Often part of the background; use library when the whole room is given over to it, and [book_stack](#book_stack) for loose piles.

entries.name: shelf
entries.description: A flat [ledge](#ledge) fixed to a wall or built into a [cabinet](#cabinet), [holding](#holding) books, bottles or ornaments. A full stacked unit built for books is [bookshelf](#bookshelf) instead.

entries.name: locker
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) lockable compartment for storing [clothes](#clothes), sports kit or books, usually one of a row of identical doors. A whole room of them is a [locker_room](#locker_room).

entries.name: clothes_hanger
entries.description: A triangular hanger shaped like a pair of shoulders, with a [hook](#hook) at the top for [hanging](#hanging) a garment. Empty or loaded, in a [closet](#closet) or held out by somebody.

entries.name: drawer
entries.description: A [sliding](#sliding) open-topped [box](#box) pulled out of a [cabinet](#cabinet), [desk](#desk) or dresser, [holding](#holding) [clothes](#clothes) or other odds and ends.

entries.name: cabinet
entries.description: A boxy storage piece with doors or drawers, [standing](#standing) free or fixed to a wall like a [kitchen](#kitchen) or [medicine](#medicine) cabinet. Part of kitchen, [bathroom](#bathroom) and [office](#office) interiors.

entries.name: chest_of_drawers
entries.description: A [cabinet](#cabinet) of stacked drawers for storing [clothes](#clothes), sometimes with a [mirror](#mirror) above it. A [dressing](#dressing) [table](#table) meant for [makeup](#makeup) is a vanity table.

entries.name: cupboard
entries.description: A [cabinet](#cabinet) with doors for storing [dishes](#dishes), tins and [groceries](#groceries), generally built against a [kitchen](#kitchen) wall. Sets a domestic [interior](#interior).

entries.name: closet
entries.description: A built-in [wardrobe](#wardrobe) or a small storage room behind a [door](#door), generally full of [clothes](#clothes). Often shown [standing](#standing) open with garments [hanging](#hanging) inside, or used as a [hiding](#hiding) place.

entries.name: getabako
entries.description: The rack of open shoe cubbies just inside a Japanese [school](#school) [entrance](#entrance), where outdoor [shoes](#shoes) are swapped for indoor [slippers](#slippers). A recurring [stage](#stage) for a love [letter](#letter) slipped into someone's slot.

entries.name: pedestal
entries.description: A raised block or short [column](#column) [holding](#holding) something up for [display](#display), a [statue](#statue), a [trophy](#trophy) or a relic, or with a character [standing](#standing) on it in the exhibit's place.

entries.name: display_case
entries.description: A glass-fronted [cabinet](#cabinet) [holding](#holding) goods or artefacts for viewing, at a [bakery](#bakery) [counter](#counter), in a [shop](#shop) or in a [museum](#museum). Different from a [bell](#bell) [jar](#jar) or a picture frame.

entries.name: in_locker
entries.description: A character [standing](#standing) or crouched inside a [locker](#locker), the [door](#door) open or ajar. Hiding and changing-room scenes are the common uses.

entries.name: wardrobe
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) freestanding [cupboard](#cupboard) for [hanging](#hanging) [clothes](#clothes), with doors and sometimes a [mirror](#mirror). A small room built for the same purpose is a [closet](#closet).

entries.name: clothes_rack
entries.description: A [standing](#standing) rail hung with garments on hangers, for storage or for [shop](#shop) [display](#display). Familiar from fitting rooms, boutiques and cluttered bedrooms.

entries.name: file_cabinet
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) metal [cabinet](#cabinet) of [sliding](#sliding) drawers for storing documents, standard [office](#office) furniture. Often drawn with one [drawer](#drawer) [hanging](#hanging) open and folders [spilling](#spilling) out.

entries.name: hinadan
entries.description: The stepped [display](#display) stand, usually carpeted in red, on which the Girls' Day dolls are arranged. Folding screens, [paper](#paper) lanterns and [festival](#festival) [sweets](#sweets) are set out around them.

entries.name: umbrella_stand
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) narrow holder by a [doorway](#doorway) for parking [wet](#wet) umbrellas upright. A small detail that fixes a scene at an [entrance](#entrance) or in a [hallway](#hallway).

entries.name: serving_cart
entries.description: A wheeled trolley for moving [food](#food) and [drink](#drink) about, usually with two or three tiers and sometimes a closed [cupboard](#cupboard) below. Found at [tea](#tea) parties and in hotels, hospitals, and trains.

entries.name: cat_tower
entries.description: A carpeted [climbing](#climbing) frame built for cats, with stacked platforms, cubby holes and posts wrapped in rough [rope](#rope) for [scratching](#scratching). It stands in the room as furniture, usually with a [cat](#cat) draped over the top perch.

entries.name: coat_rack
entries.description: A hooked stand or wall fitting for [hanging](#hanging) coats and jackets. Usually a small piece of [hallway](#hallway) or [entrance](#entrance) furniture.

entries.name: open_drawer
entries.description: A [drawer](#drawer) in a [desk](#desk), dresser or [cabinet](#cabinet) has been pulled out, usually with its contents on view. Fits rummaging scenes and pictures of somebody [caught](#caught) going through another's belongings.

entries.name: curtains
entries.description: Sheets of [cloth](#cloth) hung over a [window](#window) or a [doorway](#doorway) for privacy and to keep light out. A standard fixture of [bedroom](#bedroom) and living room backgrounds.

entries.name: mirror
entries.description: A reflective surface - wall-mounted, handheld or set on a dresser - usually shown [holding](#holding) a [reflection](#reflection) of the character or scene.

entries.name: lantern
entries.description: A portable light with its flame or bulb enclosed, carried by hand or hung from a [hook](#hook). Burning torches and electric flashlights are excluded, as are fixed stone and wooden lanterns and lampposts.

entries.name: clock
entries.description: A clock of any kind in the picture: wall, analogue, digital, [pendulum](#pendulum) or alarm. The broadcast time [display](#display) in the [corner](#corner) of an anime frame is [clockshow](#clockshow).

entries.name: jack-o'-lantern
entries.description: A [pumpkin](#pumpkin) with a face cut into it and a light set inside, the standard [autumn](#autumn) decoration. It goes with [halloween](#halloween) scenes, [witch](#witch) outfits and [candlelight](#candlelight).

entries.name: candle
entries.description: A [wax](#wax) [stick](#stick) with a wick [running](#running) through it, lit or [cold](#cold), used for light, for ceremony or as a token of hope. Candles [bound](#bound) onto the head by a band point to the Ushi [no](#no) Koku Mairi curse [ritual](#ritual), usually alongside a straw [doll](#doll) and a [mallet](#mallet).

entries.name: lamp
entries.description: A light fixture [standing](#standing) on a [table](#table) or on the [floor](#floor) to light a room or a [working](#working) surface. Street lighting is [lamppost](#lamppost) and a light that is carried is [lantern](#lantern).

entries.name: picture_frame
entries.description: A rigid surround [holding](#holding) a photograph, painting or drawing, hung on a wall or [standing](#standing) on a [desk](#desk). A decorative frame drawn around the whole image belongs to [ornate_border](#ornate_border) instead.

entries.name: vase
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) decorative vessel meant to hold cut flowers in [water](#water), often [sitting](#sitting) on a [table](#table) or [shelf](#shelf) in an [interior](#interior) scene, with or without flowers arranged in it.

entries.name: paper_lantern
entries.description: A traditional East Asian [lantern](#lantern) with a thin [paper](#paper) [shade](#shade) over a frame, often red or white and sometimes lettered. Hangs at shrines, festivals, [izakaya](#izakaya) fronts and New Year scenes.

entries.name: painting_(object)
entries.description: A framed painting stands inside the scene as a prop, [hanging](#hanging) on a wall or propped on an [easel](#easel). Someone in the act of painting is [painting_(action)](#painting_(action)), and a picture that is itself a painting is [painting_(medium)](#painting_(medium)).

entries.name: ceiling_light
entries.description: A light fitting mounted on the [ceiling](#ceiling): recessed cans, a flush-mounted panel or track lighting. An elaborate [hanging](#hanging) fixture is a [chandelier](#chandelier) instead.

entries.name: candlestand
entries.description: A holder that keeps one or more candles upright, [plain](#plain) or [ornate](#ornate), made from wood, brass, silver and the like. A branched one is a [candelabra](#candelabra), and a [hanging](#hanging) one becomes a [chandelier](#chandelier).

entries.name: light_bulb
entries.description: An electric bulb, either a fixture lighting the scene or the [comic](#comic) mark [hanging](#hanging) over a character's head to signal an [idea](#idea). Lit or [dark](#dark) both count.

entries.name: rug
entries.description: A movable [floor](#floor) covering of thick woven [fabric](#fabric) or [animal](#animal) hide that does not [cover](#cover) the whole floor. Wall-to-wall covering instead is [carpet](#carpet).

entries.name: headlamp
entries.description: A small light worn on the head so the hands stay free, strapped to a band or fixed to a hard [hat](#hat) as on a miner's [helmet](#helmet). Caves, tunnels and [night](#night) work are where it appears.

entries.name: torch
entries.description: A [burning](#burning) [stick](#stick) or brand carried for light, typical of dungeons, caves and torch-lit crowds. A hand-held electric light is [flashlight](#flashlight), even in British usage.

entries.name: alarm_clock
entries.description: A [bedside](#bedside) [clock](#clock) fitted with an alarm, either the twin-bell kind or a small digital [box](#box). It usually sits beside somebody asleep or just waking, often mid-ring.

entries.name: chandelier
entries.description: A large branching light fixture suspended from the [ceiling](#ceiling), [carrying](#carrying) many lamps or candles and often hung with cut [crystal](#crystal). A [plain](#plain) fitting with one or two lamps is a [hanging](#hanging) light.

entries.name: wind_chime
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) ornament that sounds in the breeze, from a cluster of small pieces that clink together to tubes rung by a central clapper. Hung at a [window](#window) or eave it usually marks a [summer](#summer) setting.

entries.name: window_blinds
entries.description: A [window](#window) covering made of long slats that block light from coming through. The stripes of light such slats [cast](#cast) are [window_shadow](#window_shadow), a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: desk_lamp
entries.description: A small portable [lamp](#lamp) [standing](#standing) on a [desk](#desk) or [table](#table) to light the work in front of it. Common in study, [office](#office) and late-night scenes.

entries.name: christmas_lights
entries.description: Strings of small coloured bulbs wound around a [tree](#tree) or strung along railings and eaves as holiday decoration. Generic light strings outside a festive context take [string_of_light_bulbs](#string_of_light_bulbs).

entries.name: fireplace
entries.description: The hearth [opening](#opening) of a [chimney](#chimney) with a [fire](#fire) [burning](#burning) in it, set into a room's wall. Often the [anchor](#anchor) of a warm [winter](#winter) [interior](#interior).

entries.name: analog_clock
entries.description: A [clock](#clock) with a round [dial](#dial), twelve hour marks and moving hands rather than digits. A second hand may or may not be there, and the time shown is often meant to be read.

entries.name: wall_clock
entries.description: A [clock](#clock) mounted on a wall, common in classrooms, kitchens and offices. Note the time shown if it matters to the scene.

entries.name: bulletin_board
entries.description: A soft [cork](#cork) or fibre panel that [papers](#papers) are [pinned](#pinned) to with tacks, hung in classrooms, offices and corridors. Bedrooms use them too, for photographs and keepsakes.

entries.name: hanging_light
entries.description: A simple [ceiling](#ceiling) fixture hung on a cord, [chain](#chain) or rod and [carrying](#carrying) one or two lamps, often repeated in a row over a [counter](#counter) or a [table](#table). A large branching fixture with many arms is a [chandelier](#chandelier).

entries.name: broken_mirror
entries.description: A [mirror](#mirror) whose [glass](#glass) is cracked or [shattered](#shattered), splitting the [reflection](#reflection) into pieces. Where the surface cannot be confirmed as a mirror, [broken_glass](#broken_glass) is the safer [choice](#choice).

entries.name: full-length_mirror
entries.description: A [mirror](#mirror) [tall](#tall) enough to throw [back](#back) a whole [figure](#figure) from head to [feet](#feet), either [standing](#standing) on its own base or fixed flat to a wall. Bedrooms and fitting rooms are its usual home, and it lets an artist show two views of a character at once.

entries.name: fish_tank
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) [aquarium](#aquarium) kept [indoors](#indoors) with gravel, plants and a [lamp](#lamp) over the top, [holding](#holding) live [fish](#fish). Found in homes, restaurants and [shop](#shop) windows.

entries.name: digital_clock
entries.description: A [clock](#clock) showing the hour as lit numerals, usually on a seven-segment [display](#display). Bedside models, wall panels and dashboard readouts all count.

entries.name: fluorescent_lamp
entries.description: A long [glass](#glass) [tube](#tube) [throwing](#throwing) off [cold](#cold) white or bluish light, the standard fitting in classrooms, offices and shops. It usually appears overhead, often in rows.

entries.name: sky_lantern
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [shell](#shell) open at the bottom with a small flame inside, rising on [hot](#hot) air like a tiny [balloon](#balloon). Released in numbers at festivals, making [drifting](#drifting) fields of light in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky).

entries.name: candelabra
entries.description: A branched stand [carrying](#carrying) several candles on arms that rise from one stem. It lights dining halls, chapels and gothic interiors, and comes [plain](#plain) or heavily ornamented.

entries.name: wall_lamp
entries.description: A light fixture mounted on the wall instead of [standing](#standing) or [hanging](#hanging). Sconces, bracket lamps and small [bedside](#bedside) [reading](#reading) lights all belong here.

entries.name: iei
entries.description: The framed [portrait](#portrait) of a dead person set out or carried at a Japanese [funeral](#funeral). Black [cloth](#cloth) is [folded](#folded) over both upper corners of the frame, often with a rosette between them.

entries.name: lampshade
entries.description: The [fabric](#fabric) or [paper](#paper) [cover](#cover) fitted over a bulb to soften and aim its light. It belongs to [table](#table) and [floor](#floor) lamps, and occasionally ends up worn on somebody's head as a joke.

entries.name: see-through_curtains
entries.description: Thin [net](#net) [curtains](#curtains) that leave [shapes](#shapes) behind them readable while softening the light at a [window](#window).

entries.name: oil_lamp
entries.description: A [lamp](#lamp) [burning](#burning) oil drawn up a wick, from a [plain](#plain) [clay](#clay) dish to the [ornate](#ornate) brass vessel a [genie](#genie) comes out of. A modern paraffin burner is a [kerosene_lamp](#kerosene_lamp) instead.

entries.name: noren
entries.description: Split [cloth](#cloth) [curtains](#curtains) hung across a [doorway](#doorway), each panel slit from below so [people](#people) [can](#can) push straight through. Shops, restaurants and bathhouses hang them at the [entrance](#entrance).

entries.name: disco_ball
entries.description: A mirrored sphere hung overhead that scatters points of light across a dance [floor](#floor) as it turns. Belongs to club and [party](#party) scenes.

entries.name: empty_picture_frame
entries.description: A frame with nothing in it: [no](#no) canvas, photo or print, only the moulding and whatever shows through the [opening](#opening). Hung on a wall, propped up, or held around somebody's face.

entries.name: wooden_lantern
entries.description: A [lantern](#lantern) with a wooden frame around [paper](#paper) or [glass](#glass) panels, hung from above or [standing](#standing) on a post. Shrines, inns, and [festival](#festival) paths all use them.

entries.name: folding_screen
entries.description: A freestanding room divider of hinged panels, frequently painted with landscapes or laid with [gold](#gold) [leaf](#leaf). It is not the wheeled curtain used for privacy in hospitals.

entries.name: wax
entries.description: Wax as a substance, shown in candles, sealing wax or slow drips and hardened pools. It softens near a flame and stiffens again as the heat fades.

entries.name: stage_curtains
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy) drapes framing a [stage](#stage), shown drawn, closed or parting to either side. Usually deep red, gathered with a valance [running](#running) across the top.

entries.name: grandfather_clock
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) freestanding [pendulum](#pendulum) [clock](#clock) in a wooden case, usually taller than a person, its [weights](#weights) and [swinging](#swinging) bob visible behind [glass](#glass). A fixture of hallways and [old](#old) drawing rooms.

entries.name: light_switch
entries.description: The small wall [plate](#plate) with a toggle or rocker that turns a room's lights on and off, often with a hand [reaching](#reaching) toward it.

entries.name: bamboo_screen
entries.description: A [blind](#blind) or divider made of thin [bamboo](#bamboo) strips strung together, hung across a [doorway](#doorway) or a [window](#window). It [cuts](#cuts) the light while still letting the air through.

entries.name: hanging_lantern
entries.description: A [lantern](#lantern) visibly suspended from a [hook](#hook), an eave or a strung line rather than carried. One [dangling](#dangling) from somebody's hand takes the [holding](#holding) [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: andon_(lighting)
entries.description: A Japanese [floor](#floor) [lamp](#lamp) built as a [square](#square) wooden or [bamboo](#bamboo) frame covered in [paper](#paper), [glowing](#glowing) softly from within. It lights period interiors, inns and [festival](#festival) streets.

entries.name: clock_hands
entries.description: The pointers of a [clock](#clock) face stand out as an element of the picture, sometimes blown up into a design motif rather than part of a [working](#working) timepiece. Often used to signal time passing.

entries.name: ceiling_fan
entries.description: A bladed fan mounted overhead, turning slowly above a room. Its presence alone does not make an [electric_fan](#electric_fan) picture; that wants a corded or battery-driven fan in frame.

entries.name: candle_wax
entries.description: Wax [running](#running) from a [burning](#burning) [candle](#candle) or set hard where it pooled. Drawn [dripping](#dripping) down the stem, crusted over a holder or spilled across a surface.

entries.name: bust_(sculpture)
entries.description: A sculpted head, [neck](#neck) and shoulders [standing](#standing) on a plinth, cut off before the arms. Marble, bronze, plaster and wood are the usual materials, and it normally records one person's likeness.

entries.name: lantern_on_liquid
entries.description: Paper lanterns set adrift on [water](#water), [glowing](#glowing) as they float away. The custom belongs to [ghost](#ghost) festivals and other rites of remembrance across East and Southeast Asia.

entries.name: mobile
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) decoration of balanced rods with small [shapes](#shapes) [dangling](#dangling) on threads, turning slowly in the air. Often strung above a cot. It has nothing to do with a telephone.

entries.name: kerosene_lamp
entries.description: A portable oil [lamp](#lamp) with a wick under a [glass](#glass) [chimney](#chimney), [giving](#giving) a warm and unsteady light. It is carried or set down in scenes without [electricity](#electricity).

entries.name: floor_lamp
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [lamp](#lamp) on its own stand rising from the [floor](#floor), usually shoulder [height](#height) or more. Distinct from the smaller sort that sits on a [desk](#desk) or a [bedside](#bedside) [table](#table).

entries.name: pendulum_clock
entries.description: A [clock](#clock) kept in time by a [swinging](#swinging) [weight](#weight), the [pendulum](#pendulum) visible behind [glass](#glass) or below the face. Usually a [tall](#tall) [standing](#standing) case or a [box](#box) hung on the wall.

entries.name: privacy_screen
entries.description: A curtain or panel set up to block the view of something. Hospitals use [plain](#plain) drawn [curtains](#curtains) between beds, while households use folding or fence-like panels.

entries.name: bead_curtain
entries.description: Strands of [beads](#beads) hung side by side across a [doorway](#doorway), parting as somebody steps through. They [screen](#screen) one room from another while still letting light and air pass.

entries.name: tapestry
entries.description: A large woven wall [hanging](#hanging) [carrying](#carrying) a picture or repeating pattern, draped behind a [throne](#throne), along a [castle](#castle) corridor or above a [bed](#bed). Doubles as decoration and as quick shorthand for a grand [interior](#interior).

entries.name: refrigerator_magnet
entries.description: A small decorative [magnet](#magnet) [stuck](#stuck) to a fridge [door](#door) or a metal board, either as ornament or to [pin](#pin) up [notes](#notes). Unlike a [laboratory](#laboratory) magnet, they are shaped like postcards, [food](#food), animals, or characters.

entries.name: bath
entries.description: The tub or [pool](#pool) of [water](#water) somebody bathes in, whether a Western tub, a deep Japanese [ofuro](#ofuro), a [hot](#hot) spring or an improvised [drum](#drum). Add [bathing](#bathing) for the act and [bathtub](#bathtub) for the Western fixture in particular.

entries.name: bathtub
entries.description: A Western-style tub built into a [bathroom](#bathroom), [standing](#standing) empty or filled for a soak. Traditional Japanese baths are [ofuro](#ofuro) or [onsen](#onsen), and the general [bathing](#bathing) place is [bath](#bath).

entries.name: toilet
entries.description: The [bathroom](#bathroom) fixture for relieving oneself, whether a home toilet or one in a public [toilet_stall](#toilet_stall). Add bathroom; a character on it in use is [toilet_use](#toilet_use).

entries.name: sink
entries.description: A [basin](#basin) with a tap for [washing](#washing) hands or [dishes](#dishes), set into a [bathroom](#bathroom) or [kitchen](#kitchen) [counter](#counter) or [standing](#standing) on its own. Bathroom sinks usually come with a [mirror](#mirror) mounted above them.

entries.name: shower_head
entries.description: The fixed or handheld nozzle that sprays [water](#water) in a shower stall. Tag it whether visible in use or simply [hanging](#hanging) on its mount.

entries.name: refrigerator
entries.description: A fridge, the [kitchen](#kitchen) appliance that keeps [food](#food) [cold](#cold), shown closed or open with its contents on view. A kitchen fixture, whether a character is raiding it or it just stands in the background.

entries.name: faucet
entries.description: A tap for drawing [water](#water), fixed over a [sink](#sink), a [bath](#bath) or an outdoor [basin](#basin). Japanese outdoor taps are often shown swivelled upward so somebody [can](#can) [drink](#drink) or rinse their face.

entries.name: stove
entries.description: A [cooking](#cooking) appliance with burners or a heated top, including [kitchen](#kitchen) ranges, [hot](#hot) plates and portable camp stoves.

entries.name: squat_toilet
entries.description: A [toilet](#toilet) set at [floor](#floor) level and used by crouching over it rather than [sitting](#sitting). The Japanese type is a long [porcelain](#porcelain) trough with a raised [hood](#hood) at one end.

entries.name: cutting_board
entries.description: A flat wooden or plastic slab laid down as a steady surface for [chopping](#chopping) [food](#food). Belongs to [kitchen](#kitchen) and [cooking](#cooking) scenes, usually with a [knife](#knife) and ingredients on it.

entries.name: washing_machine
entries.description: A household appliance for laundering [clothes](#clothes) with [water](#water) and [detergent](#detergent), front- or top-loading. Usually places the scene in a [laundry](#laundry) room or [bathroom](#bathroom).

entries.name: grill
entries.description: A barbecue grill: a metal frame of [bars](#bars) for [cooking](#cooking) [food](#food) over [fire](#fire) or coals, whether [outdoors](#outdoors) or at a [yakiniku](#yakiniku) [restaurant](#restaurant). Not the British sense of an overhead broiler.

entries.name: microwave
entries.description: A countertop appliance that heats [food](#food) with radiation, its [door](#door) usually hinged at the side with the [handle](#handle) [running](#running) along the top. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [toaster](#toaster) [oven](#oven), which shares a similar boxy shape.

entries.name: oven
entries.description: The closed compartment used for [baking](#baking) and [roasting](#roasting), either built into a [stove](#stove) or [standing](#standing) on its own in a [kitchen](#kitchen). Turns up in [cooking](#cooking) scenes, often with a [tray](#tray) going in or coming out.

entries.name: claw_foot_bathtub
entries.description: A freestanding tub raised on four ornamental [animal](#animal) [feet](#feet), [standing](#standing) away from the wall. Common in period bathrooms and in luxurious settings.

entries.name: drain_(object)
entries.description: The grated [opening](#opening) that carries [water](#water) away from a [sink](#sink), a [bath](#bath) or a shower [floor](#floor). Gratings set into roads and pavements are [storm_drain](#storm_drain).

entries.name: in_bathtub
entries.description: Someone [sitting](#sitting) or [reclining](#reclining) inside a [bathtub](#bathtub), usually with [water](#water) and often [foam](#foam) around them. The tub is what the [tag](#tag) pins down, not the [washing](#washing).

entries.name: heater
entries.description: An appliance that warms a single room: an electric bar or fan heater, an oil [stove](#stove), a kerosene burner. It marks a [winter](#winter) [interior](#interior), usually with somebody huddled up to it.

entries.name: wooden_spoon
entries.description: A carved wooden [spoon](#spoon) with a wide, shallow [bowl](#bowl), meant for [stirring](#stirring) rather than [eating](#eating) from. It belongs to [kitchen](#kitchen) and [cooking](#cooking) scenes.

entries.name: coffee_maker
entries.description: Any appliance that brews [coffee](#coffee), from a drip [machine](#machine) to an espresso unit. Normally [standing](#standing) on a [kitchen](#kitchen) or [cafe](#cafe) [counter](#counter) with a pot beneath it.

entries.name: rice_cooker
entries.description: The [kitchen](#kitchen) appliance that steams [rice](#rice) on its own, with a lift-out inner [bowl](#bowl) and a hinged [lid](#lid). It usually comes with a [paddle](#paddle) and a [measuring](#measuring) [cup](#cup), and sits on the [counter](#counter) in domestic scenes.

entries.name: portable_stove
entries.description: A small one- or two-burner cooker light enough to carry, fed from a [gas](#gas) [canister](#canister) or [hose](#hose). Set on the [table](#table) for [hotpot](#hotpot), or taken along [camping](#camping) and picnicking.

entries.name: washbowl
entries.description: A wide plastic or wooden [basin](#basin) used for [washing](#washing) while seated, and for rinsing small things. Common in bathrooms and [hot](#hot) spring scenes, where the yellow advertising ones are a [running](#running) joke.

entries.name: slipper_bathtub
entries.description: A freestanding tub with one or both ends raised high above the rim, so the [profile](#profile) curves up like a shoe. The [tall](#tall) [back](#back) end lets a bather recline against it.

entries.name: shichirin
entries.description: A small, usually round, portable charcoal [grill](#grill) of glazed [clay](#clay), set on a [table](#table) to cook skewers or [seafood](#seafood) over the [embers](#embers). Implies grill.

entries.name: toilet_seat
entries.description: The hinged [ring](#ring) and [lid](#lid) on a [toilet](#toilet) [bowl](#bowl), raised or lowered. Appears as an object in its own right in [bathroom](#bathroom) scenes.

entries.name: kerosene_heater
entries.description: A portable [stove](#stove) that burns kerosene for warmth, either a cylinder inside a [wire](#wire) [cage](#cage) or a [box](#box) with a wick [cover](#cover) set into the front. Its [hot](#hot) top doubles as a [cooking](#cooking) surface in [winter](#winter) rooms.

entries.name: towel_rack
entries.description: A wall-mounted bar, or set of [bars](#bars), with towels hung over it to dry. A standard [bathroom](#bathroom) fitting, drawn as part of the background rather than the main subject.

entries.name: toaster
entries.description: A small [counter](#counter) appliance with slots on top that browns slices of [bread](#bread), frequently drawn at the moment the [toast](#toast) pops into the air.

entries.name: top-load_washing_machine
entries.description: A [washing](#washing) [machine](#machine) whose [lid](#lid) opens upward onto a vertical [drum](#drum) with an agitator inside. Because nothing [can](#can) be stacked on it, it signals a roomier [laundry](#laundry) than the front-loading kind.

entries.name: blender_(object)
entries.description: The [kitchen](#kitchen) appliance with a sealed jug and a [spinning](#spinning) blade for pureeing [food](#food) and [drink](#drink). The 3D software of the same name is [blender_(medium)](#blender_(medium)).

entries.name: electric_kettle
entries.description: A [kettle](#kettle) that heats its own [water](#water), [standing](#standing) on a cordless power base with a [switch](#switch) and often a [window](#window) showing the level. Buttons, a cord or a [glass](#glass) body tell it apart from one meant for a [stove](#stove).

entries.name: serving_dome
entries.description: The polished [lid](#lid) set over a [plate](#plate) to keep a dish [hot](#hot) and out of sight until it is raised. Also known as a cloche.

entries.name: coffee_grinder
entries.description: A [device](#device) that mills roasted [beans](#beans) down to powder ready for brewing. Pictures usually show the [old](#old) hand-cranked wooden [box](#box) rather than an electric one.

entries.name: furnace
entries.description: A heating appliance [burning](#burning) [gas](#gas), oil or wood to warm air or [water](#water) for a [building](#building). The word also covers an [industrial](#industrial) forge, so the surrounding scene decides which is meant.

entries.name: refrigerator_interior
entries.description: The inside of a fridge with its shelves, jars, and [cold](#cold) blue light. Views work either way, looking into the open [door](#door) or looking out from among the shelves.

entries.name: griddle
entries.description: A flat [cooking](#cooking) surface of metal or stone heated from below, used for pancakes, [okonomiyaki](#okonomiyaki) and teppanyaki. Flattop grills, which look the same from outside, are covered by the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: kitchen_hood
entries.description: The vented canopy fixed above a [stove](#stove) to draw off [smoke](#smoke) and [steam](#steam), usually with a fan grille on its underside. It appears as part of a [kitchen](#kitchen) [interior](#interior).

entries.name: soap_dispenser
entries.description: A [pump](#pump) [bottle](#bottle) of [liquid](#liquid) [soap](#soap) fixed or [standing](#standing) at a [sink](#sink) or in a shower, a small background prop that helps establish a [bathroom](#bathroom) or [kitchen](#kitchen).

entries.name: freezer
entries.description: The [frozen](#frozen) compartment of a [refrigerator](#refrigerator) or a standalone chest freezer, generally drawn [standing](#standing) open with [frost](#frost) and packed [food](#food) inside. Kitchen scenes and jokes about cooling off use it.

entries.name: fish_grill
entries.description: The small broiler [drawer](#drawer) built into a Japanese cooktop under the burners, pulled open to lay [fish](#fish) on its rack. Its knob sits among the ones for the hob.

entries.name: toaster_oven
entries.description: A boxy countertop [oven](#oven) with a drop-down [door](#door) and a [wire](#wire) rack inside, used for toasting and light [baking](#baking); the small worktop ovens common in Japanese kitchens count too. A [microwave](#microwave) is told apart by its side-hinged door and [glass](#glass) [turntable](#turntable).

entries.name: bathroom_scale
