entries.description: A flat [platform](#platform) scale kept on the [floor](#floor) for weighing yourself, read off a [dial](#dial) or a digital panel between the [feet](#feet). It usually turns up as the punchline about the number showing.

entries.name: ofuro
entries.description: The deep wooden Japanese soaking tub with steep straight sides, sometimes [standing](#standing) free of any surround. A rounded or non-wooden tub is simply a [bathtub](#bathtub), and a [hot](#hot) spring is an [onsen](#onsen).

entries.name: wooden_bathtub
entries.description: A [bathtub](#bathtub) built from wooden staves or planks, as in a Japanese-style [ofuro](#ofuro). Rising [steam](#steam) and a small wooden [stool](#stool) usually round out the scene.

entries.name: saucepan
entries.description: A deep round [cooking](#cooking) pot with one long [handle](#handle), used on the hob for sauces, [soup](#soup) and [boiling](#boiling) [water](#water). Its [tall](#tall) narrow shape distinguishes it from a wide frying pan.

entries.name: ice_shaver
entries.description: The [machine](#machine) that scrapes a block of [ice](#ice) into soft flakes for kakigori. Art favours the hand-cranked kind, where a turning block passes a fixed blade and the flakes fall into a [bowl](#bowl); electric bench-top versions also appear.

entries.name: motor_vehicle
entries.description: Any self-propelled ground vehicle that does not run on rails, wheeled or tracked. The broad parent of cars, motorcycles, trucks and buses.

entries.name: car
entries.description: An automobile seen from outside, parked, being driven or filling the background as [traffic](#traffic). A scene set within one is [car_interior](#car_interior).

entries.name: military_vehicle
entries.description: A vehicle built specifically for warfare, such as a [tank](#tank), armored [car](#car), [warship](#warship) or fighter jet. Add the specific vehicle's own [tag](#tag) alongside this one.

entries.name: motorcycle
entries.description: A two-wheeled motor vehicle the rider sits astride, mopeds and minibikes included. Ridden, parked or being worked on.

entries.name: tank
entries.description: An armored, tracked [military](#military) vehicle [carrying](#carrying) a main [gun](#gun), covering both real and fictional designs as [well](#well) as tank-like vehicles such as tank destroyers and self-propelled [artillery](#artillery). A storage [container](#container) of the same name is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bicycle
entries.description: A two-wheeled pedal vehicle, ridden, wheeled along or left [standing](#standing) somewhere in the scene. Add [riding](#riding) when a character is on it; a motorised two-wheeler is [motorcycle](#motorcycle) instead.

entries.name: car_interior
entries.description: The scene sits inside a [car](#car), showing seats, dashboard and windows from within or through an open [door](#door). Only add car as [well](#well) when the outside of the vehicle [can](#can) also be seen.

entries.name: sports_car
entries.description: A low, fast [car](#car) built around performance and the pleasure of [driving](#driving); the most extreme examples are called supercars or hypercars.

entries.name: truck
entries.description: A motor vehicle built to haul cargo, ranging from a small pickup or kei truck to a full semi or [fire](#fire) [engine](#engine). Use a more specific type [tag](#tag) when the kind of truck is clear.

entries.name: scooter
entries.description: A small motorized two-wheeler with a step-through frame and a flat footboard, the Vespa being the classic example. A push scooter without a motor is [kick_scooter](#kick_scooter) instead.

entries.name: tank_treads
entries.description: The linked metal track a tracked vehicle runs on, wrapped around its [road](#road) wheels and drive sprocket. Also used when only the [running](#running) gear is in frame, or when treads are built into a piece of [mecha](#mecha) [machinery](#machinery).

entries.name: race_vehicle
entries.description: Any vehicle built for [racing](#racing), extending beyond ordinary racecars to motorcycles, boats, planes, and science-fiction craft like hover bikes or starfighters. Combine with the specific vehicle type; a racing [car](#car) is also [racecar](#racecar).

entries.name: spoiler_(automobile)
entries.description: The wing-like [plate](#plate) mounted on a car's rear to manage airflow at speed, standard on sports and [racing](#racing) cars. Names the vehicle part, not a plot spoiler.

entries.name: bus
entries.description: A long boxy passenger [road](#road) vehicle for public transport, seen from outside. A scene set within one takes [bus_interior](#bus_interior) instead.

entries.name: racecar
entries.description: A [car](#car) built for [competition](#competition), usually plastered with sponsor logos, ranging from Formula and Le Mans prototypes to rally and GT cars.

entries.name: license_plate
entries.description: The registration [plate](#plate) on a [car](#car), [motorcycle](#motorcycle) or other vehicle, showing its letters and numbers. Also used when the plate appears alone or is held up as a prop.

entries.name: panzer_iv
entries.description: The German medium [tank](#tank) made in greater numbers than any other German design of the Second World War, with a boxy hull and turret. Many assault guns and tank destroyers were built on its chassis.

entries.name: bicycle_basket
entries.description: A [basket](#basket) fixed to the front of a [bicycle](#bicycle) or [scooter](#scooter) so the rider [can](#can) carry bags or [shopping](#shopping) with their hands free. Tag the bicycle itself alongside it.

entries.name: unused_tire
entries.description: One or more vehicle tyres [sitting](#sitting) apart from any [wheel](#wheel) or [car](#car), stacked, [leaning](#leaning) against a wall or scattered in a yard. Common set [dressing](#dressing) for garages, gyms and [junk](#junk) lots.

entries.name: van
entries.description: A boxy enclosed [road](#road) vehicle built for [carrying](#carrying) goods or passengers, with a rear [door](#door) and usually a [sliding](#sliding) one on the side, taller and more [square](#square) than an ordinary [car](#car).

entries.name: police_car
entries.description: A marked patrol vehicle [carrying](#carrying) roof lights and force livery. Parked at a scene, [giving](#giving) chase, or simply passing in the background.

entries.name: vehicle_interior
entries.description: The scene takes place inside a vehicle, showing its seats, dashboard, [cockpit](#cockpit) or [cabin](#cabin). Being inside a [car](#car) or a plane is not counted as an indoor setting.

entries.name: wreckage
entries.description: The [broken](#broken) remains of vehicles or machines: crashed cars, downed [aircraft](#aircraft), [shattered](#shattered) [mecha](#mecha), or burnt-out tanks. A sunken [ship](#ship) keeps its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: convertible
entries.description: A [car](#car) with a folding roof, nearly always drawn with the top down and the [cabin](#cabin) open to the [sky](#sky). Cars with [no](#no) roof at all usually get the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pickup_truck
entries.description: A light [truck](#truck) with a closed cab in front and an open cargo [bed](#bed) with a drop-down tailgate behind. Used for hauling, and common in [rural](#rural) and small-town scenes.

entries.name: tank_turret
entries.description: The rotating [gun](#gun) housing of a ground armored vehicle, low and compact next to a naval one, [carrying](#carrying) a main [cannon](#cannon) and often a coaxial or roof-mounted [machine](#machine) gun. Applies when the turret alone is visible, or when a [mecha](#mecha) wears one, but not for a bare [hatch](#hatch) or cupola on its own.

entries.name: red_car
entries.description: An automobile painted red, whether parked in the scene, being driven, or [sitting](#sitting) as a background detail.

entries.name: handlebar
entries.description: The transverse bar by which a [bicycle](#bicycle), motorbike or [scooter](#scooter) is steered, capped with a grip at either end. Holding it lets the rider [swing](#swing) the front [wheel](#wheel) and stay balanced.

entries.name: box_truck
entries.description: A [truck](#truck) whose cargo [space](#space) is a rigid rectangular body [sitting](#sitting) behind the cab. A [tractor](#tractor) unit [pulling](#pulling) a box-shaped [trailer](#trailer) counts as one as [well](#well).

entries.name: sports_utility_vehicle
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), boxy passenger vehicle with high ground clearance and often four-wheel drive, bulkier than an ordinary [car](#car). Softer car-based crossovers fall under the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: armored_vehicle
entries.description: An armoured [military](#military) vehicle that is not a [tank](#tank), generally because it rides on tyres or carries [no](#no) [cannon](#cannon). Scout cars and wheeled [fighting](#fighting) vehicles are the usual examples.

entries.name: white_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) with white paintwork, parked or in motion in the scene. Only the color is asserted here; body style and make are described by other tags.

entries.name: m4_sherman
entries.description: The main American [tank](#tank) of the Second World War: [tall](#tall) and quick, moderately armoured, with a sloped front [plate](#plate) and a rounded turret [carrying](#carrying) a 75mm or 76mm [gun](#gun). Outmatched by [heavy](#heavy) German armour, it made up for it by being easy to build, repair and modify in vast numbers.

entries.name: t-34
entries.description: A Soviet medium [tank](#tank) of the Second World War, known for its heavily sloped [armor](#armor), wide tracks and rounded turret. It paired [strong](#strong) firepower and speed with a badly [cramped](#cramped) crew compartment.

entries.name: armored_personnel_carrier
entries.description: A [military](#military) vehicle built to carry troops, wheeled or tracked, armoured against bullets and shrapnel but without a tank's main [gun](#gun). Usually armed with a [machine](#machine) gun or [grenade](#grenade) launcher, and sometimes fielded by [police](#police) units.

entries.name: rear-view_mirror
entries.description: The small [mirror](#mirror) mounted at the top of a car's [windshield](#windshield) so the driver [can](#can) [watch](#watch) the [road](#road) behind. Frequently carries a reflected face or a [dangling](#dangling) charm as a compositional touch.

entries.name: blue_car
entries.description: A [road](#road) [car](#car) with blue bodywork, parked or in motion. The make and [model](#model) are not part of the claim.

entries.name: kei_truck
entries.description: A tiny pickup built to Japan's light-vehicle rules, its cab [sitting](#sitting) over the front wheels with a low flat [bed](#bed) behind. They are everywhere on farms and [building](#building) sites.

entries.name: taxi
entries.description: A [car](#car) for hire that carries passengers for a fare, marked out by a roof [sign](#sign), a livery colour and a meter on the dash.

entries.name: streetcar
entries.description: A rail vehicle [running](#running) in the roadway among cars, usually drawing power from an overhead [wire](#wire). Suspended and cable-hauled kinds belong to cable_car or suspension_railway instead.

entries.name: formula_racer
entries.description: A purpose-built open-wheel [racing](#racing) [car](#car) seating one driver in an exposed [cockpit](#cockpit), with [wings](#wings) front and rear. Formula One and its regional equivalents are the usual reference.

entries.name: stance_(vehicle)
entries.description: A [car](#car) modified to sit very low, with its wheels tilted inward and flared arches over them, a look borrowed from drift builds and pushed [well](#well) past any practical purpose.

entries.name: muscle_car
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) American performance coupe built around an oversized V8, made for straight-line speed rather than corners. The [lighter](#lighter) pony [car](#car) sits close to it but counts as a separate class.

entries.name: itasha
entries.description: A vehicle wrapped or painted with large anime artwork as a livery. Cars are the usual canvas, though the same treatment on motorcycles and [aircraft](#aircraft) counts too.

entries.name: black_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) painted black. It is the usual [choice](#choice) for executive saloons, hearses and anything meant to look official or menacing, and the colour is all the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: churchill_(tank)
entries.description: A British [heavy](#heavy) infantry [tank](#tank) of the Second World War, known for its long hull with the tracks [running](#running) right around it over many small [road](#road) wheels. Thick armour and a slow pace defined it, and it served as the base for many specialist vehicles.

entries.name: side-view_mirror
entries.description: The small [mirror](#mirror) mounted on a [car](#car) or [motorcycle](#motorcycle) so the driver [can](#can) [watch](#watch) the lane alongside and behind. Often used to frame a reflected face or a scene receding down the [road](#road).

entries.name: yellow_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) painted yellow, parked or on the move. Taxis and sports cars account for a good share of them.

entries.name: military_truck
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [army](#army) lorry for [carrying](#carrying) troops or equipment, typically canvas-topped over a bench-lined [bed](#bed) and painted in service colors.

entries.name: military_jeep
entries.description: A small, open, four-wheel-drive utility vehicle in [army](#army) service, with a flat folding windscreen, [no](#no) doors and a spare [wheel](#wheel) mounted at the [back](#back).

entries.name: pop-up_headlights
entries.description: Car headlamps hidden under the [bonnet](#bonnet) that rise or flip into place when switched on, a hallmark of eighties and nineties sports cars. Tagged only while they stand raised.

entries.name: left-hand_drive
entries.description: A vehicle whose steering [wheel](#wheel) sits on the left of the [cabin](#cabin), the arrangement used across most of the world. Worth noting in Japanese-set art, where domestic cars are built the other way round.

entries.name: right-hand_drive
entries.description: A motor vehicle with the steering [wheel](#wheel) mounted on the right side of the [cabin](#cabin). Standard in Japan, Britain and the countries that took the layout from them.

entries.name: tricycle
entries.description: A pedal-driven cycle [riding](#riding) on three wheels, ranging from a toddler's plastic trike to a rickshaw-sized carrier. A motorised three-wheeled vehicle instead takes the separate [tag](#tag) [three-wheeler](#three-wheeler).

entries.name: trailer
entries.description: A wheeled body with [no](#no) [engine](#engine) of its own, towed behind another vehicle, from a camper or utility trailer to the load section of an articulated lorry. Covers both personal and commercial towed loads.

entries.name: semi_truck
entries.description: A big [road](#road) [tractor](#tractor) built to pull a detachable freight [trailer](#trailer). Covers the cab on its own as [well](#well) as the full articulated rig.

entries.name: transit_bus
entries.description: A [city](#city) service [bus](#bus) with doors along one side and [standing](#standing) room for passengers, shown [waiting](#waiting) at a stop or moving through [traffic](#traffic). The everyday public-transport counterpart to a [coach](#coach) or [school](#school) bus.

entries.name: tank_interior
entries.description: The inside of an armored vehicle: [cramped](#cramped) seating, [ammunition](#ammunition) racks and periscope blocks close on every side. Used when a scene sits within the hull or turret rather than showing the vehicle from outside.

entries.name: grey_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) painted grey or silver. Being the most ordinary colour a car [can](#can) take, it usually just fills out a [street](#street) scene.

entries.name: moped
entries.description: A low-powered motorbike fitted with [bicycle](#bicycle) pedals to help it pull away and climb hills. A two-wheeler with a step-through frame but [no](#no) pedals is a [scooter](#scooter) instead.

entries.name: tank_destroyer
entries.description: An armored [fighting](#fighting) vehicle built around a [heavy](#heavy) anti-tank [gun](#gun), typically on a [tank](#tank) chassis with a fixed casemate or an open-topped mount instead of a rotating turret. Almost all depictions come from the Second World War.

entries.name: tank_cupola
entries.description: The raised, hatched [dome](#dome) on an armored vehicle's turret roof, where a crew member watches through periscopes or vision blocks. Wartime designs stand [tall](#tall) and obvious; modern ones sit low or are missing entirely.

entries.name: go-kart
entries.description: A tiny open four-wheeled racer with one seat, either engine-driven or coasting on pedals and gravity. Associated with rental circuits and amusement parks.

entries.name: m3_lee
entries.description: An early American medium [tank](#tank) of the Second World War, odd-looking because its 75mm [gun](#gun) sits in a sponson on the hull while a small turret with a 37mm gun rides above. The layout was a stopgap to get a big gun into service quickly.

entries.name: kv-2
entries.description: A Soviet [heavy](#heavy) [tank](#tank) of the early [war](#war) years, unmistakable for the towering slab-sided turret built around a howitzer. Thickly armoured but slow and very [tall](#tall), it has become a favourite through tank [video](#video) games.

entries.name: windshield
entries.description: The front [glass](#glass) panel of a [car](#car), [aircraft](#aircraft), or other vehicle, viewed from outside or looked through from the driver's seat. Reflections, [rain](#rain), and cracks [running](#running) across it are frequently the whole point of the picture.

entries.name: le_mans_prototype
entries.description: A purpose-built endurance [racing](#racing) [car](#car) with covered wheels, a low [cockpit](#cockpit) and a [tall](#tall) rear wing, made for the track rather than derived from a [road](#road) car. The [tag](#tag) stands in for prototype-class racers generally.

entries.name: food_truck
entries.description: A [van](#van) or [trailer](#trailer) fitted out as a [mobile](#mobile) [kitchen](#kitchen), [serving](#serving) through a [hatch](#hatch) in its side. Ice [cream](#cream) vans and street-food wagons both belong here.

entries.name: jagdpanzer_38(t)
entries.description: A small German [tank](#tank) [destroyer](#destroyer) of the Second World War, built low on a Czech chassis with steeply sloped plates and a [gun](#gun) of limited traverse. It is also known as the Hetzer.

entries.name: segway
entries.description: A two-wheeled, self-balancing [platform](#platform) with an upright [handlebar](#handlebar), steered by [leaning](#leaning) forward or [back](#back).

entries.name: steamroller
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [machine](#machine) with wide smooth drums for compacting a [road](#road) surface. The word covers modern diesel road rollers as [well](#well) as the original steam-driven ones.

entries.name: panther_(tank)
entries.description: A German medium [tank](#tank) of the later Second World War, built as an answer to the Soviet T-34. Recognisable by its steeply sloped front [plate](#plate), large interleaved [road](#road) wheels and long high-velocity [gun](#gun).

entries.name: sidecar
entries.description: A one-wheeled passenger [car](#car) bolted to the flank of a [motorcycle](#motorcycle) or [bicycle](#bicycle). Lets a second rider sit alongside the driver instead of behind.

entries.name: turretless_tank
entries.description: An armoured vehicle whose main [gun](#gun) is fixed within the hull instead of a rotating turret, so [aiming](#aiming) outside its narrow arc means turning the whole [machine](#machine). The casemate layout keeps the vehicle low and cheap while freeing [weight](#weight) for thicker armour.

entries.name: ambulance
entries.description: An emergency [van](#van) fitted out to carry the [sick](#sick) or badly injured, marked with stripes or a [cross](#cross) and topped with a light bar. It belongs to [accident](#accident) and [rescue](#rescue) scenes.

entries.name: rally_car
entries.description: A [road](#road) [car](#car) heavily rebuilt for rough-surface [competition](#competition), with a raised stance, mudflaps, a roll [cage](#cage), and sponsor livery. Group B machines from the 1980s remain the look artists reach for most.

entries.name: kettenkrad
entries.description: A small German half-track of the Second World War, steered by a [motorcycle](#motorcycle) front end with a tracked body behind. It was built to haul loads over ground that wheels could not manage.

entries.name: t-34-85
entries.description: The late-war upgrade of the Soviet medium [tank](#tank), fitted with a heavier [gun](#gun) and told apart by its noticeably larger turret with a curved mantlet.

entries.name: kei_car
entries.description: A Japanese light-class [car](#car) built to strict limits on length and [engine](#engine) size, which gives it a boxy body noticeably shorter than an ordinary saloon. A common [city](#city) runabout.

entries.name: unicycle
entries.description: A single-wheeled, pedal-driven cycle with [no](#no) handlebars, ridden by balance alone. Common in [circus](#circus), street-performance and [comic](#comic) [balancing](#balancing) scenes.

entries.name: excavator
entries.description: A tracked [digging](#digging) [machine](#machine) with a boom, an arm and a toothed [bucket](#bucket) for tearing up ground. Also called a backhoe; it belongs to [building](#building) sites and demolition scenes.

entries.name: green_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) with green bodywork, parked or in motion. The [paint](#paint) decides the [tag](#tag), whatever make or [model](#model) the vehicle is.

entries.name: dirtbike
entries.description: A light off-road [motorcycle](#motorcycle) with long [suspension](#suspension) travel, high ground clearance and knobbly tyres. Built for trails and jumps rather than for tarmac.

entries.name: is-2
entries.description: A Soviet [heavy](#heavy) [tank](#tank) of the Second World War, thickly armoured and [mounting](#mounting) a [gun](#gun) big enough to kill a German heavy in a single shot. Slow and unwieldy, it was meant for [breaking](#breaking) through fortified lines.

entries.name: tractor
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) [farm](#farm) vehicle with oversized rear wheels and a high seat or cab, built to haul implements across rough, uneven ground. A [staple](#staple) of countryside and farm scenes.

entries.name: kick_scooter
entries.description: A [standing](#standing) [scooter](#scooter): a narrow board on two small wheels with an upright [handlebar](#handlebar), pushed along by one foot against the ground. Powered versions and the larger [road](#road) scooter have their own tags.

entries.name: medium_tank
entries.description: A tracked armored [fighting](#fighting) vehicle of the middle [weight](#weight) class, [balancing](#balancing) [armor](#armor), speed and firepower rather than maximizing any one of them. Common in wartime and [military](#military) settings.

entries.name: spare_tire
entries.description: A replacement [wheel](#wheel) carried on or inside a vehicle against a puncture, often bolted to the [back](#back) of an off-roader or stowed beneath the boot [floor](#floor).

entries.name: recreational_vehicle
entries.description: A [road](#road) vehicle fitted out to live in, complete with a [bed](#bed) and a [cooking](#cooking) area and often a [toilet](#toilet). Ranges from a converted [van](#van) to a full motorhome or a towed camper [trailer](#trailer), called a [camping](#camping) [car](#car) in Japan.

entries.name: m1_abrams
entries.description: The American main [battle](#battle) [tank](#tank) in service since 1980, its slab-sided sloping turret shaped by composite armour and its [gas](#gas) turbine set under a raised rear deck. It carries a 105mm or, later, a 120mm [gun](#gun) with [machine](#machine) guns on the roof.

entries.name: three-wheeler
entries.description: A powered vehicle [running](#running) on three wheels, built on [motorcycle](#motorcycle) or [scooter](#scooter) mechanics, with either a single [wheel](#wheel) at the front or a single wheel at the [back](#back). Auto rickshaws and small [delivery](#delivery) trucks are the usual examples.

entries.name: pink_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) painted pink, parked, on the [road](#road) or being driven. The paintwork is the whole of the [tag](#tag); the make and body type are recorded elsewhere.

entries.name: orange_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) painted orange, parked, being driven or [standing](#standing) in the background.

entries.name: purple_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) painted purple, whether parked or in motion.

entries.name: brown_car
entries.description: A [car](#car) painted brown, parked or on the move. Colour variant of the ordinary automobile.

entries.name: aircraft
entries.description: Any [flying](#flying) [machine](#machine), real or invented: aeroplanes, helicopters, airships, transforming fighters, science-fiction flyers. Narrower tags such as [airplane](#airplane) or [airship](#airship) say which kind.

entries.name: airplane
entries.description: A fixed-wing [flying](#flying) [machine](#machine), from a [propeller](#propeller) fighter to a jet airliner. Wings rather than a rotor or a gasbag are what hold it up.

entries.name: train
entries.description: A connected series of rail cars seen from outside, whether a [bullet](#bullet) train, a [steam](#steam) [locomotive](#locomotive) or a [city](#city) tram. A scene shown only from inside the [carriage](#carriage) is [train_interior](#train_interior) instead.

entries.name: spacecraft
entries.description: Any vehicle built to travel through [space](#space), from one-seat starfighters and rockets to shuttles, [flying](#flying) saucers, and planet-sized warships. Fictional designs from any franchise count as long as the craft is meant for spaceflight.

entries.name: ufo
entries.description: An [alien](#alien) [spacecraft](#spacecraft) in the classic flying-saucer shape, or a sphere or cigar-shaped variant, hovering or beaming something up. A [staple](#staple) of retro [science](#science) fiction.

entries.name: booster_rocket
entries.description: The [strap-on](#strap-on) [engine](#engine) [stage](#stage) that lifts a [rocket](#rocket) or [spacecraft](#spacecraft) off the ground, most often drawn [firing](#firing) with a [plume](#plume) trailing behind. It also covers thruster packs bolted onto machines and powered armour.

entries.name: fighter_jet
entries.description: A jet-powered [military](#military) [aircraft](#aircraft) built for air combat and ground [attack](#attack), fast and armed with missiles, bombs and [cannon](#cannon). Its crew are usually drawn in g-suits and helmets with oxygen masks.

entries.name: cockpit
entries.description: The compartment an [aircraft](#aircraft), [spacecraft](#spacecraft) or [mecha](#mecha) is flown from, with its seat, controls and [instrument](#instrument) panels. The character is generally shown [sitting](#sitting) inside it.

entries.name: helicopter
entries.description: An [aircraft](#aircraft) carried by [spinning](#spinning) rotor blades instead of fixed [wings](#wings). Any kind counts, from a [military](#military) gunship to a [news](#news) chopper.

entries.name: rocket
entries.description: A rocket or rocket [engine](#engine) used for spaceflight or another non-military purpose. A [military](#military) rocket-propelled [weapon](#weapon) belongs under [missile](#missile) instead.

entries.name: propeller_fighter
entries.description: A piston-engined, propeller-driven combat [aircraft](#aircraft) styled after the World War eras, in the mould of a Zero, Spitfire, or Mustang. Jet fighters take a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: airship
entries.description: A [flying](#flying) vessel of [fantasy](#fantasy) or [science](#science) fiction, often built like a sea [ship](#ship) and held up by [magic](#magic) or invented [machinery](#machinery). Balloons and rotors may or may not be part of the design.

entries.name: locomotive
entries.description: The powered unit at the head of a [train](#train), [steam](#steam) or diesel, that hauls the carriages behind it. Use it where the [engine](#engine) itself is the subject rather than the train as a whole.

entries.name: multiple_unit_train
entries.description: A [train](#train) whose carriages carry their own motors, so nothing has to pull it — commuter and high-speed sets are built this way. Do not add a [locomotive](#locomotive) [tag](#tag) when none is actually drawn.

entries.name: dirigible
entries.description: A powered lighter-than-air craft: a long gasbag with an [engine](#engine) [car](#car) slung underneath. Covers rigid zeppelins, soft-bodied blimps and the semi-rigid middle ground, while fantastical [flying](#flying) vessels are [airship](#airship).

entries.name: spacecraft_interior
entries.description: The inside of a spaceship: cockpits, corridors, bunks, and [instrument](#instrument) panels, often with a viewport looking out onto stars. The enclosed metal environment is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: subway
entries.description: An [urban](#urban) rapid transit railway [running](#running) through tunnels, along viaducts or on segregated track. The [tag](#tag) covers the trains themselves; for the platforms use [subway_station](#subway_station).

entries.name: seaplane
entries.description: An [aircraft](#aircraft) able to take off from and land on [water](#water). It comes either as a [flying](#flying) [boat](#boat) with a hull for a fuselage, or as a [floatplane](#floatplane) balanced on a pair of pontoons.

entries.name: steam_locomotive
entries.description: A coal-fired railway [engine](#engine), bulkier than a diesel or electric one, with a long boiler, a funnel at the front and exposed [driving](#driving) rods. A fixture of period and [fantasy](#fantasy) railway scenes.

entries.name: canopy_(aircraft)
entries.description: The clear [hood](#hood) over an aircraft's [cockpit](#cockpit), hinged or [sliding](#sliding) [back](#back) to let the [pilot](#pilot) climb in. The same [tag](#tag) covers equivalent bubbles on [mecha](#mecha) and other fictional vehicles.

entries.name: starfighter
entries.description: A small, fast combat [spacecraft](#spacecraft), usually flown by a single [pilot](#pilot). A science-fiction [staple](#staple), drawn with [cockpit](#cockpit), stubby [wings](#wings) and [glowing](#glowing) [engine](#engine) nozzles.

entries.name: biplane
entries.description: An aeroplane with two pairs of [wings](#wings) stacked one above the other and joined by struts and bracing wires. It signals early aviation, barnstorming and pulp adventure.

entries.name: hot_air_balloon
entries.description: A large [fabric](#fabric) [envelope](#envelope) held aloft by heated air, with a [basket](#basket) for passengers slung beneath it. Drawn [drifting](#drifting) over a [landscape](#landscape) as often as [sitting](#sitting) on the ground.

entries.name: bomber
entries.description: A [military](#military) [aircraft](#aircraft) built to carry ordnance and drop it on targets below. Heavier than a fighter, with a deep fuselage and bay doors underneath.

entries.name: flying_saucer
entries.description: A disc-shaped [spacecraft](#spacecraft) of the classic UFO kind, often domed above and ringed with lights. Retro [science](#science) fiction and [abduction](#abduction) gags rely on it.

entries.name: a6m_zero
entries.description: The Japanese navy's carrier fighter of the Second World War, light and famously agile with an enormous range. It is drawn by its rounded wingtips and long glazed canopy, usually in wartime settings.

entries.name: space_station
entries.description: A crewed [structure](#structure) built in orbit to serve as a base, [laboratory](#laboratory), or waypoint, bristling with solar arrays and docking arms. Shown either from outside or as the setting for a scene aboard it.

entries.name: floatplane
entries.description: An [aircraft](#aircraft) carried on external pontoons so it [can](#can) settle on [water](#water) and lift off again. The bigger craft that land on a shaped hull are [flying](#flying) boats.

entries.name: jet_airliner
entries.description: A large passenger jet, a long [tube](#tube) of a fuselage with engines slung beneath swept [wings](#wings). It may be aloft, [standing](#standing) on the [apron](#apron), or seen through a terminal [window](#window).

entries.name: canards
entries.description: Small winglets mounted ahead of an aircraft's main wing, [working](#working) like a tailplane to hold and steer its pitch. The word is French for [duck](#duck), after the look of the first machines built this way.

entries.name: hover_bike
entries.description: A motorbike-shaped craft that flies instead of [rolling](#rolling), seating one or two riders with [no](#no) wheels beneath it. Science fiction draws it [racing](#racing) low over a [city](#city) or a [desert](#desert).

entries.name: attack_helicopter
entries.description: A gunship built for striking targets on the ground, hung with [rocket](#rocket) pods and missiles on stub [wings](#wings) and usually [carrying](#carrying) a [cannon](#cannon) under the [nose](#nose). Leaner and more angular than a transport [helicopter](#helicopter).

entries.name: nose_art
entries.description: Unofficial painting on an aircraft's fuselage near the [nose](#nose), in the wartime manner of pin-ups, cartoon figures and slogans. It also covers pictures drawn to imitate that look.

entries.name: rocket_ship
entries.description: A tube-shaped [spacecraft](#spacecraft) with a pointed [nose](#nose), stabilising [fins](#fins) and engines at the base. Covers both [realistic](#realistic) launch vehicles and the retro pulp-serial shape.

entries.name: airplane_wing
entries.description: A wing of an aeroplane is a visible element of the picture, whether glimpsed past a [cabin](#cabin) [window](#window) or seen from below in flight. Engines, flaps and winglets count as part of it.

entries.name: f-15_eagle
entries.description: A large twin-engine air-superiority fighter with twin vertical tails, a [bubble](#bubble) canopy and a broad wing. The ground-attack variant carries a second crew member behind the [pilot](#pilot).

entries.name: flying_boat
entries.description: A [seaplane](#seaplane) that lands on its own boat-shaped hull rather than on separate floats. These are the larger craft; the smaller pontoon-legged kind is a [floatplane](#floatplane).

entries.name: f-14_tomcat
entries.description: A big twin-engine carrier fighter with [wings](#wings) that sweep [back](#back) in flight and two crew seated one behind the other. Flown from the 1970s into the 2000s, and the shape behind more than one anime transforming jet.

entries.name: hover_vehicle
entries.description: A vehicle or [machine](#machine) [floating](#floating) a short way above the ground, with nothing touching the surface. The motorbike-shaped kind is [hover_bike](#hover_bike).

entries.name: space_shuttle
entries.description: A winged [spacecraft](#spacecraft) that launches vertically atop rockets and returns to the ground as an unpowered [glider](#glider). The American orbiter and the Soviet Buran are the models most often drawn.

entries.name: open_cockpit
entries.description: The canopy or [hatch](#hatch) of an [aircraft](#aircraft), [mecha](#mecha) or [racing](#racing) [machine](#machine) stands open, leaving the pilot's seat and controls exposed. Common where somebody is [climbing](#climbing) in or out, or the machine is being serviced.

entries.name: flying_car
entries.description: A car-shaped vehicle that hovers or flies instead of [running](#running) on wheels, a fixture of futuristic [city](#city) scenes. An ordinary [car](#car) merely airborne during a stunt does not count.

entries.name: f-22_raptor
entries.description: An American stealth fighter with faceted angular surfaces, canted twin tails and vectoring [exhaust](#exhaust) nozzles. Built above all for air-to-air combat.

entries.name: shinkansen
entries.description: Japan's high-speed rail network, its trains recognizable by their long white bodies and tapered noses, known in English as the [bullet](#bullet) [train](#train).

entries.name: f6f_hellcat
entries.description: A stubby, radial-engined carrier fighter of the Second World War, almost always painted [dark](#dark) blue. Tough and heavily armed, it outmatched its Japanese opposite number in everything but agility.

entries.name: quadcopter
entries.description: A small rotary [aircraft](#aircraft) lifted by four rotors mounted at the corners of its frame. Most often drawn as a [camera](#camera) [drone](#drone) hovering over a scene.

entries.name: glider
entries.description: An [aircraft](#aircraft) that flies without [engine](#engine) power, [riding](#riding) air currents on long slender [wings](#wings). Motor gliders carry a small engine used only to take off or to stretch a flight.

entries.name: high-speed_train
entries.description: A sleek long-nosed express [train](#train) built to run very fast on its own dedicated track. Shinkansen-style designs are what artists normally draw.

entries.name: f-35_lightning_ii
entries.description: A single-engine stealth multirole fighter with a bulged fuselage and a one-piece canopy, built in land-based, short-takeoff and carrier versions. A modern fighter, and easily [confused](#confused) with other faceted stealth designs.

entries.name: anchor
entries.description: A ship's anchor, the hooked [weight](#weight) on a [chain](#chain) that holds a vessel in place. Worn as an [emblem](#emblem) on clothing it becomes [anchor_symbol](#anchor_symbol) instead.

entries.name: watercraft
entries.description: Any water-going vehicle: ships, boats, submarines, hovercraft. Add the specific kind such as [boat](#boat), [ship](#ship) or [submarine](#submarine).

entries.name: ship
entries.description: A large seagoing vessel, as opposed to a small [boat](#boat). Submarines are excluded. Implies [watercraft](#watercraft).

entries.name: boat
entries.description: A small vessel that carries [people](#people) over [water](#water): a [rowboat](#rowboat), sailing dinghy, motorboat or [gondola](#gondola), [afloat](#afloat) or drawn up on the [shore](#shore). Larger vessels are [ship](#ship).

entries.name: warship
entries.description: An actual naval combat vessel such as a [destroyer](#destroyer), [cruiser](#cruiser) or carrier appears in the picture. Ship-girl personifications with [rigging](#rigging) do not count.

entries.name: ship_funnel
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) [stack](#stack) rising from a ship's superstructure to vent [engine](#engine) [smoke](#smoke) clear of the deck. A distinctive shape on liners and warships, and a stock feature of ship-girl costumes.

entries.name: mast
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) upright [pole](#pole) on a [ship](#ship) [carrying](#carrying) sails, [rigging](#rigging), flags or a lookout post. Tag it where the mast is a visible part of the vessel or of the [skyline](#skyline).

entries.name: inflatable_raft
entries.description: An air-filled [boat](#boat) or float used on the [water](#water) for fun or for [rescue](#rescue). It is easily [confused](#confused) with an air [mattress](#mattress), so decide by whether the thing is meant for [swimming](#swimming) or for [sleeping](#sleeping).

entries.name: battleship
entries.description: A heavily armoured [gun](#gun) [ship](#ship) of the late nineteenth to mid twentieth century, its main guns in large turrets fore and aft and a secondary [battery](#battery) along the sides. Aircraft and missiles made the type obsolete after the Second World War.

entries.name: submarine
entries.description: A vessel built to travel beneath the water's surface, with a sealed hull and a conning [tower](#tower). More often than not it is a [military](#military) craft. Implies [watercraft](#watercraft).

entries.name: sail
entries.description: The sheet of canvas that catches [wind](#wind) to drive a vessel forward, spread from a [mast](#mast) or boom. Tagged for the sail itself, whether bellied out under way or furled against the spar.

entries.name: aircraft_carrier
entries.description: A [warship](#warship) with a long flat deck for [launching](#launching) and recovering aeroplanes, [working](#working) as a [floating](#floating) airbase. It is usually drawn with parked [aircraft](#aircraft) and an [island](#island) superstructure to one side.

entries.name: sailboat
entries.description: A small wind-driven craft, usually [carrying](#carrying) one [mast](#mast) and a [couple](#couple) of sails. Bigger multi-masted vessels belong under [sailing_ship](#sailing_ship).

entries.name: rowboat
entries.description: A small open [boat](#boat) for a handful of [people](#people), moved with oars and fitted with [plank](#plank) seats across the hull. Seen on lakes, [park](#park) ponds and [drifting](#drifting) scenes.

entries.name: ship's_wheel
entries.description: The traditional spoked wooden [helm](#helm) of a sailing vessel, gripped by handles projecting past the rim. A [boat](#boat) with a car-style [wheel](#wheel) instead takes the [plain](#plain) [steering_wheel](#steering_wheel) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: banana_boat
entries.description: An inflatable yellow float shaped like a [giant](#giant) [banana](#banana), straddled by riders and towed across the [water](#water) behind a motorboat. Do not add banana unless real [fruit](#fruit) is in the picture as [well](#well).

entries.name: pirate_ship
entries.description: A sailing vessel rigged out for piracy, typically a [heavy](#heavy) square-rigged galleon bristling with [cannon](#cannon). A black [flag](#flag) at the [mast](#mast) is often the giveaway.

entries.name: fleet
entries.description: Several [military](#military) vessels or [aircraft](#aircraft) shown together as one force, often in formation on the [water](#water) or in the [sky](#sky).

entries.name: destroyer
entries.description: A fast mid-sized [warship](#warship) built for escort, [torpedo](#torpedo) work and patrol, smaller than a [cruiser](#cruiser) and larger than a frigate. A regular presence in naval and warship-girl subjects.

entries.name: shipwreck
entries.description: What remains of a vessel that sank or ran aground: a hull [broken](#broken) on rocks, a rusting hulk on the seabed, or [ribs](#ribs) half-buried in [sand](#sand).

entries.name: gondola
entries.description: The long narrow Venetian [boat](#boat), flat-bottomed and slightly asymmetric, pushed along by one rower [standing](#standing) at the stern. The curved metal ornament at the prow is its most recognisable feature.

entries.name: raft
entries.description: A flat [platform](#platform) that floats without a hull, kept [afloat](#afloat) by lashed logs, sealed drums, or inflated chambers. Usually paddled or poled rather than driven by an [engine](#engine); not to be [confused](#confused) with an inflatable swim [ring](#ring).

entries.name: cruiser
entries.description: A [warship](#warship) larger than a [destroyer](#destroyer) and smaller than a [battleship](#battleship), built to range far on its own. The [heavy](#heavy) and light types of the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries are what usually get drawn.

entries.name: jet_ski
entries.description: A small powered [watercraft](#watercraft) straddled and steered by handlebars like a [motorcycle](#motorcycle), seating one or two. It is usually drawn [kicking](#kicking) up spray as it crosses open [water](#water).

entries.name: sailing_ship
entries.description: A large vessel driven by canvas, generally with two or more masts and full [standing](#standing) [rigging](#rigging). A single-masted little [boat](#boat) is a [sailboat](#sailboat) instead.

entries.name: ship_deck
entries.description: The open top surface of a [boat](#boat) or [ship](#ship), with railings, [rigging](#rigging) or [gun](#gun) mounts around it, where a scene plays out above the waterline.

entries.name: shroud_(sailing)
entries.description: Standing [rigging](#rigging) [running](#running) from a sailing ship's [mast](#mast) down to the hull's sides, keeping the mast upright. Crossed with [rope](#rope) rungs, it doubles as a [ladder](#ladder) for crew [climbing](#climbing) aloft.

entries.name: canoe
entries.description: A slim open [boat](#boat) pointed at both ends, driven by paddlers who kneel or sit and work a single-bladed [paddle](#paddle) facing forward. Seen on rivers, lakes and calm coastal [water](#water).

entries.name: cart
entries.description: A wheeled vehicle for hauling goods, pushed or pulled by a person or an [animal](#animal): handcarts, pullcarts, [shopping](#shopping) trolleys. One built to carry passengers is a [carriage](#carriage), and the small motorised sort is a [go-kart](#go-kart).

entries.name: wheelbarrow
entries.description: A single-wheeled hand [cart](#cart) with two rear handles for moving loads short distances, common in [gardening](#gardening) and [construction](#construction) work.

entries.name: shopping_cart
entries.description: The wheeled [wire](#wire) trolley pushed around a [supermarket](#supermarket), with a deep [basket](#basket) and often a fold-down [child](#child) seat near the [handle](#handle).

entries.name: sleigh
entries.description: A large open vehicle on runners, pulled by horses or [reindeer](#reindeer) across [snow](#snow) and [ice](#ice), built to carry passengers rather than freight. A smaller hand-pulled version is a [sled](#sled).

entries.name: carriage
entries.description: A wheeled vehicle built to carry [people](#people), drawn by animals or pulled by a person, from a [horse](#horse) [coach](#coach) to a rickshaw. A vehicle meant for goods is a [cart](#cart).

entries.name: in_shopping_cart
entries.description: A character [riding](#riding) in a [supermarket](#supermarket) trolley, [sitting](#sitting) in the [basket](#basket) where the [groceries](#groceries) belong. Somebody else generally pushes.

entries.name: sled
entries.description: A small runner-mounted [platform](#platform) hauled by hand or by animals to move [people](#people) or cargo over [snow](#snow). Flat-bottomed versions without runners are toboggans; the larger horse- or reindeer-drawn kind belongs under [sleigh](#sleigh) instead.

entries.name: wagon
entries.description: A four-wheeled [cart](#cart) with [no](#no) [engine](#engine), from [heavy](#heavy) ones drawn by animals to small handcarts pushed along. A version built purely to seat [people](#people) is a [carriage](#carriage) instead.

entries.name: pullcart
entries.description: A two-wheeled open [cart](#cart) hauled from the front by a person or [animal](#animal), with long shafts that keep the puller clear of the load. Larger than a [pushcart](#pushcart); one built to carry passengers instead is a [carriage](#carriage).

entries.name: unconventional_vehicle
entries.description: A means of transport that fits none of the usual categories, whether improvised, absurd or invented purely for the setting. If a proper [tag](#tag) already exists for the [machine](#machine), this is not the one to use.

entries.name: stroller
entries.description: A wheeled pushchair for [carrying](#carrying) a [baby](#baby), steered from behind by whoever is [pushing](#pushing) it. Also called a pram or a buggy.

entries.name: pushcart
entries.description: A small open [cart](#cart) shoved along from behind, with short handles, [running](#running) on two or more wheels. A bigger, longer-handled version is a [pullcart](#pullcart); a single-wheeled one is a [wheelbarrow](#wheelbarrow).

entries.name: chariot
entries.description: A light two-wheeled [cart](#cart) pulled by horses and driven [standing](#standing) up, used in ancient warfare and [racing](#racing). Mythological figures also ride them across the [sky](#sky).

entries.name: vending_cart
entries.description: A wheeled stall for selling [food](#food) or goods in the [street](#street). The small kind used for [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) or [hot](#hot) dogs is pushed by hand, while larger versions have room for a vendor inside and are pulled.

entries.name: minecart
entries.description: A small open [wagon](#wagon) [running](#running) on rails, used to haul ore out of a mine, built from wood and steel on four wheels. Characters ride in it about as often as they load it with cargo.

entries.name: platform_truck
entries.description: A small four-wheeled hand [cart](#cart) with a flat deck and an upright push [handle](#handle), used to move [heavy](#heavy) loads. Without the handle, the same flat wheeled base is a dolly instead.

entries.name: stuffed_toy
entries.description: A soft [toy](#toy) sewn from [fabric](#fabric) and filled with batting, [beans](#beans) or cotton. Covers animals, character dolls and plush objects alike; use [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal) specifically when it depicts a [creature](#creature).

entries.name: stuffed_animal
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like an [animal](#animal) or [creature](#creature): teddy bears, bunnies, penguins and the like. Implies [stuffed_toy](#stuffed_toy); add the specific kind, such as [stuffed_rabbit](#stuffed_rabbit), alongside it.

entries.name: ball
entries.description: A round object of [no](#no) stated purpose, or one that no more specific [tag](#tag) covers. Where it is plainly a named sports ball or [toy](#toy), a [beachball](#beachball) or a [basketball](#basketball), use that instead or as [well](#well).

entries.name: doll
entries.description: A small [figure](#figure) of a person or humanlike being made for play or [display](#display), in plastic, wood, [cloth](#cloth) or rubber. A living character built with visible [ball](#ball) [joints](#joints) is [doll_joints](#doll_joints).

entries.name: teddy_bear
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like a [bear](#bear), held, hugged, or [sitting](#sitting) on a [shelf](#shelf). The classic [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal); a character [holding](#holding) one also gets [holding_stuffed_toy](#holding_stuffed_toy).

entries.name: character_doll
entries.description: A [doll](#doll) made in the likeness of a human character, held or set out as an object. Plush animals are stuffed toys, and a living doll-sized person is [minigirl](#minigirl) or [miniboy](#miniboy).

entries.name: beachball
entries.description: A big light inflatable [ball](#ball) in bright panels, sometimes printed to look like a [watermelon](#watermelon), batted about at the [beach](#beach) or [pool](#pool). It is also the classic prop for covering a [nude](#nude) character as a joke.

entries.name: stuffed_rabbit
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like a [rabbit](#rabbit) or bunny, a common companion for [child](#child) characters. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: playing_card
entries.description: Cards from a standard fifty-two [card](#card) deck of hearts, spades, clubs and diamonds, with or without jokers. Tag a visible face such as [ace_of_spades](#ace_of_spades) when it [can](#can) be read.

entries.name: chess_piece
entries.description: One or more of the pieces used in [chess](#chess), [king](#king), [queen](#queen), [knight](#knight), pawn and the rest, on a board, held in a hand, or scattered loose. A game actually being played takes chess as [well](#well).

entries.name: water_gun
entries.description: A [toy](#toy) [gun](#gun) that squirts [water](#water), from a small pistol to a pump-action soaker. A [summer](#summer) play object rather than a [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: trading_card
entries.description: A collectible [card](#card), whether a real sports card or one from a trading card game such as Magic or Yu-Gi-Oh. Add [card_game](#card_game) when the cards are actually being played rather than just displayed.

entries.name: snowman
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) built from stacked snowballs, typically two or three, dressed up with a [hat](#hat), [coal](#coal) eyes, a [carrot](#carrot) [nose](#nose), a [scarf](#scarf), and [twig](#twig) arms. Any other shape of [snow](#snow) art falls under [snow_sculpture](#snow_sculpture).

entries.name: figure
entries.description: A small [statue](#statue) of a character present as an object in the picture, from a scale figure to a poseable or chibi-styled one. It depicts a collectible rather than the character living in the scene.

entries.name: rubber_duck
entries.description: A small yellow rubber [duck](#duck) [bath](#bath) [toy](#toy), [floating](#floating) in the tub or [sitting](#sitting) by the [sink](#sink). Common in [bathing](#bathing) scenes.

entries.name: toy
entries.description: A plaything present in the scene, whether a [model](#model), a trinket or a small gadget. Use a more specific [tag](#tag) where one exists, such as [stuffed_toy](#stuffed_toy) or [toy_car](#toy_car); a [sex](#sex) toy is tagged separately as [sex_toy](#sex_toy).

entries.name: stuffed_cat
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like a [cat](#cat). Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: puppet
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) or wooden [figure](#figure) worked by a performer, either slipped over the hand like a glove or worked from above on strings. A string-operated one also takes [marionette](#marionette); a few puppets, like Pinocchio, have their own character tags.

entries.name: dice
entries.description: Throwable cubes or polyhedra marked with numbers, used in games and [gambling](#gambling), from the everyday six-sider to the four, eight, twelve and twenty-sided kinds. The [tag](#tag) serves whatever number of them are present.

entries.name: inflatable_toy
entries.description: Any air-filled [beach](#beach) or [pool](#pool) [toy](#toy), generally moulded as a [shark](#shark), [crocodile](#crocodile), [flamingo](#flamingo) or other [creature](#creature). Swim rings, inflatable rafts and beach balls have tags of their own.

entries.name: board_game
entries.description: A game played with pieces moved across a board by rules, [dice](#dice) or cards, either mid-play or laid out ready. Name the particular game as [well](#well) when it [can](#can) be recognised.

entries.name: ace_(playing_card)
entries.description: A [playing](#playing) [card](#card) showing an ace, the rank that counts as either the highest or the lowest in most games. Narrow it down with [ace_of_hearts](#ace_of_hearts), [ace_of_spades](#ace_of_spades) and their [siblings](#siblings) where the [suit](#suit) is visible.

entries.name: stuffed_shark
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like a [shark](#shark), such as the widely-owned IKEA one. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: tree_swing
entries.description: A seat or tyre hung by a [rope](#rope) from a [tree](#tree) [branch](#branch). Usually found [outdoors](#outdoors) in a [garden](#garden) or [meadow](#meadow), with someone [swinging](#swinging) on it or simply perched still.

entries.name: hand_puppet
entries.description: A [puppet](#puppet) slipped over the hand and worked from inside, so the fingers give it a moving mouth or arms. A [figure](#figure) made by the bare hands alone is a [shadow_puppet](#shadow_puppet).

entries.name: cat_teaser
entries.description: A [wand](#wand) [toy](#toy) for [playing](#playing) with cats, tipped with [feathers](#feathers), [beads](#beads) or a [bell](#bell) and dangled in front of the [animal](#animal). Cat girls get teased with it too; the marsh [plant](#plant) of a similar name is a [cattail](#cattail).

entries.name: mahjong_tile
entries.description: Thick blocky [tiles](#tiles) marked with circles, [bamboo](#bamboo), characters, winds or dragons. Use it where the tiles are visible as objects, in a hand, on the [table](#table) or built into a wall.

entries.name: party_popper
entries.description: A small handheld [cracker](#cracker) that bangs and throws [confetti](#confetti) or [streamers](#streamers) when its [string](#string) is yanked. It appears at celebrations and, despite the charge inside, is not counted as a firework.

entries.name: model
entries.description: A scaled-down [car](#car), [train](#train), [ship](#ship), [aircraft](#aircraft) or [building](#building), either played with or set out as a collector's piece. Miniatures of [people](#people), characters or [mecha](#mecha) are figures instead.

entries.name: daruma_doll
entries.description: A round, hollow, usually red Japanese [doll](#doll) [standing](#standing) for perseverance and good luck, and a common [gift](#gift) of encouragement. Its eyes start blank: one is painted in when a wish is made and the second when it comes true.

entries.name: puppet_strings
entries.description: The cords [running](#running) from a [marionette](#marionette) up to a control bar or a set of rings. Often drawn attached to an ordinary person rather than a [doll](#doll), as a visual metaphor for someone else [pulling](#pulling) the strings.

entries.name: yo-yo
entries.description: A [toy](#toy) of two discs on an axle with a wound [string](#string), thrown down and reeled [back](#back) into the hand. Add [holding](#holding) or [playing](#playing) when it is in use.

entries.name: pinwheel
entries.description: A child's [toy](#toy) [windmill](#windmill), [paper](#paper) or plastic blades [pinned](#pinned) to a [stick](#stick) so they spin in the [wind](#wind) or when carried along. Summer and [festival](#festival) scenes use it.

entries.name: ace_of_hearts
entries.description: The ace of the hearts [suit](#suit), a single [heart](#heart) pip on its face. It is a common prop in [card](#card) scenes and a favourite decorative motif.

entries.name: snowball
entries.description: A packed [ball](#ball) of [snow](#snow), thrown in play or stacked to build a [snowman](#snowman). Not the sexual practice, which has its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: sand_sculpture
entries.description: Any shaped object built from [sand](#sand) that is not a [castle](#castle), from animals to buildings. Castles have their own [tag](#tag), [sand_castle](#sand_castle).

entries.name: rook_(chess)
entries.description: The [chess](#chess) piece shaped like a [castle](#castle) [tower](#tower), moving in straight lines across the board.

entries.name: bishop_(chess)
entries.description: The [chess](#chess) piece topped with a slit [mitre](#mitre), the one that runs any distance along the diagonals. Use it where the piece itself is in view; a character merely dressed as a clergyman is something else.

entries.name: queen_(chess)
entries.description: The [chess](#chess) piece topped with a small [spiked](#spiked) [crown](#crown), representing the game's most powerful piece, able to move any number of squares in any direction. Shown on a board, held, or used as a decorative motif.

entries.name: king_(chess)
entries.description: The [chess](#chess) [king](#king), known by the small [cross](#cross) [standing](#standing) on top of its [crown](#crown). Trapping it ends the game, and it is often drawn as a symbol of a leader.

entries.name: crane_game
entries.description: An [arcade](#arcade) [cabinet](#cabinet) in which a player steers a mechanical claw over a heap of prizes, mostly plush toys. Characters are often shown trying their luck at one on a date or in an arcade.

entries.name: merchandise
entries.description: Products tied to a media franchise appearing in the picture - figures, plushies, posters, keychains or packaged goods - often modeled on real items. A character may hold goods from their own series or from another as a visual [easter](#easter) [egg](#egg).

entries.name: ace_of_spades
entries.description: The ace of spades, whose single pip is traditionally drawn far more ornately than the [plain](#plain) number cards. It carries an outlaw or gambler connotation wherever it appears.

entries.name: floating_card
entries.description: A [playing](#playing) [card](#card) or other card suspended, [flying](#flying) or [falling](#falling) through the air, for whatever reason. Common around card-themed magicians and gamblers.

entries.name: sand_castle
entries.description: A [castle](#castle) built out of [sand](#sand), the classic beach-day creation. Tagged with [sand_sculpture](#sand_sculpture).

entries.name: stuffed_winged_unicorn
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) of a winged [unicorn](#unicorn), a horse-like [creature](#creature) [carrying](#carrying) both [wings](#wings) and a horn.

entries.name: snow_rabbit
entries.description: A small [rabbit](#rabbit) shaped out of packed [snow](#snow), with leaves [standing](#standing) in for ears and berries or pebbles for eyes, a traditional Japanese [winter](#winter) craft.

entries.name: mannequin
entries.description: A life-sized [dummy](#dummy) of a body or part of one, used to fit or [display](#display) [clothes](#clothes). A [doll](#doll) character with a personality of its own is something else.

entries.name: stuffed_penguin
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like a [penguin](#penguin). Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: stuffed_dog
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) in the shape of a [dog](#dog), from floppy-eared puppies to shiba-styled ones. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: model_kit
entries.description: Parts on sprues that the buyer clips out and assembles into a finished [model](#model) or [figure](#figure). Covers both the unbuilt runners in the [box](#box) and someone at a [table](#table) putting the pieces together.

entries.name: chessboard
entries.description: A [square](#square) [playing](#playing) surface of sixty-four squares in two alternating colours, used for [chess](#chess) and draughts. Artists also press one into service as a graphic [floor](#floor) or [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: super_soaker
entries.description: A large pressurised [water](#water) [gun](#gun) with a bulky reservoir and, usually, a [pump](#pump) [handle](#handle) for [building](#building) up pressure. Bright plastic colours and an oversized [silhouette](#silhouette) set it apart from a small squirt gun.

entries.name: knight_(chess)
entries.description: The [chess](#chess) piece carved as a horse's head. It jumps in an L-shaped step and lands on the opposite colour each move, which is why it stands for unpredictability.

entries.name: stuffed_unicorn
entries.description: A plush [unicorn](#unicorn), a pony-like body with a single horn on the [forehead](#forehead), often pastel-coloured with a [rainbow](#rainbow) [mane](#mane).

entries.name: stuffed_panda
entries.description: A plush [giant](#giant) [panda](#panda) in the [familiar](#familiar) black and white, usually rounded and shown [sitting](#sitting). Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: pawn_(chess)
entries.description: The smallest [chess](#chess) piece, a [plain](#plain) stem topped with a [ball](#ball). Shown [standing](#standing) on a board, pinched between fingers, or used as visual shorthand for somebody expendable.

entries.name: temari_ball
entries.description: A [ball](#ball) wound from coloured [thread](#thread) into geometric patterns, made both as ornament and as a traditional Japanese [toy](#toy). Held, bounced, or set out purely as decoration.

entries.name: snow_globe
entries.description: A sealed [glass](#glass) or plastic [dome](#dome) [holding](#holding) a [miniature](#miniature) scene in [liquid](#liquid), with pale flecks that [swirl](#swirl) like a [snowstorm](#snowstorm) when shaken. Its flat base and enclosed scene set it apart from a [plain](#plain) [crystal](#crystal) [ball](#ball).

entries.name: rattle
entries.description: A baby's handheld [toy](#toy) that clatters when shaken, usually a small perforated [ball](#ball) or [ring](#ring) fixed to a short [handle](#handle). Appears in nursery scenes and in the hands of infant characters.

entries.name: joker_(playing_card)
entries.description: The odd [card](#card) of a deck, printed with a [jester](#jester) and belonging to [no](#no) [suit](#suit) and no rank. It often stands by itself for trickery or [blind](#blind) luck.

entries.name: inflatable_whale
entries.description: An air-filled [pool](#pool) [toy](#toy) shaped like a [whale](#whale), usually blue with a rounded body. It is ridden or leaned on in the [water](#water).

entries.name: rubik's_cube
entries.description: The twisting [cube](#cube) [puzzle](#puzzle) of coloured stickers, solved when each face shows a single colour. It stands in for cleverness, boredom or frustration depending on how it is held.

entries.name: stuffed_frog
entries.description: A plush [frog](#frog), green and round with wide eyes set on top of the head. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: slide
entries.description: Playground equipment with a smooth ramp that children climb up and glide down. It usually appears alongside swings and [climbing](#climbing) frames in [park](#park) scenes; for the act of [sliding](#sliding) across any surface, use sliding.

entries.name: stuffed_bird
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) made in the shape of a [bird](#bird), from a round little [chick](#chick) to a long-necked crane. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: hanafuda
entries.description: Japanese [flower](#flower) cards: forty-eight small stiff cards illustrated with plants, birds and moons, twelve suits for the twelve months. They turn up fanned in the hand, spread on a [mat](#mat) for a matching game, or as a motif on other objects.

entries.name: water_yoyo
entries.description: A little [water](#water) [balloon](#balloon) on an elastic [string](#string), bounced from a fingertip. They are won by hooking them out of a tub at Japanese [summer](#summer) festivals.

entries.name: puzzle_piece
entries.description: A single interlocking fragment of a jigsaw, complete with its knobs and sockets. Often used as a visual metaphor for something missing or finally fitting into place.

entries.name: kite
entries.description: A light frame covered with [paper](#paper) or [cloth](#cloth) and flown on a [string](#string) in the [wind](#wind). It appears aloft in the [sky](#sky) or held ready on the ground, and Japanese pictures often use the rectangular New Year sort.

entries.name: star_balloon
entries.description: An inflated [balloon](#balloon) cut into the shape of a five-pointed star, usually shiny foil. Party and [festival](#festival) decoration.

entries.name: stuffed_whale
entries.description: A plush [whale](#whale), a large rounded body ending in a broad [tail](#tail) fluke.

entries.name: stuffed_sheep
entries.description: A plush [sheep](#sheep) covered in curly white fleece with a [dark](#dark) face and [legs](#legs). Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: marionette
entries.description: A jointed [puppet](#puppet) worked from above by strings [running](#running) up to a control bar in the puppeteer's hand. Implies puppet.

entries.name: queen_(playing_card)
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) ranked between the jack and the [king](#king), the middle of the three court cards. Its face traditionally shows a crowned woman drawn in [profile](#profile) or mirrored top to bottom.

entries.name: stuffed_fish
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like a [fish](#fish), whether a [koi](#koi), a [tuna](#tuna) or a rounded cartoon design. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: puzzle
entries.description: Any kind of puzzle appears as an object or activity, from jigsaws to twisting mechanical puzzles and interlocking rings. For a single loose jigsaw fragment, [puzzle_piece](#puzzle_piece) is the more precise [tag](#tag).

entries.name: stuffing
entries.description: The soft springy filling packed inside plush toys and dolls, usually shown escaping through a [torn](#torn) seam or [lying](#lying) loose beside a burst [toy](#toy).

entries.name: marble_(toy)
entries.description: Small [heavy](#heavy) [glass](#glass) spheres with coloured swirls set inside, played with as toys or held up to catch the light. Often shown in a [jar](#jar) or scattered across a [floor](#floor).

entries.name: stuffed_lion
entries.description: A plush [lion](#lion), golden with a shaggy [ring](#ring) of [mane](#mane) framing the face. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: water_balloon
entries.description: A rubber [balloon](#balloon) filled with [water](#water), ready to burst on impact. Summer play, festivals and pranks supply the usual context.

entries.name: inflatable_orca
entries.description: An air-filled [pool](#pool) [toy](#toy) shaped like a killer [whale](#whale), black above and white below. It is usually straddled in the [water](#water).

entries.name: power-up
entries.description: A collectible game item that grants a new ability or a boost, drawn as a [floating](#floating) icon, capsule or [fruit](#fruit). Shown hovering in place or in the moment of being grabbed.

entries.name: king_(playing_card)
entries.description: The highest of the three court cards, ranking above the [queen](#queen) and the jack and showing a crowned monarch. One appears in each of the four suits.

entries.name: stuffed_octopus
entries.description: A plush [octopus](#octopus), a round head above a [ring](#ring) of soft [dangling](#dangling) arms, often the reversible sort that flips between two faces. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: ace_of_diamonds
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing one large diamond pip. It may be held, thrown or used as decoration; the [baseball](#baseball) manga [sharing](#sharing) the name is unrelated.

entries.name: yellow_innertube
entries.description: A yellow inflatable [ring](#ring) of the kind used to float at a [pool](#pool) or [beach](#beach). Usually worn around the waist or tucked under one arm.

entries.name: toy_hammer
entries.description: A soft, oversized [mallet](#mallet) with a squeaky head, swung for [comic](#comic) effect in [gag](#gag) scenes. Nicknamed the piko piko [hammer](#hammer) after the [sound](#sound) it makes on impact.

entries.name: stuffed_eggplant
entries.description: An eggplant-shaped plush or [cushion](#cushion), deep purple with a green cap, a novelty [toy](#toy) rather than an [animal](#animal).

entries.name: inflatable_dolphin
entries.description: An air-filled [pool](#pool) [toy](#toy) shaped like a [dolphin](#dolphin), ridden or clung to in the [water](#water). Poolside and [beach](#beach) pictures are its home.

entries.name: block_(object)
entries.description: A cube-shaped object, [standing](#standing) alone or stacked into something larger. It covers children's [building](#building) bricks, stacking-tower pieces and the terrain cubes of certain games.

entries.name: uno_(game)
entries.description: The colour-and-number [card](#card) game in which players empty their hand by matching the top of the discard [pile](#pile), with special cards that reverse turn order or force opponents to draw. Recognisable by its bright red, yellow, green and blue deck.

entries.name: bubble_pipe
entries.description: A [toy](#toy) shaped like a [smoking](#smoking) pipe that puffs [soap](#soap) bubbles from its [bowl](#bowl). A loop on a [stick](#stick) is a [bubble_wand](#bubble_wand) instead.

entries.name: ace_of_clubs
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) a single large club pip. It turns up in card games, conjuring tricks and as a motif printed on clothing or props.

entries.name: gashapon
entries.description: The capsule-toy [machine](#machine) with its crank, the rounded plastic capsule it drops, or the little [toy](#toy) inside. The name copies the [sound](#sound) of the crank turning and the capsule [falling](#falling).

entries.name: go_(board_game)
entries.description: The game of black and white stones set on the intersections of a ruled board, each side trying to surround more territory. Known as weiqi in Chinese and baduk in Korean.

entries.name: twister
entries.description: The [party](#party) game played on a [mat](#mat) of coloured [spots](#spots), where a spinner dictates which hand or foot goes where. The comedy lies in the tangled heap of limbs players end up in trying not to fall.

entries.name: toy_gun
entries.description: A gun-shaped plaything, whether a [cork](#cork) shooter, pellet [gun](#gun), [water](#water) pistol or [flag](#flag) popper. Bright plastic colouring or a harmless projectile gives away that it is not a real firearm.

entries.name: stuffed_carrot
entries.description: A carrot-shaped plush, orange with a leafy green top, made as a [toy](#toy) or a long [cushion](#cushion). Turns up most often beside rabbit-themed and horse-themed characters.

entries.name: hina_ningyou
entries.description: The ornamental [doll](#doll) set of the Japanese Girls' Day [festival](#festival): emperor, empress, attendants and musicians in Heian court [dress](#dress), ranged on a tiered stand. It also covers characters dressed up as any of those figures.

entries.name: stuffed_dolphin
entries.description: A plush [dolphin](#dolphin), smooth grey above and pale below with a long [snout](#snout), typical of [aquarium](#aquarium) [gift](#gift) shops. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: hula_hoop
entries.description: A large plastic [ring](#ring) kept [spinning](#spinning) around the waist, arms or [neck](#neck) by [swinging](#swinging) the body. It may be mid-spin, held in the hands or slung over a shoulder.

entries.name: jigsaw_puzzle
entries.description: A picture cut into interlocking irregular pieces to be fitted [back](#back) together, shown as loose pieces, a half-built board or a finished panel. A single missing piece is a [standing](#standing) visual joke.

entries.name: tenbou
entries.description: The slim scoring sticks used to track points and riichi declarations in [mahjong](#mahjong), marked with coloured bands along their length. They lie beside the [tiles](#tiles) on the [table](#table).

entries.name: string_phone
entries.description: Two [paper](#paper) cups or tin cans joined by a taut [string](#string) and spoken into as a [toy](#toy) telephone. A children's game played between two [people](#people) a short way apart.

entries.name: toy_car
entries.description: A [miniature](#miniature) [car](#car), from a pocket-sized die-cast [model](#model) to a detailed [display](#display) piece, pushed along the [floor](#floor) or held up for the [camera](#camera). Scale and detail vary widely.

entries.name: kendama
entries.description: A wooden [toy](#toy) made of a [spiked](#spiked) [handle](#handle) with two shallow cups and a [ball](#ball) tied to it by a [string](#string). The ball is swung up and [caught](#caught) in a [cup](#cup) or spiked through its [hole](#hole) in a run of tricks.

entries.name: jack_(playing_card)
entries.description: The court [card](#card) ranking between the ten and the [queen](#queen), lowest of the three face cards. It shows a young retainer rather than a crowned [ruler](#ruler), and is also called the knave.

entries.name: character_snowman
entries.description: A [snowman](#snowman) built to resemble a particular character, given the right hair, colours or props out of twigs and [cloth](#cloth). The [snow](#snow) equivalent of a character [doll](#doll).

entries.name: green_innertube
entries.description: A green inflatable [ring](#ring) of the kind floated on at a [pool](#pool) or [beach](#beach). It may be worn around the waist, sat inside, or carried under an arm.

entries.name: shogi_piece
entries.description: One of the flat, five-sided [tiles](#tiles) used in [shogi](#shogi), its rank written in kanji. Since every piece looks alike, the direction it points shows which player owns it. Implies shogi.

entries.name: slot_machine
entries.description: A coin-fed [gambling](#gambling) [cabinet](#cabinet) with [spinning](#spinning) reels of symbols and a side [lever](#lever) or button. Matching combinations pay out, which makes it a fixture of [casino](#casino) and [arcade](#arcade) scenes.

entries.name: frisbee
entries.description: A plastic [flying](#flying) disc roughly a hand-span across, spun off the fingers so that it glides. Drawn in flight, being [caught](#caught), or simply carried along at a [park](#park) or a [beach](#beach).

entries.name: toy_block
entries.description: Wooden or plastic [building](#building) blocks in simple [shapes](#shapes) and bright colours, stacked into towers during play. Their faces often carry printed letters or numbers, and small children are the usual users.

entries.name: paper_doll
entries.description: A flat printed [figure](#figure) with separate outfits that stay on by folding [paper](#paper) tabs over its edges. Drawn either as the sheet of [clothes](#clothes) or as the [doll](#doll) being dressed.

entries.name: miniature
entries.description: A faithful small-scale replica of something larger, whether a [model](#model) [building](#building), vehicle or [figure](#figure). The reduction in size compared to the real thing is the whole point of it.

entries.name: stuffed_tiger
entries.description: A plush [tiger](#tiger), orange with black stripes and a white muzzle. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: sentient_stuffed_toy
entries.description: Plush toys behaving as if alive: [walking](#walking), [flying](#flying), or reacting to what goes on around them, whether by their own will or wound-up [clockwork](#clockwork). Not for a person in an [animal](#animal) [costume](#costume), and not for sexual use of a plush.

entries.name: stuffed_dinosaur
entries.description: A plush [dinosaur](#dinosaur), often a green long-necked sort or a stubby tyrannosaur with soft felt [teeth](#teeth).

entries.name: toy_airplane
entries.description: A small [model](#model) [aircraft](#aircraft), held aloft mid-flight in play or [standing](#standing) on a [shelf](#shelf) as a [display](#display) piece. Distinct from a full-size vehicle or a real aircraft.

entries.name: stuffed_orca
entries.description: A plush killer [whale](#whale), black above and white below with the pale eye patches that make the species recognizable.

entries.name: 1up
entries.description: A pickup that hands the player another life, drawn as an item or as an on-screen icon. Games render it differently, from a [mushroom](#mushroom) to a small labelled [square](#square).

entries.name: matryoshka_doll
entries.description: A set of painted wooden Russian dolls of decreasing size nested one inside the next. Usually shown lined up by size or partway through being taken apart.

entries.name: kokeshi
entries.description: A simple lathe-turned wooden [doll](#doll) from northern Japan: a cylindrical body under a round head, with a painted face and [no](#no) arms or [legs](#legs). It is sold widely as a regional souvenir.

entries.name: spinning_top
entries.description: A [toy](#toy) with a pointed base that stays upright while spun rapidly, from a simple wooden shape twirled by hand or [string](#string) to elaborate battling versions.

entries.name: queen_of_hearts_(playing_card)
entries.description: The heart-suited [queen](#queen) [card](#card), pictured [holding](#holding) a [flower](#flower) and ranking second among the [heart](#heart) court cards. A recurring motif in Alice-themed artwork as [well](#well) as an ordinary [playing](#playing) card.
