entries.name: poi_(goldfish_scoop)
entries.description: The flimsy scoop used at [festival](#festival) [goldfish](#goldfish) stalls, a thin sheet of [paper](#paper) stretched over a round plastic [hoop](#hoop) with a grip. It [tears](#tears) as soon as it gets [wet](#wet), which is the whole game.

entries.name: stuffed_fox
entries.description: A plush [fox](#fox), orange with white cheeks, chest and [tail](#tail) tip, a favourite prop for fox-themed characters.

entries.name: inflatable_shark
entries.description: An air-filled [pool](#pool) [toy](#toy) shaped like a [shark](#shark), fin and open jaws included. It floats in pools and at the [beach](#beach).

entries.name: action_figure
entries.description: A posable plastic [toy](#toy) of a character from a game, [comic](#comic), film or show. Cheaper and simpler than a collector's [figure](#figure), since it is built to be played with.

entries.name: stuffed_dragon
entries.description: A plush [dragon](#dragon) with soft [wings](#wings), [horns](#horns) and a [tail](#tail), drawn rounder and friendlier than the real [creature](#creature). Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: stuffed_pig
entries.description: A plush [pig](#pig), pink and round with a flat [snout](#snout) and small ears. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: party_horn
entries.description: A rolled [paper](#paper) noisemaker that shoots straight and squeaks when blown, then curls [back](#back) up again. Frequently gripped in the [teeth](#teeth) at a [celebration](#celebration); also called a [party](#party) blower.

entries.name: duck_innertube
entries.description: A swim [ring](#ring) moulded as a [duck](#duck), its head and bill rising at the front. Worn round the waist or left bobbing in a [pool](#pool).

entries.name: polka_dot_innertube
entries.description: An inflatable swim [ring](#ring) [patterned](#patterned) with round [dots](#dots). Worn around the waist or [floating](#floating) beside its owner at the [pool](#pool) or [beach](#beach).

entries.name: bubble_wand
entries.description: A slim rod ending in a loop, dipped in [soap](#soap) solution and blown through to make bubbles. Not the same as a [bubble_pipe](#bubble_pipe), which is shaped like something you would [smoke](#smoke).

entries.name: roulette
entries.description: The [casino](#casino) [wheel](#wheel) game where a [ball](#ball) drops into one of the [numbered](#numbered) red and black pockets after the wheel is spun. Players bet on single numbers, colours, odds and evens, or ranges of numbers.

entries.name: stuffed_mouse
entries.description: A plush mouse with big round ears and a thin cord [tail](#tail). Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: watermelon_beachball
entries.description: An inflatable [beach](#beach) [ball](#ball) [patterned](#patterned) like the green rind of a [watermelon](#watermelon). A ball with only vague greenish [markings](#markings) doesn't qualify, and a real [melon](#melon) [lying](#lying) nearby isn't this either.

entries.name: pachinko
entries.description: A Japanese pinball-like [machine](#machine) in which steel balls fall through a [field](#field) of pins into catchers, winning more balls to trade for prizes. Many cabinets add [spinning](#spinning) digital reels, and the parlours are drawn loud, bright and [crowded](#crowded).

entries.name: stuffed_duck
entries.description: A plush [duck](#duck), yellow and round with a flat orange bill. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: stuffed_seal
entries.description: A plush seal, pale and smooth with large [dark](#dark) eyes and short [flippers](#flippers).

entries.name: stuffed_wolf
entries.description: A plush [wolf](#wolf), grey with a pale muzzle and chest, sharper-featured and bulkier than a plush [dog](#dog).

entries.name: stuffed_chicken
entries.description: A plush [chicken](#chicken) or hen, round-bodied with a small felt [comb](#comb) and [beak](#beak), a common nursery [toy](#toy).

entries.name: three_of_hearts
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) three [heart](#heart) pips, held in a hand, dealt onto a [table](#table), or shown by itself.

entries.name: balloon_animal
entries.description: A long thin [balloon](#balloon) twisted into the shape of a [dog](#dog), a [sword](#sword) or a [flower](#flower). A balloon simply moulded in an [animal](#animal) shape is a different thing altogether.

entries.name: snow_sculpture
entries.description: Any [figure](#figure) or [structure](#structure) carved and packed out of [snow](#snow) beyond the [plain](#plain) three-ball [snowman](#snowman), from animals to elaborate castles.

entries.name: rocking_horse
entries.description: A child's wooden [horse](#horse) mounted on curved rockers, straddled and rocked as pretend [riding](#riding). Appears in nursery scenes and as a nostalgic prop.

entries.name: king_of_spades
entries.description: The spade-suit [king](#king), shown [holding](#holding) a [sword](#sword) and topping that suit's court cards. One of the four kings in a standard pack.

entries.name: striped_innertube
entries.description: An inflatable ring-shaped float, the kind used at pools and beaches, [patterned](#patterned) with stripes around its circumference.

entries.name: stuffed_horse
entries.description: A plush [horse](#horse) or pony, usually finished with a [yarn](#yarn) [mane](#mane) and [tail](#tail). Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: ten_of_hearts
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) ten [heart](#heart) pips, shown in a fanned hand, laid on a [table](#table), or held up on its own.

entries.name: control_bar
entries.description: The wooden [cross](#cross) a puppeteer holds, with the marionette's strings [hanging](#hanging) from its arms. It turns up wherever puppets and puppet-master imagery are the motif.

entries.name: toy_sword
entries.description: A blunt [sword](#sword) made of wood, plastic or [foam](#foam), swung in play or worn as part of a [costume](#costume). Lacks the edge and [weight](#weight) of a real blade.

entries.name: jenga
entries.description: A [tower](#tower) of stacked wooden blocks, each turn [pulling](#pulling) one out from lower down and setting it on top until the whole thing falls. Pictures usually catch the tense moment of the pull.

entries.name: two_of_hearts
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing two red [heart](#heart) pips. Appears in hands of cards, on tables and as a decorative motif.

entries.name: two_of_spades
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing two black spade pips. Turns up in dealt hands, card tricks and [gambling](#gambling) scenes.

entries.name: deck_of_cards
entries.description: A whole [stack](#stack) of [playing](#playing) cards, boxed, fanned out or squared up on a [table](#table). One or a few loose cards take [playing_card](#playing_card) instead.

entries.name: five_of_hearts
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) five [heart](#heart) pips, seen in card games and in fortune-telling spreads.

entries.name: large_teddy_bear
entries.description: A plush [bear](#bear) far bigger than an ordinary stuffed [toy](#toy), at least as long as a character's arm. Once it reaches human size or beyond, an oversized object [tag](#tag) fits alongside.

entries.name: toy_train
entries.description: A [train](#train) built cheaply and sturdily as a plaything rather than a detailed scale [model](#model). It may simply be pulled along the [floor](#floor) or driven by [clockwork](#clockwork) or a [battery](#battery), with or without track.

entries.name: inflatable_flamingo
entries.description: An air-filled [pool](#pool) [toy](#toy) in the shape of a pink [flamingo](#flamingo), long [neck](#neck) and all. A swim [ring](#ring) or a [raft](#raft) [carrying](#carrying) a flamingo design has its own [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: stuffed_cow
entries.description: A plush [toy](#toy) shaped like a [cow](#cow), usually white with black patches and stubby [horns](#horns).

entries.name: model_ship
entries.description: A [miniature](#miniature) [boat](#boat) or [warship](#warship) built to scale, whether [standing](#standing) on a [display](#display) [cradle](#cradle), sealed inside a [bottle](#bottle) or [floating](#floating) across a [pond](#pond). Rigging and tiny painted crew are part of the appeal.

entries.name: frilled_innertube
entries.description: An inflatable swim [ring](#ring) finished with a gathered [skirt](#skirt) of [fabric](#fabric) around its rim. Turns up in [pool](#pool) and [beach](#beach) scenes, frequently matching the [swimsuit](#swimsuit) of whoever is [holding](#holding) it.

entries.name: three_of_diamonds
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) three diamond pips, held in a hand, dealt onto a [table](#table), or shown by itself.

entries.name: two_of_diamonds
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing two red diamond pips. Usually shown held, dealt or fanned out with other cards.

entries.name: sprue
entries.description: The waste frame from an injection-moulded plastic kit, [holding](#holding) a model's parts together until the builder snips them free. Drawn as a [grid](#grid) of pieces still linked by thin runners.

entries.name: model_tank
entries.description: A scale [miniature](#miniature) of a [tank](#tank), freshly assembled and painted or lined up with others as part of a collection. Often shown among paints, brushes and cut sprues on a workbench.

entries.name: karuta_(card_game)
entries.description: Japanese matching cards spread on the [floor](#floor) and snatched up as a reader calls the lines aloud. It takes in both the hundred-poem set and the simpler proverb set keyed to the syllabary.

entries.name: king_of_hearts_(playing_card)
entries.description: The heart-suit [king](#king), drawn in most decks with a [sword](#sword) raised behind his own head. That pose earned him the nickname of the [suicide](#suicide) king.

entries.name: jack-in-the-box
entries.description: A boxed [toy](#toy) worked by a crank that grinds out a tune and then lets the [lid](#lid) [fly](#fly) open, [launching](#launching) a [puppet](#puppet) on a spring. Artists usually pick the instant of the pop.

entries.name: queen_of_spades
entries.description: The spade-suited [queen](#queen) [card](#card), also shown [holding](#holding) a [flower](#flower) and ranking second among the spade court cards. Distinct from the unrelated queen of spades symbol.

entries.name: five_of_spades
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) five spade pips, drawn in a hand, in a fan of cards or face up on the [table](#table).

entries.name: red_innertube
entries.description: A red inflatable [ring](#ring) used to float in [water](#water), worn around the waist or carried under an arm. A [beach](#beach) and [pool](#pool) [staple](#staple), distinct from a [raft](#raft).

entries.name: acrylic_stand_(object)
entries.description: A flat printed character cutout set in clear plastic and propped upright on a small base. Sold as [merchandise](#merchandise) beside figures, it is usually drawn [standing](#standing) on a [desk](#desk) or [shelf](#shelf).

entries.name: paper_balloon
entries.description: A light inflatable [ball](#ball) glued together from strips of coloured [paper](#paper) and kept up by tapping it. A traditional Japanese children's [toy](#toy), usually placed in [summer](#summer) scenes.

entries.name: ten_of_spades
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) ten spade pips, shown in a fanned hand, dealt onto a [table](#table), or held up alone.

entries.name: three_of_clubs
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) three club pips, held in a hand, dealt onto a [table](#table), or shown by itself.

entries.name: four_of_clubs
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) showing four club pips. It turns up held in a hand, laid on a [table](#table), or worked in as a design motif.

entries.name: character_balloon
entries.description: An inflated [balloon](#balloon) moulded or printed to look like a character, the kind sold at fairs and theme parks. It bobs on a [string](#string) or gets carried about by hand.

entries.name: seesaw
entries.description: A [plank](#plank) balanced on a central pivot with a seat at either end, so two riders take turns shoving off the ground and rising.

entries.name: four_of_hearts
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing four [heart](#heart) pips, seen in a hand, dealt on a [table](#table), or borrowed as a [costume](#costume) motif.

entries.name: seven_of_hearts
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing seven [heart](#heart) pips. Tagged when that particular face is legible in the picture.

entries.name: star_block
entries.description: A block marked with a star on its faces, drawn either as a game object or a child's [building](#building) [toy](#toy). The star is what identifies it.

entries.name: stuffed_reindeer
entries.description: A plush [reindeer](#reindeer) with felt [antlers](#antlers), often part of Christmas decoration. Implies [stuffed_animal](#stuffed_animal).

entries.name: toy_robot
entries.description: A [robot](#robot) built as a plaything rather than a [working](#working) [machine](#machine): a tin windup, a plastic action [figure](#figure) or a small remote-controlled [model](#model). Distinct from a full-scale [mecha](#mecha) or [android](#android).

entries.name: jack_of_spades
entries.description: The jack of the spade [suit](#suit), the court [figure](#figure) set beside a black spade pip. It is one of the four jacks in a standard deck.

entries.name: five_of_diamonds
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) five diamond pips, held, dealt or laid out on a [table](#table).

entries.name: stilts
entries.description: Long poles with footrests strapped to the [legs](#legs), letting the wearer walk high above the ground. Associated with [circus](#circus) performers and [festival](#festival) parades.

entries.name: dummy
entries.description: A life-size human-shaped [model](#model) used for [training](#training), [crash](#crash) testing or [anatomy](#anatomy) reference. Also covers the head-shaped models that [recording](#recording) equipment gets fixed to.

entries.name: three_of_spades
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) three spade pips, held in a hand, dealt onto a [table](#table), or shown by itself.

entries.name: reversi
entries.description: The board game of black and white discs that flip colour when [trapped](#trapped) between opposing pieces, also sold as Othello. Play ends when the board fills, and whichever colour holds the majority wins.

entries.name: house_of_cards
entries.description: Playing cards balanced against one another into a [standing](#standing) [structure](#structure), usually in triangular tiers. Its fragility is normally the point of the picture.

entries.name: stuffed_turtle
entries.description: A plush [turtle](#turtle) with a domed [fabric](#fabric) [shell](#shell) and short soft limbs [poking](#poking) out from beneath it.

entries.name: seven_of_diamonds
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing seven diamond pips. Tagged when that particular face [can](#can) be read in the picture.

entries.name: seven_of_clubs
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) bearing seven club pips. Tagged when that particular face is legible in the picture.

entries.name: five_of_clubs
entries.description: The [playing](#playing) [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) five club pips. It turns up in hands, spreads and card tricks.

entries.name: nutcracker
entries.description: The Christmas [figure](#figure) carved as a stiff [soldier](#soldier) whose [jaw](#jaw) works as a [lever](#lever) [strong](#strong) enough to [crack](#crack) a nut. Nearly always [standing](#standing) about as an ornament rather than being put to work.

entries.name: akabeko
entries.description: A red papier-mache [cow](#cow) from northern Japan whose head nods on a loose [neck](#neck). It turns up as a charm, a souvenir or an ornament on a [shelf](#shelf).

entries.name: radio_controller
entries.description: A handheld transmitter with a visible aerial and joysticks, used to steer [model](#model) cars, boats, and [aircraft](#aircraft) over a [radio](#radio) link. The antenna is what sets it apart from an ordinary game [controller](#controller).

entries.name: grey_innertube
entries.description: A grey inflatable [ring](#ring) for [floating](#floating) on [water](#water). It may be worn around the waist, sat inside or carried.

entries.name: bell
entries.description: A hollow metal bell that rings when struck or shaken, from a small jingle bell on a [collar](#collar) or hair ornament to a [handbell](#handbell) or a great [shrine](#shrine) bell. Narrow it to the specific kind where the picture makes it clear.

entries.name: instrument
entries.description: A musical instrument is in the picture, whether played, carried or simply [lying](#lying) nearby. Add the specific [tag](#tag) too, such as [guitar](#guitar) or [violin](#violin), and use instrument_request when the type cannot be named.

entries.name: guitar
entries.description: A six-string guitar, electric or acoustic, held, played or simply present in the scene. A four-string [bass_guitar](#bass_guitar) is tagged separately, never as a guitar.

entries.name: electric_guitar
entries.description: A slim, solid-bodied [guitar](#guitar) whose [string](#string) vibration is picked up magnetically and sent to an [amplifier](#amplifier), the backbone of [rock](#rock) [music](#music). Often drawn with a flashy cutaway shape and a [cable](#cable) trailing away from it.

entries.name: whistle
entries.description: A small blown noisemaker used by referees, coaches, [police](#police) and in [music](#music). Worn on a [lanyard](#lanyard) it adds [whistle_around_neck](#whistle_around_neck); the act of pursing the [lips](#lips) to [sound](#sound) one is [whistling](#whistling).

entries.name: violin
entries.description: The four-stringed [instrument](#instrument) held under the chin and played with a [bow](#bow), or plucked. Present in the scene whether being played or merely carried; also called a fiddle in folk settings.

entries.name: drum
entries.description: A percussion [instrument](#instrument) built as a hollow cylinder or [bowl](#bowl) with skin stretched over it, struck with hands, sticks or mallets. Covers a taiko, a snare and everything between.

entries.name: flute
entries.description: A tube-shaped [wind](#wind) [instrument](#instrument) in wood or metal, blown across a [hole](#hole) and fingered along its length. The [tag](#tag) [gathers](#gathers) transverse flutes, recorders, ocarinas, shakuhachi and dizi.

entries.name: piano
entries.description: A keyboard [instrument](#instrument) whose felt hammers strike strings, from a grand down to an upright or an electric one. Tag the instrument here and add [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) when a character is at the keys.

entries.name: bass_guitar
entries.description: An electric bass: guitar-shaped but with four thick strings, four tuning pegs and a longer [neck](#neck), its [bridge](#bridge) set [well](#well) down the body. Do not [tag](#tag) it as a [plain](#plain) [guitar](#guitar), and keep the upright bowed [instrument](#instrument) as [double_bass](#double_bass).

entries.name: drumsticks
entries.description: The pair of tapered wooden sticks used to strike drums and other percussion. The name has [no](#no) bearing on [chicken](#chicken) [legs](#legs).

entries.name: instrument_case
entries.description: The rigid or padded case a musical [instrument](#instrument) travels in, shown open or shut. Guitar and [violin](#violin) cases are the usual ones, and they often appear without the instrument in them.

entries.name: plectrum
entries.description: A small flat pick used to strum or pluck a stringed [instrument](#instrument), held between the fingers or shown on its own. Often appears alongside a [guitar](#guitar).

entries.name: keyboard_(instrument)
entries.description: An electronic [instrument](#instrument) with piano-style keys that is not itself a [piano](#piano) — a [synthesizer](#synthesizer), a [stage](#stage) keyboard or a home organ. Use piano for the acoustic instrument.

entries.name: trumpet
entries.description: A brass horn with three valves and a flared [bell](#bell), held to the [lips](#lips) or simply carried. Add [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) when it is actually being played.

entries.name: staff_(music)
entries.description: The five-line musical stave with [notes](#notes) placed along it, drawn as a motif or in a background. Printed on [paper](#paper), the same thing is tagged [sheet_music](#sheet_music).

entries.name: guitar_case
entries.description: A hard or soft case for [carrying](#carrying) a [guitar](#guitar). Add guitar only when the [instrument](#instrument) itself is actually visible.

entries.name: electric_bass_guitar
entries.description: The low-voiced four-string cousin of the [guitar](#guitar), with a long [neck](#neck), a solid body and [no](#no) soundhole, plugged into an [amplifier](#amplifier). Usually slung low across the body in band scenes; the higher, six-stringed version is [electric_guitar](#electric_guitar).

entries.name: bow_(music)
entries.description: The horsehair-strung rod drawn across the strings of a [violin](#violin), viola, [cello](#cello) or double bass to [sound](#sound) them. Name the [instrument](#instrument) it belongs to, and [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) when it is in use.

entries.name: drum_set
entries.description: A kit of bass [drum](#drum), toms, snare, hi-hat and [cymbals](#cymbals) arranged so a single player [can](#can) reach them all. The band-stage percussion setup.

entries.name: sheet_music
entries.description: Printed musical notation on [paper](#paper), whether held, [resting](#resting) on a stand or [lying](#lying) about. Notes [floating](#floating) without any paper behind them take [staff_(music)](#staff_(music)) instead.

entries.name: grand_piano
entries.description: A [piano](#piano) whose strings and soundboard lie flat beneath a [lid](#lid) propped open, the whole body carried on three [legs](#legs). An upright [standing](#standing) against a wall is not one.

entries.name: acoustic_guitar
entries.description: A [guitar](#guitar) whose hollow wooden body carries the [sound](#sound) on its own, with [no](#no) pickups or [amplifier](#amplifier). The plugged-in kind is [electric_guitar](#electric_guitar).

entries.name: lyre
entries.description: A small handheld stringed [instrument](#instrument), usually U-shaped, whose strings run to a crossbar, associated with ancient Greece. A [harp](#harp) is larger and stands on the ground while it is played.

entries.name: harp
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) triangular [string](#string) [instrument](#instrument) — [pillar](#pillar), curved [neck](#neck) and [sounding](#sounding) board — whose graded strings are plucked with the fingers. The smaller U-shaped instrument held in the arms is a [lyre](#lyre), tagged separately.

entries.name: recorder
entries.description: The end-blown woodwind with eight finger holes, most [familiar](#familiar) as the plastic soprano version handed out to schoolchildren. Combine with [playing_instrument](#playing_instrument) when it is being played.

entries.name: lute_(instrument)
entries.description: A plucked [string](#string) [instrument](#instrument) with a [neck](#neck), fretted or not, and a deep rounded [back](#back). It is the instrument of [medieval](#medieval) and Renaissance minstrels.

entries.name: amplifier
entries.description: The [speaker](#speaker) [box](#box) with knobs that an electric [guitar](#guitar) or bass plugs into. It usually stands on the [floor](#floor) beside the player with a [cable](#cable) trailing across the [stage](#stage).

entries.name: conductor_baton
entries.description: The slim [wand](#wand) a [conductor](#conductor) uses to set the beat for an [orchestra](#orchestra), band or choir. A [drum](#drum) major's [mace](#mace) or a relay baton is not this.

entries.name: cello
entries.description: A large four-stringed [instrument](#instrument) bowed while seated, [standing](#standing) on an end [pin](#pin) and braced between the [knees](#knees). Deeper and bulkier than a [violin](#violin), and smaller than a double bass.

entries.name: tambourine
entries.description: A hand percussion frame ringed with pairs of small jingling discs, sometimes fitted with a drumhead on one side. Played by [shaking](#shaking), rattling or striking it against the palm.

entries.name: piano_keys
entries.description: The black and white keys of a keyboard [instrument](#instrument) shown large in the frame, or [floating](#floating) free with [no](#no) instrument visibly attached. Use it when the keys themselves carry the picture rather than a whole [piano](#piano).

entries.name: biwa_lute
entries.description: A Japanese short-necked lute with a pear-shaped body, [tall](#tall) frets and a bent pegbox, played with a large wedge-shaped [plectrum](#plectrum). Tied to narrative storytelling and to the goddess Benten.

entries.name: maracas
entries.description: Hollow [gourd](#gourd) rattles filled with [beads](#beads) or dry seeds, shaken by their handles and normally played as a pair. A [staple](#staple) of Latin percussion and of festive scenes.

entries.name: kagura_suzu
entries.description: A handheld [shrine](#shrine) [instrument](#instrument): three tiers of small bells strung on [coiled](#coiled) [wire](#wire) above a short grip, shaken during sacred dance. A [miko](#miko) is the usual bearer, and coloured ribbons often trail from it.

entries.name: cymbals
entries.description: Round brass or bronze plates that [ring](#ring) out sharply when struck, either clashed together in the hands or mounted on a [drum](#drum) kit and hit with sticks.

entries.name: kantele
entries.description: A Finnish plucked zither: a flat wooden [box](#box) strung across its face, laid on the [lap](#lap) or a [table](#table) and picked with the fingers. It belongs to the same [family](#family) as the koto and the psaltery.

entries.name: saxophone
entries.description: A brass reed [instrument](#instrument) with a flared upturned [bell](#bell), usually held on a [neck](#neck) [strap](#strap). Alto and tenor are the sizes drawn most; the straight soprano is easy to mistake for a [clarinet](#clarinet).

entries.name: taiko_drum
entries.description: A Japanese [barrel](#barrel) [drum](#drum) with a wide body and heads tacked or laced on at both ends. Sits on a stand or frame and is struck with [heavy](#heavy) sticks.

entries.name: ocarina
entries.description: A small egg-shaped [wind](#wind) [instrument](#instrument) pierced with finger holes and blown through a [whistle](#whistle) mouthpiece, normally cradled in both hands.

entries.name: euphonium
entries.description: A valved brass [instrument](#instrument) with a conical bore and a warm baritone voice, held upright against the chest with the [bell](#bell) facing up. It looks like a small [tuba](#tuba) and sounds a little higher.

entries.name: shamisen
entries.description: A three-stringed Japanese lute with a [square](#square), drum-like body and a long fretless [neck](#neck), struck with a broad [bachi](#bachi) [plectrum](#plectrum). Turns up in [geisha](#geisha), folk, and kabuki scenes.

entries.name: horn_(instrument)
entries.description: A simple funnel-shaped [wind](#wind) [instrument](#instrument) with [no](#no) valves, from an [animal](#animal) or [hunting](#hunting) horn to a plastic noisemaker or vuvuzela. It is blown for [music](#music) or to raise an alarm.

entries.name: transverse_flute
entries.description: The sideways-held member of the [flute](#flute) [family](#family), sounded by [blowing](#blowing) across a [hole](#hole) near one end rather than into a mouthpiece. Distinguishes the [concert](#concert) flute from end-blown types such as the [recorder](#recorder).

entries.name: guitar_strap
entries.description: A band [running](#running) over the shoulder that carries a [guitar](#guitar) or bass so the player [can](#can) stand while performing. Tag it when the [strap](#strap) itself is drawn, whether or not anyone is [playing](#playing).

entries.name: pipa_(instrument)
entries.description: A Chinese four-stringed lute with a pear-shaped body and a heavily fretted [neck](#neck), held upright on the [lap](#lap) and plucked with the fingers. Larger than the similar-looking liuqin.

entries.name: trombone
entries.description: A brass [instrument](#instrument) pitched by [sliding](#sliding) a U-shaped section of tubing in and out, ending in a flared [bell](#bell) like a trumpet's. The extended [slide](#slide) arm makes it unmistakable among the brass section.

entries.name: keytar
entries.description: A keyboard slung from a shoulder [strap](#strap) and played [standing](#standing) up, with a [neck](#neck) for the left hand like a guitar's. It exists so the player [can](#can) move about a [stage](#stage).

entries.name: bachi
entries.description: The broad wedge-shaped [plectrum](#plectrum) used to strike a [shamisen](#shamisen) or biwa, gripped in the whole fist rather than between fingertips. The straight wooden taiko beaters share the name but are a different implement.

entries.name: ukulele
entries.description: A small four-stringed [instrument](#instrument) shaped like a [miniature](#miniature) [guitar](#guitar), plucked or strummed. Strongly associated with Hawaiian [music](#music) and with [casual](#casual), cheerful scenes.

entries.name: french_horn
entries.description: A brass [instrument](#instrument) of tubing wound into a coil and [opening](#opening) into a broad [bell](#bell), played with one hand tucked inside that bell. Orchestra and [school](#school) band scenes bring it out.

entries.name: accordion
entries.description: A bellows [instrument](#instrument) with a rectangular middle and keys or [buttons](#buttons) on its asymmetrical sides. Symmetrical instruments with a [square](#square) or hexagonal bellows are concertinas instead.

entries.name: music_stand
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) rack that holds sheet [music](#music) at [reading](#reading) [height](#height) for a player or singer. It usually stands beside an [instrument](#instrument) or directly in front of a performer.

entries.name: erhu
entries.description: A Chinese fiddle with two strings and a small hexagonal soundbox, played upright [resting](#resting) on the [lap](#lap). Its [bow](#bow) runs between the strings and cannot be taken off the [instrument](#instrument).

entries.name: double_bass
entries.description: The largest and lowest of the bowed strings, with sloping shoulders and a body [reaching](#reaching) [well](#well) above the player's waist. Normally played [standing](#standing), though a [stool](#stool) is an option.

entries.name: clarinet
entries.description: A single-reed woodwind with a slender black cylindrical body and a keyed mechanism, its mouthpiece much like a saxophone's. Usually shown being played or carried by a band member.

entries.name: synthesizer
entries.description: An electronic keyboard [instrument](#instrument) whose sounds [can](#can) be built and shaped from scratch rather than only chosen from presets. A densely packed panel of knobs and sliders beside pitch and modulation wheels or a [joystick](#joystick) is the visual giveaway.

entries.name: marching_band_baton
entries.description: The long metal baton carried at the head of a [marching](#marching) band, including the show batons spun by twirlers. Usually held aloft or [caught](#caught) mid-throw.

entries.name: triangle_(instrument)
entries.description: A percussion [instrument](#instrument) made from a metal bar bent into an open [triangle](#triangle). It hangs from a loop of cord and is struck with a small metal beater to give a bright ringing [note](#note).

entries.name: tsuzumi
entries.description: A small hourglass-shaped hand [drum](#drum) with a skin at each end, held at the shoulder and struck with the fingers. Tightening its lacing changes the pitch, and it traditionally accompanies noh and kabuki performance.

entries.name: upright_piano
entries.description: A [piano](#piano) whose strings and frame stand vertically inside a [tall](#tall) [cabinet](#cabinet) rather than [lying](#lying) flat as in a grand. The compact shape suits homes and practice rooms at some cost to volume.

entries.name: tuba
entries.description: The deepest and bulkiest of the brass instruments, its wide conical tubing [coiled](#coiled) upright into an oblong body topped with a large [bell](#bell). Three or four valves sit under the player's hand.

entries.name: harmonica
entries.description: A small oblong mouth organ played by [blowing](#blowing) and drawing air along a row of holes. It usually sits cupped between both hands at the [lips](#lips), and turns up in blues, folk and country scenes.

entries.name: effects_pedal
entries.description: A foot-operated [box](#box) wired between an [instrument](#instrument) and its [amplifier](#amplifier) to reshape the [sound](#sound), covering [distortion](#distortion), reverb, chorus, wah and the rest. Several are often [chained](#chained) on a board at a player's [feet](#feet).

entries.name: koto_(instrument)
entries.description: A long Japanese zither played [lying](#lying) flat, its thirteen strings raised on movable bridges and plucked with picks worn on the fingers. It is widely treated as the country's national [instrument](#instrument).

entries.name: music_box
entries.description: A [clockwork](#clockwork) [box](#box) that chimes a tune when its [lid](#lid) is raised, driven by a [pinned](#pinned) cylinder plucking rows of tuned metal [teeth](#teeth). Designs often add a turning [carousel](#carousel) or a [ballerina](#ballerina) [spinning](#spinning) inside.

entries.name: castanets
entries.description: Paired hollow shells joined by a cord and clacked together in the palm to mark rhythm. A percussion [instrument](#instrument), seen mostly in [flamenco](#flamenco) and other Spanish-flavoured dance.

entries.name: violin_case
entries.description: The shaped hard case a [violin](#violin) travels in, shown closed or open with the [instrument](#instrument) inside. It appears as a musician's prop and, in crime settings, as somewhere to hide something else.

entries.name: taiko_sticks
entries.description: The thick, cylindrical wooden beaters used on Japanese drums, one held in each hand. Called [bachi](#bachi) in Japanese, a word that also names the very different [plectrum](#plectrum) used on a [shamisen](#shamisen).

entries.name: handbell
entries.description: A hollow [bell](#bell) with a [handle](#handle), swung by hand so the clapper strikes inside. It appears with carol singers, teachers [calling](#calling) a class in and [shrine](#shrine) attendants.

entries.name: melodica
entries.description: A small keyboard blown through a mouthpiece or short [hose](#hose) while the fingers work the keys like a [flute](#flute) or [piano](#piano). A [familiar](#familiar) sight in Japanese [school](#school) [music](#music) rooms.

entries.name: oboe
entries.description: A narrow woodwind whose bore widens toward a flared [bell](#bell), sounded through a double reed. The slim [dark](#dark) body and the reed at the lip tell it apart from a [clarinet](#clarinet).

entries.name: metronome
entries.description: A [device](#device) that beats out a steady tempo for a musician, either a [swinging](#swinging) [pendulum](#pendulum) in a wooden case or a small electronic [box](#box) with a [blinking](#blinking) light.

entries.name: organ_(instrument)
entries.description: A keyboard [instrument](#instrument) whose [notes](#notes) [sound](#sound) for as long as a [key](#key) is held, from [church](#church) pipe [organs](#organs) and pedal-pumped harmoniums to electric models. Look for stacked manuals, a pedalboard and rows of stops; it has nothing to do with [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: ruan
entries.description: A Chinese plucked lute with a fully circular body, a fretted [neck](#neck) and four strings. The round soundbox is what separates it from the pear-shaped pipa.

entries.name: guzheng
entries.description: A long Chinese zither whose many strings pass over movable bridges, laid flat on stands and plucked with picks taped to the fingers. Similar in look to the Japanese koto, which is a separate [instrument](#instrument).

entries.name: plectrum_in_mouth
entries.description: A [guitar](#guitar) pick gripped between the [lips](#lips) or [teeth](#teeth) so both hands stay free. Typical of a player mid-performance, tuning up, or [reaching](#reaching) for a second pick.

entries.name: alto_saxophone
entries.description: The mid-sized member of the [saxophone](#saxophone) [family](#family), a curved brass [wind](#wind) [instrument](#instrument) with a hooked [neck](#neck) and a flared [bell](#bell). It is the size most often seen in [school](#school) bands and jazz scenes.

entries.name: whammy_bar
entries.description: The [lever](#lever) fitted to some electric [guitar](#guitar) bridges, pushed or pulled to bend a note's pitch. It juts out beside the strings near the picking hand.

entries.name: bugle
entries.description: A short brass horn with [no](#no) valves, blown for [military](#military) calls and fanfares rather than melodies. The [plain](#plain) unbroken [tube](#tube) tells it apart from a [trumpet](#trumpet).

entries.name: flower
entries.description: One or more blossoms in the picture, growing, held, worn or scattered loose. The general [tag](#tag); name the particular [bloom](#bloom) too where it [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: rose
entries.description: A rose [flower](#flower), held, worn, growing or gathered into a [bouquet](#bouquet), in any colour. The classic romantic [gift](#gift), with each colour [carrying](#carrying) its own meaning.

entries.name: white_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) with white [petals](#petals), held, worn or growing in the scene. Add the species, such as lily or [rose](#rose), when it's identifiable.

entries.name: red_flower
entries.description: Any red [flower](#flower), growing, held, or worn in the hair. Combine with flower and the species, such as [red_rose](#red_rose) or [spider_lily](#spider_lily).

entries.name: pink_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) that is pink, worn in the hair, held in the hand or growing in the scene. Add the species where it [can](#can) be told, such as [pink_rose](#pink_rose) or [cherry_blossoms](#cherry_blossoms).

entries.name: blue_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) with blue [petals](#petals), held, tucked into the hair or growing in the scene. A blue [rose](#rose) has a [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: yellow_flower
entries.description: Any [flower](#flower), real or imagined, with yellow [petals](#petals), such as sunflowers, dandelions or rapeseed. Tag flower and the species if it is known.

entries.name: purple_flower
entries.description: Any purple [flower](#flower), real or invented, whether growing in a scene, held in hand, or worn as a [hair_flower](#hair_flower). Combine with flower and the specific species when it is identifiable, such as [purple_rose](#purple_rose).

entries.name: red_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) in the classic red, held, worn, growing, or in a [bouquet](#bouquet). The traditional token of love and romance, so it often accompanies confessions and Valentine scenes.

entries.name: bouquet
entries.description: An arranged bunch of cut flowers, often wrapped in [paper](#paper) or [bound](#bound) with [ribbon](#ribbon), carried by a [bride](#bride), handed over as a [gift](#gift) or thrown at a [wedding](#wedding). Add [flower](#flower) as [well](#well), and [holding_bouquet](#holding_bouquet) when somebody carries it.

entries.name: sunflower
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) [plant](#plant) with a large yellow [flower](#flower) head and [dark](#dark) centre, a fixture of [summer](#summer) imagery. Tag single blooms and bouquets here; a whole [field](#field) of them is [sunflower_field](#sunflower_field). Implies flower.

entries.name: blue_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) with blue [petals](#petals), a [bloom](#bloom) that needs dye or engineering to exist and therefore carries a meaning of the unattainable. It reads as deliberate [symbolism](#symbolism) far more often than as [garden](#garden) [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: white_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) bearing white [petals](#petals), held, worn, or growing nearby. The colour reads as a mark of purity, so it turns up often in bridal and angelic scenes; pair with rose and [white_flower](#white_flower).

entries.name: hibiscus
entries.description: The broad five-petalled [tropical](#tropical) [bloom](#bloom) whose long pistil juts out [well](#well) past the [petals](#petals), in pink, red, orange, yellow, purple or white. It is the standard [summer](#summer) [flower](#flower), most often tucked into the hair beside swimwear.

entries.name: pink_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) with pink [petals](#petals), growing, cut into a [bouquet](#bouquet) or used as decoration on clothing. Roses in other shades take their own colour tags.

entries.name: orange_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) with orange [petals](#petals), such as a [marigold](#marigold) or an orange lily. The white blossom of the orange [tree](#tree) is something else.

entries.name: lily_(flower)
entries.description: A six-petalled [bloom](#bloom), most [familiar](#familiar) in the white trumpet-shaped form, though lilies come in nearly any colour and several [shapes](#shapes). Its Japanese name [yuri](#yuri) makes it the [emblem](#emblem) of love between women, so it recurs constantly in that art.

entries.name: black_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) with black [petals](#petals), whether a [rose](#rose), a lily or a stylised [bloom](#bloom) on [cloth](#cloth) or in the hair. A black rose in particular has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hydrangea
entries.description: Hydrangea shrubs or blooms: round clusters of small flowers in blue, purple or pink. In Japan they belong to the rainy season and often appear with umbrellas and snails.

entries.name: purple_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) in a [lilac](#lilac) or purple [shade](#shade). Combine with rose and [purple_flower](#purple_flower); deep indigo roses do not occur in [nature](#nature), so they usually mark a [fantasy](#fantasy) or symbolic scene.

entries.name: spider_lily
entries.description: The red [spider](#spider) lily, a [dome](#dome) of blooms on a bare stem with long curling stamens that give it its spidery look, symbolically tied to [death](#death). Also grows in pink, white, and yellow; do not mistake thin-petalled chrysanthemums for it.

entries.name: flower_wreath
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) woven from blossoms, whether worn, carried or hung up as decoration. When it sits on somebody's head, [head_wreath](#head_wreath) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: flower_on_head
entries.description: A [bloom](#bloom) actually growing from the [crown](#crown) of the head, stem and leaves and all. In Japanese humour it paints the character as airheaded or carefree; a [flower](#flower) merely worn in the hair is [hair_flower](#hair_flower).

entries.name: yellow_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) with yellow [petals](#petals), a naturally occurring colour that stands for joy and friendship. Tag rose and [yellow_flower](#yellow_flower).

entries.name: lotus
entries.description: A pink or white lotus [bloom](#bloom) [standing](#standing) clear above the [water](#water) on its stem, with a flat [seed](#seed) pod at its centre and round leaves around it. A water lily, easily [confused](#confused) with it, floats both its flowers and its pads on the surface.

entries.name: plum_blossoms
entries.description: Blossoms of the [plum](#plum) [tree](#tree), white, pink or red, blooming on bare branches in late [winter](#winter) and early spring. Their [petals](#petals) are rounded at the tip, where [cherry](#cherry) blossom petals are notched.

entries.name: daisy
entries.description: Flowers of the daisy shape: a tight central disc ringed by many long narrow [petals](#petals), classically white around a yellow eye but drawn in any colour. Asters, gerberas and black-eyed susans look alike enough to be tagged here as [well](#well).

entries.name: black_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) with black [petals](#petals), a [bloom](#bloom) with [no](#no) natural counterpart. Stories lean on it for [death](#death), [mourning](#mourning), hatred or a final parting, so it usually arrives with a grim mood.

entries.name: tulip
entries.description: A cup-shaped spring [flower](#flower) on a straight stem with long leaves, drawn in any colour. Tag the specific colour alongside it when it matters.

entries.name: wreath
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) woven from flowers, leaves, and sometimes [fruit](#fruit), hung on a [door](#door) or wall or set on a [table](#table). Worn on the head it is a [head_wreath](#head_wreath) instead, and a Christmas version takes the holiday [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: red_spider_lily
entries.description: A blood-red [flower](#flower) with long curling stamens splayed out from a bare stem, blooming in [autumn](#autumn) without leaves. In Japanese art it is tied to graveyards, farewells and [death](#death).

entries.name: camellia
entries.description: A rounded [bloom](#bloom) from an evergreen East Asian shrub, painted red most of the time and sometimes white or pink, with a bright yellow tuft at its [heart](#heart) and a single [ring](#ring) of [petals](#petals). Common as a cut [flower](#flower) or a hair decoration in Japanese-styled work.

entries.name: green_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) whose [petals](#petals) are green, worn, held or growing in the scene. The specific [bloom](#bloom), such as [green_rose](#green_rose), [can](#can) be tagged alongside it.

entries.name: wisteria
entries.description: A [climbing](#climbing) vine whose long clusters of blossom hang down in purple, violet, pink, or white. It should not be [confused](#confused) with a [willow](#willow), a [tree](#tree) with trailing leafy branches, or a [lilac](#lilac), a fragrant flowering shrub.

entries.name: bud
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) still closed and compact, or the first shoot [pushing](#pushing) out of a [plant](#plant). Use it where the unopened bud is what shows, not a [bloom](#bloom) in full.

entries.name: lily_of_the_valley
entries.description: A woodland [plant](#plant) with little white bells [hanging](#hanging) in a row from a curved stem, known as suzuran in Japanese. Every part of it is poisonous; snowbells and bellflowers look similar and have tags of their own.

entries.name: white_lily
entries.description: A lily with white blossoms, a symbol of purity and often of [yuri](#yuri) themes. Add [flower](#flower) and lily tags alongside.

entries.name: morning_glory
entries.description: Funnel-shaped [climbing](#climbing) flowers in pink, blue, purple or red, usually with a pale star at the centre and heart-shaped leaves. A [summer](#summer) fixture, and the [plant](#plant) Japanese schoolchildren are set to raise over the holidays.

entries.name: dandelion
entries.description: The [plant](#plant) with a yellow composite [flower](#flower) head over deeply toothed leaves, or the white puffball of [parachute](#parachute) seeds it turns into. Its name traces [back](#back) to lion's [tooth](#tooth).

entries.name: orange_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) with orange [petals](#petals), a [shade](#shade) that occurs in the [garden](#garden) and is read as a [sign](#sign) of enthusiasm.

entries.name: flower_over_eye
entries.description: A blossom covers one eye and appears to hold its position unaided. Once a [string](#string), [strap](#strap) or [fabric](#fabric) backing is visible, the picture wants [flower_eyepatch](#flower_eyepatch) instead.

entries.name: peony_(flower)
entries.description: A big, full, many-petalled [bloom](#bloom), usually pink, red or white, long prized as an ornamental. A favourite motif in East Asian art and on [kimono](#kimono).

entries.name: grey_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) with grey [petals](#petals), held, worn in the hair or growing in the scene. It belongs to muted and gothic palettes far more than to natural ones.

entries.name: aqua_flower
entries.description: A [bloom](#bloom) coloured blue-green, worn in the hair, held in the hand or growing in the scene. Add the specific [flower](#flower) where it [can](#can) be named.

entries.name: anemone_(flower)
entries.description: Anemone blooms in red, white, violet or yellow, known by the [dark](#dark) button of a centre often ringed in white. Small leaves sit just beneath the [flower](#flower), where a poppy carries its leaves much lower down the stem.

entries.name: white_petals
entries.description: Loose white [petals](#petals) [drifting](#drifting) through the air or settled on the ground. Use it once the petals have come away from the [plant](#plant); a white [bloom](#bloom) still on its stem is [white_flower](#white_flower) instead.

entries.name: chrysanthemum
entries.description: A many-petalled [flower](#flower) of the [daisy](#daisy) [family](#family) in yellow, white, red or purple, bred in countless varieties. Common in East Asian art and [autumn](#autumn) scenes, and the basis of the Japanese imperial [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: green_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) with green [petals](#petals), a colour the [flower](#flower) never takes in [nature](#nature). Its [symbolism](#symbolism) is unsettled, though it is commonly read as fertility, renewal or [envy](#envy).

entries.name: poppy_(flower)
entries.description: The papery-petalled poppy, most often scarlet with a [dark](#dark) centre and a slender [hairy](#hairy) stem. Grows across fields as [scenery](#scenery) or is tucked into hair.

entries.name: brown_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) whose [petals](#petals) are brown, growing, cut into an arrangement, or worn in the hair or on clothing.

entries.name: water_lily_flower
entries.description: The cupped [floating](#floating) [bloom](#bloom) of a [water](#water) lily, [resting](#resting) on the surface of a [pond](#pond). It is [no](#no) true lily despite the name, and the round floating leaves are tagged as lily pads.

entries.name: flower_on_liquid
entries.description: A blossom [floating](#floating) on the surface of [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid), in a [bath](#bath), a [bowl](#bowl) or a still [pond](#pond). It rides on top rather than [sinking](#sinking) beneath.

entries.name: christmas_wreath
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of evergreen branches trimmed with [ribbon](#ribbon), bells or baubles, hung on a [door](#door) or wall for the holiday. Its festive decoration is what separates it from a [plain](#plain) floral [wreath](#wreath).

entries.name: plumeria
entries.description: The five-petalled [tropical](#tropical) frangipani [flower](#flower), its rounded [petals](#petals) overlapping and often shading from [cream](#cream) to yellow or pink. Common in [beach](#beach) scenes as a hair flower or strung into a [lei](#lei).

entries.name: multicolored_flower
entries.description: A [bloom](#bloom) whose [petals](#petals) carry more than one colour, either graded into one another or laid down in distinct bands. It describes the single [flower](#flower), not a mixed bunch.

entries.name: bellflower
entries.description: A campanula [bloom](#bloom): a narrow deeply lobed [cup](#cup) that hangs like a small [bell](#bell), most often violet-blue. Do not mistake it for lily of the [valley](#valley), whose bells are rounder and much shorter.

entries.name: cosmos_(flower)
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) annual with slim stems, feathery leaves and daisy-like blooms of eight broad [petals](#petals). Pink, white and crimson are the usual colours, and it reads as [autumn](#autumn).

entries.name: nemophila_(flower)
entries.description: Baby blue eyes: a low [plant](#plant) bearing cup-shaped flowers with five rounded [petals](#petals), pale blue shading to white at the centre. Whole fields of them in [bloom](#bloom) make a favourite [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: iris_(flower)
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) iris, three upright [petals](#petals) [standing](#standing) over three that curve down, on long sword-shaped leaves. Purple and blue are the usual colours, and it reads as early [summer](#summer).

entries.name: carnation
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) on a slim stem whose [petals](#petals) are ruffled and tightly packed, [giving](#giving) a frilled edge where a [rose](#rose) would be smooth. Often given as a [gift](#gift), red and pink above all.

entries.name: pink_tulip
entries.description: A [tulip](#tulip) with pink [petals](#petals), growing in a [bed](#bed), cut, or arranged in a [bouquet](#bouquet). A colour variant of the ordinary tulip.

entries.name: pansy
entries.description: A [garden](#garden) [flower](#flower) bred from viola stock, its five [petals](#petals) set three above and two below with a [dark](#dark) blotch at the centre that reads a little like a [butterfly](#butterfly). That central marking is what separates it from a [plain](#plain) violet.

entries.name: flower_on_chest
entries.description: A blossom [lying](#lying) against the chest, [pinned](#pinned) to a garment or laid directly on bare skin. Funeral scenes and formal portraits reach for it often.

entries.name: flower_basket
entries.description: A woven [basket](#basket) filled with cut blooms, carried on the arm or set down as part of the scene. Weddings, gardens and [flower](#flower) sellers are the usual settings.

entries.name: lavender_(flower)
entries.description: A purple [herb](#herb) [flower](#flower) carried in narrow [spikes](#spikes) of small blossoms up a straight stem. If the blossoms trail downward in [hanging](#hanging) clusters, [wisteria](#wisteria) is the more likely [plant](#plant).

entries.name: flower_over_mouth
entries.description: A blossom held or placed so that it screens the mouth and lower face. It works the way a raised fan or a covering hand would.

entries.name: orchid
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) of the orchid [family](#family), known by three showy [petals](#petals) with the lowest swollen into a lip of a different shape and colour. Used for an elegant or exotic [note](#note).

entries.name: rose_bush
entries.description: A living [rose](#rose) [plant](#plant) with blooms, leaves and thorned stems, growing in a [garden](#garden) or [hedge](#hedge). Distinct from cut roses held or arranged in a [vase](#vase).

entries.name: daffodil
entries.description: A spring bulb [flower](#flower) whose six [spreading](#spreading) tepals [ring](#ring) a trumpet-shaped [cup](#cup), held out [sideways](#sideways) from the stalk in white, yellow or orange. Narcissus and jonquil name the same [plant](#plant), taken in East Asia as a token of fortune.

entries.name: red_tulip
entries.description: A [tulip](#tulip) with red [petals](#petals) forming a smooth closed [cup](#cup) on a straight green stem. Drawn singly, in bouquets, or as beds of them in spring scenes.

entries.name: forget-me-not_(flower)
entries.description: A small five-petalled [bloom](#bloom) growing in sprays, most often pale blue with a bright yellow or white eye, though pink and white forms exist. Its name carries obvious sentimental [weight](#weight) in art.

entries.name: yellow_tulip
entries.description: A [tulip](#tulip) with yellow [petals](#petals), growing, cut or gathered into a [bouquet](#bouquet). The cup-shaped [bloom](#bloom) on one straight stem identifies it.

entries.name: epiphyllum
entries.description: A [cactus](#cactus) bearing wide, layered flowers on a long [tube](#tube), most often white though hybrids run to pink and orange. The blooms open after [dark](#dark) and are gone by [morning](#morning), which makes them a [standing](#standing) image for beauty that does not last.

entries.name: osmanthus
entries.description: An east Asian flowering shrub bearing dense clusters of tiny four-lobed blossoms with a [strong](#strong) sweet scent. Used to flavour [tea](#tea), [wine](#wine) and [sweets](#sweets), so it often appears alongside them.

entries.name: clover_(flower)
entries.description: The blossom of the [clover](#clover) [plant](#plant): a rounded head packed with tiny purple, red, white or yellow florets. The three-leaf [foliage](#foliage) that stands for luck is tagged separately.

entries.name: grey_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) whose [petals](#petals) sit between white and black, too [dark](#dark) for one and too light for the other. Judge it on the overall tone, since [heavy](#heavy) shading [can](#can) push a white rose into this range.

entries.name: gerbera
entries.description: A daisy-shaped [bloom](#bloom) on a single bare stem, its dense [ring](#ring) of narrow [petals](#petals) in bright pink, orange, red or yellow. A [staple](#staple) of [florist](#florist) bouquets.

entries.name: chinese_bellflower
entries.description: A five-pointed star-shaped [bloom](#bloom) in blue, purple, pink or white, which swells into a balloon-like [bud](#bud) before it opens. Its other common name overlaps with tags for actual balloons and [balloon](#balloon) [sculpture](#sculpture), so keep the three apart.

entries.name: dandelion_seed
entries.description: A single [dandelion](#dandelion) [seed](#seed) trailing its tuft of white filaments, [drifting](#drifting) on the air or pinched between fingertips. Several usually float across the scene at once.

entries.name: gold_osmanthus
entries.description: A shrub covered in dense clusters of tiny orange flowers, famous for the sweet scent it throws off in [autumn](#autumn). Its Japanese name is kinmokusei, and the blossoms flavour [tea](#tea) and [sweets](#sweets).

entries.name: white_tulip
entries.description: A [tulip](#tulip) with white [petals](#petals), cupped shut at the top of a bare stem. It appears drawn singly, gathered into bouquets, or spread across a [field](#field).

entries.name: poinsettia
entries.description: The Christmas [plant](#plant) whose broad scarlet bracts spread around a knot of tiny yellow flowers. Cream, pink and marbled varieties count as [well](#well).

entries.name: baby's-breath
entries.description: Sprays of tiny white or pale pink blossoms carried on thin, much-branched stems. Florists pack it around larger blooms as airy filler in bouquets and arrangements.

entries.name: violet_(flower)
entries.description: Small five-petalled blooms of the genus Viola, most often deep purple and paler toward the middle. African and dogtooth violets are filed here as [well](#well) even though they belong elsewhere botanically; see [pansy](#pansy) for telling those apart.

entries.name: golden_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) that is [gold](#gold), either an unnatural [bloom](#bloom) or a [flower](#flower) [cast](#cast) in metal. It carries a sense of luxury and of love that does not wither.

entries.name: strawberry_blossoms
entries.description: The small white five-petalled flowers of the [strawberry](#strawberry) [plant](#plant), each with a yellow centre. Drawn on the plant or cut and arranged.

entries.name: dahlia
entries.description: A [garden](#garden) [bloom](#bloom) made of a tight [ball](#ball) of narrow, pointed [petals](#petals). Grown in [strong](#strong) single colours and flowering from late [summer](#summer) into [autumn](#autumn).

entries.name: chinese_lantern_(plant)
entries.description: A [garden](#garden) [plant](#plant) whose [berry](#berry) hangs inside an inflated papery husk of bright orange-red, shaped like a little [hanging](#hanging) [lamp](#lamp). The husk is what makes it recognisable, and it appears constantly in Japanese [summer](#summer) imagery.

entries.name: calla_lily
entries.description: An ornamental [bloom](#bloom) shaped as a smooth funnel of petal wrapped around a finger-like yellow spike. White, yellow and pink are usual, and despite the name it is neither a calla nor a lily.

entries.name: aqua_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) in blue-green, a colour roses do not grow in, so it usually marks a [fantasy](#fantasy) or stylised design. Real or artificial, it may be held, worn or arranged in the scene.

entries.name: too_many_flowers
entries.description: Flowers filling the frame in overwhelming quantity, banked around the subject or [spilling](#spilling) out of the background.

entries.name: magnolia
entries.description: Big cup-shaped blooms in white, [cream](#cream) or deep pink, [opening](#opening) on bare branches before the leaves come. A [marker](#marker) of early spring.

entries.name: orange_tulip
entries.description: Tulip blooms in orange, growing in a [bed](#bed), held as a cut stem or arranged in a [bouquet](#bouquet).

entries.name: artificial_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) made of [fabric](#fabric), plastic, [paper](#paper) or metal rather than grown, used as decoration or worn as an ornament. Silk blooms on hats and in hair are the common case.

entries.name: brown_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) coloured brown, cut, growing or worn as an ornament. Roses do not come in this [shade](#shade) naturally, so it generally marks a stylised or symbolic palette.

entries.name: clematis_(flower)
entries.description: A [climbing](#climbing) vine bearing broad flat flowers of a few wide [petals](#petals), usually purple, white or pink. Often drawn trailing over a [trellis](#trellis) or a [fence](#fence).

entries.name: marigold
entries.description: Dense ruffled blooms in orange or yellow on a low bushy [plant](#plant), the heads packed almost round. Common in gardens and in [festival](#festival) offerings.

entries.name: wilted_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) past its prime, its [petals](#petals) [hanging](#hanging) limp or browning on a bent stem. It is often placed in a scene as a small [sign](#sign) of loss or decay.

entries.name: freesia_(flower)
entries.description: Funnel-shaped blooms carried in a one-sided row along an arching stem, usually white, yellow or pink. Tag it when the species [can](#can) actually be made out rather than for generic blossoms.

entries.name: white_spider_lily
entries.description: A [spider](#spider) lily with white [petals](#petals) and long stamens that curl outward from the [bloom](#bloom). In Japanese imagery it carries funerary and late-summer associations.

entries.name: crystal_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) formed from [crystal](#crystal) or [glass](#glass) rather than living [petals](#petals), its facets [catching](#catching) the light. A [staple](#staple) of [fantasy](#fantasy) and fairy-tale [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: lotus_pod
entries.description: The flat [seed](#seed) head left when a [lotus](#lotus) [flower](#flower) fades, pitted with a [ring](#ring) of round holes [holding](#holding) its seeds. That cluster of holes makes it a favourite prop in unsettling imagery.

entries.name: red_carnation
entries.description: A [carnation](#carnation) with red ruffled [petals](#petals) on a slender stem. It is the [flower](#flower) given on Mother's Day in Japan, so bouquets of them often mark that occasion.

entries.name: gentiana_(flower)
entries.description: A deep blue alpine [bloom](#bloom) shaped like a narrow [trumpet](#trumpet), [opening](#opening) in clusters low to the ground. Carries [autumn](#autumn) and [mountain](#mountain) associations in Japanese art.

entries.name: chamomile
entries.description: A small [daisy](#daisy) lookalike, white [petals](#petals) around a domed yellow centre, with fine feathery leaves. It is best known as a [tea](#tea) [herb](#herb), so a [cup](#cup) often stands nearby.

entries.name: mimosa_(flower)
entries.description: Fluffy yellow pompom blossoms crowding a [branch](#branch) of feathery leaves, a [sign](#sign) of early spring.

entries.name: dandelion_clock
entries.description: A [dandelion](#dandelion) that has finished flowering, the yellow head replaced by a white sphere of feathered seeds [waiting](#waiting) on a [breath](#breath) of [wind](#wind).

entries.name: bougainvillea_(flower)
entries.description: A South American climber whose colour comes from papery bracts of magenta, red, orange or violet wrapped around tiny white blooms. It sprawls over walls, arches and balconies in warm-country [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: chinese_peony
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy), many-petalled peony [bloom](#bloom) of Chinese art and [symbolism](#symbolism), usually pink, red or white. It turns up as a [garden](#garden) [flower](#flower) and as a motif painted on fans, screens and traditional [dress](#dress).

entries.name: azalea_(flower)
entries.description: Small five-petalled blossoms in pinks and purples, borne in thick clusters on a shrub from late spring into early [summer](#summer). Counting the [petals](#petals) separates them from lilies, which carry six.

entries.name: peach_blossom
entries.description: The pink five-petalled [flower](#flower) of the [peach](#peach) [tree](#tree), [opening](#opening) on bare branches in early spring. Easily mixed up with [plum](#plum) and [cherry](#cherry), though peach [petals](#petals) end in a slight point.

entries.name: purple_tulip
entries.description: The cupped, smooth-petalled [tulip](#tulip) [bloom](#bloom) in purple, on a straight green stem. Seen in gardens, vases, and bouquets.

entries.name: gladiolus
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) spike of funnel-shaped blooms stacked up one side of a straight stem, in reds, pinks and whites. A [florist](#florist) favourite for large arrangements.

entries.name: dogwood_(flower)
entries.description: The four-bracted blossom of the cornus [tree](#tree), white or pink around a small green centre, its petal-like bracts either notched or pointed by species. A spring motif that often appears beside [cherry](#cherry) blossom.

entries.name: bird_of_paradise_flower
entries.description: A strelitzia [bloom](#bloom), whose orange sepals and blue [petals](#petals) rise from a beak-shaped [sheath](#sheath) so the whole [flower](#flower) reads as a crested bird's head. Broad [paddle](#paddle) leaves fan out beneath it.

entries.name: lilac
entries.description: The shrub's cone-shaped clusters of small, strongly scented blossoms in violet, pink or white, grown as an ornamental.

entries.name: anthurium
entries.description: A glossy [tropical](#tropical) [bloom](#bloom) whose single broad petal, shaped rather like an off-centre lily pad, cups a small upright spike. Usually red or pink, occasionally green or orange.

entries.name: cornflower
entries.description: A slender wildflower with fringed [petals](#petals) in a deep blue. Grows in fields and turns up in bouquets and hair pieces.

entries.name: ranunculus
entries.description: A [garden](#garden) buttercup with tightly packed, evenly rounded [petals](#petals), grown in shades of pink, red, orange, yellow, and white. Easily mistaken for a [rose](#rose), though its stems carry [no](#no) [thorns](#thorns) and its buds are round rather than pointed.

entries.name: kamchatka_lily
entries.description: A [nodding](#nodding), bell-shaped [flower](#flower) of six [petals](#petals) in [dark](#dark) purple through to near-black, sometimes streaked or speckled, above lance-shaped leaves. Its green three-pronged pistil is what separates it from true lilies and tulips.

entries.name: hyacinth
entries.description: A bulb [flower](#flower) [carrying](#carrying) a dense spike of small six-petalled blooms above strap-shaped leaves. Garden varieties come in nearly every colour, while wild ones [bear](#bear) only a few flowers.

entries.name: snowdrop_(flower)
entries.description: A small white bell-shaped [flower](#flower) [nodding](#nodding) from a slender green stem, one of the first blooms to appear as [winter](#winter) ends.

entries.name: purple_pansy
entries.description: The broad, flat-faced [pansy](#pansy) [bloom](#bloom) in purple, often with a [dark](#dark) blotch at its centre. Appears in gardens, bouquets, and hair alike.

entries.name: lobelia_(flower)
entries.description: Small five-petalled blossoms, most often deep blue or violet, carried in dense low clusters on trailing stems. A [garden](#garden) [plant](#plant), so it turns up in beds, [window](#window) boxes and bouquets.

entries.name: multicolored_rose
entries.description: A [rose](#rose) whose [petals](#petals) hold several colours at once, whether dyed that way or lit from more than one source. Dream and [fantasy](#fantasy) scenes account for most of them.

entries.name: blue_tulip
entries.description: A [tulip](#tulip) with blue [petals](#petals), its cupped [bloom](#bloom) [sitting](#sitting) on a single upright stem. One of the coloured tulip variants.

entries.name: black_tulip
entries.description: A [tulip](#tulip) whose [petals](#petals) are black, cut, growing or held in the hand. It sits alongside the other tulip colour variants.

entries.name: leaf
entries.description: One or more leaves are a noticeable element of the picture, [falling](#falling), held in the hand or [lying](#lying) about. It is not the [studio](#studio) or the character who share the name.

entries.name: plant
entries.description: Any living plant in the picture, from [grass](#grass) and shrubs to houseplants and [vines](#vines). It is the broad [tag](#tag); add [tree](#tree), [flower](#flower), [potted_plant](#potted_plant), or [leaf](#leaf) for the specific kind.

entries.name: branch
entries.description: A limb of a [tree](#tree) or [bush](#bush), larger than a [stick](#stick) and often still [carrying](#carrying) leaves or blossom, whether growing in the scene or held in the hand. Add tree when the whole [plant](#plant) is in frame; a bare slender piece of wood is stick.

entries.name: palm_tree
entries.description: A [tree](#tree) with a [tall](#tall) bare trunk crowned by a spray of big fronds, the shorthand for [tropical](#tropical) beaches and [hot](#hot) climates. Coconut [palms](#palms) are included; a single detached frond is [palm_leaf](#palm_leaf).

entries.name: potted_plant
entries.description: A [plant](#plant) growing in a pot or [planter](#planter) of any size, from a [windowsill](#windowsill) [cactus](#cactus) to a lobby palm. Tag plant with it.

entries.name: vines
entries.description: Climbing or trailing [plant](#plant) stems, whether growing over walls and [ruins](#ruins) or wrapped around a character. Living tendrils that grab or bind [people](#people) should also take the relevant restraint tags.

entries.name: maple_leaf
entries.description: Maple leaves, most often the red Japanese momiji, [falling](#falling) or scattered as a [sign](#sign) of [autumn](#autumn). Their [outline](#outline) is close to a cannabis [leaf](#leaf), so look before tagging.

entries.name: bamboo
entries.description: Tall green bamboo stalks in the scene, from a single stem to a small stand of them. Technically a [grass](#grass), it is common in Japanese and Chinese settings and beside pandas; a whole wood of it is [bamboo_forest](#bamboo_forest).

entries.name: leaf_on_head
entries.description: A [leaf](#leaf) sits on top of a character's head without being fastened there. It is the classic [sign](#sign) of a [fox](#fox) or [tanuki](#tanuki) about to transform.

entries.name: stick
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) length of wood, held or [lying](#lying) about. A [walking](#walking) stick is a [cane](#cane) and gets that [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: thorns
entries.description: Sharp [spikes](#spikes) growing on a [plant](#plant) stem, vine or [rose](#rose), sometimes wrapped around a character or forming a barrier. Add rose or [vines](#vines) when they belong to one.

entries.name: clover
entries.description: The low three-leaflet [plant](#plant), shamrock included, growing as ground [cover](#cover) or held in the hand. A specimen with the lucky fourth leaflet takes [four-leaf_clover](#four-leaf_clover).

entries.name: lily_pad
entries.description: The round [floating](#floating) [leaf](#leaf) of a [water](#water) lily, notched on one side, [lying](#lying) flat on a pond's surface. Lotus leaves rise clear of the water and carry [no](#no) notch.

entries.name: flower_pot
entries.description: A [container](#container) for growing and displaying plants, [standing](#standing) on a sill, [balcony](#balcony), [table](#table) or step. Add [potted_plant](#potted_plant) when something is actually growing in it.

entries.name: four-leaf_clover
entries.description: The rare four-leafed [mutation](#mutation) of the [clover](#clover), carried as a token of good luck. It appears as a growing [plant](#plant), held in a hand, or reduced to a motif.

entries.name: moss
entries.description: A low green [carpet](#carpet) of flowerless [plant](#plant) growing over rocks, [tree](#tree) trunks and [old](#old) stone. Not to be mixed up with [algae](#algae), nor with mould.

entries.name: palm_leaf
entries.description: A large frond from a palm or a similar [plant](#plant), held, [lying](#lying) loose, or filling the foreground. Use [palm_tree](#palm_tree) when the whole [tree](#tree) is in view.

entries.name: holly
entries.description: Sprigs of glossy, [spiked](#spiked) evergreen leaves [carrying](#carrying) bright red berries. A fixture of Christmas decoration, worked into wreaths, hats and festive borders.

entries.name: cactus
entries.description: A spiny succulent with a thick fleshy stem and [no](#no) leaves, sometimes [carrying](#carrying) a bright [flower](#flower). It appears as [desert](#desert) [scenery](#scenery) or as a small potted [plant](#plant) [indoors](#indoors).

entries.name: ginkgo_leaf
entries.description: The fan-shaped [leaf](#leaf) of the ginkgo [tree](#tree), sometimes notched down the middle, green in [summer](#summer) and bright yellow in [autumn](#autumn). Often drawn [falling](#falling) alongside other [autumn_leaves](#autumn_leaves).

entries.name: log
entries.description: A fallen [tree](#tree) trunk or a thick cut length of [branch](#branch). It serves as a seat beside a [campfire](#campfire), as [firewood](#firewood), or as timber for [building](#building).

entries.name: pine_tree
entries.description: An evergreen [conifer](#conifer) with needles and woody cones that keeps its colour through [winter](#winter). Common in [mountain](#mountain), [forest](#forest), [snow](#snow) and New Year scenes, often drawn as a lone [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: mistletoe
entries.description: A sprig of rounded leaves hung with pale berries, strung up at Christmas so a [kiss](#kiss) beneath it is licensed by tradition. Holly, with its spiky leaves and red berries, is a different [plant](#plant) entirely.

entries.name: seaweed
entries.description: Marine [algae](#algae), drawn as green or brown fronds [underwater](#underwater), washed up on the [beach](#beach), or served as [food](#food) such as wakame or nori.

entries.name: hanging_plant
entries.description: A potted [plant](#plant) whose pot or [basket](#basket) is suspended from a [hook](#hook) or beam instead of [standing](#standing) on a surface. Trailing [foliage](#foliage) [spilling](#spilling) down over the rim is the usual look.

entries.name: acorn
entries.description: The capped nut of an oak, whether still on the [branch](#branch), scattered on the ground or clutched by a [squirrel](#squirrel). Tag the [tree](#tree) or its leaves separately where they also appear.

entries.name: plant_roots
entries.description: The roots of a [plant](#plant) or [tree](#tree), exposed above ground, [buried](#buried) in [soil](#soil), or wrapped around something. Dark regrowth at the base of dyed hair takes a different [tag](#tag) entirely.

entries.name: ivy
entries.description: Climbing ivy with its lobed leaves, [running](#running) up walls, [tree](#tree) trunks and [ruins](#ruins). It also appears as a decorative motif along borders and on clothing.

entries.name: fern
entries.description: A flowerless, seedless [plant](#plant) with feathery triangular fronds that spreads by spores. Usually part of [forest](#forest) undergrowth or [standing](#standing) in a pot [indoors](#indoors).

entries.name: coconut_tree
entries.description: The palm that bears coconuts, with its [leaning](#leaning) trunk and [crown](#crown) of long feathered fronds. Standard [scenery](#scenery) for beaches and [tropical](#tropical) islands.

entries.name: hay
entries.description: Dried [grass](#grass), loose on a [barn](#barn) [floor](#floor), scattered on the ground or piled into a [stack](#stack). No line is drawn here between fodder hay and leftover threshing straw, since the two look alike.

entries.name: bonsai
entries.description: A [miniature](#miniature) [tree](#tree) grown in a shallow [tray](#tray) and shaped by years of pruning. The knotted trunk and flattened [spreading](#spreading) canopy make it read as an ornament rather than a houseplant.

entries.name: cattail
entries.description: A marsh reed [carrying](#carrying) a dense brown [sausage](#sausage) of seeds at the top of a [tall](#tall) stalk, growing at [pond](#pond) and ditch edges. A cat's actual [tail](#tail) is [cat_tail](#cat_tail), and the feathered play [wand](#wand) is a [cat_teaser](#cat_teaser).

entries.name: lotus_leaf
entries.description: The broad round [leaf](#leaf) of a [lotus](#lotus), which rises above the [water](#water) on its stem once mature and has an unbroken rim. Its water-repellent surface is usually drawn beaded with droplets, while a lily pad lies flat on the water and carries a single notch.

entries.name: twig
entries.description: A slender broken-off shoot from a [tree](#tree) or [bush](#bush). Often clenched between the [teeth](#teeth) in place of a [cigarette](#cigarette), waved as a makeshift [sword](#sword) or [flagpole](#flagpole), or gathered as kindling.

entries.name: ginkgo_tree
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), long-lived [tree](#tree) [carrying](#carrying) fan-shaped leaves that turn brilliant yellow in [autumn](#autumn). Lines [temple](#temple) approaches and [city](#city) avenues in Japanese [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: sprout
entries.description: A young [plant](#plant) just out of the [seed](#seed), drawn as a short stem [carrying](#carrying) a pair of small leaves. An equivalent young [tree](#tree) is tagged [sapling](#sapling) instead.

entries.name: laurels
entries.description: Sprigs of bay leaves, most often [bound](#bound) into a [circlet](#circlet). They stand for [victory](#victory), glory or divinity, and turn up worn on the head or used as a heraldic motif.

entries.name: pinecone
entries.description: The brown woody cone of a [conifer](#conifer), its [scales](#scales) spiralling around the [core](#core). Autumn and [forest](#forest) scenes use it, as do seasonal wreaths and [table](#table) [decorations](#decorations).
