entries.name: fruit_tree
entries.description: Any [tree](#tree) bearing edible [fruit](#fruit), from [apple](#apple) to [peach](#peach) to citrus. Use it for the tree itself; picked or loose fruit takes its own tags.

entries.name: cherry_tree
entries.description: The [tree](#tree) that bears [cherry](#cherry) blossom, trunk and branches included, whether flowering, in [leaf](#leaf) or bare. Use it where the tree itself is the subject rather than where [petals](#petals) merely drift past.

entries.name: maple_tree
entries.description: A maple, known by its lobed star-shaped leaves. Most often drawn in [autumn](#autumn) once the [foliage](#foliage) has turned red.

entries.name: firewood
entries.description: Split logs and cut branches kept for [burning](#burning), stacked in a [pile](#pile) or laid on a [fire](#fire). It belongs with hearths, stoves and campfires.

entries.name: planter
entries.description: A [box](#box) for growing plants, usually rectangular, [standing](#standing) on the ground or hung on a [windowsill](#windowsill) or [railing](#railing). Also called a [flower](#flower) box or [window](#window) box.

entries.name: straw_(stalk)
entries.description: Dried stalks left after grain is cut, shown loose, bundled or baled. Used as bedding, thatch and scattered flooring in barns and fields.

entries.name: mandrake
entries.description: The forked root of the mandrake [plant](#plant), long gathered for supposed magical properties and said to resemble a human [figure](#figure). Where it is alive and shrieking, [mandragora](#mandragora) fits better.

entries.name: venus_flytrap
entries.description: The insect-eating [plant](#plant) whose hinged, bristle-edged leaves snap shut on anything that touches them, sometimes enlarged into a [monster](#monster) or trap in [fantasy](#fantasy) scenes.

entries.name: rowan
entries.description: The small round red berries of the rowan [tree](#tree), growing in dense clusters. They are decorative rather than edible raw, and mark [autumn](#autumn) [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: fir_tree
entries.description: A [conifer](#conifer) with a narrow triangular [silhouette](#silhouette), tiered branches and short flat needles. The shape used for [winter](#winter) forests and for Christmas trees.

entries.name: yellow_leaves
entries.description: Leaves that have turned yellow, still on the [branch](#branch) or [drifting](#drifting) down. Fan-shaped ones come from the ginkgo and take that [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: algae
entries.description: Green growth in still or slow [water](#water), coating ponds, rocks, tanks and the sea [floor](#floor). Growth of much the same look on dry land is [moss](#moss).

entries.name: rice_(plant)
entries.description: The growing [rice](#rice) [plant](#plant), with long slender green blades and drooping heads of grain once ripe. Distinct from cooked rice served as [food](#food).

entries.name: sapling
entries.description: A young [tree](#tree), thin-stemmed and barely branched, sometimes tied to a [garden](#garden) [stake](#stake) for support. The first shoots of smaller plants are tagged [sprout](#sprout) instead.

entries.name: conifer
entries.description: A cone-bearing [tree](#tree) or shrub with [needle](#needle) leaves, generally keeping them right through [winter](#winter). Pines, spruces, cypresses and Christmas trees all belong here, though a fallen [pinecone](#pinecone) by itself does not.

entries.name: apple_tree
entries.description: A [tree](#tree) [carrying](#carrying) apples among its leaves, sometimes with windfalls [lying](#lying) in the [grass](#grass) below. Orchards, gardens and picking scenes all use it.

entries.name: herb_bundle
entries.description: Herbs, flowers or roots tied with twine and hung to dry, usually head-down from a beam, a wall or a [shelf](#shelf). It sets a scene as a farmhouse, an apothecary or a witch's room.

entries.name: sheaf
entries.description: A bundle of cut grain stalks, such as [wheat](#wheat), barley, oats or rye, tied at the middle and either [bound](#bound) upright or laid across a [field](#field). Common harvest imagery.

entries.name: withered
entries.description: Plants shrunk and shrivelled from a lack of moisture, their leaves curled and their stems slumping. It sets a dry, neglected, or [dying](#dying) mood in a scene.

entries.name: strawberry_plant
entries.description: The low leafy [plant](#plant) strawberries grow on, with toothed leaves in groups of three and small white flowers. Usually drawn with ripe [fruit](#fruit) among the leaves.

entries.name: oak_leaf
entries.description: The deeply lobed [leaf](#leaf) of an oak, whether on the [branch](#branch), fallen, worked into a [wreath](#wreath) or repeated as a printed motif.

entries.name: terrarium
entries.description: A sealed [glass](#glass) [container](#container) [holding](#holding) plants and sometimes small animals, keeping its own little climate under a [lid](#lid). Kept [indoors](#indoors) as a decorative object, usually on a [desk](#desk) or [shelf](#shelf).

entries.name: monstera_deliciosa
entries.description: The big glossy houseplant whose leaves are cut by slits and round holes, nicknamed the Swiss [cheese](#cheese) [plant](#plant). Nearly always drawn in a pot as indoor greenery.

entries.name: pitcher_plant
entries.description: A carnivorous [plant](#plant) whose [leaf](#leaf) forms a deep jug-shaped trap that insects fall into and cannot climb [back](#back) out of. Jungle scenes and plant-monster designs both draw on its shape.

entries.name: dead_plants
entries.description: Withered [vegetation](#vegetation): brittle bare stems, browned leaves, a houseplant nobody watered. Usually placed to set a neglected or desolate [note](#note).

entries.name: mold
entries.description: Fuzzy fungal growth [spreading](#spreading) over spoiled [food](#food) or across damp walls and ceilings. The casting implement spelled the same way in English has a [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: book
entries.description: A [bound](#bound) volume of printed or written [pages](#pages), open or shut, carried, read or simply [lying](#lying) about. Add [reading](#reading) for somebody reading it, and [book_stack](#book_stack), [bookshelf](#bookshelf) or [open_book](#open_book) for those cases.

entries.name: paper
entries.description: A sheet or sheets of paper present in the scene as an object: a page, a [note](#note), [wrapping](#wrapping), a blank [leaf](#leaf). Not for the surface a drawing was made on, since a scanned drawing is [traditional_media](#traditional_media). Loose sheets are [papers](#papers), and a neat [pile](#pile) is [paper_stack](#paper_stack).

entries.name: open_book
entries.description: A [book](#book) held or [lying](#lying) with its [pages](#pages) spread. Add [reading](#reading) when somebody is actually reading from it.

entries.name: card
entries.description: A small flat printed card physically present in the scene: [playing](#playing) cards, trading cards, [tarot](#tarot), business or identity cards. A whole picture laid out as a card face is [card_(medium)](#card_(medium)).

entries.name: pen
entries.description: An [ink](#ink) [writing](#writing) [instrument](#instrument), ballpoint, [fountain](#fountain) or felt tip, drawn as an object or in use. A tablet [stylus](#stylus) is stylus and never this, while art made with a pen is [pen_(medium)](#pen_(medium)).

entries.name: id_card
entries.description: A [card](#card) that identifies its bearer: a student card, a [driving](#driving) licence, a [staff](#staff) [badge](#badge). It usually hangs from a [lanyard](#lanyard) or is clipped to a [pocket](#pocket).

entries.name: photo_(object)
entries.description: A photograph appearing as an item within a drawing: a snapshot held in the hand, [pinned](#pinned) to a wall, framed or tucked in a [locket](#locket). The post itself is not a photograph.

entries.name: paintbrush
entries.description: The general [tag](#tag) for a painting brush. Add the specific kind as [well](#well), whether [art_brush](#art_brush), [calligraphy_brush](#calligraphy_brush) or [trim_brush](#trim_brush), rather than leaving this one on its own.

entries.name: pencil
entries.description: A pencil present in the picture, held, tucked behind an ear or [lying](#lying) on a [desk](#desk). Work actually drawn in pencil is [graphite_(medium)](#graphite_(medium)).

entries.name: chalkboard
entries.description: A [dark](#dark) [writing](#writing) surface meant to be marked with [chalk](#chalk), as a rule hung on a [classroom](#classroom) wall. It is usually covered in lessons, notices or doodles.

entries.name: scroll
entries.description: A long sheet of [paper](#paper) rolled up at one or both ends, usually bearing [writing](#writing). Tag it whether held, unrolled, or simply [lying](#lying) about; [ofuda](#ofuda) and talismans are treated separately.

entries.name: clipboard
entries.description: A flat board with a sprung clip at the top [holding](#holding) sheets of [paper](#paper). Carried by nurses, doctors, researchers and [waiting](#waiting) [staff](#staff) who need to write [standing](#standing) up.

entries.name: book_stack
entries.description: Several books piled one on the next into a small [tower](#tower), on a [desk](#desk), on the [floor](#floor) or cradled in someone's arms. Volumes stored upright in rows are a [bookshelf](#bookshelf).

entries.name: notebook
entries.description: A [bound](#bound) [book](#book) of blank [pages](#pages) for [writing](#writing) or drawing, often spiral-bound with tear-out sheets. A notebook [computer](#computer) is [laptop](#laptop).

entries.name: poster_(object)
entries.description: A large printed picture [pinned](#pinned) or pasted on a wall inside the scene. When the entire image is itself a poster, use [poster_(medium)](#poster_(medium)).

entries.name: letter
entries.description: A written message on [folded](#folded) [paper](#paper), often with its [envelope](#envelope), being read, written, carried or handed over. A romantic one is [love_letter](#love_letter).

entries.name: envelope
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [packet](#packet) for a [letter](#letter) or a document, sealed, being opened, or held out to somebody. Love letters and invitations are the usual reason it appears. Add letter when the contents are shown.

entries.name: map
entries.description: A drawn representation of a place with roads, terrain or landmarks, on [paper](#paper), in an atlas, on a [screen](#screen) or wrapped around a [globe](#globe). Applies whether it is being studied or simply present.

entries.name: calligraphy_brush
entries.description: A round-tipped [ink](#ink) brush for East Asian [calligraphy](#calligraphy) and ink painting, broader than an ordinary art brush. A picture actually painted with one takes calligraphy_brush_(medium).

entries.name: shikishi
entries.description: A stiff, squarish sheet of paperboard used for sketches, [calligraphy](#calligraphy) and autographs, recognizable by its firm edges in photos of traditional artwork. Common for [convention](#convention) giveaway drawings; a shikishi drawn within a picture is shikishi_(object) instead.

entries.name: newspaper
entries.description: A printed sheet of [news](#news) and articles on cheap [paper](#paper), whether being read, [folded](#folded) under an arm, or [lying](#lying) about the scene.

entries.name: paint
entries.description: Wet pigment as a substance, in a [can](#can) or a [tube](#tube), laid out on a palette, or splashed and smeared over something. The brush and board are [paintbrush](#paintbrush) and [palette_(object)](#palette_(object)), and the act of using it is [painting_(action)](#painting_(action)).

entries.name: drawing_(object)
entries.description: A picture on [paper](#paper) or canvas that exists inside the scene, either being worked on by a character or already finished and set in a frame. The illustration you are looking at as a whole does not count. For the act itself, use [drawing_(action)](#drawing_(action)).

entries.name: quill
entries.description: A [writing](#writing) [pen](#pen) cut from a large feather and dipped in [ink](#ink). Typical of historical, [fantasy](#fantasy), and scholarly scenes; combine with [inkwell](#inkwell), [paper](#paper), or writing depending on what else is shown.

entries.name: tissue
entries.description: A thin sheet of soft [paper](#paper) for [wiping](#wiping) a [nose](#nose) or [cleaning](#cleaning) up, held or [lying](#lying) about. Add [tissue_box](#tissue_box) when the [box](#box) it comes from is shown.

entries.name: calendar_(object)
entries.description: A calendar hangs on a wall or stands on a [desk](#desk) within the picture. The picture itself is not a calendar page — that would be [calendar_(medium)](#calendar_(medium)).

entries.name: magazine_(object)
entries.description: A printed periodical in the scene, read, held or left [lying](#lying) about. Adult titles take [pornography](#pornography) as [well](#well); the [ammunition](#ammunition) kind is [magazine_(weapon)](#magazine_(weapon)), and a front page shown by itself is [magazine_cover](#magazine_cover).

entries.name: eraser
entries.description: A small block of rubber or plastic for [rubbing](#rubbing) out [pencil](#pencil) marks, sometimes fixed to the end of a pencil. A [desk](#desk) item in [classroom](#classroom) and study scenes.

entries.name: manga_(object)
entries.description: A [comic](#comic) volume, doujinshi or western comic [book](#book) present in the scene as a physical thing, being read or left [lying](#lying) about. Where the picture itself is drawn as a comic, that is comic.

entries.name: sketchbook
entries.description: A [bound](#bound) pad of blank [pages](#pages) for drawing, held or open in front of a character. Frequently seen with a [pencil](#pencil) and the drawing activity.

entries.name: menu
entries.description: A restaurant's printed [list](#list) of [dishes](#dishes) and prices, held by a customer or [lying](#lying) on the [table](#table). A free-standing [sign](#sign) listing the same is [menu_board](#menu_board).

entries.name: ink
entries.description: Coloured [liquid](#liquid) for [writing](#writing), drawing or printing, whether in a [bottle](#bottle), loaded on a brush or thrown across the picture as splotches and strokes. It is the substance itself that is being tagged.

entries.name: marker
entries.description: A felt-tip [pen](#pen) present in the picture as an object, held in a hand or [lying](#lying) on a [desk](#desk). Artwork actually coloured with markers takes [marker_(medium)](#marker_(medium)).

entries.name: notepad
entries.description: A small pad of blank sheets for jotting things down, often held with a [pen](#pen) by reporters, waiters or detectives.

entries.name: palette_(object)
entries.description: The painter's board or [tray](#tray) on which colours are set out and mixed, usually with a thumb [hole](#hole) at one end. A [chart](#chart) of the colours used in the picture itself is a [color_guide](#color_guide).

entries.name: love_letter
entries.description: A [letter](#letter) confessing romantic feelings, nearly always in an [envelope](#envelope) sealed with a heart-shaped [sticker](#sticker). It is typically being handed over, read, or found tucked into a shoe [locker](#locker).

entries.name: mechanical_pencil
entries.description: A click [pencil](#pencil) with a [push-button](#push-button) top that advances a thin lead through the tip, shown here as an object in the scene. A picture actually drawn with one instead takes the graphite medium [tag](#tag).

entries.name: toilet_paper
entries.description: A roll or sheets of soft [paper](#paper) for use after the [toilet](#toilet), on a holder or being unrolled. Frequently a comedic prop.

entries.name: globe
entries.description: A scale [model](#model) of the Earth, usually mounted on a tilted stand so it [can](#can) be spun. Effectively a [map](#map) wrapped onto a sphere.

entries.name: origami
entries.description: Figures [folded](#folded) from [paper](#paper), such as cranes, boats or blossoms, or the folding itself. A Japanese craft that turns up in [classroom](#classroom) and [festival](#festival) scenes.

entries.name: bookmark
entries.description: A strip of [card](#card), [ribbon](#ribbon) or plastic slipped between [pages](#pages) to hold a reader's place, shown protruding from the [book](#book) or held in the hand. It normally appears alongside a book.

entries.name: portrait_(object)
entries.description: A painted or framed [portrait](#portrait) appears inside the scene, on a wall or held, while the picture itself is not framed as a portrait. Tag [painting_(object)](#painting_(object)) as [well](#well) when relevant.

entries.name: tanzaku
entries.description: A narrow [paper](#paper) strip for [writing](#writing) a wish at the Tanabata [festival](#festival), later hung on [bamboo](#bamboo). Resembles a [bookmark](#bookmark) before it is tied on.

entries.name: pornography
entries.description: Erotic media appears as an object within the scene: a porn magazine, DVD, poster or manga a character is looking at or [hiding](#hiding). Not for pictures that are themselves pornographic.

entries.name: canvas_(object)
entries.description: Cloth stretched over a wooden frame as a surface to [paint](#paint) on, [standing](#standing) on an [easel](#easel), hung on a wall or carried under an arm. Often blank or only half worked.

entries.name: chalk
entries.description: A [stick](#stick) of chalk for marking a board or a [pavement](#pavement), held in the fingers or [resting](#resting) in a [tray](#tray). The stick has to be visible, since marks alone do not count.

entries.name: paper_airplane
entries.description: A simple [glider](#glider) [folded](#folded) from a sheet of [paper](#paper), thrown, in flight, or held ready. Often stands in for a message or for childhood.

entries.name: ruler
entries.description: A straight-edge [measuring](#measuring) [instrument](#instrument), held or [lying](#lying) on a [desk](#desk). School [stationery](#stationery); occasionally wielded as a teacher's prop.

entries.name: inkwell
entries.description: A small pot or [bottle](#bottle) of [ink](#ink) for dipping a [pen](#pen) or brush. It generally stands on a [desk](#desk) beside [paper](#paper) and quills.

entries.name: easel
entries.description: An upright [tripod](#tripod) stand [holding](#holding) a canvas or board at [working](#working) [height](#height). Belongs to studios, art classes and outdoor painting, usually beside a palette and brushes.

entries.name: crayon
entries.description: A [stick](#stick) of coloured [wax](#wax) for drawing, alone or in a boxed set, often in a child's hand. A picture actually drawn in wax crayon takes a medium [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: papers
entries.description: Many separate sheets of [paper](#paper), usually scattered about, [blowing](#blowing) through the air, or strewn across a [floor](#floor) or [desk](#desk). A tidy [pile](#pile) is [paper_stack](#paper_stack) and a single sheet is paper.

entries.name: art_brush
entries.description: A small painter's brush with a round or flat tip, held in the hand or [standing](#standing) in a [jar](#jar). Wide [decorating](#decorating) brushes and [calligraphy](#calligraphy) brushes take their own tags.

entries.name: paper_stack
entries.description: Sheets of [paper](#paper) piled neatly into a [stack](#stack), [resting](#resting) on a [desk](#desk) or carried in the arms. Suggests [paperwork](#paperwork); sheets [flying](#flying) about loose are [papers](#papers).

entries.name: nib_pen_(object)
entries.description: A [pen](#pen) that writes through a metal nib fed with [liquid](#liquid) [ink](#ink), shown as an object in the scene. Quills are counted separately, and artwork actually drawn with one is [nib_pen_(medium)](#nib_pen_(medium)).

entries.name: sticky_note
entries.description: A small [square](#square) of [paper](#paper) with a [glue](#glue) strip, [stuck](#stuck) to a [screen](#screen), wall or document as a reminder; usually yellow.

entries.name: tag
entries.description: A physical [label](#label) shown in the picture, such as a clothing tag, a name tag or a livestock ear tag.

entries.name: paper_crane
entries.description: The [folded](#folded) [paper](#paper) crane, the best known [origami](#origami) [figure](#figure), modelled on the long-necked [bird](#bird). Shown singly, strung in the thousand for a wish, or used as a motif.

entries.name: flying_paper
entries.description: Sheets of [paper](#paper) visibly airborne, thrown up by [wind](#wind), a blast or a dropped [stack](#stack). Office chaos and dramatic reveals lean on it.

entries.name: note
entries.description: A single sheet of [paper](#paper) [carrying](#carrying) a written message or a drawing, perhaps [torn](#torn) from a pad, taped to a wall or left on a [table](#table). Musical symbols are [musical_note](#musical_note).

entries.name: floating_book
entries.description: A [book](#book) [hanging](#hanging) in mid-air, generally held up by [levitation](#levitation) [magic](#magic) beside a mage or [witch](#witch).

entries.name: ticket
entries.description: A printed slip granting entry to a show, [train](#train) or venue, held or shown. Add the event or setting such as [train_station](#train_station) or [concert](#concert).

entries.name: menu_board
entries.description: A free-standing [sign](#sign) outside or inside a [restaurant](#restaurant) or [cafe](#cafe) listing [dishes](#dishes) and daily specials. Overlaps with [chalkboard](#chalkboard) when the lettering is handwritten.

entries.name: whiteboard
entries.description: A glossy white board meant for dry-erase markers, mounted on a wall or stand. Its presence marks an [office](#office), meeting room, or [classroom](#classroom), and any [writing](#writing) on it may take its own text tags.

entries.name: polaroid_photo
entries.description: An instant print, its [square](#square) image [sitting](#sitting) inside a broad white [border](#border), held up, [pinned](#pinned) to a wall, or scattered across a [table](#table). Characters are often drawn [shaking](#shaking) one, though modern film gains nothing from it.

entries.name: wanted_poster
entries.description: A notice showing a fugitive's face and name under the word WANTED, sometimes with a bounty or [list](#list) of crimes. A [staple](#staple) of Western and [pirate](#pirate) settings.

entries.name: folder
entries.description: A folding [cover](#cover) for keeping loose sheets together, carried by [office](#office) workers and students. It turns up under an arm, on a [desk](#desk), or clutched to the chest.

entries.name: wax_seal
entries.description: A [blob](#blob) of [wax](#wax) hardened over the flap of a [letter](#letter) and stamped with a [crest](#crest) or [initial](#initial). It marks correspondence as formal, secret or old-fashioned.

entries.name: hanging_scroll
entries.description: A painting or piece of [calligraphy](#calligraphy) mounted on [cloth](#cloth) backing and hung vertically, weighted by a rod along the bottom edge. In a Japanese room it hangs in the tokonoma alcove and is swapped with the season.

entries.name: map_(object)
entries.description: A [map](#map) present in the scene as a physical thing: unfolded between two hands, spread over a [table](#table), [pinned](#pinned) up on a wall. The picture is not itself a map.

entries.name: pen_in_pocket
entries.description: A [pen](#pen) clipped into a [shirt](#shirt) or breast [pocket](#pocket). A small [costume](#costume) detail that reads as [office](#office) or [school](#school) work.

entries.name: book_on_lap
entries.description: A [book](#book) [resting](#resting) on the [thighs](#thighs) of somebody [sitting](#sitting) down, open or closed. They may be [reading](#reading) it or may simply have set it there.

entries.name: paper_on_head
entries.description: A loose sheet of [paper](#paper) draped over someone's head, most often [hanging](#hanging) down in front of the face like a makeshift [mask](#mask). Not the same as wearing a [folded](#folded) paper [hat](#hat).

entries.name: stapler
entries.description: The [desk](#desk) [device](#device) that drives a [staple](#staple) through a [stack](#stack) of [paper](#paper) and folds its ends flat underneath. A fixture of [office](#office) and [classroom](#classroom) scenes.

entries.name: stick_poster
entries.description: A print made much taller and narrower than an ordinary pin-up poster, closer in proportion to a [hanging](#hanging) [banner](#banner). The elongated vertical format is the whole point of the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: diploma
entries.description: A certificate awarded for finishing a course, drawn rolled up with a [ribbon](#ribbon) or held flat in a stiff [folder](#folder). Graduation scenes almost always include one.

entries.name: crumpled_paper
entries.description: A sheet of [paper](#paper) wrinkled all over or screwed into a [ball](#ball) and thrown away. Reads as a discarded draft or a [letter](#letter) the writer could not finish.

entries.name: paint_tube
entries.description: A soft squeezable [tube](#tube) of artist's colour, its contents pressed out onto a palette. Belongs with the rest of a painter's kit.

entries.name: shochuumimai
entries.description: A midsummer greeting [postcard](#postcard) sent in Japan to ask after [friends](#friends) during the hottest weeks, [carrying](#carrying) its own set phrase and usually illustrated with a [summer](#summer) scene.

entries.name: academic_test
entries.description: A marked examination [paper](#paper), usually with the score plainly readable. Japanese marking puts circles on correct answers and check marks on wrong ones, and the [tag](#tag) wants an actual sheet rather than a figurative trial.

entries.name: binder
entries.description: A stiff-covered [ring](#ring) [folder](#folder) [holding](#holding) [punched](#punched) sheets and smaller folders inside it. For the undergarment that flattens the chest, chest_binder is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: pile_of_books
entries.description: Books heaped on one another without order rather than shelved or squared into a neat [stack](#stack). Common in study, [library](#library) and bookworm scenes, sometimes towering beside a [desk](#desk).

entries.name: pages
entries.description: Loose leaves that have come out of a [book](#book), scattered on the ground, held in the hand or [drifting](#drifting) through the air. A [bound](#bound) volume [lying](#lying) open is something else.

entries.name: postage_stamp
entries.description: A small perforated [rectangle](#rectangle) of printed [paper](#paper) [stuck](#stuck) to [mail](#mail) as proof that [carriage](#carriage) was paid. Drawn on an [envelope](#envelope), or blown up so its design frames a character.

entries.name: notes
entries.description: Written slips of [paper](#paper) in the scene, such as memos, [sticky](#sticky) notes or [pinned](#pinned) messages, usually [carrying](#carrying) a short line of text.

entries.name: test_score
entries.description: A grade written onto a returned exam or [homework](#homework) sheet, usually a number circled in [ink](#ink). A perfect mark or a humiliating one is generally the joke.

entries.name: diary
entries.description: A private [notebook](#notebook) kept for daily entries, often clasped or locked. Shown being written in, read through or hidden away.

entries.name: blueprint_(object)
entries.description: A technical drawing of a [building](#building), vehicle or [weapon](#weapon) shown as a prop: unrolled on a [table](#table), [pinned](#pinned) up or held open to read. Often but not always printed on blue [paper](#paper); a picture drawn in that style takes the medium [tag](#tag).

entries.name: book_on_head
entries.description: A [book](#book), or a whole [stack](#stack) of them, balanced on top of somebody's head. Sometimes it is deportment practice, sometimes just the nearest flat surface.

entries.name: placard
entries.description: A [sign](#sign) mounted on a [stick](#stick) and held aloft so others [can](#can) read it, used to protest, greet or announce something. The [handle](#handle) is what separates it from a sign fixed to a wall.

entries.name: colored_pencil
entries.description: Coloured pencils present as objects in the picture, held in the hand, spilled across a [desk](#desk) or [standing](#standing) in a pot. Work actually drawn with them is [colored_pencil_(medium)](#colored_pencil_(medium)).

entries.name: cardboard
entries.description: Heavy [paper](#paper) board, [plain](#plain) or corrugated, seen as flat sheets, boxes and improvised props. Cheap, brown and easily cut to shape.

entries.name: typewriter
entries.description: A mechanical [writing](#writing) [machine](#machine) with a keyboard, striking arms and a [carriage](#carriage) that steps the [paper](#paper) along one line at a time. Signals an older setting, or one deliberately styled as retro.

entries.name: photo_album
entries.description: A [bound](#bound) [book](#book) of sleeves or [pages](#pages) [holding](#holding) printed photographs, usually [lying](#lying) open or being leafed through. Memory and nostalgia scenes are its usual home.

entries.name: postcard
entries.description: A stiff [card](#card) with a picture on one face and room for a message on the other. Either an actual card held in the scene, or the whole image staged to look like one.

entries.name: textbook
entries.description: A [bound](#bound) schoolbook of lessons and exercises, [lying](#lying) open on a [desk](#desk) or carried under an arm. Classroom and study scenes are its natural home.

entries.name: mail
entries.description: Letters and parcels in the post: a bundle of envelopes, something pushed through a [door](#door) slot, a [package](#package) carried in after [delivery](#delivery). The post itself is the point, not whoever brought it.

entries.name: homework
entries.description: School assignments to be finished at home: worksheets, exercise books and problem sets spread across a [desk](#desk). The untouched [pile](#pile) facing the end of the [summer](#summer) holidays is a favourite version.

entries.name: stationery
entries.description: An assortment of [writing](#writing) and [desk](#desk) supplies shown together: pens, erasers, rulers, notepads, [tape](#tape). Use it for a spread of such items, not for a single [pencil](#pencil).

entries.name: trim_brush
entries.description: A broad, flat-tipped brush meant for painting walls, doors and furniture. Artists occasionally pick one up for actual pictures too, which is when it shows up in art-making scenes.

entries.name: stapled
entries.description: Sheets or other material held together with staples [punched](#punched) through them, the pinched metal visible at the join. Common on handouts, booklets and notices.

entries.name: too_many_books
entries.description: Books in bulk: stacked in towers, [spilling](#spilling) from shelves, heaped around a reader, usually more than the room could plausibly hold.

entries.name: character_sticker
entries.description: An adhesive [sticker](#sticker) printed with a character, pressed onto a [notebook](#notebook), [phone](#phone) case, [locker](#locker) or wall. Uncut sheets of them count as [well](#well).

entries.name: wooden_pencil
entries.description: The classic [pencil](#pencil), a graphite [core](#core) inside a painted wooden shaft sharpened to a point. It gets held for [writing](#writing) or drawing, or simply left [lying](#lying) on a [desk](#desk).

entries.name: flyer
entries.description: A single printed sheet advertising a product, a [shop](#shop) or an event, cheap enough to hand out or paste up. Look for a small poster-like page held, [pinned](#pinned) or scattered underfoot.

entries.name: ink_stamp
entries.description: A hand stamp and the coloured mark it leaves behind, from a carved name seal to a novelty rubber one. Both the tool and its impression count.

entries.name: torn_paper
entries.description: Paper ripped through with a ragged edge: a [letter](#letter), a photo, a poster or a page pulled in two.

entries.name: staple
entries.description: A small bent [wire](#wire) that clamps sheets of [paper](#paper) together, shown driven home or [lying](#lying) loose.

entries.name: business_card
entries.description: A small printed [card](#card) [carrying](#carrying) a person's name, employer, position and contact details. Often held out in both hands during a formal exchange.

entries.name: cardboard_cutout
entries.description: A character printed life-size on stiff board and stood upright, the sort used for [shop](#shop) displays and photo [spots](#spots). Flat from the side, which is often the joke.

entries.name: rolled_up_paper
entries.description: A sheet of [paper](#paper) wound into a [tube](#tube), held in the hand or tucked under an arm. Frequently used as a harmless swatting implement in comedy scenes.

entries.name: paper_boat
entries.description: A little [boat](#boat) [folded](#folded) from a sheet of [paper](#paper), floated on a [puddle](#puddle) or a [stream](#stream), or held up in the hand. A children's craft, generally with a wistful [note](#note) to it.

entries.name: yaoi_(object)
entries.description: A manga, magazine or other printed item about male-male romance, appearing as a physical object within the scene. It is usually a prop held by a fan character rather than a [label](#label) for the artwork itself.

entries.name: palette_knife
entries.description: A blunt spatula- or trowel-shaped blade used to mix [paint](#paint) and lay it on a canvas. The straight rounded sort mixes and scrapes, while the angular pointed sort lifts colour and applies it.

entries.name: marriage_certificate_(object)
entries.description: A [wedding](#wedding) document present in the scene as a sheet of [paper](#paper), held up, being signed, or [lying](#lying) on a [table](#table). What it says need not be readable.

entries.name: receipt
entries.description: A narrow printed slip listing purchases and a total, curling out of a till or held in someone's hand. Often used as a [gag](#gag) when the total shown is absurd.

entries.name: pencil_behind_ear
entries.description: A [pencil](#pencil) tucked over the ear for safekeeping, leaving both hands free. Shorthand for somebody in the middle of a job.

entries.name: file
entries.description: Papers gathered and kept together, or the [folder](#folder), [binder](#binder) or [drawer](#drawer) [holding](#holding) them. It also covers the stacked-document icons that stand for [computer](#computer) files.

entries.name: lined_paper
entries.description: Paper ruled with horizontal [guide](#guide) lines for handwriting, drawn on, written on or [serving](#serving) as the surface of the picture itself.

entries.name: paper_cutout
entries.description: A printable papercraft sheet: the flat parts of a [model](#model) laid out to be cut free and [folded](#folded) together, sometimes with the assembly [notes](#notes) printed alongside.

entries.name: pamphlet
entries.description: A thin unbound booklet or [folded](#folded) leaflet, printed on both sides and creased into panels or [stitched](#stitched) at the fold. Handed out, read, or spread open on a [table](#table).

entries.name: stone_tablet
entries.description: A flat slab of [rock](#rock) with [writing](#writing) or symbols carved into its surface. Used for inscriptions, ancient records and prophecies.

entries.name: missing_poster
entries.description: A printed notice appealing for a lost person, [pet](#pet) or object, [carrying](#carrying) a photograph and details beneath a heading. Pinned to a wall or held out for someone to read.

entries.name: phonecard
entries.description: A prepaid [card](#card) the size of a credit card, once fed into a public [phone](#phone) to pay for calls. Japanese ones often carry printed character art and are collected as [merchandise](#merchandise).

entries.name: open_magazine
entries.description: A magazine held or [lying](#lying) with its [pages](#pages) spread so a double spread [can](#can) be seen. Meant for the printed periodical, never for a firearm's magazine.

entries.name: manila_envelope
entries.description: A large light-brown [envelope](#envelope) for documents, usually closed by winding [string](#string) around a button eyelet. It takes its name from the tough [paper](#paper) it was first made from.

entries.name: script
entries.description: The [bound](#bound) [working](#working) [pages](#pages) of a play, film, or broadcast, [carrying](#carrying) the spoken lines along with the directions around them. Usually shown held open, marked up, or read aloud.

entries.name: graph_paper
entries.description: Paper ruled into a fine regular [grid](#grid) for plotting curves and data. It may be a sheet [lying](#lying) in the scene or the surface the whole picture is drawn on.

entries.name: pushpin
entries.description: A short [pin](#pin) with a rounded or spool-shaped head, pressed in to hold [paper](#paper) on a board. Where the head is flat instead, the [tag](#tag) is [thumbtack](#thumbtack).

entries.name: bamboo_slips
entries.description: Narrow strips of [bamboo](#bamboo) or wood, each brushed with a single [column](#column) of characters and [bound](#bound) side by side into a roll. They served as books in China before [paper](#paper) came into general use.

entries.name: calling_card
entries.description: A printed [card](#card) left behind to announce who came, the [signature](#signature) move of the phantom [thief](#thief). It usually carries a name, an [emblem](#emblem) or a short [taunting](#taunting) message.

entries.name: glass_pen
entries.description: A [writing](#writing) [instrument](#instrument) of solid [glass](#glass) whose twisted tip traps [ink](#ink) in its grooves and releases it like a nib. Prized for its looks in [stationery](#stationery) and letter-writing scenes.

entries.name: star_map
entries.description: A [chart](#chart) of the [night](#night) [sky](#sky) with the constellations drawn in, on [paper](#paper), parchment or a [screen](#screen). Turns up in astronomy, navigation and fortune-telling scenes.

entries.name: cookbook
entries.description: A [book](#book) of recipes, propped open on a [counter](#counter) or carried into the [kitchen](#kitchen). Usually the source of whatever dish is being attempted.

entries.name: scroll_tube
entries.description: A cylindrical case for [carrying](#carrying) a rolled [scroll](#scroll) or [map](#map), capped at one end and often slung from a cord.

entries.name: graph_(object)
entries.description: A [chart](#chart) present as a prop or as background decoration, often [carrying](#carrying) arbitrary data on a [screen](#screen), [whiteboard](#whiteboard) or poster. When the chart is the point of the picture, or a meaningful [inset](#inset), use [graph](#graph).

entries.name: passport
entries.description: The small travel booklet that lets its bearer [cross](#cross) a [border](#border), usually drawn open at the photograph page or held out to an official. A prop for [airport](#airport), customs and journey scenes.

entries.name: article
entries.description: A piece of [newspaper](#newspaper) or magazine [writing](#writing) shown in the picture, its headline and columns legible or at least suggested. It may be printed on [paper](#paper) or on a [screen](#screen).

entries.name: children's_book
entries.description: A picture [book](#book) made for young readers, big illustrations and very little text. It appears open on a [lap](#lap), read aloud, or stacked on a [shelf](#shelf).

entries.name: pop-up_book
entries.description: A [book](#book) whose spreads unfold into [standing](#standing) [paper](#paper) scenes as it opens. Often used as a framing [device](#device), with characters inhabiting the cut-out set.

entries.name: picture_book
entries.description: An illustrated [book](#book) for small children in which the pictures carry most of the story and the words are few. Usually held open, read aloud or spread across a [lap](#lap).

entries.name: list
entries.description: A written list appears in the picture, its items set out line by line on [paper](#paper), a board or a [screen](#screen).

entries.name: book_strap
entries.description: A buckled band, usually [leather](#leather), wrapped around a shut [book](#book) or a [pile](#pile) of them so the covers stay closed while they are moved. Grimoires often wear one; a [strap](#strap) that hangs the book off a [belt](#belt) is a book [holster](#holster).

entries.name: tearing_paper
entries.description: Hands pull a sheet of [paper](#paper) apart, the halves separating along a ragged line. Often a [letter](#letter), a photograph or a failing exam being [destroyed](#destroyed) in anger or grief.

entries.name: world_map
entries.description: A [map](#map) showing the continents of an entire world, whether on [paper](#paper), a [screen](#screen), or a wall. It is often spread out while a journey is being planned.

entries.name: box
entries.description: A cubic or oblong [container](#container) of [card](#card), wood, plastic or metal, open or shut, anywhere from a shipping [carton](#carton) to a small trinket case. Where the kind is obvious, add the narrower [tag](#tag) such as [cardboard_box](#cardboard_box), [gift_box](#gift_box) or [box_of_chocolates](#box_of_chocolates).

entries.name: plate
entries.description: A flat dish for [serving](#serving) [food](#food), usually round, whether empty or [holding](#holding) a [meal](#meal). Bowls and cups are tagged separately, and the food [resting](#resting) on it takes its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: tray
entries.description: A flat board with a raised rim for [carrying](#carrying) [dishes](#dishes), drinks or other small items, often held by a [waitress](#waitress) or [maid](#maid). Tag the [food](#food) or cups on it separately.

entries.name: bowl
entries.description: A round hollow dish for [soup](#soup), [rice](#rice), [ramen](#ramen), [cereal](#cereal) or [salad](#salad), empty or filled, on a [table](#table) or cupped in the hands. Name the [food](#food) in it, and use [bowl_hat](#bowl_hat) for one worn on the head.

entries.name: basket
entries.description: A [container](#container) woven from stiff fibre, or from plastic or [wire](#wire) in modern versions, with or without a [lid](#lid), used to carry [food](#food), [laundry](#laundry) or flowers. Narrow it to [picnic_basket](#picnic_basket), [shopping_basket](#shopping_basket) or [bicycle_basket](#bicycle_basket) where one of those fits.

entries.name: bucket
entries.description: An open-topped cylinder with a flat base and usually a [swing](#swing) [handle](#handle), made of metal, plastic or wood. Shown carried, tipped or [standing](#standing) full of [water](#water).

entries.name: sack
entries.description: A large [bag](#bag) of coarse material for [carrying](#carrying) bulk goods, from a [flour](#flour) sack to Santa's present sack. Small decorated bags for presents are [gift_bag](#gift_bag).

entries.name: in_container
entries.description: The catch-all for a character [sitting](#sitting) inside something meant to hold things: a [box](#box), [bucket](#bucket), [cup](#cup), [jar](#jar), [bag](#bag) or [basket](#basket). Add the specific [tag](#tag) such as [in_box](#in_box) or [in_cup](#in_cup) where one exists.

entries.name: cardboard_box
entries.description: A brown corrugated shipping [box](#box), carried, stacked, sat in by a [cat](#cat) or pulled over the head as a [hiding](#hiding) place. Usually drawn with open flaps and [tape](#tape) across the seam.

entries.name: suitcase
entries.description: A case for [carrying](#carrying) [clothes](#clothes) and belongings on a journey, made from [cloth](#cloth), [leather](#leather) or hard plastic. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [briefcase](#briefcase), which carries documents.

entries.name: heart-shaped_box
entries.description: A [box](#box) made in the shape of a [heart](#heart), the classic [wrapping](#wrapping) for Valentine chocolates. What is inside only counts once it [can](#can) be seen.

entries.name: jar
entries.description: A wide-mouthed vessel of [glass](#glass) or earthenware. What it holds is open, from [food](#food) and preserves to specimens, and a [container](#container) with a narrow [neck](#neck) counts as a [bottle](#bottle) instead.

entries.name: gourd
entries.description: The [bottle](#bottle) gourd's dumbbell-shaped [fruit](#fruit), usually drawn dried and hollowed into a [flask](#flask) for [sake](#sake) or [water](#water) and slung from a [belt](#belt). The fresh fruit or the growing [plant](#plant) counts too.

entries.name: tissue_box
entries.description: The [box](#box) that dispenses tissues one at a time through a slit on top. Often on a [bedside](#bedside) [table](#table); add [tissue](#tissue) when a sheet is out.

entries.name: paper_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) made of [paper](#paper), typically brown, of the kind used for [groceries](#groceries), takeaway or gifts. Not for any bag that merely happens to be brown; worn over the head it is paper_bag_on_head.

entries.name: cage
entries.description: An enclosure of [bars](#bars) or [wire](#wire) meant to confine a [bird](#bird) or [animal](#animal), occasionally [holding](#holding) a person for dramatic effect. Birdcages are the commonest form.

entries.name: frying_pan
entries.description: A flat-bottomed pan for frying, whether in use at a [stove](#stove) or swung as an improvised [weapon](#weapon). Nothing to do with the Japanese word pan, which means [bread](#bread).

entries.name: in_box
entries.description: A person or [creature](#creature) inside a [box](#box), settled down in it or peering over the edge. One of the [in_container](#in_container) [family](#family).

entries.name: plastic_bag
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) made of plastic, either an opaque coloured one or a clear one that shows its contents. Typically a convenience-store [shopping](#shopping) bag or a [gift](#gift) bag.

entries.name: rice_bowl
entries.description: A small rounded [bowl](#bowl) for a single [serving](#serving) of [rice](#rice), typical of Japanese and other East Asian meals. Tag with bowl and rice where the grains are visible.

entries.name: cooking_pot
entries.description: A deep vessel of metal, ceramic or [glass](#glass) for [boiling](#boiling), stewing or braising, [standing](#standing) on a [stove](#stove) or a [table](#table). A shallow pan for frying is a [frying_pan](#frying_pan) instead.

entries.name: vial
entries.description: A small [glass](#glass) [container](#container), usually sealable, for a little [liquid](#liquid) or powder such as a [medicine](#medicine), [potion](#potion) or lab sample. Use it for small glass vessels that [no](#no) more specific [tag](#tag) covers.

entries.name: barrel
entries.description: A big wooden cask of [bound](#bound) staves with metal hoops, used to age or store [wine](#wine), [beer](#beer) and spirits. A metal or plastic [drum](#drum) for fluids is [drum_(container)](#drum_(container)), and the cloth-wrapped casks stacked at shrines are sake_barrel.

entries.name: birdcage
entries.description: A [cage](#cage) built to [house](#house) [pet](#pet) birds, a domed or boxy frame of thin [bars](#bars), sometimes [hanging](#hanging) from a stand. It may hold a [bird](#bird), stand empty, or serve as a symbol placed around a character.

entries.name: halloween_bucket
entries.description: The [candy](#candy) [container](#container) carried by trick-or-treaters, usually shaped or painted like a [jack-o'-lantern](#jack-o'-lantern). Do not add the [plain](#plain) [bucket](#bucket) [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: wooden_bucket
entries.description: A [bucket](#bucket) built from wooden staves, the kind found at wells, bathhouses, and [hot](#hot) spring [onsen](#onsen). Tag bucket alongside it.

entries.name: tube
entries.description: A hollow cylinder used to hold something, open or capped at either end. A pipe carries things along rather than [holding](#holding) them and is tagged separately, and a named vessel such as [test_tube](#test_tube) gets its own specific [tag](#tag).

entries.name: treasure_chest
entries.description: A sturdy [box](#box) or chest [holding](#holding) loot such as [gold](#gold) coins, gems or [jewelry](#jewelry), [familiar](#familiar) from [pirate](#pirate) and [fantasy](#fantasy) settings. Often shown open and [overflowing](#overflowing) with its contents.

entries.name: in_bucket
entries.description: A character [sitting](#sitting) down inside a [bucket](#bucket) with only the upper body showing. One of the [in_container](#in_container) [family](#family).

entries.name: picnic_basket
entries.description: A wicker hamper, often lidded and lined with a checked [cloth](#cloth), for [carrying](#carrying) [food](#food) out to a [picnic](#picnic). Shown [swinging](#swinging) from a hand or [standing](#standing) open on the ground.

entries.name: tiered_tray
entries.description: A multi-level stand for [serving](#serving) cakes and sandwiches, typical of afternoon [tea](#tea). A single-level version is [cake_stand](#cake_stand); add [tea_set](#tea_set) when part of one.

entries.name: mixing_bowl
entries.description: A large [bowl](#bowl) for combining ingredients while [cooking](#cooking) or [baking](#baking), a fixture of birthday-cake preparation scenes.

entries.name: crate
entries.description: A large wooden or metal [box](#box) for storing and shipping goods, stacked in warehouses and on docks or used as [cover](#cover) in a fight. Smaller [cardboard](#cardboard) containers are simply a box.

entries.name: cooler
entries.description: An insulated [box](#box) that keeps [food](#food) and [drink](#drink) [cold](#cold), carried along to the [beach](#beach) or a [picnic](#picnic). Also known as an [ice](#ice) chest or ice box.

entries.name: coffin
entries.description: A six-sided [funeral](#funeral) [box](#box) with a [lid](#lid) that lifts off, the classic [graveyard](#graveyard) prop and vampire's [bed](#bed). The four-sided kind with a hinged lid is a casket.

entries.name: donation_box
entries.description: A wooden offering [box](#box) for coins, the slatted saisen-bako [standing](#standing) at the front of a [shrine](#shrine) or [temple](#temple). A box for charity collection is charity_box.

entries.name: candy_wrapper
entries.description: The [paper](#paper) or plastic [wrapping](#wrapping) from a piece of [candy](#candy), still around the sweet or dropped once it is eaten. Usually drawn with twisted ends.

entries.name: bamboo_steamer
entries.description: Round woven [bamboo](#bamboo) baskets with slatted bottoms and a domed [lid](#lid), stacked so that several layers cook at once. They are used for dumplings and buns, and are usually drawn with [steam](#steam) escaping the sides.

entries.name: pet_bowl
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) of [food](#food) or [water](#water) for an [animal](#animal), set on the [floor](#floor) and sometimes marked with a paw print or a name. It appears with cats and dogs and in [pet_play](#pet_play) scenes.

entries.name: pencil_case
entries.description: A [pouch](#pouch) or [box](#box) for [carrying](#carrying) pencils, pens and erasers, the sort students keep in a [school](#school) [bag](#bag). Shown [lying](#lying) on a [desk](#desk) or being rummaged through.

entries.name: in_cup
entries.description: A character, usually a tiny one, [sitting](#sitting) inside a [drinking](#drinking) vessel such as a [teacup](#teacup) or a tumbler. One of the [in_container](#in_container) [family](#family).

entries.name: drum_(container)
entries.description: A big cylindrical [container](#container) of metal or plastic for fluids and bulk goods, best known as the oil [barrel](#barrel). A wooden one is a barrel instead.

entries.name: pizza_box
entries.description: The flat [square](#square) [cardboard](#cardboard) [box](#box) a [pizza](#pizza) is delivered in, open or closed. Often stacked in [casual](#casual) or [party](#party) scenes, with the pizza itself tagged separately.

entries.name: cauldron
entries.description: A large metal [cooking](#cooking) pot with a [handle](#handle) and a [lid](#lid), hung or set over an open [fire](#fire). A fixture of witches' brews and camp cooking alike.

entries.name: food_wrapper
entries.description: Paper or plastic wrapped around a single [serving](#serving) of [food](#food), kept on for handling or peeled [back](#back) to eat from. Burger [papers](#papers), sweet wrappers and rice-ball film are typical.

entries.name: laundry_basket
entries.description: A deep open [basket](#basket) for [carrying](#carrying) [clothes](#clothes) to and from the wash, usually moulded plastic with pierced sides. It is generally drawn heaped with [washing](#washing).

entries.name: ketchup_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) of [ketchup](#ketchup), either the clear [supermarket](#supermarket) kind with the red contents showing or the squeezy red [diner](#diner) [tube](#tube) with a narrow spout. Its yellow twin holds [mustard](#mustard).

entries.name: carton
entries.description: A paperboard [container](#container) for [food](#food) or [drink](#drink). Prefer the narrower [tag](#tag) where one fits: [milk_carton](#milk_carton) for the gable-topped kind, [juice_box](#juice_box) for the small straw-fed sort, [box](#box) for a [plain](#plain) rectangular one.

entries.name: paint_can
entries.description: A metal tin of [paint](#paint) of the size used for walls and other large surfaces, [lid](#lid) prised off or still sealed. Decorating scenes usually put a brush or a roller beside it.

entries.name: food_packaging
entries.description: Shop packaging meant to sell [food](#food): printed cartons, sealed bags, tins and shrink-wrapped trays, usually [carrying](#carrying) a product name or [barcode](#barcode). Drink containers, single-serving wrappers and loose unwrapped produce are all excluded.

entries.name: package
entries.description: A parcel wrapped in [paper](#paper) or boxed and taped for posting, sometimes with a [label](#label) on top. Carried, handed over, or left [waiting](#waiting) at a [door](#door).

entries.name: container
entries.description: A general term for anything made to hold or carry things: bags, boxes, bottles, jars, cans, crates and the like. The specific vessel is normally tagged too, and a freight [box](#box) is [shipping_container](#shipping_container).

entries.name: fishbowl
entries.description: A round open-topped [glass](#glass) [bowl](#bowl) with a [goldfish](#goldfish) or two kept in it. Smaller and plainer than a proper [aquarium](#aquarium).

entries.name: wok
entries.description: A deep, round-bottomed pan used across Chinese [cooking](#cooking) for stir-frying and more. It is usually shown over a flame with [food](#food) being tossed inside it.

entries.name: wooden_box
entries.description: A [box](#box) or [crate](#crate) assembled from boards, [plain](#plain) and often left unpainted. It serves for storage or cargo, and gets sat on just as often.

entries.name: toolbox
entries.description: A portable case with a [handle](#handle) for [carrying](#carrying) the [tools](#tools) of a trade, shut or opened out into trays. Covers [construction](#construction), [car](#car) repair, [sewing](#sewing) and [fishing](#fishing) kits alike.

entries.name: shopping_basket
entries.description: The small plastic carry [basket](#basket) picked up near a [supermarket](#supermarket) [entrance](#entrance) and held by its [handle](#handle) while going round the aisles.

entries.name: in_bowl
entries.description: A living subject [sitting](#sitting) inside a [bowl](#bowl), usually a small character or an [animal](#animal) filling it. Food and objects served in a bowl do not count.

entries.name: pastry_box
entries.description: A [cardboard](#cardboard) [carton](#carton) built to carry cakes or doughnuts without squashing them, either a shallow [tray](#tray) or a taller [square](#square) [box](#box) with a [carrying](#carrying) slot cut in the [lid](#lid).

entries.name: lunchbox
entries.description: A single closed [box](#box) packed with a midday [meal](#meal) and carried to [school](#school) or work. Unlike a [bento](#bento) it need hold [no](#no) Japanese [food](#food) and does not [stack](#stack) into tiers.

entries.name: salt_shaker
entries.description: A small vessel with a perforated top for sprinkling [salt](#salt) at the [table](#table). Nearly always drawn beside its matching pepper twin.

entries.name: canister
entries.description: A cylindrical [container](#container), generally metal, [holding](#holding) [gas](#gas), [liquid](#liquid) or some particular item. It serves as the catch-all for cylinder-shaped vessels with [no](#no) [tag](#tag) of their own, though not for [thermos](#thermos) flasks.

entries.name: ring_box
entries.description: The small hinged case that holds a [ring](#ring), usually velvet-lined. Most often shown open in a proposal scene.

entries.name: basin
entries.description: A wide shallow [bowl](#bowl) [holding](#holding) [water](#water) for [washing](#washing) the hands, face or [laundry](#laundry). Metal, enamel or wooden ones stand on a [table](#table), a frame or the [floor](#floor).

entries.name: in_bag
entries.description: A character tucked inside a [bag](#bag) with only part of them showing over the [opening](#opening). Totes, duffels and [paper](#paper) carriers all qualify.

entries.name: nest
entries.description: A [cup](#cup) of twigs, [grass](#grass) or down built to hold eggs or young, usually a bird's. It may sit in a [tree](#tree) or on the ground, or hold a character curled up inside it.

entries.name: baking_sheet
entries.description: A flat rectangular metal [tray](#tray) with a shallow lip, used for biscuits, pastries and anything baked in a single layer. It also serves to carry a [cake](#cake) or [pie](#pie) tin in and out of the [oven](#oven).

entries.name: in_bottle
entries.description: A character enclosed in a [bottle](#bottle), which means drawn small enough to fit. Message-in-a-bottle framing and tiny figures pressed to the [glass](#glass) are the common versions.

entries.name: open_box
entries.description: A [box](#box) of any kind with its [lid](#lid) raised or its flaps [folded](#folded) [back](#back), so the contents, or the emptiness, [can](#can) be seen. Common in [gift](#gift) and parcel scenes.

entries.name: dishes
entries.description: An assortment of tableware together: plates, bowls, cups and trays stacked, [drying](#drying) or set out. A single piece takes its own narrower name, such as [plate](#plate).

entries.name: stack
entries.description: Objects piled neatly one on top of another into a [tower](#tower), whether books, boxes, plates or coins. The arrangement itself is what the [tag](#tag) is about.

entries.name: bucket_of_water
entries.description: A [bucket](#bucket) filled to the brim with [water](#water). It may be set down for [cleaning](#cleaning) or [watering](#watering), or balanced above a [door](#door) ready to fall on somebody.

entries.name: bucket_on_head
entries.description: A real [bucket](#bucket) is upended over somebody's head, covering it entirely. Headwear that merely looks like one is a [bucket_hat](#bucket_hat).

entries.name: in_cage
entries.description: A character shut inside a [cage](#cage), gripping or [leaning](#leaning) on the [bars](#bars). The cage may be room-sized or small enough to hang from a [hook](#hook).

entries.name: insect_cage
entries.description: The small [mesh](#mesh) [box](#box) Japanese children keep [caught](#caught) beetles and crickets in over the [summer](#summer). It is nearly always green plastic with a hinged [lid](#lid) on top.

entries.name: plate_stack
entries.description: Several plates set one on top of another in a [pile](#pile). Kitchens, restaurants and washing-up scenes all show them.

entries.name: lid
entries.description: The detachable [cover](#cover) of a pot, [jar](#jar), [box](#box) or [cup](#cup). Worth tagging above all when it has been taken off and sits apart from its [container](#container).

entries.name: pile
entries.description: A heap of things dumped or stacked on one another with [no](#no) order to them. Prefer the exact [tag](#tag) when the contents [can](#can) be named, such as [pile_of_books](#pile_of_books) or [pile_of_money](#pile_of_money).

entries.name: soy_sauce_bottle
entries.description: A [container](#container) built for dispensing soy [sauce](#sauce): either the small angled-spout [bottle](#bottle) used at the [table](#table) to limit the pour, or the larger brown bottle it's sold in at shops.

entries.name: bag_on_head
entries.description: A [bag](#bag) sits on top of somebody's head without being pulled down over it. Once the head is actually inside, [bag_over_head](#bag_over_head) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: broken_plate
entries.description: A [plate](#plate) chipped, cracked or smashed into [shards](#shards). It is generally the result of a drop, and spilled [food](#food) often lies beside it.

entries.name: shipping_container
entries.description: The standard steel freight [box](#box) that moves between [ship](#ship), rail and [truck](#truck). Stacked in ports and yards, or converted into a makeshift [building](#building).

entries.name: in_trash_can
entries.description: A person [sitting](#sitting) inside a rubbish bin, often with the [lid](#lid) balanced on their head. Self-deprecating jokes are the usual reason.

entries.name: sandbag
entries.description: A coarse [sack](#sack) packed with [sand](#sand) or earth. Stacked into walls against floodwater or gunfire, or hung and used as ballast and [weight](#weight).

entries.name: tank_(container)
entries.description: A rigid vessel built to hold [liquid](#liquid), [gas](#gas) or powder, usually cylindrical with rounded ends. Sizes range from [industrial](#industrial) storage drums down to the small [bottle](#bottle) [feeding](#feeding) a gas [mask](#mask); use it for the [container](#container), never for the armored vehicle.

entries.name: pepper_shaker
entries.description: The small perforated pot that dispenses ground pepper at the [table](#table), nearly always drawn beside its [salt](#salt) counterpart.

entries.name: ohitsu
entries.description: A round lidded wooden tub that cooked [rice](#rice) is turned into before it goes to the [table](#table), keeping it warm while drawing off the extra moisture.

entries.name: in_basket
entries.description: A living subject, person or [animal](#animal), [sitting](#sitting) inside a [basket](#basket). Cats and small characters curled into wicker are the usual sight.

entries.name: cake_stand
entries.description: A raised [pedestal](#pedestal) [plate](#plate) for displaying a [cake](#cake), sometimes under a [glass](#glass) [dome](#dome). It carries one level only; a [tiered_tray](#tiered_tray) is a different object.

entries.name: squeeze_bottle
entries.description: A soft plastic [bottle](#bottle) emptied by [squeezing](#squeezing), with a narrow nozzle at the top. Holds [ketchup](#ketchup), [mustard](#mustard), [syrup](#syrup), [lotion](#lotion) or [sunscreen](#sunscreen), and is sometimes called a squirt bottle.

entries.name: bird_nest
entries.description: A woven [cup](#cup) of twigs and [grass](#grass) built by a [bird](#bird), often [holding](#holding) eggs or chicks. Drawn in a [tree](#tree), on a [ledge](#ledge), or [sitting](#sitting) on somebody's head as a joke.

entries.name: hat_basket
entries.description: A [hat](#hat) put to work as a [container](#container), held brim upward and filled with [fruit](#fruit), flowers, eggs or whatever is being carried. It has come off the head to do the job.

entries.name: mikan_box
entries.description: A [cardboard](#cardboard) [crate](#crate) meant for mandarin oranges, printed with the [fruit](#fruit) or with the word written in kana. A recurring manga and anime prop: the [box](#box) a stray [kitten](#kitten) or [puppy](#puppy) is [abandoned](#abandoned) in at the roadside.

entries.name: packet
entries.description: A small sealed [pouch](#pouch) or sachet, the kind that holds snacks, seasoning, seeds or [medicine](#medicine). Held, [torn](#torn) open, or [lying](#lying) among other small things.

entries.name: honeypot
entries.description: A squat opaque crock for storing [honey](#honey). A [sticky](#sticky) smear around the rim, in the manner of a certain storybook [bear](#bear), is part of the look.

entries.name: milk_churn
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) metal [can](#can) with a narrow [neck](#neck) and a fitted [lid](#lid), used to collect and carry [milk](#milk) from the milking [shed](#shed). A farmyard prop.

entries.name: ice_bucket
entries.description: A pail packed with cubes to keep bottles [cold](#cold) away from a [refrigerator](#refrigerator). Bars, parties and [hotel](#hotel) rooms are where it appears, usually with a [bottle](#bottle) [standing](#standing) in it.

entries.name: gas_can
entries.description: A portable metal or plastic [container](#container) for [liquid](#liquid) fuel, with a [carrying](#carrying) [handle](#handle) and a [pouring](#pouring) spout. Shows up in roadside, arson and [post-apocalypse](#post-apocalypse) scenes.

entries.name: jerry_can
entries.description: A rectangular steel or plastic [can](#can) for fuel or [water](#water), known by the X-shaped press lines on each side and the row of handles across the top. Smaller petrol containers are [gas](#gas) cans.

entries.name: box_stack
entries.description: Boxes or crates piled one on another, sometimes [leaning](#leaning) or about to topple. Storerooms, warehouses, [delivery](#delivery) carts and half-finished moves are the usual settings.

entries.name: toy_packaging
entries.description: The [box](#box) or blister pack a [toy](#toy) is sold in, printed with the product name and often a [window](#window) over its contents. Sometimes drawn scaled up, with a living character [standing](#standing) inside as if they were the [merchandise](#merchandise).

entries.name: tasting_plate
entries.description: A small dish sized for sampling [soup](#soup) or [sauce](#sauce) while [cooking](#cooking), kin to the tiny [mamezara](#mamezara). Small enough to fit in one palm, it is usually held beside a pot.

entries.name: wicker_basket
entries.description: A [basket](#basket) woven from [cane](#cane) or [willow](#willow) with the plaiting left visible, usually fitted with a [handle](#handle). It carries [shopping](#shopping), [picnic](#picnic) [food](#food), or [laundry](#laundry).

entries.name: urn
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), rounded vessel with a narrow [neck](#neck) and often a footed base, used for [ashes](#ashes), storage or [plain](#plain) decoration. Turns up in classical, funerary and antique-shop settings.

entries.name: glass_bowl
entries.description: A [bowl](#bowl) of clear or tinted [glass](#glass), used for [food](#food), punch or simply as a [container](#container). The transparency is what this [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: bowl_stack
entries.description: Empty bowls piled one inside the next, stored in a [kitchen](#kitchen) or heaped on a [table](#table) once the [meal](#meal) is over. A [tall](#tall) [pile](#pile) is a [standing](#standing) joke about how much somebody has eaten.

entries.name: drop_trap
entries.description: A [box](#box), [crate](#crate) or [net](#net) propped on a [stick](#stick) with a [string](#string) [running](#running) [back](#back) to whoever waits to yank it. Baited and set for something small, and a cartoon [staple](#staple).

entries.name: qinghua_(porcelain)
entries.description: Chinese ceramic ware painted with cobalt-blue patterns under a clear glaze over white [clay](#clay), commonly called blue-and-white [pottery](#pottery). Its look shaped both Japanese Arita ware and Dutch Delftware.

entries.name: jewelry_box
entries.description: A small lidded case for rings, necklaces and [earrings](#earrings), usually lined in [fabric](#fabric) with a [mirror](#mirror) set in the [lid](#lid). It is generally drawn open, contents tumbling out.

entries.name: mayonnaise_bottle
entries.description: A soft plastic squeeze [bottle](#bottle) with a wide nozzle, built for a condiment much thicker than [ketchup](#ketchup) or [mustard](#mustard). Rarely made of [glass](#glass), since the contents are too viscous to pour cleanly from one.

entries.name: in_pot
entries.description: A character [sitting](#sitting) inside a [cooking](#cooking) pot, often up to the shoulders with the [lid](#lid) set aside. Comic stewing scenes are the usual setting.

entries.name: message_in_a_bottle
entries.description: A rolled [note](#note) sealed inside a corked [glass](#glass) [bottle](#bottle), [drifting](#drifting) at sea or washed up on the [sand](#sand). Stands in for a [letter](#letter) from an unknown sender.

entries.name: gas_cylinder
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) pressurised metal [bottle](#bottle) [holding](#holding) compressed [gas](#gas) such as propane or oxygen, with a [valve](#valve) on top. A [gas_can](#gas_can), by [contrast](#contrast), holds [liquid](#liquid) fuel.

entries.name: cereal_box
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) printed [carton](#carton) [breakfast](#breakfast) grain is sold in, a [mascot](#mascot) beaming off the front. It stands on [kitchen](#kitchen) tables and [shop](#shop) shelves, and gets read while somebody eats.

entries.name: mustard_bottle
entries.description: The squeeze [bottle](#bottle) [mustard](#mustard) is served from, either the clear [supermarket](#supermarket) kind or the narrow yellow [diner](#diner) [tube](#tube) with a pointed nozzle. The red [ketchup](#ketchup) bottle is its counterpart.

entries.name: takeout_container
entries.description: A [box](#box) or [tray](#tray) of [food](#food) meant to be carried away, such as a [folded](#folded) [paper](#paper) [carton](#carton) or a lidded plastic tray from a [delivery](#delivery) order. Marks the packaging rather than the [meal](#meal) itself.

entries.name: wooden_tray
entries.description: A flat wooden [tray](#tray) with low edges, carried with [food](#food), [tea](#tea), or [dishes](#dishes) set on top. Cafes and traditional inns use them constantly.

entries.name: in_jar
entries.description: Someone or something sealed in a [jar](#jar) and seen through the [glass](#glass). Small characters pressed against the curved wall are the usual sight.

entries.name: safe_(container)
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) lockable metal [box](#box) for keeping [money](#money), jewellery or documents away from thieves and [fire](#fire). Tagged whether it stands shut, is being cracked open, or gapes empty.

entries.name: box_on_head
entries.description: A [box](#box), usually [cardboard](#cardboard), sits over or balances on somebody's head, [hiding](#hiding) the face or simply perched there. The effect is nearly always [comic](#comic), and it often doubles as a makeshift hiding place.

entries.name: pottery
entries.description: Vessels and wares shaped from [clay](#clay) and fired hard: jars, bowls, [dishes](#dishes), pots and vases. Also takes in finer ceramic bodies such as stoneware and earthenware.

entries.name: empty_plate
entries.description: A [plate](#plate) with [no](#no) [food](#food) left on it. It reads as a [meal](#meal) already eaten, sometimes with [crumbs](#crumbs) or a smear of [sauce](#sauce) still there.

entries.name: in_sack
entries.description: A character inside a [cloth](#cloth) [sack](#sack), [peeking](#peeking) out of the mouth of it or outlined through the weave. Kidnapping gags and Santa deliveries both use it.

entries.name: juubako
entries.description: Lacquered boxes built to [stack](#stack) one on another, used to serve New Year [food](#food) or [eel](#eel) over [rice](#rice). Each tier is packed with its own arrangement.

entries.name: in_cauldron
entries.description: A character [sitting](#sitting) inside a large [cooking](#cooking) [cauldron](#cauldron), [steam](#steam) rising and often a [fire](#fire) beneath. Witch scenes and cartoon cooking gags are where it turns up.

entries.name: shoe_box
entries.description: The rectangular [cardboard](#cardboard) [box](#box) [shoes](#shoes) are sold in, with its separate [lid](#lid). Often shown stacked, or repurposed to store odds and ends.

entries.name: okamochi_(container)
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) wooden or metal case a Japanese [restaurant](#restaurant) carries deliveries in, with a [handle](#handle) over the top and shelves inside to keep bowls of [noodles](#noodles) level.

entries.name: mamezara
entries.description: A tiny dish set beside a main [plate](#plate) to hold soy [sauce](#sauce), a condiment or a small [garnish](#garnish). Common on a Japanese [table](#table) with [sashimi](#sashimi) or [cold](#cold) [soba](#soba).

entries.name: candy_jar
entries.description: A lidded [glass](#glass) or ceramic [jar](#jar) full of [sweets](#sweets), the contents showing through the sides. It sits on counters, desks and [shop](#shop) shelves.

entries.name: fish_bottle
entries.description: The little fish-shaped plastic [bottle](#bottle) of soy [sauce](#sauce) that comes with takeaway [sushi](#sushi) and [bento](#bento), capped in red. A tiny prop in [food](#food) scenes.

entries.name: porcelain
entries.description: Fine white fired ceramic, appearing as cups, plates, figurines and dolls. Its glassy, faintly [translucent](#translucent) surface sets it apart from coarser earthenware.

entries.name: storage_pot
entries.description: A large lidded crock or [jar](#jar) for keeping grain, pickles or [water](#water). Usually squat ceramic, [standing](#standing) on the [floor](#floor) or a low [shelf](#shelf).

entries.name: towel
entries.description: A piece of absorbent [cloth](#cloth) used for [drying](#drying) off, featured in [bath](#bath), [onsen](#onsen) and [beach](#beach) scenes. Where it is placed on the body earns its own [tag](#tag), such as [towel_on_head](#towel_on_head) or [towel_around_waist](#towel_around_waist).

entries.name: towel_around_neck
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) draped around the [neck](#neck) and, depending on its length, over the shoulders as [well](#well). Typical after exercise or a [bath](#bath).

entries.name: towel_on_head
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) worn or [folded](#folded) on top of the head, typical after a [bath](#bath) or in an [onsen](#onsen). Sometimes twisted into a [turban](#turban) shape rather than simply draped flat.

entries.name: beach_towel
entries.description: An outsized, brightly coloured [towel](#towel) spread on the [sand](#sand) or by a [pool](#pool) to lie on, or wrapped around a swimmer. Add [sunbathing](#sunbathing) when a character is stretched out on it in the [sun](#sun).

entries.name: handkerchief
entries.description: A small [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) for [wiping](#wiping) the face or [blowing](#blowing) the [nose](#nose). It also appears [folded](#folded) into the breast [pocket](#pocket) of a [suit](#suit) [jacket](#jacket) as a [dress](#dress) accessory.

entries.name: tablecloth
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) draped over a [table](#table), large enough to hang past its edges. A smaller piece that does not [cover](#cover) the whole surface is simply a cloth.

entries.name: napkin
entries.description: A [square](#square) of [cloth](#cloth) or [paper](#paper) used at the [table](#table) for [wiping](#wiping) the hands and mouth. It lies [folded](#folded) beside a [plate](#plate), tucked into a [collar](#collar), or held while [eating](#eating).

entries.name: doily
entries.description: A round ornamental [mat](#mat) worked in an openwork [lace](#lace) pattern, frequently used as a decorative element behind a subject. A [lace_border](#lace_border) along an edge, or a wider [lace_background](#lace_background), is a different thing.

entries.name: wet_towel
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) soaked with [water](#water), usually wrapped around a character and turning partly see-through. Add [naked_towel](#naked_towel) when nothing is worn beneath it.

entries.name: mat
entries.description: A padded [fabric](#fabric) mat laid down to [cushion](#cushion) a body, as in [gymnastics](#gymnastics) or on a [training](#training) [floor](#floor). Inflatable beds are [air_mattress](#air_mattress), [water](#water) floats [inflatable_raft](#inflatable_raft), [sleeping](#sleeping) mats [futon](#futon), [beach](#beach) mats [beach_towel](#beach_towel), and small [entrance](#entrance) mats [doormat](#doormat) or [rug](#rug).

entries.name: cloth
entries.description: A loose piece of [fabric](#fabric) put to some practical use, most often [wiping](#wiping) something down. Covering a [table](#table) makes it a [tablecloth](#tablecloth), [drying](#drying) a person makes it a [towel](#towel), and active scrubbing makes it a [cleaning](#cleaning) rag.

entries.name: towel_around_waist
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) wrapped around the hips and tucked or knotted at the side, the standard way of [stepping](#stepping) out of a [bath](#bath) or shower. Leaves the [legs](#legs) and upper body bare.

entries.name: beach_mat
entries.description: A woven or plastic [mat](#mat) spread over [sand](#sand) to sit and lie on. It appears under sunbathers alongside parasols, towels and drinks.

entries.name: picnic_blanket
entries.description: A [cloth](#cloth) spread flat on the [grass](#grass) to sit on and lay [food](#food) out, classically in red [gingham](#gingham) or check. Unlike a [bed](#bed) [blanket](#blanket) it is a ground [cover](#cover), not something drawn over a sleeper.

entries.name: furoshiki
entries.description: A [square](#square) Japanese [cloth](#cloth) used to wrap and carry things, its corners knotted into a bundle. Traditional depictions give it a green scrolling-vine pattern.

entries.name: shower_curtain
entries.description: The waterproof sheet hung around a [bathtub](#bathtub) or shower stall, frequently drawn half pulled [back](#back), or with a [silhouette](#silhouette) pressed against it from the other side.

entries.name: towel_on_one_shoulder
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) slung over a single shoulder and left [hanging](#hanging) loose. Typical after a [bath](#bath), a workout, or a stretch of manual labour.

entries.name: fabric
entries.description: Loose [cloth](#cloth) that has not been made up into anything yet: a bolt, a draped length, a scrap. Once the raw edges are hemmed or fringed it counts as a finished object instead.

entries.name: plaid_blanket
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) woven in a tartan check, thrown over a [bed](#bed), a [lap](#lap), or the ground. Often the [familiar](#familiar) red-and-black combination.

entries.name: towel_on_legs
entries.description: A seated character with a [towel](#towel) spread across the [thighs](#thighs) or [lap](#lap). Common right after a [bath](#bath) or while [drying](#drying) off in a [chair](#chair).

entries.name: plastic_wrap
entries.description: Clear stretchy film pulled over [food](#food), a dish, or a body. It clings and creases, [catching](#catching) highlights along every fold.

entries.name: towel_on_arm
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) [folded](#folded) and draped over the forearm, the way a [waiter](#waiter) or [bathhouse](#bathhouse) attendant carries one. Suggests a service role even without other uniform cues.

entries.name: striped_towel
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) woven with a striped pattern, whether draped over a shoulder, wrapped around the body or simply carried.

entries.name: doormat
