entries.description: A flat [mat](#mat) laid across a threshold for [wiping](#wiping) [shoes](#shoes). Drawn on porches and in entryways, occasionally with a spare [key](#key) hidden beneath it.

entries.name: print_towel
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) decorated with a printed motif rather than left [plain](#plain) or simply striped. Beach towels with characters, animals or [scenery](#scenery) are the usual case.

entries.name: tarpaulin
entries.description: A large sheet of waterproof material thrown over something to keep the weather off, usually blue or green with grommets along the hem. Covers crates, vehicles and [building](#building) sites, or gets rigged into a rough shelter.

entries.name: wash_cloth
entries.description: A small [square](#square) of absorbent towelling used to wash the face and body. Turns up in [bath](#bath) and shower scenes, sometimes [folded](#folded) on top of the head.

entries.name: wrapping
entries.description: Paper, [cloth](#cloth), or film [folded](#folded) around something to [cover](#cover) it, or the covering material on its own. Gift-giving scenes and packaged [food](#food) both bring it up.

entries.name: checkered_blanket
entries.description: A [blanket](#blanket) or throw woven in alternating squares, spread on a [bed](#bed), thrown over a sofa or laid out on the [grass](#grass). Picnics favour the red and white sort.

entries.name: placemat
entries.description: A small [mat](#mat) laid on a [table](#table) beneath a [plate](#plate), [catching](#catching) spills and [protecting](#protecting) the surface underneath. Distinct from a full [tablecloth](#tablecloth) covering the whole table.

entries.name: chain
entries.description: A run of metal loops linked end to end. It may hang loose, wrap around a limb or an object, serve as a [leash](#leash) or a restraint, or simply be worn as decoration.

entries.name: rope
entries.description: A length of twisted fibre cord, [coiled](#coiled), tied or in use. Serves for [climbing](#climbing), swings, [tying](#tying) things and [bondage](#bondage) alike; add [bound](#bound) or [shibari](#shibari) when it restrains someone.

entries.name: leash
entries.description: A cord or [chain](#chain) clipped to a [collar](#collar) so the wearer [can](#can) be led by the [neck](#neck). It turns up in [plain](#plain) [animal](#animal) [walking](#walking) as [well](#well) as pet-play and [bdsm](#bdsm) scenes; add [holding_leash](#holding_leash) or [leash_pull](#leash_pull) when somebody has hold of it.

entries.name: key
entries.description: A metal key for a [lock](#lock), held, hung on a cord or [lying](#lying) about in the scene. It applies only when an actual key is shown, never as a reference to anything that merely shares the word.

entries.name: string
entries.description: A thin cord of twisted fibres, shown as an object in its own right: [tying](#tying) a parcel, [dangling](#dangling) from a [kite](#kite), or strung between two points. For [thread](#thread) with romantic meaning use [string_of_fate](#string_of_fate).

entries.name: tape
entries.description: A long strip of adhesive or plastic material, such as [sticky](#sticky) tape or packing tape. An audio cassette is tagged separately.

entries.name: nail_(hardware)
entries.description: A metal spike meant for [driving](#driving) into wood or another material to hold it together. It also turns up in voodoo dolls and [torture](#torture) scenes. Not for [fingernails](#fingernails) or [toenails](#toenails).

entries.name: lock
entries.description: A [padlock](#padlock) or fitted lock [holding](#holding) a [door](#door), [chain](#chain), [box](#box) or chest shut, usually with a [keyhole](#keyhole) on show. It is frequently drawn together with a [key](#key) or a chain.

entries.name: red_rope
entries.description: Rope in red, whether tied, [coiled](#coiled), or draped. Shows up heavily in [shibari](#shibari) and other [bondage](#bondage) scenes, where red cord is traditional, but the [tag](#tag) is simply the object's colour.

entries.name: chain_leash
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) clipped to a [collar](#collar) and used to lead someone, held in another character's hand or trailing on the ground. It fits animals as readily as pet-play and [bondage](#bondage) scenes.

entries.name: gold_chain
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) of [gold](#gold), told from an ordinary one by its yellow shine. It may hang as [jewelry](#jewelry), dangle from clothing or lie loose in the scene.

entries.name: wire
entries.description: Bare metal or other non-electrical wire, including wire used as a [weapon](#weapon) or garrotte. An insulated cord [running](#running) to a [device](#device) is [cable](#cable) instead, and overhead lines are [power_lines](#power_lines); only wire with its metal exposed through a coating takes both tags at once.

entries.name: keyhole
entries.description: The slot in a [lock](#lock) where a [key](#key) goes in, on a [door](#door), a chest or a [padlock](#padlock). It also covers a composition framed as though seen through one.

entries.name: padlock
entries.description: A separate [lock](#lock) with a hinged shackle that hooks through a hasp, a [chain](#chain) or a [ring](#ring). Found on gates, chests, collars and love-lock railings.

entries.name: caution_tape
entries.description: Striped or printed barrier [tape](#tape), usually yellow with black lettering, strung between points to keep [people](#people) [back](#back). Police crime-scene tape counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: purple_rope
entries.description: A [rope](#rope) that is purple, whether shown as a prop, a binding, or a decorative cord such as a shrine's [shimenawa](#shimenawa). Combine with rope, and with the relevant restraint tags where it is used for [bondage](#bondage).

entries.name: broken_chain
entries.description: A [chain](#chain) with one or more links [torn](#torn) apart, often left [dangling](#dangling) from a wrist or ankle to show that somebody got loose. Add chain and [broken](#broken).

entries.name: reins
entries.description: The long straps [running](#running) from a horse's bit to the rider's hands, used to steer the [animal](#animal). Appears in [riding](#riding) and [carriage](#carriage) scenes, and sometimes fitted to a person in pony play.

entries.name: noose
entries.description: A [rope](#rope) tied into the [sliding](#sliding) loop used for hangings, present either as an object or as a looming [threat](#threat).

entries.name: pin
entries.description: A slender fastening pin with a small round head, used to hold [cloth](#cloth) together for [sewing](#sewing) or to tack [paper](#paper) to a board. Badges, brooches and lapel pins have tags of their own.

entries.name: thread
entries.description: A thin strand of fibre for [sewing](#sewing) or [embroidery](#embroidery), shown on a [spool](#spool), threaded through a [needle](#needle), or trailing loose. Commonly seen alongside sewing and needle.

entries.name: yarn
entries.description: Twisted fibre strands for [knitting](#knitting), shown loose or wound into a [ball](#ball), and a favourite plaything of cats. A rolled-up ball on its own is [yarn_ball](#yarn_ball).

entries.name: heart-shaped_lock
entries.description: A [padlock](#padlock) cut to a [heart](#heart) [outline](#outline), hung on a [collar](#collar), a [chain](#chain) or a [railing](#railing). It usually stands for a claim on somebody, or for keeping them safe.

entries.name: barbed_wire
entries.description: Steel [wire](#wire) with sharp points spaced along its strands, strung on a [fence](#fence), [coiled](#coiled) at a boundary, or wound around a character or object. It signals prisons, [war](#war) zones and no-go ground.

entries.name: yarn_ball
entries.description: Yarn rolled into a [ball](#ball) for storage, often being batted about by a [cat](#cat) or cat girl. Tag [yarn](#yarn) alongside it.

entries.name: net
entries.description: Cord or [thread](#thread) knotted into open [mesh](#mesh) with [no](#no) [handle](#handle), such as a [fishing](#fishing) or cargo net. A [catching](#catching) net on a [stick](#stick) is [hand_net](#hand_net) or [butterfly_net](#butterfly_net), and mesh worn as clothing is [fishnets](#fishnets).

entries.name: clothesline
entries.description: A cord or [rope](#rope) strung up [outdoors](#outdoors) with [washing](#washing) pegged along it to dry. Usually a backyard, [balcony](#balcony) or [rooftop](#rooftop) detail.

entries.name: clothes_pin
entries.description: A small sprung wooden or plastic peg that grips [laundry](#laundry) on a line, occasionally used to [pin](#pin) up hair instead. The two hinged jaws make it recognisable.

entries.name: duct_tape
entries.description: Wide cloth-backed silver [tape](#tape), seen as a roll, [holding](#holding) something [broken](#broken) together, or [stuck](#stuck) over a mouth or round a pair of wrists. Improvised repair and improvised restraint both belong here.

entries.name: hand_grip
entries.description: The [strap](#strap) and loop that dangles from a vehicle's [ceiling](#ceiling) for [standing](#standing) passengers to steady themselves by. One of these on [screen](#screen) places the scene inside a [train](#train) or [bus](#bus) almost by itself.

entries.name: white_rope
entries.description: Rope dyed or bleached white, whether [coiled](#coiled) underfoot, strung up as decoration, or knotted around a person or object. Shrine cords and [bondage](#bondage) lines in this colour both qualify; combine with [rope](#rope).

entries.name: paperclip
entries.description: A loop of bent [wire](#wire) that grips sheets of [paper](#paper) together. Drawn as a small [desk](#desk) detail, fastened to documents, or worn as an odd little accessory.

entries.name: rubber_band
entries.description: A small elastic loop used to hold things together, or stretched between fingers to be flicked. It also serves as an improvised hair tie.

entries.name: string_around_finger
entries.description: A length of [thread](#thread) tied round a finger so its owner will not forget something. A small visual joke about memory.

entries.name: spool
entries.description: A cylinder wound with [thread](#thread), [yarn](#yarn) or [wire](#wire) that pays the strand out as [sewing](#sewing) or craft work proceeds. Often drawn with a [needle](#needle) [stuck](#stuck) in it or a loose end trailing free.

entries.name: lasso
entries.description: A [rope](#rope) tied with a [running](#running) loop, thrown over a [target](#target) and pulled tight once it lands. Cowboys carry it [coiled](#coiled), and it serves for restraint in action scenes.

entries.name: string_pull
entries.description: A cord drawn taut by a hand, a [drawstring](#drawstring), a light-switch pull, a [ribbon](#ribbon) coming undone. The tension in the [string](#string) is what the picture shows.

entries.name: pull_cord
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) cord that operates something when tugged: the [switch](#switch) on a [ceiling](#ceiling) [lamp](#lamp), the [ring](#ring) on a [talking](#talking) doll's [back](#back), or the T-handled starter cord on a small [engine](#engine).

entries.name: rope_around_neck
entries.description: A [rope](#rope) looped and tied about a character's throat, whether as a lead, a restraint or a [noose](#noose). The rope sits around the [neck](#neck) itself rather than being worn as an ornament.

entries.name: cable_tie
entries.description: A ratcheted nylon [strap](#strap) that pulls tight and will not loosen again, sold for bundling wires. In pictures it mostly turns up binding wrists or thumbs.

entries.name: blue_rope
entries.description: Rope coloured blue, [coiled](#coiled), strung across a scene or wound around something. Nothing about its use follows from the colour, so mark what it is doing separately.

entries.name: pink_rope
entries.description: Rope coloured pink, [coiled](#coiled), knotted or strung across a scene. The decorative cord used for [tying](#tying) a person up falls here too.

entries.name: grappling_hook
entries.description: A [rope](#rope) ending in [claws](#claws) or a [hook](#hook), thrown so it catches on a [ledge](#ledge) and lets the user climb, [swing](#swing) or drag something in. Science fiction and [fantasy](#fantasy) versions are fired from a launcher.

entries.name: black_rope
entries.description: Rope in black, [coiled](#coiled), strung across a scene or wound around something. What it is being used for is left open by the colour alone.

entries.name: cargo_net
entries.description: A wide [net](#net) woven from [rope](#rope) in a coarse [grid](#grid), made for lashing down loads. More often climbed than loaded, on obstacle courses and playgrounds.

entries.name: carabiner
entries.description: A metal loop with a sprung or screw-locking [gate](#gate), letting [rope](#rope) and gear be clipped on and off in a moment. Climbing hardware first of all, but also hung from belts and bags.

entries.name: binder_clip
entries.description: A sprung metal clamp with two folding [wire](#wire) handles, [squeezing](#squeezing) a [stack](#stack) of [paper](#paper) together. Larger and stronger than a bent-wire [paperclip](#paperclip).

entries.name: broken_handcuffs
entries.description: Handcuffs [torn](#torn) apart, the bracelets still locked round the wrists with the [chain](#chain) snapped between them. It is shorthand for somebody [strong](#strong) enough to break free.

entries.name: ratline
entries.description: The short lengths of cord tied crosswise between a sailing ship's shrouds, forming a [rope](#rope) [ladder](#ladder) up to the masts. Drawn as a web of [rigging](#rigging) in tall-ship scenes.

entries.name: brown_rope
entries.description: Rope of a brown [shade](#shade), [coiled](#coiled), knotted or in use. This is the colour of hemp and other natural fibre cord.

entries.name: car_keys
entries.description: The keys to a [car](#car), generally on a [ring](#ring) with a fob or a remote. Held out, dangled from a finger or dropped into a [waiting](#waiting) palm.

entries.name: thumbtack
entries.description: A short [pin](#pin) with a wide flat head, pressed into a board or wall to hold up [paper](#paper), photos and [notes](#notes). Keep it for the flat-headed kind; a rounded or barrel-shaped grip belongs to [pushpin](#pushpin) instead.

entries.name: yellow_rope
entries.description: Rope coloured yellow, [coiled](#coiled), strung or in use.

entries.name: green_rope
entries.description: Rope coloured green, [coiled](#coiled), strung between points or in use. Only the cord's colour matters, not what it is doing.

entries.name: orange_rope
entries.description: Rope in orange, [coiled](#coiled), strung across a scene or in use binding something.

entries.name: grey_rope
entries.description: Rope of a grey colour, [coiled](#coiled), strung or tied. Only the cord's colour is at issue.

entries.name: umbrella
entries.description: A folding canopy on a [handle](#handle), carried against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun) and sometimes wielded as a [weapon](#weapon). A sun version is [parasol](#parasol); [shared_umbrella](#shared_umbrella) and [holding_umbrella](#holding_umbrella) describe how it is used.

entries.name: hand_fan
entries.description: A fan held in the hand and waved to push air at oneself in the heat, whether a folding one or a flat rigid [paddle](#paddle). Non-electric only; the battery-powered sort is [handheld_electric_fan](#handheld_electric_fan).

entries.name: cigarette
entries.description: A slim paper-wrapped [tobacco](#tobacco) cigarette, lit or unlit, in the mouth, between the fingers or [lying](#lying) in an [ashtray](#ashtray). Add [smoking](#smoking) where it is actually being smoked.

entries.name: spoon
entries.description: A piece of [cutlery](#cutlery) with a shallow [bowl](#bowl) at the end, used for [eating](#eating) [soup](#soup), [cereal](#cereal) or [dessert](#dessert), or for [stirring](#stirring) a [drink](#drink). Shown held, [resting](#resting) in a bowl, or set on a [table](#table).

entries.name: fork
entries.description: A pronged [eating](#eating) [utensil](#utensil), held in a hand or [lying](#lying) beside a [plate](#plate). Long [noodles](#noodles) such as [spaghetti](#spaghetti) and [ramen](#ramen) get twirled around it.

entries.name: folding_fan
entries.description: A collapsible handheld fan of [pleated](#pleated) [paper](#paper) or [cloth](#cloth) mounted on [ribs](#ribs), a [staple](#staple) of Japanese and Chinese [dress](#dress). Iron-ribbed versions double as weapons, and a shut one is [folded_fan](#folded_fan).

entries.name: oil-paper_umbrella
entries.description: The traditional East Asian [umbrella](#umbrella), built on many thin [ribs](#ribs) with a canopy of [oiled](#oiled) [paper](#paper) or [silk](#silk) and frequently red. It goes with [kimono](#kimono), [yukata](#yukata) and [geisha](#geisha) imagery.

entries.name: parasol
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) carried for [shade](#shade) from the [sun](#sun) rather than shelter from [rain](#rain), often lacy, frilled or made of [paper](#paper). The big fixed kind [standing](#standing) over a patio [table](#table) counts too.

entries.name: charm_(object)
entries.description: A small decorative trinket on a [keyring](#keyring) or short [chain](#chain), most often [hanging](#hanging) from a [phone](#phone) or a [school](#school) [bag](#bag). Acrylic or metal mascots are the usual form.

entries.name: smoking_pipe
entries.description: A [tobacco](#tobacco) pipe with a [bowl](#bowl) at one end of a stem, held or clenched in the [teeth](#teeth). Bubble pipes count; plumbing or a [lead_pipe](#lead_pipe) [weapon](#weapon) do not.

entries.name: beach_umbrella
entries.description: A big striped or brightly coloured [parasol](#parasol) on a long shaft driven into the [sand](#sand) for [shade](#shade). A fixture of [beach](#beach) scenes.

entries.name: sticker
entries.description: An adhesive-backed [paper](#paper) or plastic piece with a printed design, [stuck](#stuck) on a surface or held. One placed on a face is [sticker_on_face](#sticker_on_face).

entries.name: cane
entries.description: A [walking](#walking) [stick](#stick), straight or with a curved [handle](#handle), leaned on as a mobility aid or carried as a gentleman's accessory. Not the hooked Christmas sweet and not a magician's [staff](#staff).

entries.name: paper_fan
entries.description: A hand fan made of [paper](#paper), folding or flat on a [handle](#handle), but not the [harisen](#harisen) used for slapstick. Common with [yukata](#yukata) and [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival) scenes.

entries.name: closed_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol) [folded](#folded) shut, carried, leaned on or hooked over an arm. An open one is simply umbrella.

entries.name: folded_fan
entries.description: A folding fan in its shut state, held closed, tucked into a [sash](#sash) or tapped against a palm. An open one is simply [folding_fan](#folding_fan).

entries.name: glowstick
entries.description: A sealed plastic [tube](#tube) that lights by chemical reaction, often called a cyalume. Waved in bundles at concerts and [idol](#idol) shows, or carried as a light source in the [dark](#dark).

entries.name: kiseru
entries.description: A long, slender Japanese pipe with a tiny metal [bowl](#bowl) at the end, made for finely shredded [tobacco](#tobacco). It is a favourite prop for courtesans and gangsters in period settings.

entries.name: folded_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) shut and gathered around its shaft, carried, leaned on or stood in a stand. The [rain](#rain) has usually just stopped or has yet to begin.

entries.name: uchiwa
entries.description: A round or oval Japanese hand fan of [paper](#paper) or [silk](#silk) stretched over [bamboo](#bamboo) [ribs](#ribs), waved at [summer](#summer) festivals. A similar round Chinese fan is called [tuanshan](#tuanshan).

entries.name: cosmetics
entries.description: Makeup products and beauty [tools](#tools) as objects: [lipstick](#lipstick) tubes, compacts, palettes, brushes, nail polish, perfume, razors. The finished look worn on a face is [makeup](#makeup) instead.

entries.name: red_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) in red, held open against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun) or carried closed. A traditional Japanese oil-paper umbrella in red is often tagged [oil-paper_umbrella](#oil-paper_umbrella) as [well](#well).

entries.name: cigar
entries.description: A thick roll of cured [tobacco](#tobacco) [leaf](#leaf), larger than a [cigarette](#cigarette) and usually banded with a [paper](#paper) stamp, held, smoked or [resting](#resting) in an [ashtray](#ashtray). Often used to mark a boss, [gangster](#gangster) or officer.

entries.name: toothbrush
entries.description: A small bristled brush for [cleaning](#cleaning) [teeth](#teeth), held or in a [cup](#cup) at the [sink](#sink). Add [brushing_teeth](#brushing_teeth) when in use.

entries.name: purple_umbrella
entries.description: A purple [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol), held open or closed. Combine with umbrella.

entries.name: soap
entries.description: A bar or dispensed hygiene product used for [washing](#washing) and [bathing](#bathing). Lather worked up on the body is tagged separately as [soap_bubbles](#soap_bubbles).

entries.name: transparent_umbrella
entries.description: A clear plastic [umbrella](#umbrella) whose canopy [can](#can) be seen through, the cheap kind sold at Japanese convenience stores. The [ribs](#ribs) and rim may stay opaque; what matters is that most of the canopy itself is clear.

entries.name: comb
entries.description: A toothed grooming comb, either in use on the hair or worn in it as an ornament, including the lacquered and tortoiseshell kinds worn with [kanzashi](#kanzashi). Add [hair_ornament](#hair_ornament) when it is worn.

entries.name: lipstick_tube
entries.description: The small cylindrical case [holding](#holding) a [stick](#stick) of [lipstick](#lipstick), held in the hand or [lying](#lying) among other [cosmetics](#cosmetics). The colour on the [lips](#lips) themselves is lipstick.

entries.name: hair_brush
entries.description: A brush with bristles for smoothing and styling hair, or for grooming an animal's fur, held or [resting](#resting) on a dresser.

entries.name: magnifying_glass
entries.description: A convex lens set in a [ring](#ring) with a [handle](#handle), held up to enlarge small details or to gather [sunlight](#sunlight) into a [burning](#burning) point. The stock prop of detectives and close inspection.

entries.name: mimikaki
entries.description: A Japanese ear pick: a slim [stick](#stick) with a tiny scoop at the end, used to clean ears and often shown during lap-pillow ear-cleaning scenes.

entries.name: pacifier
entries.description: A rubber teat on a plastic [shield](#shield), sucked by a [baby](#baby) or by a character behaving like one. Appears with infants, in ageplay, and as a childish accessory.

entries.name: star_sticker
entries.description: A star-shaped [sticker](#sticker), [stuck](#stuck) on a face, an object or a page as a reward or decoration.

entries.name: lotion_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) or [pump](#pump) [container](#container) of [lotion](#lotion) or [sunscreen](#sunscreen), held in the hand or [standing](#standing) nearby. The [cream](#cream) once applied is lotion.

entries.name: white_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) with a white canopy, carried against [sun](#sun) or [rain](#rain). Tag umbrella alongside it; a decorative sun-shade may instead be a [parasol](#parasol).

entries.name: weighing_scale
entries.description: A [device](#device) for weighing, from a [bathroom](#bathroom) scale someone stands on to a [kitchen](#kitchen) or balance scale. The skin texture with the same name is the separate [scales](#scales) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: lighter
entries.description: A small handheld [device](#device) that makes a flame, chiefly for cigarettes. A metal flip-top one is also zippo_lighter, and a long-barrelled trigger type is wand_lighter.

entries.name: flashlight
entries.description: A handheld [battery](#battery) [lamp](#lamp), called a [torch](#torch) outside America. It turns up in [dark](#dark), spooky and exploring scenes.

entries.name: sunscreen
entries.description: A [lotion](#lotion), [cream](#cream) or oil applied to [guard](#guard) against [sunburn](#sunburn) or help along a [tan](#tan), commonly shown at the [beach](#beach). Implies lotion.

entries.name: crime_prevention_buzzer
entries.description: A small personal alarm that shrieks when its cord is pulled, clipped to a [school](#school) [bag](#bag) or a [belt](#belt). In art it is stereotypically carried by young girls, often on a [satchel](#satchel).

entries.name: rolling_suitcase
entries.description: A wheeled [suitcase](#suitcase) with a pull-out [handle](#handle), towed along in travel scenes.

entries.name: black_umbrella
entries.description: A black [umbrella](#umbrella), open overhead or furled and carried, held against [rain](#rain) or used as a gothic prop. A [parasol](#parasol) raised against the [sun](#sun) has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hourglass
entries.description: A timer of two [glass](#glass) bulbs joined at a narrow waist, with [sand](#sand) trickling from one into the other. For an hourglass-shaped body use [curvy](#curvy) instead.

entries.name: character_charm
entries.description: A small [hanging](#hanging) trinket made in a character's likeness, clipped to a [bag](#bag), [phone](#phone) or [keyring](#keyring). Merchandise like this decorates rucksacks and desks in everyday scenes.

entries.name: hair_dryer
entries.description: A handheld electric blow dryer for [drying](#drying) and styling hair, held or in use after a [bath](#bath).

entries.name: hand_mirror
entries.description: A small [mirror](#mirror) on a [handle](#handle), held up to check one's own face. A flip-open case [holding](#holding) both a mirror and face powder is a compact instead.

entries.name: wallet
entries.description: A small flat folding case for cash, cards and IDs, held, opened or [lying](#lying) about. Often appears in [shopping](#shopping) or empty-pockets jokes.

entries.name: blue_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) with a blue canopy, open against the [rain](#rain), carried shut or propped somewhere. Add [holding_umbrella](#holding_umbrella) when somebody has it in hand.

entries.name: perfume_bottle
entries.description: A small decorative [bottle](#bottle) or [vial](#vial) [holding](#holding) perfume, often with a spray bulb, shown [standing](#standing) on a vanity or in use.

entries.name: pink_umbrella
entries.description: A pink [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol), carried open overhead or [folded](#folded) shut. Add parasol when it is a sunshade rather than [rain](#rain) protection.

entries.name: cigarette_pack
entries.description: A [packet](#packet) of cigarettes, either the hard paperboard [box](#box) or the soft [paper](#paper) wrap, in a hand, a [pocket](#pocket) or [lying](#lying) on a [table](#table).

entries.name: soap_bottle
entries.description: A pump-top [bottle](#bottle) [holding](#holding) [liquid](#liquid) [soap](#soap), [shampoo](#shampoo), or [lotion](#lotion), typically set at the edge of a [bath](#bath) or [sink](#sink).

entries.name: leaf_umbrella
entries.description: A large [leaf](#leaf) held overhead as a makeshift [umbrella](#umbrella) against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun). The image comes out of folk tales and is often given to small characters and to animals.

entries.name: stopwatch
entries.description: A handheld timer for [measuring](#measuring) elapsed intervals. A [device](#device) that looks like a [pocket](#pocket) [watch](#watch) should be tagged as one unless its face is clearly marked in seconds.

entries.name: themed_object
entries.description: An everyday item styled to look like something else entirely, such as a leek-shaped [guitar](#guitar) or a dog-shaped purse. Tag both what it is and what it resembles.

entries.name: penlight_(glowstick)
entries.description: A battery-powered [concert](#concert) light with a long grip and a [glowing](#glowing) coloured tip, waved by fans at [idol](#idol) shows. Unlike a chemical [glowstick](#glowstick) it switches on and off and [can](#can) change colour.

entries.name: frilled_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol) whose canopy edge is gathered into ruffles. Usually a [lace](#lace) parasol carried to finish an elegant or gothic outfit.

entries.name: tuanshan
entries.description: A round Chinese hand fan of [silk](#silk) stretched over a rigid frame, often faintly see-through and held by a short [handle](#handle). Commonly paired with [hanfu](#hanfu) or a [china](#china) [dress](#dress), and sometimes raised to hide the mouth; unlike an [uchiwa](#uchiwa) it is perfectly circular and made of silk rather than [paper](#paper).

entries.name: makeup_brush
entries.description: A soft cosmetic brush for powder, [blush](#blush) or [eyeshadow](#eyeshadow), held up to a cheek or [lying](#lying) among bottles on a [dressing](#dressing) [table](#table). Belongs with getting-ready scenes rather than with worn [makeup](#makeup).

entries.name: ashtray
entries.description: A shallow dish [holding](#holding) [cigarette](#cigarette) ash and stubbed-out ends, usually on a [table](#table) or bar near whoever is [smoking](#smoking). Often drawn heaped to suggest a long [night](#night).

entries.name: compass
entries.description: A navigation [instrument](#instrument) whose [needle](#needle) swings to magnetic north, carried in the hand or set in a case. The circle-drawing tool is [compass_(instrument)](#compass_(instrument)) and the [figure](#figure) printed on a [map](#map) is [compass_rose](#compass_rose).

entries.name: shampoo_bottle
entries.description: The [pump](#pump) or squeeze [bottle](#bottle) [holding](#holding) [shampoo](#shampoo), [standing](#standing) on a [bath](#bath) [ledge](#ledge) or held in a [wet](#wet) hand. Often drawn beside matching conditioner and body wash.

entries.name: toothpick
entries.description: A slim pointed [stick](#stick), clamped between the [teeth](#teeth) after a [meal](#meal), spearing an appetiser or [standing](#standing) in a [cocktail](#cocktail).

entries.name: nail_polish_bottle
entries.description: The small [glass](#glass) [jar](#jar) that holds nail varnish, its brush usually built into the cap. It appears open on a [table](#table) or in hand during a manicure.

entries.name: yellow_umbrella
entries.description: A yellow [umbrella](#umbrella), open against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun) or carried furled. Nothing but the colour sets it apart.

entries.name: razor
entries.description: A bladed [shaving](#shaving) implement with a [handle](#handle), whether a folding straight razor or a modern safety razor. For the loose replaceable blade on its own, [razor_blade](#razor_blade) applies.

entries.name: toothpaste
entries.description: Paste squeezed from a [tube](#tube) onto a brush, or the tube itself [lying](#lying) by the [sink](#sink). Standard furniture of a [bathroom](#bathroom) scene.

entries.name: keyring
entries.description: A small [split](#split) metal loop [holding](#holding) several keys together, often with a charm or fob [dangling](#dangling) from it. It is shown gripped, clipped to a [bag](#bag) or spun round a finger.

entries.name: spork
entries.description: A single [utensil](#utensil) combining a shallow [spoon](#spoon) [bowl](#bowl) with short [fork](#fork) prongs at the tip, its name a blend of the two words. Common with fast [food](#food), [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) and packed lunches.

entries.name: animal_charm
entries.description: A small trinket [cast](#cast) as a [creature](#creature), [dangling](#dangling) from a [keyring](#keyring), a [phone](#phone) [strap](#strap) or a [bag](#bag) zip. Purely decorative, and far smaller than a plush [toy](#toy).

entries.name: planted_umbrella
entries.description: A closed [umbrella](#umbrella) jabbed tip-first into the ground so it stands on its own. Only a closed umbrella driven into a surface qualifies.

entries.name: kayari_buta
entries.description: A round ceramic [pig](#pig) with a [gaping](#gaping) mouth, made to hold a [burning](#burning) coil of insect-repelling [incense](#incense). A [thread](#thread) of [smoke](#smoke) rising from one is shorthand for high [summer](#summer).

entries.name: shampoo
entries.description: Hair-washing [liquid](#liquid) in use, worked into lather on the head, or the product itself [sitting](#sitting) in a [bath](#bath) scene. Usually appears alongside a shower, a tub, or a salon [basin](#basin).

entries.name: compact_(cosmetics)
entries.description: A small hinged case [holding](#holding) pressed face powder, a puff and a [mirror](#mirror) set into the [lid](#lid). A [plain](#plain) hand mirror is not one.

entries.name: green_umbrella
entries.description: A green [umbrella](#umbrella), open overhead against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun), or carried [folded](#folded). A green [parasol](#parasol) is close enough that the two are easily [confused](#confused).

entries.name: matches
entries.description: Short wooden sticks tipped with a compound that lights when scraped along a rough surface. Drawn [burning](#burning), being struck, or spilled loose across a surface.

entries.name: cotton_swab
entries.description: A short [stick](#stick) with cotton wound onto one or both ends, used for [cleaning](#cleaning) ears, applying [makeup](#makeup) or fine work. The Japanese ear pick with a scoop at one end is a [mimikaki](#mimikaki) instead.

entries.name: feather_fan
entries.description: A hand fan whose [leaf](#leaf) is made of [feathers](#feathers) rather than [paper](#paper) or [silk](#silk), often a wide [ostrich](#ostrich) [plume](#plume). It turns up in scholar, court and burlesque settings.

entries.name: marijuana
entries.description: The cannabis [plant](#plant) or the drug prepared from it: the jagged fingered [leaf](#leaf), a dried [bud](#bud), a rolled joint being smoked. Either the plant imagery or the finished [article](#article) counts.

entries.name: swimsuit_hanger
entries.description: A [clothes](#clothes) hanger shaped for swimwear: longer and more rectangular than an ordinary triangular hanger. The shape suits a one-piece and lets a single hanger carry both halves of a [bikini](#bikini).

entries.name: mosquito_coil
entries.description: A [spiral](#spiral) of insect-repelling [incense](#incense) that smoulders slowly through a [summer](#summer) [evening](#evening), often set in a pig-shaped ceramic holder. Stock [scenery](#scenery) beside a [wind](#wind) chime and a [paper](#paper) fan on the verandah.

entries.name: cigarette_butt
entries.description: The stubbed-out end of a smoked [cigarette](#cigarette), [crushed](#crushed) into an [ashtray](#ashtray) or dropped on the ground. Piled up, it says how long somebody has been [sitting](#sitting) there.

entries.name: stopwatch_around_neck
entries.description: A [stopwatch](#stopwatch) hung from a cord or [lanyard](#lanyard) so it rests on the chest. Standard kit for coaches and [gym](#gym) teachers.

entries.name: stirrups_(riding)
entries.description: Ring-shaped footrests [hanging](#hanging) on straps from both sides of a [saddle](#saddle), used to mount and to hold a seat while [riding](#riding). Hosiery with a loop under the foot is [stirrup_legwear](#stirrup_legwear), and the leg supports on an examination [table](#table) are a gynecology [chair](#chair).

entries.name: transparent_fan
entries.description: A folding or flat hand fan with a clear panel, keeping the face behind it visible even while held up. Often paired with a coy or bashful expression.

entries.name: hookah
entries.description: A [water](#water) pipe drawing [smoke](#smoke) through a [glass](#glass) base by way of one or more hoses. Middle Eastern settings and dreamy Wonderland scenes account for most of them.

entries.name: improvised_umbrella
entries.description: Something that is not an [umbrella](#umbrella) held overhead against the [rain](#rain): a [bag](#bag), a [jacket](#jacket), a [book](#book), a broad [leaf](#leaf). Shelter by substitution.

entries.name: hair_rollers
entries.description: Small tubes wound into the hair to set curls or pull them out, sometimes heated first. Usually drawn on somebody getting ready or [lounging](#lounging) at home.

entries.name: print_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) whose canopy carries an unusual pattern or picture. Flowers, animals and geometric repeats are common; a single flat colour does not qualify.

entries.name: razor_blade
entries.description: The thin rectangular steel blade meant for a safety [razor](#razor) or [box](#box) cutter, shown loose rather than fitted into a [handle](#handle). Its exposed edge makes it a recurring prop in tense or [self-harm](#self-harm) imagery.

entries.name: safety_razor
entries.description: A [shaving](#shaving) [razor](#razor) whose blade sits behind a [guard](#guard) so the edge cannot cut into skin. The exposed folding blade of a straight razor is a different tool.

entries.name: leaf_fan
entries.description: A fan improvised from one broad [leaf](#leaf), or woven from dried leaf [ribs](#ribs) into a [paddle](#paddle) shape, used to stir the air or fan a [fire](#fire). Tag it only when the leaf is actually being waved or held ready to be; feather fans that merely look leaf-shaped are [hauchiwa](#hauchiwa).

entries.name: handheld_electric_fan
entries.description: A small battery-driven fan held up to the face for relief in the heat, its blades [spinning](#spinning) behind a [guard](#guard). The folding [paper](#paper) sort is [hand_fan](#hand_fan).

entries.name: earplugs
entries.description: Small [foam](#foam) or silicone plugs pushed into the ear [canal](#canal) to shut out noise. Drawn for [sleeping](#sleeping), loud workshops and concerts.

entries.name: cigarette_holder
entries.description: A slender [tube](#tube) that a [cigarette](#cigarette) slots into for [smoking](#smoking), carried as an elegant affectation. Not to be mixed up with an [ashtray](#ashtray), which catches the ash instead.

entries.name: spoon_straw
entries.description: A [drinking](#drinking) straw whose end is cut away into a small scoop so it [can](#can) both suck up [liquid](#liquid) and dig out solids. Made for slush drinks and shaved [ice](#ice).

entries.name: orange_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) whose canopy is orange, held open against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun) or carried furled. Handle and [ribs](#ribs) may be any colour.

entries.name: nail_clippers
entries.description: The small hinged tool used to trim [fingernails](#fingernails) and [toenails](#toenails). It appears held mid-clip or [lying](#lying) out among other grooming things.

entries.name: polka_dot_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol) whose canopy carries a pattern of round [dots](#dots). Held open against [rain](#rain) or [sun](#sun).

entries.name: glue
entries.description: Adhesive in whatever form it comes: a [stick](#stick), a [bottle](#bottle) with a [sponge](#sponge) tip, a [tube](#tube) being squeezed. It turns up in craft, [classroom](#classroom) and repair scenes.

entries.name: tobacco
entries.description: Cured leaves of the tobacco [plant](#plant), loose or bundled, as the raw material behind pipes, cigars, snuff and [chewing](#chewing). The finished [cigarette](#cigarette) is a separate matter.

entries.name: shaving_cream
entries.description: White [foam](#foam) lathered onto skin ahead of a [razor](#razor), or the [can](#can) and brush used to work it up. Frequently smeared on a cheek purely for [comic](#comic) effect.

entries.name: grey_umbrella
entries.description: A grey [umbrella](#umbrella), open overhead or carried furled. The colour of the canopy is what is being recorded.

entries.name: spyglass
entries.description: A short collapsible [telescope](#telescope) held to one eye, standard kit for pirates, [ship](#ship) lookouts and explorers.

entries.name: electronic_cigarette
entries.description: A battery-powered [device](#device) drawn on in place of a [cigarette](#cigarette), usually with a [plume](#plume) of vapour. Covers slim pens and chunky [box](#box) models alike; anything [burning](#burning) real [tobacco](#tobacco) is a cigarette.

entries.name: women's_wallet
entries.description: A flat purse or clutch carried in the hand rather than on a shoulder [strap](#strap). It holds [money](#money) and cards while doubling as a small [handbag](#handbag).

entries.name: animal-themed_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) built to resemble a [creature](#creature), with ears on the canopy, a printed face across it or a paw at the end of the [handle](#handle). Rainy-day and childhood scenes use it most.

entries.name: broken_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) with bent [ribs](#ribs) or a [torn](#torn) canopy. Wind turning it inside out is the standard explanation.

entries.name: matchbox
entries.description: A small [cardboard](#cardboard) or wooden [box](#box) of [matches](#matches) with a striking strip down one side. Often shown beside a struck match or a small flame.

entries.name: hair_straightener
entries.description: A heated tool whose two flat plates clamp over a [lock](#lock) of hair to press the curl out of it. Appears in grooming scenes, usually near a [mirror](#mirror).

entries.name: joint_(drug)
entries.description: A cannabis [cigarette](#cigarette) rolled by hand, thinner and less even than a [factory](#factory) one and often twisted closed at the tip. It may be lit, being smoked, or halfway through being rolled.

entries.name: curling_iron
entries.description: A heated rod that hair is wound around to set it into curls. Shown mid-styling or left [lying](#lying) on a dresser.

entries.name: nail_polish_brush
entries.description: The slim applicator brush for nail varnish, normally fixed into the bottle's cap. It is generally drawn mid-stroke across a nail.

entries.name: multicolored_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) or [parasol](#parasol) whose canopy carries at least two colours. Alternating panels [running](#running) around the rim are the usual arrangement, though [rainbow](#rainbow) and blocked designs appear too.

entries.name: torn_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) with its canopy ripped, panels [flapping](#flapping) loose from the [ribs](#ribs). Often shown after a gust of [wind](#wind) has turned it inside out.

entries.name: brown_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) whose canopy is brown, held open overhead or carried furled. The [fabric](#fabric) decides the colour, not the [handle](#handle) or the [ribs](#ribs).

entries.name: bong
entries.description: A [water](#water) pipe for [smoking](#smoking), with a [tall](#tall) chamber, a side stem and a [bowl](#bowl). It works like a [hookah](#hookah) but is smaller and easier to carry.

entries.name: perfume_(cosmetics)
entries.description: Scented [liquid](#liquid) worn on the skin, usually drawn as a small [glass](#glass) [bottle](#bottle) with a stopper or an atomiser, sometimes [caught](#caught) mid-spray.

entries.name: half-split_chopsticks
entries.description: Disposable wooden [chopsticks](#chopsticks) still joined at one end, [waiting](#waiting) to be snapped apart. A [running](#running) [gag](#gag) has them tear crooked, leaving one [stick](#stick) far shorter than the other.

entries.name: two-tone_umbrella
entries.description: An [umbrella](#umbrella) whose canopy carries exactly two colours, often as alternating panels or a [border](#border). Parasols with the same [split](#split) count too.

entries.name: powder_puff
entries.description: A soft pad or [ball](#ball) for dabbing face powder on, usually with a [ribbon](#ribbon) loop on the [back](#back) to hold it by. Held near the cheek during a [makeup](#makeup) scene.

entries.name: rabbit_charm
entries.description: A small rabbit-shaped trinket hung from a [bag](#bag), [phone](#phone), or [keyring](#keyring). It may show the whole [animal](#animal) or just the ears and face.

entries.name: mascara_wand
entries.description: The slim [spiral](#spiral) brush screwed into the cap of a [mascara](#mascara) [tube](#tube), drawn black with product and raised toward the lashes. A dressing-table and getting-ready prop.

entries.name: broom
entries.description: A long [handle](#handle) with a head of stiff bristles, used for [sweeping](#sweeping) floors, or for [flying](#flying) in the hands of a [witch](#witch). Add sweeping or [holding_broom](#holding_broom) for what is being done with it, and [broom_riding](#broom_riding) when somebody is astride it.

entries.name: hose
entries.description: A long [flexible](#flexible) [tube](#tube) [carrying](#carrying) [water](#water), such as a [garden](#garden) hose or a [fire](#fire) hose. It has nothing to do with [pantyhose](#pantyhose).

entries.name: trash_can
entries.description: A bin for discarded waste, whether [indoors](#indoors) or on the [street](#street). Use it for the [container](#container) itself; loose litter scattered around it is [trash](#trash) instead.

entries.name: ladder
entries.description: A [climbing](#climbing) frame of rungs set between two rails, made of wood, metal or [rope](#rope), propped against something or fixed in place. Add a climbing [tag](#tag) when somebody is on it.

entries.name: mop
entries.description: A long-handled [floor](#floor) cleaner with a [sponge](#sponge) or fibre head, whether being pushed about, brandished like a [weapon](#weapon) or left [standing](#standing) in its [bucket](#bucket). Cleaning duty and [school](#school) corridor scenes are full of them.

entries.name: trash_bag
entries.description: A plastic [sack](#sack) for household refuse, tied off at the top or piled at a curb. A common prop in [street](#street) scenes, alleyways and cleanup or garbage-day gags.

entries.name: duster
entries.description: A small handheld [cleaning](#cleaning) tool with a feathered or [fluffy](#fluffy) head for [sweeping](#sweeping) [dust](#dust) off surfaces, and a maid's standard prop. The long [cowboy](#cowboy) [coat](#coat) of the same name has its own name.

entries.name: bamboo_broom
entries.description: A [broom](#broom) with a [bamboo](#bamboo) shaft and a bundle of twigs or bristles at its end, the [sweeping](#sweeping) tool of shrines, temples and gardens. A [miko](#miko) or a [witch](#witch) is often the one [holding](#holding) it.

entries.name: sponge
entries.description: A soft, porous pad used for [washing](#washing) [dishes](#dishes), surfaces or a person's own body, common in [bathing](#bathing) and [cleaning](#cleaning) scenes.

entries.name: spray_can
entries.description: A pressurised [can](#can) that releases its contents as a fine mist through a nozzle, covering spray [paint](#paint), deodorant and similar products. Frequently shown in [graffiti](#graffiti) scenes.

entries.name: vacuum_cleaner
entries.description: The household appliance that draws up [dust](#dust) and [dirt](#dirt) by suction, whether upright, [canister](#canister) or handheld, usually shown in [cleaning](#cleaning) scenes.

entries.name: trash
entries.description: Discarded odds and ends small enough to fit in a bin: wrappers, crumpled [paper](#paper), empty cans and [food](#food) scraps. For bulkier discarded items and scrap heaps, [junk](#junk) fits better.

entries.name: cleaning_rag
entries.description: A scrap of [cloth](#cloth) kept for [wiping](#wiping) down floors, tables or windows. Different from [rags](#rags) meaning tattered clothing, and from a [towel](#towel) meant for [drying](#drying) a person.

entries.name: spray_bottle
entries.description: A [bottle](#bottle) fitted with a trigger [pump](#pump) that puts its contents out as a fine mist. Used for [cleaning](#cleaning) products, [watering](#watering) plants and occasionally disciplining a misbehaving [pet](#pet).

entries.name: mousetrap
entries.description: The sprung bar trap mounted on a small wooden base to catch mice and other rodents, often baited with a wedge of [cheese](#cheese). Usually there as a [gag](#gag) rather than as [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: spray_paint
entries.description: An aerosol [can](#can) that lays down [paint](#paint) through a nozzle when pressed. Appears in [graffiti](#graffiti) scenes, model-building and vandalism gags.

entries.name: board_eraser
entries.description: The felt block used to wipe [chalk](#chalk) off a blackboard or [marker](#marker) off a [whiteboard](#whiteboard). School comedy throws it as a [missile](#missile), and a dusty one leaves a white [cloud](#cloud) on whoever it lands on.

entries.name: fire_extinguisher
entries.description: A pressurised cylinder with a [hose](#hose) and squeeze [handle](#handle), discharged to [smother](#smother) flames. Usually red, and often mounted on a wall in a corridor or [kitchen](#kitchen).

entries.name: feather_duster
entries.description: A [cleaning](#cleaning) tool with a [plume](#plume) of [feathers](#feathers) on a [handle](#handle), for flicking [dust](#dust) off shelves and ornaments. A stock prop in [maid](#maid) pictures.

entries.name: robotic_vacuum_cleaner
entries.description: A low, disc-shaped [cleaning](#cleaning) [robot](#robot) that wanders the [floor](#floor) on its own. Often drawn as a source of comedy with a [cat](#cat) or a small character [riding](#riding) on top.

entries.name: recycle_bin
entries.description: A [container](#container) for sorted waste headed for recycling, usually marked with the chasing-arrows symbol and [color-coded](#color-coded) by material. Also covers the same-named desktop icon when it appears on a drawn [computer](#computer) [screen](#screen).

entries.name: cleaning_brush
entries.description: A stiff-bristled scrubbing brush for floors, [tiles](#tiles), [dishes](#dishes) or a [bathtub](#bathtub). Usually held mid-scrub or set down beside a [bucket](#bucket).

entries.name: stepladder
entries.description: A short folding [ladder](#ladder) that stands on its own in an A-shape, used to reach shelves and high corners. It needs [no](#no) wall behind it, unlike a [leaning](#leaning) ladder.

entries.name: bar_soap
entries.description: A solid block of [soap](#soap) with worn rounded edges, [sitting](#sitting) in a dish or held in a [wet](#wet) hand. It belongs to [bath](#bath), shower and [washing](#washing) scenes.

entries.name: junk
entries.description: Broken [machinery](#machinery), [bald](#bald) tyres and smashed furniture heaped in the scene, rubbish too big for a bin. Smaller litter belongs to [trash](#trash).

entries.name: dustpan
entries.description: A flat scoop held against the [floor](#floor) while a [broom](#broom) sweeps [dirt](#dirt) into it. Nearly always drawn together with that broom.

entries.name: laundry_pole
entries.description: A long straight [pole](#pole) hung with [washing](#washing) to dry, the Japanese answer to a [clothesline](#clothesline). It is usually set across a [balcony](#balcony) with hangers strung along it.

entries.name: hose_nozzle
entries.description: The fitting on the end of a [hose](#hose) that [shapes](#shapes) and aims the [water](#water). Most are moulded as a pistol grip with a trigger under the finger.

entries.name: dumpster
entries.description: A big metal rubbish [container](#container) [standing](#standing) in an [alley](#alley) or behind a [building](#building). Scenery for grubby [urban](#urban) corners, and something to [duck](#duck) behind.

entries.name: plunger
entries.description: A rubber [cup](#cup) on a wooden [handle](#handle), used for clearing a blocked drain or [toilet](#toilet). It frequently turns up as an improvised [weapon](#weapon) or a joke [helmet](#helmet).

entries.name: flyswatter
entries.description: A flat perforated [paddle](#paddle) on a thin springy [handle](#handle), swung to kill insects. Comedy scenes press it into service as an improvised [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: bug_spray
entries.description: An aerosol [can](#can) of insecticide meant to kill or drive off insects. Normally shown gripped and aimed, often at something that does not deserve it.

entries.name: clothes_iron
entries.description: The heated handheld appliance pressed over [fabric](#fabric) to smooth out creases, often steaming as it goes. Usually shown on an ironing board in a housework scene.

entries.name: detergent
entries.description: Cleaning [liquid](#liquid) or powder in a [bottle](#bottle), spray or [carton](#carton), usually beside a [cloth](#cloth), a [sink](#sink) or a [laundry](#laundry) [basket](#basket). Belongs to chores and housework scenes.

entries.name: swim_ring
entries.description: A ring-shaped flotation aid, either a [colorful](#colorful) inflatable inner [tube](#tube) meant for play or a red-and-white [foam](#foam) [lifebuoy](#lifebuoy) meant for [rescue](#rescue).

entries.name: innertube
entries.description: A ring-shaped float worn round the waist to keep a swimmer up, named after the [tube](#tube) inside an [old](#old) [car](#car) tyre. Art often draws it [transparent](#transparent) or in bright colours; a [lifebuoy](#lifebuoy) looks similar but is [rescue](#rescue) gear.

entries.name: pom_pom_(cheerleading)
entries.description: The big [fluffy](#fluffy) balls of [streamers](#streamers) cheerleaders shake, usually one in each hand. The small decorative pom pom on a [hat](#hat) or shoe is [pom_pom_(clothes)](#pom_pom_(clothes)).

entries.name: baseball_bat
entries.description: A smooth club of wood or metal swung at a pitched [ball](#ball), carried by a player or taken up as a makeshift [weapon](#weapon) by a [delinquent](#delinquent). Horror scenes sometimes wrap it in barbed [wire](#wire) or drive nails through it.

entries.name: fishing_rod
entries.description: A rod with a reel and line for [catching](#catching) [fish](#fish), present as an object whether or not anyone is using it.

entries.name: skates
entries.description: Boots with wheels or blades fixed to the [soles](#soles), covering roller skates, inline skates and [ice](#ice) skates. Tag [ice_skates](#ice_skates) or [roller_skates](#roller_skates) for the specific kind.

entries.name: lifebuoy
entries.description: A rigid ring-shaped float in a high-visibility colour, thrown to somebody in the [water](#water) and often trailing a line. Unlike an inflatable [innertube](#innertube) it is made of solid buoyant material.

entries.name: basketball_(object)
entries.description: The orange pebbled [ball](#ball) used in [basketball](#basketball), held, bounced or [lying](#lying) on the ground. Use basketball for the game itself.

entries.name: boxing_gloves
entries.description: Thickly padded mitts laced or strapped at the wrist and worn for [boxing](#boxing), most often red, blue or black. Add [gloves](#gloves), and boxing when a bout is actually under way.

entries.name: soccer_ball
entries.description: The [ball](#ball) used in association football, classically [patterned](#patterned) in black-and-white pentagons and hexagons.

entries.name: paddle
entries.description: A broad flat blade on a [handle](#handle), whether for [table](#table) [tennis](#tennis) or for [spanking](#spanking). The [oar](#oar) used to row a [boat](#boat) is tagged separately.

entries.name: volleyball_(object)
entries.description: The [ball](#ball) used for [volleyball](#volleyball), present in the picture whether in play or just held. The sport as an activity is volleyball.

entries.name: surfboard
entries.description: A long narrow board for [riding](#riding) [waves](#waves), shown carried under an arm, [planted](#planted) in the [sand](#sand) or in use on the [water](#water).

entries.name: pool_ladder
entries.description: The metal [ladder](#ladder) on the side of a [swimming](#swimming) [pool](#pool), or the step recesses cut into its wall, used to climb in and out. Characters often lean on or sit by it.

entries.name: racket
entries.description: A strung bat with a rounded frame, used for [tennis](#tennis), [badminton](#badminton), or [squash](#squash). Combine with the sport being played, or with [holding_racket](#holding_racket).

entries.name: baseball_mitt
entries.description: The thick padded [leather](#leather) glove used to catch a [baseball](#baseball), worn on one hand or carried. Add baseball when a game is actually being played.

entries.name: tennis_racket
entries.description: A strung [racket](#racket) used to strike a [tennis](#tennis) [ball](#ball), whether mid-swing or simply carried.

entries.name: skateboard
entries.description: A short board on four small wheels, ridden [standing](#standing) and pushed along with one foot. Seen carried, ridden or parked beside a character.

entries.name: hagoita
entries.description: An ornately painted wooden [paddle](#paddle) used to play [hanetsuki](#hanetsuki) at New Year, often more decorative than functional.

entries.name: dumbbell
entries.description: A short bar weighted at both ends for strength [training](#training), lifted singly or one in each hand. Add [exercising](#exercising) when somebody is actually [working](#working) with it.

entries.name: snorkel
entries.description: A [diving](#diving) [mask](#mask) or [goggles](#goggles) paired with a [breathing](#breathing) [tube](#tube), letting a swimmer [watch](#watch) [underwater](#underwater) while [floating](#floating) face-down at the surface. Worn at the [beach](#beach), in a [pool](#pool), or anywhere shallow-water snorkeling is shown.

entries.name: inline_skates
entries.description: Roller [skates](#skates) with the wheels set in a single line, closer in feel to [ice](#ice) skates than to a four-wheeled pair. They also go by the name rollerblades.

entries.name: tennis_ball
entries.description: The fuzzy yellow-green [ball](#ball) used in [tennis](#tennis), whether [lying](#lying) around, being served, or held in a hand.

entries.name: ice_skates
entries.description: Boots with a narrow steel blade fixed underneath for gliding over [ice](#ice), worn for [figure](#figure) [skating](#skating) or hockey. Pair them with [ice_skating](#ice_skating) when they are actually being used.

entries.name: vaulting_horse
entries.description: The stacked, [numbered](#numbered) wooden [gym](#gym) [box](#box) [familiar](#familiar) from Japanese schools, used for vaulting during PE class. Its presence usually signals a gym or its storeroom as the setting, unlike the padded, height-adjustable bar typical of Western vaulting horses.

entries.name: hoop
entries.description: A large [ring](#ring) formed from a single band joined at the ends: a [gymnastics](#gymnastics) hoop, a [circus](#circus) ring or a plastic play hoop. Small rings such as [hoop_earrings](#hoop_earrings) are not covered.

entries.name: single_knee_pad
entries.description: A protective knee pad strapped over one knee only, the other leg left unprotected. Seen on sports and [mechanic](#mechanic) outfits; [tag](#tag) alongside [knee_pads](#knee_pads).

entries.name: exercise_ball
entries.description: A large inflatable [ball](#ball), knee to waist high, used for balance and [core](#core) work. Characters sit, bounce or stretch on it. Also called a [gym](#gym), [yoga](#yoga) or balance ball.

entries.name: golf_club
entries.description: A long shaft with a weighted head, swung to strike a [golf](#golf) [ball](#ball). Shown in hand, mid-swing, shouldered or [standing](#standing) in a [bag](#bag).

entries.name: fishing_line
entries.description: The thin line [running](#running) from a rod out to the [water](#water) or a [hook](#hook), drawn in as its own detail. It normally appears with [fishing_rod](#fishing_rod) and [fishing](#fishing).

entries.name: weights
entries.description: Dumbbells, barbells and loading plates used for lifting. They show up in [gym](#gym) scenes, [training](#training) montages and as visual shorthand for strength.

entries.name: volleyball_net
entries.description: The [net](#net) strung across a court or [beach](#beach) that divides the two sides in [volleyball](#volleyball). Usually accompanies volleyball or beach scenes.

entries.name: telstar
entries.description: The black-and-white panelled football with its thirty-two [stitched](#stitched) patches, designed for a famous 1970s World Cup. It has become the default drawn shorthand for a [soccer](#soccer) [ball](#ball) in general.

entries.name: baseball_(object)
entries.description: The hard white [ball](#ball) used in [baseball](#baseball), wrapped in [leather](#leather) and closed with a curving double seam of red [stitching](#stitching). It sits comfortably in one hand.

entries.name: jump_rope
entries.description: A [rope](#rope) passed under the [feet](#feet) and jumped over, spun either by the jumper or by two others [holding](#holding) the ends. Children's games and [training](#training) both use it.

entries.name: oar
entries.description: A shaft ending in a flat blade, used to row or [paddle](#paddle) a [boat](#boat) along. It covers both oars pivoted against a hull and loose paddles held in both hands.

entries.name: lane_line
entries.description: The [floating](#floating) [rope](#rope) of coloured discs strung across a [swimming](#swimming) [pool](#pool) to divide it into lanes. Its presence marks the [water](#water) as a [competition](#competition) or [training](#training) pool.

entries.name: kickboard
entries.description: A [foam](#foam) float held out at arm's length so the upper body stays up while the [legs](#legs) practise [kicking](#kicking). A fixture of [swimming](#swimming) lessons.

entries.name: race_bib
entries.description: The [numbered](#numbered) [marker](#marker) worn on the front of a competitor at a sporting event, letting spectators tell runners apart. It comes either as a full [bib](#bib) strapped over the shoulders and waist or as a sheet [stuck](#stuck) onto the [shirt](#shirt).

entries.name: blue_innertube
entries.description: A blue inflatable [ring](#ring) for [floating](#floating), worn around the waist or carried along. Pools and beaches are where it turns up.

entries.name: cue_stick
entries.description: The long tapered [stick](#stick) used to strike the cue [ball](#ball) at [pool](#pool) and [billiards](#billiards). Held ready for a shot, leaned on, or simply carried about as a prop.

entries.name: barbell
entries.description: A long straight bar loaded with plates at each end and lifted with both hands during [weight](#weight) [training](#training). Longer and heavier than a [dumbbell](#dumbbell), and usually shown with a rack or [bench](#bench).

entries.name: table_tennis_paddle
entries.description: The short-handled bat used in [table](#table) [tennis](#tennis), its round blade faced in rubber, typically red on one side and black on the other.

entries.name: billiard_ball
entries.description: The small hard balls used on a [pool](#pool) [table](#table), [numbered](#numbered) and either solid or striped, alongside the [plain](#plain) white cue [ball](#ball). How many there are and which colours they take depends on the cue game being played.

entries.name: basketball_hoop
entries.description: The metal [ring](#ring) with a [hanging](#hanging) [net](#net) that the [ball](#ball) must drop through, bolted to a backboard on a [pole](#pole) or wall. Street versions are often bent out of true or missing the net.

entries.name: snowboard
entries.description: A single broad board with bindings for both [feet](#feet), ridden down snowy slopes. The equipment itself; [riding](#riding) one is [snowboarding](#snowboarding).

entries.name: metal_baseball_bat
entries.description: A hollow aluminum bat of the kind used in [school](#school) [baseball](#baseball), carried as sports gear as often as it is swung as an improvised [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: target
entries.description: A marked surface meant to be aimed at, from concentric [archery](#archery) rings to a [paper](#paper) [silhouette](#silhouette) on a shooting range. Shown [standing](#standing) downrange, held up, or already [punched](#punched) full of holes and arrows.

entries.name: fishing_hook
entries.description: The small barbed metal [hook](#hook) at the end of a line. It may be shown baited, in mid-cast, or snagged in something it should not be.

entries.name: pink_innertube
entries.description: An inflatable pink swim [ring](#ring), worn around the waist, floated on or carried under an arm. Beach and [pool](#pool) scenes are its home.

entries.name: yoga_mat
entries.description: The thin rubber [mat](#mat) unrolled for [floor](#floor) exercise, shown in use or [standing](#standing) rolled up in a [corner](#corner). Its long [rectangle](#rectangle) marks out the [working](#working) [space](#space).

entries.name: starting_block
entries.description: The braced footrest a sprinter pushes off from, or the raised [platform](#platform) a swimmer dives from at the [poolside](#poolside). It marks the very start of a race.

entries.name: relay_baton
entries.description: The short hollow rod handed from runner to runner in a relay race, usually brightly coloured. It appears mid-exchange or gripped in a sprinter's fist.

entries.name: parachute
entries.description: The canopy and [harness](#harness) that slow a fall, either open overhead with the lines [fanning](#fanning) down or still packed on the [back](#back). Tag the packed rig only where it clearly reads as a parachute and not as a rucksack.

entries.name: ribbon_baton
entries.description: A short [stick](#stick) with a long streaming [ribbon](#ribbon) fixed to one end, swung to draw arcs in the air. It is the [signature](#signature) apparatus of rhythmic [gymnastics](#gymnastics).

entries.name: hane_(hanetsuki)
entries.description: The feathered [shuttlecock](#shuttlecock) used in the New Year game of [hanetsuki](#hanetsuki): a hard [dark](#dark) [seed](#seed) with bright plumes [stuck](#stuck) into it. It almost always appears alongside the flat wooden [hagoita](#hagoita) [paddle](#paddle).

entries.name: mma_gloves
entries.description: Padded [gloves](#gloves) that stop short of the fingers so the wearer [can](#can) still grip and grapple. Standard kit in [cage](#cage) [fighting](#fighting) and other combat sports that allow clinching.

entries.name: punching_bag
entries.description: The [heavy](#heavy) [hanging](#hanging) cylinder struck over and over in [boxing](#boxing) [training](#training). The Japanese term for it borrows the English word [sandbag](#sandbag), a false friend for the earth-filled kind of sandbag.

entries.name: horizontal_bar
entries.description: A single bar fixed between supports, used for [pulling](#pulling) up on or for [swinging](#swinging). It covers both the [playground](#playground) chin-up frame and the cabled high bar of competitive [gymnastics](#gymnastics).

entries.name: gymnastics_ribbon
entries.description: The long [satin](#satin) streamer on a short [stick](#stick) swung by rhythmic gymnasts, drawn trailing in spirals and loops. Use it for the apparatus, not for ribbons worn in the hair or on [clothes](#clothes).

entries.name: dart
entries.description: A short finned [missile](#missile) thrown at a [target](#target) by hand, pinched between the fingers or already sunk into a board. Turns up around a [dartboard](#dartboard) in [bars](#bars) and games rooms.

entries.name: scuba_gear
entries.description: The full [diving](#diving) outfit: air cylinder and regulator, [mask](#mask), [weight](#weight) [belt](#belt), and [fins](#fins), usually worn over a [wetsuit](#wetsuit).

entries.name: table_tennis_ball
entries.description: The light, hollow celluloid [ball](#ball) used in [table](#table) [tennis](#tennis), usually white or orange. Also turns up in [drinking](#drinking) games and [juggling](#juggling) gags.

entries.name: scuba
entries.description: Self-contained [underwater](#underwater) [breathing](#breathing) gear, cylinder, regulator and mouthpiece, carried so a diver [can](#can) stay down without a line to the surface.

entries.name: badminton_racket
entries.description: A light racquet with a small oval head on a long slim shaft, strung to strike a [shuttlecock](#shuttlecock). It is noticeably thinner and [lighter](#lighter) than a [tennis](#tennis) [racket](#racket).

entries.name: inflatable_armbands
entries.description: Air-filled rings worn on the upper arms to keep a swimmer up, known as floaties or [water](#water) [wings](#wings). They are children's gear and work on the same [idea](#idea) as a swim [ring](#ring).

entries.name: tennis_net
entries.description: The long [net](#net) strung across the middle of a [tennis](#tennis) court, its white band [running](#running) along the top edge. Play consists of [hitting](#hitting) the [ball](#ball) [back](#back) and forth over it.

entries.name: bowling_ball
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) polished [ball](#ball) drilled with three close-set finger holes, rolled down a lane at pins. Its [weight](#weight) is why it is gripped by thumb, middle and [ring](#ring) finger rather than held in the palm.

entries.name: skis
entries.description: The long narrow planks [bound](#bound) to ski [boots](#boots) for gliding over [snow](#snow). Tagged for the equipment itself, whether worn, carried or propped up in the snow.

entries.name: doughnut_innertube
entries.description: A swim [ring](#ring) moulded and coloured to look like a frosted [doughnut](#doughnut). Worn round the waist at a [pool](#pool) or [beach](#beach), or simply [floating](#floating) nearby.

entries.name: fishing_net
entries.description: Netting used to take [fish](#fish), from a small hand scoop up to the great [mesh](#mesh) towed behind a [boat](#boat). Despite the name it has nothing to do with fishnet legwear.

entries.name: white_innertube
entries.description: A white inflatable [ring](#ring) used as a [pool](#pool) or [beach](#beach) float, worn around the waist or floated on. Bright colors are the norm for these, so a [plain](#plain) white one stands out.

entries.name: scuba_tank
entries.description: The pressurised air cylinder strapped to a diver's [back](#back), with a [valve](#valve) and regulator at the [neck](#neck) and hoses [running](#running) forward.

entries.name: print_innertube
entries.description: A swim [ring](#ring) decorated with a printed design, often an [animal](#animal) face, [fruit](#fruit) or character. Worn round the waist or floated on at the [pool](#pool).

entries.name: treadmill
entries.description: An exercise [machine](#machine) with a moving [belt](#belt) for [running](#running) or [walking](#walking) in place. Usually shown in a [gym](#gym) or home workout scene with someone [jogging](#jogging) on it.

entries.name: spiked_bat
entries.description: A [baseball](#baseball) bat with nails or [spikes](#spikes) driven through the striking end, an improvised [weapon](#weapon) favored by delinquents and [wasteland](#wasteland) survivors alike. Not to be [confused](#confused) with a [kanabou](#kanabou), a [studded](#studded) Japanese club.

entries.name: barre
entries.description: The horizontal [handrail](#handrail) fixed along a dance [studio](#studio) wall or [standing](#standing) free on a frame. Dancers hold it for balance while warming up and drilling [ballet](#ballet) positions.

entries.name: twirl_baton
entries.description: A slim metal rod capped with rubber ends, spun and tossed in baton-twirling routines. Carried by majorettes and cheer performers.

entries.name: exercise_machine
entries.description: Gym apparatus built on a frame with moving parts: a [treadmill](#treadmill), [rowing](#rowing) [machine](#machine), [weight](#weight) [stack](#stack) or leg press. The machine itself, whether in use or [standing](#standing) idle.

entries.name: dartboard
entries.description: The round scoring [target](#target) darts are thrown at, cut into wedges with a [numbered](#numbered) [ring](#ring) around the rim. Hangs on the wall of a bar, club or games room.

entries.name: american_football_(object)
entries.description: The pointed brown oval [ball](#ball) of gridiron football, laced along one side and banded in white near each end. A rugby ball is blunter, usually unlaced and comes in many colours.

entries.name: scoreboard
entries.description: The big [display](#display) at a sports ground that shows the [running](#running) score to the whole [crowd](#crowd), often with the period and time remaining beside it.

entries.name: mouth_guard
entries.description: A shaped piece of plastic or rubber worn over the [teeth](#teeth) to protect them during a contact sport such as [boxing](#boxing) or hockey. Usually shown gripped between the teeth or held in the hand rather than worn constantly.

entries.name: shuttlecock
entries.description: The cone of [feathers](#feathers) or plastic set into a rounded [cork](#cork) base that [badminton](#badminton) is played with. Also called a birdie, and usually shown mid-flight or held ready to serve.

entries.name: juggling_club
entries.description: A weighted baton with a narrow grip and a [fat](#fat) end, thrown and spun by jugglers and rhythmic gymnasts. Most look like a slim [bowling](#bowling) [pin](#pin).

entries.name: diving_regulator
entries.description: The mouthpiece and [valve](#valve) that drop [tank](#tank) pressure to something breathable [underwater](#underwater). Held between the [teeth](#teeth) or left [dangling](#dangling) on its [hose](#hose).

entries.name: transparent_innertube
entries.description: An inflatable [ring](#ring) for [floating](#floating) in [water](#water), moulded from clear plastic so the body inside or behind it stays visible. Common at pools and beaches as a see-through variant of the usual coloured [tube](#tube).

entries.name: chest_protector
entries.description: Bulky padded gear shielding chest and [belly](#belly), strapped on by [baseball](#baseball) catchers and umpires or by [ice](#ice) hockey goalkeepers. Smaller plates covering only the upper chest are a chest [guard](#guard).

entries.name: hoverboard
entries.description: A flat board that levitates and carries a rider [standing](#standing) on it, straight out of [science](#science) fiction. Not to be [confused](#confused) with the wheeled self-balancing scooters sold under the same name.

entries.name: innertube_with_ears
entries.description: A swim [ring](#ring) moulded with [animal](#animal) ears on its rim, so the float reads as a creature's head. Poolside and [beach](#beach) pictures are where it shows up.

entries.name: ski_pole
entries.description: A lightweight shaft with a grip, [strap](#strap) and [basket](#basket) near the tip, [planted](#planted) by a skier for balance and push-off. Normally carried as a pair.

entries.name: golf_ball
entries.description: The small hard [ball](#ball) dimpled all over that [golf](#golf) is played with. It may sit on a tee, lie in the [grass](#grass) or be held between the fingers, with [no](#no) player needed.

entries.name: snorkel_in_mouth
entries.description: The mouthpiece of a [snorkel](#snorkel) gripped between the [teeth](#teeth) with the [tube](#tube) [running](#running) up past the face, showing the gear actually in use rather than pushed up onto the [forehead](#forehead).

entries.name: fishing_lure
entries.description: An artificial [bait](#bait) shaped like a small [fish](#fish) or insect, hung with hooks and often brightly painted, tied to a line to draw a catch in.

entries.name: catcher's_mask
entries.description: The barred face [guard](#guard) a [baseball](#baseball) catcher wears behind the [plate](#plate), a metal [cage](#cage) held in a padded frame. Older ones [strap](#strap) over a backwards cap while newer designs wrap the whole [skull](#skull).

entries.name: hurdle
entries.description: The low barrier a runner leaps on a track. Shown [standing](#standing) in a line down the lane or being cleared [mid-stride](#mid-stride).

entries.name: bowling_pin
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) white club-shaped [pin](#pin) that a [bowling](#bowling) [ball](#ball) knocks over, marked with a red band around the narrow [neck](#neck). Ten of them stand in a [triangle](#triangle) at the end of a lane, though single pins turn up as props too.

entries.name: race_flag
entries.description: The black-and-white checkered [flag](#flag) waved at the finish of a motor race, and by extension the other signal flags used around a circuit. Standard visual shorthand for auto [racing](#racing) in a picture.

entries.name: ski_gear
entries.description: The full outfit and kit for [skiing](#skiing): insulated [suit](#suit), [gloves](#gloves), [goggles](#goggles), [boots](#boots) and poles. Used when the whole set is present rather than one piece of it.

entries.name: goal
entries.description: The frame a [ball](#ball) must be driven into or over to score, built as netted posts, a crossbar or an upright [fork](#fork) depending on the sport. The [structure](#structure) is what is tagged, not the act of scoring.

entries.name: lacrosse_stick
entries.description: A long shaft ending in a shallow netted head, used to catch, carry and throw a [ball](#ball). The strung [pocket](#pocket) at the top is what identifies it.

entries.name: orange_innertube
entries.description: An inflatable orange [ring](#ring) of the kind taken to a [pool](#pool) or the sea, worn round the waist or floated on.

entries.name: purple_innertube
entries.description: A purple inflatable [ring](#ring) for [floating](#floating) in [water](#water), worn around the waist or bobbing nearby. A [poolside](#poolside) and [beach](#beach) fixture.

entries.name: rugby_ball
entries.description: The oval [ball](#ball) used in rugby, rounder at the ends than an American football and usually brightly coloured over a white base. It carries [no](#no) lacing along the seam.

entries.name: finish_line
entries.description: The marked end of a race course: a painted stripe, a stretched [tape](#tape) or a [banner](#banner) overhead. Runners or vehicles [breaking](#breaking) through it are the usual scene.

entries.name: baseball_base
entries.description: One of the flat plates marking the corners of a [baseball](#baseball) diamond. First, second and third are white rubber squares, while home [plate](#plate) is a five-sided slab; a runner has to touch each in turn.

entries.name: black_innertube
entries.description: An inflatable [ring](#ring) float in black, worn round the waist in the [water](#water) or carried down to the [beach](#beach). A colour variant of the ordinary swim ring.

entries.name: brown_innertube
entries.description: A brown inflatable [ring](#ring) float, held, worn round the waist or [drifting](#drifting) on [water](#water). Colour variant of the usual [pool](#pool) [tube](#tube).

entries.name: cross
entries.description: Two perpendicular [bars](#bars) meeting at a right angle, in any of the many variants: the long-armed Latin form, the even-armed Greek plus, the diagonal saltire, the flared iron cross. Covers the shape whether it is a solid object or a printed [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: ofuda
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [talisman](#talisman) from a Shinto [shrine](#shrine), a narrow strip brushed with characters and carried for the protection of the shrine's god. Shrine maidens and exorcists also fling them like weapons.

entries.name: wand
