entries.description: A short handheld [stick](#stick), under about two [feet](#feet), used to [cast](#cast) or channel [magic](#magic), typical of fairies and magical girls. A longer [two-handed](#two-handed) rod is [staff](#staff); an orchestra's baton is [conductor_baton](#conductor_baton).

entries.name: gohei
entries.description: A wooden Shinto [wand](#wand) hung with zigzag [paper](#paper) [streamers](#streamers), waved to purify a place or bless somebody. Shrine maidens carry it; older forms use a single rectangular strip instead of the zigzag.

entries.name: shimenawa
entries.description: A thick [rope](#rope) of braided [rice](#rice) straw, hung with [shide](#shide), that marks sacred ground in Shinto practice or is worn draped like a [sash](#sash). Implies rope.

entries.name: orb
entries.description: A sphere held, [floating](#floating) or mounted, whether ornamental, a vessel for something or the shape [magic](#magic) takes. Roughly the size of a [crystal](#crystal) [ball](#ball); anything small enough for several to sit in one palm is a marble.

entries.name: shide
entries.description: Zigzag-folded [paper](#paper) [streamers](#streamers) used in Shinto rites, hung from a [shimenawa](#shimenawa) [rope](#rope) or a [gohei](#gohei) [wand](#wand). Tagged on its own only when shown alone or as part of a [shrine](#shrine).

entries.name: white_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) drawn in white rather than the usual [gold](#gold), [floating](#floating) above an angelic character's head.

entries.name: latin_cross
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) whose lower arm runs longer than the other three, the usual Christian form. It appears as a [standing](#standing) symbol, a [pendant](#pendant) or a decorative motif.

entries.name: talisman
entries.description: A charm, [pendant](#pendant) or inscribed [paper](#paper) strip used to seal, ward off or [attack](#attack) supernatural forces.

entries.name: ofuda_on_clothes
entries.description: Paper talismans are [stuck](#stuck) to or hang from a character's garments, whether as decoration or as a seal.

entries.name: tarot
entries.description: A [card](#card) from a 78-card deck used for fortune telling, or a whole picture drawn to look like one. Add the specific arcana [tag](#tag), such as the naming of an individual card, when it is identifiable.

entries.name: prayer_beads
entries.description: A [string](#string) of [beads](#beads) used to count prayers or chants, whether a Catholic [rosary](#rosary), a Buddhist juzu, an Islamic misbaha or a Hindu mala. Worn on the wrist, around the [neck](#neck) or held in the hands.

entries.name: scepter
entries.description: An [ornate](#ornate) ceremonial rod of precious metal and gems held by royalty as a symbol of authority. Not a [staff](#staff), which is a [fighting](#fighting) or spell-casting implement.

entries.name: inverted_cross
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) [standing](#standing) on its head, also called St Peter's cross. It began as a Christian [sign](#sign) of humility but today reads mostly as satanic or anti-Christian decoration on [clothes](#clothes), jewellery and backdrops.

entries.name: ritual_baton
entries.description: A long flat baton, often [bamboo](#bamboo), held by [shinto](#shinto) priests, court nobles and hina dolls. Originally a Chinese [writing](#writing) tablet; the rod_of_remorse is a related variant with its own associations.

entries.name: potion
entries.description: A [flask](#flask), [vial](#vial) or [bottle](#bottle) [holding](#holding) a brightly coloured [liquid](#liquid), the [healing](#healing) or mana [drink](#drink) of [fantasy](#fantasy) games or an [aphrodisiac](#aphrodisiac). Often corked and [glowing](#glowing).

entries.name: dowsing_rod
entries.description: A forked or L-bent rod held out to divine [water](#water), minerals or [buried](#buried) things, sometimes swapped for a [crystal](#crystal) on a [string](#string). Reads as folk [magic](#magic) rather than as a [working](#working) [instrument](#instrument).

entries.name: ankh
entries.description: The Egyptian looped [cross](#cross) [standing](#standing) for life, appearing as a carried object, a [pendant](#pendant) or a painted symbol. Deities are often shown gripping one by the loop, sometimes a pair crossed over the chest.

entries.name: pendulum
entries.description: A [weight](#weight) hung from a pivot so that it swings freely, whether inside a [clock](#clock), [dangling](#dangling) from a dowser's hand or held up by a hypnotist. Hypnosis scenes are its most common home.

entries.name: kouhaku_nawa
entries.description: A sacred straw [rope](#rope) twisted from red and white strands, hung as a Shinto [marker](#marker) or worn as part of an outfit. It counts as a [shimenawa](#shimenawa).

entries.name: pentacle
entries.description: A magical [amulet](#amulet) or [talisman](#talisman) bearing a star [figure](#figure), hung as a [pendant](#pendant) or held up to [cast](#cast) a [spell](#spell). Despite the name it may carry a [hexagram](#hexagram); the bare five-pointed figure drawn as a shape is [pentagram](#pentagram).

entries.name: ema
entries.description: Small wooden plaques hung up at a Shinto [shrine](#shrine) with a wish or prayer written on them. The face usually carries a picture of a [horse](#horse) or another [animal](#animal). Seen in shrine visits and New Year scenes.

entries.name: oonusa
entries.description: A Shinto purification [wand](#wand) hung with many white [paper](#paper) [streamers](#streamers) on a wooden shaft or a sakaki [branch](#branch), swept over a person or an offering to draw impurity away. It is the heavily dressed relative of the [plain](#plain) [gohei](#gohei); a six- or eight-sided shaft makes it a [haraegushi](#haraegushi).

entries.name: hauchiwa
entries.description: A fan of [feathers](#feathers) carried by [tengu](#tengu), credited in folklore with raising great winds and, in some tales, with [stretching](#stretching) a [nose](#nose). Its [silhouette](#silhouette) may suggest a maple [leaf](#leaf), but a fan actually made of leaves is [leaf_fan](#leaf_fan) instead.

entries.name: animal_skull
entries.description: The [skull](#skull) of a beast rather than a person, worn on the head, carried, or [lying](#lying) in the scene. Antlers mark a [deer](#deer) skull and curling [horns](#horns) a ram's, so name the [animal](#animal) when the shape gives it away.

entries.name: hamaya
entries.description: A ceremonial Shinto arrow with a blunt tip, sold at shrines around New Year to ward off evil and bad luck. Often has talismans tied to its shaft.

entries.name: ofuda_on_head
entries.description: A [paper](#paper) [talisman](#talisman) is pasted across the [forehead](#forehead), the standard look of a [hopping](#hopping) [jiangshi](#jiangshi). Costumes and jokes built on that look count as [well](#well).

entries.name: grimoire
entries.description: A [book](#book) of [magic](#magic) or [alchemy](#alchemy), typically [old](#old), [heavy](#heavy) and ornately [bound](#bound), held or [floating](#floating) beside a spellcaster.

entries.name: spell_card
entries.description: A physical [card](#card) charged with [magic](#magic) and used to [cast](#cast) a [spell](#spell), best known from Touhou but not limited to it. Tag it only when the card object itself appears; a spell's effect in action is tagged spell instead.

entries.name: teruterubouzu
entries.description: A small ghost-shaped [doll](#doll) of white [cloth](#cloth) or [paper](#paper), hung by a [string](#string) at a [window](#window) as a Japanese charm for good weather. Hung upside down, it asks for [rain](#rain) instead.

entries.name: crystal_ball
entries.description: A clear [glass](#glass) or [crystal](#crystal) sphere gazed into by fortune tellers and magicians. Not to be mixed up with a [snow](#snow) [globe](#globe).

entries.name: portal_(object)
entries.description: A magical or technological gateway linking two distant places, usually drawn as a [glowing](#glowing) [ring](#ring), rift or [doorway](#doorway) in the air. Characters may be [stepping](#stepping) through or emerging from it.

entries.name: omikuji
entries.description: Paper fortune slips drawn at a [shrine](#shrine) or [temple](#temple), graded from great blessing down to great curse. Often shown being read at New Year, or knotted onto a [branch](#branch) or a [wire](#wire) after a bad one.

entries.name: kaname-ishi
entries.description: A sacred stone said to [pin](#pin) down the earth and hold quakes still, its name usually rendered as keystone. It is drawn as a [boulder](#boulder), sometimes [floating](#floating) and ringed with sacred straw [rope](#rope).

entries.name: hishaku
entries.description: A long-handled wooden dipper for [pouring](#pouring) [water](#water), used to rinse the hands at a [shrine](#shrine) [basin](#basin), to serve in [tea](#tea) ceremony, or to [wet](#wet) a [path](#path) in [summer](#summer). Kitchen ladles have a [tag](#tag) of their own.

entries.name: rosary
entries.description: A Catholic prayer strand of five decades of [beads](#beads) punctuated by larger ones, with a [cross](#cross) or crucifix [hanging](#hanging) at the end. Beads without a cross are prayer beads, and a cross without beads is a cross [necklace](#necklace).

entries.name: star_wand
entries.description: A [wand](#wand) or [staff](#staff) with a star fixed to the end. The standard implement of magical girls and fairy-tale witches.

entries.name: miracle_mallet
entries.description: A small wooden [mallet](#mallet) out of Japanese folk tales, said to grant a wish for whoever swings it. Often drawn with [treasure](#treasure) or sparkles [spilling](#spilling) into the air around it.

entries.name: incense_burner
entries.description: The vessel that holds [burning](#burning) [incense](#incense), from a small lidded [censer](#censer) to a great bronze [urn](#urn) outside a [temple](#temple). Thin [smoke](#smoke) usually rises from its openings.

entries.name: tarot_card
entries.description: A physical [card](#card) from a [tarot](#tarot) deck, held in the hand, dealt out or spread across a [table](#table). Use it when the card is an object inside the scene; a whole picture composed like one is [tarot_(medium)](#tarot_(medium)) instead.

entries.name: shakujou
entries.description: A Buddhist pilgrim's [staff](#staff) topped by a metal finial hung with loose rings that jangle when it strikes the ground. Carried by monks and monk-styled characters in [ritual](#ritual) scenes.

entries.name: poison
entries.description: A harmful substance in the picture, shown as a [vial](#vial) of lurid [liquid](#liquid), a tainted [meal](#meal), or a sickly [cloud](#cloud) [clinging](#clinging) to somebody. Also covers a character visibly suffering its effects.

entries.name: incense
entries.description: Fragrant material in sticks, coils, cones or powder that gives off scented [smoke](#smoke) as it burns. Use it for the substance itself; the [drifting](#drifting) smoke has a [tag](#tag) of its own.

entries.name: heart_wand
entries.description: A [wand](#wand) or [staff](#staff) topped with a [heart](#heart), standard magical-girl equipment. The heart is often jewelled or lit from within.

entries.name: omamori
entries.description: The Japanese luck charm sold at shrines and temples, a small brocade [pouch](#pouch) pulled shut with a cord and [holding](#holding) a blessing for study, love or a safe journey.

entries.name: grief_seed
entries.description: A small [dark](#dark) metal [spinning](#spinning) top left behind when a [witch](#witch) is defeated in the world of Puella Magi Madoka Magica. A magical girl uses one to cleanse the [darkness](#darkness) her Soul Gem has built up, though wearing out the same [seed](#seed) risks reviving the witch it came from.

entries.name: animal_skeleton
entries.description: The bones of a beast or other non-human [creature](#creature), mounted whole, bleached in a [desert](#desert) or set out as a [fossil](#fossil). Human remains are tagged elsewhere.

entries.name: ritual
entries.description: A ceremony carried out to a prescribed pattern, religious or occult: offerings, chanting, circles drawn on the ground, robed participants. The formality of the scene is what marks it out from an ordinary gathering.

entries.name: bible_(object)
entries.description: A copy of the Christian scriptures, usually drawn as a thick [dark](#dark) [book](#book) with a [cross](#cross) on the [cover](#cover). Carried by clergy, nuns and exorcists, or [lying](#lying) open on a [lectern](#lectern).

entries.name: crosier
entries.description: The [ornate](#ornate) ceremonial [staff](#staff) of a high-ranking Christian [cleric](#cleric), ending in a shepherd's [hook](#hook), a T-bar, or a [cross](#cross) set inside a [ring](#ring). Fantasy priests and priestesses carry stylised versions of it. A [plain](#plain) mage staff and the ringed Buddhist [shakujou](#shakujou) take their own tags.

entries.name: straw_doll
entries.description: A crude human [figure](#figure) [bound](#bound) from bundles of straw, the Japanese counterpart of a voodoo [doll](#doll). It is used in the Ushi [no](#no) Koku Mairi curse, nailed to a sacred [tree](#tree) in the small hours by someone in white with candles on a trivet.

entries.name: shrine_bell
entries.description: The round hollow [bell](#bell) hung at the front of a Shinto [shrine](#shrine), rung by [pulling](#pulling) a [rope](#rope) to announce a visitor to the enshrined deity. Also worn in [miniature](#miniature) as a charm or hair ornament.

entries.name: censer
entries.description: A metal vessel for [burning](#burning) [incense](#incense), usually pierced or lidded so a [thread](#thread) of [smoke](#smoke) escapes. Reach for it when the burner is [ornate](#ornate) or clearly on show, rather than the [plain](#plain) dish or [bowl](#bowl) a [stick](#stick) of incense normally sits in.

entries.name: celtic_cross
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) with a [ring](#ring) encircling the point where the arms meet, a form that grew up in early [medieval](#medieval) Ireland and Britain. It appears as a [grave](#grave) [marker](#marker), a [pendant](#pendant) and a heraldic [device](#device).

entries.name: voodoo_doll
entries.description: A small effigy [stuck](#stuck) with pins so that harm supposedly reaches the person it stands for. Straw figures used in Japanese [cursing](#cursing) rituals are filed here too.

entries.name: globus_cruciger
entries.description: An [orb](#orb) topped with a [cross](#cross), carried as a token of divine authority over the world. Appears in coronation regalia, [church](#church) imagery and [fantasy](#fantasy) [crown](#crown) jewels.

entries.name: philosopher's_stone
entries.description: The alchemists' legendary red stone said to turn base metal into [gold](#gold) and to grant unending life. Drawn as a [glowing](#glowing) [gem](#gem), a [crystal](#crystal) or a sealed [vial](#vial) in [alchemy](#alchemy) and [fantasy](#fantasy) scenes.

entries.name: sotoba
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), narrow wooden [plank](#plank) inscribed with sutras and [planted](#planted) at a Japanese [grave](#grave). Several usually stand together behind a [tombstone](#tombstone), making them a reliable [marker](#marker) of a [graveyard](#graveyard).

entries.name: dream_catcher
entries.description: A [willow](#willow) [hoop](#hoop) strung with a loose web and hung about with [feathers](#feathers) and [beads](#beads), an object of Ojibwe craft. Usually shown [swinging](#swinging) by a [window](#window) or above a [bed](#bed).

entries.name: sefirot
entries.description: The Kabbalistic Tree of Life [diagram](#diagram), ten spheres joined by connecting paths. Familiar to anime audiences from occult and mecha-mystic imagery; not the character whose name it resembles.

entries.name: altar
entries.description: A raised [table](#table) or stone [platform](#platform) used for offerings and rites, found in churches, shrines, temples and [ritual](#ritual) chambers. It anchors ceremonial and sacrificial scenes.

entries.name: sigil
entries.description: An occult glyph drawn as a condensed [emblem](#emblem) of a [spell](#spell), name or entity. Appears etched on the ground, [floating](#floating) in the air or burned onto skin, and is usually simpler than a full [magic_circle](#magic_circle).

entries.name: winged_wand
entries.description: A [wand](#wand) or [staff](#staff) topped with one or more [wings](#wings), often framing a [heart](#heart) or star shape. It is standard equipment for magical girls.

entries.name: the_lovers_(tarot)
entries.description: The sixth trump: a pair, classically [nude](#nude), [standing](#standing) side by side beneath a winged [figure](#figure) or deity. Drawn as the [card](#card) or restaged with two characters posed in its arrangement.

entries.name: clothes-dissolving_potion
entries.description: A magical brew that eats away garments while leaving the wearer untouched, used as a setup for stripping somebody. Usually shown being thrown, spilled or [drunk](#drunk).

entries.name: the_fool_(tarot)
entries.description: The unnumbered trump of the tarot's major arcana, a wanderer in [rags](#rags) or jester's motley [stepping](#stepping) toward a [cliff](#cliff) edge, bundle over the shoulder and often a [dog](#dog) at the heels. Decks mark it with a zero or an infinity [sign](#sign).

entries.name: shouryouuma
entries.description: Small [animal](#animal) figures made from a [cucumber](#cucumber) or an [eggplant](#eggplant) fitted with matchstick [legs](#legs), set out for the Obon festival's return of the dead. The cucumber makes a swift [horse](#horse) to bring spirits home, the eggplant an unhurried ox to carry them [back](#back).

entries.name: purple_liquid
entries.description: Purple fluid in a [container](#container), being poured, or spilled: a [drink](#drink), a [potion](#potion), or a chemical. Its unnatural colour is usually the whole point of drawing it.

entries.name: zener_card
entries.description: A [card](#card) printed with one of five [plain](#plain) symbols, a [circle](#circle), [cross](#cross), wavy lines, [square](#square) or star, used in tests for extrasensory perception. Typically shown held face-out toward a subject or spread across a [table](#table).

entries.name: vajra_(object)
entries.description: A short double-headed [ritual](#ritual) sceptre with prongs at each end, originally the thunderbolt [weapon](#weapon) of a Hindu [storm](#storm) god and later adopted as a Buddhist implement. It stands for both the hardness of diamond and the force of [lightning](#lightning), and comes in one-, three- and five-pronged forms.

entries.name: haraegushi
entries.description: A wooden Shinto [wand](#wand) hung with [folded](#folded) white [paper](#paper) [streamers](#streamers), waved over [people](#people) and places during purification rites. This particular form has its [shide](#shide) fixed to a six- or eight-sided [staff](#staff), making it a close relative of the larger [oonusa](#oonusa).

entries.name: the_magician_(tarot)
entries.description: The first trump: a [figure](#figure) with one hand raised skyward and the other [pointing](#pointing) at the ground, a [table](#table) before him bearing a [wand](#wand), a [cup](#cup), a blade and a [coin](#coin). Once a [stage](#stage) conjurer in gaming decks, he became a true sorcerer in decks built for divination.

entries.name: the_star_(tarot)
entries.description: The seventeenth trump: a woman [kneeling](#kneeling) by [water](#water) and [pouring](#pouring) from two vessels, one large star and seven smaller ones [burning](#burning) above her. Drawn as the [card](#card) or restaged with a character in her place.

entries.name: large_cross
entries.description: An outsized [cross](#cross), carried on the [back](#back), [planted](#planted) in the ground or looming in the background. Religious, gothic and exorcist characters use it as a prop.

entries.name: the_empress_(tarot)
entries.description: The third trump: a crowned woman on a [throne](#throne) set among grain or greenery, sceptre in hand and, in many decks, visibly [pregnant](#pregnant). Shown as the [card](#card) or restaged with a character [standing](#standing) in for it.

entries.name: the_moon_(tarot)
entries.description: The eighteenth trump: a full [moon](#moon) over a [night](#night) [landscape](#landscape), with a [dog](#dog) and a [wolf](#wolf) baying up at it and a [crayfish](#crayfish) [crawling](#crawling) from a [pool](#pool). Drawn as the [card](#card) or restaged with characters.

entries.name: bird_skull
entries.description: The bare [skull](#skull) of a [bird](#bird), its long [beak](#beak) making it unmistakable. Used as decoration, a [mask](#mask) or an occult prop, with the beak shape varying by species.

entries.name: the_high_priestess_(tarot)
entries.description: The second trump, seated between two lettered pillars with a [book](#book) or [scroll](#scroll) in her [lap](#lap) and a [crescent](#crescent) [moon](#moon) at her [feet](#feet). Older gaming decks show her as a female pope, while occult decks [pile](#pile) esoteric ornament onto her.

entries.name: the_sun_(tarot)
entries.description: The nineteenth trump: a large [sun](#sun), usually given a human face, [shining](#shining) over sunflowers, with a naked [child](#child) often present beneath it. Drawn as the [card](#card) or restaged with characters.

entries.name: justice_(tarot)
entries.description: The major arcana [card](#card) showing a seated [figure](#figure) with a [sword](#sword) raised in one hand and a balance held in the other, sometimes crowned. It is [numbered](#numbered) eighth or eleventh depending on the deck.

entries.name: the_hanged_man_(tarot)
entries.description: The twelfth trump: a [figure](#figure) suspended head down by one ankle, the free leg crossed behind to form the shape of a four. The face stays calm despite the position.

entries.name: love_potion
entries.description: A brewed draught that makes whoever drinks it fall in love. It is almost always coloured red or pink and often bottled in a heart-shaped [vial](#vial).

entries.name: wheel_of_fortune_(tarot)
entries.description: The tenth trump of the tarot's major arcana, a great spoked [wheel](#wheel) [standing](#standing) for luck and turning fate. Figures are often shown [riding](#riding) its rim or scrambling up the side.

entries.name: death_(tarot)
entries.description: The thirteenth [card](#card) of the Major Arcana, drawn as a skeletal [figure](#figure) with a [scythe](#scythe) or as a rider beneath a black [banner](#banner). Appears when a picture stages a [reading](#reading) or dresses a character as the card.

entries.name: the_hermit_(tarot)
entries.description: The ninth trump: a cloaked, hooded [old](#old) man alone with a lit [lantern](#lantern) raised in one hand and a [staff](#staff) in the other. Drawn as the [card](#card) or restaged with a character posed as it.

entries.name: the_emperor_(tarot)
entries.description: The fourth trump of the tarot's major arcana: a crowned [ruler](#ruler) seated on a [throne](#throne) carved with rams' heads, often [holding](#holding) a sceptre or an [orb](#orb). Drawn as the [card](#card) itself or restaged with a character posed in that role.

entries.name: skull
entries.description: The bare [bone](#bone) of a head, human or [animal](#animal), appearing as a prop, decoration or grim [scenery](#scenery). As a printed or worn motif use [skull_print](#skull_print), [skull_mask](#skull_mask) or [skull_ornament](#skull_ornament).

entries.name: shell
entries.description: The hard calcareous casing that protects a mollusc, [turtle](#turtle) or similar [creature](#creature), whether still on the [animal](#animal) or [lying](#lying) empty. A [beach](#beach) find is usually [seashell](#seashell), a turtle's specifically is [turtle_shell](#turtle_shell), an egg's is [eggshell](#eggshell), and spent [ammunition](#ammunition) is [shell_casing](#shell_casing).

entries.name: bone
entries.description: Bones as an object in the picture: a dog's chew, a heap in a [graveyard](#graveyard), one swung as a club or worn as ornament. A [skull](#skull) alone is skull, and bone-shaped hair clips are [bone_hair_ornament](#bone_hair_ornament).

entries.name: seashell
entries.description: The empty [shell](#shell) of a sea mollusc such as a [scallop](#scallop), [conch](#conch), [clam](#clam), or cowrie, [lying](#lying) on the [beach](#beach) or used as decoration.

entries.name: funerary_casket
entries.description: A [coffin](#coffin) [holding](#holding) a body, [standing](#standing) open at a wake, closed for burial or being carried by pallbearers. Belongs to [funeral](#funeral) scenes and to [vampire](#vampire) and horror settings alike.

entries.name: cartoon_bone
entries.description: The stylised [bone](#bone) icon, a shaft with two rounded knobs at either end, the shape a [dog](#dog) is always drawn [chewing](#chewing). Used as a prop, an [emblem](#emblem) or a [comic](#comic) symbol rather than as real [anatomy](#anatomy).

entries.name: fish_skeleton
entries.description: A [fish](#fish) stripped down to [spine](#spine), [ribs](#ribs), head and [tail](#tail) with the bones still [hanging](#hanging) together. The [standing](#standing) joke leftover of a finished [meal](#meal).

entries.name: pelt
entries.description: The hide of a dead [animal](#animal), fur still attached or stripped away, shown as a [rug](#rug), a [trophy](#trophy), a draped wrap or a hunter's haul. A fur garment that is plainly clothing takes [fur_coat](#fur_coat) or similar.

entries.name: fish_bone
entries.description: The fine needle-like bones taken out of a [fish](#fish) before or while [eating](#eating) it. Bones still joined into the whole frame of the [animal](#animal) make a [fish_skeleton](#fish_skeleton).

entries.name: floating_skull
entries.description: A [skull](#skull) [hanging](#hanging) in the air with nothing [holding](#holding) it up, generally there to set an ominous or occult mood. It may be a [spirit](#spirit), a summoned thing, or simply decoration.

entries.name: conch
entries.description: The [spiral](#spiral) [shell](#shell) of a large sea [snail](#snail). Held to the ear it is said to carry the [sound](#sound) of the sea, and in pictures it doubles as a horn or an ornament.

entries.name: clam_shell
entries.description: The paired hinged [shell](#shell) of a [clam](#clam) without the [animal](#animal), shut, [gaping](#gaping) or used as a dish. Common as [beach](#beach) [scenery](#scenery) and as the [container](#container) a pearl sits in.

entries.name: fossil
entries.description: The remains or imprint of a prehistoric [creature](#creature) preserved in stone, from a [coiled](#coiled) ammonite to a mounted [skeleton](#skeleton). Museums and dig sites are the usual settings.

entries.name: framed_insect
entries.description: A dead [bug](#bug) [pinned](#pinned) and mounted behind [glass](#glass) in a [display](#display) frame, most often a [beetle](#beetle), [moth](#moth) or [butterfly](#butterfly). It hangs on a wall or stands on a [shelf](#shelf) as an ornament rather than being a living [animal](#animal).

entries.name: pile_of_skulls
entries.description: Bare skulls heaped across the ground, often beneath a [throne](#throne) or strewn over a [battlefield](#battlefield). Set [dressing](#dressing) that suggests slaughter or long-past [death](#death).

entries.name: snail_shell
entries.description: The [coiled](#coiled) [spiral](#spiral) [shell](#shell) of a [snail](#snail), whether occupied by the [animal](#animal), worn by a [monster](#monster) girl or [lying](#lying) empty as a found object.

entries.name: sarcophagus
entries.description: A [coffin](#coffin) cut from stone, often with the likeness of the occupant carved or painted on the [lid](#lid). Turns up in tombs and [ruins](#ruins), sometimes [standing](#standing) open or pushed aside.

entries.name: taxidermy
entries.description: A preserved [animal](#animal) body mounted to look alive, whether a [trophy](#trophy) head on a wall or a full [figure](#figure) on a stand, [glass](#glass) eyes [standing](#standing) in for real ones. Used to furnish [hunting](#hunting) lodges, studies and unsettling rooms.

entries.name: syringe
entries.description: A plunger-and-tube injector, usually fitted with a hypodermic [needle](#needle), used to give injections or draw fluid samples. Sewing needles and needle-shaped weapons use a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: test_tube
entries.description: A slim [glass](#glass) [tube](#tube) with a rounded bottom and an open top, used in laboratories and often held in a rack or in a scientist's hand.

entries.name: pill
entries.description: A dose of [medicine](#medicine) pressed into a tablet or packed into a capsule, shown loose, in a blister pack or [spilling](#spilling) from a [bottle](#bottle). Also a recurring motif in illness- and menhera-themed art.

entries.name: flask
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) [laboratory](#laboratory) vessel with a narrow [neck](#neck), either cone-shaped or round-bottomed, [holding](#holding) [liquid](#liquid). A hip flask for [drink](#drink) is a different object.

entries.name: stethoscope
entries.description: The medical [instrument](#instrument) with earpieces and a chest piece for [listening](#listening) to [heart](#heart) and lungs, typically hung around a doctor's or nurse's [neck](#neck).

entries.name: drugs
entries.description: Narcotics or stimulants present or being taken, shown as a [syringe](#syringe), loose pills, or powder laid out for snorting.

entries.name: round-bottom_flask
entries.description: A [laboratory](#laboratory) [flask](#flask) with a spherical body and a straight [neck](#neck), seen in [chemistry](#chemistry) and [alchemy](#alchemy) scenes.

entries.name: thermometer
entries.description: An [instrument](#instrument) for [reading](#reading) [temperature](#temperature), most often a clinical one held in a [sick](#sick) character's mouth or armpit. Frequently paired with sick and [bed](#bed).

entries.name: blood_bag
entries.description: A plastic [pouch](#pouch) of donated [blood](#blood), typically [hanging](#hanging) from a stand beside a [hospital](#hospital) [bed](#bed). It also turns up as something a [vampire](#vampire) drinks from directly.

entries.name: first_aid_kit
entries.description: A [box](#box) or [bag](#bag) of basic medical supplies for treating an [injury](#injury) on the spot, usually marked with a [cross](#cross). Add [first_aid](#first_aid) when someone is actually being treated.

entries.name: pregnancy_test
entries.description: A slim plastic [stick](#stick) with a small result [window](#window), read for the lines that confirm a pregnancy. Held up or left on a [sink](#sink), usually played for shock or for a joke; the [pregnant](#pregnant) [tag](#tag) needs a visible [belly](#belly).

entries.name: scalpel
entries.description: A small surgical [knife](#knife) with an extremely keen blade, used in operations and dissection and, as a hobby knife, in fine craft work.

entries.name: erlenmeyer_flask
entries.description: The cone-shaped [laboratory](#laboratory) [flask](#flask): flat base, sloping sides, narrow cylindrical [neck](#neck), usually shown [holding](#holding) brightly coloured [liquid](#liquid). Shorthand for [chemistry](#chemistry) and mad-science scenes.

entries.name: balance_scale
entries.description: A beam pivoting at its middle with a pan [hanging](#hanging) from each end: the object goes in one and known [weights](#weights) in the other, and the beam levels when the two match. It is not the Libra [constellation](#constellation), which carries its own [symbolism](#symbolism).

entries.name: beaker
entries.description: A straight-sided cylindrical [laboratory](#laboratory) [glass](#glass) with a flat bottom and a small [pouring](#pouring) lip, used to stir, mix and heat liquids. The marks up its side are rough guides only.

entries.name: large_syringe
entries.description: A [syringe](#syringe) scaled far past anything a patient could receive, sometimes as long as an arm. It reads as a [weapon](#weapon) or a menacing prop rather than as medical equipment.

entries.name: cardiogram
entries.description: The spiking line of a [heart](#heart) trace, on a [monitor](#monitor), on a [paper](#paper) printout or laid across the picture as a graphic. Its peaks stand in for health, effort or feeling.

entries.name: digital_thermometer
entries.description: A [thermometer](#thermometer) with a numeric readout in place of a mercury [column](#column), usually a slim probe with a small [screen](#screen). Belongs to sickbed and check-up scenes.

entries.name: oxygen_mask
entries.description: A [cup](#cup) strapped over the [nose](#nose) and mouth that feeds [gas](#gas) from a cylinder to the wearer. The same [tag](#tag) covers the anaesthesia masks used in operating rooms.

entries.name: iv_stand
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) wheeled [pole](#pole) with hooked arms at the top, [carrying](#carrying) bags of fluid or [blood](#blood) that run down a line to a patient. It stands in sickrooms, and is sometimes fixed to a [bed](#bed), gurney or [wheelchair](#wheelchair).

entries.name: electrodes
entries.description: Conductive pads or contacts [stuck](#stuck) to the skin and wired [back](#back) to a [box](#box). They belong to medical scenes, science-fiction rigs and shock setups. The pads themselves are what is named, not the [machine](#machine) [feeding](#feeding) them.

entries.name: medicine
entries.description: Drugs or herbal remedies taken to maintain health or treat illness, drawn as pills, capsules, powders or a measured dose.

entries.name: science
entries.description: Research and experiment as the subject: glassware and burners, formulae chalked on a board, specimens, instruments and lab coats. A standard flavour in science fiction settings.

entries.name: oxygen_tank
entries.description: A pressurised cylinder of [breathing](#breathing) [gas](#gas), strapped to the [back](#back) or wheeled along beside a patient. Hospital, [diving](#diving) and [rescue](#rescue) scenes are where it shows up.

entries.name: pill_bottle
entries.description: A small wide-mouthed [bottle](#bottle) [holding](#holding) tablets, capsules or supplements, usually capped and labelled. Appears in medical scenes and in imagery about illness or overdose.

entries.name: armillary_sphere
entries.description: A [model](#model) of the heavens built from nested rings [standing](#standing) for the celestial circles, turning on a stand around a small central [globe](#globe). Its open framework tells it apart from a solid celestial globe.

entries.name: mercury_(element)
entries.description: The metal that stays [liquid](#liquid) at room [temperature](#temperature), drawn as mirror-bright [beads](#beads) or a [rolling](#rolling) silver [pool](#pool). Not to be [confused](#confused) with the [planet](#planet) of the same name.

entries.name: chloroform
entries.description: A colourless anaesthetic [liquid](#liquid), in pictures nearly always soaked into a [cloth](#cloth) and held over somebody's [nose](#nose) and mouth to knock them out. The scene is usually an [abduction](#abduction) rather than a [hospital](#hospital).

entries.name: double_helix
entries.description: Two strands winding around one another in a [spiral](#spiral), almost always [standing](#standing) in for DNA. Appears in [laboratory](#laboratory) backdrops, genetic themes and [science](#science) fiction imagery.

entries.name: dna
entries.description: The twisted double-helix [ladder](#ladder) of genetic material, drawn as a [floating](#floating) [diagram](#diagram) or a [glowing](#glowing) motif. Turns up in [laboratory](#laboratory), cloning and [mutation](#mutation) scenes.

entries.name: test_tube_rack
entries.description: A stand pierced with rows of holes that keep test tubes upright, often filled with brightly coloured liquids. Standard [dressing](#dressing) for any [laboratory](#laboratory) scene.

entries.name: blister_pack
entries.description: Packaging made of small sealed plastic bubbles on a foil or [card](#card) backing, each [holding](#holding) a single [pill](#pill) or item. Medicine accounts for most of it, though toys are sold this way too.

entries.name: medicine_bottle
entries.description: A capped [container](#container) for tablets or a [liquid](#liquid) remedy, sometimes fitted with a dropper set into the [lid](#lid). Usually seen on a [bedside](#bedside) [table](#table) or being handed to a patient.

entries.name: head_mirror
entries.description: The round concave [mirror](#mirror) on a [headband](#headband) that doctors once wore over one eye to throw light down a throat or into an ear. It survives mainly as [costume](#costume) shorthand for a physician.

entries.name: suppository
entries.description: A small moulded dose of [medicine](#medicine) meant to be inserted into the rectum, vagina or [urethra](#urethra), where it melts and is absorbed. Usually drawn as a smooth, bullet-shaped capsule.

entries.name: microscope
entries.description: An optical [laboratory](#laboratory) [instrument](#instrument) for viewing what the eye alone cannot resolve, with a [stage](#stage), eyepiece and turret of lenses. A common science-room and laboratory prop.

entries.name: cotton_ball
entries.description: A small puff of cotton [wool](#wool) for dabbing ointment onto a wound. It also gets wedged between the [toes](#toes) while nail varnish dries.

entries.name: celestial_globe
entries.description: A sphere on a stand with the constellations and star positions charted over its surface, a [map](#map) of the [sky](#sky) turned outside in. The [skeleton](#skeleton) of rings that does a related job is an armillary sphere.

entries.name: x-ray_film
entries.description: A radiograph from a real [x-ray](#x-ray) [machine](#machine), showing bones as pale [shapes](#shapes) against a [dark](#dark) sheet. Use it for the medical image as an object, not for cutaway drawings that reveal what is inside a body.

entries.name: eye_drops
entries.description: A small squeeze [bottle](#bottle) of [liquid](#liquid) dripped into the eye, usually with the head tipped [back](#back) and the [lid](#lid) held open. It turns up in tired-student and clinic scenes.

entries.name: chemicals
entries.description: Assorted chemical substances in the picture, kept in vials, flasks and bottles or spilled across a surface. Where the image is about practising [science](#science) with them, [chemistry](#chemistry) is the better [tag](#tag).

entries.name: breathing_tube
entries.description: A [tube](#tube) [carrying](#carrying) air to the wearer's mouth or [nose](#nose), [running](#running) [back](#back) to a [mask](#mask), a [helmet](#helmet) or a [tank](#tank). Divers, pilots, hazard suits and [hospital](#hospital) beds all involve one.

entries.name: stretcher
entries.description: A wheeled trolley or carried frame for moving an injured person [lying](#lying) flat. Belongs to [ambulance](#ambulance), [hospital](#hospital) and [rescue](#rescue) scenes.

entries.name: eye_chart
entries.description: A vision-test board whose letters or gapped rings shrink row by row down the page. A fixture of clinics and [school](#school) health checks.

entries.name: surgical_scissors
entries.description: Small ringed [shears](#shears) used in operations, with fine blunt or pointed blades and long looped handles. Drawn as an [instrument](#instrument) on a [tray](#tray) or in a gloved hand rather than as household [scissors](#scissors).

entries.name: liquid-in-glass_thermometer
entries.description: The classic [glass](#glass) [thermometer](#thermometer) whose [column](#column) of coloured fluid rises and falls in a narrow bore against a printed scale.

entries.name: stadiometer
entries.description: The upright [measuring](#measuring) rod with a [sliding](#sliding) [headpiece](#headpiece) used to take somebody's [height](#height). Appears in [school](#school) health checks and clinics, often in height-comparison jokes.

entries.name: gem
entries.description: A smooth polished precious stone, whether set in jewellery, worked into clothing or [lying](#lying) loose. Faceted stones are [crystal](#crystal), and placement tags such as [forehead_jewel](#forehead_jewel) or [chest_jewel](#chest_jewel) say where one sits on the body.

entries.name: jingle_bell
entries.description: A small hollow metal [ball](#ball) with a slit and a loose pellet inside, ringing bright and high. They hang from [winter](#winter) [decorations](#decorations), ride on [pet](#pet) collars, and are sewn onto costumes and hair pieces.

entries.name: gift
entries.description: A present wrapped in [plain](#plain) or [patterned](#patterned) [paper](#paper) and dressed with [ribbon](#ribbon), whether a [box](#box), a [bag](#bag) or another [container](#container). Common in [birthday](#birthday), Christmas and Valentine scenes.

entries.name: crystal
entries.description: A [translucent](#translucent) mineral mass with flat faces, from quartz clusters and [cave](#cave) formations to [glowing](#glowing) magical stones. Add [diamond_(gemstone)](#diamond_(gemstone)) when it has been cut for jewellery; a smooth, edgeless stone is [gem](#gem).

entries.name: gift_box
entries.description: A small [box](#box) wrapped in colourful [paper](#paper) and finished with a [bow](#bow), [holding](#holding) a present for someone.

entries.name: balloon
entries.description: An inflated [party](#party) balloon, [floating](#floating) on its [string](#string), gripped in a hand or [drifting](#drifting) loose. It comes with birthdays and celebrations; add [holding_balloon](#holding_balloon) when someone has hold of one.

entries.name: flag
entries.description: A piece of [cloth](#cloth) flown from a [pole](#pole) or carried, bearing the [emblem](#emblem) of a country, a faction or an event. It applies to cloth [hanging](#hanging) the long way across; cloth hanging lengthwise down is a [banner](#banner). Add the country's own flag [tag](#tag) where it [can](#can) be recognised.

entries.name: blue_gemstone
entries.description: A blue [gem](#gem) such as a sapphire, set into [jewelry](#jewelry), a [weapon](#weapon) [hilt](#hilt) or a [crown](#crown), or shown loose. Only the colour is claimed, not the cut or the setting.

entries.name: coin
entries.description: A round metal piece of [money](#money), single or heaped up, whether modern currency, [fantasy](#fantasy) [gold](#gold) or a traditional oval koban. Particular uses have their own tags, among them [coin_flip](#coin_flip) and [coin_on_string](#coin_on_string).

entries.name: gold
entries.description: The yellow precious metal itself, as [bars](#bars), coins, heaped [treasure](#treasure) or raw ore. Clothing and [accessories](#accessories) that merely look golden take their own gold_ tags.

entries.name: christmas_tree
entries.description: A fir or pine hung with ornaments and lights, or an object [standing](#standing) in for one such as a wire-frame [tree](#tree). Somebody dressed up as a tree takes [christmas_tree_costume](#christmas_tree_costume).

entries.name: red_gemstone
entries.description: A red jewel such as a ruby, whether set in a [ring](#ring) or [crown](#crown), [decorating](#decorating) a [weapon](#weapon), or [lying](#lying) loose. Tags the colour of the stone itself, not the metal or setting around it.

entries.name: american_flag
entries.description: The United States [flag](#flag) itself, thirteen red and white [bars](#bars) with a blue [field](#field) of stars in the [corner](#corner). Patterns or symbols [standing](#standing) in for the country without the flag are [united_states](#united_states).

entries.name: money
entries.description: Currency in the picture in any form: banknotes, coins or a stuffed [bag](#bag) of it. Particular currencies, currency symbols and actions such as [counting](#counting) it or [fanning](#fanning) it out have tags of their own.

entries.name: green_gemstone
entries.description: A green cut stone, an emerald being the obvious example. It may be set into jewellery, mounted on a [weapon](#weapon) or shown loose.

entries.name: christmas_ornaments
entries.description: Decorations hung on a Christmas [tree](#tree), most often round shiny baubles but also stars, bells and small figures. The tree itself takes [christmas_tree](#christmas_tree).

entries.name: banner
entries.description: A length of [cloth](#cloth) [carrying](#carrying) a symbol, slogan or message, usually hung the [tall](#tall) way rather than flown flat. It covers [war](#war) banners on poles as [well](#well) as [birthday](#birthday) greetings strung across a room, and any [hanging](#hanging) [fabric](#fabric) that would sit oddly under [flag](#flag).

entries.name: medal
entries.description: A flat metal disc bearing a design or inscription, awarded for merit or made to mark an event, most often worn hung from a [ribbon](#ribbon) around the [neck](#neck). Covers both sporting medals and [military](#military) [decorations](#decorations).

entries.name: chinese_knot
entries.description: Ornamental cord knotwork, symmetrical and usually worked in two layers, with two cords entering at the top and two leaving below. Flower, endless, button and panchang forms are the common ones, generally hung with a [tassel](#tassel) as a good-luck charm.

entries.name: purple_gemstone
entries.description: A purple or violet jewel, typically an amethyst, set into [jewelry](#jewelry) or a [weapon](#weapon), or simply shown loose. Combine with [gem](#gem).

entries.name: heart_balloon
entries.description: A [balloon](#balloon) made in the shape of a [heart](#heart), seen at Valentine's, weddings and confessions.

entries.name: string_of_flags
entries.description: Small pennants or flags strung along a cord as [bunting](#bunting), hung across a [street](#street), [shop](#shop) or [festival](#festival) stall. When the flags are national ones, add [flags_of_all_nations](#flags_of_all_nations).

entries.name: pearl_(gemstone)
entries.description: The lustrous sphere grown inside an [oyster](#oyster) or another mollusc, usually white but drawn in any colour. Shown loose, [resting](#resting) in a [shell](#shell) or set as decoration; strung and worn it becomes [pearl_necklace](#pearl_necklace) or [pearl_bracelet](#pearl_bracelet).

entries.name: bunting
entries.description: Small triangular flags strung along a line as festive decoration, hung for parties, fairs and [school](#school) sports days. Strings made from national flags take [flags_of_all_nations](#flags_of_all_nations) instead.

entries.name: poker_chip
entries.description: Small round [casino](#casino) tokens [standing](#standing) in for [money](#money) at the [gambling](#gambling) [table](#table), their colours marking different values. Common in card-game and casino scenes.

entries.name: banknote
entries.description: Paper currency, whether a single bill or a thick bundle, held out, thrown, tucked into clothing or heaped up. Add [money](#money) for the general [idea](#idea) and [coin](#coin) for metal currency.

entries.name: union_jack
entries.description: The [flag](#flag) of the United Kingdom, its overlapping red and white diagonal and upright crosses on a blue [field](#field), shown [flying](#flying), printed or used as a design motif. The same pattern also appears within the flags of Australia, New Zealand and Hawaii.

entries.name: japanese_flag
entries.description: The [flag](#flag) of Japan, a [plain](#plain) red disc centred on white. Do not confuse it with the rising [sun](#sun) flag, which adds rays [spreading](#spreading) out from the disc.

entries.name: streamers
entries.description: Long thin [paper](#paper) strips used as [party](#party) decoration, either hung from the [ceiling](#ceiling) or thrown into the air. Tiny versions burst out of party poppers at celebrations.

entries.name: diamond_(gemstone)
entries.description: A cut diamond, set in jewellery or [lying](#lying) loose. Only for crystals shaped the way a jeweller would cut them; the [card](#card) [suit](#suit) is [diamond_(shape)](#diamond_(shape)) and the [gem](#gem) [emoji](#emoji) is [gem_(symbol)](#gem_(symbol)).

entries.name: earth_(ornament)
entries.description: A decorative object made in the shape of the [planet](#planet): a [globe](#globe) [pendant](#pendant), a bauble, a hair piece. The planet itself as a body in [space](#space) is [earth_(planet)](#earth_(planet)).

entries.name: casino_chip
entries.description: A round token [standing](#standing) in for [money](#money) at a gaming [table](#table), coloured and edge-marked by value. Stacked, slid across the felt or rolled over the knuckles.

entries.name: star_ornament
entries.description: A decorative star object, most often the topper on a Christmas [tree](#tree) or a [hanging](#hanging) holiday decoration.

entries.name: christmas_present
entries.description: A wrapped [gift](#gift) with [ribbon](#ribbon) and [bow](#bow) in a Christmas setting, stacked under the [tree](#tree) or carried in a [sack](#sack). Gifts outside the holiday are simply gift.

entries.name: pink_gemstone
entries.description: A [gem](#gem) coloured pink, loose, set into [jewelry](#jewelry) or mounted on a [weapon](#weapon) or [staff](#staff). Its cut and setting are left to other tags.

entries.name: aqua_gem
entries.description: A blue-green jewel, set into [jewelry](#jewelry), mounted on a [weapon](#weapon) or [lying](#lying) loose in the scene. The stone's colour is what is being recorded.

entries.name: italian_flag
entries.description: The Italian tricolour, three upright bands of green, white and red. It may be [flying](#flying), carried, draped or used as a motif.

entries.name: pennant
entries.description: A triangular [flag](#flag), the sort strung as [bunting](#bunting) at festivals, waved by supporters or flown from a [mast](#mast). Strings of them are a fixture of [party](#party) scenes.

entries.name: gold_coin
entries.description: Coins struck in [gold](#gold), shown singly, stacked, scattered underfoot or [pouring](#pouring) out of a chest.

entries.name: haniwa_(statue)
entries.description: Hollow terracotta figures made in Japan's Kofun period and [buried](#buried) with the dead, shaped as armoured soldiers, horses, animals and houses with simple cut-out eyes and mouths. Their blank [staring](#staring) faces have made them a stock [comic](#comic) prop and the [model](#model) for various game creatures.

entries.name: gift_bag
entries.description: A small [fabric](#fabric) [pouch](#pouch) drawn shut with [ribbon](#ribbon), or a decorated [paper](#paper) [bag](#bag) with looped [string](#string) handles, [holding](#holding) one present. A big [sack](#sack) [carrying](#carrying) many wrapped gifts is a sack instead.

entries.name: coin_on_string
entries.description: A [coin](#coin) hung from a [string](#string) or cord. Most often it is swung as a hypnotist's [pendulum](#pendulum), though it also appears simply as a worn charm.

entries.name: aqua_gemstone
entries.description: A cut stone in aqua or turquoise, usually set into [jewelry](#jewelry) or a [costume](#costume) piece. Tag the piece it belongs to as [well](#well).

entries.name: german_flag
entries.description: The [flag](#flag) of Germany, three horizontal bands of black, red and [gold](#gold), whether flown, printed or filling the background. The Belgian flag runs its stripes vertically and is a different thing.

entries.name: holed_coin
entries.description: A [coin](#coin) with a [hole](#hole) [punched](#punched) through the middle, like the Japanese five and fifty [yen](#yen) pieces or [old](#old) Chinese cash. The hole let such coins be strung on a cord into bundles.

entries.name: skull_ornament
entries.description: Decorative [skull](#skull) [shapes](#shapes) used as ornaments on clothing, weapons, furniture or a room, such as a skull-topped [staff](#staff) or a [belt](#belt) [buckle](#buckle). Worn in the hair it is [skull_hair_ornament](#skull_hair_ornament).

entries.name: checkered_flag
entries.description: The black and white chequered [flag](#flag), waved as the leader crosses the finish line. It also turns up as motorsport decoration away from the track itself.

entries.name: rising_sun_flag
entries.description: The Japanese naval ensign: a red [sun](#sun) with sixteen rays on white, historically the [flag](#flag) of the Imperial Army and Navy and still flown by the Maritime Self-Defense Force. Carries [strong](#strong) wartime associations in neighbouring countries.

entries.name: maneki-neko
entries.description: The [beckoning](#beckoning) [cat](#cat) [figure](#figure) with one paw raised, set at [shop](#shop) and [restaurant](#restaurant) doors to draw in custom. Also used where a character copies the pose beside one.

entries.name: yellow_gemstone
entries.description: A yellow [gem](#gem), such as a topaz or citrine, loose or set into jewellery. Tag gem as [well](#well).

entries.name: united_states
entries.description: The picture references the USA, most often through the stars and stripes, an American landmark, a cultural joke, or a [cameo](#cameo) by an American public [figure](#figure). A garment printed with the [flag](#flag) pattern alone does not count unless the piece is actually about America.

entries.name: heart-shaped_gem
entries.description: A jewel faceted into a [heart](#heart), set in a [pendant](#pendant), a [ring](#ring) or a [weapon](#weapon) [hilt](#hilt), or [lying](#lying) loose. A stock magical trinket.

entries.name: trophy
entries.description: A [cup](#cup), [statuette](#statuette) or [plaque](#plaque) awarded for winning something, held aloft in [victory](#victory) or displayed on a [shelf](#shelf). Sports championships and film or entertainment awards are the usual context.

entries.name: brazilian_flag
entries.description: Brazil's [flag](#flag): a green [field](#field) [carrying](#carrying) a yellow diamond with a starred blue [globe](#globe) at its centre, shown [flying](#flying), held, worn or hung up. Add flag, and [brazil](#brazil) when the country itself is the setting.

entries.name: christmas_stocking
entries.description: An oversized red sock with a white [fluffy](#fluffy) cuff, hung up to be filled with presents overnight. It covers the prop itself, never a sock somebody is wearing.

entries.name: horseshoe
entries.description: A U-shaped metal shoe nailed to a horse's hoof, shown on the [animal](#animal) or [lying](#lying) loose as a luck charm. Horseshoe [shapes](#shapes) used as decoration on clothing or in hair are [horseshoe_ornament](#horseshoe_ornament).

entries.name: french_flag
entries.description: The blue, white and red tricolour of France, shown as a [flag](#flag) or borrowed as the basis of a print. Historical versions carry the [fleur-de-lis](#fleur-de-lis) instead.

entries.name: butterfly_ornament
entries.description: A decorative [butterfly](#butterfly) made as an object — cut from metal, [glass](#glass), [paper](#paper) or [cloth](#cloth) — rather than a living insect.

entries.name: heart-shaped_ornament
entries.description: A decorative [heart](#heart) hung or fixed on something: a charm on a [bag](#bag), a bauble on a [tree](#tree), a trim piece on furniture or a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: kadomatsu
entries.description: A New Year decoration of cut [bamboo](#bamboo) stalks bundled with pine and sometimes [plum](#plum), stood in a pair at an [entrance](#entrance) to welcome the year's spirits. It goes up after Christmas and comes down in the first week of January.

entries.name: orange_gemstone
entries.description: A cut or polished stone in orange, set into jewellery, mounted on a [hilt](#hilt) or [lying](#lying) loose among [treasure](#treasure). Only the colour of the stone is recorded.

entries.name: white_flag
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) white [banner](#banner), waved or raised as a signal of surrender or a request to parley. In motorsport it [can](#can) instead mean a slow vehicle ahead or the final [lap](#lap).

entries.name: bat_ornament
entries.description: A bat-shaped decoration hung up, [pinned](#pinned) or propped in the scene. Halloween and gothic trimmings account for most of them.

entries.name: koinobori
entries.description: Carp-shaped [cloth](#cloth) windsocks strung up a [pole](#pole) so the [wind](#wind) fills them and they seem to swim. Households raise them for the children's holiday in early May.

entries.name: russian_flag
entries.description: The tricolour of three horizontal bands, white above blue above red. The red [banner](#banner) with [hammer](#hammer) and [sickle](#sickle) is the Soviet [flag](#flag) and is kept apart from this one.

entries.name: heart_ornament
entries.description: A decorative piece formed as a [heart](#heart), attached to an object, a garment or an accessory as trim.

entries.name: garland_(decoration)
entries.description: A long [rope](#rope) of [tinsel](#tinsel), flowers or evergreen hung up for a [celebration](#celebration), usually drawn thick and [fluffy](#fluffy). Draped along mantels, banisters and trees, most often at Christmas.

entries.name: jade_(gemstone)
entries.description: The green stone long prized in Chinese craft, from milky and pale to a deep [translucent](#translucent) green. It appears as carved pendants, bangles and ornaments, or as rough uncut [rock](#rock).

entries.name: yen_sign
entries.description: The ¥ mark [standing](#standing) for Japanese currency, drawn as a symbol rather than [buried](#buried) in [running](#running) text. It shows up on [price](#price) tags, in [comic](#comic) panels and as decoration.

entries.name: treasure
entries.description: A hoard of valuables such as heaped [gold](#gold) coins, jewels, crowns and cups, often [spilling](#spilling) out of an open chest. Fits [pirate](#pirate) caches, [dragon](#dragon) hoards and [dungeon](#dungeon) rewards alike.

entries.name: gift_wrapping
entries.description: A present dressed up in [paper](#paper), [ribbon](#ribbon) and bows, either finished or in the middle of being tied. When a character is the one wrapped up like a present, use [ribbon_bondage](#ribbon_bondage) or [naked_ribbon](#naked_ribbon).

entries.name: yen
entries.description: Japanese [money](#money) in the picture, as banknotes, coins or a written sum. Often held out in payment or fanned across a hand.

entries.name: hongbao
entries.description: The red [envelope](#envelope) of [money](#money) handed over at Lunar New Year, weddings and births, usually stamped with a [gold](#gold) character for good fortune. Gold and pink versions exist, while white and black are avoided as [funeral](#funeral) colours.

entries.name: mini_flag
entries.description: A small hand-held [flag](#flag) on a [stick](#stick), the size used to [garnish](#garnish) a [plate](#plate) of [food](#food), wave at a [parade](#parade) or [plant](#plant) in a scale [model](#model).

entries.name: credit_card
entries.description: A payment [card](#card) with its stripe, chip and raised numbers, held out or [lying](#lying) on a surface. Turns up in [shopping](#shopping) and paying scenes.

entries.name: koban_(gold)
entries.description: A flat oval [gold](#gold) [coin](#coin) from Edo-period Japan, stamped and slightly dished. Beckoning [cat](#cat) figurines hold one, so cat-themed characters are often given one too.

entries.name: decorations
entries.description: The scene has been dressed for an occasion with balloons, [streamers](#streamers), [confetti](#confetti), garlands or strings of lights. Points at the festive trimming of the setting as a whole rather than at any single item.

entries.name: z_flag
entries.description: A maritime signal [flag](#flag) divided diagonally into yellow, blue, red and black quarters, historically tied to a famous Japanese naval [battle](#battle). It has since taken on [strong](#strong) nationalist associations, unrelated to any modern country's flag despite the similar name.

entries.name: united_kingdom
entries.description: Something in the picture points to Britain and Northern Ireland: the [flag](#flag), a recognisable landmark, British [dress](#dress), or a setting the piece is explicitly about. A flag-patterned [bikini](#bikini) alone does not carry the [tag](#tag) unless the country itself is the point.

entries.name: dollar_bill
entries.description: American [paper](#paper) [money](#money) of any denomination, [portrait](#portrait) and green printing visible. Currency from other countries takes other tags.

entries.name: championship_belt
entries.description: The broad [trophy](#trophy) [belt](#belt) awarded in [boxing](#boxing), mixed martial arts or professional [wrestling](#wrestling), its centre a large [gold](#gold) [plate](#plate) naming the [title](#title). Winners [buckle](#buckle) it at the waist or hang it over a shoulder.

entries.name: south_korean_flag
entries.description: The Taegukgi: a white [field](#field) [carrying](#carrying) the red-and-blue circular taegeuk at its center and four black trigrams set at the corners.

entries.name: white_gemstone
entries.description: A clear or milky white stone, faceted loose or set into [jewelry](#jewelry). Diamonds, moonstones and generic pale crystals all fall under it.

entries.name: ukrainian_flag
entries.description: The national [banner](#banner) of Ukraine, two equal horizontal bands of blue above yellow. Shown [flying](#flying), draped over something, or worn as a colour scheme.

entries.name: money_bag
entries.description: The cartoon [sack](#sack) of cash, a canvas [bag](#bag) cinched at the [neck](#neck) with a currency symbol painted on the side. Shorthand for a fortune, a bribe or the takings of a robbery.

entries.name: firecrackers
entries.description: Small powder-filled [paper](#paper) tubes that bang rather than [fly](#fly), sold singly or knotted into long strings. Set off for Chinese New Year, and also hung up as red decoration.

entries.name: nobori
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) narrow [cloth](#cloth) [banner](#banner) on a [pole](#pole), almost always lettered down its length. Once carried by armies, it is now a fixture at festivals, shops and event stalls.

entries.name: rainbow_flag
entries.description: The horizontally striped spectrum [banner](#banner) flown as an [emblem](#emblem) of LGBT pride. Appears as a waved [flag](#flag), a [cape](#cape), or a [backdrop](#backdrop) in celebratory pictures.

entries.name: kooribata
entries.description: The small [paper](#paper) [flag](#flag) that marks shaved [ice](#ice): a red ice character on white above a band of blue [water](#water), sometimes with two green birds. It stands [planted](#planted) in the [dessert](#dessert) or flies over the stall.

entries.name: jack-o'-lantern_ornament
entries.description: A carved [pumpkin](#pumpkin) [lantern](#lantern) used as decoration rather than carried, worn on an outfit or set out on a [porch](#porch), [shelf](#shelf) or [table](#table). It is usually lit from inside.

entries.name: crystal_shards
entries.description: Broken pieces of [crystal](#crystal) [lying](#lying) on the ground or [hanging](#hanging) in the air. Either the remains of something [shattered](#shattered) or fragments [drifting](#drifting) as part of a magical effect.

entries.name: red_flag
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) red [banner](#banner) on a [pole](#pole) or held in the hand. It serves as a warning [marker](#marker) in some pictures and as a socialist or communist [emblem](#emblem) in others.

entries.name: transgender_flag
entries.description: The pride [flag](#flag) in pale blue, pink and white bands, flown from a [pole](#pole), draped over the shoulders, or simply held up. Represents transfeminine, transmasculine and non-binary identities in that colour order.

entries.name: snowflake_ornament
entries.description: A decorative snowflake used purely as trim: hung on a [tree](#tree), strung across a room, or fixed to an object, without being worn on the body.

entries.name: battle_standard
entries.description: A [flag](#flag) carried into [battle](#battle) on a [pole](#pole) to show which side its bearers belong to. A [cloth](#cloth) hung the wide way is more exactly a [war](#war) flag and a [tall](#tall) one a war [banner](#banner); [military](#military) flags flown from ships take the national [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: black_gemstone
entries.description: A cut stone in black, set into jewellery, a [weapon](#weapon) or an artefact, or shown loose. Its [darkness](#darkness) usually signals something [sinister](#sinister).

entries.name: swedish_flag
entries.description: A golden Nordic [cross](#cross) shifted toward the [pole](#pole) on a mid-blue [field](#field). The panels nearest the hoist are noticeably wider than the ones near the [fly](#fly), and a longer swallow-tailed [military](#military) version also exists.

entries.name: cat_ornament
entries.description: A small decorative [cat](#cat), worn as a trinket on clothing or in the hair, or [standing](#standing) about the room as a [figure](#figure). The cat here is a made object rather than a living [animal](#animal).

entries.name: paper_chain
entries.description: Loops of coloured [paper](#paper) linked into a [hanging](#hanging) [chain](#chain) and strung up for parties and festivals. Easy enough for children to make, and usually drawn near [streamers](#streamers) or balloons.

entries.name: canadian_flag
entries.description: The [flag](#flag) of Canada — a white centre panel between two red bands, with the red maple [leaf](#leaf) set in the middle. Flown, draped, or printed onto clothing and gear.

entries.name: people's_republic_of_china_flag
entries.description: The red [flag](#flag) bearing one large golden star with four smaller ones arced beside it. Distinct from the Republic of China flag flown by Taiwan.

entries.name: award_ribbon
entries.description: A rosette or [ribbon](#ribbon) handed out as a prize, [pinned](#pinned) to the chest or held up for the viewer. A [sash](#sash) worn diagonally across the body is a separate thing entirely.

entries.name: lion_head_(ornament)
entries.description: A lion's head worked as a decorative fitting: a [door](#door) knocker, a shoulder piece on armour, a carved boss or a [brooch](#brooch).

entries.name: united_states_medal_of_honor
entries.description: The highest American [military](#military) decoration for valour, worn on a pale blue [neck](#neck) [ribbon](#ribbon) or [pinned](#pinned) to the chest. Most often drawn on one particular Kantai Collection shipgirl, though any depiction of the [medal](#medal) qualifies.

entries.name: gift_card
entries.description: A prepaid plastic [card](#card) spent like cash at one [shop](#shop) or [chain](#chain). Turns up in [shopping](#shopping) scenes and in jokes about [pouring](#pouring) [money](#money) into gacha pulls.

entries.name: christmas_star
entries.description: The star fixed at the top of a Christmas [tree](#tree), or that same star used as decoration elsewhere in the scene. Usually [gold](#gold) or silver and often lit from within.

entries.name: swiss_flag
entries.description: A bold white [cross](#cross) with arms of equal length on a red [field](#field). Unlike most national flags it is [square](#square) rather than rectangular.

entries.name: gold_bar
entries.description: A [cast](#cast) block of [gold](#gold) with sloping sides, stacked in a vault or held up as loot. Also called an ingot or bullion, and used as shorthand for sudden wealth.

entries.name: soviet_flag
entries.description: A [plain](#plain) red [field](#field) bearing a [gold](#gold) [hammer](#hammer) and [sickle](#sickle) beneath a gold-outlined star in the upper hoist [corner](#corner). Still widely used as a general communist [emblem](#emblem) beyond the country itself.

entries.name: flags_of_all_nations
entries.description: A row of national flags, real or invented, strung along a [rope](#rope) overhead. Standard decoration for sports days and [school](#school) festivals.

entries.name: lesbian_flag
entries.description: The lesbian pride [flag](#flag), most often banded in oranges, white and pinks, though several designs circulate. It appears held up, worn as a [cape](#cape) or spread behind the subject.

entries.name: finnish_flag
entries.description: A white [field](#field) crossed by a blue Nordic [cross](#cross) set toward the hoist. State versions place a [lion](#lion) [coat](#coat) of arms where the arms of the cross meet.

entries.name: piggy_bank
entries.description: A [coin](#coin) bank moulded as a [pig](#pig), usually ceramic and slotted along the [back](#back). It stands for saving up; banks made in other [shapes](#shapes) are simply coin banks.

entries.name: navy_cross
entries.description: A naval service decoration for extreme courage in combat, ranking just below the highest award for valour. It appears as the [ribbon](#ribbon) and [medal](#medal) [pinned](#pinned) to a [dress](#dress) uniform.

entries.name: republic_of_china_flag
entries.description: The red [flag](#flag) with a blue canton [holding](#holding) a white twelve-pointed [sun](#sun), flown by Taiwan. Keep it apart from the flag of the People's Republic of China, which is red with yellow stars.

entries.name: tinsel
entries.description: Long glittering plastic strands draped over a Christmas [tree](#tree) or strung up for a [party](#party). Distinct from garland, the thicker rope-shaped decoration, which may itself be made of it.

entries.name: animal_balloon
entries.description: An inflated [balloon](#balloon) moulded into a creature's shape, the kind sold at fairs and [festival](#festival) stalls. Do not mix it up with the figures twisted out of long thin balloons, which are tagged separately.

entries.name: indonesian_flag
entries.description: Indonesia's national [flag](#flag), a red band above a white one. Poland's uses the same two colours the other way round, which is the easy mistake.

entries.name: numbered_flag
entries.description: A [flag](#flag) or [pennant](#pennant) [carrying](#carrying) a numeral, of the kind [planted](#planted) at races and sports festivals to mark finishing places. It is usually [stuck](#stuck) in the ground or waved by an official.

entries.name: argentinian_flag
entries.description: Three level bands, pale blue at top and bottom with white between, often [carrying](#carrying) a golden [sun](#sun) at the centre. Turns up on poles, walls, clothing and body [paint](#paint).

entries.name: australian_flag
entries.description: Australia's [flag](#flag): a [dark](#dark) blue ground [carrying](#carrying) the Union Jack in the upper hoist [corner](#corner), a large seven-pointed star beneath it and the Southern Cross scattered across the [fly](#fly).

entries.name: pile_of_money
entries.description: Coins or banknotes heaped loosely, [spilling](#spilling) across a [floor](#floor) or filling a vault or hoard. Neatly squared towers of coins are a [stack](#stack) rather than a [pile](#pile).

entries.name: spanish_flag
entries.description: The [flag](#flag) of Spain: horizontal red, wide yellow, and red bands, with the national [coat](#coat) of arms set toward the hoist.

entries.name: signal_flag
entries.description: One of the coded maritime flags hoisted on a ship's [mast](#mast) to [spell](#spell) letters or set phrases for other vessels. Each carries a bold geometric pattern in a few flat colors.

entries.name: torn_flag
entries.description: A [flag](#flag) or [banner](#banner) ragged along its [fly](#fly), holed and fraying. Common set [dressing](#dressing) for a [battlefield](#battlefield) or a ruin.

entries.name: mexican_flag
entries.description: The green, white and red Mexican tricolor, with the [eagle](#eagle) and serpent [emblem](#emblem) in its central band, waved, hung as a [banner](#banner) or worn as a wrap.

entries.name: war_flag
entries.description: A [banner](#banner) carried into [battle](#battle) to show which side its bearers belong to, hung so the [cloth](#cloth) runs horizontally. Vertical cloth is a banner instead, and the [military](#military) context has to be clear.

entries.name: grey_gemstone
entries.description: A grey cut stone, set into jewellery, a [weapon](#weapon) or an ornament, or [lying](#lying) loose. Only the stone's colour matters here.

entries.name: sashimono
entries.description: A narrow [banner](#banner) mounted upright on the [back](#back) of a soldier's armour in feudal Japan, [carrying](#carrying) his lord's or unit's [crest](#crest). Ranks of them mark out an [army](#army) on the [march](#march).

entries.name: statuette
entries.description: A small sculpted [figure](#figure) meant to stand on a [shelf](#shelf) or [table](#table), in bronze, [porcelain](#porcelain) or plaster. Bigger than a trinket, far short of a monument.

entries.name: bisexual_flag
entries.description: The bisexual pride [flag](#flag): a magenta band above a purple one with a narrower blue stripe between them. It covers the flag itself and pictures clearly built from its colours.

entries.name: english_flag
entries.description: St George's Cross, a red [cross](#cross) on a white [field](#field), flown for England. Laid over the Scottish and Irish crosses it makes the Union Jack, which is a separate [flag](#flag).

entries.name: fai_chun
entries.description: Red [paper](#paper) squares or strips inked with lucky phrases, pasted around doors and walls for the lunar new year. The character for fortune is often hung deliberately upside down.

entries.name: amber_(gemstone)
entries.description: Fossilised [tree](#tree) resin, warm orange and [translucent](#translucent), treated as a [gem](#gem) in jewellery and ornaments. Pictures often play on its [habit](#habit) of preserving insects and leaves [caught](#caught) while it was still flowing.

entries.name: multicolored_gemstone
entries.description: A cut stone showing several colours at once, from a naturally two-toned [crystal](#crystal) to a shifting play of light through the facets. Common on magical props and jewellery.

entries.name: shimekazari
entries.description: The Japanese New Year [door](#door) ornament of twisted rice-straw [rope](#rope) dressed with [fern](#fern) leaves, [paper](#paper) strips and a bitter orange, hung above an [entrance](#entrance) to keep bad luck out.

entries.name: brown_gemstone
entries.description: A brown [gem](#gem), cut or rough, set into something or shown loose. Amber and smoky quartz shades are the usual look.

entries.name: simple_background
entries.description: The subject sits on a [plain](#plain), featureless [backdrop](#backdrop): a flat color, a gradient, or full transparency. The test is whether the [figure](#figure) could be lifted out and dropped onto a different background with [no](#no) trouble.

entries.name: white_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is entirely or mostly white, often making it a [simple_background](#simple_background) as [well](#well); it [can](#can) also describe a white-to-color gradient. Check the original [file](#file), since a [transparent](#transparent) background previews as white.

entries.name: grey_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is solid or predominantly grey, with nothing drawn behind the subject. It applies as [well](#well) when grey is one of the colours in a [gradient_background](#gradient_background).

entries.name: gradient_background
entries.description: The background blends smoothly from one colour or [shade](#shade) into another instead of [sitting](#sitting) flat. Add the colour background tags for the colours involved, such as [blue_background](#blue_background).

entries.name: blue_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) that is solid or predominantly blue, taking in ultramarine, navy and [sky](#sky) blue. Aquamarine and turquoise go to [aqua_background](#aqua_background), and a blue gradient also takes [gradient_background](#gradient_background).

entries.name: transparent_background
entries.description: The image [file](#file) carries an alpha channel with [no](#no) [backdrop](#backdrop) behind the subject, letting whatever it is placed over show through. Thumbnails and sample images typically fill that [space](#space) with white, so check the original file before tagging; [simple_background](#simple_background) [can](#can) accompany it.

entries.name: pink_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) that is solid or mostly pink, including a pink gradient or a pink [field](#field) beside another colour. Add [simple_background](#simple_background) or [gradient_background](#gradient_background) to say how it is drawn.

entries.name: black_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) behind the subject is solid or largely black, with [no](#no) [scenery](#scenery) drawn in. It also covers a gradient background where black is one of the colours; a [dark](#dark) but detailed room is not this.

entries.name: yellow_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is solid or mostly yellow. Also applies when yellow is one colour of a [gradient_background](#gradient_background); combine with [simple_background](#simple_background) where nothing else is drawn.

entries.name: red_background
entries.description: A solid or mostly red [backdrop](#backdrop) behind the subject. Also covers a [gradient_background](#gradient_background) where red is one of the colors present.

entries.name: scenery
entries.description: A picture whose main subject is the [landscape](#landscape), [cityscape](#cityscape), [architecture](#architecture) or [interior](#interior) rather than any characters in it. Often paired with [no_humans](#no_humans), [wide_shot](#wide_shot), landscape or cityscape.

entries.name: purple_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is solid or mostly purple or lavender. Also applies to a [gradient_background](#gradient_background) where purple is one of the colours; combine with [simple_background](#simple_background) when nothing else is drawn.

entries.name: two-tone_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) made of exactly two colours, [split](#split) cleanly or blended by a gradient. A solid backdrop with a third colour added counts as multicoloured instead.

entries.name: green_background
entries.description: A background solid or mostly green, in any [shade](#shade) from pale to [dark](#dark). It applies as [well](#well) when green is one of the colours in a [gradient_background](#gradient_background).

entries.name: brown_background
entries.description: The background is solid brown or predominantly so, including a gradient [running](#running) from brown into another colour. Add [simple_background](#simple_background) where it is flat and [plain](#plain).

entries.name: orange_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is solid orange or close to it. A [gradient_background](#gradient_background) counts where orange is one of the dominant colours in it.

entries.name: floral_background
entries.description: Flowers fill the background, either as a decorative pattern or as real blooms behind the subject. A catch-all for flowered backdrops.

entries.name: polka_dot_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is filled entirely or mostly with polka [dots](#dots). The pattern belongs to the background, not to any clothing in the picture.

entries.name: multicolored_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) made of several colours at once, whether flat blocks, sweeps of gradient or a colourful pattern. Nothing about the subject follows from it.

entries.name: striped_background
