entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) made entirely or mostly of stripes, whether horizontal, vertical or diagonal bands of colour. Tag with the colour of the stripes where useful.

entries.name: dark_background
entries.description: The [space](#space) behind the subject is filled with [dark](#dark) tones, rarely a flat pure black unless the [figure](#figure) is dimly lit as [well](#well). A statement about the [backdrop](#backdrop), not about how the scene is lit.

entries.name: aqua_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is solidly or mostly aqua, cyan or turquoise. Both darker navy shades and pale [sky](#sky) tones go to [blue_background](#blue_background), and it combines happily with [gradient_background](#gradient_background).

entries.name: checkered_background
entries.description: The background is a chequerboard of two evenly alternating colours, black and white most often. A [plain](#plain) background ruled into squares by lines is [grid_background](#grid_background).

entries.name: grid_background
entries.description: A background of thin parallel and perpendicular lines forming a [square](#square) [grid](#grid) over a single colour; a rotated grid still counts. Not a [checkered_background](#checkered_background), where the squares alternate two colours, nor a [border](#border) [running](#running) along the edges of the image.

entries.name: photo_background
entries.description: A drawn character placed over a real photograph [serving](#serving) as the [backdrop](#backdrop). It [no](#no) longer applies once the photo has been repainted or filtered until it blends with the drawing, and a photo used only to pose the character is [photo-referenced](#photo-referenced).

entries.name: star_symbol_background
entries.description: A background filled with drawn star symbols rather than real stars. A [night](#night) [sky](#sky) full of stars is [starry_sky](#starry_sky) or starry_background.

entries.name: abstract_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is made of unusual colours, [shapes](#shapes) or patterns instead of any place. The [figure](#figure) in front of it is drawn normally; only the ground behind is [abstract](#abstract).

entries.name: heart_background
entries.description: Hearts fill or decorate the [space](#space) behind the subject, whether one large shape or a scatter of small ones.

entries.name: argyle_background
entries.description: The [space](#space) behind the subject is filled with a [lattice](#lattice) of diamonds in the argyle manner. Add the [tag](#tag) for the dominant background colour alongside it.

entries.name: sparkle_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) made entirely of sparkles, either a few large ones or a [field](#field) of glittering glints. When the sparkles cluster around a single character or object instead of filling the whole background, use [sparkling_aura](#sparkling_aura).

entries.name: patterned_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is filled with a repeating motif, whether [dots](#dots), checks, stripes, flowers or an [abstract](#abstract) tile. Where the pattern has a [tag](#tag) of its own, such as [polka_dot_background](#polka_dot_background), add that too.

entries.name: plaid_background
entries.description: The background is filled entirely or mostly with a plaid or tartan pattern of crossing bands. The check belongs to the [backdrop](#backdrop), not to any clothing in the picture.

entries.name: 3d_background
entries.description: Hand-drawn characters sit in front of a [backdrop](#backdrop) built and rendered in three dimensions. The mismatch between the flat figures and the modelled [scenery](#scenery) is usually visible; [mixed_media](#mixed_media) covers other such combinations.

entries.name: sunburst_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) of rays [fanning](#fanning) out from the centre, typically in red and yellow so it resembles the North Macedonian [flag](#flag). Popular in meme-style images. Implies [sunburst](#sunburst).

entries.name: in-universe_location
entries.description: The setting is a place recognisable from a particular fictional work, such as a named [dungeon](#dungeon) or a school's council room, rather than a generic [backdrop](#backdrop). Being identifiable is what earns the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: faux_figurine
entries.description: The character stands on a small [patch](#patch) of [scenery](#scenery) like a figurine's base, with nothing else drawn behind. Ground that fades out rather than ending cleanly is [fading_border](#fading_border), and a large detailed base with walls or several figures is a [diorama](#diorama).

entries.name: paw_print_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is [patterned](#patterned) with repeated paw prints, common behind [cat](#cat) girls and [dog](#dog) girls. Add [patterned_background](#patterned_background) alongside it.

entries.name: monochrome_background
entries.description: A coloured subject [standing](#standing) against a background rendered in one colour or in greys, usually to push the [figure](#figure) forward. The [backdrop](#backdrop) may be blurred, sketchy or left half-finished, and this is not the same as a [plain](#plain) simple background.

entries.name: loaded_interior
entries.description: A room packed with so much stuff that the clutter itself is the subject, shelves, boxes, cables and knick-knacks filling every [corner](#corner). Keep it for interiors whose density rewards a long look.

entries.name: snowflake_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) built from stylized [snowflakes](#snowflakes), whether one large motif or a repeating pattern, [sitting](#sitting) as a flat design element behind the subject. Actual [falling](#falling) [snow](#snow) belongs under [snowing](#snowing) instead.

entries.name: starry_sky_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is a [field](#field) of actual stars in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky). Where the stars are decorative [shapes](#shapes) rather than a sky, [star_symbol_background](#star_symbol_background) applies instead.

entries.name: dotted_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) [patterned](#patterned) with circles of uneven size and irregular spacing. Where the [dots](#dots) are matched in size and evenly placed, [polka_dot](#polka_dot) applies instead.

entries.name: flag_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) carries a flag's colours or design, or an actual [flag](#flag) fills most of it. A [plain](#plain) single-colour ground does not count, even where some flag happens to use that colour.

entries.name: invisible_floor
entries.description: Figures stand or walk on nothing, their footing and shadows implying a surface that was never drawn. It is common where the background has been stripped away entirely.

entries.name: honeycomb_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is filled with hexagons packed together like a beehive. It works as flat graphic backing behind a [figure](#figure) rather than as a real place.

entries.name: game_screenshot_background
entries.description: A still lifted from a [video](#video) game and used as the [backdrop](#backdrop), with new artwork painted on top of it. If nothing has been drawn over the still, the picture is just a screenshot.

entries.name: leaf_background
entries.description: Foliage fills the [space](#space) behind the subject, either as a flat decorative spread of leaves or as a mass of greenery [standing](#standing) in for [scenery](#scenery). Use it when the leaves are the [backdrop](#backdrop) rather than something a character handles.

entries.name: rainbow_background
entries.description: The area behind the subject is filled with a [rainbow](#rainbow) gradient or banded spectrum of color. Decorative rather than a depicted place, so the [figure](#figure) reads as [standing](#standing) against pure color.

entries.name: bubble_background
entries.description: Floating bubbles or [plain](#plain) circles fill the [space](#space) behind the subject as decoration. They stand in for a setting rather than belonging to one.

entries.name: lace_background
entries.description: Lace patterning fills the [space](#space) behind the subject as decoration. It differs from a [lace](#lace) frame set around the picture's edge, and from a [doily](#doily) drawn as an object in the scene.

entries.name: fiery_background
entries.description: The [space](#space) behind the subject is filled with flame, from a blaze to an [abstract](#abstract) wash of [fire](#fire). The fire fills the [backdrop](#backdrop) rather than [burning](#burning) any object in the scene.

entries.name: food-themed_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) itself is made of [food](#food): repeating edible motifs, [dishes](#dishes) tumbling through the air, or a single [giant](#giant) item filling the [space](#space) behind the subject. It is [scenery](#scenery), not a [meal](#meal) anyone is [eating](#eating).

entries.name: splatter_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) itself is made of splashed and spattered marks, whether [ink](#ink), [paint](#paint) or [blood](#blood), rather than any depicted place. Used to suggest [violence](#violence), [energy](#energy) or artistic flourish.

entries.name: rose_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) filled with roses rather than a real setting, used to frame the subject decoratively. It reads as a flat pattern or wash of blooms, not a [garden](#garden) the character stands in.

entries.name: step_and_repeat
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) tiled edge to edge with the same [logo](#logo) or wordmark, the kind [people](#people) pose against at premieres and press calls. The regular [grid](#grid) of repeated marks behind the subject gives it away.

entries.name: paper_background
entries.description: The picture sits on a [plain](#plain) sheet of [paper](#paper): [notebook](#notebook) rules, [graph](#graph) squares, a [torn](#torn) edge, or the grain of drawing stock [standing](#standing) in for a setting.

entries.name: watercolor_background
entries.description: The [space](#space) behind the subject is washed in loose, [bleeding](#bleeding) colour the way [paint](#paint) spreads on [wet](#wet) [paper](#paper). Edges blot and run instead of [sitting](#sitting) flat.

entries.name: fruit_background
entries.description: Fruit filling the [space](#space) behind the subject, whether as a repeating pattern or a heaped mass of produce. Decoration laid behind the [figure](#figure), not part of a real scene.

entries.name: triangle_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) built from triangles, either one large shape framing the subject or a scattered geometric pattern behind them. Purely decorative, with [no](#no) depicted place behind the [figure](#figure).

entries.name: mosaic_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) tiled with [shapes](#shapes) that do not fall into a regular repeat. Keep it apart from checkered and argyle backgrounds, whose patterns are strictly ordered.

entries.name: rabbit_background
entries.description: The area behind the subject is filled with rabbits or [rabbit](#rabbit) motifs, whether repeated silhouettes, a pattern, or a scattered decorative [field](#field). The rabbits sit behind the [figure](#figure) rather than [sharing](#sharing) the same scene with it.

entries.name: silver_background
entries.description: A flat metallic-grey [backdrop](#backdrop) behind the subject. Recorded as [grey_background](#grey_background) or [white_background](#white_background) instead, since the tone is treated as a [shade](#shade) of one of those colors rather than a background of its own.

entries.name: fake_transparency
entries.description: A grey and white checkerboard is painted into the picture to imitate an empty background, copying the way editing software shows one. The [file](#file) itself is fully opaque.

entries.name: paneled_background
entries.description: The [space](#space) behind the subject is styled as a [grid](#grid) of [comic](#comic) panels instead of a real setting. A graphic [backdrop](#backdrop), not an actual comic page.

entries.name: spiral_background
entries.description: The [space](#space) behind the subject is filled by a [spiral](#spiral) winding outward from its centre, used to suggest dizziness, [hypnosis](#hypnosis) or heightened drama rather than any real location.

entries.name: cloud_background
entries.description: Nothing but [cloud](#cloud) stands behind the subject, with [no](#no) [horizon](#horizon) or [landscape](#landscape) to place the scene. It ranges from a flatly painted [sky](#sky) to stylised decorative puffs.

entries.name: animal_background
entries.description: Creatures fill the [space](#space) behind the subject, massed or repeated as a pattern rather than acting as characters. They are there to be the [backdrop](#backdrop) and nothing else.

entries.name: diagonal_striped_background
entries.description: The [space](#space) behind the subject is filled with slanting bands of colour. A flat graphic [backdrop](#backdrop) rather than any real place.

entries.name: lightning_background
entries.description: Jagged bolts fill the [space](#space) behind the subject as a graphic [backdrop](#backdrop), [standing](#standing) in for shock or sudden realisation rather than for real weather.

entries.name: green_screen
entries.description: A flat green [backdrop](#backdrop) of the kind used for chroma keying, so the colour [can](#can) be cut away and replaced with another scene. It appears left unreplaced or as a joke about compositing, and other flat colours serve the same purpose.

entries.name: backdrop
entries.description: A painted [cloth](#cloth) or canvas hung behind a [stage](#stage) or a photographic set to supply the [scenery](#scenery). It may also be left [plain](#plain), a flat [field](#field) of colour [standing](#standing) behind a [portrait](#portrait) or a broadcast.

entries.name: strawberry_background
entries.description: A [backdrop](#backdrop) made of strawberries, either one large [fruit](#fruit) filling the [space](#space) or a repeating pattern of them behind the subject.

entries.name: butterfly_background
entries.description: Butterflies fill the [space](#space) behind the subject as decoration rather than as insects that belong to a real scene.

entries.name: spider_web_background
entries.description: Cobwebs filling the [space](#space) behind the subject as a flat decorative [field](#field) rather than a real room. A common [choice](#choice) for Halloween and gothic artwork.

entries.name: dithered_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is filled with a pattern of [dots](#dots) that fakes gradients out of only a [couple](#couple) of colours, the way [old](#old) displays did. Printed [halftone](#halftone) [screentones](#screentones) are a separate effect.

entries.name: collage_background
entries.description: The [backdrop](#backdrop) is assembled from many separate pictures butted together into one surface. A comic-style backdrop that keeps its panels in [reading](#reading) order is something else.

entries.name: indoors
entries.description: The scene, or most of it, sits inside a [house](#house) or another enclosed [building](#building). It is the counterpart of [outdoors](#outdoors), and the particular room such as [bedroom](#bedroom) or [classroom](#classroom) goes alongside it.

entries.name: bedroom
entries.description: The scene is set in a bedroom, with enough of the room in view to say something about whoever lives there, such as furniture, posters or a [window](#window). A bare [bed](#bed) among nondescript objects does not earn the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: bathroom
entries.description: A room in a [house](#house) or flat with a [toilet](#toilet) and washbasin, and usually a tub or shower as [well](#well), [serving](#serving) as the setting. A public washroom is [restroom](#restroom) instead.

entries.name: kitchen
entries.description: The scene is set in a kitchen, with a [stove](#stove), a [sink](#sink), counters and [cooking](#cooking) equipment. Add cooking when somebody is actually preparing [food](#food).

entries.name: hallway
entries.description: The scene is set in a corridor connecting other rooms, such as a [school](#school) or [apartment](#apartment) hallway.

entries.name: shower_(place)
entries.description: The shower room or stall itself as a setting. The act of [washing](#washing) under it is [showering](#showering) instead.

entries.name: messy_room
entries.description: An [interior](#interior) cluttered with scattered belongings, [trash](#trash) or piled-up [clothes](#clothes). For a person themselves covered in something, use [messy](#messy) instead.

entries.name: living_room
entries.description: The room of a [house](#house) or flat given over to [relaxing](#relaxing) and entertaining, usually furnished with a sofa, low [table](#table) and [television](#television). Tag the room itself rather than whatever happens to be going on in it.

entries.name: otaku_room
entries.description: A room [crowded](#crowded) with hobby goods: figures, posters, manga volumes, body pillows, consoles and [computer](#computer) gear. Usually drawn [cramped](#cramped) and [messy](#messy), with shelves pressing in on the walls.

entries.name: garage
entries.description: A bay or [building](#building) for keeping and [working](#working) on cars and motorcycles, whether attached to a [house](#house) or part of a repair [shop](#shop). Tools, a workbench and a raised roller [door](#door) are the usual markers.

entries.name: storage_room
entries.description: A spare room given over to keeping things until they are needed again, stacked with boxes, shelving and sheeted furniture. Cramped and cluttered by [nature](#nature).

entries.name: dining_room
entries.description: The room of a home given over to [eating](#eating), built around a [table](#table) and chairs. Kept separate from the [kitchen](#kitchen) where the [cooking](#cooking) happens.

entries.name: bedside
entries.description: The narrow [space](#space) beside a [bed](#bed), with somebody [standing](#standing), [kneeling](#kneeling) or [sitting](#sitting) there next to a person [lying](#lying) down. Sickroom, waking-up and watching-over scenes use it.

entries.name: conservatory
entries.description: A room or small [building](#building) framed largely in [glass](#glass) and furnished for [sitting](#sitting) in, often attached to a [house](#house). A [structure](#structure) built for raising plants is a [greenhouse](#greenhouse).

entries.name: under_bed
entries.description: The [space](#space) beneath a [bed](#bed), with someone or something down in it. Used for [hiding](#hiding), for monsters lurking, or for whatever has rolled out of reach.

entries.name: classroom
entries.description: A [school](#school) classroom seen from inside, with rows of desks, a [chalkboard](#chalkboard) and [tall](#tall) windows. The usual setting for school uniform pictures; the [building](#building) from outside is school.

entries.name: school
entries.description: A school setting in general: the [building](#building), grounds or rooms where students are taught. Prefer a specific place such as [classroom](#classroom), [hallway](#hallway), school [rooftop](#rooftop) or [clubroom](#clubroom) when one is identifiable.

entries.name: library
entries.description: A room or [building](#building) lined with shelved books, anywhere from a single study to a whole hall. Tall shelves, [reading](#reading) tables and lamps are the usual furnishings.

entries.name: office
entries.description: A workplace [interior](#interior) of desks, chairs, computers and filing cabinets where business or clerical work is done. Usually goes with [office_lady](#office_lady), [office_chair](#office_chair) and businesslike clothing.

entries.name: gym_storeroom
entries.description: The storage room beside a [school](#school) [gym](#gym), stacked with mats, vaulting boxes and balls. A secluded spot that doubles as a setting for sexual scenes in school stories.

entries.name: infirmary
entries.description: A [school](#school) nurse's room or a small sickbay, typically with a curtained [bed](#bed), a [desk](#desk) and a [cabinet](#cabinet) of supplies. It turns up constantly in school scenes.

entries.name: laboratory
entries.description: A room fitted out for scientific work, with benches, glassware, instruments and racks of equipment. The fittings shift with the [field](#field), from a [chemistry](#chemistry) [bench](#bench) to a sterile research bay.

entries.name: kindergarten
entries.description: A Japanese preschool for children of roughly three to six, with low tables, brightly decorated rooms and a play yard outside. Both the [building](#building) and its classrooms count.

entries.name: studio
entries.description: A [working](#working) room fitted out for making something, [recording](#recording), photography, broadcasting or painting, complete with the matching equipment and lighting rigs.

entries.name: clubroom
entries.description: The room a [school](#school) club keeps for itself, generally [crowded](#crowded) with the gear of its activity, spare desks and a [kettle](#kettle). A standard setting for after-school scenes.

entries.name: recording_studio
entries.description: A soundproofed room with microphones, [headphones](#headphones), and a glazed control [window](#window) where [music](#music) or voice work is recorded. Frequently the setting for [idol](#idol), voice-actor, and band artwork.

entries.name: cubicle
entries.description: A [desk](#desk) walled in by shoulder-high partitions inside an open-plan [office](#office). Sets a scene of routine office work and the isolation that comes with it.

entries.name: cafeteria
entries.description: A large institutional dining hall with a [serving](#serving) [counter](#counter) along one side and rows of shared tables filling the rest. Trays, set meals and a noisy [crowd](#crowd) complete it.

entries.name: dojo
entries.description: A martial arts [training](#training) hall with a wooden [floor](#floor), [sliding](#sliding) panels along the walls, racked weapons and a [shrine](#shrine) alcove. The setting for practice and sparring.

entries.name: workshop
entries.description: A room dedicated to making things, with [tools](#tools), materials, and half-finished projects visible around it. Sewing, painting, carpentry, and [alchemy](#alchemy) [can](#can) all take place there.

entries.name: radio_booth
entries.description: A soundproofed room fitted with a [microphone](#microphone) and [mixing](#mixing) [desk](#desk) where characters [record](#record) or broadcast. Art set here often ties to a series' companion drama CD or [radio](#radio) show.

entries.name: shop
entries.description: A store or a department within one, selling a particular type of goods, shown from inside or from the [street](#street). Specific kinds include [convenience_store](#convenience_store), [bakery](#bakery) and [flower_shop](#flower_shop).

entries.name: bar_(place)
entries.description: A [drinking](#drinking) place as the setting, with its [counter](#counter), shelves of bottles, stools and low light. Add [bartender](#bartender) for the person [pouring](#pouring) and [beer](#beer) or [cocktail](#cocktail) for what is served.

entries.name: locker_room
entries.description: A changing room lined with lockers and benches, at a [school](#school), [gym](#gym) or [swimming](#swimming) [pool](#pool). It frequently overlaps with [changing_room](#changing_room) and with scenes of [dressing](#dressing) and [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: restaurant
entries.description: A dining establishment where meals are ordered from a [menu](#menu) and served at a [table](#table), from a [diner](#diner) to a fancy [dinner](#dinner) spot. The scene shows tables, [staff](#staff), or the dining room; a [cafe](#cafe) or bar carries its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: stripper_pole
entries.description: A vertical metal [pole](#pole) of the kind fitted for pole [dancing](#dancing) in strip clubs. Tag it whenever one appears in the scene, whether or not anyone is using it. Implies pole.

entries.name: cafe
entries.description: A [casual](#casual) [coffee](#coffee) [house](#house) [serving](#serving) [hot](#hot) drinks, pastries and light meals, shown as the setting with its [counter](#counter), small tables and fittings. A frequent [backdrop](#backdrop) for meetings and dates.

entries.name: gym
entries.description: A gymnasium or fitness gym, whether a [school](#school) sports hall or a [training](#training) room with [weights](#weights). The equipment storage room next to it is [gym_storeroom](#gym_storeroom).

entries.name: convenience_store
entries.description: The small round-the-clock [shop](#shop), or konbini, with shelves of packaged [food](#food), chilled cabinets and a service [counter](#counter) under flat bright light. Its lit shopfront seen from the [street](#street) at [night](#night) counts too.

entries.name: boxing_ring
entries.description: The raised [square](#square) [platform](#platform) [boxing](#boxing) takes place on, with a post at each [corner](#corner) and four ropes [running](#running) between them. A [wrestling](#wrestling) [ring](#ring) looks much the same but fastens its ropes differently.

entries.name: casino
entries.description: A [gambling](#gambling) hall with [card](#card) tables, [roulette](#roulette) wheels or ranks of slot machines and dealers in uniform. It serves as a glamorous or a seedy [backdrop](#backdrop), often for bunny-suited [staff](#staff).

entries.name: fitting_room
entries.description: The narrow [cubicle](#cubicle) in a [clothes](#clothes) [shop](#shop) for trying garments on, with a [mirror](#mirror), a [hook](#hook) for hangers and a curtain or a [door](#door). A common setting for changing and comparing outfits.

entries.name: movie_theater
entries.description: A cinema auditorium or its foyer: raked rows of folding seats facing a [screen](#screen), aisle lighting, a [ticket](#ticket) [window](#window) or a [popcorn](#popcorn) [counter](#counter). It applies whether or not a film is [playing](#playing).

entries.name: arcade
entries.description: A hall of coin-fed game machines, cabinets in rows under dim light and bright signage. A single [machine](#machine) on its own is [arcade_cabinet](#arcade_cabinet), and a run of [building](#building) arches is [arcade_(architecture)](#arcade_(architecture)).

entries.name: changing_room
entries.description: The anteroom of a [bathhouse](#bathhouse) or [hot](#hot) spring where visitors take their [clothes](#clothes) off before going through, fitted with woven baskets or lockers. A shop's fitting room is a different place entirely.

entries.name: hotel_room
entries.description: The inside of a rented room, given away by impersonal furnishing: paired beds with a [nightstand](#nightstand) and lamps between them, sometimes a small [desk](#desk). The [building](#building) itself is [hotel](#hotel).

entries.name: bakery
entries.description: A [shop](#shop) where [bread](#bread), cakes and pastries are baked on the premises and sold from the trays. Ovens, cooling racks, [glass](#glass) cases and small handwritten [price](#price) cards fill out the scene.

entries.name: market
entries.description: A place of trade where sellers set goods out on stands and customers pick through them before paying. Covers both a covered hall and an open row of stalls.

entries.name: supermarket
entries.description: A large grocery [shop](#shop) with aisles of shelving, refrigerated cases, trolleys and checkout counters, a bigger and more anonymous [space](#space) than a [corner](#corner) shop or convenience store.

entries.name: love_hotel
entries.description: A [hotel](#hotel) let by the hour for sexual encounters, told by a gaudy facade and a [sign](#sign) quoting short-stay rates. Use it where the [building](#building) or its signage is in frame; the room itself takes [hotel_room](#hotel_room).

entries.name: laundromat
entries.description: A public [shop](#shop) lined with coin-operated washers and dryers. The row of round [machine](#machine) doors and a [waiting](#waiting) [bench](#bench) along the wall identify it.

entries.name: tavern
entries.description: A [drinking](#drinking) [house](#house) of wooden tables, a bar [counter](#counter), stacked barrels and [lantern](#lantern) light. A fixture of [fantasy](#fantasy) settings, where adventuring parties commonly gather.

entries.name: maid_cafe
entries.description: An [eating](#eating) place where the [staff](#staff) wait on customers in frilled [maid](#maid) [dress](#dress), with the shop's tables, [counter](#counter) and patrons around them. The venue is the point, not one server in [costume](#costume).

entries.name: basketball_court
entries.description: The marked [rectangle](#rectangle) [basketball](#basketball) is played on, with a [hoop](#hoop) [standing](#standing) at each end. Indoor floors are polished maple; outdoor ones are asphalt behind [wire](#wire) fencing.

entries.name: izakaya
entries.description: A Japanese [drinking](#drinking) [house](#house) [serving](#serving) small plates alongside [beer](#beer) and [sake](#sake), patrons packed elbow to elbow along the [counter](#counter). Hand-written wooden [menu](#menu) strips on the wall are the giveaway.

entries.name: display
entries.description: Goods laid out for customers to look over: a [shop](#shop) [window](#window), a rack of [clothes](#clothes), a case of pastries. Computer screens are [monitor](#monitor) or [screen](#screen) rather than this.

entries.name: theater
entries.description: A hall built to seat an [audience](#audience) facing a [stage](#stage) or [screen](#screen), with banked seating, a proscenium and [heavy](#heavy) [curtains](#curtains). Playhouses, cinemas and [concert](#concert) halls all fall under it.

entries.name: diner
entries.description: A [casual](#casual) American [eating](#eating) place with a [counter](#counter) and stools, booths along the windows and a short-order [kitchen](#kitchen) behind. Chrome trim, neon signage and a chequered [floor](#floor) are the usual cues.

entries.name: ryokan
entries.description: A traditional Japanese inn, with [tatami](#tatami) rooms, [sliding](#sliding) [paper](#paper) doors, futons laid out at [night](#night) and often a [hot](#hot) spring [bath](#bath). It supplies the setting for trip and holiday scenes.

entries.name: nightclub
entries.description: A late-hours venue with a dance [floor](#floor), coloured lights and a bar, sometimes with a [stage](#stage) or poles. Loud [music](#music), drinks and a packed room fill the scene.

entries.name: circus
entries.description: The travelling show of acrobats, clowns, ringmasters and [animal](#animal) acts, performing in a [ring](#ring) under a big striped [tent](#tent). It covers both the venue and the whole visual theme.

entries.name: mall
entries.description: A large enclosed [shopping](#shopping) centre, its shops [opening](#opening) onto wide indoor walkways and usually anchored by a department store. Escalators, atriums and railed upper floors are the usual furniture.

entries.name: in_crane_game
entries.description: A character inside the [glass](#glass) [cabinet](#cabinet) of a claw [machine](#machine), [sitting](#sitting) among the prizes as if they were one. The claw [hanging](#hanging) overhead finishes the joke.

entries.name: flower_shop
entries.description: A [shop](#shop) trading in cut flowers and plants, its buckets, shelves and [window](#window) [crowded](#crowded) with blooms. The [tag](#tag) names the premises, not whoever works there.

entries.name: bookstore
entries.description: A [shop](#shop) whose shelves and tables are stocked with books for [sale](#sale). It marks the commercial setting, not a home [library](#library) or a [school](#school) [reading](#reading) room.

entries.name: ferris_wheel_interior
entries.description: The scene takes place inside a ferris [wheel](#wheel) [cabin](#cabin): [bench](#bench) seats, [glass](#glass) on every side and the fairground far below. A favourite spot for a quiet conversation between two [people](#people).

entries.name: theater_seating
entries.description: Rows of tip-up seats banked in front of a [stage](#stage) or [screen](#screen), whether empty or filled with an [audience](#audience). It names the furniture rather than the [building](#building) around it.

entries.name: karaoke_box
entries.description: A small room rented by the hour for [singing](#singing), fitted with a [screen](#screen), microphones and a song console. Padded benches around a low [table](#table) under dim coloured light are the usual furnishing.

entries.name: clothes_shop
entries.description: The inside or the [storefront](#storefront) of a [shop](#shop) selling garments, with racks, mannequins and fitting rooms. The setting for [shopping](#shopping) and trying-on scenes.

entries.name: conveyor_belt_sushi
entries.description: A [sushi](#sushi) [restaurant](#restaurant) where plates [circle](#circle) the room on a moving [belt](#belt) and diners lift off whatever they fancy. The belt winding past every seat is what identifies it.

entries.name: dance_studio
entries.description: A practice room with a mirrored wall, a [barre](#barre) [running](#running) along it and a bare sprung [floor](#floor). The setting for rehearsal, warm-ups and [training](#training) scenes.

entries.name: shooting_gallery
entries.description: A fairground stall where players [fire](#fire) [cork](#cork) or pellet guns at prizes lined up on a [shelf](#shelf). A facility built for real firearms is [shooting_range](#shooting_range) instead.

entries.name: skating_rink
entries.description: A sheet of [ice](#ice) laid out for [skating](#skating), whether a [frozen](#frozen) [pond](#pond) or a built rink with barriers around it. Winter sports and holiday-date scenes are its usual company.

entries.name: shooting_range
entries.description: A lane-divided facility for practicing with real firearms, [indoors](#indoors) or out, fitted with [paper](#paper) targets and ear protection. Not the prize booth at a [festival](#festival), which is [shooting_gallery](#shooting_gallery) instead.

entries.name: bowling_alley
entries.description: The venue built for [bowling](#bowling): a row of slick lanes with automatic pinsetters at the far end. Ball returns sit beside the approach and scoreboards hang overhead.

entries.name: onsen
entries.description: A Japanese [hot](#hot) spring [bath](#bath). The rock-lined open-air [pool](#pool) is the usual sight, though indoor ones exist; expect [steam](#steam), small towels and a [bamboo](#bamboo) [screen](#screen), with men and women generally kept apart.

entries.name: train_interior
entries.description: A scene set inside a rail [carriage](#carriage), with seating, [hanging](#hanging) straps and windows visible. Do not add [train](#train) unless the outside of the vehicle is also shown.

entries.name: interior
entries.description: The inside of an enclosed [space](#space), whether a room or the [cabin](#cabin) of a [car](#car), [ship](#ship), [aircraft](#aircraft) or [train](#train). Use it where being [indoors](#indoors) matters and [no](#no) more specific room [tag](#tag) applies.

entries.name: stage
entries.description: A raised [platform](#platform) where performers sing, act, dance or speak before an [audience](#audience), whether inside a hall or club or [outdoors](#outdoors) at a [festival](#festival).

entries.name: wrestling_ring
entries.description: A raised, canvas-covered [square](#square) [platform](#platform) bounded by ropes on each side, where a [wrestling](#wrestling) match takes place. A [boxing_ring](#boxing_ring) usually carries an extra [rope](#rope); add wrestling when a match is underway.

entries.name: dungeon
entries.description: An [underground](#underground) cell or vault of stone walls and torchlight, built for prisoners and equally at home as [fantasy](#fantasy) crawl or [bondage](#bondage) room. Chains, cages and instruments of restraint are the usual fittings.

entries.name: prison
entries.description: The picture is set in a jail: barred blocks, guarded corridors, or an exercise yard behind walls. For a single locked room rather than the wider institution, [prison_cell](#prison_cell) is the closer [tag](#tag).

entries.name: aquarium
entries.description: A public aquarium with large tanks of sea life, characters often silhouetted against a [glowing](#glowing) wall of [glass](#glass). A small [tank](#tank) of [pet](#pet) [fish](#fish) at home is [fish_tank](#fish_tank).

entries.name: toilet_stall
entries.description: A partitioned [cubicle](#cubicle) around a [toilet](#toilet) in a public [restroom](#restroom), with a [door](#door) and often gaps beneath the walls. Add [bathroom](#bathroom).

entries.name: restroom
entries.description: A public lavatory with a row of cubicles, shared sinks, and mirrors, as found in schools, stations, and offices. A single [toilet](#toilet) in a home belongs under [bathroom](#bathroom) instead.

entries.name: sauna
entries.description: A small heated room, wooden-walled in most depictions, where [people](#people) sit or recline in high heat to [sweat](#sweat) and relax. Characters are usually wrapped in towels; add [steam](#steam) and sweat where drawn.

entries.name: hospital
entries.description: The scene is set in a hospital: a ward, a corridor, an examination room or an operating theatre. Beds, drip stands, doctors and nurses usually come with it.

entries.name: bathhouse
entries.description: A public [bathing](#bathing) hall with shared tubs, tiled floors and rows of [washing](#washing) places along the walls. The Japanese kind is called a sento.

entries.name: prison_cell
entries.description: The small barred room where an inmate is held, whether in a jail or a [police](#police) station. Iron [bars](#bars), a bunk and bare walls are the usual furnishings. Use [prison](#prison) for the wider [building](#building).

entries.name: bus_interior
entries.description: The inside of a [bus](#bus), with its rows of seats, grab rails, windows and central aisle. The viewpoint sits within the vehicle rather than looking at it.

entries.name: arena
entries.description: A [fighting](#fighting) ground or [field](#field) ringed by banked rows of spectator seats, used for [matches](#matches), contests and shows. The tiers around the edge are what separate it from an open field.

entries.name: dressing_room
entries.description: The [backstage](#backstage) room where performers change and make up, fitted with mirrors, bright bulbs, chairs and vanity tables loaded with [cosmetics](#cosmetics). A shop's fitting room is not this.

entries.name: airplane_interior
entries.description: The inside of an aeroplane, with rows of seats, overhead lockers and small oval windows, or the [cockpit](#cockpit) up front. The [machine](#machine) seen from outside is a different matter.

entries.name: soapland
entries.description: A Japanese bathhouse-brothel where a customer bathes together with a worker and receives non-penetrative services. Scenes typically feature tiled rooms, low stools, air mattresses, and [heavy](#heavy) lather.

entries.name: museum
entries.description: Halls of exhibits behind [glass](#glass) or raised on plinths — paintings, [sculpture](#sculpture), fossils — with visitors moving between them. The gallery [space](#space) itself is the setting rather than any single exhibit.

entries.name: subway_station
entries.description: A station on an [underground](#underground) or rapid transit line, with platforms, tiled walls and track [running](#running) below [street](#street) level.

entries.name: courtroom
entries.description: The chamber where a [judge](#judge) hears a case, with its [bench](#bench), witness stand, rails and gallery seating. Trial and testimony scenes are set here.

entries.name: ashiyu
entries.description: A shallow public [bath](#bath) meant for the [feet](#feet), with [people](#people) [sitting](#sitting) along the rim and their [legs](#legs) in the [hot](#hot) [water](#water). The word also covers the small foot-soaking tub used at home.

entries.name: throne_room
entries.description: The great hall of a [palace](#palace) built around a ruler's seat, with a raised dais, a long approach, banners and [heavy](#heavy) columns. Counts whether the [throne](#throne) is occupied or [standing](#standing) empty.

entries.name: sewer
entries.description: The [underground](#underground) channels [carrying](#carrying) waste [water](#water) away: [brick](#brick) or [concrete](#concrete) tunnels, [standing](#standing) water, pipes, and iron grates overhead. A stock [backdrop](#backdrop) for chases and lurking monsters.

entries.name: ballroom
entries.description: A large hall with a polished [floor](#floor), chandeliers overhead and [space](#space) cleared for [dancing](#dancing). It is where formal balls and banquets take place.

entries.name: in_cell
entries.description: A character shut in a [prison](#prison) cell, framed by barred doors or stone walls. The confinement rather than any action is the subject.

entries.name: backstage
entries.description: The [working](#working) side of a theatre or [concert](#concert) hall: [wings](#wings), [rigging](#rigging), [dressing](#dressing) tables and performers [waiting](#waiting) on their cue. It is the part the [audience](#audience) never sees, as opposed to the [stage](#stage) itself.

entries.name: confessional
entries.description: The wooden booth in a [church](#church) where a [priest](#priest) hears [confession](#confession) through a [screen](#screen). Cramped and dim, and generally drawn as an [interior](#interior).

entries.name: planetarium
entries.description: A domed theatre where stars and planets are projected across the curved [ceiling](#ceiling) for an [audience](#audience). Also covers the small home projectors that scatter star-like light over a room.

entries.name: city
entries.description: An [urban](#urban) setting of dense buildings, streets and [traffic](#traffic), whether the characters stand in it or it rises behind them. A wide view of the built form itself also takes [cityscape](#cityscape).

entries.name: road
entries.description: A paved or improved route for foot or vehicle travel, from a [dirt](#dirt) track to a [highway](#highway). Urban paved roads with sidewalks are usually tagged [street](#street) instead; narrow passages are alleys.

entries.name: cityscape
entries.description: Scenery showing the built form of a [city](#city): skylines, rooftops, streets [running](#running) off into the distance. Use it where the [urban](#urban) view is a real part of the picture rather than a hint of buildings.

entries.name: bridge
entries.description: A [structure](#structure) [carrying](#carrying) a [road](#road), [path](#path) or railway over [water](#water), a [valley](#valley) or another road, from a small stone footbridge to a [suspension](#suspension) span across a [skyline](#skyline). Named landmark bridges have tags of their own; add [river](#river), [city](#city) or whatever surrounds it.

entries.name: street
entries.description: A paved [city](#city) [road](#road) built for cars and pedestrians alike, typically with sidewalks, crossings and [traffic](#traffic) lights. Use road for country roads and highways; every street also counts as a road.

entries.name: rooftop
entries.description: The scene takes place on top of a [building](#building), often a [school](#school) roof with a [railing](#railing) or a [city](#city) rooftop at [night](#night). Tag city or building where either is visible.

entries.name: alley
entries.description: A narrow lane [running](#running) between or behind buildings, usually just wide enough to walk. It may be paved or bare [dirt](#dirt), and one closed at the far end is a dead end.

entries.name: town
entries.description: A mid-sized settlement, larger than a [village](#village) but smaller than a [city](#city), shown as the setting or as a [backdrop](#backdrop). Add more specific tags for individual streets or buildings within it.

entries.name: train_station
entries.description: A [platform](#platform) or station [building](#building) where trains stop to load and unload passengers. Add [train](#train) when the vehicle itself is also present.

entries.name: skyline
entries.description: The [outline](#outline) of a city's buildings against the [sky](#sky) at the [horizon](#horizon). Without a [city](#city), use horizon instead.

entries.name: park
entries.description: An [urban](#urban) green [space](#space) for recreation, with lawns, trees, paths, benches and lampposts, sometimes a [playground](#playground) or a [pond](#pond). A [park_bench](#park_bench) in view is the usual giveaway.

entries.name: crosswalk
entries.description: A marked pedestrian crossing painted over a [road](#road), most often as [zebra](#zebra) stripes. Sets a [street](#street) scene, and characters are frequently drawn [walking](#walking) across it.

entries.name: real_world_location
entries.description: The scene is set at an identifiable real place, whether a famous landmark or an ordinary [street](#street), drawn accurately enough to be recognized. Photographs and photo backgrounds do not count, nor does a famous [building](#building) simply dropped into a fictional setting.

entries.name: stadium
entries.description: A large tiered venue with a [field](#field) or [stage](#stage) at its centre, ringed by seating, built for sports [matches](#matches), concerts and other big events.

entries.name: sidewalk
entries.description: A paved [walkway](#walkway) [running](#running) along the edge of a [road](#road) for pedestrians. Usually part of a [street](#street) or [city](#city) scene.

entries.name: storefront
entries.description: The front of a [shop](#shop), [cafe](#cafe) or [restaurant](#restaurant) seen from the [street](#street), with its [entrance](#entrance), signage and [display](#display) windows. Characters may be entering, leaving with purchases or being greeted at the [door](#door).

entries.name: playground
entries.description: An outdoor area laid out for children to play, with swings, a [slide](#slide), a sandpit and [climbing](#climbing) frames. Parks and [school](#school) grounds are the usual settings.

entries.name: tokyo_(city)
entries.description: A scene set recognizably in Tokyo, whether by landmarks such as Tokyo Tower, Skytree or Shibuya Crossing or by a named district.

entries.name: urban
entries.description: A large [city](#city), rather than a [village](#village) or small [town](#town), forms the subject or [backdrop](#backdrop) of the picture, with its massed buildings, streets and [skyline](#skyline).

entries.name: amusement_park
entries.description: A permanent ground of rides and attractions: a ferris [wheel](#wheel), roller [coaster](#coaster), [carousel](#carousel), [spinning](#spinning) teacups, game stalls, a haunted [house](#house). Unlike a travelling funfair or a one-day [festival](#festival) it stays put through the season.

entries.name: running_track
entries.description: The oval athletics track with its painted lane lines on a rubberised red or blue surface. It places a scene at a sports ground, [stadium](#stadium) or [school](#school) [field](#field) [day](#day).

entries.name: train_station_platform
entries.description: The raised strip beside the rails where passengers wait, marked by a painted edge line, benches, signboards and an overhead canopy. A narrower focus than the station [building](#building) as a whole.

entries.name: baseball_stadium
entries.description: A ground built for [baseball](#baseball), with tiered seating wrapped around the diamond, floodlight towers and a [scoreboard](#scoreboard). It is drawn from the stands or from out on the [grass](#grass).

entries.name: racetrack
entries.description: A purpose-built circuit for cars, motorcycles, or horses, usually ringed by grandstands and barriers. Motorsport circuits are paved while horse-racing courses are laid with [dirt](#dirt).

entries.name: traffic
entries.description: The picture is centred on [road](#road) traffic itself, a [stream](#stream) of vehicles and pedestrians moving through signals and lane [markings](#markings), rather than on any single [car](#car).

entries.name: tennis_court
entries.description: The marked rectangular [playing](#playing) surface for [tennis](#tennis), [split](#split) down the middle by a [net](#net) and ruled out with service boxes and baselines. Clay, [grass](#grass) and hard courts all count.

entries.name: parking_lot
entries.description: An open area of marked bays where cars stand, whether a flat lot, a [rooftop](#rooftop) deck or a multi-storey [garage](#garage). Often chosen for empty after-hours scenes.

entries.name: wooden_bridge
entries.description: A [bridge](#bridge) of planks laid over timber posts, crossing a [stream](#stream), [pond](#pond), or gorge. Rural, [forest](#forest), and [shrine](#shrine) settings favour it.

entries.name: airport
entries.description: The place where [aircraft](#aircraft) take off, land and are serviced, with runways or helipads, hangars, terminals and often a control [tower](#tower). Both the [apron](#apron) outside and the halls inside belong to it.

entries.name: highway
entries.description: A wide multi-lane [road](#road) built for fast long-distance [traffic](#traffic), with barriers, overhead signage and few entry points. Unlike a [street](#street) it carries [no](#no) shopfronts, crossings or pavements.

entries.name: horse_racing_track
entries.description: The oval [dirt](#dirt) or turf course of a racecourse, with rails, starting gates and grandstands. It serves as the [backdrop](#backdrop) for [racing](#racing) scenes.

entries.name: kyoto
entries.description: Japan's [old](#old) imperial capital, recognisable by its [shrine](#shrine) gates, temples, pagodas and narrow machiya streets. Scenes set among those landmarks take it.

entries.name: new_york_city
entries.description: The [skyline](#skyline), bridges and streets of the largest American [city](#city): yellow cabs, Times Square, the Statue of Liberty out in the harbour. It stands in for the modern American metropolis more often than anywhere else.

entries.name: overpass
entries.description: A [road](#road) or railway deck carried on piers above another route, crossing it instead of joining it. Frequently drawn from below in [city](#city) scenes, with [traffic](#traffic) [running](#running) underneath.

entries.name: shibuya_(tokyo)
entries.description: The Tokyo ward known for its scramble crossing, department stores and dense walls of neon signage. Landmarks in the background place a scene there.

entries.name: taiwan
entries.description: The East Asian [island](#island) shown as a subject or setting, through its real locations or its [flag](#flag). Apply it only for that flag or those places, not simply because a picture is Chinese in style.

entries.name: construction_site
entries.description: The fenced-off ground where a [building](#building) is being raised, full of [scaffolding](#scaffolding), [machinery](#machinery) and stacked materials. Often used as a rough [urban](#urban) [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: zoo
entries.description: A public [park](#park) of [animal](#animal) enclosures linked by fences, moats and signposted paths for visitors to walk between exhibits. The [tag](#tag) marks the place itself rather than any particular animal kept there.

entries.name: pedestrian_bridge
entries.description: A footbridge carried over a [road](#road) or railway so [people](#people) [can](#can) [cross](#cross) clear of the [traffic](#traffic), with [stairs](#stairs) at either end. A fixture of [urban](#urban) Japanese backdrops.

entries.name: multi-lane_road
entries.description: A [road](#road) [carrying](#carrying) two or more lanes in each direction. Add [street](#street) when it runs through [town](#town) with pavements alongside, or [highway](#highway) when it is closed to [people](#people) on foot.

entries.name: runway
entries.description: The long marked strip at an [airport](#airport) where [aircraft](#aircraft) take off and land, with its centreline and edge lights. The catwalk models walk down is a separate, unrelated thing.

entries.name: sweden
entries.description: The Scandinavian country shown as a setting or subject through its cities, landmarks or cultural shorthand. Reserve it for pictures grounded in the place itself, not simply for a blond character.

entries.name: england
entries.description: The scene is set in England, told by its landmarks, [street](#street) furniture or [landscape](#landscape): red buses, [brick](#brick) terraces, [rolling](#rolling) green fields. The [flag](#flag) on its own is [english_flag](#english_flag).

entries.name: gas_station
entries.description: A roadside stop selling fuel for cars and motorcycles, with [pumps](#pumps) [standing](#standing) under a canopy and often a small [shop](#shop). A common [backdrop](#backdrop) for [road](#road) trips and late-night scenes.

entries.name: soccer_field
entries.description: The marked [grass](#grass) pitch used for football, with painted lines, a center [circle](#circle), and goals at either end. Stands or a schoolyard [fence](#fence) often frame it.

entries.name: venice
entries.description: The Italian [canal](#canal) [city](#city), recognisable by its waterways, arched bridges, gondolas and pastel [building](#building) fronts, frequently used as a romantic [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: london
entries.description: The English capital on the Thames, identified by its bridges, red double-decker buses, the great [clock](#clock) [tower](#tower) and rows of terraced houses. Use it where the [city](#city) is recognisable, not for any generic [street](#street).

entries.name: shinjuku_(tokyo)
entries.description: The Tokyo ward built around a massive station, home to the [city](#city) hall towers, the Kabukicho nightlife district and dense high-rise streets.

entries.name: akihabara_(tokyo)
entries.description: The Tokyo district packed with electronics shops, anime goods and arcades. It is drawn through stacked signage, [tall](#tall) narrow shopfronts and the crowds at its crossings.

entries.name: junkyard
entries.description: A yard where scrap and wrecked vehicles are piled up to await [crushing](#crushing) or recycling. Rust, stacked bodyshells and hills of twisted metal give the place its character.

entries.name: vietnam
entries.description: The Southeast Asian country as the place shown, through its [landscape](#landscape), streets or landmarks. Clothing and [writing](#writing) from there have their own tags.

entries.name: baseball_field
entries.description: The ground [baseball](#baseball) is played on: a [dirt](#dirt) infield laid out as a diamond, wide [grass](#grass) beyond it and a raised mound at the centre. Netting closes off the batting end.

entries.name: korea
entries.description: The picture refers to the Korean peninsula, whether the modern states or the older kingdom. Landmarks, [scenery](#scenery) and national symbols carry it rather than the mere presence of a Korean character.

entries.name: sandbox
entries.description: A shallow wooden frame, or a hollow scooped in the ground, [holding](#holding) loose [sand](#sand) that children dig and build in. A fixture of parks and [school](#school) yards, usually with buckets, spades and a half-finished [castle](#castle).

entries.name: paris
entries.description: The French capital as a setting, given away by the Eiffel Tower, the Arc de Triomphe, the [glass](#glass) pyramid of the Louvre, or rows of Haussmann facades.

entries.name: under_bridge
entries.description: The [space](#space) beneath a [bridge](#bridge), whether a riverside underpass or the shadowed [arch](#arch) of a stone span. Reads as shelter, a [hiding](#hiding) spot or a quiet meeting place.

entries.name: hong_kong
entries.description: The [city](#city) drawn as its own setting: tightly stacked [apartment](#apartment) towers and thickets of overhanging neon signage. That look fed directly into the visual language of [cyberpunk](#cyberpunk).

entries.name: shopping_district
entries.description: A [street](#street) or covered [arcade](#arcade) lined with shops and hung with signs and banners, where [people](#people) gather to browse and buy.

entries.name: arch_bridge
entries.description: A [bridge](#bridge) carried on one or more curved spans of stone, [brick](#brick) or steel rather than a flat deck on piers. The sweep of the curve beneath the roadway is what marks it out.

entries.name: osaka_(city)
entries.description: Japan's great Kansai port, the country's third largest [city](#city), spread where the Yodo [river](#river) meets its bay. Neon-lit Dotonbori, the [castle](#castle) keep and the Tsutenkaku [tower](#tower) are the usual visual cues.

entries.name: suspension_bridge
entries.description: A [bridge](#bridge) whose deck hangs from cables strung between [tall](#tall) towers, ranging from a great steel span to a [swaying](#swaying) rope-and-plank crossing. The cables and towers are what make it recognizable. Implies bridge.

entries.name: outdoors
entries.description: The scene takes place in the open air. Best paired with a specific place [tag](#tag) such as [beach](#beach), [forest](#forest), [city](#city) or [mountain](#mountain); gardens and [hot](#hot) springs may be either inside or out.

entries.name: field
entries.description: An open stretch of land, generally [planted](#planted) with crops or [grass](#grass). Where flowers [cover](#cover) nearly all of it, add [flower_field](#flower_field) as [well](#well).

entries.name: garden
entries.description: An outdoor [space](#space) [planted](#planted) and kept on purpose, with [flower](#flower) beds, hedges or vegetables rather than wild growth. The indoor equivalents are [greenhouse](#greenhouse) and [conservatory](#conservatory).

entries.name: sunflower_field
entries.description: A [field](#field) [planted](#planted) entirely with sunflowers, a favourite [backdrop](#backdrop) for [summer](#summer) illustrations. Implies [flower_field](#flower_field) and [sunflower](#sunflower).

entries.name: wheat_field
entries.description: Rows of [tall](#tall) golden grain [running](#running) toward the [horizon](#horizon) and [bending](#bending) in the [wind](#wind). Barley, rye and other cereals of the same color are covered by the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: meadow
entries.description: Open, untilled ground thick with [grass](#grass) and wildflowers, usually [stretching](#stretching) toward a treeline or [horizon](#horizon). Reserved for flowering grassland rather than [planted](#planted) farmland.

entries.name: village
entries.description: A small [rural](#rural) settlement of scattered houses, larger than a hamlet and [well](#well) short of a [town](#town). Fields, barns and [dirt](#dirt) tracks usually surround it.

entries.name: rice_paddy
entries.description: A [field](#field) flooded with shallow [water](#water) for growing [rice](#rice), divided by low earth banks. A [staple](#staple) of Japanese countryside [scenery](#scenery), mirror-flat in spring and [gold](#gold) by [autumn](#autumn).

entries.name: rural
entries.description: A countryside setting away from any [city](#city): farmland, small villages, unpaved roads and scattered houses. It sets the tone of a picture as much as it names a place.

entries.name: battlefield
entries.description: Ground where a fight is under way or has just ended: churned earth, [wreckage](#wreckage), [drifting](#drifting) [smoke](#smoke), scattered weapons and bodies. The silence afterwards is drawn as often as the [fighting](#fighting) itself.

entries.name: dirt_road
entries.description: An unpaved track of packed earth or gravel, often rutted and grassed along its edges. Belongs to countryside and backcountry scenes.

entries.name: farm
entries.description: Worked agricultural land with its buildings and [machinery](#machinery): barns, silos, paddies, fenced plots, tractors. Livestock and rows of crops help identify it.

entries.name: scarecrow
entries.description: A straw-stuffed [dummy](#dummy) in cast-off [clothes](#clothes), propped on a [pole](#pole) in a [field](#field) to keep birds off the crop. Bird deterrents not shaped like [people](#people) are tagged bird_scarer.

entries.name: stable
entries.description: A [building](#building) that houses livestock, horses above all, divided into individual stalls with straw on the [floor](#floor). Often drawn with [hay](#hay) bales, [hanging](#hanging) tack and a wide central aisle.

entries.name: golf_course
entries.description: The landscaped ground a round of [golf](#golf) is played over: mown fairways, [sand](#sand) bunkers, [water](#water) hazards and a flagged green. The setting counts whether or not anybody is [playing](#playing).

entries.name: beach
entries.description: The flat sandy or pebbly strip where land meets [water](#water), the classic [swimsuit](#swimsuit) setting with [waves](#waves), parasols and towels. A rocky, paved or cliff-backed waterline is [shore](#shore) instead.

entries.name: pool
entries.description: A [swimming](#swimming) pool, indoor or outdoor, as the setting or a visible feature. A small inflatable one is [wading_pool](#wading_pool), a [hot](#hot) spring is [onsen](#onsen), and the cue game is [billiards](#billiards). Add [poolside](#poolside) when the character is at its edge.

entries.name: poolside
entries.description: A character stands, sits or lies at the edge of a [swimming](#swimming) [pool](#pool), or is [climbing](#climbing) in or out. The pool itself may be off-frame if the [tiles](#tiles), [ladder](#ladder) or lane lines make the place clear.

entries.name: shore
entries.description: The edge where land meets a larger body of [water](#water): a [beach](#beach), [riverbank](#riverbank), lakeshore or coastal [cliff](#cliff). Add beach, [ocean](#ocean), [river](#river) or [lake](#lake) for the specific kind of water.

entries.name: flight_deck
entries.description: The open top deck of an [aircraft](#aircraft) carrier where planes take off and land, an airfield at sea. Common in naval and [military](#military) aviation art.

entries.name: wading_pool
entries.description: A shallow inflatable or plastic kiddie [pool](#pool) set up [outdoors](#outdoors) as a makeshift place to splash around. Distinct from a built [swimming](#swimming) pool.

entries.name: pier
entries.description: A raised [platform](#platform) on posts [running](#running) out over the [water](#water) from the [shore](#shore), used as a [walkway](#walkway), a [fishing](#fishing) spot or a mooring. Usually wooden, though stone and metal ones exist; common in harbour, [lake](#lake) and [beach](#beach) scenes.

entries.name: dock
entries.description: A harbour [structure](#structure) built to hold ships for repair or for loading cargo and passengers, frequently with [tall](#tall) cranes along the waterside. Two jetties enclosing a single berth count as [well](#well).

entries.name: water_slide
entries.description: A curving chute at a [pool](#pool) or [water](#water) [park](#park) that riders shoot down on a rush of water. Drawn as bright open flumes or enclosed tubes.

entries.name: harbor
entries.description: A sheltered stretch of [water](#water) where boats and ships tie up, edged by quays, moorings, bollards and cranes. Natural inlets and artificial docks both count.

entries.name: empty_pool
entries.description: A [swimming](#swimming) [pool](#pool) drained of [water](#water), showing bare [tiles](#tiles), the sloping [floor](#floor) and painted depth [markings](#markings). Common in derelict settings and as a place to skate.

entries.name: tropical
entries.description: A picture built around the [hot](#hot) latitudes: palm trees, [hibiscus](#hibiscus), bright [sun](#sun) and sea, or dense [jungle](#jungle) greenery paired with light clothing to match. Fruit, cocktails and regional wildlife often round out the scene.

entries.name: seaside
entries.description: An outdoor scene at the edge of the sea: [beach](#beach), shoreline, cliffs, or a coastal [town](#town) with the [water](#water) in view. Add [ocean](#ocean) or water for the sea itself, and beach or [shore](#shore) when the [sand](#sand) or rocks underfoot are the focus.

entries.name: waterpark
entries.description: A leisure [park](#park) built around [water](#water) attractions such as slides, wave pools and lazy rivers. Crowds in swimwear and brightly colored plastic structures set the scene.

entries.name: tetrapod
entries.description: A [concrete](#concrete) breakwater block shaped like a four-armed jack, its limbs typically rounded. Heaped by the hundreds along harbour walls and shorelines, it reads instantly as a coastal scene.

entries.name: ruins
entries.description: Abandoned man-made structures that have crumbled with time: [broken](#broken) temples, [overgrown](#overgrown) cities, [collapsed](#collapsed) buildings. A [staple](#staple) of post-apocalyptic and [fantasy](#fantasy) exploration scenes.

entries.name: castle
entries.description: A large fortified [building](#building) with thick walls and towers, sometimes a moat, whether it is the setting itself or a landmark on the [horizon](#horizon). Japanese keeps count as readily as European ones.

entries.name: shrine
entries.description: A Shinto place of worship, ranging from a large compound to a small roadside [altar](#altar). Torii gates alone are not enough for this [tag](#tag), since they [can](#can) stand [well](#well) away from any shrine; an uncertain religion is [temple](#temple) instead.

entries.name: tombstone
entries.description: A stone [marker](#marker) over a [grave](#grave), upright or flat, alone or in rows at a [graveyard](#graveyard). Add graveyard and flowers or offerings when present.

entries.name: church
entries.description: A Christian place of worship, seen from outside with its [steeple](#steeple) or from inside among pews, [altar](#altar) and stained [glass](#glass). A frequent setting for weddings and for gothic scenes.

entries.name: graveyard
entries.description: A burial ground where the dead lie under rows of tombstones, crosses or [sotoba](#sotoba). Add [grave](#grave) as [well](#well) when one [marker](#marker) is the focus.

entries.name: grave
entries.description: A burial site marked by a [tombstone](#tombstone), [cross](#cross) or similar [marker](#marker), often [carrying](#carrying) the dead person's name. A whole burial ground full of them is a [graveyard](#graveyard).

entries.name: temple
entries.description: A [building](#building) raised for worship that is neither a [church](#church) nor a Shinto [shrine](#shrine), ranging from a Buddhist hall to a classical colonnade. When it is unclear the [structure](#structure) is religious at all, describe the [architecture](#architecture) with other tags instead.

entries.name: pyramid_(structure)
entries.description: A monumental stone [building](#building) with sloping sides meeting at an apex, taking the ancient Egyptian royal tomb as its archetype. Desert and ancient-world scenes are its natural [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: cathedral
entries.description: The chief [church](#church) of a diocese, [holding](#holding) a bishop's seat and built far grander than a parish church. Soaring vaults, pointed arches and stained [glass](#glass) are its marks; outside and nave both qualify.

entries.name: colosseum
entries.description: A large oval [arena](#arena) ringed by tiered seating, built on the [model](#model) of the Roman amphitheatre. Invented and [fantasy](#fantasy) arenas [following](#following) the same plan count too.

entries.name: shinto
entries.description: Imagery drawn from Japan's native religion of kami and shrines, shown through [torii](#torii) gates, straw ropes, purification rites, priests and [miko](#miko).

entries.name: water
entries.description: Liquid water is clearly visible: a sea, [lake](#lake), [river](#river), [pool](#pool), [bath](#bath), [puddle](#puddle) or a poured [stream](#stream). Not used together with [underwater](#underwater) when the scene is mostly beneath the surface.

entries.name: ocean
entries.description: The sea is in view, as open [water](#water) [reaching](#reaching) a [horizon](#horizon) or as surf [breaking](#breaking) along a [shore](#shore). Regularly paired with [beach](#beach) and [sky](#sky); a scene below the surface takes [underwater](#underwater) instead.

entries.name: partially_submerged
entries.description: Water covers part of a character's body: [standing](#standing) in it deeper than the waist, or [sitting](#sitting), [kneeling](#kneeling) or [lying](#lying) down in shallower [water](#water). Standing in water below waist depth is [wading](#wading), sunken objects take [partially_immersed](#partially_immersed), and a waterline crossing the frame is [partially_underwater_shot](#partially_underwater_shot).

entries.name: underwater
entries.description: The scene takes place beneath the surface of [water](#water), or the viewpoint itself is [submerged](#submerged). A view cut by the waterline instead is [partially_underwater_shot](#partially_underwater_shot).

entries.name: ripples
entries.description: Concentric rings [spreading](#spreading) across [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid) from a drop or a touch. Often used in quiet scenes with a [puddle](#puddle) or [pond](#pond).

entries.name: puddle
entries.description: A small [pool](#pool) of [liquid](#liquid) [lying](#lying) on a surface, most often rainwater on a [road](#road) or [path](#path), sometimes reflecting the scene above it. Also covers pools of [blood](#blood), urine, or other fluid collected on the ground.

entries.name: river
entries.description: A large natural flowing waterway crossing the scene. Add [riverbank](#riverbank) or [bridge](#bridge) tags where they apply; even a small [stream](#stream) is usually still tagged river.

entries.name: waves
entries.description: Rolling or [breaking](#breaking) waves on the sea or another body of [liquid](#liquid). The hand greeting is a separate [tag](#tag), and concentric rings [spreading](#spreading) on still [water](#water) are [ripples](#ripples).

entries.name: waterfall
entries.description: Water plunging over a steep or vertical drop, from a [mountain](#mountain) cascade to a [garden](#garden) feature. Often paired with mist, rocks and [forest](#forest).

entries.name: lake
entries.description: A wide sheet of still [water](#water) enclosed by land, larger than a [pond](#pond), forming part of the scene. Shoreline and [reflection](#reflection) tags usually go alongside.

entries.name: reflective_water
entries.description: A body of [water](#water) whose still surface mirrors the [sky](#sky), [scenery](#scenery), or characters. Used for lakes, puddles, flooded floors, and the sea when the [reflection](#reflection) is visible.

entries.name: in_water
entries.description: A vague placeholder for somebody or something in [water](#water). Prefer the exact [tag](#tag): [submerged](#submerged) or [partially_submerged](#partially_submerged) for [people](#people), [immersed](#immersed) for objects, and [wading](#wading), [soaking_feet](#soaking_feet), [partially_underwater_shot](#partially_underwater_shot) or [underwater](#underwater) for the rest.

entries.name: pond
entries.description: A small body of still [water](#water), in a [garden](#garden), [park](#park) or [field](#field). Larger bodies are [lake](#lake); [tag](#tag) water alongside it.

entries.name: shallow_water
entries.description: Water so shallow the bottom shows through, such as a [stream](#stream), a tide [pool](#pool), or the edge of a [lake](#lake), often with a character [wading](#wading) in it.

entries.name: stream
entries.description: A small, shallow flow of [running](#running) [water](#water) such as a creek or brook. Narrower and calmer than a [river](#river); use river for a wide, deep waterway.

entries.name: riverbank
entries.description: The strip of ground [running](#running) alongside a [river](#river), whether grassy, sandy or built up with [concrete](#concrete). A common setting for walks, talks and [fireworks](#fireworks) scenes.

entries.name: canal
entries.description: A watercourse dug by [people](#people) instead of cut by [nature](#nature), [running](#running) between built-up banks. Walls, low bridges and moored boats usually line it; a natural channel is a [river](#river).

entries.name: coral_reef
entries.description: A ridge of [coral](#coral) built up under the sea, dense with colour and [fish](#fish). Usually the [backdrop](#backdrop) of an undersea scene rather than its subject.

entries.name: flood
entries.description: Water [lying](#lying) over ground that ought to be dry, swamping streets, fields or rooms. Anything from a wholly [submerged](#submerged) [city](#city) to a [floor](#floor) under a few inches of [water](#water).

entries.name: seafloor
entries.description: The bottom of the sea as a setting: [sand](#sand), [rock](#rock), and weed beneath open [water](#water), often lit by rippling light from above.

entries.name: water_world
entries.description: The entire surface of the world is [water](#water), with [sky](#sky) above and [no](#no) land anywhere. Built structures may rise from it, but hills, islands and beaches rule the [tag](#tag) out, as does a view from below the surface.

entries.name: partially_immersed
entries.description: An object such as a [building](#building), a vehicle or a piece of furniture stands half in [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid), the surface line [cutting](#cutting) across it. A person in the same position is [partially_submerged](#partially_submerged).

entries.name: frozen_lake
entries.description: A [lake](#lake) whose surface has iced over, sometimes dusted with [snow](#snow) or [carrying](#carrying) skaters. A piece of [winter](#winter) [landscape](#landscape) rather than a weather condition.

entries.name: seascape
entries.description: A view given over to the sea itself, open [water](#water), [waves](#waves), and the [horizon](#horizon) [carrying](#carrying) the picture. Any figures present are small in the frame.

entries.name: immersed
entries.description: A [building](#building), vehicle or other object [sitting](#sitting) entirely below the surface of [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid). A person under the surface takes [submerged](#submerged) instead.

entries.name: red_ocean
entries.description: A great expanse of red [liquid](#liquid) [standing](#standing) in for the sea, whether [blood](#blood), a fictional fluid, or simply an artistic [choice](#choice). Any body of red fluid far larger than a [bathtub](#bathtub) counts, so lakes, rivers and floods of it belong here too.

entries.name: whirlpool
entries.description: Water spiraling down into a funnel-shaped [vortex](#vortex) at sea, in a [river](#river), or in a [bath](#bath). Ships, swimmers or [debris](#debris) are often shown being pulled toward the center.

entries.name: snow
entries.description: Snow [lying](#lying) on the ground or piled over the [scenery](#scenery). Reserve [snowing](#snowing) on its own for flakes still coming down, and add this [tag](#tag) too once snow has actually settled.

entries.name: rock
entries.description: A stone or [boulder](#boulder) in the scene, natural and unworked. Piles of [broken](#broken) masonry are [rubble](#rubble); a sheer [cliff](#cliff) face has its own separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: ice
entries.description: Frozen [water](#water) in the scene: a sheeted surface, a [frozen](#frozen) [pond](#pond), blocks and floes, or ice called up as a magical element. Cubes in a [drink](#drink) take [ice_cube](#ice_cube) and icy [wings](#wings) take [ice_wings](#ice_wings).

entries.name: sand
entries.description: Loose pale grains covering the ground, at a [beach](#beach), in a [desert](#desert) or a [sandbox](#sandbox). Tag beach or desert as [well](#well) when the setting is clear.

entries.name: mountain
entries.description: A large steep rise of land in the [scenery](#scenery), whether close at hand or [sitting](#sitting) far off on the [horizon](#horizon). Where a whole ridge forms the [skyline](#skyline), the mountainous horizon [tag](#tag) says it better.

entries.name: horizon
entries.description: The line where land or sea meets the [sky](#sky) is plainly visible, usually across open [ocean](#ocean), plains or [desert](#desert). A [city](#city) [outline](#outline) [standing](#standing) against it is a [skyline](#skyline), and a horizon tilted against the frame makes a [dutch_angle](#dutch_angle).

entries.name: mountainous_horizon
entries.description: The far edge of the scene is formed by a long ridge or a run of peaks. Do not add the [plain](#plain) [mountain](#mountain) [tag](#tag) as [well](#well) when they are [no](#no) more than specks in the distance.

entries.name: landscape
entries.description: Scenery itself is the subject: [forest](#forest), [field](#field), [mountain](#mountain), [river](#river) or [lake](#lake) [running](#running) [back](#back) to a [horizon](#horizon), with figures small or absent altogether. It usually sits alongside [scenery](#scenery) and [no_humans](#no_humans).

entries.name: hill
entries.description: A rounded rise of land, lower and gentler than a [mountain](#mountain). Rolling grassy slopes in the middle or far distance are the usual treatment.

entries.name: desert
entries.description: A dry, barren [landscape](#landscape) of [sand](#sand) or loose parched [soil](#soil), with little growing beyond cacti and [palms](#palms). Common ground for Middle Eastern and post-apocalyptic settings; the sweet course after a [meal](#meal) is [dessert](#dessert).

entries.name: cliff
entries.description: A steep [rock](#rock) face or precipice, whether somebody stands at its edge, climbs it, or it forms the [backdrop](#backdrop). Frequently paired with sea or [mountain](#mountain) [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: footprints
entries.description: Impressions left by bare [feet](#feet) or [shoes](#shoes) in a soft surface such as [sand](#sand), [snow](#snow) or [mud](#mud). They often trail away to show that somebody has passed through.

entries.name: cave
entries.description: A natural hollow [underground](#underground), big enough to walk into, grottos and sea caves included. Dark, rocky and a standard setting for adventures.

entries.name: rubble
entries.description: Broken [rock](#rock) and [concrete](#concrete) [lying](#lying) settled on the ground, as found in [ruins](#ruins) or after [destruction](#destruction). Pieces still [flying](#flying) through the air instead are [debris](#debris).

entries.name: lava
entries.description: Molten [rock](#rock) glows in the scene, flowing or pooled, whether from a [volcano](#volcano) or in a fiery underworld. It throws orange light over everything around it.

entries.name: island
entries.description: Land with [water](#water) all around it, from a palm-topped sandbar to a bare [rock](#rock) in the sea. It may be seen from the [shore](#shore), from the water or from the air.

entries.name: floating_island
entries.description: A piece of natural land [hanging](#hanging) in the [sky](#sky), a standard [fantasy](#fantasy) [landscape](#landscape) element. Built structures in the air are [floating_castle](#floating_castle) and [floating_city](#floating_city) instead.

entries.name: dirt
