entries.description: Bare earth or [soil](#soil) showing in the scene, as a [patch](#patch) of loose ground or a track worn through the [grass](#grass). Grime on a person or object is [dirty](#dirty) instead.

entries.name: mount_fuji
entries.description: Japan's highest [mountain](#mountain), the broad snow-capped cone that serves as a national symbol. Still an active [volcano](#volcano), and a constant distant [backdrop](#backdrop) in art.

entries.name: volcano
entries.description: A [mountain](#mountain) venting [smoke](#smoke), ash or molten [rock](#rock) from its summit. Ranges from a distant [smoking](#smoking) cone on the [horizon](#horizon) to [glowing](#glowing) [lava](#lava) close at hand.

entries.name: floating_rock
entries.description: Stones or boulders [hanging](#hanging) in mid-air, signalling [magic](#magic), thin gravity or an otherworldly place. They often accompany a [drifting](#drifting) [island](#island) or a [spell](#spell) in progress.

entries.name: boulder
entries.description: A [rock](#rock) much larger than the stones around it, big enough to sit on, scramble over or hide behind. Use it for one massive block, not for gravel or a whole [cliff](#cliff) face.

entries.name: icicle
entries.description: Tapering [spikes](#spikes) of [ice](#ice) [hanging](#hanging) from a roof edge, a [branch](#branch) or a [ledge](#ledge) where [dripping](#dripping) [water](#water) froze as it fell. They mark a scene as [cold](#cold) and fill out [winter](#winter) backdrops.

entries.name: underground
entries.description: A scene set below ground level: tunnels, caverns, sewers, mines or [buried](#buried) chambers. Earth and [rock](#rock) enclose the [space](#space), with light coming from lamps or a distant [opening](#opening).

entries.name: crater
entries.description: A bowl-shaped hollow [punched](#punched) into the ground by an impact, an [explosion](#explosion) or volcanic activity. In action pictures it marks where something landed hard.

entries.name: cave_interior
entries.description: The inside of a [cave](#cave), [rock](#rock) walls and [hanging](#hanging) formations lit by torchlight or by a distant mouth. Being [underground](#underground) does not make it [indoors](#indoors), so the indoors [tag](#tag) does not belong here.

entries.name: wetland
entries.description: Waterlogged ground whose plants and animals are built for [standing](#standing) [water](#water), from a tree-filled swamp to a reedy marsh or a peaty bog and fen. Expect still water, [mud](#mud) and dense low growth.

entries.name: pebble
entries.description: A small rounded stone, about the size of a marble or less, [lying](#lying) on the ground, cupped in a hand or skimmed across [water](#water).

entries.name: canyon
entries.description: A deep gorge cut down into [rock](#rock) by a [river](#river) over long ages, walled by cliffs on either side. Wider and more winding than a ravine, which stays narrow and straight.

entries.name: valley
entries.description: A stretch of low ground [running](#running) between hills or mountains, often with a [river](#river) along its [floor](#floor), usually shown as a wide [landscape](#landscape) view.

entries.name: stalactite
entries.description: A stone [icicle](#icicle) [hanging](#hanging) from a [cave](#cave) [ceiling](#ceiling), built up over ages by [dripping](#dripping) mineral-rich [water](#water). The formations growing upward from the [floor](#floor) are stalagmites instead.

entries.name: snowscape
entries.description: A [landscape](#landscape) given over to [snow](#snow): wide white ground, bare or frosted trees, and sometimes mountains on the [horizon](#horizon). The [scenery](#scenery) itself is the subject, distinguishing it from a scene that merely happens to have snow in it.

entries.name: soil
entries.description: Bare earth shown as a visible surface: a turned [garden](#garden) [bed](#bed), a dug [hole](#hole), or dry ground underfoot. Distinct from [mud](#mud), which is soil that has gotten [wet](#wet).

entries.name: broken_ground
entries.description: The ground has [split](#split) and buckled, cracks [running](#running) outward with slabs tilted up at their edges. It generally marks where an impact or a quake landed.

entries.name: stalagmite
entries.description: A stone cone rising from a [cave](#cave) [floor](#floor) where [dripping](#dripping) [water](#water) has left its minerals behind. Given enough time it [can](#can) meet its [ceiling](#ceiling) counterpart, the [stalactite](#stalactite), to form a [column](#column).

entries.name: iceberg
entries.description: A [mountain](#mountain) of [glacier](#glacier) [ice](#ice) adrift at sea, blue-white above the waterline. Since most of its bulk rides below the surface, pictures often show the far larger mass continuing [underwater](#underwater).

entries.name: glacier
entries.description: A vast mass of [ice](#ice) built up on land over centuries and creeping downhill under its own [weight](#weight). Drawn as blue-white walls, crevassed fields or an ice sheet meeting the sea.

entries.name: plain
entries.description: A wide flat stretch of land with little change in elevation, mostly [grass](#grass) and nearly treeless. Thick with flowers or crops it becomes a [field](#field); the [cold](#cold) and [hot](#hot) counterparts are tundra and savanna.

entries.name: wasteland
entries.description: Barren, ruined ground stripped of living things by [war](#war), fallout or disaster, strewn with [rubble](#rubble) and [blowing](#blowing) [dust](#dust). Natural deserts, glaciers and bare mountains do not qualify.

entries.name: trench
entries.description: A long ditch cut into the ground for [cover](#cover), with earthen walls and often duckboards or sandbags lining it. Strongly associated with First World War [battlefield](#battlefield) imagery.

entries.name: coal
entries.description: Lumps of black [rock](#rock) burned for fuel, seen in a scuttle, a [stove](#stove), a mine or a [sack](#sack). It is also the traditional mock present left for badly behaved children at Christmas.

entries.name: eruption
entries.description: A [volcano](#volcano) [throwing](#throwing) out ash, [smoke](#smoke) and molten [rock](#rock), with [lava](#lava) [running](#running) down its flanks. Usually the [backdrop](#backdrop) to a [landscape](#landscape) or a disaster.

entries.name: clay
entries.description: Soft mouldable earth, shown as a [wet](#wet) lump, a piece turning on a [wheel](#wheel) or a half-finished [figure](#figure). It is the raw material, not the fired ceramic result.

entries.name: oasis
entries.description: A green, watered [pocket](#pocket) in the middle of a [desert](#desert), usually drawn as a [pool](#pool) ringed by [palms](#palms) and [grass](#grass).

entries.name: sand_dune
entries.description: A wind-heaped ridge of [sand](#sand) with a knife-edge [crest](#crest) and rippled flanks, the standard furniture of [desert](#desert) [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: karst
entries.description: A [landscape](#landscape) of narrow limestone peaks rising sharply from flat ground, pitted with caves and pillars. It is the [scenery](#scenery) of southern Chinese [river](#river) country.

entries.name: tree
entries.description: One or more trees stand in the scene, from a single trunk in a [park](#park) to woodland filling the background. A dense stand of them becomes [forest](#forest), a young one is a [sapling](#sapling), and a cut one is a [tree_stump](#tree_stump).

entries.name: grass
entries.description: A noticeable spread of grass in the picture, such as a lawn, [meadow](#meadow) or [field](#field) somebody is [lying](#lying) in. Use it for real abundance, not a few blades at the edge of the frame.

entries.name: cherry_blossoms
entries.description: Pink or white sakura flowers on the [branch](#branch) or [drifting](#drifting) loose as [petals](#petals), the standard springtime motif for youth and passing beauty. Trees are almost always drawn in [bloom](#bloom), so one [carrying](#carrying) [fruit](#fruit) takes [cherry](#cherry) together with [fruit_tree](#fruit_tree).

entries.name: nature
entries.description: Scenery in which wild [vegetation](#vegetation) is plainly in view — woods, meadows, [overgrown](#overgrown) ground. It sits alongside the specific [tree](#tree), [grass](#grass) and [forest](#forest) tags rather than replacing them.

entries.name: forest
entries.description: A setting thick with trees and undergrowth, from a sunlit wood to a close [dark](#dark) thicket. Tag [tree](#tree) and [foliage](#foliage) for the individual elements within it.

entries.name: bush
entries.description: A shrub: a woody [plant](#plant) with several stems, [standing](#standing) [well](#well) short of a [tree](#tree). Garden planting, hedges and [forest](#forest) undergrowth all count.

entries.name: autumn_leaves
entries.description: Leaves in their [autumn](#autumn) colours of red, brown and yellow, still on the [branch](#branch), [drifting](#drifting) down or [lying](#lying) underfoot. Maple is commonest, with oak and ginkgo also seen; use [falling_leaves](#falling_leaves) when they hang in the air.

entries.name: bare_tree
entries.description: A [tree](#tree) stripped of leaves and blossom, whether [shed](#shed) for the [winter](#winter) or dead altogether. Bare branches lend a scene a bleak, [cold](#cold) or uneasy mood.

entries.name: flower_field
entries.description: Open ground carpeted with blossoms [stretching](#stretching) across the scene. Where the species [can](#can) be made out, add the specific [flower](#flower) [tag](#tag) alongside it.

entries.name: in_tree
entries.description: A character up among the branches and leaves of a [tree](#tree), [sitting](#sitting) on a limb, [lying](#lying) along it or [hanging](#hanging) from one. Standing at the foot of a tree does not count.

entries.name: bamboo_forest
entries.description: A dense stand of [tall](#tall) [bamboo](#bamboo) as the setting, light [falling](#falling) in strips between the [crowded](#crowded) stems and the ground left shaded. Paths through one are a favourite [backdrop](#backdrop) for [shrine](#shrine) and youkai scenes.

entries.name: overgrown
entries.description: Vegetation has taken [back](#back) something built: [vines](#vines) [swallowing](#swallowing) a ruin, [grass](#grass) splitting a [road](#road), [moss](#moss) creeping over [machinery](#machinery). A [staple](#staple) of [abandoned](#abandoned) and post-apocalyptic scenes.

entries.name: tree_stump
entries.description: What remains of a felled [tree](#tree): a short trunk base still rooted in the ground. Characters often sit on one in [forest](#forest) or clearing scenes.

entries.name: foliage
entries.description: Greenery from bushes and trees seen as an undifferentiated mass in a wild rather than tended setting. Use it where [no](#no) single [plant](#plant) is distinct enough to [tag](#tag) on its own.

entries.name: jungle
entries.description: A dense [tropical](#tropical) [forest](#forest) of thick [vines](#vines), tangled undergrowth and [animal](#animal) life. Temperate woodland is forest; jungle brings heat and humidity with it.

entries.name: hedge
entries.description: A clipped row of dense shrubs [standing](#standing) as a green wall, used as a [garden](#garden) boundary or grown into a maze. It lines paths, [park](#park) edges and the fronts of houses.

entries.name: tall_grass
entries.description: Grass grown high enough to stand as blades and stalks, often knee- or waist-height, rather than a flat green surface. Typical of meadows and untended fields.

entries.name: flower_bed
entries.description: A [planted](#planted) [patch](#patch) of ground given over to flowers, of one kind or of many. Look for cultivated rows and borders rather than blooms growing wild in a [field](#field).

entries.name: grasslands
entries.description: Open country under an unbroken [cover](#cover) of [grass](#grass) with few or [no](#no) trees on the [horizon](#horizon): plains, prairie, savanna, steppe. Wider and emptier than a mown [field](#field) or a lawn.

entries.name: vegetation
entries.description: Plant growth filling out the scene as a whole: trees, shrubs, [grass](#grass), [moss](#moss), ferns and undergrowth together, used where greenery makes up the setting rather than one identifiable [plant](#plant).

entries.name: weeds
entries.description: Scruffy wild plants [pushing](#pushing) up where nobody [planted](#planted) them, through [pavement](#pavement), along fences or across an untended lot. They signal neglect rather than [gardening](#gardening), and have nothing to do with the [smoking](#smoking) sense of the word.

entries.name: reeds
entries.description: Tall slender grasses growing in dense stands at the edge of [water](#water), with feathery [seed](#seed) heads [swaying](#swaying) above. They fill the margins of ponds, rivers and marshes.

entries.name: savannah
entries.description: Mixed [grass](#grass) and woodland where the trees never grow close enough for their crowns to meet, floored with coarse seasonal grass. Typical of the [tropical](#tropical) margins.

entries.name: willow
entries.description: A willow [tree](#tree) with slender branches [hanging](#hanging) down, most often [leaning](#leaning) out over [water](#water). Its trailing curtain of narrow leaves suits melancholy or ghostly scenes.

entries.name: susuki_grass
entries.description: Japanese pampas [grass](#grass), with [tall](#tall) stalks ending in feathery silver plumes. It is visual shorthand for [autumn](#autumn) and appears constantly in moon-viewing scenes.

entries.name: rapeseed_blossoms
entries.description: The small four-petaled yellow flowers of the [rape](#rape) [plant](#plant), usually drawn covering a [field](#field) in a solid sheet of [gold](#gold). A recurring seasonal touch in Japanese countryside [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: kelp
entries.description: Long brown [seaweed](#seaweed) rising in dense [underwater](#underwater) forests, its ribbon-like fronds [reaching](#reaching) toward the light. It sets the scene in [diving](#diving) and open-sea pictures.

entries.name: birch_tree
entries.description: A slender [tree](#tree) with papery white bark scored by black scars where its branches grew. Stands of them are shorthand for northern woodland.

entries.name: fallen_tree
entries.description: A [tree](#tree) [lying](#lying) on its side, uprooted or snapped through, often across a [path](#path) or a [stream](#stream). It turns up as [storm](#storm) damage, forest-floor detail or an improvised [bench](#bench).

entries.name: snow_on_tree
entries.description: Snow [resting](#resting) along branches and needles, weighing them down and tracing the [outline](#outline) of a [tree](#tree) in white.

entries.name: trumpet_creeper
entries.description: A [climbing](#climbing) vine bearing clusters of long, orange-red flowers shaped like flared trumpets. Usually drawn scrambling over a wall, [fence](#fence) or [trellis](#trellis) in a [summer](#summer) scene.

entries.name: sky
entries.description: The sky is a visible part of the scene, as [backdrop](#backdrop) or subject. Add [blue_sky](#blue_sky), [night_sky](#night_sky), [sunset](#sunset) or [cloud](#cloud) to say what it looks like.

entries.name: cloud
entries.description: Water vapour massed in the [sky](#sky), from a few white tufts to [heavy](#heavy) piled banks. Once roughly half the sky or more is covered, [cloudy_sky](#cloudy_sky) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: blue_sky
entries.description: A clear blue daytime [sky](#sky) taking up a real share of the frame. Leave it off when only a sliver of sky shows, and add [cloud](#cloud) where clouds appear in it.

entries.name: moon
entries.description: The moon [hanging](#hanging) in the [sky](#sky). Add the phase where it [can](#can) be read — full, gibbous or [crescent](#crescent); a crescent used purely as a decorative shape is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: cloudy_sky
entries.description: A [sky](#sky) covered by [cloud](#cloud) over roughly half its area or more. A handful of scattered puffs is only cloud, and a sky shut in completely is [overcast](#overcast).

entries.name: star_(sky)
entries.description: Actual stars visible in the [sky](#sky), typically at [night](#night). When they fill the scene, use [starry_sky](#starry_sky) instead; a drawn ★ symbol is [star_(symbol)](#star_(symbol)).

entries.name: night_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) seen after [dark](#dark), deep blue to black and often [carrying](#carrying) stars or the [moon](#moon). Add [starry_sky](#starry_sky) or moon when either is clearly shown.

entries.name: full_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) showing as a complete round disc. A fixture of [night](#night) scenes, [werewolf](#werewolf) pictures and dramatic silhouettes.

entries.name: starry_sky
entries.description: A [night](#night) [sky](#sky) thick with stars as a notable part of the scene. If the stars are incidental, [tag](#tag) [star_(sky)](#star_(sky)) only; star symbols as a [backdrop](#backdrop) are starry_background instead.

entries.name: sun
entries.description: The sun itself, shown as a visible disc in the [sky](#sky). For its light alone use [sunlight](#sunlight), for rays [breaking](#breaking) through [cloud](#cloud) use [sunbeam](#sunbeam), and for a radiating graphic design use [sunburst](#sunburst).

entries.name: space
entries.description: The scene is set in outer space, among stars, planets, or the void beyond the atmosphere. Commonly paired with science-fiction elements such as [spacecraft](#spacecraft) and spacesuits.

entries.name: crescent_moon
entries.description: The waxing or waning [crescent](#crescent) [moon](#moon) in the [sky](#sky). Only the real moon counts; crescents on hats, hair or clothing take their ornament tags.

entries.name: planet
entries.description: At least one planet is visible, seen from [space](#space) or [hanging](#hanging) in the [sky](#sky) of another world. Real and fictional planets both count.

entries.name: rainbow
entries.description: A rainbow arc appears in the [sky](#sky) or as a decorative motif elsewhere in the picture. A spectrum blend across a surface instead is [rainbow_gradient](#rainbow_gradient), and objects arranged by color is [rainbow_order](#rainbow_order).

entries.name: gradient_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) blends smoothly between colours, as at [dusk](#dusk) when orange gives way to blue. Only use it where the sky takes up a meaningful part of the picture.

entries.name: orange_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) burns orange, generally at [sunrise](#sunrise) or [sunset](#sunset). Reserve it for pictures where the sky is a real part of the frame rather than a sliver behind the subject.

entries.name: shooting_star
entries.description: An object [burning](#burning) up on atmospheric entry, seen from far away as a streak of light crossing the [night](#night) [sky](#sky). A visible [fireball](#fireball) or a recognizable lump of [rock](#rock) is [meteor](#meteor) instead.

entries.name: earth_(planet)
entries.description: Our own [planet](#planet) seen from outside, [hanging](#hanging) in [space](#space) or rising over the Moon. For the [globe](#globe) as a celestial body, not for ground-level [scenery](#scenery); the element and ornaments shaped like it are separate.

entries.name: constellation
entries.description: A recognisable [figure](#figure) picked out among the stars, sometimes with the lines between them drawn in. Printed on [cloth](#cloth) it becomes [constellation_print](#constellation_print).

entries.name: red_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) shown with a clear red tint or glow, the so-called [blood](#blood) moon. In fiction it usually signals something ominous or supernatural; in reality it is the look of a lunar [eclipse](#eclipse).

entries.name: grey_sky
entries.description: An [overcast](#overcast) grey [sky](#sky), usually the work of [heavy](#heavy) [cloud](#cloud) or [rain](#rain). It sets a dull or gloomy tone over the whole scene.

entries.name: contrail
entries.description: The white vapour line an [aircraft](#aircraft) leaves drawn across the [sky](#sky). The reverse case, a clear gap cut through a [cloud](#cloud) layer, is distrail.

entries.name: purple_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) tinted purple, as at [dusk](#dusk), in a [fantasy](#fantasy) setting, or under a magical glow. Combine with sky and, where it fits, [sunset](#sunset) or [night](#night).

entries.name: red_sky
entries.description: A [sky](#sky) coloured a deep red, beyond a normal [sunset](#sunset) glow, suggesting [apocalypse](#apocalypse), [blood](#blood), or an [alien](#alien) world. Use it only when the sky fills a meaningful part of the frame.

entries.name: cumulonimbus_cloud
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), dense thundercloud towering upward, often flattened into an [anvil](#anvil) at the top. The [signature](#signature) [summer](#summer) [sky](#sky) of Japanese illustration, and a warning of the [storm](#storm) to come.

entries.name: pink_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) tinted pink, as at [sunrise](#sunrise) or [sunset](#sunset) or in a stylised [fantasy](#fantasy) scene. Add sunset or [evening](#evening) when the time of [day](#day) is clear.

entries.name: yellow_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) is coloured yellow, from a [sunset](#sunset) glow, [dust](#dust) or a stylised palette. Tag sky; add sunset when that is the cause.

entries.name: huge_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) fills much of the [sky](#sky), drawn far larger than it would really appear. It makes a dramatic [backdrop](#backdrop) for silhouettes, [night](#night) scenes and [fantasy](#fantasy) settings.

entries.name: black_sky
entries.description: A [sky](#sky) rendered black or close to it, as on a starless [night](#night), during an [eclipse](#eclipse) or out in vacuum. Where the stars are the point, [night_sky](#night_sky) or [starry_sky](#starry_sky) serves better.

entries.name: clear_sky
entries.description: A [sky](#sky) with [no](#no) clouds or almost none, at any hour of the [day](#day). The opposite of [cloudy_sky](#cloudy_sky) and [overcast](#overcast).

entries.name: galaxy
entries.description: A [swirl](#swirl) of stars, [dust](#dust) and [glowing](#glowing) [gas](#gas) [hanging](#hanging) in the picture, drawn either as a [spiral](#spiral) disc or as a purple-blue haze speckled with white points. Use it for cosmic skies and [space](#space) backdrops.

entries.name: aurora
entries.description: Sheets and ribbons of coloured light rippling across a [night](#night) [sky](#sky), seen far to the north or far to the south. Night_sky usually goes with it, and often a snowbound [landscape](#landscape) below.

entries.name: above_clouds
entries.description: The viewpoint sits high in the [sky](#sky) with the [cloud](#cloud) layer spread out below it, as from an [aircraft](#aircraft), a peak or a [flying](#flying) character. Cloud tops rather than open ground fill the lower frame.

entries.name: white_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) itself is rendered flat white, whether from [overcast](#overcast) weather, [falling](#falling) [snow](#snow), glare, or a deliberate flat colour [choice](#choice). It differs from [white_background](#white_background), which is a blank [backdrop](#backdrop) rather than sky.

entries.name: milky_way
entries.description: The bright band of our own [galaxy](#galaxy) seen edge-on, [stretching](#stretching) across a clear [night](#night) [sky](#sky).

entries.name: red_clouds
entries.description: Cloud banks lit or painted red, either [caught](#caught) by a low [sun](#sun) or coloured that way to make the [sky](#sky) feel hostile. They set the mood of the whole background.

entries.name: nebula
entries.description: A [glowing](#glowing) [cloud](#cloud) of [gas](#gas) and [dust](#dust) in [space](#space), left over from an exploded star and the material of new ones. It is drawn as a colourful [backdrop](#backdrop) to cosmic scenes.

entries.name: moon_phases
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) shown several times over in its changing [shapes](#shapes) and lined up in sequence, [running](#running) from full through gibbous and [crescent](#crescent) to new. Often drawn as a decorative band rather than as [sky](#sky).

entries.name: pink_clouds
entries.description: Clouds tinted pink, usually by a low [sun](#sun) at [dawn](#dawn) or [dusk](#dusk), or as part of a pastel dream [sky](#sky). The colour of the sky behind them has its own tags.

entries.name: meteor_shower
entries.description: Many meteors crossing the [night](#night) [sky](#sky) at once, their trails [fanning](#fanning) out from a single point overhead. A [backdrop](#backdrop) for wish-making and quiet nighttime scenes.

entries.name: dark_clouds
entries.description: Cloud [cover](#cover) painted in deep grey, blue or black rather than white or pale grey. Whatever colour does the darkening, it reads as a gathering [storm](#storm) or a turn for the worse.

entries.name: black_hole
entries.description: A [collapsed](#collapsed) star whose gravity lets nothing escape, drawn as a [dark](#dark) disc ringed by a [glowing](#glowing) accretion [halo](#halo) and bent starlight. At home in [space](#space) and cosmic-scale scenes.

entries.name: green_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) is washed in shades of green, something that almost never occurs in life. It is chosen for [alien](#alien) worlds, strange [storm](#storm) light and generally unsettling scenes.

entries.name: comet
entries.description: An icy body trailing a long bright [tail](#tail) as it crosses the [sky](#sky). A [meteor](#meteor), which burns up [falling](#falling) through the atmosphere, is a different thing.

entries.name: orange_clouds
entries.description: Cloud banks lit orange, nearly always by a low [sun](#sun) at [dawn](#dawn) or [dusk](#dusk), setting a warm [sky](#sky) behind the scene.

entries.name: eclipse
entries.description: One heavenly body passing into another's [shadow](#shadow). A solar one is drawn as a bright [ring](#ring) round a black disc, a lunar one as a [moon](#moon) washed deep red.

entries.name: red_sun
entries.description: The [sun](#sun) rendered as a red disc, whether low and reddened near the [horizon](#horizon) or coloured that way to make the [sky](#sky) feel [alien](#alien) or apocalyptic.

entries.name: meteor
entries.description: A [rock](#rock) [burning](#burning) as it falls through the atmosphere, ranging from a bright speck to a mountain-sized mass. Use [shooting_star](#shooting_star) when only a streak of light is visible, since a [comet](#comet) never actually enters the air.

entries.name: saturn_(planet)
entries.description: The sixth [planet](#planet), known at a [glance](#glance) by the wide flat [ring](#ring) system around it. Rings drawn around any other world take [planetary_ring](#planetary_ring) instead.

entries.name: multicolored_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) overhead holds several colours at once, as it does at [sunrise](#sunrise) and [sunset](#sunset). Reserve it for pictures where the sky takes up a real share of the frame rather than a thin strip behind the subject.

entries.name: planetary_ring
entries.description: A flat band of [ice](#ice) and [dust](#dust) circling a [planet](#planet), most famous around Saturn. Seen in [space](#space) scenes or through a viewport.

entries.name: in_orbit
entries.description: A scene set circling a [planet](#planet) or [moon](#moon), with the curve of the world filling part of the frame. Stations, ships and [drifting](#drifting) figures hang against it.

entries.name: asteroid
entries.description: A rocky or metallic body [drifting](#drifting) in [space](#space), airless and irregular in [outline](#outline). Whole fields of them often serve as a science-fiction [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: star_trail
entries.description: Stars drawn with streaks behind them, [imitating](#imitating) a long-exposure photograph of the turning [sky](#sky). If only a few stars have tails, they are shooting stars instead.

entries.name: yellow_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) drawn in a yellow tone rather than white or silver. A frequent [choice](#choice) for [autumn](#autumn) nights and harvest scenes.

entries.name: big_dipper
entries.description: The seven bright stars of Ursa Major set out like a [ladle](#ladle) with a bent [handle](#handle). Drawn in a [night](#night) [sky](#sky), sometimes with lines joining them; the Little Dipper's handle curves the other way.

entries.name: gemini_(constellation)
entries.description: The star pattern of the Twins picked out in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky), its two brightest points named Castor and Pollux. Use it when the star [figure](#figure) itself is drawn, not merely the [zodiac](#zodiac) [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: starry_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon), usually a [crescent](#crescent), drawn with stars inside its [dark](#dark) portion, so it reads as a flat shape instead of a sphere [blocking](#blocking) the [sky](#sky) behind it. A stylisation or a slip; it does not apply where the moon is treated as a solid object a character [can](#can) sit on.

entries.name: black_sun
entries.description: A [sun](#sun) drawn as a [dark](#dark) disc against the [sky](#sky), usually to make a scene ominous or apocalyptic. It is neither a solar [eclipse](#eclipse), where the [moon](#moon) does the [blocking](#blocking), nor a wheel-shaped occult [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: half_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) lit on one side only, showing a clean straight edge down the middle. Corresponds to the quarter phases of the lunar cycle.

entries.name: cancer_(constellation)
entries.description: The faint [zodiac](#zodiac) star pattern of the Crab, [lying](#lying) between Gemini and Leo. Its stars are drawn either as a lopsided Y or as a small four-sided [figure](#figure) with [legs](#legs) trailing off the corners.

entries.name: leo_(constellation)
entries.description: The lion's star pattern drawn into a [night](#night) [sky](#sky) as points joined by lines. Its curved [sickle](#sickle) of a head makes it easy to pick out.

entries.name: cassiopeia_(constellation)
entries.description: The northern star group whose five bright points trace a lopsided W or M. Named for a [queen](#queen) of Greek legend, it appears mostly on drawn star charts and [night](#night) skies.

entries.name: libra_(constellation)
entries.description: The [scales](#scales) drawn as a star pattern in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky), points joined by lines. It sits in the southern sky between the neighbouring [zodiac](#zodiac) figures.

entries.name: taurus_(constellation)
entries.description: The star pattern of the [bull](#bull), its two long [horns](#horns) branching from a bright V-shaped face anchored by a prominent orange star. Drawn against a [night](#night) [sky](#sky), sometimes with lines connecting the stars into the [figure](#figure).

entries.name: multiple_moons
entries.description: More than one [moon](#moon) hangs in the [sky](#sky), quick shorthand for an [alien](#alien) world or a [fantasy](#fantasy) setting. Sizes and phases may vary freely; one moon drawn through its cycle is [moon_phases](#moon_phases).

entries.name: brown_sky
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) rendered brown, as under [dust](#dust), smog or a [sandstorm](#sandstorm). It is also a quick way to mark a ruined, poisoned or [alien](#alien) world.

entries.name: solar_eclipse
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) passing directly between the [sun](#sun) and the earth, either [biting](#biting) a piece out of the sun's disk or covering it entirely and leaving a blazing [ring](#ring) of corona. Fiction often uses it to mark an ominous turning point.

entries.name: jupiter_(planet)
entries.description: The striped [gas](#gas) [giant](#giant) of the outer solar system, picked out by its great red [storm](#storm) and a thin [ring](#ring). It hangs in [space](#space) or looms over an [alien](#alien) [sky](#sky).

entries.name: capricorn_(constellation)
entries.description: The [zodiac](#zodiac) star pattern of the sea [goat](#goat), smallest of the twelve, [sitting](#sitting) between Sagittarius and Aquarius. Its stars [sketch](#sketch) out a shape read either as an arrowhead or as a D drawn to a point.

entries.name: scorpius_(constellation)
entries.description: The [scorpion](#scorpion) [constellation](#constellation), a long hooked sweep of stars with red Antares [burning](#burning) at its [heart](#heart). Drawn as a star [chart](#chart) or picked out against a [night](#night) [sky](#sky).

entries.name: virgo_(constellation)
entries.description: The star pattern of the maiden, largest of the [zodiac](#zodiac) constellations and anchored by the bright star Spica. Drawn as joined stars in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky) rather than as the sign's glyph.

entries.name: sagittarius_(constellation)
entries.description: The archer [constellation](#constellation) of the southern [sky](#sky), whose brightest stars form the shape [people](#people) know as the Teapot. Use it for the drawn star pattern, not for the [zodiac](#zodiac) [sign](#sign) itself.

entries.name: pisces_(constellation)
entries.description: The faint V-shaped star pattern of the Fishes, [sitting](#sitting) in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky) between Aquarius and Aries. Use it for the drawn star [map](#map) itself, not for the [zodiac](#zodiac) [sign](#sign) the shape lends its name to.

entries.name: aries_(constellation)
entries.description: The ram's small star group in the northern [sky](#sky), its brightest point Hamal, drawn as [dots](#dots) joined by lines. The bare glyph is [aries_(symbol)](#aries_(symbol)) and ram-themed art is [aries_(zodiac)](#aries_(zodiac)).

entries.name: orion_(constellation)
entries.description: The hunter [constellation](#constellation), drawn or picked out in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky) by its [hourglass](#hourglass) of bright stars with the three-star [belt](#belt) across the middle. Red Betelgeuse marks one shoulder and blue Rigel the opposite foot.

entries.name: aquarius_(constellation)
entries.description: The star pattern of the Water Bearer drawn into a [night](#night) [sky](#sky), often with lines joining the stars and the little Y-shaped [jar](#jar) group at its top. Keep it for the stars themselves: the glyph is [aquarius_(symbol)](#aquarius_(symbol)) and themed artwork [aquarius_(zodiac)](#aquarius_(zodiac)).

entries.name: blue_moon
entries.description: A [moon](#moon) drawn pale blue instead of white or yellow, usually to cool the mood of a [night](#night) scene. The saying about rarity concerns a calendar quirk, not the colour.

entries.name: mars_(planet)
entries.description: The fourth [planet](#planet) out from the [sun](#sun), rust-orange from the iron oxide [dust](#dust) over its surface. Seen from [space](#space), [hanging](#hanging) in a [sky](#sky), or as a [landscape](#landscape) of red [desert](#desert).

entries.name: gibbous_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) lit across more than half its face but not yet full, so one edge stays in [shadow](#shadow). It falls between the half moon and the full moon in the cycle.

entries.name: broken_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) hangs in the [sky](#sky) [split](#split) apart or [shattered](#shattered), with fragments [drifting](#drifting) away from the main body. It is stock [scenery](#scenery) for a ruined or otherworldly world, whether or not a character caused it.

entries.name: cygnus_(constellation)
entries.description: The Swan, a northern [constellation](#constellation) laid out like a long-necked [bird](#bird) in flight and read as the Northern Cross for its bright central limbs. Deneb, one point of the Summer Triangle, is its brightest star.

entries.name: pink_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) drawn pink in the [sky](#sky), chosen for mood rather than for astronomy. Its phase is left to the other moon tags.

entries.name: solar_system
entries.description: The [sun](#sun) shown together with its orbiting planets, either as bodies in [space](#space) or as a [diagram](#diagram) of rings. Usually rendered as a decorative arrangement rather than to scale.

entries.name: venus_(planet)
entries.description: The second [planet](#planet) from the [sun](#sun), shown as a pale clouded sphere in [space](#space) or plotted in a [diagram](#diagram) of the solar system, [sitting](#sitting) between Mercury and Earth.

entries.name: universe
entries.description: The wider cosmos as [backdrop](#backdrop) or subject, with fields of stars, nebulae and galaxies [stretching](#stretching) away behind or through a [figure](#figure). Broader in [scope](#scope) than an ordinary [night](#night) [sky](#sky) over a [landscape](#landscape).

entries.name: neptune_(planet)
entries.description: The eighth [planet](#planet), a deep blue [ice](#ice) [giant](#giant) far out in the solar system. It turns up in [space](#space) scenes, through telescopes and on diagrams of the planets.

entries.name: lyra_(constellation)
entries.description: The small northern [constellation](#constellation) of the [lyre](#lyre), drawn into a [night](#night) [sky](#sky) as a parallelogram with a short arm [running](#running) off one [corner](#corner) to the bright star Vega. It is named for the [instrument](#instrument) of Orpheus.

entries.name: moon_reflection
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) mirrored on [water](#water) or another polished surface, so that the disc appears twice in the frame. A [staple](#staple) of [night](#night) scenes over a [lake](#lake), the sea or a [puddle](#puddle).

entries.name: orange_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) shown orange in the [sky](#sky), as it looks low on the [horizon](#horizon) or through haze and [smoke](#smoke). Sets an [evening](#evening) or uneasy mood.

entries.name: crux_(constellation)
entries.description: The Southern Cross, smallest of the constellations, its four bright stars forming a slightly tilted [cross](#cross) low in southern skies. Drawn as a star pattern in a [night](#night) [sky](#sky) or as the [emblem](#emblem) on several national flags.

entries.name: purple_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) rendered purple in the [sky](#sky), a shorthand for an eerie, magical, or otherworldly [night](#night). Distinct from a moon that is merely tinted by a coloured sky around it.

entries.name: uranus_(planet)
entries.description: The pale blue-green seventh [planet](#planet), shown [floating](#floating) in [space](#space) or plotted in a [diagram](#diagram) of the solar system, [lying](#lying) between Saturn and Neptune.

entries.name: black_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) shows as a solid black disc rather than the usual pale one. It belongs to ominous, occult and otherworldly skies.

entries.name: green_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) hangs green in the [sky](#sky). The colour is nearly always chosen to give the scene an eerie or magical atmosphere.

entries.name: brown_moon
entries.description: The [moon](#moon) rendered in a brown or earthen tone instead of white or pale yellow. An unusual colouring that tends to signal [dust](#dust), [eclipse](#eclipse) light or an unearthly setting.

entries.name: wind
entries.description: A breeze or gust visibly moves through the scene, [stirring](#stirring) hair, [clothes](#clothes), leaves, or [grass](#grass). Pair it with [floating_hair](#floating_hair) when hair itself is in motion, and [wind_lift](#wind_lift) when the wind lifts a garment.

entries.name: rain
entries.description: Rain falls somewhere in the scene, drawn as streaks or individual drops, often alongside umbrellas, puddles, and soaked clothing. Combine with [wet](#wet) or [umbrella](#umbrella) depending on what is shown.

entries.name: snowing
entries.description: Snow shown actively [falling](#falling) from the [sky](#sky). Add [snow](#snow) as [well](#well) only if snow has also settled on the ground.

entries.name: lightning
entries.description: Natural lightning [flashing](#flashing) across a stormy [sky](#sky). Bolts thrown by a character or [weapon](#weapon) are [electricity](#electricity), and the small zig-zag icon is [lightning_bolt_symbol](#lightning_bolt_symbol).

entries.name: fog
entries.description: Low [cloud](#cloud) [lying](#lying) along the ground or the [water](#water), softening the scene and [cutting](#cutting) how far anything [can](#can) be seen. It ranges from a faint haze to a [blanket](#blanket) that swallows the background.

entries.name: overcast
entries.description: The [sky](#sky) is sealed completely under a grey layer of [cloud](#cloud), with [no](#no) blue showing anywhere. Partial cloud [cover](#cover) belongs to [cloudy_sky](#cloudy_sky) instead.

entries.name: storm
entries.description: Violent weather with [strong](#strong) [wind](#wind) and [driving](#driving) [rain](#rain), often with [dark](#dark) clouds and [lightning](#lightning).

entries.name: thunder
entries.description: The rumble of a [storm](#storm) rather than the [flash](#flash) of it. Reserve it for posts with [sound](#sound) where the noise is actually audible, or where a drawn onomatopoeia stands in for it; a silent picture of a bolt in the [sky](#sky) is [lightning](#lightning).

entries.name: blizzard
entries.description: A violent [snowstorm](#snowstorm) with [snow](#snow) driven [sideways](#sideways) by [wind](#wind) and visibility cut to almost nothing. Far heavier and more chaotic than ordinary [falling](#falling) snow.

entries.name: snowstorm
entries.description: Heavy snowfall driven by [strong](#strong) [wind](#wind), thick enough to swallow the background. Characters lean into it, [shield](#shield) their faces, and leave tracks that fill [back](#back) in behind them.

entries.name: tornado
entries.description: A rotating funnel of [wind](#wind) [reaching](#reaching) down from a [storm](#storm) [cloud](#cloud), [dragging](#dragging) up [dust](#dust) and [debris](#debris) as it moves. In fiction it is as often conjured by a character or [device](#device) as it is ordinary weather.

entries.name: after_rain
entries.description: A scene [caught](#caught) just as a shower has passed: puddles, [dripping](#dripping) eaves, a [rainbow](#rainbow), an [umbrella](#umbrella) being shaken out or closed. No drops are [falling](#falling) in the frame itself.

entries.name: frost
entries.description: A thin white crust of [ice](#ice) crystals [lying](#lying) over [grass](#grass), [glass](#glass), branches or other surfaces. It marks a [cold](#cold) [morning](#morning); flakes coming down belong to [snowing](#snowing).

entries.name: storm_cloud
entries.description: Dark [heavy](#heavy) [cloud](#cloud) gathered for [rain](#rain) or [thunder](#thunder), often with a flat base and [lightning](#lightning) [working](#working) inside it. Sets a threatening or dramatic [sky](#sky).

entries.name: sandstorm
entries.description: Wind [driving](#driving) great clouds of [sand](#sand) across dry country, blotting out the [horizon](#horizon). Figures [caught](#caught) in one [shield](#shield) their faces and their [clothes](#clothes) [stream](#stream) [sideways](#sideways).

entries.name: day
entries.description: The scene takes place in daytime, lit by daylight. The counterpart of [night](#night), [evening](#evening) and [dawn](#dawn) among the time-of-day tags.

entries.name: night
entries.description: The scene takes place after [dark](#dark), under a black or deep blue [sky](#sky). Light comes from the [moon](#moon), lamps or windows rather than the [sun](#sun).

entries.name: sunset
entries.description: The [sun](#sun) [dropping](#dropping) below the [horizon](#horizon) in the [evening](#evening), with orange or red [sky](#sky) tones. Once the sun is gone, [tag](#tag) [dusk](#dusk); whitish or yellow hues point more toward [sunrise](#sunrise).

entries.name: winter
entries.description: A scene set during winter, shown through [cold](#cold) or snowy weather, bare trees, and thinner daylight. Winter activities like [building](#building) a [snowman](#snowman) or warming up under a [kotatsu](#kotatsu), and [heavy](#heavy) winter clothing, also count, but the setting itself must show the season rather than just a wintry mood in the background.

entries.name: summer
entries.description: A scene clearly set in summer: blazing [sun](#sun) and blue [sky](#sky), light [clothes](#clothes) and swimsuits, [beach](#beach) trips, festivals, hand fans and [cold](#cold) treats like shaved [ice](#ice). Use it for the setting itself, not for a vaguely seasonal background.

entries.name: evening
entries.description: The close of the [day](#day) as the [sun](#sun) goes down, with low warm light and long shadows. Wider than [sunset](#sunset) or [dusk](#dusk), covering the whole late part of the day, and often drawn with an orange [sky](#sky).

entries.name: autumn
entries.description: The season is on show: leaves turning red and [gold](#gold), harvest foods, and scarves and knitwear coming out again as the light shortens. The leaves themselves take [autumn_leaves](#autumn_leaves).

entries.name: twilight
entries.description: The glow left in the [sky](#sky) after the [sun](#sun) has set or shortly before it rises, with the sun's disc itself fully out of view. If any part of the sun still shows, use [sunset](#sunset) or [sunrise](#sunrise) instead.

entries.name: dusk
entries.description: The stretch just after the [sun](#sun) has gone below the [horizon](#horizon), the [sky](#sky) still [burning](#burning) orange, red and purple with [no](#no) sun in sight. If any part of the disc still shows, use [sunset](#sunset).

entries.name: sunrise
entries.description: The [sun](#sun) coming up over the [horizon](#horizon) in the [morning](#morning), with whitish or yellow [sky](#sky) tones. Without a visible sun, [tag](#tag) [dawn](#dawn) instead; reddish skies point more toward [sunset](#sunset).

entries.name: morning
entries.description: The scene is set in the early part of the [day](#day): low slanting [sun](#sun), someone getting out of [bed](#bed), [breakfast](#breakfast) on the [table](#table) or the walk to [school](#school) or work. The [tag](#tag) fixes when it happens, not what anybody is doing.

entries.name: spring_(season)
entries.description: The scene is visibly set in spring, signalled by [cherry](#cherry) blossoms, fresh flowers, new greenery or seasonal festivities.

entries.name: dawn
entries.description: The stretch before the [sun](#sun) clears the [horizon](#horizon), when the [sky](#sky) is already pale blue and yellow but [no](#no) disc shows. Once any sliver of the sun appears, [sunrise](#sunrise) takes over.

entries.name: seasons
entries.description: All four seasons shown at once, usually as four panels or as a single scene divided between spring, [summer](#summer), [autumn](#autumn), and [winter](#winter).

entries.name: day_and_night
entries.description: Daylight and [night](#night) occupy the same picture at once, often [split](#split) down the middle or mirrored across two halves. Usually there to set two characters or two moods against each other; [dusk](#dusk), [twilight](#twilight) and [sunset](#sunset) are separate tags.

entries.name: window
entries.description: A [glass](#glass) [opening](#opening) set into the wall of a [building](#building) or vehicle. Breasts pressed against the glass now fall under [breast_press](#breast_press) rather than this [tag](#tag), and a software interface window is tagged separately as [window_(computing)](#window_(computing)).

entries.name: stairs
entries.description: A flight of steps leading up or down, whether [indoors](#indoors) or out. Covers staircases, stairways and open-air steps alike.

entries.name: railing
entries.description: A low barrier with a [handrail](#handrail) [running](#running) along a [walkway](#walkway), [bridge](#bridge), staircase, [balcony](#balcony), or [platform](#platform). Often leaned on or sat upon; combine with the surrounding location.

entries.name: door
entries.description: A door of any sort, hinged, [sliding](#sliding) or revolving, set in a [building](#building), a room, a vehicle or a [cupboard](#cupboard). Japanese [shouji](#shouji) and [fusuma](#fusuma) panels count.

entries.name: sliding_doors
entries.description: Doors that [slide](#slide) [sideways](#sideways) instead of [swinging](#swinging), whether automatic [glass](#glass) doors or the [fusuma](#fusuma) and shoji of Japanese rooms.

entries.name: floor
entries.description: The floor of a room is a visible part of the picture, boarded, tiled or carpeted. Often tagged where a character lies or sits straight on it.

entries.name: pillar
entries.description: An upright shaft [holding](#holding) up a [building](#building), or a freestanding one raised as a monument, in stone, wood or metal. Ornamental classical shafts with base and capital are tagged [column](#column).

entries.name: open_door
entries.description: A [door](#door) in the scene stands open, [giving](#giving) a view of the room or the [outdoors](#outdoors) past it. A door still being pushed or pulled, with a hand on it, is [opening_door](#opening_door).

entries.name: doorway
entries.description: The framed [opening](#opening) a [door](#door) fills, or the sheltered entry just outside one. A [figure](#figure) [standing](#standing) in one is a stock composition.

entries.name: ceiling
entries.description: The upper surface of a room is in shot, usually because the view looks upward or comes from very low down. Beams, panels and fixtures on it come with the territory.

entries.name: shouji
entries.description: A Japanese [sliding](#sliding) panel of [translucent](#translucent) [paper](#paper) stretched over a wooden [lattice](#lattice), used as a [door](#door), [window](#window) or room divider that lets light through without allowing a clear view. Fusuma are the opaque, thick-papered equivalent. Implies [sliding_doors](#sliding_doors).

entries.name: smokestack
entries.description: An [industrial](#industrial) funnel venting [smoke](#smoke) from a [factory](#factory), [ship](#ship) or [locomotive](#locomotive). On a [house](#house) it is a [chimney](#chimney).

entries.name: stained_glass
entries.description: Sectioned panes of coloured [glass](#glass) set in a leaded pattern, as in [church](#church) windows. Also covers artwork drawn in that mosaic-like style.

entries.name: arch
entries.description: A curved [structure](#structure) spanning an [opening](#opening), [carrying](#carrying) [weight](#weight) around the sweep of the curve: doorways, gateways, [bridge](#bridge) spans and colonnades. It refers to the built form, not to a [spine](#spine) bent backwards, which is [arched_back](#arched_back).

entries.name: balcony
entries.description: A railed [platform](#platform) jutting out from an upper [floor](#floor), where the character stands, leans on the rail or sits looking out. Tag the wider setting too, such as [city](#city) or [night](#night).

entries.name: veranda
entries.description: A roofed open [porch](#porch) or gallery [running](#running) along the side of a [house](#house). The traditional Japanese engawa, a wooden [walkway](#walkway) under the eaves of a home, is covered by the same [tag](#tag).

entries.name: column
entries.description: A decorative [pillar](#pillar), usually stone and either round or many-sided, [carrying](#carrying) a [spreading](#spreading) capital at the top and a moulded base. Without those features it is simply a pillar.

entries.name: opening_door
entries.description: A [door](#door) [caught](#caught) mid-motion as it is opened, with a hand on the [handle](#handle) or the panel [swinging](#swinging). Once it simply stands open, [open_door](#open_door) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: open_window
entries.description: A [window](#window) that has been pushed open, letting in air and often setting the [curtains](#curtains) moving.

entries.name: round_window
entries.description: A circular [window](#window), like a ship's porthole or a round [opening](#opening) in a wall.

entries.name: chimney
entries.description: A [brick](#brick) or stone flue rising from a roof to carry [smoke](#smoke) away. The equivalent on a [ship](#ship), a [locomotive](#locomotive) or a [factory](#factory) is a [smokestack](#smokestack).

entries.name: lattice
entries.description: Ornamental wooden grille panels of the kind set into Chinese windows and furniture, making geometric patterns behind a subject. A frame for [climbing](#climbing) plants is a [trellis](#trellis), and laced clothing is [cross-laced_clothes](#cross-laced_clothes).

entries.name: stone_stairs
entries.description: A staircase made of stone, such as the steps up to a [shrine](#shrine) or through a [castle](#castle).

entries.name: windowsill
entries.description: The [ledge](#ledge) [running](#running) along the bottom of a [window](#window). Characters often sit on it, lean against it, or rest an object there.

entries.name: porch
entries.description: A roofed, open-sided [platform](#platform) at the front of a [house](#house), with wooden floorboards and steps. A typical setting for lazy [summer](#summer) scenes; the Japanese [veranda](#veranda) is engawa.

entries.name: hole
entries.description: A visible [opening](#opening), pit or cavity: a gap [punched](#punched) through a wall, [floor](#floor) or [cloth](#cloth), or a pit dug into the ground. It covers openings in objects as [well](#well) as excavations in the earth.

entries.name: broken_window
entries.description: A [window](#window) with its pane smashed or cracked, with or without [shards](#shards) drawn in. Add window and [broken_glass](#broken_glass); something crashing through at that moment also takes [breaking](#breaking).

entries.name: elevator
entries.description: A lift [carrying](#carrying) [people](#people) between floors, shown as the [car](#car) itself or as the doors on a [landing](#landing). Scenes often play out inside the [cramped](#cramped) [interior](#interior) or while [waiting](#waiting) in front of it.

entries.name: fusuma
entries.description: An opaque [sliding](#sliding) panel used as a [door](#door) or room divider in Japanese houses, with a recessed round pull and often a painted scene. Unlike [shouji](#shouji) it lets [no](#no) light through and shows no wooden [lattice](#lattice).

entries.name: doorknob
entries.description: The round grip on a [door](#door) that turns to free the latch. Lever-shaped fittings go under [door_handle](#door_handle).

entries.name: awning
entries.description: A [cover](#cover) fixed to the outside of a [building](#building) above a [window](#window), a [doorway](#doorway) or a stretch of [pavement](#pavement), keeping [rain](#rain) and [sun](#sun) off what is beneath. On shops it usually carries the business name; a freestanding four-legged canopy is not one.

entries.name: bars
entries.description: A row of upright metal bars, as across a cell [door](#door), a [cage](#cage) or a [window](#window) [opening](#opening). They stand between the viewer and whatever is behind them.

entries.name: glass_door
entries.description: A [door](#door) glazed over all or part of its area, so what lies beyond stays partly in view. Common on shopfronts, balconies and modern interiors.

entries.name: dome
entries.description: A rounded roof shaped like the top half of a sphere, crowning a [cathedral](#cathedral), mosque, capitol or observatory. Counts whether seen from outside or looked up at from within.

entries.name: entrance
entries.description: The way into a [building](#building): a [doorway](#doorway) with a step down, a [mat](#mat), and room to leave [shoes](#shoes) — the genkan of a Japanese [house](#house). It also fits the entry halls of schools, shops and other public buildings.

entries.name: handrail
entries.description: The rounded rail along the top of a balustrade or bolted to a wall, shaped to be gripped. Stairs, escalators and ramps are where it usually turns up.

entries.name: broken_wall
entries.description: A wall smashed open by force, with [rubble](#rubble) around the [hole](#hole) or a whole section [collapsed](#collapsed). It is often the route by which something large came through.

entries.name: grate
entries.description: A frame of [bars](#bars) or a [mesh](#mesh) panel set into a [floor](#floor), wall or [window](#window), letting air, light or [water](#water) through while stopping anything larger. Common over drains, vents and barred openings.

entries.name: door_handle
entries.description: The lever-shaped grip fitted to a [door](#door) for [opening](#opening) it. A round turning fitting is a [doorknob](#doorknob) instead.

entries.name: wooden_door
entries.description: A [door](#door) made of planks or panelled timber, sometimes reinforced with iron fittings. It appears equally in ordinary homes, cabins, and dungeons.

entries.name: escalator
entries.description: A moving staircase [carrying](#carrying) [people](#people) between floors, its metal treads and rubber [handrail](#handrail) [cutting](#cutting) diagonally through the frame. Familiar from [shopping](#shopping) centres, stations and airports.

entries.name: truss
entries.description: A framework of beams braced into triangles to carry a load. Seen [holding](#holding) up roofs, bridges and [stage](#stage) [rigging](#rigging), and typical of [construction](#construction) sites.

entries.name: spire
entries.description: A tapering [structure](#structure) crowning a [tower](#tower) or [rooftop](#rooftop), narrowing to a point at the top. Common on churches, castles and fantastical skylines.

entries.name: wooden_ceiling
entries.description: A [ceiling](#ceiling) made of exposed boards or timber panels overhead, often the first thing seen when a character lies on their [back](#back). Traditional houses and cabins share the look.

entries.name: steel_beam
entries.description: A long metal girder of the kind that frames a [building](#building) under [construction](#construction), often shown as an exposed span someone sits or walks along. Turns up on building sites and [scaffolding](#scaffolding). A [lattice](#lattice) support made of joined triangles is a [truss](#truss) instead.

entries.name: stairwell
entries.description: The enclosed vertical shaft inside a [building](#building) that carries [stairs](#stairs) between floors, complete with landings and a [railing](#railing). Steps out in the open air are simply stairs.

entries.name: hole_in_wall
entries.description: A wall has been [broken](#broken) open, leaving a ragged gap [punched](#punched), blasted or smashed through it. Often the aftermath of a fight, and sometimes shaped like whoever went through.

entries.name: drainpipe
entries.description: The gutters and downspouts [running](#running) along a roof and down a wall to carry rainwater away. A [staple](#staple) of [alley](#alley) and [rooftop](#rooftop) backgrounds, and occasionally climbed.

entries.name: spiral_staircase
entries.description: A flight of steps winding upward around a central [column](#column), found in towers, lighthouses and grand halls. Often drawn from directly above or below to show the coil.

entries.name: platform
entries.description: A raised flat surface built to stand on, anything from a [stage](#stage) or dais to a railway platform or a [floating](#floating) slab. Prefer a more exact [tag](#tag) once the kind of platform is clear.

entries.name: window_shutter
entries.description: Solid or louvred panels set in a frame beside a [window](#window) and hinged to close over it. Blinds, which hang loose inside the window [opening](#opening) rather than being framed beside it, are a different fitting.

entries.name: wooden_railing
entries.description: A [handrail](#handrail) and its posts made of wood, [running](#running) along a [balcony](#balcony), staircase, or [veranda](#veranda). Characters lean on it constantly.

entries.name: muntins
entries.description: The slim [bars](#bars) that divide a [window](#window) into a [grid](#grid) of small panes. They may sit purely for looks over a single sheet of [glass](#glass), or stand in a frame with [no](#no) glass behind them at all.

entries.name: hatch
entries.description: A [heavy](#heavy) sealing [door](#door) of the sort fitted to tanks, submarines, ships, [spacecraft](#spacecraft) and [mecha](#mecha), made to hold against pressure or blast. Usually round or oval, ringed with bolts or closed by a [wheel](#wheel). Nothing to do with an [egg](#egg).

entries.name: iron_bars
entries.description: Lengths of iron or steel used as [structure](#structure) or as a barrier, [plain](#plain) or angled in section. They close off cells and windows and give [industrial](#industrial) settings their [skeleton](#skeleton).

entries.name: corner
entries.description: The angle where two walls meet, [indoors](#indoors) or out. Often used to [box](#box) a character in or to tuck them away from the rest of the scene.

entries.name: skylight
entries.description: A glazed [opening](#opening) set into a roof or [ceiling](#ceiling) to let daylight down into the room below. Often used to drop a shaft of light onto the subject.

entries.name: broken_pillar
entries.description: A [column](#column) snapped off partway up, or toppled and [lying](#lying) in segments on the ground. Standard furniture for [ruins](#ruins) and ancient sites.

entries.name: arched_window
entries.description: A [window](#window) whose top finishes in a curve, rounded or pointed, instead of a straight lintel. Typical of churches, castles and older European buildings.

entries.name: vent_(object)
entries.description: An [opening](#opening) that lets air or [gas](#gas) pass into or out of an enclosed [space](#space), usually covered by a grille. The duct [running](#running) behind it is a separate object entirely.

entries.name: stone_pillar
entries.description: An upright [column](#column) cut from stone, [standing](#standing) alone or in a row. Belongs to [ruins](#ruins), [shrine](#shrine) grounds and [temple](#temple) [architecture](#architecture).

entries.name: barred_window
entries.description: A [window](#window) with iron [bars](#bars) or a metal [lattice](#lattice) fixed across the [glass](#glass), put there to keep intruders out or somebody in. Cells, basements and shopfronts carry them.

entries.name: elevator_door
entries.description: The [sliding](#sliding) doors of a lift, shut in a lobby or parting to show the [car](#car). Handy for framing someone [stepping](#stepping) in or out, and a common detail in corridor scenes.

entries.name: arcade_(architecture)
entries.description: A run of arches carried on columns or piers, each one bracing the next, often forming a covered [walkway](#walkway). Nothing to do with game halls, which take the [plain](#plain) [arcade](#arcade) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: ventilation_shaft
entries.description: The duct or [tunnel](#tunnel) [running](#running) behind a vent, drawn wide enough in fiction for a character to crawl through, a [staple](#staple) of infiltration and escape scenes.

entries.name: closing_door
entries.description: A [door](#door) [caught](#caught) mid-swing as it is pushed shut, still ajar in the frame. What sets it apart from a plainly open or closed door is the motion.

entries.name: doorbell
entries.description: A button or chime beside an [entrance](#entrance) that announces a caller. Usually a small detail on the doorframe, sometimes with a finger [reaching](#reaching) for it.

entries.name: ledge
entries.description: A flat surface set high enough above the ground that anyone [sitting](#sitting) on it has their [legs](#legs) [hanging](#hanging) free. Rooftop edges, [window](#window) sills and the tops of low walls all qualify.

entries.name: glass_wall
entries.description: A wall glazed from [floor](#floor) to [ceiling](#ceiling), as in an [office](#office) block, an [aquarium](#aquarium) or an observation deck. It keeps the far side in the picture while still dividing the [space](#space).

entries.name: radiator
entries.description: The finned metal panel that heats a room by circulating [hot](#hot) [water](#water) or [steam](#steam), usually [standing](#standing) under a [window](#window). Refers to the household [heater](#heater) rather than the cooling unit in a [car](#car) [engine](#engine).

entries.name: broken_door
entries.description: A [door](#door) knocked off its hinges, splintered or [punched](#punched) through, leaving a gap where it should have closed. Usually somebody has [forced](#forced) their way in.

entries.name: battlement
entries.description: The notched parapet [running](#running) along the top of a [castle](#castle) wall or [tower](#tower). Defenders shoot through the gaps and take [cover](#cover) behind the raised blocks between them.

entries.name: catwalk_(walkway)
entries.description: A narrow raised gangway fenced by railings, often of grated steel, [running](#running) above the [floor](#floor) of a [factory](#factory), [warehouse](#warehouse) or [ship](#ship). Industrial infrastructure, not the [runway](#runway) a [fashion](#fashion) [model](#model) walks.

entries.name: trap_door
entries.description: A hinged panel set into a [floor](#floor) or [ceiling](#ceiling) instead of a wall. Overhead it usually opens onto an attic or loft, and underfoot onto a cellar, crawlspace or hidden room.

entries.name: wooden_beam
entries.description: A structural length of timber crossing a [ceiling](#ceiling) or [holding](#holding) up a roof. Exposed beams mark [old](#old) houses, barns, and attic rooms.

entries.name: wooden_floor
entries.description: A [floor](#floor) made of wooden planks laid side by side, seen in gyms, dojos, older houses, and any room with hardwood flooring. A floor of woven mats is [tatami](#tatami) instead.

entries.name: tiles
entries.description: Square tiles covering a surface in the scene, on a [floor](#floor), wall or roof. Use [tile_floor](#tile_floor) or [tile_wall](#tile_wall) for the specific surface.

entries.name: glass
entries.description: Glass as a material: [window](#window) panes, bottles, tableware and glass art in the scene. A [drinking](#drinking) vessel is [glass_(cup)](#glass_(cup)) and spectacles are [glasses](#glasses).

entries.name: tatami
entries.description: Rectangular woven straw [floor](#floor) mats with [bound](#bound) [cloth](#cloth) edges, the standard flooring of a traditional Japanese room.

entries.name: tile_floor
entries.description: A [floor](#floor) laid with [square](#square) [tiles](#tiles) of stone, ceramic or [glass](#glass), often glossy enough to double as a [reflective_floor](#reflective_floor).

entries.name: brick_wall
entries.description: A wall built entirely of [brick](#brick), bare or painted over, [standing](#standing) behind the subject in a [street](#street), [alley](#alley), basement or loft. Add wall; loose bricks on their own are brick.

entries.name: checkered_floor
entries.description: The [floor](#floor) is laid in alternating coloured squares, as in an old-fashioned [kitchen](#kitchen) or a dreamlike hall. The pattern gives a room a graphic, faintly unreal feel.

entries.name: tile_wall
entries.description: A wall faced with [square](#square) [tiles](#tiles), typical of bathrooms, kitchens and pools.

entries.name: crack
entries.description: A [split](#split) line [running](#running) across a surface that has not yet come apart: [glass](#glass), ground, a wall, a [mask](#mask), a [screen](#screen). Add the [tag](#tag) for the specific surface where one exists; it has nothing to do with the drug.

entries.name: carpet
entries.description: Thick woven [floor](#floor) covering laid wall to wall in a room or [running](#running) down a staircase. A loose piece that [can](#can) be picked up and moved is a [rug](#rug).

entries.name: reflective_floor
entries.description: A polished [floor](#floor) that mirrors the characters and the room above it, like a marble hall or a [wet](#wet) [street](#street). Combine with [reflection](#reflection) when the mirrored image is clear.

entries.name: wooden_wall
entries.description: A wall built of wooden boards or planks, as in cabins, barns, sheds, and traditional Japanese buildings. Tag wall alongside it where that [tag](#tag) is used too.

entries.name: stone_floor
entries.description: A [floor](#floor) built or paved from stone slabs or rough blocks, as seen in castles, temples and dungeons. Colder and harder-looking than wood or tile floors.

entries.name: pavement
entries.description: Stones, bricks or slabs laid to form the surface of a [street](#street), footpath or [square](#square). Use it where the paved ground is a noticeable part of the scene, cobblestones included.

entries.name: stone_wall
entries.description: A wall built from natural or roughly shaped stones rather than [brick](#brick) or poured [concrete](#concrete). Common around gardens, [old](#old) towns and [castle](#castle) grounds.

entries.name: cracked_wall
entries.description: A wall whose surface is [split](#split) with cracks, from an impact, from age or from a fight. Add the wall's material [tag](#tag) where that matters.

entries.name: brick_floor
entries.description: A [floor](#floor) or [pavement](#pavement) laid in bricks, as in a courtyard, a patio or an [old](#old) [street](#street). Add floor; a brick-built upright surface is [brick_wall](#brick_wall).

entries.name: brick
entries.description: Individual bricks as loose objects: a [stack](#stack) of them, one held as a makeshift [weapon](#weapon), or [rubble](#rubble) scattered on the ground. A [structure](#structure) built of them is [brick_wall](#brick_wall) or [brick_floor](#brick_floor).

entries.name: glass_shards
entries.description: Glass [broken](#broken) into pieces, scattered across the [floor](#floor), [flying](#flying) from a [shattered](#shattered) [window](#window) or used as a dramatic framing element.

entries.name: cracked_floor
entries.description: A [floor](#floor) or [patch](#patch) of ground [split](#split) by visible cracks, whether from an impact, a tremor or [plain](#plain) decay. A [staple](#staple) of fight scenes and ruined settings.

entries.name: wallpaper_(object)
entries.description: Patterned or textured [paper](#paper) covering the walls of a room, visible as part of the [interior](#interior). Not the desktop-wallpaper image format.

entries.name: cobblestone
entries.description: A [street](#street) or [square](#square) laid with rounded stones set into the ground, [giving](#giving) an uneven surface. Common under European period and [fantasy](#fantasy) [town](#town) scenes.

entries.name: rust
entries.description: Iron corroded to a flaking reddish-brown crust across metal surfaces. It signals abandonment, age and decay, and is a [staple](#staple) texture of ruined and post-industrial settings.

entries.name: red_carpet
entries.description: A long strip of red [carpet](#carpet) laid as a [walkway](#walkway), [running](#running) up steps or down a hall. It signals ceremony and a grand welcome, and by extension film premieres and award nights.

entries.name: concrete
entries.description: Bare concrete makes up a noticeable part of the scene, as a wall, a [floor](#floor) or a slab. Add [against_wall](#against_wall) or [on_floor](#on_floor) when a character is up against the surface.

entries.name: running_bond
entries.description: The common brickwork pattern where rectangular bricks are laid end to end in rows, each course offset by half a [brick](#brick) from the one below. Seen on walls and paving alike.

entries.name: tactile_paving
entries.description: Paving covered in raised domes or ridges, laid to [guide](#guide) [people](#people) with impaired sight along platforms and across crossings. A standard [street](#street) and station detail, first adopted in Japan.

entries.name: tile_ceiling
entries.description: A [ceiling](#ceiling) faced in [square](#square) panels, the [grid](#grid) visible overhead. Reads immediately as an [office](#office), a [classroom](#classroom) or a [bathroom](#bathroom).

entries.name: wet_floor
entries.description: The [floor](#floor) is visibly slick with spilled [liquid](#liquid), [catching](#catching) reflections and sometimes accompanied by a warning [sign](#sign). Bathrooms, kitchens and freshly mopped corridors are typical settings.

entries.name: tile_roof
entries.description: A roof clad in overlapping [tiles](#tiles): curved ceramic ones on shrines and older Japanese houses, flat or scalloped ones elsewhere.

entries.name: brick_road
entries.description: A [road](#road) or [path](#path) surfaced in laid [brick](#brick) or paving blocks rather than asphalt, the courses [plain](#plain) underfoot. Old [town](#town) streets, squares and courtyards are where it turns up.

entries.name: plank
entries.description: A long, flat [rectangle](#rectangle) of sawn wood, longer than it is wide. Used for [building](#building), boarding things up, or improvised as a [bridge](#bridge) or a club.

entries.name: sett
entries.description: Quarried stone blocks laid as [road](#road) paving, cut to a regular [rectangle](#rectangle) and often mislabelled [cobblestone](#cobblestone). A true cobble is a natural rounded stone; setts give a [street](#street) a neat [grid](#grid) of [joints](#joints).

entries.name: wainscoting
entries.description: Wooden panelling [running](#running) along the lower part of an [interior](#interior) wall and capped with a rail. When boards [cover](#cover) the whole wall, the [plain](#plain) [wooden_wall](#wooden_wall) [tag](#tag) fits better.

entries.name: mural
entries.description: A painting worked straight onto a wall or [ceiling](#ceiling), frescoes and mosaics included. It differs from [graffiti](#graffiti), which is rougher and often just lettering, whereas this is a composed picture.

entries.name: checkered_wall
entries.description: A wall surfaced in alternating light and [dark](#dark) squares, oversized tiling turned vertical. It lends a room a graphic, faintly unreal look.

entries.name: corrugated_galvanized_iron_sheet
entries.description: Ridged metal sheeting used for roofs, fences and [shed](#shed) walls. Despite the name it is normally steel or tin, and it reads as cheap, weathered [building](#building).

entries.name: marble_(stone)
entries.description: Polished stone with a pale ground and coloured veining, formed from limestone under heat and pressure. Used for floors, columns, basins and statuary.

entries.name: rebar
entries.description: Ribbed steel rods, alone or tied into a [mesh](#mesh), used to reinforce [concrete](#concrete). Exposed lengths jutting from [broken](#broken) walls mark [construction](#construction) sites and ruined buildings alike.

entries.name: half-timbered
entries.description: Buildings whose wooden framing shows on the outside as [dark](#dark) beams against pale infill panels. Typical of old-town [architecture](#architecture) in northern and central Europe.

entries.name: cinder_block
entries.description: A grey rectangular [concrete](#concrete) [building](#building) block with hollow cores, larger and coarser than a [brick](#brick). Used in walls and rough [construction](#construction), and as a stock [heavy](#heavy) object for weighing something down.

entries.name: building
entries.description: A permanent [structure](#structure) with walls and a roof — a [house](#house), a [tower](#tower), an [office](#office) block — [standing](#standing) in the scene. It covers everything from a lone cottage to a whole [skyline](#skyline).

entries.name: architecture
entries.description: Buildings and structures in a definite style form a substantial part of the picture, from [temple](#temple) roofs and Gothic vaulting to pyramids and [torii](#torii) gates. Name the particular [building](#building) or style as [well](#well) where it [can](#can) be told.

entries.name: house
entries.description: A residential [building](#building) is shown, from outside or as the identifiable setting. Rooms inside usually take their own tags such as [bedroom](#bedroom), [kitchen](#kitchen) or [living_room](#living_room).

entries.name: east_asian_architecture
entries.description: Buildings and structures in traditional Chinese, Japanese or Korean style: shrines, pagodas, [torii](#torii) gates, paifang arches, [tatami](#tatami) rooms behind [paper](#paper) doors. Exteriors and interiors both.

entries.name: skyscraper
entries.description: A very [tall](#tall) multi-storey [building](#building) of the modern [city](#city) kind. Tag beside building; several together often form a [skyline](#skyline).

entries.name: tower
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), slender [structure](#structure) [standing](#standing) alone or rising from a larger [building](#building), from a [castle](#castle) turret to a broadcast [mast](#mast). Add castle or [city](#city) as fits the surrounding scene.

entries.name: clock_tower
entries.description: A [tower](#tower) built to carry one or more large [clock](#clock) faces, [standing](#standing) alone or rising from a [church](#church) or [town](#town) hall. Big Ben is the archetype for the shape.

entries.name: windmill
entries.description: A traditional [building](#building) with large sails turned by the [wind](#wind) to grind grain or [pump](#pump) [water](#water). A modern [tower](#tower) built to generate [electricity](#electricity) is a [wind_turbine](#wind_turbine) instead.

entries.name: apartment
entries.description: A block of [flats](#flats), or the inside of one: a multi-storey [building](#building) carved into separate homes. For an [interior](#interior), add the room as [well](#well), such as [bedroom](#bedroom) or [living_room](#living_room).

entries.name: lighthouse
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [tower](#tower) by the [water](#water) with a [lamp](#lamp) room and [walkway](#walkway) at the top, guiding ships in. Usually part of coastal [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: pagoda
entries.description: A tiered [tower](#tower) with a [stack](#stack) of overhanging eaves, the [temple](#temple) form built across China, Japan, Korea and beyond. Usually part of a [shrine](#shrine) or temple [landscape](#landscape).

entries.name: mansion
entries.description: A grand sprawling private [house](#house) of many rooms and [wings](#wings), home to the wealthy or the noble. Shown whole from outside, or through its long halls and staircases.

entries.name: hangar
entries.description: A cavernous [shed](#shed) built to [house](#house) and service [aircraft](#aircraft) or [mecha](#mecha), with a high roof and enormous doors. Gantries, tool carts, cables and painted [floor](#floor) [markings](#markings) usually fill out the [space](#space).

entries.name: european_architecture
entries.description: Buildings in European styles: stone facades, arched windows, tiled roofs, cobbled squares. Used where a [street](#street) or townscape reads as European rather than Japanese or American.

entries.name: greenhouse
entries.description: A [building](#building) framed in [glass](#glass) or plastic panels for raising plants under shelter, typically filled with benches, rows of pots and damp air. It stays a greenhouse when empty or used for storage; a [conservatory](#conservatory) built mainly as living [space](#space) looks similar but is a different [structure](#structure).

entries.name: tokyo_big_sight
entries.description: The Tokyo exhibition centre known for the four inverted pyramids of its conference [tower](#tower), home to Comiket and other large fan events. Usually drawn as an establishing shot with a [queue](#queue) snaking outside.

entries.name: barn
