entries.description: A large [farm](#farm) [building](#building) for [hay](#hay), [machinery](#machinery) and livestock, with wide double doors and a steep roof. Red boards with white trim are the usual look.

entries.name: factory
entries.description: An [industrial](#industrial) [plant](#plant) where goods are made, with machines, conveyor lines, pipework and chimneys. It covers the [working](#working) [floor](#floor) inside as much as the [building](#building) seen from outside.

entries.name: industrial
entries.description: A setting of [heavy](#heavy) industry: [factory](#factory) halls, pipework, chimneys, gantries and [machinery](#machinery). Bare [concrete](#concrete) and exposed metal set the mood.

entries.name: tokyo_tower
entries.description: The orange and white steel [lattice](#lattice) [tower](#tower) in central Tokyo, Eiffel-shaped but painted for air safety and [carrying](#carrying) two round observation decks. Shorthand for the [city](#city) in [skyline](#skyline) shots.

entries.name: gothic_architecture
entries.description: Building in the [medieval](#medieval) Gothic manner, with pointed arches, ribbed vaults, [flying](#flying) buttresses and [tall](#tall) narrow windows drawing the eye upward. Later revival work in the same idiom counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: eiffel_tower
entries.description: The wrought-iron [lattice](#lattice) [tower](#tower) on the Champ de Mars in Paris, tapering to a [spire](#spire) with viewing decks along the way. Instant shorthand for a French setting.

entries.name: hut
entries.description: A small rough dwelling raised from natural material: [mud](#mud), stone, thatch or branches. A [shack](#shack), by [contrast](#contrast), is knocked together from manufactured parts.

entries.name: elizabeth_tower
entries.description: The [clock](#clock) [tower](#tower) at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London, with four lit dials beneath a gothic [spire](#spire). It fixes a scene in the [city](#city); Big Ben is properly the [bell](#bell) [hanging](#hanging) inside it.

entries.name: treehouse
entries.description: A small shelter built up among a tree's branches, reached by a [ladder](#ladder) or steps nailed to the trunk. Reads as a childhood hideout or a rustic dwelling depending on the rest of the scene.

entries.name: dilapidated
entries.description: A [building](#building) or [structure](#structure) gone to ruin: cracked walls, a sagging roof, boarded windows, [weeds](#weeds) through the floorboards. Decay from weather or from damage nobody repaired.

entries.name: warehouse
entries.description: A big storage [building](#building) with high ceilings, racking, stacked pallets and roller doors. A favourite setting for shootouts and abandoned-building scenes.

entries.name: greco-roman_architecture
entries.description: Building in the classical Greek and Roman manner: fluted columns, pediments, entablatures and symmetrical stone facades. Later work raised to the same orders counts too.

entries.name: hotel
entries.description: An establishment renting rooms to travellers, seen from the [street](#street) or through its lobby. The guest rooms themselves are [hotel_room](#hotel_room).

entries.name: cabin
entries.description: A small wooden [house](#house), usually [standing](#standing) alone in woodland or hills. Log walls, a [chimney](#chimney) and a covered [porch](#porch) are the usual details.

entries.name: palace
entries.description: A grand residence built for royalty or nobility, with [ornate](#ornate) halls, colonnades and formal grounds. A [castle](#castle) [can](#can) stand in when it is drawn as a home rather than as a [fortress](#fortress).

entries.name: igloo
entries.description: A [dome](#dome) built from cut blocks of hard-packed [snow](#snow), meant to last a season rather than a [night](#night). A hollowed-out drift is a hastier kind of snow shelter and not this.

entries.name: middle_eastern_architecture
entries.description: Buildings and interiors in Middle Eastern traditions - domes, pointed and [horseshoe](#horseshoe) arches, minarets, tiled surfaces and shaded courtyards. Covers Arabic, Persian, Islamic and Ottoman styles alike.

entries.name: tokyo_skytree
entries.description: The pale [lattice](#lattice) broadcasting [tower](#tower) in eastern Tokyo, 634 metres to its tip and the tallest [structure](#structure) in Japan. A common [skyline](#skyline) [marker](#marker), especially lit up at [night](#night).

entries.name: shed
entries.description: A small standalone outbuilding used for storage or as a [workshop](#workshop), [standing](#standing) apart from the main [house](#house) it serves.

entries.name: floating_city
entries.description: A whole settlement suspended above the ground, spread over [drifting](#drifting) islands or with its towers [standing](#standing) in open air. A single airborne keep is a [floating_castle](#floating_castle).

entries.name: floating_castle
entries.description: A [castle](#castle) or keep held up in the [sky](#sky), perched on a [drifting](#drifting) [island](#island) or [hanging](#hanging) on nothing at all. Several such structures [sharing](#sharing) one sky make a [floating_city](#floating_city).

entries.name: megastructure
entries.description: Construction on an impossible scale - a [tower](#tower) the size of a [city](#city), an orbital [ring](#ring), a wall [running](#running) to the [horizon](#horizon) - dwarfing everything nearby. Marks [scenery](#scenery) built far beyond ordinary architectural limits.

entries.name: beach_house
entries.description: A [house](#house) built at the [shore](#shore), often raised on [stilts](#stilts) or fronted by a deck, with wide windows facing the [water](#water). Sand, dune [grass](#grass) and [beach](#beach) clutter surround it.

entries.name: bell_tower
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [tower](#tower) housing one or more bells, [standing](#standing) alone or built onto a [church](#church) or [school](#school). Also called a belfry or campanile, and a fixture of European skylines.

entries.name: fortress
entries.description: A heavily walled stronghold built to be defended, usually layered ramparts wrapped around a keep. Modern and futuristic strongpoints [serving](#serving) the same purpose belong here too.

entries.name: shack
entries.description: A crude, one-room [building](#building) thrown together from scrap boards, sheet metal, and salvage. Signals [poverty](#poverty) or an improvised settlement, unlike a [hut](#hut) built from natural materials.

entries.name: structure
entries.description: A built [construction](#construction) of [no](#no) more specific kind, a framework, [platform](#platform) or mass of [architecture](#architecture) [standing](#standing) in the scene. Prefer a narrower [tag](#tag) whenever one fits better.

entries.name: steeple
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) narrow [tower](#tower) rising above a [church](#church) or [cathedral](#cathedral), usually finished with a pointed [spire](#spire) and sometimes a [cross](#cross). Bells often hang inside. Common in skylines and [village](#village) [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: underwater_city
entries.description: A settlement of buildings, domes or towers [standing](#standing) beneath the surface of the sea. Common in [science](#science) fiction and [fantasy](#fantasy), sometimes shown as sunken [ruins](#ruins) rather than a [working](#working) [city](#city).

entries.name: fence
entries.description: A barrier of posts strung with [wire](#wire), boards or rails, bordering a yard, a [field](#field) or a [road](#road). It marks a boundary or keeps things in or out; chain-link and picket both count.

entries.name: torii
entries.description: The two-pillar [gate](#gate) marking the [entrance](#entrance) to a Shinto [shrine](#shrine), usually vermilion. Add shrine and often a [fox](#fox) [statue](#statue) or [shimenawa](#shimenawa).

entries.name: power_lines
entries.description: Electrical cables strung between utility poles or pylons, a fixture of [street](#street) and [sky](#sky) scenes. Train catenary is overhead_lines; drawn [speed_lines](#speed_lines) are something else entirely.

entries.name: lamppost
entries.description: A fixed outdoor light on a post, [gas](#gas) or electric, [standing](#standing) along a [road](#road) or through a [park](#park). It is a mainstay of [night](#night) scenes and is not a carried [lantern](#lantern).

entries.name: utility_pole
entries.description: A wooden or [concrete](#concrete) post [carrying](#carrying) overhead power or telephone lines, often with a [transformer](#transformer) or [street](#street) [lamp](#lamp) attached. Common in Japanese street scenes, and not to be [confused](#confused) with a steel-lattice transmission [tower](#tower) for high-voltage lines.

entries.name: pole
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) upright post or rod, such as a [flagpole](#flagpole), a [signpost](#signpost), or the pole a [dancer](#dancer) swings around. Utility poles [carrying](#carrying) cables [can](#can) also take a separate [tag](#tag) for the wires themselves.

entries.name: chain-link_fence
entries.description: A [fence](#fence) of steel [wire](#wire) woven into a diamond [mesh](#mesh), the sort that encloses [school](#school) yards, rooftops and [ball](#ball) courts. It often stands behind characters as [urban](#urban) [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: statue
entries.description: A freestanding [sculpture](#sculpture) of a person, [animal](#animal) or deity, from small figures to monuments. Famous works and types like [moai](#moai), [jizou](#jizou) or [gargoyle](#gargoyle) may have their own tags.

entries.name: path
entries.description: A way made for [walking](#walking) rather than for vehicles: a [hiking](#hiking) trail, a track worn through [grass](#grass), a [garden](#garden) walk or the approach to a [shrine](#shrine). A paved route [carrying](#carrying) [traffic](#traffic) is [road](#road) or [street](#street).

entries.name: swing
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) seat suspended from ropes or chains, whether tied to a [tree](#tree) [branch](#branch) or part of a larger swing set.

entries.name: vending_machine
entries.description: A coin-operated [machine](#machine) dispensing drinks, snacks or other goods, a fixture of Japanese streets and [school](#school) corridors, often [glowing](#glowing) at [night](#night).

entries.name: traffic_light
entries.description: A signal of red, yellow and green lights positioned at a crossing or intersection to control the flow of vehicles. A common fixture of [street](#street) and [city](#city) scenes.

entries.name: railroad_tracks
entries.description: Rails and sleepers [running](#running) through the scene, [carrying](#carrying) trains, trams, or minecarts. Combine with [train](#train), [train_station](#train_station), or the surrounding [landscape](#landscape).

entries.name: park_bench
entries.description: An outdoor [bench](#bench) of the sort found in parks and along paths, generally wooden slats with a backrest and one continuous seat.

entries.name: gate
entries.description: A [door](#door) set into a wall or fortification, or an arched [structure](#structure) with an [opening](#opening) through the middle. Particular kinds such as [torii](#torii), [moon_gate](#moon_gate), paifang and portcullis have their own tags.

entries.name: wooden_fence
entries.description: A [fence](#fence) built from wooden planks, posts, or pickets, typical of farms, gardens, and [rural](#rural) scenes. Tag fence alongside it.

entries.name: tent
entries.description: A [fabric](#fabric) shelter held up by poles, pitched for [camping](#camping) or set up as a temporary [structure](#structure) such as a [circus](#circus) or [festival](#festival) stall.

entries.name: ferris_wheel
entries.description: A [giant](#giant) upright turning [wheel](#wheel) with passenger cabins hung around its rim, the landmark ride of a fairground or amusement [park](#park). Often a [backdrop](#backdrop) for dates and [festival](#festival) scenes.

entries.name: stone_lantern
entries.description: A traditional Japanese stone [lantern](#lantern), carved in tiers with a hollow chamber for a light. Common in [shrine](#shrine) grounds, [temple](#temple) approaches and formal gardens.

entries.name: fountain
entries.description: An ornamental [basin](#basin) whose spouts throw [water](#water) upward in arcs, typical of parks, plazas and gardens. A fixture that dispenses [drinking](#drinking) water is [drinking_fountain](#drinking_fountain).

entries.name: traffic_cone
entries.description: An orange cone [marker](#marker) used to close off lanes at roadworks or [accident](#accident) sites, occasionally worn as a joke [hat](#hat) in [comic](#comic) scenes. Add [road](#road) or [construction_site](#construction_site) for the setting.

entries.name: food_stand
entries.description: A movable stall selling [food](#food) from one spot before shifting to another, such as a [festival](#festival) [yatai](#yatai) or a [street](#street) [cart](#cart). Rows of them line [summer](#summer) festival scenes.

entries.name: bus_stop
entries.description: A marked point at the roadside where buses take on and set down passengers, identified by a [sign](#sign), a shelter or a [bench](#bench). A common [backdrop](#backdrop) for [waiting](#waiting) and commuting.

entries.name: multiple_torii
entries.description: Several [torii](#torii) gates in one picture, frequently set in a row to form the tunnel-like approach to a [shrine](#shrine). The repetition of the gates is what the [tag](#tag) records.

entries.name: guard_rail
entries.description: A sturdy metal barrier along the side of a [road](#road) that keeps vehicles from leaving it. Common in [street](#street) and [highway](#highway) backdrops.

entries.name: billboard
entries.description: A large advertising board raised on a [rooftop](#rooftop), a wall or its own posts. It fills out [city](#city) scenes and usually carries a poster or lettering worth [reading](#reading).

entries.name: carousel
entries.description: A fairground ride of carved horses fixed to a turning [platform](#platform), rising and [falling](#falling) as it spins. Ringed with lights and mirrors around its central [column](#column).

entries.name: railroad_crossing
entries.description: The point where a [road](#road) meets railway tracks at the same level, marked by crossbucks, [flashing](#flashing) red lamps, and lowering boom gates. A [familiar](#familiar) [backdrop](#backdrop) in suburban and small-town Japanese art.

entries.name: market_stall
entries.description: A temporary booth or stand from which a trader sells wares, of the kind lining a [street](#street) [market](#market) or a [festival](#festival) lane. Usually a canopy, a [counter](#counter) of goods and a seller behind it.

entries.name: wind_turbine
entries.description: A [tall](#tall), slim [tower](#tower) [carrying](#carrying) long blades that turn in the [wind](#wind) to generate [electricity](#electricity). The older kind built for [grinding](#grinding) grain belongs under [windmill](#windmill) instead.

entries.name: transmission_tower
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) steel [lattice](#lattice) pylon [carrying](#carrying) high-voltage power lines across open country. A recurring landmark in [field](#field), railway and [rural](#rural) [landscape](#landscape) backgrounds.

entries.name: windsock
entries.description: A tapering [fabric](#fabric) [tube](#tube) mounted on a [pole](#pole) that fills with air to show which way the [wind](#wind) is [blowing](#blowing). Airfields use it for practical reasons, while festivals hang decorative versions.

entries.name: signpost
entries.description: A post [carrying](#carrying) one or more boards that name places and point the way, sometimes with distances. Common at crossroads, trailheads and [village](#village) edges.

entries.name: flagpole
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) [mast](#mast) a [flag](#flag) is run up, [planted](#planted) in the ground or bracketed to a [building](#building). It may stand bare with nothing [flying](#flying) from it.

entries.name: stop_sign
entries.description: A red [traffic](#traffic) [sign](#sign) telling drivers to halt, octagonal in most countries and an inverted [triangle](#triangle) in Japan, lettered in white. Not the same as the no-entry sign, which is a red disc crossed by a white bar.

entries.name: mailbox_(incoming_mail)
entries.description: The private [box](#box) at a [house](#house) or [gate](#gate) where a carrier leaves letters for the resident to collect, sometimes with a small [flag](#flag) signalling post to be picked up. Distinct from the public box that letters are dropped into for sending.

entries.name: yatai
entries.description: A small wheeled [street](#street) stall selling [hot](#hot) [food](#food) such as [ramen](#ramen) or [festival](#festival) snacks. Usually drawn with a [cloth](#cloth) curtain, [hanging](#hanging) lanterns and a few stools pulled up to the [counter](#counter).

entries.name: tunnel
entries.description: A passage [bored](#bored) through [rock](#rock) or earth for [road](#road), rail, foot or utility [traffic](#traffic). Framing often plays the [dark](#dark) bore of the tunnel against a bright [opening](#opening) at its far end.

entries.name: phone_booth
entries.description: A streetside kiosk enclosing a [payphone](#payphone), with glazed panes, a [door](#door) and a weatherproof roof. Reserve it for real enclosures such as the red British [box](#box) or the aluminium and [glass](#glass) Japanese one.

entries.name: swing_set
entries.description: A [playground](#playground) frame of metal or wood supporting one or more [hanging](#hanging) swings. Use it when both the frame and a seat are visible; a [swing](#swing) on its own is just a swing.

entries.name: stone_walkway
entries.description: A [path](#path) paved with large flat stones set side by side. Runs through gardens, [shrine](#shrine) approaches and [old](#old) streets.

entries.name: boom_barrier
entries.description: A long arm that pivots down across a [road](#road) or track to halt [traffic](#traffic), [standing](#standing) at level crossings, [car](#car) [park](#park) entrances and guarded checkpoints. The arm is painted in red-and-white or yellow-and-black warning bands.

entries.name: postbox_(outgoing_mail)
entries.description: The public [box](#box) on the [street](#street) where letters are posted for collection, usually a red or blue [pillar](#pillar) with a slot in its side. The box at a [house](#house) that receives [mail](#mail) is a different [tag](#tag).

entries.name: traffic_mirror
entries.description: A round convex [mirror](#mirror) mounted on a [pole](#pole) at a [blind](#blind) [corner](#corner), bulging outward to widen the view of the [road](#road) beyond it. A common fixture at narrow intersections.

entries.name: roller_coaster
entries.description: The amusement [park](#park) ride of steep track and cars full of [screaming](#screaming) riders, seen either as the [structure](#structure) looming over a scene or from a seat mid-drop. Expect raised arms and wind-blown hair.

entries.name: overhead_line
entries.description: The contact wires strung above a tramway or an electrified railway, [feeding](#feeding) current to the vehicle through a [pantograph](#pantograph) on its roof. Not the same as power lines, which run between utility poles to carry current across a district.

entries.name: manhole_cover
entries.description: The round metal [lid](#lid) closing a utility shaft in the [road](#road), [cast](#cast) with a raised design. Japanese ones frequently carry elaborate local artwork rather than a [plain](#plain) [grid](#grid).

entries.name: well
entries.description: A shaft sunk into the ground to reach groundwater, generally ringed with stone and fitted with a [bucket](#bucket) on a [rope](#rope). Village squares, [shrine](#shrine) grounds and [fantasy](#fantasy) hamlets all commonly feature one.

entries.name: komainu
entries.description: The paired lion-dog statues set at the approach to a [shrine](#shrine), one with its mouth open and one shut. They appear as stone [scenery](#scenery) and as the [model](#model) for character designs.

entries.name: no_entry_sign
entries.description: The round red [road](#road) [sign](#sign) forbidding vehicles from [driving](#driving) into a [street](#street), sometimes lettered DO NOT ENTER. The exact design differs from country to country.

entries.name: condenser_unit
entries.description: The outdoor half of an air conditioner, a boxy metal housing with a fan grille in front. Frequently bolted to [apartment](#apartment) walls in [urban](#urban) backdrops.

entries.name: jizou
entries.description: A small stone [figure](#figure) of the bodhisattva who protects children and travellers, cut as a round-faced [monk](#monk) and often given a red [bib](#bib) and a knitted cap. They stand alone or in rows beside roads and in graveyards.

entries.name: traffic_barrier
entries.description: A barricade set across a [road](#road) or footway to steer or stop movement, from striped folding rails to plastic drums. Marks off closed lanes, [construction](#construction) sites and edges [people](#people) should not [cross](#cross).

entries.name: podium
entries.description: A low block or dais that lifts someone into view, most [familiar](#familiar) as the tiered stand used to award medals at a sporting event. The stand a [speaker](#speaker) talks from behind is a [lectern](#lectern) instead.

entries.name: gazebo
entries.description: A freestanding roofed pavilion open between its posts rather than walled in, usually eight-sided under a [dome](#dome) or cone. Placed in parks, estate gardens and [wedding](#wedding) scenes.

entries.name: trellis
entries.description: A latticework frame of crossed slats that [climbing](#climbing) plants are trained to grow up. Usually stands against a wall or arches over a [garden](#garden) [path](#path), thick with [vines](#vines) or roses.

entries.name: bamboo_fence
entries.description: A [fence](#fence) built from [bamboo](#bamboo), either poles lashed upright side by side or lengths woven into panels. It encloses gardens, shrines and traditional houses.

entries.name: snow_shelter
entries.description: A shelter built from packed [snow](#snow), such as an [igloo](#igloo) or a Japanese kamakura [hut](#hut), meant to block [wind](#wind) and [cold](#cold). Characters are often shown huddled inside with a light source.

entries.name: scaffolding
entries.description: A temporary [lattice](#lattice) of poles and planks raised against a [building](#building) so workers [can](#can) reach its upper storeys. Reads as [construction](#construction) or repair in progress.

entries.name: floral_arch
entries.description: An [arch](#arch) woven from flowers and greenery, the sort set up for weddings and [garden](#garden) ceremonies. Characters generally stand beneath it or pass through.

entries.name: railroad_signal
entries.description: A post beside the tracks that tells a [train](#train) driver what the line ahead is doing, using either colored lamps or a [swinging](#swinging) semaphore arm. Signals aimed at pedestrians and motorists instead fall under [railroad_crossing](#railroad_crossing).

entries.name: iron_fence
entries.description: A [fence](#fence) of iron uprights, either [plain](#plain) railings or [ornate](#ornate) pickets tipped with spearheads. It is usually painted black and stands around gardens, parks and graveyards.

entries.name: fire_hydrant
entries.description: A squat capped fitting at the kerb that firefighters [couple](#couple) a [hose](#hose) to. Painted red or yellow, and a [familiar](#familiar) piece of [street](#street) furniture.

entries.name: sewer_grate
entries.description: The barred metal [cover](#cover) set into a [street](#street) or kerb over a drain [opening](#opening). Rain runs down through it, and lifting it opens the way to the tunnels below.

entries.name: ironwork
entries.description: Decorative pieces forged or [cast](#cast) in iron: scrolled gates, railings, [balcony](#balcony) fronts, brackets and [window](#window) grilles. Left unpainted they read as black against stone or [brick](#brick).

entries.name: stepping_stones
entries.description: A row of flat stones set in shallow [water](#water) so a person [can](#can) [cross](#cross) a [stream](#stream) or [pond](#pond) dry-footed. They may be natural or deliberately laid, and are a fixture of Japanese [garden](#garden) design.

entries.name: angel_statue
entries.description: A carved winged [figure](#figure) in stone, of the sort [standing](#standing) in churches, chapels and graveyards. It reads as [scenery](#scenery) and mood rather than as a character.

entries.name: statue_of_liberty
entries.description: The colossal robed [figure](#figure) in New York harbour, [torch](#torch) raised and tablet in the other arm, wearing a [spiked](#spiked) [crown](#crown) with a [broken](#broken) [chain](#chain) at her [feet](#feet). Shorthand for the United States, and a favourite for disaster scenes.

entries.name: doghouse
entries.description: A small kennel [standing](#standing) in a yard, usually a gabled [box](#box) with a round [opening](#opening) and [no](#no) [door](#door). A [bowl](#bowl) and a [chain](#chain) often sit next to it.

entries.name: jungle_gym
entries.description: A [climbing](#climbing) frame of [bars](#bars) or pipes bolted into an open [cage](#cage) for children to swarm over. It usually stands in [sand](#sand) or on a schoolyard, painted metal.

entries.name: manhole
entries.description: The mouth of an access shaft leading down into a [sewer](#sewer) or utility [tunnel](#tunnel), often [standing](#standing) open with its [lid](#lid) shifted aside. The lid on its own is [manhole_cover](#manhole_cover).

entries.name: spring_rider
entries.description: A [playground](#playground) fixture with a [saddle](#saddle) and handlebars mounted on a [heavy](#heavy) coil, so it rocks and wobbles as a [child](#child) rides it. Usually shaped like a [horse](#horse), [panda](#panda) or other [animal](#animal).

entries.name: moai
entries.description: The heavy-browed stone heads of Rapa Nui, or carvings copying their long flat faces and jutting chins. Because the matching [emoji](#emoji) stands for a [deadpan](#deadpan) reaction, they often appear as a joke rather than as [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: water_tank
entries.description: A large sealed [container](#container) [holding](#holding) [water](#water) for [drinking](#drinking), [farming](#farming) or firefighting, built from plastic, steel or [glass](#glass). Usually stands beside a [building](#building) or up on a roof.

entries.name: drinking_fountain
entries.description: A public fixture that throws a small arc of [water](#water) upward for [people](#people) to lean over and [drink](#drink), standard in schools and parks. Ornamental pools, outdoor taps and eyewash stations are something else.

entries.name: post_and_rail_fence
entries.description: A [rural](#rural) [fence](#fence) of stout uprights with long horizontal [bars](#bars) slotted through them, leaving wide open gaps. Typical of paddocks, farmland and country lanes.

entries.name: weather_vane
entries.description: A pivoting [pointer](#pointer), classically shaped like a [rooster](#rooster), mounted at the highest point of a roof to show which way the [wind](#wind) blows. Compass letters usually sit beneath it.

entries.name: ryoubu_torii
entries.description: A [shrine](#shrine) [gate](#gate) braced by four smaller pillars [standing](#standing) in front of and behind the two main posts. The famous gate standing in the [water](#water) at Itsukushima is of this kind.

entries.name: picket_fence
entries.description: A low [fence](#fence) of evenly spaced upright boards with pointed tops, nailed across horizontal rails. Painted white it stands for tidy suburban gardens, marking a boundary rather than [blocking](#blocking) anything.

entries.name: japanese_cylindrical_postbox
entries.description: The round red [pillar](#pillar) postbox once standard on Japanese streets, its slot sheltered by a curved eave, with a collection [plate](#plate) to one side and a small [hatch](#hatch) below. Square boxes long ago replaced it, so it reads as nostalgic [street](#street) furniture.

entries.name: no_parking_sign
entries.description: A roadside [sign](#sign) forbidding parking, drawn either as a red crossed [circle](#circle) on blue or as the same circle over a black [letter](#letter) P. It fixes a scene at the kerbside.

entries.name: fare_gate
entries.description: The [ticket](#ticket) barrier at a station [entrance](#entrance), letting one traveller through at a time, whether of the flap, [tripod](#tripod) or [swinging](#swinging) kind. Card readers or ticket slots are usually built into the top.

entries.name: water_wheel
entries.description: A bladed [wheel](#wheel) turned by flowing [water](#water) to drive a mill or [machinery](#machinery). Almost always attached to an [old](#old) [building](#building) beside a [stream](#stream).

entries.name: pedestrian_lights
entries.description: The small signal at a crossing that tells walkers when to go, showing a [standing](#standing) or striding [figure](#figure). Mounted at junctions and timed with the [traffic](#traffic) lights.

entries.name: radio_tower
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) [lattice](#lattice) or [concrete](#concrete) [mast](#mast) [carrying](#carrying) broadcast and telecommunications aerials, usually rising above a [skyline](#skyline) or hilltop. Reads as a landmark in the background of [city](#city) or countryside scenes.

entries.name: quinzhee
entries.description: A [snow](#snow) shelter built by heaping snow into a mound and hollowing out the inside, meant to be temporary unlike a block-built [igloo](#igloo). Known in Japan by its own local name for the same [structure](#structure).

entries.name: retaining_wall
entries.description: A wall built into a slope to stop the earth behind it from [sliding](#sliding) forward. Usually [concrete](#concrete) or stacked stone, seen along roads, riverbanks, and terraced gardens.

entries.name: bollard
entries.description: A short thick post [planted](#planted) in the ground, used at a quayside to tie up boats or along a [street](#street) to keep vehicles off the [pavement](#pavement). It normally appears as street furniture at the edge of a scene.

entries.name: walkway
entries.description: A [path](#path) built for [people](#people) on foot, a boardwalk, raised catwalk or covered passage. It guides the eye through the scene as much as it carries [traffic](#traffic).

entries.name: water_tower
entries.description: A [tank](#tank) held high on [legs](#legs) or a [column](#column) so gravity keeps the supply below it pressurised. A [familiar](#familiar) [silhouette](#silhouette) over small towns and [industrial](#industrial) districts.

entries.name: bus_stop_sign
entries.description: The post and [plate](#plate) marking where a [bus](#bus) halts, usually [carrying](#carrying) the stop's name or a route number. Street furniture that fixes a scene at the kerb.

entries.name: fox_statue
entries.description: A carved stone [fox](#fox), usually one of a facing pair guarding an Inari [shrine](#shrine), often wearing a red [bib](#bib) or [holding](#holding) a [key](#key) in its jaws. It is [sculpture](#sculpture) rather than a living [animal](#animal).

entries.name: stanchion
entries.description: Upright posts linked by chains or [rope](#rope) used to [guide](#guide) queues and cordon off areas. Seen at museums, cinemas and red-carpet events.

entries.name: tent_interior
entries.description: The inside of a pitched [tent](#tent), canvas close overhead, with [sleeping](#sleeping) bags, a [lamp](#lamp) and gear stacked at the edges. Used for a [camping](#camping) scene shown from within rather than from outside.

entries.name: barber_pole
entries.description: The striped cylinder that marks a barber's [shop](#shop), wound with red, white and blue helices. Many are motorised so the stripes seem to climb without end.

entries.name: totem
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) wooden [pole](#pole) carved and stacked with stylised [animal](#animal) and ancestor faces, painted in bold colour. Native to the Pacific Northwest, it is often borrowed as background set [dressing](#dressing) in unrelated scenes.

entries.name: storm_drain
entries.description: A grated [opening](#opening) at the kerb or a [concrete](#concrete) outfall that carries rainwater away and keeps streets from flooding. Also appears as the mouth of an [underground](#underground) [tunnel](#tunnel).

entries.name: wire_fence
entries.description: A [fence](#fence) built from [wire](#wire), whether [chain](#chain) link, welded [mesh](#mesh), or strands strung between posts. Schoolyards, rooftops, and [construction](#construction) sites all make use of it.

entries.name: flower_swing
entries.description: A [hanging](#hanging) [swing](#swing) dressed with blossoms along its ropes and seat, or grown outright from [vines](#vines) and flowers. A [garden](#garden) and fairy-tale prop for a character to sit on.

entries.name: moon_gate
entries.description: A perfectly circular [opening](#opening) cut through a [garden](#garden) wall to walk through. A Chinese garden feature that also turns up in Japanese [building](#building).

entries.name: obelisk
entries.description: A [tall](#tall) four-sided stone shaft that narrows as it rises and finishes in a small pyramid. It turns up mostly in ancient Egyptian scenes and in monuments modelled on them.

entries.name: gumball_machine
entries.description: A coin-operated dispenser [holding](#holding) a mound of colourful [sweets](#sweets) behind curved [glass](#glass), with a small chute below. Common set [dressing](#dressing) for shops, arcades and [street](#street) corners.

entries.name: stone_torii
entries.description: A Shinto gateway built from stone rather than the more usual painted wood, so it stands grey and weathered. Marks the boundary of [shrine](#shrine) grounds.

entries.name: full_body
entries.description: The whole of a character is in frame and takes up most of it. Hair tips, [wings](#wings), a [tail](#tail) or a trailing hem may be clipped without spoiling it, but a small distant [figure](#figure) is a [wide_shot](#wide_shot) instead.

entries.name: upper_body
entries.description: The framing shows the character from about the [navel](#navel) up, with or without the head included. The alias bust refers to this crop, not to [breasts](#breasts).

entries.name: cowboy_shot
entries.description: Framing that takes in a character from about the [thighs](#thighs) upward, face included, with the [legs](#legs) [running](#running) off the bottom edge somewhere between thigh and knee. Named for how Western films framed a gunslinger's [holster](#holster) and face together; legs ending inside the picture are [cropped_legs](#cropped_legs).

entries.name: feet_out_of_frame
entries.description: A nearly whole-body shot in which both [feet](#feet) fall past the picture edge; part of the shins may go too, but the [knees](#knees) stay in view. One foot alone [cropped](#cropped) is [foot_out_of_frame](#foot_out_of_frame), and a crop at the [thighs](#thighs) is [cowboy_shot](#cowboy_shot).

entries.name: portrait
entries.description: A framing that shows mainly the character's face, [cutting](#cutting) off around the shoulders and not far below the [armpits](#armpits) or chest. Anything lower is [upper_body](#upper_body). Not for multiple [cropped](#cropped) heads on a sheet.

entries.name: headshot_(composition)
entries.description: The frame holds the head alone, cropping at or just above the shoulders. Tighter than an upper-body shot, wider than a [close-up](#close-up) on a single feature.

entries.name: cropped_legs
entries.description: A character's [legs](#legs) stop inside the picture, with empty [space](#space) left between them and the bottom edge. Legs cut away by the [border](#border) itself belong to [cowboy_shot](#cowboy_shot) or [feet_out_of_frame](#feet_out_of_frame).

entries.name: close-up
entries.description: The subject is framed at very close range, so that a face, a body part or an object fills the frame. Tighter than [portrait](#portrait), and often paired with face_focus, [eye_focus](#eye_focus) or a similar [tag](#tag).

entries.name: cropped_torso
entries.description: A character is drawn from the waist up and the lower body stops inside the picture, a gap of empty [space](#space) below it. Shoulders-up alone is [cropped_shoulders](#cropped_shoulders), and a lower body simply out of frame is [upper_body](#upper_body).

entries.name: head_out_of_frame
entries.description: The head of the main subject is [cropped](#cropped) away by the picture's edge while the [torso](#torso) stays in view; [nose](#nose) and mouth may show but the eyes do not. It is not for background figures, nor for close shots of the [ass](#ass) or lower body where most of the [figure](#figure) is outside the frame.

entries.name: out_of_frame
entries.description: A character is barely inside the picture, only a hand, an arm or a sliver of body showing at the edge. Different from [outside_border](#outside_border), where part of a subject spills over a drawn frame.

entries.name: foot_out_of_frame
entries.description: A near full-body shot in which one foot falls outside the picture edge while the [knees](#knees) stay visible. Both [feet](#feet) [cropped](#cropped) away is [feet_out_of_frame](#feet_out_of_frame); compare [cowboy_shot](#cowboy_shot) for a higher cut.

entries.name: wide_shot
entries.description: The subject is shown in full but occupies only a small part of the frame, whether from distance or an especially broad canvas. As a rule of thumb it should still read in a thumbnail while taking up under about a quarter of the image, with [scenery](#scenery) usually dominating.

entries.name: lower_body
entries.description: The picture frames its subject from about the waist down, showing most of the lower half of the body. It is not for a shot of the backside alone, which is [close-up](#close-up) or [ass_focus](#ass_focus), nor for background or point-of-view figures.

entries.name: cropped_shoulders
entries.description: The drawing stops or fades out around the [neck](#neck) and upper shoulders, so [no](#no) [torso](#torso) is drawn and a gap is left before the edge. The head must still be visible.

entries.name: head_only
entries.description: A head is shown on its own, with [no](#no) [neck](#neck) or shoulders under it; if the shoulders are visible the picture is [cropped_shoulders](#cropped_shoulders) instead. Floating heads and small [inset](#inset) heads count too. A [headless](#headless) body in frame, or a head cut off, is [severed_head](#severed_head).

entries.name: knees_out_of_frame
entries.description: The body and upper [legs](#legs) are in shot and the lower legs come [back](#back) into it, but the [knees](#knees) themselves fall outside the picture. When the lower legs and [feet](#feet) are cut off as [well](#well), it is a [cowboy_shot](#cowboy_shot).

entries.name: eyes_out_of_frame
entries.description: The framing [cuts](#cuts) across the face above the mouth, leaving the eyes outside the picture while the rest of the head stays in. A tighter crop than [head_out_of_frame](#head_out_of_frame), and it hides the character's gaze.

entries.name: cropped_arms
entries.description: A character's arms are deliberately left [unfinished](#unfinished), ending inside the picture with a gap before the edge. Arms that simply run off the [border](#border) do not count.

entries.name: very_wide_shot
entries.description: The whole subject is in frame but occupies a tiny part of it, dwarfed by the surroundings even more than in [wide_shot](#wide_shot). If [no](#no) character is noticeable at thumbnail size, this is the [tag](#tag) to use.

entries.name: cropped_head
entries.description: Only a character's head, [neck](#neck) and perhaps [collarbone](#collarbone) are drawn, [floating](#floating) alone with [no](#no) body attached. A body that merely leaves the frame does not qualify, and this is not a [chibi](#chibi) [inset](#inset).

entries.name: negative_space
entries.description: A large stretch of empty frame is left around the subject instead of cropping close to it. The emptiness [can](#can) suggest motion or isolation, or simply leave room for lettering.

entries.name: full_composition
entries.description: An illustration worked out as a complete picture, with subject, surroundings and background all developed, rather than a [figure](#figure) set on an empty [field](#field). Used where the whole frame has been built out.

entries.name: mugshot
entries.description: A [police](#police) booking photograph: the subject [square](#square) to the [camera](#camera), often beside a [profile](#profile) view, with a [height](#height) [chart](#chart) or a [placard](#placard) of details behind. Not the same thing as an ordinary [close-up](#close-up) of a face.

entries.name: feet_only
entries.description: The frame is filled by the [feet](#feet) alone, the rest of the body [cropped](#cropped) away. A tight anatomical crop rather than a [figure](#figure) shot.

entries.name: split_crop
entries.description: The frame [cuts](#cuts) lengthwise through a character so only one side of them appears, often paired with a companion image showing the other half.

entries.name: floating_head
entries.description: A head adrift in the picture with [no](#no) [neck](#neck) or body under it. The arrangement is a [staple](#staple) of film-poster style compositions.

entries.name: arm_out_of_frame
entries.description: An arm runs off the edge of the picture, so the hand and whatever it may be doing stay out of sight. What it is [reaching](#reaching) for is left to the viewer.

entries.name: id_photo
entries.description: A stiff head-and-shoulders [portrait](#portrait) taken [square](#square) to the [camera](#camera), of the kind pasted into passports, licences and job applications. The [backdrop](#backdrop) is a flat or graduated blue and the crop sits tight around the face.

entries.name: cropped_arm
entries.description: An arm reaches into the picture from beyond its edge, the person it belongs to left entirely outside the frame. It describes the framing rather than what the arm is doing.

entries.name: from_behind
entries.description: The subject is seen from the [back](#back). Purely a matter of where the [camera](#camera) stands — an embrace, a grab or [sex](#sex) from behind each have their own tags.

entries.name: from_side
entries.description: The subject is seen from its flank, either as a full [profile](#profile) or turned as much as forty-five degrees off it. Applies to objects as readily as to characters.

entries.name: pov
entries.description: The picture is drawn from a first-person viewpoint, with some part of the viewer's own body, a hand, arm or [penis](#penis), visible to establish it. A character merely facing the [camera](#camera) is [looking_at_viewer](#looking_at_viewer), not this.

entries.name: profile
entries.description: The subject's face is seen from the side, showing one half only. For the kind of profile that lists [height](#height), [weight](#weight), or [blood](#blood) type, use [stats](#stats) or [character_profile](#character_profile) instead. Combine with [from_side](#from_side) when the whole body follows the same angle.

entries.name: dutch_angle
entries.description: The whole picture tilted so [horizon](#horizon) and verticals run at a slant. Used to fit a [tall](#tall) [figure](#figure) into a wide frame or to leave a scene feeling unsettled; if you would tilt your head to look at it straight, it applies.

entries.name: from_above
entries.description: The viewer looks down on the subject from a raised vantage point. The angle tends to make a character read as small or vulnerable, though it is just as often used simply to show a scene from overhead.

entries.name: from_below
entries.description: The viewer looks up at the subject, with the [horizon](#horizon) [sitting](#sitting) near or beneath the bottom edge of the frame. It makes a character loom, and is equally often used to see up a [skirt](#skirt).

entries.name: foreshortening
entries.description: Something aimed at the viewer is drawn compressed and enlarged to sell its depth, a fist thrust at the [camera](#camera) being the stock example. Reserve it for pictures where the effect is [strong](#strong); blurred depth is [depth_of_field](#depth_of_field), a separate thing that may or may not appear alongside.

entries.name: straight-on
entries.description: The subject faces the viewer squarely, head, [torso](#torso) and hips all pointed directly forward with [no](#no) turn to either side.

entries.name: pov_hands
entries.description: One or both of the viewer's hands reach into the frame from the bottom edge, [holding](#holding), touching or offering something. Tag [pov](#pov) with it.

entries.name: perspective
entries.description: The picture leans hard on three-dimensional depth, with dramatic [foreshortening](#foreshortening), converging lines or elements thrusting toward the viewer. Add foreshortening or [vanishing_point](#vanishing_point) where those devices stand out.

entries.name: viewfinder
entries.description: Corner brackets or a frame overlay [imitating](#imitating) a camera's viewfinder, telling the viewer the subject is being photographed or filmed. Add [recording](#recording) when a red REC indicator is shown.

entries.name: three_quarter_view
entries.description: The subject is seen at roughly a 45-degree angle, midway between [straight-on](#straight-on) and [from_side](#from_side). Not used for comics whose panels mix many angles at once.

entries.name: fisheye
entries.description: The picture imitates a fisheye lens, [bowing](#bowing) straight lines outward more and more toward the edges. A deliberate [distortion](#distortion) used for drama or for comedy.

entries.name: female_pov
entries.description: The picture is seen through the eyes of a female character, so her own hands or body may enter at the frame edge. A viewpoint shot where the watcher is known to be a woman.

entries.name: partially_underwater_shot
entries.description: The surface of the [water](#water) splits the frame so the scene appears above and below at once, as though the [camera](#camera) itself were half sunk. It describes where the view is taken from; a character [standing](#standing) in water is [partially_submerged](#partially_submerged).

entries.name: pov_doorway
entries.description: The viewpoint is in or just outside an open [doorway](#doorway), as when the viewer or the character is answering the [door](#door). Tag doorway and often [pov](#pov) with it.

entries.name: view_between_legs
entries.description: The [camera](#camera) sits low so that a [standing](#standing) figure's [legs](#legs) frame whatever lies beyond them. This describes where the viewer stands, not a character [bending](#bending) to peer through their own legs.

entries.name: from_outside
entries.description: The scene is watched from outside a room or enclosure, generally through a [window](#window) or open [doorway](#doorway). If the main subject is itself out in the open, [outdoors](#outdoors) is the truer [tag](#tag).

entries.name: vanishing_point
entries.description: The lines of the scene converge on a single point that pulls the eye inward, as in a [street](#street) seen from the middle of the [road](#road). Ordinary [perspective](#perspective) such as a checkered [floor](#floor) does not qualify on its own, and several such points [can](#can) occur in an angled view.

entries.name: isometric
entries.description: The scene is built in axonometric projection: parallel lines stay parallel instead of meeting at a vanishing point, and things keep their size however far off they are. It is [familiar](#familiar) from technical drawings and older strategy games.

entries.name: pov_across_table
entries.description: The viewer sits opposite a character across a [table](#table), [counter](#counter) or [desk](#desk), as at a [meal](#meal) or a date. Tag [pov](#pov) and table with it.

entries.name: pov_across_bed
entries.description: A character lies on a [bed](#bed) facing the [camera](#camera), framed so the viewer seems to be stretched out on the same [mattress](#mattress). The low, level eye line is what sells it.

entries.name: pov_breasts
entries.description: A chest fills the frame from the viewer's vantage, as though they were right in front of it or being pulled against it. It is the framing rather than any nudity that carries the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: taker_pov
entries.description: The picture is framed from the point of view of the partner being taken during [sex](#sex), looking up or across at the one doing the taking. The counterpart to the other partner's point of view.

entries.name: pov_peephole
entries.description: The picture is framed as though seen through a door's spyhole: a circular [field](#field) of view, [heavy](#heavy) [barrel](#barrel) [distortion](#distortion), [darkness](#darkness) all around. Only for the effect; an actual peephole drawn in the scene is tagged separately.

entries.name: optical_illusion
entries.description: The picture is built around a trick of the eye: impossible [geometry](#geometry) such as Penrose [stairs](#stairs), [forced](#forced) [perspective](#perspective), an ambiguous [figure](#figure), or an illusion of colour or motion. The [puzzle](#puzzle) has to be the point, not merely a pattern somewhere in the frame.

entries.name: from_inside
entries.description: The [camera](#camera) stands inside a room, vehicle or other enclosure and looks out through a [window](#window), [doorway](#doorway) or [opening](#opening). Where something important shares that enclosure with the camera, [indoors](#indoors) describes the shot better.

entries.name: sunrise_stance
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) thrust toward the [camera](#camera) so its tip nearly touches the lens, the blade hugely foreshortened against a small, distant [figure](#figure). The pose comes from [mecha](#mecha) animation and is a [staple](#staple) of dramatic hero shots, a framing trick as much as a [fighting](#fighting) stance.

entries.name: under_shot
entries.description: A viewpoint set low and angled upward at the [crotch](#crotch) or backside. The framing puts those areas at the centre of the picture without necessarily uncovering them.

entries.name: pov_legs
entries.description: The viewer's own [legs](#legs) or [feet](#feet) intrude into the bottom of the frame, placing them bodily inside the scene. Often paired with a character [standing](#standing) or seated in front of them.

entries.name: forced_perspective
entries.description: An optical trick that makes something look nearer, further off, larger or smaller than it is by [playing](#playing) scale against the camera's position. A hand appearing to pinch a distant [tower](#tower) is the classic version.

entries.name: pov_dating
entries.description: The image is framed from the seat opposite, so the viewer is the character's companion for the outing. Cafe tables, [festival](#festival) stalls and cinema rows are the usual staging.

entries.name: eyewear_view
entries.description: The picture is framed as though seen through the lenses of [glasses](#glasses) or [goggles](#goggles), the rims darkening the edges. Often used where the eyewear grants some special kind of sight.

entries.name: atmospheric_perspective
entries.description: Depth conveyed by the air itself: distant hills and buildings fade toward the colour of the [sky](#sky), losing [contrast](#contrast) and detail, while nearer things stay crisp. Haze deepens the effect, and it appears mostly in wide outdoor views.

entries.name: pov_adoring
entries.description: The character aims open affection at the [camera](#camera), whether a blushing [confession](#confession), warm praise, a head pat or a [kiss](#kiss) meant for the lens. The viewer stands in as the beloved, so a blank or [cold](#cold) face does not count.

entries.name: pov_bullying
entries.description: The characters direct mockery, threats or rough handling at the [camera](#camera), casting the viewer as the one being picked on. Ranges from jeering to physical or sexual aggression.

entries.name: lap_pov
entries.description: The viewpoint sits on a seated character's [lap](#lap), looking up at them from where a head would rest. It is often the setup for an ear-cleaning scene with the viewer [lying](#lying) down.

entries.name: blurry
entries.description: Part of the picture is deliberately unsharp, as a stylistic [choice](#choice), an imitation of a lens, or something seen through [glass](#glass) or [water](#water). Use [depth_of_field](#depth_of_field) for focus falloff and [motion_blur](#motion_blur) for movement; a badly scanned image is neither.

entries.name: blurry_background
entries.description: Everything behind the subject falls out of focus while the subject stays crisp, the way a wide lens aperture renders a scene. It often runs together with [depth_of_field](#depth_of_field) and [blurry_foreground](#blurry_foreground).

entries.name: depth_of_field
entries.description: Part of the picture is left soft and out of focus while another part stays sharp, [imitating](#imitating) a lens that [can](#can) only focus at one distance. The blur may sit in front, behind, or both, and it steers the eye to the subject.

entries.name: foot_focus
entries.description: The [feet](#feet) are the main subject of the picture, pushed close to the [camera](#camera) or presented toward the viewer. It asks more than feet, which only requires them to be visible.

entries.name: blurry_foreground
entries.description: Whatever sits closest to the viewer is out of focus, such as a [railing](#railing), leaves or a shoulder crossing the edge of the frame. Frequently combined with [blurry_background](#blurry_background) so only the middle distance is sharp.

entries.name: hip_focus
entries.description: The hips are what the picture is about, either by framing or by exaggerated emphasis. Hips merely being visible is not enough.

entries.name: animal_focus
entries.description: One or more real creatures are what the picture is about, as in a [cat](#cat) or [rabbit](#rabbit) [portrait](#portrait) with [no](#no) person in view. Add the species; [furry](#furry) characters fall outside it.

entries.name: motion_blur
entries.description: Part of the picture is smeared along the direction of travel to sell speed, either the moving subject itself or the background rushing past behind it. Distinct from motion lines, which are drawn strokes rather than a smear.

entries.name: vehicle_focus
entries.description: A [car](#car), [tank](#tank), plane or other vehicle is the main subject of the picture rather than a character. A picture centred on a [giant](#giant) [robot](#robot) takes [mecha_focus](#mecha_focus) instead.

entries.name: food_focus
entries.description: The picture centres on [food](#food) or [drink](#drink) itself, most often as a fairly [realistic](#realistic) still life with [no](#no) [people](#people) and an uncluttered background. The dish sits in a [tray](#tray), [bowl](#bowl), [plate](#plate) or [cup](#cup) and is the subject.

entries.name: bokeh
entries.description: Soft circular discs of light scattered through the out-of-focus parts of a picture, the way a lens renders distant points of light or airborne particles. It comes with [depth_of_field](#depth_of_field); [lens_flare](#lens_flare) is a different artefact and does not line up with any light source.

entries.name: mecha_focus
entries.description: A [mecha](#mecha) is the main subject of the composition, filling the frame or drawing the eye first, with any pilots or bystanders treated as secondary.

entries.name: eye_focus
entries.description: The eyes are the point of the picture, either through the framing or because they are rendered with unusual care. Often a close view of the upper face, not merely any picture with pretty eyes.

entries.name: armpit_focus
entries.description: The picture is built around an armpit as its subject, usually a close view with the arm lifted clear. Sleeveless tops and raised arms come with it.

entries.name: back_focus
entries.description: The upper [back](#back) is the picture's main subject, generally in a close view taken from behind. It is not [ass_focus](#ass_focus), which centres on the buttocks, and where the back is merely visible [plain](#plain) back is enough.

entries.name: object_focus
entries.description: An inanimate thing, rather than any character, is what the picture is about. Weapons, vehicles and [food](#food) have focus tags of their own, so this covers everything else; name the object with its own [tag](#tag) as [well](#well).

entries.name: hand_focus
entries.description: The composition is built around a character's hands, with the rest of the body secondary, blurred or [cropped](#cropped) away. Close studies of gestures and of fingers [holding](#holding) something typically qualify.

entries.name: pectoral_focus
entries.description: The picture centres on a character's [pectorals](#pectorals), often a close crop of the chest with the rest of the body secondary. The male counterpart of [breast_focus](#breast_focus).

entries.name: weapon_focus
entries.description: The picture centers on one or more weapons themselves, with any wielder secondary or left out entirely. Presentation shots and detail studies both qualify.

entries.name: creature_focus
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) rather than a person is what the picture is about, with human characters secondary or absent altogether.

entries.name: monster_focus
entries.description: The picture is built around one or more monsters, which hold the frame as its subject rather than lurking at the edges as a [threat](#threat). Any [people](#people) present are secondary, or absent altogether.

entries.name: sky_focus
entries.description: The open [sky](#sky) is the subject of the picture, with any figures or ground reduced to a small strip. Clouds, colour and light carry the image.

entries.name: thigh_focus
entries.description: The framing puts the [thighs](#thighs) at the centre of the picture, cropping or angling so they dominate everything else. The skin, the legwear and the shape of the leg are what the composition is about.

entries.name: flower_focus
entries.description: The blooms carry the picture: they fill the frame or [anchor](#anchor) the composition, with any [people](#people) reduced to bystanders or left out entirely. Use it when the [flower](#flower) is the subject and not merely a prop in someone's hand.

entries.name: hair_focus
entries.description: The picture is built around the hair, [giving](#giving) the style more attention than the person wearing it. Framing and detail sit on the strands rather than the face.

entries.name: plant_focus
entries.description: The picture centres on a [plant](#plant), with any figures secondary or absent altogether. A statement about composition rather than about which species is shown.

entries.name: navel_focus
entries.description: Framing that puts the [midriff](#midriff) at the centre — [navel](#navel), [stomach](#stomach), [abs](#abs) — often [cropped](#cropped) close enough to leave the head and [legs](#legs) out of frame. The rest of the body is incidental.

entries.name: footwear_focus
entries.description: The [shoes](#shoes) or [boots](#boots) are what the picture is about, filling the frame or drawn with unusual care. It applies to footwear shown on its own with nobody wearing it as [well](#well).

entries.name: clothes_focus
entries.description: The composition centres on what is being worn, framing the garment and its details rather than the wearer's face or [figure](#figure). Common in outfit designs and [fashion](#fashion) illustration.

entries.name: leg_focus
entries.description: Framing, cropping or lighting that makes a character's [legs](#legs) the subject of the picture rather than the face or the whole [figure](#figure).

entries.name: book_focus
entries.description: Books are what the picture is about, filling the frame or plainly presented as its subject. A few volumes in the background or one barely visible in a hand does not count.

entries.name: cloud_focus
entries.description: The clouds themselves are what the picture is about, filling the frame and [holding](#holding) the eye rather than [sitting](#sitting) behind a subject.

entries.name: soft_focus
entries.description: A deliberately hazy, [glowing](#glowing) blur that imitates a [camera](#camera) lens flaw, softening the edges of a shot while the subject stays reasonably sharp. A rendering [choice](#choice) about the image, not a description of anything [fluffy](#fluffy) within it.

entries.name: mouth_focus
entries.description: The mouth carries the picture, drawn close or in unusual detail while the rest of the face softens or falls outside the frame. Lips, [teeth](#teeth) and [tongue](#tongue) take the attention the eyes would normally have.

entries.name: ear_focus
entries.description: The framing centres on an ear and lets it fill much of the picture. Common for [animal](#animal) ears and for close looks at piercings.

entries.name: neck_focus
entries.description: Framing that dwells on the [neck](#neck) and throat, usually [cropped](#cropped) tight above and below. The face may be cut off altogether.

entries.name: zoom_layer
entries.description: An extra layer laid over an illustration that magnifies part of it, commonly an enlarged copy of the character placed behind them as a background element. It may be mirrored, rotated, faded or given a different expression; a view from a different 3D angle counts as a projected [inset](#inset) instead.

entries.name: chibi_inset
entries.description: Small super-deformed figures added beside or behind an otherwise normally drawn picture, usually as a [comic](#comic) aside, or a [chibi](#chibi) face on a speech [bubble](#bubble) showing who is [talking](#talking). They must not interact with the main figures, and the artist must have drawn them.

entries.name: reference_inset
entries.description: A small reference picture embedded within the artwork, usually in a [corner](#corner), showing the source the drawing is based on. Common for fanart and redraws that want to show what they were [working](#working) from.

entries.name: sequential
entries.description: Several moments drawn in one picture that read in order, like frames of a film seconds apart. A longer span between stages is [time_lapse](#time_lapse) instead; separate bordered panels are [comic](#comic).

entries.name: request_inset
entries.description: A screenshot of a fan request placed directly into the finished artwork, usually taken from an anonymous inbox service. The request text sits alongside or over the drawing it inspired.

entries.name: symmetry
entries.description: A composition whose two halves [mirror](#mirror) or rotate into each other, [reading](#reading) the same on both sides of a central line or point.

entries.name: projected_inset
entries.description: A projected image of a person appears somewhere in the background, like a [hologram](#hologram), [screen](#screen) feed, or memory overlay. When the extra layer is only a flat, zoomed-in view of another part of the same picture, use [zoom_layer](#zoom_layer) instead.

entries.name: inset
entries.description: A second, smaller picture sits inside the main one in a frame of its own, most often a [portrait](#portrait) or photograph of a character. It reads as a picture within a picture rather than as a [comic](#comic) panel.

entries.name: photo_inset
entries.description: A photograph set into the image, either as a small reference panel shown beside the drawing or as a deliberate part of the composition. It often accompanies [photo-referenced](#photo-referenced).

entries.name: split_screen
entries.description: The image divided into two halves by a line, used to compare a character's forms, place two figures side by side, or set [rivals](#rivals) against each other. More than two columns is [column_lineup](#column_lineup) instead.

entries.name: screenshot_inset
entries.description: A [captured](#captured) frame set as a smaller panel inside a bigger image, usually tucked in a [corner](#corner) as a reference or a joke.

entries.name: official_art_inset
entries.description: A piece of official artwork is set into the picture as a small panel, [standing](#standing) as a reference or a [comparison](#comparison) beside the drawn version.

entries.name: split_theme
entries.description: Two contrasting ideas shown at once with a visible divide between them, such as light against [dark](#dark), youth against age, or a character's hidden [nature](#nature) against their outward one. Often built on a [split_screen](#split_screen) layout.

entries.name: game_screenshot_inset
entries.description: A game still set inside the picture as a smaller panel or [window](#window) instead of filling the [backdrop](#backdrop). Often appears as a [screen](#screen) that a character is looking at.

entries.name: doodle_inset
entries.description: A small rough [scribble](#scribble) tucked into a [corner](#corner) of an otherwise finished picture, taking up only a fraction of the canvas. Usually a joke, an aside or a quick extra thought about the main scene.

entries.name: borderless_panels
entries.description: A [comic](#comic) whose panels have [no](#no) drawn lines or gutters between them, the scenes simply set side by side. Mark it as a comic as [well](#well).

entries.name: recurring_image
entries.description: Part of the artwork has been copied and placed again elsewhere within the same picture, so identical figures or objects repeat. Usually points to an artist reusing a drawing rather than a deliberate storytelling [device](#device).

entries.name: juxtaposition
entries.description: Two sides of one person are set against each other: a composed, respectable [figure](#figure) beside a debauched one shown on a [screen](#screen), a photograph or a second half of the picture. The gap between the two halves is the whole point.

entries.name: cut-in
entries.description: A smaller image laid over the main one so that it slices into the frame, most often a [portrait](#portrait) or a close pair of eyes added for punch. Distinct from a [cross-section](#cross-section), whose purpose is to explain rather than to intensify.

entries.name: recursion
entries.description: The picture contains a smaller copy of itself, which in turn contains a smaller copy again, and so on inward, the Droste effect. Other forms of self-reference, such as a character [holding](#holding) the very picture they appear in, count too.

entries.name: sketch_inset
entries.description: A small rough drawing set into a [corner](#corner) of an otherwise finished picture. Often an alternate expression, a detail view or a joke panel.

entries.name: screen_zoom
entries.description: The magnified projection of a performer thrown onto a large [screen](#screen) behind a [stage](#stage) so the [back](#back) rows [can](#can) see. The effect resembles a [zoom_layer](#zoom_layer) built into the scene itself.

entries.name: page_tear
entries.description: Part of the picture is drawn as [torn](#torn) [paper](#paper), and through the rip a different version of the same scene appears, often bare skin or [underwear](#underwear) where the intact surface still shows clothing. Ripping an actual sheet of paper within the scene is [tearing_paper](#tearing_paper).

entries.name: montage
entries.description: Several separate images assembled into one picture, laid side by side or overlapping. Used to compress a run of moments, or to show many sides of a subject at once.

entries.name: multiple_views
entries.description: Two or more separate depictions of the same character in one image, from different angles, in different outfits or in different [poses](#poses). It does not [cover](#cover) comics, nor a [zoom_layer](#zoom_layer) that merely repeats the main [figure](#figure), and it never goes with [solo](#solo); a duplicate within a single scene is [dual_persona](#dual_persona) or [clone](#clone).

entries.name: reference_sheet
entries.description: A design sheet laying out a subject from several angles, with [notes](#notes) and often separate close-ups of clothing, [accessories](#accessories), or a clothed and unclothed version. Applies to characters, weapons or vehicles alike; the same pose in different outfits is [variations](#variations) instead.

entries.name: multiple_persona
entries.description: Three or more distinct versions of one character share the picture, the larger sibling of [dual_persona](#dual_persona). Solo and the singular counters do not belong with it, identical copies are [clone](#clone), and a [reference_sheet](#reference_sheet) or a set of [variations](#variations) does not qualify.

entries.name: expressions
entries.description: Several drawings of the same character wearing different feelings, often laid out as a [chart](#chart). It names the set of faces rather than any single one of them.

entries.name: evolutionary_line
entries.description: A picture built around the successive forms of one [creature](#creature) [family](#family) shown together. Not every [stage](#stage) need appear, but the family link has to be what the picture is about — a [crowd](#crowd) that happens to include relatives does not count.

entries.name: character_profile
entries.description: A reference-style page setting out facts about the character shown: name, age, temperament, likes and dislikes, usually arranged around a [portrait](#portrait).

entries.name: collage
entries.description: Several separate images pasted together into one picture, such as a [grid](#grid) of screencaps or a sheet of characters drawn by different hands. A single artist's multi-panel composition is not this.

entries.name: color_guide
entries.description: The palette used for the picture is shown inside it as a row or block of swatches, commonly beside a character design or reference drawing. Printer's colour [bars](#bars) count too.

entries.name: turnaround
entries.description: The same character, in the same pose and outfit, drawn from several rotation angles, front, side and [back](#back), as on a reference sheet. A character physically [spinning](#spinning) to face a new direction in the scene is [turning_around](#turning_around) instead.

entries.name: before_and_after
entries.description: Two views of the same character, place or object separated by a stretch of time, showing what changed: aged, transformed, decayed, or cleaned up and restored. Labels saying so need not appear in the picture.

entries.name: variations
entries.description: The same character repeated several times in one picture wearing a single outfit, with only small changes to hair, colour or [accessories](#accessories) between copies. Bigger differences call for [multiple_views](#multiple_views) instead, step-by-step process images are [how_to](#how_to), and a series of separate pictures is a variant_set.

entries.name: column_lineup
entries.description: Character portraits set out in ranks of columns or rows, as in a [cast](#cast) [chart](#chart). It often runs together with [multiple_monochrome](#multiple_monochrome) or [color_coordination](#color_coordination).

entries.name: multiple_drawing_challenge
entries.description: A [chart](#chart) of several separate drawings made for a challenge, usually of one character, series or theme, laid out panel by panel. The assembled set rather than any single drawing is what the [tag](#tag) names.

entries.name: chart
entries.description: The picture arranges several subjects side by side for [comparison](#comparison), as an expression chart, a [height](#height) chart or a [grid](#grid) of outfits. Numeric data plotted spatially is a [graph](#graph), and an explanatory drawing is a [diagram](#diagram).

entries.name: comparison
entries.description: A picture laid out to show a difference: between two characters, between versions of one character, or between before and after some change. Usually side by side and often labelled.

entries.name: height_chart
entries.description: Characters drawn side by side against a scale so their heights [can](#can) be compared. A reference-sheet format designers use to keep proportions steady.

entries.name: age_comparison
entries.description: One character appears twice in the same picture, once as a [child](#child) and once grown, set up so the two ages [can](#can) be read side by side. They may simply stand together or interact, which turns it into a meeting across time.

entries.name: how_to
entries.description: A tutorial picture [giving](#giving) step-by-step instructions for whatever it shows: drawing a body part, [tying](#tying) a [sash](#sash), performing a technique. Numbered steps and explanatory text are the usual form.

entries.name: stats
entries.description: A graphic with labelled figures describing the subject, such as [measurements](#measurements), ratings or attribute [bars](#bars) laid out like a [profile](#profile) [card](#card).

entries.name: expression_chart
entries.description: A [grid](#grid) of small heads [working](#working) through a run of [expressions](#expressions), almost always [following](#following) a fixed [template](#template) and often [carrying](#carrying) jokes as [well](#well). A loose set of faces outside a grid is just expressions.

entries.name: evolution
entries.description: A [chart](#chart) or row laying out how a character or [creature](#creature) changes over time, each [stage](#stage) set beside the next. Read as one [progression](#progression) rather than as separate drawings.

entries.name: size_comparison
entries.description: A picture set up so two or more things [can](#can) be measured against each other, often with a [familiar](#familiar) object or person used as the yardstick. Also covers a character [holding](#holding) parts of their own body up beside somebody else's.

entries.name: clothes_on_and_off
entries.description: The same character appears twice side by side, dressed in one version and undressed in the other, for direct [comparison](#comparison). A paired layout rather than an act of [undressing](#undressing).

entries.name: bust_chart
entries.description: Characters lined up, usually in [profile](#profile), so their breast sizes [can](#can) be set side by side. Numbered [measurements](#measurements) may or may not be printed alongside.

entries.name: progression
entries.description: One image laid out as a series of stages, showing a process advancing step by step: a drawing being made, a pregnancy, a [transformation](#transformation). When the steps are a character getting older, add [age_progression](#age_progression) as [well](#well).

entries.name: graph
entries.description: Data plotted out as a picture in its own right: line plots, scatter plots, bar charts, [radar](#radar) charts or [pie](#pie) charts. Where the [chart](#chart) is only incidental [scenery](#scenery), [graph_(object)](#graph_(object)) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: costume_chart
entries.description: One character shown in three or more different outfits arranged together, whether or not it is drawn as a literal [chart](#chart). With only two outfits, [dual_persona](#dual_persona) usually suits better.

entries.name: relationship_graph
entries.description: A [chart](#chart) laying out how a [cast](#cast) connects, with portraits joined by labelled lines or arrows. It exists to make a tangled group of characters legible at a [glance](#glance).

entries.name: polar_opposites
entries.description: Two figures or two halves of an image set up as direct contraries: light against [dark](#dark), [angel](#angel) against devil, [day](#day) against [night](#night). Symmetry often comes with it but is tagged separately.

entries.name: expectation_vs._reality
entries.description: Two versions of the same scene set side by side: the flattering [idea](#idea) against the disappointing outcome. The joke lives in the gap between them.

entries.name: weapon_connection
entries.description: Two characters from different works are drawn together because they carry the same kind of [weapon](#weapon). The shared armament is the whole point of the [crossover](#crossover) or [comparison](#comparison).

entries.name: information_sheet
entries.description: A page setting out details of a character, setting or product, either as a reference for drawing or as promotional material. Labelled diagrams, stat blocks and annotated views are the usual form.

entries.name: equipment_layout
entries.description: Somebody's gear laid out flat and spread apart so each piece [can](#can) be read on its own: weapons, packs, [tools](#tools), clothing. The photographic knolling arrangement, drawn.

entries.name: kiss_chart
entries.description: A [grid](#grid) of small panels showing the same pair performing a different kind of [kiss](#kiss) in each cell. It belongs with the multi-panel drawing challenges rather than being one scene.

entries.name: artist_progress
entries.description: Old and new drawings of the same subject set side by side to show how the artist has changed, usually labelled with years. It overlaps with redrawing a single earlier picture.

entries.name: time_lapse
entries.description: One image built from several frames of the same scene at widely separated moments, so a long stretch of change reads at a [glance](#glance). The viewpoint holds still while the subject grows, ages or decays; when only seconds pass it is [sequential](#sequential) instead, and a drawing coming together belongs to [making-of](#making-of).

entries.name: character_select
entries.description: The picture imitates a game's roster [screen](#screen), portraits ranged in a [grid](#grid) with a [cursor](#cursor) [sitting](#sitting) on one of them. Fighting games supply the usual [template](#template).

entries.name: group_profile
entries.description: Several characters shown together in side view, their faces lined up in [profile](#profile). Common in comparisons and character lineups.

entries.name: length_markings
entries.description: Tick marks or a graduated scale drawn beside a [figure](#figure) or object to state how long or [tall](#tall) it is. Common on reference sheets and size comparisons.

entries.name: poses
entries.description: One character drawn several times over in different attitudes within a single image, as on a study or [model](#model) sheet. The repetition of the same [figure](#figure) is the point, not a [crowd](#crowd).

entries.name: sprite_sheet
entries.description: A reference image gathering many sprites, or one sprite's [poses](#poses) and palette variants, arranged in a [grid](#grid) on a flat background. Made for looking things up rather than for [display](#display).

entries.name: character_chart
entries.description: A single sheet laying out a work's [cast](#cast), arranged as a [list](#list), a [family](#family) [tree](#tree) or a web of who relates to whom. Names and brief [notes](#notes) usually sit beside each face.

entries.name: border
entries.description: A band runs along the edges of the picture, most often a [plain](#plain) single colour on all four sides. Decorated frames are [ornate_border](#ornate_border), a [figure](#figure) [spilling](#spilling) over the edge is [outside_border](#outside_border), and letterbox or pillarbox [bars](#bars) do not count.
