entries.name: white_border
entries.description: A white frame runs around the edges of the image. View the original [file](#file), since a [transparent](#transparent) [border](#border) also previews as white.

entries.name: outside_border
entries.description: Part of a character or object crosses over or beyond a drawn [border](#border), letterbox or panel edge. Never used for text, and not the same as [out_of_frame](#out_of_frame), where the subject is nearly absent.

entries.name: letterboxed
entries.description: Bars run along the top and bottom edges of the picture, as a widescreen film looks on a squarer [screen](#screen). It does not count as a [border](#border), though [outside_border](#outside_border) may be added; [bars](#bars) at the left and right are [pillarboxed](#pillarboxed).

entries.name: black_border
entries.description: A black frame runs along all four edges of the picture. Black [bars](#bars) top and bottom only are [letterboxed](#letterboxed), at the sides only [pillarboxed](#pillarboxed), and a [dark](#dark) line drawn around a [figure](#figure) is [outline](#outline).

entries.name: pillarboxed
entries.description: Vertical [bars](#bars) down the left and right of the picture, left over from fitting a narrow image into a wider frame. The horizontal counterpart is [letterboxed](#letterboxed), and the bars do not count as a [border](#border).

entries.name: grey_border
entries.description: The picture is framed by a grey band along its edges. The [border](#border) is painted into the image rather than added by the viewer's software.

entries.name: pink_border
entries.description: A pink frame [running](#running) round the edges of the picture, drawn on top of the image rather than being part of the scene. One of the [border](#border) colours.

entries.name: blue_border
entries.description: The outer edge of the image is framed by a blue band. It refers to the artwork itself, never to a coloured [border](#border) a site draws around a picture.

entries.name: inset_border
entries.description: A frame line drawn inside the picture and set in from its edge, usually one or two [plain](#plain) strokes in a single colour. Add [ornate_border](#ornate_border) when the framing is elaborate rather than simple.

entries.name: ornate_border
entries.description: The frame around the picture is worked with intricate ornament, geometric patterning or small figures rather than being a [plain](#plain) line. Often, though not always, combined with [inset_border](#inset_border).

entries.name: round_image
entries.description: The artwork is framed inside a [circle](#circle), or occasionally an ellipse, like a tondo. If the subject breaks out past the circle, add [outside_border](#outside_border) as [well](#well).

entries.name: round_border
entries.description: The picture is enclosed in a circular frame, with the corners outside it left blank or filled with a flat colour. A soft circular fade instead of a hard edge is [vignetting](#vignetting).

entries.name: red_border
entries.description: The image is framed by a red [border](#border). Historically associated with a flagged post on image boards, which gave rise to art drawn with one on purpose.

entries.name: yellow_border
entries.description: The image itself carries a yellow frame around its edges, distinct from an unrelated yellow [outline](#outline) some sites draw around linked posts. Tag [border](#border) as [well](#well).

entries.name: brown_border
entries.description: A brown frame runs around the edges of the picture, set outside the artwork itself. Add [border](#border).

entries.name: yellow_outline
entries.description: A yellow line traces the edge of a character or object to lift it from the background. Tag [outline](#outline) alongside; other colours have their own separate tags.

entries.name: rounded_corners
entries.description: The image's corners are rounded off rather than [square](#square). Common on card-style artwork and app icons.

entries.name: green_border
entries.description: The picture itself is framed by a green band along its edges. Only [paint](#paint) that is part of the image counts; coloured outlines a gallery draws around a thumbnail do not.

entries.name: purple_border
entries.description: A purple band framing the picture along its edges. A property of the picture's framing rather than anything drawn inside the scene.

entries.name: against_fourth_wall
entries.description: Hands, face or body flatten against the [invisible](#invisible) plane at the front of the picture, as though a sheet of [glass](#glass) sat where the frame is. That wall exists nowhere in the scene, only as the edge of the image.

entries.name: orange_border
entries.description: An orange band runs round the edge of the picture, separating the artwork from its margin. It is drawn as part of the image rather than a background colour showing through.

entries.name: lace_border
entries.description: A band of [lace](#lace) pattern [running](#running) round the outer edge of the picture as an ornamental frame. It may sit over a lace background, and is not the same as a [doily](#doily) drawn as an object.

entries.name: transparent_border
entries.description: The frame drawn around the picture is left [transparent](#transparent) rather than filled with colour, so whatever sits behind the [file](#file) shows through it. Check the original image, since preview thumbnails usually render such a [border](#border) as [plain](#plain) white.

entries.name: fading_border
entries.description: The edge of the picture dissolves gradually into the [space](#space) around it instead of ending at a clean [outline](#outline). The artwork thins out toward the margin rather than being cut off by a [border](#border).

entries.name: blurry_edges
entries.description: The picture goes soft towards its outer corners, steering the eye into the middle. Corners that darken instead are [vignetting](#vignetting), and an image [dissolving](#dissolving) at its rim has its own [fading](#fading) [border](#border) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: gradient_border
entries.description: The frame at the edge of the picture fades from one colour into another rather than [holding](#holding) a flat tone. The strip itself shifts, not the background it encloses.

entries.name: aqua_border
entries.description: A band of blue-green runs round the edge of the picture. The [border](#border) belongs to the image itself rather than to anything drawn inside it.

entries.name: trim_marks
entries.description: The thin [corner](#corner) lines a [printer](#printer) follows when trimming a page down to its final size, with colour deliberately bled past them so a slightly off cut still looks clean. Their presence marks the image as print-ready layout art rather than a [plain](#plain) illustration.

entries.name: floral_border
entries.description: The frame around the picture is made of flowers, or is an [ornate](#ornate) [border](#border) decorated with them. The decoration sits at the image edge rather than inside the scene.

entries.name: gold_border
entries.description: A [gold](#gold) frame runs around the edge of the picture, closing the image in. Card art, [ornate](#ornate) portraits and rarity displays use it.

entries.name: meandros_border
entries.description: The edge of the picture itself framed with a repeating meander band rather than the pattern appearing printed on an object within the scene.

entries.name: chinese_knot_border
entries.description: The picture is framed by a decorative band of Chinese knotwork [running](#running) around its edge. It records the frame itself, not a knot worn or held by somebody inside the scene.

entries.name: film_strip_border
entries.description: The picture is framed as though printed on a strip of film, perforations [running](#running) along its edges. A decorative frame rather than an actual strip inside the scene.

entries.name: multicolored_border
entries.description: The band framing the image carries more than one colour, [split](#split) into blocks or graded from one into another. What lies inside the frame is unaffected.

entries.name: x-ray
entries.description: Seeing through a normally opaque barrier such as skin, [armor](#armor) or a wall, as if by x-ray vision, drawn as a [transparent](#transparent) overlay or cut-out with the inside and outside always overlapping. A real medical [scan](#scan) is [x-ray_film](#x-ray_film), a separated internal view with [no](#no) visible barrier is [cross-section](#cross-section), and sheer or [wet](#wet) clothing is see-through instead.

entries.name: cross-section
entries.description: A cutaway drawn in its own frame revealing what sits inside something. Most often it exposes internal [anatomy](#anatomy) during [sex](#sex), with the vagina, [cervix](#cervix) and womb visible, though ordinary technical cutaways qualify too. Where the [interior](#interior) shows straight through the body, use [x-ray](#x-ray).

entries.name: chemical_structure
entries.description: A molecule drawn into the picture, its atoms shown as letters or spheres joined by bond lines, flat or in three dimensions. A formula written purely as text, such as H2O, is something else.

entries.name: diagram
entries.description: Boxes, arrows and short captions set out to show how things relate or in what order they happen. Covers relationship charts and step-by-step breakdowns drawn into the picture.

entries.name: diorama
entries.description: A [miniature](#miniature) scene that reads as lifted out of the world, a slice of room or [landscape](#landscape) enclosed in a [box](#box) or [resting](#resting) on a small base. Photographs of real physical models take the medium spelling instead.

entries.name: x-ray_vision
entries.description: Someone within the scene [can](#can) look straight through [clothes](#clothes), walls or other barriers, whether by gadget or by an innate power. Where nobody in the picture could plausibly perceive the see-through view and it exists purely for the reader's benefit, the [plain](#plain) [x-ray](#x-ray) [tag](#tag) is the right one instead.

entries.name: anatomy
entries.description: The picture opens its subject up to show what is inside, whether [bone](#bone), muscle, [organs](#organs) or [machinery](#machinery). Diagram-like cutaways of [people](#people), animals, plants and machines all belong here.

entries.name: guide
entries.description: An instructional image laid out to explain or demonstrate something, with [numbered](#numbered) steps, arrows or annotated examples. The [teaching](#teaching) arrangement is what makes the [tag](#tag), whatever the subject is.

entries.name: floorplan
entries.description: A room or [building](#building) drawn with a wall or the [ceiling](#ceiling) taken away, so the viewer looks in from outside at the furniture and the [people](#people). Bare architectural drawings with [no](#no) occupants are a layout plan.

entries.name: orbital_path
entries.description: The route an orbiting body follows is drawn into the picture as a visible line or ellipse. A diagram-like touch in [space](#space) and astronomy scenes.

entries.name: educational
entries.description: The picture is laid out to teach or explain something, often as a mock [textbook](#textbook) page, a labelled [diagram](#diagram) or a lesson under way. May be sincere or a straight-faced [parody](#parody) of one.

entries.name: hitbox
entries.description: The [collision](#collision) area of a character or an [attack](#attack) drawn onto the picture as an [outline](#outline) or a coloured [patch](#patch). Shooting games mark it as a small dot at the pilot's waist; [fighting](#fighting) games colour striking and vulnerable areas differently.

entries.name: dollhouse_view
entries.description: A [building](#building) drawn with its walls or [ceiling](#ceiling) taken away so every room and everybody inside [can](#can) be seen at once. Everything within should read as tiny; the tighter, boxed-in version of the [idea](#idea) is a [diorama](#diorama).

entries.name: tall_image
entries.description: An image at least 1024 pixels [tall](#tall) and at least four times taller than it is wide.

entries.name: wide_image
entries.description: An image at least four times wider than it is [tall](#tall) and at least 1024 pixels across, such as a [panorama](#panorama) or a long horizontal strip. The dimensions alone decide it; [tall_image](#tall_image) is the vertical counterpart.

entries.name: oval_image
entries.description: The whole picture is cut to an oval or a related rounded [outline](#outline): an [egg](#egg), a lens, a [stadium](#stadium) capsule, a [figure](#figure) of eight, or the twin circles of a view through [binoculars](#binoculars). It is the frame that takes the shape, not an oval drawn inside a rectangular image.

entries.name: panorama
entries.description: A view far wider than the eye could take in at once, so straight lines [bow](#bow) along the long axis. A full turn of the surroundings additionally takes the 360 panorama [tag](#tag).

entries.name: traditional_media
entries.description: Artwork made physically with [pencil](#pencil), [ink](#ink), [paint](#paint) or markers rather than produced on a [computer](#computer). A digital piece [imitating](#imitating) that look is [faux_traditional_media](#faux_traditional_media) instead, and a mix of physical and digital work is [mixed_media](#mixed_media).

entries.name: photo_(medium)
entries.description: The post is an actual photograph taken with a [camera](#camera), most often of traditional artwork or of art materials with a drawing among them. A photograph drawn inside an illustration is [photo_(object)](#photo_(object)).

entries.name: 3d
entries.description: The picture is rendered from [computer](#computer) three-dimensional models rather than drawn. A photograph is [photo_(medium)](#photo_(medium)), a drawing that only looks lifelike is [photorealistic](#photorealistic), and a [stereo](#stereo) pair for coloured [glasses](#glasses) is anaglyph.

entries.name: card_(medium)
entries.description: The entire image is designed as a [card](#card) face — a trading card, a [tarot](#tarot) card, a game card — or is built from several such cards. A card held as an object inside a scene is card instead.

entries.name: dakimakura_(medium)
entries.description: A body-pillow print design: a full-length [figure](#figure) [lying](#lying) on bedding, commonly in nightwear or less. Two-sided designs pair a clothed and an undressed side and count as [multiple_views](#multiple_views) rather than [solo](#solo), and a [pillow](#pillow) that merely appears in a scene is [dakimakura_(object)](#dakimakura_(object)).

entries.name: pixel_art
entries.description: Artwork built from visible individual pixels, usually with a small palette and the look of a game [sprite](#sprite) or [old](#old) GIF, whether by deliberate [choice](#choice) or software limits. Oekaki, which does not emphasise single pixels this way, is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: painting_(medium)
entries.description: The image is a real painting in acrylic, gouache, oil, watercolour or another traditional [paint](#paint), then scanned or photographed. Add the [tag](#tag) for the specific paint where it is known.

entries.name: watercolor_(medium)
entries.description: Traditional art painted with watercolours, the [transparent](#transparent) water-based pigments, showing soft washes and [paper](#paper) texture. Digital imitation of the look is [faux_traditional_media](#faux_traditional_media).

entries.name: marker_(medium)
entries.description: Traditional artwork coloured with felt-tip pens, Copics most often, leaving flat streaky fills and layered tones. Implies [traditional_media](#traditional_media); a [marker](#marker) drawn as a prop is marker.

entries.name: graphite_(medium)
entries.description: Work drawn with an ordinary or mechanical [pencil](#pencil), showing grey graphite line and shading. Do not apply it from a source's own pencil [label](#label) alone, which is widely misused.

entries.name: colored_pencil_(medium)
entries.description: Traditional artwork made with coloured pencils, recognisable by the waxy layered strokes and the [paper](#paper) grain showing through. They are also known as [pencil](#pencil) crayons.

entries.name: pen_(medium)
entries.description: Work drawn with an [ink](#ink) [pen](#pen) on [paper](#paper), [giving](#giving) thin crisp lines of largely even width, or varying width from a nib. Often paired with markers, watercolour or coloured [pencil](#pencil) for the fills, the pen [carrying](#carrying) the linework.

entries.name: mixed_media
entries.description: Artwork combining two or more media, typically traditional line work with digital color, or a drawn foreground set over a photo or 3D background. The traditional or 3D element has to stay visibly present; traced-over assets or fully obliterated pencils don't count.

entries.name: millipen_(medium)
entries.description: Line art made with a technical [pen](#pen), a hard-tipped tool that produces uniform, unvarying strokes. Easier to control than a dip nib, though it offers less variation in line [weight](#weight).

entries.name: vector_trace
entries.description: Artwork traced over a source in a vector graphics program and then exported as a raster picture. Recognisable by perfectly clean, uniform lines and flat colour fills.

entries.name: art_tools_in_frame
entries.description: A photograph of traditional or mixed-media work with some of the pens, brushes or paints that made it [lying](#lying) in shot. Tag [photo_(medium)](#photo_(medium)) and [traditional_media](#traditional_media) alongside.

entries.name: acrylic_paint_(medium)
entries.description: A traditional-media work painted in acrylics, with their flat, opaque, fast-drying finish. Brush texture and layered opaque colour usually give it away.

entries.name: emote_(medium)
entries.description: A small picture made to work as a chat or [stream](#stream) emote, built to read at a few dozen pixels. Usually a head or bust [carrying](#carrying) one clear expression, sometimes presented as a sheet of several.

entries.name: nib_pen_(medium)
entries.description: Traditional work inked with a dip [pen](#pen) that has to be recharged from an [ink](#ink) [well](#well). The tool is [awkward](#awkward) but rewards practice with unusually expressive, controlled line [weight](#weight); a picture that merely shows such a pen is [nib_pen_(object)](#nib_pen_(object)).

entries.name: unconventional_media
entries.description: Artwork made in a medium that is neither digital nor traditional drawing or painting: [food](#food) art, latte art, [sculpture](#sculpture), [carving](#carving), [clay](#clay), lego or another craft. Add the specific medium [tag](#tag) as [well](#well) where one exists.

entries.name: oil_painting_(medium)
entries.description: The picture itself is a painting in oils, photographed or scanned. A painted canvas depicted inside a drawing is a different matter and takes [painting_(object)](#painting_(object)).

entries.name: watercolor_effect
entries.description: Digital work [imitating](#imitating) watercolour, with pooling pigment, blooms and [paper](#paper) grain, though [no](#no) real [paint](#paint) was used. When the picture actually was painted, the medium [tag](#tag) applies instead.

entries.name: sculpture
entries.description: A three-dimensional work shaped from [clay](#clay), stone, metal, or wood by [carving](#carving), modelling, casting, or welding. Covers both the medium of the piece shown and figures depicted as statuary.

entries.name: ink_wash_painting
entries.description: The East Asian brush technique that builds a picture from black [ink](#ink) thinned to different strengths, so tone does the work colour usually would. Washed backgrounds and confident single strokes are its [signature](#signature).

entries.name: impasto
entries.description: Paint laid on so thickly that every stroke of brush or [knife](#knife) stands proud of the surface. It reads as physical texture and belongs to oils and acrylics rather than thin media.

entries.name: sprite_art
entries.description: Artwork made in the manner of a game asset, using a tight palette on a small canvas. Covers genuine game graphics as [well](#well) as new pictures drawn in that idiom.

entries.name: paper_child
entries.description: Characters printed on [paper](#paper), cut out and then photographed posed in real surroundings, so a flat drawing appears to stand in a physical place. A photographic format rather than a drawing style.

entries.name: sumi-e
entries.description: Japanese [ink](#ink) wash painting worked in black ink alone, with sparse confident strokes and large areas left bare. Gradations come from diluted ink rather than added colour; the game Okami is the best-known example of the look in games.

entries.name: artist's_hand_in_frame
entries.description: A photograph of physical artwork with the artist's own hand in shot, [holding](#holding) the page up, gripping a brush, or still at work on it. The hand marks it as a photograph rather than a clean [scan](#scan).

entries.name: ascii_art
entries.description: A picture assembled from typed characters, the letters and punctuation lined up in a monospaced [grid](#grid) so they read as outlines and shading. Often shown as text on a [screen](#screen) inside the picture.

entries.name: blueprint_(medium)
entries.description: The whole picture is styled as a technical plan, pale lines on a blue [field](#field), usually showing a [machine](#machine), [mecha](#mecha) or vehicle from several angles with [measurements](#measurements) written in. The look belongs to the image itself, not to a sheet of [paper](#paper) inside it.

entries.name: photo_bashing
entries.description: A picture built by [blending](#blending) pieces of several photographs into painted work, most often to fill in detailed [scenery](#scenery) quickly. It takes real manipulation; one untouched photo behind a drawing is [photo_background](#photo_background).

entries.name: kirigami
entries.description: Paper art that [cuts](#cuts) as [well](#well) as folds, so a single sheet becomes an openwork [silhouette](#silhouette) or a symmetrical [figure](#figure). It is a relative of [origami](#origami) defined by the use of [scissors](#scissors).

entries.name: pixel_text
entries.description: Lettering rendered as visible [square](#square) blocks in the style of [old](#old) game and [computer](#computer) fonts. The blocky [construction](#construction) is what matters, whatever typeface it is [imitating](#imitating).

entries.name: photoshop_(medium)
entries.description: The picture was drawn or assembled in Adobe Photoshop. When the program's own interface appears in the image, adobe_photoshop is the [tag](#tag); an image altered by somebody other than its artist is third-party_edit.

entries.name: painttool_sai_(medium)
entries.description: The picture was drawn or edited in PaintTool SAI. When the program's own interface is what the image shows, [painttool_sai](#painttool_sai) is the [tag](#tag) to use.

entries.name: clip_studio_paint_(medium)
entries.description: The picture was made or edited in Clip Studio Paint, generally known from the artist's own statement. Where the program's [window](#window) or [logo](#logo) is itself depicted, [clip_studio_paint](#clip_studio_paint) applies.

entries.name: ai-generated
entries.description: A picture produced by an image-generation [model](#model) with [no](#no) editing worth mentioning. Common giveaways are the fixed odd resolutions such models default to, generation data left inside the [file](#file), and polished art at an unusually small size. Once somebody paints over it, [ai-assisted](#ai-assisted) applies.

entries.name: photo-referenced
entries.description: A drawing based on, or traced from, a photograph or a [video](#video) frame, which artists frequently say outright. The source sometimes appears beside the work as a [photo_inset](#photo_inset); a photo used as the [backdrop](#backdrop) is [photo_background](#photo_background).

entries.name: art_program_in_frame
entries.description: The picture is a [screen](#screen) capture taken inside the drawing software, toolbars, brush panels or the canvas edge left in shot. Frequent on work in progress; name the program too where it [can](#can) be recognized, and do not use it for art deliberately faking a screenshot.

entries.name: procreate_(medium)
entries.description: Artwork drawn or edited in Procreate, the iPad painting app, often recognisable from its brush textures or a time-lapse export. Only for pictures made with the program; a picture that shows the app's interface takes [procreate_(software)](#procreate_(software)) instead.

entries.name: ai-assisted
entries.description: A picture that started as [machine](#machine) output and was then painted over or retouched by hand, or a drawing that uses generated art as its background or reference. Fully generated work with [no](#no) real editing is [ai-generated](#ai-generated).

entries.name: paint.net_(medium)
entries.description: The picture was drawn or edited in the free Windows image editor Paint.NET, usually known from the artist's own [note](#note) or from the file's metadata.

entries.name: blender_(medium)
entries.description: Work made in Blender, the free open-source 3D suite, whether a still render or an animation. It usually pairs with [3d](#3d); the [kitchen](#kitchen) appliance is [blender_(object)](#blender_(object)).

entries.name: live2d
entries.description: Animation made by deforming layered parts of one 2D drawing instead of redrawing frames, the technique behind virtual streamer models and idle motions in gacha games. Credit both the illustrator and the rigger where both are known.

entries.name: gimp_(medium)
entries.description: A picture made or edited in the GIMP image editor. Usually known from the artist's own [note](#note) or from the file's metadata.

entries.name: procreate_(software)
entries.description: The picture shows the Procreate app's own interface being used, rather than being a piece drawn with it. For artwork made in the program, use [procreate_(medium)](#procreate_(medium)) instead.

entries.name: ibispaint_(medium)
entries.description: The picture was drawn or retouched in the ibisPaint app. When the app's own interface is what appears inside the picture instead, the [plain](#plain) ibispaint [tag](#tag) covers that.

entries.name: ai-generated_art_(topic)
entries.description: The picture is about machine-generated art rather than being one: a hand-drawn version of a generated image that went around, or a joke at the technology's expense. The subject is what counts, not how the [file](#file) was made.

entries.name: clip_studio_paint
entries.description: The drawing program's own interface or [logo](#logo) is visible in the picture, toolbars and canvas and all. Work merely drawn with it takes [clip_studio_paint_(medium)](#clip_studio_paint_(medium)) instead.

entries.name: 10s
entries.description: Work belonging to the 2010s, either made in those years or drawn to look as though it were. Useful for telling one decade of anime and fan-art [convention](#convention) apart from another.

entries.name: chibi
entries.description: Characters drawn super-deformed, oversized heads on tiny simplified bodies for a cute effect. Merely cartoonish figures that keep roughly normal proportions take [deformed](#deformed) instead.

entries.name: 00s
entries.description: Work belonging to the 2000s, whether actually produced then or drawn to imitate it. Expect the shading, palettes and character designs that anime and fan art carried through that decade.

entries.name: sketch
entries.description: A rough, quick drawing with loose lines, leftover [construction](#construction) [shapes](#shapes) and little or basic colour. The picture must actually look sketchy, whatever the artist called it; a character drawing a sketch is [sketching](#sketching).

entries.name: bara
entries.description: Art in the gay men's manga tradition, built around heavily masculine bodies: soft bear-like bulk, proportioned jock musculature or leaner [toned](#toned) types. Chests and bulges are drawn larger than life and stay obvious through clothing; add the matching body tags such as [muscular](#muscular) or [fat](#fat).

entries.name: outline
entries.description: A person or object is ringed by a distinct outline, usually white or black and separate from the ordinary [lineart](#lineart), lifting it off the background. Common on stickers, logos and pasted-in figures.

entries.name: 1990s_(style)
entries.description: Anime and manga styling from the 1990s, with angular faces, sharply [spiked](#spiked) hair, cel shading and muted colour. It applies to how the picture is drawn, never to when it was made.

entries.name: retro_artstyle
entries.description: Art drawn in the look of a past decade, at least ten years or more [back](#back), such as the 1980s or 1990s anime style. Add the decade [tag](#tag) such as [1990s_(style)](#1990s_(style)); imitations of much older art are [fine_art_parody](#fine_art_parody).

entries.name: white_outline
entries.description: Characters, objects or lettering are edged with a white line so they stand out cleanly from whatever sits behind them. A common trick in stickers, sprites and busy compositions; other colors have their own [outline](#outline) tags such as [yellow_outline](#yellow_outline).

entries.name: chibi_only
entries.description: Every character in the picture is drawn super-deformed, with [no](#no) normally proportioned [figure](#figure) anywhere in it. Use [plain](#plain) [chibi](#chibi) when only some of them are.

entries.name: oekaki
entries.description: A quick doodle made with the bare-bones drawing applet built into a message board, [giving](#giving) thin, hard-edged lines and simple colour. The word means [scribble](#scribble) in Japanese; go by that look rather than applying it to every rough [sketch](#sketch).

entries.name: realistic
entries.description: Anatomy, proportion, and lighting are rendered close to life rather than in a stylized anime manner. When the result could pass for an actual photograph, use [photorealistic](#photorealistic) instead; a middle ground between the two is semi-realistic.

entries.name: silhouette
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) or object rendered as a solid [dark](#dark) shape with an [outline](#outline) and [no](#no) [interior](#interior) detail. Commonly mistaken for [shadow](#shadow), which is [cast](#cast) onto a surface rather than being the subject itself.

entries.name: unfinished
entries.description: Artwork left short of completion: a [sketch](#sketch), bare [lineart](#lineart) or a flat-colour pass shared before the final version, or a piece the artist [abandoned](#abandoned) partway through. A picture that walks through several production stages together is [making-of](#making-of) instead.

entries.name: lineart
entries.description: A finished drawing of clean solid lines with [no](#no) colour or shading, one step short of a completed piece. Rougher work is [sketch](#sketch), and lineart [carrying](#carrying) more than spot colour becomes [partially_colored](#partially_colored).

entries.name: flat_color
entries.description: Colouring laid down in solid blocks with [no](#no) shading, highlights or gradients, so the picture reads flat and gives little sense of depth. It often goes with line-heavy styles.

entries.name: jaggy_lines
entries.description: Lineart laid down with an aliased brush, so every edge steps in hard pixel blocks. It is not [pixel_art](#pixel_art), which is placed one pixel at a time.

entries.name: 1980s_(style)
entries.description: The look of 1980s anime and manga: big permed hair, soft rounded faces, cel-style shading and period [fashion](#fashion). It describes deliberate styling rather than the year the picture was finished.

entries.name: anime_coloring
entries.description: Flat colour with hard-edged shadows, the rendering used throughout [television](#television) animation, as against soft [painterly](#painterly) [blending](#blending). The same crisp look applied to 3D work, or to art [imitating](#imitating) it, is [cel_rendering](#cel_rendering).

entries.name: hatching_(texture)
entries.description: Shading made from closely set parallel or crossing strokes instead of smooth tone, the mark of [pen](#pen) and [pencil](#pencil) work. Linear, woven and crossed varieties all count.

entries.name: 2000s_(style)
entries.description: The mid-2000s anime look: [heavy](#heavy) black outlines, soft pillowy shading, glossy freeform hair highlights, and moe proportions with huge eyes that carry [no](#no) defined pupil. Only the styling matters, not whether the picture was made then.

entries.name: still_life
entries.description: A picture of arranged inanimate objects, such as a [bowl](#bowl) of [fruit](#fruit), flowers or tableware, with [no](#no) living subject as the focus.

entries.name: deformed
entries.description: Figures drawn with deliberately simplified, chibi-leaning proportions while the body still reads as roughly proportional overall. Once the head grows to about the size of the body, [chibi](#chibi) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: painterly
entries.description: Artwork that carries the look of a physical painting: visible brush strokes, blended edges, imitated watercolour or acrylic texture. It describes the style, not the material actually used.

entries.name: egasumi
entries.description: Cloud or mist drawn the traditional Japanese way, as long flat horizontal bands with rounded ends linked in a row. Belongs to [ukiyo-e](#ukiyo-e) and to backgrounds and patterns with a Japanese flavour, and is a motif rather than weather.

entries.name: surreal
entries.description: Dreamlike art that pairs impossible or mismatched elements, as if drawn from the subconscious. Melting objects, strange scale and illogical scenes are typical.

entries.name: abstract
entries.description: Artwork [leaning](#leaning) on abstract technique: scattered [paint](#paint), loose [shapes](#shapes), hypnotic patterning and strange colour play. A recognisable [figure](#figure) may still be present, since what is marked is the handling rather than the absence of a subject.

entries.name: faux_traditional_media
entries.description: A digital picture made to look like watercolour, [ink](#ink), [marker](#marker) or another analogue medium. Use it where the work was plainly done on a [computer](#computer) despite the analogue look; genuine traditional [lineart](#lineart) coloured digitally is [mixed_media](#mixed_media).

entries.name: no_lineart
entries.description: A drawing built with almost [no](#no) outlines, its forms defined by rendered colour and shading instead. Eyes are exempt from the rule.

entries.name: toon_(style)
entries.description: Art drawn in the manner of Western cartoons and comics, from classic Disney and rubberhose to modern [television](#television) cartoons or indie comics. About the drawing style, not the character's origin; a superhero look is [western_comics_(style)](#western_comics_(style)) instead.

entries.name: linear_hatching
entries.description: Shading built from closely spaced parallel lines rather than smooth tone, darkening an area by their density. A form of [hatching](#hatching) typical of [ink](#ink) and [pencil](#pencil) work.

entries.name: absurdly_detailed_composition
entries.description: Worked-out detail fills the entire frame, with elaborate props, crowds or [scenery](#scenery) rather than empty [space](#space). What is being marked is the sheer density of the picture.

entries.name: tarot_(medium)
entries.description: A whole image composed as though it were a [tarot](#tarot) [card](#card), from a light suggestion of the motif to a full card design complete with a name and number. For a physical card held as an object within a scene, use the [plain](#plain) tarot [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: black_outline
entries.description: A character or object drawn with a black line separating it from whatever lies behind, as in sticker-style art. A black frame around the whole picture is [black_border](#black_border) instead.

entries.name: red_outline
entries.description: A red line traced around the edge of a character or object, separating it from the background. A drawing [choice](#choice) rather than a garment or effect; add [outline](#outline) as [well](#well).

entries.name: chibikemo
entries.description: Animal characters drawn small and round, with outsized heads and stubby limbs, the [chibi](#chibi) treatment applied to kemono designs. The result reads as soft and toy-like.

entries.name: art_nouveau
entries.description: The decorative style of the turn of the twentieth century: bold outlines, flat rich colour, sinuous curves and an [ornate](#ornate) circular frame behind the [figure](#figure). Much used for poster-like portraits.

entries.name: child's_drawing
entries.description: Artwork deliberately made to look as though a [child](#child) drew it: crude [shapes](#shapes), wobbly lines, [crayon](#crayon) colour. It may be the whole picture or a drawing held up by a character inside it.

entries.name: pinup_(style)
entries.description: Art done in the manner of mid-century pinup posters: playful [poses](#poses), glamour lighting, retro styling and swimwear or [lingerie](#lingerie). The period styling is what counts, not mere sexiness.

entries.name: yume_kawaii
entries.description: A dreamy, pastel-saturated aesthetic that leans on nostalgic visual cues from [old](#old) shoujo art to give a picture a floaty, otherworldly softness rather than [plain](#plain) cuteness. It also names a [fashion](#fashion) style closely related to [fairy](#fairy) kei.

entries.name: blue_outline
entries.description: The [figure](#figure) or object is drawn with a blue contour line separating it from what lies behind, in place of a black one. The colour describes the line itself, not a glow around it.

entries.name: 1970s_(style)
entries.description: Follows the drawing habits of 1970s anime and manga, with [tall](#tall) shoujo faces, fine [hatching](#hatching) and the colour choices of the decade. Because it marks styling, a modern artist paying homage counts.

entries.name: pink_outline
entries.description: A pink line traced around the [silhouette](#silhouette) of a character or object, setting it off from the background like a [sticker](#sticker) edge. It wraps the whole shape, unlike ordinary [lineart](#lineart).

entries.name: western_comics_(style)
entries.description: Drawn in the manner of American [comic](#comic) books, with [halftone](#halftone) printing, restricted color palettes and English lettering. Describes the visual style itself, not merely a picture that happens to feature comic-book characters.

entries.name: photorealistic
entries.description: Rendering so lifelike that the picture reads as a photograph until you look closely at the skin, [cloth](#cloth) and lighting. It sits at the far end of [realistic](#realistic), which goes with it.

entries.name: nihonga
entries.description: Painting done by traditional Japanese methods and conventions, a term coined to set such work apart from Western-style oils. Use it for pictures made in that manner or parodying it.

entries.name: color_trace
entries.description: Line art drawn in assorted colours instead of black, a [habit](#habit) carried over from animation pre-production where each colour flagged a different [paint](#paint) layer. A finished coloured piece with tinted lines is [colored_lineart](#colored_lineart).

entries.name: crosshatching
entries.description: Shading laid down as layers of lines [running](#running) in two or more directions, packed tight where the surface is darkest and thinning out where light falls. The multi-directional relative of [plain](#plain) [hatching](#hatching), borrowed from [pen](#pen) and engraving work.

entries.name: ligne_claire
entries.description: A drawing style built on even black outlines, flat unshaded colour and backgrounds rendered as crisply as the figures. Contrast between subject and setting stays low, [following](#following) Franco-Belgian [comic](#comic) tradition.

entries.name: purple_outline
entries.description: The line enclosing a [figure](#figure) or object is drawn in purple rather than black. A treatment of the linework itself, unrelated to any glow elsewhere in the scene.

entries.name: low_poly
entries.description: Forms built from so few flat facets that the underlying [geometry](#geometry) shows, the look of early consoles [working](#working) within tight hardware limits. It covers both real 3D models and flat art [imitating](#imitating) them, and the coarse textures often bring it close to [pixel_art](#pixel_art).

entries.name: cartoonized
entries.description: A character who is normally not a cartoon [redrawn](#redrawn) in a Western animation style, whether an anime [figure](#figure) or a real person. Designs that already look toony in their own source do not count.

entries.name: ukiyo-e
entries.description: The Japanese woodblock print tradition of the seventeenth to twentieth centuries, with flat colour fields, [strong](#strong) outlines and stylised [waves](#waves), courtesans and landscapes. Covers genuine prints, parodies of famous ones, and new work drawn in the manner.

entries.name: sketch_background
entries.description: The [figure](#figure) is finished while everything behind it is left as rough lines. Marks a picture the artist stopped short of completing rather than a chosen style.

entries.name: revealing_layer
entries.description: The picture is drawn as if it were sheets of [paper](#paper) stacked on top of each other, with a [torn](#torn) or lifted layer exposing something underneath: a less clothed version of the same pose, or the [machinery](#machinery) inside a [device](#device). The trick comes from a Japanese pin-up magazine gimmick.

entries.name: thick_lineart
entries.description: Drawing whose outlines are laid down with a broad, [heavy](#heavy) stroke throughout, [giving](#giving) the whole picture a bold, poster-like edge. The [weight](#weight) carries through the [interior](#interior) lines as [well](#well), not just the [silhouette](#silhouette).

entries.name: art_shift
entries.description: The drawing style changes within one work: a character rendered quite unlike the one beside them, or a panel [dropping](#dropping) into a wholly different look and [back](#back) again. Usually done for a joke or a shock.

entries.name: orange_outline
entries.description: The [figure](#figure) or object is drawn with an orange contour instead of a [dark](#dark) one, or an orange edge is laid around it to lift it off the background.

entries.name: stick_figure
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) reduced to a [circle](#circle) for a head and a handful of straight lines for body and limbs, with [no](#no) volume or detail. Used for [comic](#comic) asides, doodles drawn inside the picture, and deliberately crude gags.

entries.name: pc-98_(style)
entries.description: Art [imitating](#imitating) the graphics of late-eighties and nineties Japanese home computers: coarse pixels in a wide, short frame, sixteen colours at most, and [heavy](#heavy) [dithering](#dithering) [standing](#standing) in for the rest.

entries.name: character_cutout
entries.description: Figures drawn as though snipped out of [paper](#paper): flat [shapes](#shapes), dotted outlines, a broad paper margin around the body. A slit or tear revealing another layer beneath is revealing layer.

entries.name: psychedelic
entries.description: Swirling, [saturated](#saturated) imagery in the visual language of a drug-induced hallucination: [melting](#melting) [shapes](#shapes), kaleidoscope repeats, and clashing [rainbow](#rainbow) colour. The style dominates the whole picture rather than [sitting](#sitting) in one [corner](#corner) of it.

entries.name: silhouette_demon
entries.description: A [silhouette](#silhouette) whose [outline](#outline) itself reads as demonic or evil, shaped with [horns](#horns), [claws](#claws) or [wings](#wings). Stands in for a menacing presence without ever showing its features.

entries.name: frutiger_aero
entries.description: The glossy commercial look of the late 2000s, [mixing](#mixing) [nature](#nature) with technology: shimmering blue [water](#water), bright [grass](#grass), bubbles, [tropical](#tropical) [fish](#fish), lens flares and [semi-transparent](#semi-transparent) [glass](#glass) panels. Palettes run to white, blue and green with the odd orange accent.

entries.name: colored_lineart
entries.description: The outlines of the drawing are in some colour other than black, obvious even at thumbnail size. Coloured outlines drawn around ordinary black lines are the [outline](#outline) tags, and uncoloured animation frames are [color_trace](#color_trace).

entries.name: thick_outlines
entries.description: The outer contour of a [figure](#figure) or object is drawn far heavier than the [interior](#interior) lines, lifting it off the background like a [sticker](#sticker). The detail inside stays comparatively fine.

entries.name: minimalism
entries.description: A style pared down to the fewest marks that still read clearly: empty backgrounds, very few props, and sometimes [faceless](#faceless) figures. Blank [space](#space) carries as much visual [weight](#weight) as the lines themselves.

entries.name: impressionism
entries.description: A loose [painterly](#painterly) manner built from short, plainly visible strokes and bright [broken](#broken) colour, [chasing](#chasing) light rather than [outline](#outline). Where the [paint](#paint) is piled thick enough to stand off the surface it shades into [impasto](#impasto).

entries.name: brush_stroke
entries.description: The mark of a [paintbrush](#paintbrush) shows in the picture, left either by the medium itself or laid in deliberately as texture. Broad sweeps behind a [figure](#figure) are a common use.

entries.name: frutiger_metro
entries.description: A later offshoot of the glossy Aero look, setting flat vector [shapes](#shapes) against busy imagery — swirls, [bokeh](#bokeh), splatters, birds, butterflies and [music](#music) motifs. Colours run to lime green, electric blue and [hot](#hot) pink.

entries.name: vaporwave
entries.description: A retro [internet](#internet) aesthetic built from 1980s and early-computer imagery: [hot](#hot) pink and cyan palettes, grids, classical busts, [old](#old) operating-system windows and stray Japanese lettering. Nostalgic and deliberately artificial in feel.

entries.name: egyptian_art
entries.description: Drawn in the manner of ancient Egyptian wall painting: figures locked in strict [profile](#profile), scenes stacked in bands, hieroglyphs, and a palette of ochre and lapis.

entries.name: nose_shade
entries.description: A [patch](#patch) of [shadow](#shadow) drawn beside or beneath the [nose](#nose). It is a shading [habit](#habit) that gives the face more depth than flat colour would.

entries.name: 1960s_(style)
entries.description: Drawn the way anime and manga looked in the 1960s: [plain](#plain) linework, flat colour and the simpler, rounder proportions of that era. What is marked is a chosen look, so a picture made today [can](#can) qualify.

entries.name: cel_rendering
entries.description: Three-dimensional work shaded to pass for hand-drawn animation, with flat textures, hard-edged highlights, and either a [heavy](#heavy) contour or none whatsoever. The flat two-dimensional technique is [anime_coloring](#anime_coloring).

entries.name: purikura
entries.description: Artwork styled after Japanese photo-sticker booth prints: decorated borders, scribbled captions, hearts, and [glitter](#glitter) pasted over posed faces. Named for the print-club machines that the look comes from.

entries.name: speedpaint
entries.description: A picture finished within a self-imposed time limit, anywhere from a few minutes to a [couple](#couple) of hours, so [shapes](#shapes) are blocked in quickly and detail stays loose. Common as practice work and in early concept art.

entries.name: monochrome
entries.description: A picture drawn in essentially one colour, which need not be black — red, blue or green [ink](#ink) count too. Add [greyscale](#greyscale) for a range of greys, or the matching theme [tag](#tag) for another colour; a single small accent of colour makes it [spot_color](#spot_color) instead.

entries.name: greyscale
entries.description: A colourless image made only of black, white and shades of grey, typical of manga and doujinshi [pages](#pages). Skip colour tags like [black_hair](#black_hair) on it, though background colour tags such as [white_background](#white_background) are fine; a small colour highlight instead adds [spot_color](#spot_color), and a mix of coloured and grey areas is [partially_colored](#partially_colored) rather than this.

entries.name: spot_color
entries.description: A mostly [greyscale](#greyscale) or muted picture where one or two colours are left vivid to draw the eye. Different from [partially_colored](#partially_colored), where the colouring is simply incomplete or confined to one area.

entries.name: blue_theme
entries.description: Blue dominates the whole palette, either as a blue-tinted near-monochrome or as an overall colour scheme. A blue [backdrop](#backdrop) behind an ordinarily coloured subject is [blue_background](#blue_background) instead.

entries.name: limited_palette
entries.description: The picture is drawn with only a handful of distinct colours, more than a single spot of colour but far short of a full range. It frequently overlaps with [partially_colored](#partially_colored).

entries.name: partially_colored
entries.description: Only parts of the picture carry colour while the rest stays as [lineart](#lineart) or [sketch](#sketch), either because the work is [unfinished](#unfinished) or to draw the eye to one element. Selective colour used as a deliberate accent is [spot_color](#spot_color), and a [greyscale](#greyscale) [figure](#figure) on a coloured [backdrop](#backdrop) is [greyscale_with_colored_background](#greyscale_with_colored_background).

entries.name: pink_theme
entries.description: Pink dominates the whole picture, either as a pink [monochrome](#monochrome) or as a palette built on pink through background, clothing and lighting alike. A single pink garment in an otherwise neutral scene is not enough.

entries.name: red_theme
entries.description: Red dominates the whole picture, whether as a red-toned [monochrome](#monochrome) or as a palette built around reds. The picture reads as red at a [glance](#glance), not just a character wearing red.

entries.name: purple_theme
entries.description: Purple dominates the whole picture, whether as a purple [monochrome](#monochrome) or a palette built around it. About the picture's overall colouring rather than one purple garment; combine with monochrome when it comes down to a single hue.

entries.name: green_theme
entries.description: Green dominates the whole picture, either as a green [monochrome](#monochrome) or as an overall green palette in a coloured image. Scattered green objects on their own are not enough.

entries.name: sepia
entries.description: A picture tinted in brownish-yellow tones like an [old](#old) photograph, [giving](#giving) a vintage feel or signalling a [flashback](#flashback). A grey-only image is [greyscale](#greyscale) instead.

entries.name: greyscale_with_colored_background
entries.description: The subject is drawn in [greyscale](#greyscale) while the background behind them, often a simple one, carries colour. Do not also [tag](#tag) greyscale, [partially_colored](#partially_colored) or [spot_color](#spot_color) for that alone, though spot_color [can](#can) join it if a small part of the subject, such as the eyes, is coloured too.

entries.name: muted_color
entries.description: Colours washed out toward grey, so the picture barely reads as coloured at all. Colours dulled with white are pale color and those sunk toward black are [dark](#dark).

entries.name: yellow_theme
entries.description: Yellow dominates the whole image, whether as a [monochrome](#monochrome) yellow rendering or an overall yellow palette. Other colours have their own theme tags.

entries.name: colorful
entries.description: The picture is packed with vivid colours as a deliberate effect, each hue given room to stand out while still [sitting](#sitting) in the subject. Ordinary full-colour art does not qualify.

entries.name: orange_theme
entries.description: Orange dominates the whole picture, whether as an orange [monochrome](#monochrome) or a palette built around the hue. For the [fruit](#fruit) itself use [orange_(fruit)](#orange_(fruit)).

entries.name: brown_theme
entries.description: Brown dominates the whole picture, either as a brown-tinted [monochrome](#monochrome) or as a palette built from its shades. Add [sepia](#sepia) where the effect imitates an aged photograph.

entries.name: white_theme
entries.description: White dominates the whole image, from the character and clothing to the background, in pale, washed-out tones throughout. It is distinct from [greyscale](#greyscale) or [plain](#plain) black-and-white line art, which fall under the [monochrome](#monochrome) tags.

entries.name: high_contrast
entries.description: Very [dark](#dark) tones set against very light ones with almost nothing between: solid blacks, blank whites, ink-like strokes. Greyscale and flat-coloured work show it most, sometimes with [halftone](#halftone); it is not the same as [spot_color](#spot_color).

entries.name: pastel_colors
entries.description: The picture is built from pale but still [saturated](#saturated) hues, [giving](#giving) a soft, sweet, low-contrast look. Pale_color describes low [contrast](#contrast) on its own and [muted_color](#muted_color) low saturation on its own, so neither is the same thing.

entries.name: pale_color
entries.description: Every colour in the image looks as though white had been stirred into it, [giving](#giving) pastel tones and low [contrast](#contrast) throughout. Colours greyed toward [monochrome](#monochrome) are [muted_color](#muted_color), and colours [sinking](#sinking) toward black are [dark](#dark).

entries.name: color_connection
entries.description: Characters or objects are grouped because they share a theme colour, or one character quotes another who wears the same colour. Where several such colour groups appear at once, [color_coordination](#color_coordination) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: aqua_theme
entries.description: Aqua or blue-green rules the whole picture, whether as an aqua [monochrome](#monochrome) or as an overall scheme everything is tinted toward. Where the hue leans further one way, [blue_theme](#blue_theme) or [green_theme](#green_theme) fits better.

entries.name: rainbow_order
entries.description: Characters or objects are lined up [following](#following) the order of the spectrum, with at minimum red, yellow, and blue appearing in sequence. The arrangement has to read clearly even at thumbnail size.

entries.name: black_theme
entries.description: Black dominates the whole picture's palette, [pulling](#pulling) every other colour toward it. Black-and-white work takes [monochrome](#monochrome) or [greyscale](#greyscale) instead, and a merely [dark](#dark) [backdrop](#backdrop) is [black_background](#black_background).

entries.name: rainbow_gradient
entries.description: A gradient [running](#running) through all or most of the spectrum in order, applied to hair, clothing, a background, or the whole picture. Combine with [gradient_hair](#gradient_hair) or [gradient_background](#gradient_background) depending on where it appears.

entries.name: blending
entries.description: Two elements share a colour with [no](#no) line dividing them, so a [figure](#figure) merges into its surroundings, most often hair against a matching flat [backdrop](#backdrop). Flat_color with [no_lineart](#no_lineart) tends to produce it; a smooth shift from one colour into another is gradient.

entries.name: grey_theme
entries.description: Grey dominates the colour scheme of a coloured picture. Greyscale images are excluded, since they carry [no](#no) colour at all, even where [spot_color](#spot_color) appears.

entries.name: multiple_monochrome
entries.description: An image built from several one-colour sections, each in a different hue, typically one colour per character. Every section must hold up as [monochrome](#monochrome) on its own; a merely [strong](#strong) colour theme is [color_coordination](#color_coordination), and an odd [patch](#patch) on a single [figure](#figure) is [spot_color](#spot_color).

entries.name: analogous_colors
entries.description: The picture works from a band of neighbouring hues on the colour [wheel](#wheel), held close together. The range is broader than a single colour theme such as [green_theme](#green_theme), but still deliberately narrow.

entries.name: contrast
entries.description: Two visual qualities are set deliberately against each other, such as bright figures before a [dark](#dark) ground or warm colours beside cool ones. The opposition is clearly intended and carries the picture.

entries.name: black_vs_white
entries.description: A picture built on black set against white, usually to [stage](#stage) light against [dark](#dark) or good against evil. The opposition may live in the clothing, the [wings](#wings), the [backdrop](#backdrop) or the palette overall.

entries.name: green_outline
entries.description: The lines enclosing the drawing are green rather than black, around the whole [figure](#figure) or on chosen parts. It softens the artwork and is often matched to the character's palette.

entries.name: grey_outline
entries.description: The lines of the drawing are grey rather than black, which softens every edge. It goes hand in hand with pale palettes and light, airy artwork.

entries.name: neon_palette
entries.description: A colour scheme built from [glowing](#glowing), heavily [saturated](#saturated) pinks, purples, blues and aquas, usually over a [dark](#dark) ground. It goes with arcades, [cyberpunk](#cyberpunk) cityscapes, nightclubs and [vaporwave](#vaporwave) imagery.

entries.name: color_contrast
entries.description: The picture is built on strongly opposed colours set beside each other. Each hue looks more intense next to its opposite, and the [clash](#clash) pulls the eye where the artist wants it.

entries.name: color_coordination
entries.description: Characters or objects fall into several matching colour groups, so the palette itself organises the picture. A single colour-linked group is [color_connection](#color_connection), and art built around one hue takes the matching theme [tag](#tag).

entries.name: color_drain
entries.description: A character or a whole panel loses its colour and turns grey in reaction to something. It marks shock, dread, fury or a mind coming apart.

entries.name: saturated
entries.description: Colours pushed to a high intensity so that hues glare rather than sit quietly, sometimes hard on the eye. The opposite treatment is [muted_color](#muted_color).

entries.name: inverted_colors
entries.description: Every colour is replaced by its opposite, as in a photographic [negative](#negative), so skin turns blue-green and white goes black. It is used for shock moments, dream passages and abrupt shifts of mood.

entries.name: rainbow_text
entries.description: Lettering colored across the spectrum, either as a gradient [sweeping](#sweeping) through the words or with each [letter](#letter) given its own hue in sequence.

entries.name: brown_outline
entries.description: The lines drawn around the [figure](#figure) or its parts are brown rather than black. It softens the drawing noticeably and usually goes with a warm palette.

entries.name: aqua_outline
entries.description: A blue-green line traced round a [figure](#figure) or an object, [holding](#holding) it off the background. A rendering [choice](#choice) rather than anything the character wears.

entries.name: color-coded
entries.description: Parts of the picture are given distinct colours so they [can](#can) be told apart at a [glance](#glance), one hue per character, per team or per [speaker](#speaker).

entries.name: negative
entries.description: Every colour is inverted as in a photographic negative, so bright areas go [dark](#dark) and each hue flips to its opposite. It often marks a shock or a sudden turn in the scene.

entries.name: color_wheel
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of hues laid out in spectral order, shown either as a [diagram](#diagram) or as a prop. It turns up in palette studies and pictures about the process of drawing.

entries.name: alternate_costume
entries.description: A character wearing something other than their usual outfit, invented by a fan: [casual](#casual) [clothes](#clothes), a themed look, a reworking of the original design. Outfits that come from the source material take [official_alternate_costume](#official_alternate_costume).

entries.name: official_alternate_costume
entries.description: A character wears an outfit other than their standard one and it comes from the rights holder: a game skin, a [beach](#beach) episode, an event [costume](#costume). It must be their own; wearing another character's [clothes](#clothes) is [alternate_costume](#alternate_costume) or [cosplay](#cosplay), and the two tags never appear together.

entries.name: alternate_hairstyle
entries.description: The hair is arranged differently from the character's default, changes of length included. Styles the source itself introduces take [official_alternate_hairstyle](#official_alternate_hairstyle).

entries.name: parody
entries.description: The picture imitates another work for [comic](#comic) or referential effect, recreating a scene, a line, a pose or an art style from somewhere else. Usually a one-off joke; a joke copied widely enough becomes a [meme](#meme). Add the specific parody [tag](#tag) where one exists.

entries.name: crossover
entries.description: Characters from two or more unrelated works [sharing](#sharing) a single scene. Not the same as [parody](#parody), which imitates another work for laughs, and one character merely cosplaying as another does not usually count.

entries.name: alternate_breast_size_(larger)
entries.description: The bust is drawn noticeably fuller than the character's usual design. The [comparison](#comparison) is with how that character normally looks, not with any average.

entries.name: adapted_costume
entries.description: A character's established outfit reworked into a new design that still reads as the original. It also covers another character's [costume](#costume) adapted onto them, in which case add [cosplay](#cosplay); a change of colour alone is [alternate_color](#alternate_color).

entries.name: casual
entries.description: A character normally shown in a uniform, [costume](#costume), armour or formal [dress](#dress) is instead wearing ordinary modern [street](#street) [clothes](#clothes). The [contrast](#contrast) with their usual look is the whole point.

entries.name: alternate_breast_size
entries.description: Breasts drawn clearly larger or smaller than the character normally has, generally by more than a [couple](#couple) of [cup](#cup) sizes. Skip it where the usual size is itself unsettled.

entries.name: dual_persona
entries.description: Two versions of one character, differing from each other, share a single scene, such as a heroine beside her corrupted counterpart. Where they act as separate [people](#people), drop [solo](#solo) and [1girl](#1girl); identical copies are [clone](#clone), and three or more are [multiple_persona](#multiple_persona).

entries.name: official_alternate_hairstyle
entries.description: A character wears a hairstyle other than the usual one and that style has an official source, such as a game [costume](#costume), an episode or promotional artwork. Fan-invented styles are [alternate_hairstyle](#alternate_hairstyle), and the two are never combined.

entries.name: alternate_color
entries.description: A character's usual outfit and colouring redone in different colours by a fan. Palette changes that come from the source itself take [official_alternate_color](#official_alternate_color).

entries.name: alternate_hair_length
entries.description: The hair is drawn longer or shorter than its established length. A change of length that the source itself introduces takes [official_alternate_hair_length](#official_alternate_hair_length).

entries.name: style_parody
entries.description: Artwork that deliberately imitates a specific artist's drawing style rather than a general era or an official [studio](#studio) look. Imitating a period belongs under [retro_artstyle](#retro_artstyle) or a decade [tag](#tag); [imitating](#imitating) official art is [official_style](#official_style). Implies [parody](#parody).

entries.name: animification
entries.description: Characters from live action, western cartoons, comics or real life [redrawn](#redrawn) in anime style. It excludes western designs that already look anime, and drawing a person as an [animal](#animal) is [animalization](#animalization).

entries.name: derivative_work
entries.description: A picture built wholly or partly on somebody else's work: a pose lifted from another drawing, a composition taken from a reference photo, a tracing, or an outright copy. The source is normally credited or linked.

entries.name: alternate_eye_color
entries.description: The eyes are drawn in a colour that never appears in the source, as a deliberate liberty rather than a mistake. It does not apply where the source itself varies, nor to [monochrome](#monochrome) or single-palette pictures, and it is not [heterochromia](#heterochromia).

entries.name: alternate_hair_color
entries.description: Hair drawn in a colour the character does not normally have. It reads as a deliberate liberty rather than a colouring error, and often travels with a changed outfit.

entries.name: dark_persona
entries.description: A darker, frequently evil counterpart of a character, marked out by an alternate [costume](#costume), changed colours or other distinguishing traits. When the ordinary version shares the picture, [dual_persona](#dual_persona) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: official_style
entries.description: Fan art drawn deliberately in the same visual style as a series' own artwork. Copying a different artist or series is [style_parody](#style_parody), and an official artist's private fan art does not qualify.

entries.name: official_alternate_hair_length
entries.description: A character's hair is officially shown longer or shorter than the default, for instance in a released [costume](#costume). It is a narrower case of [official_alternate_hairstyle](#official_alternate_hairstyle) and excludes the fan-made [alternate_hair_length](#alternate_hair_length).

entries.name: trait_connection
entries.description: A [crossover](#crossover) or [cosplay](#cosplay) pairing characters from different works who share a personality trait or a similar turn of fate in their own stories. Add crossover or cosplay along with the characters involved; a [note](#note) explaining the connection helps viewers unfamiliar with both.

entries.name: company_connection
entries.description: A [crossover](#crossover) or [parody](#parody) whose characters are drawn from different series that all belong to one company or [studio](#studio). The shared publisher is what ties the [cast](#cast) together, rather than any story link between them.

entries.name: alternate_hair_length_(longer)
entries.description: The hair falls noticeably further than in the character's usual design. Common in grown-up and what-if pictures; add the length [tag](#tag) matching what is drawn, such as [long_hair](#long_hair).

entries.name: scene_reference
entries.description: The picture recreates or nods to a well-known scene from a film, game, anime or other work, either as a [parody](#parody) or as a reference within the same franchise. Tag alongside parody when the source is a different work.

entries.name: alternate_universe
entries.description: A hypothetical, non-canon setting or turn of events: a dead character alive, a [fantasy](#fantasy) [cast](#cast) dropped into a modern [city](#city), a timeline that went another way. The premise itself is what gets recorded.

entries.name: alternate_form
entries.description: A character shown in a markedly different body from their usual one, a true change of shape the source itself recognises. Simply ageing up or down does not count.

entries.name: brand_name_imitation
entries.description: A real company's name or [logo](#logo) appears with the spelling or mark altered just enough to avoid trouble, on a [shirt](#shirt), a [can](#can) or a shopfront. The brand being copied is normally tagged alongside it.

entries.name: in-franchise_crossover
entries.description: Characters from different entries in one series meet in a scene [no](#no) official work gives them, such as the casts of two games in the same franchise. Dressing as another entry's character counts as [well](#well).

entries.name: east-west_crossover
entries.description: Characters out of Japanese works share a picture with ones from Western cartoons, comics or films. What defines it is the meeting of the two traditions rather than the particular pairing.

entries.name: east_meets_west
entries.description: Eastern and Western [dress](#dress), buildings or visual traditions set side by side in one picture, a [kimono](#kimono) in a Victorian parlour and the like. The [contrast](#contrast) itself is the subject.

entries.name: multiple_crossover
entries.description: Characters from at least three separate franchises meet in one picture, whether as a [crossover](#crossover), a [fusion](#fusion) or a [parody](#parody). Assembling a [cast](#cast) drawn from a single series does not count unless two or more outside franchises join in.

entries.name: alternate_hair_length_(shorter)
entries.description: The hair has been cut [back](#back) [well](#well) past its usual length. It often accompanies a younger or restyled take on the character; add the length [tag](#tag) that fits the picture, such as [short_hair](#short_hair).

entries.name: borrowed_clothes
entries.description: Somebody wears clothing belonging to another character for a reason other than [dressing](#dressing) up as them, such as a girlfriend in her partner's [shirt](#shirt) or a lent [jacket](#jacket). Outfits the character also wears in their own story do not count unless the lending is the subject.

entries.name: fine_art_parody
entries.description: The picture restages a recognisable painting or [sculpture](#sculpture), classical or modern, with other characters in the roles. Something that merely looks painted without quoting a particular work is [painterly](#painterly).

entries.name: screenshot_redraw
entries.description: An artist's redrawing of an actual screenshot from an anime, game, or film, done in their own style. Covers the various redraw-challenge memes built around a particular source frame.

entries.name: alternate_legwear
entries.description: Legwear the character does not normally wear, such as [thighhighs](#thighhighs) on somebody who otherwise has [pantyhose](#pantyhose). Name the legwear actually shown as [well](#well).

entries.name: creator_connection
entries.description: A [crossover](#crossover) or [parody](#parody) in which every series present came from the same author, [studio](#studio) or director. The shared hand behind them is the point of the picture.

entries.name: alternate_skin_color
entries.description: Skin drawn in a colour clearly unlike the character's usual one. Skin darkened by the [sun](#sun) is [tan](#tan) instead.

entries.name: alternate_headwear
entries.description: Somebody who normally wears one sort of [hat](#hat) is given another, a [baseball](#baseball) cap in place of a wide-brimmed one. The hat actually drawn is tagged as [well](#well).

entries.name: redesign
entries.description: A character, [mecha](#mecha), vehicle or other subject given a new original design that departs from its official look. Goes beyond a [costume](#costume) swap: the design itself has been reworked by the artist.

entries.name: if_they_mated
entries.description: Invented children of two established characters, drawn to imagine how their offspring would turn out. Tag the parents only when they appear in the picture too.

entries.name: alternate_breast_size_(smaller)
entries.description: The bust is drawn noticeably flatter than the character's usual design. It marks a departure from the established look rather than small [breasts](#breasts) in themselves.

entries.name: redrawn
entries.description: A picture that recreates an earlier work from scratch, frequently by the same artist revisiting an [old](#old) drawing. A version with only corrections or small edits to the original [file](#file) is a revision, not this.

entries.name: embellished_costume
entries.description: The character's normal outfit dressed up with extra elements while the original design stays clearly recognizable. Not [alternate_costume](#alternate_costume), which puts them in something else entirely; it sits happily beside [adapted_costume](#adapted_costume) when the additions build on the original.

entries.name: official_alternate_hair_color
entries.description: A character's hair appears in a colour other than the standard one by decision of the rights holder, through a released [costume](#costume) or dyeing within the story. Fan-invented recolours take [alternate_hair_color](#alternate_hair_color).

entries.name: alternate_weapon
entries.description: A character's [signature](#signature) [weapon](#weapon) appears in a form the source never gives it, changed in shape, kind or scale. The weapon shown is tagged for what it is as [well](#well).

entries.name: borrowed_design
entries.description: A fan-invented alternate outfit that [caught](#caught) on widely enough that other artists began drawing it too. It stands apart from designs that are official; add [alternate_costume](#alternate_costume) alongside.

entries.name: official_alternate_color
entries.description: A character appears in a recolouring of the usual palette that comes from the rights holder, such as a game skin, with a good part of the design changed. Where only the hair or the eyes differ use the narrower official tags, and never pair it with the fan-made [alternate_color](#alternate_color).

entries.name: alternate_muscle_size
entries.description: The character is drawn considerably more or less [muscular](#muscular) than usual, a slight [figure](#figure) given a builder's frame or a [heavy](#heavy) one slimmed down. Tag the build shown, such as muscular, as [well](#well).

entries.name: title_parody
entries.description: A joke built on a work's [title](#title), such as a reworked [logo](#logo) or a punning name.

entries.name: more_muscular_than_canon
entries.description: A character drawn with far more muscle than the source design gives them. The changed build is the whole point, which puts it among the deliberate off-model redesigns.

entries.name: alternate_body_size_(more_muscle)
entries.description: The character is bulked [well](#well) past their usual build, with heavier muscle across arms, chest and [legs](#legs). It is a reinterpretation of the design rather than a [transformation](#transformation) inside the story.

entries.name: official_alternate_eye_color
entries.description: A character's eyes are shown in a colour other than the usual one, and the change comes from an official source such as an alternate form or a released [costume](#costume). A fan recolour is [alternate_eye_color](#alternate_eye_color).

entries.name: alternate_hair_ornament
entries.description: The character wears a hair ornament other than their usual one. The ornament itself is tagged separately by what it is.

entries.name: card_parody
entries.description: Fan art laid out to imitate the cards of an official product, borders, stat boxes and rules text included. The joke lies in how closely the layout copies the original.

entries.name: adapted_uniform
entries.description: A recognisable uniform reworked from its usual cut, most often shortened or tightened into something more revealing. The original design has to stay readable underneath the changes.

entries.name: season_connection
entries.description: Characters from unrelated series drawn together because their shows happened to air in the same broadcast season. A [crossover](#crossover) whose only real connection is the schedule.

entries.name: alternate_species
entries.description: A humanoid character is drawn as a member of another humanoid race, a human as an [elf](#elf) or [alien](#alien), or one invented race as another. Turning somebody into an [animal](#animal), a [machine](#machine) or a slime falls to those tags instead.

entries.name: alternate_wings
entries.description: A winged character is drawn with [wings](#wings) of another kind, or with an unusual take on their own. Feathered wings turned membranous, or given a different span and colour, both count.

entries.name: alternate_pectoral_size
entries.description: The [pectorals](#pectorals) are drawn clearly bigger or smaller than the character normally has. Skip it where the usual build is unclear, or where the picture is deliberately ageing them up or down.

entries.name: out_of_character
entries.description: Characters behave in ways that contradict how they are usually written, prompting the reaction that they would never do that. Skip it where a [parody](#parody), [cosplay](#cosplay) or similar licence explains the behaviour, and use [dark](#dark) persona for a good character turned wicked.

entries.name: alternate_body_size
entries.description: A character is [redrawn](#redrawn) with markedly different proportions of [fat](#fat) or muscle than usual. Where only the bust or the [pectorals](#pectorals) change, the narrower tags [cover](#cover) it.

entries.name: power_connection
entries.description: Characters from different works are put side by side because they share the same ability, be it [fire](#fire), [lightning](#lightning) or control of time. The matching power is the whole reason for the pairing.

entries.name: alternate_facial_hair
entries.description: A [beard](#beard), moustache or [stubble](#stubble) unlike the one the character normally carries. Sometimes it is a deliberate reworking, sometimes an artist [reading](#reading) long [sideburns](#sideburns) as a full beard.

entries.name: species_connection
entries.description: A [crossover](#crossover) or [parody](#parody) built around characters from different works who share the same underlying [animal](#animal), [plant](#plant), or [creature](#creature) basis. The shared species is the point of the connection.

entries.name: mirror_image
entries.description: Either the whole picture has been flipped left for right against an earlier version, or a character's normally asymmetric features appear reversed. Not the same as a [reflection](#reflection) shown inside an actual [mirror](#mirror).

entries.name: pose_imitation
entries.description: A character strikes a stance strongly tied to somebody else, borrowing another work's [signature](#signature) posture. The pleasure of it lies in recognising the source.

entries.name: songover
