entries.description: A picture that draws imagery from two or more separate songs into one [crossover](#crossover), [mixing](#mixing) their references the way a work-based crossover mixes series. The songs, not the franchises behind them, are what's being combined.

entries.name: alternate_height
entries.description: The character is drawn markedly taller or shorter than the source makes them. It covers reinterpretation of stature, not deliberate [giant](#giant) or shrinking scenes, which have their own tags.

entries.name: genre_connection
entries.description: A [crossover](#crossover) or nod that works because two series share a genre or a theme rather than a character or a visual style. It marks the reason behind the reference.

entries.name: borrowed_hairstyle
entries.description: A character is drawn wearing somebody else's hairstyle in place of their own. It often accompanies a borrowed accessory or a complete swap of outfits.

entries.name: artist_self-reference
entries.description: The artist works their own earlier pictures into a new one, as posters on a wall, a page a character holds, or a composition staged again. A wink to anyone who knows the older work.

entries.name: poster_parody
entries.description: An image built to [mimic](#mimic) one particular famous poster, borrowing its layout, lettering and staging while swapping in other characters. It has to point at an identifiable original, not merely look poster-ish.

entries.name: alternate_footwear
entries.description: Shoes, [boots](#boots) or [sandals](#sandals) replacing the footwear the character usually has on. Use it beside the [tag](#tag) naming what is actually drawn.

entries.name: alternate_design
entries.description: A character is rebuilt with a substantially reworked look, going further than a change of [clothes](#clothes) or hair. They stay recognisable through the [redesign](#redesign).

entries.name: alternate_size
entries.description: The whole body is scaled [well](#well) above or below the character's established proportions. It is for reinterpretation of the design, since [giant](#giant), shrinking and [miniature](#miniature) scenarios have their own tags.

entries.name: palette_swap
entries.description: The same character or object shown in a different set of colours, with nothing else altered. Two characters trading colour schemes, and schemes that are exact reverses of each other, are separate tags, and inverted colours are different again.

entries.name: alternate_body_hair
entries.description: Body hair is put on a character who has none by default, or noticeably thickened or removed. It is a frequent touch in heavier, more masculine reinterpretations.

entries.name: design_speculation
entries.description: A fan's guess at how an unannounced character will look, worked up from a [silhouette](#silhouette), a name or a teaser image. The design is invention rather than anything official.

entries.name: alternate_body_fluid
entries.description: Blood, [saliva](#saliva) or another bodily fluid is drawn as something else, such as [petals](#petals) [spilling](#spilling) from a wound or [ink](#ink) where [blood](#blood) should be. Where the effect is meant to unsettle, add [body_horror](#body_horror).

entries.name: light_persona
entries.description: A brighter, gentler counterpart of a character, set apart by paler hair, [costume](#costume) or colour scheme. The [mirror](#mirror) of a darkened version.

entries.name: color_switch
entries.description: Characters keep their own outfits but trade colour schemes with one another. Altering a single character's colours is [palette_swap](#palette_swap) instead.

entries.name: adapted_weapon
entries.description: A [weapon](#weapon) built as a variation on a character's [signature](#signature) arm, keeping its [silhouette](#silhouette) or motif while changing the form. It also stretches to reworked versions of standalone weapons.

entries.name: choice
entries.description: The picture is laid out as a branching prompt from a visual novel, offering the player two or more options to pick between. These are nearly always invented screens made in imitation of adult game menus rather than genuine captures.

entries.name: alternate_sleeve_length
entries.description: An outfit is drawn with sleeves longer or shorter than the original has, a long-sleeved [jacket](#jacket) cut down to short sleeves for instance. Add the sleeve [tag](#tag) that [matches](#matches) the picture.

entries.name: adapted_object
entries.description: One kind of object is redesigned to echo the look of something else entirely, borrowing its shape, colours or [markings](#markings). The joke lies in recognising the original design under the new purpose.

entries.name: alternate_element
entries.description: A character tied to one element is shown wielding another, [ice](#ice) in place of [fire](#fire) and so on. Their effects and often their colours shift to match.

entries.name: official_cosplay
entries.description: A character dresses as someone from another work and the [costume](#costume) itself comes from the rights holders, whether as a game outfit or as a [crossover](#crossover) between properties of one company.

entries.name: borrowed_weapon
entries.description: A character holds or fights with the [weapon](#weapon) of another. The armament is recognisably somebody else's [signature](#signature) piece, which is what makes the picture worth marking.

entries.name: alternate_animal_ears
entries.description: A character who already has [animal](#animal) ears is drawn with those of a different animal. The swap only reads if the usual species is known.

entries.name: borrowed_accessory
entries.description: A character wears an accessory belonging to somebody else in the [cast](#cast), such as another's [glasses](#glasses), [hat](#hat) or hair ornament. The swap is the point of the picture.

entries.name: movie_reference
entries.description: The picture quotes a well-known film, restaging a famous shot, pose or line with other characters [standing](#standing) in for the original [cast](#cast). The joke depends on the viewer recognising the source.

entries.name: multiple_style_parody
entries.description: One artist [imitating](#imitating) several other artists' manners inside a single picture, usually a row or [grid](#grid) of the same character [redrawn](#redrawn) each way. A lone imitation is [plain](#plain) [style_parody](#style_parody).

entries.name: alternate_ears
entries.description: The ears differ from the character's usual pair, human ones turned pointed or another set put in their place. Only the ears change, and the shape actually drawn is tagged as [well](#well).

entries.name: alternate_eyewear
entries.description: Glasses, shades or another eyepiece stand in for the one the character normally wears. Name the eyewear that is actually drawn as [well](#well), such as [sunglasses](#sunglasses) or [goggles](#goggles).

entries.name: alternate_uniform
entries.description: Somebody wears a [school](#school) or service uniform belonging to a different group inside the same setting. It stays within the fiction's own [wardrobe](#wardrobe), unlike a free [costume](#costume) change or a [cosplay](#cosplay) of another work.

entries.name: alternate_tail
entries.description: A tailed character is given a [tail](#tail) unlike their own, whether another animal's, a different length or a different pattern. Tag the tail as drawn as [well](#well).

entries.name: alternate_horns
entries.description: A horned character's [horns](#horns) differ in shape, length, colour or placement from the usual pair. Tag the horns as drawn alongside it.

entries.name: actor_connection
entries.description: The picture plays on roles that share the same live-action performer, putting those characters together or [nodding](#nodding) between them. The voice-acting equivalent has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: alternate_eyebrows
entries.description: The brows are drawn in a shape, [weight](#weight) or colour the source never uses. Add the [tag](#tag) for the brows as actually drawn beside it.

entries.name: shadow
entries.description: Darkness [cast](#cast) where an object blocks the light: a figure's shadow on the ground, a wall, or another character. With [no](#no) shading present at all, [flat_color](#flat_color) may apply instead.

entries.name: glowing
entries.description: An object or character radiating light of its own rather than [catching](#catching) it. The base [tag](#tag) under [glowing_eyes](#glowing_eyes), [glowing_weapon](#glowing_weapon) and the rest of the [family](#family).

entries.name: sunlight
entries.description: Light from the [sun](#sun) [falling](#falling) into a scene, over a character or across a [landscape](#landscape). A distinct shaft of it is [sunbeam](#sunbeam), a radiating design is [sunburst](#sunburst); a single picture may deserve several.

entries.name: lens_flare
entries.description: Streaks, rings and bright blooms thrown across the picture where a [strong](#strong) light such as the [sun](#sun) scatters inside a [camera](#camera) lens, imitated in drawn art. Heaped on to excess it becomes [lens_flare_abuse](#lens_flare_abuse).

entries.name: reflection
entries.description: A mirrored image of the subject appears on a reflective surface such as a [mirror](#mirror), [glass](#glass), [water](#water), or a polished [floor](#floor). The reflection may be the focus of the picture or show something different from the subject; a reflection within a reflection is [recursion](#recursion).

entries.name: backlighting
entries.description: The light comes from behind the subject, so its edges catch a bright rim while the side facing the viewer falls into [shadow](#shadow) or [silhouette](#silhouette). A [sunset](#sunset), a [window](#window) or a bright [sky](#sky) behind a [figure](#figure) produces it.

entries.name: light_rays
entries.description: Visible beams of light [pouring](#pouring) through gaps between objects, such as trees, clouds or a [window](#window) frame. A single beam thrown down on a person is [spotlight](#spotlight), and rays from the [sun](#sun) are also [sunlight](#sunlight).

entries.name: shade
entries.description: A character or area [sitting](#sitting) in the shade, including a [hat](#hat) brim casting [shadow](#shadow) over the eyes. Not for a person's own [cast](#cast) shadow, and not [shaded_face](#shaded_face), which has [no](#no) real light source.

entries.name: dark
entries.description: Surroundings lit so poorly that detail is swallowed up. Describes how the whole picture is lit, not merely a black [backdrop](#backdrop) behind the subject.

entries.name: transparent
entries.description: An object, other than clothing, that genuinely lets light pass through it, such as [glass](#glass), clear plastic or [water](#water). Use [see-through_clothes](#see-through_clothes) for a sheer garment, [x-ray](#x-ray) for a normally opaque object drawn as if [invisible](#invisible), and [see-through_body](#see-through_body) for a character's own skin turning clear.

entries.name: sunbeam
entries.description: Visible shafts of [sunlight](#sunlight) [breaking](#breaking) through clouds, trees or a [window](#window), also called crepuscular rays or god rays. Implies [light_rays](#light_rays) and sunlight.

entries.name: dappled_sunlight
entries.description: Sunlight [broken](#broken) up by leaves and branches into a mottled scatter of bright patches and [shadow](#shadow). Light filtered instead by blinds or something covering a [window](#window) is [window_shadow](#window_shadow).

entries.name: drop_shadow
entries.description: A flat [patch](#patch) of colour in exactly the figure's own [outline](#outline), offset behind them as though [cast](#cast) on an [invisible](#invisible) wall. Once the shape is angled or distorted it becomes an ordinary [shadow](#shadow).

entries.name: sidelighting
entries.description: The main light source falls on the subject from one side, leaving the other half of the face or body in [shadow](#shadow). Compare [backlighting](#backlighting) and rim_lighting.

entries.name: purple_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) [glowing](#glowing) or drawn in purple above the head, often on a [dark](#dark) [angel](#angel) or a demonic character. Combine with halo.

entries.name: spotlight
entries.description: A beam of light [falling](#falling) on a single [figure](#figure) from above, as on a [stage](#stage) or during a moment of [despair](#despair) with someone [kneeling](#kneeling). Distinct from the broader [stage_lights](#stage_lights).

entries.name: diffraction_spikes
entries.description: Bright lines radiating out from a point of light, the star pattern lamps and stars pick up in a lens. Sparkle covers the small four-pointed default and [glint](#glint) the [flash](#flash) off metal or a blade, while this [tag](#tag) takes [realistic](#realistic) or exaggerated versions, often asymmetric or with many rays.

entries.name: city_lights
entries.description: The glow of a city's windows, signs and streetlamps, usually at [night](#night) and often seen from a [height](#height) or through a [window](#window). Commonly paired with night and [cityscape](#cityscape).

entries.name: stage_lights
entries.description: The bright coloured lamps [shining](#shining) down on a [stage](#stage) or its [audience](#audience) during a [concert](#concert), play or dance performance. A single beam trained on one [figure](#figure) is [spotlight](#spotlight) instead.

entries.name: reflective_liquid
entries.description: A [pool](#pool) or film of fluid whose surface mirrors what is above it, doubling the [figure](#figure) or the light. Rain-soaked ground, shallow [water](#water) and glossy spills all produce it.

entries.name: neon_trim
entries.description: Bright [glowing](#glowing) lines run across the surface of a [suit](#suit), a [machine](#machine) or even bare skin, as though light were piped along its edges. High [contrast](#contrast) against a [dark](#dark) body is the usual effect.

entries.name: bloom
entries.description: Bright lights [spilling](#spilling) a soft glow into everything around them, [imitating](#imitating) an overexposed photograph. Common in 3D renders and in painted highlights; [glowing](#glowing) and [lens_flare](#lens_flare) [cover](#cover) neighbouring effects.

entries.name: glasses_shine
entries.description: A blank [flare](#flare) of light [sweeping](#sweeping) across the lenses so the eyes behind them cannot be seen. Shorthand for a scheming, commanding or dramatic moment.

entries.name: sunburst
entries.description: Rays of light radiating outward from a central point, drawn as a design or a glow effect rather than the actual [sun](#sun). For a whole [backdrop](#backdrop) made of such rays, [tag](#tag) [sunburst_background](#sunburst_background) instead.

entries.name: moonlight
entries.description: Pale white to bluish light from the [moon](#moon) [falling](#falling) across a [night](#night) scene, [throwing](#throwing) long soft shadows. Often drawn with the moon itself somewhere in the frame.

entries.name: tree_shade
entries.description: A subject [resting](#resting) in the [shadow](#shadow) [cast](#cast) by a tree's canopy, typically on a bright [day](#day). Sunlight filtering through the leaves above often produces [dappled_sunlight](#dappled_sunlight) as [well](#well).

entries.name: different_reflection
entries.description: A [mirror](#mirror) or other reflective surface shows something other than what stands before it, such as a character's other self. An unintended mismatch is [bad_reflection](#bad_reflection), and a missing [reflection](#reflection) is no_reflection.

entries.name: partially_shaded_face
entries.description: A [shadow](#shadow) falls across only part of the face, often the upper half or one side, leaving the rest lit. A softer form of [shaded_face](#shaded_face), used the same way to signal menace, anger or gloom.

entries.name: caustics
entries.description: Rippling bands of bright light thrown onto a surface by light bent through [water](#water) or [glass](#glass), like the wavering pattern on a [pool](#pool) [floor](#floor). They fill [underwater](#underwater) and [poolside](#poolside) scenes.

entries.name: window_shadow
entries.description: Sunlight or [moonlight](#moonlight) passing through a [window](#window) throws its frame, blinds, or shutters as a [shadow](#shadow) pattern across a wall, [floor](#floor), or character. It is a lighting effect, distinct from the blinds themselves, which take their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: neon_lights
entries.description: Coloured [tube](#tube) lighting of the sort that fills [night](#night) streets, [bars](#bars) and shopfronts with [saturated](#saturated) glow. Modern versions often use LEDs shaped to imitate the [old](#old) gas-filled tubes.

entries.name: colored_shadow
entries.description: A [cast](#cast) [shadow](#shadow) rendered in a colour, purple or blue for instance, rather than in black or grey. A [plain](#plain) [dark](#dark) shadow needs only shadow.

entries.name: eye_trail
entries.description: A [glowing](#glowing) streak of light [dragging](#dragging) behind a character's eyes, usually signalling anger, resolve or raw power. It overlaps with [glowing_eyes](#glowing_eyes) but is its own effect.

entries.name: glowing_butterfly
entries.description: A [butterfly](#butterfly) with a visible glow about its body or [wings](#wings). Used as a magical or dreamlike touch in a scene.

entries.name: candlelight
entries.description: A [dark](#dark) scene lit chiefly by the amber glow of one or more candles, the light [falling](#falling) away quickly into [shadow](#shadow). A lit [candle](#candle) [standing](#standing) in an otherwise well-lit room does not qualify.

entries.name: searchlight
entries.description: A very bright outdoor [spotlight](#spotlight) beam [sweeping](#sweeping) the [sky](#sky) or picking out a [figure](#figure), of the kind used to hunt [aircraft](#aircraft) or escapees. Use spotlight instead when someone is simply being lit for a performance.

entries.name: reflection_focus
entries.description: The subject is mostly or entirely hidden and is seen chiefly through a [reflection](#reflection) in a [mirror](#mirror), [window](#window), or [water](#water). The reflected image carries most of the information in the picture.

entries.name: translucent
entries.description: A material in the picture that lets some light pass through without being fully clear, [sitting](#sitting) between opaque and [transparent](#transparent). Use [see-through_clothes](#see-through_clothes) when it is a garment doing this, and transparent when the object lets light through completely.

entries.name: glowing_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) [giving](#giving) off light of its own, its [petals](#petals) bright against the [dark](#dark). Enchanted woods, [night](#night) gardens and [fantasy](#fantasy) scenes are full of them.

entries.name: dark_room
entries.description: A room with the lights off or turned right down, so [shapes](#shapes) read as silhouettes against whatever spills in from a [window](#window) or a [screen](#screen). Not a photographic darkroom, which is a different thing entirely.

entries.name: refraction
entries.description: Light [bending](#bending) as it passes through [water](#water), [glass](#glass), or another clear medium, so [shapes](#shapes) seen through it appear shifted or warped. It is why a [stick](#stick) looks [broken](#broken) at the waterline, and why rippling bands of light play across a [pool](#pool) [floor](#floor).

entries.name: eyes_in_shadow
entries.description: Everything around the eyes drops into [darkness](#darkness) while the eyes themselves stay visible, glinting out of it. Different from a whole face in [shadow](#shadow), and from hair [hanging](#hanging) over the eyes.

entries.name: different_shadow
entries.description: The [cast](#cast) [shadow](#shadow) does not match the body [throwing](#throwing) it, revealing a beast, a second self or a truer form. A quiet way of saying the character is not what they appear to be.

entries.name: glowing_mouth
entries.description: Light [pouring](#pouring) out from inside an open mouth. Draws a beam or a [breath](#breath) being charged, or the hollow glare of a demonic or mechanical head.

entries.name: iridescent
entries.description: A surface that changes colour as the angle of view moves, [running](#running) through pinks, greens and blues like oil on [water](#water). Fabric, insect [wings](#wings), [scales](#scales), bubbles and glazed [pottery](#pottery) all take it.

entries.name: screen_light
entries.description: A [monitor](#monitor), [phone](#phone), or [television](#television) acting as the light source in the scene, [throwing](#throwing) pale colour over whoever sits in front of it while the rest of the room stays [dark](#dark).

entries.name: gradient_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) whose colour blends steadily from one hue into one or more others rather than [glowing](#glowing) a single tone. A particular case of a multicoloured halo.

entries.name: gleam
entries.description: A hard highlight glancing off a surface, drawn as a short bright streak or point. Used on blades, eyes, [glass](#glass) and polished metal to mark a catch of light.

entries.name: dim_lighting
entries.description: The scene is lit low, with [shadow](#shadow) filling most of the frame while [shapes](#shapes) and faces stay readable. Not full [darkness](#darkness), since detail still comes through.

entries.name: underlighting
entries.description: Light [falling](#falling) on the subject from below, so shadows run upward across the face. Gives an eerie, theatrical [cast](#cast) and is a [staple](#staple) of [campfire](#campfire) and ghost-story scenes.

entries.name: bioluminescence
entries.description: Light made by a living thing's own [chemistry](#chemistry): [glowing](#glowing) fungi, plankton, [jellyfish](#jellyfish), deep-sea [fish](#fish) or invented plants. Fireflies are deliberately kept out of it, since they would otherwise [crowd](#crowd) out every other use.

entries.name: red_light
entries.description: A red light source that noticeably colours the scene, whether a [lamp](#lamp), a neon [sign](#sign), a [screen](#screen), or [sunlight](#sunlight) through something red. The source may sit off-frame, but the red [cast](#cast) has to shape how the picture reads; a merely red surface does not qualify.

entries.name: camera_flash
entries.description: The hard white burst of a [flash](#flash) [firing](#firing), [blowing](#blowing) out the subject or [spilling](#spilling) a bright [bloom](#bloom) across the frame. Usually there is a [photographer](#photographer) somewhere in the scene.

entries.name: string_of_light_bulbs
entries.description: A run of large [globe](#globe) bulbs slung between poles or walls for decorative light. Bigger than Christmas lights and often left [hanging](#hanging) year-round over [bars](#bars) and terraces.

entries.name: crack_of_light
entries.description: A single narrow band of light [cuts](#cuts) across an otherwise [dark](#dark) scene. A [door](#door) left slightly ajar is the classic source.

entries.name: glowing_gem
entries.description: A jewel lit from within, commonly set into a [staff](#staff), a [ring](#ring), an [altar](#altar) or a piece of armour. In [fantasy](#fantasy) the light stands for stored [magic](#magic) [waiting](#waiting) to be spent.

entries.name: lens_flare_abuse
entries.description: Flares piled on far past anything a real lens would throw, [streaking](#streaking) and blooming over the whole picture.

entries.name: non-circular_lens_flare
entries.description: Flare from a light source drawn as streaks, [bars](#bars) or polygons rather than the usual round blobs. It imitates the optics of anamorphic [camera](#camera) lenses.

entries.name: outer_glow
entries.description: A soft [halo](#halo) of light spreads outward from the edge of a [figure](#figure) or object, generally laid over the finished art as an effect. Where the light clearly comes from behind, [backlighting](#backlighting) fits better, and a crisp bright edge is [white_outline](#white_outline).

entries.name: light_in_heart
entries.description: A soft glow sits on the chest over the [heart](#heart), symbolic or magical rather than any light source present in the scene.

entries.name: reflective_surface
entries.description: Something other than a [mirror](#mirror) throws [back](#back) an image, such as a polished [floor](#floor), a [car](#car) body, or a [glass](#glass) wall. Most often it is the ground the character stands on, drawn with an inverted copy beneath the [feet](#feet).

entries.name: glowing_halo
entries.description: The [ring](#ring) or disc [floating](#floating) above or behind a head is a light source in its own right. Angels, saints and characters in an exalted state wear one.

entries.name: blue_light
entries.description: A scene lit blue, by a glow, a [lamp](#lamp), a [screen](#screen) or [moonlight](#moonlight). The colour is [cast](#cast) across subject and surroundings rather than belonging to an object that is itself blue.

entries.name: glowing_clothes
entries.description: Garments that act as a light source instead of merely [catching](#catching) one. Narrower tags exist for [glowing](#glowing) armour, [headgear](#headgear), legwear, masks and shoe [soles](#soles).

entries.name: sun_glare
entries.description: Harsh direct [sunlight](#sunlight) [washing](#washing) into the frame, [blowing](#blowing) out part of the picture and often [throwing](#throwing) streaks or a bright disc across it. It is the light itself overwhelming the shot, rather than a simple [lens_flare](#lens_flare) artifact.

entries.name: glowing_earrings
entries.description: Earrings that give off light of their own rather than [catching](#catching) a highlight. Suggests magical or technological jewellery.

entries.name: green_light
entries.description: Light with a green [cast](#cast) [falling](#falling) across the scene, thrown by a [screen](#screen), signal [lamp](#lamp), [glowing](#glowing) object or the surroundings. It tints skin and clothing rather than simply being a green thing in frame.

entries.name: face_in_shadow
entries.description: Shadow swallows the whole face, [hiding](#hiding) most or all of its features. The eyes may still [glint](#glint) out of the [dark](#dark), so it [can](#can) sit beside a [tag](#tag) for shadowed eyes.

entries.name: shadow_puppet
entries.description: A [shadow](#shadow) deliberately shaped into a [figure](#figure) such as an [animal](#animal) or a person, thrown on a wall by cupped hands or by flat cut-out puppets held before a light.

entries.name: glowing_feather
entries.description: A feather that gives off light of its own, whether [drifting](#drifting) loose or still set in a wing. The glow carries angelic or spiritual [weight](#weight) rather than being a highlight [cast](#cast) from somewhere else.

entries.name: chiaroscuro
entries.description: Strong light set against deep [shadow](#shadow) across the whole composition, modelling form and [giving](#giving) figures solid [weight](#weight). Baroque painting is the reference point for the effect.

entries.name: glowing_arm
entries.description: An arm [giving](#giving) off its own light, whether from [magic](#magic), channelled [energy](#energy) or [machinery](#machinery) built into it. Marks a charged limb rather than one lit from outside.

entries.name: subsurface_scattering
entries.description: Light shown [sinking](#sinking) into skin, [wax](#wax) or another soft material and [glowing](#glowing) [back](#back) out, so thin parts such as ears and fingers read as warm and [translucent](#translucent). A rendering effect that reads as realism.

entries.name: neon_sign
entries.description: Lettering or a shape formed from [glowing](#glowing) bent tubing, hung on a shopfront, a bar or a wall. It throws coloured light onto whatever stands near it.

entries.name: flare
entries.description: A pyrotechnic that burns with a fierce light, used to signal [distress](#distress), to light up ground, or to pull heat-seeking missiles away. The optical streak a bright source leaves on a lens is [lens_flare](#lens_flare).

entries.name: glowing_headgear
entries.description: A [hat](#hat), [helmet](#helmet) or [headpiece](#headpiece) that works as its own light source. Headwear merely [catching](#catching) light from elsewhere, or swallowed by a body-wide [aura](#aura), does not count.

entries.name: ominous_shadow
entries.description: A [shadow](#shadow) falls across the scene while whatever casts it stays out of frame, around a [corner](#corner) or behind the viewer. A flat [silhouette](#silhouette) counts as readily as a detailed [outline](#outline).

entries.name: ultraviolet_light
entries.description: Light beyond the violet end of the visible range, shown through its effects: purple-cast lamps, [glowing](#glowing) whites and fluorescent [paint](#paint) lit up in the [dark](#dark). Also the light behind a suntan.

entries.name: headlight_beam
entries.description: The light of a vehicle's lamps is part of the picture: a visible cone [cutting](#cutting) through air, [dust](#dust), [rain](#rain) or [water](#water), or the bright [patch](#patch) it throws onto the [road](#road) and whoever stands there.

entries.name: golden_hour
entries.description: The low warm [sun](#sun) of the hour after [dawn](#dawn) or before [sunset](#sunset), laying amber light over everything and drawing the shadows out long. A lighting condition rather than a place.

entries.name: shining
entries.description: Something in the picture gives off light or a [strong](#strong) [gleam](#gleam), drawn with radiating rays, a soft [bloom](#bloom) or a burst of highlight around it.

entries.name: glowing_armor
entries.description: Plate or [mail](#mail) that emits light, often along its [seams](#seams), engraved [runes](#runes) or a central stone. Common on enchanted and powered suits.

entries.name: glowing_hot
entries.description: Metal or another material heated until it shines by itself, going from dull red through orange to white and even blue as the heat rises. Seen at forges, on a freshly struck blade and around molten [rock](#rock).

entries.name: glowing_crystal
entries.description: A [crystal](#crystal) [shining](#shining) from within and casting light on what surrounds it. A fixture of [cave](#cave) interiors, [ruins](#ruins) and magical [scenery](#scenery).

entries.name: floodlights
entries.description: Big high-output lamps on poles or gantries [washing](#washing) a [stadium](#stadium), a [stage](#stage) or a [building](#building) front with light. They usually read as [glaring](#glaring) points with visible beams.

entries.name: glowing_arrow
entries.description: An arrow [shining](#shining) with its own light, either nocked on the [string](#string) or in flight. Usually signals a magical or [energy](#energy) shot rather than an ordinary shaft.

entries.name: sparkle
entries.description: A small drawn [glint](#glint) of light, usually four-pointed or star-shaped, scattered in the air, on [liquid](#liquid), or inside eyes. Distinct from glint, a single [flash](#flash) on a hard or metallic surface, and from the larger, more [realistic](#realistic) [diffraction_spikes](#diffraction_spikes).

entries.name: petals
entries.description: Loose petals parted from their [flower](#flower), [drifting](#drifting) in the air, scattered on the ground or [floating](#floating) on [water](#water). An intact [bloom](#bloom) is tagged by its colour instead; variants include [falling_petals](#falling_petals) and [rose_petals](#rose_petals).

entries.name: steam
entries.description: Visible [water](#water) vapour rising from a [bath](#bath), [hot](#hot) [food](#food), a [drink](#drink) or a hot spring. Steam coming off a person's body specifically is [steaming_body](#steaming_body).

entries.name: light_particles
entries.description: Clusters of tiny [glowing](#glowing) motes [drifting](#drifting) through the scene, like [dust](#dust) [caught](#caught) in a [sunbeam](#sunbeam) or [energy](#energy) gathering around a charging [spell](#spell). Motes that do not glow are dust, [ashes](#ashes) or [debris](#debris), and a few large glints are [sparkle](#sparkle).

entries.name: breath
entries.description: Exhaled air shows as visible white vapour, either the puffs of a [cold](#cold) [winter](#winter) [day](#day) or the heat of an erotic scene. Add winter or [snow](#snow) where the weather explains it; panting drawn as an expression is [heavy_breathing](#heavy_breathing).

entries.name: steam_from_mouth
entries.description: Breath leaving the mouth as visible vapour, from [cold](#cold) air, hard exertion or [hot](#hot) [food](#food). Drawn as a small white [plume](#plume).

entries.name: smoke
entries.description: Visible smoke [drifting](#drifting) in the scene, from [fire](#fire), cigarettes, gunfire, or an [explosion](#explosion). Narrower tags include [smoke_trail](#smoke_trail) and [smoking_barrel](#smoking_barrel).

entries.name: bubble
entries.description: Thin spheres of soapy film drift through the scene, [catching](#catching) [iridescent](#iridescent) colour. The [tag](#tag) stretches to other bubbles too — [chewing](#chewing) gum blown into one, or air rising through [water](#water).

entries.name: water_drop
entries.description: Individual drops of [water](#water) held together by surface tension, round or teardrop-shaped, on skin, [glass](#glass), leaves or [flying](#flying) through the air. Includes raindrops and splashes [broken](#broken) into droplets.

entries.name: falling_petals
entries.description: Flower [petals](#petals) drift down or [swirl](#swirl) on the [wind](#wind), most often [cherry](#cherry) blossom in spring. One of the commonest romantic or wistful atmospheric touches.

entries.name: confetti
entries.description: Small scraps of coloured [paper](#paper) thrown in [celebration](#celebration), filling the air at a [party](#party) or a [birthday](#birthday). Flower [petals](#petals) are not confetti.

entries.name: air_bubble
entries.description: A [pocket](#pocket) of air [trapped](#trapped) in [water](#water) or in something soft or [frozen](#frozen), most often a [stream](#stream) of them rising past a [submerged](#submerged) [figure](#figure). It almost always accompanies [underwater](#underwater) scenes.

entries.name: snowflakes
entries.description: Individual six-pointed [ice](#ice) crystals drawn into the picture, either as decoration or [drifting](#drifting) through the air. Not to be [confused](#confused) with the [flower](#flower) that shares a Japanese name.

entries.name: splashing
entries.description: Water or another [liquid](#liquid) thrown up into the air, whether kicked by [feet](#feet), batted by hands, or displaced by something [falling](#falling) in. May leave droplets or a wider [splatter](#splatter) behind.

entries.name: falling_leaves
entries.description: Leaves drift or blow through the air, typical of [autumn](#autumn) and windy scenes. A mood effect rather than [foliage](#foliage) still on a [tree](#tree).

entries.name: rose_petals
entries.description: Petals [shed](#shed) from a [rose](#rose), scattered on a [bed](#bed) or [floor](#floor) or [drifting](#drifting) through the air.

entries.name: pink_petals
entries.description: Loose pink [petals](#petals) [drifting](#drifting) through the air or [lying](#lying) scattered on the ground, usually from [cherry](#cherry) or [plum](#plum) blossom. Only detached petals count; those still on the [flower](#flower) belong to the flower's [tag](#tag).

entries.name: paint_splatter
entries.description: Splashes and flecks of coloured [paint](#paint) used as a graphic [device](#device), most often behind the subject or thrown across the picture as a motif. Splashes of black [ink](#ink) do not count.

entries.name: debris
entries.description: Fragments thrown through the air by an impact, an [explosion](#explosion) or a burst of [energy](#energy). Wreckage already settled on the ground is [rubble](#rubble).

entries.name: embers
entries.description: Glowing orange specks [sitting](#sitting) inside a [fire](#fire) or [drifting](#drifting) up out of it. Drawn as [floating](#floating) particles around flames, campfires and [burning](#burning) [wreckage](#wreckage), adding heat to a scene.

entries.name: falling_feathers
entries.description: Loose [feathers](#feathers) drift down through the air, often [shed](#shed) from [angel](#angel) or [bird](#bird) [wings](#wings). An atmospheric touch rather than plumage on a body.

entries.name: dust
entries.description: Fine dry particles of earth or grime settled on surfaces or [hanging](#hanging) in the air, drawn as haze or speckling in [old](#old) rooms, [ruins](#ruins) and battlefields. A puff kicked up by movement is [dust_cloud](#dust_cloud).

entries.name: sparks
entries.description: Tiny [glowing](#glowing) fragments flung off by [fire](#fire), a grinder, clashing metal, or a [sparkler](#sparkler). The presence of fire alone doesn't earn the [tag](#tag); compare [embers](#embers) for the glowing remnants left after something burns.

entries.name: red_petals
entries.description: Loose red [petals](#petals) [drifting](#drifting) through the air or scattered on a surface. Only for petals separated from their [flower](#flower); a whole red [bloom](#bloom) takes [red_flower](#red_flower).

entries.name: visible_air
entries.description: Drawn air or [breath](#breath), an ambiguous catch-all. Prefer a specific [tag](#tag): [air_current](#air_current) or [wind](#wind) for moving air, breath or [puff_of_air](#puff_of_air) for exhalation, and [steaming_body](#steaming_body) for clouds around the body.

entries.name: smoke_trail
entries.description: A streak of [smoke](#smoke) drawn behind a moving source such as a [rocket](#rocket), [aircraft](#aircraft), or thrown object. Tag beside smoke.

entries.name: dust_cloud
entries.description: A puff of loose [dirt](#dirt) thrown into the air, usually by somebody [running](#running), [landing](#landing) or skidding on dry ground. A vehicle's trail or a collapsing wall raises one too.

entries.name: fireflies
entries.description: Numerous small [glowing](#glowing) [dots](#dots) or streaks [drifting](#drifting) through a scene to stand for fireflies, nearly always at [night](#night). Add [firefly](#firefly) where the insects themselves are drawn; one lone glow is firefly on its own.

entries.name: shards
entries.description: Sharp fragments of something brittle that has [shattered](#shattered): [glass](#glass), [crystal](#crystal), [ice](#ice), or [mirror](#mirror) pieces [flying](#flying) or scattered. Tag with [broken_glass](#broken_glass) or the like when the source is clear.

entries.name: petals_on_liquid
entries.description: Flower [petals](#petals) [floating](#floating) on [water](#water) or another [liquid](#liquid), as in a petal-strewn [bath](#bath), a [pond](#pond) or a [cup](#cup) of [tea](#tea).

entries.name: foam
entries.description: A mass of tiny bubbles, whether frothing from a mouth, crowning a poured [beer](#beer), or gathering on [water](#water). Lather worked up from [soap](#soap) while [bathing](#bathing) is [soap_bubbles](#soap_bubbles) instead.

entries.name: sparkling_aura
entries.description: A cluster of sparkles surrounding a particular character or object, [giving](#giving) it a glittering [halo](#halo). A lone [glint](#glint) is [sparkle](#sparkle); sparkles filling the whole [backdrop](#backdrop) instead belong under [sparkle_background](#sparkle_background).

entries.name: splatter
entries.description: A [liquid](#liquid) such as [paint](#paint), [water](#water) or [blood](#blood) spread across a surface in scattered drops and streaks. Tag the pattern it leaves rather than the act of [throwing](#throwing) it.

entries.name: blue_petals
entries.description: Blue [petals](#petals) [drifting](#drifting) through the air or [lying](#lying) scattered on the ground, separated from any [bloom](#bloom). While they are still attached to the [flower](#flower), [blue_flower](#blue_flower) is the correct [choice](#choice).

entries.name: glitter
entries.description: Tiny reflective flakes scattered across a surface or [drifting](#drifting) through the air, [throwing](#throwing) [back](#back) points of light. A lone stray highlight is [sparkle](#sparkle), and a wide scatter of them is [light_particles](#light_particles).

entries.name: condensation
entries.description: Beads of [water](#water) gathered on a surface colder than the air around it, such as a chilled [glass](#glass) or a [window](#window) pane. Fogged glass drawn on with a finger is [glass_writing](#glass_writing), while airborne moisture is [fog](#fog) or [steam](#steam).

entries.name: yellow_petals
entries.description: Loose yellow [petals](#petals) in the air, on the ground or [resting](#resting) on skin, detached from the [bloom](#bloom) they came from. An intact [flower](#flower) calls for [yellow_flower](#yellow_flower) instead, and fan-shaped ginkgo [foliage](#foliage) is a [leaf](#leaf) rather than a petal.

entries.name: exhaust
entries.description: Fumes or [steam](#steam) [blowing](#blowing) out of a vehicle or [machine](#machine) and trailing away behind it as a visible [plume](#plume). It reads as the [engine](#engine) [working](#working) hard.

entries.name: spraying
entries.description: Liquid [forced](#forced) out under pressure toward a [target](#target), from a [hose](#hose), [can](#can) or [bottle](#bottle). The word also covers a [weapon](#weapon) [firing](#firing) a rapid burst of shots.

entries.name: falling_flower
entries.description: Whole flowers, not loose [petals](#petals), drift or tumble down through the frame. Usually there for atmosphere around a [figure](#figure).

entries.name: colored_smoke
entries.description: Smoke rendered in a definite hue rather than white, grey or black. Signal flares, [stage](#stage) effects and [magic](#magic) are the usual sources.

entries.name: glowing_petals
entries.description: Drifting [petals](#petals) that shine faintly, generally pale pink, white or blue and half [transparent](#transparent). They lend a dreamlike or ghostly air to whatever they fall over.

entries.name: purple_petals
entries.description: Loose purple [flower](#flower) [petals](#petals) [drifting](#drifting) through the air or settled on a surface. Frequently used as a decorative shower [falling](#falling) around a [figure](#figure).

entries.name: bishie_sparkle
entries.description: A dreamy haze of sparkles, hearts, flowers and soft bubbles wrapped around an attractive character, usually over a pale pastel ground. Two or more of those elements together make it; a lone [sparkle](#sparkle) or [heart](#heart) [backdrop](#backdrop) has its own simpler [tag](#tag).

entries.name: dew_drop
entries.description: Beads of [water](#water) condensed onto [grass](#grass), [petals](#petals) or leaves in the cool of early [morning](#morning). Usually a small detail that sells a fresh outdoor scene.

entries.name: ashes
entries.description: Fine grey powder left behind by [fire](#fire), [drifting](#drifting) through the air, heaped in drifts, or [falling](#falling) with [embers](#embers) over a burnt-out scene. Also the remains kept in an [urn](#urn).

entries.name: gas
entries.description: A visible [cloud](#cloud) of airborne substance [drifting](#drifting) through the scene, from a [smoke](#smoke) [bomb](#bomb), [poison](#poison), [exhaust](#exhaust) or a vent. Fuel is a separate matter and belongs with gasoline.

entries.name: window_fog
entries.description: Condensation misting a [window](#window), [mirror](#mirror), or other [glass](#glass) surface, sometimes marked with finger-drawn [shapes](#shapes) or [running](#running) streaks. It signals [cold](#cold) outside, warmth within, or a steamy [bath](#bath) just taken.

entries.name: squirting_liquid
entries.description: Liquid shot out of something a character is [playing](#playing) with, such as a [bottle](#bottle), [hose](#hose) or [water](#water) [gun](#gun). Not for bodily fluids, which [female_ejaculation](#female_ejaculation) and [lactation](#lactation) [cover](#cover) instead.

entries.name: overflowing
entries.description: A [container](#container) holds more than it [can](#can) take, so the contents run over the rim. Usually a [liquid](#liquid), sometimes loose solids such as [ice](#ice) cubes; sexual fluids escaping a body have a [tag](#tag) of their own.

entries.name: in_bubble
entries.description: A character sealed inside a [soap](#soap) or air [bubble](#bubble), [floating](#floating) within its thin [shell](#shell). The curved surface warps whatever shows through it.

entries.name: falling_money
entries.description: Banknotes or coins [rain](#rain) down through the air, scattered or flung. It stands for sudden riches, or for [money](#money) being thrown away.

entries.name: sea_spray
entries.description: Salt [water](#water) flung into the air where [waves](#waves) break against [rock](#rock) or hull, [hanging](#hanging) as scattered droplets and mist.

entries.name: pink_liquid
entries.description: A pink fluid [pouring](#pouring), [splashing](#splashing) or filling a vessel. It may be a [drink](#drink), a [potion](#potion) or a substance the picture never names.

entries.name: orange_petals
entries.description: Orange [petals](#petals) loose from a [bloom](#bloom), [drifting](#drifting) through the air or scattered on a surface. Petals still on the [flower](#flower) take [orange_flower](#orange_flower).

entries.name: kakera
entries.description: Crystal [shards](#shards) [hanging](#hanging), [drifting](#drifting) or [falling](#falling) through the air and [catching](#catching) the light. They stand in for shattering [glass](#glass), [breaking](#breaking) [magic](#magic) and similar fragmentary effects.

entries.name: black_petals
entries.description: Petals in black that have come away from their [flower](#flower), scattered across a surface or [drifting](#drifting) through the air. A black [bloom](#bloom) still attached to its stem is [black_flower](#black_flower) rather than this.

entries.name: green_petals
entries.description: Green [petals](#petals) detached from a [bloom](#bloom), [falling](#falling) or scattered across the scene. They read much like falling leaves, so use the [tag](#tag) only when a green [flower](#flower) is also present.

entries.name: fire
entries.description: Open flame anywhere in the picture, from a [candle](#candle) or [campfire](#campfire) to a [burning](#burning) [building](#building) or a [cast](#cast) [spell](#spell). The [glowing](#glowing) specks that drift up off it are [embers](#embers).

entries.name: pink_halo
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of pink light hovering above the head. As often a piece of character design as a [sign](#sign) of anything holy, and its shape ranges from a [plain](#plain) ring to a [floating](#floating) [device](#device).

entries.name: red_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) [floating](#floating) over a character's head that is red rather than the usual [gold](#gold) or white. Often used for fallen angels or demonic takes on angelic designs.

entries.name: electricity
entries.description: Sparks, arcs and crackling discharge coming off a character, a [weapon](#weapon) or a [machine](#machine). Lightning in the [sky](#sky) is not covered here. Someone deliberately [calling](#calling) the current up is [electrokinesis](#electrokinesis).

entries.name: magic
entries.description: Someone is [working](#working) a [spell](#spell), or magical power is visible in the scene as glows, sigils, [runes](#runes) or conjured [shapes](#shapes). Covers any [display](#display) of supernatural [energy](#energy), whatever its source.

entries.name: hitodama
entries.description: A [floating](#floating) [ghost](#ghost) flame: a [glowing](#glowing) [ball](#ball) trailing a [tail](#tail) of [fire](#fire). They drift around spirits, ghosts and [fox](#fox) characters in Japanese-styled work.

entries.name: mechanical_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) that hovers above a character's head through technological means rather than divine ones, frequently built from ringed metal segments or fitted with small lights.

entries.name: aura
entries.description: Energy made visible around a character, drawn as a glow, a haze or rising flame [clinging](#clinging) to the body. It covers martial-arts ki and superpowers gathering, and comedy uses it for somebody radiating fury.

entries.name: explosion
entries.description: A burst of [fire](#fire), [smoke](#smoke) and [flying](#flying) [debris](#debris) from a [bomb](#bomb), a [spell](#spell) or something gone badly wrong. Drawn as a [fireball](#fireball) or a [mushroom](#mushroom) [cloud](#cloud), often behind somebody [walking](#walking) calmly away. The [device](#device) that sets it off is [explosive](#explosive).

entries.name: magic_circle
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of [runes](#runes) and geometric figures marking out the [space](#space) for a [spell](#spell) or [ritual](#ritual), drawn on the ground or [hanging](#hanging) in the air. Often [glowing](#glowing), and often layered as several rings turning at once.

entries.name: black_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) in black [floating](#floating) above a character's head, usually marking a fallen [angel](#angel) or a [dark](#dark) counterpart to an angelic design. It may be a solid [ring](#ring), a [broken](#broken) one or a flat disc.

entries.name: floating_object
entries.description: Something inanimate — a [book](#book), a [weapon](#weapon), a stone — hangs in the air with [no](#no) visible support, usually through [magic](#magic) or [telekinesis](#telekinesis). Use [floating_book](#floating_book) or [floating_weapon](#floating_weapon) for those particular cases.

entries.name: energy
entries.description: Visible power drawn from some physical, chemical or magical source, [glowing](#glowing) around a person, [weapon](#weapon) or [machine](#machine). A catch-all for effects that are not clearly [fire](#fire), [electricity](#electricity) or [magic](#magic); shaped attacks are [energy_ball](#energy_ball) and [energy_beam](#energy_beam).

entries.name: blue_fire
entries.description: Flames [burning](#burning) blue instead of orange. In fiction the colour almost always marks the [fire](#fire) as supernatural or spectral rather than merely very [hot](#hot).

entries.name: danmaku
entries.description: A screen-filling barrage of projectiles in the manner of bullet-hell shooting games, [patterned](#patterned) so tightly that only slivers of empty [space](#space) remain. The shots may be coloured balls, lasers, thrown knives, [petals](#petals) or [paper](#paper) charms.

entries.name: glowing_weapon
entries.description: Any [weapon](#weapon) that gives off light: an enchanted blade, an [energy](#energy) [gun](#gun), a charged [staff](#staff). A [sword](#sword) takes [glowing_sword](#glowing_sword) in addition.

entries.name: darkness
entries.description: Darkness handled as a substance or an element, [rolling](#rolling) in black clouds or [reaching](#reaching) out as inky tendrils. Plain poor lighting is [dark](#dark) instead.

entries.name: burning
entries.description: Something in the picture is alight and being eaten by flame — a [house](#house), a [tree](#tree), an object, a person. Once only the charred remains are left, use [burnt](#burnt).

entries.name: glowing_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) whose blade or edges emit light, from enchantment, contained [energy](#energy) or a blade made of light itself.

entries.name: pyrokinesis
entries.description: Flame that visibly answers to a character's will, curling around a hand, swirling on command, or launched as an [attack](#attack). Combine with [fire](#fire) and [magic](#magic); broader mental abilities fall under [psychic](#psychic) instead.

entries.name: energy_ball
entries.description: A [glowing](#glowing) sphere of power gathered by a character, cupped in the hands or [hanging](#hanging) in front of them before it is thrown. The standard charged [attack](#attack) of [fighting](#fighting) series; it may open out into an [energy_beam](#energy_beam).

entries.name: electrokinesis
entries.description: Generating or steering [electricity](#electricity) as a personal power, with arcs gathering around the hands or the whole body. The current it produces is electricity, which always comes with it.

entries.name: breath_weapon
entries.description: A [creature](#creature), most often a [dragon](#dragon), breathes out a [stream](#stream) of destructive [energy](#energy): [fire](#fire), [ice](#ice), [lightning](#lightning), [poison](#poison) or raw [magic](#magic). Add the specific form where there is one, such as [breathing_fire](#breathing_fire), and the creature [tag](#tag).

entries.name: breathing_fire
entries.description: Flames pour out of a mouth, from a dragon's blast to a [street](#street) performer's trick. Add [breath_weapon](#breath_weapon) and [fire](#fire).

entries.name: purple_fire
entries.description: Flames that burn mostly purple, usually read as magical or spectral [fire](#fire). Combine with fire; a [floating](#floating) will-o'-the-wisp style flame may also fit [hitodama](#hitodama).

entries.name: dark_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) [riding](#riding) above the head in a distinctly [dark](#dark) hue, whatever its exact colour. The opposite number of [glowing_halo](#glowing_halo).

entries.name: laser
entries.description: A beam of light [energy](#energy) drawn as a straight bright line, either [cutting](#cutting) and destroying or [serving](#serving) as a thin [aiming](#aiming) line. Reflective surfaces sometimes bounce it.

entries.name: dark_aura
entries.description: An [aura](#aura) in black or [heavy](#heavy) [dark](#dark) tones [boiling](#boiling) around a character. It signals rage, malice or a readiness to do harm.

entries.name: aqua_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) [glowing](#glowing) cyan or aqua rather than the usual [gold](#gold). Add halo along with whatever the [ring](#ring) marks, an [angel](#angel) or a similar being.

entries.name: hydrokinesis
entries.description: Water moved and shaped by a character's will, [hanging](#hanging) in orbs, tendrils or [waves](#waves) around them. The [water](#water) [magic](#magic) of [fantasy](#fantasy) and superpower settings.

entries.name: campfire
entries.description: An open [fire](#fire) built at a camp, ringed with stones and fed with logs, [throwing](#throwing) light and warmth over the [people](#people) around it. It belongs with tents, [night](#night) scenes and [food](#food) cooked on sticks.

entries.name: orange_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) [glowing](#glowing) orange above or behind the head. Common on angels, spirits and [idol](#idol) designs that borrow the motif.

entries.name: telekinesis
entries.description: Objects hover or move as though steered by someone's mind, with [no](#no) hands touching them. When the thing being moved has its own dedicated [tag](#tag), such as [pyrokinesis](#pyrokinesis) for [fire](#fire), prefer that instead.

entries.name: flaming_weapon
entries.description: Any [weapon](#weapon) alight with flame or made of [fire](#fire), a [burning](#burning) [spear](#spear) or [axe](#axe) as readily as a blade. Where the weapon is a [sword](#sword), use [flaming_sword](#flaming_sword).

entries.name: energy_beam
entries.description: A line of power fired as an [attack](#attack), sometimes gathering as a [ball](#ball) first and then let loose. More often a magical or superhuman ability than the output of a [machine](#machine).

entries.name: missing_halo
entries.description: A character who normally wears a [halo](#halo) appears without one. The absence itself is the point, so the rest of the design stays as usual.

entries.name: through_medium
entries.description: Something crosses the surface it is depicted on, such as a [figure](#figure) [climbing](#climbing) out of a page or a hand [reaching](#reaching) into a picture. May be a fourth-wall break but need not be; the [screen](#screen) version is [through_screen](#through_screen).

entries.name: hologram
entries.description: A three-dimensional image projected into open air, usually [glowing](#glowing) and half [transparent](#transparent). It covers projected [people](#people), maps and objects; a projected control panel is [holographic_interface](#holographic_interface).

entries.name: flaming_sword
entries.description: A [sword](#sword) [sheathed](#sheathed) in flame, or formed out of [fire](#fire) altogether. The sword-shaped case of [flaming_weapon](#flaming_weapon).

entries.name: powering_up
entries.description: A character [gathers](#gathers) [energy](#energy) in [plain](#plain) sight, an [aura](#aura) flaring, hair lifting, the ground cracking, before letting it loose. Not to be mixed up with picking up a [power-up](#power-up) item.

entries.name: muzzle_flash
entries.description: The burst of light at a gun's [barrel](#barrel) as it fires, drawn as a bright [flare](#flare) at the muzzle. It marks the shot as happening now rather than merely being aimed.

entries.name: frozen
entries.description: A character or object sealed inside solid [ice](#ice). Cold weather or ice [lying](#lying) about the scene is not enough — the subject itself is locked in.

entries.name: green_fire
entries.description: Flames [burning](#burning) green instead of orange, which reads as magical, cursed or chemical rather than ordinary. Spirit flames, will-o'-the-wisps and enchanted weapons carry it often.

entries.name: invisible
entries.description: A character cannot be seen at all, by the viewer and usually by [everyone](#everyone) in the scene, with their [clothes](#clothes) either vanishing too or [hanging](#hanging) in empty air. Partly see-through bodies are [transparent](#transparent), and sheer garments [see-through_clothes](#see-through_clothes).

entries.name: time_stop
entries.description: A character halts the world around them and keeps moving through it, [everyone](#everyone) else [caught](#caught) mid-gesture. Usually shown as a combat power, sometimes with [clock](#clock) imagery or cracks in the air.

entries.name: winged_halo
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of light [floating](#floating) above the head with [wings](#wings) attached to it. Angelic character designs and stylised video-game interface halos both use the shape.

entries.name: glowing_hand
entries.description: One hand [shining](#shining) with light, typically while a [spell](#spell) is [cast](#cast), a wound healed or an [attack](#attack) charged. Use [glowing_hands](#glowing_hands) when both are lit.

entries.name: digital_dissolve
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) or object [breaking](#breaking) apart into a drift of small squares, or assembling out of them. Reads as loading, teleporting or being deleted.

entries.name: fireball
entries.description: A [ball](#ball) of flame [flying](#flying) through the air or held ready to be thrown. It covers [cast](#cast) [fire](#fire) spells and the [burning](#burning) [energy](#energy) blasts of [fighting](#fighting) series alike.

entries.name: electrocution
entries.description: Current [running](#running) through somebody: arcs snapping around the body, hair [standing](#standing) on end, sometimes the [skeleton](#skeleton) [flashing](#flashing) into view. Played as slapstick about as often as it is played as real harm.

entries.name: liquid_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) made of fluid, most often [water](#water) or [blood](#blood), [floating](#floating) above the head. One sagging or [dripping](#dripping) apart is a [melting](#melting) halo instead.

entries.name: melting_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) that sags and drips rather than [holding](#holding) its [ring](#ring) shape, its light seeming to run like [liquid](#liquid). Reads as an angel's grace coming apart.

entries.name: flaming_hand
entries.description: Fire wraps a hand or its fingers without harming them, the mark of a pyrokinetic at work or of [energy](#energy) gathered for a strike.

entries.name: burnt
entries.description: Something has already been through [fire](#fire) and is left blackened and charred, whether an object, a surface or a person. The flames are out; only the damage remains.

entries.name: pink_fire
entries.description: Flames [burning](#burning) pink instead of orange, generally marking [magic](#magic) or a deliberately stylised effect. Everything else about the [fire](#fire) is tagged as usual.

entries.name: cryokinesis
entries.description: Cold and [ice](#ice) obeying a character's will: [frost](#frost) creeping from a hand, [shards](#shards) assembling in mid-air, a blast of freezing [wind](#wind). The power at work, not merely a wintry setting.

entries.name: energy_barrier
entries.description: A wall, [dome](#dome) or [bubble](#bubble) of [glowing](#glowing) force raised to stop attacks or block a way through, usually [translucent](#translucent) and faintly [patterned](#patterned). It [can](#can) also serve as a surface to stand on or a [cage](#cage) to hold someone.

entries.name: plasma
entries.description: Either the [glowing](#glowing) ionised state of matter, drawn as crackling coloured [energy](#energy), or the straw-coloured [liquid](#liquid) part of [blood](#blood). Which sense applies follows from the surrounding scene.

entries.name: ice_crystal
entries.description: Faceted [shards](#shards) of [ice](#ice) [hanging](#hanging) in the air or creeping across a surface. They usually belong to a [cold](#cold) [attack](#attack) or a frosty [aura](#aura) rather than to [plain](#plain) weather.

entries.name: hemokinesis
entries.description: Blood moved and shaped by will, lifted into ribbons, [spikes](#spikes) or [floating](#floating) spheres, or drawn straight out of a wound. A supernatural power rather than [plain](#plain) [bleeding](#bleeding).

entries.name: flaming_skull
entries.description: A bare [skull](#skull) wrapped in [fire](#fire), [burning](#burning) on its own or worn in place of a head. Used for [undead](#undead) figures, banners and occult props.

entries.name: summoning
entries.description: A [creature](#creature) or object being called into existence by [magic](#magic). The picture needs some of the trappings of the act, the caster, a [glowing](#glowing) [circle](#circle), [runes](#runes), a portal or surging [energy](#energy), not merely the thing that has arrived.

entries.name: lit_fuse
entries.description: A [fuse](#fuse) cord burns down toward a [bomb](#bomb) or firework, [sparks](#sparks) trailing from its tip. It marks the seconds before an [explosion](#explosion).

entries.name: bonfire
entries.description: A large open [fire](#fire) built from a heap of wood and [burning](#burning) in the open air. Sparks and [smoke](#smoke) climb from it and its light usually colours everything nearby.

entries.name: mouth_beam
entries.description: Energy fired out of an open mouth, drawn as a bright [column](#column), a [spreading](#spreading) cone or a gathering [ball](#ball) of light. Common on dragons, [giant](#giant) beasts and [mecha](#mecha).

entries.name: crescent_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) drawn as an open arc rather than a closed [ring](#ring), curving like a [crescent](#crescent) behind the head. Angel and [idol](#idol) designs both use it.

entries.name: mind_reading
entries.description: Hearing another person's thoughts, usually drawn as unspoken words or images [drifting](#drifting) from their head toward the reader. Sending thoughts in the other direction is [telepathy](#telepathy).

entries.name: black_fire
entries.description: Flames rendered black in whole or in part, often edged with purple or [dark](#dark) red. Shorthand for cursed and demonic [magic](#magic).

entries.name: flaming_halo
entries.description: The [ring](#ring) hovering above the head is alight, or is made of nothing but flame. Angelic and infernal designs both use it.

entries.name: eye_beam
entries.description: A beam of [energy](#energy) fired straight out of the eyes, a standard [attack](#attack) in action series and superhero art. The eyes often glow just before it goes off.

entries.name: geokinesis
entries.description: Stone, [soil](#soil) or [rubble](#rubble) moved by will alone, [hanging](#hanging) in the air or hurled without a hand touching it. Shown as cracked ground, [drifting](#drifting) boulders or spires driven up from below.

entries.name: whisp
entries.description: A [drifting](#drifting) [ball](#ball) or trail of pale light hovering in the air, read as a [spirit](#spirit) flame rather than a [lamp](#lamp). Forests, graveyards and magical scenes are its usual home.

entries.name: energy_drain
entries.description: One character pulls life, [magic](#magic) or strength out of another, drawn as a [thread](#thread) or [stream](#stream) of light [running](#running) between them. The victim usually pales or sags as it happens.

entries.name: teleport
entries.description: A body vanishes from, or arrives at, a place instantly, marked by [dissolving](#dissolving) edges, a [flash](#flash), streaks of light or a [ring](#ring) of [energy](#energy). The moment of transition is the point of the drawing.

entries.name: through_painting
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) steps out of, or reaches through, a painting or [portrait](#portrait) into the room in front of it. The crossing between picture and world is what makes the moment supernatural.

entries.name: umbrakinesis
entries.description: The power to summon and shape [darkness](#darkness) and [shadow](#shadow) at will. Drawn as black tendrils, [spreading](#spreading) pools of gloom, or a [swallowing](#swallowing) [aura](#aura) around the caster.

entries.name: flaming_head
entries.description: Flame covers the head or stands in place of it, whether a [burning](#burning) [skull](#skull) or a body topped by [fire](#fire) instead of a face. A [staple](#staple) of spectral and demonic designs.

entries.name: spell
entries.description: A character in the act of [working](#working) [magic](#magic), [caught](#caught) just before the incantation resolves. Usually shown with a [wand](#wand), [staff](#staff), or [grimoire](#grimoire), gathering light, [runes](#runes), or a [circle](#circle) around them.

entries.name: burning_building
entries.description: A [house](#house), [tower](#tower) or other [structure](#structure) alight, with flame and [smoke](#smoke) [pouring](#pouring) from its windows and roof. Accident, arson or [war](#war) may lie behind it.

entries.name: glowing_hands
entries.description: Both hands lit from inside, usually held out to channel or release power. When only one of them shines the [tag](#tag) is [glowing_hand](#glowing_hand).

entries.name: ice_shard
entries.description: Broken splinters of [ice](#ice) [flying](#flying) loose or driven point-first into a surface. They are usually the [wreckage](#wreckage) of a [frost](#frost) [attack](#attack) or a [shattered](#shattered) sheet.

entries.name: afterburner
entries.description: The bright cone of flame trailing a jet engine's tailpipe while extra thrust is being burned. It shows up behind [aircraft](#aircraft) [climbing](#climbing) away, turning hard or in combat.

entries.name: invisible_wall
entries.description: A barrier nothing shows, but which plainly stops somebody, given away by flattened [palms](#palms), a squashed cheek or a ripple where the body presses. It is usually played for comedy.

entries.name: mushroom_cloud
entries.description: The [tall](#tall) capped [column](#column) of [smoke](#smoke) and [debris](#debris) thrown up by a huge blast, usually seen at a distance on the [horizon](#horizon). Nuclear detonations are the classic source, though large conventional charges and eruptions raise one too.

entries.name: single_flame
entries.description: One isolated [tongue](#tongue) of [fire](#fire) [burning](#burning) in the picture, with nothing obvious [feeding](#feeding) it. Reads as a will-o'-the-wisp, a [spirit](#spirit) light, or a conjured spark.

entries.name: aerokinesis
entries.description: Wind bent to somebody's will, drawn as currents gathering and swirling around their hands or body. The air moves in a directed way rather than as ordinary weather.

entries.name: recharging
entries.description: A character is being topped up with [energy](#energy), commonly shown through a [battery](#battery) [gauge](#gauge) overhead, a plugged-in [cable](#cable), or arcs of current [running](#running) into the body. Androids and electricity-powered characters are the usual subjects; charging an ordinary [phone](#phone) or [laptop](#laptop) is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: shockwave
entries.description: A visible [ring](#ring) or front of pressure [racing](#racing) outward from an [explosion](#explosion), an [energy](#energy) blast or a sonic boom, drawn as a distorting band of air.

entries.name: laser_pointer_projection
entries.description: The visible red or green light thrown by a [laser](#laser) sight or [pointer](#pointer), shown as a beam, as a dot on the [target](#target), or both. It applies even when the [device](#device) casting it is out of frame.

entries.name: vortex
entries.description: A swirling funnel of [water](#water), air, light or [energy](#energy), drawn as tightening spirals [pulling](#pulling) inward. Often a portal or the wake of something powerful.

entries.name: red_lightning
entries.description: Arcs of [electricity](#electricity) drawn in red rather than white or blue, crackling around a [figure](#figure) or splitting the [sky](#sky). The colour usually marks the power as [sinister](#sinister) or supernatural.

entries.name: florakinesis
entries.description: Plants made to grow, move or strike at will, drawn as [vines](#vines), creepers and blossoms answering a [gesture](#gesture). The power on [display](#display) is the point, not greenery merely present in the scene.

entries.name: red_aura
entries.description: A red glow or flame-like [field](#field) radiates from a character's body, usually signaling rage, [corruption](#corruption), or a surge of power. It surrounds the [figure](#figure) rather than being [cast](#cast) by an outside light source.

entries.name: red_fire
entries.description: Flames drawn in [saturated](#saturated) red rather than ordinary orange and yellow, [giving](#giving) them an unnatural or magical [quality](#quality). Used for infernal and cursed [fire](#fire) as much as ordinary [burning](#burning).

entries.name: yellow_fire
entries.description: Flames [burning](#burning) yellow, brighter than the usual orange.

entries.name: molten_metal
entries.description: Metal heated until it runs, [glowing](#glowing) orange to near-white as it is poured or sits in a crucible. Belongs to forge, foundry and smelting scenes, and lights everything around it.

entries.name: ice_flower
entries.description: A blossom formed out of [ice](#ice), grown by [frost](#frost) [magic](#magic) or carried as a cold-themed trinket. Its [petals](#petals) are drawn [translucent](#translucent) and faceted rather than soft.

entries.name: magnetism
entries.description: Magnetic force shown at work: metal snapping together, blades [hanging](#hanging) in mid-air, nails streaming toward an outstretched hand. Usually a character's power rather than an ordinary physical effect.

entries.name: disappear
entries.description: Somebody or something vanishing out of the scene, thinning away to nothing or leaving only an [outline](#outline) behind. The going itself is what is drawn.

entries.name: photokinesis
entries.description: A character [bending](#bending) light to their will, drawn as radiant beams, hovering orbs or a blinding [flare](#flare) gathered in the hand. One of the elemental-control powers, tagged alongside the glow effects it throws off.

entries.name: intangible
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) or object passes through solid matter as though it were not there, [sinking](#sinking) through a [floor](#floor) or [stepping](#stepping) out of a wall. Ghosts and phasing powers are the usual explanation.

entries.name: air_current
entries.description: Moving air drawn as pale streaks [running](#running) through the scene, usually white or grey. It makes visible what would otherwise be nothing, and vapour or [dust](#dust) in the air [can](#can) justify it.

entries.name: white_fire
entries.description: Flames drawn white instead of orange, [reading](#reading) as unnaturally [hot](#hot) or otherworldly. Divine, ghostly and high-power [magic](#magic) effects lean on it constantly.

entries.name: materializing
entries.description: A [figure](#figure) or object shown coalescing out of nothing, part [translucent](#translucent) or built from [drifting](#drifting) particles and light before it fully resolves. The reverse process is [fading](#fading) or [dissolving](#dissolving) away.

entries.name: telepathy
entries.description: Communication passes mind to mind without speaking, drawn with a hand at the [temple](#temple), [glowing](#glowing) eyes, or visible arcs of thought between two heads. A common power across [fantasy](#fantasy) and [science](#science) fiction.

entries.name: glowing_fist
entries.description: A fist [sheathed](#sheathed) in light, generally an instant before or during a punch. The standard way of drawing a charged melee blow or channelled inner power.

entries.name: orange_fire
entries.description: Flame in ordinary orange, anywhere from a candle-sized flicker to a full blaze.

entries.name: grey_fire
entries.description: Flames drawn grey rather than in warm tones. The colour usually signals ash, [smoke](#smoke) or something unnatural about the [fire](#fire).

entries.name: motion_lines
entries.description: Comic-style streaks drawn around or trailing behind a moving [figure](#figure) or object to show how fast it goes. Lines radiating across the whole panel instead are speed lines.

entries.name: bouncing_breasts
entries.description: Breasts in motion, most often in an animation; in a still picture blur or motion lines have to carry the movement. Where the two move in opposite directions, add [unaligned_breasts](#unaligned_breasts).

entries.name: emphasis_lines
entries.description: Lines bursting outward from a spot the artist wants noticed, making that area jump forward. They mark focus, not movement — lines that show something moving are [speed_lines](#speed_lines).

entries.name: afterimage
entries.description: A faint, offset duplicate of a [figure](#figure) or object marking where it stood a moment earlier. It stands in for speed and usually appears alongside [motion_lines](#motion_lines) or [speed_lines](#speed_lines).

entries.name: speed_lines
entries.description: Streaks drawn to convey fast movement, either trailing an object or filling the background to suggest something rushing past it. Distinct from [emphasis_lines](#emphasis_lines), which draw the eye to a spot without implying motion.

entries.name: broken
entries.description: An object that [no](#no) longer does what it was made for: a snapped [sword](#sword), a smashed [phone](#phone), a [shattered](#shattered) [mirror](#mirror). Something merely chipped or dented but still usable is [damaged](#damaged), and the instant of shattering is [breaking](#breaking).

entries.name: twitching
entries.description: A sudden, sharp, involuntary jerk in reaction to stimulation, drawn with short jagged motion lines. Sustained [shaking](#shaking) is [trembling](#trembling), and a startled recoil is [flinch](#flinch).

entries.name: bouncing_ass
entries.description: Buttocks jiggle with the body's movement, shown through animation or through blur and drawn motion lines. Mark the [ass](#ass) itself as [well](#well).

entries.name: broken_glass
entries.description: Glass that has [shattered](#shattered) or cracked, mostly still in place with a web of fractures across it. Loose fallen fragments are [glass_shards](#glass_shards), and a smashed pane also takes [broken_window](#broken_window).

entries.name: light_trail
entries.description: A moving light source leaves a [glowing](#glowing) streak behind it, as with [car](#car) [tail](#tail) lights in a long exposure or a glowing blade mid-swing. When the source is a glowing eye, use [eye_trail](#eye_trail).

entries.name: shaking
entries.description: A person or object being shaken by something else, drawn with motion lines around it. When the movement instead comes from the subject itself, use [trembling](#trembling).

entries.name: bouncing
entries.description: Something soft travels up and down in quick repeated motion, carried by animation or by motion lines and blur in a still. When it is [breasts](#breasts) moving, the narrower [tag](#tag) applies instead.

entries.name: ass_ripple
entries.description: A wave of impact travels across the buttocks, from a slap or a thrust. Usually drawn with motion lines or a jiggle effect.

entries.name: bullet_hole
entries.description: A [hole](#hole) [punched](#punched) through a wall, [window](#window), vehicle or body by a fired round. It shows that shooting has taken place, or that a shot went narrowly wide.

entries.name: breaking
entries.description: An object [caught](#caught) in the act of shattering or snapping, with fragments still [flying](#flying) outward. The settled aftermath is [broken](#broken), and a pane caught mid-shatter also takes [broken_window](#broken_window).

entries.name: crushing
entries.description: Force pressing something together until it buckles or bursts: a hand closing on an object, a foot coming down, a body [pinned](#pinned) under [weight](#weight). The act itself, with [crushed](#crushed) for the aftermath.

entries.name: shattered
entries.description: Something rigid has [broken](#broken) into pieces, such as [glass](#glass), a [mirror](#mirror), [ice](#ice) or a [mask](#mask), with fragments scattering and cracks radiating out from the break point.

entries.name: ground_shatter
entries.description: The ground [breaking](#breaking) apart under an impact, cracks [running](#running) outward while chunks of [rock](#rock) are flung into the air. A visual shorthand for an enormous release of force.

entries.name: crash
entries.description: Something slams into something else, a body, a vehicle or a wall, [caught](#caught) at the moment of impact. A vehicle already [destroyed](#destroyed) is better served by [wreckage](#wreckage).

entries.name: zooming_in
entries.description: The view appears to close in on its subject as though a [camera](#camera) were [pushing](#pushing) forward, often suggested by converging speed lines or a sequence of progressively tighter frames.

entries.name: projectile_trail
entries.description: A visible streak marks the flight [path](#path) of something thrown or fired, most [familiar](#familiar) as a [glowing](#glowing) tracer behind a [bullet](#bullet). Arrows and thrown blades get the same treatment, often drawn in the manner of speed lines.

entries.name: bouncing_pecs
entries.description: A [muscular](#muscular) chest flexes so that the [pectorals](#pectorals) jump. Outside animation the movement needs blur or drawn lines to read at all.

entries.name: smear_frame
entries.description: An animation trick where a fast-moving subject is stretched and blurred into a streak across the frame. Related to motion blur and afterimages, it exaggerates speed for a single beat of movement.

entries.name: crushed
