entries.description: What is left after something has been squeezed flat or [broken](#broken) apart by force. The pressure has already done its work, where [crushing](#crushing) shows it happening.

entries.name: rapid_punches
entries.description: A flurry of blows lands so fast that the limbs are drawn as several overlapping afterimages at once. Despite the name, kicks and other rapid repeated strikes shown this way count too.

entries.name: claw_mark
entries.description: The scored trace left where a claw was dragged across a surface, drawn as parallel gouges or slashes. A pressed paw print is something else entirely.

entries.name: wheel_o_feet
entries.description: A [running](#running) character's [legs](#legs) blur into a [spinning](#spinning) disc or a figure-eight beneath them, cartoon shorthand for tremendous speed. Borrowed from classic animation and from platform-game mascots.

entries.name: attack_trail
entries.description: The [path](#path) a strike has swept through the air, drawn as a [glowing](#glowing) band or streak [following](#following) a blade, a fist or a bolt of power. Like speed lines, it exists to put movement into a still drawing.

entries.name: bouncing_hair
entries.description: Hair springs up and down with the character's movement, carried by animation or by blur and motion lines. It reads as a bounce rather than the slow drift of [floating_hair](#floating_hair).

entries.name: collision
entries.description: Two figures or objects [slam](#slam) together, drawn at the instant of contact with impact effects thrown off around them. It is the [crash](#crash) itself, not the [wreckage](#wreckage) left afterwards.

entries.name: itano_circus
entries.description: A swarm of missiles fired at once, weaving and crossing on twisting [smoke](#smoke) trails before curving hard onto the [target](#target). Borrowed from [mecha](#mecha) animation, it now describes any absurdly excessive volley.

entries.name: ricocheting
entries.description: A solid object [bouncing](#bouncing) off its [target](#target) and shooting away in a new direction without [breaking](#breaking) apart, typically a [bullet](#bullet), blade or thrown item. Hearts, sparkles and other symbols glancing away belong under a separate symbol-ricochet [tag](#tag).

entries.name: crumbling
entries.description: Something [breaking](#breaking) into fragments as it goes: stone [giving](#giving) way, a wall coming down, a [figure](#figure) disintegrating where it stands. The collapse is under way rather than over.

entries.name: zooming_out
entries.description: The view appears to pull [back](#back) from its subject, [opening](#opening) up more of the surrounding [space](#space) than the previous framing showed. The reverse motion to zooming in.

entries.name: heart
entries.description: The ♥ shape, [standing](#standing) for love, romance or [plain](#plain) delight, and one of the [card](#card) suits. It may float beside a character, be printed on something, or form part of a design. The beating organ is [heart_(organ)](#heart_(organ)), and forms such as [heart_hands](#heart_hands) or [heart_censor](#heart_censor) have tags of their own.

entries.name: heart_of_string
entries.description: A single line loops round to draw a [heart](#heart). It may be actual [string](#string), a [ribbon](#ribbon), a typographic stroke or a flourish in the background; what matters is that one unbroken line makes the shape.

entries.name: string_of_fate
entries.description: The red [thread](#thread) from East Asian folklore that links two destined lovers, drawn tied to their little fingers. Shows up in romance scenes to mark a fated pair.

entries.name: broken_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) symbol [split](#split) down the middle, drawn beside a character to show [rejection](#rejection), disappointment or heartbreak, usually for comedy. It is a drawn mark rather than an [injury](#injury).

entries.name: arrow_through_heart
entries.description: The heart-and-arrow [emblem](#emblem) of being in love, taken from Cupid's arrows. Usually drawn as a [floating](#floating) mark or a decoration rather than a wound.

entries.name: heart_(symbol)
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) drawn into the picture as a graphic mark rather than as a physical object — [floating](#floating) beside a character, filling the background, punctuating a line.

entries.name: winged_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) symbol drawn with a wing on either side, often [floating](#floating) as decoration or used as an [emblem](#emblem). It is closely associated with the VTuber Yuzuki Choco.

entries.name: loving_aura
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) of little hearts floats around the head, usually circling, to show affection welling up. A single [heart](#heart) drawn beside a character is just heart; this is the swarm of them.

entries.name: heart_on_chest
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) sits on the chest, centred or over the left side where the organ would be. It may be on the clothing or straight on the skin.

entries.name: heart_halo
entries.description: The [ring](#ring) [floating](#floating) above the head is a [heart](#heart) rather than a [circle](#circle). Angelic and love-themed characters wear one.

entries.name: heart_sticker
entries.description: A single adhesive [heart](#heart) [stuck](#stuck) on skin, clothing or a surface, as decoration or as a small [cover](#cover).

entries.name: pixel_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) drawn from visible [square](#square) blocks instead of smooth curves. It reads as a health-bar icon lifted straight out of a [video](#video) game.

entries.name: heart_stickers
entries.description: Several adhesive hearts [stuck](#stuck) about — scattered over skin, [clothes](#clothes), a [phone](#phone) case or a wall.

entries.name: drawn_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) scribbled onto the picture rather than present in the scene, [floating](#floating) beside a character or scrawled across a photograph. Marks affection or a crush.

entries.name: heart_out_of_chest
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) leaves the chest: thumping out cartoon-style at the sight of someone, or literally pulled free in a darker picture.

entries.name: smoke_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) shape formed out of [drifting](#drifting) [smoke](#smoke), exhaled or trailing from a [cigarette](#cigarette) or [fire](#fire). The symbol is made of the smoke itself rather than drawn beside it.

entries.name: glowing_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) symbol [shining](#shining) with its own light, [floating](#floating) free or drawn onto the body. An anatomical heart that glows belongs to glowing_organ instead.

entries.name: star_(symbol)
entries.description: A drawn star shape, most often the five-pointed ★, used as decoration, a print or an icon. Real stars seen in the [night](#night) [sky](#sky) are [star_(sky)](#star_(sky)), and the occult star is [pentagram](#pentagram) or [pentacle](#pentacle) instead.

entries.name: glint
entries.description: A bright burst of radiating lines thrown off a solid object, especially something metal or sharp such as a blade, jewellery or a [tooth](#tooth). It appears singly or in small numbers, where [sparkle](#sparkle) is looser and comes in crowds.

entries.name: star_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) drawn in the shape of a star rather than a simple [ring](#ring), [floating](#floating) above the head.

entries.name: red_star
entries.description: A star drawn in red as a graphic mark on clothing, vehicles or banners. The five-pointed version is the [emblem](#emblem) of the Soviet Union and of communist movements generally.

entries.name: falling_star
entries.description: Drawn star [shapes](#shapes) tumble down through the picture as symbols. Meteors [streaking](#streaking) across a [night](#night) [sky](#sky) are [shooting_star](#shooting_star) instead.

entries.name: octagram
entries.description: An eight-pointed star [figure](#figure), drawn either as a mark in its own right or as the frame a [magic](#magic) [circle](#circle) is built on. Both the sharp-rayed and the interlaced forms count.

entries.name: shooting_star_(symbol)
entries.description: A star drawn with a [streaking](#streaking) [tail](#tail) behind it, used as a graphic mark on clothing, backgrounds or effects rather than as an actual [meteor](#meteor) in the [sky](#sky).

entries.name: halo
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or disc of light hovering above or behind the head, marking an [angel](#angel), saint or otherwise pure [figure](#figure), including mechanical and stylised versions such as those worn by Blue Archive students. Not the optical ring that [can](#can) form around the [sun](#sun) or [moon](#moon), nor a lens [flare](#flare). A halo [standing](#standing) upright behind the head rather than [floating](#floating) above it takes [halo_behind_head](#halo_behind_head).

entries.name: diamond_(shape)
entries.description: The rhombus, either as a [plain](#plain) shape or as the playing-card [suit](#suit) that stands for wealth. Actual gemstones are [diamond_(gemstone)](#diamond_(gemstone)), and a [lattice](#lattice) of them across [cloth](#cloth) is argyle.

entries.name: circle
entries.description: One or more circular [shapes](#shapes) carry the picture, as a round frame, a [ring](#ring) behind a [figure](#figure) or a geometric design. Not for round objects that merely happen to sit in the scene.

entries.name: triangle
entries.description: A three-sided shape appearing in the picture as a decoration, symbol or pattern element. The percussion [instrument](#instrument) goes under [triangle_(instrument)](#triangle_(instrument)), and the drafting tool under [set_square](#set_square).

entries.name: tomoe_(symbol)
entries.description: A comma-shaped [swirl](#swirl) used in Japanese [heraldry](#heraldry) and [shrine](#shrine) crests. Three arranged in a [circle](#circle) form the mitsudomoe; commonly seen on drums, roofs and swirl-patterned eyes.

entries.name: traditional_halo
entries.description: The [plain](#plain) circular [ring](#ring) that floats above an angel's head, drawn without [spikes](#spikes) or extra ornamentation; a [broken](#broken) ring still counts as long as it keeps that simple form. Add [glowing_halo](#glowing_halo) when the ring itself shines.

entries.name: cube
entries.description: A six-sided [box](#box) shape appearing as an object or a motif, such as [dice](#dice), [floating](#floating) blocks or stacked cubes. The geometric solid itself, not a [crate](#crate) or a packing box.

entries.name: x
entries.description: A literal X shape drawn in the picture as a mark, motif or design element. Not for a diagonal heraldic [cross](#cross) on flags or coats of arms, and not a stand-in for an unrelated character or brand that happens to share the [letter](#letter).

entries.name: halo_behind_head
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) [standing](#standing) vertically behind the head rather than [floating](#floating) flat above it, as in Christian or Buddhist iconography, often drawn as a glow or flames. Not for a halo merely tilted above the head.

entries.name: red_cross
entries.description: A red plus-sign symbol, as seen on a nurse's cap, a medic's [armband](#armband), or a first-aid kit. Not the six-pointed [star_of_life](#star_of_life); combine with [cross](#cross) and [nurse_cap](#nurse_cap) where shown.

entries.name: x_(symbol)
entries.description: A cross-shaped mark used as a symbol: over an eye, on a bandage, as a [sign](#sign) of refusal or simply as decoration. The shape carries meaning on its own rather than forming part of a written word.

entries.name: multicolored_halo
entries.description: The [ring](#ring) or disc [floating](#floating) above the head is drawn in two or more colours instead of one even glow. The colours may sit in bands or blend around the [circle](#circle).

entries.name: rectangular_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) built from one or more oblong panels [floating](#floating) above or behind the head, in place of the traditional [ring](#ring). Common in game character designs where the halo doubles as a hovering interface element.

entries.name: hexagon
entries.description: A six-sided [figure](#figure) in the picture, drawn as a shape, a panel, a tile or a background element.

entries.name: dotted_line
entries.description: A line [broken](#broken) into [dots](#dots) or dashes, used as an [outline](#outline), a cut-here mark or a [path](#path) traced across the picture.

entries.name: square
entries.description: A four-sided shape with equal sides and right angles, drawn as a decorative motif or symbol. For a square-format picture, use the image-shape tags instead.

entries.name: two-tone_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) [carrying](#carrying) exactly two colours, usually [split](#split) into halves or ringed with a contrasting band. The narrower case of a multicoloured halo.

entries.name: trigram
entries.description: One of the eight three-line figures from Taoist cosmology, each line drawn whole or [broken](#broken) to represent yang or yin. Appears as clothing decoration and in [bagua](#bagua) arrangements, notably on a few specific [fantasy](#fantasy) character outfits.

entries.name: grid
entries.description: A pattern of lines crossing at right angles into regular squares. May [cover](#cover) a background, a [floor](#floor), a [screen](#screen) or any other surface in the scene.

entries.name: spiral
entries.description: A curve winding repeatedly around a central point, used as a decorative pattern, a background motif or a hypnotic visual cue. Appears on [fabric](#fabric), in effects, and drawn inside eyes.

entries.name: triquetra
entries.description: A knot of three interlaced arcs forming a three-cornered loop, also called the trinity knot. Turns up in Celtic ornament, neopagan imagery and in a handful of specific [fantasy](#fantasy) character designs.

entries.name: swirl
entries.description: A [spiral](#spiral) or curling loop drawn as an [abstract](#abstract) graphic shape, whether in a background pattern, a visual effect, or a mark on an object, rather than actual moving [water](#water) or [wind](#wind).

entries.name: plus_sign
entries.description: A plus shape somewhere in the picture, on clothing, signage, a [screen](#screen), or [floating](#floating) free as a graphic. Its equal squared arms set it apart from a religious [cross](#cross).

entries.name: pyramid_(geometry)
entries.description: The solid shape with flat triangular faces rising to a point, usually drawn on a [square](#square) base. Three faces make it a tetrahedron instead, and a curved single face makes it a cone; a built monument of the same shape is [pyramid_(structure)](#pyramid_(structure)).

entries.name: rectangle
entries.description: A four-sided [figure](#figure) with right angles and one pair of sides longer than the other, used as a graphic element or a framing [device](#device). A figure with equal sides instead is tagged [square](#square).

entries.name: celtic_knot
entries.description: An endlessly interlacing band woven into loops and plaits, the [signature](#signature) ornament of insular art. Used as [border](#border) decoration, [tattoo](#tattoo) work and detailing on metal and stone.

entries.name: stellated_octahedron
entries.description: An eight-pointed solid made of two tetrahedra passing through each other, [reading](#reading) as a [hexagram](#hexagram) given depth. Every face it shows is a [triangle](#triangle). Often floats in the scene as a magical or geometric motif.

entries.name: small_stellated_dodecahedron
entries.description: A spiky non-convex solid built from twelve [pentagram](#pentagram) faces, one of four [shapes](#shapes) obtained by extending a dodecahedron's faces outward. It shows up as a [floating](#floating) geometric motif or an ornament in stylised backgrounds.

entries.name: sound_wave
entries.description: Sound made visible, either as rings rippling outward from its source or as a jagged line rising and [falling](#falling) with the noise. Distinct from [water](#water) [waves](#waves) and from a [heartbeat](#heartbeat) trace.

entries.name: triangle_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) built from one or more triangles hovering above the head instead of the usual [ring](#ring). Common on stylised angels and on characters whose halo doubles as an interface-like symbol.

entries.name: pentagon_(shape)
entries.description: A five-sided [figure](#figure) appearing in the picture as a shape or a mark. It [can](#can) enclose a [pentagram](#pentagram) without being one itself.

entries.name: dots
entries.description: Small round marks scattered over the picture as a graphic element, in backgrounds, textures and [abstract](#abstract) decoration. Evenly printed [spots](#spots) on [fabric](#fabric) are [polka_dot](#polka_dot).

entries.name: chevron_(symbol)
entries.description: A V-shaped mark of the kind used on flags, badges and logos, often stacked in rows to show rank. It is a graphic [device](#device), not a way of [cutting](#cutting) [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: arrow_cross
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) whose four arms finish in arrowheads. The points must be a deliberate part of the design, not arms that merely taper.

entries.name: inkblot
entries.description: A [spreading](#spreading) blot of spilled [ink](#ink), ragged at the edges and often mirrored in the Rorschach manner. Keep it to black ink.

entries.name: shapes
entries.description: Plain geometric forms such as circles, squares, and triangles used as decoration, a [backdrop](#backdrop) pattern, or a graphic [device](#device).

entries.name: red_circle
entries.description: A red disc or [ring](#ring) used as a graphic element, whether a [target](#target), a [marker](#marker), a rising-sun motif, or a highlight drawn over the picture.

entries.name: geometry
entries.description: Angles, arcs and measured figures drawn into the picture, whether chalked on a board or [floating](#floating) beside a character. Suggests a maths lesson, a calculation or an ordered [abstract](#abstract) design.

entries.name: golden_spiral
entries.description: A logarithmic [spiral](#spiral) that widens by the golden ratio every quarter turn, laid over or built into the picture. It serves both as a composition [guide](#guide) and as a mathematical or occult motif.

entries.name: hex_grid
entries.description: A honeycomb [lattice](#lattice) of hexagons laid over the image, as a background pattern, a [map](#map) overlay or part of a technological [display](#display).

entries.name: crescent
entries.description: A crescent shape used as a motif, on clothing, jewellery, decoration or [floating](#floating) free. The actual [moon](#moon) in the [sky](#sky) is [crescent_moon](#crescent_moon), and ornaments [carrying](#carrying) the shape take their own tags.

entries.name: musical_note
entries.description: Note symbols drawn near a character to show [singing](#singing), [humming](#humming) or a light mood, or scattered over the [backdrop](#backdrop) and across objects. Every notation mark belongs here — rests, clefs, sharps and [flats](#flats) as [well](#well) as [notes](#notes).

entries.name: blue_halo
entries.description: A blue [ring](#ring) [floating](#floating) above a character's head. It appears on angelic designs and on modern character designs that treat the [halo](#halo) as part of the outfit.

entries.name: arrow_(symbol)
entries.description: A drawn arrow such as an arrowhead on a line, used to point something out or show direction. Not the [missile](#missile) fired from a [bow](#bow), which is [arrow_(projectile)](#arrow_(projectile)).

entries.name: yellow_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) above the head [glowing](#glowing) or coloured yellow, the classic golden [angel](#angel) [ring](#ring). Tag halo alongside.

entries.name: eighth_note
entries.description: The ♪ symbol: a filled [note](#note) head on a stem with a single [flag](#flag), drawn in the air to say [music](#music), [humming](#humming) or a light mood. The commonest musical mark in illustration.

entries.name: paw_print
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) paw mark used as a symbol or decoration: printed on [cloth](#cloth), [floating](#floating) as a motif, left as a track on the ground or [serving](#serving) as a [logo](#logo). A [backdrop](#backdrop) made of them is [paw_print_background](#paw_print_background).

entries.name: yin_yang
entries.description: The circular symbol of interlocking black and white teardrops, [standing](#standing) for balanced opposites in Chinese philosophy. Appears on clothing, as decoration or as a motif; a spherical version is [yin_yang_orb](#yin_yang_orb).

entries.name: iron_cross
entries.description: A black [cross](#cross) with flared arms and a white edge, a German [military](#military) decoration and marking. Games set in the Second World War often use it where a [swastika](#swastika) would otherwise appear.

entries.name: beamed_eighth_notes
entries.description: Two or more eighth [notes](#notes) joined at the stems by a single horizontal beam, the [familiar](#familiar) paired [music](#music) symbol. It floats near a [humming](#humming) or [singing](#singing) character or serves as [plain](#plain) decoration.

entries.name: eisernes_kreuz
entries.description: The Iron Cross: a black [cross](#cross) whose arms [flare](#flare) outward, edged in white or silver, used as a German [military](#military) award and [insignia](#insignia). Painted on vehicles, [stitched](#stitched) onto uniforms and flown on banners.

entries.name: lightning_bolt_symbol
entries.description: A stylised zig-zag bolt used as an icon, [standing](#standing) for [electricity](#electricity), speed or shock. Not for the paired [runes](#runes) of the SS [insignia](#insignia), which only resemble it.

entries.name: pentagram
entries.description: A five-pointed star drawn in five straight strokes, often set inside a [circle](#circle). It serves as a witchcraft and occult [emblem](#emblem), is turned upside down in satanic imagery, and in Japan is tied to [onmyouji](#onmyouji) practice. A star worn as an [amulet](#amulet) is [pentacle](#pentacle).

entries.name: fortissimo
entries.description: The musical dynamic for very loud, written as a [script](#script) double f. A single f is forte_(symbol); the mark often serves as a decorative motif on music-themed characters.

entries.name: mitsudomoe_(shape)
entries.description: Three comma-shaped tomoe swirling together in a circular arrangement, a Shinto [emblem](#emblem) seen on drums, [shrine](#shrine) banners and [family](#family) crests.

entries.name: spade_(shape)
entries.description: The playing-card [suit](#suit) symbol, a pointed leaf-like shape on a small stem. Tag it whenever the shape appears as a motif, decoration, or standalone symbol, not only on cards.

entries.name: treble_clef
entries.description: The curling G-clef symbol from sheet [music](#music), drawn [standing](#standing) alone or as a decorative flourish. Artists use it as general shorthand for music, and it also appears printed on some characters' outfits.

entries.name: flower_(symbol)
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) drawn as a symbol or an icon rather than as a real [plant](#plant), such as a flower [emblem](#emblem) or a decorative [bloom](#bloom) [floating](#floating) beside a character.

entries.name: smiley_face
entries.description: The yellow [circle](#circle) with two [dots](#dots) and a curved mouth, the 1970s icon, drawn on a [shirt](#shirt), [sign](#sign) or wall. Not an [emoticon](#emoticon) or [emoji](#emoji).

entries.name: skull_and_crossbones
entries.description: The [emblem](#emblem) of a [skull](#skull) above two crossed bones, marking [poison](#poison), danger or pirates. Appears on flags, labels and clothing.

entries.name: emoji
entries.description: The standard pictogram characters — smileys, hearts, hand signs — drawn into the picture or shown on a [screen](#screen) within it. Keep it for the recognizable emoji look rather than any hand-drawn symbol.

entries.name: sun_symbol
entries.description: A drawn [sun](#sun) [emblem](#emblem), a disc with a set number of rays, appearing as a print, [badge](#badge), [flag](#flag) or decoration. Not the same as the astrological sun [sign](#sign).

entries.name: quarter_note
entries.description: The [note](#note) symbol appears in the picture, a filled note head on a stem, [standing](#standing) for a quarter-length beat. Used to suggest [singing](#singing), [humming](#humming), or a light musical mood; a beamed pair of shorter [notes](#notes) is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: hexagram
entries.description: A six-pointed star built from two interlocked triangles, usually left hollow at the centre. It appears in [magic](#magic) circles, on talismans and as the Star of David; [tag](#tag) the shape whatever meaning it is [carrying](#carrying).

entries.name: power_symbol
entries.description: The on/off icon of a [circle](#circle) with a vertical line, in its closed or [broken](#broken) standby form, appearing on a [device](#device), clothing or as a motif. Drawn in the eyes it is [power_symbol-shaped_pupils](#power_symbol-shaped_pupils).

entries.name: mars_symbol
entries.description: The circle-and-arrow glyph appearing somewhere in the picture. It stands for the [planet](#planet), for alchemical iron and for the male [sex](#sex), and in artwork it usually flags a [crossdressing](#crossdressing) boy or a male-male pairing.

entries.name: flower_symbol
entries.description: A blossom rendered as a flat [sign](#sign) or motif rather than a real [plant](#plant), [floating](#floating) near a character or stamped onto a surface. It behaves the way a drawn [heart](#heart) or star does.

entries.name: beamed_sixteenth_notes
entries.description: Sixteenth [notes](#notes) tied together by a double beam across their stems. Used decoratively, or to show that a character is [singing](#singing), [whistling](#whistling) or [playing](#playing).

entries.name: crest
entries.description: An intricate heraldic [emblem](#emblem) [standing](#standing) for a noble [house](#house), [family](#family) or order, drawn on a wall, a [banner](#banner), a uniform or [floating](#floating) on its own. Simpler marks are an emblem or a [logo](#logo).

entries.name: school_emblem
entries.description: A school's [crest](#crest), [logo](#logo) or [coat](#coat) of arms, usually embroidered or printed on the uniform's [blazer](#blazer), [collar](#collar) or [bag](#bag). Tag when the [emblem](#emblem) is visible.

entries.name: battery_indicator
entries.description: The little battery-shaped charge icon from phones and gadgets, drawn into the picture as a graphic. It often floats beside a character to show they are [running](#running) out of [energy](#energy), or sits on a [robot](#robot) as a readout.

entries.name: broken_halo
entries.description: The [ring](#ring) [floating](#floating) above a character's head has a gap in it, or is cracked and [split](#split) apart. It usually marks a fallen or [damaged](#damaged) [angel](#angel); add [halo](#halo).

entries.name: hammer_and_sickle
entries.description: The crossed tool [emblem](#emblem) of [communism](#communism), a [hammer](#hammer) laid over a curved [sickle](#sickle) to stand for workers and peasants together. Its appearance on a [flag](#flag), [badge](#badge) or [banner](#banner) marks the picture as politically communist in theme.

entries.name: peace_symbol
entries.description: The circular mark enclosing a vertical line with two lines [dropping](#dropping) away from it, first a nuclear disarmament [badge](#badge) and later a general [emblem](#emblem) of peace. The two-finger hand [sign](#sign) is [v](#v).

entries.name: venus_symbol
entries.description: The circle-and-cross [sign](#sign) stands for the female [sex](#sex), the [planet](#planet) Venus, copper in [alchemy](#alchemy) or feminism as a movement, and is often paired in the same picture with the corresponding mars symbol.

entries.name: club_(shape)
entries.description: The clubs [suit](#suit) mark from a deck of cards, a three-lobed [clover](#clover) [silhouette](#silhouette) on a short stem. Used as a motif on clothing and props in [card](#card) and [casino](#casino) designs, beside [heart](#heart), [spade_(shape)](#spade_(shape)) and [diamond_(shape)](#diamond_(shape)).

entries.name: sakuramon
entries.description: A stylised five-petal [cherry](#cherry) blossom [emblem](#emblem) with notched petal tips, used on Japanese naval and Self-Defense Force badges. Appears on naval-themed characters in several franchises, and is sometimes mistaken for a [chrysanthemum](#chrysanthemum) [crest](#crest).

entries.name: spiked_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) ringed with [spikes](#spikes) or points, occasionally resembling a [compass](#compass) [rose](#rose). A variant on the [plain](#plain) halo hovering over a character's head.

entries.name: cross_halo
entries.description: A [halo](#halo) built around a [cross](#cross) shape or containing one, hovering above the head or [standing](#standing) upright behind it. Turns up on angels and on figures styled after saints.

entries.name: simple_bird
entries.description: Birds reduced to a stylized curved V or a similarly minimal shape, usually distant in a [sky](#sky). This shorthand does not warrant the [bird](#bird) [tag](#tag) itself.

entries.name: low_battery_(symbol)
entries.description: The nearly drained [battery](#battery) icon from a [phone](#phone) or gadget, drawn into the picture as a graphic. It is often floated over a character as a joke about exhaustion.

entries.name: yin_yang_orb
entries.description: A [ball](#ball) bearing the yin yang design, best known as Hakurei Reimu's [floating](#floating) weapons in Touhou but not limited to that series. Tag [orb](#orb) and [yin_yang](#yin_yang) alongside.

entries.name: androgyne_symbol
entries.description: The glyph that joins the Mars and Venus signs into one, used for [androgynous](#androgynous), intersex or non-binary characters. It may point in any direction, is often swapped with the male-female [sign](#sign), and is not the transgender symbol.

entries.name: eye_of_horus
entries.description: The stylized ancient Egyptian eye, drawn with its long [tail](#tail) and curl beneath. It appears as a [tattoo](#tattoo) or as part of an Egyptian motif, and is a symbol rather than a real eye.

entries.name: gem_(symbol)
entries.description: The cut-diamond [emoji](#emoji) used as a flat symbol, typically drawn white against blue on idol-style cards. The playing-card [suit](#suit) shape is [diamond_(shape)](#diamond_(shape)).

entries.name: family_crest
entries.description: A Japanese clan [emblem](#emblem), or mon, such as the Tokugawa hollyhock or the imperial [chrysanthemum](#chrysanthemum), shown on clothing, banners or walls.

entries.name: brown_halo
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) or disc [floating](#floating) above the head, rendered in brown. Its colour usually keys to the character's palette rather than meaning anything holy.

entries.name: star_of_david
entries.description: The six-pointed star made of two overlapping triangles, a symbol of Judaism and also used in mysticism. A form of [hexagram](#hexagram).

entries.name: jolly_roger
entries.description: A [skull](#skull) over crossed bones or crossed swords, the pirates' [device](#device), flown on a [flag](#flag) or printed on [cloth](#cloth). It serves equally as a general [sign](#sign) of danger or [poison](#poison).

entries.name: infinity_symbol
entries.description: The [sideways](#sideways) [figure](#figure) eight that stands for endlessness. It shows up as a motif, an [emblem](#emblem), a pupil shape or a piece of decoration.

entries.name: roundel
entries.description: A circular [insignia](#insignia) of concentric coloured rings, chiefly the national [markings](#markings) on [military](#military) [aircraft](#aircraft), or a similar [circle](#circle) in [heraldry](#heraldry). Tag the nation where it is recognisable.

entries.name: radiation_symbol
entries.description: The three-bladed [trefoil](#trefoil) warning [sign](#sign) for radioactivity, shown on a [container](#container), a posted sign, or printed on clothing. In fan art it frequently marks a particular nuclear-powered character rather than a real hazard.

entries.name: zodiac
entries.description: The twelve Western astrological signs [running](#running) from Aries to Pisces, appearing as symbols, constellations or themed characters. Refers only to the Western system: the Chinese [animal](#animal) cycle carries its own [tag](#tag), and each individual [sign](#sign) has a name of its own.

entries.name: bass_clef
entries.description: The F clef of musical notation, a comma-like curl with two [dots](#dots), used as a decorative mark, printed on clothing or [floating](#floating) as a [music](#music) motif. Its counterpart for the higher range is the [treble_clef](#treble_clef).

entries.name: swastika
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) whose four arms bend at right angles. The left-facing form is a long-standing Buddhist auspicious mark used in Japan on maps and at temples, while the right-facing one tilted on a red and white [field](#field) is the Nazi [emblem](#emblem); Finnish and Latvian air forces also flew versions of it.

entries.name: dollar_sign
entries.description: The crossed-S currency mark, written as text, printed on a [money](#money) [sack](#sack), or [standing](#standing) in for a character's pupils in a greed [gag](#gag).

entries.name: fleur-de-lis
entries.description: The stylised three-petalled lily of French [heraldry](#heraldry), stamped on banners, armour, [tiles](#tiles) and [cloth](#cloth). It appears as ornament far more often than as a real [plant](#plant).

entries.name: sixteenth_note
entries.description: The musical symbol worth a sixteenth of a whole [note](#note), drawn as a filled oval note head on a stem with two flags. Used decoratively around [singing](#singing) characters as often as on an actual musical [staff](#staff).

entries.name: blood_halo
entries.description: A [ring](#ring) hovering over the head formed out of [blood](#blood) rather than light. It keeps the [outline](#outline) of an angel's [halo](#halo) while [reading](#reading) as grisly instead of holy.

entries.name: pleading_face_emoji
entries.description: The pleading [emoji](#emoji) with its huge glassy eyes and small downturned mouth, drawn into the picture or laid over a character's face. Used for a needy, imploring look, most often as a joke.

entries.name: greek_cross
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) whose four arms are of equal length and meet at right angles, [giving](#giving) a plus shape. Used on flags, medical marks and [heraldry](#heraldry).

entries.name: crosshair
entries.description: The [aiming](#aiming) reticle of a [scope](#scope) or a sight drawn over the image, usually intersecting lines with a dot, tick marks or a [ring](#ring). It puts the viewer behind the [weapon](#weapon).

entries.name: double_halo
entries.description: Two rings float above or around the head where a single one would usually sit. Turns up on angels and on designs that treat the [halo](#halo) as stylised hardware.

entries.name: eye_symbol
entries.description: A stylized eye used as a [sign](#sign) or [emblem](#emblem), on a [banner](#banner), a wall, a [magic](#magic) [circle](#circle), or [hanging](#hanging) in the air. It stands for [watching](#watching), or for whoever is doing the watching.

entries.name: half_note
entries.description: The musical symbol with a hollow oval head and a [plain](#plain) stem, worth two beats in common time. Drawn [floating](#floating) in the air as a [sign](#sign) of [music](#music) as often as [sitting](#sitting) on a [staff](#staff).

entries.name: no_symbol
entries.description: The circle-and-slash prohibition mark, laid over an object, a word or a character to say that it is not allowed.

entries.name: male-female_symbol
entries.description: The glyph that fuses Mars and Venus: one [circle](#circle) [carrying](#carrying) both a [cross](#cross) below and an arrow at the upper right. Used as shorthand for [futanari](#futanari), intersex and genderswapped characters, and easily [confused](#confused) with the androgyne [sign](#sign).

entries.name: crying_emoji
entries.description: The loudly [crying](#crying) [emoji](#emoji) drawn into the picture: a round yellow face with [tears](#tears) bursting from screwed-shut eyes. Used for grief and for being overcome with delight in equal measure.

entries.name: star_of_life
entries.description: The six-pointed emergency medical [emblem](#emblem), usually blue with a white [outline](#outline) and a snake-twined rod at the centre. Painted on ambulances and hospitals and worn by paramedics; not to be [confused](#confused) with a red [cross](#cross).

entries.name: shoshinsha_mark
entries.description: The yellow-and-green arrowhead [badge](#badge) Japanese drivers must [display](#display) on their [car](#car) for their first year on the [road](#road). Appears on vehicles, and as a joke decoration on clothing or props to mark someone as a novice.

entries.name: distorted_halo
entries.description: The [ring](#ring) above the head warps, flickers or thins out instead of [holding](#holding) a clean shape, [standing](#standing) in for overwhelming sensation or a mind [slipping](#slipping) away. A [halo](#halo) drawn as [broken](#broken) pixels is its own separate design.

entries.name: sharp_sign
entries.description: The musical ♯ mark that raises a [note](#note) by a semitone, drawn with its two slanted uprights. Used as decoration or a [sound](#sound) cue, distinct from the similar-looking [hashtag](#hashtag).

entries.name: recycling_symbol
entries.description: Three bent arrows [chasing](#chasing) each other around a rounded [triangle](#triangle), [standing](#standing) for reduce, reuse, and recycle. Printed on bins, packaging, and clothing as a graphic.

entries.name: cut-here_line
entries.description: A dashed line marked with a small pair of [scissors](#scissors), showing where something is meant to be cut through. Appears as a [tattoo](#tattoo) joke and as a hint at a beheading.

entries.name: coat_of_arms
entries.description: A heraldic [emblem](#emblem) built around a charged [shield](#shield), often with [crest](#crest) and supporters, [standing](#standing) for a [family](#family), an order, a country or a [military](#military) unit. It appears on banners, shields, uniforms and [paperwork](#paperwork).

entries.name: eye_of_providence
entries.description: An eye set inside a [triangle](#triangle), usually [throwing](#throwing) out rays. It comes from older Christian art as the [watching](#watching) eye of God and is best known now from banknotes and conspiracy imagery.

entries.name: ouroboros
entries.description: The [old](#old) [emblem](#emblem) of a serpent or [dragon](#dragon) curled round to swallow its own [tail](#tail), [standing](#standing) for cycles and endless return. Drawn as a [sigil](#sigil), a motif in a [magic](#magic) [circle](#circle) or a piece of jewellery.

entries.name: no_smoking
entries.description: The [familiar](#familiar) [sign](#sign) of a lit [cigarette](#cigarette) inside a crossed red [circle](#circle), forbidding [smoking](#smoking). It is usually posted on a wall or a [window](#window) somewhere in the scene.

entries.name: play_button
entries.description: The right-pointing [triangle](#triangle) that starts [video](#video) playback, laid over a picture or shown on a [device](#device). A mock video screenshot wants a different, more specific [tag](#tag).

entries.name: japanese_postal_mark
entries.description: The mark that stands for post offices and postal addresses in Japan, drawn on signs, stamps or as decoration. Playful redesigns of it count as [well](#well).

entries.name: toilet_symbol
entries.description: The pictogram pair that marks lavatories, a [plain](#plain) [figure](#figure) in a [skirt](#skirt) beside one in trousers, printed on a [door](#door), a [sign](#sign) or a wall.

entries.name: biohazard_symbol
entries.description: The three-lobed warning mark for dangerous biological material, usually black on orange. Painted on containers, doors and hazard suits to signal contamination.

entries.name: bagua
entries.description: The eight three-line trigrams of Taoist cosmology, arranged as a [ring](#ring) around a central [emblem](#emblem). They appear on talismans, mirrors, robes and conjured circles.

entries.name: atom
entries.description: The schoolroom [diagram](#diagram) of an atom, a clustered nucleus with electrons looping around it on ringed orbits. That recognisable ringed shape is required; a shapeless [ball](#ball) of [energy](#energy) held in someone's hand does not qualify.

entries.name: crossed_out
entries.description: A [scribble](#scribble), an X or a prohibition [sign](#sign) laid over part of the picture, striking through a face, an object or a line of text. It marks something as deleted or refused rather than showing anything in the scene.

entries.name: flat_sign
entries.description: The ♭ of musical notation, which drops the [note](#note) it stands before by a semitone. It appears on sheet [music](#music) and as decoration; a [plain](#plain) lowercase b is not one.

entries.name: @_(symbol)
entries.description: An actual at [sign](#sign) is drawn in the picture. Swirled eyes, [spiral](#spiral) patterns, fingerprints and the sign inside a social media [handle](#handle) are all outside it.

entries.name: interlocked_mars_and_venus_symbols
entries.description: The male and female glyphs drawn joined together, either linked at their rings or with the Mars arrow driven through the Venus [circle](#circle). The first arrangement suggests romance between a man and a woman, the second says [sex](#sex).

entries.name: wi-fi_symbol
entries.description: The fan of curved arcs rising from a dot that stands for a [wireless](#wireless) signal. It shows up on [phone](#phone) screens, routers, and signage, or floats above a character's head as a visual joke.

entries.name: inverted_pentagram
entries.description: A five-pointed star with a single point aimed downward, read as a satanic [sign](#sign) and sometimes filled with a goat's head. It turns up on floors, charms and clothing in occult scenes.

entries.name: balkenkreuz
entries.description: A straight-armed black [cross](#cross) outlined in white, painted on German tanks and [aircraft](#aircraft) during the Second World War. Games often substitute it where a [swastika](#swastika) would be [censored](#censored); the flare-armed Iron Cross is a different [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: jupiter_symbol
entries.description: The glyph [standing](#standing) for the [planet](#planet) Jupiter, which doubles as the alchemical mark for tin. It turns up on charms, [magic](#magic) circles and [costume](#costume) trim.

entries.name: cancer_(symbol)
entries.description: The ♋ glyph [standing](#standing) for the [sign](#sign) Cancer, two curls turned away from one another. Use it where only the mark appears; [crab](#crab) imagery or the star pattern take their own tags.

entries.name: gemini_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph of the Twins, two upright [bars](#bars) joined by a curve at top and bottom. Use it when the mark alone appears; wider twin imagery goes with the [zodiac](#zodiac) [tag](#tag).

entries.name: scorpio_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph for the [zodiac](#zodiac) [sign](#sign) Scorpio, an m-shape whose last stroke ends in a barbed [tail](#tail). Use it for the sign alone, without [scorpion](#scorpion) imagery in the picture.

entries.name: aquarius_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph of the [sign](#sign) Aquarius, two stacked zigzag lines [standing](#standing) for [water](#water). It marks the sign on [cloth](#cloth), in a [magic](#magic) [circle](#circle) or across a background; add [aquarius_(zodiac)](#aquarius_(zodiac)) only where the picture carries the sign's wider imagery too.

entries.name: good_fortune_symbol
entries.description: The Chinese character for luck and blessing, used as decoration on red [paper](#paper) squares, doorways, daruma dolls and [beckoning](#beckoning) cats. A fixture of lunar new year scenes; turned upside down it is [dao](#dao) fu.

entries.name: leo_(symbol)
entries.description: The looping glyph [standing](#standing) for the star [sign](#sign) Leo, used as a decorative mark, [badge](#badge) or [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: single_letter
entries.description: One character of the [alphabet](#alphabet) shown on its own, on clothing, a [sign](#sign) or the background. Stands as a monogram or [emblem](#emblem) rather than as part of a word.

entries.name: pisces_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph for the [sign](#sign) of the Fishes, two curved arcs facing apart and joined by a crossbar. Reserve it for the symbol alone; broader themed imagery of the sign belongs to [pisces_(zodiac)](#pisces_(zodiac)) instead.

entries.name: crown_(symbol)
entries.description: A small [crown](#crown) used as a [sign](#sign) rather than worn: [floating](#floating) beside a character, printed on [cloth](#cloth), or marking the top score on a game [display](#display). Nobody has it on their head.

entries.name: quarter_rest
entries.description: The musical notation mark for one beat of silence, drawn as a small zigzag [squiggle](#squiggle). Appears on sheet [music](#music) or floats free as decoration in music-themed art.

entries.name: omega_symbol
entries.description: The Greek [letter](#letter) omega, the last of that [alphabet](#alphabet), drawn as a mark on clothing, [machinery](#machinery) or a magical [sign](#sign). Often used to [label](#label) a final or ultimate thing.

entries.name: virgo_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph for the [sign](#sign) Virgo, an M-shape closed off with a loop. Appears as decoration, on charms and within astrological layouts.

entries.name: libra_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph for the star [sign](#sign) Libra, a horizontal bar with a small arc [riding](#riding) above it, used as decoration or an [emblem](#emblem).

entries.name: taurus_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph for the [bull](#bull) [sign](#sign) of the [zodiac](#zodiac), a [circle](#circle) topped by a pair of curved [horns](#horns). It turns up on charts, jewellery and [costume](#costume) trim with [no](#no) zodiac theme necessarily behind it.

entries.name: capricorn_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph for the [sign](#sign) Capricorn, a looping mark that runs a goat's horn into a fish's [tail](#tail). Where the sea [goat](#goat) itself is drawn, the [zodiac](#zodiac) [tag](#tag) takes over.

entries.name: aries_(symbol)
entries.description: The sign's glyph, a curled pair of ram's [horns](#horns), drawn as a mark on [cloth](#cloth), skin or [backdrop](#backdrop). Add [aries_(zodiac)](#aries_(zodiac)) only where the picture also carries the sign's wider imagery.

entries.name: loading_icon
entries.description: The [spinning](#spinning) [wheel](#wheel), [ring](#ring) of [dots](#dots) or turning [hourglass](#hourglass) a [computer](#computer) shows while it is busy, drawn into the picture as a graphic. It is often floated over a character as a joke about slow [thinking](#thinking).

entries.name: sagittarius_(symbol)
entries.description: The glyph that stands for the [zodiac](#zodiac) [sign](#sign) Sagittarius, an arrow crossing a short bar. It marks the sign alone, without a [centaur](#centaur) archer or a star [map](#map) present.

entries.name: mercury_symbol
entries.description: The glyph for the [planet](#planet) Mercury, also used alchemically for quicksilver: a [circle](#circle) topped with [horns](#horns) and crossed underneath. Appears in [magic](#magic) circles, occult charts and decorative flourishes.

entries.name: eighth_rest
entries.description: The written symbol for a silence as long as an eighth [note](#note), a slanting stroke with a small hooked [flag](#flag) on its left. Turns up in written [music](#music) and as loose decoration.

entries.name: zodiac_wheel
entries.description: Zodiac symbols arranged in a [ring](#ring), whether the twelve Western signs or the Chinese [animal](#animal) cycle. Drawn as a [chart](#chart), a decorative [border](#border), or part of a [magic](#magic) [diagram](#diagram).

entries.name: onsen_symbol
entries.description: The [hot](#hot) spring mark, three curls of [steam](#steam) rising off a shallow dish, used on Japanese maps and hung outside bathhouses.

entries.name: thinking_emoji
entries.description: The yellow face with a cocked brow and a hand at the chin, drawn into the picture as a reaction mark. Its crudely [redrawn](#redrawn) variant circulates widely as an [internet](#internet) in-joke.

entries.name: skull_and_crossed_swords
entries.description: A [skull](#skull) set above two crossed blades, a variant of the [pirate](#pirate) [emblem](#emblem) that swaps swords for the usual bones. Appears on flags, banners and clothing prints.

entries.name: henohenomoheji
entries.description: A doodled face made from seven hiragana: two for the brows, two for the eyes, one for the [nose](#nose), one for the mouth, and a last one drawn round the lot. Scarecrows wear it, and it serves as a blank stand-in face.

entries.name: star_of_lakshmi
entries.description: An eight-pointed star formed by two squares overlaid at forty-five degrees. In Hindu tradition it stands for the eight forms of wealth of the goddess Lakshmi.

entries.name: star_and_crescent
entries.description: The [emblem](#emblem) pairing a [crescent](#crescent) [moon](#moon) with a star, long associated with the Ottoman Empire and with Islam, and carried on several national flags. Drawn on banners, jewellery and decorated [fabric](#fabric).

entries.name: rabbit_symbol
entries.description: A stylized [rabbit](#rabbit) shape used as a graphic mark rather than a live [animal](#animal), showing up on badges, logos, hair ornaments, and clothing prints. Often reduced to a [silhouette](#silhouette) or just a pair of long ears.

entries.name: saturn_symbol
entries.description: The crossed [sickle](#sickle) glyph that stands for the [planet](#planet) Saturn in astronomy and astrology, and for lead in alchemical [writing](#writing).

entries.name: checkmark
entries.description: A tick drawn onto the picture, [standing](#standing) for approval, a completed item or a right answer. It appears on lists and forms and also floats free beside a character.

entries.name: aquila_(symbol)
entries.description: An [eagle](#eagle) rendered as an [emblem](#emblem), [wings](#wings) spread and stylised, as it appears on standards, badges, crests and banners. It marks the [device](#device) rather than a living [bird](#bird).

entries.name: pause_button
entries.description: The two upright [bars](#bars) of the pause symbol, drawn either as a control on a player interface or [floating](#floating) over the picture as a graphic.

entries.name: neptune_symbol
entries.description: The [trident](#trident) glyph [standing](#standing) for the [planet](#planet) Neptune, used decoratively and in astrological designs. Unlike most planetary signs it carries [no](#no) alchemical meaning.

entries.name: dotted_quarter_note
entries.description: A quarter [note](#note) with a dot beside its head, which lengthens it by half again. Drawn in written [music](#music) or [floating](#floating) loose as decoration; a dot above or below the note means staccato instead.

entries.name: heraldry
entries.description: Armorial devices — a charged [shield](#shield) with [crest](#crest) and supporters — [standing](#standing) for a noble [house](#house) or an order. They appear on banners, shields and surcoats.

entries.name: cross_patty
entries.description: A [cross](#cross) whose arms pinch narrow where they meet and [flare](#flare) out toward the tips. The German iron cross is the best-known [emblem](#emblem) drawn on this shape.

entries.name: simple_fish
entries.description: A [fish](#fish) reduced to its basic [outline](#outline), often just a [silhouette](#silhouette) or a cartoon shape with a triangular [tail](#tail). Used for decoration, signs and background motifs rather than an identifiable species.

entries.name: uranus_symbol
entries.description: The astrological glyph for the [planet](#planet) Uranus, drawn as a [circle](#circle) topped by a cross-and-arrow or an H-like shape. It also serves as the alchemical mark for platinum.

entries.name: compass_rose
entries.description: The starburst [figure](#figure) printed on a [map](#map) to show which way the cardinal directions run. It also appears decoratively on charts, sails and nautical props.

entries.name: whole_note
entries.description: The musical symbol for the longest ordinary [note](#note) value: a hollow oval with [no](#no) stem attached. It floats over a scene as a [sound](#sound) cue or sits printed on a [staff](#staff).

entries.name: scorpio_(zodiac)
entries.description: Pictures themed on the eighth [zodiac](#zodiac) [sign](#sign), the [scorpion](#scorpion) set between Libra and Sagittarius. An incidental glyph or star [chart](#chart) belongs to the symbol or [constellation](#constellation) [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: pisces_(zodiac)
entries.description: A picture built around the imagery of the [zodiac](#zodiac) [sign](#sign) of the Fishes, usually a pair of [fish](#fish) [swimming](#swimming) apart or other motifs tied to its name. An incidental glyph or star [chart](#chart) alone should take [pisces_(symbol)](#pisces_(symbol)) or [pisces_(constellation)](#pisces_(constellation)) instead.

entries.name: sagittarius_(zodiac)
entries.description: Imagery built on the ninth [sign](#sign) of the [zodiac](#zodiac), the bow-drawing [centaur](#centaur) that sits between Scorpio and Capricorn. Keep it for pictures genuinely themed on the sign; a stray glyph or star [chart](#chart) takes the symbol or [constellation](#constellation) [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: taurus_(zodiac)
entries.description: A picture built around the imagery of the [bull](#bull) [sign](#sign), with [horns](#horns), bovine details and spring motifs, often staged on a character [standing](#standing) in for the sign. When only the glyph or the star pattern appears incidentally, prefer [taurus_(symbol)](#taurus_(symbol)) or [taurus_(constellation)](#taurus_(constellation)) instead.

entries.name: virgo_(zodiac)
entries.description: Imagery built around the sixth [zodiac](#zodiac) [sign](#sign), the maiden, usually a young woman with [wheat](#wheat), a [veil](#veil) or the sign's name. A glyph or star pattern that merely happens to be present does not qualify.

entries.name: caduceus
entries.description: A winged [staff](#staff) with two snakes twining up it, carried by the Greek messenger god. It is routinely mistaken for the single-snake rod that actually stands for [medicine](#medicine).

entries.name: natural_sign
entries.description: The natural mark from musical notation, which cancels an earlier sharp or flat and restores the [plain](#plain) pitch. It appears as decoration or as shorthand for [music](#music).

entries.name: chromatic_aberration
entries.description: The red, green and blue channels are offset from one another, leaving coloured fringes along edges. Drawn work has none naturally, so it is added deliberately for realism, a sense of motion, chaos or mental strain; [heavy](#heavy) use resembles anaglyph.

entries.name: film_grain
entries.description: A fine sandy speckle lies over the picture, [imitating](#imitating) the texture of photographic film. Added on purpose for a cinematic or retro feel.

entries.name: halftone
entries.description: Tones rendered as a pattern of [dots](#dots) that vary in size or spacing, as in print reproduction or manga [screentones](#screentones). Present either as an artistic [choice](#choice) or as a by-product of printing and scanning.

entries.name: halftone_background
entries.description: The background is made entirely or mostly of a [halftone](#halftone) dot pattern.

entries.name: glitch
entries.description: Deliberate digital or analogue [distortion](#distortion) used as a style: blocky displacement, [torn](#torn) lines, images bent out of register. Unintended damage is [jpeg_artifacts](#jpeg_artifacts) or [scan_artifacts](#scan_artifacts), and squares alone may be a digital dissolve.

entries.name: screentones
entries.description: Dot or line patterns used to [shade](#shade) and texture a drawing, the manga alternative to [hatching](#hatching). Originally transferred from printed adhesive sheets and now usually simulated digitally, tagged when the dotted texture is visible.

entries.name: vignetting
entries.description: The picture darkens or desaturates toward its edges compared with the centre, the photographic vignette effect. A crisp circular edge is [round_border](#round_border) instead.

entries.name: dithering
entries.description: Shading and colour blends faked with patterns of differently coloured pixels drawn from a small palette, as in [old](#old) graphics formats. Reads as a deliberate retro or pixel-art texture.

entries.name: pixelated
entries.description: Part of an otherwise normal picture is rendered as chunky blocks, often to signal something digital, virtual, or seen through a low-resolution [screen](#screen) inside the scene. Pixel blur used to hide genitals is [mosaic_censoring](#mosaic_censoring), not this.

entries.name: ben-day_dots
entries.description: Shading built from a regular [field](#field) of [dots](#dots), all the same size, shape and spacing. Borrowed from [old](#old) [comic](#comic) printing and used for retro or pop-art texture.

entries.name: distortion
entries.description: The picture is deliberately warped, smeared or [torn](#torn) up for effect, whether by editing or drawn that way from the start. Roughness left by an [unfinished](#unfinished) [sketch](#sketch) is something else.

entries.name: double_exposure
entries.description: Two images laid over one another so that one appears inside the [silhouette](#silhouette) or contours of the other. Where the filling image is a flat repeating pattern, [unmoving_pattern](#unmoving_pattern) is the [tag](#tag).

entries.name: static
entries.description: The speckled noise a [screen](#screen) shows when there is [no](#no) signal, black and white or coloured. Drawn on televisions and monitors, or laid over the whole picture as a [glitch](#glitch) effect.

entries.name: paper_texture
entries.description: The grain, [tooth](#tooth) or fibre of [paper](#paper) lies over the whole image, whether the work was made traditionally or the texture was laid on afterwards. It describes the surface, not the medium.

entries.name: scanlines
entries.description: Fine horizontal bands laid over the picture in imitation of an [old](#old) cathode-ray [screen](#screen). Gives a shot the look of a [television](#television) or [arcade](#arcade) [cabinet](#cabinet) rather than a print.

entries.name: overexposure
entries.description: The brightest parts of the image burn out to flat white instead of keeping a pale tint of their own colour. Reads as fierce [sunlight](#sunlight) or as a photograph shot far too bright.

entries.name: vhs_artifacts
entries.description: Tracking lines, smeared colour and [tape](#tape) noise of the sort an [old](#old) [videocassette](#videocassette) transfer leaves behind. Applies both to genuine captures from tape and to artwork that deliberately fakes the look.

entries.name: face_filter
entries.description: Whiskers, ears or similar [markings](#markings) drawn onto a face the way a [phone](#phone) app's [selfie](#selfie) filter would lay them there, as if the picture were a snapshot. The markings sit on top of the face rather than being part of it.

entries.name: canvas_texture
entries.description: The woven grain of painter's canvas showing through the whole finished image. Used to make a picture read as [paint](#paint) on [cloth](#cloth) rather than as a digital [file](#file).

entries.name: semi-transparent
entries.description: Part of the picture is drawn partly see-through, letting whatever lies behind it show faintly. A blunt [label](#label): prefer [see-through_clothes](#see-through_clothes) for garments, [fading](#fading) for a vanishing [figure](#figure), and [projected_inset](#projected_inset) for a background projection.

entries.name: blur_layer
entries.description: The [lineart](#lineart) is duplicated, blurred and laid [back](#back) over the drawing, leaving a soft [halo](#halo) along every edge. It is a finishing pass over the whole picture, unlike focus blur which depends on distance.

entries.name: speech_bubble
entries.description: A [bubble](#bubble) with a pointed [tail](#tail) aimed at a character, showing what they say. It may hold text or an image; an empty one is [blank_speech_bubble](#blank_speech_bubble), and a [cloud](#cloud) of unspoken thoughts is [thought_bubble](#thought_bubble) instead.

entries.name: spoken_heart
entries.description: A [heart](#heart) symbol used within dialogue, either [standing](#standing) alone or acting as a sort of punctuation, or drawn inside a speech [bubble](#bubble). Distinct from [heart_in_mouth](#heart_in_mouth), where an open mouth itself forms the heart shape.

entries.name: spoken_ellipsis
entries.description: A speech [bubble](#bubble) containing only "[...](#...)", showing a character left speechless or hesitating. The bare mark drawn outside any bubble is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: thought_bubble
entries.description: A cloud-shaped [balloon](#balloon) trailing small circles that shows what a character is [thinking](#thinking) or [dreaming](#dreaming), often paired with [imagining](#imagining). Spoken words instead use [speech_bubble](#speech_bubble).

entries.name: spoken_question_mark
entries.description: A question mark spoken on its own, typically alone in a [bubble](#bubble), expressing confusion rather than merely ending an ordinary question.

entries.name: spoken_...
entries.description: A speech or thought [bubble](#bubble) [holding](#holding) nothing but an ellipsis, showing a character who has fallen silent or has nothing to say. A [staple](#staple) of [deadpan](#deadpan) [comic](#comic) reactions.

entries.name: spoken_exclamation_mark
entries.description: An exclamation mark presented as something spoken, usually alone inside a [bubble](#bubble), marking a shout or a sudden jolt of surprise.

entries.name: spoken_musical_note
entries.description: A musical [note](#note) shown inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) or trailing from an open mouth on a short line, expressing [humming](#humming), [singing](#singing) or an upbeat mood.

entries.name: spoken_blush
entries.description: Blush marks, often rendered as diagonal slashes, placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) with or without accompanying words. Shows the [speaker](#speaker) is [flustered](#flustered) as they talk.

entries.name: imagining
entries.description: What a character is picturing is drawn for the viewer, inside a thought [balloon](#balloon) or as a separate scene beside them. Where the character is asleep, [dreaming](#dreaming) is the [tag](#tag) instead.

entries.name: spoken_squiggle
entries.description: A [squiggle](#squiggle), the round [scribble](#scribble) of annoyance or exasperation, placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) rather than beside the head.

entries.name: spoken_interrobang
entries.description: A [?](#?)! or [!?](#!?) combination placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), marking a startled question. The same mark drawn outside a bubble is its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: spoken_anger_vein
entries.description: An anger-vein mark placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) to show the [speaker](#speaker) is irritated, rather than drawn directly on their head.

entries.name: profanity
entries.description: Offensive language is written somewhere in the image, in any language, from crude swear words to racial, sexist or homophobic slurs. Applies to speech bubbles, signs and [clothes](#clothes) [writing](#writing) alike; combine with the relevant language text [tag](#tag).

entries.name: spoken_character
entries.description: A character's face or whole [figure](#figure) appears inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), showing who is being discussed or [giving](#giving) an off-screen reaction. A [letter](#letter) or digit shown the same way is [spoken_letter](#spoken_letter) or [spoken_number](#spoken_number) instead.

entries.name: spoken_sweatdrop
entries.description: A [sweatdrop](#sweatdrop) shown inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), or beading along the text itself, showing nervousness or embarrassment in what is being said.

entries.name: dialogue_box
entries.description: A message [window](#window) on a [screen](#screen), as in a game or a piece of software, often asking the viewer to confirm or choose. Visual-novel text boxes count as [well](#well).

entries.name: video_game_dialogue_box
entries.description: The framed [window](#window) games use to carry dialogue and [narration](#narration), laid over the picture. It often includes a speaker's name [plate](#plate) or a [blinking](#blinking) arrow to continue.

entries.name: text_box_(video_game)
entries.description: A dialogue [window](#window) drawn in the style of a [video](#video) game interface, complete with a [border](#border), a [portrait](#portrait) slot or a [blinking](#blinking) advance arrow. Its look usually mimics a particular game.

entries.name: adventure_text_box
entries.description: The dialogue [window](#window) of a visual novel or adventure game, laid across the lower part of the picture with a speaker's name and lines of text. It frames the whole scene as a game [screen](#screen).

entries.name: visual_novel_text_box
entries.description: The bordered dialogue panel of a visual novel drawn across the lower part of the image, often with a name [plate](#plate) at one [corner](#corner). It marks the picture as [imitating](#imitating) or taken from such a game.

entries.name: spoken_object
entries.description: A speech or thought [bubble](#bubble) holds a drawing of a specific object rather than words, a wordless way of showing what a character means or wants. Food shown this way has its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: blank_speech_bubble
entries.description: A speech or thought [balloon](#balloon) with [no](#no) words inside it. It is frequently left empty on purpose so that other [people](#people) [can](#can) fill in a line of their own.

entries.name: chat_log
entries.description: The picture is a mocked-up screenshot of a text conversation between characters, laid out like a messaging app. A character texting inside an ordinary drawn scene is [text_messaging](#text_messaging).

entries.name: colored_speech_bubble
entries.description: A speech or thought [balloon](#balloon) filled or outlined in colour instead of [plain](#plain) black and white. The tint often marks a mood or tells one [speaker](#speaker) from another.

entries.name: narration
entries.description: Text, or an implied voice, describing events or setting the scene from outside it. The narrator is seldom shown, though occasionally one appears in the frame.

entries.name: shared_speech_bubble
entries.description: A single speech [bubble](#bubble) with several tails, showing more than one character saying the same words together.

entries.name: spoken_food
entries.description: A drawing of [food](#food) inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), signalling that the character is [hungry](#hungry) or craving that particular dish.

entries.name: catchphrase
entries.description: A character's [signature](#signature) line, the phrase they are known for repeating, written into the picture. The words are part of who they are rather than ordinary dialogue.

entries.name: spoken_expression
entries.description: An [emoticon](#emoticon) such as [:3](#:3) or [^_^](#^_^) shown inside a speech [bubble](#bubble). When that emoticon also exists as its own [tag](#tag), both may be applied together.

entries.name: spoken_zzz
entries.description: The [sleeping](#sleeping) [sound](#sound) [zzz](#zzz) set inside a speech or thought [bubble](#bubble) instead of [floating](#floating) loose above the sleeper's head.

entries.name: spoken_x
entries.description: The [letter](#letter) X shown inside a speech [bubble](#bubble): a blunt refusal, a mark crossing out something disliked, or a silent [no](#no) in a wordless strip.

entries.name: source_quote
entries.description: Text or dialogue in a picture lifted word-for-word from the work it references, such as a character's famous line. Song [lyrics](#lyrics) are excluded and carry their own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: source_quote_parody
entries.description: A recognizable line from a work reused with the wording altered so a joke lands against the original. That alteration is what separates it from a straight [source_quote](#source_quote).

entries.name: caption
entries.description: Written text set outside the artwork or along its edge, remarking on what is shown rather than being spoken by anyone in it. Narration boxes and added commentary both count.

entries.name: spoken_flying_sweatdrops
entries.description: The small [flying](#flying) [sweat](#sweat) marks placed inside a speech or thought [bubble](#bubble) rather than beside the head, turning a character's awkwardness into something they say.

entries.name: spoken_animal
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) drawn inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) in place of words, [standing](#standing) in for whatever the character is [talking](#talking) or [thinking](#thinking) about.

entries.name: spoken_star
entries.description: A star drawn inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), lending cheer or added emphasis to whatever is being said.

entries.name: dialogue_options
entries.description: A [list](#list) of possible replies laid out on [screen](#screen), the way a game offers a player a [choice](#choice) of lines. The [menu](#menu) itself is drawn into the picture.

entries.name: shared_thought_bubble
entries.description: One thought [balloon](#balloon) rises from two or more characters together, showing that they are all picturing the same thing.

entries.name: spoken_emoji
entries.description: An [emoji](#emoji) placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) in place of written dialogue, delivering the reaction without any words at all.

entries.name: spoken_skull
entries.description: A [skull](#skull), sometimes over crossed bones, drawn inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) to convey [disgust](#disgust), revulsion or a veiled [threat](#threat).

entries.name: ara_ara
entries.description: The Japanese interjection あらあら, roughly 'my, my', written or spoken in the picture. It belongs to [motherly](#motherly) or big-sister types and carries a [teasing](#teasing), knowing tone toward somebody younger.

entries.name: insult
entries.description: A character says something rude, [cutting](#cutting) or demeaning to somebody else, shown in the dialogue. Swearing often comes with it, but [plain](#plain) contempt is enough.

entries.name: spoken_light_bulb
entries.description: A light bulb drawn inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), the [familiar](#familiar) shorthand for a character suddenly [hitting](#hitting) on an [idea](#idea).

entries.name: spoken_symbol
entries.description: A non-alphanumeric mark other than ordinary punctuation appearing by itself inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), [standing](#standing) in for words the character would otherwise say.

entries.name: spoken_number
entries.description: A numeral placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), used for [counting](#counting) off, naming a [price](#price), or [giving](#giving) a short curt answer.

entries.name: dirty_talk
entries.description: Explicit talk during a sexual scene, set in bubbles or laid across the picture as loose text. What is said carries the [tag](#tag), not what is being done.

entries.name: image_in_thought_bubble
entries.description: A thought [balloon](#balloon) [holding](#holding) a drawn scene or object instead of words, showing what is in the character's head. Use it where the [bubble](#bubble) carries pictures rather than dialogue.

entries.name: spoken_sparkle
entries.description: One or more sparkles placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), marking an admiring or delighted remark.

entries.name: speech_stab
entries.description: A [comic](#comic) [gag](#gag) where a speech [bubble](#bubble) turns into a [weapon](#weapon), its pointed [tail](#tail) or a blade emerging from it [running](#running) another character through. Exaggerates just how [cutting](#cutting) a remark was.

entries.name: spoken_mars_symbol
entries.description: The Mars symbol appearing in a speech [bubble](#bubble) or as part of dialogue, [standing](#standing) for maleness or for a man under discussion.

entries.name: spoken_sound_effect
entries.description: An onomatopoeia not normally spoken aloud placed inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), its [tail](#tail) [pointing](#pointing) at whatever made the noise so the object itself seems to speak.

entries.name: spoken_flower
entries.description: A [flower](#flower) drawn inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), or [floating](#floating) alone but plainly coming from a character's mouth, usually marking a sweet or [lovestruck](#lovestruck) line.

entries.name: spoken_letter
entries.description: A single [alphabet](#alphabet) [letter](#letter) shown inside a speech [bubble](#bubble), [standing](#standing) in for a [sound](#sound) effect or a very brief reply.

entries.name: stutter
entries.description: Speech [broken](#broken) by repeated [opening](#opening) syllables, written into dialogue with hyphens. Marks a character as [nervous](#nervous), [flustered](#flustered) or frightened.

entries.name: spoken_venus_symbol
entries.description: The Venus symbol appearing inside a speech [bubble](#bubble) or as part of dialogue, [standing](#standing) for femaleness or for a woman under discussion.

entries.name: sound_effects
entries.description: Words or letters drawn into a picture to represent a noise, such as onomatopoeia placed beside the action producing it. Purely visual lettering; a [file](#file) that actually plays [sound](#sound) is tagged sound instead.

entries.name: heartbeat
entries.description: A heartbeat written into the picture as a [sound](#sound) effect, typically the Japanese doki-doki. The spiky line that graphs [heart](#heart) activity is [cardiogram](#cardiogram).

entries.name: gao
entries.description: The Japanese noise for a roar, lettered beside the character making it. Usually accompanies a [claw_pose](#claw_pose) or an [animal](#animal) impression.

entries.name: nyan
entries.description: A cat's cry written out in Japanese and shown in the picture as nya, nyaa, nyan or a longer drawn-out variant in kana. Usually goes together with paw-shaped hands and other feline mannerisms.

entries.name: kupaa
entries.description: A Japanese [sound](#sound) effect lettered into the picture for something being spread wide open, most often the labia. The [tag](#tag) records the drawn lettering, not the act of [spreading](#spreading) itself.

entries.name: stomach_growling
entries.description: A [belly](#belly) rumbling audibly from hunger or digestion, usually drawn with a written [sound](#sound) effect and a hand at the [midriff](#midriff). Japanese art spells the noise ぐう.

entries.name: a_(phrase)
entries.description: The single Japanese syllable written out as the [sound](#sound) of a small startled [gasp](#gasp). It stands alone as lettering, whether meant plainly or as a nod to the works that made it a [running](#running) joke.

entries.name: sound_effects_only
entries.description: A picture whose only lettering is onomatopoeia, with [no](#no) dialogue at all. Common in wordless [comic](#comic) [pages](#pages) that carry the action through noise alone.

entries.name: ko~n
entries.description: A written [fox](#fox) cry, lettered beside a fox or fox-eared character as the noise they are making. Spelled in hiragana it reads softer than the katakana normally used for [animal](#animal) sounds.

entries.name: zawa_(onomatopoeia)
entries.description: A Japanese [sound](#sound) word for an uneasy, murmuring atmosphere, printed across a scene rather than spoken by any one character to build tension. Common in suspenseful [gambling](#gambling) and psychological drama manga.

entries.name: character_name
entries.description: The name, surname or nickname of a character in the picture is written somewhere on it, in any language or spelling. For class-based games the class name, Knight or Mage, counts as the name.

entries.name: text_focus
entries.description: Writing is a central element of the image rather than incidental lettering. Add a language [tag](#tag), such as [english_text](#english_text) or japanese_text, and [speech_bubble](#speech_bubble) where it applies.

entries.name: happy_birthday
entries.description: The greeting "Happy Birthday" is written somewhere in the image, in any language. It may be lettered across the background, on a [cake](#cake) or on a [banner](#banner).

entries.name: sign
entries.description: A flat board or panel displaying information, from [shop](#shop) and [street](#street) signs to warnings and notices. Often carries text; add [signpost](#signpost) or a more specific [tag](#tag) for particular kinds.

entries.name: happy_new_year
entries.description: The greeting "Happy New Year" is written somewhere in the image, in any language. It is common on New Year illustrations alongside [kimono](#kimono), [kadomatsu](#kadomatsu) and the year's [zodiac](#zodiac) [animal](#animal).

entries.name: merry_christmas
entries.description: The greeting 'Merry Christmas' lettered somewhere in the picture, in any language. Usually paired with santa costumes, decorated trees and snowy scenes.

entries.name: barcode
entries.description: A machine-readable block of parallel lines, some thick and some thin, [standing](#standing) for whatever it is attached to. It shows up on packaging and labels or purely as decoration; inked on skin it becomes [barcode_tattoo](#barcode_tattoo).

entries.name: thank_you
entries.description: Words of gratitude appear in the picture, in any language, such as thanks or arigatou. Common on follower-milestone posts and commission deliveries.

entries.name: road_sign
entries.description: A [traffic](#traffic) or [road](#road) [sign](#sign) posted at the roadside, [giving](#giving) directions, warnings or rules. Tagged with sign; a [shop](#shop) sign or [billboard](#billboard) does not count.

entries.name: text_background
entries.description: Writing fills most of the [space](#space) behind a character, in any language, [working](#working) as the [backdrop](#backdrop) itself rather than incidental lettering. A small [signature](#signature) or date tucked in a [corner](#corner) does not qualify.

entries.name: happy_halloween
entries.description: The words "Happy Halloween" appear written in the picture, in English or in another [tongue](#tongue). Costumes and pumpkins alone are not enough without the lettering.

entries.name: song_name
entries.description: The [title](#title) of a song or other musical piece written somewhere in the picture. Applies regardless of language or lettering style, as long as the text names a specific composition.

entries.name: happy_valentine
