entries.name: circle_cut
entries.description: A small standardised advertisement a doujin group prepares for a [convention](#convention) catalogue, with a bordered white [box](#box) in the upper left, the group's name and its stall details. Looser [announcement](#announcement) pictures naming a stall number count as [well](#well).

entries.name: poster_(medium)
entries.description: The whole image is a poster, whether a [scan](#scan) or photo of a printed one or fan art designed as one. A poster [hanging](#hanging) inside a scene is [poster_(object)](#poster_(object)).

entries.name: sprite
entries.description: A flat game asset made to be placed into a two-dimensional scene, whether a movable character or a pickup item. Usually small, frequently pixel art, and sometimes [animated](#animated).

entries.name: production_art
entries.description: Behind-the-scenes material from making an official work: animation-paper drawings, [key](#key) frames, colour traces, animatics, cel scans, storyboards, reference and [height](#height) sheets, colour guides, or [notes](#notes). Nearly always official; usually combine with the more specific kind, such as [reference_sheet](#reference_sheet) or storyboard.

entries.name: key_visual
entries.description: Official promotional artwork put out by a [studio](#studio) before a series airs, laid out like a poster with the main [cast](#cast) and the [title](#title) given prominence. Art made while the work was still being designed is [concept_art](#concept_art) instead.

entries.name: making-of
entries.description: A post showing several stages of a drawing coming together, or a timelapse of the process. A single incomplete picture on its own is [unfinished](#unfinished) instead.

entries.name: novel_cover
entries.description: The front [cover](#cover) artwork of a novel, usually a light novel, [carrying](#carrying) its [title](#title) and lead characters. It says where the picture comes from.

entries.name: alpha_transparency
entries.description: The [file](#file) carries [semi-transparent](#semi-transparent) or fully clear areas that are not merely a flat background, as a PNG [can](#can). It describes the file itself rather than anything drawn in it.

entries.name: fake_cover
entries.description: A picture built to pass as the [cover](#cover) of a real publication: a magazine, a manga volume, an album, a game [box](#box) or a film poster. Add [parody](#parody) and the imitated work's [tag](#tag) when the [target](#target) is specific.

entries.name: ad
entries.description: Promotional material aimed at selling something: an official poster, fan art plugging a real product, a scene where advertising is prominently on [display](#display), or a [gag](#gag) [parody](#parody) of one. Material [pushing](#pushing) a political cause is [propaganda](#propaganda) instead.

entries.name: dvd_cover
entries.description: The picture is the sleeve art of a home [video](#video) release, laid out with a [logo](#logo) and a [spine](#spine). Genuine releases and mock-ups drawn to look like one both count.

entries.name: fake_magazine_cover
entries.description: An illustration arranged as a magazine [cover](#cover), with a masthead, cover lines and a cover [model](#model), though [no](#no) such issue exists.

entries.name: screenshot_background
entries.description: Art drawn over a [captured](#captured) frame, so the background comes from the source material while the [figure](#figure) is newly drawn. A small captured frame set inside a larger picture is [screenshot_inset](#screenshot_inset) instead.

entries.name: end_card
entries.description: An illustration shown as an episode signs off, usually drawn by a different guest artist each week. It often carries the [title](#title) [logo](#logo) and the artist's name, and counts as official production art.

entries.name: box_art
entries.description: The illustration printed on the packaging of a physical product: a [figure](#figure), [model](#model) kit, [toy](#toy), game or boxed set of discs. Officially licensed and bootleg packaging both count, and the picture is usually a [scan](#scan) or photograph of the [box](#box) itself.

entries.name: visual_novel
entries.description: The look of a text-driven game: a dialogue [box](#box) laid across a background with a character [standing](#standing) in frame. Real screenshots and invented ones both count, while a bare background with [no](#no) box is [game_cg](#game_cg).

entries.name: movie_poster
entries.description: Artwork laid out the way a cinema poster is, with a [title](#title) treatment, a block of [credits](#credits) and the [cast](#cast) arranged across the sheet. Both the [tall](#tall) single-sheet format and the wide [landscape](#landscape) one appear.

entries.name: commissioner_insert
entries.description: The person who paid for the picture appears inside it, as their own character, an avatar or a [faceless](#faceless) stand-in. A picture showing only the wording of the request is [request_inset](#request_inset) instead.

entries.name: fake_video
entries.description: The picture is arranged as a still from a [video](#video) or a video site, with a player bar, comments or thumbnails around it. All that interface is drawn rather than [captured](#captured).

entries.name: mousepad_(medium)
entries.description: The picture is laid out as a novelty mousepad, with a body part — [breasts](#breasts), [pectorals](#pectorals) or a rear — forming the raised wrist rest. A mousepad merely [lying](#lying) in the scene takes the object [tag](#tag).

entries.name: profile_picture
entries.description: Artwork made to sit in the little avatar slot of an online account. Often composed inside a circular crop so the subject reads [well](#well) once the corners are cut away.

entries.name: animation_paper
entries.description: The [punched](#punched), trimmed sheets used for hand-drawn animation, showing peg holes and framing marks at the edges. Drawings on them often carry coloured linework, scene numbers or timing [notes](#notes) in the margins.

entries.name: fake_photograph
entries.description: A drawn or rendered picture built to pass as a photograph, with grain, [flash](#flash) and photographic framing. An actual photo [standing](#standing) as an object inside a scene is tagged differently.

entries.name: release_date
entries.description: A promotional picture announcing that a product is out or naming the [day](#day) it arrives, with the date worked into the image. Frequently the last entry in a [countdown](#countdown) series.

entries.name: omake
entries.description: A bonus piece packaged alongside the main work: a short strip, a [sketch](#sketch) page, a side scene the author threw in.

entries.name: video_thumbnail
entries.description: Art made to serve as the preview image of an actual [video](#video) somewhere online, with the video itself traceable from the post. Parodies of thumbnails and [redrawn](#redrawn) versions do not qualify.

entries.name: fake_box_art
entries.description: The picture is dressed as the packaging of a product, a game case, a [toy](#toy) [box](#box) or a disc sleeve, for goods that are invented or altered. Add [parody](#parody) and the imitated work when it copies something specific.

entries.name: key_frame
entries.description: A production drawing that fixes the start or end of a movement, with the in-between drawings made later to join them up. It is raw internal material, unlike a screenshot taken from the finished film.

entries.name: blu-ray_cover
entries.description: Artwork laid out as the sleeve of a Blu-ray case, generally [carrying](#carrying) the format's [logo](#logo) and its short, wide proportions. Fan-made imitations count as much as real releases.

entries.name: release_celebration
entries.description: Artwork drawn to mark the launch of a game, anime, album, or [book](#book). Often caps a run of [countdown](#countdown) illustrations and precedes follow-up pieces once the work is out.

entries.name: fake_ad
entries.description: The picture is laid out as an advertisement, with a product shot, a slogan and often a [price](#price), for something invented or joked about. The advertising format carries the [gag](#gag).

entries.name: social_network
entries.description: A picture built to resemble a social media post or app [screen](#screen), complete with avatars, timestamps, and reaction counts. The interface details are drawn as part of the artwork itself.

entries.name: media_player_interface
entries.description: The picture is dressed up as a screenshot of a [music](#music) or [video](#video) player, with a track [title](#title), progress bar and playback controls laid over the artwork. Sometimes mimics the layout of a real streaming app.

entries.name: fansub
entries.description: A still lifted from an anime episode [carrying](#carrying) subtitles added by fans rather than by an official release. The burnt-in translated line along the bottom gives it away.

entries.name: character_single
entries.description: Artwork for a CD released under a single character's name, generally songs performed in that character's voice. It describes the release the picture came from rather than what is drawn.

entries.name: street_snap
entries.description: A picture staged like a candid street-fashion photograph: the subject [caught](#caught) [mid-stride](#mid-stride) on a [pavement](#pavement), the whole outfit visible, a [city](#city) behind. It imitates the snapshots printed in [fashion](#fashion) magazines.

entries.name: production_note
entries.description: Written [notes](#notes) an artist leaves on the drawing itself: colour instructions, [construction](#construction) guides, or animation [markings](#markings) such as cel numbers. Mostly seen on sketches and uncoloured work.

entries.name: textless_version
entries.description: The artist's own alternate release of a picture with dialogue, a [title](#title) or rating text removed, common for [cover](#cover) art and explicit work. A third-party removal is [detexted](#detexted) instead.

entries.name: stitched
entries.description: An image assembled by joining several separate posts by the same artist into one, such as top and bottom halves into a full body. Not destructive, so not a third-party edit; unrelated to [stitches](#stitches) on skin or [cloth](#cloth).

entries.name: colorized
entries.description: A picture that began as [monochrome](#monochrome) or line art and has been coloured afterwards, usually by somebody other than the artist. It often carries third-party_edit as [well](#well).

entries.name: nude_filter
entries.description: An existing picture edited to strip a character's [clothes](#clothes) off and leave them bare. A [redrawn](#redrawn) or traced version rather than a paint-over is [derivative_work](#derivative_work).

entries.name: cropped
entries.description: The picture is a cut-out portion of a larger one, often posted alongside the full version. A crop sometimes carries more detail than the same area of the whole image does.

entries.name: sideways
entries.description: The whole picture is turned ninety degrees so the subject reads on its side. Describes the orientation of the image itself, not a character who happens to be [lying](#lying) down.

entries.name: decensored
entries.description: A picture that was [censored](#censored) when published and has had the censorship painted over by somebody else, most often a game still that carried mosaics. Such a version belongs under the censored original, and it differs from [uncensored](#uncensored), which was never covered, and from [nude_filter](#nude_filter).

entries.name: prototype_design
entries.description: A character rendered in a preliminary or scrapped design that was later changed before release, as seen in an [artbook](#artbook), a [pilot](#pilot), or an early one-shot chapter. Combine with the character's own [tag](#tag); a fan-made rework instead takes [alternate_costume](#alternate_costume).

entries.name: detexted
entries.description: A picture, typically a scanned [cover](#cover), whose lettering has been removed by somebody else and the background painted [back](#back) in behind it. A text-free version put out by the artist is [textless_version](#textless_version) instead.

entries.name: template
entries.description: A picture left deliberately incomplete so others [can](#can) fill it in, such as a blank speech [balloon](#balloon) or an empty [sign](#sign). Such images circulate as the raw material for edits and jokes.

entries.name: bubble_filter
entries.description: Circles are pasted over a clothed [figure](#figure) — or the [space](#space) between them wiped out — so that the clothing reads as bare skin. A joke edit that fakes nudity by aping the look of censorship.

entries.name: christmas
entries.description: The December holiday and its trappings, from Santa outfits and decorated firs to wrapped presents, [snow](#snow) and strings of lights. Specific items such as [christmas_tree](#christmas_tree) and [santa_costume](#santa_costume) carry their own tags.

entries.name: hbd
entries.description: Shorthand for a [birthday](#birthday) greeting: the picture wishes somebody a [happy](#happy) birthday, generally with the words written in beside [cake](#cake), candles or a [party](#party) [hat](#hat).

entries.name: halloween
entries.description: The picture is themed around Halloween, October 31st: costumes, [trick-or-treating](#trick-or-treating), pumpkins and jack-o'-lanterns, ghosts, witches and other spooky imagery.

entries.name: new_year
entries.description: Pictures marking the first of January, typically with girls in good [kimono](#kimono), [hamaya](#hamaya) arrows, zouni [soup](#soup), [hanetsuki](#hanetsuki) and the [zodiac](#zodiac) [animal](#animal) of the coming year. Greetings such as kinga shinnen or [akeome](#akeome), an English Happy New Year, or the year's number usually give it away.

entries.name: valentine
entries.description: Valentine's Day imagery, above all handmade or wrapped [chocolate](#chocolate) being prepared or handed over. In the Japanese custom it is the girls who give chocolate, with the return [gift](#gift) a month later belonging to [white_day](#white_day) instead.

entries.name: chinese_zodiac
entries.description: The twelve-year [animal](#animal) cycle of rat, ox, [tiger](#tiger), [rabbit](#rabbit), [dragon](#dragon), [snake](#snake), [horse](#horse), [goat](#goat), [monkey](#monkey), [rooster](#rooster), [dog](#dog) and [pig](#pig) used as the subject of a picture. Most often new year art built around the animal whose year it is.

entries.name: anniversary
entries.description: Art marking how long a series, game, group or event has been [running](#running), often [carrying](#carrying) a year count or a congratulatory line. The anniversary of a person's birth is [birthday](#birthday) instead.

entries.name: fireworks
entries.description: Controlled explosions set off for the look of them, from rockets bursting overhead to sparklers and ground pieces. A [blanket](#blanket) [tag](#tag); bursts up in the [sky](#sky) specifically are [aerial_fireworks](#aerial_fireworks).

entries.name: birthday
entries.description: A [celebration](#celebration) of the [anniversary](#anniversary) of someone's birth, marked by presents, candles, [party](#party) hats and [cake](#cake). Often drawn to mark a character's own recorded birthday.

entries.name: aerial_fireworks
entries.description: Large colourful bursts exploding high overhead, the [fireworks](#fireworks) of festivals and celebrations and generally shown at [night](#night). Handheld sparklers and ground fireworks are not this.

entries.name: wedding
entries.description: A marriage ceremony or its reception, with the [bride](#bride) and [groom](#groom), vows, a [bouquet](#bouquet) toss or [cake](#cake) [cutting](#cutting). Add [wedding_dress](#wedding_dress), [bridal_veil](#bridal_veil), [wedding_ring](#wedding_ring) or any traditional attire that appears.

entries.name: year_of_the_rabbit
entries.description: Art celebrating a [rabbit](#rabbit) year of the Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac), such as [2023](#2023), with bunny ears, rabbits and New Year trappings. Tag [chinese_zodiac](#chinese_zodiac) and [new_year](#new_year) alongside.

entries.name: year_of_the_tiger
entries.description: Art for a [tiger](#tiger) year in the Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac), such as [2022](#2022), with tiger ears, stripes or tiger costumes. Combine with [chinese_zodiac](#chinese_zodiac) and [new_year](#new_year).

entries.name: pocky_day
entries.description: Art made for the eleventh of November, when the date's four ones resemble the [stick](#stick) [snack](#snack). Usually shows characters with [pocky](#pocky), often in the middle of the pocky game.

entries.name: festival
entries.description: A community [celebration](#celebration) built around a theme, such as a [summer](#summer) festival with stalls, lanterns and [yukata](#yukata). Add the particular festival's [tag](#tag) where it [can](#can) be identified.

entries.name: year_of_the_ox
entries.description: New Year art for the ox's turn in the Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac), such as [2021](#2021), typically with characters dressed as or resembling cows. Combine with [chinese_zodiac](#chinese_zodiac) and cow-themed tags.

entries.name: nengajou
entries.description: A Japanese New Year greeting [card](#card), usually printed with set phrases such as kinga shinnen or akemashite omedetou. The [animal](#animal) of the coming [zodiac](#zodiac) year is a common motif.

entries.name: setsubun
entries.description: The Japanese last [day](#day) of [winter](#winter), around February 3rd, marked by [throwing](#throwing) roasted soybeans at an [oni](#oni) to drive it off and by [eating](#eating) [ehoumaki](#ehoumaki) rolls facing the year's lucky direction. Pictures usually show the bean-throwing, oni masks, or the [sushi](#sushi) roll.

entries.name: sparkler
entries.description: A handheld firework: a [stick](#stick) held at one end while the other burns with a shower of [sparks](#sparks). Japan's [senkou_hanabi](#senkou_hanabi) is a specific kind. Not to be [confused](#confused) with the [sparkle](#sparkle) light effect.

entries.name: tanabata
entries.description: The Japanese star [festival](#festival) held on July 7, marking the once-a-year meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi. In pictures it usually means wishes written on [paper](#paper) strips and hung on [bamboo](#bamboo); the related Chinese festival is tagged separately.

entries.name: year_of_the_dragon
entries.description: Art for a Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac) [dragon](#dragon) year such as [2012](#2012) or [2024](#2024), usually New Year greetings with dragon motifs or characters dressed in dragon [costume](#costume). Tag [chinese_zodiac](#chinese_zodiac) and [new_year](#new_year) as fits.

entries.name: cat_day
entries.description: Artwork drawn for the twenty-second of February, whose Japanese [reading](#reading) sounds like a cat's meow three times over. Cat girls and cat-themed pictures fill the date.

entries.name: april_fools
entries.description: Art made for the first of April, either saying so outright or [presenting](#presenting) a deliberate hoax or absurd claim. Joke and [meme](#meme) tags often ride along with it.

entries.name: summer_festival
entries.description: A Japanese [summer](#summer) [festival](#festival), usually set at [night](#night), with [yukata](#yukata), [paper](#paper) lanterns, [food](#food) stalls selling [takoyaki](#takoyaki) and shaved [ice](#ice), [goldfish](#goldfish) scooping, masks and [fireworks](#fireworks) overhead.

entries.name: bunny_day
entries.description: Artwork made for the Japanese number [pun](#pun) that reads certain August dates as 'bunny'. Characters turn up in [rabbit](#rabbit) ears or a [playboy_bunny](#playboy_bunny) outfit to mark it.

entries.name: easter_egg
entries.description: A hard-boiled [egg](#egg) with its [shell](#shell) painted in bright colours and patterns for the spring holiday. Usually piled in a [basket](#basket) or hidden in [grass](#grass) to be found.

entries.name: chinese_new_year
entries.description: The lunisolar new year [festival](#festival), [falling](#falling) between late January and late February, celebrated with red [decorations](#decorations), [paper](#paper) lanterns, [lion](#lion) dances and the [animal](#animal) of the coming year. Korean and Vietnamese new year celebrations held around the same date belong here too.

entries.name: golden_week
entries.description: The run of Japanese public holidays from late April into early May, the busiest stretch of the year for travel and leisure. Trips, crowds and time off belong to it.

entries.name: maid_day
entries.description: Pictures drawn for the tenth of May, the date artists set aside to celebrate maids. Almost always accompanied by [maid](#maid) itself.

entries.name: easter
entries.description: The spring holiday, dressed in art with painted eggs, baskets of [sweets](#sweets), [rabbit](#rabbit) ears and pastel colours. Religious imagery of the resurrection belongs here too.

entries.name: year_of_the_rat
entries.description: New Year art for a rat year of the Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac), such as [2020](#2020), with mouse ears or rats as the motif. Tag [chinese_zodiac](#chinese_zodiac) and [new_year](#new_year).

entries.name: white_day
entries.description: March 14, when boys return gifts to the girls who gave them Valentine's [chocolate](#chocolate). Pictures show gift-giving and a [happy](#happy) recipient, the [mirror](#mirror) scene to [valentine](#valentine).

entries.name: hanami
entries.description: The spring custom of gathering beneath blossoming [cherry](#cherry) or [plum](#plum) trees, generally with a [picnic](#picnic) sheet, [food](#food) and [drink](#drink). The outing itself is what the [tag](#tag) records, not merely blossoms overhead.

entries.name: graduation
entries.description: The ceremony closing a course of study: gowns and mortarboards, or in Japanese settings a [diploma](#diploma) [tube](#tube), a [corsage](#corsage) and a decorated hall. Farewells between classmates usually come with it.

entries.name: year_of_the_pig
entries.description: New Year pictures for the final [animal](#animal) of the twelve-year [zodiac](#zodiac), [following](#following) the [dog](#dog) and preceding the rat. Japanese versions put the wild [boar](#boar) in the domestic pig's place.

entries.name: year_of_the_dog
entries.description: New Year artwork celebrating the dog's turn in the twelve-year Chinese [zodiac](#zodiac) cycle, which comes round in years such as [2018](#2018) and 2030. Dog ears, puppies or dog-themed props usually appear in a festive setting.

entries.name: party
entries.description: A gathering held to celebrate something, with [food](#food) and [drink](#drink), [decorations](#decorations), hats and [streamers](#streamers) strung about. It names the occasion itself, whatever is being marked.

entries.name: twintails_day
entries.description: An observance celebrating the [twintails](#twintails) hairstyle, held on the second of February and promoted in Japan since [2012](#2012). Art for it shows characters wearing the style, often with the date noted.

entries.name: announcement_celebration
entries.description: An illustration made to celebrate good [news](#news) for a series: an adaptation, another season, a serialisation. Neighbouring occasions such as countdowns, release parties and finale pieces have tags of their own.

entries.name: hinamatsuri
entries.description: The Japanese Girls' Day [festival](#festival) on 3 March, marked by a tiered [display](#display) of dolls in Heian court [dress](#dress). Peach blossom, layered diamond [mochi](#mochi) and sweet white [sake](#sake) belong to the occasion.

entries.name: senkou_hanabi
entries.description: A slim, paper-stemmed Japanese [sparkler](#sparkler) held [pointing](#pointing) downward while a bead of [fire](#fire) forms and drips [sparks](#sparks). Watched quietly instead of being waved about like a Western sparkler.

entries.name: year_of_the_rooster
entries.description: New Year artwork for the rooster's turn in the [zodiac](#zodiac), coming after the [monkey](#monkey) and before the [dog](#dog). Artists often draw chicken-themed girls rather than the [bird](#bird) itself.

entries.name: mamemaki
entries.description: The Setsubun custom of [throwing](#throwing) roasted soybeans out of the [door](#door) or at an [oni](#oni) to drive misfortune off. The [beans](#beans) are scooped from a small [square](#square) wooden measure, the [masu](#masu).

entries.name: lgbt_pride
entries.description: The picture is built around LGBT pride, with identity or [rainbow](#rainbow) flags, pride colours worn or painted on, and Pride Month imagery. It covers the whole [family](#family) of identity flags rather than any single one.

entries.name: hatsumoude
entries.description: The first [shrine](#shrine) or [temple](#temple) visit of the Japanese new year: [crowded](#crowded) approaches, prayers at the hall, fortune slips drawn and fresh charms bought while the [old](#old) ones are handed [back](#back). Kimono and [heavy](#heavy) [winter](#winter) [dress](#dress) fill these pictures.

entries.name: sports_festival
entries.description: A [school](#school) sports [day](#day), with classes competing in relays, [tug](#tug) of [war](#war), three-legged races and [ball](#ball) [tossing](#tossing). Usually drawn [outdoors](#outdoors) with banners, headbands and [gym](#gym) uniforms.

entries.name: mother's_day
entries.description: The [day](#day) set aside to honour mothers, in most countries the second Sunday in May. Flowers are the usual [gift](#gift) shown, red carnations above all.

entries.name: breasts_day
entries.description: A date-pun observance in Japan: the first of August reads as oppai, Father's Day plays on chichi, and the eighth of November is Good Breasts Day. Themed pictures are drawn and posted for those dates.

entries.name: zanshomimai
entries.description: A late-summer greeting [postcard](#postcard), sent after the midsummer round to check on the recipient through the lingering heat. Usually shown with a seasonal illustration and a handwritten [note](#note).

entries.name: lantern_festival
entries.description: The [celebration](#celebration) closing the New Year period of the Chinese calendar, marked by hung and floated lanterns and by sweet [rice](#rice) balls. Scenes show [night](#night) streets, crowds and rows of red lanterns.

entries.name: kodomo_no_hi
entries.description: The Japanese children's holiday held on 5 May, historically a [festival](#festival) for boys. Its recurring props are [carp](#carp) [streamers](#streamers), [folded](#folded) [paper](#paper) helmets and leaf-wrapped [rice](#rice) cakes.

entries.name: kiss_day
entries.description: A minor Japanese observance on 23 May honouring the [kiss](#kiss), [dated](#dated) from the release of the country's first film to show one. Pictures [carrying](#carrying) it are themed illustrations posted for the [day](#day).

entries.name: birthday_party
entries.description: A gathering held for someone's [birthday](#birthday), with [cake](#cake) and candles, presents, hats and [decorations](#decorations). The [party](#party) itself is the subject rather than the date alone.

entries.name: tsukimi
entries.description: The [autumn](#autumn) moon-viewing observance held on the fifteenth [night](#night) of the eighth lunar month. Susuki [grass](#grass), stacked white dumplings and [sake](#sake) set out on a [veranda](#veranda) are its standard trappings.

entries.name: oktoberfest
entries.description: The Bavarian [beer](#beer) [festival](#festival), shown through litre steins, pretzels, marquees and the [dirndl](#dirndl) and lederhosen worn to it. Held in Munich at the turn of [autumn](#autumn) and copied in other countries.

entries.name: panties_day
entries.description: The second of August, read as 8/2, marked by Japanese artists with underwear-themed pictures. It goes on work drawn for the occasion, not on anything that merely happens to show [panties](#panties).

entries.name: trick-or-treating
entries.description: The Halloween custom of going [door](#door) to door in [costume](#costume) to collect [sweets](#sweets). Covers the act itself, whether the [candy](#candy) [bucket](#bucket), the doorstep, or the walk between houses; the spoken phrase alone is a separate [tag](#tag).

entries.name: funeral
entries.description: A service held for someone who has died, with mourners gathered around a [portrait](#portrait), [coffin](#coffin) or [grave](#grave). The mood is subdued and the [dress](#dress) usually black.

entries.name: year_of_the_monkey
entries.description: New Year artwork for the monkey's place in the twelve-year [zodiac](#zodiac), [sitting](#sitting) between the [goat](#goat) and the [rooster](#rooster). Monkey ears, tails or costumes are the usual treatment.

entries.name: mid-autumn_festival
entries.description: A Chinese harvest [festival](#festival) held on the full [moon](#moon) of the eighth lunar month, marked with lanterns, mooncakes and moon-viewing. The second most important holiday of the year after Lunar New Year.

entries.name: stomach_day
entries.description: A Japanese date [pun](#pun) [falling](#falling) on 7 November, whose numbers read as a phrase about good stomachs. Art posted for it plays on bellies and bare midriffs.

entries.name: otoshidama
entries.description: The New Year cash [gift](#gift) given to children in Japan, handed over in a small [envelope](#envelope) tied or printed with a red-and-white cord. Notes are [folded](#folded) in three inside, and the word on the front tells it apart from the Chinese red [packet](#packet).

entries.name: paizuri_day
entries.description: The thirteenth of August, read as a number [pun](#pun) on the word [paizuri](#paizuri) and marked with breast-sex artwork. An occasion for the drawing rather than anything visible inside it.

entries.name: year_of_the_goat
entries.description: New Year pictures for the goat's slot in the twelve-year cycle, arriving after the [horse](#horse) and before the [monkey](#monkey). Japanese usage reads the same character as [sheep](#sheep), so either [animal](#animal) may be drawn.

entries.name: convention
entries.description: A fan gathering built around a shared enthusiasm. Tables stacked with self-published books, a seller behind them and a [queue](#queue) in front, plus badges and banners overhead, are the usual signs.

entries.name: hatsuyume
entries.description: The year's first dream, an [old](#old) Japanese belief about what the coming months hold. Mount Fuji, a [hawk](#hawk) and an aubergine are the lucky sights, and pictures often [crowd](#crowd) all three into one.

entries.name: glasses_day
entries.description: The first of October, marked in Japan as a [day](#day) for spectacles because the written date resembles a pair of them. It brings a yearly wave of [bespectacled](#bespectacled) character art.

entries.name: carnival
entries.description: A loud public [celebration](#celebration) of parades, drums, feathered costumes and general excess. Not the travelling funfair that shares the word in American English.

entries.name: father's_day
entries.description: The yearly occasion honouring fathers, shown through cards, presents and [family](#family) scenes around a dad. Neckties, flowers and hand-drawn thank-you [notes](#notes) are the stock props.

entries.name: marine_day
entries.description: A Japanese public holiday in mid-July [giving](#giving) thanks for the sea, widely spent at the [beach](#beach). Artists mark it with [swimsuit](#swimsuit) pictures, and the [tag](#tag) applies once the [day](#day) itself is named.

entries.name: meat_day
entries.description: Art made for a Japanese calendar [pun](#pun) on the word for [meat](#meat), [falling](#falling) on the 29th of a month or on 9 February. Traditionally marked with [plump](#plump) or heavily muscled characters, sometimes alongside actual meat.

entries.name: chinese_wedding
entries.description: A marriage staged with Chinese custom and [dress](#dress): red robes, [gold](#gold) [embroidery](#embroidery), a veiled [bride](#bride) and the surrounding [ritual](#ritual). Apply it when the ceremony or its trappings carry the picture, not for any bridal outfit.

entries.name: dia_de_muertos
entries.description: The Mexican remembrance holiday at the start of November, when families gather to honour the dead. Sugar skulls, marigolds, candlelit altars, painted faces and bright folk [dress](#dress) are the usual markers.

entries.name: fourth_of_july
entries.description: American Independence Day, marked with [fireworks](#fireworks), parades, barbecues and red-white-and-blue colouring. Characters are commonly dressed in the flag's colours for it.

entries.name: parade
entries.description: A procession moving along a [street](#street) with marchers, floats, banners and musicians, watched by onlookers to either side. A public occasion, not simply a group [walking](#walking) together.

entries.name: announcement
entries.description: The picture exists to break [news](#news), most often a quickly drawn piece greeting word of a new [title](#title), season or adaptation. The occasion is what it records, not the subject drawn.

entries.name: solar_term
entries.description: One of the twenty-four divisions of the traditional East Asian calendar, each marking a point in the year such as the start of spring or the [summer](#summer) solstice. Pictures marking one usually [spell](#spell) its name out in text.

entries.name: pride_month
entries.description: Artwork made for the June [celebration](#celebration) of LGBTQ+ life and history, naming or plainly marking the occasion. More general [rainbow](#rainbow) imagery belongs with [lgbt_pride](#lgbt_pride).

entries.name: dragon_boat_festival
entries.description: The Chinese holiday held on the fifth of the fifth lunar month, marked by races in long dragon-headed boats and by [eating](#eating) [zongzi](#zongzi). Pictures show the [racing](#racing), the wrapped [rice](#rice) parcels or [festival](#festival) [dress](#dress).

entries.name: ancient_egyptian
entries.description: The picture draws on ancient Egypt: pharaohs, pyramids, hieroglyphs, eye-of-Horus motifs, its gods and tombs. Dress in that style takes [ancient_egyptian_clothes](#ancient_egyptian_clothes) as [well](#well).

entries.name: world_war_ii
entries.description: A scene set in or referencing the 1939-1945 global [war](#war), through period uniforms, tanks, [aircraft](#aircraft), warships, and its historical figures or fronts. It is common in military-moe and ship-girl art; add [military](#military) and a nation's own tags alongside it.

entries.name: cowboy_western
entries.description: Wild West imagery: brimmed hats, [leather](#leather) vests and [chaps](#chaps), [boots](#boots), revolvers and lever-action rifles, saloons and [desert](#desert) country. It covers characters of either [sex](#sex) dressed in the style.

entries.name: nazi
entries.description: Nazi symbols, flags or [insignia](#insignia) in the picture, or characters shown as adherents of the ideology. Wartime German forces alone are not enough, while deliberately obscured [armband](#armband) symbols still count.

entries.name: y2k_fashion
entries.description: Clothing in the late-nineties and early-2000s look: [low-rise](#low-rise) trousers, [cropped](#cropped) tops, shiny or [furry](#furry) fabrics, chunky plastic [sunglasses](#sunglasses) and colourful [accessories](#accessories). Palettes run to pink, purple and blue, often [carrying](#carrying) [butterfly](#butterfly), star or [heart](#heart) prints.

entries.name: soviet
entries.description: Imagery tied to the Soviet Union and the wider Eastern Bloc, from the [hammer](#hammer) and [sickle](#sickle) and red stars to Cyrillic lettering, period [architecture](#architecture), uniforms, and technology. Pair it with a specific country [tag](#tag) when one particular republic is shown.

entries.name: medieval
entries.description: European Middle Ages styling built around knights: [mail](#mail) or [plate](#plate) [armor](#armor), long-sleeved gowns, laced [boots](#boots) and cloaks. Distinguish it from the later, more [ornate](#ornate) renaissance look.

entries.name: imperial_japanese_army
entries.description: References to Japan's pre-1945 [army](#army) through its uniforms and colours, its equipment or a historical scene involving it. The cues have to be definite enough to point at that force rather than generic soldiery.

entries.name: victorian
entries.description: Nineteenth-century British [dress](#dress) and trappings: wide skirted gowns, corsets, top hats and frock coats. Meant for genuine period styling, not the modern lolita [fashion](#fashion) that only borrows from it.

entries.name: ainu
entries.description: The picture draws on the [indigenous](#indigenous) culture of Hokkaido and Sakhalin, through embroidered [border](#border) patterns, tattoos, carved implements or the language itself. It covers characters presented in that context as [well](#well) as the [writing](#writing).

entries.name: russia
entries.description: The country spanning northern Asia and eastern Europe, the largest nation in the world by area, evoked through [architecture](#architecture), [landscape](#landscape), uniforms or national symbols. Its Soviet and Imperial-era predecessors are usually tagged separately from the modern country.

entries.name: aztec
entries.description: Imagery drawn from the pre-conquest cultures of central Mexico: stepped stone pyramids, feathered headdresses, carved calendar discs and blocky geometric ornament. It [can](#can) drive the setting, the [costume](#costume) or merely the decoration on an object.

entries.name: imperial_japanese_navy
entries.description: References to Japan's pre-1945 navy through its warships, its [sailor](#sailor) [dress](#dress) or a historical episode. Naval-themed game casts count only where the picture points at the real service.

entries.name: historical_connection
entries.description: The picture nods to real history, a period or a [battle](#battle) or a [war](#war), or brings together characters whose real-life originals were linked. Depicting the event itself is [historical_event](#historical_event).

entries.name: viking
entries.description: A Norse raider or seafarer of the early [medieval](#medieval) north, kitted out with axes, round shields, furs and braided hair. Horned helmets show up constantly despite being a later invention.

entries.name: historical_event
entries.description: A real event from the past is shown or clearly referenced, whether ancient or very recent. The artist's own commentary is often what identifies which one.

entries.name: anachronism
entries.description: Something in the picture belongs to the wrong era for the setting, a [smartphone](#smartphone) in a Victorian parlour or a modern [rifle](#rifle) among [samurai](#samurai). The mismatch is usually deliberate and carries the joke.

entries.name: heisei_retro
entries.description: The nostalgic 1990s and 2000s Japanese girlhood look: pastel plastics, shaped hairclips, charms and flip phones, [chibi](#chibi) animals, rainbows, sparkles and hearts. English-speaking fans call it cutecore, and it sits close to Y2K [fashion](#fashion).

entries.name: world_war_i
entries.description: The 1914-1918 [war](#war), recognisable from [trench](#trench) lines, [gas](#gas) masks, biplanes, and the earliest tanks. It is the period uniforms and equipment that place a picture in this setting.

entries.name: heian
entries.description: The look of Japan's classical court age, roughly the ninth to twelfth centuries: layered robes, floor-length hair, folding fans, screens and lacquer. It covers the [dress](#dress) and the wider aesthetic alike.

entries.name: communism
entries.description: The picture invokes communist ideology or its imagery, from red stars and the [hammer](#hammer) and [sickle](#sickle) to propaganda-poster layouts. Straight references and parodies both count.

entries.name: taishou
entries.description: The Japanese era spanning 1912 to 1926, a brief [window](#window) of liberal [politics](#politics) whose [fashion](#fashion) mixed [kimono](#kimono) with Western hats, [boots](#boots) and [glasses](#glasses). Sits stylistically between Meiji-era modernization and the militarism that followed.

entries.name: kriegsmarine
entries.description: The wartime German navy of 1935 to 1945, present through its warships, [insignia](#insignia) and uniforms. Keep it for genuine references to that force rather than for any warship-themed character.

entries.name: caveman
entries.description: A stereotyped prehistoric human in [animal](#animal) hides, [holding](#holding) a club or a chipped stone tool, often beside a [fire](#fire) or a bone-in hunk of [meat](#meat). The look is cartoon shorthand rather than any accurate reconstruction.

entries.name: heisei
entries.description: The Japanese era [running](#running) from 1989 to [2019](#2019), used to place a picture's fashions, technology and mood in those decades. It followed Shouwa and gave way to Reiwa.

entries.name: vietnam_war
entries.description: The mid-century conflict in Vietnam and its neighbours as the subject: [jungle](#jungle) patrols, helicopters and the [fatigues](#fatigues) of the period. Both the American-backed south and the communist north appear.

entries.name: roman_empire
entries.description: The imperial period of ancient Rome, with its legions, marble [architecture](#architecture) and emperors ruling lands around the Mediterranean. Used as a setting or as the source of a character's trappings.

entries.name: chinese_empire
entries.description: Imperial China before 1912, shown through its dynastic courts, officials, palaces and armies. Used where [no](#no) narrower period [tag](#tag) applies, and combined with Chinese mythology for the legendary early rulers.

entries.name: renaissance_clothes
entries.description: European [dress](#dress) in the style of the 15th and 16th centuries: doublets, slashed sleeves, ruffs, corseted bodices and full skirts. Used for both historical settings and modern characters dressed up in period [costume](#costume).

entries.name: east_germany
entries.description: Imagery of the former German Democratic Republic: the hammer-and-compasses [flag](#flag), its uniforms and small cars, the divided Berlin of 1949 to 1990. A place and period rather than a story.

entries.name: jidaigeki
entries.description: A Japanese period setting out of the [samurai](#samurai) centuries, with topknots, [castle](#castle) towns, [sword](#sword) duels and era [dress](#dress). It is the Japanese counterpart of a [medieval](#medieval) setting; worlds [leaning](#leaning) on [magic](#magic) or [machinery](#machinery) do not qualify.

entries.name: fantasy
entries.description: A setting built on [magic](#magic), mythical creatures and the supernatural, usually with medieval-flavoured [dress](#dress) and [architecture](#architecture). It describes the whole picture's genre; futuristic worlds are [science_fiction](#science_fiction), though the two [can](#can) meet.

entries.name: alchemy
entries.description: The [old](#old) craft of transforming matter, shown through bubbling flasks, chalked diagrams, furnaces and [heavy](#heavy) books. Sitting halfway between experiment and [magic](#magic) is usually the point.

entries.name: buddhism
entries.description: Buddhist subject matter: temples, Buddha statues, monks, sutras and prayer [beads](#beads). It marks the religion as the picture's theme rather than any single [figure](#figure) within it.

entries.name: christianity
entries.description: Christian religious content: churches, crosses, clergy, saints and the worship built around them. Use it for the religious framing of a scene, not for a [cross](#cross) worn purely as jewellery.

entries.name: hell
entries.description: The underworld of [punishment](#punishment) as pictures show it: [fire](#fire), chains, tormented souls and demons at work, over bare [rock](#rock) and [lava](#lava) under a red [sky](#sky).

entries.name: heaven
entries.description: The afterlife of the blessed as pictures show it: banks of [cloud](#cloud), golden light, gates and [drifting](#drifting) winged figures. The counterpart to [hell](#hell).

entries.name: aquarius_(zodiac)
entries.description: A picture built around the water-bearer [sign](#sign): its name, an [urn](#urn) [pouring](#pouring) [water](#water), or a character personifying it. Where a glyph or star [chart](#chart) merely happens to be present, [aquarius_(symbol)](#aquarius_(symbol)) or [aquarius_(constellation)](#aquarius_(constellation)) is the right [choice](#choice).

entries.name: aries_(zodiac)
entries.description: A picture built around the ram [sign](#sign): its name, its [horns](#horns), or a character [standing](#standing) in for it. Where only a glyph or star pattern appears in passing, [aries_(symbol)](#aries_(symbol)) or [aries_(constellation)](#aries_(constellation)) fit better.

entries.name: capricorn_(zodiac)
entries.description: A picture themed on Capricorn and its half-goat, half-fish [creature](#creature), whether in [costume](#costume), motif or [title](#title). A glyph or star pattern present only in passing takes its own [tag](#tag).

entries.name: gemini_(zodiac)
entries.description: A picture built around Twins imagery from the [zodiac](#zodiac), [playing](#playing) on the sign's name or its paired-figure motif. When only the glyph or the star pattern turns up incidentally, use [gemini_(symbol)](#gemini_(symbol)) or [gemini_(constellation)](#gemini_(constellation)).

entries.name: cancer_(zodiac)
entries.description: A picture built around the [sign](#sign) Cancer and its [crab](#crab), in [costume](#costume), motif or [title](#title). A glyph or star pattern present only in passing belongs to [cancer_(symbol)](#cancer_(symbol)) or [cancer_(constellation)](#cancer_(constellation)).

entries.name: libra_(zodiac)
entries.description: Imagery themed on the star [sign](#sign) Libra, usually balance [scales](#scales) or the sign's name tied to a character or outfit. An ordinary weighing scale by itself does not qualify.

entries.name: leo_(zodiac)
entries.description: Imagery built around the star [sign](#sign) Leo, with [lion](#lion) motifs or the sign's name attached to a character or [costume](#costume). A glyph or star pattern turning up on its own takes [leo_(symbol)](#leo_(symbol)) or [leo_(constellation)](#leo_(constellation)).

entries.name: science_fiction
entries.description: A picture set in a futuristic world of advanced technology: spaceships, robots, aliens, elaborate [machinery](#machinery). Apply when the setting reads as sci-fi; it may sit beside [fantasy](#fantasy) when the two mix.

entries.name: time_paradox
entries.description: A scene that could not happen chronologically, such as a character meeting their own older or younger self or figures from different eras [sharing](#sharing) a moment. Add the characters involved.

entries.name: tokusatsu
entries.description: The Japanese live-action hero and [monster](#monster) genre of costumed heroes, [kaiju](#kaiju) and practical effects. Add the [parody](#parody) or [costume](#costume) tags as fitting.

entries.name: cyberpunk
entries.description: A science-fiction setting of advanced technology over social decay: neon-lit streets, [rain](#rain), [cable](#cable) runs, implants and corporations [running](#running) everything. Grimy dense cities and body modification are its visual [signature](#signature).

entries.name: super_robot
entries.description: Giant [mecha](#mecha) in the flashy old-school style of Mazinger Z or Getter Robo, with named special attacks and superpowered weapons. Contrasts with the grounded real_robot genre started by Gundam. Implies mecha.

entries.name: steampunk
entries.description: Victorian-era [science](#science) fiction with steam-driven [machinery](#machinery): [goggles](#goggles), top hats, corsets, brass [gears](#gears), pipes and [pocket](#pocket) watches. Tag the aesthetic wherever it dominates the design.

entries.name: post-apocalypse
entries.description: A world ruined by [war](#war) or catastrophe: [overgrown](#overgrown) [ruins](#ruins), wastelands, scavengers and survivors. Covers original settings as [well](#well) as ones built in the mould of well-known [wasteland](#wasteland) fiction.

entries.name: apocalypse
entries.description: The world is ending or has already ended, shown through mass [destruction](#destruction), [burning](#burning) skies or cities coming apart. It covers the catastrophe itself, while life among the [ruins](#ruins) afterwards has its own tags.

entries.name: horror_(theme)
entries.description: The picture as a whole sets out to unsettle the viewer, through dread, monsters, gore or an eerie atmosphere. Where only a character looks frightened and the image itself is not creepy, use [horrified](#horrified).

entries.name: body_horror
entries.description: Horror grounded in the human body coming apart: [mutation](#mutation), mutilation, disease, extra limbs, [joints](#joints) [bending](#bending) where they should not. The dread comes from the [flesh](#flesh) itself rather than from a [monster](#monster) [standing](#standing) outside it.

entries.name: doppelganger
entries.description: A character shares the frame with an exact double of themselves, be it a ghostly apparition, an evil twin or something wearing their face. The unsettling sameness is the point.

entries.name: urban_legend
entries.description: Modern folklore as subject matter: [ghost](#ghost) stories and cautionary tales passed from person to person or spread online, set in the present [day](#day) and often ending on a twist. They tend to voice shared fears about crime, strangers or the uncanny.

entries.name: trypophobia
entries.description: Imagery built on dense clusters of small holes, of the kind found in a [lotus](#lotus) [seed](#seed) pod or honeycomb, which many viewers find deeply unsettling. Faces and bodies pitted with such holes are the usual treatment.

entries.name: military
entries.description: A broad theme for [realistic](#realistic), [contemporary](#contemporary) military content: proper uniforms and [insignia](#insignia), soldiers actually in service, modern hardware and combat scenes. Apply with some restraint rather than to every [costume](#costume) that merely looks uniform-like.

entries.name: contemporary
entries.description: A character from a [fantasy](#fantasy), science-fiction or historical setting is shown in present-day [clothes](#clothes) or surroundings. Where the outfit itself has changed, [alternate_costume](#alternate_costume) applies as [well](#well).

entries.name: japanese_(nationality)
entries.description: The person shown is taken to be Japanese, whether from the setting, the [dress](#dress) or a [plain](#plain) statement. It carries nothing about the drawing style or the language of any [writing](#writing) in the frame.

entries.name: japan
entries.description: The picture is about Japan as a country: its [scenery](#scenery), its customs, its national symbols, or the nation personified. Particular historical eras have tags of their own, and the [flag](#flag) is [japanese_flag](#japanese_flag).

entries.name: brazil
entries.description: The picture points at Brazil, through [flag](#flag) colours, football, [carnival](#carnival), beaches or Amazon [scenery](#scenery). Portuguese [writing](#writing) in the image often turns up with it.

entries.name: germany
entries.description: Present-day Germany or German culture as the subject, shown through landmarks, [food](#food), flags or the country as a setting. Historical periods that have tags of their own go there instead.

entries.name: fujoshi
entries.description: A girl devoted to male-male romance manga, and by extension a female [otaku](#otaku) in general. Drawn [buried](#buried) in doujinshi, gushing over a pairing or [hiding](#hiding) her collection; a male fan of the same material is a fudanshi.

entries.name: italy
entries.description: The picture is set in Italy, or leans on Italian surroundings to say so. Canals and gondolas, sun-bleached piazzas, terracotta roofs and Roman [ruins](#ruins) are the usual cues.

entries.name: france
entries.description: The picture leans on the French Republic or French culture, through landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower or the Arc de Triomphe, its cities, or cultural motifs. Use it for the setting or the reference, not merely because a character happens to be French.

entries.name: china
entries.description: The country and its culture: mainland cities, imperial dynasties, landmarks and national symbols. Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau have their own tags, and the ceramic material of the same name is [porcelain](#porcelain).

entries.name: heavy_metal
entries.description: The loud, aggressive [rock](#rock) genre and everything around it: band shirts and logos, [studded](#studded) [leather](#leather), [horns](#horns) thrown up, guitars in a [stage](#stage) or [garage](#garage) setting. Album-cover parodies and lyric references count too.

entries.name: ukraine
entries.description: A reference to the Eastern European country, through its [landscape](#landscape), landmarks, [dress](#dress) or national colours. Wheat fields and a blue-and-yellow palette are common shorthand for it.

entries.name: hip_hop
entries.description: The [music](#music) and [street](#street) culture built on rap, DJing and dance, together with its look of oversized [clothes](#clothes), [sneakers](#sneakers), caps and [heavy](#heavy) [gold](#gold) chains. Album-cover parodies and lyric references count too.

entries.name: politics
entries.description: Real-world political events, slogans, or [party](#party) symbols carried by the picture, whether mocking one side or backing another. The politics is the subject of the picture, not merely part of the [backdrop](#backdrop).

entries.name: argentina
entries.description: The South American country as a subject: its landscapes, its [people](#people), or the pale blue and white that stand for it. The [banner](#banner) on its own is [argentinian_flag](#argentinian_flag).

entries.name: indonesia
entries.description: The Southeast Asian [island](#island) country as setting or reference, through its landscapes, its cities or its national symbols. It sits between Malaysia, the Philippines and Australia.

entries.name: canada
entries.description: Canadian settings and motifs: maple leaves, mounties, hockey, snowbound northern [landscape](#landscape). It places the picture in that country rather than describing anything about the figures.

entries.name: philippines
entries.description: Imagery tied to the Philippines: the [flag](#flag), landmarks, national [dress](#dress), [food](#food), or a character identified with the country. Use it for the explicit reference, not for any unnamed [tropical](#tropical) setting.

entries.name: greece
entries.description: The southeastern European country and the imagery that goes with it: whitewashed [island](#island) villages under blue domes, [olive](#olive) groves, and the marble [ruins](#ruins) of antiquity.

entries.name: finland
entries.description: The northern European country as a subject, evoked through its [landscape](#landscape), landmarks or national symbols. Lakes, pine [forest](#forest) and [snow](#snow) are the stock imagery.

entries.name: australia
entries.description: The [island](#island) continent and country as the subject of the picture, through its landscapes, its wildlife, its cities or its national colours. The [flag](#flag) on its own is [australian_flag](#australian_flag).

entries.name: finnish_army
entries.description: Finland's ground forces: their [insignia](#insignia), an identifiable vehicle of theirs, or a character in their uniform. The specific force is the point, not soldiering in general.

entries.name: fashion
entries.description: Characters dressed in genuinely modish clothing by real-world standards rather than anime ones, the sort a [runway](#runway) might show. Magazine-style [posing](#posing) counts as [well](#well). A merely nice outfit is not enough.

entries.name: truth
entries.description: An illustration built around a sincere message, whether challenging a stereotype, correcting a misconception, [sharing](#sharing) an insight, or gently satirising such attempts. A picture that pushes one viewpoint aggressively without any balance leans closer to [propaganda](#propaganda) instead.

entries.name: symbolism
entries.description: A picture that uses objects or imagery to stand for a deeper [idea](#idea), where what is visibly shown carries meaning beyond its literal appearance.

entries.name: chuunibyou
entries.description: A character strikes grand [poses](#poses) and proclaims sealed powers or a tragic past, the adolescent posturing an English [speaker](#speaker) would call edgy. Eyepatches, bandaged arms and [sweeping](#sweeping) gestures come with it. Use it only where the behaviour is actually on show.

entries.name: abandoned
entries.description: A place or object left unused and untended for a long stretch, marked by [dust](#dust), [rust](#rust), overgrowth and decay. The emptiness is the point of the picture rather than incidental.

entries.name: yami_kawaii
entries.description: A sickly-cute aesthetic that pairs pastel, girlish styling with medical and morbid props such as syringes, pills, [bandages](#bandages), [gas](#gas) masks and [toy](#toy) guns. The prettiness is meant to sit uneasily against what is actually being shown.

entries.name: mojo
entries.description: A gloomy, socially hopeless woman with [no](#no) romantic prospects, often drawn [unkempt](#unkempt) and prone to unhinged faces. It names a character type, not a job or an age.

entries.name: dojikko
entries.description: A character defined by clumsiness: [tripping](#tripping) over nothing, [dropping](#dropping) what they carry, [walking](#walking) into doorframes. Worth tagging only when the fumbling actually shows in the picture.

entries.name: fatherly
entries.description: One character shows a father's kind of warmth or protectiveness toward another, a hand on the head or a steadying arm. No [blood](#blood) relation is needed for it to read that way.

entries.name: patriotism
entries.description: The picture holds up a country, real or invented, with flags, national colours, uniforms or anthems treated with pride. Sincere tributes and send-ups both belong here.

entries.name: sinister
entries.description: A vague [label](#label) for a menacing or evil atmosphere that rests entirely on the tagger's own judgement, with nothing [concrete](#concrete) marking when it applies. Best avoided in favor of a more specific descriptive [tag](#tag).

entries.name: meme
entries.description: The picture reproduces or references a known [internet](#internet) or pop-culture joke - an image format, a recurring pose, a [catchphrase](#catchphrase). Automatically understood to apply alongside any more specific [tag](#tag) naming a particular meme.

entries.name: gameplay_mechanics
entries.description: Pictures and comics that play on a game's rules and systems, especially where those rules make [no](#no) sense outside the game. Also covers characters shown acting out in-game relationships such as one being weak against another.

entries.name: name_connection
entries.description: A joke, reference or pairing [resting](#resting) on two characters or things [sharing](#sharing) the same or a similar name, such as a [crossover](#crossover) between namesakes from separate franchises. Relatives with a [family](#family) name in common and alternate versions of one character do not count; add object namesake where the namesake is an [animal](#animal) or object.

entries.name: voice_actor_connection
entries.description: A [crossover](#crossover), [cosplay](#cosplay) or [parody](#parody) that hinges on characters [sharing](#sharing) a voice actor, or a character drawn with or [imitating](#imitating) their actor. Tag the actor's name as [well](#well); add [voice_actor](#voice_actor) only if the actor is physically present or cosplayed.

entries.name: pun
entries.description: The picture's joke rests on wordplay, or on an expression shown literally. Since the play is often on Japanese, it should be explained in a [note](#note) or comment when the joke would not land for an English reader.

entries.name: too_many
entries.description: An absurd quantity of one thing crowding the picture, such as [too_many_cats](#too_many_cats), [too_many_frills](#too_many_frills) or a [pile](#pile) of books. Prefer the specific too_many_x [tag](#tag) when one exists.

entries.name: instant_loss
entries.description: A short sequence in which a confident character is [beaten](#beaten) almost at once, set up in one image and undone in the next. It is often sexual and paired with [mating_press](#mating_press), though it need not be, and the two halves [can](#can) be separate pictures.

entries.name: object_namesake
entries.description: A visual [pun](#pun) in which a character appears beside an object or [animal](#animal) whose name is also theirs, such as a girl called Yuri [carrying](#carrying) lilies. The joke rests entirely on the name, which makes it a kind of [name_connection](#name_connection).

entries.name: too_literal
entries.description: A word or name attached to the subject is drawn out in its literal sense, so an idiom or a [pun](#pun) becomes a picture. The joke lives entirely in the mismatch.

entries.name: anatomical_nonsense
entries.description: A body is drawn in a way that openly refuses how bodies work, usually for a laugh. It is neither [clumsy](#clumsy) [anatomy](#anatomy) nor an accepted shorthand like [chibi](#chibi) proportions, but a wholesale disregard for both.

entries.name: bait_and_switch
entries.description: The picture reads as one thing at first [glance](#glance) and proves to be something else once you look properly, most often a scene that seems sexual and turns out entirely innocent. The gap between the two readings is the whole point.

entries.name: irony
entries.description: The outcome runs directly against what the setup led anyone to expect. It also covers the dramatic kind, where the viewer holds a piece of knowledge a character lacks.

entries.name: flat_chest_joke
entries.description: A picture built on [teasing](#teasing) someone for having [no](#no) bust, through dialogue, a [side-by-side](#side-by-side) [comparison](#comparison) or an outsized reaction. The [gag](#gag) has to be the subject, not an incidental body type.

entries.name: date_pun
entries.description: A joke that reads a calendar date as a word, which Japanese allows because digits stand in for syllables. The twenty-ninth of November as good [meat](#meat) [day](#day) is the stock example, and the picture illustrates the wordplay.

entries.name: euphemism
entries.description: Something blunt is swapped for a milder stand-in: a [bowl](#bowl) of [rice](#rice) [hiding](#hiding) what is under a [skirt](#skirt), a symbol replaced with a harmless one, a word misspelt on purpose to slip past a filter. The substitution itself is the joke.

entries.name: moe_(phrase)
entries.description: The word moe itself as the subject of the picture: lettered somewhere in it, or made the point of the joke. Artwork that merely feels endearing does not qualify, since that impression is far too subjective to [tag](#tag).

entries.name: explosion_gag
entries.description: A blast used as a punchline: soot-blackened faces, hair [standing](#standing) on end, small figures flung out of the [smoke](#smoke). Comedy rather than combat.

entries.name: double_entendre
entries.description: A line of dialogue or a [caption](#caption) that reads innocently on the surface while [carrying](#carrying) a second, usually sexual, meaning. The joke lives in the wording rather than in what is drawn.

entries.name: zoomer_slang
entries.description: Generation Z [internet](#internet) slang written into a picture's dialogue or captions, the kind of vocabulary that spreads through short-form [video](#video) platforms. It marks the wording used rather than the age of whoever is speaking.

entries.name: looking_for_glasses
entries.description: Somebody gropes about helplessly for missing eyewear, [squinting](#squinting) at nothing while the [glasses](#glasses) often sit pushed up on their own head. A stock [comic](#comic) beat in Japanese art.

entries.name: fat_joke
entries.description: A [gag](#gag) built on a character's [weight](#weight), usually with a punchline panel or a startled reaction. The humour is the point rather than the body itself.

entries.name: personification
entries.description: An object, [animal](#animal) or non-humanoid [creature](#creature) reimagined as a human or humanoid, the Japanese gijinka. Turning an already humanoid being into a human is [humanization](#humanization), and series built entirely on the [idea](#idea) are not tagged this way.

entries.name: animalization
entries.description: A human or humanlike character [redrawn](#redrawn) as an [animal](#animal), keeping recognisable colours, marks or [accessories](#accessories). Not the same as [animification](#animification), which puts non-anime characters into anime style; where the original person appears beside the beast, add [person_and_animalization](#person_and_animalization).

entries.name: humanization
entries.description: An already humanoid character such as a [furry](#furry), [android](#android), [monster](#monster) girl or humanoid [mecha](#mecha) is drawn more human than usual, with fur, [horns](#horns), [wings](#wings) or odd skin [toned](#toned) down or removed. For animals, creatures and non-humanoid machines use [personification](#personification) instead.

entries.name: material_growth
entries.description: Crystal, stone, [bone](#bone), wood or another foreign substance sprouting from a character's skin, from a small [patch](#patch) to a body being overtaken entirely. Falls under the wider [umbrella](#umbrella) of physical [transformation](#transformation).

entries.name: corruption
entries.description: A character turning from good to evil, or from innocent to lewd, marked by darkening colours, [glowing](#glowing) eyes or a changed outfit. It covers the change itself as [well](#well) as the finished corrupted version.

entries.name: transformation
entries.description: A character's body physically changing into another form, [caught](#caught) mid-change or shown in a before-and-after pair. Add the specific kind, such as [genderswap](#genderswap), [animalization](#animalization) or [petrification](#petrification), when it is clear.

entries.name: fusion
entries.description: Two or more characters or things merged into one new being that mixes their traits. Reserved for invented fusions; ones that happen in the original work are not tagged.

entries.name: monsterification
entries.description: An ordinary human being turned into a monstrous one — [mermaid](#mermaid), [lamia](#lamia), [centaur](#centaur), slime girl and so on. The reverse direction, a [monster](#monster) made human, is [humanization](#humanization).

entries.name: creature_and_personification
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) or [creature](#creature) and its humanised version share the picture, for instance a [cat](#cat) drawn beside the girl who personifies it. Both forms have to be present.

entries.name: furrification
entries.description: A character who is human or humanoid in the original work [redrawn](#redrawn) as a [furry](#furry). The result has to meet the furry standard, not merely [animal](#animal) ears or a [plain](#plain) animal shape; anyone already furry in canon is excluded.

entries.name: mechanization
entries.description: A person or object shown being turned into a [robot](#robot), [cyborg](#cyborg) or other [machine](#machine), either mid-process or as a before-and-after pairing. The machine counterpart of other body [transformation](#transformation) themes.

entries.name: petrification
entries.description: A living body turning to stone or metal, or the finished [statue](#statue) left behind. Common in gorgon and curse scenes, and also used for the fetish of freezing somebody mid-pose.

entries.name: henshin
entries.description: A [transformation](#transformation) sequence in the Japanese style, as in magical-girl, masked-hero and [mecha](#mecha) shows. It takes in the pose, the glow of the change and the [costume](#costume) forming around the character.

entries.name: partial_humanization
entries.description: An [animal](#animal) or other non-human given some human traits while keeping much of its original shape, [landing](#landing) between the [creature](#creature) and a full [humanization](#humanization). The result reads as neither one nor the other.

entries.name: objectification
entries.description: A character is depicted as a thing rather than a person: furniture, a [statue](#statue), a [toy](#toy), a decoration. It runs the opposite way from [personification](#personification) and is often played as a [transformation](#transformation) or a fetish.

entries.name: personality_switch
entries.description: Characters whose personalities have plainly been swapped while each keeps their own body, memories and identity, so a timid one turns brash. A swap of bodies rather than temperaments is something else.

entries.name: dissolving
entries.description: A character or object turning to [liquid](#liquid) or [smoke](#smoke) and mingling with it. Going [transparent](#transparent) is [fading](#fading), [dripping](#dripping) is [melting](#melting), and [breaking](#breaking) into [shards](#shards) is [disintegration](#disintegration).

entries.name: person_and_animalization
entries.description: A character shown together with an [animal](#animal) version of themselves in one picture, the two side by side.

entries.name: body_switch
entries.description: Two characters trade bodies outright, memories and sense of self included. Something in the picture has to show the exchange; a change of manner alone is only a personality [switch](#switch).

entries.name: vehicle_and_personification
entries.description: A vehicle is drawn together with the character who embodies it, the [machine](#machine) and its human form [sharing](#sharing) the same frame. Common in ship-girl and plane-girl artwork.

entries.name: fading
entries.description: A character is [dissolving](#dissolving) out of existence, drawn part [transparent](#transparent) or thinning away from one end of the body. Not a [translucent](#translucent) [inset](#inset) [figure](#figure), a zoom layer behind the subject, or an [x-ray](#x-ray) view through somebody.

entries.name: product_girl
entries.description: A girl drawn as the embodiment of a [branded](#branded) product, wearing its colours, packaging or shape as clothing. Parts of the item may be built into her body or extend from it. A mascot-style [personification](#personification) rather than a [costume](#costume).

entries.name: weight_gain
entries.description: A character visibly puts on [weight](#weight) and grows fatter, often shown as a before-and-after or a sequence. The resulting body may end up chubby, overweight or [obese](#obese).

entries.name: foodification
entries.description: A character turned into [food](#food) while staying alive and aware, a particular strain of [objectification](#objectification). Food merely made to resemble a character is [character-themed_food](#character-themed_food); add [body_horror](#body_horror) where the result is meant to disturb.

entries.name: disintegration
entries.description: A body or object coming apart into solid fragments, whether [shards](#shards), [petals](#petals) or butterflies, which scatter away. Melting into [liquid](#liquid) or [smoke](#smoke) is [dissolving](#dissolving), and [dripping](#dripping) away is [melting](#melting).

entries.name: gattai
entries.description: Several beings or machines locking together into one larger form, each taking the place of a limb or section. The combining sequence at the [heart](#heart) of super [robot](#robot) stories.

entries.name: zombification
entries.description: A character who is not normally [undead](#undead) shown turned into a [zombie](#zombie), or [caught](#caught) partway through the change. Greying skin, clouded eyes and [spreading](#spreading) decay mark the [transformation](#transformation).

entries.name: stretched_limb
entries.description: An arm or leg drawn out to an impossible length like rubber. A power belonging to elastic characters; for the exercise, [stretching](#stretching) is the right [tag](#tag).

entries.name: transforming_clothes
entries.description: Clothing [caught](#caught) mid-change, one outfit [dissolving](#dissolving) or reshaping into another before the eye. The standard visual shorthand for a magical-girl or hero [transformation](#transformation) sequence.

entries.name: dezombification
entries.description: A character who is [undead](#undead) in their source shown alive and whole, the pallor, wounds and rot taken away. The opposite direction from turning a living character into a [zombie](#zombie).

entries.name: crystallization
entries.description: A body turning to [crystal](#crystal), or [standing](#standing) as the finished crystal form that turning produced. Covers the change part-way through and its end state alike.

entries.name: multiple_fusions
entries.description: Two or more fused characters share one picture, each of them a merger of others in its own right. The fusions need not be related to one another.

entries.name: slimification
entries.description: A character being turned into a slime [creature](#creature), their solid body softening into [translucent](#translucent) goo. Pictures often catch the change midway, with limbs already [melting](#melting) while the face is still recognisable.

entries.name: elasticity
entries.description: A body [stretching](#stretching) far past what [flesh](#flesh) allows, limbs drawn out long and thin before snapping [back](#back). Rubber-hose cartoon physics applied to a character.

entries.name: chimerism
entries.description: Three or more characters merged into one being, a dominant body forming the [core](#core) with a single borrowed trait taken from each of the others. A more [crowded](#crowded) case than an ordinary [fusion](#fusion).

entries.name: aged_down
entries.description: A character drawn younger than they normally are, most often as a small [child](#child). The reverse is [aged_up](#aged_up), and a change that happens inside the story is [age_regression](#age_regression).

entries.name: genderswap
entries.description: A character drawn as the opposite [sex](#sex), whether through a magical change on the page or simply as a reimagining. A mind swapped into someone else's unchanged body is [personality_switch](#personality_switch); add [genderswap_(mtf)](#genderswap_(mtf)) or [genderswap_(ftm)](#genderswap_(ftm)) for the direction.

entries.name: genderswap_(mtf)
entries.description: A character who is normally male drawn as female. One [branch](#branch) of [genderswap](#genderswap), and not the same as inventing a female [personification](#personification) of something that has [no](#no) [sex](#sex).

entries.name: aged_up
entries.description: A character drawn physically older than usual, a teenager shown as a full adult or an adult as elderly. The reverse is [aged_down](#aged_down).

entries.name: genderswap_(ftm)
entries.description: A character who is normally female drawn as male, shown through a flatter chest, a heavier build or a [bulge](#bulge). A girl merely dressed in boys' clothing is [crossdressing](#crossdressing) or [reverse_trap](#reverse_trap) instead.

entries.name: age_progression
entries.description: One character shown at several ages within a single picture, [stepping](#stepping) from younger to older. Without more than one form in the frame it does not apply.

entries.name: genderswap_(otf)
entries.description: A normally sexless, [androgynous](#androgynous) or unstated character drawn as clearly female, marked by [breasts](#breasts) or visible female [anatomy](#anatomy). Feminine clothing alone does not qualify unless the fit makes the absence of a [bulge](#bulge) unmistakable.

entries.name: age_regression
entries.description: A character becomes younger inside the story, with something in the picture showing this is a real change and not a [flashback](#flashback) or a childhood [portrait](#portrait). What is left is a de-aged version of the same person.

entries.name: recursive_genderswap
entries.description: A character who is already a gender-flipped take on an earlier [figure](#figure) gets flipped once more, [landing](#landing) [back](#back) near the original [sex](#sex). A well-known example is a male take on a heroine who was herself already a female version of a male legend.

entries.name: age_switch
entries.description: Two characters trade ages, the older turning young and the younger grown up. The exchange runs both ways, unlike a single [figure](#figure) simply drawn older or younger.

entries.name: genderswap_(otm)
entries.description: A normally sexless, [androgynous](#androgynous) or unstated character drawn as clearly male, marked by [pectorals](#pectorals) or visible male [anatomy](#anatomy). One [branch](#branch) of the wider [genderswap](#genderswap) [family](#family).

entries.name: size_difference
entries.description: The picture makes a point of two or more characters being very different in size, as with [giantess](#giantess), [minigirl](#minigirl) or [giant](#giant) male scenes. Ordinary short-versus-tall [contrast](#contrast) is [height_difference](#height_difference) instead; a body-part contrast is [breast_envy](#breast_envy) or [penis_size_difference](#penis_size_difference).

entries.name: mini_person
entries.description: A person drawn extraordinarily small compared to their surroundings, whether set against a [giant](#giant) environment or ordinary-sized characters. A visible [doll](#doll) doesn't count; use [minigirl](#minigirl) or [miniboy](#miniboy) when the person's [sex](#sex) is clear.

entries.name: minigirl
entries.description: A girl drawn extraordinarily small compared to her surroundings or the [people](#people) around her. A visible [doll](#doll) doesn't count, and a merely small girl is [petite](#petite) instead; the male counterpart is [miniboy](#miniboy), and tiny creatures fall under minimized.

entries.name: giant
entries.description: A person, humanoid or [monster](#monster) drawn far larger than everything around it, often taller than the buildings. Oversized animals, things and weapons use [oversized_animal](#oversized_animal), [oversized_object](#oversized_object) and [huge_weapon](#huge_weapon) instead.

entries.name: giantess
entries.description: A female character drawn far larger than her normal-sized surroundings or companions. The female counterpart to [giant](#giant).

entries.name: oversized_object
entries.description: Someone holds or handles a thing much larger than it should be relative to them. A tiny character with a normal item counts when actually handling it, and a [weapon](#weapon) built big by design is [huge_weapon](#huge_weapon) rather than this.

entries.name: miniboy
entries.description: A male character drawn extraordinarily small next to his surroundings, the male counterpart to [minigirl](#minigirl). Tiny non-human creatures and animals fall under minimized instead.

entries.name: oversized_animal
