entries.description: An [animal](#animal) drawn far larger than it could ever be, such as a [house](#house) [cat](#cat) the size of a [horse](#horse) or of a [building](#building). Where instead the person is tiny beside a normal animal, [minigirl](#minigirl) or [miniboy](#miniboy) is the right [tag](#tag).

entries.name: oversized_food
entries.description: Food blown up to many times its proper size: a [strawberry](#strawberry) as big as a [ball](#ball), an [ice](#ice) [cream](#cream) taller than the person [eating](#eating) it.

entries.name: giant_male
entries.description: A male [figure](#figure) drawn hugely out of proportion to the buildings, [people](#people) or [landscape](#landscape) around him. The counterpart to [giantess](#giantess).

entries.name: oversized_flower
entries.description: A [bloom](#bloom) drawn on a scale [no](#no) real [plant](#plant) reaches, sometimes as [tall](#tall) as the character [standing](#standing) next to it. Used as much for decoration as for a literally [giant](#giant) [flower](#flower).

entries.name: giant_brush
entries.description: A painting or [calligraphy](#calligraphy) brush far too big to grip in one hand, hauled or swung with the whole body. Add the calligraphy or art brush [tag](#tag) as fits; an ordinary brush beside a tiny character does not count.

entries.name: giant_snake
entries.description: A serpent far bigger than any real species, thick enough to coil around a [building](#building) or a person. Used for guardian beasts, summoned creatures and monsters.

entries.name: giant_tree
entries.description: A [tree](#tree) on a scale [no](#no) real one reaches, rivalling a [tower](#tower) or [skyscraper](#skyscraper) in [height](#height). Often the landmark a whole [fantasy](#fantasy) [landscape](#landscape) is built around.

entries.name: giant_hand
entries.description: An enormous hand [reaching](#reaching) into the frame, dwarfing whatever it comes near. Its owner is usually out of view, which makes the scale the whole point.

entries.name: oversized_insect
entries.description: A [bug](#bug) scaled up until it stands as [tall](#tall) as a person, drawn as a wild [creature](#creature). Characters who merely carry insect features are a separate matter; here the [animal](#animal) itself is enormous.

entries.name: giant_mushroom
entries.description: Fungi swollen to an impossible size, [standing](#standing) as [tall](#tall) as a person or a [tree](#tree). A fixture of fairy-tale forests and [alien](#alien) wilderness.

entries.name: oversized_plant
entries.description: Leaves, stems and shoots drawn on a [giant](#giant) scale, towering over the characters beside them. Sets [fantasy](#fantasy) scenes, or ones where the [cast](#cast) has been shrunk.

entries.name: oversized_spoon
entries.description: A [spoon](#spoon) drawn far larger than it should be, sometimes big enough to sit in or to need both arms. Turns up in [dessert](#dessert) fantasies and in [gag](#gag) pictures.

entries.name: defeat
entries.description: A character [beaten](#beaten) in a fight or knocked out of a game, [caught](#caught) at the moment of losing or in the slump afterwards. The opposite of [victory](#victory).

entries.name: forced
entries.description: A character is being made to do something against their will. It is not the [tag](#tag) for [rape](#rape) itself, though both apply when a picture also shows coercion unrelated to the rape.

entries.name: death
entries.description: People, creatures or animals shown dead or [dying](#dying), or a scene making [plain](#plain) that a death is taking place. Where only the aftermath [can](#can) be inferred, [implied_death](#implied_death) fits better, and the reaper [figure](#figure) is death_(entity).

entries.name: damaged
entries.description: An object bearing visible harm that still works and still does its job. Once it stops functioning, [broken](#broken) takes over, and a damaged garment goes to [torn_clothes](#torn_clothes) instead.

entries.name: hiding
entries.description: Someone is plainly taking [cover](#cover) behind a person or an object, part of them out of sight. Peering round the edge of whatever conceals them is the usual framing.

entries.name: caught
entries.description: A character is discovered part-way through something embarrassing, freezing or [panicking](#panicking) as somebody walks in. The act may be sexual or entirely innocent.

entries.name: jealous
entries.description: A character plainly resents somebody else receiving attention or affection they feel belongs to them, often [glaring](#glaring) at a [couple](#couple) or a rival. It differs from [envy](#envy), which is wanting what another person has.

entries.name: walk-in
entries.description: Someone walks in on an intimate or embarrassing scene already under way, to the surprise and usually dismay of those involved. The intruder's reaction is often the focus.

entries.name: destruction
entries.description: Something is being wrecked as the picture happens, frequently with [debris](#debris) [flying](#flying). The settled aftermath goes to [ruins](#ruins), [rubble](#rubble) or [broken](#broken) instead.

entries.name: tied_up_(nonsexual)
entries.description: A person [bound](#bound) with [rope](#rope) or similar in a comedic, criminal or adventure context with [no](#no) sexual framing. Anything BDSM-flavoured belongs to [bondage](#bondage) instead.

entries.name: fourth_wall
entries.description: A character acknowledges being inside a work of fiction, by speaking to the [audience](#audience) or handling parts of the medium such as their own speech [bubble](#bubble). The barrier between story and reader is treated as a thing that [can](#can) be crossed.

entries.name: failure
entries.description: A character does not manage what they set out to do, or a thing does not work as intended: [burnt](#burnt) [cooking](#cooking), a dropped catch, a plan that collapses. Usually played for comedy.

entries.name: heropin
entries.description: A costumed heroine [caught](#caught) in a losing spot: cornered, seized, [beaten](#beaten) down or about to be. The genre is built around the [peril](#peril) itself rather than any [rescue](#rescue).

entries.name: bad_end
entries.description: A grim or tragic close to the story: a character dead, taken, corrupted, or a [monster](#monster) closing in as the scene stops. Bad refers to the outcome and never to the [quality](#quality) of the art, and a joking fake game-over [screen](#screen) counts only when the scene is genuinely dire.

entries.name: role_reversal
entries.description: Two characters swap their usual traits or roles, such as heights, jobs or who does the chores. Swapping only [clothes](#clothes) is [costume_switch](#costume_switch), only personalities is [personality_switch](#personality_switch), and dominant-submissive flips fall under [reversible_couple](#reversible_couple).

entries.name: confession
entries.description: A character declares love, or reacts to somebody declaring it, typically with a [letter](#letter), a [blush](#blush) and [nervous](#nervous) hands. Add [pov](#pov) when the viewer is the other [party](#party); asking for marriage is [marriage_proposal](#marriage_proposal).

entries.name: captured
entries.description: A character has been taken [prisoner](#prisoner): [bound](#bound), caged, held at weapon-point or hauled away by captors. It is the predicament that is recorded, not the particular restraint.

entries.name: weight_conscious
entries.description: A character, often a girl, is [unhappy](#unhappy) about her [weight](#weight), typically after [stepping](#stepping) on a scale, [pinching](#pinching) her [belly](#belly) or eyeing a [snack](#snack). A mood and situation rather than a body type.

entries.name: flashback
entries.description: A character is pulled [back](#back) into a past event without meaning to, set off by a [sound](#sound), a [smell](#smell) or a stray thought, and typically drawn as a faded or framed [inset](#inset). Calling something to mind deliberately is [remembering](#remembering).

entries.name: violence
entries.description: Force being inflicted on somebody, whether a slapstick beating or a grim assault. It simply marks that a violent act is happening, at any level of seriousness.

entries.name: digging_your_own_grave
entries.description: A character turning the earth on a [grave](#grave) meant for themselves, or acting in a way that plainly seals their own fate. Played straight as doom, though more often as a joke about a self-inflicted mess.

entries.name: theft
entries.description: Someone takes property that is not theirs, whether pickpocketing, shoplifting or snatching an item from another character. Add [thief](#thief) when the role defines the character.

entries.name: human_scabbard
entries.description: An object, usually a [weapon](#weapon), is drawn out of a character's body without harming them, by [magic](#magic) or by a built-in mechanism. It is neither impalement, stabbing nor object insertion, since [no](#no) wound and no ordinary [opening](#opening) is involved.

entries.name: war
entries.description: Armed conflict between nations or factions is the subject, whether an actual [battle](#battle), its aftermath of [death](#death) and ruin, or a symbolic treatment. Historical and fictional wars both count.

entries.name: abuse
entries.description: One person mistreats another for their own benefit, most often physically. It needs both halves shown: [injury](#injury) inflicted, and a victim who is visibly frightened or distressed.

entries.name: kidnapped
entries.description: Someone is being held against their will — [bound](#bound), [gagged](#gagged), shut in a room or otherwise confined. When the seizing itself is on [screen](#screen), [kidnapping](#kidnapping) fits better.

entries.name: good_end
entries.description: A picture of a story ending [well](#well), the counterpart to [bad_end](#bad_end). Often a [caption](#caption) on a comic's last panel or a [parody](#parody) of a game's ending [screen](#screen).

entries.name: trapped
entries.description: Someone shut in and unable to get free, whether wedged inside a [container](#container), locked in a room, or [pinned](#pinned) under [rubble](#rubble). The word also stretches to a figurative bind or a [sticky](#sticky) situation the character cannot easily leave.

entries.name: copy_ability
entries.description: A character reproduces somebody else's powers or techniques as their own, mimicking a rival's move or taking on a copied shape. The borrowing itself is what the picture is about.

entries.name: misunderstanding
entries.description: A comedy [device](#device) where one character misreads another's words or actions, classically someone [walking](#walking) in on an innocent scene that looks compromising.

entries.name: bullying
entries.description: One or more characters intimidate, humiliate or hurt somebody weaker — [pulling](#pulling) hair, striking, defacing a [desk](#desk), jeering. The imbalance is the point; two equals brawling is not this.

entries.name: meta
entries.description: A character engaging with their own series as though they were an ordinary fan in the real world - [watching](#watching) the show or [playing](#playing) the game they themselves come from. A form of self-aware [crossover](#crossover) between a story and its own [audience](#audience).

entries.name: protecting
entries.description: One character steps between another person, or an object, and some danger, shielding them with a raised arm or their own body. The [threat](#threat) itself may be shown or only implied.

entries.name: accident
entries.description: A character lands in trouble through clumsiness or [plain](#plain) bad luck. Mishaps that bare the body, [slipping](#slipping) garments and [road](#road) collisions each have their own narrower tags.

entries.name: suicide
entries.description: A character taking their own life, shown either mid-act or already dead by their own hand. A failed or [interrupted](#interrupted) attempt belongs under [attempted_suicide](#attempted_suicide), and mere intent under [imminent_suicide](#imminent_suicide).

entries.name: mundane_utility
entries.description: Superpowers, [magic](#magic) or advanced gadgets turned to everyday chores: [groceries](#groceries) lifted by [telekinesis](#telekinesis), a [cigarette](#cigarette) lit off an enchanted blade. The comedy comes from the mismatch between the ability and the errand.

entries.name: marriage_proposal
entries.description: One character asking another to marry them, most often down on one knee with a [ring](#ring) held out. A first declaration of love without the offer is a [confession](#confession) instead.

entries.name: entangled
entries.description: A limb or a piece of clothing has [caught](#caught) in a heap of [rope](#rope), cord, [wire](#wire) or [thread](#thread) and the character cannot get loose. Deliberate [tying](#tying) is [bondage](#bondage) or tied_up; limbs tangled together while snuggling is [cuddling](#cuddling).

entries.name: clothes_theft
entries.description: Somebody makes off with another character's garments, classically while the owner is [bathing](#bathing) or [swimming](#swimming) and [can](#can) do nothing about it. The victim is left stranded with nothing to wear.

entries.name: disguise
entries.description: A character altering their look to pass for somebody else, with a [wig](#wig), borrowed [clothes](#clothes), a [mask](#mask) or a hasty [costume](#costume). Whether anybody is actually fooled makes [no](#no) difference.

entries.name: crucifixion
entries.description: A character [bound](#bound) or nailed to a [cross](#cross), a [stake](#stake) or a similar frame with the arms spread wide. No cross is strictly needed, and the pose is borrowed for religious allusion at least as often as it stands for an [execution](#execution).

entries.name: imminent_death
entries.description: A character placed a [heartbeat](#heartbeat) away from being killed. It differs from [dying](#dying), where the fatal harm has already been done, and from [peril](#peril), where the danger is real but nothing has struck yet.

entries.name: buried
entries.description: A subject covered over by loose material — [sand](#sand), [snow](#snow), earth, leaves — with only part of them still showing. Beach gags and figures lost under a drift are the common cases.

entries.name: tied_to_chair
entries.description: Rope, [tape](#tape), belts or chains hold somebody down onto a seat so they cannot rise. Covers interrogation and capture scenes as readily as playful restraint.

entries.name: kidnapping
entries.description: The moment of grabbing someone and [carrying](#carrying) them off against their will. Snatchings by aliens, saucers or [tractor](#tractor) beams are tagged as [abduction](#abduction).

entries.name: accidental_pervert
entries.description: Someone ends up [groping](#groping), uncovering or [landing](#landing) on another person purely by chance, typically through a [collision](#collision) or a fall. Whether the culprit is actually lecherous is beside the point.

entries.name: peril
entries.description: The subject is in immediate danger and will not come through it without escape or [rescue](#rescue): tied to a track, [hanging](#hanging) over a drop, cornered by something lethal. The [threat](#threat) has not landed yet.

entries.name: for_adoption
entries.description: A character presented as needing a new home, with a [cardboard](#cardboard) [box](#box), a written plea, or wide pleading eyes. The offer has to be stated in the picture rather than merely implied by somebody [sitting](#sitting) in a [carton](#carton).

entries.name: after_battle
entries.description: The aftermath of a fight: churned ground, dropped weapons, [smoke](#smoke), and figures who are wounded or simply worn out. Nobody is still striking a blow, which is what separates it from a picture of the [fighting](#fighting) itself.

entries.name: coronavirus_pandemic
entries.description: The picture refers to the [2020](#2020) outbreak: emptied shelves, cancelled gatherings, [people](#people) kept apart, or a [note](#note) from the artist saying as much. A character merely wearing a [mask](#mask) is not enough on its own.

entries.name: rejection
entries.description: A character turns down what is being offered, such as a [confession](#confession), a [gift](#gift), or [food](#food). Only the one doing the refusing has to be in the picture; the refused [party](#party) may be out of frame.

entries.name: food_theft
entries.description: Someone taking [food](#food) that is not theirs, snatched off a [plate](#plate) or lifted from a [shop](#shop). Between [friends](#friends) and couples it usually reads as [teasing](#teasing) affection rather than crime.

entries.name: crime_prevention_buzzer_threat
entries.description: A character reaches for the cord of a personal alarm, ready to set it off at whoever is behaving suspiciously. Almost always played as a joke.

entries.name: stalking
entries.description: Someone persistently [following](#following) another without their knowledge or consent, whether out of obsession, to intimidate them, or to dig up something private. Often drawn as a [figure](#figure) [watching](#watching) from behind a [corner](#corner) or a [pole](#pole).

entries.name: underwear_theft
entries.description: One character is shown taking, [carrying](#carrying) off, or having already made away with somebody else's bras or [panties](#panties). A comedy [staple](#staple), often with the [thief](#thief) [caught](#caught) mid-act or gloating over the loot.

entries.name: late_for_school
entries.description: The stock scene of a pupil bolting out of the [door](#door) after oversleeping, half dressed with a slice of [toast](#toast) clamped in the mouth. Colliding with a stranger who turns out to matter later is part of the joke.

entries.name: ruined_for_marriage
entries.description: The stock reaction of a character, usually female, despairing that they [can](#can) never be wed now that they have been shamed or exposed. It is signalled by a spoken line to that effect, or wordlessly by one character looking satisfied while the other weeps and hides their face.

entries.name: blackmail
entries.description: One character forces another's hand by threatening to reveal a secret or by [holding](#holding) something over them. The leverage, a photograph or a captive for instance, is often part of the picture.

entries.name: imminent_suicide
entries.description: A character shown moments before taking their own life, the means already in place. The act itself is not drawn.

entries.name: love_triangle
entries.description: Two characters are drawn to the same third person, and the picture makes the [rivalry](#rivalry) legible through glances, gestures or where [everyone](#everyone) stands. The competing feelings, not the pairing itself, are what it records.

entries.name: unusually_visible
entries.description: A character normally kept unseen or [invisible](#invisible) is drawn plainly visible for once, the novelty being that the viewer finally gets a look at someone usually hidden.

entries.name: implied_murder
entries.description: A killing that happens outside the frame, understood from the aftermath: a [silhouette](#silhouette), a spatter on a wall, a [sound](#sound) effect, the shock on a face. The act is never drawn.

entries.name: arrest
entries.description: A character is being taken into custody by [police](#police) or guards, generally [cuffed](#cuffed) and held or marched away. Handcuffs and a uniformed officer are the usual signs.

entries.name: poverty
entries.description: Want made visible: threadbare [clothes](#clothes), bare rooms, empty bowls, coins counted out one by one. Slums and ramshackle housing often set the scene.

entries.name: 2011_tohoku_earthquake_and_tsunami
entries.description: The magnitude nine quake off north-eastern Japan in March [2011](#2011) and the tsunami it set off. Pictures range from memorial and encouragement pieces to depictions of the wave and the [wreckage](#wreckage) it left.

entries.name: cheating_(competitive)
entries.description: Somebody breaks the rules of a game or contest to win, by a hidden aid, sabotage or a look at the other side's hand. It has nothing to do with unfaithfulness in a relationship.

entries.name: implied_death
entries.description: Context tells the viewer a character has died without a body or a cause being shown. Empty [clothes](#clothes), a [grave](#grave), a framed [portrait](#portrait) or the bearing of the survivors carry it.

entries.name: swimsuit_theft
entries.description: One character making off with another's [swimsuit](#swimsuit), or already [holding](#holding) it while its owner is left stranded without it. The [prank](#prank) framing and the victim's predicament are the point.

entries.name: abduction
entries.description: Someone is carried off by a [flying](#flying) [saucer](#saucer) or something dressed up as one, typically lifted skyward in a beam of light. An ordinary snatch-and-grab belongs under [kidnapping](#kidnapping) instead.

entries.name: boss_fight
entries.description: The scene is staged as the climactic encounter with a [video](#video) game boss, or simply carries that air: a lone challenger, a towering opponent, sometimes a health bar or an [arena](#arena) to match.

entries.name: revenge
entries.description: A character paying somebody [back](#back) for a past wrong, from a petty [prank](#prank) in return to lethal retribution. The picture usually makes the earlier offence legible through expression or context.

entries.name: pitfall
entries.description: A concealed [hole](#hole) dug as a trap, its mouth hidden under leaves or boards until someone drops through. Both comedy gags and adventure scenes lean on it.

entries.name: car_crash
entries.description: A [car](#car) or other wheeled vehicle striking a person or an object, drawn before, during or after the impact. Wreckage, scattered [glass](#glass) and injuries usually follow.

entries.name: narcissism
entries.description: A character absorbed in their own image, gazing at a [reflection](#reflection), a [portrait](#portrait) or a double of themselves. Mirrors, clones and replicas are the usual staging.

entries.name: auction
entries.description: Goods, or sometimes [people](#people), are put up for bidding before a [crowd](#crowd). A block, a [numbered](#numbered) lot or a [forest](#forest) of raised hands shows the [sale](#sale) in progress.

entries.name: age_conscious
entries.description: Someone is reminded of how [old](#old) they really are, or treated to match it, while insisting they are older, younger or more grown-up than they look. The gap between how they are seen and how they see themselves carries the picture.

entries.name: stuck_in_a_box
entries.description: Two characters crammed together inside a [container](#container) barely big enough for them, [forced](#forced) into close contact by the [cramped](#cramped) [space](#space). Played either for romance or for comedy.

entries.name: death_flag
entries.description: A line or [gesture](#gesture) that telegraphs a character's coming [death](#death): promising to return, finally winning the person they love, [waving](#waving) off a warning. The picture plays the foreshadowing, often as a joke.

entries.name: rescue
entries.description: One character [pulling](#pulling) another out of danger, be it a fall, a [fire](#fire), [drowning](#drowning), or an attacker. The saving may also be emotional rather than physical.

entries.name: reincarnation
entries.description: Two characters are shown as the same soul across different lives, one being the reborn version of the other. Also covers unnamed figures meant to be a later life of a known character.

entries.name: destroyed
entries.description: Something has been wrecked outright: a smashed [building](#building), a [shattered](#shattered) [machine](#machine), [rubble](#rubble) where a [structure](#structure) stood. Shows the aftermath rather than the moment of [breaking](#breaking).

entries.name: muscle_envy
entries.description: One character eyeing another's bigger build with open jealousy, most often a flat chest set beside a [heavy](#heavy) pair of [pectorals](#pectorals). It mirrors breast [envy](#envy) and is generally played for laughs.

entries.name: interrupted
entries.description: Something is [broken](#broken) off part-way by an unexpected arrival or noise, and the [people](#people) [caught](#caught) in it turn startled toward the intrusion. Private moments cut short are the usual case.

entries.name: racism
entries.description: The picture's content is an [insult](#insult) directed at a race, real or invented. It also covers jabs aimed at nationalities and ethnic groups that are not races in the strict sense.

entries.name: goodbye
entries.description: A leave-taking: a hand raised to a departing [figure](#figure), a farewell in the dialogue, or a last look over the shoulder. Platforms, doorways and turned backs go with it.

entries.name: hikikomori
entries.description: Somebody who has withdrawn from the world and stayed shut inside their home or [bedroom](#bedroom) for months on end. Pictures usually show a cluttered room, [curtains](#curtains) drawn and a [screen](#screen) for company.

entries.name: escape_room
entries.description: People shut into a room who must work out how to get out, with locks, hidden clues and a ticking [clock](#clock). In drawn work the premise is often bent into a setup for something else entirely.

entries.name: booby_trap
entries.description: A concealed [device](#device) rigged to catch, hurt or startle whoever sets it off, whether a pit in the ground or a [bucket](#bucket) balanced on a [door](#door). The victim generally has [no](#no) [idea](#idea) until the instant it fires.

entries.name: seppuku
entries.description: The [samurai](#samurai) rite of [suicide](#suicide) by [opening](#opening) one's own [belly](#belly) with a short blade, often with a second [standing](#standing) ready to behead. Depicted as atonement, sentence, or protest.

entries.name: implied_suicide
entries.description: A self-inflicted [death](#death) that happens off [screen](#screen) or is signalled only by objects, a [hanging](#hanging) [noose](#noose) being the stock example. The act is never depicted.

entries.name: attempted_suicide
entries.description: A [suicide](#suicide) that did not succeed, the character still alive because the attempt went wrong or somebody stepped in. What is shown is generally the aftermath rather than the act.

entries.name: hostage
entries.description: Somebody is held captive against their will, often with a captor's arm or [weapon](#weapon) across them. Use it only where the picture or its text makes the situation [plain](#plain); a merely tied-up character is not one.

entries.name: betrayal
entries.description: One character breaks another's trust, by [lying](#lying), switching sides, [giving](#giving) away a secret or turning on the person who relied on them. The picture usually catches the moment of realisation, and the stakes need not be [grave](#grave).

entries.name: nipples
entries.description: Bare nipples visible on [breasts](#breasts) or on a man's chest. When they show only as raised bumps under [fabric](#fabric) use [covered_nipples](#covered_nipples); the two go together only where the clothing is see-through.

entries.name: nude
entries.description: Nothing worn on the chest or the [crotch](#crotch), though hats, [gloves](#gloves), legwear, jewellery and small [accessories](#accessories) may stay on, as may [pasties](#pasties) or a covering hand or object. Wearing nothing whatever is [completely_nude](#completely_nude), and it is never combined with the partial tags such as [topless](#topless), [bottomless](#bottomless), [no_bra](#no_bra) or [no_panties](#no_panties).

entries.name: completely_nude
entries.description: Nothing at all worn from the [neck](#neck) down, with the [crotch](#crotch) or lower in view. Glasses, hats, jewellery, small bands and a merely held [towel](#towel) are allowed, while [rope](#rope), belts or a towel tied on leave it as [nude](#nude) or [naked_towel](#naked_towel).

entries.name: bottomless
entries.description: A top is worn but nothing at all below the waist, leaving the [crotch](#crotch) bare. It does not apply to full nudity, to [underwear](#underwear) still on ([no_pants](#no_pants)) or to a [skirt](#skirt) [hiding](#hiding) the lack of [panties](#panties) ([no_panties](#no_panties)); [socks](#socks), [thighhighs](#thighhighs) and [shoes](#shoes) leave it [standing](#standing).

entries.name: breasts_out
entries.description: Both [breasts](#breasts) have been pulled out through or over a top that is still being worn, as from an open [collar](#collar) or a dragged-down neckline. Only one out is [one_breast_out](#one_breast_out); a raised or fully opened [shirt](#shirt) is [shirt_lift](#shirt_lift) or [open_clothes](#open_clothes), and a bare [torso](#torso) is [topless](#topless).

entries.name: topless
entries.description: A female character bare from the waist up while wearing bottoms such as [pants](#pants) or a [skirt](#skirt). The lower body must be visibly clothed, else use [nude](#nude); a [bra](#bra) or [bikini](#bikini) top makes it [no_shirt](#no_shirt) instead, and men use [topless_male](#topless_male).

entries.name: clothed_female_nude_male
entries.description: A dressed woman together with a [nude](#nude) man, a [contrast](#contrast) often used to put her in the dominant position. Abbreviated CFNM; the reverse arrangement is [clothed_male_nude_female](#clothed_male_nude_female).

entries.name: fully_nude
entries.description: Nothing at all worn anywhere on the body. Equivalent to [completely_nude](#completely_nude); partial states such as [topless](#topless) or [bottomless](#bottomless) take their own tags.

entries.name: topless_male
entries.description: A male character with nothing on his upper body but clothed below the waist, in [pants](#pants), [shorts](#shorts) or swim trunks. A [jacket](#jacket) with [no](#no) [shirt](#shirt) is [no_shirt](#no_shirt) or [naked_jacket](#naked_jacket); a fully [nude](#nude) man is nude instead.

entries.name: naked_shirt
entries.description: A [shirt](#shirt) worn over bare skin with nothing else beneath, usually [hanging](#hanging) open. Common as a morning-after or borrowed-shirt look, though a fully buttoned one qualifies too.

entries.name: one_breast_out
entries.description: One breast is bared with nipple and areola in view while the other stays inside the clothing. Both out is [breasts_out](#breasts_out), and the covered breast has to be genuinely clothed rather than merely hidden behind an arm or another [figure](#figure).

entries.name: clothed_male_nude_female
entries.description: A dressed man together with a [nude](#nude) woman. Abbreviated CMNF; the reverse arrangement is [clothed_female_nude_male](#clothed_female_nude_male).

entries.name: naked_towel
entries.description: A [towel](#towel) wrapped around the body, usually on the way into or out of a [bath](#bath) or [hot](#hot) spring; add [topless](#topless) or [bottomless](#bottomless) where it covers too little. A towel merely held in front is [nude](#nude) [cover](#cover), and one draped only over the shoulders is nude with [towel_around_neck](#towel_around_neck).

entries.name: naked_apron
entries.description: An [apron](#apron) worn with nothing beneath it, the classic teaser: it covers [breasts](#breasts) and [crotch](#crotch) from the front while leaving the [back](#back) bare. Waist-only aprons leave the chest showing, and with [underwear](#underwear) or a [swimsuit](#swimsuit) underneath, [nearly_naked_apron](#nearly_naked_apron) applies.

entries.name: naked_ribbon
entries.description: A [nude](#nude) or nearly nude character covered only by ribbons, laid so they hide the [nipples](#nipples) or [crotch](#crotch) from the viewer's angle or pass for clothing. Bows are often added to present the subject as a [gift](#gift).

entries.name: nude_cover
entries.description: A naked [figure](#figure) hides most of the body behind something held in front of it, such as a [pillow](#pillow), a [towel](#towel), a [blanket](#blanket) or a sheet.

entries.name: clothed_female_nude_female
entries.description: Two women together, one fully dressed and the other [nude](#nude). The [contrast](#contrast) between them is the whole point of the [tag](#tag), abbreviated CFNF.

entries.name: naked_sweater
entries.description: A character wearing, or appearing to wear, nothing but a [sweater](#sweater). Hats, legwear and footwear do not disqualify it.

entries.name: naked_jacket
entries.description: A [jacket](#jacket) worn straight over bare skin with nothing else beneath, a [gakuran](#gakuran) or track top included. It is usually left open so the body shows.

entries.name: bandaid_on_pussy
entries.description: An adhesive plaster [stuck](#stuck) over the vulva as its only covering, the character otherwise bare there. The [idea](#idea) is close to [maebari](#maebari), but that is a separate object and the two are not tagged together.

entries.name: naked_coat
entries.description: A [coat](#coat) of any sort — [trench](#trench), lab, [rain](#rain) — worn straight over bare skin as the only garment. It is generally left [hanging](#hanging) open or held closed by hand.

entries.name: naked_bandage
entries.description: A [nude](#nude) or nearly nude [figure](#figure) wound in [bandages](#bandages) that serve as makeshift clothing. The wrappings may or may not hide the [nipples](#nipples) and genitals.

entries.name: naked_sheet
entries.description: A [nude](#nude) character partly covered by a [bed](#bed) sheet or [blanket](#blanket), generally [lying](#lying) in bed. It overlaps with under covers.

entries.name: naked_cape
